An attacker-controlled junction / symlink swap during the TOCTOU window redirects the remediation operation against a SYSTEM-owned file, producing arbitrary-file-overwrite escalating to SYSTEM. Picus 'BlueHammer' / RedSun published a working PoC BEFORE Microsoft released a patch — true zero-day disclosure where the EDR is the vulnerability.
attack_vector.privileges_required: low — local user with ability to drop a file Defender will scan
attack_vector.complexity: high — requires winning the TOCTOU race window via symlink swap
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered. Conventional Windows-Defender internals research by Picus Security.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Defender platform-update channel separated from Windows OS-update channel and treated as a distinct patch SLA; ASR (Attack Surface Reduction) rules limiting symlink/junction creation by low-privilege processes in user-writable paths; second-EDR overlay or Defender ASR Block-Persistence-Through-WMI configured to detect post-LPE persistence even when Defender itself is the initial-access vector.
prevention.adequacy: Most operators treat Defender as 'always patched via Windows Update' without recognizing the platform-update channel is a distinct surface; ASR rules require explicit operator opt-in.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Independent EDR overlay (a second-vendor EDR or non-Defender behavioral monitor) capable of detecting Defender-process anomalous file-overwrite patterns; SYSTEM-process spawn monitoring with parentage cross-check; NTFS reparse-point creation auditing in user-writable paths.
detection.adequacy: Single-vendor EDR cannot reliably detect itself as the vulnerability source — by design, Defender is allow-listed in its own telemetry.

response.what_would_have_worked: Pre-rehearsed runbook for EDR-platform-compromise (Defender, CrowdStrike, SentinelOne, Carbon Black) treating compromise of the security control plane as a tier-1 incident; out-of-band telemetry source (network-side EDR-bypass telemetry) for the response window; documented Defender platform-update rollout SLA distinct from Windows OS update.
response.adequacy: EDR-as-vulnerability runbooks are rare; most security teams have no documented response when 'the security control IS the attack vector'.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.7.gap: Anti-malware control assumes the AV/EDR is a defense, not a vulnerability source; offers no model for 'EDR is the attack vector' and provides no compensating-control guidance for the case.

NIST-800-53-SI-3.gap: Malicious-code-protection control treats AV/EDR as a defense layer; no enhancement addresses the case where the malicious-code-protection mechanism itself is the LPE primitive.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: Flaw remediation does not separately enumerate EDR/AV platform-update channels — operators meeting OS-patch SLA may still lag the Defender platform update.

PCI-DSS-4.0-5.2.1.gap: Anti-malware solution requirement does not address EDR-as-vulnerability nor require an independent overlay capable of detecting EDR-platform compromise.

NIS2-Article-21-2-h.gap: Cybersecurity hygiene + training obligation does not address the case where the AV/EDR product is itself the LPE source; pen-test scopes routinely exclude 'security defense' products from in-scope attack surface.

new_control_requirements.name: EDR-AS-VULNERABILITY-SECONDARY-OVERLAY
new_control_requirements.description: Organizations whose primary EDR is also a high-value attack target (Defender, CrowdStrike, SentinelOne) must deploy an independent secondary overlay capable of detecting anomalous behavior by the primary EDR's own processes. The overlay can be a second-vendor behavioral EDR, network-side EDR-bypass telemetry, or out-of-band SYSTEM-process spawn monitoring — but must NOT share trust roots with the primary EDR.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2026-33825 — Defender's file-remediation pipeline was the LPE primitive; Defender's own telemetry cannot reliably surface Defender-as-attacker.

new_control_requirements.name: EDR-PLATFORM-UPDATE-DISTINCT-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: EDR / AV platform-update channels must be tracked as distinct patch surfaces with their own SLA, separate from OS-update SLA. Defender platform updates, CrowdStrike Falcon-sensor updates, SentinelOne agent updates, etc. ship outside the OS-patching cadence and require dedicated monitoring and SLA tracking.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2026-33825 — Defender platform update fixed the TOCTOU; operators tracking only Windows Update missed the patch surface.

new_control_requirements.name: PEN-TEST-SCOPE-INCLUDES-SECURITY-PRODUCTS
new_control_requirements.description: Penetration test and red-team scopes must explicitly include security-defense products (EDR, AV, DLP, identity-providers, secret-managers) as in-scope attack surface, not as defenses to evade. Scope language must call out that these products' admin interfaces, agent processes, and update channels are testable surfaces.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2026-33825 — Defender was the LPE primitive; pen tests scoping Defender as 'defense to evade' rather than 'product to test' miss this class.

compliance_exposure_score.basis: Almost no organizations operate a secondary EDR overlay against their primary EDR; pen-test scopes routinely exclude security products. Audit-passing organizations meeting ISO/NIST/PCI anti-malware controls remain materially exposed because the controls assume the AV/EDR is a defense, not a vulnerability source.

attack_vector.description: Novel supply-chain account-recovery abuse via expired maintainer email domain. The `atlantis-software.net` domain — registered as the contact email for the legitimate node-ipc maintainer npm account — lapsed and was re-registered by an attacker on 2026-05-07 via Namecheap PrivateEmail. The attacker then invoked the npm password-reset flow; the reset link was delivered to the now-attacker-controlled mailbox; the attacker took over the publish-enabled account without ever holding a leaked credential. Three malicious versions (node-ipc 9.1.6, 9.2.3, 12.0.1) were published 2026-05-14 with an 80 KB obfuscated IIFE appended to `node-ipc.cjs`. The payload fires on every `require('node-ipc')` — NOT via a postinstall hook — so consumer-side `npm install --ignore-scripts` does NOT mitigate. Exfiltration covers AWS / GCP / Azure credentials, SSH private keys, Kubernetes kubeconfig, HashiCorp Vault tokens, Claude AI configs, and Kiro IDE configs via DNS TXT queries to an Azure-lookalike spoofed domain. Class: registry-side account-recovery abuse mediated by DNS lifecycle, distinct from token-compromise (Shai-Hulud) and typosquat-orphan-commit (elementary-data) precedents.
attack_vector.privileges_required: downstream consumer runs `npm install` resolving to one of the three malicious versions; payload fires automatically on `require('node-ipc')`
attack_vector.complexity: low for downstream consumers (automatic on require); low for the maintainer-account takeover itself (any attacker monitoring maintainer-email-domain expirations can reproduce)
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered, not AI-built. The novelty is structural — expired-domain → npm password-reset → publish — not algorithmic.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: (1) Continuous WHOIS-expiry monitoring on the email domains of every critical-path package maintainer. (2) Registry-side mandatory MFA on publish-enabled maintainer accounts (npm policy gap as of 2026-05-15). (3) Lockfile pinning to versions published before 2026-05-14T00:00Z, combined with `npm ci` (which refuses lockfile drift) rather than `npm install`. (4) Registry-side hold-period on first-publish-from-recently-recovered-account (npm has no such control today).
prevention.adequacy: WHOIS-expiry monitoring is novel — no current standard treats expired-domain → account-recovery as a distinct supply-chain attack class. `--ignore-scripts` (the canonical npm-supply-chain mitigation since Shai-Hulud) does NOT mitigate this payload because it ships in the main module, not in a postinstall hook. Lockfile pinning works only if the lockfile predates 2026-05-14 AND `npm ci` is used.

detection.what_would_have_worked: DNS-resolver telemetry on developer / CI hosts — the payload's DNS TXT exfiltration channel is invisible to HTTP egress filtering but recordable at any DNS resolver (Resolved, Cloudflare DNS, internal Unbound). File-read telemetry on credential-store paths (~/.aws/credentials, ~/.ssh/id_*, ~/.kube/config, ~/.vault-token, ~/.config/Claude/, ~/.kiro/) within the lifetime of a Node process is a near-deterministic IoC for any credential-stealer in the Node ecosystem.
detection.adequacy: DNS-layer telemetry is the only channel that proves successful exfiltration; HTTP-egress monitoring will miss this class entirely. Most developer endpoints and CI runners do not retain DNS logs.

response.what_would_have_worked: npm yanked the three malicious versions on 2026-05-14. Full credential rotation for every account whose material was reachable from any host that resolved a malicious version during the exposure window — AWS access keys, GCP service-account keys, Azure tokens, SSH private keys, kubeconfig, Vault tokens. Lockfile audit + republication of any downstream package the affected host had npm-publish rights on.
response.adequacy: Yank closes new consumer exposure but does not retroactively un-harvest credentials already exfiltrated via DNS. The DNS exfil channel is one-shot; rotation is the only operational response.

NIST-800-218-SSDF.gap: Reused-OSS-component control assumes maintainer-account integrity; does not address maintainer-email-domain expiry as a supply-chain risk class.

EU-CRA-Art13.gap: SBOM requirement does not address freshness-of-published-version OR maintainer-account-recovery integrity — pinning to a malicious version is SBOM-compliant.

NIS2-Art21-supply-chain.gap: Generic supply chain controls without npm-ecosystem-specific guidance (maintainer-domain-expiry monitoring, registry-account MFA enforcement, main-module-vs-postinstall payload distinction).

SLSA-v1.0-Build-L3.gap: Build provenance attestations assert who built the artifact, not whether `who` is still the legitimate maintainer post-account-recovery.

NIST-800-53-IA-5-Federated.gap: Authenticator-management control covers operator-side credentials only; does not extend to upstream-maintainer-account recovery flow on third-party package registries.

ANY-FRAMEWORK.gap: No current standard treats `expired maintainer email domain → registry-side account recovery → malicious publish` as a distinct supply-chain attack class. NEW-CTRL-047 is the headline novel control this lesson generates.

new_control_requirements.name: PACKAGE-MAINTAINER-DOMAIN-EXPIRY-MONITORING
new_control_requirements.description: Every organization that depends on a critical-path open-source package must continuously monitor the WHOIS expiry date of the email domain associated with each upstream maintainer account on npm / PyPI / Crates / RubyGems. Alert on any maintainer-domain WHOIS expiry within 90 days. Concurrently, require dual-factor account recovery on the consuming organization's own registry accounts (no email-only password reset) — and treat the absence of registry-enforced MFA on upstream maintainers as a supply-chain risk to be tracked in the SBOM / VEX surface.
new_control_requirements.evidence: MAL-2026-NODE-IPC-STEALER — the `atlantis-software.net` domain lapsed on or before 2026-05-07 and was re-registered by the attacker via Namecheap PrivateEmail; npm's email-based password-reset flow then delivered publish rights to the attacker without any credential leak. No current framework treats expired-domain → account-recovery as a distinct supply-chain attack class.

new_control_requirements.name: NPM-MAINTAINER-MFA-ENFORCEMENT
new_control_requirements.description: npm (and equivalent registries) must enforce mandatory MFA on publish-enabled maintainer accounts for any package above a download-volume threshold (e.g. >= 100K weekly downloads). Pending registry-side enforcement, consuming organizations should require — via SLA or contractual surface — that critical-path maintainers attest to MFA-on-publish, and refuse to upgrade packages where attestation is absent.
new_control_requirements.evidence: MAL-2026-NODE-IPC-STEALER — node-ipc carries approximately 3.35M monthly downloads; npm did not require MFA on the publish-enabled maintainer account at compromise time, so the password-reset-via-recovered-email flow succeeded without a second factor.

new_control_requirements.name: LOCKFILE-INTEGRITY-VERIFIED-AT-CI-BOOT
new_control_requirements.description: CI pipelines must use `npm ci` (or `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, `yarn install --immutable`) rather than `npm install`. The strict-lockfile command refuses to resolve any version not already pinned in the lockfile, catching a maintainer-swap-induced version drift before the malicious tarball is fetched. Additionally, verify tarball integrity hashes against a known-good cache snapshot at CI boot for every dependency in critical-path packages.
new_control_requirements.evidence: MAL-2026-NODE-IPC-STEALER — consumers whose lockfile predated 2026-05-14 were safe only if they used a strict-lockfile install command; `npm install` would have happily upgraded within the declared semver range and pulled the malicious version. The strict-lockfile gate catches the swap even after a successful registry-side publish.

compliance_exposure_score.basis: Maintainer-domain-expiry monitoring is not a recognized control in any major framework; near-100% of audit-passing organizations have zero coverage of this risk class. Even organizations with strong npm hygiene (lockfile pinning, `npm ci`, `--ignore-scripts` defaults) are exposed because the payload ships in the main module — `--ignore-scripts` does not mitigate, and lockfile pinning only helps if the lockfile predates the malicious publish AND the consumer uses a strict-lockfile install command.

attack_vector.description: Linux kernel ptrace exit-race: exit_mm() runs before exit_files() during privileged-process shutdown, leaving a microsecond window where task->mm == NULL but the fd table still holds privileged file handles. Pre-fix __ptrace_may_access() skipped its get_dumpable() check when mm == NULL, silently authorizing UID-matched access. Unprivileged attacker races ssh-keysign or chage exit, calls pidfd_getfd(2) to duplicate still-open fds, reads /etc/ssh/ssh_host_*_key or /etc/shadow as root.
attack_vector.privileges_required: unprivileged local user with shell access
attack_vector.complexity: race-condition with deterministic-on-loop primitive — 100-2000 attempts typically succeed
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered. Qualys TRU human research. The underlying flaw was originally proposed in a 2020 Jann Horn patch that was never merged; 6-year dormant logic bug.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Merging the 2020 Jann Horn patch proposal. seccomp profiles blocking pidfd_getfd for unprivileged users. SUID removal from ssh-keysign + chage on hosts where host-based SSH auth + age-warn UX are not required. sysctl kernel.user_ptrace=0 to block unprivileged ptrace system-wide.
prevention.adequacy: Yama ptrace_scope is NOT a compensating control — the bypass is at the kernel access-check layer, not the LSM layer. The 2020 Horn patch would have closed the class entirely.

detection.what_would_have_worked: auditd rule on pidfd_getfd with auid>=1000 fires on unprivileged invocation. eBPF on tracepoint:syscalls:sys_enter_pidfd_getfd correlated with ssh-keysign / chage execution bursts surfaces the 100-2000-attempt race loop loudly.
detection.adequacy: Detection only; race is running by the time auditd fires. Mitigates post-exploitation cleanup, not exfil itself.

response.what_would_have_worked: Rotate SSH host keys + /etc/shadow on hosts with observed pidfd_getfd anomalies in disclosure window. Patch + reboot (kernel point releases 7.0.8 / 6.18.31 / 6.12.89 / 6.6.139 / 6.1.173 / 5.15.207 / 5.10.256). KernelCare livepatch when released.
response.adequacy: Host-key rotation is non-trivial in fleet ops — SSH known_hosts trust graph fragments. Most operators patch + accept residual window between disclosure and reboot scheduling.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: 30-day critical patch SLA is an exploitation window for a kernel LPE with two public PoCs. Reboot-required nature breaks standard SI-2 maintenance assumptions.

NIST-800-53-AC-3.gap: Access enforcement compliance assumes file-permission integrity. ssh-keysign-pwn defeats file permissions via kernel-level access-check skip — AC-3 mode-bit checks are not compensating controls.

NIST-800-53-AU-2.gap: Audit event selection should include pidfd_getfd post-disclosure; pre-disclosure the syscall was rarely on default audit rule sets.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: Appropriate timescales undefined; same problem as CVE-2026-43284 / CVE-2026-46300 / CVE-2026-31431.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: Art. 21(2)(c) measures undefined for fast-cycle kernel LPEs. No guidance on sysctl or SUID-removal as interim measures.

new_control_requirements.name: KERNEL-EXIT-RACE-CVE-CLASS-MONITORING
new_control_requirements.description: When a CVE is disclosed in the kernel ptrace / pidfd / fd-table lifecycle class, audit rules SHOULD enable pidfd_getfd / pidfd_open / pidfd_send_signal tracking for auid>=1000 within 24h. The syscall is rare in normal operation; spike volume after a same-class disclosure is high-confidence exploitation signal.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2026-46333: the 100-2000-attempt exploit loop is loud in audit but most default rule sets do not monitor pidfd_getfd.

new_control_requirements.name: SUID-MINIMIZATION-FOR-KERNEL-LPE-CARRIER-BINARIES
new_control_requirements.description: Hosts that do not use SSH host-based authentication SHOULD have ssh-keysign de-suid-ed. Hosts that do not use age-warn login UX SHOULD have chage de-suid-ed. Removes the privileged-process carrier even before the kernel patch lands.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2026-46333: ssh-keysign + chage are the canonical carriers; SUID-removal blocks the exploit at the carrier layer regardless of kernel patch state.

compliance_exposure_score.basis: Every Linux fleet running OpenSSH + shadow-utils — every default install for the last 6 years. Audit-passing orgs are exposed because the bug is in default-shipped kernels.

attack_vector.description: Threat-actor open-source release of an operational supply-chain worm under MIT license, paired with a BreachForums-hosted cash-bounty contest for downstream impact. Lowers barrier-to-entry from custom-tradecraft to clone-and-deploy. Framework targets AI-coding-assistant config files (~/.cursor, ~/.codeium, ~/.claude) alongside cloud + registry credentials; adds Claude Code startup hooks for persistence. Self-replicates via maintainer-token-pivot — stolen npm token authenticates as compromised maintainer, publishes malicious versions of other packages owned by the same maintainer.
attack_vector.privileges_required: opportunistic — any developer workstation where the package is installed and post-install or require-time activation fires
attack_vector.complexity: post-release: low. Pre-release: high (custom tradecraft).
attack_vector.ai_factor: TeamPCP self-describes as "vibe coded" — AI-coding-assistant-mediated authoring. Defenders should expect rapid variant proliferation accelerated by AI coding assistants.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Maintainer-side: hardware-key-bound npm publish + MFA-required republish + npm-token isolation (publish tokens NOT on developer workstations). Consumer-side: package-pin hash verification, --ignore-scripts for postinstall, internal Verdaccio proxy with manual gating on version-bump risk-scoring. AI-assistant-side: file-permission restriction on ~/.claude/settings.json, ~/.cursor/mcp.json, ~/.codeium/windsurf/mcp_config.json (0600 on POSIX, ACL-restricted on Windows) so unprivileged processes cannot read.
prevention.adequacy: No single control prevents the attack class. Defense-in-depth across maintainer + registry + consumer + AI-config layers reduces blast radius but does not eliminate.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Anomaly detection on npm publish events from new IPs, unusual cadence, or unusual package selection per maintainer. Monitor GitHub for repos matching "A Gift From TeamPCP" naming pattern OR with commit timestamps in year 2099 OR with agwagwagwa / headdirt / tmechen account contributors. eBPF on file-read events for ~/.aws, ~/.ssh, ~/.cursor, ~/.codeium, ~/.claude from processes spawned by node / npm / yarn / pnpm.
detection.adequacy: Detection-side is operator-feasible but reactive. By the time anomaly fires, credentials may already be in the attacker-controlled GitHub repo.

response.what_would_have_worked: Immediate npm token rotation across all developer workstations + maintainer accounts. Audit all published package versions in the disclosure window for any unauthorized publish under compromised credentials. Roll back malicious versions via npm registry security-team channel. Rotate all secrets referenced by AI-assistant config files (MCP server tokens, Anthropic API keys, OpenAI keys).
response.adequacy: Response is unbounded — once credentials leak, blast radius is the union of every API the credential can reach.

NIST-800-218-SSDF-PW.4.gap: Tooling-trust assumption invalid when maintainer workstation is compromised.

NIST-800-53-SR-3.gap: Supply-chain-tampering controls do not address legitimately-authenticated malicious upstream.

EU-CRA-Art13.gap: Vulnerability-handling treats malicious upgrades as outside scope.

SLSA-v1.0-Build-L3.gap: L3 provenance is valid for Shai-Hulud-poisoned packages — the build IS provenance-attested under the compromised maintainer identity.

new_control_requirements.name: AI-ASSISTANT-CONFIG-FILE-PERMISSION-LOCKDOWN
new_control_requirements.description: AI-assistant configuration files (~/.claude/, ~/.cursor/, ~/.codeium/, ~/.aider/, ~/.continue/) that carry MCP server tokens or LLM API keys MUST be mode 0600 on POSIX and ACL-restricted to the workstation user on Windows. Default mode on these files is typically 0644; Shai-Hulud reads them at unprivileged process scope. exceptd v0.12.41 hardened attestation sidecars to 0o600 for the same reason; the workstation-config category needs the same defensive posture.
new_control_requirements.evidence: MAL-2026-SHAI-HULUD-OSS framework explicitly reads ~/.cursor/mcp.json + ~/.codeium/windsurf/mcp_config.json + ~/.claude/settings.json as exfil targets.

new_control_requirements.name: NPM-PUBLISH-TOKEN-WORKSTATION-ISOLATION
new_control_requirements.description: npm publish tokens MUST NOT reside on developer workstations. Publish should require a hardware-key-bound CI/CD pipeline gate (GitHub Actions with OIDC + npm provisioning, or equivalent). Workstation tokens scope to read-only registry pulls.
new_control_requirements.evidence: MAL-2026-SHAI-HULUD-OSS pivot mechanism requires a write-scope npm token on the maintainer workstation.

new_control_requirements.name: GITHUB-REPO-PATTERN-MONITORING-FOR-EXFIL-CHANNELS
new_control_requirements.description: Organizations SHOULD monitor GitHub for repository creation matching known threat-actor naming patterns ("A Gift From TeamPCP", "Shai-Hulud", future variants). The attacker uses GitHub itself as the exfil channel; the GitHub Search API + Code Search API are sufficient.
new_control_requirements.evidence: MAL-2026-SHAI-HULUD-OSS pattern; pre-2026-05-12 Shai-Hulud waves used "Shai-Hulud-*" repo naming.

compliance_exposure_score.basis: Every npm-consuming engineering org. SLSA + SSDF + SR-3 compliance does not protect against legitimately-authenticated malicious-maintainer publishes.

attack_vector.description: Pod-spec attributes reach modprobe argument path in CRI-O without validation. An attacker with pod-create RBAC on a cluster using CRI-O can cause arbitrary kernel modules to load on the host node, achieving container-escape-equivalent capability.
attack_vector.privileges_required: pod-create RBAC inside the cluster (namespace-scoped is sufficient)
attack_vector.complexity: low
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered — reported by the OpenShift/CRI-O upstream security team. Conventional argument-injection class.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Upgrade to CRI-O 1.27.10 / 1.28.7 / 1.29.4. Pre-patch, AppArmor or SELinux deny-module-load profiles on the node block the exploit primitive without runtime change.
prevention.adequacy: Patch is definitive; AppArmor/SELinux deny-module-load is an effective live-patch for unpatched fleets.

detection.what_would_have_worked: auditd rules on init_module / finit_module syscalls correlated with container PIDs; alert on any module load originating from a containerd/CRI-O managed process namespace.
detection.adequacy: High-signal — module loads from container PIDs are essentially never legitimate.

response.what_would_have_worked: Cordon and drain nodes that loaded an unexpected module; rotate node-bound credentials; treat the node as compromised pending forensic review.
response.adequacy: Effective post-exploitation; relies on the detection above firing in time.

NIST-800-53-CM-7.gap: Least-functionality control presumes node-level kernel-module policy is authoritative; cluster runtimes that broker module loads invert the trust direction without framework guidance to revoke that broker capability.

CIS-Kubernetes-Benchmark-4.2.13.gap: AppArmor profile guidance is generic and does not specifically require deny-module-load.

NIS2-Art21-supply-chain.gap: Container-runtime supply chain not differentiated from application-runtime supply chain.

compliance_exposure_score.basis: AppArmor/SELinux deny-module-load is rarely enforced on container hosts; CIS-K8s benchmark passes without it. Patch cadence on Kubernetes node runtimes typically lags behind application patches.

new_control_requirements.name: KERNEL-MODULE-INVENTORY-AND-DISABLE
new_control_requirements.description: On every node running CRI-O, treat the host's loadable-module surface as the blast radius of the container runtime: inventory the modules a node actually needs for its workloads, blocklist the remainder in modprobe configuration, and enforce a locked/signed module set so a modprobe invocation carrying pod-spec-derived arguments cannot pull in a module the node's business function never requires. This is the compensating layer that survives an attacker who legitimately holds pod-create RBAC, because the module load is performed by the runtime on the host — not inside the container — so pod-level confinement (dropped capabilities, seccomp, AppArmor) never observes it. The distinguishing test: from a pod-create-capable service account on a staging CRI-O cluster, submit a pod spec whose attributes drive modprobe toward a module outside the node's approved inventory and confirm the load is refused rather than silently completed on the host; a cluster that passes image-scan and RBAC review still yields node-level module loading if the node's module set is unbounded.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet: pod-spec attributes reach the modprobe argument path in CRI-O without validation, so 'an attacker with pod-create RBAC on a cluster using CRI-O can cause arbitrary kernel modules to load on the host node, achieving container-escape-equivalent capability' (CWE-20). CVSS 8.1, RWEP 30, poc_available: true. Not CISA KEV-listed and active_exploitation is unknown — the reason a CVSS/KEV-tiered flaw-remediation cadence deprioritizes it despite node-level impact. The entry records patch_available: true and live_patch_available: true, so a runtime fix and a live-patch path both exist; the module-inventory control is what covers the window before that fix lands and the residual after it.

new_control_requirements.name: FLEET-CONTROL-PLANE-ADMIN-PRIVILEGE-TIER
new_control_requirements.description: Classify pod-create authority on a CRI-O cluster as fleet-control-plane privilege rather than application-developer privilege. This CVE collapses the distance between the two: the namespace-scoped ability to submit a pod spec is, on an unpatched CRI-O node, the ability to load an arbitrary kernel module on the host. Every identity that holds pod-create on such a cluster — human operators and CI service accounts alike — therefore needs the control-plane tier's handling: an identity separate from application admin roles, just-in-time elevation with an approval step, and access only through a privileged path; and cluster RBAC must be audited for who holds pod-create outside that tier. The CIS Kubernetes admission guidance cited against this entry inspects what a pod requests (assigned capabilities, AppArmor profile) and does not help here, because the escape requires no elevated capability in the pod at all — the privileged action is taken by the runtime on the pod's behalf.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet: 'Pod-spec attributes reach modprobe argument path in CRI-O without validation. An attacker with pod-create RBAC on a cluster using CRI-O can cause arbitrary kernel modules to load on the host node, achieving container-escape-equivalent capability.' The gap cited against this entry, CIS Kubernetes Benchmark v1.10.0 item 4.2.13, is scoped as 'Minimize the admission of containers with capabilities assigned (Kubelet / AppArmor profile guidance)'. CWE-20, CVSS 8.1, RWEP 30, poc_available: true.

attack_vector.description: MLflow tracking-server artifact endpoint resolves user-controlled paths under the artifact root without normalization. An unauthenticated HTTP request with ../ traversal reads arbitrary files from the host filesystem.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none (unauth network reachability to MLflow tracking server)
attack_vector.complexity: low
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered — disclosed via the Protect AI Huntr bug-bounty program by a named human researcher (Joseph Beeton, Contrast Security).

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Upgrade to MLflow 2.9.0+. Network-isolate tracking servers from untrusted networks until patched; MLflow shipped historically with no auth and operators routinely expose it on internal networks treating it as trusted.
prevention.adequacy: Patch is the only definitive fix; network isolation is a viable compensating control.

detection.what_would_have_worked: WAF or reverse-proxy log review for ../ patterns in tracking-server artifact-fetch URLs; HTTP access-log alerts on traversal sequences.
detection.adequacy: Effective when an HTTP front-proxy is in place. Many MLflow deployments expose the Flask server directly with no front-proxy logging.

response.what_would_have_worked: Rotate any credentials, tokens or model-artifact contents the tracking server filesystem could have leaked; audit the MLflow artifact root for sensitive sibling files (.env, ~/.aws/credentials).
response.adequacy: Reduces blast radius post-exploitation; necessary because MLflow processes typically run with broad filesystem read access.

NIST-AI-RMF-MEASURE-2.7.gap: ML-pipeline asset confidentiality is referenced but no specific control on tracking-server path normalization or web-surface review.

OWASP-ML-Top-10-2023-ML06.gap: Insufficient supply-chain controls in ML — MLflow tracking servers routinely expose model + experiment IO without auth.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.28.gap: Secure coding control does not anchor on ML-runtime web-surface review; ML platforms are treated as out-of-scope of conventional secure-coding programs.

compliance_exposure_score.basis: MLflow tracking servers are widely deployed without auth and without front-proxy logging; ML platforms typically fall outside the AppSec team's secure-coding-review remit.

new_control_requirements.name: AI-RUNTIME-API-PATH-TRAVERSAL-VALIDATION
new_control_requirements.description: MLflow's artifact endpoint joins a caller-supplied path onto the artifact root and serves the result, so containment must be enforced on the read direction and not only on uploads and extractions: resolve the requested path to an absolute canonical form, verify the resolved result is still under the artifact root (rejecting absolute paths, ../ segments, and symlinks that leave the root), and do that check before the file handle is opened rather than by filtering the request string. On a tracking server the read half is the higher-value half, because the same host holds the object-store credentials, the tracking database URI, and the operator key material that an arbitrary-file read returns.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet: the tracking-server artifact endpoint resolves user-controlled paths under the artifact root without normalization, and an unauthenticated HTTP request carrying ../ reads arbitrary files from the host filesystem (CWE-22, CVSS 7.5). A PoC is public and a patch is available.

new_control_requirements.name: AI-ML-DEVELOPER-TOOLING-INVENTORY
new_control_requirements.description: An MLflow tracking server is typically stood up by a data-science team rather than by IT, so nothing tells the application-patching program that a network-reachable artifact-read flaw exists on it — the asset is not on the list the patch SLA runs against. The inventory entry for this server must record each listening endpoint, whether any authentication sits in front of the artifact route specifically (this traversal is reachable unauthenticated), and the blast radius of a file read from that host: artifact-store credentials, registered model artifacts, and training-data paths, which is how a file read becomes model-supply-chain tampering. It needs its own patch SLA tier rather than the generic application tier.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet: an unauthenticated HTTP request to the tracking server's artifact endpoint reads arbitrary host files. The CVE is not KEV-listed and active exploitation is unknown despite a public PoC and RWEP 35 — the exact profile that never surfaces on a KEV-driven patch queue and so depends on the asset being inventoried to be remediated at all.

CVE-2024-27132.name: MLflow Recipe Template Injection XSS to Client-Side RCE

attack_vector.description: MLflow renders recipe template variables without sufficient sanitization (CWE-79, rooted in template injection), so an untrusted recipe executes script in the victim's MLflow session and can pivot to privileged tracking-server actions.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none beyond getting a victim to run/view an untrusted recipe (NVD UI:R)
attack_vector.complexity: low (NVD AC:L)
attack_vector.ai_factor: The abused surface is the recipe-rendering UI of MLflow, a widely used MLOps experiment-tracking platform. The lesson: MLOps platform UIs render user/community-supplied content (recipes, run metadata, model cards) and must output-encode it — the MLOps UI is a privileged control surface, not a passive viewer.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: Does not track the MLOps experiment-tracking platform as managed, user-facing software.

NIST-800-53-SI-10.gap: Output-encoding is not applied to recipe template variables rendered in the MLflow UI.

ALL-AI-PIPELINE-INTEGRITY.gap: No framework treats untrusted MLOps content (recipes, run metadata) as requiring sanitization before rendering.

compliance_exposure_score.basis: MLOps platforms are deployed for internal teams and assumed trusted; untrusted recipes/run metadata are rendered without output encoding.

new_control_requirements.name: MLOPS-PLATFORM-UNTRUSTED-CONTENT-ENCODING
new_control_requirements.description: An MLOps platform UI must output-encode and sanitize all user/community-supplied content it renders (recipe template variables, run metadata, model cards, artifact names) and must not expose its UI / tracking server to untrusted users. Upgrade MLflow to 2.10.0 or later. The distinguishing test: load a recipe whose template variables contain script payloads into a staging MLflow and confirm the UI renders them inert, not executed.
new_control_requirements.evidence: https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2024-27132

CVE-2024-21575.name: ComfyUI-Impact-Pack Path Traversal Arbitrary File Write to RCE

attack_vector.description: A ComfyUI custom node (CWE-35 path traversal on /upload/temp -> write into ./custom_nodes) gives an unauthenticated attacker code execution on a reachable ComfyUI instance. ComfyUI auto-loads node code, so a single vulnerable or malicious custom node is an execution boundary.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none (NVD AV:N / PR:N) — unauthenticated against a reachable ComfyUI instance
attack_vector.complexity: low (NVD AC:L)
attack_vector.ai_factor: The abused surface is the custom-node ecosystem of ComfyUI, a widely deployed AI image-generation tool. The lesson: AI tools with auto-loaded plugin/custom-node systems treat extension code as trusted, so a single vulnerable node is unauthenticated RCE and the node registry is a supply-chain surface. In April 2026 a cryptomining botnet mass-targeted exposed ComfyUI via this surface.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: Does not track third-party ComfyUI custom nodes as managed, RCE-bearing software.

NIST-800-53-SC-7.gap: Does not flag internet-exposed ComfyUI instances as a custom-node RCE surface.

ALL-AI-PIPELINE-INTEGRITY.gap: No framework treats an AI tool's auto-loaded custom nodes as an untrusted-code supply-chain and execution surface.

compliance_exposure_score.basis: AI image-gen tools are deployed with community custom nodes installed and often internet-exposed; the node ecosystem is trusted by default and not in the vulnerability program.

new_control_requirements.name: AI-TOOL-CUSTOM-NODE-EXTENSION-TRUST
new_control_requirements.description: An AI tool that auto-loads custom nodes / plugins must treat them as code: review/allow-list before install, validate any file paths or workflow strings the nodes consume, never expose the tool (or its node-install endpoint) to untrusted networks, and run least-privilege. Update affected ComfyUI custom nodes to their patched versions. The distinguishing test: from an unauthenticated client, attempt the path-traversal upload and the crafted-workflow code-injection against a staging ComfyUI and confirm neither writes outside the temp dir nor executes node-supplied strings.
new_control_requirements.evidence: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-6mx8-m8xp-f2vc

CVE-2020-10148.name: SolarWinds Orion API authentication bypass (SUNBURST chain component)

attack_vector.description: URI pattern matching against SkipI18nStrings inside Orion's HTTP routing triggers an authentication bypass — an unauthenticated request that matches the pattern reaches API write endpoints. Used by SUNBURST operators to exercise API write access against compromised Orion installations.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none (unauth network reachability to Orion)
attack_vector.complexity: low
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered — pre-AI-tooling era; surfaced during the SUNBURST incident-response investigation by Mandiant/FireEye and SolarWinds engineering.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Upgrade to Orion 2020.2.1 HF2+ and apply the documented WAF rule blocking the SkipI18nStrings URI pattern. Network-restrict Orion management surface to operator subnets.
prevention.adequacy: Patch + WAF rule together close the bypass; network restriction shrinks the unauth-reachable surface.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Web-server log alerts on requests matching the SkipI18nStrings pattern from non-operator source addresses; outbound DNS / connection-pattern detection for SUNBURST C2 (the chain consumer).
detection.adequacy: URI-pattern detection is high-signal post-disclosure; SUNBURST C2 detection was added to commercial EDR within weeks of the 2020-12 disclosure.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treat any Orion installation prior to HF2 as potentially compromised; isolate, snapshot, rotate every credential the SolarWinds service account could touch (it usually had broad domain access), rebuild from known-good media.
response.adequacy: CISA Emergency Directive 21-01 mandated the response posture for US federal civilian agencies; private-sector equivalents (incident-response playbooks) varied widely.

NIST-800-53-IA-2.gap: Identification-and-Authentication control trusted the application's URI-matching layer; framework does not address pattern-bypass classes in vendor-supplied management software.

ISO-27001-2022-A.5.15.gap: Access control reviewed at organizational level; URI-pattern auth bypass is a code-level failure under app-vendor responsibility that the organizational control cannot detect.

NIST-800-53-SA-12.gap: Supply-chain protection control predates the SolarWinds incident; pre-2020 supply-chain controls did not contemplate a trusted vendor as the breach vector.

compliance_exposure_score.basis: Direct exposure to this specific CVE is low five years post-disclosure (Orion installations are largely patched), but the lessons-class — trusted-vendor-as-pivot — remains under-addressed by most supply-chain controls.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: The Orion authentication-bypass fix has to run on the KEV clock rather than the change window an internal monitoring server normally gets. Exploitation needs nothing but a single HTTP request whose URI matches the SkipI18nStrings pattern to land on Orion's API write endpoints — there is no credential to brute-force, no user to phish and no exploit-development lead time, so exposure lasts exactly as long as the unpatched Orion web surface stays reachable. A vendor fix is available and there is no live-patch path, so the mitigation is a scheduled Orion upgrade with the API surface restricted to a management segment (or the web service stopped) until the upgrade lands, not a deferral to the next quarterly maintenance slot.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet: cisa_kev true, kev_date 2021-11-03, active_exploitation confirmed, rwep_score 75, cvss 9.8, poc_available true, patch_available true, live_patch_available false, live_patch_notes null, cwe_refs CWE-287. Vector: "URI pattern matching against SkipI18nStrings triggers bypass — unauthenticated request matching the pattern reaches API write endpoints."

new_control_requirements.name: FLEET-COMPROMISE-IR-PLAYBOOK
new_control_requirements.description: Orion is a fleet control plane — it reaches, polls and holds credentials for the monitored estate — so the response to this bypass cannot end at the upgrade. SUNBURST operators used the bypass to exercise API write access against Orion installations that were already compromised, which means patching removes the entry path and leaves whatever was written through the API in place. The playbook's exposure-window steps are what actually apply here: enumerate every API write made against Orion during the window, audit configuration and job/alert-action changes made through it, invalidate the trust state of nodes Orion administers, and rotate every credential Orion custodied or that authenticated through it. That enumeration only exists if Orion's own per-request API telemetry was collected and retained off-box — monitoring programs scoped to the estate Orion watches routinely do not collect it for the monitoring platform itself, which is the monitoring gap this closes. It also closes the supply-chain gap: after a compromise delivered through the vendor product, a vendor patch restores the code but not the trust state of the installation or of the estate reachable from it.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet attack_vector: "URI pattern matching against SkipI18nStrings inside Orion's HTTP routing triggers an authentication bypass — an unauthenticated request that matches the pattern reaches API write endpoints. Used by SUNBURST operators to exercise API write access against compromised Orion installations." Packet: cisa_kev true, kev_date 2021-11-03, active_exploitation confirmed, poc_available true, rwep_score 75, cvss 9.8. Citing gaps already record UK-CAF-C1 (Security monitoring) and NIS2-Art21-supply-chain as insufficient for this CVE.

CVE-2023-3519.name: Citrix NetScaler ADC/Gateway unauth RCE (CitrixBleed precursor)

attack_vector.description: Pre-auth stack buffer overflow in the NetScaler SAML processing path. An unauthenticated HTTP POST to /gwtest/formssso reaches the vulnerable nsppe parser; CISA AA23-201A documented in-wild exploitation by Chinese state-sponsored actors against US critical-infrastructure organizations within weeks of disclosure.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none (unauth network reachability to NetScaler appliance)
attack_vector.complexity: low
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered — independent security researchers via Citrix coordinated disclosure (CTX561482, 2023-07-18).

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Upgrade to NetScaler 13.1-49.13 / 13.0-91.13 / 12.1-66.13. Treat any pre-patch appliance reachable from the public internet as already compromised once exploitation went public.
prevention.adequacy: Patch is definitive but many operators missed the CISA KEV 21-day deadline; the same population was breached again two months later via the CitrixBleed (CVE-2023-4966) session-token vulnerability.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Mandiant + CISA published IoCs including web-shell paths under /var/vpn/themes/imgs/ and unexpected nsppe core dumps. Webserver log alerts on POST to /gwtest/formssso from non-operator source addresses.
detection.adequacy: Post-exploitation IoC matching detected breached organizations weeks after compromise — many were already at session-token-theft + lateral-movement stage.

response.what_would_have_worked: Rebuild appliance from known-good firmware; rotate all credentials, AD machine-account passwords, and SAML signing keys the appliance held; assume web-shell persistence until forensic review confirms otherwise.
response.adequacy: CISA-recommended response posture; full credential rotation is operationally expensive and was inconsistently applied across the affected population.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: 30-day patch SLA is insufficient for unauth RCE on public-facing appliances. CISA BOD 22-01 KEV deadlines (21 days) override but apply only to US federal civilian agencies.

PCI-DSS-4.0-6.3.3.gap: 1-month critical-patch window is a permission slip; mass exploitation began within 14 days of public PoC.

NIS2-Art21-vulnerability-management.gap: EU NIS2 generic vulnerability-management requirement without unauth-RCE-specific SLA.

compliance_exposure_score.basis: PCI-DSS / NIS2 / SI-2 patch SLAs are wider than the actual exploitation window. Many organizations passing those audits remained exposed during the active mass-exploitation phase.

new_control_requirements.name: PERIMETER-DEVICE-ZERODAY-SLA-TIER
new_control_requirements.description: A NetScaler ADC/Gateway is the authentication and TLS-termination boundary for the applications behind it, so the 14/30-day patch windows the citing controls grade against are the wrong clock for it — the device is not protected by the perimeter, it is the perimeter. CVE-2023-3519 argues for a distinct tier: for a pre-authentication defect on an internet-reachable NetScaler, either the fixed build is deployed or the exposed virtual server's public interface is taken offline, within hours of KEV listing, with that shutdown pre-authorized so an on-call engineer can take it without a change window. The tier must also be driven by configured role rather than by product name. Only appliances configured to serve the gateway SAML/formssso path reach the vulnerable nsppe code, so an asset inventory that records 'NetScaler present' cannot select the affected population — it has to record which virtual servers are published and which authentication paths they expose, or the compressed SLA fires against the wrong devices and misses the right ones.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Citrix NetScaler ADC/Gateway, CISA KEV-listed 2023-07-19 with confirmed in-the-wild exploitation and a public PoC available. The attack vector: an unauthenticated HTTP POST to /gwtest/formssso reaches the vulnerable nsppe parser — no credential and no prior foothold required — and CISA AA23-201A documented in-wild exploitation by Chinese state-sponsored actors against US critical-infrastructure organizations within weeks of disclosure. RWEP 80 / CVSS 9.8.

new_control_requirements.name: PERIMETER-COMPROMISE-REBUILD-NOT-PATCH
new_control_requirements.description: The nsppe stack overflow runs before authentication, which means a successful CVE-2023-3519 exploit generates no authentication event to find later and executes with the packet engine's privilege on the appliance. Upgrading to the fixed NetScaler build restores the SAML parser and says nothing about what was installed while the parser was broken. Any NetScaler that served the gateway formssso path from an untrusted network on a vulnerable build must therefore be dispositioned as compromised regardless of what a post-upgrade version scan reports: capture and diff the running configuration against the last known-good, inspect the appliance's web-served directories for files not shipped by the vendor, then rebuild from vendor media at the fixed version rather than upgrading in place, and rotate what the device held — SAML signing and session material, the LDAP/RADIUS bind accounts it authenticated against, the local administrative accounts, and any TLS private key stored on it. Version-based remediation evidence is specifically what fails here, because the attacker's artifacts are not versioned.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Pre-authentication stack buffer overflow (CWE-787) in the NetScaler SAML processing path, reachable by an unauthenticated HTTP POST per the recorded attack vector. CISA KEV-listed 2023-07-19, active exploitation confirmed, public PoC available, patch available, RWEP 80. CISA AA23-201A documented state-sponsored exploitation of US critical-infrastructure organizations within weeks of disclosure — meaning estates that patched after that interval applied the fix to devices an adversary had already entered.

attack_vector.description: Path-traversal in the auth filter — appending /SetupWizard.aspx/anything to a request URL bypasses authentication and reaches the admin setup endpoint. Attacker creates a new admin account via the setup endpoint and gains full ScreenConnect control, including the ability to push remote-control payloads to every endpoint the affected MSP manages.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none (unauth network reachability to ScreenConnect web surface)
attack_vector.complexity: low — single-request exploitation, no preconditions
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered — vendor-internal discovery; externally observed via Huntress and GreyNoise telemetry within 24 hours of the 2024-02 Patch Tuesday.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Upgrade to ScreenConnect 23.9.8+. Pre-patch, take the ScreenConnect web surface offline or front it with a WAF blocking the /SetupWizard.aspx/* pattern from unauthenticated sources.
prevention.framework_requiring_it: CISA BOD 22-01 (KEV remediation — added 2024-02-22 with 24h deadline)
prevention.adequacy: Patch is definitive; CISA's compressed deadline reflected the live mass-exploitation observed within hours of disclosure.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Webserver log alerts on /SetupWizard.aspx/* URI patterns; admin-user-creation audit alerts on any new privileged account; outbound connection alerts on managed endpoints to non-operator C2 destinations.
detection.adequacy: High-signal — the URI pattern is essentially never legitimate post-installation. Most affected MSPs had no log review at this layer.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treat the ScreenConnect server and every managed endpoint as compromised pending forensic review; rotate every managed-endpoint credential; rebuild ScreenConnect from a known-good install rather than patching in place.
response.adequacy: Operationally expensive — many MSPs patched in place without forensic review, leaving residual attacker persistence on managed endpoints.

NIST-800-53-AC-3.gap: Access enforcement assumed at the application layer; bypass occurred at the routing layer before AC-3 had any opportunity to evaluate.

NIST-800-53-IA-2.gap: MFA on admin accounts would not have prevented the breach — the bypass creates a new admin account that satisfies whatever MFA policy applies to fresh enrolment.

CIS-Controls-v8-Control6.gap: Access-control management does not require setup-endpoint hardening on production deployments; the ScreenConnect setup wizard was reachable post-install by design.

compliance_exposure_score.basis: MSP fleets passing SOC 2 / ISO 27001 audits routinely deploy remote-management tooling with default routing exposed; setup-endpoint hardening is not a benchmark requirement.

new_control_requirements.name: FLEET-CONTROL-PLANE-ADMIN-PRIVILEGE-TIER
new_control_requirements.description: ScreenConnect is not an application server that happens to have admins — it is the control plane for every endpoint the affected MSP manages, and this CVE is what that distinction costs. The bypass is a URL suffix: appending /SetupWizard.aspx/anything defeats the auth filter and lands an unauthenticated caller in the admin setup endpoint, where a new admin account is created. No credential is guessed and no session is stolen, so console password policy, admin-account review and MFA-on-the-console all attest green while the takeover proceeds. What actually bites is treating ScreenConnect administration as a privilege tier above application admin: the admin and setup surface reachable only through a PAM jumphost rather than from the open internet (so /SetupWizard.aspx is not addressable by the attacker at all), and fleet-control-plane admin identities enumerated separately from every other admin role, so an account that appears without passing the just-in-time elevation and approval workflow is a detectable anomaly rather than one more row in the user table.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet: cwe_refs CWE-287 + CWE-288, cvss 10, rwep_score 75, cisa_kev true, kev_date 2024-02-22, active_exploitation confirmed, poc_available true, patch_available true, live_patch_available false, live_patch_notes null. Attack vector as recorded: "Path-traversal in the auth filter — appending /SetupWizard.aspx/anything to a request URL bypasses authentication and reaches the admin setup endpoint. Attacker creates a new admin account via the setup endpoint and gains full ScreenConnect control, including the ability to push remote-control payloads to every endpoint the affected MSP manages."

new_control_requirements.name: FLEET-COMPROMISE-IR-PLAYBOOK
new_control_requirements.description: The vendor patch removes the bypass; it does not remove the admin account the bypass created, and it does not recall the payloads already pushed through that account. Because the packet's exploitation path ends at pushing remote-control payloads to every endpoint the affected MSP manages, one unpatched ScreenConnect server is not one compromised host — it is the whole downstream estate, and the response work is fleet-shaped rather than server-shaped. The runbook has to enumerate every admin account and remote session created since the exposure window opened, audit what was executed on managed endpoints during it, carry explicit quarantine criteria for endpoints that received a payload, and rotate credentials used on or through those endpoints. This has to be pre-rehearsed: an MSP discovering the compromise on the KEV date cannot start writing downstream-quarantine criteria while the attacker still holds an admin session.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet: cisa_kev true, kev_date 2024-02-22, active_exploitation confirmed, poc_available true, cvss 10, rwep_score 75, patch_available true. Attack vector as recorded: the attacker "creates a new admin account via the setup endpoint and gains full ScreenConnect control, including the ability to push remote-control payloads to every endpoint the affected MSP manages."

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: At CVSS 10 this reaches the top of any severity-ranked queue, so the question is not ranking but when the clock starts. The exploit primitive is a URL suffix with a public PoC — no chain to assemble, no credential to obtain, no user action to arrange — and it was KEV-listed 2024-02-22 with confirmed in-the-wild exploitation, so the interval between an operator's next maintenance window and an attacker's next internet scan is not a fair race. A patch SLA measured from the operator's monthly cycle is therefore the wrong instrument for a ScreenConnect instance: the clock has to start at the KEV listing, and where the restart cannot be booked inside it, the alternative is removing the instance from the internet, because there is no live-patch path for this entry.

CVE-2026-20182.name: Cisco SD-WAN authentication bypass to admin

attack_vector.description: Authentication bypass in the Cisco SD-WAN controller management plane (vManage / vEdge). An unauthenticated attacker reaches admin-equivalent state on the controller, giving control over the SD-WAN fabric's policy plane.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none (unauth network reachability to SD-WAN controller management surface)
attack_vector.complexity: low
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered — discovered by Rapid7 researchers Stephen Fewer and Jonah Burgess while researching the related CVE-2026-20127 vdaemon authentication-bypass.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Apply the Cisco per-train fixed build per cisco-sa-sdwan-authbypass; network-restrict the SD-WAN controller management surface to operator subnets only — controllers should never be reachable from the data plane the fabric carries.
prevention.adequacy: Patch requires controller reboot; network restriction is the appropriate compensating control during the maintenance window.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Authentication-attempt logs from the controller plane; alerts on any successful admin authentication from non-operator source addresses; configuration-change audit on SD-WAN policy.
detection.adequacy: Effective once enabled; SD-WAN controller log forwarding to SIEM is inconsistently configured across operators.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treat fabric policy as potentially altered; review all policy changes against a known-good baseline; rotate controller-plane credentials and certificates; force re-onboarding of any edge device whose trust anchors the controller could have rewritten.
response.adequacy: Operationally expensive; necessary if the detection above did not have full coverage of the exposure window.

NIST-800-53-IA-2.gap: Network-fabric controller authentication depended on the bypassed surface; IA-2 was satisfied on paper while the implementation was bypassable.

NIS2-Art21-network-security.gap: EU NIS2 critical-infrastructure rules treat SD-WAN controllers as essential service infrastructure but lack a CISA-KEV-style compressed remediation SLA.

DORA-Art-9.gap: ICT third-party risk — SD-WAN vendor risk concentrated in a single advisory cadence; DORA does not require dual-vendor fabric topology.

compliance_exposure_score.basis: SD-WAN controller management surfaces are frequently reachable beyond operator subnets in real-world deployments; NIS2 / DORA controls do not enforce management-plane isolation as a specific requirement.

new_control_requirements.name: FLEET-CONTROL-PLANE-ADMIN-PRIVILEGE-TIER
new_control_requirements.description: A Cisco SD-WAN controller is not an application server that happens to have administrators — vManage is the policy plane for the whole WAN fabric, and this CVE is what that distinction costs. Because the bypass lands an unauthenticated caller in admin-equivalent state, every identity-layer attestation the operator holds stays green while the takeover proceeds: no credential is guessed, no session is stolen, and password policy, admin-account review and MFA-on-the-console are all evaluated on a login that never happens. The control that actually bites is treating controller administration as a privilege tier above application admin — the vManage/vEdge management surface reachable only through a PAM jumphost or operator network rather than from an untrusted one, so the bypassable endpoint is not addressable by the attacker at all; and fabric-control-plane admin identities enumerated separately from every other admin role, so an admin principal that appears on the controller without passing just-in-time elevation and the approval workflow is a detectable anomaly rather than one more row in the user table.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet: cwe_refs CWE-287, cvss 10, rwep_score 65, cisa_kev true, kev_date 2026-05-14, active_exploitation confirmed, poc_available false, patch_available true, live_patch_available false, live_patch_notes null. Attack vector as recorded: "Authentication bypass in the Cisco SD-WAN controller management plane (vManage / vEdge). An unauthenticated attacker reaches admin-equivalent state on the controller, giving control over the SD-WAN fabric's policy plane." The citing gaps recorded against this entry include NIST-800-53-IA-2, ISO-27001-2022-A.5.15 and UK-CAF-B2 — all three are marked insufficient here because the bypass resolves before the authentication control fires.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: This entry is the case that a PoC-keyed remediation tier gets wrong. poc_available is false alongside active_exploitation confirmed, so any SLA ladder whose fast lane opens on "public exploit code exists" routes a CVSS 10 controller takeover into a slow bucket while it is already being used. Keying the clock to the KEV listing itself — mitigation verified within 4 hours of listing or fix availability, whichever is later — is what puts this on the right lane. A vendor fix is available and there is no live-patch path, so the deliverable inside that window is the controller upgrade itself, and where the fabric's change-control cannot absorb a controller upgrade that fast, the SLA must be satisfied by the documented compensating control instead: withdrawing the vManage/vEdge management plane from untrusted reachability until the fixed build is on it. Recording "scheduled for the next maintenance window" is not a satisfied SLA under this control.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet: cisa_kev true with kev_date 2026-05-14, active_exploitation confirmed, poc_available false, cvss 10, rwep_score 65, patch_available true, live_patch_available false, live_patch_notes null. The NIS2-Art21-network-security gap recorded against this entry states that Article 21 sets no CISA-KEV-tied response SLA for network-fabric controllers, so an operator can claim compliance with a generic 30-day patch SLA on this infrastructure; the DORA-Art-9 gap records that vendor-disclosure-to-action tempo is not differentiated per ICT-third-party-service category.

new_control_requirements.name: PERIMETER-COMPROMISE-REBUILD-NOT-PATCH
new_control_requirements.description: Upgrading the controller closes the bypass and says nothing about what was done through it. Admin-equivalent state on an SD-WAN controller is exercised through the product's own legitimate functions — creating administrative accounts and API tokens, and editing the fabric policy and device templates that the controller pushes down to edge devices — so the attacker's artifacts are ordinary controller objects and ordinary pushed configuration, which no version scan and no malware signature will flag after the fixed build is installed. Any controller that was reachable from an untrusted network on a vulnerable build therefore has to be dispositioned as compromised rather than as remediated: export and diff the running controller configuration, policy definitions and device templates against the last known-good, audit every administrative account, token and template change since the exposure window opened, rotate the controller's local administrative credentials and the certificate and shared-secret material it holds for fabric membership, and re-verify the configuration actually resident on the edge devices rather than trusting the controller's own view of it.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet: active_exploitation confirmed with cisa_kev true (kev_date 2026-05-14) — an exposed unpatched controller is an exploitation opportunity, not a hypothetical. The vector as recorded gives the attacker "admin-equivalent state on the controller, giving control over the SD-WAN fabric's policy plane" without authentication (CWE-287), so the post-exploitation actions are taken as a controller principal. patch_available true with live_patch_available false. The NIST-800-53-IA-2 gap recorded against this entry names the failure directly: an auth bypass that mints a privileged account satisfies whatever MFA policy applies, because the bypass happened at the create-account step rather than the login step, and its stated requirement is that privileged-account creation be audited independently of the MFA policy.

CVE-2024-40635.name: containerd integer overflow IP mask leak

attack_vector.description: Integer overflow in the containerd CNI IP-allocation path. A crafted CIDR specification overflows the uint32 mask conversion, causing the container to receive a spurious mask that allows traffic to leak across network namespaces.
attack_vector.privileges_required: ability to influence a container's CNI configuration (typically requires pod-create RBAC or compromise of an in-cluster component that provisions pods)
attack_vector.complexity: moderate
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered — reported via the containerd security team and Snyk Labs; conventional integer-overflow class.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Upgrade to containerd 1.6.34+ or 1.7.21+. Restrict who can create pods with custom CNI configuration via Kubernetes admission policy.
prevention.adequacy: Patch is definitive; admission policy reduces the exposed attack surface in the interim.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Network-policy violation alerts on cross-namespace traffic; periodic audit of running pods' actual IP/mask versus their declared CNI configuration.
detection.adequacy: Cross-namespace leakage is detectable when egress between namespaces is otherwise denied by NetworkPolicy.

response.what_would_have_worked: Roll affected pods; assume any data the affected container could reach via the spurious mask was potentially exfiltrated to the wrong network namespace.
response.adequacy: Routine for clusters with strong network segmentation; rare in clusters that rely on namespace isolation as the only boundary.

NIST-800-53-SC-7.gap: Boundary protection presumes network-namespace integrity; integer overflow in IPAM defeats it at a layer the boundary-protection control cannot observe.

CIS-Kubernetes-Benchmark-5.3.gap: Network policies don't address container-runtime IPAM correctness — NetworkPolicy assumes the IPAM layer is trusted.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.20.gap: Networks security control covers segmentation policy at organizational level but does not extend to container-runtime IPAM verification.

compliance_exposure_score.basis: Most clusters do not pair NetworkPolicy with IPAM-correctness audit. CIS-K8s benchmark passes without it.

new_control_requirements.name: CONTAINER-RUNTIME-PATCH-SLA-24H
new_control_requirements.description: The defect sits in containerd's CNI IP-allocation path, and a container receives its address and mask when its network is configured - so upgrading the containerd package on a node does not repair a workload that was already handed a spurious mask. Those containers keep permitting traffic across network namespaces until they are recreated on the fixed runtime, which makes the remediation unit node upgrade plus controlled recreation of every workload that was networked by the vulnerable allocation path, and makes the completion criterion 'no running container was networked by the vulnerable path' rather than 'containerd version is past the fix'. This entry is not KEV-listed and its exploitation status is unknown, so the control's KEV-triggered 24-hour clock does not fire here; what this CVE demonstrates is the recreation half of the control, the part every patch-cadence framework control omits because it assumes installing the fixed package ends the exposure. A vendor fix exists and no live-patch path is registered, so the recreation cannot be deferred in the hope of an in-place remedy.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet attack_vector: 'Integer overflow in the containerd CNI IP-allocation path. A crafted CIDR specification overflows the uint32 mask conversion, causing the container to receive a spurious mask that allows traffic to leak across network namespaces.' Citing gaps include AU-Essential-8-Patch and ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.

new_control_requirements.name: SCANNER-PAPER-COMPLIANCE-TEST
new_control_requirements.description: Two green reports coexist with this vulnerability. A CIS-Kubernetes 5.3 assessment passes by finding NetworkPolicy objects present and a policy-capable CNI, and a vulnerability scan passes by finding the containerd package at or past the fixed version. Neither verdict can see the failure: the container is handed a spurious mask by the allocation path, so traffic crosses network namespaces without any NetworkPolicy being violated - the leak is underneath the layer the benchmark inspects - and a package-version check says nothing about containers still running with a mask the vulnerable path gave them. The operational test has to touch the data plane: from a pod, attempt to reach an address in a neighbouring namespace's range that policy is supposed to forbid and confirm the packet is dropped, and enumerate running containers' allocated masks against the ranges their namespaces were meant to receive. Any assessment that reports boundary protection satisfied on the strength of policy-object presence plus a version string is paper compliance against exactly this defect.

A crafted CIDR specification overflows the uint32 mask conversion, causing the container to receive a spurious mask that allows traffic to leak across network namespaces.' Packet vector: 'Integer overflow in CNI IP-allocation path - container receives spurious mask, leaks across network namespaces.' attack_vector.description: Operator-supplied MCP server-spawn command string reaches subprocess exec without argv-array discipline. A maliciously-crafted MCP server config (delivered via supply-chain, social engineering, or a co-tenant tool) causes arbitrary command execution in the MCP client process context.
attack_vector.privileges_required: ability to influence the MCP server configuration the client loads
attack_vector.complexity: low
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered — disclosed by OX Security researchers Moshe Siman Tov Bustan, Mustafa Naamnih, and Nir Zadok as part of an April 2026 four-exploitation-family MCP advisory. Notable that the target is an AI SDK but the discovery methodology was conventional code review.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Upgrade to the post-April-2026 Anthropic MCP SDK release. Pre-patch, pin MCP server commands to immutable absolute paths in operator-owned config and refuse user-supplied server configs.
prevention.adequacy: Patch fixes the argv handling; operator-side allowlisting is the appropriate compensating control and matches the broader MCP-trust posture the mcp playbook recommends.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Process-execution telemetry on the MCP-client host correlating spawned subprocess command lines with the configured allowlist; alert on any subprocess whose argv contains shell-metacharacter sequences from operator-config fields.
detection.adequacy: Effective when EDR is deployed on developer endpoints — coverage gap is the largest constraint.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treat the MCP-client host as potentially compromised; rotate any credentials accessible in that user context (cloud CLI tokens, SSH keys, browser-stored credentials); audit MCP server configurations for unexpected entries.
response.adequacy: Necessary because the MCP client typically runs in developer-laptop context with broad credential access.

OWASP-LLM-Top-10-2025-LLM05.gap: LLM05 addresses improper output handling; this is the symmetric upstream bug — improper INPUT handling on the transport side — which OWASP LLM Top-10 does not call out separately.

NIST-AI-RMF-MEASURE-2.7.gap: MCP transport trust boundary not specifically addressed; MEASURE 2.7 treats the AI subsystem as a single trust unit.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.28.gap: Secure coding control assumed in third-party SDKs without tooling to attest.

new_control_requirements.name: MCP-SERVER-CONFIG-ALLOWLIST
new_control_requirements.description: MCP clients must pin server-spawn commands to immutable absolute paths in operator-owned config. User-supplied or per-project MCP server configs must be disallowed by default; any opt-in must go through operator review.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2026-30623 — operator-config-as-input was treated as platform-trusted by the MCP client and reached subprocess exec without argv-array discipline.

compliance_exposure_score.basis: MCP adoption is widespread across developer endpoints; operator-side allowlisting of MCP server commands is rare. Existing AI-governance audits (NIST AI RMF, ISO 42001) do not enforce MCP transport trust posture as a specific requirement.

attack_vector.description: Pre-auth RCE chain on the Synology BeeStation Manager web management surface. Demonstrated as a full chain on consumer NAS hardware at Pwn2Own Ireland 2025.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none (unauth network reachability to BeeStation web surface)
attack_vector.complexity: low (post-disclosure)
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered — Synacktiv offensive-security researchers @Tek_7987 and @_Anyfun via attack-surface enumeration and manual code auditing per the published Pwn2Own writeup.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Upgrade to BeeStation Manager 1.4.0-65374+. Do not expose consumer NAS web management to the public internet; restrict to LAN with VPN access for remote operators.
prevention.adequacy: Patch is definitive; network restriction is appropriate for consumer-IoT deployments that may delay the patch window.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Webserver log alerts on the unauth attack patterns published in the Synacktiv writeup; outbound connection alerts from the NAS to non-vendor C2 destinations.
detection.adequacy: Consumer-NAS log forwarding is rarely deployed; detection-in-place coverage is low.

response.what_would_have_worked: Rebuild appliance from known-good firmware; rotate any cloud-sync credentials and recovery codes the appliance held; treat data on the appliance as potentially read by the attacker.
response.adequacy: Operationally expensive for consumer deployments; many operators skip the rebuild step.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: Consumer-NAS patch SLA undefined; the SI-2 baseline targets enterprise systems.

EU-CRA-Art13.gap: EU Cyber Resilience Act applies to consumer-IoT in scope but enforcement begins 2027; pre-enforcement compliance is voluntary.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.9.gap: Configuration-management control covers organizational assets; consumer NAS appliances at remote sites are commonly out of scope of the enterprise CMDB.

compliance_exposure_score.basis: Consumer-NAS appliances are pervasive at branch / SMB / remote-worker sites and routinely fall outside enterprise patch and asset-management programs.

new_control_requirements.name: BACKUP-TIER-NETWORK-ISOLATION
new_control_requirements.description: A BeeStation is a consumer NAS whose whole purpose is holding the primary and backup copy of a household's or a branch site's data, and the packet's attack path reaches it with no credential and no user interaction — a pre-auth chain against the BeeStation Manager web management surface ending in OS command execution on the box that holds the data. Applied to this product, the control means the BeeStation Manager web surface answers only from an operator subnet or an authenticated VPN: not from the general user VLAN, and not from the internet via a UPnP mapping or a home-router port forward, which is how consumer NAS hardware at remote-worker and small-branch sites normally acquires exposure. The appliance's outbound path should be constrained too, so a rooted BeeStation cannot reach arbitrary destinations with the data it holds. Reachability is the entire exploit precondition for a pre-auth CWE-78 flaw, and it is the only lever an operator holds between a public exploit chain and a firmware update landing on a device that no enterprise console manages — there is a vendor patch but no live-patch path, so the appliance has to be taken through the update to remediate. The distinguishing test: from a general user VLAN and from an external address, attempt to load the BeeStation Manager web surface; anything that answers is within reach of the published chain, and "the NAS is on the internal network" is an assertion about topology, not a demonstration that the management surface is unreachable from untrusted segments.

CVSS 9.8, RWEP 45, poc_available true, cisa_kev false, active_exploitation unknown, patch_available true, live_patch_available false (live_patch_notes null). UK-CAF-B4 (system security) is already recorded as an insufficient control citing this CVE.

new_control_requirements.name: SCANNER-PAPER-COMPLIANCE-TEST

new_control_requirements.name: BACKUP-TIER-NETWORK-ISOLATION

new_control_requirements.name: BACKUP-TIER-NETWORK-ISOLATION
new_control_requirements.description: On the QNAP TS-453E the appliance is simultaneously the file store and the restore source, so code execution on it is code execution on the copy of the data an operator would recover from. Because a vendor patch exists but no live-patch path is registered for this entry, the appliance has to be taken through a firmware update to remediate — isolation is what covers the interval, and it collapses all three chain components at once rather than one CVE id at a time. The distinguishing test: from a user VLAN and from an external address, attempt to load the TS-453E's QTS / QuTS hero web management surface; anything that answers is inside the chain's reach, and a policy that merely records "NAS appliances sit on the internal network" has not demonstrated the management plane is unreachable from untrusted segments.

The distinguishing test: query the register for the TS-453E firmware build and confirm all three chain ids resolve to a closed state on that same build; a register showing one closed and the siblings absent is reporting on its feed coverage, not on whether the appliance can still be chained to privileged execution.

new_control_requirements.name: BACKUP-TIER-NETWORK-ISOLATION
new_control_requirements.description: The TS-453E is a NAS, so the box that this chain lands privileged execution on is the box holding the data. The packet places this CVE as the elevation step that converts the unauthenticated RCE foothold from the chain's earlier components into appliance-level privileged execution, which means the operator-side lever is the network position of the appliance rather than anything about the elevation primitive itself.
