new_control_requirements.name: BROWSER-MANAGED-UPDATE-NO-DEFERRAL
new_control_requirements.description: The fix for this Dawn/WebGPU use-after-free reaches endpoints only as a browser security-channel release, so any managed update ring that pins a version or holds the security channel for staging leaves the sandbox-escape link of the chain live fleet-wide. Managed browser policy has to let the security channel land within 24h and force the relaunch that actually replaces the running GPU process — an updated binary on disk beside a browser session that has not been restarted is still executing the vulnerable Dawn code.
new_control_requirements.evidence: KEV-listed 2026-04-01 with confirmed in-the-wild exploitation, a public PoC, and a patch available; the flaw is the sandbox-escape step used after the renderer is already compromised, so it is the link that converts a contained renderer bug into host code execution.

new_control_requirements.name: SCANNER-PAPER-COMPLIANCE-TEST
new_control_requirements.description: A scan that reports the installed browser version as fixed does not prove this defect is gone. Dawn is Chromium's WebGPU implementation, so the same component ships inside Chromium-derived browsers and inside desktop applications that embed Chromium, each on its own update cadence and none of them moved by the browser's updater. The operational test: does the scan enumerate every Chromium-embedding runtime on the host as a separate versioned asset, record whether WebGPU is reachable in each, and read the version of the running process rather than the installed package?
new_control_requirements.evidence: Patch available and KEV-listed 2026-04-01 with confirmed exploitation; the packet locates the flaw in Dawn/WebGPU rather than in a single vendor application, and exploitation requires prior renderer compromise, so the escape path only matters where a vulnerable Dawn build is actually loaded.

attack_vector.description: an out-of-bounds read (CWE-125) on Citrix NetScaler, disclosing adjacent memory used to steal authenticated session material. CISA KEV-listed 2026-03-30 with confirmed in-the-wild exploitation.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none (the flaw is reachable by an unauthenticated attacker on the appliance's public interface)
attack_vector.complexity: low — KEV-listed, actively exploited; treat as weaponized
attack_vector.ai_factor: No AI involvement documented in discovery or weaponization.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Apply the Citrix NetScaler security update; invalidate active sessions and rotate session secrets — a patch alone does not revoke tokens already exfiltrated from memory.
prevention.adequacy: Patch is necessary but insufficient alone: tokens already disclosed from memory survive the patch and must be revoked via session termination + secret rotation.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Monitoring on the NetScaler: exploit-shaped requests, oversized/leaked response bodies (for the OOB-read class), appliance crashes (for the memory-corruption class), and session reuse with no matching login event.
detection.adequacy: Necessary to catch token-theft and post-exploit footholds that survive patching.

response.what_would_have_worked: Patch immediately; for the OOB-read class terminate sessions and rotate secrets, for the RCE class rebuild the appliance from a known-good image and rotate all credentials it held; review for lateral movement off the edge plane.
response.adequacy: Mandatory; a patch-in-place without session revocation or appliance rebuild leaves the attacker resident or with stolen session material.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: The 30-day flaw-remediation SLA is far longer than the observed exploitation window for a KEV-listed flaw on an internet-facing perimeter appliance; CitrixBleed-class disclosures were mass-exploited within days.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: 'Appropriate timescales' is undefined; the standard 30-day reading is unsafe for an actively-exploited perimeter-appliance flaw.

NIS2-Art21-network-security.gap: Treats perimeter appliances as essential-function infrastructure but lacks a CISA-KEV-style compressed remediation SLA, and does not mandate the session-revocation/credential-rotation cleanup these memory-disclosure flaws require.

PCI-DSS-4.0-6.3.3.gap: The 30-day critical-patch window is exploitation acceptance for an internet-facing edge appliance fronting the CDE.

compliance_exposure_score.basis: Citrix NetScaler is a load-bearing perimeter device run by audited organizations on standard change-controlled patch windows; the required session-revocation/rebuild cleanup is rarely part of the documented patch procedure.

new_control_requirements.name: PERIMETER-DEVICE-ZERODAY-SLA-TIER
new_control_requirements.description: When NetScaler is configured as a SAML IDP it is the authentication enforcement point for everything behind it, so its remediation tier cannot be derived from the CVE's severity band. This entry reads as a low-severity information disclosure by CVSS, yet the memory it overreads is authenticated session material and it is KEV-listed with confirmed in-the-wild exploitation — the RWEP score is 77 against a CVSS of 5.5. A vulnerability-management program that sorts by CVSS puts this appliance in the routine maintenance window. The tier requirement for this CVE: the update is due on the KEV clock, or the SAML IDP virtual server is taken out of service until the appliance is on a fixed build. Nothing upstream compensates, because the vulnerable device is the trust boundary the upstream controls delegate to.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet: out-of-bounds read (CWE-125) on NetScaler ADC, NetScaler Gateway and NetScaler ADC FIPS/NDcPP when configured as a SAML IDP, leading to memory overread; the attack vector is described as disclosing adjacent memory used to steal authenticated session material. cisa_kev true, kev_date 2026-03-30, active_exploitation confirmed, poc_available true; cvss 5.5 against rwep_score 77.

new_control_requirements.name: PERIMETER-COMPROMISE-REBUILD-NOT-PATCH
new_control_requirements.description: Updating this appliance stops the overread but does nothing about what has already left it. The exploited primitive hands an attacker authenticated session material read out of the SAML IDP's memory, and that material stays valid after the fix is applied — the vulnerability is closed while the access it produced is not. Remediation for this CVE must be run as compromise response rather than maintenance: once the appliance is on a fixed build, terminate every active session, rotate and reissue the session and signing secrets the IDP holds, rotate credentials that traversed it, and review the authentications it brokered during the exposure window (from KEV listing back through the earliest plausible exploitation). Patch-in-place with standing sessions is the failure mode this control exists to prevent.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet: out-of-bounds read (CWE-125) in the SAML IDP path of NetScaler, disclosing adjacent memory used to steal authenticated session material; active_exploitation confirmed, cisa_kev true with kev_date 2026-03-30, poc_available true. patch_available true, live_patch_available false, live_patch_notes recording no registered live-patch tool and a vendor patch that typically requires service restart or system reboot per the KEV requiredAction.

new_control_requirements.name: PERIMETER-DEVICE-ZERODAY-SLA-TIER
new_control_requirements.description: A BIG-IP APM appliance is the trust boundary for the remote-access path it fronts, so the routine 14/30-day windows generic vulnerability-management controls allow are the wrong clock for an unauthenticated stack-based overflow reaching code execution on its data path. There is no live-patch path for this entry and the vendor fix requires a service restart or system reboot per the KEV requiredAction, so the SLA has to pre-authorize a failover or downtime window on the appliance itself. new_control_requirements.name: PERIMETER-COMPROMISE-REBUILD-NOT-PATCH
new_control_requirements.description: Confirmed in-the-wild exploitation plus a public PoC against an unauthenticated RCE on BIG-IP APM means any appliance that was network-reachable before the fix has to be treated as possibly already running attacker code, not merely as unpatched. The default IR path for this CVE is capture the running configuration off the box, rebuild the appliance from vendor media, and rotate the credentials and keys the appliance held or proxied before it returns to service. Installing the vendor fix removes the overflow; it does not remove anything an operator installed through the overflow beforehand, and the restart the fix requires is a convenient moment for an implant to reload. new_control_requirements.description: The defect here is not a coding mistake in Trivy that a newer release fixes by accident — per the packet the malicious code was embedded in what shipped as a Trivy distribution/component. attack_vector.description: Path traversal (CWE-22) in Semantic Kernel's SessionsPythonPlugin allows arbitrary file write; because the plugin runs inside an agent wired to tools, an injected prompt (AML.T0051) drives the write to a location that yields host code execution — a single prompt launched calc.exe on the agent host.

Surfaced via the Microsoft Security Blog + GHSA feeds.

new_control_requirements.description: Any AI agent wired to tools that can write files or execute code must treat its tool boundary as an attacker-reachable remote-code-execution boundary: sandbox file-writing / code-running plugins with strict path and capability confinement, validate and canonicalize all tool-supplied paths against traversal, gate code-execution tools behind out-of-band human approval for untrusted-content-triggered invocations, and track agent-framework SDK dependencies (e.g. Microsoft.SemanticKernel.Plugins.Core >= 1.71.0) as KEV-priority patch targets. Prompt injection must be modeled as a code-execution primitive, not a content-safety nuisance.

CVE-2026-24207.name: NVIDIA Triton Inference Server Authentication Bypass (Alternate Path) RCE

attack_vector.description: NVIDIA Triton Inference Server exposes a control-plane path that bypasses its authentication layer (CWE-288), so an unauthenticated network attacker reaches privileged model-control functionality without credentials.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none (NVD AV:N / PR:N) — unauthenticated over the network
attack_vector.complexity: low (NVD AC:L)
attack_vector.ai_factor: The abused surface is the authentication layer of a widely deployed AI inference server. NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: Flaw-remediation cadence does not track AI inference servers as network-exposed control planes requiring rapid patching.

ALL-AI-PIPELINE-INTEGRITY.gap: No framework requires the inference server's authentication to be proven complete across all request paths.

compliance_exposure_score.basis: Organizations assert authentication coverage for the inference API but do not test every alternate path into the model control plane; inference servers are rarely in the managed vulnerability program.

new_control_requirements.name: AI-INFERENCE-SERVER-AUTH-ENFORCEMENT

new_control_requirements.evidence: https://nvidia.custhelp.com/app/answers/detail/a_id/5828

CVE-2024-0132.name: NVIDIA Container Toolkit TOCTOU Container Escape

compliance_exposure_score.basis: Organizations treat container isolation as a given and do not track the GPU container runtime version; shared GPU clouds run mixed-tenant workloads on the same hosts.

CVE-2025-1550.name: Keras .keras Model Deserialization Arbitrary Code Execution

attack_vector.description: Keras's .keras model parser uses importlib on names from the model archive, so a crafted model executes arbitrary Python at load time (CWE-94) — no Lambda layer or custom object, no need to call the model.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none beyond getting a victim to load an untrusted .keras model
attack_vector.complexity: low
attack_vector.ai_factor: The abused surface is the ML model file format itself — the canonical AI supply-chain risk: an untrusted model artifact is executable code at load time. The lesson, sharpened by the CVE-2025-1550 -> CVE-2025-8747 sequence, is that model artifacts must be treated as untrusted code (provenance, scanning, safe formats like safetensors), and a partial mitigation such as safe_mode is necessary-but-insufficient when it can be bypassed.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: Does not track ML frameworks' model-loading paths as RCE-bearing, nor that the first fix (safe_mode) was bypassable.

NIST-800-53-SI-10.gap: Model artifacts are treated as data, but Keras executes code while parsing them; no validation is applied to the artifact.

ALL-AI-PIPELINE-INTEGRITY.gap: No framework treats an ML model file as untrusted executable input; loading one from an untrusted source is RCE.

compliance_exposure_score.basis: ML pipelines pull models from hubs and user uploads and treat them as data; safe_mode is assumed sufficient despite the documented bypass.

new_control_requirements.name: UNTRUSTED-MODEL-ARTIFACT-LOADING
new_control_requirements.description: Treat ML model artifacts as untrusted code: never load .keras / pickle-based models from untrusted sources, verify provenance, prefer safe formats (e.g. safetensors), and load untrusted models only in a sandboxed, network-isolated, least-privilege environment. The distinguishing test: load an attacker-crafted .keras archive with safe_mode enabled on a sandboxed instance and confirm no code executes.

CVE-2024-42479.name: llama.cpp RPC Backend SET_TENSOR Out-of-Bounds Write RCE

attack_vector.description: llama.cpp's RPC backend deserializes attacker-controlled tensor pointers without bounds validation (CWE-787/CWE-123 write-what-where via SET_TENSOR), so an unauthenticated TCP client to the RPC server (default port 50052) reads/writes arbitrary memory and achieves code execution.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none (NVD AV:N / PR:N) — unauthenticated TCP access to the RPC server
attack_vector.complexity: low (NVD AC:L)
attack_vector.ai_factor: The abused surface is the distributed-inference RPC backend of the most widely used local LLM runtime. The lesson: the inference RPC backend is an unauthenticated execution boundary that must validate all deserialized tensor bounds on every command path and never be network-exposed. The CVE-2024-42478/42479 -> CVE-2026-34159 sequence shows per-command patching (GET/SET) left GRAPH_COMPUTE exploitable — the fix belongs in deserialize_tensor itself.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: Does not track the local-LLM runtime's RPC backend as RCE-bearing, nor that the first fix left the GRAPH_COMPUTE path unpatched.

NIST-800-53-SC-7.gap: Does not flag the unauthenticated RPC server (port 50052) as a network-exposed execution surface.

ALL-AI-PIPELINE-INTEGRITY.gap: No framework requires the inference RPC backend to validate deserialized tensor bounds on every command path.

compliance_exposure_score.basis: Local-LLM RPC servers are run on trusted-network assumptions and rarely tracked; per-command patches are assumed complete despite the GRAPH_COMPUTE bypass.

new_control_requirements.name: AI-INFERENCE-RPC-BACKEND-HARDENING
new_control_requirements.description: The inference RPC backend (llama.cpp / ggml) must validate all deserialized tensor bounds inside deserialize_tensor itself — every command path (GET_TENSOR, SET_TENSOR, GRAPH_COMPUTE), not per-handler — and must never be exposed to untrusted networks (the RPC server on port 50052 has no authentication; bind to localhost or a trusted segment). Upgrade llama.cpp to b8492 or later — b3561 fixed only GET_TENSOR / SET_TENSOR (CVE-2024-42478 / CVE-2024-42479), and builds b3561 through b8491 remain exploitable via the GRAPH_COMPUTE buffer=0 path (CVE-2026-34159), which b8492 closes. The distinguishing test: send a crafted rpc_tensor with buffer=0 / out-of-range data pointer via GRAPH_COMPUTE to a staging RPC server and confirm it is rejected, not dereferenced.
new_control_requirements.evidence: https://github.com/ggerganov/llama.cpp/security/advisories/GHSA-wcr5-566p-9cwj

CVE-2023-43654.name: PyTorch TorchServe Management API SSRF to Remote Code Execution (ShellTorch)

attack_vector.description: PyTorch TorchServe Management API SSRF to Remote Code Execution (ShellTorch): CWE-918 SSRF in the management API. In the ShellTorch chain, an unauthenticated, network-exposed TorchServe management API accepts a remote model configuration and parses it with an unsafe YAML deserializer, yielding full remote code execution on the model server.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none (NVD PR:N) — default-configured TorchServe is open and unauthenticated
attack_vector.complexity: low (NVD AC:L)
attack_vector.ai_factor: The abused surface is an AI model server (TorchServe, maintained by Amazon and Meta) and the libraries it bundles. The lesson: a model server's management API is a privileged control plane that must authenticate, bind to loopback, and never deserialize untrusted config unsafely — Oligo found thousands of exposed instances at major organizations, so the default-open posture is the real-world exposure.

NIST-800-53-IA-2.gap: Authentication is not enforced on the model server's management API; the default deployment is open and network-exposed.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: Does not track AI model servers and their bundled deserialization libraries as managed, RCE-bearing software.

ALL-AI-PIPELINE-INTEGRITY.gap: No framework treats the model server's management API + config deserialization as an untrusted, RCE-bearing surface.

compliance_exposure_score.basis: Model servers are deployed with default-open management planes on trusted-network assumptions; bundled YAML/deserialization libraries are not tracked.

new_control_requirements.name: AI-MODEL-SERVER-MANAGEMENT-API-HARDENING
new_control_requirements.description: An AI model server's management API must authenticate every caller, bind to loopback (not all interfaces) by default, restrict model sources to an allow-list (no fetching configs/archives from arbitrary URLs), and parse configuration with safe deserializers (SafeConstructor / no arbitrary type instantiation). Upgrade TorchServe 0.8.2+ and bind the management API to loopback with authentication. The distinguishing test: from an unauthenticated remote client, attempt to register a model from an attacker URL against a staging model server and confirm it is refused and no remote content is fetched or deserialized.

CVE-2024-37032.name: Ollama Model Registry Path Traversal Arbitrary File Write RCE (Probllama)

attack_vector.description: Ollama CWE-22 path traversal via unvalidated model-blob digest: an attacker reaching the Ollama HTTP API (default port 11434) manipulates a path/digest the runtime then uses against the filesystem, writing attacker content to an arbitrary path and achieving RCE.
attack_vector.privileges_required: low / network (NVD PR:L) — reachable via the Ollama API + a rogue registry
attack_vector.complexity: low (NVD AC:L)
attack_vector.ai_factor: The abused surface is the model-pull / model API of the most widely used local LLM runtime. The lesson: the model-runtime API must validate digests and path parameters and must never be network-exposed to untrusted clients; pulling from untrusted registries is a supply-chain trust decision.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: Does not track the local-LLM runtime as managed, network-exposed software.

NIST-800-53-SI-10.gap: Input validation is not applied to model-blob digests / API path parameters in the runtime.

ALL-AI-PIPELINE-INTEGRITY.gap: No framework treats the model-runtime API's path/digest handling as untrusted input reaching the filesystem.

compliance_exposure_score.basis: Local-LLM runtimes are run on trusted-network assumptions and rarely tracked; model pulls from arbitrary registries are not gated.

new_control_requirements.name: AI-RUNTIME-API-PATH-TRAVERSAL-VALIDATION
new_control_requirements.description: The model-runtime API must validate path-bearing inputs (model-blob digests must be exactly 64-hex SHA256; API route parameters must reject traversal sequences) before touching the filesystem, must not be exposed to untrusted networks (Ollama default port 11434), and must only pull models from trusted registries. Upgrade Ollama to 0.1.34 or later. The distinguishing test: point a staging Ollama at a rogue registry whose manifest carries a traversal digest, and send api/push requests with ../ sequences, and confirm both are rejected without filesystem access.
new_control_requirements.evidence: https://www.wiz.io/blog/probllama-ollama-vulnerability-cve-2024-37032

CVE-2024-13059.name: AnythingLLM Non-ASCII Filename Path Traversal Arbitrary File Write to RCE

attack_vector.description: AnythingLLM's multer-based upload handler mishandles non-ASCII filenames so they decode into ../ traversal sequences (CWE-22), letting a manager/admin user write to an arbitrary path and achieve RCE.
attack_vector.privileges_required: manager or admin account (NVD PR:H)
attack_vector.complexity: low (NVD AC:L)
attack_vector.ai_factor: The abused surface is the document-upload handler of a self-hosted RAG / AI chat application. The lesson matches the Ollama path-traversal case: AI-app file/path handling must canonicalize and validate names (including non-ASCII / encoding transforms) before touching the filesystem, and privileged roles are not a substitute for input validation.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: Does not track self-hosted RAG / AI chat applications as managed, RCE-bearing software.

NIST-800-53-SI-10.gap: Input validation is not applied to uploaded filenames (including non-ASCII transformations) in the AI app's upload handler.

ALL-AI-PIPELINE-INTEGRITY.gap: No framework treats the AI app's document-upload filename as untrusted input reaching the filesystem.

compliance_exposure_score.basis: Self-hosted RAG apps are deployed for internal teams and assumed trusted; upload filename handling (especially non-ASCII) is not audited for traversal.

new_control_requirements.name: AI-RUNTIME-API-PATH-TRAVERSAL-VALIDATION
new_control_requirements.description: An AI application's file/path-bearing inputs (upload filenames, model digests, API route parameters) must be canonicalized and validated — including non-ASCII / encoding transforms — before touching the filesystem, and the app must not be network-exposed to untrusted users. Upgrade AnythingLLM to 1.3.1 or later. This is the same control that closes the Ollama path-traversal CVEs. CVE-2026-45498.name: Microsoft Defender Remote Denial of Service (Antimalware Platform)

attack_vector.description: Uncontrolled resource consumption (CWE-400) in the Microsoft Defender antimalware platform, reachable over the network without authentication, lets an attacker crash or hang Defender — remotely removing the host's AV/EDR coverage (defense impairment, ATT&CK T1685).
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — remote, unauthenticated (NVD AV:N / PR:N)
attack_vector.complexity: low (NVD AC:L); availability-only (C:N/I:N/A:H)
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered. The lesson: AV/EDR availability is itself a control, and its remote loss is a security event, not just an outage — a disable-able defender is an intrusion enabler. Surfaced by the CISA-KEV poller after the v0.13.17 bulk intake.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: 30-day SLA inadequate for a KEV-listed flaw; KEV due date (2026-06-03) is the binding clock.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: Does not treat remote loss of AV/EDR availability as a monitored security event distinct from a routine outage.

compliance_exposure_score.basis: Most programs verify AV/EDR is deployed but do not alarm when it is remotely disabled; a host going dark on Defender telemetry is often treated as an IT availability blip, not a defense-evasion precursor.

new_control_requirements.name: AV-EDR-AVAILABILITY-MONITORING
new_control_requirements.description: Treat loss of AV/EDR availability as a first-class security event: alarm when an endpoint stops reporting Defender/EDR telemetry or its protection service crashes/restarts abnormally, correlate with inbound network activity, and patch the Defender antimalware platform to the fixed build (4.18.26040.7) as a KEV-priority item. A remotely-disable-able defender must not fail silent.

attack_vector.complexity: low — KEV-listed, actively exploited; treat as weaponized

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Apply the Craft CMS update, rotate the Craft security key and any credentials the app held, and hunt for web shells — code-injection RCE is routinely followed by persistence.
prevention.adequacy: Patch is necessary but, for web-app RCE/upload/auth-bypass, insufficient alone — web shells and stolen credentials/secrets survive the patch and require explicit cleanup.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Monitoring on the Craft CMS: exploit-shaped requests, new web-shell files under the web root, unexpected process execution by the app, and administrative actions without a matching authenticated session.
detection.adequacy: Necessary to catch resident persistence after patching; WAF rules help but trail novel payloads.

response.what_would_have_worked: Patch immediately, hunt and remove web shells, rotate application secrets and credentials, and review data accessible through the Craft CMS for exfiltration; assume compromise of any account reachable from it.
response.adequacy: Mandatory; patch-in-place without web-shell hunting and secret rotation leaves the attacker resident.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: The 30-day flaw-remediation SLA is far longer than the observed exploitation window for a KEV-listed, unauthenticated web-application RCE/auth-bypass; these are mass-exploited within days of disclosure.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: 'Appropriate timescales' is undefined; the standard 30-day reading is unsafe for an actively-exploited, internet-facing web application.

compliance_exposure_score.basis: Internet-facing Craft CMS is run by audited organizations on a standard patch SLA and is mass-exploited within days of disclosure; the required web-shell hunt and secret rotation are rarely part of the documented patch procedure.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: A Craft CMS instance is a public web head and the flaw is unauthenticated code injection on that surface, so the mitigation clock starts at the KEV listing (2026-03-20), not at the next site-maintenance window. There is no live-patch path and the vendor fix requires a service restart per the KEV requiredAction — meaning SLA compliance here depends on the web-tier restart authorization being pre-granted rather than requested through change approval after the listing. Where a restart genuinely cannot happen inside the window, the accepted outcome is a documented, time-bound compensating control (take the affected head out of rotation and keep it out) — not a deferral note against an instance still serving the vulnerable path.

new_control_requirements.name: PERIMETER-COMPROMISE-REBUILD-NOT-PATCH
new_control_requirements.description: With confirmed in-the-wild exploitation of an unauthenticated CWE-94 flaw, every Craft CMS head that was internet-reachable before the update landed must be treated as already executed against, not merely as having been vulnerable. Installing the vendor release closes the injection path but leaves whatever the attacker wrote through it — files in the web root, template or plugin code, database-resident content, added administrative accounts — and leaves every credential the web process could read still valid. The runbook for this CVE must default to: export configuration and content for review, rebuild the web head from a known-good image on the fixed release rather than upgrading the live instance, restore content through inspection instead of restoring the running filesystem, and rotate every secret reachable from the web process.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: The remediation unit here is not an OS package but a Composer-managed component living inside every Laravel application that uses Livewire, so the KEV clock has to be run against an inventory of applications rather than an inventory of hosts. For this CVE that means: enumerate every Laravel deployment whose lockfile resolves Livewire, bump the package to the fixed release, redeploy the built artifact, and restart the PHP-FPM and queue workers so long-lived processes stop serving the old code — there is no live-patch path and the vendor patch typically requires a service restart or system reboot per the KEV required action, so the restart is part of the remediation rather than a deferral point. The packet qualifies the flaw as reaching unauthenticated remote command execution in specific scenarios, which is the reason a host-level scan is not sufficient evidence of closure: an operator cannot tell from a server inventory which applications sit in the exposed configuration. With confirmed in-the-wild exploitation from the 2026-03-20 listing, the four-hour target starts at KEV listing / patch availability rather than at the next release train, and a Laravel estate whose deploys are gated on a weekly window has no way to meet it without an out-of-band path for a single dependency bump. The distinguishing test: on a production host, confirm the Livewire version actually loaded by the running PHP workers is the fixed one — not the version declared in the repository lockfile, which says what the next deploy will ship, not what is serving traffic now.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet: CWE-94 code injection enabling unauthenticated remote command execution on the web server, described as reachable in specific scenarios. CISA KEV-listed 2026-03-20 with active_exploitation confirmed; CVSS 9.8, RWEP 77, poc_available true. patch_available true, live_patch_available false, and live_patch_notes records that no live-patch tool is registered and that the vendor patch typically requires a service restart or system reboot per the KEV requiredAction.

new_control_requirements.name: PERIMETER-COMPROMISE-REBUILD-NOT-PATCH
new_control_requirements.description: Livewire's defect runs attacker-supplied code inside the PHP process that serves the request, with no credential required, and in-the-wild exploitation is confirmed from the 2026-03-20 listing. Any internet-reachable Laravel application that was serving traffic during that window therefore has to be triaged as possibly compromised rather than closed out when the dependency is bumped: updating the package removes the injection sink but removes nothing the injected code already did — a PHP file written under the application's public or storage tree, a poisoned compiled view or cached container file, a queued job, an added administrative user, or a read of the application's environment file that handed over its database, cache, mail and third-party API credentials in one request. The control for this deployment: redeploy the application from the build pipeline onto a clean host image rather than patching the running one, restore the code tree from version control rather than editing in place, and rotate every secret the application process could read, since the exploit path could read all of them. The distinguishing test after remediation: diff the deployed file tree against the artifact the build pipeline produced, and treat any file the pipeline did not emit as the finding — a "patched per SLA" verdict recorded against the Livewire version attests to what is running now and says nothing about what ran during the exposure window.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet: CWE-94 code injection giving unauthenticated remote command execution on the web server; CISA KEV-listed 2026-03-20 with active_exploitation confirmed; poc_available true; RWEP 77 against CVSS 9.8; patch_available true with live_patch_available false.

new_control_requirements.name: MOBILE-ENDPOINT-MDM-ENFORCED-KEV-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: The affected surface spans watchOS, iOS, iPadOS, macOS, visionOS and tvOS, and the fix is a full OS build with no live-patch path — so for this entry the control means the KEV clock that opened 2026-03-20 drives the update across the managed Apple estate on a declared short SLA with user deferral disallowed, not on the estate's normal OS-upgrade cadence. Completion must be measured by each device's installed build against the fixed build for its product, and because the vendor fix typically requires a service restart or system reboot, a device that has downloaded or staged the update but not restarted is still running the vulnerable code and counts as exposed rather than remediated. Precondition: the declarative-management lever exists for enrolled iPhone, iPad and Mac. The watchOS, tvOS and visionOS units named in the same packet are commonly updated through a paired device or are not enrolled at all, so no-deferral enforcement does not reach them — those must be enumerated separately and driven manually or held outside the trust boundary until their build is confirmed. Omitting them makes the SLA report read complete while the devices nobody enrolled are the ones still carrying the flaw.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet fields for this entry: the vector states that Apple watchOS, iOS, iPadOS, macOS, visionOS and tvOS contain an improper locking vulnerability (CWE-667) that could allow a malicious application to cause unexpected changes in memory shared between processes. cisa_kev true with kev_date 2026-03-20, active_exploitation confirmed, poc_available true, cvss 8.8, rwep_score 77. patch_available true and live_patch_available false, with live_patch_notes: "No live-patch tool registered for this entry at bulk-import time. Vendor patch typically requires service restart or system reboot per the KEV requiredAction." NIST-800-53-SI-2 (Flaw Remediation) and NIS2-Art21-patch-management (Vulnerability handling and disclosure) are recorded as citing gaps against this entry.

new_control_requirements.name: MOBILE-OS-MINIMUM-PATCH-LEVEL-ENFORCEMENT
new_control_requirements.description: The recorded trigger is a malicious application causing unexpected changes in memory shared between processes, so for this entry the control's access-condition half is the load-bearing one: on any Apple device that cannot yet take the fixed build, the operator's remaining levers are constraining what code is allowed to run at all and withholding organizational data from the device until its build is at or above the fix. The fixed build must function as an access condition — mail, VPN and document access denied to a device below it — not as a row on a patch-compliance dashboard. The distinguishing test is to enrol a device pinned below the fixed build and confirm the policy actually denies it access to protected resources; an estate that surfaces the stale build on a report while the device keeps its access has recorded the exposure rather than removed it. Precondition: restricting untrusted or side-loaded application installation raises the bar for getting the attacker's application onto the device, but it does not evict an application already installed, and it does not cover one that arrived through the normal store channel. A device suspected of already running the malicious application belongs on the incident path, not the install-policy path. This is a holding measure for the window before the fixed build and its required restart land, not a substitute for them.

new_control_requirements.description: n8n is the visual workflow/agent builder class this control governs, and the defect sits in exactly the sink the control names: the workflow expression evaluation system, a dynamic-evaluation path that turns workflow-supplied content into executable code. Preconditions, all of which must be recorded rather than assumed: this bounds who can reach the evaluator, it does not repair the evaluator, so the vendor update remains the only fix for the flaw itself. Anyone already holding an editor-capable account is inside the authentication boundary and the control does nothing against them. Confinement added after the fact does not evict an attacker resident from an earlier execution on that host. And where a trigger must stay reachable by untrusted callers for the workflow to do its job, that path cannot be closed by authentication at all — for it, the update is the only remedy and the interim state is exposure, not mitigation.

attack_vector.privileges_required: none (the device is reachable by an unauthenticated attacker; exposure is amplified when the OT zone is not segmented)
attack_vector.complexity: low — KEV-listed, actively exploited; treat as weaponized
attack_vector.ai_factor: No AI involvement documented in discovery or weaponization.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Apply the vendor firmware/update where one exists; where the device cannot be patched, isolate it in a segmented OT zone (zones-and-conduits / Purdue model), block all IT and internet reachability, and restrict access to authenticated engineering workstations.
prevention.adequacy: Patching is often impossible on OT; segmentation and access restriction are the real controls, and a flat or internet-exposed OT network defeats them.

detection.what_would_have_worked: OT-network monitoring for unauthorized connections to the Rockwell Logix PLC, unexpected configuration/logic changes, and access from outside the device's intended zone.
detection.adequacy: Necessary because unpatched OT devices may stay exploitable indefinitely; behavioral detection is the backstop.

response.what_would_have_worked: Isolate the device, validate and restore its configuration/logic from a known-good baseline, rotate any credentials/keys it held, and investigate for safety-impacting manipulation; engage OT/safety engineering before any change.
response.adequacy: Mandatory; OT compromise can have physical/safety consequences, so response must include process-integrity validation, not just IT cleanup.

NIST-800-82r3-ICS.gap: OT/ICS devices often cannot be patched on an IT cadence (availability and safety constraints, vendor re-certification), so the exposure window for a KEV-listed flaw is months-to-years; the standard treats patching as primary but for OT the load-bearing control is network segmentation and access restriction.

IEC-62443-3-3-zones-conduits.gap: Zones-and-conduits segmentation is required, but it is frequently unimplemented or bypassed (flat OT networks, internet-exposed HMIs/cameras/PLCs); the device itself is exploitable whenever it is reachable, and the standard does not force a compromised-device response plan.

NIS2-Art21-OT.gap: Treats OT/ICS as essential-function infrastructure but lacks a device-level compressed remediation expectation and does not address the reality that many OT devices are end-of-life or unpatchable and must be isolated rather than fixed.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: 'Appropriate timescales' is undefined and ill-suited to OT, where patching may be impossible; compensating controls (segmentation, monitoring, restricted engineering-workstation access) carry the load and must be explicit.

compliance_exposure_score.basis: Rockwell Automation Logix controllers is OT/ICS equipment that frequently cannot be patched on an IT cadence and is often reachable on flat or internet-exposed networks; audited organizations that rely on a patch SLA rather than enforced segmentation remain exposed for this KEV-listed, actively-exploited flaw.

new_control_requirements.name: OT-DEFAULT-CREDENTIAL-ELIMINATION
new_control_requirements.description: This exploit has one access requirement: an unauthorized user would require network access to the controller. So on this entry the segmentation half of this control is the load-bearing half, and the credential-elimination half is not a lever the operator holds — the key that authenticates design software to Logix controllers is discoverable from Studio 5000 itself rather than set per site, so there is no vendor-default or blank administrative account for the operator to rotate away. Applied here, it means the Logix controllers' network interfaces answer only from a segmented engineering and management plane — the engineering workstations and servers with an operational need to program them — and not from a flat plant network, a general business VLAN, or any routable path from outside. Distinguishing test: from a segment with no programming role, attempt to open a connection to a Logix controller on a staging cell; anything that answers is within reach of the published exploit, because past that point the attacker supplies the key from the design software rather than obtaining anything from the target. Precondition: segmentation bounds the population that can reach the controller, it does not repair the key handling. The packet's stated requirement is only network access to the controller, so any compromised engineering workstation, contractor laptop or jump host already inside the permitted segment satisfies that precondition in full, and the segmentation does nothing against an unauthorized application running on a host that legitimately talks to the controller. It is a holding measure for the window before the vendor update, not a closure.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet vector: 'This key is used to verify Logix controllers are communicating with Rockwell Automation design software. If successfully exploited, this vulnerability could allow an unauthorized application to connect with Logix controllers. To leverage this vulnerability, an unauthorized user would require network access to the controller.' Packet: CISA KEV listed 2026-03-05, active_exploitation confirmed, poc_available true, RWEP 77, CVSS 8.8.

new_control_requirements.name: FRAMEWORK-DEFAULT-SECRET-DETECTION
new_control_requirements.description: The secret sits inside the product: Studio 5000 Logix Designer 'may allow a key to be discovered', and that key is what verifies Logix controllers are communicating with Rockwell design software. Because the constant an attacker needs is obtainable from the design software rather than from the target site, no amount of operator-side credential hygiene reduces the exposure — which is exactly why the least-privilege and identity-and-access-control gaps are recorded against this entry: the attacker never authenticates as any engineer, so per-account privilege scoping is never consulted and the account model an identity attestation examines is bypassed rather than abused. The control's requirement here is to inventory every Studio 5000 installation and every Logix controller in the estate as depending on a product-shipped verification key, gate each of those deployments on the vendor update rather than on a password or account policy, and re-run that check after any engineering-workstation rebuild, image restore or controller replacement, since those are the operations that quietly reintroduce an unpatched pairing at a site that had been remediated. Distinguishing test: produce, per cell, the Studio 5000 version and the controller firmware actually in service and show each is at or above the vendor's fixed level — an attestation that every engineer holds a unique Studio 5000 account passes cleanly while this flaw stays fully exploitable. Precondition: the vendor update is what removes the dependence on the discoverable key; this control is the inventory and the gate that ensure every installation reaches it, and it gives nothing on its own to a site that has not yet taken the update. It also does not detect a controller an unauthorized application has already connected to, so a cell that was reachable during the exposure window needs its controller configuration and control logic compared against a known-good copy rather than being closed on the patch.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet vector: 'Studio 5000 Logix Designer software may allow a key to be discovered. This key is used to verify Logix controllers are communicating with Rockwell Automation design software.' CWE-522. Citing gaps record NIST-800-53-AC-6 (Least Privilege) and UK-CAF-B2 (Identity and access control) against this entry. patch_available true; active_exploitation confirmed; poc_available true.

new_control_requirements.name: MITIGATION-ACTIVE-PATCH-PENDING-VERDICT-CLASS
new_control_requirements.description: There is a vendor patch, no live-patch path, and a fix that per the KEV requiredAction typically requires a service restart or system reboot. On Logix controllers driving a live process, that restart is scheduled against the process rather than against the 2026-03-05 KEV clock, which produces a long interval in which the estate's real state is 'reachability restricted, patch pending' — not remediated. This control requires that state to be recorded distinctly for each affected cell: the compensating control actually in force (the controller-reachability restriction), the residual risk it leaves (any host already inside the permitted segment still meets the exploit's only stated precondition, network access to the controller), and a dated action item tied to the next outage window in which the restart can be taken. It must not be reported as 'patched per SLA' and the KEV row must not be closed on the basis of the update having been obtained. Precondition and limit: this is a reporting-integrity control, not a technical mitigation — it changes what the audit sees, not what the attacker can reach, and it is only honest if the compensating control it records has been tested against a staging cell rather than asserted from a network diagram.

new_control_requirements.name: FLEET-CONTROL-PLANE-ADMIN-PRIVILEGE-TIER
new_control_requirements.description: Classify the Aria Operations administrators and the appliance's own integration/service identities as a management-plane privilege tier above ordinary application admins, instead of folding them into the generic admin scope that AC-6 is audited against. This does not prevent the vulnerability — no admin tiering gates an unauthenticated request, and the packet's attacker needs no credential — but it bounds what the attacker inherits the moment command execution lands on the appliance. The support-assisted product migration path named in the packet has to sit inside that tier as well: a vendor-assisted migration is a privileged-access event requiring JIT elevation and an approval record, not a standing exception on the management surface where this command-injection sink lives.

new_control_requirements.name: MOBILE-OS-MINIMUM-PATCH-LEVEL-ENFORCEMENT
new_control_requirements.description: The defect is in Qualcomm chipset code — memory corruption while using alignments for memory allocation — so no operator patches it directly. The fix reaches a device only inside the device maker's firmware/OS build, and the device's reported security-patch level is the only observable that tells an operator whether that build is actually installed. For a fleet containing devices on the affected chipsets, this control means the MDM/EMM must read the security-patch level and block or quarantine devices below the build carrying the Qualcomm fix as a condition of access to organizational data, rather than reporting the stale level on a dashboard. Because the packet's exploitation path is a local foothold escalating privilege on the device, devices that cannot yet receive an updated build must additionally be constrained against installing untrusted or side-loaded code, since that is what supplies the local execution the escalation needs. The distinguishing test: enroll a device pinned below the fixed build and confirm the policy denies it access to protected resources — a fleet that only records patch level leaves exploitable devices in production against a confirmed-exploited chipset flaw.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet: cisa_kev true, kev_date 2026-03-03, active_exploitation "confirmed", RWEP 77, CVSS 8.8, poc_available true. new_control_requirements.name: CONTROL-PANEL-PLUGIN-USER-SURFACE-MUST-NOT-REACH-ROOT-OPERATIONS
new_control_requirements.description: The Cisco SD-WAN application CLI is the constrained user surface this control governs. The packet's vector describes an authenticated local attacker gaining elevated privileges via improper access controls on commands within the application CLI, with a successful exploit allowing arbitrary commands as the root user — a user-facing surface wired straight to a root operation, which is the pattern the control forbids. Applied to this device, it means the SD-WAN privileged operations sit behind their own authorization boundary that the application CLI can only request through a constrained, validated interface, so that the CLI's own command-and-path handling is not the single thing standing between a non-root operator account and root. Preconditions: the vendor update is what repairs that boundary — the control states the property to verify, it does not implement it. Until the update is applied, the only operator-side lever is limiting which accounts can open a CLI session, which bounds the population that can attempt the escalation but does not close it, because any account that legitimately reaches the CLI still reaches root. And because active_exploitation is confirmed, a device whose CLI was reachable by a non-root account during the exposure window needs forensic triage and credential rotation; an update applied to a device that already granted root does not remove what the attacker left behind.
new_control_requirements.evidence: The packet's vector states that the Cisco SD-WAN CLI contains a path traversal vulnerability that could allow an authenticated local attacker to gain elevated privileges via improper access controls on commands within the application CLI, and that a successful exploit could allow the attacker to execute arbitrary commands as the root user. cwe_refs are CWE-25 and CWE-282. cvss 7.5, rwep_score 77, poc_available true, cisa_kev true with kev_date 2026-02-25 and active_exploitation confirmed. new_control_requirements.name: FLEET-CONTROL-PLANE-ADMIN-PRIVILEGE-TIER
new_control_requirements.description: An SD-WAN device CLI programs the WAN fabric that every site depends on, so the identities that can open a session on it belong in the fleet-control-plane tier this control defines rather than in a general network-operations account pool. For this CVE the tier is load-bearing on one half specifically: the packet's vector places the attacker at an authenticated CLI session, so routing every CLI path through a PAM jumphost with per-session step-up and just-in-time elevation shrinks the set of identities that can reach the vulnerable command handling at all, and makes each attempt attributable. The preconditions are where this control is usually recorded as holding when it does not. It only holds if every path to the device CLI is behind the same gate — console and out-of-band or serial access, recovery and break-glass accounts, and any automation or monitoring service account that logs into the device all bypass a jumphost by default and re-open the full path unless they are enumerated and brought under it. And the tier does not fix the escalation itself: an identity that legitimately passes the gate still reaches root through the flaw. This is a blast-radius and attribution measure that runs alongside the vendor update, never a substitute for it.

Note the packet is internally inconsistent on the privilege precondition: the attack_vector summary line instead describes the flaw as reachable by an unauthenticated attacker, contradicting the vector field this description relies on.

new_control_requirements.name: DEVICE-MANAGEMENT-GATEWAY-CONFIG-ENDPOINT-AUTH-INPUT-NEUTRALIZATION
new_control_requirements.description: Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Controller (formerly SD-WAN vSmart) and Catalyst SD-WAN Manager (formerly SD-WAN vManage) are the management plane in scope, and the defect sits on the interface where they authenticate fabric peers: the peering authentication mechanism in an affected system is not working properly, so crafted requests let an unauthenticated remote attacker log in as an internal, high-privileged, non-root user account, access NETCONF from it, and manipulate network configuration for the SD-WAN fabric. Bound to these two products the control means the peering interface takes its own authorization decision on every request before a session exists — a peer's asserted identity is verified rather than accepted — and that no Controller or Manager instance is left with its peering and NETCONF interfaces reachable from a segment holding no fabric role. This is also why the cited least-privilege and identity-and-access gaps cannot close the path: the account the attacker lands in is internal to the product rather than one the operator provisioned, so per-account privilege scoping is never consulted and an attestation covering administrator accounts passes cleanly while an unauthenticated caller holds administrative privileges on the system. Distinguishing test: from a segment carrying no SD-WAN fabric role, send unauthenticated peering requests to a staging Controller and Manager and confirm each is refused before any session is issued, then attempt a NETCONF session from that same origin and confirm it is refused too — an estate that audits vManage operator roles and passes remains fully exposed to the path the packet describes, because the path never touches those roles. Precondition: repairing the peering authentication mechanism is what the vendor update does; this control states the property to verify and does not implement it. Until that update and the restart the packet's live-patch note requires have landed, restricting which segments can present requests bounds who can attempt the bypass but leaves it fully available to anything inside the permitted segment — and because a fabric's peers are distributed by design, the peering interface must stay reachable to those peers for the overlay to work, so the restriction is partial by construction rather than a closure.

This vulnerability exists because the peering authentication mechanism in an affected system is not working properly... A successful exploit could allow the attacker to log in to an affected Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Controller as an internal, high-privileged, non-root user account. Using this account, the attacker could access NETCONF, which would then allow the attacker to manipulate network configuration for the SD-WAN fabric." CWE-287. CISA KEV-listed 2026-02-25, active_exploitation confirmed, poc_available true, CVSS 9.1, RWEP 77. patch_available true; live_patch_available false with the note that no live-patch tool is registered and the vendor patch typically requires a service restart or system reboot per the KEV requiredAction.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: The clock this control sets opens on this entry at the 2026-02-25 KEV listing, and what counts as verified mitigation has to be stated in these products' own terms. There is a vendor fix with no live-patch path, and the patch typically requires a service restart or system reboot, so completion is measured by each Catalyst SD-WAN Controller and Manager having taken the fixed image and come back from that restart — an instance carrying the image but not yet restarted still runs the vulnerable peering authentication code and counts as exposed, and on a fabric controller the restart is the step most likely to be deferred because taking it disturbs the overlay it serves. Where the restart cannot be scheduled inside the window, the documented-compensating-control branch is the only one this SLA leaves, and it has to be written down as a compensating control with its residual stated rather than recorded as compliant: restricting which segments can present requests to the peering and NETCONF interfaces bounds who can attempt the bypass, but it does not repair the mechanism, and every legitimate fabric peer's network remains a permitted origin. Priority follows the packet rather than the CVSS band — confirmed in-the-wild exploitation and a public PoC against a system whose compromise yields NETCONF-level authority over the fabric's configuration makes this a control-plane containment item, not a scheduled network-device update. Precondition: because exploitation is confirmed, the update does not close an instance that was reachable during the window. The packet's end state is an attacker manipulating SD-WAN fabric configuration, so a Controller or Manager exposed before the fix landed needs its fabric configuration and the accounts defined on it compared against a known-good copy; an update applied to a system that already issued an administrative session removes the entry path and nothing the attacker did through it.

new_control_requirements.description: FileZen's KEV listing opened 2026-02-24 and a public PoC already exists alongside confirmed in-the-wild exploitation, so an appliance-patch cadence measured in weeks is the wrong instrument for this entry: the CWE-78 command sink is reached through an ordinary HTTP request to the product's own web surface, so exposure is continuous for as long as a unit runs pre-fix code. On a file-transfer appliance that restart is exactly the step operators defer, because taking it interrupts in-flight transfers, and a deferral recorded as 'patched' is the specific way this goes wrong. Where the restart genuinely cannot be taken inside the window, the only remaining lever is restricting which networks can reach the FileZen web surface; that bounds who can send the crafted request and leaves the command sink fully reachable from anything inside the permitted segment, so it is a holding measure with a dated end, not a closure. new_control_requirements.name: PERIMETER-COMPROMISE-REBUILD-NOT-PATCH
new_control_requirements.description: FileZen is not placed at a network perimeter on this entry, so what triggers this control here is not topology but the exploitation facts that are recorded: the defect executes operating-system commands on the appliance itself (CWE-78), exploitation is confirmed in the wild, and a PoC is public. For any unit that untrusted callers could reach before its fix and restart landed — and the KEV listing dates confirmed exploitation to at least 2026-02-24 — the vendor update restores the code and nothing else: an added account, a scheduled job, an altered configuration, or any file written through the command sink survives the upgrade untouched, because the fix closes the path and does not undo what already traversed it. The default disposition for such a unit is therefore configuration capture, rebuild, and credential rotation rather than patch-in-place. Two preconditions are load-bearing. The rebuild only yields a clean appliance if it is built at or above the vendor's fixed level — rebuilding to the pre-fix level puts the identical vulnerable HTTP path straight back on the network — and the credentials the appliance held (its administrative accounts, any directory-integration or service accounts, any keys shared with transfer partners) must be rotated after the rebuild completes rather than before, or the clean unit is handed the same secrets. This control also does not establish what left the appliance: files that transited FileZen during the exposure window need their own disclosure assessment, which no amount of rebuilding performs. Distinguishing test: for each unit, ask what evidence excludes exploitation during the window rather than what evidence proves it — a flaw-remediation record showing the fixed version installed reads clean on an appliance that was executing attacker-supplied commands the week before.

NIST-800-53-SI-2 (Flaw Remediation) is recorded as insufficient for this entry.

new_control_requirements.name: CONTROL-PANEL-PLUGIN-USER-SURFACE-MUST-NOT-REACH-ROOT-OPERATIONS
new_control_requirements.description: The packet's vector conditions this exploit on a product login: FileZen 'contains an OS command injection vulnerability when an user logs-in to the affected product and sends a specially crafted HTTP request'. That is the shape this control forbids — a constrained user surface, here the web interface of a file-transfer product, wired through to an operating-system command interpreter on the appliance host, so that holding a FileZen account amounts to holding command execution on the box. Bound to this product, the requirement is that no FileZen request handler composes an OS command from request-supplied content, and that the transfer functions reach the operating system only through a constrained, validated interface. This is why the least-privilege gap cited on this entry stays open however carefully FileZen accounts are scoped: the request crosses out of the application into the OS regardless of which directories or transfer rights the account carries, so an access-control attestation passes cleanly while the path is fully reachable. Preconditions: handler-side neutralization is a property the vendor update establishes — this control names what to verify, it does not implement it. Until the update and its restart land, the operator's levers are reducing which accounts can log in to the appliance and restricting which networks can reach its web surface; each bounds the population that can send the request and neither closes the sink. And the packet's own attack-vector summary describes the attacker as unauthenticated, contradicting the login precondition in its vector text — under that reading the account-side lever gives nothing at all and reachability restriction is the only interim measure, so reducing accounts must not be recorded as the mitigation without first settling which reading holds. Distinguishing test: on a staging FileZen, authenticate as an ordinary transfer user and send shell metacharacters through each web handler's parameters, confirming none reach a command interpreter — an attestation that every FileZen account is confined to its own transfer directories passes while this path stays open.

Off-host is the load-bearing part: the flaw yields code execution on the mail server itself, so any log the attacker's own process can reach is not evidence.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: The number that gets this entry mishandled is CVSS 6.1. A severity-driven queue reads "Medium XSS" and buckets a webmail flaw at 30 or 90 days, while it is KEV-listed with confirmed in-the-wild exploitation and a public PoC — the conditions under which the real requirement is hours. Keying the clock to KEV status rather than to base score is the whole point here: 4 hours from listing or fix availability to a verified mitigation on every Roundcube instance. Two facts shape what that window has to contain. There is no live-patch path registered for this entry, and the vendor patch typically requires a service restart or system reboot per the KEV requiredAction — so the SLA must be planned as an upgrade plus a scheduled webmail service restart, not as a hot fix that can be slipped in without an outage. An operator whose change process cannot restart the mail front end inside the window needs the alternative recorded as a documented compensating control with a conversion deadline, not as an accepted 90-day queue position.

Vendor patch typically requires service restart or system reboot per the KEV requiredAction." new_control_requirements.name: INCOMPLETE-PATCH-SEQUENCE-SEVERITY-MULTIPLIER
new_control_requirements.description: This flaw is a later variant of the Roundcube XSS class, and that word is the finding. The sink is an animate tag inside an SVG document — markup the message renderer's sanitizer was already supposed to be filtering — so what the CVE demonstrates is not one missed tag but that the allowlist governing SVG and animation markup in the mail body renderer keeps admitting script, one element at a time. Per-CVE severity scoring cannot express that: each instance lands as another 6.1 reflected-script issue, the structural defect never surfaces, and the operator has no basis for predicting the next one. A vulnerability-management program covering webmail must therefore carry a multiplier for the Nth flaw on the same sanitizer primitive — escalating handling above what the base score alone would trigger, and treating the renderer's markup filter as a standing area of exposure that warrants defence at the rendering layer rather than a series of unrelated Medium tickets closed on the routine queue.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet attack vector as recorded: "a cross-site scripting flaw (CWE-79) in Roundcube Webmail (a later variant), letting an attacker run script in a victim's authenticated session via a crafted email" — the entry is explicitly recorded as a later variant, not a first instance. The vector field names the sink: "a cross-site scripting vulnerability via the animate tag in an SVG document." cvss 6.1 against rwep_score 77 is the scoring divergence itself. The NIS2-Art21-vulnerability-management gap recorded against this entry states that on-prem mailflow XSS is not enumerated as a distinct vulnerability class deserving accelerated handling.

new_control_requirements.name: OWA-PER-REQUEST-SIEM-INGESTION
new_control_requirements.description: The script executes inside a session the victim opened legitimately, so the authentication record for a successful exploitation of this CVE is one ordinary login by the right user from the right place. Everything the attacker then does — reading and searching the mailbox, adding a forwarding or filter rule, pulling the address book, calling the webmail API with the victim's own session — arrives as authenticated application traffic that an auth-event-only log pipeline never records. For a Roundcube deployment this means per-request access logs from the webmail front end, not just the login events, must be shipped off the mail host to a SIEM with retention long enough to cover the window between the KEV listing and the day the upgrade and its service restart actually land. That window is the operative one here: there is no vendor workaround short of the fix, so during it the only available posture is detection — a monitored interim state with a documented deadline for conversion to the vendor patch, rather than an unobserved wait.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: This is a 2021 identifier that CISA listed on 2026-02-18 — years after the vendor fix shipped and long after any normal patch window closed. That inversion is precisely why the control's 'KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later' wording matters here: the clock starts at the listing date, not at disclosure. Vulnerability programmes age findings out by disclosure year and de-prioritise anything that has been open long enough to look inert, so an instance still exposed to this flaw is by definition one that survived every prior scan-and-triage cycle — the age of the identifier is the reason it is still there, not a reason to relax. Inside that window the work is inventory-led rather than patch-led: enumerate every self-managed GitLab instance including team-run and forgotten ones (the same lack of ownership that let a years-old flaw persist is what will hide instances from the sweep), confirm each running version against the fixed release, and apply the vendor update with the service restart it requires. Confirmed in-the-wild exploitation with a public PoC on an unauthenticated flaw means the interval between listing and remediation is contested time, not a grace period.

new_control_requirements.name: MITIGATION-ACTIVE-PATCH-PENDING-VERDICT-CLASS
new_control_requirements.description: Exposure is scoped by a configuration condition rather than a version alone: the SSRF is present when requests to the internal network for webhooks are enabled. This matters more than usual on an entry whose fix predates its KEV listing by years: over that span the workaround is exactly the kind of setting that gets quietly reverted somewhere in an estate, and a version-only verdict will never surface it.

new_control_requirements.name: PERIMETER-COMPROMISE-REBUILD-NOT-PATCH
new_control_requirements.description: The packet's stated impact is not just unauthorized access but root-level persistence on the appliance's underlying operating system, with exploitation confirmed in the wild — so patching in place on an instance that was reachable while unpatched removes the credential and leaves anything installed through it running. new_control_requirements.name: BACKUP-TIER-NETWORK-ISOLATION
new_control_requirements.description: Identity controls on this appliance are inert by construction: the credential ships inside the product, so no password policy, account review, privilege assignment or authentication-strength requirement the operator configures can revoke it, and the account it hands out is root on the appliance operating system. new_control_requirements.name: SECURITY-TOOL-INTEGRITY-VERIFICATION
new_control_requirements.description: ThreatSonar is the anti-ransomware product itself, and the defect is that it does not validate the content of files uploaded to it — meaning the crafted-input path runs through the server's normal, expected input path, since ingesting attacker-adjacent artifacts is what the product is for. Bring the security-product estate under the same vulnerability-management SLA as the systems it defends: inventory the ThreatSonar server as patch-managed privileged software, run the KEV clock from the 2026-02-17 listing, and schedule the service restart or reboot the fix requires, since no live patch is registered for this entry. The trust-anchor-inversion test the control names lands directly here — upload a file whose content does not match its declared type to a staging ThreatSonar instance and confirm it is rejected rather than stored and executed. An 'endpoint protection deployed' attestation says nothing about whether the protection server is patched.
new_control_requirements.evidence: The packet's KEV description states that ThreatSonar Anti-Ransomware does not properly validate the content of uploaded files, and that remote attackers with administrator privileges on the product platform can upload malicious files which can be used to execute arbitrary system commands on the server (CWE-434). CISA KEV-listed 2026-02-17 with active_exploitation confirmed; RWEP 77, CVSS 8.8, PoC available. patch_available is true and live_patch_available is false, with the packet recording that the vendor patch typically requires service restart or system reboot per the KEV requiredAction.

new_control_requirements.name: FLEET-CONTROL-PLANE-ADMIN-PRIVILEGE-TIER
new_control_requirements.description: The packet's KEV description puts administrator privileges on the ThreatSonar platform in the exploitation precondition, which makes every path that issues, stores or reuses a console admin credential part of this vulnerability's attack surface. Classify ThreatSonar operators above application admins: a separate identity from any other admin role, FIDO2 step-up per session, just-in-time elevation with an approval workflow, and console access only from a PAM jumphost or privileged access workstation. The effect specific to this flaw is that a credential harvested elsewhere in the estate — the usual route to a console account — cannot be walked straight into the unvalidated upload handler and turned into arbitrary system commands on the anti-ransomware server, and every upload is attributable to an approved elevation rather than to a shared standing login.
new_control_requirements.evidence: The packet's KEV description states that remote attackers with administrator privileges on the product platform can upload malicious files, which can be used to execute arbitrary system commands on the server (CWE-434); CVSS 8.8, RWEP 77, PoC available, active_exploitation confirmed as of the 2026-02-17 KEV listing. NIST SP 800-53 AC-6 (Least Privilege) is among the framework controls recorded as insufficient for this CVE.

new_control_requirements.name: PEN-TEST-SCOPE-INCLUDES-SECURITY-PRODUCTS
new_control_requirements.description: Nothing about this flaw is exotic — an upload handler that does not check file content — yet it persisted in a shipping anti-ransomware product, because assessment scopes treat that product as a defense to be validated rather than a target to be attacked. Write the ThreatSonar server into the scope language by name: its administrative console, its file-upload and artifact-ingest endpoints, and its agent/update channels, with explicit authorization to attempt upload-to-arbitrary-command execution against a staging instance. The distinguishing observation for this entry is the route it took to operators — it surfaced through the KEV feed after in-the-wild use, not through any assessment of the security stack itself, which is what a scope that excludes defensive products guarantees.
new_control_requirements.evidence: This is a CWE-434 unrestricted upload of a file with a dangerous type in TeamT5 ThreatSonar Anti-Ransomware, where uploaded file content is not properly validated and uploaded files can be used to execute arbitrary system commands on the server. It carries CISA KEV listing 2026-02-17 with active_exploitation confirmed and a PoC available — i.e. it reached the catalog after exploitation, not before. UK CAF B4 (System security) is among the framework controls recorded as insufficient here.

CVE-2008-0015.name: Microsoft Windows Video ActiveX Control Remote Code Execution Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: a memory-corruption code-execution flaw (CWE-94) in the Microsoft Video ActiveX control (msvidctl), exploitable by an attacker-controlled web page in Internet Explorer for drive-by remote code execution. CISA KEV-listed 2026-02-17 with confirmed in-the-wild exploitation.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none (the victim opens or processes the attacker's file/content/repository)
attack_vector.complexity: low — KEV-listed, actively exploited; treat as weaponized
attack_vector.ai_factor: No AI involvement documented in discovery or weaponization.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Apply the Microsoft update and retire end-of-life Internet Explorer / disable the vulnerable ActiveX control via kill-bit; enforce browser hardening and web-content filtering.
prevention.adequacy: Patch is definitive on a managed estate; the lasting controls are file-provenance enforcement, application hardening, and retiring end-of-life software, since these flaws are reached through everyday file/content handling.

detection.what_would_have_worked: EDR signatures for child-process execution from the browser after web-content render.
detection.adequacy: Backstops endpoints not yet patched and catches the post-exploitation drop/execution stage.

response.what_would_have_worked: Force the patch (or retire the end-of-life component), isolate exploited endpoints, remove dropped autostart/hook payloads, hunt for follow-on loaders, and review for credential theft.
response.adequacy: Mandatory; client-side execution typically establishes persistence (autorun/hooks) and leads to credential harvest, which a bare patch does not remediate.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: The 30-day flaw-remediation SLA is far longer than the observed exploitation window for a KEV-listed, actively-exploited client-side file/content-handling flaw; weaponized archives, web content, and repositories are delivered by email, web, and supply chain and exploited within days. Long-tail unpatched and end-of-life software (Internet Explorer / ActiveX) remains exposed for years.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: 'Appropriate timescales' is undefined; the standard reading is unsafe for an actively-exploited client flaw, and the legacy re-listings exist because organizations still run vulnerable or end-of-life software.

AU-ISM-1546.gap: Essential 8 names application patching and hardening, but the load-bearing controls here are file-provenance enforcement (Mark-of-the-Web propagation to extracted files), ASR rules, disabling risky ActiveX, and hardened version-control settings (protectNTFS, disabling symlinks on clone) — none of which the framework names explicitly.

compliance_exposure_score.basis: Microsoft Video ActiveX control is ubiquitous on endpoints/developer machines; audited organizations that rely on patching alone — without file-provenance enforcement, ASR rules, ActiveX kill-bits, or hardened clone settings — remain exposed for this KEV-listed, actively-exploited flaw, and long-tail/EOL software widens the window.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For this entry the clock runs from the 2026-02-17 KEV listing, and completion has to be measured on the endpoint rather than in the management console: there is no live-patch path and the vendor patch typically requires a service restart or system reboot per the KEV requiredAction, so a workstation that has taken the update but not restarted still hosts the vulnerable Microsoft Video ActiveX control (msvidctl) and remains exposed to a crafted web page rendered in Internet Explorer. Two things this SLA must not be allowed to substitute for on this path, and both are why the corresponding gaps are recorded against the entry: the flaw yields the same rights as the logged-on user, so running users as non-administrators narrows the blast radius but does not stop the drive-by execution; and a user-application-hardening attestation covering macro, plugin and advertisement settings does not enumerate the browser-invocable ActiveX control the bug lives in. Until the restart completes on a given host, the only remaining levers are keeping that host away from untrusted web content and recording it as exposed — neither privilege posture nor the hardening baseline closes the path, so an SLA measured on 'update approved' or 'update downloaded' records the exposure instead of removing it.

new_control_requirements.name: BROWSER-MANAGED-UPDATE-NO-DEFERRAL
new_control_requirements.description: Exploitation is a crafted HTML page reaching a use-after-free in Chromium's CSS handling, so exposure is continuous for every user who browses and the browser's own update channel is the only control between the estate and an exploit already confirmed in the wild. Second, the policy cannot be Chrome-only: the packet names Microsoft Edge and Opera among the Chromium-based browsers affected, each shipping the fix on its own channel, so an estate that pins its no-deferral rule to a single browser leaves the same use-after-free reachable through the others it has installed.
