new_control_requirements.name: PERIMETER-DEVICE-ZERODAY-SLA-TIER
new_control_requirements.description: The packet's path into BeyondTrust Remote Support and Privileged Remote Access needs no credential and no user interaction — an unauthenticated remote attacker reaches the product and executes operating system commands in the context of the site user — so these systems are not servers sitting behind an access boundary, they are the boundary the exploit crosses, which is what puts them in this control's distinct SLA tier rather than in the general server population. For these two products the control means the remediation clock runs from the 2026-02-13 KEV listing rather than from the next scheduled maintenance window, and that completion is measured per system by the version actually running against the vendor's fixed version, not by 'update approved', 'update downloaded' or a closed change ticket. The packet registers no live-patch path and records that the vendor patch typically requires a service restart or system reboot per the KEV requiredAction, so a system that has taken the update but not restarted still runs the vulnerable code and has to be counted as exposed for the whole interval until it restarts. The control's alternative branch — isolating the vulnerable interface instead of meeting the clock — carries a precondition that frequently does not hold for this product: Remote Support and Privileged Remote Access exist in order to be reachable, so isolation is only available where the operator can name a user and technician population whose access can be suspended for the duration, and where it cannot, the update plus its restart is the only lever and there is no compensating control to record in its place. Priority follows the packet rather than the CVSS band alone: confirmed in-the-wild exploitation plus a public PoC against a no-authentication path means the window is being actively worked. Distinguishing test: produce, per affected system, the running version and the timestamp of the restart that activated it, set against the vendor's fixed version — a patch-management attestation that reports an SLA-compliance percentage over a 14- or 30-day window passes cleanly while a system sits updated-but-unrestarted on a KEV-listed no-authentication remote command-execution flaw.

Successful exploitation requires no authentication or user interaction.' cisa_kev true, kev_date 2026-02-13, active_exploitation confirmed, poc_available true, CVSS 9.8, RWEP 83. patch_available true; live_patch_available false; live_patch_notes: 'No live-patch tool registered for this entry at bulk-import time. Vendor patch typically requires service restart or system reboot per the KEV requiredAction.' Citing gaps closed here: AU-Essential-8-Patch (Patch operating systems), ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8 (Management of technical vulnerabilities), NIST-800-53-SI-2 (Flaw Remediation), NIS2-Art21-vulnerability-handling.

new_control_requirements.name: PERIMETER-COMPROMISE-REBUILD-NOT-PATCH
new_control_requirements.description: In-the-wild exploitation is confirmed and a public PoC exists against a path that requires no authentication and no user interaction, which changes what the response has to cover: any Remote Support or Privileged Remote Access system that was reachable before it was updated is possibly already executed against, not merely possibly vulnerable. Bound to this product, the control means the answer to the 2026-02-13 KEV listing is not the vendor update alone — for each system reachable during the exposure window, export the configuration off the box, rebuild from vendor media rather than patching in place, and rotate the credentials and key material the system held. The packet's own outcome statement is the reason: command execution in the context of the site user, with the vendor stating exploitation may lead to system compromise including unauthorized access, data exfiltration and service disruption. An attacker who reached that before the update keeps everything they wrote after it. This is also precisely why the anti-malware control cited against this entry does not close the path: an anti-malware attestation covers the hosts the agent is installed on and the content it has signatures for, whereas an operating-system command-execution foothold on this product typically leaves an added account, an altered configuration entry, or a script the platform itself executes on schedule — content with nothing to match. Distinguishing test: take a system that was reachable before remediation and diff its accounts, automated tasks and on-disk content against a freshly built system at the same fixed version; a clean anti-malware scan and a version number at or above the fixed release are both fully consistent with a system that is still implanted. Preconditions: the vendor update is what closes the injection path and this control does not substitute for it; the control applies only to systems that were actually reachable during the window, not to every unit in the inventory; and where a rebuild genuinely cannot be scheduled, the honest record is an accepted exposure with a dated review, because the system continues to be trusted with no evidence it is clean — not a remediation entry.

Vendor patch typically requires service restart or system reboot per the KEV requiredAction.' Citing gaps closed here: CIS-Controls-v8-10.1 (Deploy and Maintain Anti-Malware Software), NIST-800-53-SI-2 (Flaw Remediation).

new_control_requirements.name: FLEET-COMPROMISE-IR-PLAYBOOK
new_control_requirements.description: Remote Support and Privileged Remote Access are, by what the packet names them, the products through which support sessions into other systems are established, so command execution on them is not bounded by the systems themselves. Applied to this CVE, the control means the response includes an accounting of what passed through each affected system during the exposure window — the accounts that authenticated to or through it, the credential and session material it held for the systems it serves, and the trust those serviced systems extend to it — with each of those rotated or re-established rather than left standing because the system now reports a fixed version. Two preconditions must be stated rather than assumed. First, the scope list cannot be drawn solely from the affected system's own records: the attacker executes operating system commands in the context of the site user, and records written on a system in that state are attacker-influenceable, so an off-system record of sessions is the authoritative source where one exists, and where it does not, the defensible scope is every account that used the service during the window. Second, this control assumes the deployment actually brokers access to other systems — the packet establishes the products and the exploitation outcome, not any particular site's session inventory, so the rotation list is a deployment fact the operator has to produce and it may be narrower or wider than the product name suggests. Rotation is also not containment on its own: it invalidates what the attacker took, it does not remove what the attacker left, which is the rebuild half of the response, and it gives nothing back to a system that was never reachable during the window. Distinguishing test: name the accounts whose sessions traversed each affected system between the earliest plausible compromise and completion of its rebuild, and show a rotation timestamp after that completion for each — an identity-and-access attestation showing that every technician holds a unique account with MFA passes cleanly here, because the packet's path never authenticates as any of them and no per-account privilege decision is ever consulted.

This is the control that covers the next member of the class before its patch exists, which is the same position operators were in when this one was listed.

CISA KEV-listed 2026-02-12 with confirmed in-the-wild exploitation (Apple zero-days of this class are typically used in targeted-spyware chains).' The vector adds that an attacker with memory-write capability can execute arbitrary code. poc_available true, CVSS 8.8, RWEP 77; live_patch_available false, so there is no mid-window fix that avoids the update-and-restart cycle.

CVE-2024-43468.name: Microsoft Configuration Manager SQL Injection Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: SQL injection (CWE-89) on Microsoft Configuration Manager escalating to unauthenticated remote code execution. CISA KEV-listed 2026-02-12 with confirmed in-the-wild exploitation.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none (unauthenticated network reach to the server)
attack_vector.complexity: low — KEV-listed, actively exploited; treat as weaponized
attack_vector.ai_factor: No AI involvement documented in discovery or weaponization.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Apply the Microsoft Configuration Manager security update; ConfigMgr governs endpoint management, so treat compromise as fleet-level and review managed-client integrity.
prevention.adequacy: Patch is necessary but, for these deserialization RCEs, insufficient alone — stolen machine keys and dropped web shells survive the patch and require explicit cleanup.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Monitoring on the Configuration Manager: exploit-shaped requests, new .aspx/web-shell files under the server's web root, unexpected process execution, and anomalous use of stolen cryptographic keys.
detection.adequacy: Necessary to catch resident persistence after patching; the ToolShell-class chains specifically steal keys for durable access.

response.what_would_have_worked: Patch immediately, rotate machine keys, hunt and remove web shells, and review for lateral movement; assume credential compromise for any account reachable from the Configuration Manager.
response.adequacy: Mandatory; patch-in-place without key rotation and web-shell hunting leaves the attacker resident.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: The 30-day flaw-remediation SLA is far longer than the observed exploitation window for a KEV-listed unauthenticated server flaw; CISA KEV due dates are days. The ToolShell SharePoint chain was mass-exploited within days of disclosure.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: 'Appropriate timescales' is undefined; the standard 30-day reading is unsafe for an unauthenticated, actively-exploited flaw on an internet-facing enterprise server.

NIS2-Art21-network-security.gap: Treats the server class as essential-function infrastructure but lacks a CISA-KEV-style compressed remediation SLA, and does not require the key-rotation/web-shell-hunt cleanup these deserialization RCEs need.

PCI-DSS-4.0-6.3.3.gap: The 30-day critical-patch window is exploitation acceptance for an unauthenticated RCE on an internet-facing server in or adjacent to the CDE.

compliance_exposure_score.basis: Internet-facing Microsoft Configuration Manager is business-critical and change-controlled, so emergency patching loses to change windows; the required key-rotation and web-shell hunt is rarely part of the documented patch procedure.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: Configuration Manager is the system operators patch everything else with, which is exactly why it tends to sit outside its own SLA — the site server is treated as remediation infrastructure rather than as a remediation target. This CVE is KEV-listed 2026-02-12 with confirmed exploitation and a public PoC, and the packet describes an unauthenticated caller sending crafted requests that end in command execution on the server or its database, so the site server has to be enrolled in the same KEV clock it enforces on managed endpoints. A vendor fix exists; there is no live-patch path and the vendor patch typically requires a service restart or system reboot, so a maintenance window for the site server itself — not just for the fleet it patches — must be pre-authorised inside the SLA.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet fields for CVE-2024-43468 (Microsoft Configuration Manager SQL Injection Vulnerability): cwe_refs CWE-89; cisa_kev=true with kev_date 2026-02-12; active_exploitation=confirmed; poc_available=true; cvss 9.8; rwep_score 77; vector text states an unauthenticated attacker could exploit it by sending specially crafted requests to the target environment which are processed in an unsafe manner, enabling the attacker to execute commands on the server and/or underlying database; patch_available=true; live_patch_available=false with live_patch_notes stating no live-patch tool is registered and that the vendor patch typically requires service restart or system reboot per the KEV requiredAction.

new_control_requirements.name: DB-ABSTRACTION-LAYER-PARAMETERIZATION-VERIFICATION
new_control_requirements.description: The injectable path on Configuration Manager is reached without credentials — the packet describes crafted requests processed in an unsafe manner by the server — so the two assumptions operators normally lean on for this product ('the site server is on the internal network' and 'a WAF fronts the client-facing endpoints') are both untested inferences, and neither is evidence that a query is bound rather than concatenated. The control requires parameterization to be proven at the query layer for every request handler that accepts client-originated content, and re-proven after each site-server update, rather than inferred from upstream input validation. The distinguishing test: from an unauthenticated host that can reach the site server's request-handling endpoints on a staging hierarchy, submit request fields carrying SQL metacharacters and confirm the value is passed as a bound parameter rather than becoming part of the statement — a hierarchy that passes an application-firewall audit while a handler concatenates client-supplied content still yields command execution on the server and the database behind it.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet fields for CVE-2024-43468: cwe_refs CWE-89; attack_vector states SQL injection on Microsoft Configuration Manager escalating to unauthenticated remote code execution; vector text states an unauthenticated attacker sends specially crafted requests processed in an unsafe manner, enabling execution of commands on the server and/or underlying database; cvss 9.8; active_exploitation=confirmed; poc_available=true.

new_control_requirements.name: ENDPOINT-MGMT-DEPLOYMENT-CHANNEL-INTEGRITY
new_control_requirements.description: Configuration Manager is the fleet's software-deployment control plane, and this CVE hands an unauthenticated attacker command execution on that server and its database — the same authority the product legitimately uses to push packages, scripts and updates to every managed endpoint, which is why a single unauthenticated request here is a fleet-wide code-execution primitive rather than one compromised host. The control requires the deployment channel to be integrity-monitored independently of the site server itself: alert on deployment objects, scripts and task sequences that appear without a matching sanctioned admin action, and land that audit trail on a collector the site server cannot rewrite, so a foothold on the server cannot quietly launder itself into signed-looking fleet distribution. It also sets the post-remediation obligation the patch does not: any window in which a site server ran the vulnerable build while exposed must be treated as fleet-wide code-execution exposure and everything deployed during it reviewed — patching closes the entry point but says nothing about what the deployment channel did while it was open.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet fields for CVE-2024-43468: vector text states the unauthenticated attacker can execute commands on the server and/or underlying database of Microsoft Configuration Manager; active_exploitation=confirmed; cisa_kev=true with kev_date 2026-02-12; poc_available=true; rwep_score 77; cvss 9.8; patch_available=true with live_patch_available=false.

CVE-2025-15556.name: Notepad++ Download of Code Without Integrity Check Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: Notepad++ downloads code/components without an integrity check (CWE-494), enabling malicious-code substitution via a tampered download or planted binary for execution on the host. CISA KEV-listed 2026-02-12 with confirmed in-the-wild exploitation.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none (the attacker influences the download/update channel or the shipped artifact; no authentication to the victim is required)
attack_vector.complexity: low — KEV-listed, actively exploited; treat as weaponized
attack_vector.ai_factor: No AI involvement documented in discovery or weaponization.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Enforce cryptographic integrity verification on all downloaded code and updates (code signing with signature verification, Sigstore/in-toto, TLS-pinned update channels); for the embedded-malicious-code case, verify build provenance (SLSA) and pin/verify the tool's release artifacts before use.
prevention.adequacy: Signature and provenance verification is the definitive control; the flaw exists precisely because it was absent or unenforced — patching the version does not retroactively restore trust in artifacts already installed.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Monitoring for unexpected code/DLLs loaded by the Notepad++, updates fetched over unauthenticated channels, and anomalous outbound connections or process execution from the tool.
detection.adequacy: Necessary because supply-chain substitution is silent — the tool runs as expected while the embedded/substituted code executes alongside it.

response.what_would_have_worked: Pull the affected version, reinstall from a verified-signed release, rotate any credentials the compromised process could reach, and audit every host where the tool ran — a compromised updater or scanner has broad reach.
response.adequacy: Mandatory; supply-chain compromise propagates through every host that ran the tainted code, so response is environment-wide, not host-local.

NIST-800-53-SR-11.gap: Component authenticity / anti-counterfeit is named, but verification is not enforced at install/update time — these products fetched or shipped code without a verified signature, so the control is paper unless signed-artifact verification (Sigstore/in-toto) is mandated at the download step.

NIST-SSDF-800-218-PS.2.gap: The SSDF calls for protecting release integrity and providing provenance, but downstream consumers had no enforced way to verify it; without signed releases plus provenance a consumer cannot detect substitution or embedded malicious code.

SLSA-build-provenance.gap: SLSA build provenance and signed releases would let a consumer detect tampering or substitution; absent enforced verification at the download/update step the trust gap remains open.

EU-CRA-secure-update.gap: The EU Cyber Resilience Act requires secure update mechanisms and shipping without known exploitable defects; an unauthenticated download path or embedded malicious code violates the secure-update and integrity expectations.

compliance_exposure_score.basis: Software-distribution and update integrity is widely assumed rather than verified; audited organizations that install vendor updates or run security tooling without enforcing signature/provenance verification are exposed to substitution and embedded-malicious-code attacks — and a compromised updater or scanner reaches every host it touches.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: Notepad++ is fleet-wide desktop software that updates itself through WinGUp, so the KEV clock lands on every workstation carrying the vulnerable build rather than on a small set of managed servers. The mitigation that satisfies the SLA must be a managed software-deployment push of the fixed build, not a prompt to run the in-application update check — that check is the exact channel the flaw lets an attacker redirect, so using it as the remediation mechanism runs the attack. No live-patch path is registered for this entry and a patch of this class typically requires a restart, so the SLA has to be met with the vendor update plus that restart, or with a documented compensating control (blocking or disabling the in-app update check) until the fleet is on the fixed build.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CISA KEV-listed 2026-02-12 with active_exploitation 'confirmed', RWEP 77, CVSS 9.8, and poc_available true. patch_available is true; live_patch_available is false, and live_patch_notes states no live-patch tool is registered and that the vendor patch typically requires service restart or system reboot per the KEV requiredAction. The packet's vector states that Notepad++, when using the WinGUp updater, downloads code without an integrity check, allowing an attacker to intercept or redirect update traffic to download and execute an attacker-controlled installer with the privileges of the user.

new_control_requirements.name: INDEPENDENT-INTEGRITY-VERIFICATION-OF-SIGNED-VENDOR-INSTALLERS
new_control_requirements.description: The Notepad++ update path makes the delivery channel the trust anchor: whatever WinGUp retrieves is executed. The organization must therefore verify the Notepad++ installer against an integrity source independent of the channel that delivered it — a published per-release hash fetched over a separate path — and deploy only the verified artifact, instead of allowing endpoints to accept whatever the updater fetches. The distinguishing test for this CVE: on a staging workstation, serve a substituted installer from an operator-controlled endpoint in place of the real update host and confirm the deployment tooling refuses the artifact on hash mismatch before it runs. A software-supply-chain policy that only asserts 'we install vendor software from the vendor' passes while this exact substitution succeeds.
new_control_requirements.evidence: The packet's CWE is CWE-494 (download of code without integrity check), and the vector states the WinGUp updater downloads code without an integrity check so that intercepted or redirected update traffic results in an attacker-controlled installer being downloaded and executed. KEV-listed 2026-02-12 with confirmed active exploitation and poc_available true.

new_control_requirements.name: DOWNLOAD-PROVENANCE-ENFORCEMENT
new_control_requirements.description: Application-control and provenance policy on the endpoint must refuse to execute an installer image that an application fetched from the network unless it carries verified publisher provenance, so that a redirected Notepad++ update cannot run on a host that has not yet reached the fixed build. Reputation-service verdicts are worthless against this specific path: the defect is the absence of any integrity check on the fetched payload, so the payload never has to defeat a reputation check to be executed by the updater. The distinguishing test: on a staging endpoint, have a non-vendor-signed installer be launched by the updater process and confirm execution is blocked by policy rather than allowed on the basis of the parent application's own trust.
new_control_requirements.evidence: The vector states the attacker-controlled installer is downloaded and executed, yielding arbitrary code execution with the privileges of the user. patch_available is true and live_patch_available is false, so the only in-window alternative to deploying the fixed build is blocking the execution step.

CVE-2025-40536.name: SolarWinds Web Help Desk Security Control Bypass Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: a security-control-bypass flaw (CWE-693) on SolarWinds Web Help Desk, letting an unauthenticated attacker bypass an intended security control to reach protected functionality. CISA KEV-listed 2026-02-12 with confirmed in-the-wild exploitation.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none (the flaw is reachable by an unauthenticated attacker and defeats the access-control mechanism)
attack_vector.complexity: low — KEV-listed, actively exploited; treat as weaponized
attack_vector.ai_factor: No AI involvement documented in discovery or weaponization.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Apply the SolarWinds Web Help Desk update; review privileged-function access during the exposure window and rotate service credentials — Web Help Desk has been a repeated exploitation target.
prevention.adequacy: Patch is necessary; restricting the management plane to a trusted network is the compensating control when the access-control enforcement is itself bypassed.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Monitoring on the Web Help Desk: requests exercising the bypass, administrative actions without a matching authentication event.
detection.adequacy: Necessary because a bypass produces access that looks authorized; the anomaly is the absence of a legitimate authentication event.

response.what_would_have_worked: Patch immediately, restrict the management plane, rotate credentials and keys, review configuration/account changes during the exposure window, and audit privileged actions and (for file-transfer/secure-access) data exposure.
response.adequacy: Mandatory; an access-control bypass typically leaves administrative persistence or a code-execution foothold that a patch alone does not remove.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: The 30-day flaw-remediation SLA is far longer than the observed exploitation window for a KEV-listed access-control/security-control bypass on an internet-facing system; these grant unauthorized access to protected functionality and are mass-exploited within days.

NIST-800-53-AC-3-enforcement.gap: Access-enforcement is required, but these flaws defeat the enforcement mechanism itself (alternate channel, missing authorization check, security-control bypass, assumed-immutable parameter); restricting the management plane to a trusted network is the load-bearing compensating control when enforcement fails.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: 'Appropriate timescales' is undefined; the standard 30-day reading is unsafe for an actively-exploited, internet-facing application or appliance whose access control is bypassed.

PCI-DSS-4.0-6.3.3.gap: The 30-day critical-patch window is exploitation acceptance for an internet-facing application or appliance (file-transfer / secure-access / help-desk) in or adjacent to the CDE.

compliance_exposure_score.basis: Internet-facing SolarWinds Web Help Desk is run by audited organizations whose access-control posture is irrelevant when the enforcement mechanism is bypassed; without management-plane restriction and prompt patching the system is exposed, and the required privileged-action review / web-shell hunt is rarely documented.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: A help-desk portal is normally reachable by the people it serves, including from outside the corporate network, so an unauthenticated bypass on Web Help Desk is exploitable from the same anonymous position the deployment is designed to accept — there is no 'internal only' fallback posture to hold while a routine change window is scheduled. Start the clock at the KEV listing rather than at the next patch cycle: inventory every Web Help Desk instance including staging, disaster-recovery and departmental copies that share the same exposure, apply the vendor update, and book the service restart the packet's requiredAction implies inside that same window. An instance that has the fix staged but has not been restarted must not be recorded as remediated.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet: CWE-693 security-control bypass on SolarWinds Web Help Desk that 'could allow an unauthenticated attacker to gain access to certain restricted functionality'; cisa_kev true, kev_date 2026-02-12, active_exploitation 'confirmed', poc_available true, cvss 8.8, rwep_score 77. patch_available true; live_patch_available false, with live_patch_notes 'No live-patch tool registered for this entry at bulk-import time. Vendor patch typically requires service restart or system reboot per the KEV requiredAction.'

new_control_requirements.name: SCANNER-PAPER-COMPLIANCE-TEST
new_control_requirements.description: A protection-mechanism failure means the product's security control was present and did answer — it simply did not stop the request — so an access-control attestation and a version-based scanner verdict can both be truthful while the restricted functionality is reachable by anyone. Verification has to be behavioural rather than declarative: from an unauthenticated client against a staging Web Help Desk instance, request each restricted function the bypass reached and confirm it is refused before the function executes, then re-run the same probe after the update instead of accepting the build number as proof. An audit that records 'Web Help Desk authenticates its users' or 'Web Help Desk is on the fixed build' without that probe cannot tell an enforced control from a bypassed one, which is the exact state this CVE describes.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet: CWE-693 protection-mechanism failure letting an unauthenticated attacker bypass an intended security control to reach protected functionality; active_exploitation 'confirmed' with CISA KEV listing 2026-02-12 and poc_available true. The framework gaps already citing this CVE include UK-CAF-B2 (identity and access control) and ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8 (management of technical vulnerabilities) — the two controls an operator can satisfy on paper while the bypass works.

CVE-2026-21513.name: Microsoft MSHTML Framework Protection Mechanism Failure Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: a protection-mechanism failure (CWE-693) in the MSHTML framework that bypasses the Mark-of-the-Web / trust protection, letting attacker-controlled content run without the expected security warning. CISA KEV-listed 2026-02-10 with confirmed in-the-wild exploitation.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none (the victim opens the attacker's document or visits the attacker's content)
attack_vector.complexity: low — KEV-listed, actively exploited; treat as weaponized
attack_vector.ai_factor: No AI involvement documented in discovery or weaponization.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Apply the Microsoft security update; because this flaw defeats a protection mechanism, do not rely on that single control — enforce defence-in-depth (ASR rules, application control, mail/web content filtering, and macro restrictions) so a bypass of SmartScreen / Mark-of-the-Web / Protected View is not a single point of failure.
prevention.adequacy: Patch is required; the lasting lesson is that a single protection mechanism (the one bypassed) cannot be the only barrier — layered controls are mandatory.

detection.what_would_have_worked: EDR / endpoint telemetry for execution of content lacking Mark-of-the-Web provenance and security-prompt bypass.
detection.adequacy: Backstops endpoints not yet patched and catches the post-bypass execution stage.

response.what_would_have_worked: Force the patch across the estate, isolate exploited endpoints, hunt for follow-on payloads, and review for credential theft.
response.adequacy: Mandatory; client-side exploitation typically leads to credential harvest and lateral movement that a bare patch does not remediate.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: The 30-day flaw-remediation SLA is far longer than the observed exploitation window for a KEV-listed, actively-exploited client-side flaw; the protection-bypass variants specifically defeat the warning that would otherwise slow the user, so the patch is the only barrier left.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: 'Appropriate timescales' is undefined; the standard reading is unsafe for an actively-exploited client flaw, and security-feature-bypass flaws mean a single layered control (Protected View, SmartScreen, Mark-of-the-Web) cannot be relied on alone.

AU-ISM-1546.gap: Essential 8 names application patching, application hardening, and macro/Office controls separately, but does not require defence-in-depth for the case where the protection mechanism itself is bypassed — ASR rules, application control, and mail/web content filtering are the load-bearing layers when SmartScreen/Protected View fail.

compliance_exposure_score.basis: Microsoft MSHTML is ubiquitous on endpoints; audited organizations that lean on a single protection (SmartScreen, Protected View, Mark-of-the-Web) without layered controls are exposed when that mechanism is bypassed, and long-tail patch hygiene leaves a window for the memory-corruption variants.

new_control_requirements.name: PROTECTION-MECHANISM-FAILURE-CLASS-REGRESSION
new_control_requirements.description: The flaw here is in the protection mechanism itself — MSHTML fails to apply the Mark-of-the-Web / trust check, so attacker-controlled content renders without the warning the rest of the endpoint hardening posture assumes is present. Verifying this fix therefore means re-running the whole MOTW/trust battery against MSHTML-rendered content after the update lands (mark propagation, zone-of-origin handling, prompt-on-execute for internet-sourced content), not confirming that the single reported bypass path is closed. An application-hardening attestation is only as strong as the last end-to-end test of the primitive it depends on, and this CVE is the demonstration that the primitive can silently stop working while every hardening setting still reads as enabled. Make the class battery a standing step of patch deployment on the affected estate.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet: protection-mechanism failure (CWE-693) in the Microsoft MSHTML framework that bypasses the Mark-of-the-Web / trust protection, letting attacker-controlled content run without the expected security warning; the KEV vector describes an unauthorized attacker bypassing a security feature over a network. cisa_kev true, kev_date 2026-02-10, active_exploitation confirmed, poc_available true, RWEP 77, CVSS 8.8.

new_control_requirements.name: DOWNLOAD-PROVENANCE-ENFORCEMENT
new_control_requirements.description: Because this bug suppresses the warning rather than corrupting memory, any posture that leans on the user seeing a prompt — or on a reputation verdict rendered at the same moment — is leaning on exactly what the flaw disables. Provenance has to be enforced by policy on the affected estate instead: block execution of internet-sourced shortcuts, installers and script hosts by rule, independent of whether the Mark-of-the-Web marking survived and independent of any reputation service outcome, so content delivered through the MSHTML path is refused even when it is never evaluated. This is also what closes the least-privilege gap for this CVE: the bypassed content runs in the user's own context, so removing administrative rights does not stop it — the enforcement point has to be what the user's own process is permitted to execute.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet: protection-mechanism failure (CWE-693) in Microsoft MSHTML bypassing Mark-of-the-Web / trust protection so attacker-controlled content runs without the expected security warning, reachable over a network by an unauthorized attacker. cisa_kev true, kev_date 2026-02-10, active_exploitation confirmed, poc_available true, RWEP 77.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For most endpoint CVEs the interval between disclosure and deployment is implicitly covered by the platform's trust prompts and user caution. This entry removes that cover — the entire defect is that the warning does not fire — so the unpatched window carries no residual endpoint-side compensating control, and the deployment clock has to run from the KEV listing rather than the next scheduled update ring. There is no live-patch path, so remediation is the vendor update plus the restart the KEV requiredAction implies; hosts that cannot take it inside the SLA need the provenance-enforcement block recorded as an explicit, time-bound compensating control, not counted as patched-per-policy.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet: cisa_kev true, kev_date 2026-02-10, active_exploitation confirmed, poc_available true; patch_available true with live_patch_available false, and live_patch_notes stating no live-patch tool is registered and that the vendor patch typically requires service restart or system reboot per the KEV requiredAction. RWEP 77, CVSS 8.8; protection-mechanism failure (CWE-693) bypassing Mark-of-the-Web / trust protection.

CVE-2026-21525.name: Microsoft Windows NULL Pointer Dereference Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: a NULL pointer dereference (CWE-476) in a network-reachable Windows component, exploitable by an unauthenticated attacker; described conservatively as a network-reachable memory-safety flaw pending Microsoft's component detail. CISA KEV-listed 2026-02-10 with confirmed in-the-wild exploitation.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none (the flaw is reachable by an unauthenticated attacker over the network)
attack_vector.complexity: low — KEV-listed, actively exploited; treat as weaponized
attack_vector.ai_factor: No AI involvement documented in discovery or weaponization.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Apply the Microsoft update; restrict and segment the affected network service from untrusted networks until patched.
prevention.adequacy: Patch is necessary but the named compensating controls are what hold when the patch lags or the trust mechanism itself is defeated.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Monitoring for crafted network input that crashes or restarts the affected Windows component, and for unauthenticated requests that trigger the fault.
detection.adequacy: Backstops the window before patching and catches the post-exploitation stage.

response.what_would_have_worked: Patch immediately, segment the service, and review the affected hosts for follow-on activity given confirmed in-the-wild exploitation.
response.adequacy: Mandatory; exploitation of this class leaves persistence or a foothold that a bare patch does not remediate.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: The 30-day flaw-remediation SLA is far longer than the observed exploitation window for a KEV-listed, unauthenticated network-reachable Windows flaw; these are mass-exploited within days.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: 'Appropriate timescales' is undefined; unsafe for an actively-exploited network-reachable Windows flaw.

NIS2-Art21-network-security.gap: Treats Windows infrastructure as essential-function but lacks a CISA-KEV-style compressed remediation SLA; network segmentation of the affected service is the compensating control pending patch.

compliance_exposure_score.basis: The affected Windows service is reachable on audited-organization networks; without prompt patching and segmentation the unauthenticated flaw remains exploitable past the KEV due date.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For this entry the KEV clock opens 2026-02-10 and the unit of completion is a restarted host, not an approved update. There is a vendor patch with no live-patch tool registered, and the fix typically requires a service restart or system reboot per the KEV requiredAction, so a Windows host that has installed the update but has not taken the restart is still running the pre-patch Remote Access Connection Manager image and has to be counted as exposed rather than as remediated. Scope the rollout to every host carrying the component rather than to a subset chosen from an assumed reachability model: the packet's vector describes an unauthorized attacker denying service locally, while the packet's own summary line describes the flaw conservatively as network-reachable pending Microsoft's component detail — the two framings do not agree, and narrowing the rollout to whichever one is cheaper is how a KEV-listed defect with confirmed exploitation survives the SLA on paper. The distinguishing test: query the fleet for hosts whose installed build carries the fix AND whose RasMan service has restarted since installation; a management-console report of 'update deployed' does not answer that question.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet: cisa_kev true with kev_date 2026-02-10, active_exploitation confirmed, poc_available true, rwep_score 77 against cvss 8.8. patch_available true, live_patch_available false, live_patch_notes 'No live-patch tool registered for this entry at bulk-import time. Vendor patch typically requires service restart or system reboot per the KEV requiredAction.' Vector: 'Microsoft Windows Remote Access Connection Manager contains a NULL pointer dereference that could allow an unauthorized attacker to deny service locally' (CWE-476). The packet's attack_vector line instead reads 'a NULL pointer dereference (CWE-476) in a network-reachable Windows component ... described conservatively as a network-reachable memory-safety flaw pending Microsoft's component detail.'

new_control_requirements.name: MITIGATION-ACTIVE-PATCH-PENDING-VERDICT-CLASS
new_control_requirements.description: The state this entry forces a framework to name is 'update installed, restart deferred'. Because there is no live-patch tool and the fix typically needs a service restart or system reboot, a host in that state has not eliminated the defect — it holds a time-bound compensating position, and the audit record has to surface it as one instead of as 'patched per SLA'. The deferral pressure here is structural rather than incidental: the impact the packet describes is denial of service, and the remediation itself costs a RasMan restart or a reboot, so the operators most motivated to defer are running exactly the workloads whose interruption the cited availability gap is about. Two preconditions bound the compensating state and both belong in the record. It is valid only while a dated restart is scheduled — an open-ended deferral is exposure, not mitigation. And 'service restart or system reboot' is stated without settling which applies to a given build, so the operator has to establish that for their estate and count only hosts where the action actually completed; a host credited on the assumption that a service restart sufficed, when the build needed a reboot, is recorded as remediated while still vulnerable. Where neither has happened and no date exists, the entry is full exposure and should be scored as such.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet: patch_available true, live_patch_available false, live_patch_notes 'No live-patch tool registered for this entry at bulk-import time. new_control_requirements.name: CONTROL-PANEL-PLUGIN-USER-SURFACE-MUST-NOT-REACH-ROOT-OPERATIONS
new_control_requirements.description: FreePBX Endpoint Manager is the control-panel module this control governs, and the packet's vector is the forbidden pattern in a single line: a testconnection feature in the administration UI reaches check_ssh_connect(), which composes an OS command from caller-supplied input (CWE-78), so a form field on a user-facing surface is the only thing standing between a panel operator and command execution on the telephony server as the asterisk user. Applied to this product, the requirement is that the connection-test path pass its parameters to the SSH invocation as arguments rather than as a shell string, and that any privileged operation the module needs sit behind its own validated interface, so the module's own input handling is not the single boundary. The stake is not reduced by the outcome being the asterisk account rather than root: asterisk is the service identity the PBX runs as, so the packet's stated outcome — remote access to the system as an asterisk user — is control of the telephony service and everything it holds, not a low-privilege shell. Distinguishing test: on a staging FreePBX, submit an Endpoint Manager connection test whose host or credential field carries shell metacharacters and confirm no subcommand executes — a patch attestation taken against the FreePBX core that never enumerates installed modules reads clean while an unpatched Endpoint Manager keeps the sink. Precondition, and this is where the control is most likely to be over-claimed on this entry: the packet's detailed vector requires an authenticated known user, but the packet's own summary of the same flaw describes unauthenticated remote command execution, so restricting who holds a FreePBX administrative account bounds the population that can reach testconnection only if the authenticated precondition is the true one — it does nothing if the summary is. Constrain the module's reachability rather than the account list until the vendor update lands, and note that this control states the property the vendor fix must establish; it does not implement it.

An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to potentially obtain remote access to the system as an asterisk user.' The packet's attack_vector field summarises the same entry as 'an OS command-injection flaw (CWE-78) enabling unauthenticated remote command execution on the telephony server' — the two disagree on whether authentication is required, and this description does not resolve that disagreement in the operator's favour. patch_available true, live_patch_available false.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: On a PBX the usual patch-window argument inverts. patch_available is true, live_patch_available is false, and the vendor patch typically requires a service restart or system reboot per the KEV requiredAction — and a service restart on a production telephony server drops every call in progress, which is the specific reason this remediation gets marked done when the module update is installed rather than when the service comes back. Per the packet's own live_patch_notes, a host that has taken the update without the restart is still running the vulnerable code, so 'updated' and 'remediated' are different states here and only the second one counts. Applied to this entry, the clock starts at the 2026-02-03 KEV listing, the maintenance window is scheduled as part of the response rather than deferred into the next telephony change window, and completion is measured per host by the Endpoint Manager version actually loaded after restart rather than by an 'update applied' flag in a console. The compensating-control branch covers the interval: restrict which network segments can reach the FreePBX administration interface at all, since with a public PoC and confirmed exploitation the reachability of that interface is the remaining precondition an operator can act on. State its limits plainly — that bounds who can send the request, it does not close the injection, and it is unavailable wherever the administration interface must stay reachable for normal operation. It also does nothing for a host already reached: the packet marks exploitation confirmed, and an attacker who obtained the asterisk service identity survives the module update, so a server that was reachable during the exposure window needs its stored telephony credentials treated as disclosed and rotated rather than closed out on the patch.

new_control_requirements.name: ENTERPRISE-ERP-MANAGEMENT-FUNCTION-AUTHENTICATION
new_control_requirements.description: FreePBX's password check is where the product makes its access decision, and this CVE is that decision failing open: the packet describes unauthorized users bypassing password authentication and reaching the services provided by the FreePBX admin, ending in administrative access to the telephony server for an attacker who never held an account. Bound to this product, the control means each administrative function on the FreePBX server authorizes its caller itself rather than inheriting a verdict from the authentication layer that fronts it, and the administrative surface is segmented so an untrusted caller cannot present a request to that layer at all — the FreePBX admin interface answers only from an operator or management segment, or an authenticated VPN, and never from the internet or a general user or voice VLAN. The identity and least-privilege gaps recorded on this entry do not touch this path: because no password is presented, no password policy, lockout threshold or second factor on any operator account is ever exercised, per-account privilege scoping is never consulted, and the account model an identity attestation examines is bypassed rather than abused. Distinguishing test: from a segment with no operational need for telephony administration, issue unauthenticated requests to each administrative function on a staging FreePBX instance and confirm each refuses the caller before the function runs — an attestation that every FreePBX administrator holds a unique account with a strong password passes cleanly while this path stays fully open. Precondition: the per-function authorization property is what the vendor update establishes; this control states what to verify and what to restrict, it does not implement the fix. Restricting reachability bounds who can attempt the bypass but leaves it fully available to anything inside the permitted segment, and it is not available at all where the admin surface must stay reachable for remote administration — those instances depend on the update and its required service restart. And because active exploitation is confirmed, an instance whose admin surface was reachable during the exposure window needs its administrative accounts and the configuration reachable from that surface reviewed, and its credentials rotated; the update does not undo changes an attacker made while holding admin access.

The vector states Sangoma FreePBX 'contains an improper authentication vulnerability that potentially allows unauthorized users to bypass password authentication and access services provided by the FreePBX admin', and the attack-vector line records an unauthenticated attacker gaining administrative access to the telephony server. CVSS 9.1, RWEP 77, poc_available true, active_exploitation confirmed, CISA KEV-listed 2026-02-03. patch_available true, live_patch_available false, with live_patch_notes recording that the vendor patch typically requires a service restart or system reboot. Citing gaps include UK-CAF-B2 (identity and access control), NIST-800-53-AC-6 (least privilege) and NIS2-Art21-network-security — the first two are cited precisely because no account is authenticated anywhere on this path.

A vendor patch is available with no live-patch path and a fix that typically requires a service restart or system reboot, so an instance that has taken the update but not restarted still runs the vulnerable code and must be counted as exposed; on a PBX that restart is also the step most likely to be deferred, because taking it interrupts calls in progress, and a deferral recorded as 'patched' is the specific way this remediation goes wrong. new_control_requirements.name: PERIMETER-COMPROMISE-REBUILD-NOT-PATCH
new_control_requirements.description: A help-desk server is where an IT organization's operational secrets accumulate: the service accounts wired into directory and asset-discovery integrations, the database and mail-integration credentials, and the ticket bodies in which staff paste passwords and access instructions. The packet's path hands an unauthenticated attacker command execution on that host, and exploitation is confirmed, so an instance that was reachable before the update landed has to be handled as an incident rather than as a patch record: preserve the application and configuration state for review, rebuild the server rather than updating it in place, and rotate every credential the instance held or could reach — the directory and integration service accounts first, since those are what convert a single-host compromise into access across the estate. Applying the update to a running instance closes the deserialization path but removes nothing already placed through it: a web shell in the application's served tree, a scheduled task, an added administrative account, or a modified application file all survive the upgrade and none of them are visible to a version check. new_control_requirements.name: SERVICE-INTERNAL-PROTOCOL-DESERIALIZATION-HARDENING
new_control_requirements.description: For Web Help Desk this control means treating the service's own request listener as a trust boundary instead of an internal convenience: the defect is untrusted deserialization reaching command execution for a peer that never authenticates, and the deployment assumption that normally protects it — "the help desk is an internal ticketing system" — is not a control, it is a statement about where the box sits. The requirement for this product is that the Web Help Desk listener accepts connections only from the segments that legitimately raise and service tickets (staff networks, the management/jump network), enforced by network ACL or host firewall rather than inherited from network topology, and that no instance is published to the internet for remote-staff convenience without an authenticating gateway in front of it, since an unauthenticated request body is all the packet's path requires to reach the deserializer. Content arriving on that listener must not be permitted to construct arbitrary objects, rather than being trusted because of where it appears to come from. The distinguishing test: from a general user or guest VLAN, and from an external address, attempt to reach the Web Help Desk service port on a staging deployment and confirm the connection is refused before the application processes the request body — an instance that passes a patch-level audit while answering unauthenticated requests from any segment is exposed again the moment the next deserialization defect in this product lands.

new_control_requirements.name: DEVICE-MANAGEMENT-GATEWAY-CONFIG-ENDPOINT-AUTH-INPUT-NEUTRALIZATION
new_control_requirements.description: EPMM is the device-management gateway this control governs, and the packet places the defect squarely on its management surface: a code injection that 'could allow attackers to achieve unauthenticated remote code execution' (CWE-94). Bound to this product, the control means every request handler on the EPMM management surface makes its own authorization decision before any request content is interpreted, and never turns request-supplied content into executable code — the endpoint's own decision, not the surrounding operator account model, is what stands between an untrusted caller and code execution on the appliance. This is why the least-privilege gap cited here cannot be closed by tightening EPMM roles: the attacker holds no EPMM account, so per-account privilege scoping is never consulted and the account model an access-control attestation examines is bypassed rather than abused. Preconditions: endpoint-side authorization and input neutralization are properties the vendor update establishes — this control states what to verify, not how to build it. Until that update and the restart it typically requires have both landed, restricting which segments can reach the EPMM management surface bounds who can send the request but leaves the injection sink fully exploitable to any caller inside the permitted segment, and that lever is unavailable wherever the surface must stay reachable for normal operation. Distinguishing test: on a staging EPMM, send unauthenticated requests to each management endpoint carrying content shaped to be interpreted rather than stored, and confirm each is refused before interpretation — an estate that evidences unique, role-scoped accounts for every EPMM administrator passes its access-control review while this path stays wide open.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet vector: 'Ivanti Endpoint Manager Mobile (EPMM) contains a code injection vulnerability that could allow attackers to achieve unauthenticated remote code execution'; attack_vector: 'code injection (CWE-94) yielding unauthenticated remote code execution on the EPMM management surface'. cwe_refs CWE-94; cvss 9.8; rwep_score 77; patch_available true, live_patch_available false, with the fix typically requiring 'service restart or system reboot per the KEV requiredAction'. NIST-800-53-AC-6 (Least Privilege) and UK-CAF-B4 (System security) are recorded as insufficient for this entry.

new_control_requirements.name: FLEET-COMPROMISE-IR-PLAYBOOK
new_control_requirements.description: Unauthenticated RCE on EPMM is not an appliance incident: EPMM is the control plane the managed fleet derives its configuration and trust state from, so code execution on that box is authority over everything downstream of it — and that exploitation is confirmed in the wild with a public PoC. The playbook this CVE demands, rehearsed before the next disclosure rather than drafted during one, covers the half no patch-shaped control reaches: certificate revocation issued from a control plane whose integrity has been re-established, device-trust-state invalidation, an audit of every configuration profile pushed since the earliest point at which exploitation cannot be excluded, quarantine criteria for downstream devices, and rotation of every credential the EPMM instance held or that authenticated through it during that window. The vendor update stops further exploitation of the code path; it removes nothing an attacker already pushed to the fleet or read out of the appliance, which is precisely the residue a flaw-remediation control records as closed. Precondition: the fleet-side steps sequence after the EPMM instance itself has been rebuilt or otherwise established as trustworthy — running them from the instance that was exploited re-signs the fleet from a box of unknown integrity, so the appliance work gates the fleet work and the fleet stays in its pre-incident trust state until that completes. Distinguishing test: for one managed device chosen at random, name the certificate that would be revoked, the profile history that would be audited, and the credential set that would be rotated, and time how long producing that answer takes — an incident-response policy that cannot produce it for a single device will not produce it for the fleet under an active compromise.

NIST-800-53-SI-2 (Flaw Remediation) is recorded as insufficient for this entry.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: The KEV clock for EPMM opened 2026-01-29, and the packet pairs that with confirmed in-the-wild exploitation, a public PoC and unauthenticated remote code execution at CVSS 9.8 — the profile a routine infrastructure-patch cadence is least able to absorb, on a management appliance whose compromise is the fleet's compromise rather than one host's. Applied here, the control means the Ivanti fix is driven across every EPMM instance on that clock, with completion measured per instance by the version actually running and the restart having been taken, not by an approval sitting in a change queue. Precondition: there is no live-patch path and the fix typically requires a service restart or system reboot per the KEV requiredAction, so an instance that has taken the update but not restarted is still running the vulnerable code and must be counted as exposed — on a management appliance that restart is deferred because taking it interrupts device management, which is exactly how an instance ends up recorded as patched while it is not. Where the restart cannot be taken inside the window, restricting reachability of the EPMM management surface is the only remaining lever; it bounds who can send the request and does not remove the injection path, so it carries a dated end rather than closing the item. Distinguishing test: for each EPMM instance produce the running version and the restart timestamp that activated it — a vulnerability-management report showing the update deployed without the restart cannot distinguish a remediated instance from an exposed one.

prevention.adequacy: Patch is necessary but insufficient alone — web shells and stolen credentials survive the patch; endpoint-manager/dev-tool compromise has downstream and supply-chain reach that must be reviewed.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Monitoring on the InetUtils: exploit-shaped requests, a shell/interpreter spawned from the service process.
detection.adequacy: Necessary to catch exploitation and resident persistence after patching.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: The exploit path here needs no credential and no user interaction — setting the USER environment variable to a '-f root' value drives telnetd into an authentication bypass — so any reachable unpatched listener is exploitable by whoever can open the port, and the KEV clock has to be met on every host and image where the inetutils telnetd binary is actually in service, not only on the hosts the patch-management inventory happens to enumerate. No live-patch tool is registered for this entry, so the SLA is satisfied by the vendor update with the restart the KEV requiredAction implies; stopping or firewalling the telnetd listener is the mitigation available inside the window, and it must be recorded as a compensating control rather than as remediation.

new_control_requirements.name: MITIGATION-ACTIVE-PATCH-PENDING-VERDICT-CLASS
new_control_requirements.description: For this CVE two remediation states report identically on a vulnerability dashboard and are not equivalent: (a) inetutils updated to the fixed build, and (b) the telnetd listener stopped or firewalled while the vulnerable binary stays on disk. State (b) does close the path, but only for as long as the listener stays down — a host rebuild from an unpatched image, a re-enable of the service, or any dependent tooling that starts telnetd restores an unauthenticated path to root with no new vulnerability being introduced. Audit output must carry the state per host with a time-bound action to reach (a), instead of collapsing both into 'remediated' and losing the fact that the exposure is one service-start away.
new_control_requirements.evidence: patch_available is true and live_patch_available is false, so both a patch path and a service-disable path exist for the same entry. CVE-2026-21509.name: Microsoft Office Security Feature Bypass Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: a security-feature-bypass (CWE-807) in Microsoft Office, letting attacker-controlled documents evade an Office security control. CISA KEV-listed 2026-01-26 with confirmed in-the-wild exploitation.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none (the victim opens the attacker's document or visits the attacker's content)
attack_vector.complexity: low — KEV-listed, actively exploited; treat as weaponized
attack_vector.ai_factor: No AI involvement documented in discovery or weaponization.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Apply the Microsoft security update; because this flaw defeats a protection mechanism, do not rely on that single control — enforce defence-in-depth (ASR rules, application control, mail/web content filtering, and macro restrictions) so a bypass of SmartScreen / Mark-of-the-Web / Protected View is not a single point of failure.
prevention.adequacy: Patch is required; the lasting lesson is that a single protection mechanism (the one bypassed) cannot be the only barrier — layered controls are mandatory.

detection.what_would_have_worked: EDR / endpoint telemetry for execution of content lacking Mark-of-the-Web provenance and security-prompt bypass.
detection.adequacy: Backstops endpoints not yet patched and catches the post-bypass execution stage.

response.what_would_have_worked: Force the patch across the estate, isolate exploited endpoints, hunt for follow-on payloads, and review for credential theft.
response.adequacy: Mandatory; client-side exploitation typically leads to credential harvest and lateral movement that a bare patch does not remediate.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: The 30-day flaw-remediation SLA is far longer than the observed exploitation window for a KEV-listed, actively-exploited client-side flaw; the protection-bypass variants specifically defeat the warning that would otherwise slow the user, so the patch is the only barrier left.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: 'Appropriate timescales' is undefined; the standard reading is unsafe for an actively-exploited client flaw, and security-feature-bypass flaws mean a single layered control (Protected View, SmartScreen, Mark-of-the-Web) cannot be relied on alone.

AU-ISM-1546.gap: Essential 8 names application patching, application hardening, and macro/Office controls separately, but does not require defence-in-depth for the case where the protection mechanism itself is bypassed — ASR rules, application control, and mail/web content filtering are the load-bearing layers when SmartScreen/Protected View fail.

compliance_exposure_score.basis: Microsoft Office is ubiquitous on endpoints; audited organizations that lean on a single protection (SmartScreen, Protected View, Mark-of-the-Web) without layered controls are exposed when that mechanism is bypassed, and long-tail patch hygiene leaves a window for the memory-corruption variants.

new_control_requirements.name: ARCHIVE-CONTENT-TYPE-PROVENANCE
new_control_requirements.description: CWE-807 on this entry is Office deciding whether content is trusted from input the attacker supplies, so the durable operator-side control is to move the origin determination off the document and onto a boundary the organization operates: the mail gateway, the managed file share and the web download path apply and preserve the untrusted-origin marking themselves, and that marking survives archives, disk-image containers and renames, so the Office host is told the file is externally sourced instead of deriving it from metadata travelling with the file. This matters more than usual here because which Office security feature the bypass defeats is not named — no in-product setting can be assumed to be the intact one, which is exactly why the control that is worth attaching is the one whose input is established outside the vulnerable decision. The precondition has to be written down rather than assumed: boundary-applied marking only covers files that cross a boundary you run. A document arriving on removable media, through a personal cloud-sync client, or on any unmanaged path never passes a marking point and reaches Office unmarked, so those ingress paths must be blocked or brought under the same marking; where that is not done, this control does not cover them and the vulnerable decision is still reached with attacker-supplied input. The distinguishing test: send an externally-sourced document through each ingress path in turn and confirm it arrives at the Office host already marked untrusted, rather than confirming that a hardening policy shows as enabled in the management console.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet vector: 'Microsoft Office contains a security feature bypass vulnerability in which reliance on untrusted inputs in a security decision in Microsoft Office could allow an unauthorized attacker to bypass a security feature locally' (CWE-807). cisa_kev true, kev_date 2026-01-26, active_exploitation confirmed, poc_available true, rwep_score 77 against cvss 8.8. The specific Office security feature that is bypassed is not named. Citing gaps on this entry include ASD Essential Eight 'User application hardening' and UK NCSC CAF B4 'System security'.

new_control_requirements.name: PROTECTION-MECHANISM-FAILURE-CLASS-REGRESSION
new_control_requirements.description: This entry is the case that makes a configured-and-enabled attestation worthless: the packet's flaw is the bypass of an Office security feature, so the setting is on and the check returns the wrong answer. Treat Office document handling as a protection-mechanism class and hold a regression battery of the known bypass primitives for that class, re-run on every Office patch deployment rather than once against this CVE, with the fixed build validated by detonating the battery on a representative managed image instead of by reading a version number off an inventory. The packet's own note that some impacted products may be end-of-life or end-of-service makes the recurring form of the test the load-bearing half: those installs will not receive the next fix, so the battery is the only mechanism that tells an operator whether the posture built around them still blocks. State the limit plainly instead of recording the battery as coverage — it exercises only the primitives already known to it and says nothing about the next bypass in the class, so it establishes that this fix landed and that the surrounding controls still hold, not that Office is immune to the class.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet vector: Microsoft Office security feature bypass (CWE-807) that 'could allow an unauthorized attacker to bypass a security feature locally', carrying the note 'Some of the impacted product(s) could be end-of-life (EoL) and/or end-of-service (EoS).' active_exploitation confirmed, poc_available true, kev_date 2026-01-26, rwep_score 77. Citing gap on this entry: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 A.8.8 'Management of technical vulnerabilities'.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: The KEV clock on this entry opens 2026-01-26 with exploitation confirmed and a PoC available, and the packet splits the estate into two populations that need different completion criteria. For supported Office builds the mitigation is the vendor update driven across the fleet with the restart the fix typically requires, since no live-patch tool is registered — an install that has not restarted is not a closed item. For the installs the packet flags as end-of-life or end-of-service, no update is coming, and the packet's stated action is to discontinue use or transition to a supported version; for that population the 'verified mitigation' leg of this control is a dated transition or removal plan, and there is no patch task to track. Naming that split is the point of attaching this control here: a patch-compliance report that files the EoL/EoS installs under 'no update available' drops them out of the SLA permanently, and on an entry with confirmed in-the-wild exploitation that is exactly the population an attacker keeps.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Packet: cisa_kev true, kev_date 2026-01-26, active_exploitation confirmed, poc_available true, rwep_score 77 against cvss 8.8. patch_available true, live_patch_available false, live_patch_notes 'No live-patch tool registered for this entry at bulk-import time. Vendor patch typically requires service restart or system reboot per the KEV requiredAction.' Vector: 'Some of the impacted product(s) could be end-of-life (EoL) and/or end-of-service (EoS). Users are advised to discontinue use and/or transition to a supported version.'

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: A KEV clock on this entry is a clock on the entire virtual estate, not on one server: vCenter is the management plane for every host and VM registered to it, so the blast radius of the recorded remote code execution is the virtualization control plane rather than a single application host. The reachable surface is the DCE/RPC implementation, which processes packets before authentication — so 'only administrators use vCenter' does not bound exposure; anything with network access to the vCenter service does. There is no live-patch path and the vendor fix requires a service restart or reboot, which is the real obstacle for this asset class: vCenter restarts are typically held behind virtualization change freezes. The SLA must therefore pre-authorize the vCenter restart as part of the KEV response rather than queueing it behind the next maintenance window, and any window that cannot be met must be recorded as unremediated exposure with the DCE/RPC surface restricted in the interim.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CISA KEV-listed 2026-01-23 with active_exploitation 'confirmed' and poc_available true; CVSS 9.8, RWEP 77. The catalog vector records that vCenter Server 'contains an out-of-bounds write vulnerability in the implementation of the DCERPC protocol. This could allow a malicious actor with network access to vCenter Server to send specially crafted network packets, potentially leading to remote code execution.' patch_available is true, live_patch_available is false, and live_patch_notes reads: 'No live-patch tool registered for this entry at bulk-import time. Vendor patch typically requires service restart or system reboot per the KEV requiredAction.'

new_control_requirements.name: APPSERVER-REMOTING-PROTOCOL-RESTRICTION
new_control_requirements.description: vCenter's DCE/RPC listener is exactly the binary remoting-protocol class this control governs: a non-HTTP protocol endpoint that answers before authentication and whose parser is itself the vulnerable code, so the perimeter firewall and the web-tier hardening that most vCenter deployments are audited against never touch it. The requirement for this deployment is that DCE/RPC on vCenter accepts connections only from hosts that legitimately speak it — management and jump networks and the hosts vCenter administers — enforced by network ACL or host firewall rather than assumed from 'vCenter is internal', and that a KEV-listed defect in that parser is patched on an accelerated clock with the service restart taken rather than folded into the next quarterly virtualization window. The distinguishing test for this product: from a general user or workstation VLAN on a staging deployment, send crafted DCE/RPC packets at vCenter and confirm they are dropped before reaching the listener — an estate that passes vCenter role-and-permission audits while leaving the DCE/RPC port reachable from any internal segment is still exposed to the unauthenticated packet path.
new_control_requirements.evidence: The catalog attack_vector records 'an out-of-bounds write (CWE-787) in the vCenter Server DCE/RPC protocol implementation, exploitable by an unauthenticated attacker for remote code execution', and the vector states the trigger is 'a malicious actor with network access to vCenter Server' sending 'specially crafted network packets' — network reach to the protocol endpoint is the sole precondition. KEV-listed 2026-01-23, active_exploitation 'confirmed', poc_available true, CVSS 9.8, RWEP 77. The gaps this entry cites include NIS2 Art. 21 security of network and information systems and UK CAF B4 system security.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: The KEV clock on this entry opens 2026-01-22 against a mail server, and the scoping unit that matters is the endpoint, not the host count: every ZCS instance whose /h/rest endpoint answers remote callers is in the exploited population, which is why the ordinary multi-week application-patch cadence that mail platforms are usually audited under is the gap this entry demonstrates. The SLA record for this entry should also capture the exposure window it closes, per instance, from the 2026-01-22 KEV listing to the completed restart, because that window is the input to the compromise-assessment decision the rebuild runbook depends on; an SLA that records only a completion date destroys the information needed to decide whether patching was sufficient.

new_control_requirements.name: PERIMETER-COMPROMISE-REBUILD-NOT-PATCH
new_control_requirements.description: Zimbra ZCS sits on the internet mail boundary and the flaw gives remote code execution on that server, so this entry belongs to the class this runbook exists for: the update repairs the request-dispatch defect but removes nothing that was placed on, or read from, the server through it beforehand, and patch-in-place closes the ticket over whatever is already resident. The default for an affected instance is therefore capture configuration and forensic evidence, rebuild from a known-good image onto the fixed build, and rotate the credentials and tokens the server held, rather than update-and-close. Two preconditions have to be stated or the runbook is mis-scoped. First, the trigger is exposure during the window between the 2026-01-22 KEV listing and the completed update, not the CVE in the abstract: where per-request logs covering that window exist and show no exploitation against the /h/rest path, patch-and-verify is the proportionate response — but where those logs were never collected, absence of alerts is not evidence of absence, and the instance belongs in the rebuild path rather than being cleared by default. Second, it is not established whether the /h/rest request path requires authentication, so exposure cannot be narrowed to unauthenticated reachability; an instance reachable only by authenticated users stays in scope until vendor detail settles that, and 'the endpoint is behind login' is not a basis for skipping the assessment.

Whether the /h/rest request path requires authentication is not established. Citing gap on this entry: UK NCSC CAF B4 'System security'.

attack_vector.description: an authentication bypass using an alternate path or channel (CWE-288) letting an unauthenticated attacker reach administrative functionality on the Versa Concerto SD-WAN orchestrator. CISA KEV-listed 2026-01-22 with confirmed in-the-wild exploitation.

new_control_requirements.name: PERIMETER-DEVICE-ZERODAY-SLA-TIER
new_control_requirements.description: Versa Concerto orchestrates the SD-WAN fabric, so an unauthenticated route to its administrative endpoints is a trust-boundary failure rather than an application bug, and it belongs in the perimeter SLA tier alongside firewalls and VPN concentrators. The packet places the defect in the Traefik reverse-proxy configuration in front of the orchestrator — which is also the layer an operator can constrain immediately: the vendor fix goes on within hours of the 2026-01-22 KEV listing, or the administrative and internal Actuator routes are removed from every untrusted-network path until it does. A routine appliance-patch window does not apply to the device that defines the fabric's policy plane, and 'orchestrator, not edge device' is exactly the classification error that keeps this system on the slow tier.

new_control_requirements.name: PERIMETER-COMPROMISE-REBUILD-NOT-PATCH
new_control_requirements.description: The internal Actuator endpoint can be leveraged for heap dumps and trace logs — process memory and log content from the system that holds credentials, session material and policy for the whole SD-WAN fabric. Applying the vendor fix to a Concerto instance that was reachable during the confirmed-exploitation window closes the entry path but leaves everything already dumped valid, and it destroys nothing the attacker planted. Response for this CVE must therefore default to treating an exposed orchestrator as compromised: capture and review its configuration, rebuild the instance from a known-good image, and rotate every credential, token and key the orchestrator held or distributed to managed devices — patch-in-place is not a remediation verdict for a device whose exploitation primitive is memory disclosure.
