AU-Essential-8-MFA.gap: ML3 requires MFA for privileged users and N-able's post-incident guidance repeats the advice, but an alternate-channel bypass delivers an already-authenticated administrative session, so the second factor is never requested; MSPs that had enforced MFA on every technician account were compromised regardless, and their assessed maturity had no bearing on the outcome.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: Technical vulnerability management runs on vendor advisories, and the advisory the ISMS would have consumed — the CVE-2026-18556 fix shipped in 2026.2 — was itself the source of the residual exposure; no asset inventory, CVSS triage, patch SLA or periodic review distinguishes a complete fix from an incomplete one when the vendor has published no root cause to evaluate against.

new_control_requirements.name: INCOMPLETE-PATCH-SEQUENCE-SEVERITY-MULTIPLIER
new_control_requirements.description: Vulnerability-management programs must apply a severity multiplier when a CVE is the Nth in an incomplete-patch sequence on the same primitive (third MOTW bypass, second AMSI bypass, etc.). Framework controls treating each CVE as discrete obscure the structural defect; the Nth CVE in a sequence implies that future bypasses on the same primitive are likely.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2026-18577 is by definition the second CVE on the same N-central authentication primitive — an incomplete patch for CVE-2026-18556 that left the alternate channel open through 2026.3.1 — and attackers were working fully-patched 2026.3.1 consoles from 2026-08-01, a day before 2026.3.1.7 existed. Scoring it as a discrete item is what let "the vendor's fix is installed" and a 100-percent patch KPI stay true throughout the exposure window.

new_control_requirements.name: FLEET-CONTROL-PLANE-ADMIN-PRIVILEGE-TIER
new_control_requirements.description: Administrators of fleet-control-plane systems (MDM/UEM, EDR consoles, identity providers, container orchestrators, configuration management) must be classified as a distinct privilege tier above application admins, with: PAM-jumphost-only access, FIDO2 step-up per session, just-in-time elevation with approval workflow, separate identity from any other admin role, and dedicated PAW (privileged access workstation) hardware. Compliance frameworks must enumerate this tier explicitly rather than collapsing it into 'admin'.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2026-18577's alternate channel hands the caller an already-authenticated administrative session, so the second factor is never requested and MSPs that had enforced MFA on every technician account were compromised regardless of their assessed maturity. Only treating the RMM console as its own privilege tier — jumphost-only reachability and per-session step-up rather than login-time MFA — takes the anonymous internet caller off the path.

new_control_requirements.name: FLEET-COMPROMISE-IR-PLAYBOOK
new_control_requirements.description: Pre-rehearsed IR playbook for fleet-control-plane compromise including: MDM-pushed certificate revocation, device-trust-state invalidation, configuration-profile audit since the suspected compromise window, downstream device-quarantine criteria, and credential rotation for any account that authenticated through a compromised fleet device during the exposure period.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2026-18577 operators registered a Cloudflare tunnel as a Windows service on managed endpoints — outbound-only, encrypted, generating no inbound event, and by N-able's own statement surviving revocation of N-central access — so console remediation and inbound monitoring both end nothing. Downstream device-quarantine criteria and rotation of every credential used through a reached endpoint during the exposure window are the steps that actually close the residual access.

CVE-2026-20316.name: Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center Use of Hard-coded Password Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: A static username and password compiled into the Cisco Secure FMC appliance image authenticate a low-privileged account through the ordinary web interface, so an unauthenticated remote attacker simply logs in and reads device inventory, firewall policy and management-plane configuration. There is no exploit to write — possession of the credential is the exploit. Cisco raised its own Security Impact Rating to High because the account can be chained with other FMC vulnerabilities to escalate privileges; the follow-on privileged path invokes package_info.pl as root against a temporary file, leaving /var/tmp/license.tmp behind.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; the credential is vendor-embedded rather than operator-held, so from the attacker's side no privilege is required at all
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L with no user interaction; authenticating with a known static password requires no technique, and Cisco PSIRT confirmed in July 2026 that at least one party already holds it
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered — Cisco's advisory cisco-sa-fmc-static-cred-BET3Cjh credits Jimi Sebree of Horizon3.ai, and Horizon3 built a NodeZero Rapid Response test instead of publishing a PoC. A second, independent discovery track exists: a threat actor located the same credential before or concurrently with the coordinated report, which is the expected outcome for embedded credentials extractable offline from an appliance image. No AI tooling is credited on any track.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Apply the per-train hotfix package from Cisco's advisory (7.0 → GB-7.0.9.1-3, 7.2 → HL-7.2.11.1-4, 7.4 → HG-7.4.7.1-3, 7.6 → CY-7.6.5.1-2, 7.7 → AM-7.7.12.1-2, 10.0 → P-10.0.1.1-2) and keep the FMC management interface off the public internet on a dedicated management network.
prevention.adequacy: Incomplete by construction. Cisco states plainly there are no workarounds — the credential cannot be disabled, rotated or removed by the operator — and no hotfix is published for the 7.3 train even though 7.3.0 through 7.3.1.2 appear on Cisco's own affected list, so those deployments cannot reach a fixed state inside the three-day KEV window without a version migration.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Run Cisco's own compromise check from expert mode — zgrep "package_info.*license" /var/log/messages* — and look for /var/tmp/license.tmp on the appliance. Alongside that, alert on successful web-interface logins by a local account with no operational history in the deployment, sourced from outside the management network.
detection.adequacy: The zgrep hit and the license.tmp artifact are reliable after the fact, but the login itself succeeds normally and produces a legitimate-looking session rather than a failed-authentication pattern, so nothing in ordinary authentication monitoring flags it.

response.what_would_have_worked: Run the compromise check before declaring a patched FMC clean, assume the read access already occurred and treat device inventory and policy as disclosed reconnaissance for the whole perimeter, and review the FMC for the follow-on privilege-escalation chain Cisco warns the account enables.
response.adequacy: Because exploitation preceded the advisory, patch-then-verify is the only defensible order; and the disclosed data — the management plane of the firewall estate — cannot be rotated the way a credential can.

NIST-800-53-AC-2.gap: Account management operates over accounts the operator can enumerate, assign owners to, review and remove; this one lives inside the vendor's appliance image, never appears in an FMC user review, and cannot be disabled or rotated — a flawless AC-2 recertification of the firewall management platform enumerates none of the accounts that mattered.

DORA-Art28.gap: A register of information naming Cisco as an ICT third party supporting a critical function, with contractual terms, exit strategy and monitoring in place, would be complete and audit-clean; Art.28 monitoring addresses service performance, concentration and contractual assurance and has no mechanism that detects a password compiled into an appliance image, so the 4-hour major-incident clock only begins once someone finds /var/tmp/license.tmp.

UK-CAF-B2.gap: This is a direct B2 failure that the operator cannot remediate: the identity is vendor-embedded and authenticates over the standard web interface, so joiners/movers/leavers processes, privilege reviews and credential-rotation policy — the activities B2 is assessed on — have no reach over it, and B2 outcomes are scored against what the organisation controls.

AU-ISM-1546.gap: The control assumes a patch exists for the release in use. Cisco published hotfixes for the 7.0, 7.2, 7.4, 7.6, 7.7 and 10.0 trains and none for 7.3, despite listing 7.3.0 through 7.3.1.2 as affected, so a conformant entity on 7.3 had nothing to apply and had to plan a train migration while the exposure persisted through the whole migration window.

ISO-27001-2022-A.5.21.gap: No supplier questionnaire, security addendum or vendor attestation contains a question that surfaces a hard-coded low-privileged account inside a firewall management appliance, and the operator cannot test for one without reverse-engineering the image — A.5.21's verification step has no reachable evidence, so full conformance and this vulnerability coexist without contradiction.

new_control_requirements.name: PERIMETER-DEVICE-ZERODAY-SLA-TIER
new_control_requirements.description: Compliance frameworks must define a distinct patch SLA tier for pre-auth RCE on perimeter-trust-boundary devices (firewalls, VPN concentrators, WAFs, edge load-balancers). Tier requirement: vendor-mitigation deployed within 4 hours of KEV listing OR isolation of the vulnerable interface; standard 14/30-day SLAs do not apply because the device IS the trust boundary.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2026-20316 is a static credential compiled into the Cisco Secure FMC image that the operator cannot disable, rotate or remove, and Cisco published hotfixes for the 7.0, 7.2, 7.4, 7.6, 7.7 and 10.0 trains but none for 7.3 despite listing 7.3.0 through 7.3.1.2 as affected. For those deployments the tier's alternative limb — isolation of the vulnerable interface, keeping the FMC management interface off the public internet on a dedicated management network — is the only remediation reachable inside the three-day KEV window, and FMC is the management plane of the perimeter itself.

new_control_requirements.name: PEN-TEST-SCOPE-INCLUDES-SECURITY-PRODUCTS
new_control_requirements.description: Penetration test and red-team scopes must explicitly include security-defense products (EDR, AV, DLP, identity-providers, secret-managers) as in-scope attack surface, not as defenses to evade. Scope language must call out that these products' admin interfaces, agent processes, and update channels are testable surfaces.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2026-20316's account lives inside the vendor's appliance image, never appears in an FMC user review, and no supplier questionnaire or attestation contains a question that would surface it — the operator's only alternative is reverse-engineering the image. Scoping the firewall management console's admin interface as testable surface produces the one reachable piece of evidence: a working web-interface login for an account the operator cannot enumerate or rotate.

new_control_requirements.name: PERIMETER-COMPROMISE-REBUILD-NOT-PATCH
new_control_requirements.description: Pre-rehearsed IR runbook for any perimeter device that suffers a pre-auth RCE CVE in active exploitation MUST default to config-exfil + rebuild + credential rotation, not patch-in-place. Patch-in-place leaves attacker-installed implants intact.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2026-20316 exploitation preceded Cisco's advisory — PSIRT confirmed a party already held the credential — and the follow-on privileged chain runs package_info.pl as root, leaving /var/tmp/license.tmp behind, so a hotfixed FMC is not a clean FMC. The runbook has to default to running the compromise check before declaring the device remediated and to treating the disclosed device inventory and firewall policy as reconnaissance that cannot be rotated the way a credential can.

CVE-2020-5741.name: Plex Media Server Remote Code Execution Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: An attacker holding the server administrator's Plex account — specifically an admin X-Plex-Token — creates a new photo library via POST /library/sections, uploads a Python-pickled file named 'Dict' into it, repoints the Windows-only LocalAppDataPath preference at that library via POST /:/prefs, then restarts the com.plexapp.system plugin. On restart Plex calls pickle.load() on the attacker's file and executes arbitrary Python as the Plex service user. In the 2022 LastPass intrusion this ran against a roughly 75-versions-stale install on a DevOps engineer's home endpoint and delivered a keylogger.
attack_vector.privileges_required: high — PR:H; an admin X-Plex-Token is required, which in the LastPass case was obtained by targeting a personal home machine rather than the corporate boundary
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; pickle.load() executes deterministically with no race and no memory-corruption uncertainty, and the Metasploit module exploit/windows/http/plex_unpickle_dict_rce automates the entire library-create, upload, preference-change and restart chain
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered — Chris Lyne of Tenable reported it (advisory TRA-2020-32) and Plex shipped the fix in 1.19.3 on 2020-05-07. No AI involvement in discovery or in weaponization.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Upgrade Plex Media Server on Windows to 1.19.3 or later — and, more consequentially, bring personally-installed network-facing software on work-adjacent endpoints inside the managed patch estate, since the exploited host sat roughly 75 builds behind a fix that had been available for nearly three years.
prevention.adequacy: The patch closes the vector outright and was available from 2020-05-07; it was inadequate in practice because no control reached the asset. A fix nobody can deploy to an unmanaged host is not remediation.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alert on the exploit's own request sequence — a token-authenticated POST /library/sections creating a photo library, a 'Dict' upload into it, a POST /:/prefs changing LocalAppDataPath, then a /:/plugins/com.plexapp.system/restart — and on the Plex service process spawning a Python interpreter or other child process.
detection.adequacy: The sequence is distinctive and cheap to detect wherever endpoint telemetry exists; on the endpoint that actually mattered there was no collection at all, which is the point of the case.

response.what_would_have_worked: Hunt the photo-library paths for a leftover 'Dict' or 'Dict-1' file (a cancelled exploit leaves it behind), treat the host as compromised rather than cleanable, and rotate every credential, session token and vault secret that touched it.
response.adequacy: Credential rotation is the whole response: the payload's purpose was keylogging a developer's master credentials, and evicting the code does not un-steal what it already captured.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: A vendor fix existed from 2020-05-07 and the exploited host was roughly 75 builds behind it nearly three years later; SI-2 flaw remediation has no reach over a personally-installed media server on a home endpoint that never entered the organisation's remediation scope.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: The patch-management obligation presumes the vulnerable asset appears in the entity's inventory, and this one was a DevOps engineer's own Plex install on a home machine — a fully compliant corporate patch cadence and the actual initial-access vector never intersected, which is precisely how the credential-vault compromise began.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: B4 secure-configuration outcomes are written for systems inside the assessed boundary, and a work-adjacent consumer media server was never in it; the code path itself is Plex's plugin framework deserializing a pickled file it trusts by design, so once an admin token is held no further defect is needed.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Patch-application timeframes bind an enumerated set of business applications, and Plex Media Server on a personal endpoint is not on that list, so the control never fired while the host sat years behind an available fix.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: Remediation is scheduled from an asset and vulnerability register, and an unmanaged personal install appears in neither — so a CVSS 7.2 pickle-deserialization flaw with a public Metasploit module was never risk-rated, never scheduled, and never patched.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2020-5741 was KEV-listed 2023-03-10 against a fix that shipped in Plex Media Server 1.19.3 on 2020-05-07, with a Metasploit module automating the whole library-create, Dict-upload, LocalAppDataPath-change and plugin-restart chain — and the exploited host sat roughly 75 builds behind it. A KEV-tied 4-hour clock is what turns a three-year-old available patch into a mandated immediate sweep of work-adjacent hosts instead of a register entry that was never risk-rated or scheduled.

new_control_requirements.name: FLEET-CONTROL-PLANE-ADMIN-PRIVILEGE-TIER
new_control_requirements.description: Administrators of fleet-control-plane systems (MDM/UEM, EDR consoles, identity providers, container orchestrators, configuration management) must be classified as a distinct privilege tier above application admins, with: PAM-jumphost-only access, FIDO2 step-up per session, just-in-time elevation with approval workflow, separate identity from any other admin role, and dedicated PAW (privileged access workstation) hardware. Compliance frameworks must enumerate this tier explicitly rather than collapsing it into 'admin'.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2020-5741 was exploited on a DevOps engineer's own Plex install on a home machine — a work-adjacent consumer media server that no secure-configuration boundary ever contained — and the payload was a keylogger aimed at the credentials that unlocked a production secret store. Putting that privileged tier on dedicated PAW hardware with a separate identity removes the unmanaged endpoint from the credential path entirely, which is the only lever an outcome-based configuration assessment of the assessed estate can never reach.

CVE-2022-28810.name: Zoho ManageEngine ADSelfService Plus Remote Code Execution Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: An actor authenticates to the ADSelfService Plus admin console — frequently with the shipped admin/admin default — reads the password-policy list, and writes an OS command into a policy's post-action 'custom script' via /ServletAPI/configuration/policyConfig/setAPCDetails. The planted command then runs as NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM the next time any user performs a password reset or account unlock. A second, only partially-authenticated path injects shell metacharacters through the unsanitised %password% variable, so a reset value containing '&& <command>' executes directly.
attack_vector.privileges_required: high — PR:H for the console path, though the bar is nominal because the product shipped a default admin/admin credential; the %password% injection route needs only partial authentication
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L with UI:R, the user interaction being any password reset or account unlock that fires the planted script; Rapid7's Metasploit module automates the policy-configuration path end to end
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered — Rapid7's research and MDR team (Jake Baines, Hernan Diaz, Andrew Iwamaye, Dan Kelly) found it and disclosed under coordination: vendor notified 2022-04-06, build 6122 released 2022-04-09, public 2022-04-14. No AI tooling credited.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Upgrade to build 6122 or later, which removes web-based custom-script configuration entirely (scripts must now be placed on disk by someone with OS access) and base64-encodes script arguments — and rotate the default admin credential, which is what makes the PR:H rating meaningless in practice.
prevention.adequacy: The build closes the configuration route but leaves any script already planted in a password policy exactly where it is, so the upgrade only counts as remediation when paired with an audit of existing post-action scripts and a credential rotation.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alert on the setAPCDetails policy write that enables and populates a custom script, on cmd.exe or powershell.exe children of the ADSelfService Plus Tomcat service account, and on submitted password values carrying shell metacharacters such as '&&'.
detection.adequacy: The SYSTEM-context child process is a loud signal, but it only fires when a user next resets a password — potentially long after the implant landed — so detection catches execution and misses the plant.

response.what_would_have_worked: Rotate the default and any compromised admin credentials, strip planted post-action scripts, and treat every Active Directory credential that passed through a reset while the script was live as captured; hunt the PoC-path artefacts such as a stray C:\ProgramData\helloworld directory and outbound connections carrying harvested AD credentials.
response.adequacy: Because the SYSTEM-context script sits directly on the self-service password path, response has to assume domain-wide credential theft rather than a single-host compromise.

NIST-800-53-IA-2.gap: IA-2 governs the login exchange, which a shipped admin/admin default satisfies trivially; worse, the %password% value the control exists to protect is echoed unsanitised into a SYSTEM-context script, and that downstream use is entirely outside what IA-2 addresses.

NIS2-Art21-identity-management.gap: The obligation inverts here: the exploited product is the entity's own identity and self-service-password tool, and its default credential combined with a privileged post-action-script feature turns the identity control into the SYSTEM command-execution path rather than a defence against one.

UK-CAF-B2.gap: B2 presumes 'authorised user' is a meaningful constraint, but a vendor-shipped admin/admin password makes it trivially satisfiable, and nothing gates the custom-script feature behind stronger authentication once a session exists.

AU-Essential-8-MFA.gap: Multi-factor authentication is not enforced on the ADSelfService Plus admin role in the affected builds, so an actor holding only the default credential reached SYSTEM-context command execution with no second factor anywhere along the path.

ISO-27001-2022-A.5.15.gap: A.5.15 expects access control to be realised through identity and entitlement policy, but a vendor-default credential paired with a privileged script feature reachable immediately after login means the command-execution path opened regardless of what access-control policy the operator had written.

new_control_requirements.name: FLEET-CONTROL-PLANE-ADMIN-PRIVILEGE-TIER
new_control_requirements.description: Administrators of fleet-control-plane systems (MDM/UEM, EDR consoles, identity providers, container orchestrators, configuration management) must be classified as a distinct privilege tier above application admins, with: PAM-jumphost-only access, FIDO2 step-up per session, just-in-time elevation with approval workflow, separate identity from any other admin role, and dedicated PAW (privileged access workstation) hardware. Compliance frameworks must enumerate this tier explicitly rather than collapsing it into 'admin'.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2022-28810 needs only the shipped admin/admin credential to write an OS command into a password-policy post-action script that then runs as SYSTEM, and the affected ADSelfService Plus builds enforce no second factor on the admin role anywhere along that path. The product is the organisation's identity provider, so its administrators need per-session step-up, a separate identity and jumphost-only reachability rather than an application-admin login that a vendor default satisfies trivially.

new_control_requirements.name: PEN-TEST-SCOPE-INCLUDES-SECURITY-PRODUCTS
new_control_requirements.description: Penetration test and red-team scopes must explicitly include security-defense products (EDR, AV, DLP, identity-providers, secret-managers) as in-scope attack surface, not as defenses to evade. Scope language must call out that these products' admin interfaces, agent processes, and update channels are testable surfaces.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2022-28810 inverts the entity's own self-service password tool into the SYSTEM command-execution path: a default credential reaches setAPCDetails immediately after login, and an unsanitised %password% field executes a reset value containing '&& <command>' with only partial authentication. Testing the identity product's admin interface and its post-action-script feature as attack surface — rather than treating it as a defence — is what surfaces both routes before an intruder walks them.

attack_vector.description: A single unauthenticated GET to the Spark UI carrying a doAs parameter with backtick command substitution — /?doAs=`echo <base64> | base64 -d | bash` — reaches HttpSecurityFilter's impersonation handling, which builds a Unix group-membership shell command out of the attacker-supplied username and executes it as the Spark process user. Execution is blind, so public PoCs confirm with a timing sleep rather than returned output. The code path exists only where the non-default spark.acls.enable=true has been set.
attack_vector.privileges_required: low — PR:L, but the metric encodes a configuration precondition (spark.acls.enable=true) rather than any credential the attacker must hold; the request itself carries no authentication
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L, one GET, no race and no memory-corruption uncertainty; an Excellent-rank Metasploit module and a ProjectDiscovery Nuclei template make it point-and-shoot against any reachable Spark UI with ACLs on
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered — Kostya Kortchinsky of Databricks reported it to the Apache Spark project, and Apache fixed it on 2022-07-18 in maintenance releases 3.1.3, 3.2.2 and 3.3.0. No AI tooling credited in discovery or weaponization.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Upgrade to Spark 3.1.3, 3.2.2 or 3.3.0 or later; where an upgrade cannot be scheduled, set spark.acls.enable=false, since the injection path only exists while the ACL feature is on, and keep the master and worker UI (default 8080 / 4040) off untrusted networks.
prevention.adequacy: Adequate but late — fixed releases existed from July 2022, eight months before the KEV listing. The awkward part is the interim mitigation: it asks operators to switch off the access-control feature they had enabled for security reasons.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Log and alert on doAs= values containing backticks or shell metacharacters against the Spark UI, and on child processes under the Spark service account — crypto-miners, reverse shells — with no corresponding job submission in the cluster history.
detection.adequacy: The request signature is unmistakable in access logs, but the injection is blind: a successful run returns nothing to the attacker and raises no application-level error, so process telemetry rather than application logging is the reliable half.

response.what_would_have_worked: Rebuild or redeploy exploited Spark nodes rather than killing the injected process, rotate the credentials and data-source secrets the Spark process user could read, and review cluster job history for tasks submitted through the stolen context.
response.adequacy: Response has to assume data-plane exposure: the Spark process typically holds credentials for the data sources the cluster reads, so eviction without rotation leaves the attacker's actual prize untouched.

NIST-800-53-SI-10.gap: Input validation is the precise missing control — the doAs username is concatenated into a Unix shell invocation with no validation whatsoever — but SI-10 binds the systems the organisation builds and operates, not a shipped HttpSecurityFilter the operator has no ability to modify.

NIS2-Art21-vulnerability-management.gap: Score-driven patch cadence assumes severity tracks urgency, yet fixed releases existed from July 2022 while KEV listing came only in March 2023; a public Metasploit module and Nuclei template made every internet-reachable Spark UI with ACLs enabled trivially exploitable across that entire gap.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: The hardening advice and the vulnerable surface are the same toggle: enabling spark.acls.enable is the secure-configuration step, and it is also what opens the impersonation-to-shell path — a distinction B4's outcome-based assessment has no vocabulary for.

AU-ISM-1546.gap: Patch-application timeframes key off advisory date rather than exploit availability, so the control cannot express that a turnkey Metasploit module and a Nuclei template moved this from patchable to point-and-shoot well inside the nominal window.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.28.gap: Secure coding is the right control for a shell command built from an unvalidated impersonation username, but it governs code the organisation writes; the defect shipped inside Apache Spark, where A.8.28 offers the operator nothing to enforce.

new_control_requirements.name: CONFIGURATION-SIDE-LIVE-PATCH-INVENTORY
new_control_requirements.description: For any web-fabric vulnerability with a configuration-side mitigation path: that path must be inventoried, tested, and deployable independent of the vendor-patch path. Operators cannot wait for nginx 1.30.1+ if a named-capture refactor mitigates immediately.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2022-33891's injection path exists only while spark.acls.enable=true, so setting it to false removes the doAs-to-shell code path in one configuration change, independent of the 3.1.3 / 3.2.2 / 3.3.0 upgrade — and it is the operator's only substitute for the input validation they cannot add to a shipped HttpSecurityFilter. Because that toggle is also the hardening step, it has to be inventoried and tested in advance rather than discovered mid-incident.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2022-33891 had fixed maintenance releases from 2022-07-18 while KEV listing came only on 2023-03-07, and across that eight-month gap an Excellent-rank Metasploit module and a ProjectDiscovery Nuclei template made every reachable Spark UI with ACLs enabled point-and-shoot. A clock keyed to KEV listing and exploit availability — with network restriction of the master/worker UI as the documented compensating control — is what an advisory-date patch timeframe cannot express.

CVE-2022-35914.name: Teclib GLPI Remote Code Execution Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: An unauthenticated POST to the web-reachable /vendor/htmlawed/htmlawed/htmLawedTest.php with a body of sid=foo&hhook=exec&text=<command> reaches htmLawed's bundled test harness. The 'h'-prefixed hhook parameter maps onto htmLawed's 'hook' configuration option after the prefix is stripped, so naming a PHP callable such as exec, system or passthru runs the attacker-supplied text as an OS command under the web-server user. One request, no credential, no user interaction.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; the test harness answers unauthenticated requests because it sits under a web-served vendor/ path
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L and fully deterministic; a Metasploit module, a Nuclei template and several GitHub PoCs automate it, and EPSS near 0.997 matches the internet-wide exploitation the vendor confirmed from 2022-10-03
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered — a code-injection defect in htmLawed's test harness bundled inside GLPI's vendor tree, disclosed September 2022 and fixed in GLPI 10.0.3 / 9.5.9 alongside a coordinated htmLawed 1.2.9 release. No individual discoverer is confirmed in the primary advisories and no AI tooling is credited.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Upgrade GLPI to 10.0.3 or 9.5.9 (both released 2022-09-14). Where that cannot happen immediately, delete vendor/htmlawed/htmlawed/htmLawedTest.php — keeping the legitimate htmLawed.php — and block web access to the vendor/ directory outright.
prevention.adequacy: Either action closes the endpoint, and both were available five months before the KEV listing; neither helps a host already exploited during the mass-scanning wave that began 2022-10-03, which is where most of the damage landed.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Watch web-server access logs for any request at all to /vendor/htmlawed/htmlawed/htmLawedTest.php, particularly carrying hhook= with a callable name and a payload in text=, and for the web-server user (e.g. www-data) spawning shell processes.
detection.adequacy: The endpoint has no legitimate production use, so a single hit is a high-confidence signal — the weakness is that operators had to know to look for a file bundled by a dependency of a dependency.

response.what_would_have_worked: Assume web-shell persistence: sweep the GLPI files/ and vendor/ trees for dropped shells, rotate the database and directory credentials held in GLPI's configuration, and rebuild rather than clean any host that logged a successful hhook request before patching.
response.adequacy: GLPI holds the organisation's IT asset inventory and often its credential records, so the response scope is the inventory data itself, not just the compromised web host.

NIST-800-53-CM-7.gap: Least functionality should have stripped a test harness from a production deployment, but the harness arrived inside a third-party library's vendor/ tree that GLPI left web-reachable by default — the unnecessary function was never enumerated because it was never the operator's function to enumerate.

NIS2-Art21-network-security.gap: The system acquisition, development and maintenance obligation covers hardening what is deployed, and here an internet-facing IT-asset-management application shipped a dependency's debug script that answers unauthenticated POSTs with command execution; nothing in the obligation drives a review of bundled vendor test files.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: B4's vulnerability-management outcome assumes there is a defect to find and fix, but exploitation needs only a file that should never have been published — one unauthenticated POST with hhook=exec — and the secure-configuration outcome never enumerated removing vendor-bundled test scripts.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: The patch window is measured from advisory date, and this CVSS 9.8 unauthenticated RCE was being mass-exploited from 2022-10-03 with EPSS at near certainty; a timeframe control offers no protection during automated internet-wide exploitation that outruns any scheduled upgrade.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.9.gap: Configuration management detects drift against a documented baseline, and there was no drift here — the shipped baseline itself published htmLawedTest.php under a web-reachable vendor/ path, so the defect lives in the reference state A.8.9 presumes trustworthy.

new_control_requirements.name: TIER-3-DEPENDENCY-INVENTORY
new_control_requirements.description: Supply chain inventory must extend to tier-3 dependencies (dependencies of dependencies of direct dependencies). SBOM coverage for libsystemd-class transitive dependencies cannot be omitted under SR-3.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2022-35914 is htmLawed's bundled test harness, htmLawedTest.php, shipped inside GLPI's vendor/ tree by a dependency of a dependency and left web-reachable, where one unauthenticated POST with hhook=exec runs an OS command as the web-server user. The unnecessary function was never enumerated because it was never the operator's function to enumerate — only an inventory that reaches transitive dependencies surfaces a debug script published under a web-served path.

new_control_requirements.name: CONFIGURATION-SIDE-LIVE-PATCH-INVENTORY
new_control_requirements.description: For any web-fabric vulnerability with a configuration-side mitigation path: that path must be inventoried, tested, and deployable independent of the vendor-patch path. Operators cannot wait for nginx 1.30.1+ if a named-capture refactor mitigates immediately.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2022-35914 has a vendor-published configuration-side mitigation that closes the endpoint in minutes — delete vendor/htmlawed/htmlawed/htmLawedTest.php, keeping the legitimate htmLawed.php, and block web access to vendor/ — while the GLPI 10.0.3 / 9.5.9 upgrade is a scheduled change. During the mass-scanning wave that began 2022-10-03 that difference was the entire exposure, and the file's presence was the shipped baseline rather than drift, so the removal has to be a pre-tested deployable path.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2022-35914 carries EPSS near 0.997 with a Metasploit module, a Nuclei template and vendor-confirmed internet-wide exploitation from 2022-10-03 — five months before the 2023-03-07 KEV listing and after fixes had been available since 2022-09-14. An advisory-date patch timeframe offers nothing during automated mass exploitation; a 4-hour clock that accepts the documented file-removal mitigation does.

attack_vector.description: An unauthenticated POST to /zkau/upload carrying uuid=, sid=, dtid= and a nextURI= parameter makes the ZK AuUploader servlet forward the request to an internal URI and return files from the web context, including WEB-INF configuration and secret IDs. Against ConnectWise R1Soft Server Backup Manager, operators used the leaked secret IDs to upload a malicious JDBC database driver — dropped as {r1soft_install}/bin/mysql.jar containing Driver.class — to gain code execution on the backup server, then used the R1Soft REST API to push payloads and Lockbit ransomware to high-privilege agents on every registered downstream host.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; the AuUploader request requires no authentication and no session
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L for the base file read, a single deterministic request with no race; the escalation to fleet-wide RCE needs the follow-on JDBC-driver upload, but that path is documented in public PoCs and in NCC Group Fox-IT's forensics
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered — Markus Wulftange of Code White GmbH reported it to Potix in May 2022 with fixes released 2022-05-04; the RCE chain against R1Soft was disclosed by Huntress in October 2022 and reconstructed forensically by NCC Group Fox-IT in February 2023. No AI tooling credited.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Upgrade the ZK Framework to 9.6.2, 9.6.0.2, 9.5.1.4, 9.0.1.3 or 8.6.4.2 (released 2022-05-04) and ConnectWise R1Soft Server Backup Manager to 6.16.4 or later (2022-10-28), and stop exposing a backup manager's web interface to the internet.
prevention.adequacy: Necessary and demonstrably insufficient — Fox-IT found hundreds of servers already backdoored, so an upgrade applied over an existing implant leaves the attacker's JDBC driver, ZK filter and agent access untouched.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alert on POSTs to /zkau/upload containing nextURI=, on follow-on GETs to /zkau/jquery returning 200, on a ZK filter registered under the name fa0sifjasfjai0fja, and on the server.log line recording a successful MySQL database-driver upload.
detection.adequacy: The implant leaves unusually specific artefacts, but by the time they appear the attacker already holds command push to every registered agent — this is compromise confirmation, not prevention.

response.what_would_have_worked: Rebuild the backup manager rather than cleaning it, remove r1soft-cdp-server-mysql-driver*.jar from /tmp along with the planted mysql.jar and Driver.class, rotate every agent credential, and treat all downstream hosts carrying a registered high-privilege agent as inside the blast radius.
response.adequacy: Because the backup channel was the ransomware distribution path, response has to cover the protected estate and the recovery data itself — restoring from backups produced by a compromised manager reintroduces the compromise.

NIST-800-53-AC-6.gap: Least privilege is the control the R1Soft architecture contradicts: agents run with high privileges on every connected host, so a single unauthenticated file read on the backup server converted directly into privileged execution across the fleet — AC-6 would have bounded a blast radius the trusted-agent design deliberately maximised.

DORA-Art28.gap: Third-party risk is handled through contract, register and monitoring, none of which models a bundled Java web framework inside a concentrated backup provider yielding an unauthenticated file read that reaches every downstream financial entity's hosts; the register can be complete and current while the dependency two layers down is the failure.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: B4's system-security outcome never treated a Java framework embedded inside a backup appliance as an internet-facing pre-authentication attack surface, and the exploit needs no memory corruption and no credential — one request forwards internally and returns WEB-INF secrets.

AU-Essential-8-Backup.gap: The control presumes the backup system is a trustworthy recovery asset, but here it became the ransomware distribution channel, with Lockbit pushed through the very agents that exist to protect the estate — maturity in this control was measuring the strength of the attack path.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.13.gap: A.8.13 takes backup-system integrity as an assumption rather than something to verify, yet the compromise entered through the backup manager's own web framework and used the backup channel to reach production — the safeguard inverted into the vector that defeats recovery.

new_control_requirements.name: BACKUP-TIER-NETWORK-ISOLATION
new_control_requirements.description: Backup-orchestration appliances and backup-data destinations must be network-isolated from the data-plane networks they protect. Management surfaces must be reachable only from operator subnets; backup-data paths must use unidirectional or pull-only patterns from the backup tier to the protected systems where possible.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2022-36537 let an unauthenticated POST to /zkau/upload read WEB-INF secrets from an internet-exposed ConnectWise R1Soft Server Backup Manager; the leaked secret IDs became a malicious mysql.jar on the manager and then LockBit pushed through high-privilege agents on every registered downstream host. Restricting the management surface to operator subnets and using pull-only backup paths bounds the fleet-wide privileged reach the trusted-agent design deliberately maximised.

new_control_requirements.name: TIER-3-DEPENDENCY-INVENTORY
new_control_requirements.description: Supply chain inventory must extend to tier-3 dependencies (dependencies of dependencies of direct dependencies). SBOM coverage for libsystemd-class transitive dependencies cannot be omitted under SR-3.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2022-36537 is a defect in the ZK Framework's AuUploader servlet, a third-party Java web framework bundled two layers below the backup service named in the third-party register — so the register, its contract terms and its monitoring can be complete and current while the actual pre-authentication surface is a dependency nobody enumerated. Only inventory that reaches transitive components identifies an embedded framework as the internet-facing attack surface of a backup appliance.

new_control_requirements.name: FLEET-COMPROMISE-IR-PLAYBOOK
new_control_requirements.description: Pre-rehearsed IR playbook for fleet-control-plane compromise including: MDM-pushed certificate revocation, device-trust-state invalidation, configuration-profile audit since the suspected compromise window, downstream device-quarantine criteria, and credential rotation for any account that authenticated through a compromised fleet device during the exposure period.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2022-36537 turned the backup fleet's control plane into the ransomware distribution channel, and NCC Group Fox-IT found hundreds of managers already backdoored with a planted mysql.jar, a Driver.class and a ZK filter named fa0sifjasfjai0fja — so upgrading over an implant changes nothing. The playbook has to define agent-credential rotation, quarantine criteria for every downstream host carrying a registered high-privilege agent, and the rule that restores from a compromised manager reintroduce the compromise.

CVE-2023-0669.name: Fortra GoAnywhere MFT Remote Code Execution Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: An attacker with network reach to the GoAnywhere administrative console (default TCP 8000/8001) POSTs to /goanywhere/lic/accept with a `bundle` parameter holding a Base64, AES-encrypted serialized Java object. The AES key, IV and PBKDF2 parameters are hardcoded in the shipped LicenseEncryptor class, so the blob can be forged offline by anyone holding the JAR; LicenseResponseServlet decrypts it and hands the plaintext to ObjectInputStream.readObject() with no validation, and because commons-beanutils-1.9.4 ships in the distribution the ysoserial CommonsBeanutils1 gadget chain reaches command execution as the GoAnywhere service account.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none in practice — NVD's 7.2 vector carries PR:H from an administrative-console framing, but both NVD's description and Fortra's advisory call the flaw pre-authentication; the only real precondition is network reach to the admin console
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L and deterministic: no race window, no memory-corruption reliability tax, and the hardcoded crypto parameters let a valid `bundle` be forged entirely offline
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered — surfaced through Cl0p's in-the-wild exploitation and Fortra's incident response, with Florian Hauser independently reverse-engineering it one day before the fix shipped. No AI tooling is credited by Fortra, Rapid7 or the researcher.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Upgrade to GoAnywhere MFT 7.1.2 (released 2023-02-07) or, ahead of it, apply Fortra's interim mitigation — delete the LicenseResponseServlet servlet and servlet-mapping entries from the administrative console's web.xml so /goanywhere/lic/accept no longer routes — and keep the administrative console off untrusted networks entirely.
prevention.adequacy: Patching was necessary but arrived too late to help the victims: Cl0p had been exploiting the endpoint since 2023-01-18 and no fixed build existed until 2023-02-07. The only control with a positive defender window was keeping the admin console unreachable, or stripping the servlet by hand — neither of which is a patch.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alerting on unauthenticated POSTs to /goanywhere/lic/accept carrying a Base64 `bundle`, on the GoAnywhere Java process spawning a child shell or writing files immediately afterward, and on GoAnywhere administrative or web users appearing with no owner — Rapid7's hunting guidance singles out accounts whose creator reads `system`.
detection.adequacy: Detection is the only control that could have fired during the zero-day window, but it identifies the compromise after arbitrary code has already run as the service account; Fortra's own timeline shows accounts created and Errors.jsp plus Netcat staged within days of first access.

response.what_would_have_worked: Inventory every GoAnywhere administrative and web account against a known-good baseline for the 2023-01-28 to 2023-01-31 window, sweep for Errors.jsp and staged Netcat, treat every file stored or transited by the MFT as disclosed, and rebuild — Fortra reprovisioned its hosted MFTaaS tenants onto clean environments for exactly this reason.
response.adequacy: Response is the decisive phase because the exploit's payoff is bulk file exfiltration and Cl0p's extortion followed weeks later; a host patched without credential rotation and a data-exposure assessment remains breached in every sense that matters to the victim's customers.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: SI-2 measures time-to-patch from vendor release, and Fortra had no build to release until 2023-02-07 — three weeks after exploitation began. An organisation that installed 7.1.2 within days records a clean four-day SI-2 turnaround while its entire file store had already been enumerated through attacker-created accounts.

NIS2-Art21-network-security.gap: Art.21 network-security measures look for misconfigured exposure, but GoAnywhere's administrative listener on TCP 8000/8001 is the product's documented administration surface and the License Response Servlet answers ahead of authentication; over a thousand deployments had it internet-facing as designed, so an Art.21 assessment finds nothing to correct.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: B4 assumes the operator can interpose something between attacker-supplied data and a parser. Nothing in a GoAnywhere deployment constrains an in-process Java deserialization gadget executing inside the application's own JVM with commons-beanutils already on the classpath — no host hardening, service-account restriction or B4 evidence artefact changes the outcome.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: The 48-hour internet-facing patch target starts when a vendor ships, and during the exploited window there was nothing to ship. The control that actually worked — hand-editing web.xml to remove a servlet mapping inside a third-party product — is not scored at any Essential Eight maturity level.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.22.gap: Segregation of networks would have removed the attack path outright, but it is evidenced at corporate-LAN and DMZ boundaries rather than at the management interface of a file-transfer appliance; certified organisations kept /goanywhere/ answering anonymous internet clients with a fully conformant statement of applicability.

new_control_requirements.name: PERIMETER-DEVICE-ZERODAY-SLA-TIER
new_control_requirements.description: Compliance frameworks must define a distinct patch SLA tier for pre-auth RCE on perimeter-trust-boundary devices (firewalls, VPN concentrators, WAFs, edge load-balancers). Tier requirement: vendor-mitigation deployed within 4 hours of KEV listing OR isolation of the vulnerable interface; standard 14/30-day SLAs do not apply because the device IS the trust boundary.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2023-0669 was exploited by Cl0p from 2023-01-18 against GoAnywhere administrative consoles published to the internet on TCP 8000/8001, and no fixed build existed until 2023-02-07 — so for three weeks the only control with a positive defender window was isolating the vulnerable interface, exactly the alternative this tier permits. A.8.22 segregation is evidenced at corporate-LAN and DMZ boundaries, never at the management port of a file-transfer appliance that sits on the data trust boundary.

new_control_requirements.name: MITIGATION-ACTIVE-PATCH-PENDING-VERDICT-CLASS
new_control_requirements.description: Compliance verdicts must distinguish three states: (a) binary patch deployed (vulnerability eliminated), (b) vendor-mitigation rule active, no binary patch (residual risk: any defect in the mitigation rule reopens the vulnerability), (c) no mitigation, no patch (full exposure). Audit reports must surface (b) as a distinct compensating-control state with an associated time-bound action item, not as a 'patched per SLA' outcome.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2023-0669's only pre-patch remediation was Fortra's interim instruction to delete the LicenseResponseServlet servlet and servlet-mapping from the administrative console's web.xml — a mitigation that strips the /goanywhere/lic/accept deserialization sink without changing any version string, so neither a scanner nor an SI-2 report can distinguish it from an unremediated host. That state needs its own audit verdict with a time-bound upgrade action rather than a pass or fail against a patch SLA that had nothing to measure.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2023-0669 was KEV-listed on 2023-02-10 with confirmed Cl0p ransomware use, three days after 7.1.2 shipped; because SI-2 measures time-to-patch from vendor release, an organisation that installed 7.1.2 within days books a clean four-day turnaround while its entire file store had already been enumerated through accounts the actor created between 2023-01-28 and 2023-01-31. A KEV-triggered deadline is what makes the listing itself, not the vendor's release date, the start of the clock.

attack_vector.description: An unauthenticated multipart POST to /OA_HTML/BneViewerXMLService, BneDownloadService, BneOfflineLOVService or BneUploaderService carrying bne:uueupload=true. All four servlets inherit from BneAbstractXMLServlet and require no session, so a .uue-suffixed upload is uudecoded and unzipped by BneUnZip, which concatenates the staging directory with the ZIP entry name without validation — an entry named ../../../../../ escapes the staging path. Published payload routes either overwrite the Perl CGI txkFNDWRR.pl and fire it via /OA_CGI/FNDWRR.exe, or write a JSP under the forms directory and invoke it as /forms/<name>.jsp?cmd=<command>.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; no session, token or credential, only HTTP reach to /OA_HTML/
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L, a single unauthenticated POST with no race and no memory-corruption tax; the only variable is the absolute traversal target, since both published payload routes assume the default /u01/install/APPS/fs1 APPL_TOP layout and a non-standard install directory forces the attacker to fingerprint first
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered — reported through Oracle's vulnerability-handling process by a researcher credited as @l1k3beef in the October 2022 Critical Patch Update, with root-cause analysis published later by Viettel Cyber Security and extended by Rapid7. Manual analysis of a Java servlet's upload and unzip path; no AI involvement claimed by any party.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Apply the Oracle Critical Patch Update of October 2022 (or any later cumulative CPU) to EBS 12.2.3 through 12.2.11; where the adop cutover cannot be scheduled immediately, deny unauthenticated requests carrying bne:uueupload to /OA_HTML/Bne*Service at the reverse proxy or WAF and disable the WebADI upload entry points.
prevention.adequacy: The fix existed from 2022-10-18, so prevention was achievable — but only for organisations willing to break the quarterly ERP change cadence, and the KEV listing landed roughly four months later. Patching also does not remove a Perl or JSP shell already written outside the staging directory, so txkFNDWRR.pl must be restored from a known-good source and the forms directory swept.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alert on unauthenticated multipart POSTs to the four Bne*Service endpoints carrying bne:uueupload, on .uue files appearing in the WebADI staging directory with no matching legitimate activity, on a recently-modified txkFNDWRR.pl, and on the EBS application tier initiating curl or wget to an external address — Rapid7 observed the dropped Perl shell fetching a second stage that enrolled the host in a botnet.
detection.adequacy: These signatures are precise but fire at or after the file write; by the time outbound curl from the application tier is visible the attacker already holds command execution on the ERP server. Absence of a successful exploit in logs is also not evidence of a patched host, since mass-scan attempts fail against non-default install paths.

response.what_would_have_worked: Restore txkFNDWRR.pl from a known-good source, remove unexpected .jsp files under the forms directory, rotate database and application credentials reachable from the EBS tier, and scope which financial and HR data the instance serves.
response.adequacy: Necessary because remediation-by-CPU leaves any already-written shell in place; the compromised component is the ERP application tier, so scoping the data exposure is a materially larger exercise than evicting the webshell.

NIST-800-53-AC-3.gap: There is no authenticated subject for AC-3 to evaluate. The Bne* servlets accept the multipart upload with no session at all, so an EBS deployment with fully modelled roles and segregation of duties still hands an anonymous HTTP client an arbitrary file write; every AC-3 artefact for this system describes what authenticated users may do, and this exploit never creates one.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: Oracle ships EBS fixes only inside quarterly, downtime-bearing adop bundles that change boards schedule against a business calendar. A patch programme entirely conformant with Art.21 for a quarterly-CPU vendor still left months between the October 2022 fix and the February 2023 KEV listing on an unauthenticated file-write endpoint.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: The failure lives in closed-source vendor extraction code — BneUnZip joining the staging path to an attacker-chosen ZIP entry name. No configuration setting, host hardening measure or B4 evidence artefact available to the EBS operator controls where the extracted file lands; only the CPU or a proxy-level block on the upload parameter does.

AU-ISM-1546.gap: ISM 1546 keys off vendor patch availability and treats an internet-facing ERP servlet the same as an internal batch component, so a legitimate compliance record shows the CPU scheduled for the next quarterly maintenance window while an unauthenticated arbitrary file write to the application tier stays live and, by February 2023, exploited.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.28.gap: Secure coding is exactly the control this defect violates and exactly the one an EBS operator cannot evidence, because the vulnerable servlet is Oracle's. The certified organisation carries A.8.28 in its statement of applicability, cannot test it against the component, and cannot exercise it against this CVE.

new_control_requirements.name: ENTERPRISE-ERP-MANAGEMENT-FUNCTION-AUTHENTICATION
new_control_requirements.description: An enterprise ERP platform (Oracle PeopleSoft, Oracle E-Business Suite, SAP, and similar) must authenticate every management-plane and environment-management function before it can be invoked, and must not expose any takeover-capable function to an unauthenticated network caller. Segment the ERP management surface from untrusted networks and place it behind authenticated access control. The distinguishing test: send an unauthenticated network request to each environment-management / configuration endpoint on a staging instance and confirm it is refused before any privileged action runs - paper 'ERP access control' policies that attest user-login authentication while leaving a critical management function reachable without credentials still permit unauthenticated takeover.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2022-21587 lets an unauthenticated multipart POST to /OA_HTML/BneUploaderService and its three sibling Bne*Service servlets on Oracle E-Business Suite 12.2.3-12.2.11 write a file anywhere the application tier can reach, because all four inherit from BneAbstractXMLServlet and require no session, token or credential. AC-3 has no authenticated subject to evaluate here, so an EBS deployment with fully modelled roles and segregation of duties still hands an anonymous HTTP client an arbitrary file write on the ERP tier.

CVE-2023-22952.name: Multiple SugarCRM Products Remote Code Execution Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: The attacker sends a login request to /index.php; loadUser() in include/MVC/SugarApplication.php does not destroy the session after the failed authentication, so subsequent requests are honoured as though authenticated. Using that session the attacker POSTs a PNG file with a PHP payload appended to /index.php?module=EmailTemplates&action=AttachFiles; the attachment handler validates nothing, the file lands under /cache/images/, and fetching it back over HTTP executes the embedded PHP as the web service user, typically www-data.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none in practice — NVD scores PR:L for the code-injection primitive alone, but the published exploit chains the loadUser() session-handling defect in front of it, so the real requirement is network access to /index.php
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L, two requests and a fetch, with no race and no memory corruption; the one conditional step is whether the web server routes the dropped extension to PHP, which is why Censys counted 3,059 exposed instances but only 354 carrying the webshell
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered — released as a complete working zero-day exploit by an anonymous researcher using the handle sw33t.0day on the Full Disclosure list on 2022-12-30, ahead of any vendor process. No AI-assisted discovery or exploit generation is claimed by the author, SugarCRM, Censys or Unit 42.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Apply hotfix 91155 or its 11.0 equivalent, or upgrade to SugarCRM 11.0.5 / 12.0.2, and independently configure the web server to refuse PHP execution under /cache/ so an uploaded image can never be interpreted as code.
prevention.adequacy: The vendor hotfix landed 2023-01-05, six days after a complete public exploit, so for most on-premise operators mass webshell installation preceded the patch. The web-server configuration control is the one that would have held through the gap, and no framework asked for it.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alert on a failed login that is not followed by session teardown, on POSTs to module=EmailTemplates&action=AttachFiles, and on the PHP interpreter executing anything under /cache/images/; downstream, on a CRM host making AWS control-plane calls such as GetCallerIdentity, Organizations ListAccounts, DescribeOrganization or GetCostAndUsage.
detection.adequacy: Monitoring was nominally required and structurally blind here: stage one looks like an ordinary authenticated POST followed by an image fetch, and stage two is legitimate AWS API traffic authenticated with stolen long-term keys. Only a rule specific to PHP execution inside a cache directory separates it from normal use.

response.what_would_have_worked: Sweep /cache/images/ for image files containing PHP tags, rotate every AWS access key, database credential and instance-role token readable from the host, and review the AWS account for the follow-on activity Unit 42 documented — RDS snapshot creation, security-group modification, AMI creation, imported SSH key pairs and EC2 launches in non-standard regions.
response.adequacy: Response rather than patching is what ends this incident: Censys still counted 354 hosts carrying the webshell on the day the fixed releases shipped, and the documented monetisation path runs entirely through cloud credentials harvested from the compromised host.

NIST-800-53-SI-10.gap: SI-10 names this defect exactly — a file declared PNG whose content is PHP — yet it is assessed at design level for systems the organisation builds, not for a purchased CRM whose upload handler cannot be inspected or modified. The operator's only SI-10-adjacent lever was denying PHP execution under /cache/images/, which no SI-10 assessment of a bought application asks about.

NIS2-Art21-incident-handling.gap: The Art.21 clock assumes detection follows disclosure. Here the complete exploit was public on 2022-12-30 and hosts were compromised within days, so a conformant handling process produced a 24-hour significant-incident obligation whose triggering event predated the organisation's ability to learn about it.

UK-CAF-B2.gap: Identity control was defeated inside the application: loadUser() left the session alive through a failed login, so the CRM itself vouched for an identity that never authenticated. SSO, MFA and privileged-access management — the artefacts a B2 assessment actually collects — all sit in front of that code path, so B2 maturity buys no reduction in exploitability.

AU-Essential-8-App-Hardening.gap: User application hardening is scoped to browsers, Office macros, PDF readers and web-content handlers on workstations. It says nothing about a server-side PHP interpreter executing a file dropped into an application cache directory, and the single configuration change that would have contained this exploit sits outside every Essential Eight control at every maturity level.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.16.gap: Monitoring evidence for A.8.16 is typically failed-login spikes, malware signatures and known-bad IPs. Neither stage of this attack registers against that set — an authenticated-looking POST then an image fetch, then legitimate AWS API calls with stolen keys — so a conformant programme detects neither the compromise nor the cloud-account lateral movement that follows.

new_control_requirements.name: ECOMMERCE-PLATFORM-EXTENSION-UNTRUSTED-DESERIALIZATION-GUARD
new_control_requirements.description: An e-commerce platform (Magento / Adobe Commerce and similar) and every third-party extension it loads must never pass request-supplied data (cookies, headers, body, query parameters) to a native deserialization function (PHP unserialize(), and equivalents in other runtimes) on an unauthenticated storefront request path. Patch-management and secure-coding programs must enumerate every installed extension as part of the storefront's code-execution surface, not only the core platform. The distinguishing test: send an unauthenticated storefront request carrying a crafted serialized object in each cookie / header an extension reads, on a staging store, and confirm it is rejected before any deserialization runs - paper 'platform patched' attestations that ignore the installed extensions still permit unauthenticated RCE through an extension's object-injection sink.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2023-22952 carries a PNG with appended PHP through SugarCRM's module=EmailTemplates&action=AttachFiles handler onto /cache/images/ and executes it as www-data on refetch — request-supplied content reaching an in-process code-execution sink in a purchased PHP business platform, on a path the loadUser() session-handling defect makes effectively unauthenticated. SI-10 is assessed at design level for systems the organisation builds, so only a programme that enumerates the bought platform's whole request-handling surface as code-execution surface — rather than attesting 'platform patched' — reaches this upload handler.

CVE-2017-11357.name: Telerik UI for ASP.NET AJAX Insecure Direct Object Reference Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: An attacker POSTs to /Telerik.Web.UI.WebResource.axd?type=rau with a rauPostData configuration blob encrypted under the RadAsyncUpload keys — hardcoded shipped defaults on builds up to 2017.2.621, otherwise recovered from web.config. The blob's TempTargetFolder value is the insecure direct object reference: the handler writes the uploaded file wherever the IIS worker process can write instead of the intended temporary location, producing an .aspx web shell or a staged DLL. The same recovered key material is what makes the chained CVE-2019-18935 deserialization RCE reachable, which is why CISA AA23-074A and ACSC Advisory 2020-004 both treat key knowledge as the gating factor.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; the handler answers unauthenticated requests, and the only real gate is knowledge of the RadAsyncUpload encryption keys, which are shipped defaults on affected builds
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L on vulnerable builds, where EDB-43874 and the RAU_crypto tool automate the whole flow; the durable difficulty sits on the defender's side, because the vulnerable assembly is a DLL inside someone else's application rather than a named product
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered — Paul Taylor of Foregenix reverse-engineered the .NET upload handler and its AES key derivation in 2017 and published both the analysis and the RAU_crypto tooling. No AI involvement is claimed by the researcher or the vendor, and no such workflow existed for this class of work at the time.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Upgrade Telerik UI for ASP.NET AJAX to R1 2020 (2020.1.114) or later — not merely to the 2017 service packs, which leave the chained CVE-2019-18935 path open — or, where an application rebuild cannot be scheduled, set a per-deployment RadAsyncUpload encryption key, set Telerik.Web.DisableAsyncUploadHandler to true in web.config, and supply a custom upload handler.
prevention.adequacy: A fix has existed since June 2017 and the exposure survives anyway, because prevention here depends on finding the assembly rather than installing the update: CISA located a vulnerable Telerik.Web.UI.dll at a federal agency in a file path the organisation's own vulnerability scanner did not cover. Inventory has to run on DLL file version, not application name.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alert on POSTs to /Telerik.Web.UI.WebResource.axd with type=rau — AA23-074A records two IIS events with identical timestamps per exploitation, one returning 200 and one 302 — on w3wp.exe writing to or executing from C:\Windows\Temp, and on .NET stack traces naming Telerik.Web.UI.AsyncUploadHandler.GetConfiguration, EnsureSetup or ProcessRequest, which is what a failed or key-guessing attempt looks like.
detection.adequacy: The IIS-log signature is strong but only exists where handler requests are logged and reviewed; the actor's cleanup malware deletes the epoch-named DLLs from C:\Windows\Temp, so the file-level indicator decays while the log-level one persists.

response.what_would_have_worked: Rotate the RadAsyncUpload encryption keys and machine keys, remove epoch-named [10 digits].[7 digits].dll artefacts and PNG-masquerading DLLs from the upload and temp directories, hunt for a base64 small.txt decoded to an ASPX web shell small.aspx, and rebuild the IIS host where execution is confirmed.
response.adequacy: Key rotation is the part that matters beyond eviction: both CISA and the ASD treat knowledge of the upload keys, not the upload bug, as the precondition for the chained CVE-2019-18935 RCE, so an unrotated key leaves the follow-on path open even after the assembly is upgraded.

NIST-800-53-CM-7.gap: Least functionality would have removed the primitive — most applications that link Telerik UI never use RadAsyncUpload — but CM-7 baselines enumerate operating-system roles, installed packages and server features, not individual third-party ASP.NET HTTP handlers registered in an application's web.config. The vendor's own DisableAsyncUploadHandler switch is not something a CM-7 baseline knows to assert.

NIS2-Art21-supply-chain.gap: Art.21 supply-chain measures operate through supplier relationships, and for most affected entities Telerik is not a supplier — the assembly is vendored inside a purchased or bespoke ASP.NET application, frequently without the operator ever encountering the name. No questionnaire, contract clause or due-diligence artefact surfaces a DLL sitting in a path the scanner does not enumerate.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: B4 presumes an asset inventory that resolves to named, patchable products, while the exposure is a build number embedded in someone else's web application — CISA's actual finding was Telerik UI 2013.2.717 on an agency IIS server. A B4 assessment confirming that every internet-facing system is patched and supported passes cleanly while /Telerik.Web.UI.WebResource.axd keeps answering.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Nine years of patch availability did not close this, because the control has no answer for a component whose version is invisible to the application-level inventory the maturity model assumes. That the ASD had to publish Advisory 2020-004 instructing operators to recover and rotate RadAsyncUpload keys is itself the evidence that patch-timeliness maturity did not address the exposure.

ISO-27001-2022-A.5.7.gap: Threat intelligence should have caught a 2017 CVE with a 2018 public exploit, a 2023 KEV listing and a 2023 CISA advisory, but A.5.7 programmes match advisories keyed by product name against an asset register. 'Telerik UI for ASP.NET AJAX' appears in almost no asset register because it is a control library inside another application, so a fully conformant process consumes AA23-074A, finds no matching asset and closes the item.

new_control_requirements.name: FRAMEWORK-DEFAULT-SECRET-DETECTION
new_control_requirements.description: Deployment gating that fails any release shipping or running an unrotated framework default cryptographic secret (APP_KEY / SECRET_KEY and equivalents), which turn a leaked constant into unauthenticated deserialization RCE.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2017-11357 is gated entirely on the RadAsyncUpload encryption keys, which shipped as hardcoded defaults on Telerik UI builds up to 2017.2.621; Progress's own interim mitigation is to set a per-deployment key, and both CISA AA23-074A and ACSC Advisory 2020-004 treat knowledge of that constant as the precondition for the chained CVE-2019-18935 deserialization RCE. A CM-7 baseline that enumerates operating-system roles, installed packages and server features never asserts that a shipped default upload key was rotated.

new_control_requirements.name: TIER-3-DEPENDENCY-INVENTORY
new_control_requirements.description: Supply chain inventory must extend to tier-3 dependencies (dependencies of dependencies of direct dependencies). SBOM coverage for libsystemd-class transitive dependencies cannot be omitted under SR-3.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2017-11357 lives in Telerik.Web.UI.dll vendored inside someone else's ASP.NET application — CISA found build 2013.2.717 on a federal agency IIS server in a file path the agency's own scanner did not enumerate — so Progress is not the operator's supplier of record and no NIS2 Art.21 questionnaire, contract clause or due-diligence artefact surfaces the assembly. Only inventory that descends past the named product to component build numbers finds it.

CVE-2022-47966.name: Zoho ManageEngine Multiple Products Remote Code Execution Vulnerability (CVE-2022-47966)

attack_vector.description: An unauthenticated HTTP POST of a crafted SAML response to the product's SSO assertion-consumer endpoint. The bundled Apache Santuario (xmlsec) 1.4.1 leaves XSLT-transform restrictions to the calling application by design and the ManageEngine products never imposed them, so a <ds:Transform> carrying an XSLT stylesheet is evaluated during signature verification — before any assertion is trusted. XSLT extension functions then instantiate Java classes, yielding code execution as the ManageEngine service account, which is SYSTEM on Windows installations.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; the XSLT executes during signature verification, ahead of any authentication decision. The only precondition is that SAML SSO is currently configured (16 products) or was ever configured at any point in the past (8 products, including ServiceDesk Plus and ADSelfService Plus)
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L: one HTTP POST, no authentication state to establish, no memory corruption and no race window; the sole exception is the ADSelfService Plus path, which needs two target-specific values recovered before the public PoC fires
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered — reported through the ManageEngine bug-bounty programme by Khoadha of Viettel Cyber Security and independently reproduced from the patch diff (bundled xmlsec 1.4.1 moving to 2.2.3) by Horizon3.ai. No AI-assisted discovery, patch-diffing or exploit generation is claimed by Zoho, Viettel, Horizon3.ai, Rapid7 or Cisco Talos.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Upgrade every affected ManageEngine product to its own fixed build — the vendor advisory lists all 24, released 2022-10-27 through 2022-11-07 — because the fix is the replacement of bundled xmlsec 1.4.1 with 2.2.3. For the eight products exploitable if SAML SSO was EVER configured, turning SSO off is not a mitigation; only the upgrade is.
prevention.adequacy: Fixes were available two to three months before the KEV listing, so prevention was achievable — but it required a per-product build inventory rather than a product-family patch decision, and the ever-configured-SSO clause means an operator who 'reduced attack surface' by decommissioning SSO stayed fully exploitable.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alert on unauthenticated POSTs of base64 SAMLResponse data to ManageEngine SSO endpoints, on the ManageEngine Java runtime spawning cmd.exe or powershell.exe as SYSTEM, on an encoded payload written to ..\webapps\ROOT\scripts\ae_commons.js and decoded to ..\custom\login\commons.jsp, and on tunneling tooling — renamed plink, the Chisel SOCKS tunneler, svhost.exe and ekern.exe forwarding 3389.
detection.adequacy: The web-shell and tunneling indicators are concrete but strictly post-execution; the exploiting request is a well-formed SAML POST to an endpoint that legitimately receives them, so detection here depends on outcome behaviour rather than on request inspection.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treat an exploited host as a compromise of everything it administers: rotate every credential held in Password Manager Pro, PAM 360 and Key Manager Plus, reset the Active Directory accounts these products manage, review Endpoint Central and Patch Manager Plus deployment queues for attacker-staged packages, and hunt for QuiteRAT (notify.exe / acres.exe) and Monero miners on the server.
response.adequacy: This is the only phase proportional to the blast radius. The affected estate is the security tooling itself, so patching the product without rotating what it stores leaves the attacker holding the organisation's credentials and a trusted software-deployment channel.

NIST-800-53-SR-3.gap: SR-3 evidences supply-chain process against named suppliers, and Zoho is the supplier of record — but the defect is a decade-stale Apache Santuario xmlsec 1.4.1 carried unchanged inside 24 products at once. No SR-3 artefact for the ManageEngine relationship can surface a bundled XML-signature library, and no SBOM obligation attached to these products at the time, so the control produced assurance about the vendor rather than visibility into what the vendor shipped.

NIS2-Art21-supply-chain.gap: The operator cannot act on this dependency: xmlsec 1.4.1 is statically bundled in each product, invisible to the operator's own dependency scanning and replaceable only by the vendor's upgrade pack. Art.21 conformance yields a questionnaire and a contract clause, and the signal that mattered — the same stale library present in 24 products simultaneously — is exactly what per-supplier assessment cannot see.
