CVE-2022-2856.name: Google Chromium Intents Insufficient Input Validation Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: A crafted HTML page passes unvalidated input into Chrome's Intent handling, and the browser navigates to an attacker-chosen destination without a click or a confirmation. Nothing is disclosed and nothing is disrupted — C:N and A:N — the integrity that falls is the browser's decision about where to go, which makes this a delivery primitive whose severity is inherited from whatever it lands on: a second-stage exploit page or a credential-harvest host. In telemetry it appears as the hop before the payload rather than as the payload.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; UI:R means only that the user opens a page the attacker controls or can inject into
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; nothing is groomed or raced, only a page served. The hard part is scoping rather than exploitation: NVD's description names Chrome on Android while its CPE set covers Windows, macOS, Linux and Android, and CISA notes the affected code reaches Edge, Opera and other Chromium browsers.
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered — Google Threat Analysis Group's Ashley Shen and Christian Resell reported it on 2022-07-19 from hunting live intrusions, and Google stated an exploit already existed in the wild. Chrome's coverage-guided fuzzing infrastructure is credited separately in the same release post; this CVE is not among those findings, and no source attributes the exploit's construction to AI tooling either.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Update to Chrome stable 104.0.5112.101 (Mac, Linux) or 104.0.5112.102/101 (Windows), released 2022-08-16, and update every Chromium downstream on its own release line — Microsoft Edge 104.0.1293.47, plus Opera and other Chromium-derived browsers per the CISA KEV note, and the Fedora 37 chromium rebuild. There is no configuration workaround: Intent handling cannot be disabled by enterprise policy, and the fix does not take effect until every browser window closes.
prevention.adequacy: Patching works; the inventory does not. An estate keyed on the Chrome version string alone under-reports the exposed population by every Edge, Opera and Chromium-derived install it runs, and the Android half of that population frequently sits on personally-owned handsets the organisation cannot force to update. Google had known of in-the-wild exploitation since 2022-07-19, so the exposure window opened well before any operator could act on it.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Browser history or proxy logs showing an intent:// or scheme-handler navigation from a page the user did open to a host the user never selected, with no intervening click event — the observable is a page transition nobody initiated, typically landing on a second-stage exploit or credential-harvest host.
detection.adequacy: The signal exists in proxy telemetry but is easy to lose in ordinary redirect noise, and on the Android population most likely to be affected there is usually no proxy or browser-history collection at all.

response.what_would_have_worked: Chase the destination rather than the browser: identify what the forced navigation delivered, treat any host that reached a second-stage exploit page as potentially compromised, and read Google TAG involvement as a targeting signal — TAG hunts government-backed operators and commercial surveillance vendors, so a 2022 encounter pointed at targeted intrusion sets rather than commodity crimeware.
response.adequacy: Response only works if the hop was recorded, and because this primitive causes no compromise of its own it produces nothing to investigate until the next stage does.

NIST-800-53-SI-10.gap: Input validation is the failing control, but the failure executes inside a vendor binary the operator cannot inspect, configure or instrument. SI-10 is written for systems the organisation develops or configures; when the failing check lives in a third-party browser's scheme dispatcher, the compliant answer is 'inherited from the vendor' — precisely the position that offered no protection between the vendor learning of the flaw and shipping the fix.

NIS2-Art21-network-security.gap: Art.21 measures apply to the network and information systems the entity uses, and a large share of the affected population is outside that boundary — Chrome on personally owned Android handsets reaching corporate services through a browser. The entity carries the consequence of a forced navigation while the vulnerable component sits on a device it does not own and cannot force to update: the obligation and the remediation authority are held by different parties.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: B4 treats the browser as a hardened client, but the boundary this breaks is the Intent dispatcher arbitrating between a web origin and an OS-level navigation, and no B4 configuration control — managed policy baseline, extension allowlist, download restriction, enterprise proxy — changes its input validation. An outcome rated achieved describes hardening this path never had to pass through.

AU-ISM-1546.gap: ISM-1546 is scoped to applications in the Standard Operating Environment, so Chrome on a personally owned handset is neither measured nor compelled. For the desktop estate the exploited-vulnerability window starts at the KEV listing, while the vendor had known of in-the-wild use for a month before that — compliance was achievable throughout the exposure window without shortening it by a day.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.9.gap: This CVE has no configuration expression at all: Intent handling cannot be disabled, restricted or policy-gated by an administrator. A fully enforced hardened-Chrome baseline — policies applied, drift monitored, deviations remediated — leaves the vulnerable code path identically reachable, because the control's entire mechanism is settings management and the defect ships the same way at every setting.

new_control_requirements.name: BROWSER-MANAGED-UPDATE-NO-DEFERRAL
new_control_requirements.description: Enterprise update rings must not defer security-channel browser updates beyond 24h.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2022-2856 cannot be policy-gated at all — Chrome's Intent handling cannot be disabled or restricted by enterprise policy, and the fix does not take effect until every browser window closes — so a fully enforced hardened-Chrome baseline leaves the dispatcher identically reachable and only the move to 104.0.5112.101/102 removes it. Any update ring that defers the security channel extends a window Google already knew was being exploited.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2022-2856 was reported by Google TAG on 2022-07-19 with an exploit already in the wild, fixed on 2022-08-16 and KEV-listed 2022-08-18, and CISA's note records that the same Chromium defect reaches Edge, Opera and other derivatives — so a routine application-patch cycle scoped to the Chrome version string moved neither fast enough nor across the whole exposed population, while a 4-hour KEV-triggered mitigation deadline compresses the remaining window to hours.

CVE-2022-26923.name: Microsoft Active Directory Domain Services Privilege Escalation Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: An ordinary domain user creates a computer account under the default ms-DS-MachineAccountQuota of 10, clears the servicePrincipalName entries carrying its own hostname, and rewrites dNSHostName to a domain controller's DNS name — dNSHostName carries no uniqueness constraint where SPN does, and that asymmetry is the entire defect. Enrolling the account against the default Machine template makes the enterprise CA honour CT_FLAG_SUBJECT_ALT_REQUIRE_DNS and issue a legitimately signed certificate bearing the spoofed name; PKINIT with that certificate makes the KDC map it to the domain controller machine account and return its TGT and NT hash, after which DCSync completes the domain takeover. No exploit payload appears anywhere in the chain — every step is a legitimate LDAP write or certificate request.
attack_vector.privileges_required: low — PR:L; one ordinary authenticated domain user with no special rights and no delegated permissions
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L, and honestly so: no race, no grooming, no memory corruption. Public tooling reduces it to a handful of commands and every prerequisite ships at its default value, so the 8.8 base understates it — the vendor rated it Critical because the CVSS scope metric cannot express 'any domain user becomes domain admin'.
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered — Oliver Lyak of Institut For Cyber Risk, reporting through Trend Micro ZDI, found it by reading how the KDC maps a certificate to a principal. Certipy and the Metasploit module are conventional hand-written tooling; no AI assistance is reported for discovery or weaponisation.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Install the 2022-05-10 updates on every domain controller and member system, then finish the job the update leaves open: set StrongCertificateBindingEnforcement to 2 (Full Enforcement), because the update defaults to 1 (Compatibility), which logs KDC events 39/41 and permits the authentication anyway. Alongside that, drop ms-DS-MachineAccountQuota from its default of 10 to 0 and audit GenericWrite over computer objects — post-patch, any principal holding it can still rewrite dNSHostName.
prevention.adequacy: 'Patched' meant 'auditing' for close to three years. The phased enforcement plan slipped repeatedly, Disabled mode was only removed in April 2023, and devices without an explicit registry setting only reached Full Enforcement on 2025-02-11 — so an estate that applied the May 2022 update and never touched the key was compliant, logging the forged bindings, and still exploitable throughout.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Event 4741 (computer account created) by a non-administrative user followed by 4742 setting dNSHostName to a value matching an existing domain controller and removing SPNs on the same object; certificates issued without the szOID_NTDS_CA_SECURITY_EXT SID extension (OID 1.3.6.1.4.1.311.25.2) or templates carrying CT_FLAG_NO_SECURITY_EXTENSION; KDC events 39/41 and 40/48 indicating Compatibility mode; and a certificate request from a freshly created machine account followed within minutes by a DRSGetNCChanges replication request from that same account.
detection.adequacy: The detections are precise and cheap to build, but they fire on a chain that completes in minutes and whose every individual step is legitimate directory and PKI activity, so a pipeline tuned for suspicious binaries or anomalous logons sees nothing worth escalating until the DCSync at the end.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treat it as full domain compromise: rotate krbtgt twice, reset domain controller machine accounts and every privileged credential, revoke certificates issued from the Machine template during the exposure window, delete attacker-created computer objects, and enable Full Enforcement before returning the estate to service.
response.adequacy: Recovery is well understood but expensive, and the certificate dimension is the part most incident plans miss — a certificate issued during the window remains a usable credential until it is revoked and strong binding is enforced, regardless of how many passwords were reset.

NIST-800-53-AC-6.gap: Least privilege is assessed against privileges the organisation grants deliberately, and the privilege that makes this work is one nobody granted: the machine-account quota ships at 10, so every authenticated user can create computer objects and automatically holds validated-write over the new object's dNSHostName. A review of group memberships, admin tiers and delegated OU rights finds nothing wrong, because the excess privilege is a schema-level default attached to Authenticated Users.

NIS2-Art21-identity-management.gap: Identity and access management assumes the identity assertion is the control point. The attacker never defeats an authentication decision — the CA issues a valid certificate and the KDC correctly maps it to the principal the certificate names; the failure is that the name was attacker-chosen. Account lifecycle, PAM and credential hygiene sit nowhere between account creation and issuance, and the resulting session behaves exactly as that machine account is entitled to.

UK-CAF-B2.gap: Every verification step in the chain succeeds legitimately: the attacker authenticates as a real user to create the account, the CA validates the enrolment against a template the account may use, and the KDC validates a properly signed certificate. B2 has no outcome asking whether an unprivileged principal can name itself after a domain controller in an attribute that lacks a uniqueness constraint.

AU-Essential-8-MFA.gap: The mitigation strategy counts certificate-based authentication as a strong factor, and here that mechanism is the abused one rather than the defence. An organisation at Maturity Level Three has by construction deployed the AD CS infrastructure the attack requires, so higher MFA maturity corresponds to a larger attack surface — and no MFA prompt occurs anywhere in the escalation path.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.24.gap: Cryptography was correct throughout: sound algorithms, a properly signed certificate with a valid chain and lifetime, and faithful signature validation by the KDC. The defect is a binding failure between a cryptographic identity and a directory identity, because before the SID extension existed nothing cryptographic tied the certificate to the requester's objectSid. An audit of key lengths, HSM protection, CA hardening and revocation passes cleanly on an infrastructure one enrolment away from issuing domain-admin-equivalent credentials.

new_control_requirements.name: CLOUD-CONTROL-PLANE-CROSS-TENANT-CLAIM-VALIDATION
new_control_requirements.description: IdPs must validate originating-tenant claim on every cross-tenant token-bearing call and log it to a tenant-immutable channel. Customers must monitor for impossible-actor patterns.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2022-26923 never defeats an authentication decision: the enterprise CA signs a valid certificate and the KDC faithfully maps it to the principal the certificate names, but before the szOID_NTDS_CA_SECURITY_EXT extension (OID 1.3.6.1.4.1.311.25.2) existed nothing bound that name to the requester's objectSid, so an ordinary user's freshly created machine account authenticated as a domain controller. Validating the originating-identity claim at issuance and at PKINIT, plus alerting on the impossible-actor pattern of a minutes-old machine account issuing DRSGetNCChanges, is the only control anywhere in the chain.

new_control_requirements.name: SCANNER-PAPER-COMPLIANCE-TEST
new_control_requirements.description: A vulnerability scanner that reports 'patched' based on kernel package version alone is paper compliance. The operational test: does the scan account for the module-unload mitigation surface, AND does it verify the kernel is on a build that includes the specific Fragnesia patch (not just any version newer than the Dirty Frag patch that introduced Fragnesia)?
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2022-26923's 2022-05-10 update leaves StrongCertificateBindingEnforcement at 1 (Compatibility), which logs KDC events 39/41 and permits the forged binding anyway, and devices without an explicit registry setting only reached Full Enforcement on 2025-02-11. A patch-level check therefore reported the domain remediated for nearly three years while an ordinary user could still take it over, so the operational test has to verify the enforcement value and the ms-DS-MachineAccountQuota setting, not the KB build.

CVE-2022-21971.name: Microsoft Windows Runtime Remote Code Execution Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: A crafted RTF opened in Microsoft Word, WordPad or Office Word 2019 causes the Windows Runtime WapAuthProvider class in prauthproviders.dll to be instantiated; WapAuthProvider::CreateInstance allocates a 0x78-byte object but leaves the pointer at offset 0x50 uninitialised, and the destructor passes that stale value to LocalFree — an attacker-influenced free that corrupts the document process's heap. The delivery path steps around the controls most Office-hardening programmes rely on: no macro executes, no OLE object is embedded and no external content is fetched.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; UI:R is a user opening a mailed or downloaded RTF
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; an uninitialised pointer freed on a deterministic code path, with no race and no timing-constrained heap groom, although converting the LocalFree into reliable execution needs heap shaping that the public PoC demonstrates only as a crash. The vendor's own FAQ notes that 'Remote' in the title refers to the attacker's location while the attack executes locally, so AV:L should not be read as requiring prior access.
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered — the vendor credits Anonymous, Jinquan of DBAPPSecurity Lieying Lab, and Zesen Ye and Zhiniang Peng of Sangfor, a pattern consistent with independent parallel discovery on a heavily fuzzed surface. The public PoC is a post-patch reverse-engineering exercise against prauthproviders.dll by a researcher who appears in none of the credits, so neither the discovery nor the weaponisation involved AI.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Install the 2022-02-08 cumulative updates: build 10.0.17763.2565 via KB5010351 (Windows 10 1809 and Server 2019), 10.0.18363.2094 via KB5010345 (1909), 10.0.19043.1526 via KB5010342 (20H2, 21H1, 21H2), 10.0.20348.524 via KB5010354 (Server 2022), plus KB5010456 and KB5010386 for Windows 11 21H2 and Server version 20H2 Core. There is no configuration workaround — the vulnerable WinRT class is activated during document parsing, so neither macro blocking nor Protected View intervenes.
prevention.adequacy: The update fully closes it where it can be applied, and what failed was prioritisation rather than remediation: the vendor published it as Important with a temporal metric of E:U (exploit code unproven), the public PoC appeared roughly a month later invalidating that, and CISA asserted active exploitation six months after publication — anyone reasoning from the vendor's temporal score at publication scheduled it into a routine monthly cycle. Every affected Windows 10 branch has since passed end of servicing (Windows 10 support ended 2025-10-14), so a surviving host receives no new cumulative updates; the February 2022 packages remain individually obtainable from the Microsoft Update Catalog, but migration to a serviced release is the correct answer.

detection.what_would_have_worked: WER crash reports or Application-log faults for winword.exe or wordpad.exe naming prauthproviders.dll, and heap-corruption stop conditions (STATUS_HEAP_CORRUPTION) in a document process — the natural failure mode when the freed offset-0x50 value does not land where the exploit expects. For scoping, inbound RTF attachments reaching users on builds predating the February 2022 cumulative updates.
detection.adequacy: The one distinguishing signal is an Office crash, which most SOCs suppress as noise because Word crashes constantly for benign reasons — so the detection technically exists and is filtered out by the same tuning that keeps the console usable.

response.what_would_have_worked: Isolate the host, capture the RTF and the crash dump before the process restarts, hunt for post-exploitation on the assumption that a successful run left no crash at all, and move end-of-servicing Windows 10 hosts off the branch rather than hand-installing a 2022 KB.
response.adequacy: Response is sound but starts blind: a successful exploitation creates no file, no service, no scheduled task and no distinctive network event, so the responder is usually working from a crash that represents the attempt that failed.

NIST-800-53-CM-7.gap: Least functionality is expressed in installed roles, features, services and executables, and has no vocabulary for Windows Runtime activatable classes. prauthproviders.dll and the WapAuthProvider class it exports are present and reachable on every Windows 10 1809-and-later and Windows 11 host no matter how aggressively the baseline is trimmed, and no unnecessary-function review would have identified a WinRT authentication-provider class reachable from a document parser as removable.

NIS2-Art21-incident-handling.gap: Incident handling and the 24-hour early-warning clock both start at detection, and this defect produces almost nothing to detect: a successful run yields code execution with no new file, service, scheduled task or distinctive network event, while failed runs surface as ordinary application crashes nobody escalates. The vendor's Important rating with 'exploit code unproven' then argued against prioritisation for six months.

UK-CAF-C1.gap: Security monitoring is assessed on whether coverage produces signals an analyst can act on. The only reliable host artifact is a Word or WordPad crash referencing prauthproviders.dll — an event stream most SOCs deliberately suppress — so an outcome rated achieved on comprehensive endpoint and network collection describes an estate in which this CVE's single distinguishing signal has been filtered out by design.

AU-Essential-8-App-Hardening.gap: User application hardening and the separate Office macro control together define the document-borne-threat posture: block internet macros, disable OLE, harden the browser, block Flash and Java. None of it is in this path — the trigger is RTF parsing instantiating a WinRT class, with no macro to block and no OLE object to disable — so Maturity Level Three opened the same document into the same uninitialised free as Maturity Level Zero.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.7.gap: Protection against malware presumes there is malware to detect. The delivery vehicle is a structurally valid RTF carrying no executable code, no macro and no dropper — the exploit is the document's effect on an uninitialised pointer, not its content — so signature scanning, macro-keyed attachment filtering and 'don't enable content' user training all miss it by construction and never reach a decision point.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2022-21971 shipped on 2022-02-08 rated Important with a temporal metric of E:U (exploit code unproven); a public PoC against prauthproviders.dll appeared roughly a month later and CISA only asserted active exploitation on 2022-08-18. Triage reasoning from the vendor's severity signal scheduled it into a routine monthly cycle for six months, which a KEV-listing-triggered mitigation deadline overrides by construction.

new_control_requirements.name: EOL-ASSET-DECOMMISSION
new_control_requirements.description: Network-reachable end-of-life devices with no vendor patch path must be isolated and decommissioned within a bounded window; mandatory compensating segmentation applies until removal since no remediation exists.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2022-21971's only remediation is the February 2022 cumulative build (10.0.17763.2565, 10.0.18363.2094, 10.0.19043.1526, 10.0.20348.524), and every affected Windows 10 branch has since passed end of servicing, so a surviving host receives no cumulative updates at all and hand-installing a 2022 KB from the Update Catalog leaves an unserviced OS still exposing a WinRT class that any RTF can activate with no macro and no OLE object to block.

CVE-2026-63077.name: JetBrains TeamCity Deserialization of Untrusted Data Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: An unauthenticated attacker POSTs to TeamCity's agent-polling endpoint /app/agents/v1/register to enroll a synthetic build agent (agentAddress=127.0.0.1, agentPort=9090, a random authToken) and receives a TeamCity-AgentSessionId, then posts an XStream XML gadget chain to /app/agents/v1/commands/error carrying that session header. XStream 1.4.20.3 is configured with an allowlist that retained the library's default type permissions, so the document deserializes into a working chain that drives an in-memory HSQLDB SCRIPT command and writes a JSP polyglot to ../webapps/ROOT/<hex>.jspws. A single GET of the dropped file compiles the polyglot and runs java.lang.Runtime.getRuntime().exec() with the attacker's OS command as the TeamCity server process - one unauthenticated request chain from network reachability to code execution over the whole CI secret store and build-artifact surface.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none - CVSS PR:N. The exploit mints its own agent session at /app/agents/v1/register, so no TeamCity account, API token or agent authorization token is required; the only precondition is network reachability to the server.
attack_vector.complexity: low - AC:L/UI:N/S:U. The gadget chain is deterministic, there is no race and no user interaction, and Rapid7's 446-line Python PoC reduces the whole path to one command. CISA's SSVC decision records exploitation=active, automatable=yes, technicalImpact=total.
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered - reported privately to JetBrains by external researcher Antoni Tremblay on 2026-07-10 and disclosed with a fix on 2026-07-27; the public exploit was hand-written by Rapid7's Stephen Fewer. No AI tooling is credited in the JetBrains advisory, the JetBrains active-exploitation update, the Rapid7 root-cause analysis, or the PoC, and no AI assistance is documented in weaponization.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Upgrade TeamCity On-Premises to 2025.11.7 or 2026.1.3, or install JetBrains' security patch plugin (available for 2017.1+, hot-loads without a restart on 2018.2 and later), and keep the agent-polling surface off untrusted networks so /app/agents/v1/register is unreachable from the internet in the first place.
prevention.adequacy: The upgrade removes the deserialization sink outright and needs no live-patch tooling, but the fix shipped 2026-07-27 and exploitation followed within days, so patching alone does not account for the window between disclosure and deployment: any server that was internet-reachable during it must be treated as potentially compromised rather than merely patched. TeamCity Cloud was mitigated by JetBrains and required no customer action.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Grep teamcity-server.log for com.thoughtworks.xstream.converters.ConversionException (attempted or successful exploitation) and com.thoughtworks.xstream.security.ForbiddenClassException naming HSQLMetadataStorage$SchemaMismatchException (a blocked attempt on a patched server), alongside freemarker.core._TemplateModelException on the 'connection' property and org.hsqldb.HsqlException 'file input/output error' for .jspws paths; alert on build agents registering with 'scan'-prefixed names; and file-integrity-monitor webapps/ROOT for unexpected *.jspws files.
detection.adequacy: These signals are high-fidelity and free to deploy, but on an unpatched server they are post-compromise: the ConversionException is only written once the gadget chain has already deserialized, and the .jspws artifact only appears after the webshell is on disk. The ForbiddenClassException on a patched server is the one pre-impact signal, and it exists only because the patch already blocked the class.

response.what_would_have_worked: Remove every *.jspws file from the TeamCity webroot, delete attacker-registered agents (notably the 'scan'-prefixed ones JetBrains named), rotate all credentials the server held - VCS tokens, artifact-repository and cloud keys, signing material, agent authorization tokens - and review builds and artifacts produced during the exposure window for tampering before they propagate downstream.
response.adequacy: Credential rotation is the only reliable containment, because execution as the TeamCity server process reads the entire CI secret store, and artifact review is the only way to bound downstream impact on the pipelines the server feeds. Nothing in scope mandates either step after a build-server compromise, so operators who treat the upgrade as closure leave stolen secrets valid and tampered artifacts unexamined.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: SI-2 had almost no slack to work with here. JetBrains shipped the fix on 2026-07-27, reports of in-the-wild exploitation of the unauthenticated agent-polling RCE followed within days, and CISA allowed three days on the KEV clock (added 2026-08-05, due 2026-08-08). An SI-2 flaw-remediation cadence measured in weeks - which is what most implementations actually attest to - leaves an internet-facing TeamCity server exploitable for the entire period an automatable, PoC-backed pre-auth RCE is being weaponized.

NIS2-Art21-supply-chain.gap: Art.21's supply-chain clauses point outward at supplier vetting and third-party assurance, but the injection point here is the organization's own build server. Code execution as the TeamCity process reads the CI credential store, tampers with build artifacts and reaches every downstream pipeline the server feeds - a supply-chain compromise originating inside internal build infrastructure that no amount of supplier due diligence detects or prevents.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: CAF B4 secure-configuration outcomes assume untrusted network input never reaches an unsafe deserializer, so the operator-side measures B4 drives - configuration baselines, hardening guides, firewalling - never inspect the XStream 1.4.20.3 allowlist that shipped with the library's default type permissions retained. The unauthenticated /app/agents/v1/commands/error path deserialized attacker XML into a working gadget chain by product design, and no B4 activity remediates that short of the vendor fix.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: The 48-hour internet-facing patch requirement was technically satisfiable - the fix existed from 2026-07-27 - but Essential Eight never asks whether a CI server should be internet-facing at all. With no control requiring network isolation of the build plane, an instance still reachable while the 48-hour clock ran was exposed to a one-shot, automatable pre-auth RCE, and the maturity model records a compliant patching outcome either way.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: A.8.8 programmes that rank remediation by score would have buried this: EPSS read 0.010 (58th percentile) on the KEV date even though JetBrains had already reported exploitation in the wild. A CVSS-plus-EPSS queue defers a 9.8 unauthenticated RCE behind higher-probability, lower-impact items; the KEV listing and the vendor's exploitation update were the real prioritization signals, and A.8.8 does not require them to override the probabilistic score.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2026-63077 — JetBrains fixed it on 2026-07-27 and confirmed in-the-wild exploitation days later; CISA added it to KEV on 2026-08-05 with a 2026-08-08 due date while EPSS still read 0.010 (58th percentile), so score-driven queues deprioritized it. A KEV-triggered 4-hour clock — satisfied by the 2025.11.7 / 2026.1.3 upgrade, the 2017.1+ security patch plugin (no restart on 2018.2+), or documented isolation of the agent-polling surface — is the only cadence that beats a one-shot, automatable pre-auth RCE with a public 446-line PoC to an internet-facing build server.

new_control_requirements.name: SERVICE-INTERNAL-PROTOCOL-DESERIALIZATION-HARDENING
new_control_requirements.description: A server product that exposes an internal coordination protocol — build-agent polling, cluster membership, node replication, management RPC — must not deserialize input arriving on it without both authenticating the peer and constraining the deserializer to an explicit allow-list of expected types, and the listener must be bound to the coordination network rather than to all interfaces. Default-permissive type handling in the serialization library counts as no allow-list at all. The distinguishing test: from an unauthenticated host on a segment that can reach the coordination port, send a serialized object of a type the protocol never legitimately carries and confirm the connection is refused or the type rejected before any object is constructed — a product whose internal protocol is documented as trusted, but which listens on 0.0.0.0 and accepts whatever the library will rehydrate, is exploitable by anyone who can reach the port.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2026-63077 — TeamCity's agent-polling protocol accepts XML from an unauthenticated caller and hands it to an XStream instance still carrying the library's default type permissions, so a gadget chain writes a JSP polyglot into the webroot and runs as the build server. CVE-2026-34486 is the same shape one product over: the Tomcat cluster receiver forwarding a message whose decryption failed into an unfiltered ObjectInputStream. Both are internal coordination protocols the vendor documented as trusted and shipped listening to anyone who could reach the port.

attack_vector.description: An attacker who can reach the LoadMaster management API sends one unauthenticated POST to /accessv2 whose apiuser value is nothing but single quotes, forcing escape_quotes() to allocate an uninitialized heap buffer it never null-terminates, while dozens of sibling JSON keys in the same request spray a shell-metacharacter payload across freed chunks of the same size. The escaped username is then placed into a single-quoted shell argument that reads past its own bytes into the sprayed data, and the appliance executes the attacker's command.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; unauthenticated, and the quote-only apiuser is a trigger rather than a credential guess
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L, no user interaction and no race; the constraint is reachability (AV:A, and only when the management API is enabled) rather than exploit difficulty
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered. Reported through Trend Micro's Zero Day Initiative by Syed Ibrahim Ahmed and Jacky Yang of TrendAI Research (ZDI-26-340/341/342, all published 2026-06-09); the 'TrendAI' name is Trend Micro's branding for ZDI's research arm and is not a claim of AI-assisted discovery. No AI involvement is credited in any advisory or in the public analysis.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Upgrade to Kemp LoadMaster 7.2.63.2 (GA) or 7.2.54.18 (LTSF), or 7.2.63.2 for ECS Connection Manager and Connection Manager for ObjectScale — and, independently of the upgrade, disable the management API where it is not needed or confine it to a management network the attacker cannot reach.
prevention.adequacy: The upgrade closes it, but the configuration-side control is the one that was available for the two months between the 2026-06-04 fix and the 2026-08-07 KEV listing, and it needs no maintenance window. Neither helps an appliance already reached: command execution on the ADC precedes any patch.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alert on any /accessv2 request whose apiuser field contains a single quote, and on request bodies carrying repeated undefined sibling keys with identical padded values — then treat a 200 text/json response containing command output rather than an API result as confirmation.
detection.adequacy: Detection is unusually clean here because the trigger is a malformed username rather than a plausible one, so the signature has almost no legitimate traffic to compete with. It only works if the appliance forwards management-API request logs somewhere the attacker cannot reach once they own the device.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treat a confirmed hit as full appliance compromise: rebuild from known-good firmware rather than patching in place, rotate every TLS private key and certificate the LoadMaster terminated, invalidate the API key store, and review the balanced applications for onward access gained through the device.
response.adequacy: Rebuild is the only reliable eviction path for an edge appliance, and key rotation is the part most often skipped — the attacker had code execution on the device holding the private keys for everything behind it.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: SI-2 is satisfied by a documented remediation cadence, and a monthly or quarterly appliance-patch cycle is a defensible one. It left roughly two months between Progress shipping the fix on 2026-06-04 and CISA's 2026-08-07 listing, during which watchTowr had published the patched function byte for byte and a Nuclei template was in the public catalog.

EU-CRA-Art13.gap: Art.13 places the duty on the manufacturer to ship without known exploitable vulnerabilities, which does nothing for a deployer running an appliance already in the field. No CRA obligation tells the operator to treat their own edge ADC as an attack surface with its own patch clock, so a compliant purchase leaves the exposure exactly where it was.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: B4 records the appliance as hardened on the strength of its data-plane configuration and never asks the question that decides this CVE: is the management API enabled, and who can reach it. The single control that turns pre-auth RCE into an unreachable code path is outside what a B4 assessment routinely inspects.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: The 48-hour band applies to internet-facing services, and a LoadMaster management API on a management network is often not classified as one, so the appliance inherits a slower target. The classification tracks network position rather than consequence, while CISA's SSVC rates the technical impact of this flaw as total.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: A.8.8 ranks by risk score, and here the score was loud enough — EPSS 0.85 at the 99.7th percentile. What it cannot express is that the asset is a control plane: compromising the ADC hands over the TLS keys, the traffic and the WAF that other A.8 controls assume are intact, so ranking it alongside an ordinary server patch understates the blast.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2026-8037 — KEV-listed 2026-08-07 with a three-day due date against an appliance whose fix had been public since 2026-06-04 and whose patched function watchTowr had published byte for byte on 2026-06-29. The KEV clock's compensating-controls limb is what covers this case, because disabling or network-confining the LoadMaster management API removes reachability immediately and needs no maintenance window, while the firmware upgrade needs one.

new_control_requirements.name: PERIMETER-DEVICE-ZERODAY-SLA-TIER
new_control_requirements.description: Compliance frameworks must define a distinct patch SLA tier for pre-auth RCE on perimeter-trust-boundary devices (firewalls, VPN concentrators, WAFs, edge load-balancers). Tier requirement: vendor-mitigation deployed within 4 hours of KEV listing OR isolation of the vulnerable interface; standard 14/30-day SLAs do not apply because the device IS the trust boundary.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2026-8037 — a pre-authentication command injection on a load balancer that terminates TLS for the applications behind it, rated EPSS 0.85 at the 99.7th percentile with a public Nuclei template. A standard 14- or 30-day appliance-patch SLA prices this like an ordinary server, which is exactly the mismatch a perimeter-device tier exists to correct: the device IS the trust boundary.

new_control_requirements.name: PERIMETER-COMPROMISE-REBUILD-NOT-PATCH
new_control_requirements.description: Pre-rehearsed IR runbook for any perimeter device that suffers a pre-auth RCE CVE in active exploitation MUST default to config-exfil + rebuild + credential rotation, not patch-in-place. Patch-in-place leaves attacker-installed implants intact.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2026-8037 — exploitation yields OS command execution on the appliance holding the TLS private keys and API key store for everything it fronts, so patching in place leaves any implant and any stolen key material intact. Recovery has to default to rebuild from known-good firmware plus rotation of every certificate the LoadMaster terminated.

CVE-2006-2492.name: Microsoft Word Malformed Object Pointer Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: A crafted .doc carries an object record with a malformed pointer and an invalid length. Word follows the pointer and copies without validating the length against the destination buffer, corrupting memory and executing attacker code as the logged-on user. Delivery in the original attacks was a targeted mail attachment; a web link to the same file works identically.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; the attacker needs no account on the target, only a way to put a file in front of a user
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; no race and no info leak, but UI:R is real: someone must open the document in an affected Word or Works Suite build. On the Word 2000 path Office does not prompt Open/Save/Cancel first, removing one click.
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Reported by Shih-hao Weng of the Information & Communication Security Technology Center per the MS06-027 acknowledgments — manual file-format analysis in 2006, with no AI tooling in the discovery chain and no AI-branded research arm involved.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Retiring Office 2000/XP/2003 and Works Suite rather than patching them, and — during the May-to-June 2006 window before MS06-027 — the bulletin's own workarounds: Group Policy removing Word as the mail editor, and forcing Word Safe Mode.
prevention.adequacy: Honest limit: the workarounds narrow delivery, they do not repair the parser, and a user who opens the file from disk still reaches it. The patch itself is complete for this defect but leaves the host on a product line with no further servicing, so prevention here ends in migration, not in a hotfix.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alerting on WINWORD.EXE spawning a child process or making an outbound connection immediately after a document open, and on new autostart entries appearing on a host that just opened an external attachment.
detection.adequacy: Process-lineage telemetry of that kind did not exist on the 2006 estate and does not exist on most surviving legacy hosts today — the machines still running Office 2003 are precisely the ones outside EDR coverage. Detection also fires after code execution, so it bounds the incident rather than preventing it.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating a confirmed open as a host compromise: rebuild rather than clean, and rotate every credential used on that host, since the reported 2006 payload was a rootkit-capable backdoor with shell access.
response.adequacy: Rebuild is the right call and is rarely taken for a 'document malware' alert, which is triaged as commodity infection. Rotation scope is also hard to bound on a legacy host with no session logging.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: Flaw remediation is nominally met by a 2006 hotfix. It cannot be met in substance on a product line that stopped receiving fixes in 2014, and SI-2 does not force that distinction.

NIST-800-53-SC-44.gap: Detonation of inbound .doc is an elective enhancement, and a sandbox running a supported Office build will not reproduce a crash in the Word 2000/2002 parser the victim actually runs.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: The vendor update exists and has since 2006, so the patch-management duty is dischargeable while the real obligation — retiring an unserviced suite — is never triggered.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: 'Maintained to reduce vulnerabilities' is evidenced from patch records, which are clean here; the asset still cannot be maintained into a secure state.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: The patch half of the control scores green from scanner output; the remove-unsupported-applications half, which is the operative one for Office 2003 and Works Suite, goes unmeasured.

AU-Essential-8-App-Hardening.gap: Macro, ActiveX and OLE settings are consulted after the binary .doc parser has already run, so full hardening maturity does not touch this path.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: The vulnerability record can be documented, actioned and closed while the host remains on a Word build that will never receive another fix.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.7.gap: Anti-malware coverage acts on the dropped payload, not on the legitimate application parsing a legitimate file type; the first stage has no malicious artefact to match.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Microsoft Word in Office 2000/XP/2003, Word Viewer 2003 and Works Suite 2000-2006 carried this defect from the May 2006 zero-day through the 2006-06-13 MS06-027 fix, and CISA still judged it worth a KEV entry on 2022-06-08 with a 2022-06-22 due date. EPSS holds it at 0.48387, 98.758th percentile, on 2026-08-13. The control's 'whichever is later' clause is the operative half for this entry: patch availability long predates KEV listing, so the clock runs from 2022-06-08, and the verified mitigation for an unsupported suite is documented removal rather than a hotfix.

new_control_requirements.name: ARCHIVE-CONTENT-TYPE-PROVENANCE
new_control_requirements.description: For this CVE the requirement is that Word's Protected View decision be taken from verified provenance of the file — established outside the document — rather than from metadata that travels with the document and that an attacker controls, and that the untrusted-origin marking survive whatever container the document is delivered in so the handler still sees it as externally sourced. The operator-side expression of the control: the mail gateway and file-share boundary apply and preserve the untrusted-origin marking themselves, so the sandbox decision does not depend on the application deriving it from attacker-supplied input. The distinguishing test: deliver an externally-sourced document through each ingress path and confirm it reaches Word marked untrusted, instead of confirming only that Protected View is enabled in policy.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Delivery is the whole precondition for this Word CVE — MS06-027 describes both the mail-attachment and the web-link scenario, and the 2006 attacks used targeted mail. Note the precondition honestly for the products MS06-027 names: Word 2000, Word 2002, Word 2003 and Word Viewer 2003 have no Protected View, so on those builds only the gateway half of this control is deliverable, and it is a holding measure until the suite is migrated and the viewer removed. On a migrated estate the sandbox half applies in full, and gateway-applied provenance is what makes it fire on a document extracted from an archive rather than downloaded directly.

CVE-2007-5659.name: Adobe Acrobat and Reader Buffer Overflow Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: A PDF carries JavaScript in an /OpenAction. On open, the script calls a Reader JavaScript API method — Collab.collectEmailInfo() in the public exploit — with an argument longer than the fixed buffer the implementation copies it into. The overflow gives control of execution inside the Reader process at the user's privilege, after a heap spray has placed the payload at a predictable address.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; the attacker supplies a file, nothing more
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; no race, no leak, no foothold. UI:R means the user must open the PDF, but the script fires from /OpenAction so opening is the entire interaction. Disabling Acrobat JavaScript is the one configuration that removes the path.
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Reported through iDefense Labs' contributor programme in 2007 by manual analysis of the Reader JavaScript API; NVD still carries the (now dead) iDefense advisory reference. No AI tooling and no AI-branded research arm in the chain.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Disabling JavaScript in Adobe Reader and Acrobat across the fleet, and enumerating both the Reader and the Acrobat update tracks — including per-user installs — before declaring the 8.1.2 upgrade complete.
prevention.adequacy: Disabling JavaScript is unusually strong here — it removes reachability for the whole API-overflow family, not just this CVE — but it breaks document workflows that use forms and Collab features, which is why estates leave it on. The upgrade half is complete for this defect and incomplete as a security posture, since 8.1.2 sits on a line that no longer receives fixes.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Gateway inspection that decompresses /FlateDecode and /ASCIIHexDecode streams and inspects the embedded script for API calls with oversized arguments, plus process-lineage alerting on AcroRd32.exe spawning children.
detection.adequacy: The public module deliberately encodes the script under two filters and randomises identifiers, so a scanner matching on literal method names misses it; the honest detection is structural — script present, argument length pathological — not signature-based. Process-lineage alerting fires only after execution.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating a confirmed open as a user-context compromise: rebuild the endpoint, rotate the credentials that user held, and check whether the same PDF reached other mailboxes.
response.adequacy: Correct but rarely executed at this severity, because 'PDF opened, AV alert' is triaged as commodity. With a public Metasploit module the payload is operator-chosen, so absence of a known-malware signature says nothing about what ran.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: Closed on the inventoried Reader track while a separate Acrobat track or a per-user install keeps 8.1.1 in service; and the 'fixed' version is itself on a dead product line.

NIST-800-53-CM-7.gap: Least functionality would have closed this by disabling Acrobat JavaScript, but a scripting engine inside a document reader is never enumerated as a disableable function.

NIS2-Art21-vulnerability-management.gap: Tracking is met; reachability is not. With a public Metasploit module since 2009 and EPSS 0.94222, exposure is set by whether any uninventoried 8.1.1 install survives.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: A patched-to-8.1.2 fleet with JavaScript enabled evidences secure configuration while leaving the entire API-overflow family reachable.

AU-Essential-8-App-Hardening.gap: PDF settings are in scope, but assessment samples web content and browser settings rather than the Acrobat JavaScript toggle that closes this path.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Scores from inventoried applications only; the unmanaged per-user Reader copy is not a finding, so full maturity is consistent with an 8.1.1 install being present.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: Nothing re-opens an evaluated-and-closed record when a public weaponized module appears a year later, which is exactly what happened here in 2009.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.9.gap: Desktop configuration baselines pin an approved version and install source, not a per-application feature posture, so nothing records whether the approved Reader build executes document-supplied script.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Adobe Reader and Acrobat 8.1.1 and earlier are the affected products, fixed in 8.1.2 in February 2008 and 7.1.0 in May 2008, and CISA opened the KEV clock on 2022-06-08 with a 2022-06-22 due date. EPSS reads 0.94222 at the 99.841st percentile on 2026-08-13 and a Metasploit module has been public since 2009, so the 'documented compensating controls' arm of this control is the one operators actually need: disabling Acrobat JavaScript is deployable in minutes on every affected version and removes the reachable path, where the upgrade to a supported Acrobat release is a project.

new_control_requirements.name: EMBEDDED-MEDIA-PARSER-LIBRARY-INVENTORY-AND-PATCH-PARITY
new_control_requirements.description: The packet names the affected product as Adobe Acrobat and Reader, which on a real estate is never one install: Reader and Acrobat ship as separate products on separate update tracks, and per-user copies land outside managed software distribution. The control here means enumerating every installed Acrobat and Reader copy across those tracks and confirming each reports the fixed build, rather than closing the flaw-remediation ticket when the single inventoried Reader package updates. Scope it to those products: the packet ties the CWE-1321 sink to Acrobat and Reader and provides no mapping from the vulnerable code into other PDF-handling software, so instructing operators to treat every PDF-capable binary in the estate as an instance of this CVE manufactures findings and removal work against renderers no evidence implicates. Widen the inventory only where a verified source identifies another product carrying the same component. The distinguishing test: after the managed update lands, enumerate the Acrobat and Reader installs on the estate and confirm none still report a pre-fix version — an estate that patches the inventoried Reader while a second Acrobat track keeps the old build still opens crafted PDFs into the sink, with a flaw-remediation attestation that reads clean. Precondition: this reaches only copies the inventory can see and the operator can update; an unmanaged per-user install is remediated by removing it, not by recording it as patched. The packet registers no live-patch path, so each copy carries the service restart or system reboot the vendor fix requires, and a copy updated but not restarted is not yet remediated.
new_control_requirements.evidence: The affected set here is exactly the two-track case the control describes: Adobe Reader and Adobe Acrobat Professional/Standard/3D at 8.1.1 and earlier, fixed on separate tracks at 8.1.2, with the 7.x line served by a third fix at 7.1.0 under APSB08-13, plus distribution repackages (RHSA-2008-0144, Gentoo, Solaris) carrying their own update paths. The parity test is the operative half: with a public Metasploit module targeting Reader 8.1.1 specifically, a single surviving Acrobat copy below 8.1.2 makes the whole estate exploitable regardless of how clean the Reader record reads. Note the restart nuance for this product — no host reboot, but Reader/Acrobat and any browser hosting the plugin must be relaunched before the fix is live.

CVE-2008-0655.name: Adobe Acrobat and Reader Unspecified Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: Document-supplied JavaScript in a PDF calls this.getPrintParams(), sets the returned object's interactive field to interactionLevel.silent, and then calls this.print() repeatedly. Adobe's documentation reserves silent printing for batch, console and menu events; the implementation did not enforce that, so a file the user merely opened drives unbounded prompt-free print jobs. The published proof loops ten thousand times.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; the attacker supplies a PDF and needs nothing on the target
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; no memory corruption, so no groom, no spray and no version-specific offsets. UI:R only: the file must be opened in a Reader or Acrobat below 8.1.2 that executes document JavaScript.
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Found by the researcher publishing as cocoruder by reading Adobe's documented event restrictions against the shipped implementation, and disclosed with working code on Full-Disclosure in May 2008. No AI tooling and no AI-branded research arm.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Disabling JavaScript in Adobe Reader and Acrobat, which removes this defect entirely on every affected version without waiting for the 8.1.2 upgrade, and reaching 8.1.2 / 7.1.0 on both the Reader and the Acrobat update tracks.
prevention.adequacy: Complete for this member of the bundle, since the flaw lives wholly inside the JavaScript API. It breaks form and Collab workflows, which is why it is not the default. It also does not address the other, unspecified members NVD folds under this id.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Print-server alerting on job-count anomalies per submitting host, and gateway inspection of PDF JavaScript for this.print() called from a loop or with interactionLevel.silent set.
detection.adequacy: Print-queue telemetry is rarely wired to security monitoring at all, so the detection exists in principle and is unmonitored in practice. It also fires after the resource loss has started.

response.what_would_have_worked: Purging the spooler queue, isolating the submitting workstation, and retaining the offending PDF for analysis rather than deleting it as a printer fault.
response.adequacy: Adequate for the resource impact and inadequate as a security response, because the same file could carry a code-execution member of the same 8.1.2 bundle. Triaging the event as a printing problem is how the security half gets missed.

NIST-800-53-CM-7.gap: Disabling Acrobat JavaScript closes this outright, but an embedded scripting engine is treated as part of the product rather than as a function requiring justification, so CM-7 never enumerates it.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: A remediation record against an aggregate id proves the version bump and nothing about which individual defects were in scope — including the overflow NVD says may be subsumed here.

NIS2-Art21-vulnerability-handling.gap: NVD describes the id as unknown impact and unknown attack vectors, so handling reduces to applying a version bump; the mechanism is only recoverable from the researcher's own disclosure.

NIS2-Art21-availability.gap: The documented outcome is exhaustion of shared physical output devices and consumables, which no availability or continuity control in the article is written to cover.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: An upgraded fleet with document script still enabled evidences secure configuration while leaving the whole class — untrusted script reaching a privileged application capability without consent — live.

AU-Essential-8-App-Hardening.gap: PDF settings are in scope but the sampled artefacts are web content, Java and Flash blocking; the Acrobat JavaScript toggle that closes this is not what an assessor examines.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: Evaluation is defeated by the source: an 'unknown impact' NVD entry cannot be ranked, and the control does not require going to the disclosure post that states the mechanism.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.9.gap: Desktop baselines pin approved versions and install sources, not per-application feature posture, so the setting that decides reachability is outside the evidence trail.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Adobe Reader and Acrobat before 8.1.2 are the named products; the fix shipped February 2008 (APSA08-01) with 7.1.0 for the 7.x line in May 2008 (APSB08-13), and CISA opened the KEV clock on 2022-06-08 with a 2022-06-22 due date. EPSS is 0.36844 at the 98.369th percentile on 2026-08-13. The compensating-control arm carries this entry: because the silent-print defect lives wholly in the Acrobat JavaScript API, disabling document JavaScript is a verified mitigation deployable fleet-wide inside the 4-hour window, where migrating off a dead 8.x line is not.

new_control_requirements.name: EMBEDDED-MEDIA-PARSER-LIBRARY-INVENTORY-AND-PATCH-PARITY
new_control_requirements.description: The packet names the affected product as Adobe Acrobat and Reader, which on a real estate is never one install: Reader and Acrobat ship as separate products on separate update tracks, and per-user copies land outside managed software distribution. The control here means enumerating every installed Acrobat and Reader copy across those tracks and confirming each reports the fixed build, rather than closing the flaw-remediation ticket when the single inventoried Reader package updates. Scope it to those products: the packet ties the CWE-1321 sink to Acrobat and Reader and provides no mapping from the vulnerable code into other PDF-handling software, so instructing operators to treat every PDF-capable binary in the estate as an instance of this CVE manufactures findings and removal work against renderers no evidence implicates. Widen the inventory only where a verified source identifies another product carrying the same component. The distinguishing test: after the managed update lands, enumerate the Acrobat and Reader installs on the estate and confirm none still report a pre-fix version — an estate that patches the inventoried Reader while a second Acrobat track keeps the old build still opens crafted PDFs into the sink, with a flaw-remediation attestation that reads clean. Precondition: this reaches only copies the inventory can see and the operator can update; an unmanaged per-user install is remediated by removing it, not by recording it as patched. The packet registers no live-patch path, so each copy carries the service restart or system reboot the vendor fix requires, and a copy updated but not restarted is not yet remediated.
new_control_requirements.evidence: This entry is the two-track case exactly: Adobe Reader and Adobe Acrobat Professional/Standard/3D before 8.1.2 on separate update tracks, with the 7.x line served by a third fix at 7.1.0 under APSB08-13. Parity matters more than usual because the id is an aggregate — NVD carries it as multiple unspecified vulnerabilities before 8.1.2 — so a copy left below the fixed build is exposed to the whole bundle, not to one characterised defect. Restart nuance for this product: no host reboot, but Reader/Acrobat and any browser hosting the plugin must be relaunched before the fix is in force.

CVE-2009-0557.name: Microsoft Office Object Record Corruption Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: A crafted .xls carries a malformed record describing an embedded object. Excel's binary-format parser mis-indexes off that record and then uses the corrupted object reference, letting attacker-supplied data steer execution inside the Excel process at the user's privilege. The same parser is present in Excel Viewer and the Office Compatibility Pack, so a licence-free host is equally exploitable.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; the attacker needs no account, only a way to get the workbook in front of a user
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; no race, no leak, no foothold. UI:R is the constraint: someone must open the workbook in an affected build. File Block on the legacy binary format removes the path entirely at a real functional cost.
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. MS09-021 records a responsible disclosure in 2009 and credits Bing Liu of Fortinet's FortiGuard Global Security Research Team for the Object Record Corruption Vulnerability, along with two sibling Excel defects in the same bulletin. Manual file-format research; FortiGuard is a team brand, not an AI claim, and no AI tooling appears anywhere in the chain.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: MS09-021 applied across every product carrying the parser — including Excel Viewer and the Office Compatibility Pack, not just licensed Excel — and File Block (FileOpenBlock BinaryFiles) on hosts with no business need to open legacy .xls.
prevention.adequacy: The patch is complete for this defect. File Block is stronger but blunt — it stops every legacy workbook, legitimate ones included, which is why estates that exchange .xls with customers cannot hold it. Neither addresses the 2026 position, where the affected products no longer receive fixes at all.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Process-lineage alerting on EXCEL.EXE spawning children or writing executables, and correlating repeated Excel crashes on the same document hash across multiple recipients.
detection.adequacy: Crash correlation is the strongest signal available for a memory-corruption file-format bug with no public exploit to signature, and almost nobody collects application crash telemetry centrally. Process-lineage alerting fires only after code has run.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating a confirmed open as a user-context compromise — rebuild the host, rotate that user's credentials, and sweep mail for the same attachment across other mailboxes.
response.adequacy: Right in principle and rarely triggered, because with no public exploit and no named campaign there is no signature to raise the alert that starts this. The response depends on detection that mostly is not there.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: Remediation is scored against the Office inventory, which omits Excel Viewer and the Compatibility Pack — the hosts where the parser survives — and cannot express that the fixed products are now unsupported.

NIST-800-53-SC-44.gap: Elective rather than baseline, and a sandbox running a current Office build will not reproduce a fault in the Office 2003 or Excel Viewer parser the recipient actually runs.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: A 2009 vendor update makes the duty dischargeable while the real finding — unserviced Office suites and a retired Viewer still opening untrusted workbooks — never becomes a non-conformity.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: Patch records evidence 'maintained' on an asset that cannot be maintained into a secure state, and B4 never asks why the legacy binary format is still accepted.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Scores from inventoried applications, so Excel Viewer and the Compatibility Pack escape; the remove-unsupported half, which is the operative one, is not sampled.

AU-Essential-8-App-Hardening.gap: Macro, OLE and ActiveX policies are evaluated after the binary-format parser has already processed the malformed record.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: Nothing reopens a closed record when the exploitation picture inverts — no known exploitation in 2009, KEV-listed in 2022.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.7.gap: Anti-malware acts on the dropped payload; the first stage is a legitimate file type opened by a legitimate application, with no artefact to match.

This entry is the case the control's compensating-control arm exists for: the vendor bulletin recorded no known exploitation and no public proof-of-concept, so nothing in the 2009 record would have prompted an accelerated response, and the KEV listing thirteen years later is the only trigger. On a legacy estate the verified mitigation inside the window is File Block on the binary format, not the migration.

new_control_requirements.name: DOWNLOAD-PROVENANCE-ENFORCEMENT
new_control_requirements.description: Exploitation here requires the victim to open an attacker-supplied Office document, so on an estate that has not yet reached the fixed build the delivery path is the only enforceable control. Require Mark-of-the-Web on every Office file arriving by mail, web download, or untrusted file share, and require MOTW-tagged documents to open in Protected View — an isolated, reduced-privilege render — instead of the full parsing path that carries the CWE-94 sink at the user's own process privilege. Provenance must survive the container: files extracted from an archive, mounted from an ISO or VHD, or renamed must inherit the tag rather than lose it, and 'Enable Editing' on externally sourced documents must be blocked by policy rather than left to the user. The distinguishing test: mail a MOTW-tagged spreadsheet nested inside a ZIP to a managed workstation, extract it, and confirm the extracted file still opens in Protected View — a user-application-hardening attestation that covers only macro and ActiveX/OLE settings still lets a provenance-stripped document reach the vulnerable parser with full user privileges.
new_control_requirements.evidence: The control's framing matches this entry exactly: NVD assigns CWE-94 to CVE-2009-0557, the sink is reached by opening a crafted Excel workbook, and MS09-021 confirms that opening the file is the only interaction required. The delivery half is the enforceable lever for the products the packet names — Office 2000/XP/2003, the 2007 Office System, Excel Viewer and the Compatibility Pack — with one precondition stated honestly: Protected View does not exist on Office 2003 and earlier, so on those builds only the gateway-side provenance marking and File Block are deliverable, and the sandbox half arrives with migration to a supported Office release.

attack_vector.description: A crafted .doc carries a tag with an invalid length field. Word reads that length from the file and uses it to copy data into a stack-allocated buffer without validating it, overflowing the buffer and overwriting the saved return address. Execution continues under attacker control inside the Word process at the logged-on user's privilege. Word Viewer and the Office Compatibility Pack ship the same parser.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; the attacker supplies a document and needs nothing on the target
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; no race, no leak, no groom, no foothold. UI:R only: the document must be opened in an affected build. File Block on the legacy binary format removes the path at a real functional cost.
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Credited by MS09-027 to Wushi of team509 working with the Zero Day Initiative, and by ZDI-09-035 to ling and wushi of team509, reported to Microsoft on 2008-07-08. Manual research routed through a commercial acquisition programme; no AI tooling, no AI-branded research arm.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: MS09-027 applied to every product carrying the parser — including Word Viewer and the Office Compatibility Pack, not just licensed Word — plus File Block (FileOpenBlock BinaryFiles) on hosts with no business need for legacy .doc.
prevention.adequacy: The patch is complete for this defect. File Block is stronger but blunt — MS09-027 notes users without a configured exempt directory lose access to every Office 2003-and-earlier file, which is why estates exchanging .doc externally cannot hold it. Neither addresses the eleven months between ZDI's 2008-07-08 report and the fix, when no operator control existed at all.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Central collection of Office application-crash telemetry, correlating repeated Word faults on one document hash across recipients, plus process-lineage alerting on WINWORD.EXE spawning children.
detection.adequacy: Crash correlation is the strongest available signal because the public artefact is a Metasploit module — the payload is operator-chosen, so there is nothing stable in the second stage to signature, and the failed-landing crash is the part that does not vary. It is also the telemetry organisations least often ship off-host. Process lineage fires only after execution.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating a confirmed open as a user-context compromise: rebuild the endpoint, rotate that user's credentials, and sweep mail for the same attachment elsewhere in the estate.
response.adequacy: Correct and rarely triggered, because no named campaign is attached to this id and the public module's payload is operator-chosen, so nothing raises the alert that starts it. The response is gated on detection that mostly is not collected.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: Scored against the Word inventory, which omits Word Viewer and the Compatibility Pack, and unable to express that the fixed products are now unsupported.

NIST-800-53-SC-44.gap: Elective rather than baseline, and a detonation host on a current Office build will not reproduce a fault in the Word 2002/2003 or Word Viewer parser the recipient runs.

NIST-800-53-CM-7.gap: Least-functionality enumerations list applications, not the file formats an application accepts, so the vendor-documented File Block switch is never treated as a disableable capability.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: Measures the entity's patching, not the eleven-month vendor fix window from the 2008-07-08 ZDI report nor the seventeen years of no servicing since.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: Patch records evidence 'maintained' on abandoned software, and B4 never asks why legacy binary documents are accepted from untrusted senders.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Word Viewer and the Compatibility Pack escape the application inventory the maturity rating is computed from, and the remove-unsupported half is not sampled.

AU-Essential-8-App-Hardening.gap: Macro, OLE and ActiveX policies are consulted after the record parser has already overflowed the stack buffer.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: Nothing reopens a closed evaluation when the exploitation picture inverts — no known exploitation and no published proof-of-concept in 2009, public exploit code in 2010 filed under the sibling CVE tag, KEV-listed in 2022.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.7.gap: Anti-malware acts on the dropped payload, and the public artefact for this CVE is a Metasploit module whose payload the operator chooses, so a clean scan on the second stage proves nothing about the first.
