With grooming, that overwrite becomes control of execution inside the Flash or AIR process at the viewing user's privilege. Adobe never disclosed the specific ActionScript object involved.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none - PR:N; the attacker needs only to get the victim to load attacker-controlled Flash content
attack_vector.complexity: low - AC:L; the practical constraint is heap grooming to place a corruptible object next to the undersized allocation, which is why it was fielded in limited targeted attacks rather than commodity kits at disclosure
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Found by Kaspersky Lab's behavioural zero-day exploit detection running on live attack traffic, then analysed by human researchers. Automated exploit detection inside a security product is not AI-assisted vulnerability discovery.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Removing Flash Player and the AIR runtime, or - in March 2016 - moving to 18.0.0.333 / 21.0.0.182 / 11.2.202.577 and AIR 21.0.0.176. Click-to-play for plugin content bounds the delivery path where removal is not yet possible.
prevention.adequacy: Patching was adequate only after 2016-03-10, and it was already too late for the targets Adobe described - the exploit was in use before the fix existed. Today there is no supported build to reach, so prevention means removal.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Behavioural exploit detection on the browser and AIR processes - the capability that actually caught this one - plus renderer-crash telemetry and software inventory that flags any Flash or AIR runtime present.
detection.adequacy: This is the rare case where detection outperformed prevention, but only for the vendor operating the telemetry. Signature-based endpoint tooling had nothing to match on a zero-day, and an estate without behavioural browser telemetry would have seen the compromise only through its second-stage effects.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treat a host that loaded untrusted Flash content while carrying a vulnerable build as executed-code, not merely exposed: rotate credentials and tokens available to the browser session and look for second-stage persistence rather than closing on plugin removal.
response.adequacy: Limited by evidence. With no public sample and no published indicators for this CVE, scoping depends entirely on whatever endpoint and network telemetry the operator already retained across the exposure window.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: A remediation record pointing at 2016 builds looks closed while those builds sit on a runtime that has had no vendor since 2020-12-31; SI-2 has no trigger that reopens a finding when the product line ends.

NIST-800-53-CM-7.gap: Least-functionality baselines permitted Flash as business-required and were never re-decided after end of life, so the control passed on hosts still carrying the vulnerable virtual machine.

NIS2-Art21-vulnerability-handling.gap: Vulnerability handling can be fully evidenced while the only available treatment - decommissioning an unsupported runtime - sits outside the process with no owner and no date.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: B4 measured as update currency returns achieved on unmaintained software; measured as support status it fails, and only the second reading reflects the real exposure.

AU-Essential-8-App-Hardening.gap: The Essential Eight names Flash removal, but self-assessment at a maturity level that tolerates Flash for a business application records the control as met while the exploited runtime stays installed.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: The register records a fixed version rather than a removal date, so the documented treatment no longer exists as a supported target.

ISO-27001-2022-A.5.7.gap: Threat intelligence built on published advisory feeds had nothing to ingest before 2016-03-10, because the first signal of this exploit was a security vendor's private detection telemetry rather than a public disclosure.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Adobe Flash Player and AIR CVE-2016-1010 was exploited in limited, targeted attacks before Adobe shipped 18.0.0.333 / 21.0.0.182 / 11.2.202.577 and AIR 21.0.0.176 on 2016-03-10, and CISA listed it on 2022-05-25 (due 2022-06-15) with a required action of disconnection because Flash Player had been end-of-life since 2020-12-31. The control's 'documented compensating controls' branch is the operative one for this product: with no supported build to deploy, the mitigation that closes the clock is removing the Flash runtime and the SWF content that requires it, evidenced per host. EPSS remains 0.19785 at the 97.165th percentile on 2026-08-13.

new_control_requirements.name: INCOMPLETE-PATCH-SEQUENCE-SEVERITY-MULTIPLIER
new_control_requirements.description: Vulnerability-management programs must apply a severity multiplier when a CVE is the Nth in an incomplete-patch sequence on the same primitive (third MOTW bypass, second AMSI bypass, etc.). Framework controls treating each CVE as discrete obscure the structural defect; the Nth CVE in a sequence implies that future bypasses on the same primitive are likely.
new_control_requirements.evidence: The NVD record for CVE-2016-1010 states it is 'a different vulnerability than CVE-2016-0963 and CVE-2016-0993' - three separate memory-safety defects in one Adobe Flash Player release, and one of a run of Flash zero-days caught in the wild across 2016 by Kaspersky Lab. Scored discretely, each looked like a single high-severity browser-plugin bug with an available update; scored as a sequence on the same runtime, the correct conclusion was that Flash Player would keep producing in-the-wild-exploited memory corruption and that the treatment was removal rather than the next Flash update. The multiplier this control requires is what converts 'apply APSB16-08' into 'schedule the runtime out of the estate'.

CVE-2016-1646.name: Google Chromium V8 Out-of-Bounds Read Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: A crafted page gives an array a custom prototype carrying a getter on a hole index, then calls Array.prototype.concat. The getter runs mid-copy, shrinks the array and forces a garbage collection, and concat keeps copying against the pre-shrink element count - reading past the end of the backing store and handing out-of-bounds heap contents back to attacker JavaScript.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none - PR:N; no account, no prior foothold, nothing but getting the victim's browser to load the page
attack_vector.complexity: low - AC:L; the trigger is a short script with no timing or grooming precondition. The constraint is on the payoff, not the trigger: this is a read, so an attacker still needs to build a leak chain on it and then escape the renderer sandbox.
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Manual analysis of V8's elements kinds and the concat slow path by outside researchers - credited as Wen Xu of Tencent KeenLab, with the public exploit crediting @antlr7 and @oldfresher.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Chrome 49.0.2623.108 or later actually running - not merely staged - on every host, and every embedded Chromium runtime rebased off the Chromium 49 line.
prevention.adequacy: Adequate for the browser and inadequate for everything else. The update reaches Chrome automatically and reaches an Electron application only when its vendor rebases, which for an abandoned application never happens.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Renderer-crash telemetry and site-correlated tab-crash clustering, plus inventory that records the Chromium version inside every embedded runtime rather than only the browser.
detection.adequacy: Poor against a clean exploit. A successful out-of-bounds read produces no crash, no process, no file - the only reliable signal is exposure, which is why the inventory half matters more than the telemetry half here.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treat a browser or embedded-Chromium process that rendered untrusted content while below the fixed version as having leaked renderer memory: rotate session tokens and cookies reachable in that process and force a full browser relaunch across the fleet rather than waiting for natural restart.
response.adequacy: Bounded. Nothing distinguishes a host that was read from one that was not, so response has to be driven by exposure window rather than by evidence.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: Flaw remediation measured against installed package version marks a host fixed while its running renderer still executes the vulnerable V8 until the browser is relaunched.

NIST-800-53-SR-3.gap: Component inventory that stops at the vendor application never records the Chromium version embedded inside it, so the supply-chain control reports coverage it does not have.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: An auto-updating browser estate satisfies the article while the copies of V8 that do not ride Chrome's update channel stay unenumerated and unpatched.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: Assessed at application level the software looks supported and current; the failure is one layer down, in an embedded engine B4 never inspects.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: The control's scoping names web browsers; an application that embeds a browser engine is not obviously in scope, so maximum maturity on browser patching leaves the embedded population untouched.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: Obtaining vulnerability information presumes the register names the component. Organised by product name, it cannot answer which software embeds V8 or at what version.

new_control_requirements.name: BROWSER-MANAGED-UPDATE-NO-DEFERRAL
new_control_requirements.description: Enterprise update rings must not defer security-channel browser updates beyond 24h.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Google shipped the fix for this V8 out-of-bounds read in Chrome 49.0.2623.108 on 2016-03-24, and a working trigger plus an annotated exploit page were public in the same month. For Chrome the control is the whole remediation, and it has to be written to bite on the running browser rather than the staged package: an update ring that installs within 24 hours but never forces a relaunch leaves the pre-49.0.2623.108 V8 executing in long-lived sessions. CISA's 2022-06-08 KEV listing with a 2022-06-22 due date, and EPSS at 0.4811 / 98.75th percentile on 2026-08-13, show the exposure outliving the fix by six years on copies that were never made to restart.

new_control_requirements.name: TIER-3-DEPENDENCY-INVENTORY
new_control_requirements.description: Supply chain inventory must extend to tier-3 dependencies (dependencies of dependencies of direct dependencies). SBOM coverage for libsystemd-class transitive dependencies cannot be omitted under SR-3.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Chrome was fixed on 2016-03-24; V8 was not, everywhere else it lives. The same engine ships inside Chromium forks, Android System WebView and every Electron or CEF application pinned to Chromium 49, and those appear in an asset register under the application's own name with no Chromium version recorded at all. This control is what makes the question answerable: enumerate the embedded engine as a component in its own right, so that 'do we run V8 below 49.0.2623.108' can be answered from inventory rather than guessed. Without it a KEV entry with a public exploit page stays open on hosts the browser-patching report has already marked clean.

attack_vector.description: An unauthenticated SOAP request to the UDDI security service on SAP NetWeaver AS Java carries SQL inside the permissionId element of deletePermissionById, which the server concatenates into a query. The published exploit uses response timing as a boolean oracle to read the UME tables one character at a time and recover the SHA-512 password hash of the AS Java administrator account.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none - PR:N; the endpoint answers before any authentication decision is made
attack_vector.complexity: low - AC:L; the only requirement is network reachability of the AS Java instance port. Blind extraction is slow, but it is fully automated in public code and needs no version-specific tuning.
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Manual research by Vahagn Vardanyan of ERPScan into a default-enabled SOAP endpoint, reported to SAP on 2015-12-04.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: SAP Security Note 2101079 applied and the Java instance restarted. Where that could not be scheduled, blocking or authenticating /UDDISecurityService/ at the web dispatcher or reverse proxy in front of AS Java, and removing any exposure of the instance port to untrusted networks.
prevention.adequacy: The note is a complete fix; the filter is not. A path-based block holds only while no other route reaches the same servlet, and it does nothing about an attacker already inside a segment that legitimately reaches AS Java.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Reverse-proxy or dispatcher logging of request paths and bodies for the AS Java front end, forwarded off the host, plus database-side monitoring for repeated COUNT queries against the UME tables from the application connection pool.
detection.adequacy: Effective in principle because the attack is noisy - blind extraction means thousands of near-identical requests - but only where request-level logging exists in front of AS Java. Authentication logging alone sees nothing, because the attacker never authenticates.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treat any instance that was reachable while unpatched as having lost its UME contents: rotate the AS Java administrator and service-account credentials, force portal password resets, and review the database for other tables the attacker could have read, rather than closing on the support-package deployment.
response.adequacy: Applying the note stops further reads but does not invalidate a hash already extracted. Anything recoverable from that hash stays recoverable until the credential is changed, so patch-only closure leaves the actual asset - the administrator credential - in the attacker's hands.

NIST-800-53-SI-10.gap: Input-validation assurance built around the organisation's own code and configured interfaces never examines a default-enabled vendor SOAP handler that concatenates a request element into SQL.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: A fix existed from 2016, but SI-2 timelines do not model an SAP support-package deployment with an instance restart and a full regression cycle, so the control is met by a schedule that runs months behind.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: SAP notes are tracked on the Basis team's own cadence rather than in the enterprise vulnerability register, so an unapplied note is not visible as an open finding alongside everything else.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: The exposed endpoint is default-enabled and appears in no configuration document, so B4 evidence assembled from architecture and configured-interface reviews never records it as attack surface.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Maturity is measured against the named software categories, which do not include an ERP application server, so high maturity coexists with an unauthenticated 9.8 on the instance port.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.28.gap: Secure coding covers software the organisation develops; the injection is in vendor code, and the control places no obligation to require or verify the same standard from the platform supplier.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: Tracking SAP Security Notes satisfies the information-gathering half while the exposure-evaluation half never elevates a note with a public credential-extraction exploit above the routine queue.

OWASP-Top-10-2021-A03.gap: Injection testing is scoped to the applications the organisation runs, not to the platform hosting them; a WAF tuned for portal URLs is not inspecting SOAP bodies posted to the UDDI security service.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: SAP NetWeaver AS Java CVE-2016-2386 is unauthenticated, scores 9.8, and has had a scripted public exploit that extracts the Administrator or j2ee_admin SHA-512 hash since Exploit-DB 39840 on 2016-05-19; CISA listed it on 2022-06-09 with a 2022-06-30 due date and EPSS reads 0.7106 at the 99.349th percentile on 2026-08-13. SAP Security Note 2101079 is the binary fix but requires a support-package deployment and a Java instance restart, which is exactly why the control's compensating-control branch matters here: the four-hour action an operator can actually take is blocking or authenticating /UDDISecurityService/ at the web dispatcher, recorded as an interim mitigation with the note deployment scheduled behind it.

new_control_requirements.name: MITIGATION-ACTIVE-PATCH-PENDING-VERDICT-CLASS
new_control_requirements.description: Compliance verdicts must distinguish three states: (a) binary patch deployed (vulnerability eliminated), (b) vendor-mitigation rule active, no binary patch (residual risk: any defect in the mitigation rule reopens the vulnerability), (c) no mitigation, no patch (full exposure). Audit reports must surface (b) as a distinct compensating-control state with an associated time-bound action item, not as a 'patched per SLA' outcome.
new_control_requirements.evidence: The realistic interim posture for an AS Java estate is state (b): SAP Security Note 2101079 queued behind the next support-package window while a dispatcher rule blocks /UDDISecurityService/. That rule is a path filter in front of a servlet, so any alternate route to the same endpoint, any bypass of the dispatcher, or any attacker already inside a segment that legitimately reaches port 50000 reopens the full unauthenticated SQL-injection path against the UME tables. Recording that state as 'patched per SLA' is what lets a 2016 note with a public exploit sit unapplied on a 7.1-7.5 instance for years; recording it as a distinct compensating-control state with a deployment date is what forces the restart to be scheduled.

attack_vector.description: An unauthenticated HTTP request to a Web Dynpro test or utility application shipped with SAP NetWeaver AS Java - JWFTestAddAssignees, or the real-time-collaboration Chat and Messages resources - drives a user-search dialog that returns the platform's user list to the caller. No session, no role and no UME permission is involved because the endpoint answers before any access decision.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none - PR:N; the endpoints are served anonymously under a documented path prefix
attack_vector.complexity: low - AC:L; an ordinary browser navigation. The only precondition is reachability of the AS Java instance port.
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Manual exploration of default-shipped Web Dynpro applications by Vahagn Vardanyan of ERPScan, reported to SAP on 2015-09-15.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: SAP Security Note 2256846 applied with a Java instance restart, and - independently of the note - denying unauthenticated access at the web dispatcher to the /webdynpro/resources/sap.com/ test and utility applications no business process uses.
prevention.adequacy: The note fixes the named component. The dispatcher deny is broader and more durable but only if it is written against the path prefix rather than the single application in the advisory - blocking JWFTestAddAssignees alone leaves the Chat and Messages resources in the public exploit still answering.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Request-path logging in front of AS Java forwarded off-host, alerting on anonymous requests to /webdynpro/resources/sap.com/ paths, and correlation of those requests with subsequent SOAP traffic to the UDDI endpoint on the same instance.
detection.adequacy: Only works where request-level logging exists ahead of the Java stack. Authentication logging sees nothing at all here, because the attacker never authenticates and the transaction looks like an ordinary anonymous page fetch.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treat an instance that was anonymously reachable while unpatched as having leaked its user directory: assume the account names are known to an attacker, review the paired CVE-2016-2386 exposure on the same host, and drive credential and MFA posture for the disclosed accounts rather than closing on the support-package deployment.
response.adequacy: Bounded and permanent. Applying the note stops further enumeration but does not un-disclose account names already read, and account names are not rotatable - the response is to raise the cost of using them, not to invalidate them.

NIST-800-53-AC-3.gap: The endpoints answer before any access decision, so role assignments and UME permissions are never consulted; an AC-3 assessment sampling business transactions passes while the user directory is read anonymously.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: A 5.3 note loses the AS Java support-package window to higher-scored items, which is defensible on CVSS and wrong in fact given that this disclosure is the enabling step for the 9.8 injection on the same server.

NIS2-Art21-network-security.gap: Network-security evidence enumerates deployed business services; the exposed surface is a set of platform-shipped test applications that no such inventory records.

UK-CAF-B2.gap: Identity and access processes can all be sound while the directory of identities is anonymously readable; CAF has no question that surfaces anonymous user enumeration.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Priority is driven by severity and by named software categories, both of which push an ERP-platform 5.3 below the threshold that gets acted on.

ISO-27001-2022-A.5.15.gap: The approved access-control rules govern the portal's business applications; the platform's default-shipped Web Dynpro utilities sit outside the policy entirely.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: Exposure evaluated per CVE rates this low; evaluated as the reconnaissance step of the chain it is part of, it is not low, and nothing in the control forces the chained reading.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CISA listed SAP NetWeaver CVE-2016-2388 on 2022-06-09 alongside CVE-2016-2386 against the same product, both due 2022-06-30, and a public exploit for the disclosure has existed since Exploit-DB 39841 on 2016-05-19; EPSS reads 0.51553 at the 98.844th percentile on 2026-08-13 despite the 5.3 rating. Binding the clock to the KEV listing rather than to the CVSS band is the point for this entry, because a 5.3 information leak never wins an AS Java support-package window on severity alone. SAP Security Note 2256846 requires a Java instance restart, so the mitigation deployable inside the clock is the documented compensating control - a web dispatcher deny on the unauthenticated /webdynpro/resources/sap.com/ test applications - with the note deployment scheduled behind it.

new_control_requirements.name: MITIGATION-ACTIVE-PATCH-PENDING-VERDICT-CLASS
new_control_requirements.description: Compliance verdicts must distinguish three states: (a) binary patch deployed (vulnerability eliminated), (b) vendor-mitigation rule active, no binary patch (residual risk: any defect in the mitigation rule reopens the vulnerability), (c) no mitigation, no patch (full exposure). Audit reports must surface (b) as a distinct compensating-control state with an associated time-bound action item, not as a 'patched per SLA' outcome.
new_control_requirements.evidence: The interim posture for this CVE is a path-based deny in front of AS Java, and its defect surface is specific and known: ERPSCAN-16-010 names JWFTestAddAssignees while the public exploit source names two further resources, rtc~coll.appl.rtc~wd_chat Chat and Messages, so a rule written from the advisory alone leaves the other two answering anonymously. That is exactly state (b) - a mitigation rule whose own gaps reopen the exposure - and recording it as 'patched per SLA' hides both the residual anonymous-read path and the fact that SAP Security Note 2256846 and its instance restart are still outstanding. Surfacing it as a distinct compensating-control state also keeps the access-control claim honest: the organisation is asserting a proxy filter, not that its access-enforcement or identity controls cover these endpoints, which they do not.

CVE-2016-3393.name: Microsoft Windows Graphics Device Interface (GDI) Remote Code Execution Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: A crafted TrueType font makes win32k.sys overflow the size calculation in cjComputeGLYPHSET_MSFT_GENERAL while parsing the cmap table, so the kernel allocates an undersized buffer and the per-segment write loop overruns it into adjacent pool memory. Loaded from memory with AddFontMemResourceEx by a process the attacker already controlled, that corruption escapes the browser sandbox and elevates to SYSTEM.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none as scored - PR:N - but the honest reading is that the attacker needed prior code execution on the host, which the observed chain obtained with a separate browser exploit before this module ran
attack_vector.complexity: low - AC:L; the font is fully attacker-controlled so the overflow length and contents are chosen rather than discovered. The real constraint is kernel pool grooming to place a useful object after the undersized allocation.
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Caught by Kaspersky Lab's exploit-detection telemetry on live attack traffic and root-caused by human reverse engineering; no AI-branded research arm or automated discovery is involved.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: MS16-120 deployed with a reboot, across the Windows graphics component and the Office, Skype for Business, Silverlight and Lync components in the same bulletin. Preventing the first stage matters as much: this module only ran because a browser exploit had already succeeded, so browser and plugin currency is part of the prevention story for a kernel bug.
prevention.adequacy: Complete from October 2016 for hosts that could take the update, and unavailable now for the population that still needs it. Every Windows line named here is past end of support, so on those hosts the only real prevention is rebuilding onto a supported OS.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Behavioural endpoint telemetry on in-memory font loading and on process-lineage anomalies - PowerShell descending from a content-rendering process - shipped off-host. Kernel-fault telemetry catches the failed attempts.
detection.adequacy: This is the only stage where an operator had a chance, and most did not take it. Nothing is written to disk, no service or scheduled task is created and no signature exists for a zero-day, so file-oriented and signature-oriented tooling produced no signal at all.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treat a host where this fired as kernel-compromised: rebuild rather than clean, rotate every credential that was cached or used on it during the exposure window, and escalate on the attribution rather than closing the alert as a PowerShell malware infection.
response.adequacy: Rebuild is the only defensible outcome once SYSTEM was reached through a kernel defect, and the point at which most responses fail is classification - the visible artefacts are PowerShell activity, which triage routinely dispositions as commodity.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: Windows update compliance can read complete while the same bulletin's Office, Skype for Business, Silverlight and Lync components remain unpatched, and SI-2 has no state for a fix whose target OS is out of support.

NIST-800-53-SI-4.gap: Signature and file-write monitoring saw nothing: the font was loaded from memory and the payload was PowerShell. Detection required behavioural telemetry most SI-4 attestations do not describe.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: Complete patch-management evidence for the supported estate says nothing about the unsupported hosts, which is where every remaining instance of this exposure lives.

NIS2-Art21-incident-handling.gap: The visible stage is PowerShell activity, which standard triage closes as a commodity infection - under-scoping an intrusion in which the attacker held kernel privilege.

UK-CAF-C1.gap: Monitoring evidenced by log coverage and file/process-creation use cases has no rule that fires on an in-memory font load followed by PowerShell from a sandboxed process.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: The maturity self-assessment records patching cadence for supported hosts; the requirement that operating systems remain vendor-supported is where the estate carrying this CVE actually fails.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: A register entry offering MS16-120 as the treatment understates the finding: a host still missing a 2016 kernel bulletin needs rebuilding, not a bulletin.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.16.gap: Monitoring baselines built on network flow and authentication anomalies contain no signal from in-memory font loading or from browser-spawned PowerShell, so the control operates while blind to this chain.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Microsoft Windows CVE-2016-3393 was a zero-day in win32k.sys used by the FruityArmor APT as the sandbox-escape and elevation stage of a live chain before MS16-120 shipped in October 2016; CISA listed it on 2022-05-25 with a 2022-06-15 due date and EPSS reads 0.68684 at the 99.278th percentile on 2026-08-13. The control has to be applied with the reboot counted, because the fix is in a kernel driver and a host that has taken the update but not restarted is still running the vulnerable parser. Where the host is on a Windows line that can no longer receive MS16-120 - which is every line the NVD record names - the mitigation deployable inside the clock is isolation with a dated rebuild onto a supported OS, recorded as the compensating control rather than as a patch exception with no end.

new_control_requirements.name: NATION-STATE-INITIAL-ACCESS-IR-ESCALATION
new_control_requirements.description: IR runbooks must include an explicit nation-state-initial-access escalation path triggered by APT28/APT29/Lazarus/Volt-Typhoon/etc. attribution on a confirmed exploit chain. Standard malware-infection IR under-escalates nation-state activity by treating it as commodity threat.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Kaspersky documents this exact failure mode for CVE-2016-3393: FruityArmor ran a browser exploit, then this in-memory kernel elevation loaded through AddFontMemResourceEx, then a PowerShell meterpreter payload on a platform built entirely around PowerShell. The only stage a defender sees without behavioural kernel telemetry is the PowerShell activity, which standard triage closes as a commodity infection - and that disposition is wrong by an order of magnitude, because the attacker reached SYSTEM through a win32k.sys pool overflow and the host cannot be cleaned, only rebuilt. The escalation path this control requires is what converts a PowerShell alert on a host missing MS16-120 into a kernel-compromise response with full credential rotation for the exposure window.

CVE-2016-5198.name: Google Chromium V8 Out-of-Bounds Memory Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: A crafted page warms JavaScript functions until V8 optimises them against an assumption about a global object's map that the runtime can still invalidate. Once the assumption is broken the optimised code reads and writes the object through a layout that no longer matches it, giving the attacker arbitrary read and write across the renderer heap and, from there, code execution in the renderer.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none - PR:N; the attacker needs only to have the page loaded
attack_vector.complexity: low - AC:L; the only precondition is enough iterations to reach the optimising compiler, which plain loops satisfy. The residual constraint is the sandbox: in Chrome the payoff is renderer-scope until a separate escape is chained, whereas in a weakly confined embedded runtime it is host-scope immediately.
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Human analysis of V8's optimisation and deoptimisation behaviour, credited to Tencent Keen Security Lab.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Chrome 54.0.2840.87 / 54.0.2840.90 / 54.0.2840.85 or later actually running after a full browser relaunch, and every embedded Chromium runtime rebased off the Chromium 54 line.
prevention.adequacy: Adequate where the update channel reaches. It does not reach Electron, CEF or WebView copies pinned to Chromium 54, and for an application whose vendor no longer rebases there is no fix at all - only removal.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Renderer-crash telemetry correlated by site, child-process monitoring on Electron and CEF applications, and inventory that records the embedded Chromium version rather than only the application version.
detection.adequacy: Weak for the browser case, where a clean exploit leaves nothing on disk and no new process. Stronger for the embedded case, where weak renderer confinement means successful exploitation usually produces an observable child process or outbound connection.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treat any process that rendered untrusted content on a pre-fix engine as having executed attacker code: rotate credentials and session tokens available to it, and for embedded runtimes with host-level reach, triage the host rather than closing on a version bump.
response.adequacy: Scoping is driven by exposure window, not evidence - there is no artefact that separates a host that was exploited from one that merely could have been.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: Remediation measured at install time marks the host fixed while the running renderer keeps executing the vulnerable V8 until the browser relaunches.

NIST-800-53-SC-39.gap: Process isolation attested for the browser does not describe the embedded runtimes on the same host, where the identical primitive escalates from page scope to host scope.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: The article is satisfied by the auto-updating population and silent about the embedded copies that do not take the vendor's update channel.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: Assessed at application level the software is supported and current; the unmaintained engine inside it is never inspected.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Scoping names web browsers, so an application that embeds a browser engine falls outside it even at the highest maturity level.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: A register organised by product name cannot answer which software embeds V8 or at what version, so exposure evaluation is impossible even where vulnerability information is being collected diligently.

new_control_requirements.name: BROWSER-MANAGED-UPDATE-NO-DEFERRAL
new_control_requirements.description: Enterprise update rings must not defer security-channel browser updates beyond 24h.
new_control_requirements.evidence: This V8 defect gives arbitrary read and write in the renderer from a crafted page with no chained second bug, and a working trigger is public in js-vuln-db with the Tencent Keen Security Lab credit and Chromium issue 659475. Google fixed it in Chrome 54.0.2840.87 (Windows/Mac), 54.0.2840.90 (Linux) and 54.0.2840.85 (Android). The control has to be enforced on the running browser, not the staged package - Chrome swaps in the fixed V8 only on relaunch, so a 24-hour install ring without a forced restart still leaves the pre-54.0.2840.x engine executing. CISA's 2022-06-08 KEV listing with a 2022-06-22 due date, and EPSS 0.34814 at the 98.282nd percentile on 2026-08-13, are what deferral costs.

new_control_requirements.name: TIER-3-DEPENDENCY-INVENTORY
new_control_requirements.description: Supply chain inventory must extend to tier-3 dependencies (dependencies of dependencies of direct dependencies). SBOM coverage for libsystemd-class transitive dependencies cannot be omitted under SR-3.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Chrome took the 54.0.2840.x fix automatically; the copies of V8 inside Chromium forks, Android System WebView and Electron or CEF applications pinned to Chromium 54 did not, and they appear in the asset register under the application's own name with no engine version recorded. That is the population still exposed to a published arbitrary-read/write trigger, and it is also the population where the primitive is worth most, because those runtimes confine renderer content far less than Chrome does. Enumerating the embedded Chromium as a component in its own right is what makes 'do we still run V8 below 54.0.2840.87' answerable from inventory instead of assumed from the browser-patching report.

CVE-2016-7256.name: Microsoft Windows Open Type Font Remote Code Execution Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: A crafted embedded font in a web page or a document is parsed by the kernel-mode ATMFD font driver, which mishandles it and lets the attacker execute code with the driver's privilege. The observed samples carried per-victim hardcoded kernel addresses, so a second tool generated the font once the target's memory layout was known.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; the attacker needs no account on the target, only the ability to place content in front of it
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L with UI:R; the trigger is a page view or a document open, and the only real work is the per-target address patching the escalation needed
attack_vector.ai_factor: None claimed by any source. Microsoft's write-up describes scripted generation of the exploit font from the target's kernel layout, which is ordinary tooling, not AI-assisted discovery or weaponization.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Installing MS16-132 (KB3199120) on release, or — where the patch window was longer than days — applying the bulletin's own workaround immediately by renaming atmfd.dll or setting DisableATMFD to 1 and restarting.
prevention.adequacy: The patch is complete for hosts that can take it, but by 2022 the KEV listing was mostly an instruction to find machines that could not: Vista, 7, 8.1 and Server 2008/2012 hosts get nothing. The workaround is the only control that works on those, and it costs correct rendering of embedded OpenType fonts.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alerting on kernel bugchecks correlated with recent rendering of untrusted content, and on Henkray-family implant detections; both were available signals during the 2016 campaign.
detection.adequacy: Weak and late. A successful exploit produces no crash, and a kernel-level implant installed by a driver-privilege primitive is well placed to blind endpoint tooling. Detection here bounds dwell time; it does not prevent the compromise.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating a host that rendered attacker content while unpatched as compromised at kernel level: rebuild from known-good media and rotate every credential that was used on or cached by that machine.
response.adequacy: Correct but expensive, and it depends on knowing which hosts were exposed. Applying MS16-132 to a machine that already ran the exploit removes the flaw and leaves the implant.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: Installing KB3199120 satisfies flaw remediation, but SI-2's cadence does not react to the Exploited: Yes flag Microsoft set on 2016-11-08, and it produces no output at all for the out-of-support Windows lines that make up most of the affected list.

NIST-800-53-CM-7.gap: Least-functionality baselines enumerate services and ports, not kernel-mode font parsing, so the atmfd.dll rename and the DisableATMFD registry value — both documented by the vendor and available without a patch window — never appear as candidate hardening on a CM-7 attestation.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: Article 21 gets MS16-132 scheduled but treats this CVE identically to the three non-exploited CVEs in the same KB, and it has no mechanism to escalate an estate whose platform can no longer receive the fix.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: B4 maintenance evidence reads clean because the vulnerable component is an uninventoried kernel driver, and the delivery path is normal business activity — viewing a page, opening a document — which no user-facing control constrains.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Patch-timer maturity is meaningless nine years after release; the binding Essential Eight requirement for this CVE is vendor-supported operating systems, and an estate can show full patch compliance while running Windows 7 hosts that will never receive another ATMFD fix.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: The technical-vulnerability process ingests the bulletin and schedules it, but is not required to treat the vendor's exploited flag as a distinct severity input, nor to record that a compensating control existed on day one that was faster than the patch window.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Microsoft published MS16-132 (KB3199120) on 2016-11-08 with CVE-2016-7256 already marked Exploited: Yes, against Henkray operators who had been active since June 2016. The 'documented compensating controls' clause is the load-bearing half for this Windows font driver: the bulletin's own atmfd.dll rename and the DisableATMFD registry value were deployable the same day, without waiting for a patch window, on every affected build from Windows 8 upward. CISA's own clock (KEV 2022-05-25, due 2022-06-15) is a 21-day window on a flaw whose EPSS still reads 0.64835 at the 99.175th percentile on 2026-08-13.

new_control_requirements.name: BUG-FAMILY-MITIGATION-PERSISTENCE
new_control_requirements.description: When a CVE patch lands, retain the pre-patch compensating controls (module blacklists, sysctl restrictions) until the patched code has soaked for a stated review period. Patches for one bug in a primitive class can introduce sibling bugs in the same class; the original compensating control may still apply to the sibling.
new_control_requirements.evidence: MS16-132 fixed two ATMFD bugs at once — CVE-2016-7256 (this one, RCE) and CVE-2016-7210 (information disclosure) — and Microsoft was still issuing font-parsing guidance for the same component years later, with the DisableATMFD registry workaround reappearing verbatim in later Type 1 font-parsing advisories. An estate that set DisableATMFD to 1 in November 2016 and left it set was covered for the whole family; one that reverted it after installing KB3199120 re-enrolled itself in every subsequent ATMFD defect on Windows 7 and 8.1 hosts that had no need for embedded OpenType fonts in the first place.

CVE-2017-0022.name: Microsoft XML Core Services Information Disclosure Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: A page instantiates Microsoft.XMLDOM and asks it to load a res:// URI naming a local file. Absent files return error 0x80070485 from the failed LoadLibraryExW; present files return 0x80004005 when the retrieved resource fails DTD parsing. The difference is a reliable file-existence oracle over arbitrary paths, used to decide whether the machine is a real victim before any payload is served.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; the attacker needs only to get content in front of the browser
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L with UI:R; deterministic, one probe per path, no memory manipulation and no bootstrap primitive required
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Found by Trend Micro and Proofpoint reverse engineering captured AdGholas and Neutrino samples and reported to Microsoft in September 2016.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Denying ActiveX and active scripting in the Internet zone, or removing Internet Explorer as a usable browser — either removes the instantiation path without depending on a patch, and would have covered the whole July 2016 to March 2017 zero-day window.
prevention.adequacy: Complete for the delivery path, but it is a browser-configuration decision an operator must have taken in advance; nothing in the vulnerability-management cycle produces it, and it does not reach the Windows Embedded Compact 7 devices in the affected list.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Proxy or endpoint inspection flagging res:// URIs naming local binaries in externally sourced HTML, and alerting on Microsoft.XMLDOM instantiation from a browser rendering external content.
detection.adequacy: Useful and cheap, but it only sees the reconnaissance stage. By design the operators served nothing further to hosts that looked instrumented, so the machines most likely to generate the alert are the ones that were never going to be exploited.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating a host that produced this traffic as having been profiled, and hunting for the follow-on exploit the profile was selecting for, rather than closing the ticket on a 6.5 information disclosure.
response.adequacy: Correct framing, rarely applied. The CVSS score invites closure; the operational meaning is that someone measured this machine and decided what to send it next.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: Flaw remediation had nothing to remediate for the eight months this was a zero-day inside a commercial exploit kit, and it does not require the alternative — removing the ActiveX delivery path — to be considered at all.

NIST-800-53-CM-7.gap: Least-functionality baselines do not enumerate legacy browser ActiveX hosting as a disableable function, which is the one control that closes this oracle without a patch, and they do not extend to Windows Embedded Compact 7 devices carrying the same MSXML surface.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: Article 21 schedules the March 2017 rollup and stops there; it has no mechanism to raise priority because this CVE is the third file-probing primitive the same actor used after CVE-2016-3298 and CVE-2016-3351 were patched.

NIS2-Art21-vulnerability-management.gap: Handling each CVE as a discrete finding hides the sequence. Nothing in the obligation records that a patched primitive was replaced twice by the same operator, which is the evidence that the class, not the instance, needed the response.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: B4 can be met with default Internet Explorer ActiveX behaviour across the estate — the exact precondition this bug needs — and its asset scope rarely reaches the embedded devices Microsoft patched separately in June 2017.

AU-Essential-8-App-Hardening.gap: Hardening evidence concentrates on Java, Flash and Office macros; an attestation covering those passes while Microsoft.XMLDOM instantiation through mshtml stays available on the same host.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Time-from-release measurement gives nothing for a zero-day window and nothing for Windows Embedded Compact 7, which will receive no further updates.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: The process schedules by CVSS, and a 6.5 information disclosure loses every prioritisation contest on a Patch Tuesday — even though its function is to raise the success rate of the higher-scored exploits fired after it.

new_control_requirements.name: INCOMPLETE-PATCH-SEQUENCE-SEVERITY-MULTIPLIER
new_control_requirements.description: Vulnerability-management programs must apply a severity multiplier when a CVE is the Nth in an incomplete-patch sequence on the same primitive (third MOTW bypass, second AMSI bypass, etc.). Framework controls treating each CVE as discrete obscure the structural defect; the Nth CVE in a sequence implies that future bypasses on the same primitive are likely.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2017-0022 is the third file-presence-probing primitive the AdGholas operators used in succession: they ran CVE-2016-3298 and CVE-2016-3351 for the same purpose, and moved to the MSXML res:// oracle after Microsoft patched those. Each was triaged as a discrete moderate-severity Windows information disclosure — this one at CVSS 6.5 — and each was patched individually, so nothing in the pipeline recorded that the sandbox-fingerprinting capability itself was being re-acquired every few months. A programme that had scored the primitive rather than the instance would have treated the MSXML surface, and the Internet Explorer ActiveX path that reaches it, as a standing exposure rather than a 6.5 to be scheduled.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Microsoft fixed this MSXML oracle on 2017-03-14, after it had run as a zero-day in AdGholas from July 2016 and in Neutrino EK from September 2016. The compensating-controls clause is what mattered during that window and still matters for the Windows Embedded Compact 7 devices in the affected list: denying ActiveX and active scripting in the Internet zone removes the Microsoft.XMLDOM instantiation path without any vendor update. CISA's listing (2022-05-24, due 2022-06-14) puts a 21-day clock on a CVE whose EPSS still reads 0.18069 at the 96.927th percentile on 2026-08-13.

CVE-2017-0147.name: Microsoft Windows SMBv1 Information Disclosure Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: An unauthenticated peer sends crafted SMBv1 transaction requests to 445/tcp and reads back kernel pool memory the request never owned — connection, session and tree-connect addresses and a pool list pointer. Those addresses make the type-confusion write primitive in the same bulletin reliable, and the chain finishes by overwriting the session as an administrator and running a psexec-style payload as SYSTEM.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; SMBv1 grants the anonymous IPC$ session the leak needs before any authentication takes place
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L with UI:N; one TCP connection, no user action, no grooming for the read half. The only constraints are SMBv1 enabled (the default on every affected build) and 445 reachable
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. The working exploits came from the leaked Equation Group tooling published by the Shadow Brokers on 2017-04-14, a month after Microsoft patched.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Disabling SMB1.0/CIFS File Sharing Support estate-wide, which removes the vulnerable server outright and does not depend on a patch level, alongside applying MS17-010 and blocking 445/tcp at every segment boundary.
prevention.framework_requiring_it: CISA BOD 22-01 (KEV remediation, added 2022-05-24, due 2022-06-14, ransomware: Known)
prevention.adequacy: The patch closes this CVE; disabling SMBv1 closes the whole protocol and everything found in it since. Neither reaches the non-Windows SMBv1 servers on the same network — storage heads, imaging devices, industrial equipment — for which isolation or replacement is the only answer.

detection.what_would_have_worked: SMB-protocol-aware inspection alarming on NT_TRANSACT / NT_TRANSACT_SECONDARY pairs with an undersized MaxBufferSize, and on anonymous IPC$ tree-connect sweeps followed by SVCCTL service creation.
detection.adequacy: It works, but it must be in place before the event and most estates only inspect SMB at the perimeter, where this traffic never travels. The leak stage itself is silent on the host — nothing crashes and no authentication event is generated.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating a host that answered this traffic as SYSTEM-compromised: isolate, rebuild, and rotate every credential cached on or used from it, then sweep for lateral SMB movement to the rest of the segment.
response.adequacy: This is the right response and it is also the one the ransomware history shows nobody had rehearsed. By the time WannaCry and NotPetya made the movement visible, the propagation had already outrun the response.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: Deploying KB4013389 satisfies the control, but SI-2 measures package deployment rather than whether a deprecated protocol was ever needed, and it has no scope over embedded SMBv1 servers on the same network.

NIST-800-53-CM-7.gap: Least-functionality attestations list file and print sharing as required without distinguishing SMBv1 from SMBv2/3, so the deprecated dialect the bulletin's own workaround removes stays enabled.

NIST-800-53-SC-7.gap: Boundary protection is evidenced at the internet edge; the MS17-010 family propagates on internal 445/tcp, and an estate with 445 blocked outbound and open everywhere inside passes SC-7 while remaining the exact topology the worms were built for.

NIST-800-53-SI-4.gap: Monitoring keyed on malware detections and authentication anomalies sees nothing during the leak stage, which is well-formed SMB traffic over an anonymous session; the first observable event is service creation after the write has already run.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: The obligation schedules the bulletin but never requires protocol removal over patching, and gives no path for estates on Windows lines that receive no further SMBv1 fixes.

NIS2-Art21-network-security.gap: Having segmentation satisfies the obligation; proving it blocks lateral SMB reachability specifically does not, which is the only version of the control that would have contained this propagation path.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: A fully patched Windows estate evidences B4 while SMBv1 stays enabled on hosts and on the appliances beside them, because B4's asset scope and the Windows patch scope are different sets.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Time-to-patch from 2017-03-14 is no longer the operative measure; the binding requirement is vendor-supported operating systems, and most lines here receive nothing further.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: Scored on its own as an Important-rated 7.5 information disclosure, this CVE is deprioritised beneath the Critical RCEs in the same bulletin that it exists to make reliable.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.22.gap: Segregation is documented rather than demonstrated; A.8.22 accepts a network diagram where the control that mattered was a proven inability to reach 445/tcp across segment boundaries.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: MS17-010 (KB4013389) shipped 2017-03-14; the Shadow Brokers published the working Equation Group SMB tooling on 2017-04-14 and WannaCry followed in May 2017, so the interval between patch availability and mass exploitation of this Windows SMBv1 server flaw was measured in weeks. CISA's KEV entry (added 2022-05-24, due 2022-06-14) records knownRansomwareCampaignUse as Known, and EPSS still reads 0.99693 at the 99.95th percentile on 2026-08-13. The documented-compensating-controls clause is what makes this control deployable on the affected hosts that can no longer take a Microsoft update: disabling SMB1.0/CIFS File Sharing Support removes the vulnerable server without any patch.

new_control_requirements.name: BUG-FAMILY-MITIGATION-PERSISTENCE
new_control_requirements.description: When a CVE patch lands, retain the pre-patch compensating controls (module blacklists, sysctl restrictions) until the patched code has soaked for a stated review period. Patches for one bug in a primitive class can introduce sibling bugs in the same class; the original compensating control may still apply to the sibling.
new_control_requirements.evidence: MS17-010 fixed six SMBv1 defects at once — CVE-2017-0143 through CVE-2017-0148 — of which this CVE is the disclosure primitive that makes the others reliable. An estate that disabled SMB1.0/CIFS File Sharing Support in March 2017 and left it disabled was outside WannaCry, NotPetya and BadRabbit regardless of patch state; one that re-enabled the feature after KB4013389 landed put itself back in scope for every SMBv1 defect found since. Nine years on, EPSS 0.99693 at the 99.95th percentile shows the protocol, not the individual CVE, is what is still being attacked.

CVE-2017-15944.name: Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS Remote Code Execution Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: An unauthenticated request to the PAN-OS management web interface corrupts a PHP session file through a broken strtok()-based parser, passing the authentication filter. XML injection in the administrator handler then creates an attacker-named directory anywhere on disk, and a root cron script that feeds unquoted find output into a second find executes commands from that directory name as root. The result is root on the firewall with no credentials.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; the first stage is reachable on the management interface before any authentication
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L with UI:N; every stage is deterministic. The practical gates are management-interface reachability and the 15-minute cron tick before the root step fires
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Manual reverse engineering of PAN-OS PHP, a shared object and a shell script by Philip Pettersson, reported to the vendor on 2017-07-09.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Binding the management interface to a dedicated management network with permitted-IP access lists — which removes reachability of the entry endpoint entirely — plus upgrading to 6.1.19 / 7.0.19 / 7.1.14 / 8.0.6, and installing content update 756 for signatures 40483 and 40484 as the interim step that needs no reboot.
prevention.adequacy: Reachability restriction is the strongest of the three and the only one available immediately, but it is unavailable where management must stay reachable for operational reasons, and it does nothing against an attacker who already has a foothold on the management network. The signature mitigation is a compensating control whose own defects reopen the path.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Forwarding PAN-OS management-plane and authentication logs to a SIEM in a separate trust zone, and alerting on unauthenticated hits to /esp/cms_changeDeviceContext.esp and on genindex_batch.sh spawning an interpreter.
detection.adequacy: Only works if the telemetry left the device before the compromise. The chain ends as root on the appliance, so anything retained locally is under the attacker's control — on-box logging is not a detection control for this class of finding.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating a reachable, unpatched appliance as compromised: capture the configuration, rebuild from a known-good image, rotate administrator credentials, API keys and certificates, and check for /api/c.php and a setuid /bin/x before deciding the device is clean.
response.adequacy: This is the correct response and the one patch-in-place skips. Upgrading to 8.0.6 removes the three defects; it does not remove a web shell or a setuid binary that was already written.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: The standard flaw-remediation clock for an appliance is the next reboot window, which is the wrong tier for pre-auth root RCE on the trust boundary, and SI-2 gives no credit for the vendor's no-reboot content-update mitigation.

NIST-800-53-SC-7.gap: SC-7 evidence describes traffic policy on the data plane and passes while the management web interface — the entry point — answers on a data interface or from an untrusted segment.

NIST-800-53-SI-4.gap: Monitoring relies on logs the firewall stores locally, and this chain ends with root on that firewall, so the telemetry meant to detect the compromise is owned by the attacker unless it was already forwarded out of the trust zone.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: The firewall is scheduled as one asset among many, with no distinct tier for the perimeter enforcement point and no separate tracking for the interim signature path.

NIS2-Art21-network-security.gap: Having a firewall satisfies the obligation; nothing in it addresses which network that firewall's own management interface sits on, which is the whole precondition for the chain.

NIS2-Art21-incident-handling.gap: The runbook is written for detection and notification, not for the perimeter-device case where patch-in-place leaves the attacker's web shell at /api/c.php and setuid binary at /bin/x untouched.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: B4 evidence for a firewall centres on policy correctness and firmware currency, so an operator can hold B4 while the appliance's web management answers requests from a user VLAN.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: All four fixed branches (6.1, 7.0, 7.1, 8.0) are now end of life, so patch-timing maturity has nothing to measure — the binding requirement is vendor support, met only by migration or replacement.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: The process cannot distinguish a device protected by content update 756 signatures from one running 8.0.6, so an audit records the same outcome for a compensating control and an actual fix.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.22.gap: A documented management VLAN satisfies A.8.22 without any demonstration that the PAN-OS management interface refuses connections originating anywhere else.

new_control_requirements.name: PERIMETER-DEVICE-ZERODAY-SLA-TIER
new_control_requirements.description: Compliance frameworks must define a distinct patch SLA tier for pre-auth RCE on perimeter-trust-boundary devices (firewalls, VPN concentrators, WAFs, edge load-balancers). Tier requirement: vendor-mitigation deployed within 4 hours of KEV listing OR isolation of the vulnerable interface; standard 14/30-day SLAs do not apply because the device IS the trust boundary.
new_control_requirements.evidence: PAN-OS and Panorama are the perimeter enforcement point, and this is unauthenticated root on their management web interface with a public Metasploit module (Exploit-DB 44597, modules/exploits/linux/http/panos_readsessionvars.rb) available since 2018-05-08. The tier's two alternatives are both concretely available for this product: Palo Alto's content update 756 with signatures 40483 and 40484 deploys without the reboot the PAN-OS upgrade to 6.1.19 / 7.0.19 / 7.1.14 / 8.0.6 requires, and isolating the vulnerable interface means binding management to a dedicated network with permitted-IP lists. A standard 30-day appliance window against CISA's KEV listing of 2022-08-18 and an EPSS of 0.9834 at the 99.914th percentile leaves the trust boundary itself exploitable for a month.

new_control_requirements.name: PERIMETER-COMPROMISE-REBUILD-NOT-PATCH
new_control_requirements.description: Pre-rehearsed IR runbook for any perimeter device that suffers a pre-auth RCE CVE in active exploitation MUST default to config-exfil + rebuild + credential rotation, not patch-in-place. Patch-in-place leaves attacker-installed implants intact.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Pettersson's published exploit for this PAN-OS chain ends by writing a web shell to /api/c.php and a setuid-root binary to /bin/x. Upgrading the firewall to 8.0.6 repairs readSessionVarsFromFile(), the getXpath XML injection and genindex_batch.sh, and removes neither artefact — so an operator who patched a reachable appliance after the 2022-08-18 KEV listing and closed the ticket has a remediated vulnerability and a live implant on the trust boundary. The runbook has to default to capturing the configuration, rebuilding from known-good image, and rotating administrator credentials, API keys and certificates.

new_control_requirements.name: FIREWALL-EGRESS-TELEMETRY-SEPARATE-TRUST-ZONE
new_control_requirements.description: Firewall and other perimeter-trust-boundary devices must forward syslog, threat logs, and authentication logs to a SIEM hosted in a separate trust zone (different management plane, different credentials, different authentication path). Telemetry stored on the compromised device is destroyed by the attacker; telemetry on a separate-trust-zone collector survives.
new_control_requirements.evidence: The only host-side evidence that this chain ran — unauthenticated requests to /esp/cms_changeDeviceContext.esp, the anomalous directory under /opt/pancfg/session/pan/user_tmp/, genindex_batch.sh spawning an interpreter as root — is produced by the very device the chain ends up owning as root. On a PAN-OS appliance where logs stay local, an attacker who completed the chain controls the record of it. Forwarding management-plane and authentication logs to a collector with different credentials and a different authentication path is what makes the 2022-08-18 KEV listing actionable as a retrospective hunt rather than only as a patch instruction.

CVE-2017-5030.name: Google Chromium V8 Memory Corruption Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: A page defines an Array subclass whose Symbol.species getter returns a Proxy, so attacker script runs inside Array.prototype.concat. That callback truncates the array and forces a garbage collection, moving the elements backing store while concat still holds the old pointer, and the following accesses fall outside the live allocation.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; the attacker needs only to get JavaScript in front of the browser, including via a third-party ad or iframe
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L with UI:R; the trigger is pure script with no bootstrap primitive required. The remaining work is heap shaping and a separate sandbox escape, because V8 runs in the renderer
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Credited to Brendon Tiszka from manual analysis of V8's Array.prototype.concat implementation, reported January 2017.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Running Chrome 57.0.2987.98 or later and confirming the browser process actually relaunched onto it, plus applying the same version discipline to every Chromium-derived browser and embedded Chromium runtime in the estate.
prevention.adequacy: Complete for the Chrome package and effectively automatic. It fails where the estate has copies of V8 that Chrome's updater does not own — Electron and CEF applications, appliance browsers — and where enterprise update rings defer the security channel.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alerting on repeated renderer crashes in V8 array code on pre-57 hosts, and on renderer processes spawning children or writing to disk after loading third-party content.
detection.adequacy: A crash means the attempt failed. A successful trigger is silent, and the only observable event is whatever the paired sandbox escape does afterwards — so detection here is a signal that someone is trying, not that they succeeded.

response.what_would_have_worked: On evidence of renderer compromise, treating browser-held credentials, session cookies and stored passwords on that profile as exposed and rotating them, then confirming the running Chrome version rather than the installed one.
response.adequacy: Proportionate, but it depends on knowing a renderer was compromised, which without the paired escape doing something visible is rarely established.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: Auto-update satisfies flaw remediation for the Chrome package, but SI-2 measures deployment rather than process relaunch, and its asset scope omits the Electron and CEF applications carrying the same pre-57 V8.

NIST-800-53-CM-7.gap: Least functionality has no lever against a JavaScript engine, and CM-7 baselines do not enumerate which embedded Chromium runtimes are permitted, so the number of independent V8 copies on a host is unknown.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: Article 21 accepts browser auto-update as the control without requiring proof that the fixed build is the build executing, and does not extend to Chromium engines shipped inside other applications.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: B4 is met by an auto-updating browser fleet and offers no test for a client running a stale binary despite a current install, or for a line-of-business Electron application nobody version-checks.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: The aggressive browser-patching window is scored against browsers in the software inventory; an Electron application rendering untrusted content on a pre-57 engine is scored as an ordinary application on a slower tier.

AU-Essential-8-App-Hardening.gap: Hardening evidence covers Java, Flash, ads and Office content, none of which touch a V8 defect reached by ordinary first-party script; the sandbox and site-isolation posture that actually bounds this bug is not what the attestation examines.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: One register entry closes on the Chrome advisory while several unlisted copies of the same vulnerable engine keep running elsewhere in the estate.

new_control_requirements.name: BROWSER-MANAGED-UPDATE-NO-DEFERRAL
new_control_requirements.description: Enterprise update rings must not defer security-channel browser updates beyond 24h.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Google shipped the fix for this V8 Array.prototype.concat defect in Chrome 57.0.2987.98 (desktop) and 57.0.2987.108 (Android) on 2017-03-09, with the public trigger PoC in js-vuln-db pointing at Chromium bug 682194. Because patch_required_reboot is false but the browser process must relaunch to run the new binary, deferral here has two forms and both need closing: a management ring that holds the security channel, and a client that installed the update but never restarted. The control's 24-hour ceiling has to be measured against the running Chrome version each endpoint reports, not against 'update approved'.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CISA listed this Chromium V8 defect on 2022-06-08 with a 2022-06-22 due date, and its KEV description names Microsoft Edge and Opera as downstream products carrying the same engine. That is the clause that makes this control non-trivial here: 'verified mitigation' cannot be satisfied by Chrome's own auto-update alone, because the estate's Electron, CEF and vendor-rebadged Chromium copies of a pre-57 V8 are remediated by their own vendors on their own schedules. Verification means enumerating every engine, not confirming one package. EPSS 0.41603 at the 98.556th percentile on 2026-08-13.

CVE-2017-5070.name: Google Chromium V8 Type Confusion Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: Script drives V8's Crankshaft optimizer into a bad alias-analysis result by comparing against a constant node, then swaps an array's contents so the optimized code reads an unboxed double as an object pointer and an object pointer as a double. The two-way confusion gives addrof and fakeobj directly, which is arbitrary read and write inside the renderer.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; the attacker needs only to get JavaScript in front of the browser, including through a third-party ad or iframe
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L with UI:R; the primitive is strong enough on its own for a reliable exploit, which is why the recovered in-the-wild versions worked unchanged across dozens of Chrome builds
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Reported by Zhao Qixun (@S0rryMybad) of the Qihoo 360 Vulcan Team in May 2017 from manual JIT research; the team name is not evidence of AI involvement.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Running Chrome 59.0.3071.86 or later and confirming the browser relaunched onto it, plus applying the same version discipline to every Chromium-derived browser and embedded Chromium runtime — and keeping the renderer sandbox and site isolation intact so the bug stays renderer-scope.
prevention.adequacy: The Chrome fix is complete. What it does not cover is the frozen-build problem Project Zero's Chrome 37-58 exploit range exposes: an embedded Chromium that stopped moving anywhere in that window is exposed to a capability that was maintained and used for years, and no Chrome update reaches it.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alerting on repeated renderer crashes in optimized JavaScript array code on pre-59 hosts, and on renderer processes spawning children or writing to disk after loading third-party content.
detection.adequacy: Weak by construction. The recovered exploits were stable across many builds, so successful runs did not crash; a crash indicates a build mismatch on the attacker's side, not a defended host.

response.what_would_have_worked: On evidence of renderer compromise, treating browser-held credentials, session cookies and stored passwords on that profile as exposed and rotating them, and verifying the running engine version across every Chromium copy on the host rather than only the Chrome package.
response.adequacy: Proportionate but late, and it depends on the paired sandbox escape producing something visible — a renderer-scope compromise on its own leaves little for the host to report.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: Auto-update satisfies the control while attackers maintained working exploits across Chrome 37 through 58; SI-2 measures deployment rather than relaunch and excludes the embedded V8 copies its asset scope never lists.

NIST-800-53-CM-7.gap: No least-functionality lever exists against a JIT optimizer, and CM-7 baselines neither enumerate permitted embedded Chromium runtimes nor treat the renderer sandbox and site isolation as non-optional settings.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: Browser auto-update is accepted as the control without proof the executing build is the fixed build, and the obligation does not follow the engine into other products.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: B4 has no test for a stale running binary behind a current install, and no visibility of appliance and kiosk browsers frozen on an old Chromium.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: The browser tier covers Chrome; an Electron or appliance UI on a pre-59 engine is scored on the slower application tier while carrying a bug with proven multi-year in-the-wild exploitation.

AU-Essential-8-App-Hardening.gap: Hardening attestations cover Java, Flash, ads and Office content, not the sandbox and site-isolation posture that keeps this renderer-scope bug from becoming a host compromise.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: The register closes on Google's Chrome 59 advisory without carrying the same CVE against the other products in the estate running the same engine.

new_control_requirements.name: BROWSER-MANAGED-UPDATE-NO-DEFERRAL
new_control_requirements.description: Enterprise update rings must not defer security-channel browser updates beyond 24h.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Google fixed this Crankshaft type confusion in the initial release of Chrome 59 — 59.0.3071.86 desktop, 59.0.3071.92 Android — on 2017-06-05, after Zhao Qixun reported it in May 2017. Project Zero later recovered two attacker exploits for the same bug that worked across Chrome 37-58 and 47-58, so every week of ring deferral was a week inside a range an operator already had reliable code for. patch_required_reboot is false, which makes the control cheap to meet and easy to fake: the 24-hour ceiling must be measured against the running Chrome version on each endpoint, because an installed-but-not-relaunched browser is still executing the vulnerable V8.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CISA listed this Chromium V8 type confusion on 2022-06-08 with a 2022-06-22 due date, and its KEV description names Microsoft Edge and Opera as downstream carriers of the same engine. The 'verified' half is the work: Chrome's own updater proves nothing about the Electron, CEF and appliance Chromium copies in the estate, and Project Zero's Chrome 37-58 exploit range means any of those frozen inside that window is exposed to code that already existed. Verification here means enumerating every V8 in service and its version, not confirming one package updated. EPSS 0.31212 at the 98.109th percentile on 2026-08-13.

CVE-2017-6862.name: NETGEAR Multiple Devices Buffer Overflow Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: An unauthenticated HTTP request to the router's web administration application carries an over-long parameter that is copied into a fixed-size buffer with no length check. The overflow both bypasses the interface's authentication check and redirects execution, giving command execution on the router itself.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; the overflow defeats the authentication check rather than requiring credentials to get past it
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L with UI:N; a single request. The practical gate is network position: NETGEAR requires the attacker to be on the network the router serves, or remote management to be enabled, and remote management is off by default
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Discovered by Maxime Peterlin of ON-X through manual reverse engineering of the router firmware and reported to NETGEAR as PSV-2016-0261.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Updating to WNR2000v3 1.1.2.14 / WNR2000v4 1.0.0.66 / WNR2000v5 1.0.0.42 or later and confirming the unit rebooted onto it, keeping remote management off, and replacing any revision — including R2000 units with no published fixed version — that cannot be verified against the Download Center.
prevention.adequacy: The firmware fix is complete for units that can take it. Disabling remote management bounds the attacker population to the served network but does not close the path, because that is the vendor's own stated precondition — on a router whose purpose is serving a client network, no segmentation removes it.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Watching for the router rebooting or its admin daemon restarting without an administrative action, and for the device's own WAN address making connections unrelated to its normal services.
detection.adequacy: Very weak. These devices produce almost no exportable telemetry, nothing collects it, and the signals that exist — a reboot, a DNS setting change — look like ordinary consumer-hardware behaviour to anyone not already looking.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating an exposed unit as compromised: factory-reset it, rebuild the configuration and administrative credential from a known-good baseline rather than restoring a saved config, verify DNS settings and port forwards, and rotate credentials that transited the device.
response.adequacy: Correct, and rarely done because nobody attributes the incident to the router. Applying firmware to a unit that already executed the attacker's commands removes the flaw and leaves whatever was changed in the configuration.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: Flaw remediation needs an inventory entry and an update mechanism; this device has neither, and for the R2000 NETGEAR publishes no fixed version at all, so the control produces no finding and no target.

NIST-800-53-SC-7.gap: SC-7 treats the router as the boundary while the boundary device's own admin webapp is the target, reachable unauthenticated from every host on the network it serves.
