NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: A consumer router at a home-worker or branch site has no owner in the patch programme — no agent, no inventory entry, manual per-revision firmware pulls — so the obligation is met by a programme that never had the device in scope.

NIS2-Art21-network-security.gap: The obligation is satisfied by perimeter controls and never asks whether a branch or remote-access site's router is a supported device still receiving firmware, nor treats its admin surface as needing isolation from its own users.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: B4 evidence rarely reaches consumer network equipment at remote-working locations, so it can be held while a device with a pre-auth RCE sits between a corporate laptop and the internet.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Router firmware is an operating system the standard's tooling does not see; the requirement that actually binds is vendor-supported products, and for revisions with no fixed firmware the compliant action is removal.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: Without an asset register entry the advisory is never received as applicable, and a register built from the NVD text carries three WNR2000 revisions and misses the R2000 that only NETGEAR's advisory names.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.22.gap: Segregation is evidenced against the corporate network design, not against the untrusted consumer segment a remote worker's corporate device shares with the vulnerable router — which is where the vendor's own precondition is satisfied.

ENISA-IoT-security-baseline.gap: The baseline's defined-support-lifetime and working-update-mechanism expectations cannot be evidenced for these units: no stated end-of-support date, no automatic update path, and no published fixed version for the R2000. Only the remote-management-off default is met.

new_control_requirements.name: PERIMETER-DEVICE-ZERODAY-SLA-TIER
new_control_requirements.description: Compliance frameworks must define a distinct patch SLA tier for pre-auth RCE on perimeter-trust-boundary devices (firewalls, VPN concentrators, WAFs, edge load-balancers). Tier requirement: vendor-mitigation deployed within 4 hours of KEV listing OR isolation of the vulnerable interface; standard 14/30-day SLAs do not apply because the device IS the trust boundary.
new_control_requirements.evidence: A WNR2000 or R2000 is the trust boundary for whatever sits behind it, and this is unauthenticated command execution on that device's administration webapp. The tier's isolation alternative is the honest one to reach for first here — confirm remote management is off so the interface is not WAN-reachable — because the patch alternative is a manual Download Center pull per hardware revision (1.1.2.14 / 1.0.0.66 / 1.0.0.42, with no published fixed version for the R2000) and a reboot, which no standard 30-day application-patch window is built to drive. CISA's clock ran from 2022-06-08 to 2022-06-22; EPSS still reads 0.42696 at the 98.594th percentile on 2026-08-13.

new_control_requirements.name: PERIMETER-COMPROMISE-REBUILD-NOT-PATCH
new_control_requirements.description: Pre-rehearsed IR runbook for any perimeter device that suffers a pre-auth RCE CVE in active exploitation MUST default to config-exfil + rebuild + credential rotation, not patch-in-place. Patch-in-place leaves attacker-installed implants intact.
new_control_requirements.evidence: This flaw yields command execution on the NETGEAR router itself, and the artefacts an attacker leaves on such a device — altered DNS servers, a new port forward, a changed administrative password, remote management switched on — all live in the configuration, which survives a firmware update and is usually restored verbatim afterwards from a saved backup. For a WNR2000 or R2000 that was reachable during the exposure window opened by the 2022-06-08 KEV listing, the runbook has to default to capturing the configuration for evidence, factory-resetting, rebuilding settings from a known-good baseline rather than restoring the saved config, and rotating credentials that transited the device.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: NETGEAR published fixed firmware for PSV-2016-0261 well before CISA listed CVE-2017-6862 on 2022-06-08 with a 2022-06-22 due date, so the 'whichever is later' clock started at the KEV listing. The 'verified' requirement is what this device makes hard and important: there is no console to report compliance from, the fixed level differs per hardware revision, the R2000 has no published fixed version in the advisory, and a unit that downloaded firmware but did not reboot is still running the vulnerable code — so verification means reading the running firmware version off each unit, not recording that an update was issued.

CVE-2018-17463.name: Google Chromium V8 Remote Code Execution Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: A crafted HTML page runs JavaScript that gets a function optimized by TurboFan, then calls Object.create on an object the optimized code holds. Because JSCreateObject was annotated as having no heap side effect, redundancy elimination removes the map check that would have caught Object.create converting the object's properties to dictionary mode. The optimized code then reads a NameDictionary as if it were a PropertyArray, giving a controllable out-of-bounds read/write in the renderer heap and arbitrary code execution inside the renderer sandbox.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; the attacker needs no account and no prior access, only that the victim's browser loads the page. UI:R because a page load is required, which advertising and compromised-site delivery both satisfy at scale.
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; the trigger is deterministic JavaScript through the normal optimization pipeline, with no race and no info leak required. The real constraint is not exploitation difficulty but containment: the primitive lands in the sandboxed renderer, so a second flaw (or a --no-sandbox launch) is needed to reach the user's own privileges.
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Discovery was manual review of V8's operator side-effect annotations, and the published exploitation methodology is hand-written JIT reasoning rather than automated analysis. No AI-branded research arm is involved in the attribution.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Enforced browser currency measured on the running process — every Chromium-based process, including runtimes embedded in desktop applications, at or above 70.0.3538.64, with a forced relaunch so the delivered update actually retires the vulnerable V8.
prevention.adequacy: Adequate for managed browsers and inadequate for everything else. The KEV clock reaches federal agencies' Chrome installs but says nothing about the Chromium version inside an Electron application, and no framework here requires that inventory. Where the embedding application is abandoned there is no update to enforce and removal is the only terminal state.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alerting on renderer-process crash bursts per origin and on any process creation or executable write originating from a Chromium renderer — both are visible to standard endpoint telemetry and neither has a benign explanation at volume.
detection.adequacy: Partial at best. It fires on unreliable exploitation, and a clean run may produce no crash at all; it also cannot distinguish exploitation from a badly behaved page without correlating the process-creation half. It gives an incident window, not prevention.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating a confirmed renderer compromise as credential exposure for everything that browser profile held — session cookies, saved passwords, OAuth tokens — and rotating on that basis rather than closing the case on a browser update.
response.adequacy: Necessary but rarely scoped this way. Because the primitive is sandbox-contained, response teams routinely downgrade it to 'browser crash, patched' and never rotate the session material the renderer could read, which is the asset that actually moved.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: Flaw remediation is evidenced from a patch cycle that never enumerates self-updating browsers or embedded Chromium runtimes, and has no notion of 'updated but not relaunched' — so the control reads satisfied while a pre-70.0.3538.64 V8 keeps executing.

NIST-800-53-CM-7.gap: Least functionality is assessed on services and ports, so it neither forbids the --no-sandbox launch flag the public Metasploit target depends on nor surfaces a Chromium runtime bundled inside a desktop application.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: Art. 21(2)(e) vulnerability handling is implemented against server and endpoint OS patching; the exploitable code path here ships inside third-party applications and is invisible to that evidence.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: B4 accepts 'a browser update policy exists' as secure configuration and maintenance, without requiring proof that no process on the estate is still executing a pre-70 V8 build.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: The 48-hour tier is triggered by the existence of a working exploit (Exploit-DB 48184 / Metasploit chrome_object_create), but maturity is evidenced from a scanner's installed-application view, which does not report the Chromium version inside an Electron package.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: A.8.8 evidence is a scan cadence plus a patch SLA; neither answers which running processes execute a V8 earlier than 70.0.3538.64, which is the only question this CVE poses.

OWASP-Top-10-2021-A06.gap: A06 places component-currency duty on the software builder, not on the organization deploying it, so nothing obliges an operator to enumerate the Chromium version each vendor application ships.

new_control_requirements.name: BROWSER-MANAGED-UPDATE-NO-DEFERRAL
new_control_requirements.description: Enterprise update rings must not defer security-channel browser updates beyond 24h.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Google fixed this V8 type confusion in the October 2018 Chrome 70 desktop stable channel (NVD boundary 70.0.3538.64; shipped build 70.0.3538.67), yet CISA still had cause to list it on 2022-06-08 with a 2022-06-22 due date, and its EPSS remains 0.84564 at the 99.682nd percentile as of 2026-08-13 because Exploit-DB 48184 and the Metasploit chrome_object_create module keep a packaged exploit in circulation. A Chrome estate on a deferred update ring, or one that delivers the update without forcing a relaunch, is the population that stayed exploitable across those four years.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: For Google Chrome/Chromium the patch predates the KEV listing by nearly four years, so the clock this control starts is the 2022-06-08 listing itself, and 'verified' is the load-bearing word: verification here means the running browser process reports 70.0.3538.64 or later, not that the update was pushed. There is no compensating control available — JIT cannot be policy-disabled in this Chrome era — so for an Electron or CEF application pinned to a pre-70 runtime the documented mitigation is removal of the application.

CVE-2018-17480.name: Google Chromium V8 Out-of-Bounds Write Vulnerability (CVE-2018-17480)

attack_vector.description: A page sends a crafted structured-clone payload through postMessage. V8's deserializer allocates the declared-length array, keeps a raw handle to its backing store, and then calls back into attacker JavaScript while filling elements. That callback shrinks the elements store; the loop keeps writing through the stale handle past the end of the new allocation. The attacker uses the overflow to corrupt a neighbouring object's length, reaches an ArrayBuffer's backing-store pointer and size, and turns that into arbitrary read/write and code execution inside the renderer sandbox.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; no account and no prior access, only that the victim loads the page. UI:R because a page load is needed, which malvertising and compromised sites supply at scale.
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; the callback re-entry is deterministic and attacker-timed, with no race and no information leak required. The genuine constraint is heap layout, and the containment constraint is the sandbox: the primitive is renderer-local until a second flaw escapes it.
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Google's Chrome 71 release note credits Guang Gong of Alpha Team, Qihoo 360, reporting via Tianfu Cup on 2018-11-16 — a human competition submission, with nothing in the account indicating automated or AI-assisted discovery; the public exploit is hand-written analysis of the deserializer loop.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Browser currency enforced on the running process — every Chromium-based process, including runtimes embedded in desktop applications, at or above 71.0.3578.80, with a forced relaunch so the vulnerable deserializer is actually retired.
prevention.adequacy: Sufficient for managed browsers, silent on embedded Chromium. The KEV clock reaches an agency's Chrome installs and not the Chromium version inside a vendor's Electron application, and where that application is abandoned there is no update to enforce — removal is the terminal state.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alerting on renderer crash bursts per origin and on any process creation or executable write from a Chromium renderer process, both visible to ordinary endpoint telemetry.
detection.adequacy: Partial. It catches unreliable exploitation rather than successful exploitation, and a clean run may not crash at all. It buys an incident window, not prevention, and only if renderer processes are modelled at all.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating a confirmed renderer compromise as exposure of everything that browser profile could read — session cookies, saved credentials, OAuth tokens — and rotating on that basis rather than closing on the browser update.
response.adequacy: Rarely scoped this way. Because the primitive is sandbox-contained, incidents get closed as 'browser patched' and the session material the renderer held is never rotated.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: Flaw remediation evidence comes from an OS/application patch cycle that neither enumerates embedded Chromium runtimes nor recognises 'updated but not relaunched', so the control reads satisfied while a pre-71.0.3578.80 V8 keeps running.

NIST-800-53-SI-4.gap: Monitoring baselines cover hosts and network flows, not renderer-process crash bursts or RWX execution inside a sandboxed child process — the only observable signals this bug produces.

NIS2-Art21-vulnerability-handling.gap: Vulnerability handling is operationalized against servers and endpoint OSes, so an entity can evidence the process while the exploitable deserializer ships inside a third-party desktop application it never version-tracks.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: 'Chrome updates automatically' satisfies the outcome without any demonstration that no running process executes a V8 earlier than 71.0.3578.80, and without weight on the relaunch step.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: The 48-hour working-exploit tier applies given the public gist, but maturity is evidenced from a scanner's installed-application inventory that cannot see the Chromium version inside an Electron package.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: Scan cadence and patch SLA are the audited artefacts; neither answers which running processes execute a pre-71 V8, which is the entire question at EPSS 0.35640 with exploit code public since April 2019.

OWASP-Top-10-2021-A06.gap: Component-currency duty sits with the software builder, not the deploying organization, so nothing obliges an operator to learn which Chromium version each vendor application embeds.

new_control_requirements.name: BROWSER-MANAGED-UPDATE-NO-DEFERRAL
new_control_requirements.description: Enterprise update rings must not defer security-channel browser updates beyond 24h.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Google fixed this deserializer out-of-bounds write in the December 2018 Chrome 71 desktop stable channel (71.0.3578.80), a complete exploit was published on 2019-04-03, and CISA still listed the CVE on 2022-06-08 with a 2022-06-22 due date — EPSS 0.35640 at the 98.315th percentile as of 2026-08-13. A deferred update ring, or one that delivers Chrome updates without forcing a relaunch, is exactly the population that remained exploitable across that span.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: For Chrome and Chromium the fix predates the 2022-06-08 KEV listing by more than three years, so the clock starts at the listing and 'verified' carries the weight: verification means the running Chromium process reports 71.0.3578.80 or later, not that an update was pushed. No compensating control exists — structured clone and postMessage cannot be disabled by policy — so for an Electron or CEF application pinned to a pre-71 runtime the documented mitigation is removing the application.

CVE-2018-19943.name: QNAP NAS File Station Cross-Site Scripting Vulnerability (CVE-2018-19943)

attack_vector.description: An attacker with write access to any share stores markup in a file or folder name. File Station renders that name into its web UI unencoded, so the script executes in the browser of the next QTS user who lists the directory, inside their authenticated session and with reach into the QTS administration surface rather than only the file manager.
attack_vector.privileges_required: low — PR:L; the attacker needs somewhere to write a name the victim will see. On a NAS that is a low-privilege user share, a guest-writable share, or an unauthenticated upload path such as an FTP drop folder — not administrative access.
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; there is no memory corruption, no race and no chain. The only real constraint is UI:R and it is not a lure: the attacker plants the name and waits for the directory to be browsed, and the payoff scales with the privilege of whoever browses it.
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Independent Security Evaluators found it during hands-on assessment of a TS-870 as part of SOHOpelessly Broken 2.0; no automated or AI-assisted analysis is involved.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Getting each appliance onto its branch's fixed QTS build (4.4.2.1270 build 20200410 and the five sibling branches), and in the interim keeping the QTS web interface off any untrusted network so the population that can plant a filename and the population that browses it are both bounded.
prevention.adequacy: Adequate where the model can reach a fixed build and the operator can take the restart. It gives nothing to a unit whose newest supported QTS branch is below the fix — there the only terminal state is replacement — and network restriction alone does not help when the users who browse the share are the intended users of the appliance.

detection.what_would_have_worked: A periodic directory walk over SMB/NFS looking for file and folder names containing markup characters, plus alerting on QTS administrative changes that follow a File Station page view with no matching operator ticket.
detection.adequacy: The filename sweep is genuinely cheap and needs no agent on the appliance, but it detects the stored payload rather than its execution. The administrative-change half depends on QTS logs being forwarded off the box, which most deployments never configure — and a NAS that has already been compromised is the last place to trust for its own logs.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating any confirmed execution as compromise of the administrator session that ran it: rotate QTS administrator credentials, review users, installed applications, scheduled jobs and share permissions against a known-good baseline, and check for changes made through the web API rather than only for malware on disk.
response.adequacy: Correct scope but rarely applied, because a 5.4-rated XSS is triaged as a low-severity web defect. With CISA recording ransomware campaign use against this appliance class, the NAS review matters more than the browser.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: Appliance firmware requiring a storage outage lands in quarterly change windows, and SI-2 evidence drawn from server and endpoint patching never enumerates which QTS branch each unit runs.

NIST-800-53-SI-10.gap: Input-validation evidence covers request parameters, not the encoding of stored object names when a management UI renders them — so the control is attested while the filename path stays unencoded.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: A NAS bought as storage is frequently absent from the entity's managed-asset scope, so the six branch-specific remediation targets cannot even be expressed, let alone evidenced.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: The appliance holding the data supports the essential function but sits outside the assessed server and endpoint estate, and B4 does not require the test that matters — that the management UI renders untrusted stored names inert.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Appliance firmware fits neither the operating-system nor the application patching strategy, and branch-plus-build remediation targets are not something an unauthenticated scanner can evaluate.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: Coverage depends entirely on whether the NAS is inventoried as a system rather than as a storage volume; where it is not, the scan-and-SLA evidence is clean over an unpatched File Station.

OWASP-Top-10-2021-A03.gap: Injection guidance binds the vendor building the product, not the operator running it; the operator's only lever remains the firmware version.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: QNAP's fixed builds for this File Station defect were dated 2020-04-10 and earlier and QSA-20-01 published 2020-06-05, so on the control's own terms the clock ran from the 2022-05-24 KEV listing, against a 2022-06-14 CISA due date, with ransomware campaign use recorded as Known. 'Verified' is what this appliance class fails: the check must be the build string the NAS itself reports (4.4.2.1270 build 20200410 or the sibling branch target), because the update needs a restart of a live file server and an update staged but not restarted leaves File Station serving the unencoded filename.

new_control_requirements.name: MITIGATION-ACTIVE-PATCH-PENDING-VERDICT-CLASS
new_control_requirements.description: Compliance verdicts must distinguish three states: (a) binary patch deployed (vulnerability eliminated), (b) vendor-mitigation rule active, no binary patch (residual risk: any defect in the mitigation rule reopens the vulnerability), (c) no mitigation, no patch (full exposure). Audit reports must surface (b) as a distinct compensating-control state with an associated time-bound action item, not as a 'patched per SLA' outcome.
new_control_requirements.evidence: QSA-20-01 offers no interim mitigation for the File Station filename rendering — there is no setting that makes QTS escape stored names — so every QNAP unit below its branch's fixed build is in state (c), full exposure, not the softer state (b) that a 'compensating controls in place' entry on a risk register implies. This matters most for models whose newest supported QTS branch never reached 4.4.2.1270 build 20200410 or a sibling fix: those cannot leave state (c) by patching at all, and recording them as risk-accepted without a replacement date leaves a KEV-listed flaw with ransomware campaign use in service indefinitely.

CVE-2018-19949.name: QNAP NAS File Station Command Injection Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: A username containing shell metacharacters is stored when an account is created. QTS later interpolates that name into a command line when the account authenticates, and the shell executes the attacker's payload on the NAS. The result is command execution on the appliance that holds the file shares — and, in most deployments, the backups of those shares.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none per NVD — PR:N/UI:N, scored 9.8 as a fully unauthenticated network path; the finder's own title places the trigger after account creation and authentication, so the practical gate is the ability to create or influence the creation of an account, which several of the sixteen sibling TS-870 findings (CVE-2018-19941 through CVE-2018-19957) shorten.
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; no race, no memory corruption, no chain once the name is stored. The payload detonates on an ordinary login event, so the attacker does not need to be present when it fires.
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Found by Independent Security Evaluators through hands-on assessment of a TS-870 in SOHOpelessly Broken 2.0; no automated or AI-assisted discovery is involved.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Getting each appliance to its branch's fixed QTS build and taking the restart, with the QTS web interface removed from the internet and from general user VLANs in the meantime so the account and authentication surface is only reachable from an operator segment.
prevention.adequacy: Reachability restriction bounds who can reach the surface but does not close the path for anything already inside the permitted segment, and it is unavailable where the NAS exists to serve a general user network. Patching is definitive only where the model's newest supported QTS branch reached a fixed build; where it did not, replacement is the only terminal state.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Reviewing the QTS user list for names carrying shell metacharacters — the payload sits in the account before it fires — and forwarding QTS logs plus the appliance's outbound network flows to a collector off the device.
detection.adequacy: The user-list review is the rare pre-execution check and costs nothing, but it only catches payloads planted through account creation. Everything downstream depends on telemetry leaving the box, which most QNAP deployments never configure — and once command execution lands, on-device logs are the attacker's to edit.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating an exposed unpatched appliance as compromised rather than as patched: rebuild the configuration from a known-good baseline, remove unrecognised accounts, applications, scheduled jobs and autorun entries, rotate every credential the NAS held or authenticated, and recover from a copy the appliance itself could not write.
response.adequacy: This is the step most often skipped, because a firmware update looks like closure. It is also the step that decides the outcome, since a NAS that holds both the data and its backup gives the attacker both halves of the recovery plan in one device.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: Patch-cycle evidence over servers and endpoints does not enumerate which of six QTS branches an appliance runs, and a firmware update needing a storage outage falls out of the SLA the control is attested against.

NIST-800-53-SI-10.gap: Validation evidence covers request parameters, not stored identity attributes reaching a command interpreter on a later code path — the deferred-execution shape this bug uses.

NIST-800-53-SC-7.gap: Boundary-protection attestations describe the enterprise perimeter and omit the router port-forward, UPnP mapping or vendor remote-access service through which the NAS actually answers.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: The appliance is routinely outside the entity's managed-asset scope, so a functioning vulnerability-handling measure can be evidenced while a 9.8 command-injection path runs on a 2019 build.

NIS2-Art21-incident-handling.gap: The only logs of the account creation and the detonating authentication live on the compromised appliance; with nothing forwarded off the box, the incident-handling process starts when the shares are already encrypted.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: The NAS is assessed as storage media rather than as a system that executes code, and B4 does not require proof that identity attributes accepted by the appliance cannot reach a shell.

UK-CAF-D1.gap: Response plans assume rebuild-and-restore, but on this asset the backup, the replication credentials and the primary data are all reachable from the same command execution.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Appliance firmware belongs to neither the operating-system nor the application patching strategy, and branch-plus-build targets are not evaluable from an unauthenticated scan.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: A unit inventoried as a storage volume never enters the vulnerability-management population, leaving the scan-and-SLA evidence clean over a KEV-listed 9.8 with ransomware campaign use.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.13.gap: Backup schedules and restore tests are attested without ever asking whether the backup is reachable from the system being backed up, which on this appliance it is.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: QNAP's fixed builds for this command-injection path date from January to March 2020 per NVD, with QSA-20-01 published 2020-06-05, so the clock this control runs is the 2022-05-24 KEV listing against CISA's 2022-06-14 due date — on a CVSS 9.8 path that CISA also flags for known ransomware campaign use. The documented-compensating-control branch is the one operators actually reach for on a NAS, and it must be written honestly: removing the QTS web interface from untrusted networks bounds who can create an account, it does not close the injection, and it is not available where the appliance serves a general user network.

new_control_requirements.name: PERIMETER-COMPROMISE-REBUILD-NOT-PATCH
new_control_requirements.description: Pre-rehearsed IR runbook for any perimeter device that suffers a pre-auth RCE CVE in active exploitation MUST default to config-exfil + rebuild + credential rotation, not patch-in-place. Patch-in-place leaves attacker-installed implants intact.
new_control_requirements.evidence: NVD scores this QNAP path as unauthenticated network-reachable command execution (AV:N/PR:N/UI:N, 9.8), CISA listed it on 2022-05-24 with ransomware campaign use recorded as Known, and QNAP NAS units routinely sit at the perimeter through a port-forward, a UPnP mapping or the vendor's remote-access service. A QTS firmware update to 4.4.2.1270 build 20200410 or its sibling branch target closes the injection and removes nothing an attacker already installed — added accounts, QTS applications, scheduled jobs and autorun entries all survive it, which is why an exposed unpatched unit needs configuration capture, rebuild from a known-good baseline and rotation of every credential the appliance held or authenticated.

CVE-2018-19953.name: QNAP NAS File Station Cross-Site Scripting Vulnerability (CVE-2018-19953)

attack_vector.description: File Station's share-link creator reflects a caller-supplied value into its response without encoding it. A crafted link to the victim's own NAS therefore executes attacker script in the browser of any QTS user who follows it, inside that user's authenticated session and with reach into the QTS administration surface rather than only the file manager.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; the attacker needs no account and no write access on the appliance, only the NAS's reachable address and a way to get the link in front of a QTS user.
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; the whole exploit is a URL. UI:R is the only genuine constraint and it is a social one, not a technical one, satisfied by a mail or chat message.
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Found by Independent Security Evaluators during hands-on assessment of a TS-870 in SOHOpelessly Broken 2.0; no automated or AI-assisted analysis is involved.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Each appliance on its branch's fixed QTS build with the restart taken, and the QTS web interface removed from the internet so an externally-sent link cannot reach a vulnerable renderer at all.
prevention.adequacy: Patching is definitive where the model reaches a fixed build; where it does not, replacement is the terminal state. Network restriction is only a partial holding measure — it closes external delivery, but the appliance stays reachable from the users it exists to serve, and those are the sessions worth stealing.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Watching for reflected markup in requests to the NAS at a reverse proxy or web filter, and alerting on QTS administrative changes that follow a user session with no matching change record.
detection.adequacy: Both halves depend on telemetry that does not exist in a typical deployment: the NAS is usually reached directly rather than through a proxy, and QTS logs stay on the appliance. Detection here is realistically a post-incident reconstruction, not an alert.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating a confirmed click as compromise of that QTS session: rotate the administrator credential, review users, installed applications, scheduled jobs and share permissions against a known-good baseline, and look for changes made through the web API rather than only for malware on disk.
response.adequacy: Correctly scoped but seldom performed, because a 6.1-rated reflected XSS is triaged as a browser-side nuisance. On an appliance where the clicking user is usually also its administrator, the session that ran the script is the one that controls the data.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: Firmware needing a storage outage falls outside the patch cycle SI-2 is attested against, and that evidence never records which of six QTS branches a unit runs.

NIST-800-53-SI-10.gap: The control governs input validation while the defect is missing output encoding; a value can pass ingress validation and still become script when echoed into the page.

NIS2-Art21-vulnerability-handling.gap: A NAS bought as storage sits outside the managed-asset scope, so the branch-specific remediation target cannot be expressed and the measure is evidenced over a population that excludes the vulnerable device.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: The appliance is assessed as storage media rather than as a web application, and B4 requires no proof that its management UI renders reflected parameters inert.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Appliance firmware belongs to neither patching strategy, and branch-plus-build remediation targets are not evaluable from an unauthenticated scan.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: A unit inventoried as a storage volume never enters the vulnerability-management population, so scan and SLA evidence stays clean over a KEV-listed flaw with ransomware campaign use recorded.

OWASP-Top-10-2021-A03.gap: Injection guidance binds the product's builder, not the operator deploying it; the operator's only lever remains the firmware version.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: QNAP's fixed builds for this File Station reflection date from January to March 2020 per NVD, with QSA-20-01 published 2020-06-05, so the clock runs from the 2022-05-24 KEV listing against CISA's 2022-06-14 due date, on an entry CISA also flags for known ransomware campaign use. Verification has to be the build string the appliance reports — one restart onto 4.4.2.1270 build 20200410 or its sibling branch target closes all three QSA-20-01 CVEs, and an update staged but not restarted leaves the share-link creator reflecting unencoded input.

new_control_requirements.name: MITIGATION-ACTIVE-PATCH-PENDING-VERDICT-CLASS
new_control_requirements.description: Compliance verdicts must distinguish three states: (a) binary patch deployed (vulnerability eliminated), (b) vendor-mitigation rule active, no binary patch (residual risk: any defect in the mitigation rule reopens the vulnerability), (c) no mitigation, no patch (full exposure). Audit reports must surface (b) as a distinct compensating-control state with an associated time-bound action item, not as a 'patched per SLA' outcome.
new_control_requirements.evidence: QSA-20-01 offers no setting that makes File Station encode the reflected share-link parameter, so a QNAP unit below its branch's fixed build is in state (c), full exposure — and the network restriction operators reach for is weaker than state (b), because it removes external delivery while leaving every internal user able to reach the vulnerable renderer. Units whose newest supported QTS branch never reached 4.4.2.1270 build 20200410 or a sibling fix cannot leave state (c) by patching; recording those as risk-accepted without a replacement date leaves a KEV-listed flaw with ransomware campaign use in service indefinitely.

CVE-2018-4344.name: Apple Multiple Products Memory Corruption Vulnerability (CVE-2018-4344)

attack_vector.description: Code the user has been induced to run on the device corrupts XNU kernel memory and executes with kernel privileges, per Apple's own impact line. That defeats the boundaries the platform is built on — application sandbox, code-signing enforcement, inter-application data separation — so its role is the escalation stage that turns a compromised or malicious application into control of the device. Apple names no function and publishes no root cause.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; once the attacker's code is executing on the device it needs no privileged account. The gate is getting that code to run, which is what UI:R records.
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L per NVD, but the vendor publishes nothing about preconditions, so whether a heap groom, information leak or race is needed cannot be stated. The real constraint is strategic rather than technical: a local kernel bug is only useful behind a separate remote or sandbox bug, and era mitigations (KASLR, PAC on newer silicon) dominate its practical cost.
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Apple credits the UK's National Cyber Security Centre, a government technical authority; no discovery method is published and nothing suggests automated or AI-assisted analysis.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Driving every Apple device to iOS 12 / macOS Mojave 10.14 / tvOS 12 / watchOS 5 or later with the restart completed, enforced as an access condition — organizational mail, VPN and document access denied to a device below the fixed build — rather than reported on a compliance dashboard.
prevention.adequacy: Complete where the hardware can take the release and the restart is taken; it does nothing for a Mac outside the Mojave supported-model list, where replacement is the only terminal state, and nothing for tvOS and watchOS devices that are not enrolled and therefore never measured.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alerting on kernel-panic clusters on devices below the fixed builds and on repetitive privileged system-call patterns from an installed application — the observable residue of a race or corruption attempt that loses before it wins.
detection.adequacy: Weak on Apple platforms and honest about why: there is no endpoint agent inside iOS, tvOS or watchOS to carry the rule, panic telemetry is not centrally collected in most estates, and a clean run may produce no panic at all. On macOS the telemetry exists but is rarely retained. This bounds an incident window at best.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating a device suspected of having run the attacker's code as compromised at kernel level: recover it by wipe and rebuild rather than by removing an application, rotate every credential and token the device held, and review configuration profiles and MDM state for changes with no matching command.
response.adequacy: Correct and expensive, which is why it is skipped. Kernel-level compromise cannot be reasoned away by uninstalling the app that carried it, and an OS upgrade applied to a device that already granted kernel execution does not remove what was left behind.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: The remediation is a major OS upgrade rather than a patch — and on High Sierra 10.13 there is no update at all — while SI-2 evidence has no state for 'downloaded but not restarted' and no reach into tvOS or watchOS.

NIST-800-53-CM-7.gap: Least functionality is assessed on services and ports, so it never requires blocking side-loaded or untrusted application installation on a device below the fixed build — the one interim lever against a bug that needs local code execution.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: Vulnerability handling is implemented over servers, laptops and phones; the tvOS and watchOS devices running the same XNU kernel are outside the measure entirely.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: An OS-currency policy satisfies the outcome without demonstrating that no device sits below iOS 12 / macOS 10.14 / tvOS 12 / watchOS 5, and the control has no answer for hardware that cannot reach the fixed build.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: The control assumes a patch exists for the running OS; where the fix is a hardware-gated major upgrade, an unsupported Mac cannot satisfy it at any maturity level except through an exception that never expires.

AU-Essential-8-App-Hardening.gap: User application hardening is scoped to browser, Office and PDF settings on Windows; it does not restrict side-loaded iOS applications, does not reach tvOS or watchOS, and does not evict an application already installed.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: There is no scanner inside iOS or watchOS, so the only evidence is the MDM-reported build and unenrolled devices produce none — while EPSS 0.02908 pushes an escalation-stage kernel bug to the bottom of any EPSS-driven triage.

ISO-27001-2022-A.7.10.gap: Apple Watch and Apple TV are inventoried as devices holding data rather than as systems executing code, which is precisely what keeps the affected watchOS and tvOS population outside every patch and vulnerability control above.

new_control_requirements.name: MOBILE-ENDPOINT-MDM-ENFORCED-KEV-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: iOS / iPadOS / macOS estates must enforce KEV-class updates within 24h via DDM; user-deferral disallowed.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Apple shipped the fix for this XNU kernel defect in September 2018 as iOS 12, macOS Mojave 10.14, tvOS 12 and watchOS 5, and CISA still listed it on 2022-06-27 with a 2022-07-18 due date — the interval is user deferral plus unenrolled devices, not vendor delay. Two things this estate must add to the control as written: enforcement has to be measured on the completed restart, because a device that downloaded the update and never rebooted is still running the vulnerable kernel; and the enforcement scope has to include tvOS and watchOS, which carry the same kernel and are named in the KEV entry as 'Multiple Products' while sitting outside most mobile-device-management populations.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: For this Apple defect the patch predates the 2022-06-27 KEV listing by nearly four years, so the clock starts at the listing, and both other branches of the control carry real weight here. 'Verified' means the device reports a build at or above iOS 12 / macOS 10.14 / tvOS 12 / watchOS 5 after a restart — no live-patch path exists on any Apple platform. 'Documented compensating controls' means what is actually available in the interim: blocking untrusted and side-loaded application installation, since the bug requires local code execution, and withholding organizational data from a device below the fixed build. For a Mac outside the Mojave 10.14 supported-model list neither branch resolves, and the documented mitigation is a dated replacement schedule.

CVE-2018-4990.name: Adobe Acrobat and Reader Double Free Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: A PDF carries JavaScript that drives a form-field button object holding a crafted JPEG2000 icon, freeing the same allocation twice. The attacker reclaims the freed memory with sprayed content to obtain read/write over the process, builds a ROP chain and runs shellcode as the user. In the wild the same document also carried the Windows win32k flaw CVE-2018-8120, so the outcome of opening the attachment was SYSTEM, not a user-context foothold.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; no account, no network position, no prior access. The document does everything once opened.
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; the trigger is deterministic through the PDF JavaScript API, with no race and no external information leak needed. The genuine cost is exploit engineering — a heap spray reliable enough to reclaim the second free, plus a ROP chain for DEP — and ESET's assessment that the recovered sample carried no final payload suggests it was caught while that engineering was still in progress.
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. ESET found the weaponized sample in a public malware repository and reverse-engineered both zero-days by hand, with Microsoft collaborating on the Windows half; no automated or AI-assisted discovery is involved in the account.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Every Acrobat and Reader install across all three tracks at the APSB18-09 fixed build with the process relaunched, and — for the window before that lands, and as a standing posture on high-risk mailboxes — PDF JavaScript disabled by policy, which removes the API surface this exploit drives.
prevention.adequacy: Patching is definitive for the defect but only reaches copies the inventory can see; a per-user Acrobat install outside managed distribution is remediated by removal, not by a patch report. Disabling JavaScript is a real control with a real cost — interactive forms stop working — and it is a holding measure, not a fix, since it removes this exploit's path rather than the double free.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alerting on Acrobat/Reader spawning a child process, writing an executable or making outbound connections, and on a user-context Reader process being followed by SYSTEM-context activity on the same host — the observable half of the chained privilege escalation.
detection.adequacy: Genuinely useful and widely available in endpoint telemetry, but it fires after the memory corruption has already succeeded. It is an incident-window control. Anti-malware detection specifically did not work here — the sample sat in a public repository until researchers analysed it, and it carried no payload to signature.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating a confirmed open of a malicious PDF as host compromise at whatever privilege the paired escalation reached — SYSTEM in the documented chain — so rebuild and credential rotation rather than removing the document and updating Reader.
response.adequacy: Correctly scoped and routinely under-scoped in practice, because 'user opened a bad PDF' is triaged as a phishing event. The pairing with a privilege-escalation flaw is exactly what makes closing on the Reader update the wrong verdict.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: Software-distribution evidence covers one inventoried Reader package while Acrobat's separate tracks and per-user installs go unenumerated, and the control has no state for a Reader process that never relaunched after updating.

NIST-800-53-SI-3.gap: Anti-malware was deployed and current and did not stop it: the harm is a memory-corruption sequence inside a structurally valid PDF, and the recovered sample carried no final payload to detect.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: Acrobat and Reader update through a vendor-supplied updater outside the entity's distribution system and report different version schemes per track, so the measure can be evidenced while pre-fix builds open mail attachments.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: 'Kept up to date' satisfies the outcome without proving no install on any track reports a pre-fix build, and the outcome gives no weight to disabling PDF JavaScript, the one configuration lever that blocks this path.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: The 48-hour working-exploit tier plainly applies — the exploit predated the patch — but maturity is evidenced from a scanner view that frequently omits per-user Acrobat installs.

AU-Essential-8-App-Hardening.gap: Hardening assessments centre on browsers, Office macros and ActiveX; PDF-reader JavaScript is not consistently tested, so the attestation passes while Reader still executes document-supplied script into the double-free sink.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: The audit sees one updated Reader entry and never asks whether an Acrobat 2017 or Classic 2015 copy exists elsewhere on the estate — which is precisely where the residual exposure sits.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.7.gap: Deploying and maintaining anti-malware is met in full while the attack succeeds, and the paired privilege escalation leaves the attacker holding higher privileges than the agent that satisfies the control.

new_control_requirements.name: EMBEDDED-MEDIA-PARSER-LIBRARY-INVENTORY-AND-PATCH-PARITY
new_control_requirements.description: The packet names the affected product as Adobe Acrobat and Reader, which on a real estate is never one install: Reader and Acrobat ship as separate products on separate update tracks, and per-user copies land outside managed software distribution. The control here means enumerating every installed Acrobat and Reader copy across those tracks and confirming each reports the fixed build, rather than closing the flaw-remediation ticket when the single inventoried Reader package updates. Scope it to those products: the packet ties the CWE-1321 sink to Acrobat and Reader and provides no mapping from the vulnerable code into other PDF-handling software, so instructing operators to treat every PDF-capable binary in the estate as an instance of this CVE manufactures findings and removal work against renderers no evidence implicates. Widen the inventory only where a verified source identifies another product carrying the same component. The distinguishing test: after the managed update lands, enumerate the Acrobat and Reader installs on the estate and confirm none still report a pre-fix version — an estate that patches the inventoried Reader while a second Acrobat track keeps the old build still opens crafted PDFs into the sink, with a flaw-remediation attestation that reads clean. Precondition: this reaches only copies the inventory can see and the operator can update; an unmanaged per-user install is remediated by removing it, not by recording it as patched. The packet registers no live-patch path, so each copy carries the service restart or system reboot the vendor fix requires, and a copy updated but not restarted is not yet remediated.
new_control_requirements.evidence: The three-track inventory problem is literal on this CVE: NVD fixes the vulnerable boundary separately for the Continuous track (Acrobat DC / Acrobat Reader DC <= 2018.011.20038), the 2017 track (<= 2017.011.30079) and the Classic 2015 track (<= 2015.006.30417), each closed by its own APSB18-09 update in May 2018. The weakness here is a double free (CWE-415) reached through PDF JavaScript rather than the CWE-1321 sink the control text cites from the entry it was written for; the inventory-and-parity requirement is what carries across, not that classification. Sweep scope should stay on Adobe Acrobat and Reader — no verified source maps this vulnerable code into other vendors' PDF software. On the restart clause, adjust for this product: no host reboot is needed, but a resident Acrobat or Reader process keeps the vulnerable parser loaded until it relaunches, so 'updated' without a relaunch is not remediated.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Adobe shipped APSB18-09 in May 2018 after ESET and Microsoft found the flaw already weaponized in a live PDF sample, and CISA listed it on 2022-06-08 with a 2022-06-22 due date; EPSS is 0.36614 at the 98.356th percentile as of 2026-08-13. The documented-compensating-control branch is what an operator can actually reach for on Acrobat and Reader before the update lands, and it is real: disabling PDF JavaScript removes the API path this exploit drives, at the cost of interactive forms. It must be recorded as a holding measure with an expiry, not as remediation, because it removes this exploit's route and not the double free — and for an unmanaged per-user copy the documented mitigation is removing the install.

CVE-2018-6065.name: Google Chromium V8 Integer Overflow Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: A crafted web page drives an integer overflow in V8's object-size computation, allocating an undersized object whose use corrupts the renderer heap and yields remote code execution in the browser process.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; no account needed, but the victim must load the attacker's page (UI:R).
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; the only real cost is a per-version heap groom, which the public PoC automates with a server-side offset patcher.
attack_vector.ai_factor: Human-found and human-weaponized; Project Zero and the Pwn2Own team 'fluoroacetate' are credited. No AI assistance is claimed.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Same-day rollout of Chrome 65.0.3325.146 with an enforced browser relaunch across the fleet.
prevention.adequacy: A patch alone is insufficient until the renderer relaunches; managed update rings that permit multi-day deferral leave the exploitable binary running.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Endpoint telemetry alerting on renderer crashes and RWX allocations following untrusted navigation.
detection.adequacy: Crash-based detection fires at or after exploitation, not before, and a clean exploit may not crash the renderer at all.

response.what_would_have_worked: Isolating hosts that rendered the delivery URL and forcing browser relaunch estate-wide.
response.adequacy: Renderer compromise leaves little on-disk residue, so response depends on network records of the delivery page rather than host artifacts.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: Flaw remediation shipped the fix but set no browser-specific accelerated clock and does not compel the relaunch that lands it.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: No accelerated tier for a 99th-percentile-EPSS browser RCE with a public PoC.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: Treats browser patching as routine maintenance, not KEV-clock remediation.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Two-week application-patch window is the whole exposure for a crafted-page RCE.

AU-Essential-8-App-Hardening.gap: Hardening levers do not touch a memory-corruption bug inside V8.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: Vulnerability tracking marks 'patched' without verifying the running renderer relaunched onto 65.0.3325.146.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Google Chrome V8 CVE-2018-6065, KEV-listed 2022-06-08 with a public Exploit-DB PoC (44584) and EPSS 0.60304 / 99th percentile as of 2026-08-13; the fixed build 65.0.3325.146 predates the KEV listing by years, so exposure is a deployment-and-relaunch problem the standard SLA does not compress.

new_control_requirements.name: BROWSER-MANAGED-UPDATE-NO-DEFERRAL
new_control_requirements.description: Enterprise update rings must not defer security-channel browser updates beyond 24h.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Chrome/Chromium is the internet-facing application on every endpoint; CVE-2018-6065 is reachable by any crafted page, so any update-ring deferral of the 65.0.3325.146 security channel directly extends the window a public V8 RCE PoC can be used.

CVE-2018-8611.name: Microsoft Windows Kernel Privilege Escalation Vulnerability (CVE-2018-8611)

attack_vector.description: A local process races the Kernel Transaction Manager into a use-after-free, grooms it into arbitrary kernel read/write, and swaps its token to SYSTEM — below the win32k sandbox boundary.
attack_vector.privileges_required: low — PR:L; the attacker must already run code on the host (a sandboxed renderer suffices).
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L in CVSS, but reliable exploitation is a scheduling race needing thread-affinity/priority control and a heap groom.
attack_vector.ai_factor: Kaspersky found it by behavioral in-the-wild detection; no AI involvement in discovery or weaponization is claimed.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Installing the December 2018 cumulative update and rebooting every affected host on the KEV clock.
prevention.adequacy: The fix only loads on reboot; a host patched-but-not-rebooted is still exploitable, and least-privilege controls do not contain an already-authorized local user.

detection.what_would_have_worked: EDR rules on anomalous KTM syscall bursts from unprivileged processes and on low-integrity-to-SYSTEM spawns.
detection.adequacy: KTM APIs are legitimate, so detection rests on rare-usage anomaly rather than a signature; a careful exploit generates little else.

response.what_would_have_worked: Nation-state-initial-access IR escalation on FruityArmor/SandCat attribution, with credential rotation for any account active on the host.
response.adequacy: Standard malware IR under-escalates APT activity; a SYSTEM-level compromise mandates full host rebuild and credential rotation, not cleanup.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: Counts a host patched at install, not at reboot, for a kernel UAF whose fix loads only on reboot.

NIST-800-53-AC-6.gap: Least privilege is bypassed — an authorized low-priv process reaches SYSTEM through the kernel, so AC-6 scoping is never consulted.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: Art21 counts patch management by deployment, and the December 2018 rollup is deployed once installed. The KTM fix lives in ntoskrnl and loads only at reboot, so a fleet reported compliant can be largely unrebooted and still one race away from SYSTEM.

NIS2-Art21-incident-handling.gap: Under-escalates confirmed APT (FruityArmor/SandCat) exploitation as commodity malware.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: Does not distinguish a reboot-gated kernel patch from a userspace update.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: One-month OS-patch window is exploitable time for an APT-used kernel LPE.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: Measures remediation by approval, not by installed-and-rebooted kernel build.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Windows KTM CVE-2018-8611, KEV-listed 2022-05-24, fixed by Microsoft in December 2018; because the fix is a kernel binary it is only mitigated after reboot, so the SLA has to measure installed-and-rebooted build (EPSS 0.04196 / 90th percentile as of 2026-08-13, public PoC available), not install approval.

new_control_requirements.name: NATION-STATE-INITIAL-ACCESS-IR-ESCALATION
new_control_requirements.description: IR runbooks must include an explicit nation-state-initial-access escalation path triggered by APT28/APT29/Lazarus/Volt-Typhoon/etc. attribution on a confirmed exploit chain. Standard malware-infection IR under-escalates nation-state activity by treating it as commodity threat.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2018-8611 was found in the wild by Kaspersky and attributed to the FruityArmor and SandCat (FinFisher/FinSpy) APT groups as the SYSTEM-escalation stage of a browser exploit chain; a detection of this LPE is a targeted-intrusion signal, not a commodity-malware event, and must trigger nation-state IR escalation.

CVE-2019-15271.name: Cisco RV Series Routers Deserialization of Untrusted Data Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: An authenticated user sends a crafted HTTP payload to the RV-series management interface; unvalidated deserialization turns it into arbitrary OS commands executed as root on the perimeter router.
attack_vector.privileges_required: low — PR:L; a valid credential or active session token to the management interface, often trivially met on SMB edge routers with default/weak admin logins.
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; a single crafted request over the network, no user interaction and no race.
attack_vector.ai_factor: Reported by Michel Gaschet-Clousier of Orange Cyberdefense; no AI assistance indicated.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Firmware 4.2.3.10 on RV042/RV042G and decommissioning the EoL RV016/RV082, with WAN-side management disabled everywhere.
prevention.adequacy: Patching only covers two of the four models; for the EoL pair the only real fix is removal, and no CVSS-driven SLA mandates that.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alerting on config changes and outbound connections initiated by the router, and on WAN-sourced management sessions.
detection.adequacy: These SMB routers offer thin logging and no on-box EDR, so detection depends on upstream network monitoring the sites often lack.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating a compromised perimeter router as rebuild-and-replace with credential rotation, not patch-in-place.
response.adequacy: Root RCE on the edge device can leave persistent config/implant changes a firmware update does not remove.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: No patch exists for RV016/RV082 and SI-2 mandates no decommission alternative.

NIST-800-53-SC-7.gap: Does not require the router's own management plane be unreachable from untrusted networks.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: No branch for an unpatchable, actively-exploited perimeter device.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: Treats the edge router as routine infrastructure with a patch expectation the EoL models cannot meet.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Patch-applications is written around applying a vendor fix inside a window. RV042 and RV042G have one in firmware 4.2.3.10; the RV016 and RV082 reached end of software maintenance without one, so for half the exploited models the control has no satisfiable action.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: Remediation logic dead-ends without an asset-retirement decision it does not itself require.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Cisco RV-series CVE-2019-15271, KEV-listed 2022-06-08 with Cisco PSIRT confirming attempted in-the-wild exploitation in June 2022; RV042/RV042G reach mitigation via firmware 4.2.3.10 while RV016/RV082 have no fix, so the SLA's 'documented compensating controls' branch (disable WAN management, isolate, replace) is the only path for the EoL models.

new_control_requirements.name: PERIMETER-DEVICE-ZERODAY-SLA-TIER
new_control_requirements.description: Compliance frameworks must define a distinct patch SLA tier for pre-auth RCE on perimeter-trust-boundary devices (firewalls, VPN concentrators, WAFs, edge load-balancers). Tier requirement: vendor-mitigation deployed within 4 hours of KEV listing OR isolation of the vulnerable interface; standard 14/30-day SLAs do not apply because the device IS the trust boundary.
new_control_requirements.evidence: The RV016/RV042/RV042G/RV082 are edge VPN routers that ARE the perimeter, and CVE-2019-15271 yields root RCE on that management plane; with two models unpatchable and active exploitation confirmed, the isolate-the-interface half of this tier (disable WAN-side management) is the load-bearing control until firmware 4.2.3.10 or replacement lands.

attack_vector.description: A local user abuses xscreensaver's -log switch to make a privileged process write an attacker-controlled library under /usr/lib/secure, then LD_PRELOADs it into a setuid helper to run code as root.
attack_vector.privileges_required: low — PR:L; any local logon, plus a compiler on the host to build the payload library.
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; deterministic once the arbitrary write plants the library, no race, no user interaction (S:C, escaping to root).
attack_vector.ai_factor: Discovered and weaponized by researcher Marco Ivaldi; no AI involvement.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Applying the October 2019 Solaris CPU and restarting X sessions across all multiuser hosts on the KEV clock.
prevention.adequacy: The package fix is sufficient once installed and sessions restart; least-privilege controls do not help because the privileged binary itself grants the write.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Auditing for xscreensaver '-log' to writable paths, new files under /usr/lib/secure, and LD_PRELOAD-set setuid invocations.
detection.adequacy: Each artifact is individually plausible; the escalation is distinguished only by the sequence, so detection needs correlated host audit rather than a single signature.

response.what_would_have_worked: Rotating credentials and reviewing account creation on any shared host where the sequence appeared, since root was obtained.
response.adequacy: Root access on a multiuser host implies full compromise; a patch afterward does not undo persistence or unauthorized accounts created during exposure.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: No KEV-accelerated clock for a locally-exploitable EoP with a public PoC.

NIST-800-53-AC-6.gap: Least privilege is bypassed — the privileged xscreensaver itself performs the attacker-directed write.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: No accelerated tier for a published-exploit local escalation on shared hosts.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: Treats OS package hygiene generically, not as expedited KEV remediation.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: One-month OS-patch window is exploitable time for a working local root PoC.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: Measures patch approval, not the session restart that lands the fixed binary.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Oracle Solaris 11 xscreensaver CVE-2019-3010, KEV-listed 2022-05-25 with a public working exploit (Marco Ivaldi's raptor_xscreensaver, tested on 11.3/11.4) and EPSS 0.13399 / 96th percentile as of 2026-08-13; the October 2019 CPU fix long predates the KEV listing, so any exposed multiuser host is a deployment-and-session-restart gap the SLA must close.

CVE-2019-5825.name: Google Chromium V8 Out-of-Bounds Write Vulnerability (CVE-2019-5825)

attack_vector.description: A crafted page corrupts a V8 float-array length, giving out-of-bounds and then arbitrary renderer read/write, which WebAssembly RWX allocation turns into code execution.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; no account, but the victim must load the crafted page (UI:R).
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; the public exploit targets --no-sandbox and needs a separate escape for a default browser, but weaponization was proven against the shipping stable channel.
attack_vector.ai_factor: Human-found — Google credits Gengming Liu, Jianyu Chen, Zhen Feng and Jessica Liu at Tencent Keen Security Lab, reported 2019-03-13, while the Metasploit module credits dmxcsnsbh with discovery — and human-weaponized by Exodus Intelligence; no AI assistance claimed.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Same-day rollout of the Chrome build carrying the 941743 fix — 74.0.3729.131 or later — with enforced browser relaunch.
prevention.adequacy: Patch alone is insufficient until relaunch, and the vendor clock started late: Exodus published exploit code on 2019-04-03 and Google named the CVE on 2019-04-30, so an estate keyed to CVE publication was already behind before it had anything to track.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alerting on renderer RWX allocations and crashes following untrusted navigation, and flagging --no-sandbox browser launches.
detection.adequacy: Detection fires at or after exploitation; a clean exploit may avoid a crash entirely.

response.what_would_have_worked: Isolating hosts that loaded the delivery page and forcing estate-wide relaunch.
response.adequacy: Renderer compromise leaves scant host residue; response depends on network records of the delivery URL.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: No clock for a fix that shipped weeks before Google named the CVE, and no requirement to verify the browser relaunched onto it.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: No accelerated tier for a V8 RCE with a public Metasploit module.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: Treats browser updates as routine maintenance, not KEV-clock remediation.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: The two-week internet-facing application window is the interval Exodus published into on 2019-04-03, with a working exploit against the shipping 73.0.3683.86 build. With a Metasploit module (chrome_array_map) public, that window is the entire exposure.

AU-Essential-8-App-Hardening.gap: Application hardening blocks ads and disables Flash and Java — the delivery decoration, not the defect. The Array.map length corruption sits inside V8 and is reached by any page the renderer parses, so only a build past the fixed V8 revision removes it, and 73.0.3683.86 is not that build.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: Marks 'patched' without verifying the renderer relaunched onto a build past the fixed V8 revision.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Google Chrome V8 CVE-2019-5825, KEV-listed 2022-06-08 with a public Exodus exploit and a Metasploit module (chrome_array_map), EPSS 0.55925 / 99th percentile as of 2026-08-13; the fix shipped before Google named the CVE on 2019-04-30 in the 74.0.3729.131 release note, so the deployment-and-relaunch delay this SLA compresses is the whole of the exposure.

new_control_requirements.name: BROWSER-MANAGED-UPDATE-NO-DEFERRAL
new_control_requirements.description: Enterprise update rings must not defer security-channel browser updates beyond 24h.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Exodus Intelligence published working exploit code against the shipping Chrome 73.0.3683.86 build on 2019-04-03, three weeks before Google named CVE-2019-5825 with the 74.0.3729.131 release; any update-ring deferral of the Chrome security channel directly widens a window a public exploit and the chrome_array_map Metasploit module already occupy.

CVE-2019-7192.name: QNAP Photo Station Improper Access Control Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: Photo Station API endpoints fail to enforce access control, letting an unauthenticated attacker read a cached token and traverse to arbitrary files — the pre-auth foothold of the QNAP root-RCE chain.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; fully unauthenticated (UI:N) against any reachable Photo Station.
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; a short sequence of unauthenticated HTTP requests, no race or user interaction.
attack_vector.ai_factor: Found by Henry Huang of CyCarrier CSIRT (CyCraft); the 'CyCraft' name is branding, not evidence of AI-assisted discovery.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Updating Photo Station to the fixed build and removing the NAS from direct internet exposure on the KEV clock.
prevention.adequacy: Patching closes the flaw, but a device exposed while unpatched during a ransomware-active period may already be compromised; de-exposure is the other half.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alerting on unauthenticated photo-API traversal requests and on the slideshow.php exposure fingerprint from the internet.
detection.adequacy: Consumer/SMB NAS devices offer thin logging, so detection typically relies on upstream network monitoring the sites lack.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating a previously-exposed NAS as potentially ransomware-compromised: offline integrity check, credential rotation, backup validation.
response.adequacy: An app update does not remove attacker persistence or restore data already encrypted; response must assume prior compromise for exposed devices.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: No accelerated clock for a ransomware-flagged CVSS 9.8 pre-auth NAS flaw.

NIST-800-53-SC-7.gap: Did not require the NAS app surface be unreachable from untrusted networks.

NIST-800-53-AC-3.gap: Access enforcement is bypassed — the endpoints do not enforce it (CWE-863).

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: No accelerated tier for a pre-auth ransomware-associated NAS chain.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: Treats the appliance as ordinary infrastructure, not expedited KEV remediation.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Two-week internet-facing-app window is the whole exposure for a CVSS 9.8 chain.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: Measures patch approval, not de-exposure or prior-compromise triage.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: QNAP Photo Station CVE-2019-7192, KEV-listed 2022-06-08 with known ransomware campaign use, CVSS 9.8 and EPSS 0.88213 / 99.7th percentile as of 2026-08-13; a public pre-auth chain (gundy.py) and ~312,000 exposed devices make the standard patch window unacceptable, and the SLA's compensating-control branch (remove Photo Station, de-expose) applies where the app cannot be updated immediately.

new_control_requirements.name: PERIMETER-COMPROMISE-REBUILD-NOT-PATCH
new_control_requirements.description: Pre-rehearsed IR runbook for any perimeter device that suffers a pre-auth RCE CVE in active exploitation MUST default to config-exfil + rebuild + credential rotation, not patch-in-place. Patch-in-place leaves attacker-installed implants intact.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2019-7192 is the pre-auth entry of a root-RCE chain on internet-exposed QNAP NAS with CISA-recorded ransomware use; a NAS reachable while unpatched may already hold attacker persistence or encrypted data, so a Photo Station update alone does not remediate — the device needs integrity validation, credential rotation and, where compromised, rebuild.

CVE-2019-7193.name: QNAP QTS Improper Input Validation Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: A remote attacker with no credentials reaches a QTS handler that does not validate its input and injects code into the system (NVD, CWE-20); chained with the other three CVEs QNAP fixed in NAS-201911-25, that ends at root on the NAS. Which stage of CyCraft's published chain this identifier names was never disclosed.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; unauthenticated (UI:N), exercised as part of the CVE-2019-7192..7195 chain.
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; network-reachable and unauthenticated, though the only public tooling automates the CVE-2019-7192 file read rather than this stage.
attack_vector.ai_factor: Found by Henry Huang of CyCarrier CSIRT (CyCraft); the name is branding, not evidence of AI-assisted discovery.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Updating QTS to the fixed build and rebooting, plus removing the NAS from direct internet exposure on the KEV clock.
prevention.adequacy: The firmware fix only loads on reboot, and a device exposed while unpatched during a ransomware-active period may already be compromised.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alerting on unauthenticated Photo Station API activity from untrusted addresses, and on root-owned files or new administrative accounts appearing on the NAS without an admin session behind them.
detection.adequacy: NAS logging is thin, so detection relies on upstream network monitoring the affected sites frequently lack.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating a previously-exposed NAS as ransomware-suspect: offline integrity check, credential rotation, backup validation.
response.adequacy: A firmware update removes neither attacker-written files nor already-encrypted data; response must assume prior compromise for exposed devices.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: Counts a NAS patched at download, not at reboot, for a firmware fix.

NIST-800-53-SI-10.gap: Input validation is the failing control (CWE-20), and QNAP never published which unvalidated field it was.

NIST-800-53-SC-7.gap: SC-7 is satisfied by a boundary existing, not by the QTS surface being unreachable from it. The chain carrying this write primitive only runs against a NAS answering from the internet, so the control passes while a CVSS 9.8 pre-auth path stays addressable.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: No reboot-completion measurement and no accelerated tier for the ransomware-flagged chain.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: Does not distinguish a reboot-gated firmware fix from an app update.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Pre-reboot window is exploitable time for a CVSS 9.8 internet-facing chain.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: Measures patch approval, not installed-and-rebooted build or de-exposure.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: QNAP QTS CVE-2019-7193, KEV-listed 2022-06-08 with known ransomware campaign use, CVSS 9.8 and EPSS 0.14367 / 96th percentile as of 2026-08-13; the fix is QTS firmware (4.4.1 build 20190918+ / 4.3.6 build 20190919+) that only mitigates after reboot, so the SLA must measure installed-and-rebooted build, and its compensating-control branch (de-expose) applies until the reboot lands.

new_control_requirements.name: PERIMETER-COMPROMISE-REBUILD-NOT-PATCH
new_control_requirements.description: Pre-rehearsed IR runbook for any perimeter device that suffers a pre-auth RCE CVE in active exploitation MUST default to config-exfil + rebuild + credential rotation, not patch-in-place. Patch-in-place leaves attacker-installed implants intact.
