new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2019-7193 is one of the four QNAP QTS flaws NAS-201911-25 fixed together and that chain into pre-auth root RCE on an internet-exposed NAS, with CISA-recorded ransomware use; a NAS reachable while unpatched can hold attacker-written files that a QTS firmware update does not remove, so remediation must include integrity validation, credential rotation and rebuild where compromise is found.

CVE-2019-7194.name: QNAP Photo Station Path Traversal Vulnerability (CVE-2019-7194)

attack_vector.description: An unauthenticated attacker abuses a non-canonicalized `filename` parameter in Photo Station's media API to traverse out of the album root and read or modify system files; chained with the pre-auth album/access-code leak this reads /etc/shadow and SSH keys for pre-auth root on an internet-exposed QNAP NAS.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; the sample-album and slideshow endpoints answer before any authentication.
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; a single crafted POST after two discovery requests, fully automated by the public exploit.
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Found by Henry Huang of CyCarrier CSIRT and weaponized by Yunus Yildirim (Th3Gundy) — human research, no AI-assist claim.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Removing the Photo Station web surface from the public internet and updating to Photo Station 6.0.3 / 5.7.10 / 5.4.9 / 5.2.11 within the KEV window.
prevention.adequacy: Patching closes the traversal, but on a NAS that was internet-exposed while vulnerable it does not evict ransomware or attacker-planted persistence — the update must be paired with isolation, credential rotation and rebuild.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alerting on ../ sequences in Photo Station request parameters and on unauthenticated access to /photo/p/api/video.php.
detection.adequacy: Most home/SMB QNAP deployments forward no web logs to a SIEM, so detection is theoretical unless the NAS is fronted by a logging reverse proxy.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treat any WAN-exposed, unpatched QNAP NAS as compromised: take it offline, rebuild configuration, rotate all stored and transiting credentials, and restore data from an isolated backup.
response.adequacy: Effective only if an isolated, immutable backup exists; the ransomware families that hit QNAP specifically targeted the on-device backup copies.

NIST-800-53-SC-7.gap: Boundary protection is nominally in place, but nothing in SC-7 forced the Photo Station endpoint off the public internet, which is the exploit precondition.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: Flaw remediation exists but on a cadence far slower than the 14-day KEV due date for a 9.8 pre-auth traversal with EPSS 0.831.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: Patch management is required but with no expedited KEV/ransomware clock for an internet-facing appliance.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: A maintenance process satisfies B4 without removing the reachable vulnerable app or accelerating the fix.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Self-assessed patch maturity routinely omits unmanaged internet-facing NAS appliances.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: Technical-vulnerability management is evidenced while the KEV pre-auth traversal stays unpatched and exposed.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: QNAP Photo Station CVE-2019-7194 was KEV-listed 2022-06-08 with ransomware use Known and EPSS 0.831; the vendor fix (Photo Station 6.0.3 etc.) shipped in November 2019, so the binding clock is the KEV listing. A 4-hour SLA forces isolation-or-update on an internet-exposed NAS instead of the 30-day cadence that let DeadBolt-class ransomware reach the box first.

new_control_requirements.name: BACKUP-TIER-NETWORK-ISOLATION
new_control_requirements.description: A BeeStation is a consumer NAS whose whole purpose is holding the primary and backup copy of a household's or a branch site's data, and the packet's attack path reaches it with no credential and no user interaction — a pre-auth chain against the BeeStation Manager web management surface ending in OS command execution on the box that holds the data. Applied to this product, the control means the BeeStation Manager web surface answers only from an operator subnet or an authenticated VPN: not from the general user VLAN, and not from the internet via a UPnP mapping or a home-router port forward, which is how consumer NAS hardware at remote-worker and small-branch sites normally acquires exposure. The appliance's outbound path should be constrained too, so a rooted BeeStation cannot reach arbitrary destinations with the data it holds. Reachability is the entire exploit precondition for a pre-auth CWE-78 flaw, and it is the only lever an operator holds between a public exploit chain and a firmware update landing on a device that no enterprise console manages — a vendor patch exists but there is no live-patch path, so the appliance has to be taken through the update to remediate. The distinguishing test: from a general user VLAN and from an external address, attempt to load the BeeStation Manager web surface; anything that answers is within reach of the published chain, and "the NAS is on the internal network" is an assertion about topology, not a demonstration that the management surface is unreachable from untrusted segments.
new_control_requirements.evidence: The identical reachability logic governs QNAP Photo Station CVE-2019-7194: a pre-auth traversal chain on a consumer/SMB NAS web surface, with ~312K units found internet-exposed by CyCarrier and no operator-side lever other than reachability once the public chain (Exploit-DB 48531) exists. Restricting the Photo Station / QTS web surface to an operator subnet or VPN removes the exposure that the KEV listing (2022-06-08) and EPSS 0.831 make attacker-attractive.

CVE-2019-7195.name: QNAP Photo Station Path Traversal Vulnerability (CVE-2019-7195)

attack_vector.description: An unauthenticated attacker uses a non-canonicalized path parameter in Photo Station's media API to escape the album root and read or modify system files; combined with the pre-auth access-code leak it reaches /etc/shadow and SSH keys for pre-auth root on an internet-exposed QNAP NAS.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; the Photo Station discovery and media endpoints answer before authentication.
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; mechanical crafted requests, fully automated by the public chain.
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Human research (CyCarrier CSIRT) and human weaponization (Th3Gundy); no AI-assist claim.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Take the Photo Station web surface off the public internet and update to the fixed Photo Station build within the KEV window.
prevention.adequacy: Patching removes the traversal but does not clean a NAS that was exposed while vulnerable; isolation and rebuild must accompany it.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Detecting ../ sequences in Photo Station request parameters and unauthenticated access to the media API.
detection.adequacy: Rarely instrumented on home/SMB NAS without a logging reverse proxy in front.

response.what_would_have_worked: Offline rebuild, credential rotation, and restore from an isolated backup for any exposed, unpatched NAS.
response.adequacy: Depends on an isolated backup surviving the ransomware that specifically hunted on-device copies.

NIST-800-53-SC-7.gap: SC-7 leaves the Photo Station endpoint internet-reachable, which is the whole exploit precondition.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: Remediation cadence lags the 14-day KEV clock for a 9.8 traversal at EPSS 0.897.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: No expedited KEV/ransomware clock for an internet-facing NAS.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: A maintenance process meets B4 without removing the reachable vulnerable app.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Self-assessed maturity misses unmanaged internet-facing appliances.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: Vulnerability management is evidenced while the KEV traversal stays exposed.

attack_vector.description: A malicious app disconnects and reconnects an IPv6 socket to trigger a dangling freed socket-options pointer in XNU's in6_pcbdetach, reclaims it, and escalates the use-after-free to kernel code execution with system privileges.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; the app needs no special entitlement, only to be running on the device.
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; reliable enough to have powered public jailbreaks, though the attacker must first land an app (UI:R / local).
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Found by Ned Williamson of Google Project Zero; the 'Google Security Research' brand is Project Zero, not an AI-discovery tool.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Enforcing iOS 12.3 (and 12.4.1 after the re-introduction) / macOS 10.14.5 via MDM with user deferral disabled.
prevention.adequacy: The OS update requires a restart to take effect, so a downloaded-but-not-restarted device is still vulnerable; enforcement must gate on the running build, not the installed one.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Kernel-panic and app-behavior telemetry flagging in6_pcbdetach faults and jailbreak indicators after untrusted-app execution.
detection.adequacy: On-device forensic depth is limited on iOS; most estates see only MDM compliance state, not kernel-fault detail.

response.what_would_have_worked: Quarantine and reimage devices showing jailbreak/UAF indicators, and rotate credentials that were entered on a suspected-compromised device.
response.adequacy: System-privilege compromise defeats app-level containment, so a suspected device must be rebuilt rather than cleaned.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: Patch cadence and user-deferrable updates let the fixed build lag on BYOD hardware while public exploit code exists.

NIST-800-53-CM-7.gap: Least functionality does not restrict app execution on personal devices, which is the exploit precondition.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: No expedited clock for a KEV kernel LPE on mobile endpoints.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: A mobile-update policy that permits deferral satisfies B4 while the UAF persists.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Self-assessed OS-patch maturity misses unmanaged BYOD Apple devices.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: Technical-vulnerability management is evidenced while devices stay below the fixed build.

new_control_requirements.name: MOBILE-ENDPOINT-MDM-ENFORCED-KEV-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: iOS / iPadOS / macOS estates must enforce KEV-class updates within 24h via DDM; user-deferral disallowed.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2019-8605 is a KEV-listed (2022-06-27) XNU kernel UAF with public SockPuppet exploit code and proven mass exploitation via jailbreaks; the fix is iOS 12.3/12.4.1 and macOS 10.14.5. DDM-enforced, non-deferrable updates are what stop the fixed build from lagging on user-managed Apple devices.

new_control_requirements.name: MOBILE-OS-MINIMUM-PATCH-LEVEL-ENFORCEMENT
new_control_requirements.description: The recorded trigger is a malicious application causing unexpected changes in memory shared between processes, so for this entry the control's access-condition half is the load-bearing one: on any Apple device that cannot yet take the fixed build, the operator's remaining levers are constraining what code is allowed to run at all and withholding organizational data from the device until its build is at or above the fix. The fixed build must function as an access condition — mail, VPN and document access denied to a device below it — not as a row on a patch-compliance dashboard. The distinguishing test is to enrol a device pinned below the fixed build and confirm the policy actually denies it access to protected resources; an estate that surfaces the stale build on a report while the device keeps its access has recorded the exposure rather than removed it. Precondition: restricting untrusted or side-loaded application installation raises the bar for getting the attacker's application onto the device, but it does not evict an application already installed, and it does not cover one that arrived through the normal store channel. A device suspected of already running the malicious application belongs on the incident path, not the install-policy path. This is a holding measure for the window before the fixed build and its required restart land, not a substitute for them.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2019-8605 is triggered by a malicious app manipulating freed kernel socket-options memory, and iOS 12.4 re-introduced it — so a device pinned below 12.3/12.4.1 (or macOS 10.14.5) is exposed. Making the fixed build an access condition, plus restricting untrusted app installation, is the holding measure for devices that have not yet taken the reboot-gated update.

CVE-2020-3837.name: Apple Multiple Products Memory Corruption Vulnerability (CVE-2020-3837)

attack_vector.description: A malicious app submits a crafted IOAccelKernelCommand whose size check omits the 8-byte header; the timestamp-collect command then writes out of bounds into the next kernel page, and the app grooms that write into kernel code execution.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; any installed app can open the IOAcceleratorFamily user client.
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L per CVSS, though weaponizing the 1-8 byte write to full code execution needs shared-memory timing beyond the public trigger.
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Found by Brandon Azad of Google Project Zero; 'Google Security Research' is Project Zero, not an AI-discovery tool.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: MDM-enforced iOS 13.3.1 / macOS 10.15.3 with user deferral disabled.
prevention.adequacy: The fix needs a restart to load, so an updated-but-not-restarted device is still exposed; enforce on the running build.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Kernel-panic telemetry flagging IOAcceleratorFamily faults after untrusted-app execution.
detection.adequacy: iOS gives estates little kernel-fault visibility; detection is largely limited to MDM compliance state.

response.what_would_have_worked: Reimage devices showing IOAcceleratorFamily kernel faults from untrusted apps and rotate credentials entered on them.
response.adequacy: Kernel-privilege compromise requires rebuild, not cleanup.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: Deferrable updates let the fixed build lag while a public trigger exists.

NIST-800-53-CM-7.gap: Least functionality does not restrict apps reaching the IOAcceleratorFamily user client.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: Art21 obliges vulnerability handling but has no tier that pulls a kernel-privilege write forward. At EPSS 0.145 this entry never reaches the top of a risk-ranked queue, so iOS/iPadOS 13.3.1 rolls out on the ordinary mobile cadence.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: B4 asks for a maintenance process, and a mobile-update policy that lets the user postpone is one. Nothing in it reaches the restart that loads iOS/iPadOS 13.3.1 or macOS Catalina 10.15.3, so a device holding the downloaded update still runs the vulnerable driver.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Patch-operating-systems maturity is scored against the estate an organisation counts, and personally-owned iPhones and iPads carrying corporate mail rarely enter that inventory. A handset below iOS/iPadOS 13.3.1 is uncounted rather than remediated.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: Vulnerability management is evidenced while devices stay below 13.3.1.

CVE-2020-9907.name: Apple Multiple Products Memory Corruption Vulnerability (CVE-2020-9907)

attack_vector.description: A malicious app drives the AVEVideoEncoder kernel extension into a memory-corruption state through its user client and escalates to kernel code execution; Apple removed the vulnerable routine in the fix.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; any installed app can reach the AVEVideoEncoder user client.
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L per CVSS; no public exploit exists to confirm reliability.
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Credited to 08Tc3wBB working with ZecOps — human researchers, no AI-discovery claim.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: MDM-enforced iOS 13.6 / tvOS 13.4.8 with user deferral disabled.
prevention.adequacy: The fix needs a restart to load, so an updated-but-not-restarted device is still exposed; enforce on the running build.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Kernel-panic telemetry flagging AVEVideoEncoder faults after untrusted-app execution.
detection.adequacy: iOS gives estates little kernel-fault visibility; detection is largely limited to MDM compliance state.

response.what_would_have_worked: Reimage devices showing AVEVideoEncoder kernel faults from untrusted apps and rotate credentials entered on them.
response.adequacy: Kernel-privilege compromise requires rebuild, not cleanup.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: Deferrable updates let the fixed build lag despite Apple deleting the unsafe routine.

NIST-800-53-CM-7.gap: Least functionality does not restrict apps reaching the AVEVideoEncoder user client.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: Art21's patch obligation draws no line between a kernel-privilege flaw and a cosmetic one. EPSS 0.03875 with no public exploit makes this the entry a risk-ranked queue defers, though Apple judged the AVEVideoEncoder path unsafe enough to delete outright.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: A documented update policy meets B4 even where it permits indefinite user deferral. Apple did not bound the AVEVideoEncoder routine, it removed it, so only the restart onto iOS/iPadOS 13.6 or tvOS 13.4.8 closes the path — and B4 never asks whether that restart happened.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: The Essential Eight maturity level is self-assessed against the managed inventory, and Apple TV boxes on tvOS below 13.4.8 and personal iPads below 13.6 are exactly what that inventory omits. Uncounted devices are the ones that never take the update.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: Vulnerability management is evidenced while devices stay below 13.6.

CVE-2021-30533.name: Google Chromium PopupBlocker Security Bypass Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: A crafted nested iframe defeats Chromium's PopupBlocker navigation-policy check, letting attacker script force a redirect or popup the browser should have suppressed — the primitive behind malvertising forced-redirect chains across every Chromium browser.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; the attacker only needs the victim to load a page carrying the iframe.
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; a crafted iframe, no memory grooming, though the victim must view the page (UI:R).
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Reported by Eliya Stein (Confiant) via the Chrome bug bounty — human research, no AI-discovery claim.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Updating every Chromium browser to 91.0.4472.77+ within the KEV window and enforcing a relaunch so the fix loads.
prevention.adequacy: The fix only loads on full browser relaunch, so an updated-but-still-running browser stays bypassable; enforcement must confirm relaunch, not just install.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Proxy/DNS telemetry flagging redirect chains that originate inside third-party ad iframes.
detection.adequacy: Distinguishing an abusive forced redirect from ordinary ad navigation is noisy and rarely instrumented per-user.

response.what_would_have_worked: Blocking the abusing ad network / frame source and reviewing users who reached scam landing pages.
response.adequacy: Only reduces the delivery channel; the underlying bypass persists until browsers relaunch on the fixed build.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: Deferral and un-enforced relaunch leave the bypassable PopupBlocker live after the patch is 'deployed'.

NIST-800-53-SI-3.gap: The malicious-code posture relies on the very navigation restriction this CVE defeats.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: No expedited clock for a KEV browser bypass, easy to deprioritize as non-RCE.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: A deferral-permitting or relaunch-agnostic update process still meets B4.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Self-assessed maturity and unmanaged personal browsers miss Chromium instances below the fix.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: Browser-patching is evidenced while Chromium stays below 91.0.4472.77.

new_control_requirements.name: BROWSER-MANAGED-UPDATE-NO-DEFERRAL
new_control_requirements.description: Enterprise update rings must not defer security-channel browser updates beyond 24h.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2021-30533 is a KEV-listed (2022-06-27) Chromium PopupBlocker bypass fixed in Chrome 91.0.4472.77 (2021-05-25) that affects Chrome, Edge and Opera alike; because the fix only loads on relaunch, a no-deferral update ring plus enforced relaunch is what actually removes the live bypass.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2021-30533 was KEV-listed 2022-06-27; because it is a navigation bypass rather than RCE it is exactly the KEV entry an SI-2/patch-management programme deprioritizes. A KEV-tied SLA forces the Chromium 91.0.4472.77+ update and relaunch onto managed browsers rather than letting it wait behind higher-CVSS items.

attack_vector.description: A malicious app supplies malformed parameters to the IOMobileFrameBuffer kernel driver, overflowing a kernel buffer and escalating to kernel code execution; demonstrated at the Tianfu Cup and fixed in iOS/iPadOS 15.2.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; any installed app can reach the IOMobileFrameBuffer user client.
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L per CVSS, though only competition-grade (privately reported) exploitation is known, not public code.
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Found by the Pangu team at the Tianfu Cup — human researchers, no AI-discovery claim.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: MDM-enforced iOS/iPadOS 15.2 with user deferral disabled.
prevention.adequacy: The fix needs a restart to load, so an updated-but-not-restarted device is still exposed; enforce on the running build.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Kernel-panic telemetry flagging IOMobileFrameBuffer faults after untrusted-app execution.
detection.adequacy: iOS gives estates little kernel-fault visibility; detection is largely limited to MDM compliance state.

response.what_would_have_worked: Reimage devices showing IOMobileFrameBuffer kernel faults from untrusted apps and rotate credentials entered on them.
response.adequacy: Kernel-privilege compromise requires rebuild, not cleanup.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: Deferrable updates let the fixed build lag while a competition-proven overflow is known exploitable.

NIST-800-53-CM-7.gap: Least functionality does not restrict apps reaching the IOMobileFrameBuffer user client.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: Art21 requires managed vulnerability handling but sets no accelerated clock for a KEV kernel LPE. A privately-reported competition bug carries low EPSS — 0.02923 here — so iOS/iPadOS 15.2 lands on the routine mobile cadence while the overflow stays locally reachable.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: Having an update process meets B4, and an iOS policy that lets the user defer the restart is still a process. The IOMobileFrameBuffer fix ships only in iOS/iPadOS 15.2 and loads at reboot, so a deferred handset keeps the overflow Pangu demonstrated at the Tianfu Cup.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Self-assessment sets the bar here: an iPhone or iPad below iOS/iPadOS 15.2 that no MDM enrols never enters the patch-operating-systems score, so the maturity rating can rise while the un-enrolled handsets keep the framebuffer overflow.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: Vulnerability management is evidenced while devices stay below 15.2.

new_control_requirements.name: MOBILE-ENDPOINT-MDM-ENFORCED-KEV-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: iOS / iPadOS / macOS estates must enforce KEV-class updates within 24h via DDM; user-deferral disallowed.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2021-30983 is a KEV-listed (2022-06-27) IOMobileFrameBuffer kernel buffer overflow fixed in iOS/iPadOS 15.2 and demonstrated at the Tianfu Cup. DDM-enforced non-deferrable updates prevent the fixed build lagging on user-managed devices.

new_control_requirements.name: MOBILE-ZERO-CLICK-HARDENING
new_control_requirements.description: For the population plausibly inside the targeting set this class of Apple flaw serves — executives, journalists, legal and security staff — the reboot-gated update is not fast enough on its own, because the packet describes the overflow as a sandbox-escape / privilege step inside a chain rather than a standalone bug. Place those users in a reduced-attack-surface mode so untrusted web content, message attachments, fonts and link previews are not processed automatically, narrowing the delivery path into the CWE-119 primitive during the window between the 2026-03-20 KEV listing and completed fleet restart. This has to be a standing posture for the high-risk cohort assigned before the next disclosure, not a reaction to this CVE — the mode only helps if it was already on when the chain arrived.
new_control_requirements.evidence: IOMobileFrameBuffer bugs like CVE-2021-30983 are the privilege step of iOS chains, and a sibling IOMobileFrameBuffer flaw was exploited as a zero-day the same year; a reduced-attack-surface mode (Lockdown-style) assigned to the high-risk cohort narrows the delivery path into this kernel-buffer-overflow primitive during the window before the reboot-gated iOS 15.2 update lands.

CVE-2021-38163.name: SAP NetWeaver Unrestricted File Upload Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: An authenticated non-admin user uploads a JSP through the Visual Composer VCParMigrator servlet and uses a parName path-traversal to place it in a web-served directory, then requests it to run OS commands as the SAP Java process account.
attack_vector.privileges_required: low — PR:L; any authenticated non-administrative NetWeaver portal account suffices, no admin role needed.
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; deterministic traversal once a session exists, no race or memory-corruption primitive.
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Fixed by SAP product security via Note 3084487; no AI-assisted discovery is claimed.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Apply SAP Note 3084487 and restart AS Java, or disable the unused Visual Composer runtime and block external access to the VCParMigrator servlet.
prevention.adequacy: Patching closes the traversal, but any JSP already dropped before remediation survives the update — an exposed instance needs its web-served trees audited for planted files, not just the note applied.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alert on VCParMigrator POSTs with ../ in parName and on new JSPs appearing under servlet_jsp trees outside a deployment.
detection.adequacy: Web-access logs capture the upload, but a defender who logs only authentication events misses the traversal request that flows over an already-authenticated session.

response.what_would_have_worked: Remove planted JSPs, rotate the SAP Java service-account credentials, and review server data the process could read or modify.
response.adequacy: Effective only if the web root and servlet_jsp trees are baselined; without a known-good comparison an implant is easy to miss.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: Patch existed from August 2021 yet the flaw was KEV-listed in June 2022; SI-2 cadence did not force KEV-tier urgency on an exposed portal.

NIST-800-53-SI-10.gap: Input validation is nominally required, but the missing canonicalization is inside shipped SAP code the operator cannot patch.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: Patch-management is mandated but the AS Java restart window is routinely deferred under ERP change control.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: Secure configuration is expected, yet the default Visual Composer runtime exposes VCParMigrator to any portal user.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: A 30-day internet-facing patch SLA is far longer than the exploitation window this KEV entry implies.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: Vulnerability management logs the note but does not distinguish a KEV RCE from routine bugs in prioritization.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: SAP NetWeaver Visual Composer 7.0 RT (7.30–7.50) had SAP Note 3084487 available from August 2021, yet CVE-2021-38163 was not KEV-listed until 2022-06-09 (due 2022-06-30) and sits at EPSS percentile 0.98333 — a KEV-tier 4-hour clock against listing/patch-availability is the control that would have compressed the ~10-month exposure window on internet-facing portals.

CVE-2021-4034.name: Red Hat Polkit Out-of-Bounds Read and Write Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: An unprivileged local user runs pkexec with argc==0 to trigger an out-of-bounds array access, re-injects a stripped environment variable (GCONV_PATH) pointing at a malicious gconv module, and pkexec loads it as root.
attack_vector.privileges_required: low — PR:L; any local unprivileged account, no prior escalation.
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; deterministic memory access, no race or ASLR defeat, portable across distributions.
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Found by the Qualys Research Team through manual analysis of pkexec; no AI tooling is credited.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Install the patched polkit package, or immediately strip the setuid bit (chmod 0755 /usr/bin/pkexec) as a stopgap.
prevention.adequacy: Both are effective and the de-suid mitigation is instant, but the patch-only framing misses that the setuid bit itself is the exploitable primitive an operator can remove before the errata lands.

detection.what_would_have_worked: auditd/eBPF rules alerting on pkexec execve with empty args or with GCONV_PATH in the environment.
detection.adequacy: High-signal because normal pkexec use never runs with argc==0, but it requires the audit telemetry to be collected and shipped off-host before the attempt.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treat any host that ran the primitive as root-compromised: rebuild or rotate all credentials the root account could reach.
response.adequacy: Necessary given full root, but detection has to have fired first — the exploit leaves no on-disk artifact of its own after cleanup.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: Patch closes it, but the flaw lived for ~12 years so SI-2 gave no protection across the entire pre-disclosure period.

NIST-800-53-AC-6.gap: pkexec is legitimately setuid-root; least privilege cannot prevent an escalation built into a needed helper.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: Names patching but not the immediate de-suid stopgap the Known-ransomware EPSS 0.999 profile demands.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: Secure config as assessed does not require minimizing setuid helpers a default install ships.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: A 30-day OS-patch SLA outlasts the post-access escalation timeline for a universal LPE.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: Vuln-management cadence does not surface the over-privileged-setuid least-functionality gap until a CVE forces it.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: polkit pkexec CVE-2021-4034 (PwnKit) is Known-ransomware-linked, sits at EPSS percentile 0.99854, and was KEV-listed 2022-06-27; it has a distribution patch AND an instant compensating control (chmod 0755 /usr/bin/pkexec), so a 4-hour KEV clock keyed to listing/patch-availability — with the de-suid stopgap as the documented compensating mitigation — is directly satisfiable.

new_control_requirements.name: SUID-MINIMIZATION-FOR-KERNEL-LPE-CARRIER-BINARIES
new_control_requirements.description: Hosts that do not use SSH host-based authentication SHOULD have ssh-keysign de-suid-ed. Hosts that do not use age-warn login UX SHOULD have chage de-suid-ed. Removes the privileged-process carrier even before the kernel patch lands.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2021-4034 escalates only because pkexec carries the setuid bit; the documented interim mitigation is exactly to strip it (chmod 0755 /usr/bin/pkexec). Applying this control's setuid-minimization discipline to pkexec on hosts where interactive polkit elevation is unneeded removes the privileged carrier before the polkit errata (RHSB-2022-001-equivalent) is deployed.

CVE-2022-22047.name: Microsoft Windows Client Server Runtime Subsystem (CSRSS) Privilege Escalation Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: A local authenticated user triggers a CSRSS state-resolution flaw so the SYSTEM-privileged subsystem acts on attacker-controlled input, escalating the user to SYSTEM.
attack_vector.privileges_required: low — PR:L; requires prior code execution as a normal user, so this is a second-stage escalation.
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; once developed the exploit runs deterministically, though Microsoft withheld the reachability detail.
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Reported and fixed internally by Microsoft; no AI-assisted discovery is claimed.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Install the July 2022 Windows security update and reboot every affected host on the KEV clock.
prevention.adequacy: The patch is the only fix, but completion must be measured by rebooted build — a host patched-but-not-restarted still runs vulnerable CSRSS.

detection.what_would_have_worked: EDR rules on unexpected SYSTEM-integrity process creation from user-context parents and on anomalous csrss.exe behavior.
detection.adequacy: Behavioral only — with no public IoC signature, detection relies on the escalation's effect rather than a known exploit artifact.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treat a host where the escalation fired as SYSTEM-compromised: isolate, rebuild, and rotate credentials cached on it.
response.adequacy: Appropriate for a SYSTEM LPE, but depends on detection firing since the bug leaves no distinctive on-disk trace.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: Exploited as a zero-day; patch and in-the-wild use arrived together, so SI-2 gave no pre-July-2022 coverage.

NIST-800-53-AC-6.gap: CSRSS runs as SYSTEM by design; least privilege cannot contain the crossed boundary.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: Routine monthly cadence, not the KEV-clock reboot an actively-exploited LPE needs.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: Host hardening does not address a failing SYSTEM privilege boundary in a chained escalation.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Right tier only if measured by rebooted build; downloaded-not-restarted hosts stay exploitable.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: Periodic assessment does not elevate an in-the-wild SYSTEM LPE above the monthly Windows backlog.

new_control_requirements.name: ACTIVELY-EXPLOITED-OS-LPE-REMEDIATION-WINDOW-ENFORCEMENT
new_control_requirements.description: The packet's vector places this in Windows Remote Desktop Services and describes an authorized attacker elevating privileges locally (CWE-269) — the account is already legitimate, so no account model is being abused; a privilege boundary inside the service is failing. For this CVE the control means the Windows update carrying the fix is driven across every affected host on the KEV clock that opened 2026-02-10 rather than folded into the next monthly rollup, with completion measured by each host's installed build against the fixed build for its SKU rather than by 'approved' or 'downloaded' in the management console. Hosts running the Remote Desktop Services role are the population to enumerate first, because a machine where many non-administrative users hold interactive sessions is a machine where the precondition this flaw needs — an already-authorized local user — is the normal operating state rather than an anomaly. There is a vendor patch with no live-patch path, and the fix typically requires a service restart or system reboot, so a host that has taken the update but not restarted still carries the vulnerable code and must be counted as exposed; on a session host that restart is also the step most likely to be deferred, because taking it evicts logged-on users, and a deferral recorded as 'patched' is the specific way this remediation goes wrong. The control's second half is the load-bearing one here: since the attacker is already authorized, tightening account privilege does not contain the escalation, which is exactly why the least-privilege and identity-and-access controls cited on this entry can pass their attestations while the flaw stays fully exploitable. Priority follows the packet rather than the CVSS band: a public PoC, confirmed exploitation, and the packet's own note that LPEs of this class are routinely paired with an initial-access flaw by ransomware operators make this the containment step for a chain, not a standalone endpoint item.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2022-22047 is a Windows CSRSS local escalation to SYSTEM that Microsoft flagged exploited-in-the-wild at the July 2022 Patch Tuesday and CISA KEV-listed 2022-07-12 (due 2022-08-02). Like the RDS case the control was written for, it is a same-host escalation of an already-authorized user across a service privilege boundary, the fix requires a reboot with no live-patch path, and completion must be measured by rebooted build — session/server hosts where the deferred reboot is most tempting are exactly where it stays exposed.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2022-22047 was exploited as a zero-day and KEV-listed on 2022-07-12; with no configuration-only mitigation and reboot-gated remediation, a KEV-tier SLA is what forces the July 2022 update and its restart across the Windows estate on the compressed clock the in-the-wild use demands.

CVE-2022-26134.name: Atlassian Confluence Server and Data Center Remote Code Execution Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: An unauthenticated attacker embeds an OGNL expression in the Confluence request URI; the server evaluates it and runs OS commands as the Confluence process, commonly dropping a web shell.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; no authentication required.
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; a single crafted GET, network reachability the only precondition.
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Found by Volexity via in-the-wild forensics; no AI tooling is credited.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Block internet traffic to affected products immediately (CISA required action), then upgrade to a fixed release and restart Confluence.
prevention.adequacy: Isolation was the only prevention during the pre-patch window; the upgrade closes the sink but does not evict a web shell dropped beforehand.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alert on ${...} OGNL patterns in request URIs and on the Confluence process spawning shells or writing JSPs.
detection.adequacy: Strong signal, but per-request web logs must be forwarded off-box — an attacker with RCE can tamper with local logs.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treat an exposed instance as compromised: rebuild or forensically clear it, hunt for memshells, and rotate all credentials it held.
response.adequacy: Essential given persistence-through-patch, but only effective with an off-host log/forensic baseline to compare against.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: Zero-day discovered in active exploitation; no patch existed during the initial window.

NIST-800-53-SI-10.gap: The OGNL-evaluation sink is in vendor code an operator's input-validation program cannot reach.

NIS2-Art21-incident-handling.gap: Does not force the rebuild/rotation response a persistence-through-patch web shell requires.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: Exploitation preceded the patch; the operative control was network isolation, not patching.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: OGNL URI evaluation is default application behavior, not a configurable option.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: No patch to apply for the first days; isolation was the real lever.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: Assessment cadence is irrelevant during a zero-day window and does not trigger emergency isolation.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Confluence CVE-2022-26134 was KEV-listed 2022-06-02 with a four-day due date (2022-06-06) and EPSS percentile 0.99994; the KEV entry's own required action was to block internet traffic immediately. A 4-hour KEV SLA keyed to listing — with the CISA internet-block as the documented compensating control until the fixed release and restart land — is exactly the response this zero-day needed.

new_control_requirements.name: PERIMETER-COMPROMISE-REBUILD-NOT-PATCH
new_control_requirements.description: Pre-rehearsed IR runbook for any perimeter device that suffers a pre-auth RCE CVE in active exploitation MUST default to config-exfil + rebuild + credential rotation, not patch-in-place. Patch-in-place leaves attacker-installed implants intact.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2022-26134 is a pre-auth RCE that Volexity found already exploited in the wild, and attackers dropped in-memory Godzilla/Behinder web shells that survive an Atlassian version upgrade. For any internet-exposed Confluence Server/Data Center, patch-in-place is insufficient — the rebuild-and-rotate default this control mandates is what removes the implant the fixed 7.18.1/7.4.17-branch build leaves behind.

CVE-2022-26138.name: Atlassian Questions For Confluence App Hard-coded Credentials Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: An unauthenticated attacker logs into Confluence as the disabledsystemuser account created by the Questions for Confluence app, using the app's shipped hardcoded password, and reads all confluence-users-group content.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; the hardcoded credential is the only requirement.
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; a single login request once the public password is known.
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Self-disclosed by Atlassian; no AI-assisted discovery is claimed.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Upgrade Questions for Confluence to 2.7.38+/3.0.5+, which removes the disabledsystemuser account as well as stopping it being created — or delete/disable the account directly where the app cannot.
prevention.adequacy: The upgrade is genuine remediation, but the two adjacent responses are not: uninstalling the app leaves the account enabled, and on a read-only external directory (Crowd) the fixed app cannot delete it. Both cases need the account removed by hand, and only a directory query proves it is gone.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alert on any authentication as disabledsystemuser and on the account's existence in the user directory.
detection.adequacy: Simple and high-fidelity, but only if authentication events for that specific account are actually monitored — a service-style name is easy to overlook.

response.what_would_have_worked: Audit disabledsystemuser access history and treat any content it could reach as potentially exposed.
response.adequacy: Bounded by what confluence-users can see, but requires login history retention to reconstruct the exposure window.

NIST-800-53-AC-2.gap: The account is created programmatically outside provisioning; AC-2 review rarely catches it before the public password is used.

NIST-800-53-IA-2.gap: The authenticator is a public compile-time constant; IA-2 authenticates the attacker as designed.

NIS2-Art21-identity-management.gap: Identity governance does not inherently detect a vendor-injected static-password account.

UK-CAF-B2.gap: Does not force enumeration of app-created accounts for hardcoded authenticators.

AU-Essential-8-MFA.gap: The machine-style account is typically outside interactive MFA scope.

ISO-27001-2022-A.5.16-Federated.gap: The disabledsystemuser account is created by an app install rather than by provisioning, so it never enters Confluence's managed identity lifecycle and no joiner-mover-leaver review ever reaches it.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: Uninstalling Questions for Confluence leaves the account enabled, and a read-only external directory blocks the fixed app from deleting it — version evidence proves neither.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2022-26138 was KEV-listed 2022-07-29 (due 2022-08-19) at EPSS percentile 0.99911 with a public hardcoded password; the fastest verified mitigation is disabling/deleting the disabledsystemuser account. A 4-hour KEV SLA — with account-disablement as the documented compensating control ahead of the app upgrade — is what closes the window before the circulating credential is used.

new_control_requirements.name: FRAMEWORK-DEFAULT-SECRET-DETECTION
new_control_requirements.description: The secret sits inside the product: Studio 5000 Logix Designer 'may allow a key to be discovered', and that key is what verifies Logix controllers are communicating with Rockwell design software. Because the constant an attacker needs is obtainable from the design software rather than from the target site, no amount of operator-side credential hygiene reduces the exposure — which is exactly why the least-privilege and identity-and-access-control gaps are recorded against this entry: the attacker never authenticates as any engineer, so per-account privilege scoping is never consulted and the account model an identity attestation examines is bypassed rather than abused. The control's requirement here is to inventory every Studio 5000 installation and every Logix controller in the estate as depending on a product-shipped verification key, gate each of those deployments on the vendor update rather than on a password or account policy, and re-run that check after any engineering-workstation rebuild, image restore or controller replacement, since those are the operations that quietly reintroduce an unpatched pairing at a site that had been remediated. Distinguishing test: produce, per cell, the Studio 5000 version and the controller firmware actually in service and show each is at or above the vendor's fixed level — an attestation that every engineer holds a unique Studio 5000 account passes cleanly while this flaw stays fully exploitable. Precondition: the vendor update is what removes the dependence on the discoverable key; this control is the inventory and the gate that ensure every installation reaches it, and it gives nothing on its own to a site that has not yet taken the update. It also does not detect a controller an unauthorized application has already connected to, so a cell that was reachable during the exposure window needs its controller configuration and control logic compared against a known-good copy rather than being closed on the patch.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2022-26138 is the same class as the control's premise — a product-shipped secret an operator cannot manage away: the Questions for Confluence app hardcodes the disabledsystemuser password (disabled1system1user6708) identically across every install, so no site-side credential hygiene reduces exposure, exactly as the discoverable Studio 5000 key. The requirement here is to inventory every Confluence instance that ever installed the vulnerable app and verify by directory query that no disabledsystemuser account remains — the fixed versions 2.7.38+/3.0.5+ delete it, but an instance that uninstalled the app instead, or that authenticates against a read-only external directory the app cannot write to, still holds it — and to re-check after any app reinstall or instance restore.

attack_vector.description: An attacker coerces a domain controller to authenticate over NTLM via the unauthenticated LSARPC/MS-EFSRPC surface, then relays that authentication to AD CS to obtain a DC certificate and pivot to domain compromise.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; the coercion call needs no authentication.
attack_vector.complexity: high — AC:H; full impact depends on a relay-able target (AD CS web enrollment without EPA/channel binding) being present.
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Coercion technique published by Gilles Lionel (PetitPotam); no AI tooling is credited.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Apply the May 2022 update (per CISA DC guidance) AND enable Extended Protection for Authentication / HTTPS on AD CS web enrollment, and restrict NTLM.
prevention.adequacy: The patch closes the coercion path but not the relay target; without AD CS EPA hardening the domain can still fall, and naive DC patching risks breaking PIV/CAC.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Monitor for LSARPC/EFSRPC coercion calls to DCs and for NTLM-authenticated AD CS enrollment of machine accounts.
detection.adequacy: Effective where AD CS and RPC telemetry is collected, but many estates do not log certsrv enrollment provenance.

response.what_would_have_worked: Revoke certificates issued via relayed enrollment, rotate the DC machine account (krbtgt if abused), and hunt for persistence.
response.adequacy: Necessary if the relay succeeded, but requires enrollment logging to identify the fraudulent certificates.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: Patch closes the coercion path only; the AD CS relay target must be hardened separately.

NIST-800-53-IA-2.gap: Authenticated identity is forged via coercion-and-relay, which IA-2 assurance does not anticipate.

NIS2-Art21-network-security.gap: Does not mandate the NTLM egress restrictions and AD CS EPA hardening that break the chain.

UK-CAF-B2.gap: Rarely tests machine-identity resistance to forced authentication and relay.

AU-ISM-1546.gap: A coerced NTLM exchange is a legitimate credential use steered to the wrong endpoint.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: Does not capture the patch-plus-configuration nature of the fix or the DC PIV/CAC caveat.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2022-26925 was KEV-listed 2022-07-01 (due 2022-07-22); because the May 2022 patch must be paired with AD CS EPA/channel-binding hardening — and applied to DCs per CISA guidance to avoid breaking PIV/CAC — a KEV-tier SLA with those documented compensating controls is what drives the complete, not partial, remediation across the domain within the exploitation window.

CVE-2022-27924.name: Synacor Zimbra Collaboration Suite (ZCS) Command Injection Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: An unauthenticated attacker injects memcached commands via unescaped CRLF in a Zimbra lookup key, overwriting route-cache entries so a victim's proxied mail session is redirected to an attacker host that captures cleartext credentials.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; the injection request is unauthenticated.
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; a single crafted request poisons the cache, with the victim's next proxied login completing the theft.
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Reported by SonarSource research; no AI tooling is credited.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Apply 9.0.0 Patch 24.1 on the 9.0.0 line or 8.8.15 Patch 31.1 on the 8.8.15 line, restart services, then force resets for potentially-proxied credentials.
prevention.adequacy: The patch stops new injection, but credentials harvested before remediation stay valid until reset — patching alone does not close the credential-theft loop.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Monitor for CRLF in proxy lookup parameters and for route-cache entries pointing mailboxes at hosts outside the mailstore pool.
detection.adequacy: Requires proxy-layer request logging and cache-state visibility that many ZCS deployments do not retain.

response.what_would_have_worked: Force password resets across affected mailboxes and review for unauthorized mailbox access during the exposure window.
response.adequacy: Bounded by mailbox scope, but effective only with access logs to identify which credentials were exposed.

NIST-800-53-SI-10.gap: The unescaped-CRLF sink is in Zimbra proxy code an operator's input-validation program cannot reach.

NIST-800-53-SC-8.gap: Cache poisoning reroutes proxied credentials to the wrong endpoint; SC-8 on the internal hop does not detect the redirection.

NIS2-Art21-network-security.gap: Does not mandate segmentation/neutralization of the internal memcached lookup path.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: The vulnerable key construction is default ZCS behavior, not configurable.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: A 30-day tier is far longer than the KEV clock for a Known-ransomware credential-theft bug.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: Does not force the post-patch credential-reset a cleartext-theft flaw requires.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Zimbra CVE-2022-27924 is Known-ransomware-linked, sits at EPSS percentile 0.99701, and was KEV-listed 2022-08-04 (due 2022-08-25) with vendor patches (8.8.15 P31.1 / 9.0.0 P24.1) already shipped since 2022-05-10; a 4-hour KEV SLA against patch availability is what compresses the window during which an unauthenticated request can poison the mail proxy and steal cleartext credentials.

CVE-2022-27925.name: Synacor Zimbra Collaboration Suite (ZCS) Arbitrary File Upload Vulnerability (CVE-2022-27925)

attack_vector.description: A ZIP archive posted to the mboximport endpoint is extracted without normalising entry names, so entries carrying ../ segments are written outside the import directory. Planting a JSP in the Zimbra web root and then requesting it yields code execution as the zimbra service account on a server that holds every mailbox in the organisation.
attack_vector.privileges_required: high — PR:H on paper, an administrator account per the vendor note; in practice the same servlet's authentication check did not enforce, so the observed attacks needed no account at all
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; a single HTTP POST with a crafted archive, no race, no memory grooming, and the account-name parameter hardcoded to admin in every public exploit
attack_vector.ai_factor: None claimed or evidenced. No vendor or third-party source attributes the discovery to AI-assisted analysis, and the vendor names no reporter at all.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Applying 9.0.0 Patch 24 or 8.8.15 Patch 31 when it shipped on 2022-03-30, treating an internet-facing mail platform's remote-code-execution fix as expedited regardless of the vendor's Medium rating.
prevention.adequacy: BOD 22-01's clock started on 2022-08-11 with a 2022-09-01 due date — after Volexity had already counted over 1,000 compromised instances. The directive would have driven the patch, but months after the exposure that mattered.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Diffing the deployed JSP set under the ZCS web root against the vendor's default file list for the installed release, and alerting on mboximport POSTs that draw a 40x.
detection.adequacy: Effective but only available after Volexity published the reference JSP lists on 2022-08-10; before that an operator had no baseline to diff against, and the webshell's zero-byte 200 response gives signature tooling nothing to match.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating any ZCS instance that ran an unpatched build while internet-facing as compromised: exporting configuration, rebuilding, and rotating mailbox and service credentials rather than upgrading in place.
response.adequacy: This is the only response that removes the implant, and it is expensive — a rebuild of a production mail server. Most operators upgraded in place, which closes the traversal and leaves the webshell.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: Flaw remediation was performed against the vendor's Medium rating and its authenticated-administrator precondition, both of which were wrong about real reachability. SI-2 has no re-triage trigger for third-party research that invalidates a vendor's stated precondition.

NIST-800-53-AC-6.gap: Least privilege over the Zimbra administrator population is genuinely in place and irrelevant — the extraction path never consults the caller's privilege, and the companion bypass meant no account was held.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: The clock most operators ran started at the 2022-08-11 KEV listing rather than the 2022-03-30 vendor release, which puts the compliant deadline six weeks after mass exploitation began.

NIS2-Art21-incident-handling.gap: Incident handling needs an incident to detect. A planted JSP that answers unknown requests with a zero-byte 200 produces no alert, so the process is never triggered and the upgrade closes the ticket with the implant in place.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: B4's levers are supported builds and removing unnecessary interfaces; on Network Edition the backup extension serving mboximport is a bought feature that cannot be dropped without losing mailbox import, so patch cadence is the whole control, and a quarterly cadence left Patch 23 running when exploitation started in June 2022.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: The two-week internet-facing window is adequate on its own terms, but only if ZCS is classified as an internet-facing application. Estates that classified their mail server as internal inherited the longer window and were exposed through the June-to-August 2022 campaign.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: A.8.8 is satisfied by acting on the advisory as written. The advisory understated both severity and reachability, so a fully compliant programme deferred the patch for a quarter.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Zimbra shipped the mboximport fix in ZCS 9.0.0 Patch 24 on 2022-03-30 and rated it Medium; CISA listed CVE-2022-27925 on 2022-08-11 with ransomware use Known. The 'whichever is later' clause is what makes this control bite on this entry — it forces the KEV date to reopen a patch the vendor's own severity had already let an operator defer, and at EPSS 0.98586 (99.919th percentile as of 2026-08-13) this remains one of the most-attacked CVEs in the corpus four years on.

new_control_requirements.name: PERIMETER-COMPROMISE-REBUILD-NOT-PATCH
new_control_requirements.description: Pre-rehearsed IR runbook for any perimeter device that suffers a pre-auth RCE CVE in active exploitation MUST default to config-exfil + rebuild + credential rotation, not patch-in-place. Patch-in-place leaves attacker-installed implants intact.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Volexity found over 1,000 internet-facing ZCS instances already carrying JSP webshells when it published on 2022-08-10, with exploitation dating to the end of June 2022. Upgrading those hosts to 9.0.0 Patch 24 removes the traversal and leaves every planted JSP exactly where it was written, which is why an exposed Zimbra server belongs on the rebuild-and-rotate path rather than the patch path.

CVE-2022-29499.name: Mitel MiVoice Connect Data Validation Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: An unauthenticated request to vtest.php makes the Service Appliance fetch a URL of the attacker's choosing, which satisfies the appliance's own local-caller restriction. A second request to ucbsync.php then places shell metacharacters into a parameter that is interpolated into a curl command line, so the appliance executes attacker-supplied commands. From there the intruder holds a Linux host inside the voice network.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; no credential, no session and no prior foothold, only HTTP reach to the Service Appliance
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; two GET requests in sequence, with the SSRF step existing only to defeat a source-address check rather than to leak any information the attacker needs
attack_vector.ai_factor: Found by Patrick Bennett of CrowdStrike during incident response on a compromised appliance and reported privately to Mitel. Nothing in the advisory or the write-up indicates automated or AI-assisted analysis.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Keeping the Service Appliance's HTTP interface off any internet-reachable path, so the two unauthenticated requests could not be delivered at all, and obtaining the remediation named in Mitel Security Bulletin 22-0002-001 as soon as advisory 22-0002 appeared on 2022-04-19.
prevention.adequacy: BOD 22-01 gave a 2022-07-18 due date, nearly five months after the 2022-03-01 exploitation CrowdStrike logged. Segregation is the only control on this list that would have been in place before the vendor knew the bug existed.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Network inspection of traffic to the telephony appliance, where the Emerging Threats rule for the vtest.php request pattern fires on the inbound exploit rather than depending on logs the appliance itself holds.
detection.adequacy: Sound, and the only detection that is out of the intruder's reach — the on-appliance logs were deleted and dd was run to fill free space so they could not be carved back; they were recovered only because /tmp happened to be a separate partition. It also only exists after the signature was written, which is after the intrusion that produced it.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating a Service Appliance reachable from an untrusted segment while unremediated as compromised: rebuilding from vendor media, hunting for the pdf_import.php webshell and the renamed Chisel binary, and rotating every credential that transited the appliance.
response.adequacy: Necessary but slow. The appliance is the voice platform's front door, so a rebuild takes the phone system down, which is exactly the pressure that pushes operators toward remediating in place and leaving the implant.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: The fixed build number is portal-gated behind Security Bulletin 22-0002-001, so version-comparison flaw remediation produces 'no fix identified' and drops the asset from the queue.

NIST-800-53-SC-7.gap: Boundary protection is implemented to keep the internet out of the enterprise, not to stop a UC appliance's own management surface from answering the internet — which is the only precondition this exploit has.

NIST-800-53-SI-4.gap: Monitoring the appliance means trusting logs the intruder can reach; on the box CrowdStrike examined they were deleted and dd was run to fill free space, and they came back only because /tmp was a separate partition.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: The three-week KEV window assumes an obtainable patch; the remediation needs a Mitel portal entitlement that in reseller-maintained estates nobody in the organisation holds.

NIS2-Art21-incident-handling.gap: The process triggers on detection, and the only detection surface was a telephony appliance's web log that the attacker destroyed.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: The deployment was on a current, supported Connect release; B4 does not force the operator to enumerate a telephony appliance's web interface as internet-facing attack surface.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: A VoIP service appliance is classified as telephony infrastructure rather than an application, so the internet-facing patch window is never applied to it.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: Acting on Mitel advisory 22-0002 the day it published on 2022-04-19 still leaves the operator seven weeks behind the 2022-03-01 exploitation.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.16.gap: Monitoring rarely covers traffic to the UC appliance, which is where the only reliable signature for this exploit fires.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.22.gap: Segregation treats the UC platform as a segment to protect rather than as a device whose management interface must itself be segregated, so the appliance kept answering unauthenticated HTTP from outside.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Mitel MiVoice Connect Service Appliances were exploited on 2022-03-01 per CrowdStrike's recovered logs, advisory 22-0002 followed on 2022-04-19, and CISA listed CVE-2022-29499 on 2022-06-27 with ransomware use Known and a 2022-07-18 due date. The control's 'documented compensating controls' branch is the operative one for this product, because the vendor publishes no fixed build number publicly — removing the SA 100 / SA 400 / Virtual SA web interface from untrusted segments is the mitigation an operator can actually deploy inside four hours.

new_control_requirements.name: PERIMETER-COMPROMISE-REBUILD-NOT-PATCH
new_control_requirements.description: Pre-rehearsed IR runbook for any perimeter device that suffers a pre-auth RCE CVE in active exploitation MUST default to config-exfil + rebuild + credential rotation, not patch-in-place. Patch-in-place leaves attacker-installed implants intact.
new_control_requirements.evidence: This is a PR:N, CVSS 9.8 remote-code-execution flaw on an internet-reachable Mitel Service Appliance, and CrowdStrike documented what the intruders left behind on it: a pdf_import.php webshell, Chisel renamed to memdump, and a persistent mkfifo/openssl reverse shell. Applying the Security Bulletin 22-0002-001 remediation removes the injection path and none of those artefacts, so an SA that was exposed before 2022-07-18 belongs on the rebuild-and-rotate path.

new_control_requirements.name: FIREWALL-EGRESS-TELEMETRY-SEPARATE-TRUST-ZONE
new_control_requirements.description: Firewall and other perimeter-trust-boundary devices must forward syslog, threat logs, and authentication logs to a SIEM hosted in a separate trust zone (different management plane, different credentials, different authentication path). Telemetry stored on the compromised device is destroyed by the attacker; telemetry on a separate-trust-zone collector survives.
new_control_requirements.evidence: On the Mitel Service Appliance CrowdStrike examined, nohup.out and the HTTP access log carrying the 2022-03-01 vtest.php and ucbsync.php requests both sat on the compromised box; the intruder deleted them and ran dd to fill the device's free space so the contents could not be recovered. They were recovered anyway, but only because /tmp was on a different partition from the log storage — an accident of that appliance's layout. Had the SA shipped its web and system logs to a collector in a separate trust zone, the exploit requests would have been out of the intruder's reach by design rather than by luck.

CVE-2022-30190.name: Microsoft Windows Support Diagnostic Tool (MSDT) Remote Code Execution Vulnerability (CVE-2022-30190)

attack_vector.description: An Office document pulls a remote HTML template that redirects to an ms-msdt: URI. Windows hands the URI to the Support Diagnostic Tool, which expands a $( ) sub-expression inside the IT_BrowseForFile parameter instead of treating it as a path, running PowerShell at the privilege of the Office process that opened the file. No macro, no prompt, and with RTF no need for the user to open the document at all.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; the attacker holds no account and the payload inherits whatever the victim's Office process already has
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L with UI:R, where the interaction is opening or previewing a document; the practical constraints are hosting the HTML template and keeping the first-stage URI payload ANSI-safe and under 76 characters
attack_vector.ai_factor: Recovered by the nao_sec research team from a sample already circulating in the wild, then analysed through public human channels — sandbox reports, researcher posts and a community write-up. No AI-assisted discovery is claimed.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Unregistering the ms-msdt URL protocol handler across the estate as soon as the technique was public in late May 2022, then installing the June 2022 cumulative Windows update and rebooting.
prevention.adequacy: The workaround is genuinely effective and genuinely disruptive — it breaks the built-in troubleshooting wizards, so helpdesks push back. BOD 22-01's 2022-07-05 due date lands after weeks of public exploit availability.

detection.what_would_have_worked: A process-lineage rule on msdt.exe or sdiagnhost.exe launched from an Office process, which is not a legitimate pattern on a managed workstation.
detection.adequacy: High-fidelity and cheap, and it is the only reliable signal — every binary in the chain is signed by Microsoft, so file-reputation and anti-malware controls have nothing to reject until a second-stage payload lands.

response.what_would_have_worked: Scoping by the first stage rather than the document: for any host that ran an MSDT-from-Office chain, review what PowerShell did next and rotate the credentials that were resident in that user session.
response.adequacy: Bounded and workable, but it depends on the process-lineage telemetry above having been collected before the event; retrospective hunting across an estate with no such logging returns nothing.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: The item routes to the wrong ring: the attack is a Word document, the fix is a Windows cumulative update, and an estate that patched Office closed the ticket without deploying the fix.

NIST-800-53-CM-7.gap: Least-functionality baselines enumerate services, ports and software, never registered URL protocol handlers, so ms-msdt was an unreviewed entry point in every standard image.

NIST-800-53-SI-3.gap: Macro blocking is the control operators believed covered malicious Office documents; no macro is involved, and in RTF form execution precedes any decision about an opened file.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: A monthly cadence is fast enough here; separating the OS ring from the Office ring is what caused the wrong one to be patched.

NIS2-Art21-vulnerability-handling.gap: Nothing in Article 21 obliges an entity to deploy a vendor-documented registry workaround ahead of a patch, so the compliant response was to wait while public exploits circulated.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: B4 assessments do not examine registered protocol handlers or reboot completion, which are the two things that decide exposure on this CVE.

AU-Essential-8-App-Hardening.gap: User application hardening targets macros, OLE and web content; the exploit uses a legitimate remote-template relationship, so Maturity Level 3 and Level 0 estates were equally exploitable.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Workstations sit in the one-month OS tier, putting the compliant deadline after the 2022-06-14 KEV listing and after 97 public exploit repositories existed.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.7.gap: Execution happens inside signed Microsoft binaries handed a URI by a signed Office process, so anti-malware is never presented with a file to reject.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: Consuming and applying the June 2022 advisory satisfies A.8.8; the exposure that mattered was in the late-May-to-July window the control does not govern.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2022-30190 reached KEV on 2022-06-14 with ransomware use Known, three weeks after the technique was public and while Microsoft's only remedy was the ms-msdt protocol-handler workaround. The control's compensating-controls branch is what makes it deployable inside four hours on a Windows fleet that cannot take a cumulative update and a reboot that fast, and at EPSS 0.99374 (99.937th percentile on 2026-08-13) this remains among the most-attacked entries in the catalogue.

new_control_requirements.name: DOWNLOAD-PROVENANCE-ENFORCEMENT
new_control_requirements.description: Exploitation here requires the victim to open an attacker-supplied Office document, so on an estate that has not yet reached the fixed build the delivery path is the only enforceable control. Require Mark-of-the-Web on every Office file arriving by mail, web download, or untrusted file share, and require MOTW-tagged documents to open in Protected View — an isolated, reduced-privilege render — instead of the full parsing path that carries the CWE-94 sink at the user's own process privilege. Provenance must survive the container: files extracted from an archive, mounted from an ISO or VHD, or renamed must inherit the tag rather than lose it, and 'Enable Editing' on externally sourced documents must be blocked by policy rather than left to the user. The distinguishing test: mail a MOTW-tagged spreadsheet nested inside a ZIP to a managed workstation, extract it, and confirm the extracted file still opens in Protected View — a user-application-hardening attestation that covers only macro and ActiveX/OLE settings still lets a provenance-stripped document reach the vulnerable parser with full user privileges.
new_control_requirements.evidence: The Metasploit module for this CVE ships both DOCX and RTF generators, and its documentation records that the RTF variant fires from the Explorer preview pane rather than on open — so on Windows without the June 2022 cumulative update, provenance marking is the difference between a document that renders in an isolated Protected View instance and one that reaches the remote-template relationship at full user privilege. The control's warning about macro-and-OLE-only hardening attestations is exactly the Essential Eight application-hardening gap recorded on this entry: none of those settings touch the ms-msdt path.

attack_vector.description: UnRAR checks a symlink target for ../ before it converts Windows backslashes to forward slashes, so a target written as ..\..\..\tmp/shell passes validation and becomes a traversal afterwards. Extraction then writes wherever the attacker chose, at the privilege of whatever invoked the extractor — on an internet-facing mail server that is the account running the attachment scanner, reached by sending a message.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; on the mail-server path the attacker needs only a deliverable address, and the extraction happens before any authentication or user decision
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L with UI:N on the Amavis path; the real work is choosing a write target that the extracting account owns and that something else will later execute or trust, and SonarSource notes the web-root target does not work on distributed installations
attack_vector.ai_factor: Manual source review by SonarSource's research team led by Simon Scannell, reported to RarLab on 2022-05-04. The finding is an ordering defect between two functions — the kind of reasoning published as human analysis, with no AI-assisted discovery claimed.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Updating every unrar copy on hosts that extract untrusted archives to 6.12 or later — or removing the extractor outright where RAR handling is not required — before the 2022-08-30 KEV due date.
prevention.adequacy: Correct and cheap to apply, but the directive names a component that most estates cannot locate: it is a helper binary, often present more than once per host, and absent from the software inventory the remediation process reads.

detection.what_would_have_worked: File-integrity monitoring on the paths a mail-scanning service account can write — its home directory, ~/.ssh, cron directories and the platform's web root — alerting on writes that coincide with attachment processing.
detection.adequacy: This is the only signal the primitive produces, since nothing crashes and no memory is corrupted. It needs the write targets enumerated in advance; a monitor scoped to system binaries misses ~/.ssh/authorized_keys entirely.

response.what_would_have_worked: For any mail server that scanned RAR attachments while running unrar below 6.12, auditing every authorized_keys file, cron entry and web-servable file owned by the scanning account, and rotating that account's keys.
response.adequacy: Bounded and achievable, and it is the step operators skip — updating the binary stops future writes and removes nothing already written.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: RARLAB issued no advisory; CISA's own remediation reference is a tarball URL. Advisory-driven flaw remediation has no input to act on and the component appears in no patch report.

NIST-800-53-SR-3.gap: The supply-chain register names Zimbra; the vulnerable code is an extractor two steps down the invocation chain that no supplier in the chain declared.

NIST-800-53-SI-3.gap: The extractor runs because malicious-code protection asked it to unpack the attachment, so strengthening SI-3 increases exposure to this flaw rather than reducing it.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: Patch currency is measured against the mail platform's release level, which stays green while the unrar binary beneath it remains pre-6.12.

NIS2-Art21-supply-chain.gap: A transitive dependency two steps down with no advisory to propagate falls outside what the supplier obligation reaches.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: Removing RAR extraction is a complete mitigation and no B4 assessment asks whether the attachment scanner needs to unpack RAR at all.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: unrar is not in the application inventory, so the internet-facing patch window never applies to it while the server reports compliant on the platform's own patch level.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.7.gap: Anti-malware scanning is the delivery mechanism here; no A.8.7 setting distinguishes unpacking for inspection from unpacking that writes to authorized_keys.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: The process is fed by product advisory feeds, and none carried this until the 2022-08-09 KEV listing — three months after RarLab was notified.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
