ISO-27001-2022-A.8.9.gap: Configuration management is the control with the right shape and the wrong scope. The two settings that decide exposure — Alarm Notification licence present, WAP port explicitly enabled — are application-internal state that no host or OS baseline captures, and the vulnerable configuration is not the default. An A.8.9 attestation covering operating-system hardening and change control passes cleanly on a VTScada 11.1 installation whose legacy listener is answering unauthenticated WAP requests on 9201/TCP.

IEC-62443-3-3.gap: The zone-and-conduit model handles this correctly in principle and fails in practice through obsolescence. The WAP interface predates both replacements Trihedral shipped — the Mobile Internet Client in 2013 and the Anywhere Client in 2016 — so a site that migrated mobile access years ago can retain a documented, approved conduit for a service with no remaining business function. Every 62443-3-3 system requirement can be evidenced against that conduit while the unauthenticated parser behind it stays reachable.

new_control_requirements.name: MITIGATION-ACTIVE-PATCH-PENDING-VERDICT-CLASS
new_control_requirements.description: Compliance verdicts must distinguish three states: (a) binary patch deployed (vulnerability eliminated), (b) vendor-mitigation rule active, no binary patch (residual risk: any defect in the mitigation rule reopens the vulnerability), (c) no mitigation, no patch (full exposure). Audit reports must surface (b) as a distinct compensating-control state with an associated time-bound action item, not as a 'patched per SLA' outcome.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Trihedral's guidance for VTScada puts most affected sites squarely in state (b): current WAP users are told to disable the WAP port through Trihedral support, which removes the exposure while leaving the installed version below 11.2.02 and therefore reading as unpatched. Without this verdict class the same site is scored as non-compliant when it is mitigated, or an unmitigated 11.1 install is scored on version alone, and neither reflects the fact that ICS-CERT dated the advisory 2016-06-07 while KEV only opened the clock on 2022-04-15.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CISA listed CVE-2016-4523 on 2022-04-15 with a 2022-05-06 due date against a Trihedral VTScada component whose fix — removal of the WAP code in 11.2 — had shipped in 2016. On a SCADA operator station serving water, energy or transport, the control's documented-compensating-control branch is the one that lands inside four hours: close 9201/TCP at the segment boundary or have the WAP port disabled, then schedule the 11.2.02 upgrade and the migration to the Mobile Internet Client or Anywhere Client behind it.

attack_vector.description: Code already running inside an application sandbox sends IOKit a binary-serialized dictionary whose OSNumber declares a larger size than it was given storage for. Reading the property back copies the declared length out of the kernel, returning adjacent stack memory containing saved return addresses. From those the caller computes the KASLR slide — the piece of knowledge that turns a kernel memory-corruption bug into a usable kernel write.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N in CVSS terms, but read this as 'no elevated rights required'; the caller must already be executing on the device, which in the observed chain meant an unprivileged sandboxed context reached through a WebKit bug
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L with AV:L and UI:R; the leak is deterministic, with no race and no grooming, and the user interaction is the tap on an SMS link that started the chain rather than anything the kernel stage needs
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Citizen Lab and Lookout found the chain from artefacts a targeted individual supplied, and the OSUnserializeBinary analysis that followed was manual reverse engineering by Stefan Esser and jndok. No AI-assisted discovery is claimed.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Enforcing the fixed build as a condition of access rather than a reporting metric — no mail, VPN or document access to a device below iOS 9.3.5, and below 10.0.1 once the iOS 10 line shipped — with the restart onto the new build counted, not the download.
prevention.adequacy: It closes the flaw and nothing before it. Apple shipped iOS 9.3.5 on 2016-08-25, so the exposure window that mattered ran up to that date and no operator control shortened it. The KEV clock opened 2022-05-24, five and a half years later, by which point the population still on iOS 9 was old hardware where the honest answer is replacement rather than an update.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Watching for the sequence that defines the primitive — a process submitting binary-serialized IOKit dictionaries and immediately reading back oversized properties — and for devices that report an approved update but never change build.
detection.adequacy: Largely unavailable to an operator on iOS: there is no host-level telemetry surface where such calls could be observed, so this is a platform-side capability rather than a fleet one. The build-drift half is genuinely actionable from MDM and is the only reliable operator-visible signal here.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating a device plausibly inside a commercial-intrusion targeting set as an incident rather than a patch item — forensic capture before update, credential rotation for everything the device held, and escalation appropriate to a state customer rather than commodity malware.
response.adequacy: Updating destroys the evidence, so the response only works if capture precedes remediation, which conflicts with every patch SLA. It also assumes the target population is identified in advance, and the Ahmed Mansoor case became known only because the target himself was suspicious enough to forward the links.

NIST-800-53-SC-39.gap: Process isolation is asserted, not tested, and this defect is the assertion being false. Any sandboxed process on an affected build could hand IOKit a crafted serialized dictionary and receive kernel stack memory back, so the confinement that justifies running untrusted code on the device was absent on that path. Nothing an operator configures restores it — only Apple's 2016-08-25 iOS 9.3.5 build and its 2016-09-01 macOS and 2016-09-13 iOS 10 counterparts — so the control reads implemented on an unpatched fleet.

NIS2-Art21-vulnerability-management.gap: The process is built around advisories and scanner findings, and this defect entered through a targeted individual forwarding SMS links to Citizen Lab. It then needed a second fix: iOS 9.3.5 on 2016-08-25 and iOS 10.0.1 on 2016-09-13 for the same kernel bug on the newer line, which one-CVE-one-fixed-version tracking closes after the first. Article 21 also cannot express that the exposed population is a named handful of high-risk individuals rather than a percentage of the estate.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: Mobile secure configuration under B4 reaches passcode policy, encryption, restrictions and minimum OS version, and only the last of those has any bearing on a kernel deserializer reachable from every sandbox. Even that lever works only when the minimum build is enforced as an access condition; a device on iOS 9.3.4 carrying a fully compliant configuration profile leaked kernel memory to any application that asked, and its B4 evidence would have been complete and accurate at the time.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Two mismatches. Apple issued this fix on three dates across three trains — 2016-08-25, 2016-09-01 and 2016-09-13 — so a single per-CVE interval under-describes the verification work. And the rung is normally evidenced from update approval or download state, whereas the fix is inert until the device restarts onto the new build; on personally-held phones that restart is the most-deferred and least-measured step in the whole sequence.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.28.gap: Secure coding is the control that names the actual defect — an attacker-supplied length used to size a kernel copy with no bounds check in the kOSSerializeNumber path — and it is unenforceable by the party carrying the risk. Only Apple can apply A.8.28 to OSUnserializeBinary. An operator's A.8.28 evidence covers code the operator writes, so the control is fully satisfied and entirely disconnected from the deserializer deciding whether its fleet's kernel memory stays private.

new_control_requirements.name: MOBILE-ENDPOINT-MDM-ENFORCED-KEV-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: iOS / iPadOS / macOS estates must enforce KEV-class updates within 24h via DDM; user-deferral disallowed.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Apple shipped this kernel information-disclosure fix as iOS 9.3.5 on 2016-08-25, then again as iOS 10.0.1 on 2016-09-13 for the newer line, and as Security Update 2016-001 El Capitan / 2016-005 Yosemite on 2016-09-01. Each is a full OS update that is inert until the device restarts, and the exposed asset is the KASLR slide that every subsequent kernel stage of the Pegasus chain depended on. User-deferrable updates on an estate holding iPhone 4s and later leave the leak answering to any sandboxed application.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CISA listed CVE-2016-4655 on 2022-05-24 with a 2022-06-14 due date against an Apple kernel leak that any iOS or OS X sandbox could reach. Because Apple offers no live-patch path and the fix requires a device restart, the only mitigation that verifies is the device reporting a build at or above iOS 9.3.5, iOS 10.0.1, or the 2016-09-01 OS X security updates — and on hardware that can no longer take a current Apple release the documented compensating control is withdrawal of organisational data from the device.

attack_vector.description: An application sends IOKit a binary-serialized dictionary. The kernel indexes every deserialized object without taking a reference, and when a key arrives as an OSString it converts it to an OSSymbol and frees the OSString while the freed pointer stays in the index. A later back-reference to that index entry retains and uses freed memory the attacker has re-filled, and the resulting use-after-free becomes code execution with kernel privileges — enough to jailbreak the device and install a persistent implant without the user seeing anything.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; no elevated rights are needed, only execution inside an ordinary application sandbox, which in the observed chain was supplied by a WebKit bug rather than by an installed app
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L with AV:L and UI:R; triggering the free is trivial, but a reliable exploit needs the KASLR slide from the paired information leak plus heap grooming, and Pegasus carried separate 32-bit and 64-bit kernel exploits to cover the device range
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Citizen Lab and Lookout recovered the chain from links a targeted individual forwarded, and the OSUnserializeBinary reference-counting defect was identified by manual analysis at SektionEins and by jndok. No AI-assisted discovery is claimed by any party.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Being on iOS 9.3.5 or later from 2016-08-25, or on the 2016-09-01 OS X security updates, enforced as an access condition with the device restart counted rather than the download. Nothing an operator configures below that removes the path, because the deserializer is reachable from every sandbox.
prevention.adequacy: Effective and late. The chain was already deployed when Apple shipped the fix, and BOD 22-01's clock opened 2022-05-24, so for the targeted population prevention never existed — only the vendor's response time did. On devices too old for any current Apple release the control degrades to replacement, which no patch SLA expresses.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Watching for kernel panics and unexplained reboots on affected builds, and for the off-device consequence — credentials or accounts belonging to a high-risk individual being used from somewhere the individual is not.
detection.adequacy: Very weak by design: the exploit's purpose was a silent jailbreak, and a successful run produces no panic. iOS offers no enterprise host-telemetry surface, so the only reliable detection is downstream of the implant, after the data it wanted has already moved.

response.what_would_have_worked: Escalating a plausible commercial-intrusion compromise on its own path — forensic capture before any update, device rebuild or replacement rather than patch-in-place, and rotation of every credential the device held — instead of routing it through the standard malware-infection playbook.
response.adequacy: It is the only response that matches the threat, and it collides with the patch clock: updating the device is the fastest way to destroy the evidence that would establish whether it was targeted. The sequencing has to be written down in advance, because it will not be improvised correctly under a KEV due date.

NIST-800-53-SI-4.gap: Monitoring depends on the monitored system remaining trustworthy, and this bug delivered kernel code execution and a silent jailbreak — everything that could report sits above what the attacker now controls. On iOS there is no host telemetry surface for an enterprise agent to occupy in the first place, so the practical SI-4 coverage is a fleet view of build numbers. That view shows which devices are exposed and can never show which were compromised.

DORA-Art-9.gap: Article 9 assumes layered protection constrains post-access movement, and the layer in question is the application sandbox. OSUnserializeBinary takes serialized dictionaries from any application, so the distance between untrusted code and kernel privileges was one missing retain in an index table. A financial entity fully implementing Article 9 had nothing between the WebKit stage and kernel control except Apple's 2016-08-25 build, which is a supplier control, not an entity control.

UK-CAF-D1.gap: Response plans are scoped to estate-level incidents and this is a single phone belonging to a single high-risk individual, compromised at kernel level by a commercial intrusion product. The plan typically omits the one ordering decision that determines whether anything can be established afterwards — forensic capture before the update, since updating destroys the evidence — putting D1 in direct conflict with the KEV due date unless the conflict is written into the plan. It also gives no criterion for retiring a device rather than repairing it.

AU-Essential-8-App-Hardening.gap: The rung targets desktop browsers, Office and PDF handling and has no direct iOS expression; the nearest lever is restricting application installation, which is relevant because the CVSS AV:L rating exists for a crafted app. But the chain that actually ran did not install anything — the code reaching IOKit came from a compromised WebKit renderer. Hardening the install path leaves the render path open, and the render path is the one that was used.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.16.gap: A.8.16 asks that networks, systems and applications be monitored for anomalous behaviour, and a silent kernel-level jailbreak is designed to produce none where an operator can see it. The signal that did exist was outside the estate entirely: a targeted individual judging that unsolicited SMS links looked wrong and forwarding them to researchers. No monitoring programme over corporate networks would have generated that, and Apple exposes no on-device interface where the exploitation itself could have been logged.

new_control_requirements.name: MOBILE-OS-MINIMUM-PATCH-LEVEL-ENFORCEMENT
new_control_requirements.description: The trigger is a malicious application causing unexpected changes in memory shared between processes, so for this entry the control's access-condition half is the load-bearing one: on any Apple device that cannot yet take the fixed build, the operator's remaining levers are constraining what code is allowed to run at all and withholding organizational data from the device until its build is at or above the fix. The fixed build must function as an access condition — mail, VPN and document access denied to a device below it — not as a row on a patch-compliance dashboard. The distinguishing test is to enrol a device pinned below the fixed build and confirm the policy actually denies it access to protected resources; an estate that surfaces the stale build on a report while the device keeps its access has recorded the exposure rather than removed it. Precondition: restricting untrusted or side-loaded application installation raises the bar for getting the attacker's application onto the device, but it does not evict an application already installed, and it does not cover one that arrived through the normal store channel. A device suspected of already running the malicious application belongs on the incident path, not the install-policy path. This is a holding measure for the window before the fixed build and its required restart land, not a substitute for them.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Apple's fixed builds for this Apple iOS kernel memory-corruption flaw are iOS 9.3.5 (2016-08-25, iPhone 4s and later) and, on the desktop side, Security Update 2016-001 El Capitan and 2016-005 Yosemite (2016-09-01). Because the defect sits in IOKit's binary deserializer, every sandboxed application on a device below those builds can reach kernel code execution, so the build level is the access decision. The control's install-restriction caveat is exactly right here: the observed chain reached IOKit through a compromised WebKit renderer, not an installed app, so install policy narrows one path and leaves the one that was used.

new_control_requirements.name: NATION-STATE-INITIAL-ACCESS-IR-ESCALATION
new_control_requirements.description: IR runbooks must include an explicit nation-state-initial-access escalation path triggered by APT28/APT29/Lazarus/Volt-Typhoon/etc. attribution on a confirmed exploit chain. Standard malware-infection IR under-escalates nation-state activity by treating it as commodity threat.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Citizen Lab and Lookout attributed this iOS kernel bug's use to NSO Group's Pegasus, deployed against UAE human-rights defender Ahmed Mansoor in August 2016 through a three-zero-day chain ending in a silent jailbreak and a persistent implant. Routing that through a commodity malware playbook produces the wrong actions in the wrong order: the device gets updated, the evidence is destroyed, and the credentials it held are never rotated. The escalation path is what makes forensic capture precede the KEV-clocked update rather than follow it.

CVE-2016-4657.name: Apple iOS Webkit Memory Corruption Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: A page defines properties on a JavaScript object in a way that leaves JavaScriptCore holding a stale reference. Script reclaims that memory with a typed array it controls, overwrites the array's backing pointer, and gains arbitrary read and write inside the renderer, then native code execution in the browser process. Delivered as a link, it needs one tap; in the Pegasus chain the code it ran then fetched the kernel stages that jailbroke the device.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; the attacker needs no account and no foothold, only that the victim open a URL in an affected WebKit build
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L with UI:R; the exploit is deterministic enough to have been sold as a one-tap capability, and since qwertyoruiop published Exploit-DB 44213 in March 2017 the grooming work is public, so what remains is finding an unpatched engine rather than developing anything
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Citizen Lab and Lookout recovered it from a live chain their target forwarded to them, and the public exploitation is credited to named humans — qwertyoruiop, with Retr0id and Ando — building on saelo's Phrack work on JavaScript engine exploitation.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: iOS 9.3.5 from 2016-08-25 or Safari 9.1.3 from 2016-09-01, with the corresponding restart actually taken — a device reboot for iOS, a browser relaunch for Safari. For the embedded population, knowing which purchased devices render web content through WebKit at all, so the question can be asked of the right vendor.
prevention.adequacy: Complete for Apple's own products and structurally incomplete elsewhere. BOD 22-01 obliges an agency to remediate its Apple fleet; it has no reach into a console browser or an appliance web view whose vendor never shipped the fix, and those instances remained exploitable long after Apple's tree was clean.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Correlating repeated WebContent crashes on unpatched builds with the browsing that preceded them, and monitoring outbound traffic from devices that render web content but are not managed as browsers.
detection.adequacy: Crash correlation only catches failed attempts — a successful run is silent by design. The embedded-device half is more useful but depends on those devices being on an instrumented segment, which is precisely the assumption that fails for signage players, panels and consoles.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating a rendered malicious link on an unpatched engine as a possible first stage rather than a browser incident: capture before updating, assume the kernel stages ran, and rotate what the device held.
response.adequacy: Sound but expensive and rarely triggered, because the visible artefact — a link that no longer resolves — looks like nothing. It also does not scale to the embedded estate, where there is no forensic surface at all and the only available response is removing the device from the network.

NIST-800-53-SR-3.gap: Supply chain controls track acquisition relationships, and this defect travels by source embedding instead. The vulnerable JavaScriptCore code is compiled into other vendors' firmware, which is why a proof of concept written against iOS 9.3.4 executes on Nintendo Switch launch-era system software unchanged. An SR-3 programme captures the manufacturer of the finished device and never records that its HTML renderer is a WebKit fork governed by Apple's 2016-08-25 fix, so the supplier is assessed and the vulnerable component is invisible.

EU-CRA-Art13.gap: The manufacturer obligations that would fit this case — component-level SBOM, upstream vulnerability tracking, notification of actively exploited flaws — did not exist when it mattered. In 2016 nothing required a console or appliance vendor to notice that Apple had fixed its WebKit tree on 2016-08-25, so downstream builds carried the defect for as long as the vendor chose. This entry is the pre-CRA baseline that motivated the article rather than a case the article governs, and legacy devices in service remain outside its reach.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: Secure configuration covers the browsers an organisation manages and has no expression for the rendering engines inside equipment nobody files under 'browser' — meeting-room panels, signage players, kiosks, a console on a guest VLAN. Each renders untrusted web content through a WebKit build that no MDM policy reaches and that the estate usually cannot enumerate. B4 evidence over the managed fleet can be complete while several unmanaged renderers on the same network are running a pre-2016-08-25 engine.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Two release dates and two different restart semantics defeat a single-interval measure: iOS 9.3.5 on 2016-08-25 takes effect on device reboot, while Safari 9.1.3 on 2016-09-01 takes effect only when the browser process relaunches, so a long-uptime Mac scores patched and runs the vulnerable engine. The rung further assumes a vendor release exists for every affected instance, which is exactly what an embedded WebKit consumer that stopped shipping updates does not provide.

ISO-27001-2022-A.5.21.gap: Supplier assessments under A.5.21 establish that a manufacturer has security processes and a contact, and stop above the component layer where this defect lives. CISA's KEV entry states plainly that the flaw reaches non-Apple products relying on WebKit for HTML processing, and the public exploit demonstrates it on a games console. Without a bill of materials naming the rendering engine, the control produces a satisfactory supplier file for a product whose browser has not tracked Apple's fix in years.

new_control_requirements.name: BROWSER-MANAGED-UPDATE-NO-DEFERRAL
new_control_requirements.description: Enterprise update rings must not defer security-channel browser updates beyond 24h.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Apple released Safari 9.1.3 on 2016-09-01 and iOS 9.3.5 on 2016-08-25 against a WebKit flaw that gives native code execution from a single tapped link, and a public proof of concept followed in March 2017 as Exploit-DB 44213. The detail this control has to carry for Safari specifically is that installing the update is not the finish line — the patched engine loads only when the browser process relaunches, so a deferral ring and a long-uptime Mac produce the same outcome.

new_control_requirements.name: TIER-3-DEPENDENCY-INVENTORY
new_control_requirements.description: Supply chain inventory must extend to tier-3 dependencies (dependencies of dependencies of direct dependencies). SBOM coverage for libsystemd-class transitive dependencies cannot be omitted under SR-3.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CISA's own KEV description for this Apple WebKit flaw warns that it reaches HTML parsers using WebKit, including non-Apple products, and qwertyoruiop's proof of concept demonstrates it against Nintendo Switch launch-era system software rather than against an iPhone. The engine is a transitive component inside purchased hardware, so an inventory that stops at the finished product records a console or an appliance and never records that it ships a WebKit snapshot predating Apple's 2016-08-25 fix and receives no Apple update.

CVE-2016-6366.name: Cisco Adaptive Security Appliance (ASA) SNMP Buffer Overflow Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: A crafted IPv4 SNMP packet sent to an SNMP-enabled ASA interface overflows a buffer in the appliance's SNMP parser. The leaked EXTRABACON tool uses that to take control of the LINA process and patch the authentication check in memory, after which management logins are accepted without a valid password while the firewall carries on forwarding and filtering as normal.
attack_vector.privileges_required: low — PR:L; the attacker must know the SNMP community string for v1 or v2c, or hold valid v3 credentials, and community strings are commonly shared across a fleet and recoverable from monitoring platforms and configuration backups
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L with UI:N; no race and no user action, only IPv4 reachability to the appliance's own address. The practical constraint is version fidelity: the leaked tool covered 8.x, the public rewrite added 9.x with an offset finder, and x64 builds with DEP and ASLR resist the generic payload while remaining reloadable
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. The bug surfaced through the Shadow Brokers publication of Equation Group tooling on 2016-08-15, so it was found inside an offensive programme rather than by research, and no AI involvement is claimed anywhere in that chain.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Restricting SNMP to named management hosts with the snmp-server host command and rotating community strings, which is the workaround Cisco published on 2016-08-17 when no fixed software yet existed, followed by the upgrade to 9.0.4(40) / 9.1.7(9) / 9.2.4(14) / 9.3.3(10) or the migration off the 7.2 through 8.7 trains.
prevention.adequacy: The SNMP restriction is genuine containment and bounded: any host inside the permitted set that is itself compromised satisfies the precondition in full, and the community string it needs is often in the monitoring platform on that very host. Upgrading is complete for the 9.x trains and unavailable for FWSM and PIX, where Cisco states no fixed software will be produced.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Cisco's Snort rule 3:39885 on the path to the appliance's own addresses, plus alerting on any IPv4 SNMP to ASA interface addresses from outside the snmp-server host list, and on ASA reloads with no change record.
detection.adequacy: Network-side detection is the only reliable kind here, because after exploitation the device's own logging is under the attacker's control. That also means the telemetry has to leave the appliance to a collector in a different trust zone before the event, and an estate that keeps ASA logs only on the appliance has nothing afterwards.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating a suspected EXTRABACON hit as a device compromise rather than a software defect: capture the configuration for comparison, rebuild the appliance from a known-good baseline on fixed code, and rotate every credential the device held, including the SNMP community strings and any VPN or AAA secrets.
response.adequacy: This is the only response that matches an in-memory authentication patch, and it costs a firewall outage on a device whose outage is a business event. Its weakness is evidentiary: the patch lives in the running LINA process, so a reload destroys it, and a reload is exactly what applying fixed software does.

NIST-800-53-SC-7.gap: Boundary protection is evidenced from the firewall's ruleset, zones and default-deny posture, none of which apply to a packet addressed to the firewall itself. Cisco makes the distinction explicit — only traffic directed at the affected system can exploit this — so the appliance's policy enforcement is irrelevant to its own exposure. An SC-7 assessment can be fully satisfied on an ASA running an 8.4 image with SNMP reachable from the internal estate, which is precisely the configuration EXTRABACON was built for.

NIS2-Art21-network-security.gap: The measures assume that upgrading to fixed code restores a known-good device, and EXTRABACON breaks that assumption by patching authentication inside the running LINA process rather than altering anything on disk. An operator who reaches 9.1.7(9) and reloads has fixed the defect and inherited the configuration and credentials of a device that had been open, because nothing in Article 21 distinguishes upgrading a compromised perimeter appliance from rebuilding one.

UK-CAF-B2.gap: Identity and access control on an ASA is evidenced through named administrators, AAA integration and privilege levels, and this attack touches none of them. The credential that gates it is the SNMP community string, which sits outside every identity lifecycle process, is shared fleet-wide and lives in monitoring platforms and configuration backups. After the overflow lands the administrator model is not abused but bypassed, since authentication is patched out in memory, so a clean B2 attestation and an open device are compatible.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Cisco's fixed-software table refuses the rung's premise twice. Releases 7.2 through 8.7 have no fix on their own trains and require migration to 9.1.7(9) or later, which is a platform change with hardware and feature consequences rather than a patch applied inside a window. FWSM and PIX have no fix at all, since Cisco states fixed software will not be made available for products past their last day of software support, so the compliant action there is decommissioning, which the rung cannot record.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.22.gap: Network segregation is normally documented as a traffic-forwarding design — user, server, DMZ and management zones and the rules between them — while the fact that decides this exposure is management-plane reachability of the appliance's own interfaces by IPv4 SNMP. That is the snmp-server host restriction Cisco names as its workaround. A carefully segregated forwarding design that still lets any internal subnet address the ASA directly leaves the vulnerable parser reachable from the entire estate.

new_control_requirements.name: PERIMETER-DEVICE-ZERODAY-SLA-TIER
new_control_requirements.description: Compliance frameworks must define a distinct patch SLA tier for pre-auth RCE on perimeter-trust-boundary devices (firewalls, VPN concentrators, WAFs, edge load-balancers). Tier requirement: vendor-mitigation deployed within 4 hours of KEV listing OR isolation of the vulnerable interface; standard 14/30-day SLAs do not apply because the device IS the trust boundary.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Cisco published cisco-sa-20160817-asa-snmp on 2016-08-17 with no fixed software in the initial revision and the Fixed Software table completed only by 2016-09-19, two days after the Shadow Brokers had already posted working EXTRABACON code — later archived as Exploit-DB 40258. On the ASA 5500-X, Firepower 9300 ASA Security Module and ISA 3000 the device is the trust boundary, so the control's isolation branch is the one that had to fire during that month: restrict IPv4 SNMP to named management hosts via snmp-server host until the reload onto 9.1.7(9) or later can be scheduled.

new_control_requirements.name: PERIMETER-COMPROMISE-REBUILD-NOT-PATCH
new_control_requirements.description: Pre-rehearsed IR runbook for any perimeter device that suffers a pre-auth RCE CVE in active exploitation MUST default to config-exfil + rebuild + credential rotation, not patch-in-place. Patch-in-place leaves attacker-installed implants intact.
new_control_requirements.evidence: EXTRABACON's payload patches the authentication check inside the running Cisco ASA LINA process, so an exploited appliance keeps enforcing policy while accepting management logins without a valid password. Upgrading to 9.1.7(9) and reloading removes the defect and carries forward the configuration, the SNMP community strings and every VPN and AAA secret the device held — all of which the attacker had access to. For an ASA that was SNMP-reachable during the exposure window opened by the 2016-08-15 leak, config capture, rebuild from a known-good baseline and full credential rotation are the remediation, not the upgrade.

CVE-2016-6367.name: Cisco Adaptive Security Appliance (ASA) CLI Remote Code Execution Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: An attacker holding valid telnet/SSH credentials, connecting from a permitted source address, submits invalid CLI commands that the ASA parser mishandles to force a reload or execute code with elevated privilege — the mechanism the Equation Group's EPICBANANA tool automated.
attack_vector.privileges_required: low — PR:L; a valid but low-privilege telnet/SSH login on the appliance, reachable only from an IP the ssh/telnet ACL permits.
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; once access is held the malformed-command trigger is deterministic, with no race or memory-groom needed.
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Cisco PSIRT confirmed the flaw from the leaked Equation Group toolset; discovery was human, and no 'AI'-branded tooling is involved.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Upgrading every ASA to 8.4(3)/9.0(1) or later and restricting telnet/SSH to the management interface and trusted source IPs with TACACS+ command authorization.
prevention.adequacy: Effective, but the upgrade forces a firewall reload, which is the reason operators left the 7.2-8.7 trains in service long after 8.4(3) shipped.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alerting on invalid-CLI-command bursts and CLI-parser tracebacks forwarded to an off-box collector, plus unexpected privilege-15 escalations.
detection.adequacy: On-appliance logs are within reach of an attacker who can reload the device, so detection is only durable if telemetry leaves the firewall first.

response.what_would_have_worked: Rotating device credentials, rebuilding configuration from a known-good baseline, and decommissioning end-of-life PIX/FWSM after any suspected compromise.
response.adequacy: Patch-in-place does not evict changes an authenticated attacker made to the running configuration or accounts.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: SI-2 is nominally met by having a patch process, but the ASA 8.4(3) fix predated the 2022-05-24 KEV listing by roughly a decade and firewalls stayed below it; the control counts a released fix as remediation rather than requiring every appliance to actually cross 8.4(3)/9.0(1).

NIST-800-53-AC-6.gap: AC-6 is satisfied by role assignment, yet the exploit promotes a legitimate low-privilege telnet/SSH session through the CLI parser; without TACACS+/AAA command authorization the least-privilege model never governs which commands the account can submit, so the attestation passes while the escalation path stays open.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: Article 21 patch management is in place, but ASA upgrades to 8.4(3)/9.0(1) require a reload of a perimeter firewall and a standard 14/30-day cadence does not treat a KEV-listed firewall RCE with a 2022-06-14 due date as the accelerated case; the routine window absorbs the reload indefinitely.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: CAF B4 update management is asserted, yet a decade-old fix left uninstalled on an internet-facing Cisco ASA is the exact failure it should prevent; the principle does not by itself compel the enumerate-and-reload discipline needed to bring every appliance above 8.4(3).

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Essential Eight patch-application maturity covers OS and application patching but not firewall appliance images sitting at ASA 7.2-8.7; there is no distinct accelerated tier for a KEV-listed perimeter-device flaw whose fix shipped years before the listing.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: A.8.8 technical vulnerability management tracks the CVE, but tracking is not remediation: an ASA below 8.4(3) with EPICBANANA public since 2016 is a tracked-yet-unremediated firewall, and the control does not force the CLI-parser finding on an authentication-boundary device into a scheduled reload.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.15.gap: A.8.15 logging is present, but ASA syslog and CLI-audit records reside on a device the authenticated attacker can reload; parser-traceback and privilege-change evidence survives only if forwarded off-box, which the control does not require before trusting the firewall to record its own compromise.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2016-6367 in Cisco ASA sat unremediated on the 7.2-8.7 trains until CISA listed it on 2022-05-24 with a 2022-06-14 due date, despite the 8.4(3) fix existing since ~2011 and EPICBANANA (Exploit-DB 40271) being public since 2016 and EPSS 0.226 (97.5th pct); a KEV-clock SLA that measures every ASA against 8.4(3)/9.0(1) is what forces the deferred reload.

new_control_requirements.name: FIREWALL-EGRESS-TELEMETRY-SEPARATE-TRUST-ZONE
new_control_requirements.description: Firewall and other perimeter-trust-boundary devices must forward syslog, threat logs, and authentication logs to a SIEM hosted in a separate trust zone (different management plane, different credentials, different authentication path). Telemetry stored on the compromised device is destroyed by the attacker; telemetry on a separate-trust-zone collector survives.
new_control_requirements.evidence: EPICBANANA (CVE-2016-6367) can reload an ASA and runs as an authenticated CLI session, so the parser-traceback and privilege-escalation records that would prove exploitation live on a device the attacker controls; forwarding ASA syslog and telnet/SSH auth logs to a separate-trust-zone SIEM is the only way that evidence outlives the compromise.

CVE-2017-0005.name: Microsoft Windows Graphics Device Interface (GDI) Privilege Escalation Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: A crafted application overflows a GDI heap allocation to corrupt a PALETTE object's pfnGetNearestFromPalentry pointer, then calls NtGdiEngBitBlt so win32k invokes the corrupted handler in kernel context, and a token swap yields SYSTEM — the ZIRCONIUM in-the-wild GDI elevation of privilege.
attack_vector.privileges_required: low — PR:L; the attacker must already run code on the host to launch the crafted application.
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; but reliability depended on specific 64-bit Windows 7/8 kernel layouts the exploit gated on.
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. A trusted partner reported the zero-day exploit to Microsoft, whose researchers then reverse-engineered the captured ZIRCONIUM samples; both halves are human work, not AI-assisted discovery.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Installing MS17-013 with a reboot across all affected supported builds, and migrating end-of-life Windows 7/Vista/early-Windows-10 hosts off unsupported kernels.
prevention.adequacy: The patch removes the flaw, but the reboot requirement and the end-of-life population are where deployment stalls.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Monitoring for process-token-field state changes (Microsoft's stated signal) and win32k bugchecks on 64-bit Windows 7/8.
detection.adequacy: The escalation is entirely in-kernel with no dropped artifact, so only token-manipulation telemetry catches it — coverage most estates lack.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating any confirmed use as nation-state initial-access and reviewing the foothold that launched the crafted application, not just the GDI escalation.
response.adequacy: SYSTEM was already obtained by the time the token swap is visible, so response starts from an assume-compromise posture on that host.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: SI-2 is met by MS17-013 approval, but the flaw was exploited before the 2017-03-14 fix and KEV relisted it in 2022; estates ran the vulnerable GDI on unpatched and end-of-life Windows 7/8 long after, because the control closes on approval rather than installed-and-rebooted.

NIST-800-53-SI-4.gap: SI-4 monitoring is asserted, yet it seldom inspects the process token field that Microsoft named as the detection point for this token-swap-to-SYSTEM exploit; an estate can claim coverage while owning no rule that fires on the NtGdiEngBitBlt kernel path.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: Article 21 patching is in place, but MS17-013 needs a reboot and much of the affected population was Windows 7/8 hosts deferred or past end-of-support; the routine cadence never applies the accelerated clock this KEV-listed actively-exploited kernel LPE warrants.

NIS2-Art21-incident-handling.gap: Incident handling exists, but a win32k escalation used by ZIRCONIUM drops no tool and crashes no service, so a process lacking token-manipulation telemetry has no trigger; the control does not mandate instrumenting this in-memory escalation class.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: CAF B4 update management is asserted, yet the affected builds include end-of-life Vista/Server 2008 and early Windows 10 where MS17-013 was never applied or no longer applies; B4 does not compel the EoL-migration decision those hosts require to remove the GDI path.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Essential Eight OS-patch maturity runs a rolling window too slow for a kernel LPE ZIRCONIUM weaponized before MS17-013 shipped; the model provides no accelerated tier for a confirmed in-the-wild kernel escalation relisted in KEV in 2022.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: A.8.8 records CVE-2017-0005 but recording does not remove it from the 64-bit Windows 7/8 hosts the exploit targeted; the control does not force this actively-exploited kernel-GDI finding into a verified reboot-and-confirm across that exact build population.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2017-0005 was a ZIRCONIUM in-the-wild kernel LPE fixed by MS17-013 on 2017-03-14 yet relisted by CISA on 2022-05-24 (EPSS 0.110, 95.5th pct), showing estates carried it on unpatched and end-of-life Windows 7/8 x64 hosts for years; a KEV-clock SLA measuring installed-and-rebooted against MS17-013 is what forces closure.

new_control_requirements.name: VENDOR-PUSH-MITIGATION-OPT-IN-PRE-DISCLOSURE
new_control_requirements.description: For vendors offering push-mitigation services (Microsoft EEMS, Palo Alto Threat Prevention auto-update, etc.), opt-in must be enabled BEFORE the next disclosure event, not in response to it. Compliance frameworks must require operators to enable available vendor-push-mitigation services as a baseline control — opt-in late means the mitigation rule arrives after exploitation, not before.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2017-0005 was exploited by ZIRCONIUM before MS17-013 and detected via the process-token-field signal Microsoft published; enabling Microsoft's push-mitigation and token-swap detection ahead of disclosure is the only way that telemetry and any interim rule is in place when the in-kernel escalation arrives rather than after.

CVE-2017-0148.name: Microsoft SMBv1 Server Remote Code Execution Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: An unauthenticated attacker sends crafted SMB_COM_TRANSACTION2 packets whose OS/2 FEA list triggers the DWORD-into-WORD size miscalculation in SrvOs2FeaListSizeToNt, so SrvOs2FeaToNt overflows the non-paged pool and executes code in the kernel — EternalBlue, the engine of WannaCry and NotPetya.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; network reachability to TCP 445 is the only requirement.
attack_vector.complexity: high — AC:H; reliable pool grooming varies by target build, but no authentication or user interaction is needed, which made it wormable.
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. ETERNALBLUE was a state-built capability leaked by the Shadow Brokers; no AI-assisted discovery is involved.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Applying MS17-010 with a reboot and disabling SMBv1 estate-wide so the legacy protocol is not reachable at all.
prevention.adequacy: Both are effective; the patch needs a reboot and SMBv1 disablement removes the primitive, but neither was applied fast enough before WannaCry.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alerting on malformed Trans2/FEA traffic to TCP 445 and on internal 445 scanning bursts.
detection.adequacy: Detection helps contain lateral spread but the initial kernel RCE completes before most signatures fire.

response.what_would_have_worked: Immutable/offline backups and network segmentation to blunt the ransomware payload once a host was hit.
response.adequacy: Backups aid recovery but do not prevent the worm's spread across an SMBv1-enabled flat network.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: SI-2 is met by MS17-010 being released on 2017-03-14, but WannaCry hit unpatched estates in May 2017 and KEV relisted the CVE in 2022 with Known ransomware use; the control counts a released patch as remediation while wormable SMBv1 servers stayed exposed for years.

NIST-800-53-CM-7.gap: CM-7 should have retired SMBv1 as unused legacy functionality before any patch was needed, but assessed as a documented baseline rather than enforced disablement it left SMBv1 enabled by default, keeping the FEA-parsing overflow reachable on TCP 445.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: Article 21 patching is in place, but it did not convert MS17-010 into an emergency reboot-inclusive rollout faster than the worm; the 2022-04-27 KEV due date and the 2017 timeline both show the routine cadence trailed a wormable pre-auth SMB RCE.

NIS2-Art21-vulnerability-handling.gap: Vulnerability handling treated CVE-2017-0148 as discrete, but it is one of five SMBv1 FEA siblings; a per-CVE process hides that removing the primitive means disabling SMBv1, so patching one path while SMBv1 stays enabled understates the exposure.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: CAF B4 update management is asserted, yet SMBv1 servers missing MS17-010 carried WannaCry and NotPetya; B4 does not force the disable-SMBv1 step, so an estate 'patched' on paper still exposes the legacy protocol the worm rides.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Essential Eight OS-patch maturity runs a monthly-scale window that a wormable SMBv1 RCE with a public Metasploit module and Known ransomware use outpaces once released; there is no accelerated tier for a no-interaction network kernel RCE.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: A.8.8 records the MS17-010 family but recording does not disable SMBv1 or reboot hosts; the control does not force this wormable, ransomware-associated SMB RCE into a verified estate-wide patch-and-disable across every host with TCP 445 reachable.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2017-0148 (EternalBlue family, EPSS 0.994 / 99.9th pct, KEV 2022-04-06 ransomware Known) was fixed by MS17-010 on 2017-03-14 but drove WannaCry in May 2017 and remains a lateral-movement staple; a 4-hour KEV-clock SLA measuring installed-and-rebooted MS17-010, or SMBv1 disablement, is what closes the wormable window.

new_control_requirements.name: INCOMPLETE-PATCH-SEQUENCE-SEVERITY-MULTIPLIER
new_control_requirements.description: Vulnerability-management programs must apply a severity multiplier when a CVE is the Nth in an incomplete-patch sequence on the same primitive (third MOTW bypass, second AMSI bypass, etc.). Framework controls treating each CVE as discrete obscure the structural defect; the Nth CVE in a sequence implies that future bypasses on the same primitive are likely.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2017-0148 is one of five SMBv1 FEA-parsing CVEs (CVE-2017-0143/0144/0145/0146/0148) fixed together in MS17-010; treating them as discrete hides that the whole SMBv1 primitive must be removed by disabling the protocol, so the multiplier is what flags SMBv1 for retirement rather than serial per-CVE patching.

CVE-2017-0149.name: Microsoft Internet Explorer Memory Corruption Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: A victim views a crafted page in IE 9-11; the browser mishandles objects in memory, an out-of-bounds write corrupts memory, and the attacker runs code as the current user — full control if that user is an administrator.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; but UI:R, the user must open the attacker's page.
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; a single crafted or compromised page suffices once the user visits it.
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Microsoft identified the in-the-wild exploitation itself; no AI-assisted discovery is claimed.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Installing MS17-006 with a reboot and retiring Internet Explorer in favour of a supported browser so the vulnerable renderer is not used for untrusted content.
prevention.adequacy: The patch removes the flaw, but because IE stayed the default renderer in many estates the exposure recurred until IE itself was disabled.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Monitoring for mshtml crashes and for iexplore.exe spawning child processes or downloading executables after a page view.
detection.adequacy: Crash and post-exploitation telemetry catch some attempts, but the code execution completes in-process before most controls react.

response.what_would_have_worked: Isolating the host and hunting for the follow-on payload the browser RCE delivered, plus disabling IE fleet-wide.
response.adequacy: Response starts after user-context code already ran, so it is containment rather than prevention.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: SI-2 is met by MS17-006 approval, but the flaw was Exploited: Yes at the 2017-03-14 release and KEV relisted it in 2022; browsers rendered with the vulnerable mshtml long after, because the control closes on approval rather than installed-and-IE-retired.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: Article 21 patching is in place, but it does not treat a browser RCE exploited at release as the accelerated case; the IE cumulative needs a restart and update rings defer browser channels, leaving the post-2017-03-14 window open to drive-by exploitation.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: CAF B4 update management is asserted, yet an in-the-wild IE memory-corruption RCE needed a compressed browser-update clock or retirement for Edge; B4 does not force browser-specific no-deferral, so IE 9-11 kept rendering untrusted content past the fix.

AU-Essential-8-App-Hardening.gap: Application hardening tunes browser configuration but does not compel replacing or disabling Internet Explorer as an actively-exploited surface; with IE 9-11 left as the default renderer for untrusted content, CVE-2017-0149 stays reachable regardless of settings.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Essential Eight OS/app patch maturity runs a rolling window too slow for a browser RCE exploited at release; there is no accelerated tier for a client-side memory-corruption flaw where one crafted page equals code execution.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: A.8.8 records CVE-2017-0149 but recording does not remove IE 9-11 from desktops or force MS17-006 installed and IE retired; the control does not convert an actively-exploited browser RCE into a verified estate-wide update-and-decommission of the vulnerable renderer.

new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2017-0149 was marked Exploited: Yes in MS17-006 on 2017-03-14 (EPSS 0.292, 98th pct) and relisted by CISA on 2022-05-24, yet IE 9-11 kept rendering untrusted content in many estates; a KEV-clock SLA measuring MS17-006 installed-and-rebooted, or IE disabled, is what closes the drive-by window.

new_control_requirements.description: Enterprise update rings must not defer security-channel browser updates beyond 24h.

CVE-2017-0210.name: Microsoft Internet Explorer Privilege Escalation Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: A victim opens a crafted page in IE 10/11; the browser fails to enforce its cross-domain policy, so the attacker reads one domain's data, injects content back into it, and lifts script from low to medium integrity — most potent chained with a code-execution bug to escape protected mode.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; UI:R, the user must open the attacker's page.
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; once the page loads, the origin-validation failure is deterministic.
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Microsoft recorded the flaw as already publicly known and under active attack when the fix shipped; no finder is named and no AI-assisted discovery is involved.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Installing the April 2017 IE cumulative with a reboot and disabling Internet Explorer for untrusted browsing in favour of a supported browser.
prevention.adequacy: The update restores same-origin enforcement, but with IE left as the default renderer the cross-domain surface persisted until IE was disabled.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Watching for cross-origin DOM and cookie access within an IE session, and for user-integrity activity emerging from a protected-mode tab.
detection.adequacy: UXSS activity rides an already-authenticated browser session, so it is hard to distinguish from legitimate scripting without deep browser telemetry.

response.what_would_have_worked: Assuming cross-origin data disclosure and hunting for the chained RCE payload, plus disabling IE fleet-wide.
response.adequacy: By the time the UXSS is observed, cross-domain data may already be exfiltrated, so response is containment.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: SI-2 is met by the April 2017 IE cumulative, but the flaw was under active attack at the 2017-04-11 release and KEV relisted it in 2022; IE 10/11 enforced broken cross-domain policies long after, because the control closes on approval rather than installed-and-IE-retired.

NIST-800-53-AC-3.gap: AC-3 access enforcement is asserted, yet this IE 10/11 flaw bypasses the origin boundary AC-3 nominally protects; that decision lives inside the browser's same-origin logic, not in any policy an AC-3 attestation inspects, so the control passes while cross-domain reads and injection succeed.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: Article 21 patching is present, but it does not treat an actively-attacked browser UXSS/EoP as accelerated; the IE cumulative needs a restart and rings defer browser channels, so the post-2017-04-11 window is where cross-origin theft and integrity uplift happen, especially chained with an RCE.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: CAF B4 update management is asserted, yet an in-the-wild IE cross-domain flaw needed a compressed browser-update clock or retirement for Edge; B4 does not force browser-specific no-deferral, so IE 10/11 kept rendering untrusted content with a broken same-origin boundary.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Essential Eight patch maturity runs a rolling window too slow for a browser flaw flagged under active attack at release; there is no accelerated tier for a same-origin-bypass primitive whose danger is amplified by chaining with a code-execution bug.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: A.8.8 records CVE-2017-0210 but recording does not remove IE 10/11 or force the April 2017 update installed and IE retired; the control does not convert an actively-attacked cross-domain UXSS into a verified estate-wide update-and-decommission of the vulnerable browser.

CVE-2017-11317.name: Telerik UI for ASP.NET AJAX Unrestricted File Upload Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: An unauthenticated attacker encrypts a malicious RadAsyncUpload configuration with the hardcoded default key and POSTs it to Telerik.Web.UI.WebResource.axd?type=rau, writing a webshell to a chosen path and executing code on the server.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; only the vulnerable build (default keys present) needs to be internet-reachable.
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; the default key is public, so the crafted upload is deterministic and scriptable.
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Outside human researchers (Paul Taylor and the RadAsyncUpload research line) found and published it; no AI-assisted discovery.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Upgrading Telerik.Web.UI to R2 2017 SP2 (2017.2.711)+ across every application that embeds it and setting unique encryption/hash keys in web.config.
prevention.adequacy: Effective, but only if the bundled component is found in every dependent app — the enumeration is the hard part, not the upgrade.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alerting on unauthenticated POSTs to ...WebResource.axd?type=rau and on new executable files in upload directories.
detection.adequacy: Detects the upload stage, but a webshell dropped before detection persists until removed.

response.what_would_have_worked: Hunting for webshells in RadAsyncUpload target folders and rotating any secrets exposed via the same key/web.config leak.
response.adequacy: The upgrade closes the upload path but does not remove a shell already written, so response must include artifact hunting.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: SI-2 is nominally met, but Telerik.Web.UI is bundled, so the 2017.1.118/2017.2.711 fix must reach every app embedding it; CISA's 2022-04-11 relisting shows vulnerable builds persisted, because a product-tracking patch process misses the assembly inside OEM and in-house web apps.

NIST-800-53-SR-3.gap: SR-3 supply-chain protection assessed against direct vendors never enumerates a UI library bundled two levels down, so the estate cannot identify which internet-facing ASP.NET applications carry the hardcoded-key RadAsyncUpload handler.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: Article 21 patching does not treat a pre-auth RCE in an embedded web component with public Exploit-DB tooling (43874) as accelerated; the upgrade needs only an app-pool recycle, yet the 2022-05-02 KEV due date shows routine cadence still left vulnerable Telerik builds exposed.

NIS2-Art21-supply-chain.gap: Article 21 supply-chain security via vendor assurance misses a UI library redistributed inside many ASP.NET products; without enumerating which apps bundle Telerik.Web.UI below R2 2017 SP2, the control cannot surface the unauthenticated upload RCE the default key exposes.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: CAF B4 update management is asserted, yet RadAsyncUpload lives in an embedded component many operators do not know they run; B4 does not force the bundled-dependency enumeration needed to upgrade every pre-2017.1.118 Telerik.Web.UI reachable from the internet.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Essential Eight application-patch maturity misses a Telerik.Web.UI build embedded in a line-of-business app that falls outside the maintained pipeline; the model has no mechanism to push an unauthenticated component RCE with public tooling to the front of the queue.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: A.8.8 records CVE-2017-11317 but recording does not upgrade the assembly inside every dependent app or set unique web.config keys; the control does not convert a bundled-component pre-auth RCE into a verified sweep across all applications that embed it.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.24.gap: A.8.24 use of cryptography is defeated because RadAsyncUpload protected rauPostData with a static hardcoded key that provided no confidentiality against anyone holding the public value; A.8.24 as assessed checks that cryptography is used, not that keys are unique and secret per deployment.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2017-11317 in Telerik.Web.UI (EPSS 0.835, 99.7th pct, KEV 2022-04-11 due 2022-05-02) has public exploit code (Exploit-DB 43874, RAU_crypto) and needs only an app-pool recycle to remediate, yet vulnerable builds stayed internet-facing for years; a KEV-clock SLA measuring every dependent app against 2017.2.711 and unique keys is what forces closure.

new_control_requirements.name: TIER-3-DEPENDENCY-INVENTORY
new_control_requirements.description: Supply chain inventory must extend to tier-3 dependencies (dependencies of dependencies of direct dependencies). SBOM coverage for libsystemd-class transitive dependencies cannot be omitted under SR-3.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2017-11317 hides in the Telerik.Web.UI assembly bundled inside OEM and in-house ASP.NET applications, so an operator patching only directly-installed packages leaves the hardcoded-key RadAsyncUpload handler internet-facing; a tier-3 dependency inventory that records Telerik.Web.UI wherever it is embedded is what makes the pre-2017.1.118 builds findable.

attack_vector.description: An unauthenticated attacker reaches KaseyaCwWebService/ManagedIT.asmx on a Kaseya VSA server and runs arbitrary SQL through ExecuteSQL/GetDataSet (including EXEC xp_cmdshell), resets the kaseyasupport admin, and uses the RMM's SYSTEM-level agent procedures to deploy ransomware to every managed endpoint — the February 2019 GandCrab campaign.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; only ManagedIT.asmx reachable through the VSA web interface.
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; no authentication step, and public tooling (owlky) automates fingerprinting and SQL execution.
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Found by the human researcher behind kbni/owlky and analyzed by Huntress; no AI-assisted discovery.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Removing the ManagedITSync integration or restricting ManagedIT.asmx by IP/domain, and never exposing the VSA web interface to untrusted networks.
prevention.adequacy: Removal closes the path, but the product is end-of-life so the terminal state is disconnection, not continued patching.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alerting on unauthenticated ManagedIT.asmx access and on agent procedures pushing downloads fleet-wide.
detection.adequacy: Detection at the endpoint stage may fire only as ransomware deploys across the fleet, which is late for a control-plane compromise.

response.what_would_have_worked: A fleet-control-plane IR playbook: revoke agent trust, audit procedures pushed during the exposure window, quarantine downstream devices, and rotate VSA credentials.
response.adequacy: Server-only recovery leaves the endpoints the RMM reached compromised, so response must be fleet-wide from the first alert.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: SI-2 failed structurally because the flaw was a ConnectWise integration on the Kaseya VSA server, so patching Kaseya's core product never touched the ManagedITSync assembly; the 2022-05-24 KEV relisting with Known ransomware use, years after the 2019 GandCrab campaign, shows it lingered unremediated.

NIST-800-53-SI-10.gap: SI-10 input validation is violated outright: ManagedIT.asmx operations pass caller-supplied strings to the VSA database with no parameterization or auth, so an attestation covering normal input paths never reaches the unauthenticated SOAP operations that concatenate raw SQL, including xp_cmdshell.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: Article 21 patching did not convert the ManagedITSync exposure into emergency removal; between 2017 disclosure and the February 2019 GandCrab campaign it stayed installed on internet-facing VSA servers, and routine cadence never treated an RMM control-plane RCE as a fleet-wide event.

NIS2-Art21-incident-handling.gap: Incident handling under-scopes an RMM compromise: one unauthenticated ManagedIT.asmx call can push GandCrab to every managed endpoint via SYSTEM agent procedures, but a process scoped to the VSA host alone misses the downstream fleet; the control does not require treating control-plane compromise as multi-endpoint from the first alert.

UK-CAF-D1.gap: CAF D1 response and recovery is inadequate for this blast radius: recovering the VSA server does not recover the endpoints its agent procedures encrypted, and without a fleet-wide plan that revokes agent trust and audits pushed procedures, D1 treats the incident as a single-server event.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Essential Eight patch maturity targets OS and application patching, but the ManagedITSync integration is a third-party RMM add-on outside that pipeline; there is no accelerated tier for an unauthenticated SQLi-to-RCE in a management-plane component that administers an entire downstream estate.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: A.8.8 records CVE-2017-18362 but recording does not remove the integration or restrict ManagedIT.asmx; the control does not force an unauthenticated, database-owning RMM flaw with public tooling into a verified removal-and-credential-rotation across every VSA server that ran it.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2017-18362 (Kaseya VSA / ConnectWise ManagedITSync, EPSS 0.868 / 99.7th pct, KEV 2022-05-24 ransomware Known) had public tooling (owlky) and a Nuclei template yet stayed installed on internet-facing VSA servers into the February 2019 GandCrab campaign; a KEV-clock SLA that forces removal or ManagedIT.asmx restriction within hours is what closes the control-plane path.

new_control_requirements.name: FLEET-COMPROMISE-IR-PLAYBOOK
new_control_requirements.description: Pre-rehearsed IR playbook for fleet-control-plane compromise including: MDM-pushed certificate revocation, device-trust-state invalidation, configuration-profile audit since the suspected compromise window, downstream device-quarantine criteria, and credential rotation for any account that authenticated through a compromised fleet device during the exposure period.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2017-18362 let a single unauthenticated ManagedIT.asmx call push GandCrab to every Kaseya VSA-managed endpoint in February 2019 via SYSTEM-level agent procedures; a pre-rehearsed fleet-control-plane IR playbook — revoke agent trust, audit procedures pushed during the exposure window, quarantine downstream devices, rotate VSA credentials — is what turns a single-server alert into a fleet-scoped response.

attack_vector.description: A crafted EPS/PostScript document abuses .rsdparams type confusion to bypass the -dSAFER guard and set an /OutputFile of '%pipe%<command>', executing OS commands as the Ghostscript process — typically triggered server-side when ImageMagick or Pillow renders an uploaded file.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; the attacker only needs their document to be processed by gs, with no account on the target.
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; a single deterministic document, no race or memory grooming; CVSS UI:R is satisfied automatically by any pipeline that auto-converts uploads.
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Found and reported by the Atlassian Security Team via the public Ghostscript bug tracker; the Metasploit weaponization was written by a human researcher (hdm).

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Upgrading Ghostscript to 9.22 (or a distro backport) AND disabling the ImageMagick PS/EPS/PDF delegates for untrusted input, then restarting the conversion workers.
prevention.adequacy: Effective only if the transitive gs inside ImageMagick/Pillow is also updated and the workers recycled; patching the standalone package alone leaves the loaded library vulnerable.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alerting when an image/document-conversion process spawns a shell or egresses to the network.
detection.adequacy: Catches successful execution but not the initial parse; a payload that only writes a local file may not egress.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating any conversion host that ran a crafted EPS as executed-upon: rotate its credentials and inspect for dropped files.
response.adequacy: Depends on retaining process-lineage logs, which upload workers rarely keep.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: SI-2 is nominally satisfied by patching the gs package before the 2022-06-14 KEV due date, but the control does not require enumerating ImageMagick, GraphicsMagick and Pillow as carriers of the same interpreter, nor restarting the daemons that hold the pre-9.22 library resident, so the vulnerable .rsdparams path survives a clean SI-2 report.

NIST-800-53-CM-7.gap: CM-7 credits the -dSAFER sandbox as the least-functionality boundary, which is exactly what CVE-2017-8291 defeats; it does not mandate disabling the PostScript/EPS coder in ImageMagick policy.xml, the config change that actually severs the '%pipe%' command path regardless of gs version.

NIS2-Art21-vulnerability-management.gap: NIS2 vulnerability handling presumes the affected component appears in the asset inventory; because gs is reached through image libraries rather than declared directly, the 2017-era flaw generates no finding on a 2022 KEV listing for services whose dependency graph stops at ImageMagick or Pillow.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: B4 secure configuration is evidenced by a current OS package, but the exploit is a data file, so the review passes while the actual hardening lever — refusing the PS/EPS delegate for untrusted documents — is left unset and attacker EPS still reaches the confused operator.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: The Patch Applications control clocks named internet-facing apps and can show gs 9.22 installed on the host, yet a separately packaged conversion worker that bundles an older gs keeps the maturity attestation green while the vulnerable interpreter is still what renders the upload.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: A.8.8 is typically evidenced by an OS patch scan; scoped that way it never binds the CVE to the document-conversion service that actually calls the interpreter, so the ImageMagick delegate reaching the vulnerable gs can remain enabled and unrestarted under a conformant report.

OWASP-Top-10-2021-A06.gap: A06 names the class exactly — an outdated component pulled in transitively — and the standard failure is scoping the component scan to declared dependencies, which hides a gs <= 9.21 embedded beneath the image library the developer actually selected.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2017-8291 (CVSS 7.8, EPSS 0.9614) was exploited in the wild in April 2017 and added to KEV on 2022-05-24 with a 2022-06-14 due date; because gs is embedded in ImageMagick/Pillow, a 4-hour mitigation clock forces the operator to identify and restart the conversion workers, not just patch the standalone package.

new_control_requirements.name: MITIGATION-ACTIVE-PATCH-PENDING-VERDICT-CLASS
new_control_requirements.description: Compliance verdicts must distinguish three states: (a) binary patch deployed (vulnerability eliminated), (b) vendor-mitigation rule active, no binary patch (residual risk: any defect in the mitigation rule reopens the vulnerability), (c) no mitigation, no patch (full exposure). Audit reports must surface (b) as a distinct compensating-control state with an associated time-bound action item, not as a 'patched per SLA' outcome.
new_control_requirements.evidence: For CVE-2017-8291 the ImageMagick policy.xml delegate-disable is a state-(b) compensating control distinct from the gs 9.22 binary patch; a program that records 'delegate disabled' as 'patched' hides that the pre-9.22 interpreter is still loaded in the conversion daemon and re-exposed the moment the coder is re-enabled.

CVE-2017-8543.name: Microsoft Windows Search Remote Code Execution Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: Crafted Windows Search Protocol messages delivered to the WSearch service over the SMB named pipe \pipe\MsFteWds make it mishandle objects in memory, giving an unauthenticated remote attacker code execution as the high-privileged service and the ability to create accounts on the host. Microsoft never published the underlying corruption primitive, and NVD's CWE-281 assignment does not name one.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; no account or prior access is needed, only SMB reachability to the Search service.
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; Microsoft states a remote unauthenticated attacker can trigger it through an SMB connection, and no source establishes a race or heap-groom precondition; the only documented constraint is that the WSearch named pipe is reachable over SMB.
attack_vector.ai_factor: None established. No public finder credit was resolvable from Microsoft's advisory; discovery source recorded as unknown, with no AI attribution.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Installing the June 2017 update and rebooting, plus blocking SMB from untrusted networks and disabling WSearch where unused.
prevention.adequacy: Fully effective on supported hosts once rebooted; for the EoL XP/2003 hosts in scope, decommissioning is the only durable answer.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Monitoring for WSearch/svchost crashes correlated with inbound SMB and for SYSTEM-context process spawns.
detection.adequacy: Sees the crash-and-execute stage but not the initial malformed packets unless SMB traffic is inspected.

response.what_would_have_worked: Isolating any host whose Search service crashed after untrusted SMB and auditing for new local accounts.
response.adequacy: Depends on SMB and account-creation logging being retained on the affected host.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: SI-2 is met by installing the June 2017 update, but the fix is inert until reboot and the affected set includes off-ring EoL XP and Server 2003 hosts, so a downloaded-not-rebooted or unmanaged legacy machine keeps answering Windows Search Protocol requests on the vulnerable service under a clean SI-2 report.

NIST-800-53-SC-7.gap: SC-7 is nominally satisfied by a perimeter firewall, yet enterprise baselines allow SMB 139/445 internally for file sharing, so the pre-auth WSearch code-execution path remains reachable from any compromised same-segment host regardless of the boundary posture.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: Article 21 patch management assumes a supported product with a reboot cadence; the XP/2003 hosts this CVE also hits were served only by an exceptional out-of-band package and have no ongoing support, so a modern-fleet attestation can be green while legacy Windows Search hosts stay the 9.8 exposure.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: B4 secure configuration would call for disabling unused Windows Search and restricting SMB, but a review evidenced only by applied patches overlooks that WSearch is on by default and reachable across internal SMB, leaving the unauthenticated path open.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Patch Operating Systems can show the June 2017 update approved without forcing the reboot that activates the fix, and its scope excludes the out-of-support XP/2003 hosts in range, so a maturity attestation coexists with hosts still holding the un-restarted vulnerable service.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: A.8.8 evidenced by a patch scan treats install as remediation, but this fix needs a reboot to bind and the affected set spans EoL Windows the inventory often omits, so a conformant report can sit alongside a host whose Search service still runs the vulnerable code.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2017-8543 (CVSS 9.8, EPSS 0.64856) is an unauthenticated SMB RCE added to KEV on 2022-05-24 with a 2022-06-14 due date; a 4-hour clock forces either the reboot that activates the June 2017 fix or the documented SMB-block compensating control, rather than accepting an installed-but-un-rebooted host as remediated.

new_control_requirements.name: MITIGATION-ACTIVE-PATCH-PENDING-VERDICT-CLASS
new_control_requirements.description: Compliance verdicts must distinguish three states: (a) binary patch deployed (vulnerability eliminated), (b) vendor-mitigation rule active, no binary patch (residual risk: any defect in the mitigation rule reopens the vulnerability), (c) no mitigation, no patch (full exposure). Audit reports must surface (b) as a distinct compensating-control state with an associated time-bound action item, not as a 'patched per SLA' outcome.
new_control_requirements.evidence: For CVE-2017-8543, blocking SMB 139/445 and disabling WSearch is a state-(b) compensating control while the reboot is pending, and for EoL XP/Server 2003 hosts with no durable fix it is state (c) until decommission; recording either as 'patched per SLA' hides that the WSearch code-execution path is still reachable on the affected host.

CVE-2018-10561.name: Dasan GPON Routers Authentication Bypass Vulnerability
