attack_vector.description: Appending '?images' to any protected URL on a Dasan GPON router's web interface makes the device treat the request as a public image resource and skip authentication, giving an unauthenticated attacker access to management functions and, chained with CVE-2018-10562, root command execution.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; a single unauthenticated crafted URL, no credentials.
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; deterministic path suffix, no timing or brute force; the only gate is reachability of the management interface, which is frequently WAN-exposed.
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Manual analysis by vpnMentor researchers; no AI-assisted discovery.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Decommissioning the end-of-life router or removing WAN reachability of its management interface.
prevention.adequacy: Decommissioning is durable; WAN-blocking helps but a LAN client on the served network still reaches the vulnerable interface.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alerting on '?images'-suffixed requests to management paths and on unauthenticated config changes.
detection.adequacy: Consumer ONTs rarely emit usable logs, so detection often depends on upstream network telemetry.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating any exposed unit as compromised: replace it and rotate any credentials that transited it.
response.adequacy: Firmware alone cannot clean a device with an unfixable bypass; replacement is the reliable response.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: SI-2 presumes an available patch, but no general fix reaches these EoL Dasan ONTs, so the control has nothing to deploy against the 2022-04-21 due date and does not itself compel the decommission-or-isolate that alone removes the '?images' bypass.

NIST-800-53-SC-7.gap: SC-7 would contain the flaw by denying WAN access to the admin interface, yet enterprise boundary baselines seldom extend to consumer-grade GPON CPE at remote sites, so the default WAN exposure of these units falls outside the reviewed perimeter and the unauthenticated path persists.

NIS2-Art21-network-security.gap: NIS2 network-security segmentation cannot help a router whose purpose is to serve every client on its LAN; there is no segment that removes the path to the management interface, so the control as applied to enterprise cores does not address this consumer-edge exposure.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: B4 secure configuration assumes the device can be hardened to a baseline, but the '?images' bypass is unfixable in the shipped firmware, so the objective is unreachable by configuration and is met only by retiring the router — an action B4's hardening framing does not require.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: With no fixed firmware for the affected ONTs, Patch Applications has no artefact to apply and grants no credit for decommissioning, so the maturity attestation stays silent while the unauthenticated bypass remains in service on every deployed unit.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: A.8.8 flags the CVE but expects a patch as remediation; because the device is EoL with no fix, conformance hinges on a risk-treatment decision to retire it, which an inventory-and-patch reading of A.8.8 does not enforce.

new_control_requirements.name: PERIMETER-COMPROMISE-REBUILD-NOT-PATCH
new_control_requirements.description: Pre-rehearsed IR runbook for any perimeter device that suffers a pre-auth RCE CVE in active exploitation MUST default to config-exfil + rebuild + credential rotation, not patch-in-place. Patch-in-place leaves attacker-installed implants intact.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2018-10561 (CVSS 9.8, EPSS 0.93041) is a pre-auth bypass on an internet-facing Dasan GPON router that botnets mass-exploited from May 2018; with no vendor fix and the device end-of-life, any exposed unit must be treated as compromised and rebuilt or replaced with credential rotation, never 'patched in place'.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: For CVE-2018-10561, added to KEV on 2022-03-31 with a 2022-04-21 due date and no available patch, the KEV SLA's 'documented compensating controls' branch is the only reachable path — decommission or WAN-isolation — forcing action where SI-2 patching and Essential Eight have no artefact to deploy.

CVE-2018-10562.name: Dasan GPON Routers Command Injection Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: A POST to /GponForm/diag_Form?images/ injects shell commands through the 'dest_host' ping parameter, running them as root; the router saves output to /tmp and returns it on a later /diag.html request. Chained with the '?images' auth bypass it is unauthenticated root RCE.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; unauthenticated when combined with CVE-2018-10561's bypass.
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; a single crafted POST, no race or memory corruption; EPSS 0.99944 shows exploitation is effectively certain.
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Manual research by vpnMentor; no AI involvement.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Decommissioning the end-of-life router or isolating its management interface from WAN and untrusted LAN clients.
prevention.adequacy: Decommissioning is durable; isolation reduces reach but any client on the served LAN can still reach the CGI.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Detecting the router fetching external payloads or the CGI spawning shell children.
detection.adequacy: Needs upstream network telemetry because the ONT itself rarely logs usefully.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating any exposed unit as rooted: replace it, rebuild configuration from known-good, and rotate transited credentials.
response.adequacy: Firmware update alone does not evict an implant placed during the exposure window.

NIST-800-53-SI-10.gap: SI-10 is the missing input-validation control, but it binds the firmware developer and no fixed build enforcing neutralisation of 'dest_host' reaches these EoL routers, so the operator cannot meet SI-10 on the device and the shell-metacharacter injection remains.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: SI-2 has no patch to deploy because DASAN shipped no general fix; the 2022-04-21 due date is unreachable by patching and SI-2 does not itself compel the decommission-and-rebuild a Known-ransomware, EPSS-0.99944 device warrants.

NIS2-Art21-network-security.gap: NIS2 segmentation cannot remove the path on a router that exists to serve its LAN clients and is often WAN-exposed by default, so the unauthenticated injection stays reachable from exactly the population the device serves.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: B4 secure configuration cannot harden away a root command injection built into unfixable firmware; the objective is met only by retiring the router, which B4's hardening framing does not require.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Patch Applications has no firmware to apply and gives no credit for decommissioning, so a maturity attestation stays silent while a near-certain-to-be-exploited root-RCE device remains deployed.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: A.8.8 flags the CVE but expects patching; with the device EoL and no fix, conformance rests on a documented retire-and-rebuild decision that an inventory-and-patch reading of the control does not enforce.

new_control_requirements.name: PERIMETER-COMPROMISE-REBUILD-NOT-PATCH
new_control_requirements.description: Pre-rehearsed IR runbook for any perimeter device that suffers a pre-auth RCE CVE in active exploitation MUST default to config-exfil + rebuild + credential rotation, not patch-in-place. Patch-in-place leaves attacker-installed implants intact.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2018-10562 (CVSS 9.8, EPSS 0.99944, KEV ransomware Known) is unauthenticated root RCE on an internet-facing GPON router that Mirai-class botnets mass-exploited from May 2018; an exposed unit must be rebuilt and its credentials rotated, since a later firmware update cannot evict an implant placed during the exposure window.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: For CVE-2018-10562, added to KEV on 2022-03-31 (due 2022-04-21) with no patch and Known ransomware use, the KEV SLA's compensating-control branch — immediate isolation or decommission — is the only reachable mitigation, driving action where SI-2 patching and Essential Eight have no artefact.

CVE-2018-20753.name: Kaseya VSA Remote Code Execution Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: An unprivileged remote attacker reaches Kaseya VSA's managed-script path and executes arbitrary PowerShell across every endpoint the VSA server manages, because the control plane does not properly authorize the execution request — turning one request into fleet-wide code execution.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; no VSA account and no user interaction, only network reachability to the VSA server.
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; a single unauthorized request drives the built-in script-execution feature; the blast radius is the managed fleet, not one host.
attack_vector.ai_factor: None established. Surfaced via in-the-wild exploitation and Kaseya's Q1 2018 update; no researcher credit resolvable and no AI attribution.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Upgrading VSA to R9.3 9.3.0.35 / R9.4 9.4.0.36 / R9.5 9.5.0.5 and restricting the VSA admin interface to trusted networks.
prevention.adequacy: Effective once the fixed build is running; network restriction bounds who can reach the control plane while the update is deployed.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alerting on agent procedures run fleet-wide outside a change window and on mass PowerShell spawns from the Kaseya agent.
detection.adequacy: Detects the fan-out stage; requires VSA audit logging and endpoint process telemetry to be collected and correlated.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating a VSA compromise as a fleet event: audit pushed procedures, quarantine affected endpoints, rotate credentials that authenticated through the fleet.
response.adequacy: Requires a pre-rehearsed fleet-control-plane IR playbook; host-scoped IR under-escalates the fan-out.

NIST-800-53-AC-6.gap: AC-6 least privilege is nominally met by scoping VSA operator accounts, but the attacker never authenticates as any operator, so the account model is bypassed rather than abused and the unauthorized fleet-execution path stays open on builds below the Q1-2018 fixes.

NIST-800-53-AC-3.gap: AC-3 is evidenced by confirming the application's access rules are configured, but this CVE is the enforcement point failing open pre-authentication, which a configuration review of access rules does not detect — the January-2018 abuse shows the decision itself being skipped.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: SI-2 fixes this by upgrading to the patched VSA builds, yet a program scoped to OS patching can miss a self-hosted RMM application, leaving the 2022-05-04 KEV due date unmet on the very control plane that reaches every endpoint.

NIS2-Art21-incident-handling.gap: NIS2 incident handling scoped to individual hosts under-escalates an RMM compromise, missing that one CVE-2018-20753 event means simultaneous execution across the whole managed fleet with a Known ransomware history.

UK-CAF-B2.gap: B2 identity and access control is evidenced by VSA admins authenticating at login, but the vulnerable execution path never consults an identity, so the review passes while an unauthenticated caller drives the privileged fleet-execution function.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Patch Applications read as end-user software lets a self-hosted VSA server sit outside the patch clock, keeping the single control-plane point that reaches every managed endpoint on a pre-fix build.

ISO-27001-2022-A.5.15.gap: A.5.15 access control is documented via VSA role assignments, which are nominally met, but the flaw is the authorization rules failing on the script-execution endpoint, so an unauthenticated request still reaches fleet-wide PowerShell under a conformant policy.

new_control_requirements.name: FLEET-COMPROMISE-IR-PLAYBOOK
new_control_requirements.description: Pre-rehearsed IR playbook for fleet-control-plane compromise including: MDM-pushed certificate revocation, device-trust-state invalidation, configuration-profile audit since the suspected compromise window, downstream device-quarantine criteria, and credential rotation for any account that authenticated through a compromised fleet device during the exposure period.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2018-20753 (CVSS 9.8, KEV ransomware Known, exploited in the wild January 2018) turns one Kaseya VSA request into fleet-wide PowerShell execution, so a control-plane compromise requires a pre-rehearsed fleet playbook — audit pushed agent procedures, quarantine downstream endpoints, rotate credentials that authenticated through the fleet — that host-scoped IR does not provide.

new_control_requirements.name: FLEET-CONTROL-PLANE-ADMIN-PRIVILEGE-TIER
new_control_requirements.description: Administrators of fleet-control-plane systems (MDM/UEM, EDR consoles, identity providers, container orchestrators, configuration management) must be classified as a distinct privilege tier above application admins, with: PAM-jumphost-only access, FIDO2 step-up per session, just-in-time elevation with approval workflow, separate identity from any other admin role, and dedicated PAW (privileged access workstation) hardware. Compliance frameworks must enumerate this tier explicitly rather than collapsing it into 'admin'.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Because a Kaseya VSA instance reaches every managed endpoint, the CVE-2018-20753 fan-out shows the RMM must be governed as a distinct fleet-control-plane tier — jumphost-only, network-restricted, separately identified — rather than collapsed into generic application admin, which is what let an unauthenticated caller reach the fleet-execution function.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2018-20753 was added to KEV on 2022-04-13 (due 2022-05-04) with Known ransomware use; a 4-hour clock on the RMM forces the self-hosted VSA server onto the patch path to R9.3 9.3.0.35 / R9.4 9.4.0.36 / R9.5 9.5.0.5, which an OS-scoped patch program otherwise misses.

CVE-2018-5002.name: Adobe Flash Player Stack-based Buffer Overflow Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: A malformed try-catch-with-static-initializer construct in ActionScript overflows a stack buffer in Adobe Flash Player, running code as the current user; in the wild the lure .xlsx contained no exploit at all — only an OLE object pointing Office's Flash ActiveX control at a remote SWF, which was fetched and decrypted on open and then staged shellcode over the same RSA+AES channel.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; runs at the opening user's privilege, so it is an initial-access primitive usually chained with a separate escalation.
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L but UI:R; a user must open the weaponized document, after which the deterministic ActionScript triggers the overflow.
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Independently caught in telemetry by ICEBRG, Qihoo 360, and Tencent; no AI-assisted discovery.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Disabling or removing the Flash plugin (application hardening), or at minimum updating to 30.0.0.113 and enforcing click-to-play.
prevention.adequacy: Removing Flash is durable and is now the only correct state; patching alone left the runtime present and reachable via documents.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alerting on Office spawning children after loading Flash and on document-triggered outbound SWF retrieval.
detection.adequacy: Catches execution and staging but not the initial open; the remote-staged design reduced static-scan signal.

response.what_would_have_worked: Isolating any host that opened the lure and hunting for the chained follow-on payload and escalation.
response.adequacy: Depends on process-lineage and network logs from the endpoint that opened the document.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: SI-2 was met by moving to Flash 30.0.0.113 in 2018, but Flash reached hosts through browser bundles and through Office's own Flash ActiveX control on separate update tracks, so a standalone-player patch could lag those; post-2020 the only correct SI-2 state is removal, not a 'patched' blocked runtime.

NIST-800-53-CM-7.gap: CM-7 would neutralise the exploit by disabling Flash or enforcing click-to-play, but 2018 baselines widely permitted Flash for business content and left the Office ActiveX control enabled, so the .xlsx lure's remotely fetched SWF executed at user privilege under a nominally compliant least-functionality posture.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: NIS2 patch management presumes a supported runtime; Flash's 2020-12-31 end-of-life means no ongoing support, so a host still running Flash cannot satisfy the control by patching and only removal closes the exposure, which the cadence framing does not itself require.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: B4 secure configuration evidenced by 'Flash is current' misses the document-delivery path, since the vulnerable player still runs when a user opens an Office file whose OLE object names a remote SWF, regardless of the plugin version.

AU-Essential-8-App-Hardening.gap: Application Hardening explicitly requires disabling or removing browser Flash, which would have blocked this outright; an estate that enforced it only in the browser still let Office's Flash ActiveX control reach the overflow, and the hardening gap rather than the patch state is what was decisive.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Patch Applications can track the browser plugin while missing Flash bundled into other software or hosted by Office's ActiveX control, so a maturity attestation reads compliant while a document-triggered remote SWF still reaches the overflow.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: A.8.8 evidenced by a patch scan can show the June-2018 update applied while the now-end-of-life runtime remains installed; after 2021 the correct remediation is removal, which an inventory-and-patch reading of A.8.8 does not enforce.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2018-5002 (CVSS 7.8, EPSS 0.25353) was a targeted zero-day fixed in Flash 30.0.0.113 (APSB18-19, 2018-06-07) and added to KEV on 2022-05-23 (due 2022-06-13); because Flash is now end-of-life, the KEV SLA's verified-mitigation branch resolves to removal of the runtime, forcing a definite action rather than a stale 'patched' record.

new_control_requirements.name: MITIGATION-ACTIVE-PATCH-PENDING-VERDICT-CLASS
new_control_requirements.description: Compliance verdicts must distinguish three states: (a) binary patch deployed (vulnerability eliminated), (b) vendor-mitigation rule active, no binary patch (residual risk: any defect in the mitigation rule reopens the vulnerability), (c) no mitigation, no patch (full exposure). Audit reports must surface (b) as a distinct compensating-control state with an associated time-bound action item, not as a 'patched per SLA' outcome.
new_control_requirements.evidence: For CVE-2018-5002, click-to-play or plugin-disable is a state-(b) compensating control while Flash 30.0.0.113 is deployed, and any post-2020 host still carrying the end-of-life runtime is state (c) until Flash is removed; recording either as 'patched per SLA' hides that a document-delivered SWF can still reach the stack overflow.

CVE-2018-6882.name: Synacor Zimbra Collaboration Suite (ZCS) Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: An email attachment's crafted Content-Location header is rendered unescaped by Zimbra webmail's getAttachmentLinkHtml, so opening the message executes attacker HTML/JavaScript in the victim's authenticated session — used in the wild to silently create auto-forwarding rules and exfiltrate mail.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; the attacker only sends an email, needing no account on the target server.
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L but UI:R; the victim must open the message in the Zimbra web client, after which the injected handler fires (scope-changed, S:C).
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Manual research by Securify via the Zimbra bug tracker; no AI-assisted discovery.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Upgrading ZCS to 8.7 Patch 1 or 8.8.7, which encodes the Content-Location value in getAttachmentLinkHtml.
prevention.adequacy: Fully effective once the server is patched; it does not remove attacker-created forwarding rules placed before patching.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alerting on webmail filter/forward-rule creation and on script execution when messages are viewed.
detection.adequacy: Requires per-request webmail logging; authentication-only logging misses the in-session XSS stage.

response.what_would_have_worked: Auditing exposed accounts for malicious mail filters and forwarding rules and revoking them, plus resetting affected sessions.
response.adequacy: Necessary because the espionage payload — auto-forwarding — persists in account settings after the server is patched.

NIST-800-53-SI-10.gap: SI-10 is the missing output-encoding control at the getAttachmentLinkHtml sink, but it binds the ZCS developer and no build enforced it until 8.7 Patch 1 / 8.8.7, so an operator could not satisfy SI-10 on the affected client and the Content-Location payload ran in the victim's session.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: SI-2 fixes this by upgrading ZCS, but a self-managed mail platform on its own cadence can lag the 2022-05-10 KEV due date, keeping the XSS reachable via ordinary email even as other assets are patched.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: NIS2 patch management can deprioritise a CVSS 6.1 XSS behind server-RCE flaws, but the 2022 CERT-UA campaign shows that framing understates it — the flaw enabled silent auto-forwarding espionage on unpatched ZCS.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: B4 secure configuration evidenced as 'mail server patched' can miss that the vulnerable path fires when a user merely reads an email, so the objective looks met while the attachment-header injection remains until the ZCS upgrade lands.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Patch Applications can read compliant while a 6.1 XSS is deprioritised behind higher-scored flaws, leaving the webmail server on a pre-8.7-Patch-1 / pre-8.8.7 build that still renders the injected Content-Location value.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: A.8.8 evidenced by a CVSS-weighted patch report can leave a 6.1 XSS unremediated, yet the real-world mail-forwarding exploitation shows the score understates impact, so a conformant report can coexist with an exposed webmail server.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.28.gap: A.8.28 secure coding would have required encoding the Content-Location header, but as a control on the vendor's development it cannot be evidenced by the operator, and until 8.7 Patch 1 / 8.8.7 shipped that encoding the operator's A.8.28 posture had no bearing on the injected-attachment path.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2018-6882 (CVSS 6.1, EPSS 0.2542, KEV ransomware Known) was used by CERT-UA-tracked actors to auto-forward Ukrainian government mail; a KEV 4-hour clock forces the webmail server onto the upgrade to 8.7 Patch 1 / 8.8.7 by the 2022-05-10 due date rather than letting a low CVSS defer it.

new_control_requirements.name: MITIGATION-ACTIVE-PATCH-PENDING-VERDICT-CLASS
new_control_requirements.description: Compliance verdicts must distinguish three states: (a) binary patch deployed (vulnerability eliminated), (b) vendor-mitigation rule active, no binary patch (residual risk: any defect in the mitigation rule reopens the vulnerability), (c) no mitigation, no patch (full exposure). Audit reports must surface (b) as a distinct compensating-control state with an associated time-bound action item, not as a 'patched per SLA' outcome.
new_control_requirements.evidence: For CVE-2018-6882, filtering inbound attachments with anomalous Content-Location headers is a state-(b) compensating control while the ZCS upgrade to 8.7 Patch 1 / 8.8.7 is pending; recording it as 'patched per SLA' hides that the getAttachmentLinkHtml sink still fires for any message that slips the filter.

CVE-2018-7602.name: Drupal Core Remote Code Execution Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: An attacker holding any Drupal account that can reach a confirmation form appends render-array keys to the `destination` query parameter. Those keys are cached with the form, and a follow-up request to the AJAX file endpoint with the returned form_build_id makes Drupal's renderer invoke the PHP callable named in `#post_render` with the attacker's `#markup` string, producing command execution as the web-server user.
attack_vector.privileges_required: NVD scores PR:N, but the published exploit chains authenticate first and use a form the account is entitled to reach — an account able to cancel its own account or delete content. On a site with open registration that is a self-service precondition, which is why the practical difference from PR:N is small.
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; two HTTP requests plus a form token scraped from the confirmation page. No race, no memory-layout knowledge, no information leak, and the vulnerable path is present in the default configuration of every 7.x and 8.x install.
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. The Drupal Security Team found this by continuing to audit the subsystem SA-CORE-2018-002 had just been patched in; the advisory credits four named humans and describes no automated analysis.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Upgrading to 7.59 / 8.4.8 / 8.5.3 within hours of the 2018-04-25 release, and — for sites that could not move that fast — taking authenticated form submission offline by disabling open registration and blocking the `file/ajax` route at the reverse proxy until the upgrade landed.
prevention.adequacy: The upgrade is a complete fix for this sink, but BOD 22-01's clock started in 2022, nearly four years after mass exploitation. For the sites actually compromised, no framework required the hours-not-days response the timeline demanded.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alerting on `%23post_render` and `%2523post_render` in query strings at the reverse proxy, plus process-lineage alerting on shell children of the PHP worker pool — the second signal catches successful execution even when the injected keys arrive in an encoding the first rule missed.
detection.adequacy: Both signals are cheap and specific, but they fire at exploitation, not before it. A site that detects the `#post_render` request has already served it; the value is scoping the compromise window for the credential rotation and file-integrity work that follows.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating any exposed site as compromised: rebuild the document root from a clean checkout rather than upgrading over the running tree, rotate database and API credentials, and audit user and role tables for accounts added during the exposure window.
response.adequacy: Necessary but frequently skipped, because an upgraded version number reads as remediation. The upgrade closes the injection sink and removes nothing the attacker wrote through it — web shells dropped in sites/*/files survive the core upgrade untouched.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: SI-2 was satisfied by any organisation with a documented Drupal patch process, and satisfying it did not help. The control's timeline anchors on patch availability, and here public exploit code trailed the 2018-04-25 fix by hours — a window shorter than most change-approval cycles. SI-2 also has no concept of a repeat defect in a subsystem just patched, so the second emergency Drupal upgrade in four weeks arrived as an unexpected event rather than an anticipated one.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: An in-scope entity that reached Drupal 7.59 inside its stated window can evidence Article 21 compliance cleanly. What the article does not reach is the branch that version sits on: Drupal 8 ended support 2021-11-17 and Drupal 7 on 2025-01-05, so the same attestation covers a site whose codebase will never receive another security fix. Patch-management compliance and end-of-life exposure are orthogonal here, and only one of them is measured.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: CAF B4 evidence for a Drupal estate normally consists of a hardened build standard, a WAF in front, and a maintenance record. None of the three touch this flaw: `destination` handling is core code with no configuration switch, and a generic WAF rule set does not treat `#post_render` in a redirect parameter as hostile. B4's per-advisory framing also hides the pattern — that SA-CORE-2018-004 is a bypass of the SA-CORE-2018-002 fix in the same subsystem.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Essential Eight's 48-hour target for exploited critical flaws in internet-facing applications was faster than most organisations achieved and still slower than this event: working exploit code was public the same day as the 2018-04-25 release. The maturity model's other requirement — running a vendor-supported version — is now unmeetable for this CVE's affected lines, since Drupal 7 support ended 2025-01-05 and no maturity level can be reached by patching a dead branch.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: A.8.8 asks for timely vulnerability information and an evaluation of exposure. Subscribing to drupal.org security advisories satisfies the first half literally, and the organisations that lost sites in April 2018 were largely subscribed. The control produces a finding when the intake is missing, never when the intake works and the downstream approval-and-deploy path is measured in days against an exploitation window measured in hours.

OWASP-Top-10-2021-A03.gap: A03 review practice looks for untrusted strings reaching an interpreter. Here the untrusted object is a PHP array whose `#`-prefixed keys are executable directives inside Drupal's own renderer, and the sink is CWE-94 code injection rather than a query or command string. A reviewer applying standard injection heuristics reads `destination` as a redirect URL and moves on, which is precisely how the same subsystem produced two critical CVEs in a month.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Drupal core released 7.59, 8.4.8 and 8.5.3 on 2018-04-25 and public exploit code (Exploit-DB 44542) was dated the same day; CISA later listed CVE-2018-7602 in KEV on 2022-04-13 with a 2022-05-04 due date and a ransomware flag. EPSS now stands at 0.99236 (99.933rd percentile, 2026-08-16), the top of the distribution. The 4-hour clock measured from patch availability is the only SLA shape that would have beaten the scanning wave against Drupal's install base, and the documented-compensating-controls branch matters here because disabling open registration and blocking the file/ajax route is deployable in minutes on sites that cannot upgrade immediately.

new_control_requirements.name: INCOMPLETE-PATCH-SEQUENCE-SEVERITY-MULTIPLIER
new_control_requirements.description: Vulnerability-management programs must apply a severity multiplier when a CVE is the Nth in an incomplete-patch sequence on the same primitive (third MOTW bypass, second AMSI bypass, etc.). Framework controls treating each CVE as discrete obscure the structural defect; the Nth CVE in a sequence implies that future bypasses on the same primitive are likely.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Drupal SA-CORE-2018-004 is the second highly critical remote code execution in the same Form API / render-array primitive within four weeks of SA-CORE-2018-002, and Drupal's own advisory text ties the two together. An organisation that treated the April 2018 upgrade as a discrete event had no reason to keep an emergency change window open, which is exactly why exploitation of CVE-2018-7602 outran remediation. A multiplier applied on the second render-array CVE would have kept the Drupal estate on heightened footing through the whole sequence rather than resetting after each advisory.

CVE-2018-7841.name: Schneider Electric U.motion Builder SQL Injection Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: One unauthenticated HTTP request to the reporting module's export endpoint carries an `object_id` value that is concatenated into a SQLite query, and that query is then interpolated into the shell command line used to invoke the sqlite3 binary through PHP `exec()`. A backtick expression in `object_id` therefore executes as an OS command on the building-automation server, with the vendor's `$`-stripping filter left intact and irrelevant.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; the script is served with no session, token or referer check, so the only requirement is the ability to send an HTTP request to the U.motion Builder web service.
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; a single request with a shell backtick in one parameter. The real constraint is network reachability of a building-automation front end, which on a flat facilities network is not a constraint at all.
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Julien Ahrens found it by reading the product's PHP source and quoting the query-construction and `exec()` lines; the finding is a bypass of the vendor's own earlier fix for CVE-2018-7765, which is the kind of result manual review of a patch produces.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Removing U.motion Builder from service, which is what both Schneider Electric's SEVD-2019-071-02 and the CISA KEV required action instruct — and, before removal completes, taking the web service off every routable path rather than relying on any product-side control.
prevention.adequacy: Removal is complete and permanent, and it is the only complete answer because no fixed build exists. Its limit is operational rather than technical: the software configures live building systems, so removal needs a replacement plan, and that is exactly the reason these units stay online past their retirement notice.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Egress monitoring on the facilities segment plus an alert on any request to `/smartdomuspad/modules/reporting/track_import_export.php` — the exploit's out-of-band callback is what the public detection template relies on, so it is also what a defender can see.
detection.adequacy: Workable only where the building-automation network is monitored at all, which is the common gap. On an unmonitored facilities VLAN there is no telemetry to write a rule against, and the host itself keeps no logs an investigator would find useful.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating a reachable U.motion Builder instance as compromised rather than as an exposure: pull it from the network, image it before wiping, and rotate any credential the automation network shares with corporate systems.
response.adequacy: Correct and rarely done, because a building-automation appliance is not in the asset inventory the incident-response process draws from. The primitive is command execution as the web-server user, so the unit is a Linux foothold inside the facility, not merely a leaked configuration file.

NIST-800-82r3.gap: The OT guide's vulnerability-management chapter is built around vendor patches arriving on a slower but real cadence. For U.motion Builder there is no cadence: Schneider Electric retired the product on 2019-03-12 rather than fixing CVE-2018-7841, so every recommendation collapses onto compensating controls. The guide also consistently treats building-automation as a lower-consequence subclass of OT, which is how a system with an unauthenticated shell sink stays outside the ICS patch and monitoring programme.

NIS2-Art21-vulnerability-handling.gap: Handling this vulnerability under Article 21 means recording SEVD-2019-071-02 and noting that no fix is available — which is true and complete as an administrative act. The software keeps running afterwards, because nothing in the article turns a permanent no-fix condition into a removal obligation with a date. The gap is precisely the difference between the KEV required action ('should be disconnected if still in use') and what compliant vulnerability handling actually produces.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: B4 will flag unsupported software and accept a documented risk decision, and for a system that controls lighting and HVAC that decision gets written once and rolled forward. The risk statement is usually framed around loss of building function, not around the fact that a single unauthenticated request yields command execution on a Linux host inside the facilities network — which makes the unit a pivot into whatever else that network reaches. B4 provides no mechanism forcing the acceptance to expire.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: This control cannot be met at any maturity level for U.motion Builder, because its foundation is running vendor-supported software and Schneider Electric withdrew support on 2019-03-12. The honest outcome is a standing exception, and the Essential Eight offers no intermediate state that converts that exception into the dated decommissioning the CISA KEV entry requires. Recording the exception is the whole of what the model asks for.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: An organisation can produce complete A.8.8 evidence for this CVE — advisory logged, severity assessed, treatment recorded as 'no patch available, compensating controls applied' — and still be running the vulnerable software years later. The control asks whether a treatment was decided, never whether it has a completion date, which is the single question that separates a managed retirement from an indefinite risk acceptance on a product with public one-request exploit code.

IEC-62443-3-3.gap: SR 1.1 and SR 1.2 require identification and authentication for human users and software processes, and `track_import_export.php` authenticates nothing at all — so the requirement is failed at the component itself rather than met imperfectly. Assessments of the surrounding zone, covering engineer accounts and workstation role separation, pass cleanly while the actual entry point never consults an identity. The zone-and-conduit segmentation that would bound this is the part most often deferred on a building-automation retrofit.

new_control_requirements.name: MITIGATION-ACTIVE-PATCH-PENDING-VERDICT-CLASS
new_control_requirements.description: Compliance verdicts must distinguish three states: (a) binary patch deployed (vulnerability eliminated), (b) vendor-mitigation rule active, no binary patch (residual risk: any defect in the mitigation rule reopens the vulnerability), (c) no mitigation, no patch (full exposure). Audit reports must surface (b) as a distinct compensating-control state with an associated time-bound action item, not as a 'patched per SLA' outcome.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Schneider Electric U.motion Builder is permanently in state (b) or (c) and can never reach state (a): the vendor retired the product on 2019-03-12 and issued SEVD-2019-071-02 instead of a fixed build, and the CISA KEV entry added 2022-04-15 tells operators to disconnect rather than patch. With EPSS at 0.72675 (99.397th percentile) and a one-request public exploit at Exploit-DB 46846, an audit line reading 'no patch available — accepted' is materially different from 'patched', and only a verdict class that separates the two produces the time-bound removal action this product needs.

new_control_requirements.name: INCOMPLETE-PATCH-SEQUENCE-SEVERITY-MULTIPLIER
new_control_requirements.description: Vulnerability-management programs must apply a severity multiplier when a CVE is the Nth in an incomplete-patch sequence on the same primitive (third MOTW bypass, second AMSI bypass, etc.). Framework controls treating each CVE as discrete obscure the structural defect; the Nth CVE in a sequence implies that future bypasses on the same primitive are likely.
new_control_requirements.evidence: The researcher advisory states plainly that CVE-2018-7841 is a bypass of the fix implemented for CVE-2018-7765 in the same U.motion Builder input path: the vendor's filter removed `$` to stop command substitution and left backticks working. A site that had applied the CVE-2018-7765 remediation and closed the ticket was fully exploitable the whole time. Applying a multiplier on the second defect in one sanitiser would have escalated U.motion Builder to the decommissioning track before the product was retired out from under its operators in March 2019.

attack_vector.description: A local process spins up two threads sharing one window class and window procedure, then has each move the other's window from inside a WM_NCCALCSIZE callback. Killing the opposite thread at maximum recursion makes win32k copy in the attacker's lParam structure after validation, so user-supplied pointers are consumed with kernel privilege and code runs as LOCAL SYSTEM.
attack_vector.privileges_required: low — PR:L; the attacker must already be logged on and executing code as a normal user. Every operation the exploit performs is one an unprivileged desktop application is entitled to perform, so no additional grant is needed once code runs.
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; the race is between two threads the attacker owns, so the window is constructed rather than awaited and failures cost only a retry. The genuine constraint is target coverage: the observed exploit worked on 32-bit Windows 7 only.
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Kaspersky's Automatic Exploit Prevention flagged the sample in October 2018 and Igor Soumenkov and Boris Larin reversed it by hand. Behavioural exploit heuristics in an endpoint product are not AI-assisted vulnerability discovery, and no such claim is made.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Installing the 2018-11-13 update and rebooting — KB4467107 / KB4467106 for Windows 7 and Server 2008 R2, KB4467700 / KB4467706 for Server 2008 — and, for the estate as a whole, retiring these SKUs rather than carrying them past 2020-01-14.
prevention.adequacy: The update fixes this race completely, and it arrived after the attacks Kaspersky observed — prevention was unavailable to the victims. Today its limit is different: the fix lands on an operating system that has received nothing since the ESU programme closed in January 2023.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Behavioural exploit-prevention on the endpoint, which is literally how this was found, backed by process-lineage alerting on a SYSTEM-context child appearing under a user-session parent with no service or task explaining it.
detection.adequacy: The escalation itself produces almost no artefact — no compilation, no driver load, no file change — so detection keys on the outcome rather than the technique. That means the alert fires after the attacker holds SYSTEM, which bounds the incident rather than preventing it.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating a host that executed an untrusted installer while unpatched as SYSTEM-compromised: rebuild rather than clean, audit local accounts and services created in the window, and rotate every credential cached on the machine.
response.adequacy: Appropriate but expensive, and it is skipped when the escalation is read as a secondary finding to the malware that carried it. The exploit's documented purpose was obtaining the privileges the installer needed for persistence, so the persistence is the thing that survives the patch.

NIST-800-53-AC-6.gap: An estate with no standing local administrators, tiered admin accounts and just-in-time elevation evidences AC-6 fully, and this exploit is unaffected by all of it. Registering a window class and sending WM_NCCALCSIZE messages are ordinary user rights, and the privilege transition happens inside win32k.sys beneath the account model. The control's own success criteria are met at the moment the flaw hands out LOCAL SYSTEM.

NIS2-Art21-vulnerability-management.gap: Article 21 vulnerability management is satisfiable here in the narrow sense — the November 2018 update was available and can be evidenced as applied. What it does not reach is that Windows 7 SP1, Server 2008 and Server 2008 R2 left extended support on 2020-01-14 and lost ESU on 2023-01-10, so the same asset has been accumulating unfixed kernel defects for years while its record for this CVE reads clean.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: B4 evidence for these hosts is a hardening baseline, a patch report and administrative-account hygiene, none of which touches a message-locking race in the graphical subsystem. There is also no least-functionality lever to pull: win32k.sys is not an optional component and is present on Server Core installations of Server 2008 and 2008 R2. The finding B4 should be producing is the migration off unsupported SKUs, which is the one most readily deferred.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: The Essential Eight one-month OS patching window is irrelevant to this event, because Kaspersky observed exploitation in October 2018 and Microsoft did not ship until 2018-11-13 — the victims had no patch to apply inside any window. Going forward the model's vendor-supported-OS baseline cannot be met on Windows 7 or Server 2008 at all, and the maturity model reports that as a patching shortfall rather than as the replacement programme it is.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: The organisation's A.8.8 intake would have shown CVE-2018-8589 on 2018-11-13 as one of sixty-odd entries in that month's Microsoft release. The information that mattered — that a working exploit had been running against 32-bit Windows 7 in the Middle East for weeks — appeared in Kaspersky's Securelist analysis, a research blog no A.8.8 implementation is required to consume. Timely intake and useful intake are not the same thing here.

NIST-800-53-SI-4.gap: SI-4 evidence is typically log collection plus an endpoint agent, and this exploit generates almost nothing for either. No module is loaded, no binary is dropped by the escalation itself, and the two-thread window manipulation is indistinguishable from ordinary GUI activity in event logs. Kaspersky caught it with in-memory behavioural exploit prevention, which is a capability SI-4 permits but does not require, so a fully compliant SI-4 posture can be blind to it.

new_control_requirements.name: PRIMARY-SOURCE-INTAKE-VENDOR-BLOG-COVERAGE
new_control_requirements.description: Threat-intake pipelines must cover vendor security blogs (Microsoft / Sysdig / Trail of Bits / Project Zero) in addition to advisory feeds (Qualys / RHSA / USN / ZDI / kernel.org / oss-security / JFrog / CISA). Silent kernel patches with delayed-disclosure research publications fall through advisory-only feeds — vendor blogs are the canonical signal channel for that class.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Microsoft's 2018-11-13 advisory for CVE-2018-8589 says only that Windows improperly handles calls to Win32k.sys and marks publiclyDisclosed as 'No'. Everything an operator needed to prioritise it — that the race is in win32k!xxxMoveWindow, that a working exploit had been in use since at least October 2018, that targeting was limited to 32-bit Windows 7 in the Middle East — was published on Kaspersky's Securelist, a research blog outside every advisory feed. An estate running Windows 7 SP1 and Server 2008 R2 would have re-ranked this CVE above the rest of that month's release on the strength of the blog alone.

new_control_requirements.name: NATION-STATE-INITIAL-ACCESS-IR-ESCALATION
new_control_requirements.description: IR runbooks must include an explicit nation-state-initial-access escalation path triggered by APT28/APT29/Lazarus/Volt-Typhoon/etc. attribution on a confirmed exploit chain. Standard malware-infection IR under-escalates nation-state activity by treating it as commodity threat.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Kaspersky describes CVE-2018-8589 being used by the first stage of a malware installer in a very limited set of attacks with victims in the Middle East — the shape of targeted espionage rather than commodity crimeware, even though no group was named. An endpoint that reports a generic exploit verdict on a 32-bit Windows 7 host and is then reimaged as a routine malware cleanup destroys the evidence that would establish targeting. The escalation path is what converts a single detection into a scoped investigation of the accounts and data the SYSTEM-level foothold reached.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Microsoft shipped KB4467107 / KB4467106 and KB4467700 / KB4467706 on 2018-11-13 and CISA listed CVE-2018-8589 in KEV on 2022-05-23 with a 2022-06-13 due date — a three-and-a-half year interval during which unpatched Windows 7 and Server 2008 R2 hosts stayed exploitable to a technique Kaspersky had already published. Because win32k.sys is boot-loaded there is no live-patch path, so the SLA has to be measured to completed reboot rather than to update approval; a host that downloaded the KB and never restarted is still running the vulnerable driver.

CVE-2019-0676.name: Microsoft Internet Explorer Information Disclosure Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: A visitor loads an attacker-controlled page in Internet Explorer. Faulty handling of objects in memory lets the page's script establish whether a nominated path exists on the local disk, giving the attacker a repeatable yes/no oracle over the victim's filesystem — enough to fingerprint installed security tooling, sandbox artefacts and applications before deciding whether to deliver a code-execution stage.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N with UI:R; the attacker needs no account and no foothold, only the victim's visit. In practice that visit came from a watering hole, malvertising or a mailed link, or from an intranet application that forced Internet Explorer.
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; the disclosure needs no memory-layout knowledge, no grooming and no chained bug. Its real constraint is scope rather than difficulty: C:H/I:N/A:N means it discloses and does nothing else, so it is only valuable as the reconnaissance leg of a longer chain.
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Clément Lecigne of Google's Threat Analysis Group found it by detecting live exploitation and reversing the delivered exploit — a human-telemetry-driven find. No AI-assisted discovery is claimed by Google, and Microsoft's advisory records no automated attribution.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Applying the 2019-02-12 IE cumulative or rollup for the host's Windows version, rebooting, and relaunching every browser process — with the durable answer being removal of standalone Internet Explorer and moving legacy applications to a controlled Edge IE-mode site list.
prevention.adequacy: The update closes this specific oracle. It leaves the legacy engine present and reachable, which is why the mitigation that actually reduced this class of exposure was retiring the browser in 2022, not any single February 2019 patch.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Browser-process telemetry that surfaces iexplore.exe reaching external destinations and spawning children, paired with an inventory alert on any host where the IE desktop application is still launchable after the 2022-06-15 retirement.
detection.adequacy: Weak against the disclosure itself, which produces no file write, no process creation and no obviously malicious content — the page just runs script. The detectable moment is the stage after it, so telemetry here bounds the incident rather than catching the reconnaissance.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating a confirmed visit as targeting rather than as an exposure: preserve the browser history and cache, hunt the same user for the follow-on stage, and check whether the disclosed information (security products installed, sandbox absent) would have made this host attractive.
response.adequacy: Proportionate only for the population Google TAG's reporting implies — the primitive discloses and does not compromise, so a blanket rebuild is unwarranted, but closing the case on 'information disclosure only' misses that the oracle exists to select the next target.

NIST-800-53-CM-7.gap: CM-7 baselines enumerate services and features to disable, and Internet Explorer does not appear in them because it is the OS-integrated rendering engine rather than an installed application — which is why Microsoft's affected list for this browser CVE spans Windows Server 2008 R2 through Server 2019. Least functionality would genuinely have removed the surface, and the control as implemented never had it in scope.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: The 2019-02-12 rollups reach affected hosts on the normal Windows cadence and the entity can evidence that cleanly. Two things escape the measurement: the fixed MSHTML is only in a browser process after that process relaunches, so long-lived IE sessions stay vulnerable on a fully patched machine, and the article has no view on the browser having been retired outright on 2022-06-15, which is the exposure that outlives this CVE.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: A CAF B4 review of a Windows estate treats Internet Explorer as part of the operating system, so IE inherits the OS's support status on the asset register and never raises an unsupported-software finding of its own. After 2022-06-15 that inheritance is wrong: the browser is retired while the OS underneath it is fully supported, and B4's evidence model has no natural place to record the difference.

AU-Essential-8-App-Hardening.gap: This is the control that matches the flaw — the Essential Eight's user application hardening explicitly calls for Internet Explorer 11 to be disabled or removed — and it is routinely the least-implemented of the eight, because the intranet applications that require the legacy engine are the ones nobody will break. An organisation patching on cadence while leaving IE launchable has bought protection against this one oracle and none against the next MSHTML defect.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: The 48-hour target for exploited flaws technically applied from release day, since Microsoft's record shows 'Exploitation Detected' on 2019-02-12. But that status was derived from Google TAG telemetry and never published as a public exploit or an advisory banner, so an organisation triaging the month's rollup had nothing distinguishing this CVE from the other information-disclosure entries and applied it on the two-week application track.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.7.gap: Web filtering, reputation blocking and awareness training are the usual A.8.7 evidence, and none of them engage a page whose only behaviour is asking whether a file exists. There is no payload to scan, no download to block, and a watering hole on a compromised legitimate site carries a clean reputation by definition. The control can be fully implemented while the oracle runs on every visit to the attacker's page.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: Consuming Microsoft's monthly release satisfies A.8.8's intake requirement, and CVE-2019-0676 appeared there on 2019-02-12 rated Important. The fact that would have moved it up the queue — that Google's Threat Analysis Group had caught it in use against live targets — was never in any feed the control requires, and the control has no obligation to seek exploitation status from a source other than the vendor.

new_control_requirements.name: BROWSER-MANAGED-UPDATE-NO-DEFERRAL
new_control_requirements.description: Enterprise update rings must not defer security-channel browser updates beyond 24h.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Microsoft's record for CVE-2019-0676 shows 'Exploitation Detected' on the release date of 2019-02-12, meaning the Internet Explorer engine on every Windows 7 SP1 through Server 2019 host was under live attack the day the fix shipped. Because IE is serviced through the Windows cumulative and monthly rollups rather than its own channel, the browser inherits whatever deferral an organisation applies to Windows updates — commonly one to four weeks — and there is no separate 24-hour browser lane to place it in. Applying this control to the IE and Edge servicing streams is what converts a browser zero-day from a monthly-rollup item into a same-day one.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CISA listed CVE-2019-0676 on 2022-05-23 with a 2022-06-13 due date, three years after Microsoft's 2019-02-12 fix and a fortnight before the Internet Explorer 11 desktop application was retired on 2022-06-15. For this CVE the documented-compensating-controls branch of the SLA is the one that matters: disabling or removing Internet Explorer is deployable by policy in minutes and removes the surface permanently, whereas the cumulative update leaves the legacy engine present and reachable for the next MSHTML defect. Verification has to reach the browser process, not just the update record, because the fixed engine is only loaded after iexplore.exe relaunches.

CVE-2019-0703.name: Microsoft Windows SMB Information Disclosure Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: An attacker holding any credential that can open an SMB session sends a crafted request to the Windows SMB Server, which returns memory contents the request should not have exposed. In the tooling Symantec recovered, that leak supplied the state needed to drive a separate SMBv1 memory-corruption bug to reliable remote kernel code execution on 64-bit and newer Windows.
attack_vector.privileges_required: low — PR:L; Microsoft's advisory states the attacker must be able to authenticate and send SMB messages to the server. On a domain-joined estate that is any ordinary user, service or machine account, so the bar is a foothold rather than administrative rights.
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; once a credential exists the request is straightforward over port 445, with no race, no grooming and no second information leak needed. The genuine constraint is reachability plus a credential, both of which an actor already inside the network has.
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Symantec's analysts found it by reverse-engineering the attacker's own exploit binary and reported it to Microsoft in September 2018. That is human malware analysis; no automated discovery pipeline is claimed or implied.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Applying the 2019-03-12 SMB Server updates and rebooting, plus removing the SMBv1 feature entirely so the corruption half of the documented chain has no target even when a disclosure primitive exists.
prevention.adequacy: The update closes this leak, and removing SMBv1 closes the chain. Neither addresses the underlying reachability: any future SMB Server defect is exploitable from the same position, because the estate permits authenticated 445 sessions between essentially everything.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Baselining which principals legitimately open SMB sessions to which servers and alerting on new pairings, together with hunting for DoublePulsar's SMB handshake — the backdoor Bemstour existed to deliver.
detection.adequacy: The disclosure itself looks like normal authenticated file-service traffic and will not stand out. The detectable artefact is the implant that follows, so this bounds how long a compromise runs rather than stopping the leak that enabled it.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating any host where this chain succeeded as kernel-compromised — rebuild rather than clean, since the endpoint of the chain is DoublePulsar — and rotating every credential that opened an SMB session to the affected servers during the exposure window.
response.adequacy: Correct but slow to trigger, because nothing in the disclosure declares an incident. Symantec's finding that a Bemstour sample was compiled eleven days after the 2019-03-12 patch also means patch date is a poor lower bound for the exposure window.

NIST-800-53-SC-7.gap: SC-7 evidence for a Windows estate is a perimeter that blocks 445 inbound, and that is genuinely in place almost everywhere — and irrelevant. The Bemstour operator worked from inside, against servers it could already authenticate to. The internal-segmentation portion of SC-7 is where this would have been addressed, and it is the portion implemented as guidance rather than as an enforced control in most environments.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: Flaw remediation drove the 2019-03-12 update out on the normal Windows cadence, typically two to four weeks for file servers because of the reboot. Symantec recovered a Bemstour sample compiled eleven days after that patch, which shows the actor betting on exactly that lag. SI-2 sets its window from patch availability and has no input from the fact that a named group is rebuilding tooling against this specific CVE.

NIS2-Art21-network-security.gap: An entity can evidence Article 21 network security through segmentation between business functions and still permit SMB broadly within each segment, because Group Policy, printing, file services and administrative tooling all depend on it. That is precisely the reachability this flaw requires — an authenticated session on 445, not a boundary crossing — so the control's evidence and the attack path do not intersect.

UK-CAF-B2.gap: Because exploitation needs authentication, B2 identity and access control is the control an assessor would nominate as the mitigation, and it is not one. Any ordinary user, service or machine account suffices, and Buckeye ran this tooling from positions it had already established inside victim networks. Multi-factor authentication and credential hygiene raise the cost of the first foothold and do nothing about what an ordinary session then extracts from server memory.

UK-CAF-D1.gap: D1 response planning is exercised against incidents that declare themselves. This leak produces a successful logon and a normal file-service exchange — no alert, no failure, no trigger — so the plan is never invoked, while the chain it enables ends in a DoublePulsar implant. The response that would matter, rebuilding rather than cleaning a kernel-compromised host, sits behind a detection that the disclosure step does not generate.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: A one-month OS patching window would have placed the 2019-03-12 update in April 2019 — better than many estates achieved, and still weeks of exposure to an operator actively compiling against this CVE. The model also cannot be satisfied at all on several of the affected SKUs: Windows 7 SP1, Server 2008 SP2 and Server 2008 R2 SP1 have failed its supported-OS baseline since 2020-01-14.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.21.gap: A.8.21 asks for the security mechanisms, service levels and management requirements of network services to be identified and specified. SMB inside a Windows domain is almost never written down as a network service in that sense — there is no service definition, no stated exposure boundary and no rule saying which principals may open sessions to which hosts. The control's evidence tends to be about supplier connectivity, so the internal protocol carrying this flaw is outside its scope in practice.

new_control_requirements.name: NATION-STATE-INITIAL-ACCESS-IR-ESCALATION
new_control_requirements.description: IR runbooks must include an explicit nation-state-initial-access escalation path triggered by APT28/APT29/Lazarus/Volt-Typhoon/etc. attribution on a confirmed exploit chain. Standard malware-infection IR under-escalates nation-state activity by treating it as commodity threat.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2019-0703 was found by Symantec inside Trojan.Bemstour, the bespoke exploit tool the group it tracks as Buckeye (APT3 / Gothic Panda) used to install DoublePulsar, chained with CVE-2017-0143 to reach remote kernel code execution. A DoublePulsar detection handled as commodity malware ends in a reimage; handled as a nation-state initial-access chain it triggers an investigation of which SMB servers were reachable, which credentials opened sessions to them, and how far back the exposure runs — Symantec's recovery of a sample compiled eleven days after the 2019-03-12 patch shows that window extends past the patch date.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Microsoft shipped the SMB Server fix on 2019-03-12 (advisory revised 2019-05-07) and CISA listed CVE-2019-0703 in KEV on 2022-05-23 with a 2022-06-13 due date; EPSS sits at 0.0964, the 95.066th percentile. Because srv2.sys and lanmanserver load at boot there is no live-patch route, so the SLA has to be measured to completed reboot on file servers rather than to update approval — which is exactly where a four-hour clock forces the maintenance decision that a quarterly window defers. The compensating-control branch has a concrete form here: narrowing which principals and segments may open port 445 sessions to a given server bounds exposure while the reboot is scheduled.

attack_vector.description: Code already running at low integrity — typically inside a browser sandbox — spawns splwow64.exe, connects to the LPC port it opens, and maps a shared section. A crafted value at one offset steers GdiPrinterThunk into a memcpy whose destination, source and length all come from attacker-controlled shared memory, giving an arbitrary write inside a medium-integrity process and with it control of that process.
attack_vector.privileges_required: low — PR:L; the attacker must already be executing on the host, which is the point of the bug rather than a limitation. Its intended position is inside a sandboxed renderer that Internet Explorer's elevation policy allows to launch splwow64.
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; both ends of the LPC exchange belong to the attacker, the offsets are fixed and documented, and a failed attempt costs nothing. The gain is bounded rather than difficult: low to medium integrity, so a chain needs a further step to reach SYSTEM.
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Resecurity reported it to Microsoft, and the public analysis a year later came from a researcher reversing splwow64's message dispatch by hand. Neither is an automated or AI-assisted find, and neither party claims otherwise.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Applying the 2019-07-09 update and rebooting, and — where printing is not required — disabling the print spooler so splwow64.exe cannot be spawned and the LPC surface does not exist.
prevention.adequacy: The update fixes the handler; the spooler decision removes the surface. The second is stronger and available on servers and kiosks, and unavailable on exactly the workstations where a sandbox escape has value, because users there print.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Process-lineage alerting on splwow64.exe launched by a sandboxed renderer, and on any medium-integrity process whose parent is low-integrity with no broker in between — the integrity transition is the observable, not the memcpy.
detection.adequacy: Specific and cheap, but late by construction: it fires once the write has landed, so it scopes the incident rather than preventing the escape. It also depends on integrity-level telemetry that many endpoint configurations do not collect.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating a host that showed the transition as compromised beyond the browser: the escape is a chain step, so the question is what the chain installed after reaching medium integrity, not whether splwow64 has since been patched.
response.adequacy: Right in principle, hard to trigger in practice, because the escape produces no artefact of its own. Microsoft's record of exploitation detected on older releases at the 2019-07-09 release date means the exposure window opens before the patch, not at it.

NIST-800-53-CM-7.gap: Least functionality would close this outright — no spooler, no splwow64, no LPC port — and it is the control least likely to be applied, because the spooler is enabled by default across all 31 affected product rows and turning it off on a workstation removes a function users depend on daily. Server baselines usually leave it running against a possible future print role, so hosts that never print keep the surface with a compliant CM-7 record.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: Applying the July 2019 rollup satisfies the article and can be evidenced without dispute. It does not encode priority, and priority was the whole issue: Microsoft's own exploitability index marked older releases 'Exploitation Detected' on the 2019-07-09 release date, and a second separately exploited escalation, CVE-2019-1132, shipped in the same batch. Uniform rollup application treats both as ordinary.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: B4 evidence for a workstation fleet — hardening baseline, patch currency, admin-rights hygiene — has no line that constrains an LPC exchange between a sandboxed renderer and the print thunking host. The configuration change that would help, removing the spooler where unused, is treated as a business-functionality decision rather than a security baseline item, so both assessor and operator sign off on a configuration that leaves the surface intact.

AU-Essential-8-App-Hardening.gap: Application hardening is aimed at the delivery stage — blocking Flash, Java, ads and untrusted web content so the initial memory-corruption bug never runs. This CVE is the stage after that: the attacker is already inside the low-integrity renderer, and the LPC write to splwow64 is how they leave it. An estate at high maturity for browser hardening with the spooler enabled has secured the entrance and left the exit unlocked.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: The one-month internal OS patching window places this update in August 2019, while Microsoft recorded exploitation on older releases as already detected on 2019-07-09. The maturity model has no mechanism for lifting one CVE out of a monthly rollup onto a shorter clock, so an actively exploited sandbox escape travels at the same speed as the routine content of the same release.

NIST-800-53-SI-4.gap: There is almost nothing for SI-4 to collect. The escape is a memcpy executed inside a signed Microsoft binary, driven over an LPC channel that carries ordinary print thunking traffic constantly, with no file write, service creation or module load attributable to the exploit. Whatever monitoring exists begins to see something only after the integrity boundary has been crossed and the attacker acts through the medium-integrity process.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: The July 2019 Microsoft release enters an A.8.8 intake as a batch, and CVE-2019-0880's CVSS of 7.8 with an Important rating sorts it into the middle of the queue. The fields that should have moved it — the exploitability index reading 'Exploitation Detected' for older releases, and a sibling exploited escalation in the same batch — are in the vendor record but not in the score most intake pipelines rank on.

new_control_requirements.name: MITIGATION-ACTIVE-PATCH-PENDING-VERDICT-CLASS
new_control_requirements.description: Compliance verdicts must distinguish three states: (a) binary patch deployed (vulnerability eliminated), (b) vendor-mitigation rule active, no binary patch (residual risk: any defect in the mitigation rule reopens the vulnerability), (c) no mitigation, no patch (full exposure). Audit reports must surface (b) as a distinct compensating-control state with an associated time-bound action item, not as a 'patched per SLA' outcome.
new_control_requirements.evidence: For CVE-2019-0880 the compensating control is disabling the print spooler, which prevents splwow64.exe from being spawned at all — a genuinely different security state from having the 2019-07-09 update installed, and one that reverses the moment a print role is added to the host. Microsoft marked older releases 'Exploitation Detected' at release, so the interim state mattered. An audit line that records 'mitigated' without distinguishing spooler-disabled from update-applied loses the fact that the mitigation is a service-configuration setting any administrator can undo without touching the vulnerability record.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Microsoft shipped the splwow64 fix on 2019-07-09 marking older releases 'Exploitation Detected', and CISA listed CVE-2019-0880 in KEV on 2022-05-23 with a 2022-06-13 due date; EPSS remains low at 0.02404 precisely because no exploit code was ever published, which is the case where a CVSS- or EPSS-driven queue under-ranks a confirmed in-the-wild sandbox escape. splwow64 is spawned from the spooler infrastructure and there is no live-patch route, so the clock has to run to completed reboot — and the documented-compensating-control branch has an immediate form here in disabling the spooler on hosts that do not print.

CVE-2019-1003029.name: Jenkins Script Security Plugin Sandbox Bypass Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: A user with Overall/Read posts a crafted Groovy script to the Script Security plugin's own form-validation endpoint. The sandbox intercepts operations at execution time, so a payload placed in a class initialiser, constructor, annotation or meta-programming construct runs during parsing, compilation or instantiation — before interception applies — and executes unsandboxed in the Jenkins controller's JVM, where the credentials store and agent secrets live.
attack_vector.privileges_required: low — PR:L; Overall/Read, the least permission Jenkins grants, and one commonly given to all authenticated users so build results are visible. Public tooling additionally chains a dynamic-routing ACL bypass against Jenkins core 2.137 and earlier that removes even that requirement.
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; a Groovy source file posted to an endpoint whose purpose is checking scripts. No memory corruption, no race, no second bug, and Script Security is present on any controller running pipelines because the Pipeline plugins depend on it.
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. The Jenkins advisory of 2019-03-06 credits Georgy Noseevich (@webpentest) of SolidLab, who later appears among the Metasploit module's authors. This is manual security research against a sandbox with a known history of bypasses.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Upgrading Script Security to 1.54 and Pipeline: Groovy to 2.64 together and restarting the controller, alongside removing blanket Overall/Read grants to all authenticated and anonymous users and moving Jenkins core past 2.137 so the ACL-bypass gadget no longer applies.
prevention.adequacy: The plugin upgrades close this specific bypass. They do not change the structural position — the Groovy sandbox has produced repeated bypasses, so a controller reachable by low-trust users remains a standing exposure to the next one.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alerting on requests to the SecureGroovyScript checkScript descriptor endpoint from accounts that hold only Overall/Read, and on the controller's Java process spawning shell children or fetching code from outside the update centre.
detection.adequacy: Both signals are specific and would fire on the published tooling. Neither is collected by default — Jenkins access logs are frequently not shipped anywhere, and the controller's process tree is rarely monitored as a security-relevant asset.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating an exploited controller as a credential breach rather than a software defect: rotate the credentials store, agent connection secrets and API tokens, and review published artefacts and deployments from the exposure window for tampering.
response.adequacy: Essential and disproportionately skipped, because a plugin version bump reads as closure. The payload ran in the JVM that holds every secret the CI estate uses, so anything it read stays valid until rotated and anything it published stays trusted until reviewed.

NIST-800-53-AC-6.gap: The Jenkins permission model is a least-privilege implementation, and this CVE bypasses it rather than abusing it: Overall/Read, the lowest grant the product offers, is enough to run code in the controller JVM. An AC-6 attestation listing three Administer holders and everyone else at Read describes a fully exploitable controller, because the boundary being measured — which account holds which permission — is not the boundary that fails.

NIS2-Art21-supply-chain.gap: Article 21 supply-chain measures look outward at suppliers and their products, and an entity can hold complete supplier assurance while the build controller that produces its own artefacts lets any authenticated reader execute code with the credentials that push to production. The inward-facing half — that the CI system is itself a supply-chain component for everyone downstream of it — is not what the assurance documentation covers.

UK-CAF-B2.gap: B2 evidence is authenticated accounts under a role-based authorization strategy, and the widespread practice of granting Overall/Read to all authenticated users so build results are visible is exactly the precondition this CVE needs. On Jenkins core 2.137 or earlier the public tooling chains a dynamic-routing ACL bypass that removes the authentication step entirely, so the access control B2 attests to is not consulted at all.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Script Security 1.54 was available on 2019-03-06 and applying it is a two-minute action, so the Essential Eight two-week application window looks comfortably achievable. What defeats it is the controller restart required to load the new plugin, which evicts running builds and gets scheduled rather than taken. The model measures update availability and installation, not whether the process carrying the fixed code has actually restarted.
