The two that survive are iTunes 12.9.4 and iCloud for Windows 7.11, which reach hosts through Apple Software Update on Windows rather than the Apple device-management channel and are frequently user-installed outside managed distribution, so they are neither measured nor pushed by the process that recorded the CVE as remediated.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: The patch plan covers registered systems, and the populations that carried this engine longest are not on the register: an Apple TV commissioned as meeting-room AV, a personally-owned Watch, and an iTunes install left on a finance workstation. All three ran the same JavaScriptCore until 25 to 27 March 2019 with no owner accountable for their build.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: Configuration hardening is applied to Safari and has no expression for a JIT inferred-type violation. The scoping error B4 encourages is treating the browser as the unit of exposure: on iOS every in-app web view renders through the same engine, so a policy that restricts or removes Safari leaves the vulnerable component running in every application that shows web content.

AU-Essential-8-App-Hardening.gap: Hardening measures aimed at Flash, Java, OLE and unwanted plugins are all irrelevant to plain JavaScript reaching the regular-expression path. The single item that reduces exposure is blocking advertisements and untrusted third-party script, which shortens the delivery path for a drive-by, and it is routinely waived for business reasons on the same estates that claim full maturity.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: The application-patching control names browsers and would carry Safari 12.1, while iTunes and iCloud for Windows are not browsers and tvOS and watchOS are not the workstation operating systems the OS control is usually scoped to. Full maturity is therefore compatible with three of the six affected products in the estate still running the pre-fix engine.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: Evaluation requires six version facts plus the Red Hat webkitgtk package state, and a register organized by device cannot express that they are one defect in one shipped component. The predictable outcome is that the item is closed when the iOS fleet crosses 12.2 and the Windows and Linux instances of the same engine are never compared to anything.

new_control_requirements.name: MOBILE-ENDPOINT-MDM-ENFORCED-KEV-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: iOS / iPadOS / macOS estates must enforce KEV-class updates within 24h via DDM; user-deferral disallowed.
new_control_requirements.evidence: For the Apple mobile and desktop populations this CVE resolves to iOS 12.2 (25 March 2019) and Safari 12.1, both reboot- or relaunch-gated, and the KEV clock opened 2022-05-04 with a 2022-05-25 due date. Enforcement rather than notification is what matters here because the exposure is drive-by: a deferred device keeps rendering untrusted web content through the vulnerable JavaScriptCore every time any application on it opens a web view, not only when the user chooses to browse.

new_control_requirements.name: BROWSER-MANAGED-UPDATE-NO-DEFERRAL
new_control_requirements.description: Enterprise update rings must not defer security-channel browser updates beyond 24h.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Safari 12.1 carried this fix on the macOS side, and the control has to be read as covering the engine rather than the branded browser: the same JavaScriptCore ships in iTunes 12.9.4 for Windows and iCloud for Windows 7.11, which arrive through Apple Software Update on Windows and sit outside most enterprise browser rings entirely. A ring that ships Safari inside 24 hours and never enumerates the Windows components leaves the identical defect deployed on the workstations.

attack_vector.description: Crafted web content processed by WebKitGTK or WPE WebKit corrupts memory in the rendering process and leads to arbitrary code execution; the upstream advisory publishes no further detail, and on a Linux desktop the content need not arrive through a browser at all.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; the attacker needs no account and no foothold, only that some application on the host render content they supply, which an HTML mail preview satisfies as readily as a browser visit.
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L with UI:R. The real difficulty is not triggering the bug but scoping it: with no public root-cause detail, an operator cannot determine which of the applications linking the engine are reachable, and must treat all of them as in scope.
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. WSA-2019-0005 credits Wen Xu of SSLab at Georgia Tech, an academic lab reporting through the coordinated channel; the lab's name carries no AI branding and no automated discovery method is claimed in the advisory.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: WebKitGTK and WPE WebKit at 2.26.0 or later — via RHSA-2020:4035 or RHSA-2020:4451 on Red Hat Enterprise Linux — followed by restarting every process holding the old library, and disabling remote-content rendering in mail clients so the engine is not fed untrusted HTML by default.
prevention.adequacy: Available but hard to evidence: the package update is the easy half, and the process restarts are the half nobody tracks. For embedded WPE devices whose vendor stopped publishing images, prevention does not exist and replacement is the only remaining action.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alerting on WebKitWebProcess crashes and core dumps, and on outbound connections initiated by a rendering process belonging to a non-browser application.
detection.adequacy: Reasonable on a managed Linux desktop with crash reporting enabled, and absent on the population that matters most — embedded WPE devices ship no crash telemetry anywhere an operator can read it.

response.what_would_have_worked: Enumerating every application on the host that links the engine, restarting or replacing each, and treating the rendering process's own access — the user's mail store, home directory and session keyring — as the exposure to reason about.
response.adequacy: Sound in principle and blocked in practice by the absence of a component inventory: without one, the responder cannot list the applications that embed the engine, and closing on the package version misses every process still running the old code.

NIST-800-53-SR-3.gap: Supply-chain controls are implemented against suppliers the organization contracts with, and the engine arrives underneath all of them as a library inside a mail client, a help viewer and a package UI. There is no acquisition record, no agreement and no supplier contact to which the 2.26.0 requirement can be attached, so the control passes while the component it should govern is invisible to it.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: Flaw remediation was structurally unable to fire during the window it mattered. CISA listed the CVE on 2022-05-23 with a 2022-06-13 due date, and NVD did not publish a record until 2023-03-06 — so an inventory-to-NVD matching pipeline had nothing to match for nine and a half months, and the upstream WSA-2019-0005 advisory is a project feed most enterprise vulnerability programmes do not ingest.

NIS2-Art21-supply-chain.gap: Supplier due diligence runs against the distribution and the appliance vendors and never asks the question that matters: which web engine does this product embed, at which version. The shared component reaches the estate through several counterparties at once, each of whom can answer their own questionnaire truthfully while none of them reports the pre-2.26.0 engine inside their product.

UK-CAF-A1.gap: Governance assigns ownership by system, and this component belongs to no system. The desktop team owns the distribution, the messaging team owns Evolution, facilities owns the signage player, and the WebKitGTK version inside each is nobody's stated responsibility — which is why an advisory naming 2.26.0 has no recipient and no one accountable for confirming it landed.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: Update management is in place and measures the wrong state. Because the fix ships as a shared library, a host reports the patched package while every process that mapped the old one keeps executing it, so a desktop that has not been logged out since RHSA-2020:4451 landed is recorded as remediated and is not. Nothing in a B4 assessment asks for process-level evidence.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: The control drives updates to the operating system, the browser and the mail client, all of which exist here, and none of which is the unit of exposure. Whether those updates carry WebKitGTK 2.26.0 is a packaging decision the assessed organization does not measure, so maturity level three is fully compatible with an engine two major versions behind on every desktop.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: The register lists applications and their versions, and this CVE is only expressible at component granularity. Nothing in an inventory that records Evolution, GNOME Web and Yelp as three separate products can be compared against 2.26.0, so the control cannot determine which of its own listed entries are instances of the vulnerability.

CycloneDX-v1.6-SBOM.gap: The artefact that would resolve this is not produced on either side. The desktop applications embedding WebKitGTK ship no component-level bill of materials to the consuming organization, and the appliance and signage images embedding WPE ship none either — so the inventory that would enumerate every pre-2.26.0 instance across the estate simply does not exist, and the control is unmet rather than inadequate.

new_control_requirements.name: TIER-3-DEPENDENCY-INVENTORY
new_control_requirements.description: Supply chain inventory must extend to tier-3 dependencies (dependencies of dependencies of direct dependencies). SBOM coverage for libsystemd-class transitive dependencies cannot be omitted under SR-3.
new_control_requirements.evidence: WebKitGTK is exactly the transitive class this control names: nobody procures it, and it reaches a Linux desktop underneath Evolution, GNOME Web, Yelp and the software centre, and underneath third-party set-top and signage images through WPE. The fix is a single version — 2.26.0, delivered downstream as RHSA-2020:4035 and RHSA-2020:4451 — and an inventory that stops at the applications cannot tell an operator which of them are instances of it. That the NVD record did not exist until 2023-03-06, nine and a half months after the 2022-05-23 KEV listing, makes the inventory the only thing that could have driven remediation on the KEV clock.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: WebKitGTK entered KEV on 2022-05-23 with a 2022-06-13 due date, and the verification half of this SLA is the whole exercise here: the packaged engine must be at 2.26.0 or later, and every process holding the previous library must have been restarted, because no reboot is required and the host will otherwise report itself remediated while running the old code. Where the engine is WPE inside a vendor image with no newer build, the SLA's compensating-control branch has to name the network isolation applied and the date the device leaves service.

CVE-2020-0638.name: Microsoft Update Notification Manager Privilege Escalation Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: A user-level foothold plants a link where a SYSTEM-context Windows update-notification component expects a real file; the component follows the link and performs its file operation against the attacker's chosen target, converting an ordinary account into SYSTEM.
attack_vector.privileges_required: low — PR:L; the attacker must already run code as a normal user, which NVD states outright, so this is a second-stage tool rather than an entry point.
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; no race or memory-corruption groom is documented, and the real constraint is arranging for the privileged component's file operation to run while the planted link is in place.
attack_vector.ai_factor: Microsoft credits Zhiniang Peng (@edwardzpeng) of Qihoo 360 Core Security and Jiadong Lu, two outside researchers reporting to the vendor. The acknowledgement names the finders and not the method, and Microsoft published no mechanism detail, so nothing in the record supports an AI-assisted or automated-discovery claim.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Installing the 14 January 2020 cumulative update for the running build (KB4534276 / KB4534293 / KB4534273 / KB4528760) and rebooting, and thereafter keeping hosts on a Windows servicing branch that still receives updates.
prevention.adequacy: The patch removes the flaw outright, but it only helps a host whose branch can still take it: on Windows 10 1709-1909 the update is the last one that branch will ever get, so patching is a point fix on a platform that keeps accumulating unfixed flaws.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alerting on SYSTEM-context file writes that resolve through a reparse point into a user-writable location, and on junction creation by non-administrative accounts in directories privileged Windows components touch.
detection.adequacy: Link-following abuse looks like ordinary filesystem activity, and Windows does not audit reparse-point traversal by default, so this needs auditing deliberately enabled beforehand and produces noise on developer workstations that use junctions legitimately.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating a confirmed escalation on an affected build as a host compromise: rebuild rather than patch-in-place, rotate every credential cached on the machine, and check shadow copies and backup agents given the KEV ransomware flag.
response.adequacy: Response starts after SYSTEM has already been granted, so it bounds damage rather than preventing it, and on an end-of-support build the rebuild has to target a different Windows release or the same exposure returns.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: SI-2 is nominally met the moment KB4528760 or its successor is installed, and that is exactly why it fails here: on the 1709-1909 branches this CVE names, 'fully patched' and 'on a stream that ended' are the same reported state. Nothing in SI-2 forces a re-look when the risk picture changed on 2022-05-23, 28 months after the fix shipped, because the control keys on update availability rather than on exploitation intelligence.

NIST-800-53-AC-6.gap: An estate can hold clean AC-6 evidence — no standing local administrators, scoped roles, reviewed entitlements — and still be fully exposed, because the attacker uses only the privileges an ordinary user is supposed to have and the escalation happens inside a SYSTEM component's own file handling. Least privilege bounds what the initial foothold can reach; it does not touch the CWE-59 defect that carries the attacker past it.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: A risk-proportionate patch programme reading Microsoft's Important rating and a local-only 7.8 in the January 2020 release would legitimately have queued this behind the remotely reachable items, and Article 21 would have accepted that judgement. It provides no trigger to revisit the decision when CISA later recorded ransomware campaign use on 2022-05-23, so the control's proportionality test is evaluated once, against inputs that turned out to be wrong.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: B4 evidence — a hardened build standard plus an update-compliance report — reads green on a Windows 10 1909 host that installed KB4528760 and will never receive another Windows update. The outcome B4 is written for is a system that stays secure over time, and a servicing branch past end of support cannot deliver that no matter how complete the configuration baseline looks in the audit pack.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: The maturity model measures the interval from vendor release to deployment, which the 2020-01-14 update satisfied, and it has no expression for a CVE whose exploitation signal landed 28 months later in the KEV catalogue. The part of Essential Eight that actually bites — use only vendor-supported operating systems — is scored separately from patch timeliness, so an organisation can be rated well on this control while every host it names sits on a dead branch.

AU-Essential-8-Backup.gap: Tested restores answer the consequence the KEV ransomware flag warns about, not the path: SYSTEM obtained through this component is precisely the privilege level needed to delete shadow copies, stop backup agents and reach cached backup credentials on the same host before any encryption begins. A backup regime scored on restore success but not on isolation from a local SYSTEM attacker is measuring the wrong property for this CVE.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: The evidence A.8.8 usually rests on is a credentialed scan showing no missing updates, and that output cannot separate a supported host from one stranded on the 1709-1909 branches — both report clean. The control also asks for vulnerability information from appropriate sources, but the decisive source for this CVE was CISA's 2022-05-23 ransomware annotation, which does not appear anywhere in patch-level scan data.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Microsoft shipped the fix for the Update Notification Manager flaw on 2020-01-14 and CISA did not list it until 2022-05-23, with the ransomware flag set and a 2022-06-13 due date. An estate driven by patch-release cadence alone had 28 months in which this Important-rated local escalation sat in a backlog behind network-facing criticals; a KEV-triggered clock is the only mechanism that would have re-raised it, and by then many affected hosts were on 1709-1909 branches where the January 2020 KB is the last update available. EPSS on 2026-08-16 is 0.03042 at the 86.4th percentile — a rank that a CVSS-only queue never surfaces for a local-only bug.

new_control_requirements.name: MITIGATION-ACTIVE-PATCH-PENDING-VERDICT-CLASS
new_control_requirements.description: Compliance verdicts must distinguish three states: (a) binary patch deployed (vulnerability eliminated), (b) vendor-mitigation rule active, no binary patch (residual risk: any defect in the mitigation rule reopens the vulnerability), (c) no mitigation, no patch (full exposure). Audit reports must surface (b) as a distinct compensating-control state with an associated time-bound action item, not as a 'patched per SLA' outcome.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Every servicing branch this CVE names — Windows 10 1709 through 1909, Windows Server 2019 and the Server Core releases version 1803, 1903 and 1909 — reports state (a) once the 2020-01-14 cumulative update is installed, and on the branches that have since left support that report is indistinguishable from a host that is genuinely current. The verdict class that is missing is 'last available update installed, platform no longer receiving fixes', which for this CVE is the real posture of most remaining exposure and which needs the time-bound action item — a dated migration off the branch — that a 'patched per SLA' outcome never generates.

CVE-2020-1027.name: Microsoft Windows Kernel Privilege Escalation Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: Any local process, including a sandboxed browser renderer, sends CSRSS an ALPC message whose UNICODE_STRING carries an oversized MaximumLength; the side-by-side manifest parser trusts that field for a memcpy and overflows the heap with fully controlled content, which the in-the-wild exploit turned into a write-what-where against PEB_LDR_DATA and a CFG-bypassing ROP chain.
attack_vector.privileges_required: low — PR:L; the CSRSS side-by-side ALPC endpoint answers every process by default, which is precisely what made it usable from a stripped-down renderer sandbox.
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; the overflow itself is deterministic with no race, and the difficulty sits after the corruption, in shaping the XML node objects and defeating Control Flow Guard.
attack_vector.ai_factor: Google Project Zero and TAG recovered a live exploit sample and analysed it manually; Project Zero's own note is that the bug could have been found by a manual audit of CSRSS IPC handlers, and nothing in the record indicates AI-assisted discovery or exploit development.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Installing the 14 April 2020 cumulative update and rebooting, combined with keeping the browser on a no-deferral security-update channel so the renderer bug that opened the chain was already closed.
prevention.adequacy: The update removes the unchecked MaximumLength path, but the KEV listing that would have forced it to the front of the queue arrived two years after the patch, and on the Windows 7 / 8.1 / Server 2012 hosts in the same affected list the update is the last stop before an unsupported platform.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Watching for a sandboxed renderer talking to the CSRSS side-by-side interface at all, and treating csrss.exe crashes correlated with browsing as an exploitation signal rather than a stability event.
detection.adequacy: ALPC activity is not logged by Windows by default and endpoint tooling rarely instruments the side-by-side path, so this needs deliberate telemetry that most estates do not collect; a clean escape also produces no crash at all.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating a workstation that browsed to a compromised site during the exposure window as fully compromised — rebuild, rotate credentials cached on it, and review what the account reached afterwards, since the escape yields privileged execution outside the sandbox.
response.adequacy: Response is bounded by the fact that the chain leaves little on disk; without the browser-side and ALPC telemetry above, an investigator has no reliable way to decide which machines to scope in.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: The April 2020 rollup satisfies SI-2 on the day it lands, and an SI-2 programme that ranks by CVSS ranks this 7.8 local-privilege item below the network-facing criticals in the same release — the opposite of its real priority, since its only observed role was completing a drive-by chain. The failure is the ranking input, not the intelligence: Microsoft's own 2020-04-14 entry says 'Exploited:Yes' and 'Exploitation Detected', a field a severity-ordered queue never reads. Only the chain context stayed unpublished, until Project Zero's 2021-01-12 analysis named the pairing with Chrome's CVE-2020-6418.

NIST-800-53-CM-7.gap: CM-7 is the control that corresponds to the structural fix Project Zero recommended — cutting sandboxed processes off from CSRSS — and there is no operator-side way to implement it, because the side-by-side activation-context endpoint is a default ALPC interface the platform requires. An estate can produce complete least-functionality evidence covering services, ports and installed features and none of it narrows the surface this exploit used.

NIS2-Art21-vulnerability-handling.gap: An entity handling vulnerabilities from vendor advisories was told on 2020-04-14 that this one was being exploited — Microsoft's entry reads 'Exploited:Yes' with 'Exploitation Detected' — so the measure delivered the fact that should have moved it up the queue. What it could not deliver was that the bug was the sandbox-escape half of an in-the-wild chain with Chrome's CVE-2020-6418, which stayed inside Google's threat-intelligence output until 2021-01-12, leaving nine months in which an advisory-driven programme could not tell that patching Windows here also broke a browser attack path.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: B4 records that the host is configured to a baseline and kept updated, which is true of a machine carrying KB4549951. What it cannot express is that this host's entire browser-sandbox boundary rests on one non-restartable system process being current, or that the Windows 7 and 8.1 machines sitting in the same B4 scope reached their last possible fix for this flaw and now carry the accumulated remainder.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Patch-operating-systems and patch-applications are scored as separate mitigations, and the observed chain deliberately spanned both — a Chrome renderer bug feeding this CSRSS overflow. An organisation strong on one and weak on the other is the exact configuration the chain monetised, and the maturity model has no combined question that would surface it.

AU-Essential-8-App-Hardening.gap: Application-hardening settings act on what content the browser will process, and by the time this CVE is in play the attacker is already executing inside the renderer with the sandbox as the only remaining boundary. Full hardening evidence — Flash blocked, Java disabled, ads filtered — leaves the ALPC path to CSRSS entirely untouched, so the control reduces the chance of stage one and contributes nothing to stage two.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: The evaluation A.8.8 requires is normally performed against NVD plus a credentialed scan, and neither carries an exploitation field — so the score came out as a 7.8 local escalation even though Microsoft's April 2020 release document already said 'Exploited:Yes'. The vendor's exploitation state and the enterprise's evaluation feed are different channels, and A.8.8 does not require reconciling them; nothing re-opened the closed evaluation until CISA listed the CVE on 2022-05-23, 25 months after the patch.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.22.gap: Network segregation is the control most estates would cite against a drive-by, and it does not touch this defect: the privilege transition happens between two processes on one workstation, over local ALPC, with no packet leaving the host. Segmentation shapes what the attacker reaches after the escape, so its evidence is complete and simultaneously irrelevant to whether the escape succeeds.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Microsoft patched this CSRSS overflow on 2020-04-14 and marked it 'Exploited:Yes' with 'Exploitation Detected' the same day; Project Zero disclosed the in-the-wild chain on 2021-01-12 and CISA listed the CVE on 2022-05-23 with a 2022-06-13 due date. A CVSS-ordered queue reads 7.8 AV:L/PR:L and buries an item the vendor had already flagged as under attack, which is precisely the failure a KEV-triggered clock removes — it converts a catalogue listing into action on hosts still carrying pre-April-2020 builds — including the Windows 7, 8.1 and Server 2012 machines in the affected list, where the April 2020 KB is the only fix that will ever exist. EPSS on 2026-08-16 sits at 0.04547, 90.8th percentile, well above what a 7.8 local-privilege score implies.

new_control_requirements.name: BROWSER-MANAGED-UPDATE-NO-DEFERRAL
new_control_requirements.description: Enterprise update rings must not defer security-channel browser updates beyond 24h.
new_control_requirements.evidence: This CSRSS overflow was never an entry point — it was reached only after CVE-2020-6418 gave the attacker code execution inside a Chrome renderer, and Project Zero records that on older Windows the same actor swapped in a different escalation while keeping the browser bug. That makes the browser update ring the first of the two clocks that decide whether the chain completes: a workstation whose Chrome security-channel update was deferred by a week hands the attacker stage one regardless of how quickly the April 2020 Windows rollup lands. On an estate where Windows updates need a reboot window, the browser ring is also the faster of the two levers.

CVE-2020-2509.name: QNAP Network-Attached Storage (NAS) Command Injection Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: An unauthenticated request to the QTS or QuTS hero web management stack carries shell metacharacters into a command the appliance builds and runs, so the attacker's own commands execute on the NAS — the same box that holds the primary shares and, in most deployments, the backup copy of them.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; no account, no token and no user interaction, so reachability of the management interface is the complete precondition.
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; a single request with no race or memory-corruption work, though QNAP withheld the vulnerable endpoint, so constructing that request means analysing firmware rather than reading QSA-21-05.
attack_vector.ai_factor: Reported to QNAP by Omri Mallis and Yaniv Puyeski of SAM Seamless Network through ordinary manual research; no automated or AI-assisted tooling is named anywhere in the disclosure.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Taking the branch-specific fixed firmware — QTS 4.5.2.1566 Build 20210202, or the matching 4.2.6 / 4.3.3 / 4.3.4 / 4.3.6 build for legacy hardware, or QuTS hero h4.5.1.1491 — and removing every path from an untrusted network to the NAS management interface, UPnP mappings included.
prevention.adequacy: The firmware fix is complete where it can be installed, but it requires an appliance restart and it is unavailable on models whose product support status has ended — for those the only real control is removing reachability, and ultimately replacing the unit.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Forwarding QTS system and web-access logs off the appliance and alerting on shell-utility execution by the web-service account and on outbound connections initiated by the NAS to new destinations.
detection.adequacy: Logs held on the NAS are under the attacker's control the moment command execution succeeds, so this only works if the forwarding was configured before the compromise; most QNAP deployments log locally by default.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating an exposed unit as compromised rather than as unpatched: capture the configuration, rebuild the appliance from a known-good baseline, rotate every share, admin and cloud-link credential it held, and verify backup copies against an offline source before trusting them.
response.adequacy: Rebuild is the only reliable way to remove attacker-written content, but it depends on a restore source that is not the same appliance — which is exactly what an organisation using the NAS as its backup target does not have.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: Flaw remediation is only as good as the asset record behind it, and a QNAP NAS updating itself through QTS Live Update is invisible to the patch pipeline SI-2 evidence is drawn from. The branch-specific nature of the fix compounds it: an operator who reads 'update to the latest QTS' and finds 4.5.2 unavailable on a unit pinned to 4.3.4 may conclude no fix exists, when Build 20210324 on that branch is the fix.

NIST-800-53-SC-7.gap: SC-7 is the control that would actually neutralise an AV:N/PR:N flaw, and the product routinely defeats it without any human decision — UPnP and consumer-router port forwarding put a QTS management interface on the internet with no firewall rule for an SC-7 review to catch. Boundary-protection evidence describing the corporate edge is entirely accurate and entirely silent about a NAS at a home-worker or branch location.

NIS2-Art21-network-security.gap: The measure covers the entity's networks, and the exposure that makes this exploitable often sits at a site the entity does not treat as one of its networks, holding the same data. Nothing in Article 21 requires enumerating management surfaces that an appliance publishes for itself, so complete network-security documentation coexists with a QTS 4.3.6 console answering unauthenticated requests from the internet.

NIS2-Art21-incident-handling.gap: Handling a pre-authentication command-execution flaw on a storage appliance is a data-breach response, not a patch event, and Article 21 does not force that distinction. An entity that records the incident as closed when the QTS firmware update finishes has neither removed what the attacker wrote to the volumes nor rotated the share and cloud-link credentials the appliance held, both of which survive the upgrade intact.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: B4 assesses systems the organisation knows it manages, and departmentally purchased NAS hardware administered through its own web console is the canonical asset that never reaches the inventory. Without the unit in scope there is nothing to hold the branch-specific build requirement against, and QNAP's product support status — the fact that decides whether a fixed build exists at all — has no field in a typical B4 asset record.

UK-CAF-D1.gap: D1 planning names systems and their recovery routes, and this CVE collapses the two: the appliance an unauthenticated attacker executes commands on is frequently also the recovery target for everything else. A plan that satisfies D1 by pointing at the NAS has no independent path left once the flaw is used, and the plan gives no signal that this dependency exists.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Both patch mitigations presume a centrally driven update stream, and QTS updates are pulled per unit by the appliance itself, so maturity scoring reflects the servers and workstations while saying nothing about the NAS. The vendor-supported-product requirement is the part that matters most and is scored elsewhere: a model past QNAP's product support status has no fixed build on any of the seven patched branches and cannot be remediated at all.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: The control depends on vulnerability information arriving, and QSA-21-05 published on 2021-04-16 into QNAP's own advisory feed, which few vulnerability-management programmes monitor for storage hardware. Because the advisory withholds the vulnerable endpoint, exposure cannot be confirmed by testing either — the only usable evidence is the firmware build string, which network-scan-based A.8.8 evidence does not collect.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.22.gap: Segregating the QTS management interface away from general user and untrusted networks is the compensating control that works when firmware cannot be applied, and A.8.22 evidence is normally produced for datacentre and office network zones where the appliance does not live. A fully satisfied segregation statement is compatible with a QuTS hero unit sitting on a flat branch LAN with its console reachable from every workstation there.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: QNAP published QSA-21-05 on 2021-04-16 rating this Critical, and CISA listed it on 2022-04-11 with a 2022-05-02 due date — a year in which unpatched QTS and QuTS hero appliances stayed unauthenticated-RCE-reachable. The four-hour clock matters on this product because the mitigation half of the control is the one most units can actually meet immediately: removing the management interface from untrusted reachability takes minutes, while the branch-specific firmware update needs an appliance restart and a storage outage window. EPSS on 2026-08-16 is 0.33381 at the 98.2nd percentile.

new_control_requirements.name: PERIMETER-COMPROMISE-REBUILD-NOT-PATCH
new_control_requirements.description: Pre-rehearsed IR runbook for any perimeter device that suffers a pre-auth RCE CVE in active exploitation MUST default to config-exfil + rebuild + credential rotation, not patch-in-place. Patch-in-place leaves attacker-installed implants intact.
new_control_requirements.evidence: A QNAP NAS that was internet-reachable while running below QTS 4.5.2.1566 Build 20210202 (or the matching legacy-branch build) is the exact case this runbook exists for: CVE-2020-2509 is unauthenticated command execution, CISA confirmed in-the-wild use on 2022-04-11, and the QTS firmware update replaces system binaries without touching a web-shell, cron entry or altered share the attacker left on the data volumes. Rotation scope on this product is wider than a firewall's — share credentials, admin accounts, myQNAPcloud links and any application password stored on the appliance all leave with the compromise.

attack_vector.description: Two threads race recvmsg with MSG_PEEK against the af_unix garbage collector over descriptors passed with SCM_RIGHTS, so the collector frees a socket whose reference count is being raised outside the lock; the freed sk_buff is then reoccupied with fake pipe_buffer structures to give arbitrary kernel read and write, and root.
attack_vector.privileges_required: high — PR:H; NVD records that System execution privileges are needed, which is why this appeared as the final stage of a browser-to-kernel chain rather than as a standalone escalation.
attack_vector.complexity: high — AC:H; the race needs simultaneous receivers, heap spray, kernel-structure repair and scheduler affinity manipulation, with garbage objects created deliberately to widen the collection window.
attack_vector.ai_factor: Reported anonymously; Project Zero traces the underlying bug to a 2016 finding by a developer exercising SCM_RIGHTS with MSG_PEEK, whose correct patch the kernel community declined. Nothing in the record involves AI-assisted discovery or exploit development.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Moving devices to the 2021-11-05 Android security patch level or later, and on Linux hosts taking the kernel package carrying commit cbcf01128d0a and rebooting; enabling CONFIG_SLAB_FREELIST_RANDOM, which Project Zero names as the mitigation that makes the heap shaping this exploit needs materially harder.
prevention.adequacy: The kernel fix is complete where it is obtainable, and on Android it is not obtainable by the organisation at all — only the handset manufacturer can produce the build, and devices past vendor support never receive it.

detection.what_would_have_worked: auditd or eBPF rules on Linux hosts watching for the exploit's syscall shape — bursts of SCM_RIGHTS descriptor passing with concurrent MSG_PEEK receives — and alerting on unexplained kernel oops events on either platform.
detection.adequacy: This only exists on the server side; Android provides the organisation no kernel telemetry at all, so on handsets the detection column is empty and the whole defence rests on patch level.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating a handset that reached root through this chain as unrecoverable — wipe and re-provision rather than clean, and rotate every credential, token and session the device held, since the escalation follows browser-delivered remote code execution.
response.adequacy: A wipe removes attacker persistence but returns the device to the same patch level it started on, so unless the manufacturer has since shipped 2021-11-05 or later the re-provisioned handset is exploitable again immediately.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: SI-2 measures the organisation's remediation of flaws, and on Android the organisation cannot remediate — commit cbcf01128d0a is upstream, but it becomes actionable only when a manufacturer publishes a 2021-11-05 patch level for that specific model. The control has no state for 'fix exists, is not obtainable here', so the SI-2 record for a mixed handset fleet is really a report on vendor release cadence.

NIST-800-53-SI-4.gap: The behaviour worth monitoring is scheduler and syscall-level — deliberate garbage-object generation alongside threads pinning CPU cores and tweaking affinity — and no standard Android telemetry or MDM agent surfaces any of it. SI-4 evidence for a mobile fleet consists of compliance and app-inventory reporting, which cannot observe this exploit at any stage, leaving monitoring a paper control on the population most affected.

NIS2-Art21-supply-chain.gap: The delivery chain for this fix runs upstream Linux, Android common kernel, SoC vendor tree, handset manufacturer build — four hops, none under the entity's control. The bug was publicly reported with a correct patch in 2016 and that patch was refused, so five years of exposure came from a decision inside an upstream community that no supplier-assurance clause in Article 21 reaches, and nothing requires patch-level cadence to be a purchase criterion.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: B4 asks whether systems are securely configured and maintained, and for a handset past manufacturer support the honest answer is that maintenance has ended — the device is pinned below 2021-11-05 permanently, which B4 can only record as an unclearable non-compliance. The Linux servers carrying the same af_unix defect usually sit in a different assessment scope, so the CVE appears in one B4 record and not the other despite being one bug.

UK-CAF-C1.gap: Security monitoring depends on the asset producing telemetry, and an Android handset reports its security patch level and compliance posture to the MDM and nothing about kernel behaviour. C1 therefore monitors the attribute this CVE has already rendered unfixable on out-of-support devices, while the exploitation activity itself — the recvmsg race and the slab spray — passes entirely unobserved on devices that are still supported.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: The mitigation's clock starts at vendor release, and for Android the relevant vendor is each handset manufacturer, not Google — the 2021-11-05 patch level was available upstream well before many models received it. The maturity model also cannot represent a fleet split between current devices, devices months behind their manufacturer's cycle, and devices that will never receive another patch level, which is the normal composition of an Android estate.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: Evaluated on its own numbers this is a 6.4 with AV:L, AC:H and PR:H — a bug that any severity-driven A.8.8 process would rank near the bottom. The missing input is its role: it was the kernel-escalation stage of an in-the-wild chain behind the Samsung browser zero day CVE-2021-38000 and the Chrome n-day CVE-2020-16040, and A.8.8 evaluation has no field for a component's position in an observed chain.

ENISA-mobile-secure-baseline.gap: The baseline treats OS currency as a device-management setting, and the only lever an organisation truly holds is withholding corporate data from a handset below the 2021-11-05 patch level — it cannot cause that patch level to be built. A baseline discharged by an MDM policy that reports the stale patch level while the device keeps its mail, VPN and document access has documented the exposure rather than removed it.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Google shipped the fix at the 2021-11-05 Android patch level and CISA listed the CVE on 2022-05-23 with a 2022-06-13 due date, six months later. The documented-compensating-control branch of this SLA is the one that carries the weight for this CVE, because on Android the patch is not the organisation's to deploy: with EPSS at 0.00811 and a 6.4 CVSS, nothing in a severity-driven queue would have raised this handset population, and the KEV clock is the only trigger that forces a decision on devices pinned below the fixed patch level.

new_control_requirements.name: KERNEL-EXPLOITATION-DETECTION
new_control_requirements.description: Deploy auditd or eBPF-based monitoring rules for kernel privilege escalation indicators. Alert within 60 seconds of detection.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Project Zero's own 0-day detection note for this bug gives the rule content: a program generating a number of garbage objects while other threads pin different CPU cores and tweak task affinity, alongside concurrent MSG_PEEK receives on unix sockets. That is auditd- and eBPF-observable on the Linux server population that carries the same af_unix defect — Ubuntu fixed it in 4.15.0-159.167, 5.4.0-88.99 and 5.11.0-37.41 — and it is the only telemetry available at all, since Android hands the operator no kernel visibility. The rules have to be in place before the attempt; authored afterwards against telemetry nobody collected, they produce nothing.

attack_vector.description: An unprivileged local process arranges epoll instances so the kernel's loop check reaches a file object already being destroyed, and ep_loop_check_proc calls get_file on it despite holding only a weak reference — resurrecting a dying struct file into a use-after-free that yields kernel control flow and root.
attack_vector.privileges_required: low — PR:L; NVD records no additional execution privileges are needed, so any code already running as an ordinary user or inside an app sandbox is a sufficient starting point.
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; no wide race window or heap-grooming prerequisite is documented, and the practical gate is kernel version rather than exploitation skill, since only a narrow set of point releases carry the defect.
attack_vector.ai_factor: Found upstream by syzbot/syzkaller, which is coverage-guided fuzzing over human-written syscall descriptions rather than AI-assisted discovery; the party that found and used it on Android is unknown.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Running a kernel carrying commit 77f4689de17c — upstream 5.9-rc4, 5.8.8, 5.4.64, 4.19.144, 4.14.197, 4.9.236 or 4.4.236 from September 2020, or on Android the 2021-11-06 security patch level — and rebooting onto it.
prevention.adequacy: The fix is exact and verifiable by kernel version, which is unusually good; the weakness is entirely in delivery, since the upstream fix existed eleven months before Android devices received it and the 5.7 branch reached end of life without ever getting it.

detection.what_would_have_worked: eBPF or audit rules on Linux hosts flagging epoll_ctl nesting patterns combined with concurrent descriptor close, plus treating any kernel oops referencing eventpoll teardown as an exploitation attempt rather than a stability fault.
detection.adequacy: Nothing equivalent exists on Android, where the affected population lived, and on Linux the rules must be deployed in advance — a clean exploit produces no oops at all, so the crash signal only catches failed attempts.

response.what_would_have_worked: Wiping and re-provisioning a handset that reached root, rotating the accounts and tokens it held, and using the exact kernel-version ranges to scope which other devices and hosts in the estate were ever reachable.
response.adequacy: The precise version ranges make scoping genuinely tractable here, but re-provisioning returns an Android device to whatever patch level its manufacturer offers — if that is still below 2021-11-06, the device is exploitable again on first boot.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: This CVE has an exact affected-version answer — a handful of point releases between 2020-08-26 and mid-September 2020 — and SI-2 evidence expressed as 'no missing updates' cannot represent it. The result is inverted accounting: unaffected hosts are counted as remediated, while an Android device left below the 2021-11-06 patch level for eleven months by its manufacturer shows up as one overdue line.

NIST-800-53-SI-4.gap: Detecting this means observing epoll nesting against concurrent descriptor teardown — file-lifecycle behaviour that neither Android nor a default Linux audit configuration records. An SI-4 programme evidenced by authentication, network flow and process-creation telemetry is complete on its own terms and contains nothing at all about the path this exploit takes.

NIS2-Art21-supply-chain.gap: Commit a9ed4a6560b8 introduced the defect while fixing something else and 77f4689de17c closed it within weeks upstream; the eleven-month exposure was created downstream, by handset vendors tracking Security Bulletins instead of merging full LTS trees. Article 21 gives an entity no requirement to ask a supplier how it tracks stable releases, which is precisely the question that separated an exposed device from a safe one.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: An advisory-driven patch process could not have acted before November 2021, because the September 2020 stable releases that carried the fix had no CVE attached and syzbot's thread was a bug report rather than a bulletin. The measure's proportionate-to-risk framing is fine; the input arrived fourteen months after the code was fixed, and nothing in the measure requires tracking the stable branch itself.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: Being on a supported branch is not sufficient here — the requirement is a specific point release carrying 77f4689de17c. The 5.7.18 case is the one B4 handles worst: that branch went end of life before the fix existed, so no maintenance action on that host reaches a secure state and the only route is a branch change, which B4 treats as an architecture decision rather than a maintenance obligation.

UK-CAF-C1.gap: On the Android population where exploitation was actually observed, the organisation receives no kernel telemetry whatsoever, so C1's monitoring outcome has nothing to act on. On a Linux server the escalation produces no network artefact and no anomalous process ancestry, so even comprehensive log collection evidenced under C1 would not have surfaced it.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: There were two vendor release dates eleven months apart — the September 2020 upstream stable point releases and the 2021-11-06 Android patch level — and scoring against the later one certifies an estate as compliant across the whole window. Project Zero's reading is that attackers were deliberately hunting Android kernels missing fixes that already existed upstream, which is the exact population this scoring marks compliant.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: For more than a year the only source that would have told an organisation it was exposed was the kernel stable-tree changelog: the September 2020 fix shipped without a CVE identifier and syzbot's report was not a security advisory. A.8.8 discharged by subscribing to distribution and vendor advisory feeds — the ordinary reading of 'appropriate sources' — was structurally blind until the Android bulletin published.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: The eventpoll fix reached Android at the 2021-11-06 patch level and CISA listed the CVE on 2022-05-23 with a 2022-06-13 due date. With EPSS at 0.00776 and no public exploit, nothing in a risk-scored queue would have prioritised this Android and Linux kernel population — the KEV listing is the only signal that raises it, and the 'whichever is later' clause is what makes the SLA meaningful on devices where the manufacturer's build, not the upstream fix of September 2020, is the moment remediation becomes possible.

new_control_requirements.name: KERNEL-EXIT-RACE-CVE-CLASS-MONITORING
new_control_requirements.description: When a CVE is disclosed in the kernel ptrace / pidfd / fd-table lifecycle class, audit rules SHOULD enable pidfd_getfd / pidfd_open / pidfd_send_signal tracking for auid>=1000 within 24h. The syscall is rare in normal operation; spike volume after a same-class disclosure is high-confidence exploitation signal.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2021-1048 is squarely in the class this control names: ep_loop_check_proc taking a reference on a struct file that is already at refcount zero and mid-destruction in eventpoll_release is a file-descriptor lifecycle defect, and Jann Horn's CVE-2021-4083 in the same area confirms the class is productive rather than isolated. On the Linux hosts carrying the affected point releases — 5.4.61 to 5.4.63, 4.19.142 to 4.19.143 and the rest — descriptor-lifecycle syscall telemetry is the only in-flight signal available, since the escalation produces no setuid execution, no sudo event and no network artefact. The rules have to be enabled while the affected kernel is still running, not after the reboot onto 4.19.144 makes them moot.

CVE-2021-1789.name: Apple Multiple Products Type Confusion Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: A page of crafted script pushes WebKit into treating an object as a type it is not; the confused state becomes a memory read and write inside the renderer and then code execution in the process handling the content, reached through Safari, any iOS browser, or any embedded web view that loads remote content.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; no account or prior access, only that the target's device renders the attacker's content.
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L with UI:R; the visit is the only user action required, which a watering hole supplies, and the real work sits after the renderer, since the sandbox forces the attacker to chain a second bug to reach the system.
attack_vector.ai_factor: Credited by Apple to @S0rryMybad of 360 Vulcan Team, a manual browser-exploitation research team; Google TAG's analysis of the in-the-wild use names no automated or AI-assisted tooling on the discovery or the weaponisation side.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Deploying both release waves — iOS and iPadOS 14.4, tvOS 14.4 and watchOS 7.3 from 2021-01-26, then macOS Big Sur 11.2, Security Update 2021-001 for Catalina and Mojave, and Safari 14.0.3 from 2021-02-01 — with the restart or Safari relaunch completed, and enforcing those builds as an access condition rather than a reporting line.
prevention.adequacy: The update removes the flaw, but it was already available for seven months when TAG found the campaign, so the control that failed was deployment speed rather than availability — and it gives nothing to hardware that cannot reach iOS 14.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Treating repeated Safari or WebKit renderer crashes on a specific site as an exploitation signal, and hunting for the injected-iframe delivery pattern in web proxy logs for the sites the population actually visits.
detection.adequacy: Apple gives third-party tooling no visibility inside the WebKit renderer, so on iOS this reduces to crash telemetry and network egress; a successful chain that does not crash the renderer produces no detectable local artefact at all.

response.what_would_have_worked: Scoping by exposure window and site rather than by device alert: identify which managed devices below the fixed builds visited the affected sites, and re-provision those rather than trusting an in-place update, given the chain's kernel-escalation stage.
response.adequacy: Scoping depends on egress logging that mobile devices off the corporate network do not generate, and TAG's campaign targeted a community rather than an enterprise, so the visited sites were ordinary reading rather than anything an access policy would have blocked.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: The mobile fix was available from 2021-01-26 and the macOS fix from 2021-02-01, and the campaign TAG uncovered was running in late August 2021, so remediation availability was never the constraint — deployment latency was. The SI-2 detail that catches organisations out here is the Catalina and Mojave path: remediation is Security Update 2021-001 plus Safari 14.0.3, shipped in the second wave, so an SI-2 record keyed to the macOS build alone reports those hosts wrongly in both directions and a due-date computed from the iOS ship date is already short by a week.

NIST-800-53-CM-7.gap: The usual CM-7 evidence on Apple devices — an approved-application list and a single sanctioned browser — buys nothing here, because Apple requires every iOS and iPadOS browser and web view to use the system WebKit, so all of them share this defect. On macOS the same engine sits behind WKWebView in mail, chat and documentation clients, so restricting installed software leaves the vulnerable renderer reachable through applications nobody classifies as browsers.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: Apple explicitly flagged three other CVEs in the iOS 14.4 release as possibly actively exploited and did not flag this one, so a risk-proportionate programme reading the vendor's own signal would reasonably have treated CVE-2021-1789 as routine. TAG's disclosure ten months later that it had been the entry stage of a state-backed watering hole is precisely the kind of revised input the measure provides no mechanism to re-run the proportionality judgement against.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: For mobile devices B4 is normally evidenced by an MDM compliance report, and reporting is not the control this CVE needs — enforcement is, in the form of denying mail, VPN and document access to any device below iOS 14.4. An assessment that accepts a dashboard listing stale devices as evidence of maintenance has documented the exposure while leaving every entitlement on those devices intact.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: The same CVE is an operating-system patch on iOS and iPadOS, where Safari ships with the OS, and an application patch on Catalina and Mojave, where Safari 14.0.3 updates independently. Essential Eight scores those two mitigations separately, so an organisation strong on OS patching and weak on application patching remains exposed on its older Macs while its overall maturity reads well.

AU-Essential-8-App-Hardening.gap: The mitigation's content — disable Flash, Java, ads and unneeded plug-ins — targets features this exploit does not use. A JavaScriptCore type confusion needs only script execution, which is the browser's core function, so an estate at the highest application-hardening maturity has not narrowed the delivery path for crafted web content by any measurable amount.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: The evaluation available in early 2021 was an 8.8 with UI:R and no exploitation flag from the vendor, and no authoritative source recorded in-the-wild use until CISA's KEV listing on 2022-05-04, sixteen months after the fix shipped. A.8.8 has no re-evaluation trigger, so the risk record produced under it during that window understated a CVE that was, by then, already the opening move of a state-backed campaign.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.7.gap: Anti-malware controls have essentially no purchase on this CVE's iOS half: Apple gives third-party endpoint products no visibility into the WebKit renderer, so there is no scanning, no behavioural hook and no telemetry from the process being exploited. An A.8.7 statement that is fully accurate about managed Macs and Windows endpoints says nothing about the mobile population the hostile iframe was aimed at.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Apple published iOS and iPadOS 14.4, tvOS 14.4 and watchOS 7.3 on 2021-01-26 and macOS Big Sur 11.2, Security Update 2021-001 for Catalina and Mojave, and Safari 14.0.3 on 2021-02-01; Google TAG found the flaw being used as an n-day in a Hong Kong watering hole in late August 2021; CISA listed the CVE on 2022-05-04 with a 2022-05-25 due date. On this CVE the SLA has to reach five platforms across two release dates a week apart, so a clock started on the first wave expires on Macs before their fix exists — and an estate that closes the ticket on iPhones alone leaves Apple TVs, Watches and older Macs rendering the same engine. EPSS on 2026-08-16 is 0.1322, 96.0th percentile.

new_control_requirements.name: MOBILE-ENDPOINT-MDM-ENFORCED-KEV-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: iOS / iPadOS / macOS estates must enforce KEV-class updates within 24h via DDM; user-deferral disallowed.
new_control_requirements.evidence: The mobile builds existed from 2021-01-26 and the macOS and Safari builds from 2021-02-01, and the campaign TAG documented was still finding unpatched targets some seven months later, which is a deferral problem rather than an availability one — and on iOS the deferral is usually the user's, since the update requires a restart the user chooses when to take. Enforcement has to treat iOS/iPadOS 14.4, Big Sur 11.2 and the Catalina/Mojave Safari 14.0.3 route as one access condition, because Apple requires every browser and web view on iOS to use system WebKit, so there is no per-application remediation available and the OS build is the only lever. Devices that cannot reach iOS 14 at all fall outside enforcement entirely and belong on a dated replacement schedule.

CVE-2021-21551.name: Dell dbutil Driver Insufficient Access Control Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: A local process opens the dbutil_2_3.sys device, which is created without an ACL restricting access, and issues IOCTL 0x9B0C1EC8 with chosen source, destination and length; the driver performs the memmove in kernel context, giving arbitrary kernel read and write that the public exploits convert into a SYSTEM token swap — and because the driver stays validly signed, it can be brought to any Windows host and loaded there.
attack_vector.privileges_required: low — PR:L; on a Dell client with the driver present this is user-to-SYSTEM, while the bring-your-own-driver variant needs administrator to install the service first and buys the attacker the kernel rather than administrator.
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; a single deterministic IOCTL with no race, no heap groom and no information leak, which is why independent working exploits appeared within weeks of the 2021-05-04 disclosure.
attack_vector.ai_factor: Kasif Dekel of SentinelLabs found it after a Process Hacker service-creation notification led him to reverse the driver's IOCTL handlers by hand; no fuzzing infrastructure and no AI-assisted tooling appear in the discovery or exploitation record.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Running Dell's DSA-2021-088 removal utility (or sc.exe delete DBUtil_2_3 plus file deletion) and restarting, updating the Dell management software to the remediated packages that install DBUtilDrv2.sys, and enabling HVCI with Microsoft's vulnerable-driver blocklist so the signed binary cannot be reloaded.
prevention.adequacy: Removal closes the Dell-hardware exposure but not the class: the certificate was never revoked, so without blocklist enforcement any administrator-level process — including the attacker's — can put the driver back, which is precisely the path ESET observed.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alerting on creation of a kernel service named DBUtil_2_3, on the presence of dbutil_2_3.sys outside Dell installation paths, and on abrupt loss of endpoint telemetry following any driver load.
detection.adequacy: The detection has to reach a collector outside the compromised host's own agent, because the whole point of the FudModule stage is disabling the monitoring that would otherwise report it — telemetry that stops is only a signal if something off-host notices the silence.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating a host where this driver loaded without a Dell firmware operation as kernel-compromised: rebuild rather than clean, discount its own endpoint telemetry for the exposure window, and rotate the credentials and tokens it held.
response.adequacy: Rebuild is the only sound answer once an attacker has held the kernel, but it depends on noticing at all — and on restoring from an image that does not itself carry the vulnerable driver, which is a common way the exposure returns.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: SI-2 expects a fixed version to install, and Dell shipped a removal utility and a renamed driver instead — DBUtilDrv2.sys — so there is no version comparison that resolves this component to 'remediated'. The control also scopes to the organisation's own installed software, while the exploitable artefact is a still-signed file an attacker supplies, so every SI-2 action can complete with the bring-your-own-driver path untouched.

NIST-800-53-SI-4.gap: This driver's operational value is that it defeats the monitoring SI-4 describes: ESET recorded Lazarus using the kernel write to run FudModule and disable seven Windows monitoring mechanisms. SI-4 evidence drawn from one EDR product's coverage report is therefore circular here — the coverage is real until the moment it matters, and nothing in the control requires a second, independently trusted source to observe the primary going quiet.

NIST-800-53-CM-7.gap: Removing unneeded functionality collides with an operational need on Dell client hardware: the driver arrives with Command Update, SupportAssist and the BIOS flash utilities, which are the tools that keep firmware current. CM-7 has no way to record a component that is simultaneously a liability and a dependency, so the workable answer — delete it and enforce a driver load policy so it cannot come back — sits outside what the control scores.

NIS2-Art21-vulnerability-handling.gap: The measure produces a closed item when the DSA-2021-088 utility has run, and that is the moment the residual exposure starts, because the driver remains validly signed and loadable by any administrator-level process. Handling a defect that persists as a reusable attack tool after the affected product is remediated is a shape the measure does not describe, and the ongoing obligation — blocklist enforcement — has no advisory to attach itself to.

NIS2-Art21-incident-handling.gap: Once this driver has loaded, the host's own telemetry is evidence the attacker was in a position to shape — that is what the FudModule stage exists to achieve. Article 21 sets incident-handling processes and notification clocks but gives no rule requiring an investigator to discount endpoint logs from a machine whose kernel was held, so an incident assessment and any subsequent notification can rest on data that was manipulated.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: Running Dell's removal utility and updating the management software satisfies B4's maintained-and-configured outcome while leaving the durable control unexamined: HVCI plus Microsoft's vulnerable-driver blocklist, enforced and re-verified after image rebuilds and backup restores. Asset records supporting a B4 assessment do not usually carry driver-blocklist state, so the configuration that keeps this closed over years is not the one the assessment looks at.

UK-CAF-C1.gap: C1 measures monitoring coverage and response, both of which assume the monitoring stack is running, and the FudModule stage ESET documented removes that assumption on the specific host that matters. Nothing in C1 requires a telemetry source outside the primary EDR's trust root, so an endpoint that goes silent after a driver load produces no alert and reads as an ordinary gap in reporting.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: The mitigation frames remediation as updating a vulnerable application, and here the component is a kernel driver installed as a side effect of Dell management tooling and remediated by deletion. It also has nothing to say about the bring-your-own-driver case, where the vulnerable file is not on the host until the attacker writes it — no patch cadence on any machine affects that, which is why blocklist enforcement rather than patch timeliness is the control that matters.

AU-Essential-8-App-Hardening.gap: User application hardening addresses browsers, Office and PDF readers and has no expression for kernel-driver load policy, which is the only surface that stops a signed vulnerable driver from being loaded. Top maturity on this mitigation is fully compatible with an estate where any administrator-level process can drop dbutil_2_3.sys and start it as a service.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: The control cannot evaluate a vulnerability it never identifies, and dbutil_2_3.sys is installed silently by Dell firmware-update tooling rather than appearing as a listed application, so most software inventories omit it. Where it is found, A.8.8's remediation expectation is a patched release, and the correct action is deletion plus a driver load-policy change — neither of which the control's evidence format has a field for.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.9.gap: The setting that keeps this closed permanently is a configuration item — HVCI on, Microsoft's vulnerable-driver blocklist enforced — and standard baselines enumerate installed software, services and policy rather than kernel-driver load policy, so the item is usually absent from the baseline altogether. The drift path is also specific and fast: a host rebuilt from an older image or restored from backup reacquires both the driver file and, often, the pre-blocklist configuration, and a periodic configuration review will not see that before an administrator-level attacker can use it.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Dell published DSA-2021-088 on 2021-05-04, independent working exploits followed within weeks — Metasploit's cve_2021_21551_dbutil_memmove carries a 2021-05-04 disclosure date and Exploit-DB 49893 landed 2021-05-21 — and CISA did not list the CVE until 2022-03-31 with a 2022-04-21 due date. The 'documented compensating controls' branch is what carries this one past the removal utility: for the bring-your-own-driver path there is no patch to deploy at all, so the mitigation Dell itself names — Microsoft's recommended driver block rules with HVCI — is the deliverable the SLA has to demand. EPSS on 2026-08-16 is 0.53116 at the 98.9th percentile.

new_control_requirements.name: EDR-AS-VULNERABILITY-SECONDARY-OVERLAY
new_control_requirements.description: Organizations whose primary EDR is also a high-value attack target (Defender, CrowdStrike, SentinelOne) must deploy an independent secondary overlay capable of detecting anomalous behavior by the primary EDR's own processes. The overlay can be a second-vendor behavioral EDR, network-side EDR-bypass telemetry, or out-of-band SYSTEM-process spawn monitoring — but must NOT share trust roots with the primary EDR.
new_control_requirements.evidence: ESET's 2022-09-30 report on Lazarus in the Netherlands and Belgium describes exactly the failure this control anticipates: the kernel write obtained through dbutil_2_3.sys was used to run FudModule and disable seven Windows monitoring mechanisms, so the primary endpoint product stopped reporting rather than alerting. An overlay that does not share the primary's trust root is what turns that silence into a signal — the observable is a DBUtil_2_3 service starting on a host with no Dell firmware operation under way, immediately followed by telemetry loss. This is the control that still has value after the DSA-2021-088 removal utility has run, because the driver remains validly signed and any administrator-level process can bring it back.

attack_vector.description: A local process drives the AF_PACKET ring-buffer setup through an error path that frees the rx_owner_map allocation which the caller then frees again. The attacker reclaims the freed slab slot with pipe_buffer objects, corrupts one into an arbitrary kernel read/write primitive, overwrites modprobe_path and gets a script executed as root. The reachable precondition is CAP_NET_RAW in the socket's network namespace, which an ordinary user obtains through an unprivileged user namespace.
attack_vector.privileges_required: low — PR:L; any local account, and on a distribution permitting unprivileged user namespaces the CAP_NET_RAW requirement is self-served rather than granted. A container workload able to create a user namespace satisfies it from inside the container against the host kernel.
attack_vector.complexity: high — AC:H; the syscall sequence that produces the double free is deterministic, but privilege escalation depends on winning the slab-reclaim race with a groomed object. Losing it panics the host, which makes the attempt loud but does not make it rare.
attack_vector.ai_factor: No AI involvement is claimed or evidenced. The CVE reached NVD through a CNA rather than the kernel.org channel and no individual finder was named in the distribution trackers, so the discovery route is recorded as unknown.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Booting a kernel built past ec6af094ea28f0f2dda1a6a33b14cd57e36a9755 — Ubuntu 5.4.0-100.113 or 4.15.0-169.177, SUSE 5.3.18-150300.59.49.1 or 5.14.21-150400.22.1 — and, for the window before that reboot, disabling unprivileged user-namespace creation and withholding CAP_NET_RAW from workloads that do not capture traffic.
prevention.adequacy: The package upgrade is complete only after reboot, and no live patch for this CVE was resolvable, so the remediation carries an availability cost on exactly the hosts most exposed. The namespace and capability restrictions genuinely remove the precondition but break container runtimes and packet-capture tooling that legitimately need them.

detection.what_would_have_worked: auditd or eBPF rules on socket(AF_PACKET) creation and setsockopt on packet sockets from non-root uids, correlated with user-namespace creation and with writes to the module-loader path; plus treating kernel panics referencing packet_set_ring as security events rather than stability tickets.
detection.adequacy: This requires host telemetry that is already collected and shipped off-host before the attempt, which on shared multi-user and container hosts is where it is least often enabled. Detection also arrives after the escalation has already happened; it bounds the window to response time rather than preventing root.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating any host that panicked with a packet_set_ring or slab-corruption signature during the exposure window as suspect: reboot onto the fixed kernel, then rebuild rather than clean, and rotate every credential and key that lived on that host, because a successful run ends with arbitrary kernel write and there is no artefact left behind to scope from.
response.adequacy: Rebuild is the only defensible outcome once kernel-level write has been reached, and it is expensive enough that it is routinely skipped in favour of patching in place — which removes the vulnerability and nothing the attacker installed.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: Flaw remediation is satisfied by installing the fixed kernel package, but the vulnerable code is the running kernel image. A 20.04 LTS host holding linux 5.4.0-100.113 in its package database while still booted on the previous build produces exactly the evidence an SI-2 assessment asks for and remains exploitable. SI-2 also has no mechanism to express that Ubuntu 16.04 and 22.04 were never affected while 18.04 and 20.04 were, so a fleet-level currency statement conceals which hosts actually carried the defect.

NIST-800-53-SC-39.gap: Process isolation is presumed by every container deployment on these hosts, and this CVE is that presumption failing: the escalation crosses from a confined workload into the host kernel, so the isolation boundary the architecture is drawn around is not a boundary for this primitive. SC-39 describes the property but prescribes nothing that maintains it against a kernel defect reachable from an unprivileged user namespace, which is the specific route a container workload uses to obtain CAP_NET_RAW here.

NIST-800-53-CM-7.gap: Least functionality is evidenced through package minimisation and service baselines, neither of which touches the two settings that determine reachability: unprivileged user-namespace creation and CAP_NET_RAW assignment. A host that passes a CM-7 review with a minimal package set and no listening services still lets any interactive user reach packet_set_ring(), because the capability is evaluated against a namespace the user can create for themselves.

NIST-800-53-SI-4.gap: System monitoring is deployed but keyed on network connections, process creation and file modification, and this exploit produces nothing in those channels until it has already succeeded. The distinguishing telemetry — AF_PACKET setsockopt sequences from an unprivileged uid, bulk pipe resizing, a modprobe_path write — needs auditd or eBPF rules authored in advance, and the kernel panic that a failed attempt produces is routed to operations as a stability incident rather than to security as an exploitation signal.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: The Article 21 patch obligation completes at deployment, but for a kernel defect the exposure ends at reboot, and the entities holding the most affected hosts — container platforms and shared compute estates — are the ones with the longest reboot deferrals. The KEV window here was 2022-04-11 to 2022-05-02; a production node's maintenance cycle commonly exceeds three weeks, and nothing in the obligation classes an installed-but-unrebooted host as still exposed.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: B4 evidence for a Linux estate is normally a hardening baseline plus package currency, and this defect is invisible to both. The vulnerable code is compiled into the kernel rather than configured, and the configuration item that decides whether an ordinary user can reach it — unprivileged user-namespace creation — is absent from the benchmark scores CAF submissions are built from, so a high B4 score coexists with every local account holding the escalation path.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Patch-operating-systems maturity measures elapsed time from vendor release to deployment, which mis-describes this remediation on two counts. The fix is defined by an upstream commit that each distribution and appliance vendor backported at a different package version, so there is no single release date to measure from; and the Linux kernels inside storage controllers, network appliances and embedded products are updated as firmware, outside the operating-system patch pipeline the maturity level is assessed against.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: Technical-vulnerability management is in place and its scanner reports this closed once the fixed kernel package is installed. The control never requires reconciling the running kernel against the installed package, which is the only test that distinguishes a rebooted host from one that merely downloaded the fix, and its asset scope typically excludes the appliance population whose vendor-supplied Linux kernels carry the same defect with no package manager to interrogate.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: The Linux kernel packet-socket double free was listed in KEV on 2022-04-11 with a 2022-05-02 due date, and the vendor builds that carry the fix — Ubuntu 5.4.0-100.113 and 4.15.0-169.177, SUSE 5.3.18-150300.59.49.1 and 5.14.21-150400.22.1 — only take effect at reboot.
