The compensating-controls clause is what makes this control usable here: on a host that cannot reboot inside the window, disabling unprivileged user-namespace creation and withholding CAP_NET_RAW removes the precondition an unprivileged account needs to reach packet_set_ring(), and that decision has to be recorded as the mitigation rather than left as an open exception until the next maintenance cycle.

new_control_requirements.name: LIVE-PATCH-CAPABILITY
new_control_requirements.description: For any system that processes production workloads and cannot tolerate unplanned reboots: live kernel patching capability (kpatch, livepatch, kGraft, or equivalent) must be deployed and tested quarterly.
new_control_requirements.evidence: This is the case that exposes the difference between holding a live-patching subscription and being able to use it. No published live patch for CVE-2021-22600 was resolvable, so on Ubuntu 18.04 and 20.04 and on SUSE Linux Enterprise 15 the only path to the fixed packet_set_ring() was a kernel package upgrade plus a boot — inside a KEV window that ran 2022-04-11 to 2022-05-02. The requirement is therefore that the capability be deployed and exercised before the disclosure, and that its coverage for a given CVE be checked rather than assumed, because an estate that defers the reboot on the strength of a live-patching contract that does not cover this fix is running unremediated kernels with a compliance record that says otherwise.

new_control_requirements.name: KERNEL-EXPLOITATION-DETECTION
new_control_requirements.description: Deploy auditd or eBPF-based monitoring rules for kernel privilege escalation indicators. Alert within 60 seconds of detection.
new_control_requirements.evidence: The published exploit for this CVE leaves no network or file artefact until it has already won: it opens an AF_PACKET socket with TPACKET_V3, sprays pipe_inode_info and eventfd objects, then writes modprobe_path and executes a non-ELF file to run a script as root. Those are auditd- and eBPF-observable events and nothing else in the host's telemetry is, which is why a fleet with full network monitoring saw nothing on this class. The rules have to exist before the attempt, and the kernel panic produced by a lost reclaim race has to be routed to security rather than filed as a stability fault on the affected Ubuntu 18.04/20.04 or SUSE 15 host.

CVE-2021-26085.name: Atlassian Confluence Server Pre-Authorization Arbitrary File Read Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: An anonymous GET to /s/<token>/_/;/WEB-INF/... exploits a disagreement between Confluence's security filter and its static-resource loader about where a URL path ends when a semicolon path parameter appears. The filter authorises the request as a static asset; the loader serves a protected application file. The attacker gets web.xml, the Seraph authentication configuration, the decorator configuration and the exact Maven build version, from a webapp that has never seen a credential.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; the request carries no session, no token and no header the attacker must obtain first, and the cache-busting segment is arbitrary rather than issued.
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; a single request with no timing, encoding or state requirement. The real constraint is scope rather than difficulty: the read is confined to the deployed web application, so it yields configuration and version rather than the database credentials in the Confluence home directory.
attack_vector.ai_factor: Discovered by a human researcher — Amit Laish of the GE Digital Cyber Security Lab, per Atlassian CONFSERVER-67893 — and weaponised by hand afterwards in Exploit-DB 50377 and a Nuclei template. No AI-assisted discovery or exploit development is evidenced.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Upgrading to 7.4.10, 7.12.3 or 7.13.0 and restarting the application on every node, from 2021-07-21 when the fix shipped — eight months before the KEV listing. In the interim, rejecting request paths containing a semicolon under /s/ at the reverse proxy.
prevention.adequacy: The upgrade is complete and cheap, and its only real limit is that it lands per node — a Data Center cluster is remediated only when the last node restarts. The proxy rule is a pattern block on a parser mismatch, so it holds against the published requests and not necessarily against a re-encoded variant.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alerting on unauthenticated 200 responses to /s/ paths containing a semicolon, and on any response carrying '<display-name>Confluence</display-name>' to a request with no session — both are available from the reverse proxy's own access log without touching the application.
detection.adequacy: It detects the published tooling exactly, because Exploit-DB 50377 and the Nuclei template both use the ';/' shape. It also detects it only after the file has been returned; the request is a single GET, so there is no window in which to interdict, and the value of detection here is knowing what an attacker learned rather than stopping them learning it.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating a confirmed read as configuration disclosure with a defined scope: review seraph-config.xml for anything environment-specific, assume the exact build is known to the attacker, and re-check the instance against every other Confluence CVE affecting that build, since build identification is what this bug is actually worth in a chain.
response.adequacy: Scoping is unusually tractable here because the read cannot leave the web application — confluence.cfg.xml and the database credentials are in the Confluence home directory and out of reach. That bounds the response, but it does not undo the reconnaissance, and CISA's ransomware marking means the instances that were read were not always left alone.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: Flaw remediation was fully available from 2021-07-21 and the estate still had to be told about it by CISA on 2022-03-28. The reason is that SI-2 prioritisation runs on vendor severity, and Atlassian scored this 5.2 while NVD scored 5.3 — so an instance with an EPSS score of 0.99937, an Exploit-DB entry from October 2021 and a Nuclei template in general circulation was queued behind higher-CVSS bugs with no exploitation activity at all.

NIST-800-53-AC-3.gap: Access enforcement exists in Confluence and is bypassed rather than misapplied here, which is why an AC-3 attestation passes while the flaw is open. Assessors examine space permissions, global permissions and group membership; the attacker presents no identity and is answered by the static-resource route, so none of those objects is ever consulted. The specific irony is that the file returned — WEB-INF/classes/seraph-config.xml — is the configuration of the authentication framework whose correctness the AC-3 evidence asserts.

NIST-800-53-SC-7.gap: Boundary protection is normally the fallback for an unpatched web application, and for Confluence it usually is not one: the instance is deliberately reachable by staff and often partners, so there is no segment that removes the path without removing the service. Where a WAF is in front, SC-7 evidence records its presence rather than its behaviour on this input, and the exploit is an ordinary GET with no payload or encoding for a generic rule set to key on — only an explicit rule against a semicolon under /s/ intercepts it.

NIS2-Art21-vulnerability-handling.gap: The obligation is met on paper by having a handling process, and the process closes when the upgrade to 7.4.10 or 7.12.3 is scheduled. What it never asks is what left the building during the eight months between the vendor fix and the 2022-03-28 KEV listing, which matters here because Confluence holds the runbooks, network diagrams and joiner-mover-leaver notes of the essential entities in scope — the disclosure is an input to a later incident rather than an incident with its own log entry.

UK-CAF-B2.gap: B2 evidence for a Confluence estate is SSO enforcement, space-level permissions and administrator separation, and this request path consults none of them. The caller is anonymous, the route is the static-asset handler, and the response is an application-internal file — so the identity and access-control architecture the CAF outcome describes is stepped around rather than broken, and a strong B2 rating coexists with anonymous read access to the Seraph authentication configuration on an instance still running 7.12.2.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Patch applications sets its clocks from vendor severity, and both Atlassian's 5.2 and NVD's 5.3 place this outside the accelerated track that maturity levels reserve for critical ratings. So an application-layer flaw with an EPSS score of 0.99937, public exploit code since October 2021 and a CISA ransomware marking was handled on the routine cycle by an organisation correctly implementing the strategy — the mitigation has no input for observed exploitation, only for the vendor's own score.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.28.gap: Secure coding is a supplier-side control and the consuming organisation holds none of it for a commercial product. The specific defect — the security filter and the static-resource loader normalising the same URL differently once a semicolon path parameter appears — is the class that coding standards, peer review and dependency scanning are worst at surfacing, because each component is individually correct. Nothing an ISO-conformant customer does under A.8.28 would have found it in Confluence 7.12.2, and nothing they do prevents the next instance of it.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Atlassian Confluence Server and Data Center are the case for a KEV-driven clock overriding a CVSS-driven one. The fix existed from 2021-07-21 in 7.4.10 and 7.12.3; the CVSS score is 5.3 and Atlassian's own is 5.2, so nothing in a severity-ranked queue moved it; the EPSS score is 0.99937 and CISA listed it on 2022-03-28 with knownRansomwareCampaignUse marked Known and a 2022-04-18 due date. Applied here the control means the KEV listing, not the score, sets the clock, and completion is measured per Data Center node with the application restarted — a cluster where one node still runs 7.12.2 still answers the request.

new_control_requirements.name: MITIGATION-ACTIVE-PATCH-PENDING-VERDICT-CLASS
new_control_requirements.description: Compliance verdicts must distinguish three states: (a) binary patch deployed (vulnerability eliminated), (b) vendor-mitigation rule active, no binary patch (residual risk: any defect in the mitigation rule reopens the vulnerability), (c) no mitigation, no patch (full exposure). Audit reports must surface (b) as a distinct compensating-control state with an associated time-bound action item, not as a 'patched per SLA' outcome.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Confluence deployments that could not take a version upgrade inside the KEV window typically put a proxy or WAF rule in front that rejects a semicolon path parameter under /s/, and then recorded the finding as closed. That is state (b), and its residual risk is concrete for this CVE: the rule is a pattern block on the exact shape used by Exploit-DB 50377 and the Nuclei template, not a repair of the filter-versus-loader path disagreement, so any re-encoding that the proxy normalises differently reopens the read. The action item that has to stay attached is the upgrade to 7.4.10, 7.12.3 or 7.13.0 with an application restart on every node.

CVE-2021-27852.name: Checkbox Survey Deserialization of Untrusted Data Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: Checkbox Survey 6.x rolls its own view state: CheckboxWeb.dll reads the _VSTATE request argument and reconstructs it with LosFormatter. Because the product handles the blob itself, ASP.NET's ViewState MAC is never applied, so an unauthenticated attacker supplies a crafted serialized object graph and the framework builds it — executing a gadget chain as the IIS application-pool identity. No credential, no machineKey, no user interaction.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; the request is anonymous, and unlike a normal ViewState attack there is no machineKey to recover first because the integrity check is bypassed rather than validated.
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; a single HTTP request with a crafted parameter. The real difficulty in this entry is on the defender's side, not the attacker's: there is no patch for the affected line, so the only levers are migration to 7.x, decommissioning, or removing reachability.
attack_vector.ai_factor: CERT/CC records only that the reporter wished to remain anonymous. Human coordinated disclosure with no vendor research arm involved and no indication of automated discovery; the vendor published no advisory, so CERT/CC published in its place.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Removing Checkbox Survey 6.x from service, or migrating to 7.0 or later where view state no longer exists. Before that lands, taking the survey application off any internet-reachable path, since the whole exploit is one unauthenticated request to a published endpoint.
prevention.adequacy: Migration to 7.x is a project with data-migration and survey-rewrite costs, which is exactly why installs persisted. Reachability restriction contradicts the product's purpose for public-facing surveys, and rotating the machineKey — the reflex answer for ViewState problems — accomplishes nothing here because the MAC is never evaluated on this path.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alerting on any child process spawned by the w3wp.exe worker pool serving the survey site, and on unexpected file writes under the Checkbox web directory. Both are process- and file-level signals that do not depend on recognising the payload, which matters because the request itself looks like a normal parameterised POST.
detection.adequacy: It catches the second stage rather than the deserialization, and it needs endpoint telemetry on an IIS host that in many estates is a low-attention application server. Nothing in the request shape reliably distinguishes a malicious _VSTATE from a legitimate one, so request-level detection is not a substitute.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating any confirmed exploitation as full compromise of the IIS host: rebuild rather than clean, rotate the application-pool identity's credentials and anything that identity could reach, and use the incident as the trigger for the decommissioning decision the KEV requiredAction already mandated.
response.adequacy: Rebuild is the only defensible outcome after arbitrary code execution as the pool identity, and it is complicated here by there being nowhere safe to rebuild to — restoring a 6.x install restores the vulnerability, so the response and the remediation are the same project.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: Flaw remediation is fully implemented and has nothing to deploy. Checkbox stopped developing version 6, so a CVSS 9.8 unauthenticated deserialization RCE reported as exploited in the wild in May 2021 produces an open SI-2 finding that can only ever be closed by risk acceptance. CISA had to write a non-standard KEV requiredAction — remove versions 6 and earlier from agency networks — because the control framework itself has no state in which the remediation is deletion of the asset.

NIST-800-53-SR-3.gap: Supply chain controls and processes were satisfied at procurement and never re-tested against the supplier's actual support posture. The organisation held a live vendor relationship for a product line the vendor had already stopped developing, and found that out from CERT/CC's VU#706695 rather than from its own supplier review — which is the concrete failure, because knowing the 6.x line was abandoned would have converted this from a patch-management item into a migration project before a critical flaw arrived.

NIST-800-53-CM-7.gap: Least functionality is normally evidenced at the Windows host level — services disabled, ports closed, roles minimised — and the attacker never touches that layer. The functionality that needed restricting is the publication of the survey application itself, because a single unauthenticated request to a published Checkbox endpoint is the entire exploit. A CM-7 attestation on a benchmarked IIS host reads clean while the vulnerable site is reachable from the internet.

NIS2-Art21-supply-chain.gap: The supply-chain measures required by Article 21 look at the relationship with the supplier, not at whether the specific version in service is still maintained. For Checkbox Survey 6.x those two diverged: the relationship was intact and the product was abandoned. An essential entity operating this in 2022 needed CISA's 2022-04-11 listing to state that versions 6 and earlier must be removed — a supplier-support fact its own supply-chain process should have surfaced first.

UK-CAF-A1.gap: Governance is where this one actually lives, because with no fix available the decision is budgetary: fund the migration to 7.x, or fund the removal. CAF A1 evidence is typically policy documents and a risk register, and a register entry for a KEV-listed unfixable CVSS 9.8 with a review date and no removal date is a governance outcome that keeps the exposure in service indefinitely. Nothing in A1 forces a no-fix KEV entry to become a dated decommissioning commitment.

AU-Essential-8-App-Hardening.gap: User application hardening addresses workstation software — browser, Office, PDF, Java, ads — and Checkbox Survey 6.x is a server-side ASP.NET application in IIS. The exploit is an anonymous HTTP request to that server and involves no workstation, no macro and no browser component, so an organisation at the top maturity level for this mitigation has done nothing that touches CheckboxWeb.dll's unauthenticated LosFormatter path. The strategy is well implemented and structurally out of scope.

ISO-27001-2022-A.5.21.gap: Managing information security in the ICT supply chain is evidenced through supplier agreements and periodic review, and none of those instruments has a trigger for a vendor quietly ceasing development of a major version. Here the organisation's supplier control produced no signal at all: the abandonment of the 6.x line reached it as a CERT/CC coordination note in May 2021 and as a CISA removal instruction in April 2022, after in-the-wild exploitation had already been reported.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Checkbox Survey 6.x is the case where the control's 'documented compensating controls' clause is the only branch available, because the patch branch does not exist — the vendor stopped developing version 6 and CISA's 2022-04-11 KEV entry sets a requiredAction of removal rather than update, with a 2022-05-02 due date. Applied to this product the control means the four-hour clock buys an immediate reachability decision: pull the survey site off every internet-facing binding and restrict it to an authenticated segment on the day of listing, record that as the compensating control with the migration or decommissioning date attached, and never let it stand as the closure. Rotating the machineKey must not be accepted as the mitigation, because the ViewState MAC is bypassed on the _VSTATE path rather than validated.

new_control_requirements.name: EOL-ASSET-DECOMMISSION
new_control_requirements.description: This entry is the case the control exists for, and both halves are on record. patch_available is true — a fixed build carrying this JavaScriptCore fix exists — and the vector itself states that the impacted product could be end-of-life and/or end-of-service and that users should discontinue product utilization. Those facts together define the requirement: on a unit whose hardware can still take an Apple security update, reaching the fixed build is an interim state; on a unit that can no longer take one, the terminal state is removal or replacement, because that device is exposed not only to this code-execution flaw but to everything found in that engine since its last build. Scope to what the packet names — macOS, iOS, tvOS, Safari and watchOS — and inventory those. The packet ties the CWE-94 sink to JavaScriptCore in those products and gives no mapping into other vendors' browsers or other software that embeds a web engine, so treating every renderer in the estate as an instance of this CVE manufactures findings and replacement work against software no evidence implicates. In operational terms: enumerate every macOS, iOS, tvOS, watchOS and Safari install that renders untrusted web content, record for each whether its hardware can still receive a build carrying the fix, put those on the interim clock against the 2025-10-20 KEV listing, and put the rest on a dated replacement schedule — a risk acceptance with no removal date leaves a KEV-listed flaw with a public PoC and confirmed exploitation in service indefinitely. Precondition on the interim half: live_patch_available is false and the vendor patch typically requires a service restart or system reboot per the KEV requiredAction, so a device that downloaded the update but has not restarted still runs the vulnerable code and is not remediated. And because exploitation is confirmed and delivery is attacker-controlled web content, a device that rendered untrusted content while exposed belongs on the incident path rather than being closed on the patch record.
new_control_requirements.evidence: For Checkbox Survey there is no interim half at all, which is what makes the decommissioning requirement absolute rather than conditional. CERT/CC VU#706695 records that Checkbox is no longer developing version 6, so no build carrying a fix exists for the affected line; version 7.0 removed view state from the product entirely and is a migration target, not an update. CISA said the same thing in its own words on 2022-04-11: versions 6 and earlier are end-of-life and must be removed from agency networks, due 2022-05-02. The inventory to produce is every Windows host with CheckboxWeb.dll at a 6.x product version, with its IIS bindings and application-pool identity recorded, and each entry needs a dated migration-or-removal commitment — a risk acceptance with no removal date leaves a CVSS 9.8 unauthenticated deserialization RCE, reported exploited in the wild since May 2021, answering anonymous requests indefinitely.

attack_vector.description: HBS 3 shipped with a credential compiled into the application instead of provisioned per device. Anyone who could reach the appliance's login surface authenticated as that account without holding anything the owner issued, and QNAP's fix was to remove the account. Qlocker used that access to enumerate shares, move their contents into password-protected 7z archives, delete snapshots and leave ransom notes — encrypting the primary data and its backups in one session.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; the attacker presents an identity the vendor built into the product, so no credential theft, phishing or brute force precedes it and no per-device secret is involved.
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; the attack is a login, not an exploit. Reach is the only variable, and NAS appliances acquire internet reach through owner-side conveniences such as port-forwarding and UPnP rather than through a firewall decision anyone reviews.
attack_vector.ai_factor: Found by ZUSO ART, an outside human research firm, and credited in QNAP's QSA-21-13 acknowledgements. Locating an embedded credential is static product review; no automated or AI-assisted discovery is claimed or evidenced.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Updating HBS 3 through App Center to the fixed build for the running line — v16.0.0415, v3.0.210412, v3.0.210411 or v16.0.0419 — from 2021-04-22, and keeping the appliance's administrative and SSH surfaces off the internet by removing port-forwards and disabling UPnP mappings on the router in front of it.
prevention.adequacy: The update removes the account and is quick, but it is driven from the device's own App Center rather than any enterprise patch system, so it depends on someone logging into each NAS. Reachability restriction bounds who can attempt the login and is unavailable where the appliance is deliberately published for remote access — and for QuTScloud it is not available at all.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alerting on any successful authentication to the appliance by a name absent from its own user list, and on snapshot deletion outside a retention schedule — the second is the step that removes the recovery path and precedes the owner discovering the encryption.
detection.adequacy: Both signals live on the appliance, which in most affected estates forwards nothing to a collector, so the telemetry existed and nobody was reading it. Detection would have bounded the damage rather than prevented it: by the time the archiving is observable, the snapshots are usually already gone.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating an affected appliance as compromised rather than as patched: update HBS 3, then rebuild its configuration from a known-good baseline, rotate every credential stored on or used through it, and recover data from a copy that was never reachable from the same login surface.
response.adequacy: The last clause is the hard one, because for many owners no such copy existed — Qlocker deleted the snapshots on the same device. Rotation and rebuild are achievable; the recovery step depends on a design decision that had to be made before the incident.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: Flaw remediation was available from QSA-21-13 on 2021-04-22 and CISA did not list the CVE until 2022-03-31, so the whole Qlocker campaign fell inside a period when the fix existed and the KEV clock had not started. SI-2's deeper problem for this asset is delivery: HBS 3 updates arrive through the QTS App Center on the device, outside every enterprise patch pipeline, so an SI-2 coverage figure is computed over the estate the tooling can see and the NAS holding the backups is not in it.

NIST-800-53-IA-2.gap: Identification and authentication is implemented for every account the organisation created, and the account exploited here was created by the vendor and compiled into HBS 3. It appears in no directory, cannot be disabled, rotated or recertified at the site, and does not surface in the appliance user list an IA-2 assessor would review. The control is genuinely met against its own scope and the scope is the problem — it never contemplates an identity the operator did not issue and cannot remove.

NIST-800-53-SC-7.gap: Boundary protection is attested against firewall rule sets and network diagrams, and NAS exposure is not created there. It arrives through a router port-forward set up so someone could reach their files from home, through a UPnP mapping the appliance requested itself, or through a vendor remote-access service — none of which appears in the change record an SC-7 review reads. QuTScloud c4.5.1 through c4.5.4 makes the point sharper still: those instances are externally reachable by deployment model, so there is no boundary to draw.

NIS2-Art21-identity-management.gap: The identity-management measures required under Article 21 operate on accounts the entity administers, and the account that admitted Qlocker was administered by QNAP and deleted by a QNAP update. An entity with complete access recertification, privileged-account review and joiner-mover-leaver discipline over its NAS estate had all of it bypassed, because nothing in those processes enumerates identities embedded in supplied software — and nothing in the obligation requires testing an appliance for them.

UK-CAF-B5.gap: Resilient networks and systems is normally evidenced by backup coverage and successful restore tests, and this incident is that evidence being satisfied by the very configuration that failed. The NAS was the backup, so when the embedded credential admitted the attacker, the archiving of the shares and the deletion of the snapshots removed the primary copy and the recovery copy in one session on one device. B5 as assessed does not ask whether the backup shares an authentication surface and a failure domain with what it protects.

AU-Essential-8-MFA.gap: Multi-factor authentication is the reflex compensating control for any credential-based attack and it has no purchase on this one. The HBS 3 account is not enrolled by the owner, so there is no enrolment point at which a second factor attaches, and it authenticates outside the policy scope the owner's MFA configuration governs. An estate at the top maturity level for this mitigation, with MFA on every account it knows exists, was still admitted — the credential belonged to the application rather than to a person.

AU-Essential-8-Backup.gap: Regular backups was implemented, and for most affected owners the QNAP appliance was the entire implementation. Qlocker archived the shares into password-protected 7z files and removed the snapshots in the same operation, so both copies died together. The maturity levels ask about backup frequency, retention periods and restoration testing, and a deployment can answer all three correctly while keeping the only copy on a single internet-reachable appliance whose authentication the owner did not control.

ISO-27001-2022-A.5.15.gap: Access control is implemented against the organisation's documented access rules, and this credential exists outside them entirely. Every artefact the audit collects — the policy, the rule set, the periodic review of who may reach the NAS — is generated from identities the organisation issued, so an account compiled into HBS 3 v16.0.0414 leaves no trace in any of them. Conformity is real and the finding is structural: A.5.15 never asks whether a supplied appliance admits anyone the organisation did not create.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: The QNAP HBS 3 case shows why the control's clock runs from patch availability and not only from the KEV listing: QNAP published QSA-21-13 with fixed builds on 2021-04-22, the Qlocker campaign that QSA-21-12 attributes to this CVE began the week of 2021-04-19 and extorted roughly $350,000 within a month, and CISA did not list the CVE until 2022-03-31 with a 2022-04-21 due date. An organisation running the clock from the KEV entry was eleven months late. Applied to this product the control means each appliance is driven to the fixed HBS 3 build for its own line — v16.0.0415, v3.0.210412, v3.0.210411 or v16.0.0419 — with completion measured from the installed application version on the device, because the App Center update is per-appliance and no enterprise patch console reports it.

new_control_requirements.name: PERIMETER-COMPROMISE-REBUILD-NOT-PATCH
new_control_requirements.description: Pre-rehearsed IR runbook for any perimeter device that suffers a pre-auth RCE CVE in active exploitation MUST default to config-exfil + rebuild + credential rotation, not patch-in-place. Patch-in-place leaves attacker-installed implants intact.
new_control_requirements.evidence: A QNAP NAS published through a router port-forward, a UPnP mapping or a QuTScloud deployment is a perimeter device in every sense that matters here, and the access this CVE granted was interactive rather than function-limited — QNAP confirmed the embedded HBS 3 account was abused by Qlocker from the week of 2021-04-19. Updating HBS 3 to v16.0.0415 or v16.0.0419 removes the account and nothing else: it does not evict a session, remove anything written to the appliance, or restore shares already moved into 7z archives with the snapshots deleted. So for any unit that was externally reachable while running a pre-fix HBS 3 build, the default has to be exporting the configuration for review, rebuilding the appliance, rotating every credential stored on or used through it, and recovering from a copy that never shared that login surface.

CVE-2021-30883.name: Apple Multiple Products Memory Corruption Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: An application running inside the sandbox calls external method 78 on AppleCLCD with operands chosen so that the driver's 32-bit allocation-size calculation wraps. The undersized allocation is then written past its end, corrupting adjacent kernel heap objects, and the application ends up executing with kernel privileges. The same driver ships across iOS, iPadOS, macOS, tvOS and watchOS, so one defect crosses every Apple platform in the fleet.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none in CVSS terms — PR:N with UI:R, meaning no account or elevation is needed but the victim must run the attacker's application. Operationally the precondition is code execution at app level on the device, which in the observed use came from an earlier stage of a chain rather than from the user installing something.
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; the overflow is arithmetic the caller controls outright, with no race and no information leak needed to reach it. What the public artefact does not supply is the heap grooming that turns reliable corruption into a stable escalation, so the difference between a panic and a working chain is engineering effort rather than luck.
attack_vector.ai_factor: None evidenced. Apple credits the issue to an anonymous researcher and reports separately that it may have been actively exploited, so the finder is unnamed and the route unstated; the public analysis that established the mechanism came afterwards from manual reverse engineering of Apple's patch.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Driving every Apple device onto its fixed build and confirming the restart: iOS/iPadOS 15.0.2 or 14.8.1, macOS 12.0.1 or 11.6.1, tvOS 15.1, watchOS 8.1 — with the fixed build enforced as an access condition for organisational mail, VPN and documents rather than tracked as a dashboard row.
prevention.adequacy: There is no partial credit and no fallback: no setting disables IOMobileFrameBuffer, no live patch exists, and the update is inert until restart — a step that on personally owned handsets the operator can encourage but not compel. Devices whose hardware no longer receives Apple updates cannot reach any fixed build at all, and for those the only honest control is replacement.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Collecting panic logs from managed Macs and treating repeated IOMobileFrameBuffer or AppleCLCD panics as a security signal, and reconciling reported build numbers against the fixed releases at every check-in so a device stuck at 'downloaded' is visible as still exposed.
detection.adequacy: This is thin by design, because the platform gives almost nothing to work with: no endpoint agent on iOS, no network artefact from the exploit, and no indicators published by Apple. It detects failure rather than success, and on the phone population — where the fleet mostly lives — it does not apply at all.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating a device suspected of running the attacker's application as an incident rather than a patch item: get it onto the fixed build and restarted, then rotate the credentials, tokens and certificates that lived on it, because kernel-level execution means anything the device held is assumed read.
response.adequacy: Scoping is close to impossible with no indicators and no on-device forensics available for iOS, so response degrades to credential rotation and device replacement on suspicion. That is expensive enough that it is usually skipped, which is why the prevention branch carries essentially the whole defence here.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: Flaw remediation is reported from the device-management console in states the console can observe — approved, downloaded, installed — and the state that ends the exposure is booted onto the fixed kernel, which it cannot. A handset holding iOS 15.0.2 and still running the prior build produces clean SI-2 evidence with the vulnerable IOMobileFrameBuffer resident. The six-build spread across iOS 15, iOS 14, Monterey, Big Sur, tvOS and watchOS compounds it: one fleet-level percentage cannot say which lines were actually driven.

NIST-800-53-SI-3.gap: Malicious code protection is implemented where the platform allows an agent — the Macs — and satisfied for iPhones and iPads by citing app review and the application sandbox. That reasoning collapses on this specific CVE, because the sandbox is what the flaw escapes: a malicious application reaching AppleCLCD external method 78 ends with kernel privileges, so the control's stated compensating mechanism for the largest part of the estate is the boundary the vulnerability removes.

NIST-800-53-SI-4.gap: System monitoring is genuinely mature in most estates and reaches none of this. iOS and iPadOS expose no host telemetry to collect, the exploit is entirely on-device and generates no traffic, and Apple released no indicators with the exploitation report, so there was nothing to write a rule against. The one observable — a kernel panic on a device below iOS 15.0.2 — arrives through a helpdesk ticket about instability rather than through any SI-4 channel.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: The patch obligation is satisfied by an entity that has a policy, a management platform and an update ring, and none of those completes the remediation on a phone: the fix begins at restart and the restart belongs to the user. Apple shipped on 2021-10-11 and CISA listed on 2022-05-23, and across that span an essential entity could report full compliance while a material fraction of its handsets ran the vulnerable kernel with the update sitting downloaded.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: Secure configuration and maintenance is the outcome, and for this CVE there was no configuration lever at all — no profile setting disables IOMobileFrameBuffer and no baseline removes external method 78 from a sandboxed app's reach. So CAF evidence assembled from configuration profiles and compliance policies is accurate and irrelevant, and the whole weight of B4 falls on getting the fixed build installed and restarted on devices whose restart the operator frequently cannot enforce.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Patch operating systems measures the interval from vendor release to deployment and stops there, so a fleet scored at a high maturity level on the strength of fast deployment of iOS 15.0.2 gets no penalty for devices that never restarted onto it. The strategy also assumes one operating system per device class, while this defect needed six builds — and the tvOS 15.1 and watchOS 8.1 populations are usually missing from the asset register the score is computed over.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: Technical-vulnerability management runs from an asset inventory, and the inventory is where this CVE escapes. Apple TVs and Apple Watches carry the same driver and are rarely enrolled; bring-your-own iPhones report a compliance verdict rather than a build number. The register therefore shows the managed iPhone estate assessed against iOS 15.0.2 and says nothing at all about the tvOS and watchOS devices that needed 15.1 and 8.1 — a scope failure that reads on the report as coverage.

ENISA-mobile-secure-baseline.gap: The baseline's measures — device configuration, application provenance, work-personal data separation — all assume the sandbox holds, and this CVE is the sandbox not holding. App vetting and installation restrictions narrow how the attacker's application arrives and do nothing once it is running, since the escalation is a legitimate IOKit call with hostile arguments; and none of the baseline's configuration controls reduces the reachable surface of IOMobileFrameBuffer on a device below iOS 15.0.2.

new_control_requirements.name: MOBILE-ENDPOINT-MDM-ENFORCED-KEV-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: iOS / iPadOS / macOS estates must enforce KEV-class updates within 24h via DDM; user-deferral disallowed.
new_control_requirements.evidence: This Apple defect is the case the control is written for, and it also shows where the control has to be measured more carefully than it is usually implemented. One CVE spans iOS/iPadOS 15.0.2, iOS/iPadOS 14.8.1, macOS Monterey 12.0.1, macOS Big Sur 11.6.1, tvOS 15.1 and watchOS 8.1, so a declarative-management policy that drives only the current iOS line leaves the devices held back on 14 and the Macs on Big Sur running the same vulnerable IOMobileFrameBuffer. Because there is no live-patch path and the fix takes effect only at restart, compliance has to be measured from the build the device reports after rebooting rather than from the update's deployment state — a handset showing iOS 15.0.2 as downloaded is not remediated. Apple shipped on 2021-10-11 and CISA's clock did not open until 2022-05-23, so the deferral-disallowed half is what closes the window this fleet actually lost.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: The whichever-is-later clause is what makes this control correct for CVE-2021-30883 rather than seven months late. Apple published the fixed builds on 2021-10-11 with the statement that the issue may have been actively exploited, and CISA did not list it until 2022-05-23 with a 2022-06-13 due date; an organisation that ran its clock from the KEV entry left a kernel escalation reachable from the app sandbox in service across that entire period. Applied to this fleet the control also has to name what the compensating-controls branch can and cannot be: there is no setting that disables IOMobileFrameBuffer and no live patch on any Apple platform, so the only defensible interim measure is withholding organisational data and access from devices below the fixed build, and devices whose hardware can no longer receive an Apple update are replacement items rather than exceptions.

CVE-2021-31166.name: Microsoft HTTP Protocol Stack Remote Code Execution Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: A single unauthenticated HTTP request with a malformed Accept-Encoding value — an empty element between commas — drives http.sys down a path that frees the parsed content-coding entries while a stack-resident LIST_ENTRY root still points at them. The dangling pointers are dereferenced in kernel mode, producing at minimum a bugcheck and at most kernel code execution. Every service terminating HTTP through http.sys is a route to the same driver, IIS and WinRM alike.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; no account, session or cookie, and the request is a well-formed HTTP transaction with one malformed header, so nothing needs to be obtained from the target first.
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L for the crash. Reaching code execution instead of a bugcheck needs kernel pool grooming that no public artefact performs, which is why the Metasploit module ships under auxiliary/dos. Wormability is the property that matters operationally: no user interaction, no credential, so propagation needs no operator on either end.
attack_vector.ai_factor: Found internally by the Microsoft Platform Security and Vulnerability Research team per ZDI's analysis, which is why the advisory carries no external credit. Manual vendor research; the trigger and the Metasploit module were written by outside researchers after the patch shipped.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Installing the May 2021 cumulative update KB5003173 on every Windows 10 and Server host on the 2004 or 20H2 branch and rebooting, then continuing to service that branch so the January 2022 update lands too. Before the reboot, restricting reach to every port registered through the HTTP Server API — enumerated on the host, not inferred from whether IIS is installed.
prevention.adequacy: The update is complete and there is no live-patch alternative, so the whole control depends on the reboot landing. The reachability measure genuinely bounds the attacker population but is often unavailable in practice, because the ports involved are the management ports the estate needs open across segments.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Treating a KERNEL_SECURITY_CHECK_FAILURE bugcheck on an affected build as a security event and routing it to the security function, and alerting on Accept-Encoding headers containing an empty element at any reverse proxy or load balancer in front of the affected hosts.
detection.adequacy: The header signature is precise because the public tooling all uses it, but it only helps where traffic passes an inspecting device — and WinRM on 5985 usually does not. The bugcheck signal is reliable and arrives after the fact; it is worth most as the tripwire that reveals a wormable attempt spreading, which is exactly the pattern a single-host stability ticket conceals.

response.what_would_have_worked: On a confirmed crash cluster, patching and rebooting the whole 2004/20H2 population rather than the machines that fell over, and reviewing the management segment's reachability — because with no credential involved, the propagation set is defined by which hosts could receive the request, not by which accounts were used.
response.adequacy: Scoping by reachability is achievable and unusually reliable here since there is no authentication to trace. Where the attempt reached code execution rather than a bugcheck there is no artefact at all, so a host that stayed up cannot be cleared on the absence of a crash.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: Flaw remediation deployed KB5003173 on schedule and the vulnerable http.sys kept running on every host that had not rebooted, because the fix is a kernel-mode driver replacement. The control's per-CVE framing compounds it: a machine that took the May 2021 update, closed this finding and stayed on the 2004/20H2 branch without the January 2022 update is exploitable again on the same content-coding path through CVE-2022-21907, with a clean remediation record for CVE-2021-31166.

NIST-800-53-SC-7.gap: Boundary protection is implemented and scoped to the wrong assets. Operators bound the exposure to hosts they consider web servers, when the defect lives in a kernel driver shared by every consumer of the HTTP Server API — so a machine with no IIS role but a WinRM listener on 5985 is equally exploitable. The firewall policy that satisfies SC-7 typically permits management traffic broadly across the server estate, which is precisely the path this request travels.

NIST-800-53-CM-7.gap: Least functionality is assessed against installed roles, features and services, and none of those views answers the question this CVE poses: what is currently registered through http.sys on this host. WinRM passes any CM-7 review as required management functionality, and management agents register URL prefixes without appearing as a role at all, so a host correctly minimised by every CM-7 criterion still terminates HTTP in the kernel and remains reachable through the vulnerable parser.

NIS2-Art21-network-security.gap: Article 21's network-security measures are satisfied by zone segmentation and traffic control between business functions, and this defect propagates inside the management plane those zones all share. The request carries no credential, so none of the identity controls paired with the segmentation are consulted; and because the bug is wormable, one reached host on the 2004 or 20H2 branch turns permitted management connectivity into a propagation path with no operator action at either end.

UK-CAF-C1.gap: Security monitoring is in place with SIEM coverage and a use-case library, and the one event this CVE reliably generates is not in it. A KERNEL_SECURITY_CHECK_FAILURE bugcheck on a Windows Server is triaged by infrastructure as a driver or hardware fault and closed there, so a wormable pre-authentication kernel bug being probed across the estate presents to the organisation as a run of unrelated stability tickets rather than as the correlated exploitation signal C1 exists to surface.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Patch operating systems measures deployment latency from release and stops there, so a host that installed KB5003173 within the maturity window and never rebooted scores as compliant while running the vulnerable driver. The affected population is also defined by servicing branch — 2004 and 20H2 — rather than by product, and an aggregate operating-system patching figure cannot show which machines were on those branches, so neither the exposure nor the remediation is visible at the granularity the strategy reports.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.22.gap: Network segregation conforms and is drawn between user, server and perimeter zones, while the reachable surface for this bug is the management ports that segregation intentionally leaves open across those zones. Since the request needs no credential, nothing in the access controls layered on top of the segmentation constrains it, so a conforming design with a management VLAN spanning the server estate hands a wormable http.sys defect exactly the lateral reach the control was meant to deny.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Microsoft shipped KB5003173 on 2021-05-11 and CISA listed this on 2022-04-06 with a 2022-04-27 due date, so the patch-availability branch of the clock is the one that governs — eleven months earlier than the KEV branch, for a wormable pre-authentication kernel defect with a public trigger and a Metasploit module. Applied to Windows 10 and Server 2004/20H2 the control means completion is measured from the host's installed build after a reboot, because http.sys is a kernel-mode driver and an installed-not-rebooted host still runs the vulnerable parser. The compensating-controls branch has one concrete form here and it must be stated as a port list rather than a role list: restrict reach to every URL prefix registered through the HTTP Server API, including WinRM on 5985, not only IIS bindings.

new_control_requirements.name: INCOMPLETE-PATCH-SEQUENCE-SEVERITY-MULTIPLIER
new_control_requirements.description: Vulnerability-management programs must apply a severity multiplier when a CVE is the Nth in an incomplete-patch sequence on the same primitive (third MOTW bypass, second AMSI bypass, etc.). Framework controls treating each CVE as discrete obscure the structural defect; the Nth CVE in a sequence implies that future bypasses on the same primitive are likely.
new_control_requirements.evidence: http.sys content-coding parsing is a documented sequence, not a one-off. CVE-2021-31166 was patched in May 2021, and CVE-2022-21907 landed eight months later on the same parsing path — researchers reproducing the second found the crash identical to the first, reached through HTTP trailers rather than through the empty Accept-Encoding element. An organisation that treated the May 2021 fix as closing 'the http.sys bug' and left hosts on the 2004/20H2 branch unserviced was exposed again on the same primitive with a clean record for this CVE. The multiplier means an http.sys parsing defect on that branch is triaged as a recurring structural weakness in a kernel-mode network parser reachable without authentication, with continued servicing of the branch as part of the remediation rather than a separate ticket.

attack_vector.description: Running sudoedit -s sets MODE_EDIT and MODE_SHELL together and skips the escaping guard, so an argument ending in a single backslash makes set_cmnd()'s unescape loop step past the argument's NUL terminator and copy uncounted bytes into user_args. The attacker controls the length and content of the resulting heap overflow, and the whole sequence completes before sudoers is consulted — so no sudo rights and no password are needed to reach root.
attack_vector.privileges_required: low — PR:L; any local account is sufficient, including one deliberately kept out of sudoers and including a service account used only by automation, because the policy file is never read on this path.
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L to trigger; the difficulty is per-target heap layout rather than the bug itself. Qualys demonstrated Ubuntu 20.04 with sudo 1.8.31, Debian 10 with 1.8.27 and Fedora 33 with 1.9.2, and NCC Group had to rebuild the technique for vCenter 7.0 because Photon OS 3.0's glibc 2.28 disables tcache.
attack_vector.ai_factor: Human source audit by the Qualys Research Team, disclosed 2021-01-26 on a decade-old code path introduced in July 2011. No AI-assisted discovery is claimed, and the follow-on exploit work — Exploit-DB 49521, the Metasploit module, the vCenter adaptation — is manual engineering.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Upgrading sudo to the distribution's fixed package — the change takes effect on the next invocation with no reboot or restart — and separately driving the appliance and container-image population to vendor-updated builds, since sudo bundled inside a vCenter Server 7.0 or similar image is not reachable from any package channel the operator drives.
prevention.adequacy: On managed hosts this is about as clean as remediation gets: zero availability cost and immediate effect. It is entirely inadequate for the bundled population, where the operator has no lever at all until the vendor ships, and there is no sudo configuration that substitutes — hardening sudoers does not help because the overflow precedes the policy check.

detection.what_would_have_worked: auditd rules on execution of sudoedit — an uncommon binary in most estates, which makes it low-noise — flagging invocations with -s or with arguments ending in a backslash, and alerting on sudo or sudoedit crashes and malloc corruption messages, which is what a failed heap-layout attempt produces.
detection.adequacy: The trigger is unusually specific and cheap to watch for, which makes this better than most LPE detection. Its limit is that a successful escalation leaves no authorisation record to correlate with, since sudoers is never consulted, so a clean first attempt produces nothing but the resulting root process.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating a confirmed escalation as full host compromise — rebuild, and rotate every credential, key and token that lived on the host — and then re-scoping: any account with shell access on an unpatched host was a root-capable account, so the exposure window covers every service account and automation identity, not just interactive users.
response.adequacy: Scoping is broader than teams expect and that is the value of doing it explicitly. The weakness is evidentiary: with no sudo grant logged and the exploit leaving no persistent artefact of its own, a host cannot be cleared by the absence of evidence, only by the absence of the vulnerable package.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: Flaw remediation reaches everything the package manager owns and nothing else, and this CVE's residual risk lives entirely in the remainder. Distribution backports mean the reported sudo version does not compare meaningfully against upstream 1.9.5p2, so scanner output needs per-distribution interpretation; and the sudo 1.8.30-1.ph3 inside a vCenter Server 7.0 appliance has no package channel at all, so an SI-2 report showing full coverage can coexist with a root escalation available on the virtualization control plane.

NIST-800-53-AC-6.gap: Least privilege on a Unix host is implemented through sudo, and this defect makes the implementation irrelevant rather than weak. set_cmnd() overflows before sudoers is parsed, so an account intentionally excluded from sudoers reaches root by the same path as an administrator, and every artefact the control produces — sudoers review records, privileged-account inventories, approval workflows — documents decisions the vulnerable code never consults. The control is fully attested and provides no reduction in exploitability whatsoever.

NIST-800-53-SR-3.gap: Supply chain controls enumerate suppliers rather than components, so sudo — acquired incidentally inside virtualization appliances, management platforms and container base images — never appears as an item with its own remediation owner. VMware vCenter Server 7.0 makes it concrete: the operator bought a hypervisor management platform and received sudo 1.8.30-1.ph3 on Photon OS 3.0, which NCC Group showed escalating from vsphere-ui to root, and no SR-3 artefact in the organisation names that binary.

NIS2-Art21-vulnerability-management.gap: Vulnerability management is in place and its triage rule is severity-first, which puts a local escalation scoring 7.8 behind remote findings — despite an EPSS score of 0.99295 and a Metasploit exploit module available since February 2021. The obligation has no notion of chaining, so the remote-access finding and the local-root finding are worked as unrelated tickets when their combination is the actual risk: on an unpatched host, every foothold anywhere in the estate is a root foothold.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: Secure configuration evidence for Unix hosts leans heavily on sudoers — least-privilege command lists, password requirements, NOPASSWD review — and none of it constrains this flaw, because the escalation completes before the policy file is read. A CAF submission demonstrating an exemplary sudoers regime describes a control the exploit walks past, so the entire B4 outcome for this CVE rests on the maintenance half, which must extend to appliance images the organisation cannot patch itself.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Patch operating systems is scoped to the operating systems the organisation patches, and sudo's most dangerous instances are the ones it does not: bundled inside a vCenter Server 7.0 appliance, inside network and storage management virtual machines, inside container base images that are rebuilt rather than patched. An estate at the highest maturity level for this mitigation, measured over its server and workstation fleet, can still be running sudo 1.8.30 on the appliance that administers its entire virtual infrastructure.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: Technical-vulnerability management identifies this quickly on scanned hosts and misreports at both ends. Backported fixes leave patched Debian and Red Hat systems reporting sudo versions below 1.9.5p2, producing findings that are not real; appliances reporting sudo 1.8.30-1.ph3 are usually outside scan scope, producing an absence that is not safety. The register renders both as version numbers of equal standing, with nothing recording which of them the organisation can actually act on.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: sudo is the case where a four-hour clock is genuinely achievable and the organisation still has to decide what to do about the part it cannot reach. Qualys disclosed on 2021-01-26 with distribution fixes coordinated for the same day, CISA listed on 2022-04-06 with a 2022-04-27 due date, and the package upgrade takes effect on the next sudo invocation with no reboot and no service restart — so on managed Linux hosts there is no availability argument for deferral at all. The clause that has to be exercised deliberately is the compensating-controls one, for hosts where sudo arrives inside a vendor image such as vCenter Server 7.0's sudo 1.8.30-1.ph3: hardening sudoers is not a compensating control here because the overflow precedes the policy check, so the only real interim measure is removing local shell access from the appliance until the vendor image ships.

new_control_requirements.name: TIER-3-DEPENDENCY-INVENTORY
new_control_requirements.description: Supply chain inventory must extend to tier-3 dependencies (dependencies of dependencies of direct dependencies). SBOM coverage for libsystemd-class transitive dependencies cannot be omitted under SR-3.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Baron Samedit is the non-language-ecosystem form of the same omission: sudo is nobody's declared dependency and it is inside almost everything. The organisation's inventory names VMware vCenter Server 7.0, and what is actually deployed is a Photon OS 3.0 image carrying sudo 1.8.30-1.ph3, which NCC Group demonstrated escalating from the vsphere-ui account to root. The same applies to storage and network management appliances and to container base images. The requirement here is that the component inventory record the sudo version inside every vendor-supplied image and container base in service, alongside the packages the operating-system channel owns, so that a CVE affecting sudo 1.8.2 through 1.8.31p2 and 1.9.0 through 1.9.5p1 produces a remediation owner for each of those images rather than a clean scan over the hosts that happen to be scannable.

CVE-2021-34484.name: Microsoft Windows User Profile Service Privilege Escalation Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: An unprivileged local user swaps a directory in the temporary profile the User Profile Service is building for a junction, so the SYSTEM-context copy follows the link and creates a writable directory in a protected location; that write is then used to get code running as SYSTEM. Microsoft's first fix blocked the reported proof of concept rather than the link-following behaviour, so the primitive returned twice more under new CVE identifiers.
attack_vector.privileges_required: low — PR:L; an ordinary interactive logon is enough, and the reported exploit path needs valid account credentials because the vulnerable code only runs while a profile is being created at logon
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; there is a race, but it re-arms on every logon so the attacker simply retries. The vendor draws no distinction between code bases here: Microsoft's August 2021 exploitability index rates both 'Latest Software Release' and 'Older Software Release' as Exploitation Less Likely, so Windows 7 SP1, 8.1 and Server 2008 through 2012 R2 are not a lower-priority population than the Windows 10 and Server 2016-2019 line.
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Abdelhamid Naceri found this by reading the User Profile Service and then read Microsoft's patched binary to show the fix was incomplete — manual reverse engineering, with no AI tooling claimed by the researcher, by Microsoft, or in any of the coverage.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Taking the August 2021 cumulative update and then the January 2022 and April 2022 updates on the same hosts, measured against the fixed build number for each SKU rather than against update-approval state — because only the third of those closes the junction primitive.
prevention.adequacy: BOD 22-01 gave a due date of 2022-04-21 against a CVE whose vendor fix had already been publicly bypassed for six months, so an agency that met the date on this identifier alone was still exposed. Prevention here also cannot help the largest affected population any more: every Windows line named in the advisory has passed end of support, so for those hosts the preventive control is replacement.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alerting on reparse-point creation under C:\Users by a non-administrative process, and on SYSTEM-context writes by the User Profile Service that land outside the profile tree.
detection.adequacy: Junction creation is a legitimate operation and profile directories change on every logon, so this rule carries real noise on a session host — which is exactly where the exploit's precondition is normal. It also fires after the write primitive already exists, so it bounds the window rather than preventing the escalation.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating a host that ran an unpatched build with ordinary interactive users as a SYSTEM-compromise candidate: audit for content planted in the paths the junction can reach and rotate credentials that were used on that host during the exposure window.
response.adequacy: The update removes the primitive and removes nothing already written through it, so a host closed on the patch record alone can still carry an attacker-placed file in a privileged path. Against this CVE that judgement has to be made without campaign attribution, since KEV listing is the only exploitation evidence available.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: The August 2021 cumulative update satisfies SI-2 flaw remediation on this CVE identifier while leaving the junction-following defect reachable, because Microsoft fixed the submitted proof of concept rather than the mechanism. A host at 10.0.19043.1165 is compliant against CVE-2021-34484 and still exploitable through the path later assigned CVE-2022-21919 and CVE-2022-26904, so SI-2 evidence organised around CVE identifiers records three remediations of one defect that was closed once.

NIST-800-53-AC-6.gap: AC-6 is fully attestable here and irrelevant to the outcome: the vector is PR:L and the only account the exploit needs is an ordinary interactive logon. Removing local administrator rights, the usual AC-6 remediation for a Windows elevation finding, changes nothing about whether an unprivileged user can plant a junction in the temporary profile the service is building for that same user, so the control passes on every affected host without reducing exposure.

NIS2-Art21-vulnerability-handling.gap: The vulnerability-handling obligation runs on supplier advisories, and no advisory feed carried the fact that mattered — that the August 2021 fix had been publicly bypassed by late October 2021, five months before CISA's 2022-03-31 KEV listing. An entity following Microsoft's advisories precisely would have marked this closed in August 2021 with no trigger to reopen it, and would have learned otherwise only from a researcher's own publication.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: B4 assesses system security through build currency and hardening baselines, and neither distinguishes an August 2021 build carrying an incomplete fix from one that also carries the January and April 2022 updates that actually closed the primitive. CAF has no outcome requiring a fix to be verified against the underlying mechanism, so on this CVE an estate at 10.0.17763.2114 and an estate that is genuinely remediated present identical evidence.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: This CVE was patched inside the Essential Eight window in August 2021 on every affected build, so patch-application maturity scores clean. The model has no expression for a fix that shipped on time and did not work, and nothing at all to say about the position operators are in now: Windows 7, 8.1, Server 2008 through 2012 R2 and every Windows 10 build in the advisory are past end of support, so the required 'current version' does not exist for them.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: A.8.8 evidence is the advisory-to-closure chain, and on this CVE that chain is clean and wrong: advisory August 2021, update deployed, ticket closed. The control never asks for the primitive to be re-tested after the vendor declares it fixed, which is exactly the step that surfaced the October 2021 bypass and exactly why the same User Profile Service junction drew two further CVE identifiers before being closed.

new_control_requirements.name: INCOMPLETE-PATCH-SEQUENCE-SEVERITY-MULTIPLIER
new_control_requirements.description: Vulnerability-management programs must apply a severity multiplier when a CVE is the Nth in an incomplete-patch sequence on the same primitive (third MOTW bypass, second AMSI bypass, etc.). Framework controls treating each CVE as discrete obscure the structural defect; the Nth CVE in a sequence implies that future bypasses on the same primitive are likely.
new_control_requirements.evidence: The Windows User Profile Service junction primitive is a three-CVE sequence: Microsoft patched it in August 2021 as CVE-2021-34484, again in January 2022 as CVE-2022-21919, and again in April 2022 as CVE-2022-26904, and the Metasploit module that weaponises it states both earlier patches were insufficient. CISA listed only the first of the three in KEV, on 2022-03-31 with a 2022-04-21 due date, which is the exact failure this control names — an operator meeting that due date on the CVE identifier alone was running a build that the public exploit still worked against. The EPSS score of 0.21661 at the 97th percentile on 2026-08-16 reflects the sequence, not the August 2021 fix.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: The word that matters for Windows User Profile Service is 'verified'. Microsoft shipped a fix for CVE-2021-34484 in August 2021 and CISA listed it on 2022-03-31 with a 2022-04-21 due date, by which point the fix had been publicly bypassed for five months — so deploying the named update inside the SLA produced an unverified mitigation on every affected build from Windows 7 SP1 through Windows 10 21H1 and Server 2019. Verification here means the installed build meets or exceeds the fixed build for the SKU and the host also carries the January and April 2022 updates.

new_control_requirements.name: RESEARCHER-HANDLE-ACTIVITY-TRACKER
new_control_requirements.description: When a researcher handle is named in any catalog entry's discovery_attribution_note or poc_description, their public code-platform activity (GitHub events or a GitLab activity feed) must be polled by the threat-intake pipeline. The handle becomes a known signal source after a single catalog-grade drop and warrants prioritized surfacing of subsequent drops.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Abdelhamid Naceri reported CVE-2021-34484 to Microsoft, then published the bypass of the August 2021 fix on GitHub in late October 2021 — five months before CISA's 2022-03-31 KEV listing and with no vendor advisory carrying the fact. For this CVE the researcher's own publication channel was the only place the reopening appeared, so polling the handle that produced the original report is the difference between learning in October 2021 and learning from a KEV entry the following spring.

CVE-2021-34486.name: Microsoft Windows Event Tracing Privilege Escalation Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: A local user drives NtTraceControl()'s periodic capture-state path through three requests: allocate and arm a 0x30-byte ETW timer context, force it to be freed early with invalid GUIDs, then set a new timer that reuses the freed block. The reclaimed object supplies a WorkerRoutine function pointer the kernel calls, turning an ordinary user account into kernel-mode code execution.
attack_vector.privileges_required: low — PR:L; any account able to issue the syscall from a normal user session, with no group membership or service account required
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; the free is driven deterministically by request sequence rather than by a race, and the remaining difficulty is grooming the 0x30-byte non-paged pool allocation, which is why the public exploit is build-specific and was demonstrated on Windows 10 21H1 builds in the 19043.985-19043.1083 range
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Yong Chuan Koh reverse-engineered the ETW notification worker by hand and credits Wei Lei for the RtlSetAllBits() gadget; no fuzzing harness, automated triage or AI assistance is claimed anywhere in the disclosure.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Deploying the August 2021 cumulative update (KB5005030 / KB5005031 / KB5005033) and verifying the installed build against the fixed build for the SKU, with the host reboot actually taken.
prevention.adequacy: The update genuinely removes the defect, which is more than can be said for several elevations of the same era — but the clock that mattered ran from the 2021-08-30 mechanism publication, not from CISA's 2022-03-28 listing seven months later. And the update is unavailable as a control today for the whole affected set, since Windows 10 1809 through 21H1 and Server version 2004/20H2 are all past end of support.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Hunting for bursts of capture-state update requests through NtTraceControl() from a non-administrative token, and treating an unexplained drop in a host's ETW-derived telemetry as a security event rather than an agent fault.
detection.adequacy: Both signals require the detection stack to instrument the subsystem the exploit attacks, which is circular by construction: once the exploit succeeds, kernel-mode code can shape what the tracing pipeline reports. The realistic value is catching failed or repeated attempts, not the successful one.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating any unpatched host that carried ordinary interactive users as a kernel-compromise candidate rather than an endpoint finding, and rebuilding rather than trusting the host's own telemetry to prove nothing happened.
response.adequacy: Honest limit: kernel-mode execution invalidates on-host evidence, so the response decision has to be made on exposure — build number and account model — rather than on detection output. With no named campaign attribution behind the KEV listing, there is also no indicator set to scope the search against.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: SI-2 is satisfied by the August 2021 cumulative update, but the control's cadence is set against advisory publication and this defect's public mechanism write-up landed 2021-08-30, about three weeks later, with working exploit code following. An 'Important'-rated local elevation folded into routine monthly work therefore sits unpatched through the period when the root cause is public, and CISA's 2022-03-28 KEV listing arrived far too late to be the trigger.

NIST-800-53-AU-9.gap: AU-9 protects audit records from unauthorised modification and assumes the mechanism generating them is sound. Here the vulnerable object is an ETW timer-callback context inside that mechanism, and the exploit outcome is kernel-mode execution — from which trace sessions can be altered or silenced at the source. An AU-9 attestation covering log integrity controls on the collector is entirely consistent with this flaw being fully exploitable.

NIS2-Art21-incident-handling.gap: Article 21 incident handling presumes an evidence base that outlives the incident. Successful exploitation of this CONTEXTINFO use-after-free puts the attacker in kernel mode inside Event Tracing for Windows, which is the pipeline most endpoint-detection products on Windows 10 1809-21H1 read from, so the documented handling process can be complete while the record of what happened after the escalation is not trustworthy.

UK-CAF-C1.gap: C1 grades monitoring on collection coverage and rule quality — both measured through the ETW pipeline this defect corrupts. No CAF outcome asks whether the monitoring channel is itself an escalation surface, so an operator can evidence strong C1 coverage across a Windows Server 2019 estate that was exploitable through NtTraceControl() function code 0x25 for the entire assessment period.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Applying the August 2021 update inside the Essential Eight window does remediate this defect, so the maturity score is honest as far as it goes. It stops being useful for the current estate: Windows 10 1809, 1909, 2004, 20H2 and 21H1 and Windows Server version 2004/20H2 are all past end of support, so a host still exposed to this CVE has no compliant patch destination and needs a replacement date the model does not ask for.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.15.gap: A.8.15 evidence concerns log production, retention and protection at the store. This CVE sits a layer below that boundary — the 0x30-byte EtwU allocation is part of the trace producer, so an attacker reaching kernel mode through it controls what is emitted rather than what is retained. Retention periods and repository access restrictions can all be in order while the producer is the thing under attacker control.

new_control_requirements.name: EDR-AS-VULNERABILITY-SECONDARY-OVERLAY
new_control_requirements.description: Organizations whose primary EDR is also a high-value attack target (Defender, CrowdStrike, SentinelOne) must deploy an independent secondary overlay capable of detecting anomalous behavior by the primary EDR's own processes. The overlay can be a second-vendor behavioral EDR, network-side EDR-bypass telemetry, or out-of-band SYSTEM-process spawn monitoring — but must NOT share trust roots with the primary EDR.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Windows Event Tracing is the shared trust root this control warns about: the defect is a use-after-free on a 0x30-byte EtwU CONTEXTINFO object reached through NtTraceControl(), and the outcome is kernel-mode execution inside the subsystem nearly every Windows endpoint-detection product consumes. On the affected builds — Windows 10 1809 through 21H1 and Server 2019 and version 2004/20H2, everything below 10.0.17763.2114 / 10.0.18363.1734 / 10.0.19041.1165 / 10.0.19042.1165 / 10.0.19043.1165 — a detection stack reading only from ETW is asking the compromised component to report its own compromise. Public exploit code has been available since 2021 and CISA listed the CVE on 2022-03-28, so this is a standing condition rather than a hypothetical.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: For Windows Event Tracing the 'whichever is later' clause resolves to patch availability, August 2021, not the 2022-03-28 KEV listing — the root-cause write-up published 2021-08-30 and public exploit code followed, so the exposure window opened seven months before CISA named it. There is no live-patch path for this component and disabling ETW is not available as a compensating control, so the only verified mitigation is the cumulative update plus the reboot, measured on the installed build for each affected SKU.

CVE-2021-38646.name: Microsoft Office Access Connectivity Engine Remote Code Execution Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: The victim opens an attacker-supplied data-source file; Office hands it to the Access Connectivity Engine, whose parser reaches a state Microsoft classifies as remote code execution, and the attacker's code runs inside the Office process at the user's own privilege. No macro is enabled and no elevation is involved, so nothing in the sequence looks like a security prompt to the user. Microsoft states the Preview Pane is not an attack vector for this CVE, so the open is a real user action rather than a mail-client render.
