attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; the attacker supplies a file rather than an account, and the code inherits whatever privilege the person who opened it already had
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L with UI:R; the only real constraint is delivery and a click, which is the ordinary phishing-attachment shape. The engine is a shared Office component rather than an Access feature, so the victim does not need to be an Access user for the file to reach the parser.
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Microsoft's September 2021 advisory credits Eugene Lim of the Government Technology Agency of Singapore — a named outside researcher, not an automated pipeline — and no AI assistance is claimed by him, by Microsoft, or in any coverage. The MITRE record's empty credits array is an artefact of how MSRC issues CVEs and says nothing about the finder.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Enforcing Mark-of-the-Web on every Office file arriving by mail, web download or untrusted share so it opens in Protected View, combined with bringing every Office version track — not just the inventoried one — to the September 2021 security release and relaunching the applications.
prevention.adequacy: Protected View is a real reduction and not a closure: it bounds the parse to a reduced-privilege render, and it is defeated whenever the untrusted-origin marking is stripped by an archive, ISO or VHD container, or whenever a user chooses Enable Editing. The patch is the closure, and its weak point is the version-track sprawl on a real Office estate rather than the patch itself.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alerting on an Office process spawning a shell or network-capable child immediately after a file open, and on Office processes crash-looping against a particular attachment.
detection.adequacy: Both fire after the parser has already run attacker code in the user's context, so they scope the response rather than prevent the compromise. Neither has an exploit signature behind it — no public exploit artefact for this CVE resolved — so detection here is generic post-exploitation behaviour, not a rule keyed to this defect.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating a user who opened an untrusted data-source file on an unpatched Office build as a credential-compromise and lateral-movement case, given CISA's ransomware-campaign flag, and rotating what that user held rather than closing on an anti-malware scan.
response.adequacy: The KEV ransomware flag is the reason this needs a real response path, and the absence of any named campaign report is the reason the response cannot be scoped by indicator — there is no published operator, lure or infrastructure set to hunt against, so the scoping has to come from Office version and file-arrival telemetry the organisation collected itself.

NIST-800-53-CM-7.gap: Least functionality cannot reach this component. The Access Connectivity Engine is a shared data-access layer inside the Office install rather than a separately installable feature, so an organisation that standardised on a build without the Access application still ships the vulnerable parser to every desktop. CM-7 offers no supported way to disable the engine while keeping Office functional, which forces the intervention onto the delivery path instead.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: SI-2 closes on the inventoried package, and a real Office estate is several packages: Microsoft 365 Apps on a servicing channel, MSI-based Office 2016 and 2019, Office 2013 SP1 survivors, and per-user installs outside managed distribution. Updating the managed channel while an Office 2013 copy stays below 15.0.5381.1000 or an Office 2016 copy below 16.0.5215.1000 leaves the parser reachable with a clean flaw-remediation attestation behind it.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: The patch window is not what failed. Microsoft shipped the fix in September 2021 and CISA set 2022-04-18 as the remediation date; what Article 21 never states is that this remediation only lands when every Office process exits and relaunches, because the fixed engine binaries do not load into a running process. A fleet reporting full deployment can still be parsing untrusted data sources with the vulnerable engine in every long-lived Outlook session.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: B4 asks for supported and patched software and this CVE splits the two apart. Office 2013 ended support in April 2023 and Office 2016 and 2019 in October 2025, so an install can sit at the exact version that closes CVE-2021-38646 and still receive nothing for anything found since. CAF has no distinct state for 'patched against the named CVE, unsupported for everything after it', which is where most remaining exposure to this defect now lives.

AU-Essential-8-App-Hardening.gap: Essential Eight application hardening is built around blocking web content, macros and Office child processes, and none of those is in this path. The attacker's artefact is a data-source file, so no macro policy is consulted, and execution happens inside the parsing engine before a child-process rule has anything to act on. Maximum application-hardening maturity and none produce the same outcome once the file is opened.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.7.gap: A.8.7 is evidenced through anti-malware coverage and signature currency, and this defect arrives as a data file the victim is meant to open rather than as an executable. With CISA recording ransomware-campaign use, the artefact that anti-malware can plausibly catch is the second stage — by which point the parser has already executed attacker code in the user's context, so the control is being credited for a detection that comes after the compromise it is meant to prevent.

new_control_requirements.name: DOWNLOAD-PROVENANCE-ENFORCEMENT
new_control_requirements.description: Exploitation here requires the victim to open an attacker-supplied Office document, so on an estate that has not yet reached the fixed build the delivery path is the only enforceable control. Require Mark-of-the-Web on every Office file arriving by mail, web download, or untrusted file share, and require MOTW-tagged documents to open in Protected View — an isolated, reduced-privilege render — instead of the full parsing path that carries the CWE-94 sink at the user's own process privilege. Provenance must survive the container: files extracted from an archive, mounted from an ISO or VHD, or renamed must inherit the tag rather than lose it, and 'Enable Editing' on externally sourced documents must be blocked by policy rather than left to the user. The distinguishing test: mail a MOTW-tagged spreadsheet nested inside a ZIP to a managed workstation, extract it, and confirm the extracted file still opens in Protected View — a user-application-hardening attestation that covers only macro and ActiveX/OLE settings still lets a provenance-stripped document reach the vulnerable parser with full user privileges.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Microsoft Office Access Connectivity Engine is exactly the delivery-path case: CVSS PR:N with UI:R means the attacker supplies a file and the victim's click is the whole precondition, and because the artefact is a data source rather than a macro-bearing document, no macro policy is consulted anywhere in the sequence. The engine ships with Microsoft 365 Apps, Office 2013 SP1, Office 2016 and Office 2019 rather than only with Access, so the exposed population is every Office desktop until its version is verified against 15.0.5381.1000 or 16.0.5215.1000. With CISA's KEV entry of 2022-03-28 carrying knownRansomwareCampaignUse 'Known' and no public exploit artefact to build a signature from, the provenance-to-Protected-View path is the only control an operator can actually enforce on a machine that has not yet been updated and relaunched.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: For the Office Access Connectivity Engine, 'verified' has to mean a per-install version check across every Office track in the estate rather than a deployment percentage: Office 2013 SP1 at 15.0.5381.1000 or later, Office 2016 at 16.0.5215.1000 or later, and Microsoft 365 Apps and Office 2019 at their September 2021 security release. CISA listed the CVE on 2022-03-28 with a 2022-04-18 date and a ransomware-campaign flag, and there is no live-patch path — so the verified mitigation is the update plus the application relaunch, on the unmanaged per-user copies as well as the inventoried package.

attack_vector.description: An unprivileged Android application creates a Mali memory object marked CPU-writable but not GPU-writable and imports read-only pages through it. Because kbase_jd_user_buf_pin_pages() checks only KBASE_REG_GPU_WR when deciding whether to pin for write, the driver returns a writable CPU mapping of read-only pages — shared-library text and file-backed page-cache pages included — and the attacker rewrites privileged content in memory without touching disk.
attack_vector.privileges_required: low — PR:L; an ordinary installed application with access to the Mali device node, which on Android is the default for any app rather than a special grant
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; a flag-check logic error fires deterministically, with no race to win, no heap groom and no prior information leak needed. The real constraint is reachability of the GPU driver from the app sandbox, which Android's design grants, making this a standard second stage behind a browser or messaging compromise.
attack_vector.ai_factor: None claimed and none evidenced. Project Zero records the reporter as unknown and notes the defect resembles a variant of CVE-2021-28664, consistent with patch analysis; the analysis itself was written from an in-the-wild sample. Jann Horn's follow-on audit that produced five more Mali bugs was manual review of the same driver, not automated discovery of this one.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Enforcing a minimum Android security patch level of 2022-03-05 or later as an access condition — organizational mail, VPN and document access withheld from any device below it — with the device restart completed, and refusing enrolment for Mali-equipped models whose vendor never shipped a build carrying ARM's fix.
prevention.adequacy: BOD 22-01 assumes a patch the operator can deploy, and on the non-Pixel share of a Mali estate that patch may never exist for a given model — so for those devices the only honest preventive control is withholding access and replacing the hardware, on a dated schedule. Where the update does exist, prevention is real but reboot-gated: a device that took the OTA and has not restarted is still running the vulnerable driver.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Comparing page-cache and on-disk reads of sensitive files on a device under suspicion, and treating an app process that obtains root or loads a kernel module after GPU driver activity as a compromise signal.
detection.adequacy: Neither is available to a typical mobile-device-management stack, which sees patch level and app inventory and not kernel-level behaviour. The page-cache-versus-disk comparison is the only check that would surface the primitive's distinctive effect, and it requires host access most managed Android estates do not have.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating a device that ran a pre-2022-03-05 patch level in a targeted-risk role as a full-device compromise: wipe and rebuild rather than update in place, and rotate every credential and token the device held.
response.adequacy: Because Google states the flaw may have been under limited, targeted exploitation rather than mass exploitation, this response is proportionate for the exposed cohort — executives, journalists, legal and security staff — and disproportionate for a general fleet. The judgement has to be made on role rather than on any indicator, since no campaign infrastructure has been published to hunt against.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: SI-2 measures whether the flaw was remediated and presumes the operator can remediate it. Google closed this at Pixel patch level 2022-03-05, but the same mali_kbase code ships in other vendors' Android kernels and each vendor decides independently whether to integrate ARM's fix — so on a mixed fleet the control is measuring N vendor decisions the organisation does not control, with no feed that reports which vendors have shipped it.

NIST-800-53-SR-3.gap: SR-3 addresses suppliers the organisation contracts with, and the vulnerable component sits two tiers upstream of that relationship: ARM authors mali_kbase, a chipset or handset vendor integrates it, and the enterprise buys the finished handset. No SR-3 artefact an organisation holds would surface 'this device carries a Mali driver predating the KBASE_REG_CPU_WR fix', because the driver appears in no inventory the buyer maintains.

NIS2-Art21-supply-chain.gap: This is the clearest failure of the five. The fix existed upstream at ARM and only reached devices as each downstream vendor integrated it — Project Zero documented that for the sibling Mali defects, test devices from Pixel, Samsung, Xiaomi and Oppo were still vulnerable months after ARM published fixes publicly. Complete supplier assurance documentation for a handset vendor gives an entity no way to detect that an upstream driver fix has not propagated to the devices it already owns.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: B4 assesses whether devices are supported and current, and on Android 'current' means whatever patch level the vendor last shipped for that model. A handset reporting the newest patch level available to it can still carry mali_kbase without the KBASE_REG_CPU_WR check, and CAF has no outcome that distinguishes 'as current as this device can be made' from 'carries the fix for this defect', so both present the same evidence.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: The Essential Eight patch control assumes patching is an operation the organisation can perform. For a vendor-locked or personally-owned Mali-equipped handset it is not: if the manufacturer never shipped a build carrying this fix, there is no compliant action, and the model offers no state between patched and unpatched for that case. The real control — refusing enrolment below patch level 2022-03-05 and replacing the hardware on a dated schedule — is not something the maturity model scores.

ISO-27001-2022-A.5.21.gap: A.5.21 is evidenced against direct ICT suppliers, and the security property that failed here was decided three hops upstream: ARM wrote the driver, a chipset vendor integrated it, a handset vendor shipped it, and the organisation bought the device. An auditor can be shown a complete supply-chain assurance pack for the handset contract while the defect and its fix were both settled by parties that pack does not name.

new_control_requirements.name: TIER-3-DEPENDENCY-INVENTORY
new_control_requirements.description: Supply chain inventory must extend to tier-3 dependencies (dependencies of dependencies of direct dependencies). SBOM coverage for libsystemd-class transitive dependencies cannot be omitted under SR-3.
new_control_requirements.evidence: The ARM Mali GPU kernel driver is the tier-3 item exactly as this control describes it: ARM authors mali_kbase, a chipset or handset vendor integrates it into an Android kernel, and the organisation buys the handset — so the component carrying CVE-2021-39793 appears in no inventory the buyer holds. Google closed it at Pixel patch level 2022-03-05, but the same code ships across other vendors' devices, and Project Zero recorded that for the sibling Mali flaws found by Jann Horn, test devices from Pixel, Samsung, Xiaomi and Oppo were still vulnerable months after ARM published public fixes. Without a driver-level inventory an operator cannot even ask which of their devices carry a pre-fix mali_kbase, let alone which vendor has shipped the fix.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: For this Mali defect the SLA has to be expressed as a minimum security patch level enforced as an access condition, because there is no live-patch path for a GPU kernel driver and the fix is reboot-gated: Google's Pixel bulletin puts it at patch level 2022-03-05, CISA listed the CVE on 2022-04-11 with a 2022-05-02 date, and a device that took the OTA without restarting is still executing the vulnerable driver. The documented-compensating-control branch is the one that carries the non-Pixel fleet — for a Mali-equipped model whose vendor never shipped the fix, the only defensible mitigation to document is withholding organizational data from the device and scheduling its replacement.

attack_vector.description: A local user with an ordinary account drives the win32k syscall surface — the kernel-mode window manager and GDI, reachable from any interactive-session process including sandboxed ones — into mishandling a kernel object, and turns that into kernel-mode code execution as SYSTEM. Microsoft published the impact and nothing else, so the specific object and syscall remain undisclosed; the affected range is what distinguishes this defect from its October 2021 siblings, reaching back to Windows 10 1809 and Windows Server 2019.
attack_vector.privileges_required: low — PR:L; an ordinary local account, which on a session host or virtual-desktop pool is the normal operating state for most of the user population
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; Microsoft assessed the conditions as reliably reproducible, but with no published root cause the practical constraint for an attacker is rediscovering the primitive from the October 2021 patch diff, which is also why no public exploit exists
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Microsoft's October 2021 acknowledgment names H4iiluv of 73lab, with Qingteng, so this came from an outside report by a named researcher rather than from an internal find, and no AI-assisted discovery is claimed by any party. Read the empty credits array on the MITRE record as an MSRC publishing artefact, not as an absent finder.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Deploying the October 2021 cumulative update across every affected build and taking the reboot, verified against the fixed build number for each SKU rather than against 'update applied' in the management console.
prevention.adequacy: The update closes the defect and there is no partial credit available — win32k is kernel-resident, so no configuration, sandbox or service-restart mitigation stands in for it. The honest limit is the reboot on session hosts, which is both the step that completes the fix and the step most likely to be deferred, and the fact that most of the affected range is now unsupported.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Watching for a sandboxed or low-integrity process making anomalous win32k syscalls ahead of a SYSTEM process appearing in the same session, and treating repeated win32kfull bugchecks on a multi-user host as a security event.
detection.adequacy: There is no signature to write, because no public analysis of this defect exists — these are behavioural approximations of the class, not detections keyed to this CVE. Bugchecks catch failed attempts against an unmatched build; a successful attempt reaches kernel mode, from which the telemetry that would record it is under attacker control.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating an unpatched multi-user host that showed either signal as a kernel-compromise candidate — rebuild rather than patch in place, and rotate the credentials of every account that held a session on it during the exposure window.
response.adequacy: With no named campaign and no published indicator set behind the KEV listing, the response cannot be scoped by threat intelligence and has to be scoped by exposure — build number, session-host role and the exposure window between October 2021 and the reboot. That is a blunt instrument, but on an undisclosed kernel defect it is the only one available.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: SI-2 prioritises on the vendor rating, and Microsoft rated this 'Important' in October 2021, which routes it into ordinary monthly work. That rating tracks the local attack vector rather than the defect's role: an undisclosed win32k elevation is the escalation stage of a chain whose entry point is a critical-rated remote bug, so the control's own inputs schedule the containment step behind the flaw it contains.

NIST-800-53-CM-3.gap: Change control decides when the restart happens and the restart is the remediation, because win32k lives in the kernel: a Server 2019 host that installed KB5006672 and is waiting on the next change window is still running the vulnerable code. The population where the change window is longest — Remote Desktop session hosts, where a reboot evicts logged-on users — is exactly the population where an ordinary interactive account, the flaw's only precondition, is the normal state.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: One rollup closes CVE-2021-40449, CVE-2021-40450 and CVE-2021-41357, so an entity tracking the obligation per CVE files three items against one action and reports three remediations. What the obligation has no field for is the pattern behind the count: Microsoft shipped three distinct Win32k elevations in a single month with one of them already exploited in the wild, which says more about the component than any of the three CVE records does.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: B4 credits application sandboxing and least-privilege configuration as system-security evidence, and this defect crosses precisely that boundary — win32k is callable from low-integrity and sandboxed processes on Windows 10 1809 through Windows 11 21H2, so the sandbox that the assessment counts as a control is the launch point for the elevation. CAF has no outcome asking whether a sandbox's permitted syscall surface is itself a kernel attack surface.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Applying the October 2021 rollup inside the window scores clean, and the score conveys none of what makes this urgent — that the defect is the escalation half of an intrusion chain rather than a standalone endpoint item. It is also unattainable for most of the affected range now: Windows 10 1909, 2004, 20H2 and 21H1 and Server version 2004/20H2 have all passed end of support, so there is no current build for those hosts to reach.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: A.8.8 ranks technical vulnerabilities by score, and both scores available here are artefacts of Microsoft's silence rather than measures of risk. The CVSS 7.8 and the EPSS of 0.02076 at the 80th percentile reflect a published one-line title and no technical detail; the giveaway is that CVE-2021-41357, a different defect in the same component, carries byte-identical EPSS values, which is what a model produces when it is scoring the same sentence twice.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: For this Win32k defect there is no live-patch branch and no compensating-control branch — the component is kernel-resident, Microsoft published no workaround, and no configuration change removes the syscall surface — so 'verified mitigation' collapses to the October 2021 cumulative update plus the reboot, measured on the installed build: 10.0.17763.2237 for Windows Server 2019, 10.0.20348.288 for Server 2022, 10.0.22000.258 for Windows 11 21H2, 10.0.19043.1288 / 10.0.19042.1288 / 10.0.19041.1288 for the Windows 10 lines. CISA listed it on 2022-04-25 with a 2022-05-16 date, roughly six months after the fix shipped, so the SLA's 'whichever is later' clause resolves to the October 2021 release and the exposure window was already long before CISA named it.

new_control_requirements.name: BUG-FAMILY-MITIGATION-PERSISTENCE
new_control_requirements.description: When a CVE patch lands, retain the pre-patch compensating controls (module blacklists, sysctl restrictions) until the patched code has soaked for a stated review period. Patches for one bug in a primitive class can introduce sibling bugs in the same class; the original compensating control may still apply to the sibling.
new_control_requirements.evidence: October 2021 is the month that makes this control's premise concrete for Win32k: Microsoft shipped fixes for CVE-2021-40449, CVE-2021-40450 and CVE-2021-41357 in the same rollup, three distinct elevations in one kernel component, with the first already exploited in the wild. Treating the October update as closing 'the Win32k problem' is the mistake the control names — the sibling density says the primitive class is live, so whatever containment an operator had for win32k reachability from sandboxed and low-integrity processes belongs in place through a stated soak period after 10.0.17763.2237 / 10.0.19043.1288 / 10.0.22000.258 land, not retired on the strength of the patch.

attack_vector.description: A local user exercises the kernel-mode Win32k syscall surface to corrupt kernel object handling and lands as SYSTEM. Microsoft disclosed only the impact and the fact that this defect is distinct from CVE-2021-40449 and CVE-2021-40450, and the affected list starts at Windows 10 version 2004 — so this is the newer-code sibling of the three Win32k elevations that shipped in the October 2021 rollup, and a Windows Server 2019 estate is outside its scope entirely.
attack_vector.privileges_required: low — PR:L; an ordinary local account with no group membership requirement, which is the standing condition on any multi-user Windows Server 2022 session host
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L per Microsoft's own assessment, not per any external demonstration, since no public analysis of this defect exists. For an attacker the practical work is rediscovering the primitive from the October 2021 patch diff, which is also why no public exploit has appeared in five years.
attack_vector.ai_factor: Unknown. The MITRE record's credits array is empty and no acknowledgement resolved, so whether this came from an outside report or from internal variant analysis after CVE-2021-40449 is not public. No AI involvement is claimed by anyone.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Applying the October 2021 cumulative update on the Windows 10 2004-and-later population and taking the reboot, with the scope drawn from Microsoft's affected-version list rather than from the KEV vulnerability name.
prevention.adequacy: The update is the only closure — no configuration or sandbox control substitutes for a kernel fix. Its practical limit on this CVE is scoping rather than deployment: an operator working from the KEV name alone will chase Server 2019 hosts this defect cannot touch while possibly leaving the Server 2022 hosts it can.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Watching sandboxed processes on Windows 10 2004-and-later builds for anomalous win32k syscall activity ahead of a SYSTEM process in the same session, and treating win32kfull bugchecks on Server 2022 as security events.
detection.adequacy: These are class-level behavioural approximations, not detections for this defect — with no published root cause there is nothing specific to key on. They also depend on telemetry a successful kernel-mode exploit can shape, so their realistic value is catching build-mismatched failures rather than a working attempt.

response.what_would_have_worked: Scoping any investigation by Microsoft's affected-version list first, then treating an unpatched Windows 11 or Server 2022 session host that showed either signal as a kernel-compromise candidate requiring rebuild and credential rotation for its session holders.
response.adequacy: There is no campaign attribution and no indicator set behind the KEV listing, so the investigation is bounded by exposure rather than by intelligence — and on this CVE the exposure boundary is unusually easy to get wrong, because the identical KEV name and identical scores shared with CVE-2021-40450 invite an analyst to work the wrong host population.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: SI-2 depends on scoping the flaw to the correct hosts, and every field a scanner normally scopes from is shared with a different defect: CISA gives this CVE the same vulnerabilityName as CVE-2021-40450, NVD gives it the same 7.8, and EPSS gives it the same 0.02076. Only Microsoft's affected list, which starts at Windows 10 2004, separates them — so an SI-2 process fed by KEV metadata produces findings against unaffected Server 2019 hosts and can miss that those hosts need the sibling CVE.

NIST-800-53-CM-7.gap: Least functionality would bound this defect if the win32k syscall surface could be restricted per process, and on the affected builds — Windows 10 2004 through Windows 11 21H2 and Server 2022 — no supported configuration does that and Microsoft published no workaround for this CVE. CM-7 remains attestable through general hardening baselines while offering nothing that changes whether an unprivileged process can reach the vulnerable code.

NIS2-Art21-vulnerability-management.gap: The obligation presumes a vulnerability record detailed enough to act on. Here the record is a title, an impact class and a uniqueness note against two sibling CVEs — no CWE from NVD, no root cause from Microsoft, no independent analysis in five years. An entity cannot assess reachability, cannot design a compensating control, and can distinguish this defect from CVE-2021-40450 only by affected version, which is the entirety of the actionable content it received.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: B4 counts application sandboxing as system-security evidence while this defect is reached from inside the sandbox — win32k is callable from low-integrity processes on every affected build from Windows 10 2004 to Windows 11 21H2. The narrow version range compounds it: an assessor sees the same B4 evidence from an estate full of exposed Server 2022 session hosts and from one running only Server 2019, which this CVE cannot touch.

AU-Essential-8-App-Hardening.gap: Application hardening governs what runs inside the browser and Office sandboxes an attacker uses to reach this primitive, and it stops at the sandbox boundary. Blocking web content, macros and Office child processes leaves untouched the kernel syscall surface those sandboxed processes are still permitted to call, so a Windows 11 21H2 host below 10.0.22000.258 at maximum hardening maturity is exposed identically to one at the minimum.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: A.8.8 requires vulnerabilities to be identified and evaluated, and identification fails first here: two distinct Win32k defects from one October 2021 rollup share a KEV vulnerabilityName, a CVSS score and byte-identical EPSS values, so a register built from those fields holds one entry where there are two problems. The evaluation step then inherits a scope that is wrong for whichever of the two the register happened to capture.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: There is no live-patch and no compensating-control branch available for this Win32k defect — the component is kernel-resident, Microsoft published no workaround, and no supported configuration removes the syscall surface — so verified mitigation means the October 2021 cumulative update plus the reboot, checked as installed build 10.0.22000.258 (Windows 11 21H2), 10.0.20348.288 (Server 2022), 10.0.19043.1288 / 10.0.19042.1288 / 10.0.19041.1288 (Windows 10 21H1 / 20H2 / 2004). Verification also has to include scope: because the KEV entry carries the same vulnerabilityName as CVE-2021-40450, an SLA closed on name-matched hosts will report remediation on Server 2019 machines this CVE never affected.

new_control_requirements.name: PROTECTION-MECHANISM-FAILURE-CLASS-REGRESSION
new_control_requirements.description: Detonation chambers, EDR rules, and AppLocker/WDAC policies covering protection-mechanism classes (MOTW, SmartScreen, AMSI, ASR, WDAC, Driver Block Rules) must include class-level regression testing executed on every patch deployment, not just one-off bypass-CVE remediation. The test battery for class-X must include all historic class-X bypass primitives — incomplete patches re-introduce risk that one-off testing does not detect.
new_control_requirements.evidence: The protection mechanism at stake for this CVE is the browser and Office sandbox that an attacker's first stage runs in, and win32k reachability is the class-level property that decides whether that sandbox holds. Microsoft shipped three Win32k elevations in the October 2021 rollup — CVE-2021-40449, CVE-2021-40450 and this one, scoped to Windows 10 2004 and later up to Windows 11 21H2 and Server 2022 — which is the sibling density this control exists to respond to. Testing the sandbox boundary once against the exploited sibling, rather than as a standing class-level battery re-run on every deployment through 10.0.22000.258 and 10.0.20348.288, leaves the estate assuming a containment property that three separate defects in one month contradicted.

CVE-2021-42278.name: Microsoft Active Directory Domain Services Privilege Escalation Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: Any authenticated domain user creates a computer account using the default machine-account quota of ten, renames its sAMAccountName to a domain controller's name with the trailing dollar sign removed, obtains a TGT under that name, renames the account back, and requests a service ticket — the KDC cannot find the original principal, appends a dollar sign, and issues a ticket for the real domain controller. Chained with CVE-2021-42287, the result is domain administrator from a standard user account.
attack_vector.privileges_required: low — PR:L; any domain account at all, including a service or contractor account, because the exploit needs a credential rather than a privilege
attack_vector.complexity: high — AC:H per the CVSS vector, reflecting the need to chain with CVE-2021-42287 and to time the renames rather than any real skill barrier. Public tooling automates the whole sequence, Sophos measured it at roughly sixteen seconds, and the 0.70207 EPSS at the 99th percentile is the market's answer to the AC:H rating.
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Microsoft credits Andrew Bartlett of Catalyst IT for both this CVE and CVE-2021-42287, and the chaining technique was then worked out by researchers reading Kerberos PAC handling and SAM validation behaviour and testing against lab domains, published as sam-the-admin and then as the noPac tooling in December 2021. No automated discovery, fuzzing or AI assistance appears anywhere in that work.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: KB5008102 on every domain controller in the forest together with the CVE-2021-42287 fix, plus setting ms-DS-MachineAccountQuota to 0 and delegating computer-account creation to a named group — the quota change removes the object-creation step even before the update lands.
prevention.adequacy: The pairing is the limit: patching this CVE alone leaves the noPac chain intact, so a BOD-22-01 record closed against this identifier can describe a still-exploitable forest. Setting the quota to zero is the strongest operator-side control available before patching, but it is not a closure either — the tooling falls back to abusing an existing computer object the attacker can already write to.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alerting on Directory-Services-SAM events 16990 and 16991 on patched controllers, and on 4741/4742 computer-account creation and sAMAccountName rename by a non-administrative subject, correlated with a TGT request naming a domain controller without its trailing dollar sign.
detection.adequacy: Genuinely good detection for once, because Microsoft shipped purpose-built events with the fix — but 16990 and 16991 only exist on a patched controller, so the detection arrives with the remediation rather than before it. On an unpatched forest the operator is left correlating 4741/4742 against Kerberos ticket requests, which needs DC audit policy and ticket logging that many estates do not collect.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating a confirmed sAMAccountName spoofing event as a full domain compromise: reset the krbtgt account password twice with the required replication interval between, rotate privileged and service credentials, and audit computer objects created or renamed during the exposure window.
response.adequacy: This is the only response that removes the attacker's position, because the ticket obtained through this chain is a valid domain-administrator ticket and patching the controllers does not invalidate it. It is also the response operators most often defer, since a double krbtgt rotation is disruptive — and with CISA recording ransomware-campaign use, deferring it leaves an operator with domain administrator inside the forest.

NIST-800-53-AC-6.gap: AC-6 reviews enumerate administrative membership, standing elevation and service-account rights, and the grant that enables this attack appears in none of them: ms-DS-MachineAccountQuota defaults to 10, letting every authenticated user create ten computer objects. That default is the first step of the chain and it is invisible to a least-privilege attestation, which is why AC-6 can be fully evidenced on a forest where any standard user reaches domain administrator.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: Flaw remediation for this defect is only real as a set and only real at 100 percent: KB5008102 has to reach every domain controller in the forest, because one unpatched DC still answers the spoofed request, and it has to be paired with the CVE-2021-42287 fix or the noPac chain still completes. SI-2 evidence expressed as a percentage of hosts patched, or as this CVE closed on its own, describes an environment that remains fully exploitable.

NIS2-Art21-identity-management.gap: Nothing in the identity lifecycle is contested by this attack. The attacker authenticates honestly with a real domain account, never abuses a privileged identity, and the domain-administrator ticket is issued by the KDC because the directory failed to validate that a computer object's sAMAccountName ends in a dollar sign. Provisioning, authentication strength and access review can all be evidenced correctly while the escalation takes about sixteen seconds.

UK-CAF-B2.gap: B2 examines authentication strength, privileged-access separation and access review, and this chain steps around all three: the standard user authenticates legitimately, no privileged account is touched, and the escalation is a ticket the KDC itself issues. An assessment that credits strong B2 outcomes against a forest whose domain controllers are below 10.0.17763.2300 or 10.0.20348.350 is describing controls that never enter the attack path.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: The Essential Eight patch control scores per patch, and this remediation only exists as a pair. Applying the November 2021 update for CVE-2021-42278 without the one for CVE-2021-42287 leaves the noPac chain complete while both the compliance report and the CVE-level finding show remediated — and Windows Server 2008 SP2 through 2012 R2 domain controllers, all past end of support, have no compliant destination at all.

ISO-27001-2022-A.5.15.gap: A.5.15 evidence is an access-control policy over users, administrators and services, and computer-account creation sits outside the vocabulary such a policy normally uses. Yet the default that hands every authenticated user ten machine accounts is what supplies the object the attacker renames to a domain controller's name, so a complete and accurate A.5.15 attestation is entirely consistent with a directory whose own object-creation default enables domain takeover.

new_control_requirements.name: FLEET-CONTROL-PLANE-ADMIN-PRIVILEGE-TIER
new_control_requirements.description: Administrators of fleet-control-plane systems (MDM/UEM, EDR consoles, identity providers, container orchestrators, configuration management) must be classified as a distinct privilege tier above application admins, with: PAM-jumphost-only access, FIDO2 step-up per session, just-in-time elevation with approval workflow, separate identity from any other admin role, and dedicated PAW (privileged access workstation) hardware. Compliance frameworks must enumerate this tier explicitly rather than collapsing it into 'admin'.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Active Directory Domain Services is the identity control plane this control names, and CVE-2021-42278 is that tier being reached without any administrator ever being involved: a standard domain user creates a computer object under the default ms-DS-MachineAccountQuota of 10, renames it to a domain controller's name without the trailing dollar sign, and chained with CVE-2021-42287 walks out with a domain-administrator ticket in roughly sixteen seconds per Sophos. That is why frameworks collapsing this tier into 'admin' produce clean attestations on an exposed forest — the account model they examine is bypassed rather than abused. Bound to this product, the control's enumeration requirement means naming the directory's own object-creation defaults as control-plane privileges: the quota belongs in the tier definition alongside DC logon rights, and every domain controller below 10.0.17763.2300 (Server 2019) or 10.0.20348.350 (Server 2022) belongs on the tier's remediation clock rather than in general server patching.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: For Active Directory Domain Services the SLA has to be written against the forest, not the host: KB5008102 shipped 2021-11-09 and CISA listed the CVE on 2022-04-11 with a 2022-05-02 date, but the mitigation is not verified until every domain controller in the forest carries it — one unpatched DC still answers the spoofed request — and until the CVE-2021-42287 fix is applied alongside it, because either alone leaves the noPac chain complete. There is no live-patch path for a domain controller, so this is a DC reboot window; the documented compensating control that genuinely bounds the interim is setting ms-DS-MachineAccountQuota to 0, which removes the object-creation step the exploit opens with.

CVE-2021-42287.name: Microsoft Active Directory Domain Services Privilege Escalation Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: A standard domain user creates and renames a machine account to impersonate a domain controller, then abuses the KDC's principal re-resolution (append-'$') during S4U2self to obtain a service ticket in the DC's privilege context, achieving Domain Admin from a low-privileged account.
attack_vector.privileges_required: low — PR:L; any authenticated domain user with the default machine-account creation quota
attack_vector.complexity: high — AC:H; a timed multi-step rename/TGT/rename/S4U2self sequence, but reduced to one command by public tooling
attack_vector.ai_factor: None; coordinated disclosure fixed in Microsoft's November 2021 updates, no AI-assisted discovery reported.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Install KB5008380 on all DCs and drive PacRequestorEnforcement to enforcement, and lower ms-DS-MachineAccountQuota to 0 so ordinary users cannot create machine accounts.
prevention.adequacy: Patching plus enforcement fully closes it, but the multi-phase rollout means 'update installed' is not 'enforced'; the quota reduction is an independent hardening that blocks the machine-account precondition even pre-enforcement.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alert on Event IDs 35/36/37/38 and on machine-account creation followed by a sAMAccountName rename to a DC name by a non-admin.
detection.adequacy: Detection catches the forged-ticket window but only if DC security event forwarding is in place; it does not prevent the escalation, which can complete in seconds.

response.what_would_have_worked: Reset the krbtgt account twice, invalidate outstanding tickets, and treat any DA-equivalent ticket issued to a user account as a domain compromise requiring credential rotation.
response.adequacy: Effective only after the fact; a successful noPac run already grants DC-context access, so response is containment, not prevention.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: The control is met by evidencing KB5008380 on each DC, but the flaw remains live until PacRequestorEnforcement is at value 2 fleet-wide; a domain that patched on 2021-11-09 and never advanced enforcement passes SI-2 reporting while a standard user still forges DC tickets, and the KEV due date of 2022-05-02 is not actually satisfied by update-install alone.

NIST-800-53-IA-2.gap: IA-2 is nominally satisfied because every principal authenticates with valid Kerberos material, yet the defect makes the KDC bind that material to a domain controller identity; the authentication event succeeds and looks legitimate, so IA-2's identity assurance is subverted at the protocol layer rather than at any credential the control governs.

NIS2-Art21-identity-management.gap: Article 21 identity-management measures are documented and enforced at the directory level, but the escalation exploits the default ms-DS-MachineAccountQuota of 10 and a KDC logic flaw, so an operator can show mature joiner/mover/leaver provisioning while any unpatched domain controller still issues Domain-Admin-equivalent tickets to ordinary users.

UK-CAF-B2.gap: A CAF B2 access-rights review confirms which users hold which privileges, but noPac requires only a standard account plus the default machine-account quota; the privilege gain occurs inside the KDC, so the domain passes a B2 assessment of granted rights while a low-privileged user reaches Domain Admin without any right ever being granted to them.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: The Essential Eight patch-OS control counts a DC compliant once the 2021-11-09 update is installed, but this PAC-requestor change only protects once enforcement (default 2022-10-11) is active; the maturity metric measures update timeliness and cannot express the update-installed-but-pre-enforcement state, so a 'patched' domain can remain exploitable.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: A.8.8 technical vulnerability management keyed to scanner build data flags a DC remediated when KB5008380 is present, but the true remediation event is enforcement, not KB presence; because this is a Kerberos logic flaw with no service-version signature, an A.8.8 programme under-reports residual exposure against the KEV clock opened 2022-04-11 until enforcement is confirmed.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Microsoft Active Directory Domain Services CVE-2021-42287 was added to CISA KEV on 2022-04-11 (due 2022-05-02) with knownRansomwareCampaignUse=Known and EPSS 0.74; the fix (KB5008380) shipped 2021-11-09, so the SLA clock is driven by the enforcement rollout rather than update install, which is exactly the state an SLA that measures 'patched' misses.

CVE-2021-45382.name: D-Link Multiple Routers Remote Code Execution Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: An unauthenticated attacker POSTs shell metacharacters in the DDNS ddnsHostName/ddnsUsername fields to /ddns_check.ccp; the ncc2 binary concatenates them into a system() call, executing arbitrary commands on the router.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; no authentication required
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; a single crafted HTTP request, reachable from the LAN or a WAN-exposed web UI
attack_vector.ai_factor: None; found via manual binary analysis, not AI-assisted.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Replace the EOL router with a supported device; there is no firmware fix, so removal is the only durable prevention. Interim: block WAN access to the web UI and segment the device.
prevention.adequacy: Decommissioning fully removes the exposure; the interim isolation only reduces reachability and does not fix the unpatchable sink.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Egress monitoring for the router fetching and running downloader scripts, and IDS signatures for '${IFS}'/metacharacter payloads to /ddns_check.ccp.
detection.adequacy: Consumer/SOHO routers rarely emit telemetry to a SIEM, so detection depends on network-side sensors the device sits behind.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treat any exposed unit as compromised: power off, replace, and rotate any credentials that transited it.
response.adequacy: A firmware reset cannot be trusted on an unpatchable device once exploited; replacement is the only clean state.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: SI-2 is exercised — the CVE is tracked and an 'apply update' action assigned — but no D-Link update exists for these EOL models per SAP10264, so the control loops on an impossible remediation; without an explicit end-of-life disposition, SI-2 leaves this actively-exploited RCE open against the KEV clock opened 2022-04-04 indefinitely.

NIS2-Art21-network-security.gap: Article 21 network-security controls can be documented and even enforced around the device, but a WAN-reachable /ddns_check.ccp endpoint still yields pre-auth command execution with no patch to close it; the measure reduces to isolation or removal, which a network-security control focused on in-place hardening does not compel for a device it treats as maintainable.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: CAF B4 expects a maintained, securely-configured system, yet these routers cannot be configured into a secure state — the ncc2 command-injection sink is unpatchable and support ended in 2017-2018; a B4 assessment accepting the newest available firmware as 'up to date' is signing off a build that permanently carries a CVSS 9.8 RCE.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: The Essential Eight patch-applications control is unreachable here because the vendor ceased firmware development; its window-based metric has no meaning when no patch will ever exist, so an estate holding these EOL routers cannot satisfy the control by patching and must record retirement as the only compliant outcome.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: A.8.8 would normally close a 9.8 finding by patching, but SAP10264 confirms no fix will ship for this model line; an A.8.8 vulnerability register lacking an EOL-decommission workflow keeps the Beastmode-exploited RCE permanently open, with a remediation (device removal) the control as written does not provide.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: D-Link DIR-810L/820L/826L/830L/836L CVE-2021-45382 was KEV-listed 2022-04-04 (EPSS 0.976) with no vendor patch per SAP10264, so the SLA's 'documented compensating controls' branch — isolate WAN, segment, schedule replacement — is the only satisfiable path, which is exactly why an SLA that presumes a patch fails on this entry.

new_control_requirements.name: PERIMETER-COMPROMISE-REBUILD-NOT-PATCH
new_control_requirements.description: Pre-rehearsed IR runbook for any perimeter device that suffers a pre-auth RCE CVE in active exploitation MUST default to config-exfil + rebuild + credential rotation, not patch-in-place. Patch-in-place leaves attacker-installed implants intact.
new_control_requirements.evidence: A SOHO router IS the network perimeter, and Beastmode's in-the-wild exploitation (Fortinet, Feb-Mar 2022) drops a downloader on the device; with no D-Link firmware fix available, patch-in-place is impossible and the runbook's rebuild/replace-and-rotate default is the only sound response to an exploited unit.

CVE-2022-0543.name: Debian-specific Redis Server Lua Sandbox Escape Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: An attacker sends an EVAL Lua script to a reachable Debian/Ubuntu Redis; the packaged interpreter leaves the 'package' global reachable, so package.loadlib pulls luaopen_io back in and io.popen runs shell commands as the redis process.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; default Redis has no authentication
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; a single deterministic EVAL command, scope-changed to the host (S:C)
attack_vector.ai_factor: None; a manually-found Debian packaging defect.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Apply the fixed redis-server package for the distribution actually installed — Debian's on 2022-02-18, Ubuntu's on 2022-03-08, both setting 'package' to nil — and restart the service; require AUTH and bind Redis to a trusted interface.
prevention.adequacy: The package fix fully closes the escape; the network/auth controls are independent hardening that also blocks the unauthenticated EVAL precondition even before patching.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alert on redis-server spawning shell/child processes and on EVAL scripts containing package.loadlib/io.popen.
detection.adequacy: Effective where host process telemetry exists, but a fast Muhstik infection can execute before an alert is triaged.

response.what_would_have_worked: Isolate the host, remove dropped binaries, rotate any credentials/keys stored in Redis, and rebuild if a miner or backdoor landed.
response.adequacy: Response is containment; the deterministic RCE means a reachable unpatched server should be assumed compromised.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: SI-2 is exercised but defeated by the unchanged redis_version: the Debian/Ubuntu fix does not bump the banner, so a version-keyed scanner marks the CVSS 10.0 server remediated while the vulnerable liblua-linked package remains installed, and the KEV clock opened 2022-03-28 is not actually met by what SI-2 reports.

NIS2-Art21-vulnerability-handling.gap: Article 21 vulnerability handling that keys on upstream Redis version cannot distinguish the safe statically-linked build from the vulnerable Debian dynamically-linked one; the same version string is both affected and unaffected depending on packaging, so a handling process deduplicating by version silently drops the exposed Debian/Ubuntu hosts from its worklist.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: CAF B4 secure configuration typically treats Redis Lua scripting as a feature, but on the affected packages an unauthenticated EVAL is a direct RCE via package.loadlib; a B4 baseline that does not disable or authenticate scripting and does not bind Redis to a trusted segment leaves the exact primitive the Muhstik botnet used fully reachable.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: The Essential Eight patch-applications control can log this host compliant because the fixed distro package leaves redis_version unchanged; a maturity assessment relying on version reporting therefore records patched status while a build below the installed distribution's own fix (Debian 2022-02-18, Ubuntu 2022-03-08) is still present, understating the actively-exploited exposure.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.9.gap: A.8.9 configuration management is the control that should have caught this, because the root cause is a linking/packaging configuration exposing the Lua 'package' global; an A.8.9 baseline that omits Redis authentication, interface binding, and fixed-package assertions permits the unauthenticated sandbox escape and cannot demonstrate the host is on the corrected build.

new_control_requirements.name: DATABASE-SERVER-SIDE-SCRIPTING-DEFAULT-DENY
new_control_requirements.description: In-memory and document datastores must ship with server-side scripting disabled by default; re-enabling requires documented threat-model acceptance.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Debian/Ubuntu Redis CVE-2022-0543 (KEV 2022-03-28, CVSS 10.0, EPSS 0.99) turns the default-reachable EVAL scripting surface into unauthenticated RCE via package.loadlib; a default-deny scripting posture removes the primitive the Muhstik botnet used regardless of the packaging defect.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2022-0543 was KEV-listed 2022-03-28 with fixes already shipped for both affected distributions — Debian DSA-5081-1 on 2022-02-18 and Ubuntu USN-5316-1 on 2022-03-08; because the fixed redis-server package leaves redis_version unchanged, the SLA's 'verified mitigation' requirement forces a dpkg-level confirmation against the right distribution's build rather than a banner check, which is the step a version-only SLA skips.

attack_vector.description: An unprivileged local user primes a pipe so its buffers carry a stale PIPE_BUF_FLAG_CAN_MERGE flag, splices bytes from a read-only file into the pipe, and writes attacker data that the kernel merges into the file's page-cache page, overwriting content the user cannot write — e.g. /etc/passwd — for local root.
attack_vector.privileges_required: low — PR:L; any unprivileged local account, no capability required
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; deterministic, no race or heap groom
attack_vector.ai_factor: None; found by manual investigation of file corruption by Max Kellermann.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Upgrade to the fixed kernel (5.16.11/5.15.25/5.10.102 or distro backport) and reboot, or apply a live kernel patch where reboot must be deferred.
prevention.adequacy: The kernel fix fully closes it, but only once the fixed kernel is actually running; installed-not-rebooted hosts remain exploitable, which is where live patching earns its place.

detection.what_would_have_worked: auditd/eBPF rules for splice-into-pipe privilege gains, unexpected root shells, and modification of /etc/passwd or setuid binaries.
detection.adequacy: Kernel LPE leaves little forensic trace; detection depends on watching the escalation's effect rather than the primitive itself.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treat a confirmed exploitation as host compromise: rotate local credentials, review for added UID 0 accounts and implants, rebuild if integrity is in doubt.
response.adequacy: Response is containment; a reliable local-root primitive means an exploited multi-user host should be rebuilt.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: SI-2 is satisfied by installing the fixed kernel package, but Dirty Pipe stays exploitable until the host reboots into that kernel; a fleet whose package inventory shows 5.10.102/5.15.25/5.16.11 while still running the old kernel from memory reports remediated under SI-2 yet fails the 2022-04-25 KEV due date in reality.

NIST-800-53-SI-4.gap: SI-4 monitoring generally has no coverage for this LPE: the exploit spawns no new process, changes no file permission, and does not crash, writing directly into the page cache; unless SI-4 is explicitly instrumented for unexpected root shells or read-only-file modification, there is no telemetry for it to alert on.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: Article 21 patch management counts a host complete when the fixed kernel package is deployed, but the activating reboot is routinely deferred on production Linux; the completion metric therefore records remediation before the fix is live, so an Article 21 attestation can be clean while the running kernel is still 5.8-5.16.10 and locally exploitable.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: CAF B4 least-functionality and secure configuration cannot block this, because the exploit uses ordinary required syscalls (pipe, splice, write) available to every local user; a B4 baseline can be fully evidenced while an unprivileged account overwrites root-owned files, since the defect is in the kernel rather than in any configurable surface B4 governs.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: The Essential Eight patch-OS control's window metric measures kernel-package installation, not the reboot that activates the fix; a fleet reported at target maturity can still be running the vulnerable kernel in memory, so the control overstates remediation for this reboot-gated kernel fix and the local-root exposure persists.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: A.8.8 keyed to scanner package data marks a host remediated once the fixed kernel package is present, but the running kernel may remain the vulnerable one pending reboot, and distro backports keep older version strings; without a running-vs-installed kernel comparison, A.8.8 under-reports the Dirty Pipe local-root exposure.

new_control_requirements.name: LIVE-PATCH-CAPABILITY
new_control_requirements.description: For any system that processes production workloads and cannot tolerate unplanned reboots: live kernel patching capability (kpatch, livepatch, kGraft, or equivalent) must be deployed and tested quarterly.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Dirty Pipe (CVE-2022-0847, KEV 2022-04-25, EPSS 0.886) is fixed only in 5.16.11/5.15.25/5.10.102 and the fix is reboot-gated; on production Linux where reboots are deferred, a live-patch is the only way to reach the running-kernel remediation the 4-hour-class KEV clock demands.

new_control_requirements.name: KERNEL-EXPLOITATION-DETECTION
new_control_requirements.description: Deploy auditd or eBPF-based monitoring rules for kernel privilege escalation indicators. Alert within 60 seconds of detection.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Dirty Pipe writes into the page cache with no new process, permission change, or crash, so on the multi-user Linux hosts most exposed to a local-root primitive, only auditd/eBPF rules watching for the escalation's effect (unexpected root shell, /etc/passwd modification) give any signal before the fixed kernel is running.

attack_vector.description: An unauthenticated attacker sends a POST to the Sophos Firewall User Portal/Webadmin Controller servlet with non-printable or non-ASCII characters in the JSON keys, bypassing the authentication filter to reach privileged handlers and chain to remote code execution on the appliance.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; no valid credentials required
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; a single crafted request against a reachable management interface
attack_vector.ai_factor: None; reported via Sophos bug bounty by a human researcher, exploited as a 0day by the DriftingCloud APT.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Ensure automatic hotfix installation is enabled (or apply the hotfix / upgrade to v18.5 MR4 / v19.0 GA), and remove WAN access to User Portal and Webadmin.
prevention.adequacy: The hotfix closes the bypass, but on a firewall exposed during the 0day window it does not evict DriftingCloud's webshells and VPN accounts; taking the management plane off the WAN is the independent control that would have prevented reachability.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alert on non-ASCII JSON keys in Controller requests, new VPN accounts/certificate pairs, and BEHINDER-consistent request patterns forwarded to an off-box SIEM.
detection.adequacy: Detection is effective only if firewall logs are shipped off the device, since an attacker with RCE can tamper with on-box telemetry.

response.what_would_have_worked: For any exposed appliance: config exfil, rebuild, rotate all credentials and remove attacker VPN accounts/certificates, and review outbound systems the firewall could reach.
response.adequacy: Patch-in-place is insufficient after 0day exploitation; only rebuild-and-rotate returns the boundary device to a trusted state.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: SI-2 is met for most Sophos estates by default auto-hotfix, yet it cannot account for the DriftingCloud 0day window from early March 2022: a firewall SI-2 marks patched on 2022-03-24 may already hold BEHINDER webshells and rogue VPN accounts from days earlier, and nothing in SI-2 forces the post-exposure compromise assessment that would find them.

NIST-800-53-SC-7.gap: SC-7 treats the Sophos appliance as the boundary enforcer, but the vulnerability is in the appliance's own WAN-reachable User Portal/Webadmin; an SC-7 design that allows the management plane to face untrusted networks exposes the unauthenticated Controller endpoint, and SC-7 as applied does not compel moving that surface behind VPN or Sophos Central.

NIS2-Art21-network-security.gap: Article 21 network security counts the firewall as a protective control while the User Portal is deliberately internet-published for remote users; that exposure makes the non-ASCII-key auth bypass reachable from anywhere, and an Article 21 posture that does not segregate the User-Portal/administrative surface from untrusted networks leaves the CVSS 9.8 pre-auth RCE open.

UK-CAF-B2.gap: CAF B2 identity and access control is evidenced through admin accounts and granted rights, but this bug bypasses the authentication decision itself: a request with non-printable or non-ASCII JSON keys reaches privileged Controller handlers with no valid session, so a B2 assessment of who may administer the firewall passes while an unauthenticated attacker administers it anyway, because the enforcement code fails below the account model B2 examines.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Essential Eight patch-applications is largely satisfied by Sophos auto-hotfix, but its timeliness metric says nothing about the pre-patch 0day exposure DriftingCloud used; a firewall recorded 'patched' on 2022-03-24 could have been compromised in early March, and the patch control neither detects nor triggers response to that prior compromise.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.22.gap: A.8.22 segregation of networks would keep the firewall management and User Portal surfaces off untrusted segments, yet deployments routinely publish the User Portal to the internet for remote access; an A.8.22 assessment that accepts that as a business need leaves the unauthenticated Controller bypass reachable from anywhere, which is exactly the reachability the DriftingCloud intrusion required.

new_control_requirements.name: PERIMETER-DEVICE-ZERODAY-SLA-TIER
new_control_requirements.description: Compliance frameworks must define a distinct patch SLA tier for pre-auth RCE on perimeter-trust-boundary devices (firewalls, VPN concentrators, WAFs, edge load-balancers). Tier requirement: vendor-mitigation deployed within 4 hours of KEV listing OR isolation of the vulnerable interface; standard 14/30-day SLAs do not apply because the device IS the trust boundary.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Sophos Firewall CVE-2022-1040 (KEV 2022-03-31, CVSS 9.8, EPSS 0.998) is a pre-auth RCE on the perimeter device itself, exploited as a 0day by DriftingCloud; the standard patch SLA is irrelevant because reachability of the User Portal/Webadmin is the whole exposure, so the tier's 'isolate the vulnerable interface' branch is the operative control.

new_control_requirements.name: PERIMETER-COMPROMISE-REBUILD-NOT-PATCH
new_control_requirements.description: Pre-rehearsed IR runbook for any perimeter device that suffers a pre-auth RCE CVE in active exploitation MUST default to config-exfil + rebuild + credential rotation, not patch-in-place. Patch-in-place leaves attacker-installed implants intact.
new_control_requirements.evidence: DriftingCloud exploited CVE-2022-1040 as a 0day to plant BEHINDER webshells and create rogue VPN accounts on the Sophos Firewall before the hotfix; on any exposed appliance the auto-hotfix leaves those implants intact, so the rebuild-and-rotate default is the only response that restores the boundary device to a trusted state.

CVE-2022-1096.name: Google Chromium V8 Type Confusion Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: A crafted HTML page triggers a V8 property-access interceptor type confusion (via a toString callback during property assignment on an interceptor object) that duplicates an owned property and corrupts the object, giving heap corruption a remote attacker can develop into renderer code execution.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; served to any visitor
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L but UI:R; the victim must load the malicious page
attack_vector.ai_factor: None; reported anonymously to Google, no AI-assisted discovery claimed.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Update every Chromium browser to the build carrying the V8 fix (Chrome 99.0.4844.84) and enforce a browser relaunch so the patched renderer is running.
prevention.adequacy: The update fully fixes it, but only after relaunch and only across every Chromium browser present; staged-not-restarted browsers and un-inventoried Chromium downstreams remain exposed.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alert on renderer crashes tied to specific pages and on browsers running below the fixed build via endpoint inventory.
detection.adequacy: Renderer exploitation is quiet; detection mostly surfaces exposure (stale versions) rather than the exploit itself.

response.what_would_have_worked: Force-relaunch updated browsers, and for suspected drive-by targets review the endpoint for follow-on payloads.
response.adequacy: A successful renderer exploit is a foothold; response depends on catching post-exploitation activity, since the renderer compromise itself leaves little trace.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: SI-2 marks Chrome remediated at 99.0.4844.84 by installed version, but the fix is only live after the browser process relaunches; a user holding a long session on the pre-99.0.4844.84 build is still exploitable by the in-the-wild drive-by, so SI-2 keyed to installed rather than running version overstates remediation against the 2022-03-28 KEV listing.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: Article 21 patch management scoped to Chrome misses that the same V8 defect ships in Edge, Opera, Brave and other Chromium browsers; an estate that patches Chrome and closes the finding leaves every other Chromium browser exposed until its vendor build lands, so the shared-engine reach defeats a product-scoped Article 21 programme.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: CAF B4 managed updates assume a deployed update is an effective one, but a Chrome update requires a relaunch to take effect; a B4 baseline that measures deployment without enforcing browser restart leaves users on the vulnerable renderer against a drive-by exploit already observed in the wild, so the control is nominally met yet ineffective.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Essential Eight patch-applications counts Chrome patched on install, but the metric captures neither the relaunch requirement nor the multi-browser Chromium spread; a fleet at target maturity can still run the vulnerable V8 renderer in a stale session or in a secondary Chromium browser the inventory never enumerated, understating the exposure.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: A.8.8 keyed to installed-version scanning flags Chrome remediated at 99.0.4844.84 but does not verify the process relaunched nor enumerate other Chromium browsers carrying the same V8 build; against an exploit confirmed in the wild, that leaves residual drive-by exposure the A.8.8 register does not surface.

new_control_requirements.name: BROWSER-MANAGED-UPDATE-NO-DEFERRAL
new_control_requirements.description: Enterprise update rings must not defer security-channel browser updates beyond 24h.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Chrome V8 CVE-2022-1096 (KEV 2022-03-28, exploit in the wild) is fixed in 99.0.4844.84 but only after relaunch; a no-deferral browser-update ring that also forces relaunch is what actually moves users off the vulnerable renderer within the KEV window, closing the gap that update-installed-but-not-restarted leaves open.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2022-1096 was KEV-listed 2022-03-28 with an exploit already in the wild and the same V8 defect present across Chromium browsers; the SLA's 'verified mitigation' requirement forces confirming the running build across Chrome and every Chromium downstream, not just installing the Chrome update, which is the product-scoped gap Article-21-style patching leaves.

CVE-2022-1364.name: Google Chromium V8 Type Confusion Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: A crafted HTML page drives a V8 Turbofan escape-analysis inconsistency that materializes an ArgumentsObject multiple times over a shared backing store, corrupting the heap in a way a remote attacker develops into renderer code execution.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; served to any visitor
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L but UI:R; the victim must load the page and Turbofan must optimize the trigger
attack_vector.ai_factor: None; reported by Clément Lecigne of Google TAG — a threat-hunting team whose name is not evidence of AI-assisted discovery.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Apply the 2022-04-14 emergency update (Chrome 100.0.4896.127) across every Chromium browser and enforce a relaunch so the patched Turbofan is running.
prevention.adequacy: The update fully fixes it after relaunch, but staged-not-restarted browsers and un-inventoried Chromium downstreams stay exposed, and it does not address the likelihood of further Turbofan bypasses.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alert on page-specific renderer crashes and on browsers below the fixed build via endpoint inventory.
detection.adequacy: JIT exploitation is quiet; detection largely surfaces exposure (stale versions) rather than the exploit.

response.what_would_have_worked: Force-relaunch updated browsers and review endpoints of likely targeted users for follow-on activity given TAG-observed targeting.
response.adequacy: A renderer compromise is a foothold; response depends on catching post-exploitation, since the renderer bug itself leaves little trace.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: SI-2 marks Chrome remediated at 100.0.4896.127 by installed version, but the emergency fix is only live after the process relaunches; a user on a long session with the pre-100.0.4896.127 Turbofan build stays exploitable by the in-the-wild drive-by, so an SI-2 status keyed to installed rather than running version overstates remediation against the 2022-04-15 KEV listing.

NIS2-Art21-vulnerability-handling.gap: Article 21 vulnerability handling that closes this on the Chrome product misses the shared V8 Turbofan defect in Edge, Opera and Brave; those browsers stay unhandled until each vendor build lands, and being the third actively-exploited Chrome 0day of 2022 signals further Turbofan bypasses are likely — context a product-scoped handling process does not carry forward.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: CAF B4 managed updates assume a deployed update takes effect, but the 2022-04-14 emergency Chrome update needs a relaunch to activate; a B4 baseline measuring deployment without enforcing browser restart leaves users on the vulnerable Turbofan renderer against a drive-by already active in the wild, so B4 is nominally met yet ineffective here.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Essential Eight patch-applications counts Chrome patched on install of 100.0.4896.127, but the metric captures neither the relaunch requirement nor the multi-Chromium spread; a fleet reported at target maturity can still run the vulnerable V8 JIT in a stale session or a secondary Chromium browser the inventory omits, understating the real exposure.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: A.8.8 keyed to installed-version scanning flags Chrome remediated at 100.0.4896.127 but does not confirm the process relaunched nor enumerate other Chromium browsers carrying the same Turbofan build; against an exploit confirmed in the wild, that leaves residual drive-by exposure the A.8.8 register does not surface.

new_control_requirements.name: BROWSER-MANAGED-UPDATE-NO-DEFERRAL
new_control_requirements.description: Enterprise update rings must not defer security-channel browser updates beyond 24h.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Chrome Turbofan CVE-2022-1364 (KEV 2022-04-15, emergency update 2022-04-14, exploit in the wild) is fixed in 100.0.4896.127 but only after relaunch; a no-deferral browser-update ring that forces relaunch is what actually moves users off the vulnerable JIT within the KEV window, closing the installed-but-not-restarted gap.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2022-1364 was KEV-listed 2022-04-15 with an exploit in the wild and the same Turbofan defect across Chromium browsers; the SLA's 'verified mitigation' requirement forces confirming the running build across Chrome and every Chromium downstream rather than logging the Chrome install, which is the exact gap a product-scoped vulnerability-handling process leaves.

attack_vector.description: Two authentication checks in front of the same service, each believing the other performed the check. A request that names the admin user, attaches a junk auth token and asks the reverse proxy to strip that token before forwarding satisfies the proxy's presence test and then arrives at a back end that treats a token-free request as pre-authenticated. The caller then runs shell commands as root through /mgmt/tm/util/bash.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; no credential, session or prior foothold is needed, and the password field in the Authorization header is never checked
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; one HTTP POST, no race, no memory corruption, no information leak. The real constraint is network reachability of iControl REST, and public tooling automates the whole sequence
attack_vector.ai_factor: No AI involvement in discovery or weaponization. F5 credits no external finder that resolves publicly, and the technical mechanism entered the public record through manual patch analysis by Horizon3.ai after the advisory.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Upgrading to 16.1.2.2 / 15.1.5.1 / 14.1.4.6 / 13.1.5 and booting the new volume, or — on the End of Technical Support branches where no fix exists — removing iControl REST reachability from every network except a dedicated management segment and scheduling the unit's replacement.
prevention.adequacy: The BOD clock allowed 21 days for a bug that had public exploit code within 8 days of the advisory and ransomware association recorded at listing. Management-plane isolation bounds the attacker population but does not repair the bypass, and it is unavailable to any team that administers the appliance from a general corporate network.
