There is no configuration-side alternative to fall back on, because CLFS cannot be disabled or blocked, so a host that cannot take the restart has no mitigation at all.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Endpoint telemetry that alarms when a process's token changes to SYSTEM without a new process being created, correlated with .blf file creation by a non-administrative process in the preceding seconds.
detection.adequacy: The token-swap signal is high fidelity and rarely collected; most estates alert on new SYSTEM processes and services, which this exploit never creates. File-integrity and signature-based tooling have nothing to match, since the attacker's artefact is a data file the kernel is designed to read and a small binary that runs once.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating a host where the escalation ran as compromised at SYSTEM — rotating every credential cached on it, reviewing what the SYSTEM context reached, and rebuilding rather than patching forward.
response.adequacy: The April 2022 update removes the flaw and nothing the attacker did with it, which on a ransomware chain means the operator still holds a host that has already surrendered its cached credentials. Because Cuba used this as the escalation stage rather than the objective, the correct scope of response is the intrusion the escalation served, not this CVE.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: SI-2 is met by deploying the April 2022 cumulative update, and it accepts deployment as the evidence of correction. Because clfs.sys stays vulnerable until the host restarts, a fleet reported fully remediated can be fully exploitable, and the control provides no place to record the difference. It also treats this as one flaw in one month, while CLFS has produced ten KEV escalation entries between 2019 and 2025, so the recurrence never accumulates into a changed posture.

NIST-800-53-SI-4.gap: SI-4 monitoring is genuinely deployed on most Windows estates and has almost nothing to see here: no service creation, no driver load, no binary replacement, no crash. The observable is a running process whose token becomes SYSTEM without a new process, which standard event collection does not surface. A monitoring capability that passes its own assessment can therefore be blind to the whole escalation, which is why the Cuba operators could use it as a routine chain step.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: The patch-management obligation drives the April 2022 update through the normal monthly cycle, and Microsoft's record for this CVE already read Exploitation Detected on 2022-04-12. Starting a monthly cadence against an adversary with functional exploit code at publication means the obligation is met and the exposure window is set by the cadence rather than by the threat. The obligation also cannot weight a Remote Desktop session host above a single-user laptop, though only one of them makes the exploit's precondition routine.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: B4's secure-configuration and least-functionality expectations produce real hardening across an estate and produce nothing for a core kernel driver. CLFS cannot be disabled, blocklisted or scoped to a subset of callers, so between disclosure and reboot there is no configuration change that reduces exposure. An operator with an exemplary B4 position holds precisely one lever on this CVE, and it is the restart.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Patch operating systems classifies this as a local escalation on interior hosts and assigns it the slower maturity window accordingly. Cuba ransomware used it from early May 2022 as the escalation stage of an intrusion, which is exactly the interior scenario the slower window presumes is less urgent. Reporting by patch-installed state rather than running build compounds it, because an unrebooted host counts toward the maturity score while still executing the vulnerable driver.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: A.8.8 was discharged correctly for this CVE — the advisory was ingested on 2022-04-12, exposure evaluated and a change raised. The clause's unit of assessment is the individual vulnerability, so the record closes and carries nothing forward into CVE-2022-37969 in September 2022 or CVE-2023-28252 the following April, both in the same driver. An exposure evaluation with no memory of the component's history will keep scoring the eleventh CLFS defect the way it scored the first.

new_control_requirements.name: INCOMPLETE-PATCH-SEQUENCE-SEVERITY-MULTIPLIER
new_control_requirements.description: Vulnerability-management programs must apply a severity multiplier when a CVE is the Nth in an incomplete-patch sequence on the same primitive (third MOTW bypass, second AMSI bypass, etc.). Framework controls treating each CVE as discrete obscure the structural defect; the Nth CVE in a sequence implies that future bypasses on the same primitive are likely.
new_control_requirements.evidence: The Windows Common Log File System driver is the clearest instance of this pattern in the KEV catalog: ten CLFS privilege-escalation entries are listed, running CVE-2019-1214, CVE-2021-36955, CVE-2022-24521, CVE-2022-37969, CVE-2023-23376, CVE-2023-28252, CVE-2024-49138, CVE-2025-29824, CVE-2025-32701 and CVE-2025-32706, with five flagged for ransomware campaign use including this one. Scoring this entry as a discrete Important-severity local escalation in April 2022 is what let the next four arrive at the same weight; the multiplier is what turns 'patch clfs.sys again' into a standing expectation that another CLFS defect is coming and that hosts with many interactive non-administrative users need the shortest reboot window every time.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Microsoft published this fix on 2022-04-12 already recording Exploitation Detected, CISA listed it on 2022-04-13 with a 2022-05-04 due date, and Unit 42 observed Cuba ransomware using it from early May 2022. Because CLFS cannot be disabled, the control's compensating-control option is unavailable here and the four-hour clock reduces to one measurable thing: hosts reaching the fixed build and restarting onto it. Verification must be the running build — 10.0.22000.613, 10.0.20348.643, 10.0.19044.1645 and the rest per SKU — rather than the console's update state, because an unrebooted host still runs vulnerable clfs.sys.

CVE-2022-26871.name: Trend Micro Apex Central Arbitrary File Upload Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: An unauthenticated request uploads a file to Apex Central, whose content check tests against an incomplete set of rejected cases rather than an allowed set, so content the server will subsequently execute passes; the outcome is remote code execution on the console that manages every Apex One agent in the estate.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N with UI:N; the vulnerable upload path answers before any authentication decision, so no console account, agent certificate or session is required
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; a single request with no race, no grooming and no chained precondition. The only gate is reaching the console's web surface, which every managed agent must be able to do, so the reachable population is normally the whole managed estate.
attack_vector.ai_factor: No finder is credited by Trend Micro as CNA, and the vendor's own confirmation that attacks preceded the fix means the flaw may have surfaced through incident response rather than research. Nothing in the vendor notice or the JPCERT/CC alert indicates automated or model-assisted discovery on either side.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Applying Apex Central Patch 3 (Build 6016) on 2022-03-29, the day Trend Micro published it alongside its confirmation of active attacks, and confining the console's web surface to the segments that host managed agents rather than leaving it broadly reachable.
prevention.adequacy: The directive's 2022-04-21 due date is three weeks after the vendor had already confirmed exploitation, so meeting it on time is compatible with having been exploited before the clock started. The patch is also only half the required action here: because attacks preceded it, an exposed console needs examination for what was written through the upload path, and BOD 22-01 asks only for the update.

detection.what_would_have_worked: File-integrity monitoring on the Apex Central web application directories alerting on any file that does not belong to a vendor package, and alerting on the console's web worker process spawning a command interpreter.
detection.adequacy: Both are reliable and neither is common, because a security-management server is usually treated as a source of monitoring rather than a monitored subject — the console is frequently excluded from endpoint tooling to avoid conflicts. Without a public exploit or a published request shape the network-side signature option does not exist, which leaves host-side integrity monitoring as the only workable detection.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating an exposed pre-6016 console as compromised: rebuilding it from vendor media, rotating its credentials and any integration secrets it held, and reviewing every policy and agent-configuration change it issued during the exposure window.
response.adequacy: The policy-review step is the one that matters and the one nobody performs, because code execution on this console means the attacker could alter exclusions or push configuration to protected endpoints, and those changes survive the console being patched. Rebuilding the management server is also disruptive enough that it needs pre-authorisation rather than an argument during the incident.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: SI-2 is met by moving every Apex Central installation to Build 6016, and the vendor made that easy by publishing the patch on 2022-03-29. Because Trend Micro confirmed attacks before the patch existed, remediation and compromise assessment were required at the same moment and the control captures only the first. A closed SI-2 record for this CVE says the console is no longer vulnerable and says nothing about what reached it while it was.

NIST-800-53-SI-3.gap: SI-3 is satisfied by the very product this CVE compromises: Apex Central is how the organisation demonstrates malicious-code protection across its endpoints. The control's evidence is agent coverage and definition currency, none of which is affected by the console being remotely executable by an unauthenticated caller. Treating the protection platform as the source of assurance rather than as an asset in scope is what leaves its control plane unexamined.

NIST-800-53-SC-7.gap: SC-7 would remove the precondition and is hard to apply to a console every managed agent must reach. Assessments record that reachability as required functionality and rarely separate the agent check-in surface from the administrative surface. The consequence is that an unauthenticated upload path is reachable from every segment that hosts an endpoint, which in most estates means all of them.

NIS2-Art21-vulnerability-management.gap: The measure obliges handling and remediation and treats a security console as ordinary software, so this CVE entered the intake queue at the same tier as an office application. Trend Micro and JPCERT/CC both stated on 2022-03-29 that exploitation was already occurring, so an ordinary triage cadence began behind the adversary. Nothing in the measure elevates the asset whose compromise reaches every managed endpoint simultaneously.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: B4 assesses the security of systems in scope, and a security-management console is usually cited in a CAF submission as supporting evidence for other principles rather than assessed as a system under B4. Its patch level, its web exposure and its account model therefore fall outside the examination. That is how an operator holds a credible B4 position while the console managing every endpoint runs below Build 6016 with an unauthenticated upload path.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Patch applications drives the update to Build 6016 and depends on the application inventory containing Apex Central in the first place, which security-management servers frequently are not — and secondary, DR and lab consoles almost never are. The control also has no way to represent that Apex Central as a Service was remediated by the vendor at Build 202203 while the on-premises installations are the operator's work, so a hybrid estate reports a single patch state for two different remediation obligations.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.7.gap: A.8.7 requires protection against malware and is evidenced by the Apex Central console's own coverage reporting, which makes the compromised asset the auditor's source of assurance. The clause never asks whether the malware-protection management plane is itself defended, patched or network-restricted. An organisation can therefore demonstrate complete, current endpoint protection administered from a server that any unauthenticated caller can execute code on.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: Obtaining the vulnerability information was trivial here — a vendor notice and a JPCERT/CC alert on 2022-03-29 — and A.8.8 was discharged by raising the change to Build 6016. The clause scopes action to the vulnerability, while the vendor's confirmation of prior attacks meant the required action also covered inspecting the console's web directories and reviewing the policy changes it had issued. The record closes on the build number and leaves the console's own integrity unassessed.

new_control_requirements.name: SECURITY-TOOL-INTEGRITY-VERIFICATION
new_control_requirements.description: Security tools (AV/AM, EDR, vulnerability scanners) must be treated as in-scope of vulnerability management with the same SLAs as other privileged software. Definition-update channels must use TLS with certificate pinning. Compliance audits must include a trust-anchor-inversion test: deliver a crafted input to the security tool in a sandbox and confirm rejection.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Apex Central is the management console for Trend Micro's endpoint-protection estate, and this CVE is an unauthenticated arbitrary file upload leading to code execution on it — the malware-protection control plane as the target rather than the defence. The trust-anchor-inversion test is the exact check that matches the defect: the console's upload path tested content against an incomplete rejected set, so delivering crafted upload content to a staging Apex Central below Build 6016 and confirming rejection is what distinguishes a working check from a paper one. Trend Micro confirmed attacks on 2022-03-29, the same day it shipped Patch 3, which is why holding the console to the same patch SLA as other privileged software is the load-bearing half of the control here.

new_control_requirements.name: PEN-TEST-SCOPE-INCLUDES-SECURITY-PRODUCTS
new_control_requirements.description: Penetration test and red-team scopes must explicitly include security-defense products (EDR, AV, DLP, identity-providers, secret-managers) as in-scope attack surface, not as defenses to evade. Scope language must call out that these products' admin interfaces, agent processes, and update channels are testable surfaces.
new_control_requirements.evidence: The vulnerable surface on this entry is Apex Central's unauthenticated web upload path — an antivirus product's administrative interface, which is precisely the surface this control says must be inside the test scope rather than treated as the defence being evaded. No public proof of concept exists for CVE-2022-26871 and Trend Micro never published a request shape, so an operator cannot buy assurance from a template or a scanner signature; the only route to knowing whether the console answers unauthenticated uploads from a given segment is to have someone test it. Scoping in the console also surfaces the reachability question, since a server every Apex One agent must reach is rarely confined to an administrative segment.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Trend Micro published Apex Central Patch 3 (Build 6016) on 2022-03-29 while simultaneously confirming that attacks exploiting the flaw had been observed, JPCERT/CC issued alert at220008 the same day, and CISA listed the CVE on 2022-03-31 with a 2022-04-21 due date. A four-hour clock from patch availability is the only cadence that closes an unauthenticated CVSS 9.8 path on the endpoint-security console before the three-week regulatory window elapses, and the control's compensating-control clause covers the interim step available immediately on every installation, which is restricting the console's web surface to the segments that host managed agents.

CVE-2022-26904.name: Microsoft Windows User Profile Service Privilege Escalation Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: A standard user races the SYSTEM-privileged User Profile Service between its validation of a directory and its use of it, substituting a junction so the service writes where the user cannot; the published chain uses that to plant a DLL in a system directory and triggers a UAC prompt so ProfSvc loads and executes it as SYSTEM.
attack_vector.privileges_required: low — PR:L with AV:L; an ordinary logged-on account is enough, plus credentials for a second non-administrative account that has previously logged on to the same host
attack_vector.complexity: high — AC:H; Microsoft's FAQ states the attacker must win a race condition, and the public chain adds the second-account and UAC Always-notify preconditions. The rating overstates the practical difficulty on shared hosts, where those preconditions are normal and the shipped Metasploit module is rated crash-safe with a repeatable session.
attack_vector.ai_factor: Credited by Microsoft to KLINIX5, who also authored the original proof of concept that Grant Willcox turned into the Metasploit module — human research on a SYSTEM service's junction handling, published before the fix, which is why Microsoft's record reads Publicly Disclosed: Yes. Nothing indicates AI involvement in discovery or weaponisation.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Installing the April 2022 cumulative update and restarting, prioritising hosts that carry multiple standard-user profiles, since the same servicing operation also closes CVE-2022-24521 on the same machines.
prevention.adequacy: The 2022-05-16 due date is over a month after working exploit code was already public, so the directive's clock never led the threat here. There is also no fallback: the User Profile Service cannot be disabled on a machine that hosts user sessions, and the one configuration precondition in the chain — UAC at Always notify — is a setting that should be kept, not weakened.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Endpoint telemetry alarming on a non-administrative process creating a junction or reparse point whose target resolves into a system directory, correlated with a DLL appearing in that directory and being loaded by the ProfSvc service host.
detection.adequacy: Reparse-point creation by unprivileged processes is rare enough to be a usable signal and is rarely collected, because it is not a default audit category. The race itself is noisy — repeated create-and-delete against another profile's directories — but that noise looks like ordinary filesystem churn unless it is correlated with the junction creation that follows it.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating a host where the escalation ran as compromised at SYSTEM: rotating credentials cached on it, reviewing what the SYSTEM context reached on the network, and rebuilding rather than patching forward.
response.adequacy: On a shared session host this is expensive and disruptive, which is exactly why it gets skipped in favour of applying the update. The update removes the flaw and leaves whatever the attacker did with SYSTEM, and on a machine carrying many users' sessions the credential exposure is proportional to how many of them were logged on during the window.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: SI-2 is met by deploying the April 2022 cumulative update and accepts deployment as evidence of correction, while the User Profile Service keeps its vulnerable behaviour until the host restarts. It also treats this as a single flaw, when three User Profile Service escalation entries reached the KEV catalog between 2022-03-31 and 2022-04-25. A remediation record that closes on one build number cannot express that the same service produced three KEV-listed escalations in a month.

NIST-800-53-AC-2.gap: AC-2 governs the lifecycle of accounts in the directory and produces good evidence of provisioning, review and disablement, none of which touches the exploit's actual precondition. The published chain needs a second ordinary account that has previously logged on to the specific host, and account management never asks how many stale standard profiles have accumulated on a given session host. An estate with immaculate account hygiene can still have machines where that precondition is satisfied dozens of times over.

NIST-800-53-AC-6.gap: Least privilege is genuinely implemented wherever ordinary users hold no administrative rights, and that is the exact population this exploit is written for. The boundary that fails is inside a SYSTEM service's own handling of directories, which no account-privilege decision reaches, and the attacker never needs a privileged account at any point. An AC-6 attestation is therefore accurate and describes the attacker's starting position rather than an obstacle.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: The obligation drives the April 2022 update through the standard monthly cycle, starting from a position where Microsoft's own record already read Publicly Disclosed: Yes — working exploit code preceded the fix. A cadence that is timely by the measure's standard is late against code that was already in circulation. The obligation also cannot weight a Remote Desktop session host above a laptop, though only the former routinely supplies the second logged-on standard account the chain needs.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: B4 drives secure configuration, and here the flaw sits in a service that cannot be removed or scoped on any machine hosting user sessions, so almost none of that hardening applies. The one relevant configuration item inverts the usual logic: User Account Control at the default Always notify is a precondition of the published chain, and it is nevertheless a setting to keep rather than weaken. B4 has no way to record a hardening control that is simultaneously part of an exploit path and correct to retain.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Patch operating systems places this in the slower maturity window on the strength of a 7.0 score and an AC:H rating, and the shipped Metasploit module is rated crash-safe with a repeatable session — the complexity that justified the slower tier has been engineered away in public tooling. Reporting by patch-installed state rather than running build compounds it, because a host that has taken the update and not restarted counts as compliant. Neither adjustment is available inside the control as written.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: A.8.8 was discharged properly for this CVE: the April 2022 advisory was ingested, exposure evaluated and a change raised. Its unit of assessment is the individual vulnerability, so the record closes with nothing carried forward from CVE-2021-34484 or CVE-2022-21919 in the same service, all three of which reached the KEV catalog within four weeks of each other. An exposure evaluation with no memory of the component cannot produce the conclusion that the User Profile Service warrants standing attention.

new_control_requirements.name: INCOMPLETE-PATCH-SEQUENCE-SEVERITY-MULTIPLIER
new_control_requirements.description: Vulnerability-management programs must apply a severity multiplier when a CVE is the Nth in an incomplete-patch sequence on the same primitive (third MOTW bypass, second AMSI bypass, etc.). Framework controls treating each CVE as discrete obscure the structural defect; the Nth CVE in a sequence implies that future bypasses on the same primitive are likely.
new_control_requirements.evidence: The Windows User Profile Service produced three KEV-listed privilege escalations inside a single month — CVE-2021-34484 added 2022-03-31, then CVE-2022-21919 and CVE-2022-26904 both added 2022-04-25 — and the Metasploit module for this entry cites a write-up on the patch iterations for that service. Treating this one as a discrete AC:H local escalation scored 7.0 is what keeps it in the slow patch tier; the multiplier is what makes an operator schedule the April 2022 restart on shared session hosts first and expect the same service to produce another bypass.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Microsoft shipped the fix on 2022-04-12 with its own record already reading Publicly Disclosed: Yes, and CISA listed the CVE on 2022-04-25 with a 2022-05-16 due date — over a month after working exploit code existed. Because the User Profile Service cannot be disabled, the control's compensating-control option is unavailable and the four-hour clock reduces to hosts reaching the fixed build and restarting; verification must be the running build (10.0.22000.613, 10.0.19044.1645 and the rest per SKU) rather than the console's update state. The same servicing operation also closes CVE-2022-24521 on these hosts, so one restart discharges two KEV clocks.

CVE-2022-29464.name: WSO2 Multiple Products Unrestrictive Upload of File Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: An unauthenticated caller posts a multipart form to the Carbon management console's file-upload endpoint with a filename that walks out of the staging directory and into the Tomcat webapp tree. The next request to that path executes the uploaded JSP inside the WSO2 JVM. From there the attacker is running code on the box that terminates API traffic or issues identity tokens for everything downstream of it.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; the /fileupload endpoint answers before any Carbon console authentication, and the public exploit needs nothing beyond the base URL of the management listener.
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; a single multipart POST carrying a traversal filename, with no race to win and no leak to chain, and the destination webapp path identical across every affected product.
attack_vector.ai_factor: Manual research by Orange Tsai of DEVCORE, credited in WSO2-2021-1738. No AI-branded research arm is involved, and no tooling-assisted discovery is claimed in the advisory or in the Metasploit module metadata.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Restricting the Carbon management listener to an administrative segment, plus the deployment.toml / carbon.xml mitigation WSO2 published on 2022-04-01, would have removed the unauthenticated path well before the 2022-05-16 KEV due date.
prevention.adequacy: Neither is complete alone. The configuration mitigation is a state a later product upgrade or a rebuilt node reverts silently, and segmentation does nothing about an attacker who already reaches the management port from a DMZ or partner segment that legitimately needs it.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alerting on any JSP appearing under repository/deployment/server/webapps that is not part of the shipped distribution, and on child processes of the Carbon JVM.
detection.adequacy: File-integrity monitoring on the deployment directory is noisy on a node that legitimately hot-deploys artefacts, and a webshell that only ever executes Java in-JVM produces no child process to catch.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating any exposed instance as compromised: rebuild from a clean distribution at the fixed update level, rotate the service account and every key or token the node held, and review federation trust where the node was an Identity Server.
response.adequacy: Rebuild is decisive only when the exposure window is known, and for a flaw KEV-listed on 2022-04-25 with exploit code public within weeks the window usually predates whatever log retention the node has.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: A flaw-remediation programme that tracks whether the WSO2 node is on a supported release reports green throughout, because remediation for this CVE is an update level layered onto an unchanged product version. The evidence an auditor accepts — a patch report showing API Manager 3.2.0 current — is the same evidence a compromised node produces. Closing the finding honestly also requires proving nothing was written into the deployment directory between the 2022-04-01 advisory and the update, which no flaw-remediation record carries.

NIST-800-53-CM-7.gap: Least functionality is attested with a services-and-ports baseline, and every affected WSO2 install passes it: the only listener involved is the Carbon HTTPS management port the product legitimately needs. The functionality that had to be removed is one servlet inside that listener. No least-functionality implementation reaches that granularity, and the operator generally learns the tools upload executor exists only when the vendor tells them to disable it in carbon.xml.

NIST-800-53-SC-7.gap: Boundary protection was in place on the deployments that were hit, because putting API Manager in a DMZ is the reference architecture. The control governs where the node sits relative to the internal network and is silent on which of the node's own ports the internet may reach, so the management listener carrying /fileupload/toolsAny stayed exposed to exactly the population that consumes the API gateway.

NIS2-Art21-vulnerability-handling.gap: The vendor half worked: a coordinated report, an advisory on 2022-04-01, fixes delivered from February 2022. The entity half breaks on distribution. An open-source deployment has no update channel, so 'handle vulnerabilities per the supplier's instructions' resolves to applying two GitHub pull requests to carbon-kernel and carbon-identity-framework by hand — a step no vulnerability-handling procedure in an essential-entity submission describes, and one that needs a Java build capability the operations team may not have.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: The CAF outcomes here are assessed on secure build and maintained configuration, and a WSO2 node deployed from the vendor distribution with the documented hardening applied achieves them. The exposure came from a default that the hardening guidance did not mention until the advisory added it, so the assessment records a securely configured system that accepts an unauthenticated traversal filename. The principle also gives no weight to whether the management-interface population is bounded, which is what actually mattered.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Maturity Level 2 demands the 48-hour clock for a critical internet-facing flaw, and this qualifies at CVSS 9.8 with an EPSS score of 0.99999. The maturity model assumes the vendor artefact is a patch that patch-management tooling can deploy and verify; here it is a per-product update level. The evidence trail the model expects — scanner before, scanner after — cannot distinguish the patched from the unpatched state on a Carbon node at all.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: Subscribing to WSO2 advisories satisfies the information-gathering half of this control and produced the 2022-04-01 notification on time. The evaluation half fails on scoping: the asset register lists products, the defect lives in the shared Carbon kernel, and an organisation that checked only its API Manager estate left Enterprise Integrator 6.6.0 and Identity Server as Key Manager nodes running the identical executor unassessed and unremediated.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.28.gap: Secure coding is not a control the deploying organisation holds here. The defective join of an attacker-supplied multipart filename onto a filesystem path is in WSO2's own code, shipped across seven product lines and versions reaching back to Identity Server 5.2.0. The only consumer-side expression is a supplier-assurance question, and a vendor answering it affirmatively is entirely compatible with this defect surviving to a 2022-04-25 KEV listing with ransomware use recorded.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: WSO2 published WSO2-2021-1738 on 2022-04-01 and CISA listed CVE-2022-29464 on 2022-04-25 with a due date of 2022-05-16 — a 21-day window against a flaw whose EPSS score is 0.99999, with a Metasploit module, a Nuclei template and a public Python exploit all targeting WSO2 API Manager and Identity Server. The 'documented compensating controls' branch is the operative one for this product family, because the vendor fix is a subscription-gated update level while the deployment.toml / carbon.xml mitigation is the only action available within hours to an open-source Identity Server or Enterprise Integrator node.

new_control_requirements.name: MITIGATION-ACTIVE-PATCH-PENDING-VERDICT-CLASS
new_control_requirements.description: Compliance verdicts must distinguish three states: (a) binary patch deployed (vulnerability eliminated), (b) vendor-mitigation rule active, no binary patch (residual risk: any defect in the mitigation rule reopens the vulnerability), (c) no mitigation, no patch (full exposure). Audit reports must surface (b) as a distinct compensating-control state with an associated time-bound action item, not as a 'patched per SLA' outcome.
new_control_requirements.evidence: WSO2-2021-1738 offers two remediation states for the same CVE — the per-product update level, and a deployment.toml / carbon.xml configuration mitigation for installs that cannot take it — and a report recording both as 'remediated' loses the distinction that matters. A Carbon node running on the configuration mitigation is state (b): the tools upload executor is disabled by a setting that a later product upgrade, a rebuilt node or a restored configuration reverts silently, across an affected range spanning API Manager 2.2.0 to 4.0.0 and Identity Server 5.2.0 to 5.11.0. The time-bound action item this control demands is what carries the node from the 2022-04-25 KEV listing to an actual update level rather than leaving it indefinitely on a config flag.

new_control_requirements.name: PERIMETER-COMPROMISE-REBUILD-NOT-PATCH
new_control_requirements.description: Pre-rehearsed IR runbook for any perimeter device that suffers a pre-auth RCE CVE in active exploitation MUST default to config-exfil + rebuild + credential rotation, not patch-in-place. Patch-in-place leaves attacker-installed implants intact.
new_control_requirements.evidence: WSO2 API Manager is the internet-facing gateway in most deployments and Identity Server is the identity provider behind it, so both sit on the trust boundary this control governs, and CVE-2022-29464 is pre-auth RCE in active exploitation with CISA recording ransomware campaign use on the 2022-04-25 listing. The primitive writes a JSP into repository/deployment/server/webapps, which a WUM update level or the carbon-kernel PR 3152 patch does not remove — patch-in-place on a node exposed between the 2022-04-01 advisory and the 2022-05-16 due date leaves the webshell exactly where it was written. Configuration export, rebuild from a clean distribution and rotation of the service account plus any federation signing key the Identity Server node held is the only sequence that ends the exposure.

CVE-2022-30525.name: Zyxel Multiple Firewalls OS Command Injection Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: A JSON POST to the firewall's provisioning handler asks it to set a WAN port's MTU, and that MTU value is pasted into a shell command. The attacker supplies a semicolon and their own command instead of a number, and the firewall runs it as the nobody user. Everything the site's segmentation and VPN policy depends on is then being enforced by a device an anonymous internet host executes commands on.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; /ztp/cgi-bin/handler answers before any authentication decision is taken, so the console's administrator credentials, lockout policy and any second factor on the admin login are never reached.
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; one POST, no race and no memory corruption, and the real constraint is reachability of the device web service rather than anything about the payload.
attack_vector.ai_factor: Human reverse-engineering by Jake Baines at Rapid7. Rapid7 is a vendor research team with no AI-branded discovery claim attached to this finding, and neither the Zyxel advisory nor the Metasploit module metadata mentions automated discovery.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Keeping the device web service off WAN-reachable interfaces, and taking ZLD V5.30 within days of its 2022-04-28 release rather than at the next appliance-maintenance window.
prevention.adequacy: Restricting the web service bounds the attacker population but closes nothing — the ZTP handler cannot be disabled independently, so anything that legitimately reaches the device web interface, including a management VLAN an attacker already stands in, still reaches the injection point. And ZLD V5.30 needs a reboot of a device in the traffic path, which is why the window slips.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Forwarding the appliance's own web-service access log off-box and alerting on any request to /ztp/cgi-bin/handler reaching a unit that has already been provisioned.
detection.adequacy: The signal is clean but was almost never collected on 2022-era branch estates, and it only helps if the log leaves the device before the second stage lands — a firewall logging to itself gives an investigator whatever the attacker chose to leave behind.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating any WAN-reachable unit on ZLD V5.21 Patch 1 or below as compromised: export the configuration for analysis, rebuild on ZLD V5.30, and rotate the VPN pre-shared keys, administrator passwords and any RADIUS or LDAP bind credential the device held.
response.adequacy: Complete but expensive per site, and it depends on knowing the exposure window; with no off-box logging the honest window opens at the 2022-04-28 firmware release rather than at the first alert.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: Zyxel published ZLD V5.30 on 2022-04-28, two weeks before Rapid7's write-up and eighteen days before the KEV listing, so a flaw-remediation programme keyed to vendor releases had the artefact in hand early. What such a programme does not carry is the appliance-reboot dependency: firmware staged on a branch firewall but not activated leaves the ZTP handler running, and the remediation record shows the download rather than the running image.

NIST-800-53-SI-10.gap: This is the control the defect is an instance of, and it is not one an operator can hold for closed firmware. The mtu field is validated nowhere before the WAN-settings helper concatenates it into a string for os.system, and no customer-reachable configuration changes that. For a Zyxel firewall the control is meaningful only as a procurement requirement on the vendor, which is why it appears satisfied in an inherited-controls matrix and prevents nothing.

NIS2-Art21-network-security.gap: Network security under Article 21 assumes the firewall is the instrument of the control rather than its subject. Every segmentation, filtering and access-policy claim an entity makes about its branch sites is enforced by the same ATP or USG FLEX unit this unauthenticated POST executes commands on, so compromise invalidates the evidence base wholesale. The article does not oblige an entity to assess the enforcement device's own exposure as a separate asset.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: A branch firewall on ZLD V5.21 Patch 1 with strong administrator credentials and a second factor on the console satisfies the secure-configuration and access expectations here. The ZTP handler ignores all of it, answering before authentication, so credential strength, lockout policy and admin-account hygiene are never consulted. Assessment questions about who may administer the device return good answers about a path the attacker never uses.

UK-CAF-C1.gap: Security monitoring on these deployments generally means the firewall's own logs, which is the failure mode: the injected command runs as nobody on the device producing the telemetry, and the local log store is within reach of whatever it stages next. Without a requirement to ship perimeter-device logs in real time to a collector under separate credentials, the record of a 2022-era exploitation attempt is typically gone or tampered with by the time the unit is examined.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Essential Eight patching covers operating systems and applications; network-appliance firmware sits awkwardly outside both, and the 48-hour window for internet-facing critical flaws is written against tooling that has no agent on a Zyxel firewall. Compliance here reduces to a manual attestation that somebody logged into each branch unit and confirmed ZLD V5.30 — which across a multi-site estate is exactly the work that slips past the 2022-06-06 due date.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: The exposure evaluation this control asks for is unusually easy to get wrong here: the advisory lists model families, and an operator checking whether they run 'USG FLEX' can miss that the VPN series is affected from ZLD V4.60 while USG FLEX 100 is only affected from V5.00. One firmware line, a different lower bound per range, and an inventory that records model but not ZLD version cannot resolve either question.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.16.gap: Monitoring activities is typically evidenced by SIEM ingestion of firewall logs, and that ingestion existed on most affected estates. It captures the traffic the firewall forwards, not the requests made to the firewall's own web service, so an unauthenticated POST to /ztp/cgi-bin/handler and the HTTP 500 the published template expects generate nothing in the SIEM unless the device's own web-service log is separately forwarded.

new_control_requirements.name: PERIMETER-DEVICE-ZERODAY-SLA-TIER
new_control_requirements.description: Compliance frameworks must define a distinct patch SLA tier for pre-auth RCE on perimeter-trust-boundary devices (firewalls, VPN concentrators, WAFs, edge load-balancers). Tier requirement: vendor-mitigation deployed within 4 hours of KEV listing OR isolation of the vulnerable interface; standard 14/30-day SLAs do not apply because the device IS the trust boundary.
new_control_requirements.evidence: A Zyxel ATP, USG FLEX or VPN series unit is the trust boundary itself, and CVE-2022-30525 is unauthenticated command execution on it at CVSS 9.8 with an EPSS score of 0.99944. The standard tiers are exactly what failed: ZLD V5.30 shipped 2022-04-28, Rapid7 published on 2022-05-12 with more than 15,000 units visible on Shodan, CISA listed on 2022-05-16 and set 2022-06-06 — and a 30-day appliance-patching SLA still sits inside that window while the internet is already probing /ztp/cgi-bin/handler. For a multi-site estate the isolation branch is the realistic one: make the device web service unreachable from untrusted interfaces the same day, then take the reboot window site by site.

new_control_requirements.name: FIREWALL-EGRESS-TELEMETRY-SEPARATE-TRUST-ZONE
new_control_requirements.description: Firewall and other perimeter-trust-boundary devices must forward syslog, threat logs, and authentication logs to a SIEM hosted in a separate trust zone (different management plane, different credentials, different authentication path). Telemetry stored on the compromised device is destroyed by the attacker; telemetry on a separate-trust-zone collector survives.
new_control_requirements.evidence: The injected command executes as nobody on the same Zyxel unit that generates the security telemetry for its site, so any record of the POST to /ztp/cgi-bin/handler, the HTTP 500 that follows it, or the outbound fetch of a second stage sits on the device the attacker now runs commands on. For an estate of branch ATP and USG FLEX firewalls listed by CISA on 2022-05-16, the difference between knowing which sites were hit before the ZLD V5.30 upgrade and guessing is whether the device web-service and system logs were already leaving for a collector reached with different credentials.

new_control_requirements.name: PERIMETER-COMPROMISE-REBUILD-NOT-PATCH
new_control_requirements.description: Pre-rehearsed IR runbook for any perimeter device that suffers a pre-auth RCE CVE in active exploitation MUST default to config-exfil + rebuild + credential rotation, not patch-in-place. Patch-in-place leaves attacker-installed implants intact.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Zyxel firewalls hold the site's VPN pre-shared keys, administrator credentials and routing policy, and this CVE hands an unauthenticated caller command execution on them as nobody — enough to read that configuration and stage further tooling before the ZLD V5.30 upgrade lands. The firmware upgrade preserves the configuration partition, so a unit exposed between the 2022-04-28 firmware release and the 2022-06-06 KEV due date is not cleaned by the reboot that installs the fix. Defaulting the runbook to configuration export, rebuild on ZLD V5.30 and rotation of every credential and pre-shared key the unit held is what separates a remediated device from a patched one.

attack_vector.description: A single GET to /stainfo.cgi on an AirOS radio puts shell metacharacters into the ifname parameter, which reaches a shell unfiltered. The caller needs no account: Ubiquiti's advisory for this flaw says it grants remote users administrative access to AirOS v3/4 and v5 'without requiring authentication' and describes an http-server bug 'allowing users to bypass authentication and run commands', and NVD scores it PR:N. Changing the radio's management password is therefore not a partial mitigation — authentication is the thing being bypassed, and a radio behind a fresh credential is exposed exactly as much as one on the default. Exploit-DB 14146 happens to fire the request from a read-only account; that is how one write-up demonstrated it, not the boundary. The proof-of-concept reads the users block out of /tmp/system.cfg on that first request, handing over the administrative credential, and the same parameter executes anything else on the device thereafter. On 2011-12-19 Ubiquiti reported a worm spreading between AirOS radios through that same authentication bypass.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N in NVD's v3.1 vector and Au:N in its v2 vector, matching the vendor's own statement that the AirOS http server can be reached 'without requiring authentication'. The read-only account used in Exploit-DB 14146 is that write-up's convenience rather than a precondition, and no credential the operator controls stands between an attacker and the shell
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; one HTTP GET, no timing and no second stage, and CISA's SSVC decision of 2025-02-07 records automatable yes. The binding constraint is which networks can reach the AirOS management interface, and on subscriber CPE the served client network reaches it by construction
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Published as a hand-found zero-day on Exploit-DB in 2010 by an individual researcher; no vendor research arm and no automated discovery appear anywhere in the record.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Upgrading each radio to its own line's fixed build — v4.0.1, v5.3.5 or v5.4.5 — and binding the AirOS HTTP/HTTPS management interface to an address the subscriber and wireless-facing networks cannot route to.
prevention.adequacy: Partial by construction. The management-address restriction is unavailable on subscriber CPE, whose whole purpose is serving the network the attacker is on, and the firmware upgrade only takes effect after a reboot that drops the link a backhaul radio carries — so on the units hardest to take out of service the remaining prevention carries a customer outage as its price, and for as long as that price goes unpaid the radio keeps answering stainfo.cgi from the pre-fix build.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Central syslog from the radio fleet with alerting on shell metacharacters in stainfo.cgi requests, configuration-drift monitoring that flags an administrative password change outside a change window, and a fleet-wide sweep for the artefacts Ubiquiti published — adm.cgi in place of admin.cgi, and .skynet and rc.poststart under /etc/persistent.
detection.adequacy: A unit that forwards nothing gives an alerting rule nothing to fire on, and one that does forward can stop the moment the attacker has shell on the device generating the log. The artefact sweep asks that same unit what is on it, and it finds only what Ubiquiti documented for its worm — adm.cgi, .skynet, rc.poststart — not a hand-driven use of the same GET, which leaves none of those marks.

response.what_would_have_worked: Rebuilding an exposed radio from a known-good configuration rather than upgrading in place, rotating the administrative credential across every unit that shared it, and running the vendor's documented cleanup — removing /etc/persistent/rc.poststart and .skynet, then cfgmtd -w -p /etc/ and a reboot — on anything reachable while unpatched.
response.adequacy: Firmware upgrade alone is not remediation here: the credential left the device before the upgrade and stays valid afterwards, and Ubiquiti's own instructions say the new firmware prevents the worm returning without removing an infection already present — which is why the vendor shipped a separate removal tool. A WISP that reuses one administrative password across the fleet has a rotation scope equal to the whole fleet.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: A flaw-remediation programme that tracks 'AirOS version' as one field cannot express this CVE, because the fixed level is v4.0.1 on one product line, v5.3.5 on another and v5.4.5 on a third.

NIS2-Art21-network-security.gap: Article 21's network security measures are satisfied by segmenting an entity's networks from untrusted ones, and that framing has no place to put a subscriber CPE, which is simultaneously the operator's asset and a device whose management interface faces the untrusted network by design. An operator can hold a complete Article 21 attestation while every subscriber sits one unauthenticated GET away from shell on their own radio: Ubiquiti's 2011-12-19 advisory for CVE-2010-5330 states the AirOS http server grants administrative access without requiring authentication, and the worm described in the same thread moved between radios on that basis rather than by defeating any segmentation.

UK-CAF-B5.gap: B5's resilience outcomes are met by redundant wireless paths and tested failover, neither of which helps against a defect that is identical on both paths. A fleet built entirely from AirOS radios below v5.3.5 has a single correlated failure mode that redundancy amplifies rather than mitigates, and the CAF assessment records the redundancy without ever asking whether the two paths fail independently.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Essential Eight measures patching as elapsed time from a vendor release, and Ubiquiti's releases here — v4.0.1, v5.3.5 and v5.4.5 — long predate the 2022-04-15 KEV listing, so any radio below them is years outside every timeframe the model defines. The measurement records the deployment date and not the reboot that puts the new firmware in service, which on a point-to-point link is the step the operator schedules around a customer outage. A WISP can hold the maturity rating while the AP-info page on a subscriber radio still passes an unsanitized ifname to a shell.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.21.gap: A.8.21 is evidenced through identified security mechanisms and service levels for network services, which an ISMS will document for the carrier links and the managed monitoring. None of that documentation reaches the CGI on the operator's own radios, so an organisation can hold a clean A.8.21 finding while stainfo.cgi passes an unsanitized ifname to a shell on every unit in the fleet.

new_control_requirements.name: PERIMETER-COMPROMISE-REBUILD-NOT-PATCH
new_control_requirements.description: Pre-rehearsed IR runbook for any perimeter device that suffers a pre-auth RCE CVE in active exploitation MUST default to config-exfil + rebuild + credential rotation, not patch-in-place. Patch-in-place leaves attacker-installed implants intact.
new_control_requirements.evidence: A Ubiquiti AirOS radio is the perimeter for the network behind it, and CVE-2010-5330 satisfies both halves of this control's trigger outright. Pre-auth: Ubiquiti's advisory of 2011-12-19 — the reference NVD tags Vendor Advisory and Patch for this CVE — says the flaw grants remote users administrative access to AirOS v3/4 and v5 'without requiring authentication', matching NVD's AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N and its v2 Au:N. Active exploitation: CISA listed it on 2022-04-15 with a 2022-05-06 due date and recorded an SSVC decision of exploitation active, automatable yes on 2025-02-07, and the same vendor advisory documents a self-propagating worm that renamed admin.cgi to adm.cgi and wrote .skynet and rc.poststart into /etc/persistent. That worm is the implant case this control exists for: Ubiquiti had to publish manual removal steps and a removal tool because the fixed firmware prevents reinfection without clearing what is already on the device, so uploading v5.3.5 to an airMAX unit that was reachable while unpatched restores the code and preserves everything the attacker left and took — persistence, configuration changes, and the administrative credential the proof-of-concept reads out of /tmp/system.cfg on its very first request. Rebuild and rotate is what turns a firmware upgrade into remediation, and on a WISP that reuses one administrative password the rotation scope is the entire fleet, not the one radio.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Ubiquiti published fixed AirOS builds long before CISA listed this on 2022-04-15, so for every radio whose hardware can take one the SLA clock started at the KEV listing and the 2022-05-06 due date is already years past. The control's value on this product is that it forces per-line verification rather than a fleet-wide version assertion: v4.0.1 on the 802.11 line, v5.3.5 on airMAX and v5.4.5 on AirSync, each confirmed after the reboot the firmware upload requires. Where a legacy radio's fixed build can no longer be obtained, the same clock forces the documented compensating control — management-interface binding — instead of an open exception against an exploit that is a single URL.

CVE-2022-21919.name: Microsoft Windows User Profile Service Privilege Escalation Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: A SYSTEM service that copies files into a directory a standard user controls, and a user who decides what the paths inside it point to. Holding the second account's profile hive open forces the User Profile Service to fall back to a temporary profile under C:\Users\TEMP; a symbolic link planted partway down the destination path then redirects the Local System copy into C:\Windows\System32\osk.exe.local, and a comctl32.dll dropped in that DotLocal directory is loaded by the On-Screen Keyboard as SYSTEM when a UAC prompt is raised.
attack_vector.privileges_required: low — PR:L; an ordinary interactive local account, plus the credentials of a second non-administrative user who can log on locally and already has a profile directory under C:\Users for the exploit to lock open
attack_vector.complexity: high — AC:H; the symlink has to be swapped in while the Local System copy into C:\Users\TEMP is still running, and 0patch records that reproducing that race 'depends on lots of factors' and that on older Windows builds the vulnerable code differs and the window is extremely narrow
attack_vector.ai_factor: None recorded. Microsoft lists no acknowledged finder and marks the issue publicly disclosed before the January 2022 fix, so the route into the public record was discussion of the previous patch in this family rather than any tooling-assisted discovery.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Installing the January 2022 cumulative update and rebooting, verified by installed build rather than by the management console's approval state — 6.3.9600.20246, 6.2.9200.23584, 6.1.7601.25829, 6.0.6003.21349 or the branch's 2022-01-11 build.
prevention.adequacy: There is no configuration workaround to fall back on — the User Profile Service cannot be disabled on a machine that logs users in — so for most of the estate the rollup is the whole remediation. The one alternative is 0patch's micropatch, which applies without a reboot but only to Windows 10 v1809 through v21H1 and Server 2016 / 2019 at their late-2021 patch levels, leaving Windows 11, Server 2022 and the 8.1-and-earlier lines with the update as their only route. The deeper limit is that this code path was fixed and bypassed twice around this CVE, so a host correctly on the January build was exposed again to CVE-2022-26904 on 2022-04-12.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Auditing junction and symbolic-link creation by standard users under profile paths, and alerting when the User Profile Service writes outside the profile tree it was invoked for.
detection.adequacy: Link creation under a user's own profile is not rare enough to alert on by itself, so this only works paired with the SYSTEM-context process creation that follows. On workstations with no host-level audit policy shipped off-box there is nothing to key on at all.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating a confirmed escalation on a multi-user host as a credential-exposure event: rotating every account whose session or cached credential lived on that machine, not just remediating the build.
response.adequacy: Scoped correctly this contains the blast radius, but it depends on knowing the escalation happened, and this technique compiles nothing, loads no driver and crashes no process. Without pre-existing audit telemetry there is no artefact to trigger the response at all.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: An estate with documented flaw remediation was compliant on this CVE from the moment it absorbed the January 2022 rollup, and compliant equally if it deferred that rollup into its normal testing cycle. The control gives no way to distinguish those two states against a bug CISA only listed on 2022-04-25, three and a half months after the fix shipped. Its second limit is measurement: SI-2 evidence is the update record, while Microsoft marks every affected product restart-required, so an unrebooted host reports remediated and runs the vulnerable service.

NIST-800-53-AC-6.gap: An estate can satisfy least privilege completely — no standing local administrators, tiered administration, separate accounts for privileged work — and every bit of that remains true while an ordinary user takes SYSTEM. The escalation happens inside the User Profile Service, which runs as SYSTEM by design, so the account model is never consulted. Worse for the attestation, the published exploit needs a second ordinary user profile on the host, which a well-run shared workstation supplies as a matter of course.

NIS2-Art21-vulnerability-handling.gap: An entity running a documented handling process ingested Microsoft's 2022-01-11 advisory, read exploited: No on the vendor record, and scheduled the January rollup accordingly — which is what that record still says today, even though it also flags the CVE publicly disclosed with a proof-of-concept exploit. The obligation contains nothing that forces a re-rating when CISA lists the same CVE on 2022-04-25 with a 2022-05-16 deadline. Where vendor and catalog disagree on exploitation status, a compliant process silently follows the vendor and under-prioritises the entry.

UK-CAF-B2.gap: B2 is achieved through account lifecycle management, privilege separation and control of administrative rights, and none of that changes state while this flaw is exploited. The privilege boundary that fails sits inside a SYSTEM service, not in the identity system, so an assessor could examine every account on the host and find nothing wrong. The outcome is inverted here as well: the second standard user profile that good access management produces on a shared machine is the precondition the published exploit requires.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Operating-system patching under the Essential Eight is straightforward to evidence, and its monthly window for non-internet-facing systems makes mid-February 2022 a compliant remediation date for a 2022-01-11 update — before the KEV listing existed, which reads as adequate until you notice the model would say the same about a host patched after 2022-05-16. It records the update rather than the required reboot, and it draws no distinction between a single-user laptop and a session host where dozens of standard accounts satisfy this exploit's own precondition.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: The control was met on 2022-01-11 when the January bulletin was received, assessed and scheduled, and the exploitation input that assessment had was the vendor's exploited: No — a field Microsoft has never changed. Nothing in A.8.8 obliges the organisation to revisit the decision when the same CVE appears in an external exploited-vulnerability catalog on 2022-04-25 carrying a 2022-05-16 deadline. The result is a documented risk decision, still traceable to its evidence, that has quietly become wrong and that no scheduled review will surface.

new_control_requirements.name: INCOMPLETE-PATCH-SEQUENCE-SEVERITY-MULTIPLIER
new_control_requirements.description: Vulnerability-management programs must apply a severity multiplier when a CVE is the Nth in an incomplete-patch sequence on the same primitive (third MOTW bypass, second AMSI bypass, etc.). Framework controls treating each CVE as discrete obscure the structural defect; the Nth CVE in a sequence implies that future bypasses on the same primitive are likely.
new_control_requirements.evidence: The Windows User Profile Service produced three CVEs on one primitive across eight months: CVE-2021-34484 on 2021-08-10, then CVE-2022-21919 on 2022-01-11 closing the bypass of that fix, then CVE-2022-26904 on 2022-04-12, which Rapid7's module documentation states is a patch bypass for both of the earlier two. Rating this CVE on its own merits gives Important, a 7.0 base score and exploited: No; rating it as the second entry in a live bypass sequence predicts the third, which is the one that carries a functional-exploit temporal rating and a Metasploit module with full source. CISA's listing on 2022-04-25 landed thirteen days after that third CVE shipped.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Microsoft's record for CVE-2022-21919 still reports exploited: No, so nothing in the vendor feed would ever start a clock on this bug — the 2022-04-25 KEV listing is the only trigger that exists, and it arrived three and a half months after the 2022-01-11 fix. Keying the SLA to the KEV listing rather than to the vendor's exploitation field is what makes the deferred January rollup visible as an overdue item on shared workstations and session hosts, which is where the second standard-user profile this exploit needs is the normal state. Where a host cannot take the rollup inside the window, the only reboot-free option is 0patch's micropatch, and it reaches Windows 10 v1809 through v21H1 and Server 2016 / 2019 at their late-2021 patch levels and nothing beyond them.

attack_vector.description: A kernel graphics driver reads beyond the end of a buffer and returns the surplus to whoever asked. An ordinary application running as a local user calls into the graphics driver kernel extension — 'Intel Graphics Driver' in Apple's Monterey advisory, 'Graphics Drivers' in the Big Sur one — receives kernel memory it should never see, and reads kernel pointers out of it — the layout information that makes the next stage of a kernel exploit reliable.
attack_vector.privileges_required: low — PR:L; the attacker needs code already running as some local user on the Mac, which means this sits behind an initial-access step and is never the entry point
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; no race, no heap shaping, no information leak needed first, because this bug is the information leak. Whether hardware constrains it is unsettled: Apple names the component 'Intel Graphics Driver' on Monterey but 'Graphics Drivers' on Big Sur and Catalina
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Apple credits an anonymous researcher and publishes nothing about method; there is no research-lab brand on this entry that could be mistaken for evidence of automated discovery.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Moving Macs to macOS 12.3.1 or 11.6.6, or applying Security Update 2022-004 on Catalina, and confirming each machine restarted into the new build rather than merely staging it.
prevention.adequacy: This is the only remediation — the driver cannot be unloaded on a Mac with a display, so there is no compensating control to hold the line while the update rolls out. Its limit is enforcement: without management that can require the restart, the fixed build sits downloaded on laptops that keep running the vulnerable extension.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Endpoint telemetry that records unprivileged processes making sustained low-level graphics driver calls, correlated with application provenance so a newly arrived binary doing so stands out.
detection.adequacy: Weak on its own. A kernel read produces no crash, no file and no network artefact, and macOS endpoint tooling has limited visibility below the userland boundary — so this detects an unusual pattern rather than the exploitation itself, and only where such telemetry was already being collected.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating a Mac that ran an unvetted application while below the fixed build as a chain-exposure case: reviewing what else that application did, and rotating credentials the machine held rather than closing the ticket on the OS update.
response.adequacy: Proportionate given that this CVE alone yields only a read, but it depends on knowing which application to look at. There is no hash or signature to hunt with and the response has to start from behaviour rather than indicators.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: A Mac estate under a documented flaw-remediation programme absorbed macOS 12.3.1 within its normal cycle and was compliant either way. The control's measurement is the problem on Apple endpoints specifically: SI-2 evidence comes from the management console's update record, and a kernel-extension fix does nothing until the machine reboots. SI-2 also has no state to describe a Catalina Mac, which Security Update 2022-004 remediated in 2022, which Apple has kept issuing occasional updates for since, and whose latest such update — Security Update 2026-001 Catalina, 02 Feb 2026 — Apple annotates as having no published CVE entries. That machine is patched for this CVE, still receiving something from the vendor, and evidenced by nothing that shows it is still getting CVE fixes; SI-2 records the install date and none of that.

NIST-800-53-SC-39.gap: Process isolation is provided by macOS and any assessment of it passes on both a vulnerable and a fixed Mac, because the architecture that separates address spaces is untouched. What fails is a single driver's bounds check, which hands kernel bytes to a caller through an interface the isolation model expects to be safe. The control is nominally met and structurally blind: there is no SC-39 test whose result differs between macOS 12.3 and 12.3.1, and the entire security value of this CVE's fix lives in that difference.

NIS2-Art21-vulnerability-management.gap: An entity with a risk-proportionate vulnerability-management process received Apple's 2022-03-31 advisory and ranked a CVSS 5.5 local read below the remote critical items in the same queue, which is what proportionality instructs. That ranking is defensible on the CVE's own impact and wrong on its role, because a kernel-memory disclosure exists to make the next stage of someone else's exploit reliable. Apple's own actively-exploited notice was in the same advisory and carries no weight in a scoring model driven by CVSS.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: A managed Mac fleet evidences B4 convincingly — hardened baseline, System Integrity Protection enabled, Gatekeeper enforcing provenance, disk encryption on. Every one of those remains true while an application already running as a local user reads kernel memory through a driver call, because SIP does not police what a kernel extension returns and Gatekeeper's decision was made before execution. B4 also has no field in which to record that the fleet's exposure boundary is itself unresolved — Apple files this CVE under an Intel-specific component on one macOS line and a generic one on the two others, so 'which Macs on this build are affected' has no evidenced answer and the fleet has to be patched as though all of them are.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Workstation operating systems get one month from release at Maturity Levels One and Two, where the clause carries no conditions. At Maturity Level Three it reads, verbatim from the ACSC Essential Eight maturity model, Appendix C: 'Patches, updates or other vendor mitigations for vulnerabilities in operating systems of workstations, non-internet-facing servers and non-internet-facing network devices are applied within one month of release when vulnerabilities are assessed as non-critical by vendors and no working exploits exist.' Neither limb of that clause is settled on Apple's advisory wording: Apple's advisories carry no severity rating at all, so no vendor has assessed this vulnerability as non-critical, and no exploit code for CVE-2022-22674 was ever published while Apple's 2022-03-31 advisory says the issue may have been actively exploited. Catalina is a second unsettled edge — Apple still shipped that line an update on 02 Feb 2026, so calling it vendor-unsupported is a judgement, while Maturity Level Three's 'latest or previous release' rule reaches those Macs whichever way it goes. What no maturity level distinguishes is a downloaded update from a rebooted Mac — which is the whole difference between a fixed kernel extension and a vulnerable one still resident in memory.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.28.gap: Secure coding is the control that names this defect precisely — an unvalidated length reaching a kernel buffer read — and it is also the one the operator has no way to exercise. A.8.28 applies to software the organisation writes or procures against its own requirements, and the Intel Graphics Driver ships inside a closed operating system with no source, no review and no operator-side test. The control is genuinely in place for the organisation's own code and contributes nothing to assurance about the kernel extension that actually failed.

new_control_requirements.name: MOBILE-ENDPOINT-MDM-ENFORCED-KEV-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: iOS / iPadOS / macOS estates must enforce KEV-class updates within 24h via DDM; user-deferral disallowed.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Apple shipped macOS Monterey 12.3.1 and macOS Big Sur 11.6.6 with this graphics-driver fix, and CISA listed the CVE on 2022-04-04 with a 2022-04-25 due date, four days after Apple's advisory said the issue may have been actively exploited. The fix is a kernel extension, so a Mac remains vulnerable until it restarts into the new build — which makes user deferral, not download failure, the mechanism by which an estate stays exposed. Enforcing the update and the restart through management is the only way the remediation record and the running state agree.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVSS 5.5 with C:H/I:N/A:N puts this Intel Graphics Driver read at the bottom of any severity-ordered queue. Keying the clock to the 2022-04-04 KEV listing instead removes the scoring judgement from the decision entirely, which is the right outcome for a bug whose value is supplying kernel addresses to another exploit rather than causing damage itself. There are no compensating controls to fall back on here — the driver cannot be unloaded — so the patch and its restart are the only mitigation the SLA can accept.

CVE-2005-2773.name: HP OpenView Network Node Manager Remote Code Execution Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: One unauthenticated GET to an OvCgi Perl script, with shell metacharacters in the node parameter, runs commands on the network-management server and returns the output in the HTTP response.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; the CGI is reachable before any authentication step and the request carries no session
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; a single request with no groom, no race and no callback channel, since output is returned in-band
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Found by James Fisher of Portcullis Computer Security during a 2005 network security assessment and disclosed on Bugtraq; no AI-branded research arm is involved and no AI assistance is claimed by anyone.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Deleting the four vulnerable OvCgi scripts, or refusing the NNM web listener from any segment without a management role, and retiring the 6.x/7.x installation outright.
prevention.adequacy: Deleting the scripts closes these four paths and nothing else in a product that has received no security maintenance since 2005. Reachability restriction bounds who can send the request but leaves it fully exploitable from inside the permitted segment, and a management server is reachable from operator networks by design.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Web-server access logging for the NNM listener shipped off-host, alerting on shell metacharacters in the node parameter, paired with process-execution telemetry on the CGI account.
detection.adequacy: Both signals are high-confidence because the legitimate node value is a hostname and the CGI account legitimately spawns almost nothing. The limit is collection: the detection only exists if the logs were being shipped before the request arrived.

response.what_would_have_worked: Rebuilding the NNM host from a known-good baseline and rotating every SNMP community string and device credential it held, rather than deleting the CGI and closing the item.
response.adequacy: This is the only response that survives the absence of a patch, but it is expensive and it does not reach devices whose credentials were reused elsewhere. Where one community string was shared across the managed estate, the rotation scope is the managed estate.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: An SI-2 programme can be fully implemented and still leave this open, because its output is a decision about updates and CVE-2005-2773 has none — no HP bulletin and no fixed build appear in NVD's references. The control produces a defensible 'no update available' record for OpenView NNM 6.2 through 7.50 and stops there, while the unauthenticated CGI shell remains exactly as reachable as it was on 2005-08-25.

NIS2-Art21-vulnerability-handling.gap: The handling process opens an item on a KEV-listed CVE and can never close it, because the closure condition it is built around — a vendor fix — will not arrive for a product line that stopped receiving security maintenance long before the KEV listing on 2022-03-25. An organization with excellent vulnerability handling ends up carrying this as a permanent accepted risk rather than as the decommissioning decision it actually is.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: B4 evidence is normally baselines, hardening standards and change records, none of which touch a Perl CGI that interpolates a query parameter into a shell command line before any authentication happens. The action that works here is file deletion from the OvCgi directory followed by decommissioning, and an assessment that reads as compliant on secure configuration says nothing about whether connectedNodes.ovpl is still present on the disk.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: The mitigation is framed around applying vendor patches, updates or other vendor mitigations, and for this CVE none of the three exists, so the affected host is out of the mitigation's scope rather than failing it. On the reading applied here — an interpretation of scope, not a quotation — a high maturity rating for patching is compatible with running an NNM server that hands a shell to any unauthenticated caller on TCP 3443.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: Vulnerability information is obtained correctly — NVD, KEV since 2022-03-25, EPSS 0.7409 on 2026-08-17 — and the evaluation step then has to produce a measure, which in practice means a patch record. No patch record can exist for CVE-2005-2773, so the control's own evidence trail cannot express the one adequate measure, which is removing the host from service.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: HP OpenView Network Node Manager 6.2 through 7.50 has been KEV-listed since 2022-03-25 against a 2022-04-15 due date, and the patch branch of that clock never starts because no HP fix exists in NVD's reference set. The control's third option — documented compensating controls — is the only executable one here, and naming it explicitly is what stops the exposure being recorded as 'awaiting vendor'. With EPSS at 0.7409 on 2026-08-17 and a working exploit public since 2005, the compensating control has to be deletion of the OvCgi scripts or removal of the host, documented as such.

new_control_requirements.name: MITIGATION-ACTIVE-PATCH-PENDING-VERDICT-CLASS
new_control_requirements.description: Compliance verdicts must distinguish three states: (a) binary patch deployed (vulnerability eliminated), (b) vendor-mitigation rule active, no binary patch (residual risk: any defect in the mitigation rule reopens the vulnerability), (c) no mitigation, no patch (full exposure).
