Audit reports must surface (b) as a distinct compensating-control state with an associated time-bound action item, not as a 'patched per SLA' outcome.
new_control_requirements.evidence: An OpenView NNM 6.2-to-7.50 host sits in state (c) permanently unless someone acts, and the three-state verdict is what makes that visible: with no HP advisory in NVD's references, the audit line for CVE-2005-2773 cannot be 'patched per SLA' and must not be left blank. Where an operator has deleted connectedNodes.ovpl, cdpView.ovpl, freeIPaddrs.ovpl and ecscmg.ovpl, that is state (b) with the residual risk named — any reinstall or upgrade of the NNM package restores the scripts — and it carries a time-bound decommissioning item rather than closing the finding.

CVE-2009-0927.name: Adobe Reader and Adobe Acrobat Stack-Based Buffer Overflow Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: A PDF whose embedded JavaScript calls Collab.getIcon with an over-long string argument overflows a stack buffer in Reader or Acrobat and executes the attacker's code as the user who opened the file.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; the attacker holds no account and no position on the network, only the ability to put a file in front of someone
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L with UI:R; the real constraint is getting the document opened, and public tooling already spans the 7.x, 8.x and 9.x branches
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. The researchers credited on the Metasploit module authored the exploit rather than discovering the flaw; no AI-branded research arm is involved.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Disabling Acrobat JavaScript by policy, and driving every Reader and Acrobat copy — managed and per-user, both tracks — to 9.1, 8.1.3 or 7.1.1 for its line with a forced application relaunch.
prevention.adequacy: Disabling the scripting engine closes this path completely and costs any workflow that relies on document JavaScript. The update is adequate for this CVE and no further: a 2009 fixed build is not a safe place to stop, and an update that lands without a relaunch has changed the version string and nothing else.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Process-lineage alerting on Reader and Acrobat spawning child processes or opening outbound connections, plus mail-gateway inspection of PDF script objects for Collab references.
detection.adequacy: Lineage alerting is the durable half — a PDF reader has almost no legitimate reason to spawn a shell — and it fires after code execution, not before. Static inspection of script objects is weaker: Collab appears in benign documents, and the distinguishing feature is argument length rather than presence.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating a workstation that opened a suspect document as compromised at user privilege: collect the document, rotate what that user could reach, and check for persistence rather than closing on the Reader version.
response.adequacy: Sound but bounded by identification — the triggering document often arrives by mail and is deleted, so the response depends on retention at the mail gateway. The update itself removes nothing an attacker placed on the host before it landed.

NIST-800-53-CM-7.gap: A least-functionality baseline that enumerates installed software, services and ports can be fully satisfied on a workstation running Reader 9.0.x with Acrobat JavaScript enabled, because the feature carrying the sink is a setting inside an approved application rather than an approved application itself. The control's unit of granularity is one level coarser than the exposure, so it produces genuine evidence about the wrong layer.

NIST-800-53-SI-3.gap: SI-3 is satisfied by deployed, updated anti-malware, and the artefact here is a syntactically valid PDF calling a documented API with a long argument — no dropper and no packed code until after the overflow. Two Metasploit modules regenerate the document on demand, so the detection surface the control attests to is chasing output that changes per build while the underlying primitive does not.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: The measurable outcome is 'update applied', and for a user-space PDF reader that is not the same as 'vulnerable code no longer running'. A workstation that took the 9.1 update while Reader and the browser PDF plugin stayed open reports the fixed version to inventory and keeps executing the 9.0.x image until relaunch, so the control's own metric certifies a machine that is still exploitable.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: Clean B4 evidence for the Reader estate says nothing about Acrobat 9.0.x installs on the same hosts, and a per-user install of either sits outside the inventory that the evidence was drawn from.

AU-Essential-8-App-Hardening.gap: The single most effective action against CVE-2009-0927 — turning off Acrobat JavaScript — is available and free, and the hardening mitigation covers browser-side content rather than the PDF reader's own scripting engine. Reading it to include Acrobat JavaScript is an interpretation of its intent, and until an estate makes that interpretation explicit it can hold a strong hardening rating with the sink reachable on every workstation.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: The vulnerability information is obtained and the exposure is evaluated, but evaluation against the software inventory is only as good as the inventory, and this product ships as two independently updating installs plus per-user copies. An A.8.8 record showing the Reader package remediated is truthful and incomplete, and the incompleteness is invisible from inside the control.

new_control_requirements.name: EMBEDDED-MEDIA-PARSER-LIBRARY-INVENTORY-AND-PATCH-PARITY
new_control_requirements.description: The packet names the affected product as Adobe Acrobat and Reader, which on a real estate is never one install: Reader and Acrobat ship as separate products on separate update tracks, and per-user copies land outside managed software distribution. The control here means enumerating every installed Acrobat and Reader copy across those tracks and confirming each reports the fixed build, rather than closing the flaw-remediation ticket when the single inventoried Reader package updates. Scope it to those products: the packet ties the CWE-1321 sink to Acrobat and Reader and provides no mapping from the vulnerable code into other PDF-handling software, so instructing operators to treat every PDF-capable binary in the estate as an instance of this CVE manufactures findings and removal work against renderers no evidence implicates. Widen the inventory only where a verified source identifies another product carrying the same component. The distinguishing test: after the managed update lands, enumerate the Acrobat and Reader installs on the estate and confirm none still report a pre-fix version — an estate that patches the inventoried Reader while a second Acrobat track keeps the old build still opens crafted PDFs into the sink, with a flaw-remediation attestation that reads clean. Precondition: this reaches only copies the inventory can see and the operator can update; an unmanaged per-user install is remediated by removing it, not by recording it as patched. The packet registers no live-patch path, so each copy carries the service restart or system reboot the vendor fix requires, and a copy updated but not restarted is not yet remediated.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2009-0927 is the dual-track problem in its plainest form: NVD gives one set of boundaries — 9 before 9.1, 8 before 8.1.3, 7 before 7.1.1 — that applies identically to Adobe Reader and Adobe Acrobat, two products that update independently on the same workstation. An estate that drives its inventoried Reader package to 9.1 and closes the KEV item opened 2022-03-25 still opens crafted PDFs into the Collab.getIcon sink through any Acrobat 9.0.x copy beside it. The restart half of the control applies with a correction specific to this product: the vendor fix needs no host reboot, but it is inert until Reader, Acrobat and any browser hosting the PDF plugin are relaunched, so the enumeration must confirm the running build rather than the installed one.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: For Adobe Reader and Acrobat this control's documented-compensating-controls branch is the one that carries weight, because it is executable in minutes and the update is not: disabling Acrobat JavaScript by policy removes the only path to Collab.getIcon with no package deployment and no relaunch dependency. That matters against an EPSS of 0.96632 on 2026-08-17 and two Metasploit modules, one of which delivers through the browser. The control also forces the verification step the KEV listing of 2022-03-25 does not — mitigation deployed and verified, which for this flaw means confirming the setting on both the Reader and the Acrobat track.

attack_vector.description: An unauthenticated POST to phpMyAdmin's setup script supplies a serialized configuration whose server-name key breaks out of the generated PHP assignment, so the wizard writes the attacker's statements into config/config.inc.php and every later request executes them as the web server user.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; the setup script answers before any phpMyAdmin or database authentication
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L in the request, with two real preconditions the CVSS vector does not carry: a wizard-style install and a writable /config/ directory
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Reported by Greg Ose of Neohapsis and credited as such in PMASA-2009-3; the public script came from pagvac of GNUCITIZEN. No AI-assisted discovery is claimed and none is evident.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Deleting scripts/setup.php, setup/ and the /config/ directory once installation completed, and upgrading to 2.11.9.5 or 3.1.3.1.
prevention.adequacy: Removing the setup surface is decisive and version-independent, which is why it beats the upgrade as the first move. The upgrade is adequate for future injections only — it does not inspect or rewrite a config file that already carries code, so on an already-exploited host prevention has nothing left to prevent.

detection.what_would_have_worked: File-integrity monitoring on config/config.inc.php, and web-server logging that surfaces POSTs to setup scripts from unauthenticated sources.
detection.adequacy: Integrity monitoring is the strong signal because that file legitimately changes almost never after installation, and the injected code is human-readable in it.

response.what_would_have_worked: Rebuilding config/config.inc.php from a known-good copy, rotating the database credentials it stores, and reviewing what those credentials could reach.
response.adequacy: Necessary and frequently skipped, because the upgrade feels like closure. It does not address anything the attacker did with the shell before the file was rebuilt, and where the same database credentials were reused by other applications, the rotation scope is those applications too.

NIST-800-53-SI-10.gap: The application does validate the structure it receives — a well-formed serialized PMA_Config — and then emits one of its string values into PHP source. Validation that confirms type and shape is exactly the kind SI-10 evidence records, and it is orthogonal to the defect, because the injected value is a legitimate string until the generator writes it into a language. Nothing in a conventional input-validation assessment reaches a code-emitting path that runs once at install.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: Flaw remediation presumes an identifiable owner of the fixed version. phpMyAdmin arrives through upstream tarballs, distribution packages and hosting control panels, and on shared hosting the organization holding the SI-2 obligation is not the party able to deploy 2.11.9.5 or 3.1.3.1 at all. The control records a remediation process that is genuinely running against a copy of the software it cannot reach.

NIS2-Art21-vulnerability-management.gap: Tracking and closing the vulnerability is not the same operation as closing the compromise it produced, and this CVE separates them cleanly: the payload persists in config/config.inc.php, which the upgrade preserves as site data. A vulnerability-management record showing the fixed version deployed on 2022-04-15 is accurate and entirely compatible with the injected code still executing on every page load.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: The most effective securing action for this flaw is a deletion — scripts/setup.php and /config/ after installation — which is neither a patch nor a configuration setting and so lands outside both of B4's usual evidence streams. An assessment can hold clean baselines and clean patch records while the wizard endpoint that generates executable configuration is still answering unauthenticated POSTs.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: The mitigation measures how quickly the assessed organization applies available patches. The maturity rating can be honest and high while a 2.11.x install below 2.11.9.5 serves the organization's own database administration surface.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.9.gap: config/config.inc.php is the artefact the attack produces and the artefact configuration management is least likely to examine, because it is generated by the application, holds live database credentials, and is preserved across upgrades by design. A.8.9 evidence built from approved baselines and change tickets has no mechanism that would notice executable statements appended to a server-name key in it.

OWASP-Top-10-2021-A03.gap: The category is right and the standard remediation vocabulary does not apply: there is no query to parameterise and no output context to encode, because the sink writes PHP source. Fixing it properly means emitting configuration as parsed data rather than as executed code, a design change that an injection-focused review driven by scanner findings will not raise and a WAF ruleset will not compensate for.

new_control_requirements.name: CONFIGURATION-SIDE-LIVE-PATCH-INVENTORY
new_control_requirements.description: For any web-fabric vulnerability with a configuration-side mitigation path: that path must be inventoried, tested, and deployable independent of the vendor-patch path. Operators cannot wait for nginx 1.30.1+ if a named-capture refactor mitigates immediately.
new_control_requirements.evidence: phpMyAdmin gives the operator a configuration-side path that beats the vendor path on both speed and coverage, and CVE-2009-1151 is the case for inventorying it: deleting scripts/setup.php, setup/ and the /config/ directory removes the sink on any 2.11.x or 3.x build, works on a hosting-panel-bundled copy the operator cannot upgrade, and needs no coordination with a package maintainer. Exploit-DB 8921 records the /config/ directory as an explicit attack requirement, which is what makes its removal a real mitigation rather than a cosmetic one. Against EPSS 0.95438 on 2026-08-17 and a maintained Nuclei template that puts this CVE in default scan coverage, the mitigation has to be deployable on its own clock rather than behind the upgrade to 2.11.9.5 or 3.1.3.1.

new_control_requirements.name: MITIGATION-ACTIVE-PATCH-PENDING-VERDICT-CLASS
new_control_requirements.description: Compliance verdicts must distinguish three states: (a) binary patch deployed (vulnerability eliminated), (b) vendor-mitigation rule active, no binary patch (residual risk: any defect in the mitigation rule reopens the vulnerability), (c) no mitigation, no patch (full exposure). Audit reports must surface (b) as a distinct compensating-control state with an associated time-bound action item, not as a 'patched per SLA' outcome.
new_control_requirements.evidence: A phpMyAdmin install whose setup scripts have been deleted but whose version is still below 2.11.9.5 or 3.1.3.1 is state (b), and recording it as state (a) is a specific and recurring error on this product. The residual risk has a concrete trigger worth writing on the action item: reinstalling or upgrading the phpMyAdmin package restores scripts/setup.php and the setup/ directory, so a mitigation applied by deletion is undone by the next routine package operation. The three-state verdict also forces the question the version number hides — whether config/config.inc.php was rebuilt after the exposure window, since the upgrade preserves it either way.

CVE-2009-2055.name: Cisco IOS XR Border Gateway Protocol (BGP) Denial-of-Service Vulnerability (CVE-2009-2055)

attack_vector.description: A BGP UPDATE carrying one specific invalid path attribute makes the IOS XR BGP process reset the peering session instead of discarding the announcement, and the reset repeats for as long as the announcement keeps being re-advertised.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N in CVSS terms, though the announcement has to reach the BGP process, whether over a direct session or by propagating through one
attack_vector.complexity: high — AC:H; it needs a specific invalid attribute and a path into the target's BGP process, not an arbitrary malformed packet from an arbitrary host
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. No finder is credited in Cisco's advisory and the defect surfaced from an announcement seen in the wild on 17 August 2009; there is no research arm involved, AI-branded or otherwise.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Installing the SMU from cisco-sa-20090818-bgp on every IOS XR router between 3.4.1 and 3.8.1, and migrating 3.2.x and 3.3.x devices to 3.4.1 or later, which is the only path the advisory offers them.
prevention.adequacy: The SMU is the only thing that removes the defect, and installing it costs at minimum a BGP process restart on the adjacency it protects. It also does nothing for the two other BGP defects in the same advisory unless their SMUs are installed too, and it leaves the device on a superseded 3.x train.

detection.what_would_have_worked: BGP notification and neighbour-state logging shipped to a collector off the router, alerting on a neighbour that resets repeatedly at a steady interval with an UPDATE-message-error cause.
detection.adequacy: This is the signal that separates the defect from ordinary link flap, and it is only available if BGP-level logging was already being exported. Reachability polling and interface counters see brief blips and a device that is up.

response.what_would_have_worked: Coordinating with the upstream peer to filter the announcement carrying the invalid attribute at its source, as the advisory directs, while the SMU window is arranged.
response.adequacy: Reactive by construction: the filter can only be written once the flapping has been observed and the offending prefix identified, and it depends on a peer's willingness and speed. It restores the adjacency without removing the defect, so the next unfamiliar announcement produces the same outcome.

NIST-800-53-SC-5.gap: Every conventional denial-of-service defence is volumetric or protocol-agnostic, and this is neither — one authorised, structurally valid UPDATE inside an established session drops the adjacency. There is no rate to limit, no flood to scrub and no anomaly in traffic volume to key on, so an SC-5 implementation that is complete on its own terms contributes nothing to an IOS XR router between 3.4.0 and 3.8.1.

NIST-800-53-SI-4.gap: What identifies this defect is the repetition interval and the UPDATE-message-error cause in BGP notifications, telemetry that has to be exported off the router deliberately, and a monitoring programme evidenced by interface and reachability metrics satisfies SI-4 while being blind to it.

NIS2-Art21-availability.gap: Availability planning is scoped to the entity's own estate, and the input that causes the outage originates outside it — an announcement from a party the entity has no contract or relationship with, propagating into its BGP process. The obligation is met by continuity measures the entity controls, none of which prevent a conformant-looking prefix from reaching an unpatched IOS XR 3.4.0-to-3.8.1 router and resetting its adjacency.

UK-CAF-B5.gap: Redundancy is the standard B5 answer and it is undone by common-mode software: a redundant pair of IOS XR routers on the same 3.x train receives the same announcement and both drop their sessions. The B5 evidence — diverse paths, tested failover — is real and describes a resilience that does not exist against this defect, because the assessment does not ask whether the redundant units share a software release.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Network-device software sits awkwardly inside a mitigation whose evidence model is host operating systems and applications; an IOS XR SMU is per-release, installed in admin mode, and carries a service impact that ranges from a BGP process restart to a reload. Treating router software as in scope here is an interpretation of intent rather than a quotation, and without it a strong patching rating is compatible with a carrier router that never took the 2009 SMU.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.16.gap: Monitoring exists on any managed router estate; what is missing is the specific stream that makes this defect legible. Neighbour-down notifications carrying an UPDATE-message-error cause, correlated against the prefixes present at each reset, are what distinguish CVE-2009-2055 from a flapping circuit, and an A.8.16 programme evidenced by SNMP availability polling holds no data that could make that distinction.

new_control_requirements.name: FIREWALL-EGRESS-TELEMETRY-SEPARATE-TRUST-ZONE
new_control_requirements.description: Firewall and other perimeter-trust-boundary devices must forward syslog, threat logs, and authentication logs to a SIEM hosted in a separate trust zone (different management plane, different credentials, different authentication path). Telemetry stored on the compromised device is destroyed by the attacker; telemetry on a separate-trust-zone collector survives.
new_control_requirements.evidence: An IOS XR router carrying eBGP sessions is the perimeter-trust-boundary device this control governs, and CVE-2009-2055 shows why its telemetry has to leave the box. The only evidence that separates this defect from ordinary circuit flap is the router's own BGP notification stream — repeated neighbour-down events with an UPDATE-message-error cause, at a steady interval, against a constant prefix set — and a router that is resetting sessions is also a router whose local buffered log is rotating and whose reachability from a management station is intermittent. Off-box collection is the difference between diagnosing an unpatched 3.4.0-to-3.8.1 release in minutes and treating the symptom as a transport problem for weeks; the control's rationale differs from its original one, since nothing here is destroying logs deliberately, but the requirement is identical.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: This CVE is where the control's three branches have to be read as alternatives rather than a preference order, because on a carrier IOS XR router the patch branch is not a four-hour operation: the SMU from cisco-sa-20090818-bgp is per-release, needs an admin-mode install activate, and carries a service impact that may be a full reload. The executable branch inside the clock that opened on 2022-03-25 is the documented compensating control — the advisory's peer-coordinated filtering of the offending announcement — recorded as a compensating control with the SMU window as its time-bound follow-up. For IOS XR 3.2.x and 3.3.x, which get no SMU at all, that documented control is the only branch that exists short of a train migration.

attack_vector.description: One unauthenticated request to a ColdFusion administrator console page, with traversal sequences and a NUL in the locale parameter, returns an arbitrary file — in practice lib/password.properties, whose administrator and RDS passwords then buy legitimate console access and, through it, code execution.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; the vulnerable pages answer before the console's own login, which is the whole point of the flaw
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; a single request, with the only variability being which install layout holds password.properties, which the public tooling resolves by enumeration
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. The working request form is credited to carnal0wnage in Exploit-DB 14641 and the analysis was published by independent researchers in 2010; no AI-assisted discovery is claimed by anyone in the chain.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Refusing /CFIDE/ and /CFIDE/administrator/ from untrusted networks at the reverse proxy, and applying the APSB10-18 hotfix with a ColdFusion service restart.
prevention.adequacy: Path-level blocking is immediate, needs no vendor artefact and stops the anonymous read outright, but it does nothing against a caller already inside the permitted segment and is unavailable where administrators need remote console access. The hotfix removes the traversal and leaves the credentials it already exposed untouched.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Web-tier alerting on any locale parameter containing %00 or traversal sequences, plus alerting on successful ColdFusion administrator authentication from a new source.
detection.adequacy: The request signature is unusually clean — a legitimate locale value is a short language token, so NUL bytes and dot-dot sequences in it are unambiguous. The second signal is the one that catches an attacker who read the file before logging was tuned, and it depends on console authentication events being collected at all.

response.what_would_have_worked: Rotating the ColdFusion administrator and RDS passwords, then auditing scheduled tasks, datasources and CFM files under the web root against a known-good baseline.
response.adequacy: This is the part the hotfix cannot do. Its limit is baseline quality: where no known-good inventory of scheduled tasks and CFM files exists, the audit degrades into judgement about which files look wrong.

NIST-800-53-SC-7.gap: The boundary is correctly implemented at the layer SC-7 evidence describes — hosts, ports, network zones — and the exposure lives one layer below it, in which URL prefixes a permitted host serves to a permitted network. /CFIDE/administrator/ travels over the same allowed HTTPS as the business application, so no firewall rule is violated, and the corrective action is a proxy path rule that a network-tier control catalogue has no line for.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: APSB10-18 closes the traversal and the SI-2 item closes with it, but the asset that was stolen is a static credential in lib/password.properties that the hotfix does not change. The result is a remediation record that is accurate about the software and silent about the account, so a host counted as fixed can still be accessed by whoever read that file before the restart.

NIS2-Art21-network-security.gap: Segmentation and access control between zones are satisfied and irrelevant: the attack is an anonymous GET over the published HTTPS service, crossing no boundary that was not deliberately opened. The measure that actually reduces exposure is a single URL-prefix denial at the publication point, which is finer-grained and more application-specific than the network-security assessment is built to record or verify.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: Patch currency and hardening baselines both look healthy while the administrative console of a ColdFusion 9.0.1-or-earlier instance is published to the internet, because B4 evidence does not enumerate externally reachable URL prefixes per application. The console ships enabled and reachable, so exposure is inherited from the deployment rather than chosen in a configuration setting an assessment would review.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: The mitigation assesses how fast known patches are applied to inventoried assets. A KEV due date of 2022-04-15 and an EPSS of 0.99721 on 2026-08-17 describe an asset the patching process would treat as urgent, if the process had ever been told the asset exists.

ISO-27001-2022-A.5.15.gap: Access control is never exercised, let alone bypassed: the attacker reads the file holding the administrator and RDS passwords and then logs in the ordinary way, so every subsequent access decision is correct on its own terms. Account provisioning, review cycles and password-strength policy — the evidence A.5.15 attestations rest on — remain fully satisfied while an unauthorised party holds a valid console credential.

new_control_requirements.name: PERIMETER-COMPROMISE-REBUILD-NOT-PATCH
new_control_requirements.description: Pre-rehearsed IR runbook for any perimeter device that suffers a pre-auth RCE CVE in active exploitation MUST default to config-exfil + rebuild + credential rotation, not patch-in-place. Patch-in-place leaves attacker-installed implants intact.
new_control_requirements.evidence: An internet-facing ColdFusion server is the perimeter asset here, and CVE-2010-2861 is the pattern this control names: a pre-authentication path that ends in console administrator access, with CISA recording knownRansomwareCampaignUse as 'Known' on the KEV entry of 2022-03-25. Patch-in-place is specifically insufficient on this flaw for a reason visible in the mechanism — APSB10-18 removes the traversal but does not rotate lib/password.properties, so the administrator and RDS passwords an attacker read remain valid through the hotfix and the service restart. The credential-rotation and rebuild defaults are what convert the hotfix into remediation, and the rebuild half is what addresses the scheduled task, datasource or CFM file written under the web root after the attacker logged in legitimately.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: With EPSS at 0.99721 on 2026-08-17 and a maintained Nuclei template that puts /CFIDE/administrator/enter.cfm in default scan coverage, a ColdFusion instance's exposure window is measured against mass scanning rather than against targeted interest. The control's compensating-control branch is what fits the four-hour clock on this product: denying /CFIDE/ at the reverse proxy is a single rule that lands immediately, whereas the APSB10-18 hotfix needs a change window and a ColdFusion service restart. Verification is the part worth insisting on — confirm from an external address that /CFIDE/administrator/enter.cfm no longer answers, rather than recording the proxy rule as deployed.

CVE-2010-3035.name: Cisco IOS XR Border Gateway Protocol (BGP) Denial-of-Service Vulnerability (CVE-2010-3035)

attack_vector.description: A prefix announced with a valid but unrecognised optional transitive attribute is corrupted by IOS XR on re-advertisement, and the neighbours receiving the corrupted announcement — of any vendor — drop their sessions, so the outage propagates outward from the router holding the defect.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; the originator needs no session with the affected router, only the ability to put a prefix into the global table
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; the announcement is specification-conformant rather than malformed, which is precisely why nothing upstream filters it
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Surfaced by the operators of the RIPE NCC and Duke University BGP experiment from their own measurement data on 27 August 2010 and reported to Cisco the same day; no research arm, AI-branded or otherwise, is involved.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Installing the SMU from cisco-sa-20100827-bgp on every IOS XR router between 3.4.1 and 3.9.1, with a reload window booked for the 3.4.3 and 3.6.1 units.
prevention.adequacy: The SMU is the whole of prevention, because Cisco states there are no workarounds that proactively mitigate the issue. Its cost is asymmetric across the fleet — a BGP process restart for most releases, a full system reload for 3.4.3 and 3.6.1 — and until it lands the router keeps corrupting attributes for its neighbours.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Correlating peer-reported attribute-error notifications against the AS paths those prefixes traverse, so that a cluster of drops resolves to a common IOS XR speaker rather than to each affected peer in isolation.
detection.adequacy: This is the only analysis that identifies the responsible device, and it needs BGP notification detail retained across multiple operators' routers. Each individual peer sees a neighbour sending it something malformed, which points at the wrong router; the correlation is what redirects attention upstream.

response.what_would_have_worked: Filtering the prefixes carrying the unrecognised attribute once route flaps appeared, as the advisory directs, while the SMU and any reload window were arranged.
response.adequacy: Available only after the disruption starts, since the attribute type is not known in advance — the 2010 event involved a type never previously announced on the internet. It restores sessions and leaves the corruption behaviour intact, so the next unfamiliar transitive attribute reproduces the outcome.

NIST-800-53-SC-5.gap: Denial-of-service protection built on capacity, thresholds and scrubbing has no engagement point with a single conformant route announcement that the protected device itself then corrupts for its neighbours. The RIPE measurement of the 27 August 2010 window — up to 1.4% of prefixes unstable, around 0.5% unreachable, over roughly thirty minutes — describes an outage that no volumetric control would have registered as an attack at any point.

NIST-800-53-CM-3.gap: Change control is working exactly as designed when it declines to reload a carrier router outside a booked window, and that correctness is what leaves the defect in service. The advisory's split — process-restart SMUs for most releases, reload-required SMUs for 3.4.3 and 3.6.1 — means one remediation generates two change classes, and the harder class is the one that slips past a KEV due date of 2022-04-15.

NIS2-Art21-business-continuity.gap: The entity operating the defective router may record no continuity event at all, because the sessions that drop are its neighbours'. Continuity obligations written around restoring the entity's own services give no prompt to assess harm the entity's equipment causes downstream, and with no proactive workaround available there is nothing the plan could hold short of the SMU.

UK-CAF-B5.gap: Diverse transit paths are the standard resilience answer and they share fate here, because every IOS XR speaker between 3.4.0 and 3.9.1 on any of those paths corrupts the same attribute for its own neighbours. The B5 evidence describing path diversity is accurate about topology and silent about software homogeneity, which is the variable that determines whether the diversity survives this announcement.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: The mitigation's evidence model is host operating systems and applications, and an IOS XR SMU fits it badly: per-release, installed in admin mode, and carrying a service impact that varies from a process restart to a reload within one advisory. Bringing carrier routing software inside the mitigation is an interpretation of its intent, and where an estate has not made that interpretation, the fleet is not assessed rather than assessed and failed.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.21.gap: Security of network services is normally evidenced through the terms agreed with transit providers, and this defect is the organization degrading a service it provides rather than a provider failing one it sells. No clause in a peering or transit agreement would identify an unpatched 3.4.0-to-3.9.1 release as the cause of a neighbour's dropped session, so the control's evidence trail cannot reach the condition.

new_control_requirements.name: MITIGATION-ACTIVE-PATCH-PENDING-VERDICT-CLASS
new_control_requirements.description: Compliance verdicts must distinguish three states: (a) binary patch deployed (vulnerability eliminated), (b) vendor-mitigation rule active, no binary patch (residual risk: any defect in the mitigation rule reopens the vulnerability), (c) no mitigation, no patch (full exposure). Audit reports must surface (b) as a distinct compensating-control state with an associated time-bound action item, not as a 'patched per SLA' outcome.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Cisco states in cisco-sa-20100827-bgp that there are no workarounds that proactively mitigate this issue, which puts every IOS XR router between 3.4.0 and 3.9.1 in state (c) until its SMU is activated — there is no state (b) to occupy in advance. Where an operator has applied the advisory's reactive prefix filter after observing flaps, that is state (b) with a residual risk worth naming: the filter targets one attribute type, and the 2010 event turned on a type never previously announced, so the next unfamiliar one is not covered. The verdict class is also what stops a 3.4.3 or 3.6.1 unit whose reload window has not yet been booked from being recorded alongside the process-restart units as patched per SLA.

new_control_requirements.name: LIVE-PATCH-CAPABILITY
new_control_requirements.description: For any system that processes production workloads and cannot tolerate unplanned reboots: live kernel patching capability (kpatch, livepatch, kGraft, or equivalent) must be deployed and tested quarterly.
new_control_requirements.evidence: A carrier IOS XR router is the archetype of a system that cannot absorb an unplanned restart, and this advisory shows the equivalent capability existing for most of the fleet and missing for part of it: the SMUs for most affected releases restart only the BGP process, while those for 3.4.3 and 3.6.1 require a full system reload. The control's quarterly-test half is the operative one for this platform — an SMU install path that has not been exercised on a lab unit before a KEV clock opens becomes the reason a 2022-04-15 due date passes with the router still corrupting transitive attributes for its neighbours. Where a release offers no in-service path, that is a fact to record against the device now rather than discover during the change window.

attack_vector.description: Two MAIL commands in one anonymous SMTP session: the first sends headers large enough that Exim's rejection logging overflows an 8192-byte buffer and corrupts the in-memory MAIL ACL, and the second makes Exim expand the attacker's data as configuration and run a shell command as the Exim user, with a companion local flaw taking that to root.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; an anonymous SMTP connection to port 25 is the entire access requirement
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; no leak, no user interaction and no credential, with the heap state reached by message size rather than by a disclosed address
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Reported from a live compromise by Sergey Kononenko on 7 December 2010 and assigned by Mark J Cox of Red Hat Security Response on 10 December 2010; no AI assistance is claimed by anyone involved.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Exim 4.70 or the distribution equivalent — 4.69-9+lenny1 or 4.70-1 on Debian — with the exim daemon restarted, and the CVE-2010-4345 escalation fix confirmed present alongside it.
prevention.adequacy: This is complete prevention for hosts that took it before being attacked. On an already-compromised host it prevents nothing, because the escalation artefact the attacker left survives the upgrade.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alerting on the exim run-time user spawning a shell, and on inbound headers carrying Exim expansion syntax, with mail logs shipped off the host.
detection.adequacy: Process-lineage alerting is the high-confidence half: an MTA daemon has no legitimate reason to spawn an interactive shell, and this fires whether or not the specific CVE is known. Header inspection is weaker on its own, and both depend on telemetry leaving a host that the attacker reached as root.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating any host that answered on port 25 while below 4.70 as compromised: hunt the spool directory for setuid artefacts, rebuild rather than upgrade in place, and rotate every credential the mail host held.
response.adequacy: It is the only response that matches an attack which reached root, and it is expensive on a mail server. Where the same credentials were reused elsewhere on the estate, the rotation scope extends to those systems too.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: The control's own completion signal misleads: the package updated to 4.70 while the exim daemon has not restarted still runs the vulnerable code, so a correct SI-2 record can describe a still-exploitable mail exchanger.

NIST-800-53-SC-7.gap: There is no boundary control that helps and the control should be recorded as inapplicable rather than partially met. A mail exchanger must accept anonymous SMTP from the whole internet on port 25 to do its job, so restricting sources removes the service rather than the exposure, and the only residual SC-7 value is constraining what the daemon can reach outbound once it has already been taken.

NIS2-Art21-incident-handling.gap: DSA-2131 announced the remote fix on 10 December 2010 while stating that the CVE-2010-4345 escalation fix was still in compatibility testing and not included, so handling the incident by applying the announced update closed the path to the Exim user and left the path to root open. The control assumes an advisory delivers a complete fix, and here the advisory said in its own text that it did not.

UK-CAF-D1.gap: Where a mail-server response plan reads as patch, restart, resume, it does not reach what this attack left: the December 2010 reports describe a setuid-root binary under the spool directory, an artefact untouched by the package upgrade and by the daemon restart, so the plan executed exactly as written produces a host reporting Exim 4.70 while still carrying the attacker's escalation primitive.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: The mitigation is satisfied by the installed package version, and on this flaw the installed version and the executing code diverge until the exim daemon restarts. Reading the mitigation to mean the running service rather than the package on disk is an interpretation of its intent, and without it an estate reports timely patching of exim4 to 4.69-9+lenny1 or 4.70-1 while the process handling internet mail is still the old build.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: The control's inputs are CVE feeds and vendor advisories, and this flaw ran ahead of both: the exploitation report reached the exim-dev list on 7 December 2010, the CVE identifier followed on 10 December, and the distribution advisories after that.

new_control_requirements.name: PERIMETER-COMPROMISE-REBUILD-NOT-PATCH
new_control_requirements.description: Pre-rehearsed IR runbook for any perimeter device that suffers a pre-auth RCE CVE in active exploitation MUST default to config-exfil + rebuild + credential rotation, not patch-in-place. Patch-in-place leaves attacker-installed implants intact.
new_control_requirements.evidence: An internet-facing Exim mail exchanger below 4.70 is exactly the case the control is written for, and this CVE supplies the proof that patch-in-place is insufficient rather than merely suboptimal: the December 2010 reports describe the attacker compiling a setuid-root binary under the Exim spool directory, an artefact the package update to 4.70 and the daemon restart both leave untouched. Exploitation was confirmed independently of any KEV listing — DSA-2131 states exploits had been seen in the wild and CERT VU#682457 says the same — so the rebuild default applies to every host that answered on port 25 while unpatched, not only to hosts with a specific indicator. Credential rotation is the second half and covers what the mail host held, since the chain ended at root.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: The word that earns its place on this entry is verified. Exim's fix lands as a package — 4.70 upstream, 4.69-9+lenny1 or 4.70-1 on Debian per DSA-2131 — and the vulnerable code keeps running until the daemon restarts, so a deployment record alone certifies nothing about the process accepting mail on port 25. Verification here means checking the running exim build rather than the installed package, and confirming the CVE-2010-4345 escalation fix is present, since DSA-2131 shipped the remote fix while that one was still in compatibility testing. Against a flaw whose exploitation was reported three days before the CVE existed, the clock the control imposes is the only thing that would have compressed the exposure window on a mail exchanger.

attack_vector.description: An attacker holding the Exim run-time account writes a configuration file and starts the setuid-root exim binary against it with -C, or overrides a macro with -D. Exim honours the file with root privilege, so a directive containing a ${run{...}} expansion runs commands as root. In the December 2010 incidents the foothold on that account came from a separate remote flaw in header expansion, making the combination a network-to-root path against a mail server.
attack_vector.privileges_required: low — PR:L in NVD's vector, and the privilege that matters is specifically the exim run-time account; CERT/CC states the requirement in VU#758489 as 'a local attacker with the ability to execute commands as the Exim user'
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L in NVD's vector; no race, no memory corruption, no information leak. The attacker supplies a file and invokes a setuid binary, and the outcome is deterministic once the account is held
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. The escalation was identified by the Exim maintainers during investigation of live compromises reported to exim-dev in December 2010, and tracked as Bugzilla 1044.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Building Exim with ALT_CONFIG_ROOT_ONLY before 4.73 made it unconditional, which is the mitigation CERT/CC published in VU#758489, and after 4.73 keeping TRUSTED_CONFIG_LIST narrow so only root-owned files on the list retain privilege.
prevention.adequacy: Partial before the fix and awkward after it. CERT/CC's own note records that the build option restricts functionality where multiple configurations are used, and after 4.73 a site with a non-default configuration path must maintain the whitelist correctly or lose function, which is the pressure that reopens the gap.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Process-level auditing of the exim account: alerting on exim invoked with -C or -D by the service account, and on any shell or interpreter whose parent is an exim process.
detection.adequacy: It sees the escalation but not before it lands, and only where host auditing was already collecting exec events on the mail server and shipping them off-host. It offers nothing against the persistence a root-level attacker establishes in the same session.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating a compromised Exim host as root-compromised: rebuild rather than upgrade, rotate every credential the mail server held or relayed, and compare the configuration tree against a known-good copy rather than inheriting it through the package update.
response.adequacy: Correct but expensive, and it depends on knowing the host was reached. Where the chained remote flaw was the entry point, the only evidence may be mail-log anomalies that were rotated away long before the CVE was read.

NIST-800-53-AC-6.gap: Exim's separation of a non-root run-time account from root is itself the least-privilege implementation an AC-6 assessment records as satisfied. The control never asks whether that account can re-enter root through the setuid binary it is designed to invoke, so the attestation and the vulnerability coexist without contradiction.

NIST-800-53-CM-7.gap: Least functionality is assessed at the level of installed services and open ports. It does not reach a mail agent's command-line options, and pre-4.73 Exim shipped with ALT_CONFIG_ROOT_ONLY off by default, so the exposed behaviour was the vendor default rather than a deviation an assessor could have flagged against a baseline.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: Exploitation was reported to exim-dev on 2010-12-07 and the upstream fix came in 4.73 afterwards, so the window that mattered predates anything a patch-management obligation can measure. Distribution fixes then landed on independent schedules across DSA-2154, RHSA-2011:0153 and USN-1060-1, meaning compliance dates differ by estate for the same flaw.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: System security review of an SMTP relay concentrates on the listener — TLS, authentication, relay policy, exposure. The failing trust relationship here is internal to the host, between the exim account and the configuration parser, and its remediation is a compile-time option plus a file whitelist. Neither is visible to a hardening review of the network service.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Patching does close this once a 4.73-derived build is installed, but the update is not configuration-transparent: Red Hat's errata added /etc/exim/trusted-configs and stopped honouring -D as root. A site with a non-default configuration path can be fully patched and broken at the same time, and restoring service by widening the whitelist undoes the fix while the patch level still reads compliant.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.9.gap: Configuration management protects the approved configuration from unauthorised change. This flaw does not change exim.conf at all — it presents a second, attacker-authored file to the same binary. Evidence of a baselined, change-controlled exim.conf is fully compatible with the escalation remaining available to the exim account.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Exim was reached in the wild before any fix existed — the exim-dev report of live root compromises is dated 2010-12-07 and Exim 4.73 followed it — so the 'whichever is later' clause is the operative half for this MTA. CISA put the CVE on the KEV clock on 2022-03-25 with a 2022-04-15 due date, and its EPSS pair for 2026-08-17 is score 0.18105 at percentile 0.96947, which keeps it in the band that still attracts routine scanning against internet-facing mail servers.

new_control_requirements.name: BUG-FAMILY-MITIGATION-PERSISTENCE
new_control_requirements.description: When a CVE patch lands, retain the pre-patch compensating controls (module blacklists, sysctl restrictions) until the patched code has soaked for a stated review period. Patches for one bug in a primitive class can introduce sibling bugs in the same class; the original compensating control may still apply to the sibling.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Exim is the case the control describes. Debian DSA-2154 and Ubuntu USN-1060-1 both cover CVE-2010-4345 together with CVE-2011-0017, a missing setuid/setgid return-value check that let the Debian-exim user make root append log data to arbitrary files — a sibling in the same privilege-retention family, disclosed after the first fix. Exim 4.74 then had to relax the 4.73 permission checks that were rejecting /dev/null. A site that dropped its compensating restrictions the day 4.73 landed had roughly two months of exposure to the sibling.

CVE-2010-4398.name: Microsoft Windows Kernel Stack-Based Buffer Overflow Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: A standard user writes an oversized REG_BINARY SystemDefaultEUDCFont value into their own registry hive, then triggers the font lookup with an ordinary graphics call. win32k.sys reads the value through RtlQueryRegistryValues without checking its type or length, overflows a stack buffer in kernel context, and the attacker executes code in ring 0 — which also puts them past User Account Control without a consent prompt.
attack_vector.privileges_required: low — PR:L; Microsoft's stated requirement is valid logon credentials and the ability to log on locally, and the bulletin states the vulnerability cannot be exploited remotely or by anonymous users
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; both the registry write and the trigger are unprivileged operations with no race and no prerequisite leak. The engineering difficulty is in resuming the kernel cleanly afterwards, which is why the public code enumerates the builds it supports and bug-checks outside them.
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Reported by Zhengwenbin of 360safe, Guo Bojun and Wei Zhang per MS11-011, with the public proof-of-concept credited to noobpwnftw. Hand reverse engineering of a kernel routine, in an era before automated discovery pipelines were part of this class of work.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Installing MS11-011 / KB2393802 and taking the mandatory restart, or — for the Windows 7 and Server 2008 R2 population — moving to Service Pack 1, which MS11-011 lists as non-affected.
prevention.adequacy: Complete once installed and rebooted, and unavailable for eleven weeks. Between the 2010-11-24 exploit publication and the 2011-02-08 bulletin there was no patch and, by Microsoft's own statement, no workaround — the only levers were restricting who could log on locally to affected hosts and accelerating the SP1 rollout where it applied.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alerting on writes of a SystemDefaultEUDCFont value from a non-administrative process, and on token elevation to SYSTEM in a process with no matching service or consent event.
detection.adequacy: It fires after ring 0 is already reached, which on a kernel compromise means the telemetry source itself is within the attacker's reach. It also depends on registry auditing having been enabled on user hives before the attempt, which is not the default.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating any affected host that showed a SYSTEM-privilege transition without provenance as kernel-compromised: rebuild from known-good media rather than patch in place, and rotate every credential cached or entered on the host.
response.adequacy: Sound but poorly triggered. Kernel execution lets an attacker remove the very artefacts that would justify the rebuild.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: SI-2 timeliness runs from patch availability, and for eleven weeks there was no patch and no workaround to deploy against public exploit code. The control also cannot express the version boundary that decides the work: Windows 7 SP1 is non-affected and Windows 7 RTM is not, and an inventory reporting product names rather than service-pack levels cannot tell them apart.

NIST-800-53-SI-10.gap: Input validation is assessed on data crossing an application's external boundary. The untrusted input here is a registry value the kernel reads from its own configuration store, and the fix was a change to RtlQueryRegistryValues itself. No estate-level SI-10 evidence covers whether an OS routine type-checks the data it retrieves from a user-writable hive.

NIS2-Art21-vulnerability-handling.gap: The handling process is anchored on advisory intake, and this flaw arrived as exploit code first: published on Exploit-DB on 2010-11-24, covered by SANS ISC and Sophos within days, and only assigned a bulletin on 2011-02-08. An advisory-driven pipeline produced no work item until the exposure was almost over.

UK-CAF-B2.gap: The identity and access model records User Account Control as the elevation boundary and evidences that administrative action requires consent. This escalation crosses that boundary from a standard token into ring 0 without generating a consent event, so nothing in the account, group or elevation policy an assessment inspects is either consulted or violated.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Operating-system patching does close this flaw, but MS11-011 makes the restart mandatory on every affected platform and marks HotPatching not applicable. A management console reporting KB2393802 as approved, downloaded or even installed is reporting a state in which the vulnerable kernel is still running until each host reboots.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: Technical vulnerability management assumes timely vulnerability information leads to an evaluable exposure and a defined action. For eleven weeks the information was a public exploit with no CVSS to score, no vendor advisory to route and — per MS11-011 — no workaround to apply, so a correctly executing A.8.8 process produced documentation rather than risk reduction.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: The control's 'or documented compensating controls' branch is the whole value here for Windows: from 2010-11-24 to 2011-02-08 there was public exploit code, no KB2393802 and — per MS11-011 — no vendor workaround, so the only deployable mitigation was a documented restriction on local logon rights for affected hosts. CISA later put the CVE on the KEV clock on 2022-03-28 with a 2022-04-21 due date, and its EPSS pair for 2026-08-17 is 0.08661 at percentile 0.9465.

new_control_requirements.name: VENDOR-PUSH-MITIGATION-OPT-IN-PRE-DISCLOSURE
new_control_requirements.description: For vendors offering push-mitigation services (Microsoft EEMS, Palo Alto Threat Prevention auto-update, etc.), opt-in must be enabled BEFORE the next disclosure event, not in response to it. Compliance frameworks must require operators to enable available vendor-push-mitigation services as a baseline control — opt-in late means the mitigation rule arrives after exploitation, not before.
new_control_requirements.evidence: MS11-011 is the shape of disclosure this control is written for: exploit code for the win32k.sys registry read was public on 2010-11-24 and Microsoft's fix did not arrive until 2011-02-08, with the bulletin recording no workarounds at all. An estate that had already enrolled in whatever pre-patch mitigation channels its OS vendor offered had a delivery path during those eleven weeks; one that went looking for the channel after reading the Exploit-DB entry did not.

CVE-2011-2005.name: Microsoft Ancillary Function Driver (afd.sys) Improper Input Validation Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: A user who can log on locally runs a program that passes a crafted pointer to afd.sys through a socket I/O control request. The driver uses it without checking that it addresses user space, giving the caller a controlled write into kernel memory; the published exploit points that write at the HAL dispatch table and triggers execution of its own shellcode in ring 0, ending as SYSTEM.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none beyond a local logon — the CISA-ADP vector reads PR:N/UI:R, and MS11-080's stated requirement is that 'an attacker must have valid logon credentials and be able to log on locally'
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; no race and no information leak are needed. The real constraint is build coverage: the public exploit hard-codes HAL offsets per operating system, covers x86 only, and the Metasploit port declares CRASH_OS_RESTARTS because a mismatch corrupts the kernel.
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Reported to Microsoft by Bo Zhou of the National University of Defense Technology through coordinated disclosure, with the public exploit written independently by Matteo Memelli of Offensive Security.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Installing MS11-080 / KB2592799 with the mandatory restart, and — for the far larger problem the CVE exposes — removing Windows XP and Windows Server 2003 from service, since those are the only platforms affected.
prevention.adequacy: The patch closes this defect completely and nothing else. Microsoft published no workarounds, HotPatching is unsupported on the Server 2003 package, and both platforms exited support in 2014 and 2015, so KB2592799 is the last afd.sys fix those hosts will ever receive.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Watching for the escalation's side effects rather than its trigger: a standard-user process becoming SYSTEM with no service or task to explain it, and bug checks naming afd.sys clustered on one host and account.
detection.adequacy: Weak on exactly the population that is affected. Where a host still running Windows XP or Windows Server 2003 carries no endpoint agent, the exec and bug-check telemetry this detection reads does not exist on the machine the vulnerability lives on.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating a kernel-privilege transition on a legacy host as a rebuild trigger, and using it as the forcing event for the migration that was already overdue rather than restoring the same image.
response.adequacy: Where the application on a Server 2003 host cannot be ported, restoring that host from the same image reinstates the exposure the rebuild was meant to remove.

NIST-800-53-SC-39.gap: The kernel-user separation SC-39 attests to is exactly what afd.sys breaks by acting on an unvalidated user-supplied pointer. Because the control is evaluated as a property of the operating system rather than of each shipped driver, the attestation stays true in the abstract while a default Winsock component hands every local user a kernel write primitive.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: Flaw remediation resolves this one CVE with KB2592799 and then runs out of road. Windows XP left support on 2014-04-08 and Windows Server 2003 on 2015-07-14, so for the affected population SI-2 can be fully satisfied for this entry while offering no mechanism at all for the next defect in the same driver.

NIS2-Art21-vulnerability-management.gap: Scoping from the CVE summary rather than the bulletin inverts the work. KEV says 'Ancillary Function Driver (afd.sys)' and NVD says 'Microsoft Windows', but MS11-080 lists Vista SP2, Server 2008 SP2, Windows 7 and Server 2008 R2 as non-affected — so a summary-driven programme raises findings against supported hosts that were never in scope.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: System security correctly identifies unsupported operating systems as a finding. What the outcome cannot supply is a route: where a Windows Server 2003 machine is kept alive by an application that cannot be ported, the finding restates a condition the operator already knows about, and CVE-2011-2005 becomes one more line under it.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Patch currency and support status diverge completely here. A host that has installed KB2592799 scores as patched for this CVE while running an operating system Microsoft stopped fixing in 2014 or 2015, and the update requires a mandatory restart with HotPatching unsupported on the Server 2003 package, so the compliant reading is generated before the fixed driver is the one running.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: A.8.8 depends on receiving timely information about vulnerabilities in the systems in use, and no such stream exists any more for Windows XP or Windows Server 2003. This CVE is closable because the 2011 bulletin still exists; the exposure the control cannot address is everything found in those kernels since, which generates no advisory and therefore no work item.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: For afd.sys the mitigation is unambiguous and the clock is the only thing missing: KB2592799 has existed since 2011-10-11, CISA added the CVE on 2022-03-28 with a 2022-04-18 due date, and the EPSS pair for 2026-08-17 is score 0.31761 at percentile 0.98147, which puts it in the top two percent of the whole EPSS population despite affecting only platforms that left support in 2014 and 2015. Because MS11-080 publishes no workaround, the control's compensating-control branch reduces on these hosts to withdrawing local and terminal-server logon rights from non-administrative accounts, which is the precondition the bulletin names.

attack_vector.description: An attacker crafts a link into the Oracle Application Server Single Sign-On login endpoint of Oracle Identity Management 10g 10.1.4.3.0 with a redirect destination the component does not constrain to its own domains. The victim sees and follows a URL on the organisation's SSO hostname and lands on the attacker's page, typically a credential-collection replica of the login form they were expecting.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N in the packet vector, and Oracle's risk matrix marks the row remotely exploitable without authentication
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L, but UI:R is load-bearing: the victim must follow the link, so this is a phishing enabler rather than a self-contained compromise, and Oracle's own CVSS 2.0 row rates the access complexity Medium
attack_vector.ai_factor: Unknown by construction. Oracle Critical Patch Updates credit reporters in one aggregate statement for the whole release, so no finder and no discovery method can be attributed to this CVE from the advisory.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Applying the October 2012 Critical Patch Update to Oracle Identity Management 10g 10.1.4.3, and in front of it constraining redirect destinations at the Oracle HTTP Server or reverse proxy to the deployment's own domains.
prevention.adequacy: The patch is authoritative but unverifiable from outside: Oracle names no parameter, so an operator cannot demonstrate before or after that the specific path is closed. The proxy-side constraint is testable, and it is the only control that also covers whatever redirect handling the unpatched instance retains.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alerting on 302 responses from the OSSO virtual host whose Location header points outside the organisation's domains, from the Oracle HTTP Server access and error logs.
detection.adequacy: It sees the abuse but not the harm — the credential theft happens on the attacker's site, so the log tells you a redirect was issued, not whether anyone typed a password. It also depends on those logs being shipped somewhere they are read: where the Oracle HTTP Server logs for a 10g middle tier stay on the host, the alert has nowhere to fire.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating a confirmed redirect abuse as a credential-exposure event for whichever population received the link: reset the affected accounts and check for authentications from unfamiliar sources against every partner application registered with that SSO instance.
response.adequacy: Scoping is the weak point. The redirect leaves a record on the SSO tier, but nothing there identifies which users followed the link, so the response either overreaches to the whole population that could have received the mail or under-reaches to the few visible in the logs.

NIST-800-53-SI-10.gap: The control demands validated input and the advisory withholds what would make that testable. Oracle's October 2012 row is an unspecified vulnerability under the sub-component 'Cookies/Tokens, Redirects', with no parameter named, so an operator holding OSSO 10.1.4.3.0 can satisfy SI-10 on paper and still have no way to demonstrate this particular path is constrained.

NIST-800-53-AC-3.gap: Access enforcement is never engaged. The endpoint grants no resource and authenticates nobody — it forwards the browser — which is why Oracle scores confidentiality as none and integrity as partial. An AC-3 attestation across the Oracle Identity Management deployment is entirely accurate while the login hostname works as phishing infrastructure.

NIS2-Art21-identity-management.gap: The obligation is discharged through authentication strength and account lifecycle controls on the SSO tier, none of which the flaw touches. The redirect fires before any authentication decision is reached on the genuine endpoint, so even multi-factor authentication on OSSO 10.1.4.3.0 leaves the abuse untouched: what is stolen is the hostname's credibility, not a session.

UK-CAF-B2.gap: An identity and access review of this deployment covers authentication policy, session handling and registered partner applications, and finds them adequate. The CVSS Scope:Changed rating names what the review misses: the impact lands outside the assessed component, on the Portal and Forms users who trust that login endpoint because it is the one they are told to trust.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Application patching does close this once the October 2012 CPU is applied, and the friction is upstream of the operator. Oracle produces patches for historically inactive Application Server platform/version combinations only on customer request, so the artefact for a 10.1.4.3.0 tier may not exist until asked for; CISA set the same 2022-04-18 due date as for the critical entries added that day.

ISO-27001-2022-A.5.15.gap: Access control policy governs who may reach which resources under which conditions, and has no vocabulary for a resource whose whole function on this path is to forward the requester elsewhere. An A.5.15 statement covering the OSSO 10.1.4.3.0 deployment can be complete, current and correct while the endpoint remains usable as a redirector by anyone who can reach it.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Oracle Application Server Single Sign-On 10.1.4.3.0 carries a 4.7 CVSS with confidentiality and availability both none and an EPSS pair for 2026-08-17 of 0.04685 at percentile 0.91009, yet CISA added it to KEV on 2022-03-28 with the same 2022-04-18 due date as the critical entries alongside it. The control's compensating-control branch is what makes it actionable on a legacy Oracle Identity Management 10g tier where the CPU patch may have to be requested from Oracle before it exists: constrain redirect destinations at the Oracle HTTP Server or reverse proxy in front of OSSO, which is testable in a way the undocumented vendor fix is not.

attack_vector.description: The attacker sends one HTTP request whose query string carries no '=' and begins with '-'. Apache, following the CGI specification's indexed-query rule, splits it on '+', URL-decodes the words and passes them to php-cgi as command-line arguments; php-cgi honours them as switches. Setting allow_url_include and auto_prepend_file to php://input makes PHP execute the request body, giving remote code execution as the web-server user.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; a single unauthenticated request, with no session, cookie or prior access needed
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L/UI:N; the payload is generic across targets. The only real gate is deployment shape: PHP must be invoked as CGI through a handler or wrapper that forwards argv, and the server must implement RFC 3875 section 4.4, which Apache does and FastCGI setups do not.
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Found by the Eindbazen team during Nullcon CTF from a '?-s' source disclosure, then traced by hand to a 2004 change that removed PHP's CGI argument guard.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: PHP 5.3.13 or 5.4.3 or later, or — during the window when no fix existed — PHP's own mod_rewrite rule rejecting query strings that start with '-' and contain no '=', or Eindbazen's wrapper binary that strips argv from php-cgi invocations. Structurally, running PHP under php-fpm or mod_php removes the path entirely.
prevention.adequacy: The version fix was twice incomplete — CVE-2012-2311 defeated it with %3D in 2012, and CVE-2024-4577 defeated it again on Windows in 2024 — so 'upgrade' has a poor record here on its own. The configuration mitigation is precise and was deployable before any patch existed, which is why it, not the version, is the durable half of this lesson.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Web-server log rules for query strings beginning with '-' or %2d and containing no '=', and process-lineage alerting on php-cgi spawning shells or writing .php files into the document root.
detection.adequacy: The query-string rule is unusually reliable because the pattern is defined by the CGI specification rather than by a payload, so it survives obfuscation of the arguments themselves. It fires at exploitation time, though, and a successful request installs a web shell that no longer needs the vulnerable path.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating a matching request that returned 200 as a compromise of the web root: compare the document tree against source control, rotate every credential in the application configuration the interpreter could read, and rebuild rather than clean.
response.adequacy: Correct and frequently too late. The code runs as the web-server user with read access to database credentials and API keys in application configuration, so the exposure is decided in the first request and rotation scope is the whole configuration, not the file that was written.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: The advisory's own fixed versions, 5.3.12 and 5.4.2, are still exploitable through the %3D form tracked as CVE-2012-2311 and fixed in 5.3.13 and 5.4.3. SI-2 has no field for an incomplete fix, so a remediation record naming the version the vendor published is a compliant record of a vulnerable host — and the same failure recurred in 2024 with the Best-Fit bypass CVE-2024-4577.

NIST-800-53-CM-7.gap: Least functionality would have eliminated the class outright, because Apache with mod_php, nginx with php-fpm and FastCGI installations are all unaffected. It is applied to packages and services, and a vulnerable php-cgi handler and a safe php-fpm pool are the same installed PHP package, so the baseline never expresses the property that decides exploitability.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: There was nothing to patch when exploitation began. PHP's news entry of 2012-05-03 records that its own bug tracker toggled the report public before solutions had been tested to the project's standard, and Eindbazen published on the same date because the report had already reached reddit. An obligation measured from fix availability scores those days as compliant, and they are the only days in this CVE's history when no version-based remediation existed at all.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: System security assessment of a web tier covers the server build, its modules and its exposure, and passes on all three for an Apache host serving PHP through CGI. The property that decides exploitability is that Apache implements the indexed-query rule of RFC 3875 section 4.4 and forwards the split query string as argv — a specification behaviour that appears in no configuration inventory and no hardening checklist.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Patching the application does close this, but the interpreter is restarted rather than the host, so a php-cgi process pool that was never recycled keeps executing the old binary while the package inventory reports the fixed version. There is no reboot event to expose the divergence, which makes patch-currency evidence and running code disagree silently on precisely the hosts that stay up longest.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: At CVSS 9.8 with an EPSS score of 0.99998 for 2026-08-17 this ranks first in any severity-ordered queue, so the control's prioritisation works. Its scoping does not: an estate that identifies exposure by PHP version alone cannot separate the CGI-handled sites that were exploitable from the php-fpm sites that never were, and produces either wasted remediation or a false clean.

OWASP-Top-10-2021-A03.gap: Injection testing is aimed at the application's own handling of parameters, and here the injection completes before application code executes: the web server splits the query string per the CGI specification and the interpreter accepts the words as its own switches. An application-layer injection test can be thorough, correct and entirely blind to this path.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: PHP-CGI is the case for the four-hour clock rather than a weekly window: the EPSS pair for 2026-08-17 is score 0.99998 at percentile 0.9999, the payload is one unauthenticated request, and CISA put it on the KEV clock on 2022-03-25 with a 2022-04-15 due date. The 'or documented compensating controls' branch was the only usable one between the accidental public disclosure of PHP bug 61910 and the release of 5.3.12 and 5.4.2, since PHP itself published a mod_rewrite rule before it published a fix.

new_control_requirements.name: INCOMPLETE-PATCH-SEQUENCE-SEVERITY-MULTIPLIER
new_control_requirements.description: Vulnerability-management programs must apply a severity multiplier when a CVE is the Nth in an incomplete-patch sequence on the same primitive (third MOTW bypass, second AMSI bypass, etc.). Framework controls treating each CVE as discrete obscure the structural defect; the Nth CVE in a sequence implies that future bypasses on the same primitive are likely.
new_control_requirements.evidence: PHP's CGI argument guard has now failed three times on the same primitive: CVE-2012-1823 itself, then CVE-2012-2311 — which NVD records as existing 'because of an incomplete fix for CVE-2012-1823', reachable through a %3D sequence and fixed in 5.3.13 and 5.4.3 — and then CVE-2024-4577, which DEVCORE describes as bypassing 'the previous protection of CVE-2012-1823 by specific character sequences' through Windows Best-Fit encoding conversion, fixed in 8.3.8, 8.2.20 and 8.1.29. Treating each as discrete is what let estates land on 5.3.12 and record the work as finished.

new_control_requirements.name: CONFIGURATION-SIDE-LIVE-PATCH-INVENTORY
new_control_requirements.description: For any web-fabric vulnerability with a configuration-side mitigation path: that path must be inventoried, tested, and deployable independent of the vendor-patch path. Operators cannot wait for nginx 1.30.1+ if a named-capture refactor mitigates immediately.
new_control_requirements.evidence: PHP published the configuration-side path itself in the 2012-05-03 news entry, before 5.3.12 and 5.4.2 existed: reject query strings that begin with '-' and contain no '=', in the Apache form 'RewriteCond %{QUERY_STRING} ^(%2d|-)[^=]+$ [NC]' plus 'RewriteRule ^(.*) $1? [L]', with Eindbazen's argv-stripping wrapper as an alternative.
