Both are deployable without touching the PHP build, and both would have held through the CVE-2012-2311 bypass that the 5.3.12 upgrade did not.

CVE-2012-2034.name: Adobe Flash Player Memory Corruption Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: The victim's browser or AIR application renders attacker-supplied Flash content and the runtime corrupts memory in a way Adobe states could lead to code execution, at the privilege of the process hosting the runtime. Adobe names no file, function or object, and NVD records the trigger as unspecified vectors, so the mechanism below 'memory corruption in the Flash Player runtime' is not on the public record.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; the attacker needs no account, only that content they control reaches the runtime
attack_vector.complexity: high — AC:H; a JIT-backed runtime of this era needed a heap groom plus an ASLR and DEP defeat for reliable execution, and Adobe published no starting point. UI:R applies because the content must actually be rendered.
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Reported by wushi of team509 through iDefense's Vulnerability Contributor Program per APSB12-14 — manual research submitted to a commercial vulnerability-purchase programme.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Removing Adobe Flash Player and Adobe AIR from the endpoint, which is what CISA's required action on this KEV record calls for; failing that, the APSB12-14 versions for each platform, with the browser restarted afterwards so the new plugin is loaded.
prevention.adequacy: Removal is complete and blocked by content rather than by technology: an organisation with internal material authored in Flash cannot uninstall the runtime until that material is replaced. The version fix was complete for this defect and lasted until the next Flash bulletin, which is the pattern that eventually made removal the only durable answer.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Treating plugin-process crashes as security telemetry rather than stability noise: correlating repeated Flash or AIR host crashes with the origin being rendered at the time.
detection.adequacy: Weak against a working exploit and useful only against a failing one. Adobe published no sample and no signature exists, so there is nothing to match on content; crash correlation catches unreliable attempts and misses the reliable ones entirely.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating an endpoint that executed unknown Flash content during the exposure window as user-context compromised: rebuild, and rotate credentials the browser session held.
response.adequacy: With no indicators of compromise from the vendor and no public sample, the decision rests on crash telemetry or on downstream evidence, so the realistic response is the removal the KEV record already requires rather than per-endpoint triage.

NIST-800-53-CM-7.gap: Removing the Flash runtime is a least-functionality decision that CM-7 can express and cannot force. CISA had to write the removal into this record's required action — 'The impacted product is end-of-life and should be disconnected if still in use' — which is the control's own outcome arriving as an external instruction a decade later.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: APSB12-14 gives a fixed version per platform and SI-2 tracks whether it is installed. The plugin runs inside a long-lived browser process, so a workstation carrying 11.3.300.257 on disk keeps executing 11.2.202.235 until that process is restarted — a divergence between remediation evidence and running code with no reboot event to make it visible.

NIS2-Art21-vulnerability-management.gap: Scoping from the KEV product string 'Flash Player' misses two populations the same Adobe bulletin lists: Adobe AIR 3.2.0.2070 and earlier, which embeds the identical runtime, and the Flash build bundled inside Google Chrome, whose remedy Adobe expressed as verifying Chrome 19.0.1084.56. An inventory of standalone plugin installs reports clean on both.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: System security identifies unsupported software and calls for its removal, and Flash is the least ambiguous case there is. The finding is still unactionable inside a security programme wherever the content that depends on the runtime was authored in Flash, because what unblocks it is re-authoring that content rather than any endpoint change.

AU-Essential-8-App-Hardening.gap: User application hardening targets exactly this class of browser-rendered plugin content and stops at the browser. Adobe AIR renders through the same runtime inside installed desktop applications with no browser in the path, and hardening the browser does not uninstall the runtime, which is what this record's KEV required action demands.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: The control's evaluate-then-decide cycle needs something to evaluate. Adobe named no file, function or object for this flaw and NVD records unspecified vectors, so exposure cannot be assessed more finely than 'the runtime is present'. That collapses A.8.8's decision space to a single question and gives it a single defensible answer, which is removal.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: For Adobe Flash Player this record is unusual in what CISA asked for: the required action is 'The impacted product is end-of-life and should be disconnected if still in use', not an instruction to apply vendor updates, so the verified mitigation the control demands is removal of the runtime rather than reaching 11.3.300.257. CISA opened the clock on 2022-03-28 with a 2022-04-18 due date, and the 2026-08-17 EPSS pair of 0.078 at percentile 0.94146 is a statement about a product that should no longer be installed at all.

new_control_requirements.name: BROWSER-MANAGED-UPDATE-NO-DEFERRAL
new_control_requirements.description: Enterprise update rings must not defer security-channel browser updates beyond 24h.
new_control_requirements.evidence: One of the two remediation paths APSB12-14 published for this CVE is a browser update rather than a plugin update: Flash Player shipped inside Google Chrome as a bundled component, and Adobe's instruction was that Chrome users verify they had reached Chrome 19.0.1084.56, which carried 11.3.300.257. On that path the browser update ring is the Flash patch channel, and deferring it defers the runtime fix with no plugin-inventory record showing anything outstanding. The same channel is what applies the restart that makes the new runtime live.

CVE-2012-2539.name: Microsoft Word Remote Code Execution Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: An attacker sends RTF data whose listoverridecount handling corrupts memory in Word's parser. The victim opens the file, or simply previews an RTF message in Outlook where Word is the mail reader, and code runs with that user's rights. On SharePoint Server 2010 the same parser is reached through Word Automation Services, which converts submitted documents unattended, so the document need never be opened by a person at all. MS12-079's second mitigating factor records a further route: the attacker hosts the crafted RTF on a website, including a compromised site or one that accepts user-provided content or advertisements, with 'no way to force users to visit these websites'.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; the attacker holds no account on the target and needs only a delivery route for the file or message
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L with UI:R, and the user interaction can be as little as a preview-pane render, which Microsoft names as the sharpest path because Word is the default mail reader in Outlook 2007 and Outlook 2010. On the SharePoint conversion path there is no user interaction at all.
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Reported by an anonymous contributor through Beyond Security's SecuriTeam Secure Disclosure program per MS12-079 — a commercial brokerage route, with no indication of automated discovery.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: The per-product MS12-079 updates, remembering that Word 2007 needs KB2760421 and KB2760416 together and that SharePoint's Word Automation Services has its own KB2760405. Before they land, the bulletin's own workarounds: reading email as plain text, and the Office File Block policy for Word 2003-and-earlier formats.
prevention.adequacy: The updates are complete for the flaw; the workarounds are not free. MS12-079 states that messages viewed in plain text 'will not contain pictures, specialized fonts, animations, or other rich content', and File Block on Office 2003-and-earlier formats blocks or protects legacy documents.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Process-lineage alerting on WINWORD.EXE spawning children or writing executables, extended to the SharePoint Word Automation Services conversion worker, plus treating repeated Word crashes tied to one sender as a security signal.
detection.adequacy: It sees the consequence rather than the document, which is the right trade here because no sample was published and no content signature exists. It gives nothing before code runs, and on the SharePoint path it depends on the Word Automation Services conversion worker being instrumented at all.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating a Word process that spawned a child as a user-context compromise: isolate the endpoint, rotate the user's credentials, and search mail for the same RTF attachment or message across other recipients.
response.adequacy: Scoping depends on retention. The preview-pane path means the message need not have been opened or saved, so the mail-gateway record may be the only trace, and where Word Automation Services was the entry point the affected asset is a content farm rather than an endpoint.

NIST-800-53-SI-3.gap: The control depends on recognising malicious content, and none was ever published for this flaw: MS12-079 records it as privately reported with no public sample, and describes the trigger only as specially crafted RTF data. Signature-based scanning has nothing to key on, and the carrier is a legitimate document format that arrives in ordinary mail traffic every day.

NIST-800-53-AC-6.gap: Least privilege genuinely bounds this on the endpoint — the first of MS12-079's two mitigating factors is that the attacker gains the same rights as the current user — and bounds nothing on the server path. SharePoint 2010's Word Automation Services converts submitted documents under a service identity selected for its reach into the content farm, and there is no user whose rights the outcome could be limited to.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: MS12-079 is seven KBs across seven products, and Word 2007 alone needs KB2760421 together with KB2760416 for the Compatibility Pack before it is protected. Completion measured per bulletin, or by an endpoint agent that only sees the Word package, reports success while Word Viewer, the Compatibility Pack or a SharePoint 2010 Word Automation Services farm still runs the pre-fix parser.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: System security assessment of an Office estate concentrates on macro policy, ActiveX and add-in control. None of those are in this path: the corruption occurs while the parser lays out RTF list-override data, and the delivery route Microsoft singles out is the Outlook preview pane with Word as mail reader — a default configuration rather than a hardening failure the assessment would flag.

AU-Essential-8-App-Hardening.gap: Application hardening concentrates on content types that carry executable payloads, and RTF list-override data is not one. The mitigations MS12-079 actually offers sit outside that strategy — plain-text mail reading and the Office File Block policy for Word 2003-and-earlier formats.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.7.gap: Malware protection assumes recognisable content at a scanning point. The file here is structurally valid RTF whose anomaly is a control word's value rather than an embedded object; the preview-pane path means it need never be written to disk for an on-access scanner to see; and on SharePoint it arrives as ordinary submitted content for conversion. Gateway and endpoint attestations are accurate and blind to all three.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: For MS12-079 the control's value is in what counts as complete. The bulletin is seven KBs across Word 2003, 2007 and 2010, Word Viewer, the Office Compatibility Pack, SharePoint Server 2010 Word Automation Services and Office Web Apps 2010, with Word 2007 requiring KB2760421 and KB2760416 together — so verification has to be per product rather than per bulletin. CISA opened the clock on 2022-03-28 with a 2022-04-18 due date, and the compensating-control branch has real content here because MS12-079 publishes two: plain-text mail reading and the Office File Block policy.

new_control_requirements.name: ARCHIVE-CONTENT-TYPE-PROVENANCE
new_control_requirements.description: For this CVE the requirement is that Word's Protected View decision be taken from verified provenance of the file — established outside the document — rather than from metadata that travels with the document and that an attacker controls, and that the untrusted-origin marking survive whatever container the document is delivered in so the handler still sees it as externally sourced. The operator-side expression of the control: the mail gateway and file-share boundary apply and preserve the untrusted-origin marking themselves, so the sandbox decision does not depend on the application deriving it from attacker-supplied input. The distinguishing test: deliver an externally-sourced document through each ingress path and confirm it reaches Word marked untrusted, instead of confirming only that Protected View is enabled in policy.
new_control_requirements.evidence: MS12-079's own workaround is a coarse version of this control — the Office File Block policy for Word 2003-and-earlier formats, which on Office 2010 opens blocked files in protected mode rather than refusing them — and it is coarse precisely because it keys on the format rather than on where the file came from. Applying provenance at the ingress boundary is what makes the sandbox decision survive the delivery paths this CVE actually uses: an RTF body previewed in Outlook with Word as the mail reader, and a document submitted to SharePoint 2010 Word Automation Services for unattended conversion, neither of which is a user opening a downloaded file.

CVE-2012-5076.name: Oracle Java SE Sandbox Bypass Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: A web page serves an unsigned applet to a Java SE 7 runtime at or below Update 7. The runtime's own deny-list fails to restrict com.sun.org.glassfish.external and com.sun.org.glassfish.gmbal, so the applet loads classes reserved for privileged runtime internals and leaves the sandbox without corrupting anything. Arbitrary Java then runs as the account whose browser loaded the page.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none - PR:N; the applet arrives with no permissions at all, which is the substance of the bug: no-permission code reaches packages the deny-list was supposed to keep it out of.
attack_vector.complexity: low - AC:L; deterministic Java with no memory corruption and no race. The binding constraint is reachability, meaning a browser with the Java plug-in registered and a runtime at or below 7 Update 7.
attack_vector.ai_factor: No source read for this entry claims AI involvement in the discovery, and no research arm with 'AI' in its brand name appears anywhere in the attribution chain.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Removing the Java browser plug-in and the javaws association from workstations that do not run internal applets, which closes the delivery path without depending on the runtime version at all.
prevention.adequacy: Complete for the drive-by path and useless for the residual case: a host that must run internal Java applets keeps the plug-in and therefore keeps the exposure until the runtime is updated.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alerting when a Java plug-in or javaws process spawns a child process or writes an executable within seconds of a browser navigation.
detection.adequacy: It fires only once arbitrary Java is already running as the user, so it bounds dwell time rather than preventing the escape, and it stays silent for a payload that never leaves the JVM.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating the workstation as having executed attacker-supplied code at user privilege: rebuild rather than close on the runtime update, and rotate credentials that were used on the host during the exposure window.
response.adequacy: Scope follows what the account could reach, which is not knowable from the endpoint alone. A JRE update applied to a host that already ran the payload removes the flaw and nothing the attacker left behind.

NIST-800-53-CM-7.gap: An organisation can evidence CM-7 with an approved-software list on which Oracle Java is a legitimate entry, and still be fully exposed. The unit of exposure is not the Java package but the browser plug-in registration and the .jnlp handler that let untrusted web content reach a 7u7 runtime, and CM-7 evidence is not usually collected at that granularity.

NIS2-Art21-vulnerability-handling.gap: An entity can run a conforming vulnerability-handling process and never see this flaw, because the process consumes advisories and this advisory is Oracle's October 2012 Critical Patch Update. What the CISA listing of 2022-03-28 exposed was not slow triage but runtimes that no inventory had enumerated in the nine years since the fix shipped.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: B4 evidence for a Java estate typically records vendor provenance, version and patch cadence. None of those distinguish a runtime whose shipped deny-list omits the two glassfish packages from one whose deny-list is complete, so a system can be assessed as securely configured while carrying the precise defect that makes an unsigned applet a full compromise.

AU-Essential-8-App-Hardening.gap: Blocking Java from the internet in the managed browser is the right mitigation and is measurable, which is why it is where assessment stops. The javaws path around it is not a browser setting, so a maturity rating earned on browser configuration alone overstates the protection an affected 7u7 host actually has.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.9.gap: A.8.9 is a drift-detection control: it compares a running configuration against an approved baseline. Here the running configuration and the vendor baseline agree, because the missing package.access entries are what Oracle shipped through 7 Update 7, so a conforming configuration-management programme returns no finding on the file that decides exploitability.

OWASP-Top-10-2021-A06.gap: Component scanning that reads manifests, lockfiles and build outputs cannot see an endpoint browser plug-in, because nothing declares it. An organisation with excellent A06 coverage over its own applications can therefore hold a fleet of workstations running the affected runtime with no signal in any component report.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Oracle's fix for this Java SE 7 sandbox bypass shipped with the October 2012 Critical Patch Update; CISA listed it on 2022-03-28 with a 2022-04-18 due date. The control's 'whichever is later' clause is what makes it operable on an entry like this, where patch availability predates the KEV listing by nine years and the four-hour clock therefore starts at the listing. EPSS of 0.91013 at the 99.799th percentile (2026-08-17) leaves no argument for a longer window.

new_control_requirements.name: MITIGATION-ACTIVE-PATCH-PENDING-VERDICT-CLASS
new_control_requirements.description: Compliance verdicts must distinguish three states: (a) binary patch deployed (vulnerability eliminated), (b) vendor-mitigation rule active, no binary patch (residual risk: any defect in the mitigation rule reopens the vulnerability), (c) no mitigation, no patch (full exposure). Audit reports must surface (b) as a distinct compensating-control state with an associated time-bound action item, not as a 'patched per SLA' outcome.
new_control_requirements.evidence: For Oracle Java SE 7 at or below Update 7, disabling the browser plug-in is a state (b) outcome and is routinely recorded as remediation. It is not: the vulnerable runtime is still installed, the javaws handler can still reach it, and a single browser re-enable or a re-imaged workstation restores full exposure. Only replacing the runtime, or removing it, reaches state (a) on the flaw CISA listed on 2022-03-28.

CVE-2013-1690.name: Mozilla Firefox and Thunderbird Denial-of-Service Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: A crafted page fires onreadystatechange and aborts the load, freeing Gecko's DocumentViewerImpl while a reference to it is still live. The engine then calls through the dangling reference. Losing the allocation race gives a crash into unmapped memory; winning it gives code execution in the browser process, which on the affected builds runs with the user's own rights.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none - PR:N; the attacker needs no account on the target and no prior foothold, only a page the victim loads.
attack_vector.complexity: low - AC:L with UI:R. Reaching the bug is trivial; making it execute rather than crash requires winning a heap reallocation, which is why the public module pins specific builds instead of covering the affected range.
attack_vector.ai_factor: Attribution is to Nils per MFSA 2013-53, with separate credit in the Metasploit module for one-day exploit analysis. Neither of those records claims automated or AI-assisted discovery.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Driving Firefox to 22 or ESR 17.0.7, Thunderbird to 17.0.7 and SeaMonkey to 2.19, and forcing an application restart so the fixed binary is the process actually running.
prevention.adequacy: Complete once the process restarts, and worth nothing before that. It also depends on the inventory naming every Gecko build on the host, including mail clients and repackaged bundles.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Collecting browser and mail-client crash telemetry and alerting on repeated faults at unmapped addresses tied to a single origin.
detection.adequacy: It sees the failures, not the successes. A reallocation the attacker wins produces no crash, so the signal is strongest against unreliable exploitation and weakest against the runs that matter.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating a host that loaded the delivering content as having run code at user privilege: rebuild the endpoint and rotate the credentials it held, rather than closing on the browser update.
response.adequacy: Bounded by knowing which hosts loaded the content, which without proxy or DNS retention for the exposure window cannot be reconstructed after the fact.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: SI-2 records remediation as of update installation. For this CVE the vulnerable code keeps running until the browser or Thunderbird process is relaunched, so the control's own completion evidence is generated at a moment when the flaw may still be live on the endpoint. Nothing in SI-2 requires the process-restart step to be measured or reported.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: The Article 21 obligation is met by acting on MFSA 2013-53, and the fix was trivially available. The exposure it leaves behind is scope: the advisory covers Thunderbird, Thunderbird ESR and SeaMonkey, and a patch policy that enumerates browsers rather than Gecko engines conforms while leaving a mail client on a pre-17.0.7 build.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: B4 assurance over the managed browser gave no visibility into the build the August 2013 attack ran against, which was a repackaged Gecko bundle inventoried under its own name rather than as Firefox. Secure-configuration evidence gathered per named application does not generalise to a second copy of the same engine sitting on the same host.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Patch-applications maturity is measured on installed version, which for a browser is a proxy rather than the fact of interest. An estate reporting Firefox 22 or ESR 17.0.7 everywhere is still exposed in every session whose process predates the update, and the Essential Eight measurement has no way to express that residual.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: A.8.8 works when the asset register lists the affected software. Here the register has to contain SeaMonkey 2.19 and any repackaged Gecko bundle as separate entries, not just Firefox and Thunderbird - and an A.8.8 process that acts correctly on every entry it holds still misses whatever the register never enumerated.

NIST-800-53-SI-4.gap: The distinctive artefact this flaw produces is a browser crash executing unmapped memory, which sits below the threshold of most SI-4 collection and is indistinguishable from ordinary browser instability without the faulting-address detail. The successful case produces no crash, so the control's best signal comes precisely from the attempts that did not work.

new_control_requirements.name: BROWSER-MANAGED-UPDATE-NO-DEFERRAL
new_control_requirements.description: Enterprise update rings must not defer security-channel browser updates beyond 24h.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Mozilla shipped this fix in Firefox 22 and ESR 17.0.7, and the August 2013 attack ran against Tor Browser Bundle builds that had not taken it - the Tor Project named the fixed bundle versions on 2013-08-05 and pointed at the ESR 17.0.7 fix. The control is the right one for a browser flaw with a free, automatic vendor update and an EPSS of 0.69021 at the 99.293rd percentile (2026-08-17), and it has to be paired with a forced relaunch, because the ESR 17.0.7 binary on disk does not protect a Gecko process started before it arrived.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CISA listed this Gecko use-after-free on 2022-03-28 with a 2022-04-18 due date, almost nine years after MFSA 2013-53. Applied to Mozilla products the SLA is only meaningful if the inventory it runs against names Firefox, Firefox ESR, Thunderbird, Thunderbird ESR and SeaMonkey separately - the advisory's own product list - because a four-hour clock started against an incomplete asset set finishes on time and changes nothing on the unlisted builds.

CVE-2013-2251.name: Apache Struts Improper Input Validation Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: An unauthenticated HTTP request to any mapped .action endpoint carries a parameter named action:, redirect: or redirectAction:. Struts 2's DefaultActionMapper evaluates the text after the prefix as an OGNL expression against the value stack, which reaches the full Java object graph, and the expression executes commands as the account running the application server.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none - PR:N; the prefix is handled while the request is being mapped, ahead of any authentication or authorisation the application performs.
attack_vector.complexity: low - AC:L, UI:N. One request, no groom, no leak, no race. The only real precondition is a struts2-core jar in the 2.0.0 to 2.3.15 range behind the endpoint.
attack_vector.ai_factor: The Metasploit module credits Takeshi Terada with the vulnerability discovery, and neither it nor Apache's 2013 announcement attributes the find to automated or AI-assisted analysis.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Upgrading struts2-core to 2.3.15.1 or later and redeploying, which removes the OGNL evaluation of the prefixed parameter rather than filtering requests that carry it.
prevention.adequacy: Complete for the application whose jar is replaced, and unavailable for a vendor-packaged product the operator cannot rebuild - there the residual is a supplier obligation, not a patch.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alerting on any request parameter whose name begins with action:, redirect: or redirectAction:, and on the container process spawning a command interpreter.
detection.adequacy: The parameter-name signal is high fidelity because legitimate traffic has no reason to carry it, but it fires on attempts rather than outcomes; the process-spawn signal fires only after code has already run.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating a hit as web-tier code execution: search the deployment for files written outside a release, review the container's outbound connections for the exposure window, and rotate every credential the application process could read.
response.adequacy: The database and service credentials in an application's configuration are readable by the process, so the rotation scope is whatever those credentials reach, and upgrading the jar removes the flaw without removing anything already written through it.

NIST-800-53-SI-10.gap: An SI-10 assessment examines the validation an application applies to accepted input. This exploit never reaches that code, because the OGNL evaluation happens in DefaultActionMapper while the request is being resolved. The control can therefore be fully satisfied on an application running Struts 2.3.15, with the finding recorded against code the attacker does not execute.

NIS2-Art21-supply-chain.gap: Supplier assurance under Article 21 typically reaches the direct vendor and its declared components. struts2-core in the 2.0.0 to 2.3.15 range is often neither declared nor direct - it arrives inside a purchased application - so an entity can hold current supplier attestations and still run the vulnerable mapper with no way to see the framework level from outside.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: There is no misconfiguration here for B4 assurance to find. DefaultActionMapper is the default mapper and the prefix handling is its shipped behaviour through 2.3.15, so a system that is hardened, current on OS patches and correctly configured in every respect a B4 review inspects remains unauthenticated-RCE exposed on the framework version alone.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Patch applications assumes the operator can obtain and apply a fix. For an embedded struts2-core the fix is a supplier rebuild against 2.3.15.1, and until that ships the operator has no update to deploy - so the maturity model records either a persistent exception or, worse, a compliant rating derived from the wrapping product's own patch level.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.28.gap: Secure coding under A.8.28 governs the organisation's own source, and the vulnerable code belongs to Apache. Review, static analysis and coding standards applied to a Struts 2.3.15 application will all pass, because the injection sink is in the framework's request resolution rather than in anything the development team wrote or could have written differently.

OWASP-Top-10-2021-A03.gap: Classifying this as injection is correct and yet misdirects the remediation A03 normally implies. Parameterised queries, output encoding and input allowlists in the application change nothing, because OGNL is evaluated before the application runs; the only fix that touches the sink is moving to struts2-core 2.3.15.1 or later.

new_control_requirements.name: INCOMPLETE-PATCH-SEQUENCE-SEVERITY-MULTIPLIER
new_control_requirements.description: Vulnerability-management programs must apply a severity multiplier when a CVE is the Nth in an incomplete-patch sequence on the same primitive (third MOTW bypass, second AMSI bypass, etc.). Framework controls treating each CVE as discrete obscure the structural defect; the Nth CVE in a sequence implies that future bypasses on the same primitive are likely.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Struts 2.3.15.1, the release that fixes this CVE, carries two bulletins at once - S2-016 for the OGNL code execution and S2-017 for an open redirect through the same short-circuit prefixes, per Apache's own 2013 announcement. The primitive is the parameter-prefix handling in DefaultActionMapper, and a programme that filed S2-016 as a discrete item took the version to 2.3.15.1 without recording that the same mechanism had just produced a second defect.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Apache published the fixed Struts release on 2013-07-16 and CISA listed the flaw on 2022-03-25 with a 2022-04-15 due date. The control's compensating-control branch is the operative one for embedded struts2-core, where the four-hour action is blocking action:, redirect: and redirectAction: parameters upstream while the supplier rebuild is pursued - at EPSS 0.99998, 99.99th percentile (2026-08-17), leaving the endpoint reachable while waiting for a vendor release is not a defensible position.

attack_vector.description: An applet supplies an image whose channel description disagrees with its raster. The native storeImageArray() routine in the JRE's 2D code indexes the channel array without validating it, corrupting JVM memory, and the corruption is used to leave the sandbox. Arbitrary Java then runs as the account whose browser loaded the applet.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none - PR:N; the applet runs unsigned and unprivileged, and the flaw is what converts that into full user-context execution.
attack_vector.complexity: low - AC:L; no ASLR or DEP work is needed because the corruption and the escape both stay inside the JVM. The constraint is version and reachability: 7u21, 6u45 or 5.0u45 and below, reachable from a browser or javaws.
attack_vector.ai_factor: The finder is not named by NVD or by any advisory retrievable for this entry, and the public exploit is credited to Packet Storm. No AI-assisted discovery is claimed anywhere in that chain.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Moving every runtime to 7u25 or the equivalent distribution package, and removing the Java browser plug-in on hosts with no internal applet requirement.
prevention.adequacy: Effective on the Java 7 line where the update is obtainable. It gives no answer on a Java 6 or 5.0 runtime an operator cannot update, where removal rather than patching is the only terminal state.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alerting when a browser-launched JVM spawns a child process, writes an executable, or opens a connection unrelated to the page that started it.
detection.adequacy: It cannot see the escape itself, which produces no crash and no module load. The earliest reliable signal is the second stage, by which point attacker code is running with the user's rights.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating an alerting host as user-context compromise and, because CISA flags this CVE for ransomware association, verifying that backup copies reachable from that user account were not modified during the window.
response.adequacy: Rebuilding the endpoint and rotating its credentials is bounded by knowing the window; where a backup share was writable by the compromised account, the recovery copy is inside the blast radius rather than outside it.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: SI-2 assumes remediation means installing something. That is true for Java 7, where 7u25 shipped on 2013-06-18, and it is the wrong frame for the Java 6 and 5.0 runtimes NVD also lists: with no obtainable public update the control produces a documented exception, and an exception is not the removal decision the asset requires.

NIS2-Art21-vulnerability-management.gap: Acting on the advisory satisfies Article 21, and updating Java 7 is the visible act. The exposure persists in the runtime that was left behind for a legacy application, because the delivery path is any browser or javaws handler on the host and it resolves to whichever JVM is registered, not to the one the remediation ticket named.

UK-CAF-C1.gap: There is very little for C1 monitoring to key on. The sandbox escape leaves no crash, loads no module and drops no file; it happens inside a JVM the user legitimately launched. Monitoring built around process creation and file writes therefore starts observing at the second stage, which means C1 coverage of this technique is detection of the consequence rather than of the compromise.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: B4 evidence drawn from the inventoried runtime version is the right check applied to an incomplete population. Hosts carrying a second, older JVM for a legacy application present a compliant primary version while the browser and javaws handler can still resolve to a runtime at or below 7u21, 6u45 or 5.0u45.

AU-Essential-8-App-Hardening.gap: Blocking Java from the internet in the managed browser is the strongest operator-side lever this CVE admits and is measurable, which is why assessment concentrates there. The javaws path is outside browser configuration, so a hardened rating earned on the browser understates what an affected runtime on the same host can still be handed.

AU-Essential-8-Backup.gap: The Essential Eight backup mitigation is about having and testing regular backups. CISA's ransomware flag on this KEV entry makes a further property decisive: the exploit runs at the privilege of the browsing user, so any backup location that user account can write to is reachable by the same payload, and a tested backup on a user-writable share is not a recovery path against this delivery route.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: A.8.8 supports evaluating an exposure and accepting the risk where no fix is obtainable, which is where a Java 6 or 5.0 runtime lands. The standard does not require the acceptance to carry a removal date, so a runtime CISA listed on 2022-03-28 can sit inside a conforming ISMS indefinitely with an annually re-signed acceptance and no change to its exposure.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Oracle shipped the fix as Java SE 7u25 on 2013-06-18 and CISA listed the flaw on 2022-03-28 with a 2022-04-18 due date and a known-ransomware association. Bound to this product the four-hour action is unambiguous on the Java 7 line and has to fall back to the documented-compensating-control branch on the Java 6 and 5.0 runtimes NVD names, where no obtainable public update may exist and the compensating control is removing the plug-in path to that JVM.

new_control_requirements.name: MITIGATION-ACTIVE-PATCH-PENDING-VERDICT-CLASS
new_control_requirements.description: Compliance verdicts must distinguish three states: (a) binary patch deployed (vulnerability eliminated), (b) vendor-mitigation rule active, no binary patch (residual risk: any defect in the mitigation rule reopens the vulnerability), (c) no mitigation, no patch (full exposure). Audit reports must surface (b) as a distinct compensating-control state with an associated time-bound action item, not as a 'patched per SLA' outcome.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Disabling Java in the browser on a host still running 7u21, 6u45 or 5.0u45 is a state (b) outcome for this CVE and is habitually recorded as remediation. The vulnerable runtime is still installed, javaws can still reach it, and a re-image or a browser policy change restores full exposure - only reaching 7u25, or removing the runtime, is state (a).

attack_vector.description: A crafted page causes Internet Explorer to free an object while a reference to it survives, then fills the freed allocation with attacker data before the stale reference is used. The resulting virtual call runs attacker code with the rights of the browsing user. The public implementation reaches the defect through VML dashstyle array handling in vgx.dll.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none - PR:N; the attacker needs no account and no foothold, only that the target load the page.
attack_vector.complexity: low - AC:L with UI:R for the bug itself; reliability is the expensive part, which is why the public module pins Internet Explorer 8 on Windows 7 SP1 and accepts only two ntdll builds.
attack_vector.ai_factor: Reported by VUPEN Security at Pwn2Own 2013 through HP's Zero Day Initiative, per Microsoft's own acknowledgements. Human competition research; no AI-assisted discovery is claimed by any source.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Applying MS13-037 (KB2829530) and restarting the host, or removing Internet Explorer and the MSHTML dependency where the browser is not required.
prevention.adequacy: Complete on a serviced platform once the reboot lands. It is unavailable on a Windows edition that no longer receives updates, where the only prevention left is removing the engine or the host.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Collecting browser crash telemetry and alerting on repeated iexplore.exe faults tied to one origin, alongside child-process creation from any MSHTML host.
detection.adequacy: Crashes surface the attempts that failed the reallocation race, not the ones that won it, and the child-process signal only appears once the payload has already executed as the user.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating the host as user-context compromise and, given CISA's ransomware association for this CVE, moving straight to credential rotation and lateral-movement review rather than waiting for a payload to be identified.
response.adequacy: The scope is whatever the browsing account could reach. Where one account's credentials were reused elsewhere, the rotation scope extends to everything that credential opened, and MS13-037 removes the flaw without removing an established foothold.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: The control's completion evidence is that KB2829530 is installed, and MS13-037 explicitly requires a system restart afterwards. A fleet report showing full installation therefore overstates remediation by however many hosts have not rebooted, and SI-2 provides no field in which that difference is recorded or measured.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: For a serviced host the obligation is met by ordinary update management. The population that kept this CVE alive to a 2022-03-28 KEV listing is the one where no update can be obtained at all, and Article 21 patch management has no mechanism for an asset whose only remaining remediation is replacement of the operating system underneath it.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: An unserviced Windows host running Internet Explorer can present strong B4 configuration evidence - restricted zones, Enhanced Security Configuration, constrained scripting - and none of it addresses maintenance, which is unachievable. The bulletin's Moderate server rating is itself derived from that hardening, which is a reduction in exposure rather than a fix for the object-lifetime defect.

UK-CAF-D1.gap: Response plans for this CVE tend to start at a recovered payload or an encryption event, which is late for a chain CISA associates with ransomware. What D1 rarely forces is a decision rule for the earlier state - a suspected browser exploit with no artefact recovered - and without it the containment step waits for evidence that a successful exploit is designed not to leave.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Maturity is assessed on whether browser patches are applied within the required window, and MS13-037 is applied through the ordinary channel. The measurement omits the reboot MS13-037 requires, so a fleet can be rated at its target maturity while every host that has not restarted continues to execute the vulnerable engine.

AU-Essential-8-App-Hardening.gap: Hardening the browser genuinely narrows the script surface that drives the object into its use-after-free, so this is partial protection rather than none. It stops short in two ways: the defect is in engine teardown rather than in any switchable feature, and applications hosting the MSHTML control run the same engine irrespective of browser policy.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: Identifying and evaluating this exposure is easy where the asset register names the browser. The register has to name the rendering engine instead, because MS13-037 covers Internet Explorer 6 through 10 and every embedded MSHTML consumer on the same host - an A.8.8 process that acts perfectly on the browser entry leaves those consumers unevaluated.

CIS-Controls-v8-Control7.gap: Control 7 delivers exactly the finding it should - a missing MS13-037 - and on an unserviced Windows edition that finding cannot be closed by patching, re-appearing on every scan cycle. The control has no state for 'correct, unfixable, requires replacement', so the true remediation leaves the vulnerability-management process entirely and lands in a capital decision nobody is scanning for.

new_control_requirements.name: BROWSER-MANAGED-UPDATE-NO-DEFERRAL
new_control_requirements.description: Enterprise update rings must not defer security-channel browser updates beyond 24h.
new_control_requirements.evidence: MS13-037 shipped as KB2829530 on 2013-05-14 covering Internet Explorer 6 through 10, and CISA listed this use-after-free on 2022-03-28 with a known-ransomware association. Applied to Internet Explorer the control has to be read with the bulletin's own restart requirement, since a deferral ring that installs KB2829530 inside 24 hours but leaves the reboot to the user's convenience has not removed the vulnerable engine from the running host.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: The KEV clock on this Internet Explorer flaw opened 2022-03-28 with a 2022-04-18 due date, almost nine years after MS13-037. The documented-compensating-control branch is the one that carries the weight for unserviced Windows editions, where no vendor fix is obtainable and the four-hour action is removing the browser and the MSHTML dependency or isolating the host, with a dated replacement rather than a renewed exception.

CVE-2013-2729.name: Adobe Reader and Acrobat Arbitrary Integer Overflow Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: A PDF carries an RLE-compressed BMP, delivered by the public generator inside an XFA form. A size computation in the decode path overflows, the allocation comes back too small, and run-length decoding writes past its end into the heap. Code execution follows in whatever context the reader process holds - Protected Mode on Reader X and XI, the user's own context on the 9.x line.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none - PR:N; the attacker needs no account on the target, only that the document be rendered.
attack_vector.complexity: low - AC:L; parsing alone reaches the overflow, with no race or leak required. The recorded vector is UI:N, which holds where a plug-in or preview handler renders the file without a deliberate open.
attack_vector.ai_factor: APSB13-15's acknowledgements credit Felipe Andres Manzano via the iSIGHT Partners GVP Program for this CVE and CVE-2013-2730. No AI-assisted discovery is claimed by that bulletin or by the exploit repository.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Reaching 9.5.5, 10.1.7 or 11.0.03 on every Reader and Acrobat copy on the host - both update tracks, and per-user installs as well as managed ones - and closing running reader and browser processes so the fixed parser takes effect.
prevention.adequacy: Complete for every copy the inventory can see and the operator can update. A per-user install outside software distribution is remediated by removing it, not by recording a version.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alerting on reader-process crashes during document rendering and on any child process or executable write originating from AcroRd32 or Acrobat.
detection.adequacy: Crashes indicate an unreliable attempt rather than a successful one, and against Reader X or XI a successful overflow lands inside Protected Mode, where its immediate effects are constrained and correspondingly quiet.

response.what_would_have_worked: Retaining the delivered document for analysis, identifying every other recipient of the same file, and treating a 9.x host that rendered it as user-context compromise rather than as a sandboxed event.
response.adequacy: The distinction between a sandboxed and an unsandboxed outcome depends on which product line the host was running, so the response scope cannot be set without an accurate per-copy inventory of Reader and Acrobat versions.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: Flaw remediation is recorded against inventoried software, and this product is not one inventory entry. Reader and Acrobat update independently, and per-user copies are invisible to deployment tooling, so an SI-2 report showing 11.0.03 can coexist with a second copy on the same workstation still at 11.0.02 and still parsing crafted PDFs.

NIST-800-53-CM-7.gap: CM-7 is usually implemented at the granularity of whether an application is authorised, and Adobe Reader legitimately is. The exposure-relevant decisions sit one level down - browser plug-in registration, preview handler, XFA rendering - and leaving those enabled is what converts a delivered file into a parse with no deliberate open, which no application-level authorisation records.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: An entity that consumed APSB13-15 and drove its managed estate to 9.5.5, 10.1.7 or 11.0.03 has met the obligation. The workstations that keep a 2022-03-28 KEV entry live are the ones holding a per-user copy outside managed distribution, which Article 21 patch management neither reaches nor requires an entity to enumerate.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: Version-based B4 evidence answers a narrower question than the one that decides exposure. It does not show whether the second Adobe product on the other update track is present and stale, and it does not show whether the reader process running right now was started before or after the update replaced the parser.

AU-Essential-8-App-Hardening.gap: Disabling the browser PDF plug-in, JavaScript and XFA rendering meaningfully narrows the paths that carry a crafted image to the decoder, so this is partial protection rather than none. It cannot be a substitute, because the overflow is in BMP RLE decoding rather than in a scriptable feature - any surviving render path still reaches it.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: The quality of an A.8.8 outcome here is set by the asset register rather than by the process. A register with one 'Adobe Reader' line produces a correct, conforming evaluation about one of several vulnerable copies per host, and the Acrobat track and the per-user installs are never evaluated at all.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Adobe's fixed builds for Reader and Acrobat - 9.5.5, 10.1.7 and 11.0.03 - long predate CISA's listing of 2022-03-28 with its 2022-04-18 due date, so the four-hour clock runs from the listing. Applied to this product the SLA is only satisfied when both update tracks are counted: a run that closes on the inventoried Reader while an Acrobat copy stays at 11.0.02 has met the deadline against part of the estate.

new_control_requirements.name: MITIGATION-ACTIVE-PATCH-PENDING-VERDICT-CLASS
new_control_requirements.description: Compliance verdicts must distinguish three states: (a) binary patch deployed (vulnerability eliminated), (b) vendor-mitigation rule active, no binary patch (residual risk: any defect in the mitigation rule reopens the vulnerability), (c) no mitigation, no patch (full exposure). Audit reports must surface (b) as a distinct compensating-control state with an associated time-bound action item, not as a 'patched per SLA' outcome.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Disabling the browser PDF plug-in, JavaScript and XFA rendering on an Adobe Reader or Acrobat install still below 9.5.5, 10.1.7 or 11.0.03 is a state (b) outcome and is frequently reported as hardened-and-therefore-covered. The RLE decoder is untouched by any of those settings, so a document reaching the reader through a surviving render path still lands on the overflow, and only the fixed build reaches state (a).

attack_vector.description: An unprivileged local process primes paged pool, exhausts it so a new PATHRECORD is allocated over primed data, and calls FlattenPath repeatedly. win32k!EPATHOBJ::pprFlattenRec follows the record's uninitialised next pointer and writes through it, giving an arbitrary kernel write that the published exploit turns into ring-0 execution and an elevation of the calling process.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none in CVSS terms - PR:N - but AV:L is the real gate: the attacker must already be running code on the host as some user, so this is a chain step rather than an initial access vector.
attack_vector.complexity: low - AC:L; the technique is mechanical but not instant, needing paged-pool exhaustion and many FlattenPath calls, and its reliability varies enough by Windows build that the public module ships per-OS targets.
attack_vector.ai_factor: Discovered and publicly exploited by Tavis Ormandy, per Exploit-DB 25912 and the Metasploit module's author list. No automated or AI-assisted discovery appears in that chain.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Applying MS13-053 (KB2850851) and rebooting every affected host, prioritising machines where non-administrative users hold interactive sessions.
prevention.adequacy: Complete on a serviced platform once the reboot lands, and unavailable on the Windows editions in the MS13-053 list that no longer receive updates, where removal or replacement is the only remaining action.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alerting on a non-administrative process that drives heavy paged-pool consumption and then issues a burst of GDI path operations, and on any token transition to SYSTEM with no service start or scheduled task behind it.
detection.adequacy: The pool-pressure signal is noisy on a busy multi-user host, and the token-transition signal fires after the escalation has already succeeded - it bounds response time rather than preventing the elevation.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating an escalation on a shared host as compromise of that host's full user population: rotate credentials for every account with a session during the window, not only the account that ran the exploit.
response.adequacy: Bounded by session records for the exposure window. On a session host the population is large, and applying MS13-053 afterwards removes the flaw without invalidating anything the attacker took while running as SYSTEM.

NIST-800-53-AC-6.gap: This is the clearest case of a control passing while the flaw stays open. The exploit's precondition is an ordinary authorised user, so removing administrative rights from standard accounts - the substance of an AC-6 attestation - is the configuration the exploit is written for, not a barrier to it. Nothing in the path from FlattenPath to a kernel write consults an account's privilege at all.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: MS13-053 is inside SI-2's scope and installs through the normal channel, so the control reports success. Because win32k.sys is a kernel driver, the vulnerable code keeps running until the host reboots, and on a session host - the machine class this flaw most favours, since an already-authorised unprivileged user is its only precondition - that reboot evicts every logged-on user.

NIS2-Art21-vulnerability-handling.gap: The obligation begins when the entity learns of the vulnerability, and here the first public account was a Full Disclosure post of 2013-05-17, roughly two months before MS13-053 on 2013-07-09, with complete exploit code published as Exploit-DB 25912 on 2013-06-03. Article 21 does not require an intake channel that reads full-disclosure mailing lists, so a conforming entity could first learn of this from the bulletin.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: B4's configuration levers do not reach this defect. win32k.sys backs the window manager on every affected edition, so it cannot be stopped, blocklisted or removed by any hardening decision, and a complete B4 assurance package describing disabled services and minimised roles leaves the uninitialised pointer reachable from any interactive session.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Patch operating systems is graded from the update-management record, which flips to compliant when MS13-053 is installed. The kernel driver in memory is unchanged until the reboot, so the grade and the exposure can diverge for as long as a host stays up.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: From 2013-07-09 A.8.8 handles this like any other bulletin. The interval it does not address is the one that mattered: from 2013-06-03 there was public exploit code in Exploit-DB 25912 and no vendor fix, and the standard sets out no requirement for what an organisation does with a KEV-class escalation whose exploit is published before the patch exists.

new_control_requirements.name: INCOMPLETE-PATCH-SEQUENCE-SEVERITY-MULTIPLIER
new_control_requirements.description: Vulnerability-management programs must apply a severity multiplier when a CVE is the Nth in an incomplete-patch sequence on the same primitive (third MOTW bypass, second AMSI bypass, etc.). Framework controls treating each CVE as discrete obscure the structural defect; the Nth CVE in a sequence implies that future bypasses on the same primitive are likely.
new_control_requirements.evidence: MS13-053 fixed eight win32k.sys defects in one bulletin - CVE-2013-1300, 1340, 1345, 3129, 3167, 3172, 3173 and this one - which is the structural signal the control exists to capture. A programme that filed CVE-2013-3660 as a discrete Windows escalation and closed it on KB2850851 recorded no expectation that the same kernel-mode driver would keep producing the same class of finding, and win32k has been a recurring escalation surface since.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CISA listed this win32k escalation on 2022-03-28 with a 2022-04-18 due date; MS13-053 had been available since 2013-07-09. Bound to this flaw the SLA has to be measured on the reboot rather than on installation, because win32k.sys admits no live-patch path, and the population to drive first is the multi-user hosts where an already-authorised unprivileged user - the exploit's only precondition - is the normal state.

CVE-2013-4810.name: HP Multiple Products Remote Code Execution Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: A network-management console exposes its bundled application server's RMI-over-HTTP invoker servlets without authentication. Posting a serialized Java invocation object reaches the MBean server and installs an attacker-chosen application, giving code execution on the host that programs the switch estate.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; the invoker servlets answer before any authentication decision is made, so an attacker needs only routing to the PCM console port.
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; a single HTTP POST with a prebuilt marshalled object. The real constraint is reachability of the console, not exploit difficulty.
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Found by the researcher handle rgod and reported through ZDI (case ZDI-CAN-1760, advisory ZDI-13-229) by manual inspection of an exposed servlet surface.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Denying network reach to /invoker/* — either by removing the servlets from the bundled JBoss instance or by confining the PCM console to a management segment — closes the path with no dependence on HP shipping or the operator finding a patch.
prevention.adequacy: Segmentation bounds who can send the POST; it does not repair the deserialization. Any host inside the permitted management segment — a compromised admin workstation or jump host — still reaches the endpoint with full effect.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alerting on any request to /invoker/EJBInvokerServlet or /invoker/JMXInvokerServlet, and on the PCM JBoss process spawning a child interpreter.
detection.adequacy: The request itself is unambiguous — nothing legitimate calls those paths — so the detection is high-confidence. It fires at the moment of code execution, though, so it bounds dwell time rather than preventing compromise, and it needs the console's own web logs to be shipped off-box before the attacker owns the box.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating a confirmed hit as compromise of the management plane: rebuild the PCM host from a known-good image and rotate every switch and IDM credential the console held.
response.adequacy: Patching in place leaves whatever application the attacker deployed, and the credentials PCM stores for the devices it manages stay valid until rotated. Rebuild is the only action that addresses both.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: A programme tracking HP's own advisory feed records emr_na-c03897409 and closes the item. It never learns that the same unauthenticated invoker surface is the subject of CVE-2007-1036, CVE-2010-0738 and CVE-2012-0874, so remediation is scoped to one PCM release rather than to the primitive, and the identical servlet path bundled in another vendor's appliance is not enumerated at all.

NIST-800-53-CM-7.gap: Least-functionality reviews of a PCM 3.20 or 4.0 host examine Windows services and listening ports and find nothing objectionable, because the offending surface is a URL path inside a bundled JBoss instance rather than a separate service. The control is nominally met while the deserialization endpoint answers unauthenticated on the console port.

NIS2-Art21-vulnerability-handling.gap: The handling process depends on a readable vendor advisory, and this one has decayed: emr_na-c03897409 returns no body on the HPE portal and the archived 2014 capture holds only the page shell. An entity can execute its documented vulnerability-handling procedure faithfully in 2026 and still not obtain the fixed version string for PCM 4.0, which leaves the compensating control as the actual remediation and the process with nothing to record.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: Assessments routinely scope B4 to the network devices delivering the essential function. PCM is the console that configures those devices, so a 9.8 unauthenticated RCE on it is a compromise of everything downstream, and an assessment that treats the management console as supporting infrastructure rather than as in-scope system security records adequate coverage over the highest-leverage host on the estate.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Patch-status tooling reports the PCM application version, which does not move with the bundled JBoss runtime that carries the defect. An estate can show every PCM and IDM install at its expected version and satisfy the maturity evidence while /invoker/EJBInvokerServlet still answers, because nothing in the version string describes the servlet surface.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: A.8.8 exposure evaluation is only as good as its inputs, and here both are weak. The vendor advisory does not resolve, and the EPSS score of 0.79003 (99.563rd percentile, 2026-08-17) reflects exploitation of the generic JBoss invoker surface rather than of HP PCM, so a risk assessment built on it can neither confirm the fixed release nor size the product-specific exposure.

new_control_requirements.name: INCOMPLETE-PATCH-SEQUENCE-SEVERITY-MULTIPLIER
new_control_requirements.description: Vulnerability-management programs must apply a severity multiplier when a CVE is the Nth in an incomplete-patch sequence on the same primitive (third MOTW bypass, second AMSI bypass, etc.). Framework controls treating each CVE as discrete obscure the structural defect; the Nth CVE in a sequence implies that future bypasses on the same primitive are likely.
new_control_requirements.evidence: NVD's own record for HP ProCurve Manager states this is 'probably a duplicate of CVE-2007-1036, CVE-2010-0738, and/or CVE-2012-0874' — the same exposed JBoss EJBInvokerServlet/JMXInvokerServlet primitive NVD ties to three earlier CVE ids, arriving again bundled inside PCM and PCM+ 3.20 and 4.0, IDM 4.0 and Application Lifecycle Management. Treating it as a discrete 2013 HP item is what left it exploitable long enough for CISA to list it on 2022-03-25, nine years after ZDI reported it to HP on 2013-02-22.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: The KEV clock on HP PCM opened 2022-03-25 with a 2022-04-15 due date, and the control's 'documented compensating controls' branch is the operative one for this product: HP's fix document emr_na-c03897409 no longer returns a body, so an operator cannot verify a patched build. Blocking or authentication-gating /invoker/* and confining the PCM console to a management segment is a mitigation that can actually be deployed and evidenced against the clock.

CVE-2013-5223.name: D-Link DSL-2760U Gateway Cross-Site Scripting Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: An ADSL gateway's configuration CGIs render stored field values without encoding them. A user with gateway credentials plants script in one of sixteen parameters; it runs in the next administrator's browser, in the gateway's own origin and inside their authenticated session, which is what lets it reach beyond the vulnerable component.
attack_vector.privileges_required: low — PR:L; the attacker must authenticate to the gateway first. On a device whose administration surface answers to the whole LAN it serves, that bar is met by anyone with credentials to the site's own router.
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; a single stored value. The real constraint is UI:R — someone else has to open the affected configuration page, which the published exploit engineers by disabling gateway features.
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Manual testing of a router web interface; the original 2013 disclosure went to Full Disclosure and Packet Storm, D-Link SAP10002 credits Liad Mizrachi for CVE-2013-5223, and the later exploit code is credited to XLabs Information Security in its own source.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Flashing firmware 1.12 or later, which is the only change that removes the unencoded output; before that, confining the administration interface to a management VLAN so the PR:L precondition cannot be met by ordinary users of the site.
prevention.adequacy: Firmware 1.12 is a real fix, but the flash reboots the gateway and drops the site's uplink. The VLAN measure is weaker than it sounds on a device whose purpose is serving the client network attached to it — for a general-user site there is no segment that removes the path, only isolation of that network from anything else.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Periodically exporting the gateway's running configuration and checking that structural fields — NTP server, SNMP community, SSID, share names — contain no markup.
detection.adequacy: This finds a planted payload reliably because those fields have a narrow legitimate form. It depends on someone collecting configuration from branch gateways on a schedule, and it detects the stored payload rather than the session already hijacked through it.

response.what_would_have_worked: Clearing the injected values, flashing 1.12, and rotating the gateway administrator credential plus anything an affected administrator session could have changed.
response.adequacy: Firmware alone leaves the planted value in the configuration and leaves any credential the script captured valid. Where one administrator password was reused across a fleet of branch gateways, the rotation scope is the fleet rather than the unit.

NIST-800-53-SI-10.gap: An SI-10 attestation covers the input validation the organisation implements in systems it builds. Every one of the sixteen sinks in this CVE — sntpcfg.cgi, samba.cgi, wlcfg.wl and the rest — lives in D-Link firmware the operator cannot read or modify, so the control is fully satisfied on paper by applications that have nothing to do with the exposure, while the gateway keeps rendering stored script.

NIS2-Art21-network-security.gap: Network-security measures are scoped to the networks an entity has enumerated, and an ADSL gateway is reached through the site it terminates rather than through that estate. Where the unit was installed to give a branch or a remote worker connectivity, the population able to satisfy this flaw's authenticated precondition is everyone using that connection, and a segmentation measure written around a datacentre perimeter neither covers the device nor reduces who can reach its configuration pages.

UK-CAF-B2.gap: B2 is nominally met and genuinely irrelevant here. The payload does not defeat authentication — it runs inside a session that authenticated correctly, in the gateway's own origin, with the administrator's authority. An assessor verifying that gateway logins are controlled and accounts are managed will find no defect, because the control operates one layer away from where the compromise happens.

AU-Essential-8-App-Hardening.gap: User-application hardening classifies content by origin, and this content comes from the local gateway's own address — the most trusted origin on a branch network. An estate at the target maturity level for browser hardening blocks the untrusted-internet content the control enumerates and applies none of it to a stored payload served by the router the endpoint is connected through.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.28.gap: Secure-coding principles apply to code the organisation develops or acquires with the ability to influence. For purchased gateway firmware the operator's compliant action collapses to supplier assurance plus applying firmware 1.12 from SAP10002 — an A.8.28 statement can be entirely true of the entity's own development while the CGIs that carry this CVE are never in its scope.

OWASP-Top-10-2021-A03.gap: A03 correctly names this as injection, and that classification generates no operator-side remediation. The sinks are compiled into vendor firmware, so an A03 finding raised against the DSL-2760U resolves to a firmware version to chase rather than a defect to fix, and a programme measuring A03 closure through code review and encoding will show clean results that say nothing about this device.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: For the DSL-2760U the control's 'whichever is later' clause resolves entirely to the KEV side: D-Link shipped firmware 1.12 on 2013-11-26, more than eight years before CISA listed the CVE on 2022-03-25 with a 2022-04-15 due date. The fix was sitting available for the whole interval, so what this device demonstrates is that a KEV listing has to drive an inventory sweep of unmanaged branch gateways, since nothing else was going to notice a rev E1 unit still below 1.12.

new_control_requirements.name: FIREWALL-EGRESS-TELEMETRY-SEPARATE-TRUST-ZONE
new_control_requirements.description: Firewall and other perimeter-trust-boundary devices must forward syslog, threat logs, and authentication logs to a SIEM hosted in a separate trust zone (different management plane, different credentials, different authentication path). Telemetry stored on the compromised device is destroyed by the attacker; telemetry on a separate-trust-zone collector survives.
new_control_requirements.evidence: The DSL-2760U is the perimeter device for the site it serves, and every trace of this attack — the authentication that satisfied PR:L, the write that stored the payload into todmngr.tod or urlfilter.cmd, and the administrator's later load of that page — exists only on the gateway itself. Because the payload runs with administrator authority in the gateway's own origin, that same local record is within reach of the attacker, so off-box collection is what makes the S:C scope change observable at all.

CVE-2014-0130.name: Ruby on Rails Directory Traversal Vulnerability (CVE-2014-0130)

attack_vector.description: A web framework feature that renders a template when no matching action exists takes the template name from the URL without sanitising it. Where the application declares a globbed route bound to :action, the glob carries traversal sequences into that lookup and the framework returns arbitrary readable files instead of a view.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; the render happens before any controller action runs, so authentication filters attached to actions are never reached.
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; one GET request. The binding constraint is not attacker skill but application shape: the route must combine globbing with :action, a pattern the Rails advisory describes as uncommon.
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Disclosed through the Rails security process and announced on oss-security on 2014-05-06, whose Credits section thanks Ville Lautanala of Flowdock for reporting the vulnerability and working on the fix; no automated discovery is claimed.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Upgrading actionpack to 3.2.18, 4.0.5 or 4.1.1 and restarting the application processes; or, without an upgrade, applying the vendor's routing workaround so no route binds a glob to :action.
prevention.adequacy: Both are complete fixes for first-party applications, and the routing workaround is unusually good — it needs no dependency change and takes effect on the next deploy. Neither reaches an embedded copy: Red Hat Subscription Asset Manager at 1.3.0 or below is remediated by RHSA-2014:1863 on the vendor's schedule.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alerting on encoded traversal sequences in request paths, and on responses to application routes whose bodies look like configuration or system files rather than rendered views.
detection.adequacy: Traversal patterns in a URL are cheap to match and the published payload's encoded backslash form is distinctive. It is a signature check, so an equivalent encoding the rule does not enumerate passes it — the routes.rb audit is the more reliable of the two because it establishes exposure without depending on seeing the attack.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating any confirmed read as disclosure of every secret the application process could read — rotating database credentials and the Rails secret token, since a leaked secret token allows session cookie forgery.
response.adequacy: Upgrading the gem stops further reads and revalues nothing already taken. Where the same database credential or secret token was deployed to more than one application, the rotation scope is every application sharing it.

NIST-800-218-SSDF-PW.7.1.gap: Code review is performed and finds nothing, correctly: the traversal is in actionpack's implicit-render implementation, not in the reviewed application, and the application's contribution is a single routes.rb line that reads as a routing choice. A PW.7.1 attestation covering every merged change is truthful while the exposure is created by a line no reviewer had reason to challenge.

NIST-800-53-AC-3.gap: The application's authorisation is enforced in controller actions and their filters, and this request never reaches one — implicit render answers it directly. An AC-3 control assessment that traces every action to an authorisation decision passes, and the same application hands database.yml to an unauthenticated caller, because the enforcement point sits downstream of where the file read happens.

NIS2-Art21-supply-chain.gap: Supplier assurance evidence is assembled per supplier and per first-party dependency manifest, and this flaw occupies both categories at once: a transitive gem inside applications the entity builds, and a purchased product — Red Hat Subscription Asset Manager at 1.3.0 or below — whose remediation is RHSA-2014:1863 rather than any bundle update the entity controls. An organisation can complete its own upgrade to 4.1.1, evidence the supply-chain measure in full, and keep an affected appliance running.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: Secure configuration is assessed against hardening baselines for operating systems and services, none of which model application routing. The exact configuration that decides exploitability — a glob bound to :action in routes.rb — is invisible to that assessment, so B4 can be evidenced as adequate for a Rails host whose single deciding setting was never examined.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Maturity evidence rests on version currency, and version currency neither proves nor disproves exposure here. An application on actionpack 4.1.0 with no globbed route is not exploitable; one on the same version with such a route is fully exploitable; and neither state is distinguishable from the patch report, which is also blind to the embedded copy inside Subscription Asset Manager.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.9.gap: Configuration management covers infrastructure and platform settings held against a baseline. Rails routing lives in source control and is governed by change management rather than configuration management, so the one item worth baselining for this CVE — the absence of a glob bound to :action — falls into the seam between the two, and A.8.9 evidence is complete without ever recording it.

new_control_requirements.name: TIER-3-DEPENDENCY-INVENTORY
new_control_requirements.description: Supply chain inventory must extend to tier-3 dependencies (dependencies of dependencies of direct dependencies). SBOM coverage for libsystemd-class transitive dependencies cannot be omitted under SR-3.
new_control_requirements.evidence: actionpack is exactly this shape for a Rails estate: applications depend on rails, rails depends on actionpack, and the traversal is in actionpack's abstract_controller/base.rb. NVD then extends the same defect into a purchased product, Red Hat Subscription Asset Manager up to 1.3.0, which no application-level bundle inventory enumerates. Without inventory reaching that depth, an operator cannot answer which systems carry actionpack below 3.2.18, 4.0.5 or 4.1.1 — the question the 2022-03-25 KEV listing asks.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
