new_control_requirements.evidence: SEC Consult's coordination in April 2015 and TP-Link's dated builds - 150302 for the Archer C9 (1.0) through 150317 for the Archer C5 (1.2) - predate the KEV listing by close to seven years, so what this SLA demands is not a wait on the vendor but a determination per unit: model, hardware revision, running date code, fixed date code. Where that determination returns no build for the revision, only the documented-compensating-control branch remains, and it has to record plainly that every client the router serves still reaches the vulnerable interface.

new_control_requirements.name: FIREWALL-EGRESS-TELEMETRY-SEPARATE-TRUST-ZONE
new_control_requirements.description: Firewall and other perimeter-trust-boundary devices must forward syslog, threat logs, and authentication logs to a SIEM hosted in a separate trust zone (different management plane, different credentials, different authentication path). Telemetry stored on the compromised device is destroyed by the attacker; telemetry on a separate-trust-zone collector survives.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Where a client reaches its own gateway directly, the only witness to a /login/ traversal against one of these routers is the router itself, and its local log does not survive the reboot that the remediating firmware flash requires - so the act of fixing the device destroys the evidence of whether it was read. Forwarding what logging these units do offer to a collector outside the device is the only way an operator can later scope which units were probed and therefore which stored credentials need rotating.

CVE-2015-4068.name: Arcserve Unified Data Protection (UDP) Directory Traversal Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: An unauthenticated HTTP request to the UDP Management Service names a file path, and reportFileServlet or exportServlet resolves it without normalisation, returning or deleting a file anywhere the SYSTEM-level service can reach on the backup control-plane host.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; the servlets answer before any session or token is established, which is also why UI:N holds: no operator has to click anything
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; one HTTP request, no race, no heap groom, no information leak needed first. The only precondition is routing to the Management Service port
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Credit in ZDI-15-241 and ZDI-15-242 goes to rgod through the Zero Day Initiative, reported 2015-04-03 and published 2015-05-26; neither advisory describes automated discovery.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Installing Arcserve UDP 5.0 Update 4 and restarting the Management Service, with the console's HTTP port restricted to an administrative segment in the interim.
prevention.adequacy: The update closes the servlets, but BOD 22-01 only binds federal civilian agencies and only from 2022 — seven years after the vendor fix. The port restriction is a real interim control here because no credential is involved, but it fails wherever the console must stay reachable to the administrators who use it.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Logging and alerting on requests to reportFileServlet and exportServlet carrying traversal sequences, plus file-access monitoring on the console host for reads outside the Arcserve install tree.
detection.adequacy: Both are only available where the Management Service's HTTP access log is shipped off-host and where the backup server carries host-level file monitoring — neither is standard on a backup appliance. Detection also arrives after the read has already returned the file.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating an exposed console as a credential-exposure event: rotating the service and agent credentials the backup tier holds, and comparing the console host against a known-good build rather than closing the ticket on the update.
response.adequacy: Rotation scope is only knowable if the operator knows which files the backup tier stores credentials in. The update does not remove anything a prior read already returned, and file deletions performed as SYSTEM leave no application-level record to reconstruct from.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: An organisation running any structured patch programme is compliant with SI-2, and this CVE still sat unremediated widely enough for CISA to enrol it on 2022-03-25 against a vendor fix published in the UDP 5.0 Update 4 release notes in 2015. SI-2 asks whether flaws are identified and corrected on a defined schedule; it does not require the backup console to sit inside that schedule, and where the console is given a separate window because updating it interrupts protection, nothing in SI-2 reaches into that window.

NIST-800-53-SC-7.gap: SC-7 governs external and key internal boundaries, and the UDP Management Service answers from inside them, so the control can be fully implemented while the servlets answer PR:N requests from anywhere inside the estate. The CVSS vector's AV:N is a statement about that reachability. SC-7 does not compel a separate segment for the backup control plane, which is the one interim measure that actually removes the path before 5.0 Update 4 is installed.

NIS2-Art21-business-continuity.gap: Article 21(2)(c) obliges business continuity, backup management and disaster recovery measures, all of which an entity can evidence while the console that operates them is the vulnerable component. Because the deletion primitive runs as SYSTEM on the backup control-plane host, the continuity capability and the attack surface are the same machine, and a plan that treats the backup tier as the fallback has no fallback for the backup tier itself.

UK-CAF-B5.gap: B5's resilience outcome can be argued entirely from redundancy of the protected systems and the existence of recovery points, without reaching the availability of the management service. The A:H component of the 9.1 score comes from unauthenticated file deletion on that management host, so the asset a B5 assessment relies on for recovery is the asset degraded here, and nothing in B5 requires the recovery tier to be isolated from the network it serves.

AU-Essential-8-Backup.gap: The regular-backups mitigation strategy governs what is backed up, how long it is kept and whether restoration is tested. None of that examines the version or the network exposure of the backup product's management tier, so a site with tested restores can still be running a pre-Update-4 UDP 5.0 console. Restoration testing would not reveal it either, since the flaw touches the console host rather than the backup data.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.13.gap: Annex A 8.13 (information backup) directs attention to backup copies, their frequency and their recoverability. An organisation can implement it completely while reportFileServlet and exportServlet answer unauthenticated traversal requests, because the control never asks which build the management service runs or whether its HTTP tier authenticates. The 2022-03-25 KEV enrolment carried operational information that an A.8.13 control set does not produce.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Arcserve published the UDP 5.0 Update 4 fix in 2015 and CISA still enrolled CVE-2015-4068 on 2022-03-25 with a 2022-04-15 due date, so the gap being closed is deployment latency on the backup control plane rather than fix availability. EPSS on 2026-08-17 is 0.63643 (99.146th percentile) for a PR:N, UI:N, AC:L path into a SYSTEM-context servlet, which is why the clock has to start at the listing rather than at the next backup-infrastructure maintenance window.

new_control_requirements.name: MITIGATION-ACTIVE-PATCH-PENDING-VERDICT-CLASS
new_control_requirements.description: Compliance verdicts must distinguish three states: (a) binary patch deployed (vulnerability eliminated), (b) vendor-mitigation rule active, no binary patch (residual risk: any defect in the mitigation rule reopens the vulnerability), (c) no mitigation, no patch (full exposure). Audit reports must surface (b) as a distinct compensating-control state with an associated time-bound action item, not as a 'patched per SLA' outcome.
new_control_requirements.evidence: An Arcserve UDP console whose Management Service port has been restricted to an administrative segment but which still runs a pre-Update-4 5.0 build is squarely in state (b): reportFileServlet and exportServlet are unchanged and answer any caller that reaches them, so the whole control is an ACL that one firewall change or one added management route reverses. Recording that as remediated against the 2022-04-15 KEV due date hides the fact that the SYSTEM-context read and delete primitive is still present on the backup control-plane host.

CVE-2016-0040.name: Microsoft Windows Kernel Privilege Escalation Vulnerability (CVE-2016-0040)

attack_vector.description: An already-logged-on user runs a crafted program that reaches an uninitialised stack variable in the kernel's WMI handling, then grooms GDI bitmaps so the resulting corrupted pointer yields arbitrary kernel read and write, and copies the SYSTEM token onto its own process.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N as NVD scores it, but read that alongside AV:L and UI:R: MS16-014 requires the attacker to log on first and run a specially crafted application, so an ordinary account is the real precondition
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; there is no race to win and no information leak needed first. The constraint is offset accuracy, which is why the shipped Metasploit targets are Windows 7 SP0/SP1 x64 rather than every affected SKU
attack_vector.ai_factor: None established. No finder is credited in MS16-014, and the named individuals in the public record — smmrootkit, de7ec7ed and the Rootkitsmm-zz repository owner — are exploit authors whose work carries no description of automated discovery.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Installing update 3126593 and rebooting each affected host, then measuring completion by the running build rather than by the update's approval state.
prevention.adequacy: The update is definitive but arrives only on reboot, and MS16-014 records no mitigating factors and no workarounds, so there is no interim measure to hold the line. BOD 22-01 also binds only federal civilian agencies, and it fired in 2022 against a fix from 2016.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alerting on a non-elevated process acquiring a SYSTEM token outside a service start.
detection.adequacy: The signal requires process-level telemetry already collected and shipped off-host before the attempt; where one of these releases is still running because the host cannot be changed, adding that telemetry is the same change the host is not taking.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating a host where the escalation succeeded as SYSTEM-compromised: rebuilding rather than patching, and rotating every credential that was cached or authenticated on it during the exposure window.
response.adequacy: Scoping the rotation depends on knowing which accounts touched the host, which is exactly the record a SYSTEM-level attacker can alter. Installing 3126593 afterwards removes the flaw and removes nothing the attacker established with the token they already took.

NIST-800-53-AC-6.gap: AC-6 is the control an assessment reaches for when compensating an elevation-of-privilege finding, and it is inert against this one. The attacker holds a legitimate non-administrative account — MS16-014 says the attacker would first have to log on to the system — so no privilege assignment is abused and the escalation happens inside the kernel where AC-6 has no reach. A least-privilege attestation passes cleanly on a host that never received 3126593.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: The fix has existed since 2016-02-09 and the KEV enrolment came on 2022-03-28, so SI-2 compliance and this exposure coexisted for six years. The control's severity-driven scheduling also works against the operator here: MS16-014 is rated Important and the CVSS is 7.8 with AV:L, which routes a local escalation into a slower tier than the 2018 publication of Exploit-DB 44586 justified.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: Article 21(2)(e) requires vulnerability handling within systems maintenance, and an entity can satisfy it while leaving this unremediated, because the obligation does not distinguish an update that has been installed from one the host has rebooted onto. For a kernel fix that distinction is the entire remediation, and the affected releases — Vista SP2, Server 2008 SP2, Windows 7 SP1, Server 2008 R2 SP1 — are retained for workloads that cannot be changed, and the reboot the fix depends on is exactly that kind of change.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: B4 System Security asks that systems be configured and maintained to resist attack, but on these four releases the maintained state it presumes no longer exists, since none of them receives current servicing. An operator can only evidence that the final available updates were applied, and B4 supplies no trigger to convert that into a dated removal plan. A local escalation also produces no perimeter evidence, so it tends not to surface in B4 assessment material at all.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: The patch-operating-systems mitigation strategy expects both timely vendor updates and the use of operating systems that are currently supported. Vista SP2, Server 2008 SP2, Windows 7 SP1 and Server 2008 R2 SP1 fail the second expectation outright, so a host running them cannot be brought into coverage by installing 3126593 — the update produces a compliant-looking patch record on a platform the strategy would have retired.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: A.8.8 requires that technical vulnerability information be obtained and acted on, and the information here has been public since the 2016 bulletin, so the control was met and the exposure persisted. What A.8.8 does not require is re-ranking an already-triaged local escalation when working exploit code later appears — Exploit-DB 44586 landed in 2018 and the KEV listing in 2022, and neither event has a hook in the control text.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Microsoft shipped update 3126593 for this Windows kernel flaw on 2016-02-09 and CISA listed CVE-2016-0040 on 2022-03-28 with a 2022-04-18 due date, so the exposure being closed is deployment latency on Vista SP2, Server 2008 SP2, Windows 7 SP1 and Server 2008 R2 SP1 hosts. The documented-compensating-control branch of this control cannot be used here, because MS16-014 records no mitigating factors and no workarounds for this CVE — the only compliant outcome is the update plus the reboot, which makes the verification step the reboot rather than the install.

CVE-2016-0151.name: Microsoft Windows CSRSS Security Feature Bypass Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: A logged-on user hooks the client-side CSRSS stub in its own process, impersonates an anonymous token across a privileged subsystem call, and has CSRSS create a process in Session 0 carrying administrator-level rights — the subsystem mismanages which token it is acting under rather than corrupting memory.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N as scored, but AV:L and UI:R carry the real precondition: MS16-048 requires the attacker to log on to the system and then run a specially crafted application
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; deterministic API sequencing with no race, no groom and no information leak. The published code is ordinary C++ against documented Windows interfaces
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. The proof of concept at Exploit-DB 39740 is published under the Google Security Research name and is hand-written code against specific Windows API behaviour; no automated or AI-assisted discovery is described anywhere in it or in MS16-048.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Installing update 3146723, or cumulative update 3147461 or 3147458 on the Windows 10 branches, and rebooting each host so the fixed csrss image is the running one.
prevention.framework_requiring_it: CISA BOD 22-01 (KEV remediation, added 2022-03-28, ransomware: Known, due 2022-04-18)
prevention.adequacy: The update is the only real prevention, since MS16-048 lists no mitigating factors and no workarounds, and it only takes effect at reboot because CSRSS cannot be restarted in place. BOD 22-01 binds federal civilian agencies only, and it fired in 2022 against a bulletin published in April 2016.

detection.what_would_have_worked: A correlation rule pairing process creation in Session 0 with a parent in an interactive session, tied to token-impersonation activity from the same process.
detection.adequacy: The rule has to be authored deliberately — each half is common on its own, and Session 0 process creation is normal service behaviour. It also depends on process and token telemetry already being collected and shipped off-host, and it alerts after the administrator-level process exists rather than preventing it.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating a host where the escalation succeeded as administrator-compromised — rebuilding from a known-good image, rotating credentials that authenticated on it during the exposure window, and checking backup integrity before relying on it.
response.adequacy: The backup check is the step CISA's ransomware flag on this entry makes load-bearing: administrator rights on the host reach whatever backup targets that host can write to. Installing 3146723 afterwards closes the flaw and removes nothing the attacker established.

NIST-800-53-AC-3.gap: Access enforcement is the property being defeated, so it cannot also be the compensating control. Windows makes its access decision from the token CSRSS holds, and the defect is in which token that is, so every ACL, group membership and privilege assignment an AC-3 assessment reviews can be correct while a logged-on user reaches administrator-level execution. The control has no visibility into the subsystem's own token bookkeeping.

NIST-800-53-SI-4.gap: SI-4 requires monitoring to be deployed and reviewed, and this exploit gives it almost nothing distinctive: no crash, no driver load, no file-integrity change, just documented API calls inside the attacker's own process plus a Session 0 child. The distinguishing signal is a correlation between an interactive-session parent and a Session 0 child, which SI-4 does not require anyone to author, so a fully compliant monitoring programme can carry no rule that fires.

NIS2-Art21-incident-handling.gap: Article 21(2)(b) requires incident handling, and CISA's ransomware-campaign flag on this entry is what makes it the relevant obligation — but incident handling starts at detection, and the escalation itself produces little to detect. In practice the clock starts at whatever the operator does after obtaining administrator rights, and nothing in the article requires a host where this succeeded to be rebuilt rather than patched, which is the decision that actually bounds the damage.

UK-CAF-C1.gap: C1 Security Monitoring is assessed on coverage of important systems and on alerts being acted upon, and both can be true while no rule exists for this sequence. The published code hooks CsrClientCallServer in its own address space and calls documented interfaces; only the Session 0 process creation from an interactive parent stands out, and that is a correlation an analyst has to build on purpose. C1 does not name it.

AU-Essential-8-Backup.gap: Regular backups is the Essential Eight strategy that matters given the ransomware-campaign flag, and it governs recovery rather than the escalation. Its specific weakness against an administrator-level escalation is reach: backups writable by an account the attacker now controls are backups they can destroy, and restricting access to backup storage is a distinct requirement from performing and testing them. Tested restores prove the backups function; they say nothing about whether 3146723 is present on the hosts being restored.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: A.8.8 was met from 2016-04-12 onward and the exposure still reached a 2022 KEV listing. The inputs available at the time — MS16-048 recording Publicly disclosed: No and Exploited: No, and an Important rather than Critical rating — legitimately place this low in a compliant queue. The control offers no trigger to re-rank when working exploit code appeared on 2016-04-27, fifteen days after the bulletin, which is the event that changed the real risk.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Microsoft published MS16-048 and update 3146723 on 2016-04-12 and CISA enrolled CVE-2016-0151 on 2022-03-28 with a 2022-04-18 due date and a known-ransomware-campaign flag, so what this control governs is the interval between listing and a rebooted host on Windows 8.1, Server 2012, Server 2012 R2, RT 8.1 and the Windows 10 1507/1511 branches. The compensating-controls branch is unavailable for this CVE — MS16-048 records no mitigating factors and no workarounds — so verification has to be the reboot onto the fixed csrss image, not the install record.

CVE-2016-0189.name: Microsoft Internet Explorer Memory Corruption Vulnerability (CVE-2016-0189)

attack_vector.description: Attacker-controlled web content drives the VBScript engine into an out-of-bounds write after an array resize, and the public chain turns that into a leaked address and an overwritten function pointer, executing code as the logged-on user inside the browser process.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; the attacker holds no account on the target and needs only to have their content rendered
attack_vector.complexity: high — AC:H; the chain needs a heap groom, an out-of-bounds read to leak an address and a pointer overwrite at a fixed offset, and Exploit-DB 40118 states plainly that it is not 100% reliable and may need a refresh or a browser restart
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. The reverse engineering and exploitation credited in the Metasploit module belongs to the Theori team, with Brian Pak named on Exploit-DB 40118; the artefacts describe manual analysis of the engine and no automated discovery.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Deploying update 3154070, or 3156387/3156421 on the Windows 10 branches, out of cycle on the strength of Microsoft's own Exploited: Yes flag, and applying MS16-053 wherever the older engine hosts are present.
prevention.framework_requiring_it: CISA BOD 22-01 (KEV remediation, added 2022-03-28, ransomware: Known, due 2022-04-18)
prevention.adequacy: Adequate once landed, but the landing has two gates — the host reboot and the browser process actually being restarted — and BOD 22-01's clock started in 2022, close to six years after Microsoft had already recorded in-the-wild use in the May 2016 bulletin.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alerting on iexplore.exe creating a child process or opening an outbound connection outside the page's own content delivery, and on repeated tab crashes against a single site.
detection.adequacy: The child-process signal fires only after code is already running as the user, and the crash signal is a by-product of unreliable exploitation rather than a guaranteed artefact. Both depend on endpoint process telemetry being collected from user workstations, and neither identifies which of the several scripting-engine CVEs in MS16-051 was used.

response.what_would_have_worked: Applying the MS16-051 workaround — takeown plus cacls denying Everyone on vbscript.dll and jscript.dll — as an immediate containment step, then treating any workstation that rendered the content as user-context compromised and rotating what that user could reach.
response.adequacy: The workaround is real and immediate but carries Microsoft's stated impact that sites using VBScript or JScript may not work properly, so it is a decision to take before it is needed rather than during an incident. Because the code runs as the logged-on user, the rotation scope is that user's credentials and tokens, and it is larger wherever the browsing account also held administrative rights.

NIST-800-53-CM-7.gap: CM-7 is satisfied by a baseline that removes unnecessary services and functions, and no standard baseline goes to the granularity Microsoft's own workaround uses — file ACLs denying Everyone on vbscript.dll and jscript.dll. The engines stay enabled because legacy intranet applications need them, which is the same reason Internet Explorer was retained at all, so the control is honestly met while the exact component this CVE lives in remains reachable from any rendered page.

NIST-800-53-SI-3.gap: Malicious code protection acts on payloads, and the entire corruption chain — array resize, UnEscape() groom, address leak, function-pointer overwrite at offset 0x174 — completes inside the browser process before any payload exists on disk. SI-3 also does not reach EMET, which MS16-051 names as able to help mitigate this class, so the mitigation the vendor actually recommends is outside the control an organisation would point to.

NIS2-Art21-vulnerability-handling.gap: The obligation covers vulnerability handling in systems maintenance, and the decisive input was on the page from the start: MS16-051 marked CVE-2016-0189 Exploited: Yes on 2016-05-10 while marking it undisclosed. Article 21(2)(e) sets no distinct clock for a vendor-confirmed in-the-wild browser flaw against the rest of a monthly bulletin, so a compliant entity can fold it into an ordinary cycle — and CISA's listing, with a ransomware-campaign flag, did not arrive until 2022-03-28.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: B4 expects systems to be configured and maintained to resist attack, assessed across the estate, and this flaw is serviced through two bulletins at once — MS16-051 for Internet Explorer 9 and later and MS16-053 for Internet Explorer 7 and earlier and the other hosts of the JScript 5.8 and VBScript 5.7/5.8 engines. An estate can be fully current on one and exposed through the other, and B4 offers nothing for the non-browser path MS16-051 names, where a safe-for-initialization ActiveX control in an Office document reaches the same engines.

AU-Essential-8-App-Hardening.gap: User application hardening targets browsers processing internet content, and the browser settings available to evidence it are the ones policy exposes — Flash, Java, advertisements — alongside Office macro settings. Hardening the component at issue here means denying access to vbscript.dll and jscript.dll, which breaks the legacy applications Internet Explorer was kept for, so the strategy can be credibly claimed while the vulnerable engine stays fully enabled on every workstation.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.7.gap: A.8.7 is implemented as endpoint anti-malware plus awareness, and both address the wrong stage. Nothing recognisable as malware exists until after the in-process corruption succeeds, and awareness has no purchase on the delivery MS16-051 contemplates — compromised sites and advertising, where there is no suspicious link for the user to decline. The interim measures that would have helped, the file-ACL workaround and EMET, are not anti-malware controls and sit outside A.8.7 entirely.

new_control_requirements.name: BROWSER-MANAGED-UPDATE-NO-DEFERRAL
new_control_requirements.description: Enterprise update rings must not defer security-channel browser updates beyond 24h.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Microsoft recorded this Internet Explorer scripting-engine flaw as Exploited: Yes in the MS16-051 table on 2016-05-10, before it was publicly disclosed, so the deferral window under discussion is one in which the vendor has already confirmed in-the-wild use. Update 3154070 and the Windows 10 cumulative packages 3156387 and 3156421 were available that day; CISA's listing with a known-ransomware-campaign flag did not follow until 2022-03-28. For this entry the 24-hour clock has to be measured to a rebooted host with the browser process restarted, since a running browser keeps the old engine mapped after the update lands.

new_control_requirements.name: BUG-FAMILY-MITIGATION-PERSISTENCE
new_control_requirements.description: When a CVE patch lands, retain the pre-patch compensating controls (module blacklists, sysctl restrictions) until the patched code has soaked for a stated review period. Patches for one bug in a primitive class can introduce sibling bugs in the same class; the original compensating control may still apply to the sibling.
new_control_requirements.evidence: MS16-051 fixes CVE-2016-0189 alongside CVE-2016-0187, described in NVD as a different vulnerability in the same JScript and VBScript engines, so the sibling case this control anticipates is present inside the single bulletin. The pre-patch compensating control here is Microsoft's own: takeown on vbscript.dll and jscript.dll followed by cacls denying Everyone, in system32 or syswow64. Retaining that ACL after 3154070 lands keeps the engine unreachable while the fix soaks, at the stated cost that sites using VBScript or JScript may not work properly — a cost an organisation should decide once rather than re-open at each engine CVE.

CVE-2016-0752.name: Ruby on Rails Directory Traversal Vulnerability (CVE-2016-0752)

attack_vector.description: An unauthenticated request supplies a traversal sequence to a route that passes user input into Action View's render, and Rails loads and returns a file outside the application's view directory at the application process's privilege; the public module extends that into code execution by rendering an uploaded file containing ERB.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; no account or session is involved, and UI:N because no operator has to act
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L for the request itself. The precondition sits in the application rather than the framework: a controller must pass request data into render, which is why a gem-version scan cannot answer whether a given deployment is reachable
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. The Rails announcement credits John Poulin as reporter and the exploitation work on Exploit-DB 40561 credits mr_me; both are manual analysis of how render resolves its argument.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Upgrading to 3.2.22.1, 4.1.14.1, 4.2.5.1 or 5.0.0.beta1.1 and restarting the application servers, or applying the announcement's validation workaround so the parameter is checked before it reaches render.
prevention.adequacy: The upgrade is definitive but only once the worker processes cycle, and BOD 22-01 binds federal civilian agencies from 2022 against a fix published in January 2016. The workaround is the stronger option for applications with a pinned framework version, since it removes the sink regardless of the Rails release.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alerting on traversal sequences and on proc/self/fd in request paths, and on the application process reading files outside its own tree.
detection.adequacy: Request-path matching sees the base read attempt but is blind to input that reaches render indirectly rather than through the path. File-access monitoring of the application process is the more reliable half, and it is an additional agent on the application server rather than a configuration change. Both alert after a file has already been returned.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating a successful read as credential exposure: rotating whatever the application's configuration and secret files held, including session-signing material, and reviewing upload endpoints for files planted before remediation.
response.adequacy: Rotating session-signing material invalidates live sessions, which is why it is deferred, and the upgrade removes the read path without removing anything already read. Where the same secrets were reused across environments, the rotation scope is every environment that shared them.

NIST-800-53-SI-10.gap: SI-10 names input validation, and an organisation implementing it validates the inputs it has classified as security-relevant — query identifiers, stored values, uploaded content. The argument to render was classified as routing, not as a filesystem path, so a compliant SI-10 programme had no rule covering it. The Rails announcement's own workaround is an SI-10 action that nobody had recognised as one until the sink was published on 2016-01-25.

NIST-800-218-SSDF-PW.7.1.gap: The practice requires an organisation to decide when code review and automated analysis apply and to define what they check for, and both decisions can be fully documented while missing this. Rails-aware analysers treated render as framework plumbing rather than a file-loading sink before this disclosure, and a reviewer reading a one-line controller sees idiomatic code. Compliance with PW.7 says the process exists; it does not require the rule set to include framework-specific sinks.

NIS2-Art21-supply-chain.gap: Article 21(2)(d) governs supply chain security and relationships with direct suppliers, and there is no supplier here to hold to account — the framework arrives through a package manager and the advisory arrived as a public mailing-list post on 2016-01-25. Where Rails came from a distribution rebuild, listed in NVD as Debian 8.0, openSUSE 13.2 and Leap 42.1, SUSE Linux Enterprise Module for Containers 12 and Red Hat Software Collections 1.0, the entity's remediation is gated on the packager's release rather than its own supplier process.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: B4's maintenance evidence for a web application is the dependency version, and that measurement is wrong in both directions here: applications on a vulnerable Rails release with no controller feeding render from params were never reachable, while the one that does is reachable regardless of how well the rest of the estate is patched. B4 also provides no prompt to confirm the application server processes restarted after the upgrade, which is the step that makes the new Action View the one serving traffic.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: The patch-applications strategy is built around inventorying and updating installed software, and a framework bundled into a deployed application does not appear in that inventory. Remediation runs through the release pipeline — dependency change, rebuild, test, redeploy — and for a 4.0.x application it is a series upgrade to 4.1.14.1 or later because the 4.0 line received no fix. An assessment scoped to installed packages can pass while every deployed application still carries a pre-fix Action View.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.28.gap: A.8.28 (secure coding) is the right home for this defect and its standards did not contain it. Coding standards in January 2016 enumerated SQL parameterisation, output encoding and authentication handling; `render params[:id]` violated none of them, which is why the Rails announcement had to publish the pattern itself. A fully implemented secure-coding programme would have reviewed the controller and passed it.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Rails published fixed releases 3.2.22.1, 4.1.14.1, 4.2.5.1 and 5.0.0.beta1.1 on 2016-01-25 and CISA enrolled CVE-2016-0752 on 2022-03-25 with a 2022-04-15 due date, so what this control governs is the six-year deployment gap on a flaw whose EPSS reached 0.95537 (99.864th percentile) by 2026-08-17. The documented-compensating-control branch is genuinely available for this CVE — the announcement's validation workaround removes the sink without a framework bump — which makes it the compliant option for an application whose Rails version is pinned. Verification has to be an application-server process restart, since no host reboot is involved and a lockfile change alone leaves the old Action View resident.

CVE-2016-10174.name: NETGEAR WNR2000v5 Router Buffer Overflow Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: A request to the router's language-check handler carries an oversized hidden_lang_avi value, which region_search() copies into a fixed stack buffer with strcpy, overwriting saved registers and the return address and giving the caller execution on the router.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N on the /apply_noauth.cgi path, which needs a timestamp value the advisory describes as brute-forceable or absent on first access rather than a credential; the /apply.cgi path expects an authenticated session
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; a single request with a long parameter, no race and no groom. The practical constraint is reachability, since the advisory records that without remote administration enabled the attack is only possible from the LAN
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Pedro Ribeiro of Agile Information Security performed hardware testing on a WNR2000v5 and static analysis for the v3 and v4 models; no automated discovery is described.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Turning remote management off on every affected unit and flashing the current production firmware from the NETGEAR Download Center for that model and hardware revision.
prevention.adequacy: Disabling remote management removes the internet-facing path NETGEAR itself warns about, but the advisory is explicit that LAN-side exploitation remains, so it is a bound rather than a fix. The firmware is the fix and it requires per-unit action with no fleet mechanism; BOD 22-01 binds federal civilian agencies only.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alerting on requests to apply_noauth.cgi and apply.cgi carrying an oversized hidden_lang_avi value, and on the router's web server crash-looping or the device rebooting unexpectedly.
detection.adequacy: Both require telemetry from the device or from a monitoring point in front of it, and a consumer router has no agent, so log export has to have been configured on the unit beforehand. Where remote management is enabled the request arrives on the WAN side, where there is nothing between the internet and the router to observe it.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating an exposed unit as compromised: rebuilding its configuration from a known-good baseline rather than carrying it through the flash, rotating the administrative credential, and rotating anything that transited the device while it was reachable.
response.adequacy: This is the step the vendor guidance does not cover — PSV-2016-0255 stops at the firmware update — and it is the only one that removes attacker-made changes, since flashing preserves the existing configuration. It depends on a known-good baseline existing for the unit, which is a record that has to have been captured before the exposure, not after it.

NIST-800-53-SC-7.gap: SC-7 positions the boundary device as the enforcement point, and this CVE makes it the target: the request lands on the router's own web server and yields execution there, so there is no further boundary to appeal to. The researcher counted over 10,000 units with remote management enabled on Shodan at disclosure, which is the WAN-side population. SC-7 also does not address the residual LAN path, where every client the router serves reaches the vulnerable handler by design.

NIST-800-53-CM-7.gap: Least functionality would have removed the internet-facing exposure outright, because remote administration is optional — the advisory states it is not enabled by default on the WNR2000v5's latest firmware and that without it the attack is LAN-only. The control is applied to servers and workstations rather than to branch and home-office network equipment, and a router absent from the configuration baseline is reached by none of it. On the LAN side CM-7 offers nothing further, since lang_check.html is not a function an operator can disable.

NIS2-Art21-network-security.gap: Article 21(2)(e) obliges security in acquisition, development and maintenance, and a consumer-class router bought for a branch or a remote worker and never entered into the register is outside that process, so its maintenance clock never starts. NVD lists 28 affected model families, and PSV-2016-0255 points at the Download Center without naming versions, so satisfying the obligation means a per-model, per-revision lookup that no fleet mechanism performs.

UK-CAF-B5.gap: B5 treats network equipment as the substrate resilience is built on rather than as an asset an attacker can occupy, and code execution on the router inverts that. Resilience claims that assume traffic integrity across the device stop holding once the device is attacker-controlled. B5 also gives no trigger for the step the vendor guidance omits: flashing new firmware carries the existing configuration and administrative credential forward, so an exposed unit is not restored to a known state by the update.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: The Essential Eight patching strategies assume enumerable software updated through a management channel, and router firmware has neither — the update is a per-model, per-hardware-revision download applied by flashing, with no console to report from, and PSV-2016-0255 does not even name the target version. An organisation can satisfy the strategies across its servers and workstations while every branch router in the estate runs pre-fix firmware, with nothing in the assessment that would surface it.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.22.gap: Segregation of networks is the control that would bound the residual path, and its usual scope does not extend there. With remote management disabled the attack moves to the LAN, and the router's purpose is to serve that LAN, so every client on it reaches the web interface by design — segregation can isolate that network from things that matter but cannot remove the path to the router itself. A.8.22 implemented at the corporate and datacentre level says nothing about the branch segment these units sit in.

new_control_requirements.name: PERIMETER-COMPROMISE-REBUILD-NOT-PATCH
new_control_requirements.description: Pre-rehearsed IR runbook for any perimeter device that suffers a pre-auth RCE CVE in active exploitation MUST default to config-exfil + rebuild + credential rotation, not patch-in-place. Patch-in-place leaves attacker-installed implants intact.
new_control_requirements.evidence: This is a pre-authentication stack overflow yielding execution on the NETGEAR router itself through /apply_noauth.cgi, on a device that is the perimeter for whatever sits behind it, and CISA listed it on 2022-03-25 with a 2022-04-15 due date. NETGEAR's PSV-2016-0255 guidance stops at flashing production firmware, and flashing carries the existing configuration and administrative credential forward — so for any of the 28 NVD-listed model families that was internet-reachable with remote management enabled, the runbook has to be capture the configuration, reset to factory, rebuild from a known-good baseline and rotate the administrative credential, not update in place.

new_control_requirements.name: MITIGATION-ACTIVE-PATCH-PENDING-VERDICT-CLASS
new_control_requirements.description: Compliance verdicts must distinguish three states: (a) binary patch deployed (vulnerability eliminated), (b) vendor-mitigation rule active, no binary patch (residual risk: any defect in the mitigation rule reopens the vulnerability), (c) no mitigation, no patch (full exposure). Audit reports must surface (b) as a distinct compensating-control state with an associated time-bound action item, not as a 'patched per SLA' outcome.
new_control_requirements.evidence: NETGEAR's own advisory offers exactly the two-state choice this control exists to separate: it warns that the potential for remote access and command execution remains if you do not turn off remote management or update your firmware. A unit with remote management disabled and pre-fix firmware is in state (b) — region_search() still copies hidden_lang_avi with strcpy, and the whole control is one settings toggle that a factory reset, a support call or a firmware rollback reverses, with the researcher's advisory recording that the LAN path stays open regardless. Recording that as remediated against the 2022-04-15 due date loses the fact that the overflow is untouched.

CVE-2016-11021.name: D-Link DCS-930L Devices OS Command Injection Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: An authenticated request to the camera's setSystemCommand endpoint carries an operating-system command in the SystemCommand parameter, which the firmware passes to the shell unneutralised; the published exploit uses it to start a telnet daemon on a random high port with /bin/sh and then connects to it.
attack_vector.privileges_required: high — PR:H; the endpoint sits behind the camera's administrative login, so the credential is the precondition. The published module supplies no credential-discovery step and defaults to admin with an empty password
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; one POST once authenticated, with no race, no memory corruption and no device-specific offsets to derive
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Exploit-DB 39437 credits Nicholas Starke and the artefact is a hand-written Metasploit module against a named endpoint and parameter set; no automated discovery is described.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Flashing firmware 2.12 or later, setting a non-default administrative password, and placing the camera on a segment no general user network routes to with no port forward or UPnP mapping exposing it.
prevention.adequacy: The firmware is the fix and it is per-unit work with no management console to drive it. The password and segmentation measures bound who can reach the endpoint but leave the injection intact, and BOD 22-01 binds federal civilian agencies only.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alerting on a listening telnet service appearing on a camera, on POSTs to /setSystemCommand, and on outbound connections initiated by the camera rather than by its video client.
detection.adequacy: None of this comes from the device, which has no agent and no useful log export; it has to be obtained from the network — a scan that would notice a new high-port listener, or a monitoring point in front of the camera segment. Where the camera is exposed through a port forward, the request arrives from the internet with nothing in between to observe it.

response.what_would_have_worked: Factory resetting the camera, reconfiguring from a known-good baseline, rotating the administrative password, and rotating any credential the camera held or that transited it — then flashing 2.12 or later.
response.adequacy: The reset is what removes attacker changes, since flashing preserves the existing configuration, and it is the step no advisory prompts because no D-Link advisory for this CVE was resolved. It depends on a known-good configuration existing for the unit.

NIST-800-53-IA-2.gap: IA-2 is evidenced against directory-integrated systems, and the DCS-930L is not one — it carries a single local administrative account with no enrolment path and no central attestation. The published module's defaults, the username admin with an empty password, describe the state an unconfigured unit is in. The organisation's identification and authentication programme can be complete while the credential gating a command-injection endpoint is a shared password nobody in that programme can see.

NIST-800-53-SC-7.gap: Reachability is the interim bound SC-7 would supply, and it is undone below the level the control is assessed at: a port forward or a UPnP mapping created so someone can view the camera remotely places its web interface on the internet without any change to the enterprise boundary. SC-7 evidence covers the perimeter rather than the segment a camera is installed onto, so the control passes while the camera answers from a general user VLAN or from outside.

NIS2-Art21-identity-management.gap: The access-control and authentication obligations under Article 21(2)(i) and (j) presume systems an entity's identity processes can reach, and this camera supports one administrative credential over its web interface and nothing more. Rotation, review and revocation all become per-device manual work, so an entity with a fully compliant identity-management programme still has no process touching the secret that gates setSystemCommand.

UK-CAF-B2.gap: B2 Identity and Access Control is the principle that matters for an authenticated endpoint, and a camera owned as facilities equipment rather than as a networked system is excluded from the scope that assessment covers. That exclusion is the failure: the credential in front of setSystemCommand is precisely the one no B2 review examined. B2 also stops at access to enumerated data, whereas the outcome here is an interactive shell on the device itself.

AU-Essential-8-MFA.gap: The multi-factor authentication strategy cannot be applied to this interface at all — the DCS-930L supports a single password and offers no second factor, so there is no configuration that brings the device into coverage. It is the strategy an assessor would naturally reach for on a PR:H flaw, since the entire privilege requirement rests on one reusable secret, and it is unavailable at exactly the point where it would matter.

ISO-27001-2022-A.5.15.gap: A.5.15 (access control) expects access rules derived from business requirements, and a camera's management interface is covered only if it is in the register those rules address. The specific omission is that access to the camera's administrative function — equivalent on this firmware to shell access to the device — is not separated from access to the footage it produces, so a policy governing who may view video says nothing about who may authenticate to the interface carrying setSystemCommand.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: A.8.8 depends on a channel that supplies vulnerability information for the assets in the register, and for this CVE that channel is nearly empty: no D-Link advisory was resolved, the MITRE record carries a single Exploit-DB reference, and the identifier sits in the late-assigned 2016-11xxx range. A fully compliant process would have had nothing to ingest until the CISA listing on 2022-03-25, long after firmware 2.12 was already the fixed level.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Firmware 2.12 was already the fixed level for the DCS-930L when CISA enrolled CVE-2016-11021 on 2022-03-25 with a 2022-04-15 due date, so for this entry the listing is the first signal an operator was likely to receive — no D-Link advisory for it was resolved and the MITRE record carries only Exploit-DB 39437. That makes the whichever-is-later clause resolve to the KEV date here rather than to patch availability, and the compensating-controls branch is the realistic one for a camera fleet: a non-default administrative password plus a segment no general user network routes to, recorded with a dated action item to flash 2.12.

new_control_requirements.name: MITIGATION-ACTIVE-PATCH-PENDING-VERDICT-CLASS
new_control_requirements.description: Compliance verdicts must distinguish three states: (a) binary patch deployed (vulnerability eliminated), (b) vendor-mitigation rule active, no binary patch (residual risk: any defect in the mitigation rule reopens the vulnerability), (c) no mitigation, no patch (full exposure). Audit reports must surface (b) as a distinct compensating-control state with an associated time-bound action item, not as a 'patched per SLA' outcome.
new_control_requirements.evidence: A DCS-930L on pre-2.12 firmware whose administrative password has been changed and whose segment is restricted is in state (b): setSystemCommand still passes the SystemCommand parameter to the shell unneutralised, and the whole control is a password and a routing decision that a factory reset, a re-added port forward or a UPnP mapping reverses in one step. Because the published module defaults to admin with an empty password and performs no credential discovery, the password change is doing more work than it appears to — which is exactly why it needs recording as a compensating state with a dated action to reach 2.12, not as remediation.

CVE-2016-1555.name: NETGEAR Multiple WAP Devices Command Injection Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: Five unauthenticated provisioning pages in ProSAFE access-point firmware hand POST form fields to a shell. One POST to /boardDataWW.php with a semicolon in the macAddress field executes commands on the device.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none - PR:N; the boardData pages are served before any login, so an attacker needs no account, session or token, only network reach to the management interface
attack_vector.complexity: low - AC:L; a fixed request shape with no groom, race or leak, which is why a Metasploit module and a Nuclei template both automate it end to end
attack_vector.ai_factor: Found through FIRMADYNE firmware emulation, which is automated dynamic analysis rather than AI-assisted discovery; no research brand with 'AI' in its name is involved in this attribution at all.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Flashing WN604 units to 3.3.3 and the WNAP/WNDAP units to 3.5.5.0, and in the interim restricting the access points' HTTP management interface to a management VLAN unreachable from wireless clients.
prevention.adequacy: Reachability restriction bounds who can send the POST but does not close it: an access point exists to serve the clients attached to it, so any host on a permitted segment still reaches the provisioning pages, and the firmware upgrade is the only closure.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Logging HTTP requests to the access points' management interface at the switch or firewall in front of them, and alerting on POSTs to the boardData paths from any source outside the provisioning range.
detection.adequacy: The device generates no usable local record, so detection has to be built off-box; where the AP is reached from the same VLAN it serves, there is no inline point to observe the request at all.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating an exploited unit as compromised infrastructure: reflash from vendor media, rebuild the configuration from a known-good baseline rather than restoring the running config, and rotate the administrative password and any PSK or RADIUS secret the device held.
response.adequacy: This is a full rebuild per device and does not scale to a large wireless estate quickly; it also depends on a known-good configuration baseline existing before the incident.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: An estate can evidence SI-2 with a firmware report showing 3.5.5.0 across every WNAP320 and still be wrong about its exposure, because the control's question ends at the version. It never asks what happened during the window between the February 2016 disclosure and the upgrade, and a device whose administrative password and configuration survived the reflash carries that window forward.

NIST-800-53-CM-7.gap: Least functionality assumes the unnecessary function can be turned off. NETGEAR gives no setting that disables boardData102.php, boardData103.php, boardDataJP.php, boardDataNA.php or boardDataWW.php, so a CM-7 review of these access points has nothing to act on below the firmware upgrade and passes while five unauthenticated command sinks stay published.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: The article's process obligations are satisfiable with an asset inventory that never contained the access points. A WN604 or WNDAP660 has no agent and reports firmware only through its own web interface, so the entity's patch-management evidence can be complete while a device below 3.3.3 or 3.5.5.0 keeps serving the wireless network.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: B4 outcomes are written for centrally managed systems, and these units are flashed individually from their own interface. An organisation that can demonstrate current patch levels on servers and workstations may have no mechanism at all that would surface a 2016-era firmware level on the wireless infrastructure carrying that traffic.

UK-CAF-D1.gap: Response planning only helps once something starts the plan. Command execution through /boardDataWW.php leaves no host telemetry, no authentication event and no endpoint alert, so the D1 plan for this asset class is never triggered - the failure is in the trigger, not in the plan, which is why a tabletop exercise on this scenario passes.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Reading the Essential Eight's patch mitigations as covering operating systems and applications leaves network-device firmware outside their stated scope, so a high patching maturity rating and a fleet of WNDAP360 units on pre-3.5.5.0 firmware are compatible findings. That reading is this catalog's interpretation of the mitigation's scope and should be re-checked against the current maturity model rather than quoted as its text.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: A.8.8 depends on vulnerability information reaching the organisation. NETGEAR's statement for this flaw is a support-site article, KB 30480, and the only machine-readable mapping of SKU to fixed level is NVD's CPE list; a vulnerability-management process built on vendor feeds and scanner plugins can run correctly for years and never emit a finding for these seven models.

new_control_requirements.name: PERIMETER-COMPROMISE-REBUILD-NOT-PATCH
new_control_requirements.description: Pre-rehearsed IR runbook for any perimeter device that suffers a pre-auth RCE CVE in active exploitation MUST default to config-exfil + rebuild + credential rotation, not patch-in-place. Patch-in-place leaves attacker-installed implants intact.
new_control_requirements.evidence: These NETGEAR ProSAFE access points meet every condition the control names: a pre-authentication command-execution path on a network-boundary device, KEV-listed on 2022-03-25 with a 2022-04-15 due date, and public since February 2016 with a Metasploit module available from November 2018. Flashing a WNAP320 to 3.5.5.0 removes the defect and keeps the running configuration and administrative password, so an account or startup script added through /boardDataWW.php survives the upgrade.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: NETGEAR published fixed firmware - 3.3.3 for the WN604, 3.5.5.0 for the WNAP and WNDAP models - and CISA set a three-week clock from 2022-03-25 to 2022-04-15. With EPSS at 0.98325 (99.914th percentile) and a shipped Metasploit module, the interval between listing and flashing is the entire exposure decision for these devices, and a per-unit firmware push with a documented management-VLAN restriction as the interim control is what closing it looks like.

CVE-2016-4171.name: Adobe Flash Player Remote Code Execution Vulnerability (CVE-2016-4171)

attack_vector.description: A crafted SWF supplies '.key' and '.value' members that Flash Player uses as array indexes without bounds checking, reading and writing past the constant-pool array and giving the attacker arbitrary memory access inside the plugin process.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none - PR:N; the attacker needs no account on the target, only that the victim reach a page serving the SWF chain with a Flash runtime enabled for that origin
attack_vector.complexity: low - AC:L; the out-of-bounds index yields read and write in one step, so no heap groom, race or separate information leak is required
attack_vector.ai_factor: Identified by Kaspersky Lab's human analysis of captured campaign stages; no AI-assisted discovery is claimed by any party and no 'AI'-branded research arm appears in the attribution.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Removing the Flash runtime, or gating it behind click-to-play with an allow-list of origins, before June 2016 - and after 2016-06-16, installing APSB16-18 and relaunching every browser process.
prevention.adequacy: Removal is the only complete answer and it was unavailable to estates with Flash-dependent internal applications; the patch closed the defect but arrived after the campaign, and the KEV clock in 2022 post-dates the product's end of support by more than a year.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alerting on Flash plugin-process crashes and on script execution that follows a browser render without a corresponding process creation, plus certificate-anomaly checks on newly written executables.
detection.adequacy: The DDE execution path was chosen precisely to avoid the process-creation API that behaviour-based tooling keys on, and the spoofed Tencent signature is only anomalous if the certificate chain is validated rather than the publisher name read; both detections have to exist beforehand.

response.what_would_have_worked: Escalating on the ScarCruft attribution rather than treating the infection as commodity malware: scoping the exposure window from the March 2016 campaign start, and reviewing what the affected users could reach.
response.adequacy: Attribution arrived with Kaspersky's publication, well after the intrusions; response scoped from a public report is always retrospective, and it bounds damage rather than preventing it.

NIST-800-53-CM-7.gap: For the two days between APSA16-03 and APSB16-18 the only available defence was not having the Flash runtime loaded, which is a CM-7 decision. The control asks whether unnecessary functions are disabled, and a plugin that internal applications require is not answerable as unnecessary, so an estate can hold a clean CM-7 assessment while carrying the exact component the ScarCruft chain targeted.

NIST-800-53-SI-3.gap: SI-3 evidence is current signatures, scheduled scans and clean results, all of which this campaign is compatible with. The loader executed script through WM_DDE_EXECUTE window messages instead of CreateProcess, and its payloads carried a certificate impersonating Tencent Technology built on a serial copied from a real one, so the two things malicious-code protection keys on - process behaviour and publisher trust - were both addressed by the attacker before the control saw them.

NIS2-Art21-vulnerability-handling.gap: The obligation assumes a fix exists to be scheduled. In June 2016 this CVE had an Adobe advisory, exploitation confirmed against named victims, and no update for two days, so a compliant handling process consumed the advisory and could produce no remediation. The gap is structural: the article has no state for 'disclosed, exploited, unfixed' other than accepting risk.

NIS2-Art21-incident-handling.gap: Incident handling only engages on a detected event, and this chain was delivered by a link to a compromised third-party site, executed inside a plugin process, and continued through DDE messaging. Kaspersky's victim list spans law enforcement, trading, advertising and sport, so there is no sector-specific tuning that would have raised the priority either; the process is adequate and simply never receives the input.

UK-CAF-C1.gap: C1 is the outcome that has to carry an unpatched, actively exploited flaw, and this campaign was built against it. Per-hit re-encryption of the second stage removes the static signature, DDE execution removes the process-creation event, and the only durable observable is an abnormal plugin process on an ad path - which a monitoring capability built on endpoint process-creation events and signature hits does not collect.

AU-Essential-8-App-Hardening.gap: Blocking web browser processing of Flash content is the mitigation that maps directly onto this CVE, and it is the one an organisation with a Flash-dependent internal application carries a documented exception for. The exception is written per application but takes effect per browser, so the runtime kept alive for the internal system is the runtime that rendered the attacker's three chained SWF objects; the assessment records the exception and not the residual path.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.7.gap: Where A.8.7 is evidenced by endpoint anti-malware coverage and user awareness training, neither touches an out-of-bounds array index reached by loading a page: there is no attachment to refuse, no macro to disable, and the execution step deliberately avoids the process-creation API. The control is fully implemented and contributes nothing to this outcome.

new_control_requirements.name: NATION-STATE-INITIAL-ACCESS-IR-ESCALATION
new_control_requirements.description: IR runbooks must include an explicit nation-state-initial-access escalation path triggered by APT28/APT29/Lazarus/Volt-Typhoon/etc. attribution on a confirmed exploit chain. Standard malware-infection IR under-escalates nation-state activity by treating it as commodity threat.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Kaspersky attributes this Adobe Flash Player zero-day to ScarCruft and describes a multi-stage chain - three Flash objects, per-hit payload encryption, DDE-based execution and a spoofed Tencent Technology signing certificate - against a law-enforcement agency, a major Asian trading company and an advertising firm from March 2016. An organisation handling that as a routine plugin-crash-plus-malware ticket scopes the incident to one endpoint, when the actor's interest is the access that endpoint provides.

new_control_requirements.name: MITIGATION-ACTIVE-PATCH-PENDING-VERDICT-CLASS
new_control_requirements.description: Compliance verdicts must distinguish three states: (a) binary patch deployed (vulnerability eliminated), (b) vendor-mitigation rule active, no binary patch (residual risk: any defect in the mitigation rule reopens the vulnerability), (c) no mitigation, no patch (full exposure). Audit reports must surface (b) as a distinct compensating-control state with an associated time-bound action item, not as a 'patched per SLA' outcome.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Adobe published APSA16-03 for this Flash Player flaw before any fix existed and shipped APSB16-18 on 2016-06-16, so estates passed through a period in which the honest verdict was state (c) for anyone still rendering Flash and state (b) only for those who had disabled or gated the runtime. A vulnerability report that shows Flash Player 21.0.0.242 with no available update as simply 'no patch published' loses the distinction between a host that had removed the plugin and one that had not.

attack_vector.description: A page overrides Symbol.species on an Array subclass so Chakra's filter writes pointer-sized values into a native integer array, leaking heap addresses to script and writing past the buffer's element count.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none - PR:N; no account, token or local foothold, only that the target's Edge loads the attacker's page
attack_vector.complexity: low - AC:L; deterministic, with no groom or race, though converting the leak into execution requires a second defect, which the public chain supplies with CVE-2016-7201
attack_vector.ai_factor: Human source-level auditing of Chakra's species protocol by Google Project Zero; no AI assistance is claimed in discovery or in the later weaponization.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Installing the November 2016 Windows 10 cumulative - KB3198585, KB3198586 or KB3200970 - and restarting the host, inside the ten days between the 2016-11-08 bulletin and the 2016-11-18 publication of working code.
prevention.adequacy: The cumulative is the only fix and it is all-or-nothing; where an update ring defers Windows 10 cumulatives for application compatibility, this browser fix is deferred with them and no partial mitigation is offered.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alerting on Edge content-process faults attributed to chakra.dll and on any process created by an Edge content process, correlated against the page loaded at the time.
detection.adequacy: Content-process crashes are common enough that the signal needs the faulting-module attribution and clustering by referrer to be actionable; the successful case may not crash at all.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating a confirmed exploitation as user-context code execution: reviewing what the browser's user account could reach and rotating credentials entered in that session.
response.adequacy: Bounded by what the browser process could do, but the chain runs at the current user's rights, so the scope is the user's whole reachable surface rather than the browser alone.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: The control is met by an installed, approved update, and on this platform that is a Windows 10 cumulative rather than a fix for this CVE. Because the update only takes effect after a restart, a fleet report showing KB3200970 installed across every 1607 host can coexist with those hosts still executing the pre-fix chakra.dll, and nothing in SI-2's evidence model distinguishes the two states.

NIS2-Art21-vulnerability-management.gap: MS16-129 shipped this CVE together with seven other Chakra memory-corruption CVEs and no per-CVE fix exists, so per-vulnerability risk decisions have no corresponding per-vulnerability action. The entity's process can be fully documented and still reduce, in practice, to a single yes-or-no on the monthly cumulative - which is a servicing decision, not the vulnerability-management decision the article describes.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: Edge on Windows 10 has no update channel of its own, so its patch timeline is the operating system's ring policy. An organisation that defers cumulatives for compatibility testing defers its browser's script engine at the same time, and B4 is assessed against the ring's documented period rather than against the fact that this component parses untrusted script on every page.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: The operating-system patch mitigation is the right one for this fix, since KB3198585, KB3198586 and KB3200970 are cumulative Windows updates. What the maturity assessment counts is deployment, and this update is inert until the host restarts, so a high rating is achievable on a fleet where a meaningful share of machines have staged the package and not rebooted.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: Where A.8.8 prioritisation is driven by severity scores, this CVE's 8.8 did not move when Google's proof of concept appeared on 2016-11-18 or when a working WinExec chain appeared on 2017-01-05. The information that should have re-ordered the queue - exploit code became public ten days after the bulletin - is not an input the control asks for.

new_control_requirements.name: BROWSER-MANAGED-UPDATE-NO-DEFERRAL
new_control_requirements.description: Enterprise update rings must not defer security-channel browser updates beyond 24h.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Edge on Windows 10 is patched only through the operating system's cumulative channel - KB3198585, KB3198586 and KB3200970 for MS16-129 - so any ring that defers Windows 10 cumulatives defers the browser's Chakra engine with them. The margin here was ten days: Microsoft published on 2016-11-08 and Google's working leak proof of concept appeared on 2016-11-18, with a full WinExec chain by 2017-01-05.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: For this Microsoft Edge Chakra flaw the KEV clock ran from 2022-03-28 to 2022-04-18, more than five years after MS16-129 shipped, so the operative deadline is patch availability rather than listing - and with EPSS at 0.8249 (99.636th percentile) and a public RCE chain since January 2017, an unpatched Windows 10 host in that window was exposed to code that already existed. Verified mitigation here means the installed cumulative confirmed after a restart, not the approval state in the update console.

attack_vector.description: A Proxy's getPrototypeOf trap returns a native integer array during Chakra's prototype-fill path, so script-chosen integers are consumed as absolute pointers and the engine dereferences and writes through an address the attacker picked.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none - PR:N; no account or foothold on the target, only that Edge renders the attacker's content
attack_vector.complexity: low - AC:L; the Proxy trap removes any timing dependence, though a second defect is needed to supply the address, which the public chain takes from CVE-2016-7200
attack_vector.ai_factor: Manual analysis of a JavaScript specification feature against an engine's internal type assumptions, by Google Project Zero; no AI involvement is claimed in discovery or weaponization.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Taking the November 2016 Windows 10 cumulative and restarting, which closes this defect and its seven Chakra siblings in one action.
prevention.adequacy: Complete for this defect, but it is an all-or-nothing servicing action with no per-CVE granularity, and it leaves the engine primitive that produced eight CVEs at once unchanged.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Correlating Edge content-process faults attributed to chakra.dll with the URL rendered at the time, and alerting on any process created by a browser content process or by an application hosting the Edge rendering engine.
detection.adequacy: Crash telemetry catches failed attempts; a working exploit of a deterministic type confusion need not crash at all, so the process-creation half of the rule is the one that carries the detection.

response.what_would_have_worked: Scoping a confirmed exploitation to everything the browsing user could reach, and re-checking the host's chakra.dll version after the restart rather than trusting the update console.
response.adequacy: Bounded by the current user's rights, which on an unmanaged local-administrator account is the whole machine; the version re-check confirms remediation but says nothing about the exposure window.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: Tracking this CVE to closure under SI-2 produces a record about KB3200970, because Microsoft published no fix for it alone. The same evidence would exist if the seven sibling Chakra CVEs in MS16-129 had gone unnoticed, so the control cannot distinguish an organisation that understood it was patching one engine primitive eight ways from one that installed a monthly update.

NIST-800-53-SI-4.gap: SI-4 detection for browser exploitation leans on crash and error telemetry, and a Proxy-driven type confusion is deterministic - the successful path does not fault. What remains observable is the consequence, a process created under the browser, which requires endpoint telemetry that attributes parentage rather than the browser-health signal that crash reporting supplies.

NIS2-Art21-network-security.gap: The component at risk exists to render untrusted content, so bounding its input at the network is not achievable in the way the article's measures assume. Microsoft's bulletin names ActiveX embedding of the Edge rendering engine inside an application or Office document as a delivery route for this class, which reaches the same chakra.dll without a browsing session for a proxy to inspect.

UK-CAF-B5.gap: Resilience planning wants a degraded-but-safe state, and this defect offers none: the content process runs with the user's rights and the published chain goes straight to WinExec. There is no partial-failure mode for an operator to design around, so B5 evidence about network and system resilience is orthogonal to what actually happens when this page loads.

AU-Essential-8-App-Hardening.gap: The mitigation targets browser features an organisation can switch off - advertisements, Java, Flash. This exploit uses Proxy objects and prototype lookups, which are core JavaScript that no hardening baseline disables, so an estate assessed at the top maturity level for user application hardening has exactly the same exposure to CVE-2016-7201 as one at the bottom.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.28.gap: Secure coding names the cause precisely - the engine trusted a type invariant that the language specification lets a Proxy break - but the control governs the organisation's own development, and here the code belongs to the browser vendor. The operator's version of A.8.28 becomes supplier assurance, and MS16-129 shows what that assurance was worth on this component: eight Chakra memory-corruption CVEs shipped in a single bulletin.

new_control_requirements.name: BROWSER-MANAGED-UPDATE-NO-DEFERRAL
new_control_requirements.description: Enterprise update rings must not defer security-channel browser updates beyond 24h.
new_control_requirements.evidence: This Chakra type confusion has no standalone fix: KB3198585, KB3198586 and KB3200970 are the only delivery, so every day a Windows 10 ring defers a cumulative is a day Edge keeps the vulnerable FillFromPrototypes path along with seven sibling Chakra CVEs from the same bulletin. Public exploit code landed 2016-11-18 and a full WinExec chain on 2017-01-05, against a bulletin dated 2016-11-08.

new_control_requirements.name: BUG-FAMILY-MITIGATION-PERSISTENCE
new_control_requirements.description: When a CVE patch lands, retain the pre-patch compensating controls (module blacklists, sysctl restrictions) until the patched code has soaked for a stated review period. Patches for one bug in a primitive class can introduce sibling bugs in the same class; the original compensating control may still apply to the sibling.
new_control_requirements.evidence: MS16-129 fixed this defect alongside CVE-2016-7200, -7202, -7203, -7208, -7240, -7242 and -7243 - eight Chakra memory-corruption CVEs in one bulletin, several of them array and prototype type-confusion primitives. Treating the November 2016 cumulative as retiring the class is what this control forbids: the primitive that let a Proxy return a native int array into an array-fill path is the same primitive family that kept producing findings, so browser-side restrictions adopted while it was unpatched should stay in place through a stated review period rather than being lifted at install time.

attack_vector.description: A crafted SWF frees the object behind a Flash TextField while still holding a reference to it, then reuses that reference after the memory has been reallocated with attacker-chosen content, yielding code execution in the process hosting the runtime.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none - PR:N; the attacker needs no account and no foothold, only that the victim's browser render the SWF
attack_vector.complexity: low - AC:L with UI:R; the heap reclamation that makes the stale reference useful happens inside the attacker's own file rather than depending on the target's state
