attack_vector.ai_factor: Adobe's APSB16-39 credits "An anonymous researcher working with JPCERT/CC (CVE-2016-7892)"; no AI-branded research arm is associated with it.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Reaching 24.0.0.186 on every channel present on the host - Adobe's runtime, the Chrome-bundled copy, and KB3209498 for the Internet Explorer and Edge copy - and relaunching the browsers; or, where Flash had no business use, setting the ActiveX kill bit and the Group Policy that turns it off in Internet Explorer.
prevention.adequacy: Complete only if every channel is covered; the containment settings are documented by Microsoft for the Internet Explorer path and do not stop Flash being invoked from other applications, which Microsoft states directly for the Office-specific variant of the workaround.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alerting on Flash runtime process terminations and on any process created by a plugin-container or browser tab process, correlated with the origin serving the SWF.
detection.adequacy: A use-after-free that succeeds need not crash, so the crash signal covers the failures; the process-parentage signal is the one that would catch a working exploit, and it has to be collected before the fact.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating an exploited host as user-context compromise and, separately, re-checking every Flash channel on the machine rather than the one the inventory names.
response.adequacy: The second half is what makes the first stick: closing an incident with the Adobe runtime at 24.0.0.186 and KB3209498 still missing leaves the same defect reachable through the browser the following day.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: SI-2 assumes a flaw maps to a component and a component to a fix. On a Windows host this Flash defect lives in two components on two update tracks, and the installed-programs entry that a scanner reads belongs only to the Adobe runtime. Showing 24.0.0.186 in that entry while KB3209498 is absent is a clean SI-2 finding and a browser still loading the vulnerable TextField code.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: A documented patch-management process ties a vulnerability to an update and tracks that update to deployment. This CVE required Adobe's 24.0.0.186 and Microsoft's KB3209498, issued a day apart in December 2016 through channels with different owners and different change windows, and nothing in the article's measures forces the process to recognise that one vulnerability produced two obligations.

UK-CAF-A1.gap: Keeping Flash in service for a dependent application is a governance decision, and A1 evidences that such decisions are owned, documented and reviewed. What it does not require is an expiry: an acceptance recorded in 2016 for this CVE could still be renewed at each review until the runtime left support on 2020-12-31, with every renewal fully compliant and the exposure unchanged.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: The application-patching mitigation is measured against installed application versions, which is the wrong denominator for a runtime that ships four ways. A host can show Flash Player 24.0.0.186 in its software inventory, satisfy the assessment, and still be running 23.0.0.207 inside Internet Explorer because the Windows package that services that copy was never applied.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.9.gap: The containment configuration for this defect - the ActiveX kill bit on CLSID {D27CDB6E-AE6D-11CF-96B8-444553540000} and the Group Policy that turns off Flash in Internet Explorer - is published by Microsoft in MS16-154, not by the application's own vendor. A configuration baseline assembled from Adobe guidance therefore has no entry for it, and A.8.9 review of that baseline finds nothing missing.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: For this Adobe Flash Player TextField use-after-free the KEV clock ran 2022-03-25 to 2022-04-15, more than a year after the product left support on 2020-12-31, so 'verified mitigation' for a host still carrying the runtime in that window means removal rather than reaching 24.0.0.186. The documented-compensating-control branch of this SLA is the one that applies where an application dependency blocked removal, and MS16-154's kill bit and Group Policy are what that branch has to point at.

new_control_requirements.name: BROWSER-MANAGED-UPDATE-NO-DEFERRAL
new_control_requirements.description: Enterprise update rings must not defer security-channel browser updates beyond 24h.
new_control_requirements.evidence: The browser is a distinct delivery channel for this defect: Internet Explorer 10/11 and Edge carry their own Flash runtime, patched only by MS16-154 (KB3209498) on 2016-12-13, independently of the Adobe installer that produced 24.0.0.186. An update ring that treats the browser channel as deferrable holds the vulnerable TextField code inside the browser on hosts whose Adobe runtime already reports the fixed build.

CVE-2017-0037.name: Microsoft Edge and Internet Explorer Type Confusion Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: Mutating CSS column properties against a table with a column-spanning element drives mshtml.dll's multi-column box builder to read one object as another type and dereference a pointer the script supplied as an integer, giving a controlled read and write in the browser process.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none - PR:N; no account or foothold is needed, only that the target opens the page in Internet Explorer 10/11 or EdgeHTML
attack_vector.complexity: high - AC:H; the confusion requires a specific layout state the proof of concept reaches by looping the style mutation, and Microsoft states that full code execution also requires combining this with other exploits, which is why both public builds are platform- and architecture-specific
attack_vector.ai_factor: Google Project Zero's manual exploration of a single layout path in mshtml.dll; no AI-assisted discovery is claimed, and no research brand carrying 'AI' in its name is involved.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Applying MS17-006 and, where Edge is present, MS17-007 on 2017-03-14 and restarting; before that date, retiring Internet Explorer as a rendering path for untrusted content, since no vendor fix existed between 2017-02-24 and 2017-03-14.
prevention.adequacy: Complete once both bulletins land, but for the eighteen-day window there was nothing to apply, and Microsoft published no workaround for this CVE - only pre-existing postures such as server-side Enhanced Security Configuration and EMET, which reduce likelihood rather than removing the defect.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alerting on mshtml.dll-attributed browser faults correlated with the rendered URL, and on any process created by a browser tab process.
detection.adequacy: The crash signal covers failed attempts on the wrong platform build, which is likely given how version-specific both public chains are; the successful case is only visible through process parentage or memory-protection telemetry.

response.what_would_have_worked: Scoping a confirmed exploitation to the browsing user's full reachable surface, and separately verifying that both the Internet Explorer and the Edge update landed on the host rather than one of them.
response.adequacy: The two-bulletin check is what prevents a repeat on the same machine; the user-scope review is bounded by the account's rights, which on a local-administrator account is the whole host.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: The obligation is to install updates within a period measured from vendor release, and for this CVE the vendor released nothing for eighteen days after public trigger code appeared on 2017-02-24. An organisation that installed MS17-006 and MS17-007 on the day they shipped has an unblemished SI-2 record and was nonetheless exposed for the entire window in which the flaw was public and unfixed.

NIST-800-53-SI-3.gap: With no patch available, the residual controls Microsoft actually points to for this group are Enhanced Security Configuration on server SKUs and EMET configured for Internet Explorer. Both must already be deployed to help, so an SI-3 implementation centred on anti-malware definitions had no action available on 2017-02-24, and its compliance state was identical before and after the disclosure.

NIS2-Art21-vulnerability-handling.gap: Handling practices are built around scheduling a fix against a disclosure. This disclosure carried working trigger code and no fix for eighteen days, and Microsoft's own bulletins later confirmed the public-disclosure status, so a compliant process could produce nothing but a documented risk acceptance. The article has no state that obliges an interim posture change when a browser defect is public and unpatched.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: Remediation for this CVE is two separate bulletins - MS17-006 for Internet Explorer and MS17-007 for Edge - and a Windows 10 host may need both. An estate that moved to Edge and left Internet Explorer installed can apply the Edge update, evidence B4 against its browser fleet, and leave the same mshtml.dll defect reachable through the browser that no longer appears in its usage statistics.

AU-Essential-8-App-Hardening.gap: The mitigation is aimed at optional browser functionality, and this exploit needs only CSS multi-column layout and DOM attribute mutation - features no hardening baseline disables. Enhanced Security Configuration is the nearest applicable measure and Microsoft frames it as reducing the likelihood of running crafted content from outside the Trusted Sites zone on servers, which leaves client hosts, the actual target population here, untouched.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: Where prioritisation under A.8.8 follows severity, this CVE scores 8.1 with AC:H and nothing more. The fact that should have driven it to the top of the queue on 2017-02-24, that Project Zero's trigger code was public with no available fix until 2017-03-14, is not an input the control's ranking asks for.

new_control_requirements.name: VENDOR-PUSH-MITIGATION-OPT-IN-PRE-DISCLOSURE
new_control_requirements.description: For vendors offering push-mitigation services (Microsoft EEMS, Palo Alto Threat Prevention auto-update, etc.), opt-in must be enabled BEFORE the next disclosure event, not in response to it. Compliance frameworks must require operators to enable available vendor-push-mitigation services as a baseline control — opt-in late means the mitigation rule arrives after exploitation, not before.
new_control_requirements.evidence: This Internet Explorer and Edge type confusion was public with working trigger code from 2017-02-24 and unpatched until Microsoft shipped MS17-006 and MS17-007 on 2017-03-14, after skipping the February 2017 update cycle. The only measures Microsoft names for this vulnerability group during that window - Enhanced Security Configuration on Windows Server 2008 through 2012 R2, and EMET configured for Internet Explorer - deliver nothing unless they were already enabled, which is precisely the pre-disclosure posture this control requires.

new_control_requirements.name: BROWSER-MANAGED-UPDATE-NO-DEFERRAL
new_control_requirements.description: Enterprise update rings must not defer security-channel browser updates beyond 24h.
new_control_requirements.evidence: The fix for this mshtml.dll defect arrives only through Windows servicing, and on a Windows 10 host it arrives twice: MS17-006 (KB4013073) for Internet Explorer 11 and MS17-007 (KB4013071) for Edge, both dated 2017-03-14 and both inert until the host restarts. Given eighteen days of public exposure before that date, a ring that then defers the March cumulatives for compatibility testing extends the window past the point where the vendor had done its part.

CVE-2017-0059.name: Microsoft Internet Explorer Information Disclosure Vulnerability (CVE-2017-0059)

attack_vector.description: A form reset dispatches a nested iframe's readystate handler, the handler reassigns the textarea's defaultValue and releases its text buffer, and the reset then copies out of the released block; because that allocation sits on the process heap rather than under MemGC, the copy returns reclaimed memory the attacker shaped.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none - PR:N; the page needs no account or prior access, only that Internet Explorer render it
attack_vector.complexity: low - AC:L with UI:R; no race and no groom is needed to obtain the read, though useful contents require the attacker to reclaim the freed block with allocations of their choosing
attack_vector.ai_factor: Google Project Zero's manual reasoning about which Internet Explorer allocations MemGC protects; no AI-assisted discovery is claimed by anyone, and none of the three published artefacts references a model or an 'AI'-branded research programme.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Applying MS17-006 on 2017-03-14 and restarting, or removing Internet Explorer as a rendering path on hosts that had already moved to another default browser - Microsoft does not list Edge for this CVE, so retiring the Internet Explorer engine removes it outright.
prevention.adequacy: The update is complete for this defect, but it is a single KB per platform that also carries eleven other Internet Explorer CVEs, so it cannot be applied selectively; and disabling the browser does not help where an application hosts the Internet Explorer engine directly.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Browser-level telemetry on form resets whose nested-iframe readystate handler reassigns a textarea property mid-reset, and endpoint alerting on any process created by iexplore.exe.
detection.adequacy: The first is not something Internet Explorer emits, so it is aspirational rather than deployable; the second only fires once the chain reaches execution, which means detection here begins after the stage this CVE covers has already succeeded.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating any confirmed exploitation of the paired CVE-2017-0037 chain as including this leak, and scoping the response to what the browsing user could reach rather than to the browser.
response.adequacy: Reactive by construction: the leak leaves no artefact, so response is scoped from the execution stage and the earlier read can never be confirmed or timed from host evidence.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: Severity-tiered remediation timeframes are permitted under SI-2, and this defect presents as Important-rated information disclosure at CVSS 4.3. Because the same KB4013073 update also carries CVE-2017-0037, a policy that would have patched the type confusion quickly and this leak slowly is describing two halves of one published chain that ship in one package - the tiering has no effect except to justify delay.

NIST-800-53-SI-4.gap: A successful read of freed heap memory generates no crash, no authentication record and no new process, so there is no indicator for SI-4 to detect at this stage. The monitoring capability is not misconfigured - the event simply does not exist outside the renderer, and the first host-visible artefact belongs to the chained execution defect rather than to this one.

NIS2-Art21-vulnerability-management.gap: Risk-based measures assess a vulnerability on its own impact, and on its own this one leaks process memory to a page. The assessment is accurate and the conclusion is still wrong, because public code has combined it with CVE-2017-0037 into Internet Explorer 11 code execution since 2017-07-24; the article gives no mechanism for a low-impact defect to inherit the priority of the chain it enables.

UK-CAF-D1.gap: Response planning depends on an incident being recognisable. This stage produces no alert and no artefact, so a D1 plan is only triggered by the execution stage, and when it is, the timeline cannot be walked back to when the leak occurred. That makes exposure-window scoping - which hosts read what, and when - unanswerable from the evidence the estate holds.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: The mitigation counts days from the vendor release of 2017-03-14 and treats each application update as one item. It offers no way to record that this particular update closes a component of a published exploit chain, so an organisation applying its standard timeframe for an Important information disclosure is assessed as compliant while the leak that supplies a module base to CVE-2017-0037 stays live on its Internet Explorer hosts.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.16.gap: A.8.16 asks for monitoring of networks, systems and applications for anomalous behaviour. The anomaly here is a defaultValue assignment issued from a nested iframe's readystate handler in the middle of a form reset, entirely inside the renderer and never emitted as telemetry, so an implementation covering network flows, authentication events and endpoint process activity is complete within its scope and sees none of it.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: A KEV-driven SLA is what overrides the CVSS 4.3 rating that would otherwise put this Internet Explorer memory disclosure at the back of the queue: CISA listed it on 2022-03-28 with a 2022-04-18 due date, and its EPSS of 0.61968 sits at the 99.104th percentile despite the low base score. There is no live-patch option and Microsoft published no workaround for this vulnerability group, so the only mitigations this SLA can accept are MS17-006 with a restart, or removal of the Internet Explorer engine from the host.

new_control_requirements.name: BROWSER-MANAGED-UPDATE-NO-DEFERRAL
new_control_requirements.description: Enterprise update rings must not defer security-channel browser updates beyond 24h.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Internet Explorer has no update channel of its own - this fix reaches Windows 7, 8.1 and the server SKUs as KB4012204 or a monthly rollup, and Windows 10 as KB4012606, KB4013198 or KB4013429 - so browser patching here is entirely a function of the operating-system ring policy. A ring that defers those packages holds the pre-fix mshtml.dll on hosts where Internet Explorer is no longer the default browser and therefore no longer visible in browser-usage reporting.

CVE-2017-0146.name: Microsoft Windows SMB Remote Code Execution Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: A crafted sequence of SMBv1 Transaction requests drives the server's request handling into a kernel write-what-where primitive, which the public exploits use to rewrite the session's security context and then create and run a service over a named pipe. The fix corrects how SMBv1 parses those requests; removing the SMB1 feature removes the parser.
attack_vector.privileges_required: low — PR:L; the exploit implementations need access to a named pipe over IPC$, which since Windows Vista is not available to an anonymous session, so a guest or low-privilege credential or a host still permitting null-session pipe access is the entry condition.
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; no race window to win and no heap grooming on these paths, which is why a stock Metasploit module drives it. The real constraint is reachability of TCP/445 plus the pipe, not exploit reliability.
attack_vector.ai_factor: None recorded. Microsoft credits no finder for this CVE in MS17-010, and neither the Metasploit modules nor worawit's repository indicates automated or AI-assisted discovery or weaponization.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Removing SMB1.0/CIFS File Sharing Support per KB2696547 on every host that does not serve an SMB1-only client, and installing the MS17-010 package for the SKU where the feature must stay.
prevention.adequacy: Protocol removal is complete but costs a restart and breaks any client that cannot negotiate a later dialect; the update is complete only on SKUs Microsoft still services, and the exposed population in 2026 is dominated by hosts that cannot take one.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alerting on SMB1 dialect negotiation on TCP/445 and on named-pipe opens over IPC$ that are followed by service creation on the same session.
detection.adequacy: Both signals are visible to network and Windows security logging, but on an estate that still runs SMB1 for a legacy client the dialect signal is not anomalous on its own — it has to be paired with the service-creation step to mean anything.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating a confirmed hit as a host compromise with SYSTEM-level code execution: rebuild rather than patch in place, and rotate every credential that authenticated to the host during the exposure window.
response.adequacy: Rebuild removes attacker-installed persistence that an update leaves untouched, but it does not reach lateral movement already completed, and CISA records ransomware campaign use for this CVE — so a positive finding is an incident, not a patch ticket.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: Flaw remediation is nominally met the moment the estate's patch pipeline reports no missing MS17-010 packages. The pipeline cannot report a missing package for a Windows Vista or Server 2008 host that Microsoft no longer services, so the hosts carrying the highest residual exposure to a 0.89862 EPSS defect are the ones SI-2 evidence renders as clean.

NIST-800-53-CM-7.gap: Where least functionality is evidenced by a hardened build standard, SMBv1 travels with that standard rather than against it, because it was an enabled feature on the SKUs this bulletin lists. CM-7 as assessed produces no per-host record of which machines still negotiate NT LM 0.12, which is the one fact that decides whether this CVE is reachable.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: An Art. 21 patch-management measure is satisfied by a documented cycle and a compliant in-support fleet. It does not force the entity to declare the Windows 7, Vista and Server 2008 population that cannot take the 14 March 2017 update, and CISA's 2022-04-15 KEV due date came and went five years after that update shipped without any of it applying to that population.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: B4 is met by demonstrating managed, consistent builds, which is exactly how SMBv1 propagates: the golden image carries the optional feature and every host inherits it. Nothing in a B4 attestation about build currency proves the SMB1 dialect is unavailable estate-wide, and that is the only outcome that removes this parser from reach.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Patching maturity is measured against vendor release timelines, so a 2017 Microsoft update scores as fully mature or as not applicable. Neither verdict describes the actual state of an unserviced host still answering SMB1 on TCP/445 in 2026, and the Essential Eight gives an assessor no maturity level in which to record it.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: Technical vulnerability management is evidenced by scanner coverage and remediation SLAs against MS17-010 KB detection. A credentialed scan of an unserviced Windows 7 or Server 2008 host returns no applicable update and the finding closes, so A.8.8 evidence is strongest precisely where the exposure is worst.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CISA added this Microsoft Windows SMBv1 remote code execution flaw to KEV on 2022-03-25 with a 2022-04-15 due date and knownRansomwareCampaignUse 'Known', five years after MS17-010 shipped on 14 March 2017; EPSS on 2026-08-17 stands at 0.89862 (99.781st percentile). The three-week federal clock is the wrong tempo for a defect whose exploit is a stock Metasploit module, and the 'documented compensating controls' branch of this control is the one that matters here, because removing SMB1.0/CIFS per KB2696547 remediates hosts that can no longer receive a Microsoft update.

new_control_requirements.name: BUG-FAMILY-MITIGATION-PERSISTENCE
new_control_requirements.description: When a CVE patch lands, retain the pre-patch compensating controls (module blacklists, sysctl restrictions) until the patched code has soaked for a stated review period. Patches for one bug in a primitive class can introduce sibling bugs in the same class; the original compensating control may still apply to the sibling.
new_control_requirements.evidence: MS17-010 fixed six SMBv1 defects in a single bulletin on 14 March 2017 — CVE-2017-0143 through CVE-2017-0148, with this entry among them — which is the clearest possible demonstration that one Windows SMBv1 request-handling primitive carried siblings. The compensating control Microsoft itself named, removing SMB1.0/CIFS File Sharing Support per KB2696547, survives the patch and keeps a host out of reach of the next defect in that same parser; backing it out once the March 2017 packages are installed re-exposes the surface the bulletin was written about.

attack_vector.description: An out-of-process COM object reached through IRemUnknown2 can return a local proxy for an interface other than the one requested, so the caller drives a mismatched vtable. The published exploit routes that confusion through the BITS service's SetNotifyInterface, redirects the type-library load, and executes a scriptlet moniker inside a SYSTEM service.
attack_vector.privileges_required: low — PR:L; the attacker needs nothing more than the interactive local account they were issued, which is why privilege-restriction controls never engage.
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L, with UI:R because the exploit is compiled and launched from a user-writable directory. There is no race and no memory grooming once the confused proxy is handed to BITS.
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Exploit-DB 42020 credits Google Security Research and the analysis is manual reasoning about COM interface identity; no AI-branded tooling or automated discovery is claimed anywhere in the advisory or the exploit entry.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Installing the May 2017 Windows update for the SKU, which corrects how the COM marshaler processes interface requests, and retiring interactive multi-user roles from SKUs Microsoft no longer services.
prevention.adequacy: The update is complete on serviced SKUs and needs a reboot, but it does nothing for the Windows 7, 8.1, Server 2012 and Windows 10 1703 hosts in the affected set, where the only remaining lever is removing the ability of untrusted users to run code at all.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alerting on a BITS-hosting svchost.exe spawning a shell or script host, and on SYSTEM services loading type libraries or scriptlets from user-writable paths.
detection.adequacy: Both are high-signal because a service running as SYSTEM has no legitimate reason to load code out of a user profile, but they require process-lineage and image-load telemetry to be collected and shipped before the attempt — a rule authored afterwards has nothing to read.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating a hit as SYSTEM compromise of the host: rebuild rather than patch in place, and rotate every credential cached on or authenticated through that host during the exposure window.
response.adequacy: Rebuild removes persistence the update leaves intact, but on a shared session host the credential-rotation scope is every account that held a session there, and establishing that scope depends on session records retained off the host from before the exposure window.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: Flaw remediation was satisfied by the ordinary May 2017 cycle and stayed satisfied. What it never captured is that working exploit source appeared on Exploit-DB eight days after release, so the interval an operator was actually racing was days rather than the monthly window SI-2 evidence documents — and on unserviced SKUs the control has nothing left to measure.

NIST-800-53-AC-6.gap: An estate can hold a complete least-privilege attestation — no standing local administrators, admin accounts separated — and remain fully exploitable, because the exploit consumes only the ordinary interactive account AC-6 is designed to leave in place. The control is not weakened here; it is bypassed, which is why an AC-6 finding will never be raised against this host.

NIS2-Art21-vulnerability-management.gap: The measure is met by a documented triage process, and that process, reading CVSS 7.3 with AV:L, defensibly ranks this below network-facing work. The CISA KEV entry of 2022-03-28 with ransomware use recorded as Known is the fact that should reorder it, and nothing in a severity-driven triage definition obliges the entity to ingest that signal.

UK-CAF-B2.gap: Identity and access control is evidenced through account lifecycle, privileged-access separation and authentication strength, none of which this exploit touches — the attacker authenticates normally as themselves. B2 therefore stays green on a host where any issued account reaches SYSTEM, and the attestation and the exposure are entirely independent of one another.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Operating-system patching maturity measures elapsed time from the 2017-05-09 release, so serviced hosts score at the top of the model and unserviced ones fall outside it. The Essential Eight has no cell for a shared session host running Windows 7 or Server 2012 whose ordinary users each hold the exact precondition this flaw needs.

ISO-27001-2022-A.5.15.gap: Access control is evidenced by policy, role definitions and enforcement records, all of which remain true after exploitation because the escalation happens inside a process the user was entitled to run. An auditor sampling A.5.15 evidence on a patched host and an unpatched one collects the identical artefacts, so the control cannot distinguish them.

ISO-27001-2022-A.5.7.gap: Threat intelligence is met by subscribing to vendor advisories, and the vendor advisory dated 2017-05-09 said the flaw was neither publicly disclosed nor exploited. Publication of full exploit source by a named research handle on 2017-05-17 is the event that changed the risk, and advisory-only intake has no mechanism to re-rank an entry on that basis.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Microsoft published the COM marshaler fix on 2017-05-09; Exploit-DB 42020 published working source on 2017-05-17; CISA added the Windows COM Aggregate Marshaler elevation to KEV on 2022-03-28 with a 2022-04-18 due date and knownRansomwareCampaignUse 'Known'. EPSS on 2026-08-17 is 0.84138 at the 99.673rd percentile. The eight-day gap between vendor fix and public exploit is the interval this control is scaled to, and the compensating-control branch is what an operator uses on the unserviced SKUs in the affected set, where no package remains to deploy.

new_control_requirements.name: RESEARCHER-HANDLE-ACTIVITY-TRACKER
new_control_requirements.description: When a researcher handle is named in any catalog entry's discovery_attribution_note or poc_description, their public code-platform activity (GitHub events or a GitLab activity feed) must be polled by the threat-intake pipeline. The handle becomes a known signal source after a single catalog-grade drop and warrants prioritized surfacing of subsequent drops.
new_control_requirements.evidence: The exploit for this Windows COM elevation is attributed on Exploit-DB 42020 to the handle 'Google Security Research', published 2017-05-17 — eight days after Microsoft's 2017-05-09 advisory that recorded the flaw as neither publicly disclosed nor exploited. An intake pipeline watching that handle's public drops would have re-ranked the entry on the day the source appeared, five years before the 2022-03-28 KEV listing; an advisory-only feed re-ranked it never.

CVE-2017-12615.name: Apache Tomcat on Windows Remote Code Execution Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: With PUT enabled on the Default servlet, a crafted request writes JSP source into the web application directory past the servlet's own refusal to accept JSP uploads; requesting the written path makes Tomcat compile and run it as the service account. One PUT and one GET is the whole chain.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; no session, no credential and no prior foothold. The service account the JSP inherits is whatever identity the Tomcat process runs as, which is the variable that decides how bad the outcome is.
attack_vector.complexity: high — AC:H; not because the request is hard to build but because two non-default conditions must both hold: readonly set to false on the Default servlet, and a Windows host. Neither is discoverable from a version banner alone.
attack_vector.ai_factor: None recorded. The Apache Tomcat 7 security page credits the report to 'iswin from 360-sg-lab' on 26 July 2017 and describes no automated discovery method.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Leaving the Default servlet's readonly parameter at its default of true, so HTTP PUT is never accepted, and upgrading to Tomcat 7.0.81 or later where PUT is genuinely required.
prevention.adequacy: The configuration change is complete and immediate and needs only a service restart, but it removes a capability someone enabled deliberately, so it has to be reconciled with whatever publishing workflow depends on PUT rather than simply imposed.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alerting on any HTTP PUT reaching a Tomcat context, and on JSP compilation under work/Catalina/localhost for pages absent from the deployed application.
detection.adequacy: PUT is a high-signal method on a container that should not accept it, and the compilation artefact is durable evidence rather than a transient event. Both need the access log and the work directory to be shipped off-host, or a rebuilt instance destroys them.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating a written JSP as code execution already achieved: redeploy the application from a known-good artefact, rotate any credential in the container's configuration or datasource, and search for files written outside the deployment.
response.adequacy: Upgrading to 7.0.81 closes the write path but removes nothing already written through it, so a shell placed before remediation survives the upgrade untouched — which is why the response step cannot be collapsed into the patch step.

NIST-800-53-CM-7.gap: Least functionality is evidenced through build standards, package inventories and port exposure, none of which reach a servlet initialisation parameter. The single fact that decides exploitability on Windows Tomcat 7.0.0-7.0.79 — whether readonly is false in conf/web.xml — is invisible to every artefact a CM-7 assessment normally collects.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: Flaw remediation is discharged by installing the vendor's fixed release, and 7.0.81 is that release. Because Apache archived the 7.0.x branch on 2021-03-31, an instance that fully satisfies SI-2 sits on a line that will never receive another fix, so the control certifies as remediated a service whose remaining lifetime carries no patch path at all.

NIS2-Art21-vulnerability-handling.gap: The measure is met by an advisory-driven handling process, which works when the entity knows it runs Tomcat. Where a Tomcat 7.0.0-7.0.79 build is embedded in an appliance console or a packaged Java product, the CVE feed names a component the asset register does not list, and the handling process never binds the advisory to an owner.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: B4 is satisfied by demonstrating a managed configuration baseline for the container. This flaw lives entirely in the exception to that baseline — readonly=false, set deliberately so content can be published over PUT — and a B4 attestation evidences that a baseline exists without enumerating the instances holding a documented departure from it.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Application patching maturity measures how quickly the 2017 fixed release was adopted, and an instance on 7.0.81 or later scores well. The measure cannot register that the branch has been archived since 2021-03-31, and it gives no credit for the cheaper and more complete remediation of restoring readonly to true, which changes no version number at all.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.9.gap: Configuration management is evidenced by documented secure configurations and change control. Where that evidence is the documented baseline rather than a per-instance attestation of current state, the estate cannot produce the list of Windows Tomcat 7 instances that currently accept PUT — and against an EPSS of 0.99607 on 2026-08-17, not knowing the list is the exposure.

new_control_requirements.name: CONFIGURATION-SIDE-LIVE-PATCH-INVENTORY
new_control_requirements.description: For any web-fabric vulnerability with a configuration-side mitigation path: that path must be inventoried, tested, and deployable independent of the vendor-patch path. Operators cannot wait for nginx 1.30.1+ if a named-capture refactor mitigates immediately.
new_control_requirements.evidence: This Apache Tomcat entry has a configuration-side mitigation that is strictly stronger than the upgrade: restoring the Default servlet's readonly parameter to true removes HTTP PUT and the whole write path, on any 7.0.0-7.0.79 Windows instance, without moving off a branch Apache archived on 2021-03-31. An estate that can enumerate which instances have readonly=false can remediate the KEV entry CISA added 2022-03-25 in one configuration change; an estate that only tracks versions has to wait for an upgrade window on a dead branch.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CISA added the Apache Tomcat on Windows RCE to KEV on 2022-03-25 with a 2022-04-15 due date and knownRansomwareCampaignUse 'Known', and EPSS on 2026-08-17 stands at 0.99607 (99.946th percentile) against a maintained Nuclei template that scans for it continuously. The control's compensating-control branch is what makes a four-hour clock achievable on a Tomcat 7 estate: readonly=true plus a service restart lands far faster than an upgrade off an end-of-life branch.

CVE-2017-12617.name: Apache Tomcat Remote Code Execution Vulnerability (CVE-2017-12617)

attack_vector.description: A PUT to a path ending '.jsp/' slips past the Default servlet's JSP-upload restriction because the filter reads the request name rather than the file that gets written; the source lands as a JSP and the next GET compiles and runs it as the Tomcat service account. Two requests, no credential, four release lines.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; the request pair is unauthenticated. What the resulting web shell can do is bounded only by the identity the Tomcat process runs under.
attack_vector.complexity: high — AC:H; the one precondition is readonly=false on the Default servlet. No platform constraint applies, which is the difference from the Windows-scoped sibling flaw, and Metasploit ships both Java/Windows and Java/Linux targets.
attack_vector.ai_factor: None recorded. Apache's per-branch advisories credit no reporter for this entry, and neither the Metasploit module nor the Nuclei template indicates automated or AI-assisted discovery or weaponization.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Keeping the Default servlet's readonly parameter at true so PUT is never accepted, and where PUT is genuinely needed, upgrading to 9.0.1 or later and preferring a supported branch over 8.5.23, 8.0.47 or 7.0.82.
prevention.adequacy: Turning PUT off is complete and needs only a service restart, but the branch-selection half is the part operators skip: three of the four fixed releases land on lines Apache has since ended, so the fix can be applied correctly and still leave the service without a future patch path.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alerting on any PUT reaching a Tomcat context, with the trailing-slash '.jsp/' form treated as confirmed exploitation rather than reconnaissance.
detection.adequacy: The trailing-slash form has no legitimate use, so it is a clean signal, but it appears only in the access log — an instance whose logs are not shipped off-host loses the evidence the moment it is redeployed.

response.what_would_have_worked: Redeploying the application from a known-good artefact, rotating datasource and configuration credentials held by the container, and hunting for files written outside the deployment path.
response.adequacy: Upgrading closes the write path and removes nothing already written, so a shell dropped before remediation survives; the response step is the only one that reaches what the patch leaves behind.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: The control certifies remediation against the vendor's stated fixed release, and here the stated fixed release for the earlier Windows-scoped defect — 7.0.81 — falls inside this CVE's affected range of 7.0.0 through 7.0.81. An estate that did exactly what SI-2 asked between August and October 2017 was compliant and exploitable at the same moment, and nothing in the control detects that state.

NIST-800-53-CM-7.gap: Least functionality is assessed over installed software, running services and network exposure, and the capability being exploited is none of those — it is an init-param inside conf/web.xml. Because CM-7 evidence never descends to the servlet configuration, an estate can hold a complete least-functionality position while every one of its Tomcat instances accepts PUT.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: The measure is satisfied by reaching the per-branch fixed release, and there are four of them: 9.0.1, 8.5.23, 8.0.47 and 7.0.82. Three sit on branches Apache ended on 2018-06-30, 2021-03-31 and 2024-03-31, and nothing in a patch-management measure reopens a closed finding when the branch that carried the fix is retired underneath it.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: B4 is met by managed, documented configuration, and the underlying defect is not a configuration error at all — the servlet's own filter checks a name the attacker chooses instead of the file it writes. The only B4-actionable lever is refusing PUT, so the control is adequate exactly to the degree the estate has treated PUT as a capability requiring justification rather than a default to inherit.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Application patching maturity measures adoption latency after the September and October 2017 releases, so an instance on 8.5.23 scores as fully patched and keeps that score permanently. The model has no way to express that 8.5.x reached end of life on 2024-03-31, so its highest maturity rating and an unsupported container are compatible states.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: Technical vulnerability management is evidenced by scan coverage and remediation timelines, and a banner-reading scan flags every Tomcat in the four affected ranges without being able to tell which ones accept PUT. The result is a large finding set triaged on guesswork, when the single question that resolves it — is readonly false on this instance — is not something A.8.8 evidence is built to answer.

new_control_requirements.name: MITIGATION-ACTIVE-PATCH-PENDING-VERDICT-CLASS
new_control_requirements.description: Compliance verdicts must distinguish three states: (a) binary patch deployed (vulnerability eliminated), (b) vendor-mitigation rule active, no binary patch (residual risk: any defect in the mitigation rule reopens the vulnerability), (c) no mitigation, no patch (full exposure). Audit reports must surface (b) as a distinct compensating-control state with an associated time-bound action item, not as a 'patched per SLA' outcome.
new_control_requirements.evidence: An Apache Tomcat instance remediated by setting the Default servlet's readonly parameter back to true is in state (b), not state (a): the vulnerable upload path is unreachable but the 9.0.0.M1-9.0.0, 8.5.0-8.5.22, 8.0.0.RC1-8.0.46 or 7.0.0-7.0.81 code is still installed, and anyone re-enabling PUT for a publishing workflow reopens it silently. Recording that as 'patched per SLA' against the KEV entry CISA added 2022-03-25 hides both the residual risk and the fact that three of the four fixed branches are themselves end of life.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: This Apache Tomcat upload bypass carries an EPSS of 0.99988 on 2026-08-17 — the 99.984th percentile — with a Metasploit module targeting Java on Windows and Linux, two Exploit-DB entries and a maintained Nuclei template all available. CISA's KEV listing of 2022-03-25 with a 2022-04-15 due date sets a three-week clock against a flaw that any internet-wide scan finds in one PUT, and the control's compensating-control branch (readonly=true plus a service restart) is the only remediation that can land inside four hours on a Tomcat 7 or 8 estate.

CVE-2017-3881.name: Cisco IOS and IOS XE Remote Code Execution Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: CMP signalling rides inside Telnet options between cluster members, but the device processes those options on any Telnet connection and mishandles malformed ones. Malformed CMP options sent while opening a Telnet session either reload the device or execute code with elevated privileges; the published exploit reaches privilege level 15 on a Catalyst 2960 with no credential presented.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; the device only has to accept inbound Telnet on a VTY line. No account, no key and no prior access to the management network beyond routability.
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; the request is a Telnet option sequence with no race and no memory-layout dependency. Code execution is image-specific, demonstrated against Catalyst 2960 12.2(55)SE1 and 12.2(55)SE11, while the reload outcome reaches more broadly.
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Cisco attributes the finding to its own analysis of Vault 7 documents — human document review followed by code inspection — and the follow-on public exploit was written by a named outside researcher, with no automated or AI-assisted method claimed anywhere.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Removing telnet from 'transport input' on every VTY line and managing the devices over SSH, which Cisco states eliminates the exploit vector, alongside the per-platform fixed image resolved through the IOS Software Checker.
prevention.adequacy: Telnet removal is complete and instant against this vector, but it is a change to how the device is operated and can break scripted tooling and out-of-band console workflows that assume Telnet; the image upgrade is complete but reloads the switch, and for some listed platforms no fixed image exists.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alerting on inbound Telnet to network device VTY lines from outside the management segment, and correlating any device reload against change records and AAA authorization events.
detection.adequacy: Both signals require the devices to be shipping syslog and AAA accounting to a collector outside the device, because an attacker at privilege level 15 controls what the local buffer retains — and the reload outcome erases that buffer by itself.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating a confirmed hit as device compromise: compare the running and startup configuration against a known-good baseline, verify the image, and rotate every credential the device held or that transited it.
response.adequacy: An image upgrade does not remove configuration an attacker added at privilege level 15, and a switch that was exploited before remediation carries that change forward through the reload — which is why the baseline comparison cannot be folded into the upgrade step.

NIST-800-53-CM-7.gap: Least functionality is normally evidenced across servers and endpoints, and the network estate is assessed by a separate team against its own build standard. Nothing in a CM-7 package therefore lists which Catalyst, IE Industrial Ethernet or EtherSwitch service-module instances still admit Telnet, even though Cisco's stated mitigation is precisely to stop admitting it.

NIST-800-53-SC-7.gap: Boundary protection evidence concentrates on the perimeter, while the advisory's own alternative mitigations — VTY access-class lists and infrastructure ACLs — are configured on the device itself. An SC-7 attestation built from firewall rule reviews is entirely silent on whether a switch answers Telnet to the whole management VLAN.

NIS2-Art21-network-security.gap: The measure is met by documented segmentation and secure network management, and this flaw makes the management protocol the attack surface. Cisco confirmed PSIRT awareness of exploitation in 2017 and CISA listed the CVE on 2022-03-25, yet a network-security measure written around segmentation never produces the per-device VTY inventory that decides exposure.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: Secure configuration for network devices is evidenced by a build standard and sampled compliance, and Telnet acceptance on this platform generation is inherited from that standard rather than introduced against it. A B4 sample that checks banners, passwords and SNMP strings passes a device whose 'transport input' still admits the exact protocol Cisco names as the vector.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: The Essential Eight patching mitigations are written for operating systems and applications, and an assessor has to decide for themselves whether IOS on a switch or an SM-X service module belongs to either — the model gives no rule. Even once scoped in, Cisco delivers fixed software per platform and release train through the IOS Software Checker rather than as one version, so there is no single target for a latency metric to measure against.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.22.gap: Where network segregation is documented, reviewed and genuinely in place, it is the reason leaving Telnet enabled on the management VLAN reads as defensible. Segregation bounds the population that can open the session and closes nothing: a compromised jump host or an unmanaged monitoring box inside the management segment meets the vector's only precondition completely.

new_control_requirements.name: MITIGATION-ACTIVE-PATCH-PENDING-VERDICT-CLASS
new_control_requirements.description: Compliance verdicts must distinguish three states: (a) binary patch deployed (vulnerability eliminated), (b) vendor-mitigation rule active, no binary patch (residual risk: any defect in the mitigation rule reopens the vulnerability), (c) no mitigation, no patch (full exposure). Audit reports must surface (b) as a distinct compensating-control state with an associated time-bound action item, not as a 'patched per SLA' outcome.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Cisco states both halves of this control's problem in one advisory: 'There are no workarounds that address this vulnerability' and 'Disabling the Telnet protocol as an allowed protocol for incoming connections would eliminate the exploit vector.' A Catalyst or IE Industrial Ethernet switch with Telnet removed but still running an image vulnerable to CSCvd48893 is squarely in state (b) — anyone re-enabling Telnet for a maintenance task reopens a 9.8 pre-auth RCE that Cisco PSIRT confirmed was being exploited. Recording that switch as 'patched per SLA' against the 2022-03-25 KEV listing loses the distinction entirely.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Cisco published cisco-sa-20170317-cmp on 17 March 2017 and public exploit code followed on 10 April 2017; CISA added the CVE on 2022-03-25 with a 2022-04-15 due date, and EPSS on 2026-08-17 stands at 0.98975 (99.927th percentile). Because Cisco resolves fixed images per platform through the Software Checker and an IOS upgrade reloads the switch, the documented-compensating-control branch of this control is the only one that fits a four-hour clock: removing telnet from 'transport input' takes effect immediately and needs no outage window.

CVE-2017-6316.name: Citrix Multiple Products Remote Code Execution Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: The management web tier passes the session-cookie value into a shell command without neutralising metacharacters, so an HTTP request whose cookie contains a command substitution runs that command as root. CGISESSID is the cookie on NetScaler SD-WAN, CAKEPHP on CloudBridge; the published proof of concept posts it to login.cgi.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; the injection fires at the login endpoint, before any authentication decision, so no credential is presented at any point.
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; one HTTP request with a crafted cookie header. Nothing races, nothing is groomed, and the only variable is whether the attacker can reach the management interface.
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Both Exploit-DB entries credit an outside researcher, xort of Critical Start, and neither indicates automated tooling or AI assistance in discovery or exploit development.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Restricting the management interface to an operator segment or authenticated VPN so no untrusted host can present the cookie, and applying the fixed build named in CTX225990 for each product line in service.
prevention.adequacy: Reachability restriction is the whole exploit precondition and lands immediately, but it bounds rather than closes: anything inside the permitted segment can still send the request. The upgrade closes it, and needs both an entitled support account to identify the build and a WAN maintenance window to install it.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Inspecting requests to the appliance management interface for shell metacharacters in the session cookie, and alerting on root-owned shell processes spawned by the web tier.
detection.adequacy: The cookie signal is unambiguous because a session identifier has no legitimate reason to contain a backtick, but it needs a proxy or sensor in front of the management interface — the appliance's own logs are written by the tier the attacker just took as root.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating a confirmed hit as full compromise of the appliance: rebuild from vendor media rather than upgrade in place, and rotate every credential, certificate and key the unit held.
response.adequacy: An upgrade replaces the vulnerable code and preserves configuration, which is exactly where an attacker with root would leave persistence, so the rebuild path is the only one that reaches it — at the cost of reconstructing WAN policy from a known-good source.

NIST-800-53-SI-10.gap: Information input validation is attested over the inputs a design review recognises as user-supplied — parameters, bodies, uploads. The session cookie is treated as the application's own state, so it escapes that inventory entirely, and on these Citrix units it is the value that reaches a shell running as root.

NIST-800-53-SC-7.gap: Boundary protection evidence describes the enterprise perimeter, and an SD-WAN appliance is part of that perimeter rather than a host behind it. SC-7 as assessed therefore never establishes which internal segments can open an HTTP session to the unit's own management interface, which is the single fact that decides whether the published exploit is deliverable.

NIS2-Art21-network-security.gap: The measure is met by documenting WAN segmentation and secure management practice, and it treats the SD-WAN unit as a policy enforcement point. It does not require the entity to record that this enforcement point answers unauthenticated HTTP as root, nor to enumerate the segments that can reach it — which is where the remaining exposure lives after 2022-03-25.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: B4 is evidenced through vendor hardening guidance applied to the appliance build, and no setting in that guidance stops a cookie value reaching a system call. The control can be completely satisfied on a NetScaler SD-WAN or CloudBridge unit that a single crafted HTTP request turns into root shell access.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Patching maturity requires knowing the fixed version and the elapsed time since its release, and CTX225990 — NVD's listed vendor reference for this CVE — requires an entitled Citrix account to read. Without that account an assessor cannot state the target build, so the appliance is scored against an unverified version or quietly excluded from the patching population.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.28.gap: Secure coding is held by the operator for code the operator writes, and the defect is in a purchased appliance's web tier. A.8.28 gives the buyer no verification mechanism over the supplier's practice, so the control reads as fully implemented while the supplied product concatenates an attacker-controlled cookie into a root-privileged shell command.

new_control_requirements.name: PERIMETER-COMPROMISE-REBUILD-NOT-PATCH
new_control_requirements.description: Pre-rehearsed IR runbook for any perimeter device that suffers a pre-auth RCE CVE in active exploitation MUST default to config-exfil + rebuild + credential rotation, not patch-in-place. Patch-in-place leaves attacker-installed implants intact.
new_control_requirements.evidence: A NetScaler SD-WAN or CloudBridge unit is a perimeter device by construction — it terminates the WAN path — and this CVE is a pre-auth root RCE on it, listed by CISA on 2022-03-25 with working exploits public on Exploit-DB since July 2017. Upgrading to the build named in CTX225990 replaces the vulnerable code and carries the existing configuration forward, which is precisely where an attacker holding root would have left persistence, so patch-in-place is the wrong default for a unit that was reachable during the exposure window.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CISA listed this Citrix multi-product RCE on 2022-03-25 with a 2022-04-15 due date; EPSS on 2026-08-17 is 0.72596 at the 99.393rd percentile. The fixed builds sit behind the access-restricted CTX225990 and the upgrade needs a WAN maintenance window, so the patch branch of this control cannot land in four hours — the documented-compensating-control branch can, by removing the management interface of every SD-WAN, CloudBridge and XenMobile Server instance from segments with no operational need to reach it.

CVE-2017-6334.name: NETGEAR DGN2200 Devices OS Command Injection Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: The gateway's DNS-lookup diagnostic page passes its host_name field into a shell unneutralised, so a POST to /dnslookup.cgi carrying 'www.google.com;<command>' executes that command on the router. The attacker authenticates first over HTTP Basic, which on a unit still holding the shipped default credential is not a meaningful step.
attack_vector.privileges_required: low — PR:L; the exploit and the Metasploit module both authenticate before injecting. This is only a real barrier on units whose administrative credential was changed from the factory default.
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; a single POST with a semicolon in a form field. The constraint is reachability of the administration interface, which is unconditional from the LAN and depends on remote-management settings from the WAN.
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Exploit-DB 41459 credits SivertPL and the Metasploit module records the same attribution for discovery; the finding reads as manual inspection of a diagnostic CGI, with no automated or AI-assisted method claimed.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Replacing the DGN2200 with a supported gateway, which is what CISA's required action for this entry calls for; interim, changing the administrative credential off the shipped default and disabling WAN-side management.
prevention.adequacy: Replacement is the only complete answer because no fixed firmware exists. The interim measures remove the easy authentication step and the internet-side path, but every client on the LAN still reaches /dnslookup.cgi, so they narrow the attacker population rather than closing the flaw.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Watching for POSTs to /dnslookup.cgi carrying shell metacharacters in host_name, and for the gateway's DNS or DHCP configuration changing outside a maintenance action.
detection.adequacy: Both are observable in principle, and on this hardware the practical obstacles are concrete: the device has no agent, its log storage is local and small, and where the unit sits at a remote-worker site nothing is positioned in front of it to see the request unless a collector was deployed there deliberately.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating a confirmed hit as loss of the gateway: replace the unit, rebuild its configuration from scratch rather than restoring a backup, and rotate any credential that traversed it while it was exposed.
response.adequacy: Restoring a saved configuration onto a replacement carries forward whatever the attacker changed, and an attacker holding the gateway held DNS for every client behind it — so the credential-rotation scope is every account used from that site during the window, and establishing that scope depends on authentication records held somewhere other than the gateway.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: Flaw remediation is evidenced by patch coverage against available vendor updates, and no update is available for any DGN2200 revision. The control's own reporting therefore renders this device as clean — 'no applicable update' — while CISA's required action for the same CVE is to disconnect it, and SI-2 has no field in which that instruction can be recorded.

NIST-800-53-SC-7.gap: Boundary protection is nominally satisfied because the site has a gateway performing NAT and filtering. The gateway is the vulnerable asset, so a command injection on it inverts the control rather than evading it: the device attesting the boundary is the device an attacker now owns, along with DNS and routing for every client behind it.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: A patch-management measure is met by documented cadence and deployment evidence, and it has no object here because NETGEAR published no fix for this defect. The measure cannot fail, which is the problem: the entity's compliance record is untouched by a permanently open 8.8 injection whose only remedy is decommissioning.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: B4 is partially achievable on this device — the default credential can be changed and remote management turned off — and the resulting hardening record reads well. It records a configuration state while the vulnerable CGI stays reachable from every LAN client, so the better the B4 evidence looks, the more it obscures that the only real remediation is removing the unit.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Patching maturity is assessed over the operating systems and applications the assessment can see, and a consumer ADSL gateway at a remote-worker site is enrolled in nothing and scanned by nothing. The device is outside the measured population entirely, so the Essential Eight score of an estate holding hundreds of them is unaffected by any of them.

ISO-27001-2022-A.5.21.gap: Supply-chain security is evidenced by supplier assessment at procurement and by contractual security terms. Neither addresses the failure mode that occurred: the supplier ceased issuing firmware while the product stayed in service, converting an 8.8 command injection with public exploit code into a permanent condition that no supplier questionnaire completed at purchase time would have surfaced.

ISO-27001-2022-A.5.7.gap: Threat intelligence is met by consuming vendor and national advisories, and NVD's reference set for this CVE contains no NETGEAR advisory to consume. The events that actually mattered were an Exploit-DB publication in February 2017 under a named handle and a Metasploit module derived from it, so an intake keyed on vendor disclosure had nothing to ingest for five years until CISA listed it.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CISA listed the NETGEAR DGN2200 command injection on 2022-03-25 with a 2022-04-15 due date, and its required action is 'The impacted product is end-of-life and should be disconnected if still in use' — so the patch branch of this control is unavailable and the documented-compensating-control branch is the entire clock. On a DGN2200 v1 through v4 at or below firmware 10.0.0.50, with EPSS at 0.72199 on 2026-08-17 and exploit code public since February 2017, the compensating controls that can land in hours are removing the default credential, disabling WAN-side management, and isolating the segment the unit serves pending replacement.

new_control_requirements.name: MITIGATION-ACTIVE-PATCH-PENDING-VERDICT-CLASS
new_control_requirements.description: Compliance verdicts must distinguish three states: (a) binary patch deployed (vulnerability eliminated), (b) vendor-mitigation rule active, no binary patch (residual risk: any defect in the mitigation rule reopens the vulnerability), (c) no mitigation, no patch (full exposure). Audit reports must surface (b) as a distinct compensating-control state with an associated time-bound action item, not as a 'patched per SLA' outcome.
new_control_requirements.evidence: A DGN2200 that has had its default credential changed and WAN management disabled is in state (b) and can never reach state (a), because no fixed firmware exists for any of the four revisions — and the residual risk is precise rather than theoretical: every client on the LAN the unit serves still reaches /dnslookup.cgi with an authenticated session. A device with no state (a) available needs the time-bound action item this control demands to be a replacement date, or the risk acceptance never expires and the gateway stays in service indefinitely.

CVE-2018-0125.name: Cisco VPN Routers Remote Code Execution Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: One crafted HTTP request to the RV132W or RV134W web management interface reaches code that trusts the request data, and the attacker gets arbitrary execution as root on the branch router or forces it into a reload. The compromised asset is the WAN termination, the NAT and firewall policy and the VPN endpoint for everything behind it.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; the interface answers before any credential is presented, which is why an administrator-password policy on the router changes nothing about this path
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; no race, no memory grooming and no prior foothold. The only variable is whether the management interface is reachable from where the attacker sits, and on the LAN side it always is
attack_vector.ai_factor: Cisco credits Beyond Security's SecuriTeam Secure Disclosure program and an independent researcher. That is a paid disclosure channel, not automated discovery, and the advisory describes no tooling.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Upgrading both models to firmware 1.0.1.11 and rebooting onto it, with the web management interface restricted to an administrative segment and WAN-side remote management disabled in the interim.
prevention.adequacy: Sufficient to close the path, but it only fires if the router is in the inventory the patch programme reads. Four years separate the February 2018 firmware from the exploitation Cisco recorded in March 2022.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Remote syslog from the router to a collector off the device, with alerting on unscheduled reloads and on configuration changes that have no corresponding administrator session.
detection.adequacy: Partial. It records the reload and the config change but not the request that caused them, and it only helps where remote logging was configured before the event — telemetry left on the device is discarded by the reload the same defect can trigger.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating an exposed unit as compromised rather than patched: rebuild the configuration from a known-good baseline instead of carrying it across the upgrade, and rotate the administrative password and any pre-shared key held on the device.
response.adequacy: This is the step that removes attacker-planted configuration, and it is skipped wherever the firmware upgrade is read as completion. It costs a second outage on top of the reboot.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: An SI-2 programme can be fully implemented and still never see this device. Cisco published the fix in February 2018 and only appended the exploitation note in March 2022, and throughout that interval the control is measured against whatever software inventory the organisation maintains. Where that inventory is built from servers, endpoints and their installed applications, a branch RV132W procured as network hardware appears nowhere in it, produces no flaw-remediation ticket, and leaves the control reporting green on a router still running its shipped firmware.

NIST-800-53-SC-7.gap: SC-7 is assessed by examining the rules that mediate traffic crossing a boundary, and every one of those rules on an RV134W lives on the RV134W. A request addressed to the router's own management interface is not traffic crossing the boundary; it is traffic terminating on the enforcement point. Root on the device rewrites the firewall and NAT policy that the assessment sampled, so the artefact the auditor reviewed becomes attacker-controlled output rather than a control.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: Article 21 asks for measures proportionate to risk, and proportionality is where this device loses. Where a branch VPN router is ranked below the application servers it fronts, it inherits a longer patch window — yet the defect needs one unauthenticated HTTP request to reach root, and the same request can reload the device and take the site's connectivity with it. On that ranking, the fastest path to compromise is given the slowest clock.

NIS2-Art21-incident-handling.gap: The incident-handling obligation presumes the affected system can be interrogated after the fact. This router logs locally, and the flaw includes a reload primitive, so the operator's first symptom — the device restarting — is also the event that clears the evidence. Unless remote syslog to an off-device collector was configured before March 2022, an organisation can meet the procedural requirement in full and still have nothing to analyse when the RV132W comes back up.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: B4 expects known weaknesses to be removed by maintaining secure configuration, and upgrading two SKUs to 1.0.1.11 satisfies that at trivial cost. The failure is upstream of the control: CAF assessments scope to the systems supporting the essential service, and where a branch demarcation router is treated as connectivity plumbing rather than as such a system, it is excluded before any B4 judgement is made. The weakness is not tolerated by B4, it is simply never presented to it.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: The Essential Eight separates patching operating systems from patching applications, and network appliance firmware sits in neither list unless the organisation extends the population itself. An estate can therefore evidence a high maturity level against both mitigation strategies while every RV132W and RV134W in its branch sites runs firmware from before 1.0.1.11 — the assessment is accurate about what it measured and silent about the device that terminates the branch VPN.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: A.8.8 requires timely information about technical vulnerabilities in the systems in use, and an audit that accepts the existence of an advisory-intake process as evidence never tests that process's coverage. Cisco publishes small-business router advisories on a separate stream from its enterprise platform advisories, so an intake subscribed only to the latter receives neither cisco-sa-20180207-rv13x nor its March 2022 exploitation update, and A.8.8 is signed off as operating throughout.

new_control_requirements.name: PERIMETER-DEVICE-ZERODAY-SLA-TIER
new_control_requirements.description: Compliance frameworks must define a distinct patch SLA tier for pre-auth RCE on perimeter-trust-boundary devices (firewalls, VPN concentrators, WAFs, edge load-balancers). Tier requirement: vendor-mitigation deployed within 4 hours of KEV listing OR isolation of the vulnerable interface; standard 14/30-day SLAs do not apply because the device IS the trust boundary.
new_control_requirements.evidence: The Cisco RV132W and RV134W are VPN termination points at a branch edge, which puts them squarely in the device class this tier exists for. Cisco shipped firmware 1.0.1.11 in February 2018 and recorded attempted in-the-wild exploitation four years later in March 2022; CISA added the CVE to KEV on 2022-03-25 with a 2022-04-15 due date, and EPSS still reads 0.55186 at the 98.944th percentile on 2026-08-17. A standard appliance patch window measured in weeks is the wrong instrument for an unauthenticated request that reaches root on the device holding the site's firewall policy, and Cisco published no workaround, so the tier's alternative — isolating the vulnerable interface — means disabling WAN-side management and restricting the interface to an administrative segment until the reboot lands.

new_control_requirements.name: PERIMETER-COMPROMISE-REBUILD-NOT-PATCH
new_control_requirements.description: Pre-rehearsed IR runbook for any perimeter device that suffers a pre-auth RCE CVE in active exploitation MUST default to config-exfil + rebuild + credential rotation, not patch-in-place. Patch-in-place leaves attacker-installed implants intact.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Cisco's own advisory for the RV132W and RV134W records attempted exploitation in the wild in March 2022, so units whose management interface was reachable during that period are candidates for having already been touched. The upgrade to 1.0.1.11 carries the existing configuration forward, which means an attacker-added port forward, VPN peer or administrative account survives the remediation that closes the defect. The runbook step that matters here is rebuilding the router's configuration from a known-good baseline and rotating its administrative password and pre-shared keys, rather than reading the post-reboot firmware version as closure.

CVE-2018-0147.name: Cisco Secure Access Control System Java Deserialization Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: ACS rebuilds a Java object graph supplied by the network without restricting which classes it will instantiate, so a crafted serialized object drives gadgets already on the appliance's classpath into running operating-system commands as root. The prize is the AAA server itself: the RADIUS and TACACS+ shared secrets, the administrative accounts and the authorisation policy for the network devices that trust it.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none on releases before 5.8 Patch 7 — PR:N, scored 9.8 by Cisco; on 5.8 Patch 7 and 8 the same path requires authentication first and Cisco scores it 8.8
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; deserialization is deterministic once a usable gadget chain exists on the appliance image, so the constraint is network reachability of the ACS web tier rather than any runtime uncertainty
attack_vector.ai_factor: Reported by Mikhail Klyuchnikov and Yury Aleynov of Positive Technologies. Two named human researchers at a security firm; the advisory describes no automated analysis.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Applying the 5.8.0.32.9 cumulative patch, and in the interim restricting the ACS web tier so it answers only from the network-administration segment, since Cisco publishes no on-box workaround.
prevention.adequacy: The patch closes the path completely. Its cost is an outage of network-device authentication during the window.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alerting on shell or root process creation on the ACS appliance with no matching administrative session, and shipping ACS logs to a collector on a different trust boundary than the appliance itself.
detection.adequacy: Limited by what an appliance exposes. ACS is a closed image with no operator-installed endpoint agent, so the practical telemetry is what it forwards plus network-side observation of who is reaching its web tier.

response.what_would_have_worked: Rotating every RADIUS and TACACS+ shared secret and every ACS administrative credential for any instance reachable during the exposure window, and reviewing the authorisation policy against a known-good copy.
response.adequacy: Necessary and expensive: the shared secrets are configured on every network device that authenticates against ACS, so rotation is a fleet-wide change. Patching without it leaves credentials that root on the appliance already exposed.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: SI-2 is satisfied by remediating within the organisation's defined timeframe. Cisco published the advisory in March 2018 and the exploitation note in March 2022, and across those four years an ACS below 5.8.0.32.9 can consume every scheduled window and still be recorded as remediated on time, because the control measures adherence to the window and not the appliance's actual patch level.

NIST-800-53-IA-2.gap: This is the control ACS implements, and on releases before 5.8 Patch 7 the vulnerable path runs before it is ever consulted. An IA-2 assessment can evidence unique identification of every ACS administrator, multifactor on the management interface and complete authentication logging, and none of that touches an attacker who sends a serialized object to the web tier and receives root. The account model the control examines is bypassed rather than abused, which is why the attestation passes and the exposure is unchanged.

NIST-800-53-SC-7.gap: Discharging SC-7 for ACS with the observation that the appliance carries no internet exposure states something true and insufficient. The exploit precondition is a route to the ACS web tier from anywhere, so a compromised workstation, a contractor laptop or a jump host inside the permitted segment satisfies it in full. Cisco offers no on-box workaround, which means the internal reachability boundary is the only variable available before 5.8.0.32.9 lands — and it is the one an internal-versus-external boundary assessment does not examine.

NIS2-Art21-vulnerability-handling.gap: A vulnerability-handling process is evidenced by intake, triage and a tracked disposition.
