new_control_requirements.evidence: Juniper's own advisory makes this control's premise explicit rather than inferred: it publishes the httpd.log patterns "=*;*&" and "*%3b*&" as the indicators of compromise, then states that a skilled attacker would likely remove these entries from the local log file, effectively eliminating any reliable signature that the device had been attacked. On a Junos edge device the log in question is /var/log/httpd.log and its rotations httpd.log.0.gz and httpd.log.1.gz, all held on the box the attacker is executing on. Forwarding httpd.log to a collector on a separate management plane is what turns the vendor's published indicator from a pattern that only helps against an unskilled attacker into evidence that survives, and it is the only way to answer retrospectively whether a device exposed before its train's fixed release was actually reached.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Juniper shipped fixed releases across every affected train and CISA listed CVE-2020-1631 on 2022-03-25 with a 2022-04-15 due date, so the KEV listing is the later trigger. This is one of the cases where the documented-compensating-control branch is strictly better than the patch branch on speed: Juniper states devices with HTTP/HTTPS services disabled are not affected, so disabling the service meets the four-hour window on a device that cannot take a reboot, whereas a Junos upgrade requires one. Verified is the operative word for both halves - `show system processes | match http` returning httpd-gk or httpd is the check that a service-disable actually landed, and the per-train fixed release is what an upgrade has to be measured against, since Juniper publishes a different fixed build for each of 12.3 through 20.1 rather than one target.

CVE-2020-1956.name: Apache Kylin OS Command Injection Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: An authenticated low-privilege Kylin user sends a cube-migration request whose project name carries shell metacharacters; Kylin builds a kylin.sh command line by concatenation and the shell executes the injected command as the service account.
attack_vector.privileges_required: low — PR:L; a session holding MANAGEMENT or ADMIN on any single project reaches the migrate API
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; one crafted request, no race or memory-corruption primitive needed
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Discovered by RIPS Technologies / SonarSource via static code analysis, which is human-led review, not AI-assisted discovery.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Upgrading to Kylin 2.6.6 / 3.0.2, which validates the migrate input, and restricting project MANAGEMENT/ADMIN grants to trusted operators.
prevention.adequacy: The upgrade eliminates the sink; the privilege restriction only narrows who can reach it and does not fix the concatenation.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alerting on the Kylin JVM spawning shell/child processes and on migrate requests containing shell metacharacters.
detection.adequacy: Process-spawn telemetry catches the post-injection stage; it does not prevent the first execution and depends on the Kylin host shipping process logs.

response.what_would_have_worked: Rotating credentials reachable from the Kylin host and reviewing job/config artifacts written since the exposure window.
response.adequacy: Response bounds damage after execution but assumes the intrusion was detected; a quiet single-command run may leave little trace.

NIST-800-53-SI-10.gap: An SI-10 input-validation attestation at the web tier does not reach the shell sink where the project name is concatenated into kylin.sh; only the 2.6.6/3.0.2 code fix enforces the check, so the control reads satisfied while an affected build stays exploitable.

NIS2-Art21-vulnerability-handling.gap: Vulnerability handling under Art 21 presumes advisory feeds surface exploitable flaws promptly, but CVE-2020-1956 sat between its 2020-05-22 NVD publication and its 2022-03-25 KEV listing at EPSS 0.97337 — a nearly-certain exploit an advisory-only program would have deprioritized for twenty-two months.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: CAF B4 seeks services resilient to known attack classes, yet no configuration of Kylin 2.3.0-3.0.1 removes the injection; resilience is only reached by moving to the 2.6.6 or 3.0.2 build, so a B4 self-assessment on an affected version overstates the actual posture.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: The patch-applications control targets exactly this profile — a network-reachable application with a public exploit — but delivers nothing until the 2.6.6/3.0.2 upgrade lands and the JVM restarts; a maturity rating counts the policy, not whether this particular Kylin instance was actually raised off the vulnerable range.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.28.gap: A.8.28 secure-coding controls govern the operator's own development, but the concatenation defect is in the upstream Kylin product, so an A.8.28 program can be fully in place while the deployed engine still passes a REST parameter into an OS command.

OWASP-Top-10-2021-A03.gap: A03 injection coverage via a WAF assumes web-shaped payloads, but the backtick lives in a REST path segment feeding kylin.sh, which the Nuclei template reaches at /kylin/api/cubes/{cube}/{project}/migrate.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Apache Kylin CVE-2020-1956 (CVSS 8.8, EPSS 0.97337) shipped a fix in 2.6.6/3.0.2 in 2020 yet only reached KEV on 2022-03-25; a KEV-triggered SLA forces the upgrade-and-restart to a bounded clock instead of leaving a 99.9th-percentile exploit path unremediated across releases.

CVE-2020-2021.name: Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS Authentication Bypass Vulnerability (CVE-2020-2021)

attack_vector.description: With SAML SSO enabled and IdP-certificate validation disabled, an unauthenticated network attacker submits a crafted SAML assertion that PAN-OS accepts without proper signature verification, gaining a legitimate user session or, against the web UI, administrator access.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; only network access to the SAML-authenticating service is needed
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; the sole gating condition is the device configuration (SAML in use, 'Validate Identity Provider Certificate' unchecked)
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Reported by Monash University researchers Salman Khan and Cameron Duck via coordinated disclosure.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Disabling SAML authentication, or — where the IdP signing certificate is CA-signed — configuring the Identity Provider Certificate and enabling 'Validate Identity Provider Certificate'; then upgrading to PAN-OS 8.1.15/9.0.9/9.1.3, and migrating EoL 8.0 devices.
prevention.adequacy: Where the IdP signing certificate is self-signed the advisory states that the 'Validate Identity Provider Certificate' option cannot be enabled, leaving only disabling SAML or the upgrade; the upgrade removes the defect permanently, but the 8.0 line has no fix and must be replaced.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Correlating gateway/web-UI logins against IdP authentication events and alerting on sessions with no matching primary auth.
detection.adequacy: Detects a forged session after the fact; it depends on the IdP and firewall logs being centralized and time-correlated.

response.what_would_have_worked: Invalidating active sessions, rotating administrator credentials, and auditing configuration changes since the exposure window.
response.adequacy: Bounds an admin-level compromise but assumes detection; because integrity of regular-user sessions is not affected, the initial access may look like a normal login.

NIST-800-53-IA-5-Federated.gap: Federated IA-5 is nominally met by configuring SAML SSO, but the assertion-verification that IA-5 depends on hinges on a per-profile option; on PAN-OS below 8.1.15/9.0.9/9.1.3 an unverified signature is accepted, so the control passes while the trust it certifies is absent. The PAN-OS 9.1 admin guide states: "If your IdP signing certificate is a self-signed certificate, there is no chain of trust; as a result, you cannot enable this option."

NIS2-Art-21-Federated-Identity.gap: A NIS2 federated-identity control reads as satisfied whenever SSO is deployed, yet CVE-2020-2021 lets an unauthenticated attacker forge an accepted GlobalProtect assertion on PAN-OS 8.1 before 8.1.15, 9.0 before 9.0.9 and 9.1 before 9.1.3 — the operator believes end-to-end verification is in force when it is not.

UK-CAF-B2.gap: CAF B2 is undercut because the access-enforcement point itself — the firewall authenticating VPN and management access — accepts a forged identity, up to administrator on the web UI; no downstream authorization control can recover once the authentication decision is bypassed at the gateway.

AU-ISM-1559-IdP.gap: ISM 1559 is treated as met once IdP integration exists, but on an affected PAN-OS with validation disabled the trust anchor is missing entirely and any assertion is honoured; a compliant-on-paper SSO integration is materially broken until the validation toggle is confirmed set.

ISO-27001-2022-A.5.16-Federated.gap: A.5.16 federated identity management is asserted by the presence of SAML SSO, yet the CVSS 10.0 flaw means unsigned or unverified identities are accepted while IdP-certificate validation is off; the control is nominally covered and materially inadequate until validation is enforced or the fixed build is deployed.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: SI-2 flaw remediation assumes every affected branch is patchable, but PAN-OS 8.0 is end-of-life with no fix; a remediation plan that queues 8.0 alongside 8.1/9.0/9.1 for a patch will never close those devices, whose only terminal remediation is migration to a supported release.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: PAN-OS CVE-2020-2021 is a CVSS 10.0 authentication bypass on internet-facing GlobalProtect gateways, KEV-listed 2022-03-25 with known ransomware use; a KEV-tied SLA forces the 8.1.15/9.0.9/9.1.3 upgrade — or, on a CA-signed IdP certificate, the advisory's configuration route — onto a bounded clock rather than an appliance patch window, and puts EoL 8.0 units on a migration clock instead.

CVE-2020-2506.name: QNAP Helpdesk Improper Access Control Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: An unauthorized actor reaches privileged functionality in the QNAP Helpdesk add-on that should require authorization it does not hold, gaining privileges or reading sensitive information on the QTS appliance.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none stated — PR:N in the NVD vector; the practical gate is that Helpdesk is installed and reachable
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; a single request against the exposed functionality, though public reproduction detail is thin
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Reported to QNAP by researcher Jose Antonio Pérez Piedra.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Updating Helpdesk to 3.0.3 via the App Center, or uninstalling the app where unused, and keeping the QTS management surface off untrusted networks.
prevention.adequacy: The update fixes the authorization check; removing the app eliminates the surface entirely, which is the stronger control where Helpdesk is not needed.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Monitoring the Helpdesk app for access outside its scope and for privilege changes not tied to an admin session.
detection.adequacy: NAS appliances offer limited process-level telemetry, so detection leans on QTS event logs that may not capture add-on-level authorization bypass.

response.what_would_have_worked: Reviewing accounts and shares for unauthorized changes and rotating any credentials the Helpdesk app could reach during the exposure window.
response.adequacy: Bounds disclosure after the fact but assumes the access was noticed; a read-only information leak may leave no durable artifact.

NIST-800-53-AC-3.gap: AC-3 is attested at the QTS account layer, but the Helpdesk add-on before 3.0.3 fails to enforce authorization on privileged functionality of its own, so the appliance's access-enforcement evidence does not reach the surface where the CVSS 9.8 bypass lives.

NIS2-Art21-vulnerability-management.gap: Vulnerability management under Art 21 assumes reachable components are inventoried, yet Helpdesk is an optional App-Center add-on installed and updated separately from QTS firmware; the fix in 3.0.3 was available from 2020-10-07 while the flaw did not surface on KEV until 2022-03-25.

UK-CAF-B2.gap: A CAF B2 review scoped to the NAS user and permission model misses that the privilege break is inside the Helpdesk app rather than in QTS; the account controls can be sound while an installed add-on grants access those accounts were never given.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: The patch-applications control is rated on policy coverage, but a QTS estate that patches base firmware and leaves Helpdesk on a pre-3.0.3 build still carries the CVSS 9.8 access-control flaw; the maturity level does not distinguish base-OS patching from add-on-app patching.

ISO-27001-2022-A.5.15.gap: A.5.15 is asserted through the appliance's role model, yet the Helpdesk flaw lets an actor obtain privileges or read data without traversing that model, so the control is nominally covered by account policy and materially bypassed until the add-on reaches 3.0.3.

NIST-800-53-AC-6.gap: An AC-6 least-privilege review of QTS accounts passes cleanly while Helpdesk before 3.0.3 exposes privileged functions to unauthorized callers; the component grants access the least-privilege model never sanctioned, which an account-scoped attestation cannot see.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: QNAP Helpdesk CVE-2020-2506 (CVSS 9.8) shipped a fix in Helpdesk 3.0.3 on 2020-10-07 but only reached KEV on 2022-03-25; a KEV-triggered SLA forces the App-Center update — or removal of the add-on — onto a bounded clock instead of leaving an access-control bypass on an internet-adjacent NAS.

CVE-2020-25223.name: Sophos SG UTM Remote Code Execution Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: An unauthenticated attacker POSTs to /var (which rewrites to webadmin.plx without the SID sanitizer) with a SID like "|cmd|"; Perl's open() on that string executes the command as root on the UTM.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; unauthenticated network access to WebAdmin
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; the /var rewrite deterministically bypasses the InputSed filter that would otherwise strip the pipe
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Fix shipped by Sophos in September 2020; the preauth-RCE mechanism was reconstructed and published by Atredis Partners in 2021 via binary diffing.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Applying the Up2Date MR fix (v9.705 MR5 / v9.607 MR7 / v9.511 MR11) and restricting WebAdmin to a management network.
prevention.adequacy: The MR update removes the /var bypass; restricting WebAdmin reachability narrows who can send the POST but does not fix the sink.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alerting on POSTs to /var carrying a piped SID and on the webadmin/confd tree spawning shells.
detection.adequacy: Catches the request and the post-exploitation stage, but a compromised UTM can tamper with its own local logs, so off-box telemetry is needed.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating a confirmed-hit UTM as fully compromised: rebuild, rotate credentials that transited it, and audit configuration changes.
response.adequacy: A root-level preauth RCE on a perimeter device warrants rebuild-not-patch; patching in place leaves any implant intact.

NIST-800-53-SI-10.gap: SI-10 is nominally met by the product's InputSed filter, but that filter is bound to the webadmin.plx route while /var reaches the same handler unfiltered; a present-but-bypassable validation control passes an audit yet still lets a piped SID reach Perl's open().

NIST-800-53-SC-7.gap: SC-7 boundary protection cannot compensate here because the UTM is itself the boundary being attacked; an unauthenticated POST to /var runs as root on the firewall, so segmentation around it is irrelevant to a flaw in its own WebAdmin.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: Art 21 patch management reads as covered wherever Up2Date is enabled, but the September-2020 fix only protects units that actually took the MR build and rebooted; a UTM with automatic updates off carried a preauth-root RCE from that fix until the 2022-03-25 KEV listing and beyond.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: CAF B4 expects the management plane of a security appliance to resist unauthenticated command injection, yet no configuration of an affected SG UTM removes the /var bypass; B4 is only truly met once the vendor MR update is applied.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: The patch-applications maturity rating counts the update policy rather than the delivered state, so an estate can rate well while a specific internet-facing UTM still runs below v9.705 MR5 / v9.607 MR7 / v9.511 MR11 with a public Metasploit module against it.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: A.8.8 is asserted by having a vulnerability-management process, but closing this flaw requires that process to have delivered the specific MR fix and rebooted the appliance; the attestation is met on paper while a UTM on an older MR stays exploitable to unauthenticated root.

new_control_requirements.name: PERIMETER-COMPROMISE-REBUILD-NOT-PATCH
new_control_requirements.description: Pre-rehearsed IR runbook for any perimeter device that suffers a pre-auth RCE CVE in active exploitation MUST default to config-exfil + rebuild + credential rotation, not patch-in-place. Patch-in-place leaves attacker-installed implants intact.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Sophos SG UTM CVE-2020-25223 is an unauthenticated root RCE on a perimeter firewall with a public Metasploit module and Nuclei template, KEV-listed 2022-03-25; a UTM that was reachable while unpatched must be rebuilt and its transiting credentials rotated, because the Up2Date MR fix closes the /var path but removes nothing already planted as root.

new_control_requirements.name: PERIMETER-DEVICE-ZERODAY-SLA-TIER
new_control_requirements.description: Compliance frameworks must define a distinct patch SLA tier for pre-auth RCE on perimeter-trust-boundary devices (firewalls, VPN concentrators, WAFs, edge load-balancers). Tier requirement: vendor-mitigation deployed within 4 hours of KEV listing OR isolation of the vulnerable interface; standard 14/30-day SLAs do not apply because the device IS the trust boundary.
new_control_requirements.evidence: SG UTM CVE-2020-25223 sits on a perimeter-trust-boundary firewall at EPSS 0.96693 with unauthenticated root execution; a standard appliance patch window is the wrong tier — either the MR update lands fast or WebAdmin's reachability is restricted, which is exactly the distinct perimeter SLA this control defines.

attack_vector.description: An unauthenticated attacker sends a crafted HTTP request to the SonicOS management or SSL VPN interface, overflowing a stack buffer to crash the service and, potentially, execute code on the firewall.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; unauthenticated network access to the web/VPN interface
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; a single crafted request triggers the overflow, though reliable RCE beyond DoS requires defeating memory protections
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. The SonicWall CNA record for CVE-2020-5135 carries no credits field, and the SNWLID-2020-0010 page returns no advisory body to a direct fetch.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Applying the branch-correct SonicOS hotfix from SNWLID-2020-0010 and restricting the management/SSL-VPN interface to trusted sources.
prevention.adequacy: The firmware fixes the overflow; interface restriction reduces who can send the request but does not remove the flaw on an unpatched build.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alerting on SonicOS service crashes/restarts and on malformed inbound HTTP to the web/VPN front end.
detection.adequacy: Crash telemetry is a strong signal for the DoS outcome but arrives after the impact and relies on off-box logging that a crashed device cannot guarantee.

response.what_would_have_worked: Failing over to a standby firewall, applying the hotfix, and reviewing for any post-crash anomalous behavior consistent with attempted code execution.
response.adequacy: Restores availability but cannot rule out RCE without deeper forensic review of the appliance.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: SI-2 assumes one fix per flaw, but SonicOS spans several branches (Gen 6 6.5.4/6.5.1/6.0.5, SonicOSv, Gen 7) each needing its own SNWLID-2020-0010 hotfix; a remediation applied to one branch leaves devices on the others crashable, which a single-build attestation hides.

NIS2-Art21-network-security.gap: A NIS2 network-security posture treats the firewall as an enforcing control, yet the overflow makes the firewall a target an unauthenticated request can take offline; availability of the boundary device is assumed by the control and directly attacked by the flaw.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: CAF B4 expects the exposed HTTP/SSL-VPN service to withstand malformed input, but on an affected SonicOS build a crafted request overflows a stack buffer; no configuration hardens the parser, so B4 is only met after the branch-correct firmware is applied.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: The patch-applications maturity rating counts the update policy, not whether each internet-facing SonicWall was actually raised past its affected build before the 2022-03-15 KEV clock; a well-rated estate can still run an unpatched SSL-VPN portal.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: A.8.8 is asserted by having a firmware-update process, but this flaw closes only when that process delivers the branch-correct hotfix and reboots the appliance; the attestation reads satisfied while a firewall on an unpatched branch stays crashable by one request.

NIST-800-53-SC-7.gap: SC-7 boundary protection cannot defend the boundary device against an attack on its own management/VPN interface; segmentation around the firewall is irrelevant when the crafted HTTP request targets the firewall itself, so restricting that interface's exposure is the operative control.

new_control_requirements.name: PERIMETER-DEVICE-ZERODAY-SLA-TIER
new_control_requirements.description: Compliance frameworks must define a distinct patch SLA tier for pre-auth RCE on perimeter-trust-boundary devices (firewalls, VPN concentrators, WAFs, edge load-balancers). Tier requirement: vendor-mitigation deployed within 4 hours of KEV listing OR isolation of the vulnerable interface; standard 14/30-day SLAs do not apply because the device IS the trust boundary.
new_control_requirements.evidence: SonicWall SonicOS CVE-2020-5135 is an unauthenticated overflow on a perimeter firewall's SSL VPN/management interface, KEV-listed 2022-03-15; the required response is the branch-correct SNWLID-2020-0010 hotfix on a fast clock or isolation of the web/VPN interface, which is the distinct perimeter SLA tier this control defines rather than a standard 14/30-day window.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: SonicOS CVE-2020-5135 (CVSS 9.8) reached KEV on 2022-03-15 with a fix already available in SNWLID-2020-0010; a KEV-triggered SLA forces the branch-correct firmware or interface isolation onto a bounded clock across the Gen 6, SonicOSv and Gen 7 branches rather than a routine appliance patch window.

CVE-2020-5410.name: VMware Tanzu Spring Cloud Config Directory Traversal Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: An unauthenticated attacker sends a crafted, double-encoded traversal URL to Spring Cloud Config Server, which resolves it out of the configuration directory and returns arbitrary files the process can read.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; unauthenticated network access to the config-server endpoint
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; one crafted GET, with double-URL-encoding to bypass intermediate decoding
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. The spring.io advisory credits Fei Lu and a second reporter; no AI involvement indicated.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Upgrading to Spring Cloud Config 2.2.3 / 2.1.9 and restricting the config server to internal clients behind Spring Security.
prevention.adequacy: The upgrade normalizes the path; internal-only exposure plus authentication removes unauthenticated reach but does not fix the traversal on an affected build.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alerting on config-server responses containing OS file content and on requests carrying encoded traversal sequences.
detection.adequacy: Detects exploitation attempts and successful reads, but depends on the config server's access logs being collected and inspected.

response.what_would_have_worked: Rotating any secrets stored on the config-server filesystem and reviewing what files were served during the exposure window.
response.adequacy: Bounds disclosure after the fact; a read-only leak of a credential file may already have compromised downstream systems before rotation.

NIST-800-53-SI-10.gap: SI-10 is nominally met by the framework's request routing, but the config-server module resolves a double-encoded ..%252F path out of its directory; input validation that does not normalize before resolving the label is defeated until the 2.2.3/2.1.9 fix lands.

NIS2-Art21-vulnerability-management.gap: Vulnerability management under Art 21 presumes prompt surfacing of exploitable flaws, yet this dependency-level traversal shipped a fix on 2020-06-01 and did not reach KEV until 2022-03-25 at EPSS 0.95586 — the kind of transitive-library flaw an advisory-only program deprioritizes.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: CAF B4 expects a reachable configuration service to resist traversal, but no configuration of an affected Spring Cloud Config build prevents the ..%252F read; resilience is only reached by upgrading to 2.2.3/2.1.9, so a B4 assessment on 2.2.2 overstates the posture.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: The patch-applications maturity rating counts the update policy rather than whether each service embedding spring-cloud-config-server was rebuilt onto 2.2.3/2.1.9 and redeployed; a config server left on 2.2.2 discloses arbitrary files while the estate rates well.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.28.gap: A.8.28 secure-coding controls govern the operator's own development, but the traversal defect is in the Spring Cloud Config library; an A.8.28 program can be complete while the embedded config-server module still serves /etc/passwd on an unpatched build.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Spring Cloud Config CVE-2020-5410 (CVSS 7.5, EPSS 0.95586) had a fix in 2.2.3/2.1.9 from 2020-06-01 but only reached KEV on 2022-03-25; a KEV-triggered SLA forces the dependency upgrade-and-redeploy — or internal-only exposure with authentication — onto a bounded clock instead of leaving an unauthenticated arbitrary-file-read endpoint live.

attack_vector.description: A remote attacker opens an SMTP session and sends a MAIL FROM whose local part carries shell metacharacters; smtp_mailaddr() wrongly returns success, and mbox delivery executes the injected command as root.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; an unauthenticated remote SMTP session
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; a single crafted MAIL FROM in the default 'uncommented' configuration, no memory-corruption primitive
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Discovered and published by the Qualys Security Advisory team in January 2020.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Updating to OpenSMTPD 6.6.2p1 / OpenBSD errata 019 / the fixed distro package and restarting smtpd, plus restricting inbound SMTP where possible.
prevention.adequacy: The update fixes the validation return value; inbound restriction reduces exposure but a public-facing MTA must accept mail, so patching is the real fix.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alerting on smtpd spawning shells and on MAIL FROM values containing shell metacharacters.
detection.adequacy: Process-spawn and SMTP-log telemetry catch the injection, but a root-level compromise can tamper with local mail logs, so off-host collection is needed.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating a hit host as root-compromised: rebuild or thoroughly triage, rotate credentials reachable from the mail host, and review delivery logs.
response.adequacy: Bounds a root compromise but assumes detection; a quiet single-command run through mail delivery may leave little durable trace.

NIST-800-53-SI-10.gap: SI-10 is embodied by the smtp_mailaddr() address check, but that routine returns success on an invalid local part with an empty domain, so the validation control is the exact code that fails and lets MAIL FROM metacharacters reach the shell until 6.6.2p1.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: Art 21 patch management reads as covered wherever a distro update channel exists, but OpenSMTPD reaches hosts via upstream source, OpenBSD base and distro packages; a source-built or lagging-repo smtpd on 6.4.0-6.6.1 stays unpatched while the estate's package policy looks compliant.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: CAF B4 expects the MTA to resist command injection through its own protocol handling, yet OpenSMTPD 6.4.0-6.6.1 in its default configuration executes MAIL FROM metacharacters as root; no mailer configuration removes the flaw short of the 6.6.2p1 update.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: The patch maturity rating counts the update policy, not whether each internet-facing OpenSMTPD host actually reached 6.6.2p1 / errata 019 and restarted the daemon before the 2022-03-25 KEV clock; a well-rated estate can still run a vulnerable public MTA.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: A.8.8 is asserted by having a vulnerability-management process, but this flaw closes only when that process delivers the fixed opensmtpd package and restarts smtpd; the attestation reads satisfied while a server on 6.4.0-6.6.1 remains exploitable to unauthenticated root.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: SI-2 flaw remediation assumes a single delivery channel, but OpenSMTPD arrives via upstream source, OpenBSD base and distro packages; a plan keyed to one channel leaves smtpd instances installed through the others on 6.4.0-6.6.1 unpatched.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: OpenSMTPD CVE-2020-7247 (CVSS 9.8, EPSS 0.98946) is an unauthenticated root RCE with a Metasploit module and multiple Exploit-DB entries, fixed in 6.6.2p1 / errata 019 in January 2020 but only KEV-listed 2022-03-25; a KEV-triggered SLA forces the package update and smtpd restart onto a bounded clock across every install channel.

CVE-2020-9054.name: Zyxel Multiple NAS Devices OS Command Injection Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: A pre-authentication OS command injection in weblogin.cgi: an unsanitised username parameter breaks out of a shell string, and a bundled setuid helper elevates the injected command to root, giving unauthenticated root RCE on the NAS.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; the injection is in the login CGI before any authentication
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; a single crafted GET/POST, deliverable directly or via a same-network browser per CERT VU#498544
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Discovery was human — exploit code found for sale on a criminal forum by Hold Security.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Flashing the fixed firmware and physically retiring the end-of-support NSA-series, with the management interface kept off untrusted networks.
prevention.adequacy: Prevention is only complete for the patchable lines; for the NSA-series no patch exists, so 'prevention' can only mean decommissioning, which a patch-only programme does not prescribe.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alerting on weblogin.cgi requests carrying shell metacharacters and on anomalous outbound scanning/beaconing from the NAS.
detection.adequacy: Where the appliance does not ship its web-server log off-box, the weblogin.cgi request is only observable in network telemetry. The Mukashi indicators Unit 42 published — TCP/23 scanning and beacons to 45.84.196.75 — sit on the network side and remain available either way, but they fire after root has already been taken.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating an exposed unit as compromised: rebuild or replace, and rotate any credential stored on or reachable from the NAS.
response.adequacy: Root RCE means implant persistence survives a firmware flash on a still-supported unit unless the device is rebuilt from a known-good state.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: SI-2 is nominally satisfied, but it offers no mechanism for the end-of-support NSA-series where the remediation is removal; a flaw-remediation register scoped to available updates leaves those units perpetually open against a top-EPSS pre-auth root RCE.

NIST-800-53-SC-7.gap: SC-7 is met on paper by not exposing the NAS to the internet, yet CERT VU#498544 shows the injection can be induced from a same-LAN browser, so boundary controls that still permit routine client reachability to the appliance do not remove the unauthenticated weblogin.cgi path.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: Article 21 patch-management is exercised for the patchable models but has no answer for the unpatchable NSA-series; with Mukashi weaponisation from March 2020 and a 2022-03-25 KEV listing, those units need a decommission decision that a 'firmware up to date' metric never surfaces.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: CAF principle B4 is treated as satisfied by keeping firmware current, but resilience is unattainable for the NSA-series through patching; B4 assessed only on patch state records a device carrying a setuid-to-root injection path as secure when the sole real control is retirement.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: The ATP, USG, VPN, ZyWALL and NAS models in NVD's CPE set each have a fixed build for a maturity assessment to measure against; the NSA-series has none. The Essential Eight Maturity Model's clause for unsupported operating systems is 'Operating systems that are no longer supported by vendors are replaced.', while its firmware clauses, introduced at Maturity Level Three, set patch deadlines rather than a replacement duty — so the assessment reaches these appliances only if their firmware is read as an operating system or as one of the application categories the Patch applications removal clauses name.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: A.8.8 technical vulnerability management closes cleanly for the flashed models but has no disposition for the NSA-series beyond disposal; without an explicit 'unpatchable — retire by date' state, the register logs these appliances as accepted risk and never forces their removal.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Zyxel CVE-2020-9054 has EPSS 0.99986, a public Nuclei template and PoC, and was weaponised by Mukashi from March 2020; it entered KEV on 2022-03-25. For each of the 27 NAS and firewall firmware products in NVD's CPE set the verified mitigation is that model's fixed build; for the end-of-support NSA-series the 'documented compensating control' is disconnection, and both must land on the KEV clock.

new_control_requirements.name: MITIGATION-ACTIVE-PATCH-PENDING-VERDICT-CLASS
new_control_requirements.description: Compliance verdicts must distinguish three states: (a) binary patch deployed (vulnerability eliminated), (b) vendor-mitigation rule active, no binary patch (residual risk: any defect in the mitigation rule reopens the vulnerability), (c) no mitigation, no patch (full exposure). Audit reports must surface (b) as a distinct compensating-control state with an associated time-bound action item, not as a 'patched per SLA' outcome.
new_control_requirements.evidence: This CVE splits across the three states: the four fixed NAS lines and the 23 ATP/USG/VPN/ZyWALL firewall models reach state (a) after flashing, while the end-of-support NSA-series sits in state (c) — no patch, only network isolation. An audit that folds them into a single 'patched per SLA' outcome hides that the NSA units are fully exposed to a KEV-listed root RCE.

CVE-2020-9377.name: D-Link DIR-610 Devices Remote Command Execution

attack_vector.description: An authenticated command injection: the cmd parameter to command.php is passed to a shell, and a request with a valid uid cookie executes arbitrary commands on the router.
attack_vector.privileges_required: low — PR:L; a valid uid session cookie is required, but the paired CVE-2020-9376 credential dump through getcfg.php supplies one
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; a single POST once a session cookie is held
attack_vector.ai_factor: None.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Retiring the DIR-610 and replacing it with a supported router, since no firmware fix exists.
prevention.adequacy: Replacement is the only real prevention; changing credentials narrows who can reach command.php but does not remove the injection for an authenticated on-network client.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Monitoring for command.php POSTs with shell content and for anomalous outbound activity from the router.
detection.adequacy: Where the router does not forward its web-server log to a collector, the command.php POST is only observable in upstream network telemetry, and a session that used valid credentials looks like administration until the cmd value is inspected.

response.what_would_have_worked: Removing a compromised unit from service and rotating any credential that transited it.
response.adequacy: Command execution on the router means firmware alone cannot be trusted; the device must be replaced rather than cleaned.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: SI-2 is formally in scope but unexecutable — the DIR-610 rev Ax has had no firmware development since 2014, so there is no update to deploy and the control can only be discharged by removing the device, which a patch-oriented SI-2 process does not initiate.

NIST-800-53-CM-7.gap: CM-7 least functionality is nominally met by a hardened configuration, but command.php cannot be disabled without removing the router, so a CM-7 baseline that tolerates end-of-life hardware leaves the injectable endpoint running for every authenticated on-network client.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: Article 21 patch-management is satisfied on paper because no updates are pending, yet that is precisely the failure — an abandoned 2014-era router with a KEV listing needs a decommission trigger, and a control that measures only outstanding patches never produces one.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: CAF B4 reads as compliant when firmware is 'current', but current here means final and vulnerable; resilience for the DIR-610 is achievable only by retirement, so a B4 judgement based on patch state understates a fully exploitable authenticated RCE.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: The Essential Eight Maturity Model brings firmware into scope only at Maturity Level Three, and then as a deadline — patches 'applied within 48 hours of release when vulnerabilities are assessed as critical by vendors or when working exploits exist' — which a router abandoned in 2014 never triggers because no release follows. The model's remove-and-replace duties are written for online services, applications and operating systems, so a maturity assessment of the DIR-610 turns on whether its firmware counts as one of those rather than on the 2022-03-25 KEV listing or the public gist exploit.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: A.8.8 lacks a disposition for an unpatchable device: the item cannot be closed (no patch) and should not stay open indefinitely, so absent an explicit 'dispose by date' state the DIR-610 becomes silent accepted risk despite a public PoC and 2022-03-25 KEV entry.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: The DIR-610 CVE-2020-9377 entered KEV on 2022-03-25 with a public PoC (renatoalencar/dlink-dir610-exploits) and no vendor fix; because D-Link ships no patch for a 2014-EoL router, the only KEV-clock-compliant mitigation is the compensating control D-Link itself documents in SAP10182 — immediately retiring and replacing the device.

new_control_requirements.name: MITIGATION-ACTIVE-PATCH-PENDING-VERDICT-CLASS
new_control_requirements.description: Compliance verdicts must distinguish three states: (a) binary patch deployed (vulnerability eliminated), (b) vendor-mitigation rule active, no binary patch (residual risk: any defect in the mitigation rule reopens the vulnerability), (c) no mitigation, no patch (full exposure). Audit reports must surface (b) as a distinct compensating-control state with an associated time-bound action item, not as a 'patched per SLA' outcome.
new_control_requirements.evidence: The DIR-610 can never reach state (a): D-Link issues no binary patch, and the steps SAP10182 offers an owner who keeps the device do not remove the command.php sink, so the appliance sits in the compensating-control state with retirement as the only terminal action. An audit that treats an empty patch backlog as a pass for this end-of-life router records that state as compliance, which is exactly the misclassification this control forces into a time-bound removal action.

CVE-2021-20028.name: SonicWall Secure Remote Access (SRA) SQL Injection Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: A pre-authentication SQL injection on the SRA management interface: an unsanitised parameter is concatenated into a backend query, letting a remote attacker read or manipulate the appliance database and pivot toward remote-access compromise.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; the injection is reachable before authentication on the internet-facing gateway
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; a single crafted request to the exposed management interface
attack_vector.ai_factor: None; disclosed via SonicWall PSIRT with no AI involvement claimed.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Disconnecting the end-of-life SRA hardware and migrating remote access to a supported SMA appliance on 9.0.0.10-28sv or later.
prevention.adequacy: For the SRA hardware CISA's required action is disconnection; the supported SMA line can be taken to 9.0.0.10-28sv, and the two must not be treated as one estate.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Forwarding appliance and application logs to an off-box SIEM and alerting on SQL-injection patterns and anomalous remote-access sessions.
detection.adequacy: Logs stored on a compromised gateway can be tampered with; a separate-trust-zone collector is needed for reliable telemetry.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating a reachable appliance as compromised: rebuild or replace, and rotate every credential and session that transited it.
response.adequacy: Given ransomware affiliates use such gateways as an entry point, patch-in-place does not evict an implant already placed through the pre-auth path.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: SI-2 can be discharged for the SMA line by deploying 9.0.0.10-28sv, but the SRA hardware in scope is end-of-life and CISA's instruction for it is disconnection; a remediation programme measuring firmware currency never escalates those units to that action, which the ransomware flag on the 2022-03-28 KEV entry makes urgent.

NIST-800-53-SC-7.gap: SC-7 assumes a boundary enforcement point protecting internal assets, but the SRA is that enforcement point and the injection is pre-auth on its own interface, so boundary controls elsewhere in the network do not reduce the exposure of the gateway itself.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: Article 21 patch-management, applied as a standard cadence, files a KEV, ransomware-associated pre-auth SQLi on an EoL perimeter concentrator as a routine update; the gap is the missing accelerated disconnect-or-migrate tier for a device that is itself the trust boundary.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: CAF B4 judged on patch currency reports the SRA compliant whenever its installed firmware matches what the box last shipped, which says nothing about an appliance CISA instructs operators to disconnect. Resilience here is achieved by migrating remote access off the EoL platform onto an SMA at 9.0.0.10-28sv, an action patch-state scoring does not surface.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Essential Eight Patch Applications derives its maturity level from how far a product trails a fixed release, and an SRA the CVE record marks unsupported-when-assigned yields no lag figure for that calculation. The number is unaffected by the appliance either way, while ransomware affiliates retain a reachable pre-auth SQLi on the remote-access gateway.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: A.8.8 lacks an EoL disposition for the SRA hardware, so an item whose required action is disconnection rather than an update has no closing state and cannot sensibly be held open; without a scheduled disconnection the appliance becomes accepted residual risk despite a KEV listing carrying a ransomware flag.

OWASP-Top-10-2021-A03.gap: A03 Injection controls presume a maintained codebase whose queries can be parameterised or fronted by validation; the SRA's vulnerable query builder is end-of-life and will not be refactored, so injection-class guidance offers no remediation beyond removing the appliance.

new_control_requirements.name: PERIMETER-DEVICE-ZERODAY-SLA-TIER
new_control_requirements.description: Compliance frameworks must define a distinct patch SLA tier for pre-auth RCE on perimeter-trust-boundary devices (firewalls, VPN concentrators, WAFs, edge load-balancers). Tier requirement: vendor-mitigation deployed within 4 hours of KEV listing OR isolation of the vulnerable interface; standard 14/30-day SLAs do not apply because the device IS the trust boundary.
new_control_requirements.evidence: The SonicWall SRA is a remote-access (VPN) concentrator — a perimeter-trust-boundary device — and CVE-2021-20028 is a pre-auth defect on its own management interface with known ransomware use, added to KEV 2022-03-28. On the end-of-life SRA hardware the tier-compliant action is isolation or disconnection of the interface, which is what CISA's KEV entry requires.

new_control_requirements.name: PERIMETER-COMPROMISE-REBUILD-NOT-PATCH
new_control_requirements.description: Pre-rehearsed IR runbook for any perimeter device that suffers a pre-auth RCE CVE in active exploitation MUST default to config-exfil + rebuild + credential rotation, not patch-in-place. Patch-in-place leaves attacker-installed implants intact.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2021-20028 carries a KEV ransomware flag and a pre-auth path into a remote-access gateway that terminates untrusted sessions; a SonicWall SRA reachable during the exposure window must be rebuilt or replaced with credentials and sessions rotated, because migrating to a patched SMA build does not evict an implant placed through the SQL-injection path.

CVE-2021-22941.name: Citrix ShareFile Improper Access Control Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: A pre-authentication path traversal in the ShareFile storage zones controller's upload handler lets an attacker write outside the upload directory; overwriting a Razor view injects server-side C# that compiles and runs, yielding unauthenticated RCE.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; the upload endpoint is reachable without authentication
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; one crafted multipart POST plus a follow-up request to trigger the injected view
attack_vector.ai_factor: None; reported by Markus Wulftange of Code White GmbH, a human research firm.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Upgrading the on-premises storage zones controller to 5.11.20+ so uploadid is validated before path construction, and keeping the controller off unnecessary internet exposure.
prevention.adequacy: The upgrade closes the write path but does not remove a web shell already dropped, so prevention must be paired with a compromise assessment for previously exposed instances.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alerting on traversal in upload query parameters, on modifications to Razor views, and on IIS worker outbound connections.
detection.adequacy: The malicious upload flows over an unauthenticated request, so authentication-only logging misses it; request-level web telemetry is required.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating a reachable pre-patch controller as compromised: rebuild, remove attacker-written views, and rotate credentials the host held.
response.adequacy: PROPHET SPIDER used the access as a broker to ransomware, so an incomplete eviction hands the foothold onward.

NIST-800-53-SI-10.gap: SI-10 is nominally satisfied by input validation on application forms, yet the vulnerable field is the uploadid path component, which pre-5.11.20 code trusts; unless SI-10 explicitly treats path-construction inputs as untrusted, the CWE-284 write it enables passes validation review.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: SI-2 is met when 5.11.20 is deployed, but a register scoped to host OS patching shows green while the customer-managed ShareFile controller application lags below the fixed build, leaving the pre-auth write-to-RCE live on an asset the OS-patch view does not cover.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: Article 21 patch-management is exercised at the OS layer but must reach the storage zones controller application; a 2021-08-25 fix and a ransomware-flagged 2022-03-25 KEV listing mean an on-prem controller below 5.11.20 is an unauthenticated RCE that host-centric cadence never inspects.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: CAF B4 measured on version currency reports the controller secure once at 5.11.20, but PROPHET SPIDER's Error.cshtml web shell persists across a naive upgrade, so resilience requires the post-patch compromise assessment that a patch-state judgement omits.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Essential Eight Patch Applications is assessed against the applications the software inventory names, and the storage zones controller is a component an administrator installs beneath the ShareFile service rather than a product in its own right. Where the inventory carries the service and not the controller version, the metric passes with an instance still below the 5.11.20 released on 2021-08-25.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: A.8.8 must enumerate the storage zones controller version as a discrete asset; where the register records ShareFile only as a supported service, an instance below 5.11.20 closes the item on abstraction while remaining an unauthenticated write-to-RCE.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Citrix ShareFile CVE-2021-22941 was fixed in 5.11.20 (2021-08-25), entered KEV on 2022-03-25 with a ransomware flag, and has public exploit code (hoav18/CVE-2021-22941); the verified mitigation is upgrading the on-prem controller to 5.11.20, which must land on the KEV clock rather than the site's normal application-update cadence.

new_control_requirements.name: PERIMETER-COMPROMISE-REBUILD-NOT-PATCH
new_control_requirements.description: Pre-rehearsed IR runbook for any perimeter device that suffers a pre-auth RCE CVE in active exploitation MUST default to config-exfil + rebuild + credential rotation, not patch-in-place. Patch-in-place leaves attacker-installed implants intact.
new_control_requirements.evidence: PROPHET SPIDER overwrote ConfigService\Views\Shared\Error.cshtml on internet-facing ShareFile controllers and installed a ConPtyShell to 107.181.187.184:4242; the 5.11.20 upgrade closes the CWE-284 write path but leaves that Razor web shell in place, so an exposed controller must be rebuilt with credentials rotated rather than merely patched.

CVE-2021-42237.name: Sitecore XP Remote Command Execution Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: A pre-authentication insecure deserialization at Report.ashx: an XML body carrying a Process.Start gadget is deserialised without type restriction, launching an attacker-chosen process on the Sitecore server.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; the Reporting endpoint requires no authentication
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; a single POST of a known gadget to a fixed URL
attack_vector.ai_factor: None; analysed and disclosed by the human research firm Assetnote.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Removing Report.ashx from every instance (KB1000776) as the immediate mitigation, and upgrading to XP 9.0.0+ as the durable fix.
prevention.adequacy: File removal closes the sink at once where an upgrade cannot be scheduled quickly; it must be applied to all server instances, not just the content-delivery role.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alerting on POSTs to Report.ashx and on Sitecore worker processes spawning shells or making outbound DNS.
detection.adequacy: Deserialization runs in-process, so detection depends on request-level and process-spawn telemetry rather than authentication logs.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating a reachable pre-mitigation server as compromised and rebuilding it, given ransomware associations.
response.adequacy: RCE during deserialization can plant persistence that survives the file removal, so eviction requires rebuild rather than mitigation alone.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: SI-2 framed as 'upgrade to 9.0.0' understates the exposure window because a 7.5-8.2 estate upgrade is a project; SI-2 that does not recognise the KB1000776 file-removal mitigation as an interim closure leaves a pre-auth deserialization RCE open across that window.

NIST-800-53-CM-7.gap: CM-7 is nominally met by a hardened server build, yet Report.ashx — which Sitecore records as driving a Silverlight dashboard deprecated at 8.0 Initial Release — remains reachable by default on 7.5 through 8.2.7. A least-functionality baseline that had inventoried and disabled it would have removed the deserialization sink before the KEV listing.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: Article 21 patch-management tracks version upgrades but is not built to deploy a config-side file deletion, so the fastest remediation for this ransomware-flagged, EPSS-0.979 pre-auth RCE falls outside the cadence the control measures.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: CAF B4 judged on Sitecore version currency reports the CMS insecure until 9.0.0 lands, but the resilient interim action is removing Report.ashx; B4 that omits the mitigation both overstates the remediation timeline and misses the compromise-assessment need for previously reachable servers.

AU-Essential-8-App-Hardening.gap: Essential Eight application hardening focuses on browser, Office and script settings and does not reach a CMS-internal handler like Report.ashx, so the maturity control reads satisfied while the very endpoint whose removal KB1000776 prescribes stays enabled.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: A.8.8 has no natural disposition for a config-side file-removal mitigation and tends to record closure only on upgrade, so a register following A.8.8 literally keeps a pre-auth RCE open pending an upgrade project while KB1000776 offers same-day closure.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Sitecore XP CVE-2021-42237 (EPSS 0.97904, ransomware-flagged, KEV 2022-03-25) has a public Nuclei template and Assetnote payload; where the XP 9.0.0 upgrade cannot meet the KEV clock, the documented compensating control from KB1000776 — deleting Report.ashx from all instances — is the verified mitigation that must land within the window.

new_control_requirements.name: CONFIGURATION-SIDE-LIVE-PATCH-INVENTORY
new_control_requirements.description: For any web-fabric vulnerability with a configuration-side mitigation path: that path must be inventoried, tested, and deployable independent of the vendor-patch path. Operators cannot wait for nginx 1.30.1+ if a named-capture refactor mitigates immediately.
new_control_requirements.evidence: This Sitecore RCE has exactly such a config-side path: KB1000776 lets 7.5-8.2 operators delete /sitecore/shell/ClientBin/Reporting/Report.ashx to neutralise the deserialization sink without the XP 9.0.0 upgrade, so that removal must be inventoried and deployable on its own track ahead of the version bump.

CVE-2022-21999.name: Microsoft Windows Print Spooler Privilege Escalation Vulnerability (CVE-2022-21999)

attack_vector.description: A local privilege escalation: the all-users-writable SpoolDirectory plus a directory junction and the CopyFiles\ key make the SYSTEM spooler load an attacker DLL, taking a local user to SYSTEM.
attack_vector.privileges_required: low — PR:L; an existing local user session is required (AV:L), no remote reach
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; reliable by default on desktop Windows once local access is held
attack_vector.ai_factor: None; discovered and published by independent researcher Oliver Lyak.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Installing the February 2022 update and rebooting, and disabling the Print Spooler on hosts that do not print.
prevention.adequacy: The update fully fixes it once rebooted; before the reboot, disabling the spooler is the only complete interim control, and it is unavailable on print servers that must run it.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Monitoring spoolsv.exe DLL loads and SpoolDirectory changes, and alerting on unexpected local-admin account creation.
detection.adequacy: As a local post-foothold action the escalation produces host-level artifacts; without endpoint telemetry the SYSTEM transition is silent.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating a host where the primitive fired as compromised to SYSTEM and rebuilding, plus rotating credentials exposed on it.
response.adequacy: SYSTEM access lets an attacker persist beyond the spooler fix, so patching alone does not evict a foothold already taken.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: SI-2 is met by the February 2022 update, but because the fix is reboot-gated with no live-patch path, a host recorded as 'update installed' yet not rebooted still runs the vulnerable spooler; SI-2 measured on package presence overstates removal of a ransomware-chained SYSTEM LPE.

NIST-800-53-CM-7.gap: CM-7 is nominally satisfied by a standard build, yet that build runs the Print Spooler on servers that never print; least functionality applied to the spooler would remove the SpoolDirectory primitive on those hosts, which a default-enabled baseline does not.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: Article 21 patch-management treats this as a routine monthly OS update, but a public Metasploit module and ransomware use make it a compressed-clock item; folding it into the next rollup leaves an actively-tooled SYSTEM escalation available through the deferral.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: CAF B4 assumes a privilege boundary between local user and SYSTEM, but SpoolFool crosses it through a spooler defect; because the attacker is already an authorised user, B4 controls built on account privilege tiers do not contain the escalation and pass their attestations while the flaw stays exploitable.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Essential Eight Patch Operating Systems requires the update within the window, but the reboot requirement means 'deployed' is not 'effective'; workstations that defer the reboot remain exposed, and the maturity metric does not separate installed-not-rebooted from remediated.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: A.8.8 closes on 'February 2022 update installed', but the effective-remediation test is the post-reboot build; without asserting reboot completion, the register logs the CWE-59/CWE-22 spooler flaw as fixed while the vulnerable code remains loadable via CopyFiles\.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: SpoolFool CVE-2022-21999 is a ransomware-flagged SYSTEM LPE (KEV 2022-03-25) with a public repo and Metasploit module; the verified mitigation is the February 2022 update with a completed reboot, and where that cannot land the documented compensating control is disabling the Print Spooler — both must meet the KEV clock rather than the next monthly rollup.

new_control_requirements.name: BUG-FAMILY-MITIGATION-PERSISTENCE
new_control_requirements.description: When a CVE patch lands, retain the pre-patch compensating controls (module blacklists, sysctl restrictions) until the patched code has soaked for a stated review period. Patches for one bug in a primitive class can introduce sibling bugs in the same class; the original compensating control may still apply to the sibling.
new_control_requirements.evidence: The Print Spooler has produced a run of privilege-escalation defects, and SpoolFool (CVE-2022-21999) is one more in that lineage; disabling the spooler on hosts that do not print is the compensating control that survives across siblings in the family and should be retained on those hosts rather than re-enabled the moment the February 2022 update installs.

CVE-2022-26143.name: MiCollab, MiVoice Business Express Access Control Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: An unauthenticated diagnostic interface (tp240dvr) on UDP 10074 accepts a startblast command that emits a large packet burst; a small spoofed request yields a huge response, making the appliance a reflective UDP amplifier and, via the same missing auth, a denial-of-service target.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; the UDP command interface requires no authentication (CWE-306)
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; a single spoofed datagram to the exposed port
attack_vector.ai_factor: None; identified through human DDoS traffic analysis by coordinated responders.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Blocking UDP 10074 from untrusted networks immediately, and applying MiCollab 9.4 SP1 FP1.
prevention.adequacy: The firewall block closes the reflective vector at once and needs no change on the appliance itself. The update is the durable fix, and PSA 22-0001 as published names no fixed release for MiVoice Business Express, so that line's durable path has to be confirmed with Mitel.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Monitoring for inbound UDP/10074 from untrusted sources and for anomalous outbound UDP bursts from the appliance.
detection.adequacy: Amplification traffic is visible at the network boundary; the appliance itself may not alert on being used as a reflector.

response.what_would_have_worked: Restricting the interface, confirming the appliance is not still emitting amplification traffic, and coordinating with the upstream provider if it was.
response.adequacy: This is a config/patch-and-contain response; there is no host-implant eviction because the abuse is protocol-level, not code execution.

NIST-800-53-SC-5.gap: SC-5 is nominally in place for inbound flood protection, but this defect makes the owned appliance an outbound reflective amplifier via startblast on UDP 10074; SC-5 posture that only absorbs inbound traffic does not stop the operator's own device from attacking third parties.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: SI-2 is met by MiCollab 9.4 SP1 FP1. Where the appliance is upgraded on a planned telephony change cadence rather than a security-update one, UDP 10074 stays reachable through the deferral, and the TP240PhoneHome campaign Cloudflare dates from 2022-02-18 ran during exactly that kind of interval — while the boundary rule (udp.dstport eq 10074) would have closed the reflector the same day.

NIS2-Art21-availability.gap: Article 21 availability measures presume the risk is to the PBX's own uptime, but the larger exposure is the appliance harming external victims as an amplifier; an availability control scoped to keeping the phone system running does not address the operator's role as an unwitting reflection source.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: B4 that does not require tp240dvr to be unreachable from untrusted networks leaves the amplification vector open on an otherwise well-run MiCollab.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Essential Eight Patch Applications scores only the applications an assessment can see. Where the MiCollab appliance is not an entry in the software inventory that assessment draws on, its build never enters the metric, so the score is unaffected while UDP 10074 answers on an appliance below 9.4 SP1 FP1 and the boundary rule that would stop it sits outside the control entirely.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: A.8.8 closes on the MiCollab update, but the immediately effective mitigation is a boundary rule blocking UDP 10074; without recognising that network control as a valid interim closure, A.8.8 leaves the CWE-306 amplification interface exposed on the appliance's slow patch timeline.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Mitel TP240PhoneHome CVE-2022-26143 (KEV 2022-03-25) was abused in a live amplification campaign from 2022-02-18; the documented compensating control — blocking UDP/10074 from untrusted networks, which Cloudflare records Mitel advising in its 2022-02-22 advisory — is the KEV-clock-compliant mitigation available immediately, ahead of the MiCollab 9.4 SP1 FP1 appliance update.

new_control_requirements.name: MITIGATION-ACTIVE-PATCH-PENDING-VERDICT-CLASS
new_control_requirements.description: Compliance verdicts must distinguish three states: (a) binary patch deployed (vulnerability eliminated), (b) vendor-mitigation rule active, no binary patch (residual risk: any defect in the mitigation rule reopens the vulnerability), (c) no mitigation, no patch (full exposure). Audit reports must surface (b) as a distinct compensating-control state with an associated time-bound action item, not as a 'patched per SLA' outcome.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Cloudflare records that when the campaign began Mitel's guidance was to block exploitation attempts 'using a firewall, until a software patch is made available', putting affected MiCollab/MiVoice appliances in state (b) — mitigation active, no binary patch — where any gap in the boundary rule reopens the amplifier; an audit must record that as a time-bound compensating-control state, not as 'patched'.

CVE-2022-26318.name: WatchGuard Firebox and XTM Appliances Arbitrary Code Execution

attack_vector.description: An HTTPS POST to /agent/login on the appliance's management port reaches the wgagent XML-RPC parser before authentication. The parser appends each tag name it encounters to a fixed global buffer with strcat and no bounds check, so an oversized tag name overwrites past the buffer and the public exploits drive that into a ROP chain, giving command execution on the firewall as the nobody account.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; the /agent/login path answers before any credential check, and the resulting execution context is the unprivileged nobody account rather than root
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; a single POST, no user interaction, no information-leak stage in the public implementation, and the only real precondition is that TCP 8080 or 4117 answers the attacker
attack_vector.ai_factor: Manual reverse engineering of the wgagent binary by Charles Fol (Lexfo/Ambionics Security); neither the write-up nor the Metasploit credit block claims any automated or model-assisted discovery

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Confining the WatchGuard System Manager management ports (8080 and 4117) to a dedicated management segment, then upgrading each unit to its branch's fixed build — 12.7.2_U2, 12.1.3_U8 or 12.5.9_U2 — and taking the restart the upgrade requires.
prevention.adequacy: Segmentation bounds who can send the POST; it does not repair the parser, and any host already inside the permitted segment reaches the vulnerable endpoint in full. The upgrade is the only closure, and it is inert until the appliance restarts onto the new image.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alerting on unauthenticated POSTs to /agent/login, on wgagent restarts, and on any outbound connection initiated by the appliance itself, with syslog forwarded off-box to a collector on separate credentials.
detection.adequacy: Once code runs on the appliance the local telemetry is under the attacker's control, so only the off-box copy is trustworthy. And where the firewall is onboarded as a log source for the traffic it inspects but not as a monitored host in its own right, no rule is watching the management interface itself.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating a reachable unexpatched appliance as compromised: extract the configuration, rebuild from a known-good image rather than upgrading in place, and rotate the secrets the device held — administrative accounts, VPN pre-shared keys, and authentication-server secrets.
response.adequacy: Expensive and window-bound — it needs a spare unit or an outage — and it is the only response that survives the possibility of an implant, because a Fireware upgrade carries the existing configuration forward rather than replacing it.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: An organization can hold a fully conformant flaw-remediation programme and still miss this, because the remediation unit is a traffic-interrupting firmware upgrade rather than a package update. The three-week KEV window that closed 2022-04-15 assumes a change window exists for the device every other remediation path depends on, and SI-2 records the outcome as installed-or-not without asking whether the pre-auth path was reached before the image landed.

NIST-800-53-SC-7.gap: Boundary protection is attested through the policy the Firebox enforces, which says nothing about which segments may open a management session to TCP 8080 or 4117 on the appliance itself. The vulnerable XML-RPC endpoint sits on those ports, separate from the 80/443 user interface, so the control most likely to be judged mature on this asset is the one that never inspects the exposed surface.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: Vulnerability-handling measures are evidenced at entity level, and this CVE needs a per-unit answer: an appliance on the 12.1.x branch is remediated by 12.1.3_U8 and by nothing on the 12.7.x line. A policy attestation and a "latest available firmware" statement can both be true while a specific unit sits below its own branch's fixed build.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: Secure configuration is the control carrying the interval before the reboot-bearing upgrade, and for this CVE it reduces to one item — which networks reach 8080 and 4117. B4 evidence for a firewall is usually the ruleset the device applies to other traffic, so the configuration property that actually bounds this exploit is not the one being assessed.

UK-CAF-D1.gap: Response planning exists but is written around the systems the firewall protects rather than the firewall as a victim. Because execution here lands on the device holding VPN and authentication material, and Lexfo records a further escalation to root on the same appliance, a plan without a rebuild-and-rotate branch closes the incident on a device whose configuration the upgrade carried forward unchanged.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Reading the model's internet-facing-services provision as reaching an appliance management plane is already an interpretation, and even under it the assessment measures scanner-visible patch state. Fireware images are staged through the vendor's management tooling rather than the scanner's remediation path, so the Firebox tends to be absent from the counted population instead of failing within it.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: The control depends on receiving timely vulnerability information, and this fix surfaced as resolved issue FBX-22786 in the Fireware 12.7.2 release notes rather than as a numbered advisory. With NVD carrying only that release-notes page and the CISA catalogue link, an intake process built on advisory feeds first learns of the flaw from the 2022-03-25 KEV listing, three weeks before the deadline it sets.

new_control_requirements.name: PERIMETER-DEVICE-ZERODAY-SLA-TIER
new_control_requirements.description: Compliance frameworks must define a distinct patch SLA tier for pre-auth RCE on perimeter-trust-boundary devices (firewalls, VPN concentrators, WAFs, edge load-balancers). Tier requirement: vendor-mitigation deployed within 4 hours of KEV listing OR isolation of the vulnerable interface; standard 14/30-day SLAs do not apply because the device IS the trust boundary.
new_control_requirements.evidence: A WatchGuard Firebox or XTM appliance is the trust boundary itself, and this CVE is an unauthenticated POST to its own management port ending in code execution on it — CVSS 9.8, KEV-listed 2022-03-25 with a 2022-04-15 due date, and EPSS 0.78157 at the 99.539th percentile on 2026-08-17. The tier's second limb is what makes it usable here: the fixed builds (12.7.2_U2, 12.1.3_U8, 12.5.9_U2) each require a reboot that drops all traffic, so isolating 8080 and 4117 to a management segment is the action available on the KEV clock while the outage window is scheduled.

new_control_requirements.name: PERIMETER-COMPROMISE-REBUILD-NOT-PATCH
new_control_requirements.description: Pre-rehearsed IR runbook for any perimeter device that suffers a pre-auth RCE CVE in active exploitation MUST default to config-exfil + rebuild + credential rotation, not patch-in-place. Patch-in-place leaves attacker-installed implants intact.
new_control_requirements.evidence: This is the case the default is written for: a Firebox or XTM appliance with a public Metasploit module and a standalone PoC against a pre-auth endpoint, listed by CISA on 2022-03-25 as exploited. Execution lands as nobody and Lexfo's analysis records a follow-on escalation to root on the same device, so an operator cannot assume the attacker stayed unprivileged. A Fireware upgrade to 12.7.2_U2 or its branch equivalent preserves the existing configuration, which is exactly the state a rebuild-and-rotate runbook refuses to inherit on a device holding VPN and authentication secrets.

attack_vector.description: A developer visits an attacker-controlled page, or is served a malicious advertisement. The page's script sets a User-Agent that does not begin with "Mozilla" — which Firefox and Safari permit — defeating the only guard on Ray's job endpoints, and DNS rebinding re-points the page's own hostname at 127.0.0.1 so the POST lands on the dashboard listening on 8265 of that developer's machine. Ray accepts the job because the endpoint takes no credential, and the job's entrypoint executes as the account running Ray.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; the job endpoints take no credential, and execution inherits the privileges of whichever account started Ray, which on a workstation is the developer's own
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L with UI:P; the difficulty is not the exploit but the precondition, namely the developer loading attacker content in Firefox or Safari while a Ray dashboard is listening locally
attack_vector.ai_factor: Human research credited in GHSA-q279-jhrf-cc6v to avilum (Oligo Security) as finder and JLLeitschuh (Socket) as reporter. The product being an AI compute engine is a statement about the target, not about the discovery method, and neither firm is described in the advisory as using model-driven discovery here.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Not running the Ray dashboard on a machine used for general web browsing, fronting it with an authenticating proxy where it must run, and — after upgrading to 2.52.0 — turning on the token authentication that release introduces.
prevention.adequacy: The upgrade only takes effect when the Ray processes relaunch, and it hardens browser detection rather than adding an access decision; token authentication ships off, so an upgraded cluster still authenticates nobody until it is configured. Binding to loopback is not part of the answer — rebinding delivers the request to loopback by design.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Reviewing submitted-job history for entrypoints no operator submitted, and resolver logs for short-TTL answers flipping a single hostname to 127.0.0.1 on hosts that run Ray.
detection.adequacy: Job history sits on the same host the attacker reached, so it is only trustworthy if shipped off-box. Rebinding is visible at the resolver only where workstation DNS queries are logged centrally and retained.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating an affected workstation and any cluster it drove as having run attacker-supplied code: rotate the cloud, registry and object-store credentials the Ray process could read, and review job history and model artifacts produced during the exposure window.
response.adequacy: Unless dashboard access logs were retained off-host, the window has to be bounded by the upgrade date rather than by per-job attribution, which makes the rotation scope the whole set of credentials reachable from the machine rather than a demonstrated subset.

NIST-800-53-IA-2.gap: The control is met for every system in the authorization boundary and the vulnerable one is not in it — a developer's locally started Ray dashboard on 8265, whose job endpoints accepted submissions with no credential and substituted a User-Agent prefix test for authentication.
