Upgrading to 2.52.0 does not change that verdict on its own, because the token authentication it adds is off until someone enables it.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: Flaw remediation is exercised against inventoried hosts and applications, while the affected artifact is a pinned Python dependency inside a project environment. With a KEV due date of 2026-08-20 set three days after listing, the programme has neither the visibility to find every environment resolving ray below 2.52.0 nor a mechanism to confirm the Ray processes relaunched onto the fixed build.

NIS2-Art21-network-security.gap: Every network measure the article contemplates can be in place and none of them is on the path: the malicious request originates inside the victim's browser and is delivered to 127.0.0.1 after the attacker's hostname re-resolves. Because nothing crosses a segment boundary, the control's own evidence — firewall policy, segmentation, egress control — cannot distinguish an exposed workstation from a safe one.

UK-CAF-B2.gap: Identity and access control is assessed where identities exist, and Ray's job API had none: the vendor's position was deployment on a trusted network, so the browser-denial middleware carried the whole burden. An estate can demonstrate strong authentication everywhere it enumerates and still hand code execution to a web page, because the vulnerable interface was never on the list of things that authenticate anyone.

AU-Essential-8-App-Hardening.gap: Hardening the browser removes the malvertising route the advisory names and leaves the visited-website route intact, which is enough on its own. Nothing in a browser-hardening posture prevents a page's own script from setting a permitted header value and issuing a POST to a service on the same machine, so the control reduces one of two delivery paths without touching the mechanism.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.9.gap: Configuration management assumes a documented baseline that drift is measured against, and here the vulnerable state is the product default: an unauthenticated dashboard on 8265. A baseline written as a version floor is satisfied by 2.52.0 while token authentication remains off, so the configuration item that actually decides exposure is not the one the control is monitoring.

new_control_requirements.name: AI-COMPUTE-CONTROL-PLANE-AUTHENTICATION
new_control_requirements.description: An AI compute framework's job/control API must authenticate every caller; 'deploy only on a trusted network' is an assumption, not a control, and must not substitute for authentication. Enable Ray token authentication (2.52.0+), never expose the dashboard / Job Submission API to untrusted networks, front it with an authenticating proxy, and treat any internet-exposed cluster as compromised (rotate model artifacts and cloud credentials). The distinguishing test: from the public internet, attempt to reach the Ray dashboard (default 8265) and submit a job unauthenticated on a staging cluster; it must be refused.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Ray-Project Ray below 2.52.0 is the framework this names, and the authentication half of the control is the load-bearing half for this CVE: the reachability half gives nothing, because the request arrives on 127.0.0.1 from the developer's own browser after DNS rebinding, so a cluster that is not exposed to any untrusted network is still exploitable. What defended /api/jobs and /api/job_agent/jobs/ was a User-Agent prefix test, which Firefox and Safari let script defeat. CISA listed it 2026-08-17 with a 2026-08-20 due date; the fixed release ships token authentication off by default, so enabling it is the action the control demands beyond the upgrade.

new_control_requirements.name: AI-ML-DEVELOPER-TOOLING-INVENTORY
new_control_requirements.description: Organizations using AI/ML systems must maintain a separate inventory of developer-tooling control planes (notebook servers, experiment trackers, model registries, vector-DB admin UIs, agent frameworks) with: exposed network endpoints (HTTP, WebSocket, gRPC), authentication mechanism per endpoint, blast-radius mapping (which model artifacts/training data/production deployments are reachable from each tool), and patch SLA tier separate from generic application patching.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CISA's own framing of this Ray entry is that developers using Ray as a development tool are the exposed population, which is the class a server-oriented asset inventory is not built to cover — a dashboard on 8265 started by a developer, with no authentication mechanism recorded against either job endpoint. The inventory's per-endpoint authentication column is what would have surfaced the exposure before 2026-08-17, and its separate patch tier is what makes a three-day due date on a pinned Python dependency actionable, since the fix requires both ray >= 2.52.0 and a relaunch of the Ray processes to take effect.

CVE-2018-8373.name: Microsoft Scripting Engine Memory Corruption Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: A crafted page or Office document drives attacker VBScript through the IE engine into a use-after-free in vbscript.dll: a Default Property Get overload ReDims the array mid-assignment, freeing pvData while AssignVar still holds the stale element address. Reclaiming that block with a SAFEARRAY and inflating its length yields arbitrary read/write, and from there code execution as the current user.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; the attacker needs no account, only that the victim open the content
attack_vector.complexity: high — AC:H; reliable exploitation needs heap grooming to control the reused allocation, and UI:R means the victim must open the crafted content
attack_vector.ai_factor: None; discovered as an in-the-wild zero-day by human analysts at Trend Micro, no AI attribution.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Apply the August 2018 IE update, or disable VBScript in the Internet zone and retire Internet Explorer for browsing.
prevention.adequacy: The patch is complete for the browser path, but leaves the Office-hosted IE-engine path open until IE/VBScript is actually disabled, so patch-plus-hardening is needed, not patch alone.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alert on IE or Office processes spawning script interpreters or making anomalous outbound connections after opening untrusted content.
detection.adequacy: Catches the post-exploitation stager but not the in-memory UAF itself; a fileless shellcode run can complete before a child process appears.

response.what_would_have_worked: Isolate a host that ran the crafted content, rotate credentials used on it, and hunt for what the shellcode or the ShellExecute'd cmd launched next.
response.adequacy: Effective only if the initial script execution was detected; a silent UAF leaves little host artifact beyond the delivery document.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: SI-2 is nominally met by an August-2018-current patch baseline, yet the 3.5-year lag to the 2022-03-25 KEV listing shows organizations were counting OS currency while the Internet Explorer scripting component stayed unpatched; the still-elevated EPSS of 0.545 confirms the control was not closing the real exposure.

NIST-800-53-CM-7.gap: CM-7 least functionality is claimed once VBScript is disabled in the browser, but the CVE-2018-8373 delivery path runs through an Office document that hosts the IE engine, so a control scoped to interactive Internet Explorer does not remove the engine that the document reaches.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: NIS2 Article 21 patch-management obligations are satisfied on paper by a monthly cumulative cadence, but they do not force retirement of Internet Explorer 9/10/11 kept for legacy applications, and those retained browsers carry this actively exploited engine flaw for the entire life of the compatibility exception.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: CAF B4 assumes the software estate can be kept current; where IE is retained for compatibility, B4 does not mandate disabling the VBScript engine that carries this UAF, so a green self-assessment coexists with an open crafted-document path into vbscript.dll.

AU-Essential-8-App-Hardening.gap: The Essential Eight user-application-hardening controls that bear on this path are the Internet Explorer and Microsoft Office settings, and blocking Office macros disables neither OLE object activation nor the IE engine those objects reach. CVE-2018-8373 arrives through an embedded object that invokes the engine rather than through a macro, so where hardening is evidenced by macro configuration alone the assessment can be satisfied while vbscript.dll stays callable from a document.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: A.8.8 technical-vulnerability management identifies IE 9/10/11 as vulnerable only if the inventory tracks the scripting component distinctly from the browser shell; where it records only the OS build, the August 2018 fix appears applied while the engine remains exploitable to the public HacTF exploit.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2018-8373 was fixed by Microsoft in August 2018 but not KEV-listed until 2022-03-25; a KEV-tied SLA measured against the Internet Explorer scripting component rather than OS currency would have driven the August 2018 update or the URLACTION 0x140C VBScript disable onto every IE 9/10/11 host, closing a vbscript.dll path Trend Micro caught in live web traffic on 2018-07-11 and whose EPSS is still 0.545.

new_control_requirements.name: BROWSER-MANAGED-UPDATE-NO-DEFERRAL
new_control_requirements.description: Enterprise update rings must not defer security-channel browser updates beyond 24h.
new_control_requirements.evidence: The exposure here is the Internet Explorer scripting engine; an update ring that deferred IE cumulative updates left vbscript.dll exploitable to the public CVE-2018-8373 exploit for the length of the deferral, exactly the browser-currency failure this control forbids.

attack_vector.description: An unprivileged local process forces a NULL pointer dereference in win32k popup-menu handling, maps a fake tagPOPUPMENU at address 0x0, flips a tagWND bit to gain kernel execution, and swaps its token for SYSTEM.
attack_vector.privileges_required: low — PR:L; the attacker needs unprivileged local code execution first
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L on the affected legacy systems; the real constraint is that only Windows 7 / Server 2008 permit the NULL-page mapping the exploit depends on
attack_vector.ai_factor: None; discovered in the wild by ESET, no AI attribution.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Apply the July 2019 update on Windows 7 / Server 2008, or migrate off the now-unsupported platforms.
prevention.adequacy: The patch fully closes the dereference, but the affected platforms are end-of-support, so on surviving hosts only migration is a durable control.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Kernel telemetry alerting on NULL-page mapping or an unexpected SYSTEM token swap.
detection.adequacy: Weak in practice: ESET's analysis places the trigger, the fake tagPOPUPMENU and the token swap in kernel memory, so a host without kernel-mode telemetry sees nothing of the escalation.

response.what_would_have_worked: Isolate a suspected host, treat it as SYSTEM-compromised, and prioritize its retirement.
response.adequacy: Reactive only; a SYSTEM-level LPE gives the attacker full control before response begins.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: SI-2 reads as satisfied on a supported baseline, but the Windows 7 / Server 2008 hosts that actually carry this win32k flaw are the frozen legacy islands a currency metric excludes, and the July 2019 fix never reaches them; the 2.5-year lag to the 2022-03-15 KEV listing is the measure of that blind spot.

NIST-800-53-SI-4.gap: SI-4 would need to observe the NULL-page allocation or the SYSTEM token swap, but ESET's analysis puts every step after the MN_CANCELMENUS message inside win32k.sys kernel memory, and the user32.dll HMValidateHandle call the exploit uses to leak the tagWND address is an ordinary API call. On a host whose telemetry stops at the user-mode boundary there is nothing distinctive left for this control to key on.

NIS2-Art21-vulnerability-management.gap: NIS2 vulnerability management is met on paper through documented legacy-application exceptions, and those exceptions are exactly where an end-of-support Windows 7 box keeps this foothold-to-SYSTEM path alive at EPSS 0.098 with no remaining vendor fix; the July 2019 update is the last one that ever addressed CVE-2019-1132, and extended support ended in January 2020.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: CAF B4 assumes a maintainable estate; after Windows 7 / Server 2008 reached end of extended support in January 2020 there is no update stream, so B4 cannot be discharged by patching and only migration satisfies it — a distinction a patch-centric B4 review misses.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Essential Eight OS patching is unattainable on these unsupported platforms, and its own maturity logic then requires removing the unsupported OS; a Windows 7 host reporting zero outstanding patches because none exist has satisfied the letter while leaving this KEV-listed kernel LPE in place.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: A.8.8 rates this LPE critical but its remediation path presumes a deployable fix; on the surviving Windows 7 / Server 2008 hosts the fix is only historical, so A.8.8 must trigger a decommission decision that inventories tracking patch state alone never raise.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2019-1132 was fixed in July 2019 but not KEV-listed until 2022-03-15; a KEV-tied SLA applied to the Windows 7 / Server 2008 population would have forced either the July 2019 update or a documented decommission plan for hosts that can no longer take it, closing the win32k kernel LPE, EPSS 0.098, that ESET caught being used as a zero-day in June 2019.

CVE-2019-1129.name: Microsoft Windows AppX Deployment Service (AppXSVC) Privilege Escalation Vulnerability (CVE-2019-1129)

attack_vector.description: A local user races AppXSVC between folder creation and DACL write by relaunching Edge/Cortana, hard-links a package path to a SYSTEM-owned file, and gains full control of the target to run code as SYSTEM via DiagHub.
attack_vector.privileges_required: low — PR:L; the attacker needs unprivileged local execution first
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L in CVSS terms, but a multi-core host and repeated triggering are needed to win the race reliably
attack_vector.ai_factor: None; publicly dropped by SandboxEscaper, no AI attribution.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Apply the July 2019 update and reboot every AppXSVC-hosting endpoint so the fixed service binary loads.
prevention.adequacy: Complete once rebooted; the reboot dependency is the gap that leaves patched-but-unrebooted hosts exploitable.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alert on hard-link creation from package folders to system files and on unexpected SYSTEM DLL loads via DiagHub.
detection.adequacy: Detectable but noisy; the repeated Edge/Cortana relaunch pattern can resemble normal use on shared hosts.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treat a suspected host as SYSTEM-compromised, given the ransomware association, and rebuild rather than clean.
response.adequacy: Necessary for a ransomware-linked LPE but reactive; the escalation completes before response.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: SI-2 appears met by a July-2019-current baseline, but this AppXSVC fix is inert until the reboot reloads the service, so a program that credits 'installed' without confirming reboot has recorded remediation that did not occur — and the KEV ransomware flag makes the unrebooted window a real escalation path.

NIST-800-53-AC-6.gap: AC-6 least privilege is fully in place and still irrelevant here: the attacker starts as an ordinary user and the defect abuses AppXSVC's own SYSTEM identity to perform the privileged DACL write on a hard-linked target, so scoping the user's rights never touches the vulnerable service action.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: NIS2 patch management is satisfied by cadence, and cadence is what this fix defeats: the July 2019 update stays inert until AppXSVC restarts. Where restarts are not enforced, an essential entity's deployment report reads complete across the eighteen products Microsoft lists — servers included — while the ransomware-associated escalation remains reachable.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: The B4 outcome for CVE-2019-1129 turns on a distinction build-number evidence does not carry: an installed July 2019 update versus a restarted AppXSVC. Microsoft's advisory lists eighteen affected products, Windows Server 2019 and the 1803/1903 Server Core installations among them, so a B4 attestation assembled from workstation builds passes over both the unrestarted endpoints and the server population.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Essential Eight patch-application maturity is scored against the deployed build. CVE-2019-1129's July 2019 build only becomes the executing code once AppXSVC restarts, so an estate can hold its rating with every one of the eighteen listed products at the fixed level while the Edge and Cortana package-folder race stays winnable on any host awaiting restart.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: A.8.8 rates CVE-2019-1129 accurately — KEV-listed 2022-03-15, ransomware association recorded, EPSS 0.018 — and points at the July 2019 update. What it does not specify is that closure evidence must be the AppXSVC restart rather than the package version, so an inventory reporting July-2019 currency across Windows 10 1703 to 1903 and Windows Server 2019 records a race remediated that a defender can still lose.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2019-1129 was fixed in July 2019 but not KEV-listed until 2022-03-15 (ransomware: Known); a KEV-tied SLA that measures completion by the reboot loading the fixed AppXSVC binary — not by 'update installed' — would close the ransomware-associated race across all eighteen products Microsoft lists for this CVE, Windows Server 2019 and the 1803/1903 Server Core installations included, which a patched-but-unrestarted estate leaves open at EPSS 0.018.

CVE-2019-1069.name: Microsoft Task Scheduler Privilege Escalation Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: A legacy .job import drives Task Scheduler to impersonate SYSTEM and call SetSecurityInfo on a task file; hard-linking that file to a protected target has SYSTEM rewrite the target's DACL, giving an unprivileged user control of arbitrary system files.
attack_vector.privileges_required: low — PR:L; the attacker needs unprivileged local execution and the legacy schtasks/schedsvc binaries
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; deterministic, no race, reliable on Windows 10 and Server 2016/2019 per CERT/CC
attack_vector.ai_factor: None; publicly dropped by SandboxEscaper, no AI attribution.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Apply the June 2019 update and reboot so Task Scheduler runs the corrected file-operation validation.
prevention.adequacy: Complete after reboot; the reboot dependency is the residual gap on deferred hosts.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Deploy Microsoft's published bearlpe query on schtasks /change /TN /RU /RP from below-High integrity.
detection.adequacy: Effective where process command-line telemetry is collected; blind on estates logging only authentication and network events.

response.what_would_have_worked: Given the ransomware association, treat a triggered host as SYSTEM-compromised and rebuild.
response.adequacy: Reactive; the DACL overwrite and SYSTEM code path complete before response.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: SI-2 reads met on a June-2019-current baseline, but the corrected validation runs only after the Task Scheduler service restarts at reboot, so a record stopping at 'update installed' overstates closure of a ransomware-associated SYSTEM escalation with EPSS 0.061, and the 2022-03-15 KEV lag shows how long that went unaddressed.

NIST-800-53-SI-4.gap: SI-4 is technically achievable because Microsoft published a precise signal, but it fires only where schtasks.exe /change command lines and process integrity are logged; an SI-4 program built on authentication and network telemetry never observes the bearlpe .job-import invocation.

NIS2-Art21-vulnerability-handling.gap: NIS2 vulnerability handling is satisfied by a triage-and-patch workflow that does not verify the Task Scheduler service reloaded after reboot, so the CVE-2019-1069 ticket can close while unrebooted hosts still impersonate SYSTEM during the .job import.

UK-CAF-C1.gap: CAF C1 security monitoring is judged adequate on network and authentication coverage, but detecting bearlpe requires Task Scheduler process telemetry keyed on schtasks /change parameters and integrity level, which that scope excludes — so C1 passes while blind to this local exploit.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Essential Eight patching credits the June 2019 build, but the corrected file-operation validation is inert until the service restarts at reboot, so an estate at that patch level with unrebooted Windows 10 / Server 2016 / 2019 hosts has met the number while the deterministic DACL-overwrite path stays open.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.16.gap: A.8.16 monitoring is nominally in place, but catching this exploit needs a rule on the exact schtasks.exe /change command pattern and low integrity Microsoft documented; a baseline alerting only on failed logons and signatures leaves the bearlpe behavior unmonitored.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2019-1069 was fixed in June 2019 but not KEV-listed until 2022-03-15 (ransomware: Known); a KEV-tied SLA measured by the post-reboot Task Scheduler restart, and interim removal of legacy schtasks/schedsvc where the reboot lags, would close a ransomware-associated SYSTEM escalation with EPSS 0.061.

CVE-2019-1064.name: Microsoft Windows AppX Deployment Service (AppXSVC) Privilege Escalation Vulnerability (CVE-2019-1064)

attack_vector.description: A local user deletes a package folder to trigger AppXSVC recreation, then hard-links a path to SYSTEM.INI during the window before the DACL write, so SYSTEM grants the user Full Control of a protected file and a route to SYSTEM code execution.
attack_vector.privileges_required: low — PR:L; the attacker needs unprivileged local execution first
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L in CVSS terms, though winning the folder-recreation timing window makes exploitation probabilistic
attack_vector.ai_factor: None; human-published PoC, no AI attribution.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Apply the June 2019 update and reboot every AppXSVC-hosting endpoint.
prevention.adequacy: Complete after reboot; unrebooted hosts stay exposed to the folder-recreation race.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alert on hard links from package folders to protected files and on AppXSVC-attributed DACL changes on system files.
detection.adequacy: Detectable but timing-sensitive; the window is brief and the deletion of one's own package folder looks benign.

response.what_would_have_worked: Given the ransomware association, treat a triggered host as SYSTEM-compromised and rebuild.
response.adequacy: Reactive; the DACL overwrite completes before response.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: SI-2 reads met on a June-2019-current baseline, but AppXSVC keeps the vulnerable folder-recreation timing until the post-update reboot, so a record stopping at 'installed' overstates closure of a ransomware-associated escalation with EPSS 0.069; the lag to the 2022-03-15 KEV listing measures that miss.

NIST-800-53-AC-6.gap: AC-6 is fully in place and still ineffective: the attacker only deletes their own package folder, and AppXSVC's SYSTEM identity performs the DACL write onto the hard-linked SYSTEM.INI, so no reduction of the user's rights reaches the vulnerable service action.

NIS2-Art21-vulnerability-management.gap: NIS2 vulnerability management is met by cadence but does not compel confirming the AppXSVC restart, so any of the twenty-three listed products — Windows Server 2016 and 2019 as much as Windows 10 — keeps the SYSTEM.INI race open until it reboots, while the June 2019 fix reads as deployed.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: B4 for CVE-2019-1064 is really two checks: the June 2019 update present, and AppXSVC restarted. Evidence recording only the first discharges the outcome over hosts still recreating package folders with the vulnerable DACL timing, and since the advisory spans twenty-three products up to Windows Server 2019 Server Core, a workstation-sampled review leaves the server estate unassessed as well.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Patch-application maturity is measured on deployment speed toward the fixed build. Because CVE-2019-1064's June 2019 build does not execute until AppXSVC restarts, the rating can be held with all twenty-three listed products at the fixed level while the hard-link race against SYSTEM.INI remains winnable on every host awaiting restart.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: A.8.8 identifies CVE-2019-1064 accurately — KEV since 2022-03-15, ransomware association recorded, EPSS 0.069 — and names the June 2019 update. The control does not state what counts as closure, so an inventory reporting package version across Windows 10 1607 to 1903, Windows Server 2016 and Windows Server 2019 marks the item done while the SYSTEM.INI hard-link window survives on unrestarted hosts.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2019-1064 was fixed in June 2019 but not KEV-listed until 2022-03-15 (ransomware: Known); a KEV-tied SLA that measures completion by the reboot loading the fixed AppXSVC binary would close the folder-recreation race, EPSS 0.069, across all twenty-three products Microsoft lists for this CVE — Windows Server 2016 and Windows Server 2019 included — which a patched-but-unrestarted estate leaves open.

CVE-2019-0841.name: Microsoft Windows AppX Deployment Service (AppXSVC) Privilege Escalation Vulnerability (CVE-2019-0841)

attack_vector.description: A low-privileged user hard-links an Edge package file to a SYSTEM-owned file and relaunches Edge, so AppXSVC impersonating SYSTEM overwrites the target's DACL; the user then loads a DLL as SYSTEM via the Diagnostics Hub collector.
attack_vector.privileges_required: low — PR:L; the attacker needs unprivileged local execution first
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; deterministic given the correct installed Edge version string in the package path
attack_vector.ai_factor: None; discovered by Nabeel Ahmed, no AI attribution.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Apply the April 2019 update and reboot every AppXSVC-hosting endpoint and server.
prevention.adequacy: Complete after the restart. There is no upgrade-instead option: Microsoft lists Windows 10 Version 1809 (build 17763) and Windows Server 2019 among the affected products, so an unrestarted host stays exposed whatever release it runs.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alert on Edge kill/relaunch with settings.dat deletion and on hard links from Edge package paths to system files.
detection.adequacy: Detectable, but an Edge restart is common and the malicious hard link is the distinguishing signal.

response.what_would_have_worked: Given the ransomware association, treat a triggered host as SYSTEM-compromised and rebuild.
response.adequacy: Reactive; the DACL overwrite and DiagHub load complete before response.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: SI-2 reads met on an April-2019-current baseline, but this flaw is reboot-gated and its EPSS of 0.414 sits at the 98.6th percentile; a record stopping at 'installed' overstates closure of a Metasploit-armed, ransomware-associated escalation, and the lag to the 2022-03-15 KEV listing measures the exposure window.

NIST-800-53-AC-6.gap: AC-6 is fully applied and still ineffective: the attacker only manipulates their own Edge package files, and AppXSVC's SYSTEM impersonation performs the DACL overwrite on the hard-linked win.ini/HOSTS, so no reduction of the user's rights reaches the vulnerable service action.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: NIS2 patch management is met by cadence, but a public Metasploit module means the reboot-gated April 2019 fix must actually be live. Hosts among the fifteen affected products that installed the update and never restarted keep a commoditized SYSTEM escalation open at EPSS 0.414 while the patch reads as deployed.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: B4 credits currency without settling what currency means for this CVE: the April 2019 update installed, and AppXSVC restarted. Because Windows 10 Version 1809 (build 17763) and Windows Server 2019 are themselves on the affected list, an attestation leaning on being on a later release passes over hosts Microsoft records as vulnerable to the same Metasploit module.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Patch-application maturity scores the April 2019 build as applied, but the fixed AppXSVC binary is not the running one until restart, and moving release is no substitute when 1809 and Windows Server 2019 are affected. The rating can be held while the Edge package hard-link into win.ini and the DiagHub-to-SYSTEM chain remain available.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: A.8.8 rates CVE-2019-0841 correctly — KEV since 2022-03-15, ransomware association recorded, EPSS 0.414 — and names the April 2019 update. Closure evidence has to be the AppXSVC restart across all fifteen listed products; a metric ending at package version, or one crediting a 1809 or Server 2019 build as unaffected, reports remediation the AppX handling has not received.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2019-0841 was fixed in April 2019 but not KEV-listed until 2022-03-15 (ransomware: Known), carries EPSS 0.414 and a public Metasploit module; a KEV-tied SLA measured by the post-reboot AppXSVC restart across all fifteen products Microsoft lists — Windows 10 Version 1809 and Windows Server 2019 included — would close a commoditized SYSTEM escalation that a patched-but-unrestarted estate leaves open.

attack_vector.description: A passwordless SEC_WINNT_AUTH_IDENTITY_EX loopback authentication makes LSASS return a session-0 network token; the attacker impersonates it and spawns a process in session 0 via the COM activator, positioning to elevate through global named objects or a chained flaw.
attack_vector.privileges_required: low — PR:L; the attacker needs unprivileged local execution able to perform the loopback authentication
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; a deterministic SSPI call sequence with no race, though full elevation usually needs a follow-on primitive
attack_vector.ai_factor: None; discovered by James Forshaw of Google Project Zero, no AI attribution.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Apply the January 2019 update and reboot so LSASS stops returning the session-0 network token.
prevention.adequacy: Complete after reboot; unrebooted hosts keep the abusable loopback behavior.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alert on processes spawned in session 0 by interactive users and on anomalous loopback NTLM authentication.
detection.adequacy: Session-0 process creation is a usable signal, but distinguishing a genuine service from an abused token needs careful baselining.

response.what_would_have_worked: Given the ransomware association CISA records on this listing, treat a host that produced an unexplained session-0 process as compromised and rebuild it rather than clean, and hunt for the follow-on primitive the session-0 token was chained into.
response.adequacy: Reactive, and complicated by this being a chaining step: the impactful escalation may be a separate flaw exploited alongside it, so incident scope cannot stop at CVE-2019-0543.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: SI-2 reads met on a January-2019-current baseline, but the reboot-gated LSASS fix means a host that installed the update without restarting still returns the abusable token; the lag to the 2022-03-15 KEV listing — which carries a ransomware association — shows how long this authentication escalation with EPSS 0.047 stayed live across the Windows 7-to-Server-2019 range.

NIST-800-53-IA-2.gap: IA-2 assumes a loopback authentication yields a token faithful to the caller, but this flaw makes LSASS return a session-0 network token for a passwordless SEC_WINNT_AUTH_IDENTITY_EX request; the control does not test the identity carried by a returned token, which is the precise assumption the bug violates.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: NIS2 patch management is met by cadence, but the reboot-gated LSASS fix leaves a January-2019-patched-but-unrebooted host returning the abusable token, so a broad Windows estate can report the patch deployed while the session-0 escalation path stays live.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: CAF B4 credits Windows currency but does not separate a downloaded update from an applied-and-rebooted one; for this reboot-gated authentication fix that separation is the control, so B4 can pass over hosts whose LSASS still yields the session-0 network token.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Essential Eight patching scores the January 2019 build applied, but the fix is inert until reboot reloads LSASS, so an estate at that patch level with unrebooted hosts has met the number while the loopback-reflection primitive remains available as a chaining step.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: A.8.8 flags this KEV-listed authentication flaw, but its closure evidence must include the post-patch reboot; where the metric ends at OS build, the January 2019 fix is recorded applied while LSASS still returns the session-0 token on the loopback path.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2019-0543 was fixed in January 2019 but not KEV-listed until 2022-03-15 (ransomware: Known), carries EPSS 0.047 and a public Forshaw PoC (EDB-46156); a KEV-tied SLA measured by the post-reboot LSASS restart across the Windows 7-through-Server-2019 range would close a ransomware-associated session-0 authentication-token escalation that a patched-but-unrebooted fleet leaves live.

attack_vector.description: A local unprivileged process drives win32k's SetImeInfoEx into dereferencing an unvalidated data pointer on a freshly created window station, then uses a pre-mapped null page — with a pointer set at offset 0x2C, per ESET's analysis — to convert the NULL dereference into an arbitrary kernel write and SYSTEM privileges.
attack_vector.privileges_required: low — PR:L; the attacker must already run local code, typically obtained from a preceding client-side RCE such as CVE-2018-4990 in Adobe Reader.
attack_vector.complexity: high — AC:H; the null-page-mapping technique works only on Windows 7 / Server 2008-era kernels, which bounds where the exploit is reachable.
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Found by ESET researchers analyzing an in-the-wild PDF sample; no AI-assisted discovery is claimed.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Deploying the May 2018 win32k update and, because the line is EoL, migrating off Windows 7 / Server 2008 R2 to a supported OS that blocks null-page mapping.
prevention.adequacy: The patch closes this CVE but does nothing for the dozens of later win32k flaws an out-of-support kernel will never receive; only migration removes the standing exposure.

detection.what_would_have_worked: EDR alerting on null-page mapping followed by a win32k call, and on Adobe Reader spawning a SYSTEM-integrity child.
detection.adequacy: Behavioral detection fires only after the Reader stage already executed attacker code; it narrows dwell time rather than preventing the escalation.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating any host that ran the chain as SYSTEM-compromised: rebuild and rotate credentials, not just patch.
response.adequacy: Patching the Reader flaw leaves the kernel foothold intact if the chain already ran.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: SI-2 is nominally met once the May 2018 update is approved, but the control does not verify win32k.sys reached the fixed build on every Windows 7 SP1 host, so the EPSS 0.737 exposure persisted long enough for KEV enrollment on 2022-03-15.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: Patch-management under Article 21 records the last available update as compliant, yet Windows 7 SP1 and Server 2008 R2 SP1 lost ESU on 2023-01-10; the durable remediation is migration, which the patch metric never demands.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: CAF B4 secure-maintenance can be attested against the May 2018 build while the underlying kernel is out of vendor support and will receive no fix for any subsequent win32k defect, understating the real maintenance debt.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Essential Eight OS-patching maturity is scored on currency windows, but an EoL Windows 7 host can read as fully patched to its last update and still run a permanently frozen kernel, which is precisely the condition this SYSTEM escalation needs.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: A.8.8 closes the vulnerability record on patch deployment without forcing the EoL risk-acceptance-versus-decommission decision, leaving a host reachable by the CVE-2018-4990-to-CVE-2018-8120 chain marked remediated.

NIS2-Art21-incident-handling.gap: Incident handling scoped to the malicious-document event treats CVE-2018-4990 as the incident, but the CVE-2018-8120 escalation yields a SYSTEM foothold that survives Reader remediation and requires host rebuild-class response.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2018-8120 was enrolled in KEV on 2022-03-15 with a 2022-04-05 due date and known ransomware use, while the May 2018 win32k update (KB4103712 security-only, KB4103718 rollup) had been available for almost four years. The control's three branches are what make it usable on a Windows 7 SP1 / Server 2008 R2 SP1 host: the patch branch closes the CVE but requires a reboot, so a host that took the update and has not restarted is not yet mitigated; the live-patch branch does not exist for this platform; and the compensating-controls branch is the one an estate still running these editions after ESU ended on 2023-01-10 has to write down, because migration is the only durable answer and it does not fit inside a four-hour window. At EPSS 0.737 with a public Metasploit module and confirmed use chained behind CVE-2018-4990, the verified-mitigation bar is what separates a host the management console reports as done from one the exploit no longer works on.

CVE-2017-0101.name: Microsoft Windows Transaction Manager Privilege Escalation Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: A crafted local application mishandles a Kernel Transaction Manager object to corrupt kernel memory and swap the process token for SYSTEM, on the four rows MS17-017 marks affected for this CVE: Vista SP2, Server 2008 SP2, Windows 7 SP1 32-bit, and the Server 2008 R2 x64 Server Core installation.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none at the CVSS layer — PR:N — but a local foothold is required in practice; UI:R captures that a user action launches the crafted application.
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; the KTM path is directly reachable once local code runs, with no race or leak required.
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Remediated via Microsoft's March 2017 servicing; no AI-assisted discovery.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Applying MS17-017 promptly and migrating the end-of-life editions off unsupported kernels.
prevention.adequacy: The bundled bulletin fixes this CVE but leaves EoL editions exposed to any later KTM defect they will never receive a patch for.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alerting on mid-execution token changes to SYSTEM absent a legitimate logon event.
detection.adequacy: Detection fires after local code already ran, reducing dwell time rather than preventing escalation.

response.what_would_have_worked: Rotating credentials and rebuilding any host on which a token-swap-to-SYSTEM was observed, given the ransomware association.
response.adequacy: Patching alone does not evict a SYSTEM foothold established before remediation.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: SI-2 was satisfiable from 2017-03-14, yet the control's approval-based measurement let this KTM escalation persist to KEV enrollment on 2022-03-15; verifying the actual kernel build against the MS17-017 fix is what SI-2 as commonly implemented omits.

NIS2-Art21-vulnerability-handling.gap: Handling scoped to 'MS17-017 applied' cannot tell whether the specific Transaction Manager driver reached the fixed build, because the bulletin folded four separate kernel EoP CVEs into one package and one applied flag.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: B4 secure-maintenance attested against the March 2017 rollup treats Vista SP2 and Server 2008 as maintained, though they are out of support and will receive no fix for KTM defects disclosed after 2017.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: OS-patch currency scoring can read as complete on an EoL Windows 7 SP1 / Server 2008 host patched to its last available update, while the frozen kernel still exposes this CWE-119 token-swap primitive.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: A.8.8 closes the CVE-2017-0101 record on MS17-017 deployment without forcing the EoL decommission decision, so an unsupported host retains a SYSTEM escalation marked remediated.

AU-Essential-8-App-Hardening.gap: Application-hardening maturity that does not restrict unsigned local executables leaves the crafted-application foothold (UI:R) this LPE requires unconstrained, so a host patched for MS17-017 elsewhere still admits the delivery step.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2017-0101 entered KEV on 2022-03-15 with a 2022-04-05 due date and known ransomware use, five years after MS17-017 shipped the fix on 2017-03-14. The control's 'verified' qualifier is what this CVE needs most, and for two reasons specific to it: MS17-017 bundles four kernel elevation-of-privilege CVEs into one package, so an 'MS17-017 approved' record does not establish that the Transaction Manager fix reached a given kernel; and the bulletin marks the CVE-2017-0101 column 'Not applicable' on most of the rows the NVD list names, so a verification step is also what stops the four-hour clock being spent on Windows 10 and Server 2016 hosts that were never affected. With public code in Exploit-DB 44479 and EPSS 0.575, the population that matters is the small one — Vista SP2, Server 2008 SP2, Windows 7 SP1 32-bit, Server 2008 R2 x64 Server Core — where the same clock also has to carry the end-of-life migration decision that no reboot resolves.

CVE-2016-3309.name: Microsoft Windows Kernel Privilege Escalation Vulnerability (CVE-2016-3309)

attack_vector.description: A local process overflows an integer multiplication in win32kfull!bFill so the kernel under-allocates a pool buffer, then grooms GDI bitmap or palette objects around the overflow to gain kernel read/write and SYSTEM.
attack_vector.privileges_required: low — PR:L; the attacker runs local unprivileged code and reaches bFill through the GDI API.
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; a pool groom is needed but no info leak or race, and public exploits automate it.
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Discovery credited to @bee13oy of CloverSec Labs; exploitation developed by siberas/SensePost.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Applying MS16-098 and, on Windows 10, verifying the build carries the reinstated ULongMult check rather than merely being newer than MS16-098.
prevention.adequacy: The 2016 patch was undone by the vendor's own later Windows 10 builds, so a one-time 'patched' verdict is not durable for this primitive.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alerting on win32kfull!bFill pool corruption and on GDI-heavy grooming from unprivileged processes.
detection.adequacy: Detects the exploit attempt, not the latent regression; fires only once code runs.

response.what_would_have_worked: Re-testing the primitive class on every Windows 10 build to catch the fix being removed, and rebuilding hosts where a SYSTEM escalation was observed.
response.adequacy: Ordinary response treats each CVE as discrete and misses that this one re-regressed on later builds.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: SI-2 anchored to MS16-098 accepts any newer build as fixed, but the ULongMult regression on Windows 10 v1607/v1703 means a newer build can be re-vulnerable; verifying the specific overflow check is what the control omits.

NIST-800-53-CM-3.gap: CM-3 governs the operator's changes, not the vendor's removal of ULongMult from the Windows 10 codebase that reintroduced CVE-2016-3309, so estate-level change control has no signal for an upstream fix being rolled back.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: Patch-management currency assumes version progress is monotonic, yet a current v1703 x64 host was re-exposed by the vendor regression, a state the KPI cannot represent.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: B4 secure-maintenance attested against 'MS16-098 applied' overstates protection on the later Windows 10 builds where the win32kfull!bFill fix was stripped and the overflow returned.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Essential Eight OS-patch scoring cannot separate a build carrying the reinstated check from a regressed one, so a v1607 32-bit host reads patched while re-exposing the integer overflow.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: A.8.8 closes CVE-2016-3309 on MS16-098 deployment with no mechanism to reopen it when the vendor's later builds remove the fix, leaving regressed hosts exposed to the public siberas exploit while recorded remediated.

new_control_requirements.name: INCOMPLETE-PATCH-SEQUENCE-SEVERITY-MULTIPLIER
new_control_requirements.description: Vulnerability-management programs must apply a severity multiplier when a CVE is the Nth in an incomplete-patch sequence on the same primitive (third MOTW bypass, second AMSI bypass, etc.). Framework controls treating each CVE as discrete obscure the structural defect; the Nth CVE in a sequence implies that future bypasses on the same primitive are likely.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2016-3309 is the textbook incomplete-patch case: MS16-098 introduced ULongMult in 2016, Windows 10 v1607 (32-bit) removed it, and the v1703 Creators Update undercut it again on x64, re-exposing win32kfull!bFill with a public siberas exploit and KEV enrollment 2022-03-15; treating the CVE as discrete hides that later builds re-regressed the same primitive at EPSS 0.206.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2016-3309 entered KEV on 2022-03-15 (due 2022-04-05) with ransomware use; because its fix regressed on later Windows 10 builds, the KEV SLA's requirement of verified mitigation (not just 'a newer build') is what forces confirmation that the deployed build actually carries the reinstated overflow check.

attack_vector.description: A crafted application corrupts a win32k kernel object to escalate from a low-privilege/sandboxed context to SYSTEM; in the field it was the second stage behind an Office EPS RCE, delivered in a .docx that FireEye describes as appearing to be a resume.
attack_vector.privileges_required: low — PR:L; the foothold was supplied by the CVE-2015-2545 Office exploit rather than a pre-existing shell.
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L with S:C; the win32k path is directly reachable and success crosses the sandbox boundary to SYSTEM.
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Found by FireEye researchers analysing an in-the-wild attack that paired the flaw with CVE-2015-2545; no AI involvement.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Applying MS15-097 promptly, blocking untrusted Office documents from reaching the EPS filter, and migrating EoL editions.
prevention.adequacy: The patch closes this CVE but the chain also depends on the Office EPS stage, so document-delivery hardening is needed alongside the kernel fix.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alerting on a document-rendering process making win32k calls and transitioning to SYSTEM.
detection.adequacy: Fires after the Office stage already executed attacker code; reduces dwell time only.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating any host that ran the chain as SYSTEM-compromised and rebuilding, given the KEV record's known ransomware use and the post-escalation stage FireEye describes — a thread injected into explorer.exe that downloads and runs a further DLL.
response.adequacy: Patching does not evict a SYSTEM foothold established before remediation.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: SI-2 was actionable from 2015-09-08 yet the approval-based measurement let this win32k fix persist unapplied to KEV enrollment on 2022-03-15; verifying the driver build against MS15-097 is what the control as implemented omits.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: Currency-based patch-management shows the last available update as compliant on EoL Vista/Server 2008/Windows 7 SP1 editions, though only migration durably removes this CWE-119 escalation.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: B4 secure-maintenance attested against MS15-097 treats a past-support platform as maintained, though it receives no fix for later win32k defects.

AU-Essential-8-App-Hardening.gap: Application-hardening that does not stop untrusted Office documents opening the EPS filter leaves the CVE-2015-2545 stage that supplied this LPE's foothold in place, so the kernel patch alone does not break the observed chain.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: OS-patch currency can read complete on an EoL edition patched to its last update while the frozen win32k driver still exposes the escalation FireEye observed behind the CVE-2015-2545 EPS stage on 2015-09-08. The currency measure asks whether the host is on the newest build its vendor will ever ship it, which an unsupported Vista SP2 or Windows 7 SP1 machine can satisfy permanently.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: A.8.8 closes the CVE record on MS15-097 deployment without forcing the EoL decommission decision, leaving a sandbox-escape-to-SYSTEM primitive on an unsupported host marked remediated.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: MS15-097 shipped the win32k fix on 2015-09-08, the same day FireEye published the attack, and CISA enrolled CVE-2015-2546 in KEV on 2022-03-15 flagging known ransomware use — so the control's 'whichever is later' clause puts the clock at 2022, six and a half years after the patch existed. What the four-hour window has to produce on this CVE is not a download but a rebooted host: the MS15-097 package patches the win32k kernel-mode driver and takes effect on restart, and every affected line (Vista SP2, Server 2008 SP2/R2 SP1, Windows 7 SP1) is now out of support, so the documented-compensating-controls branch is where an estate still running them records its migration plan. Public exploit source exists (k0keoyo, leeqwind) and EPSS is 0.109 — low on its own, and beside the point for a bug whose value is as the SYSTEM half of the CVE-2015-2545 chain.

attack_vector.description: A compromised content process sends a crafted WebGPU IPC sequence that reuses a freed context in the privileged parent (mContext freed but not nulled at shutdown), corrupting the parent and escaping the browser sandbox.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none at the CVSS layer — PR:N — but in practice a content-process foothold is required, typically from the paired CVE-2022-26485.
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L with S:C; the shutdown-then-message groom is deterministic once the content-process stage exists, and success crosses from sandbox to parent privilege.
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Reported by Qihoo 360 ATA; 'ATA' is a human team brand, not AI-assisted discovery.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Deploying the 2022-03-05 Firefox 97.0.2 / ESR 91.6.1 build (which nulls mContext) and forcing a relaunch of the privileged browser process.
prevention.adequacy: The patch closes the escape, but only after relaunch; until then a chained content-process compromise still reaches the parent.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alerting on GPU/parent-process use-after-free crashes near WebGPUParent shutdown and on anomalous WebGPU IPC sequences.
detection.adequacy: Clean exploitation avoids the crash; detection catches failed or unstable attempts, and no public exploit code exists to derive a precise signature from.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating any host where the paired content RCE fired as sandbox-escaped, forcing relaunch fleet-wide, and reviewing browsing telemetry for the exposure window.
response.adequacy: Because this is a chain stage, response must correlate with CVE-2022-26485 activity rather than treating it in isolation.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: SI-2 is met by the 2022-03-05 97.0.2 release, but the mContext fix is inert until the privileged process relaunches; as the sandbox-escape half of a chain, an installed-not-restarted browser still admits a content-process compromise into the parent.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: A monthly patch cadence is too slow for a KEV-listed (2022-03-07) out-of-band sandbox escape; the gap between emergency release and browser relaunch is exactly where the chained escape crosses into the privileged parent.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: B4 maintenance attesting Firefox 97.0.2 deployed does not confirm the parent process was relaunched across running sessions, which is the build that matters for the WebGPU IPC escape.

AU-Essential-8-App-Hardening.gap: Firefox already shipped this feature off — dom.webgpu.enabled is disabled by default in every version, and Firefox 94 added a check that declines to allocate a WebGPUParent when it is disabled — and the sandbox escape worked anyway, because the precondition is a compromised content process rather than a page that asks for WebGPU. An application-hardening attestation recording the pref as off is accurate and buys nothing on this CVE, which is the limit of hardening as a control class against a second-stage bug: it constrains what content may request, not what an already-compromised child process may do to the parent.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Application-patch scoring tests the installed browser version, not the running one, so a fleet reads as patched to 97.0.2 while pre-fix WebGPU parent processes remain resident and escapable.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: A.8.8 closes the CVE on 97.0.2 deployment without forcing verification of a relaunched privileged process, and its EPSS 0.023 understates a bug whose real value is as the second stage behind a content-process RCE.

new_control_requirements.name: BROWSER-MANAGED-UPDATE-NO-DEFERRAL
new_control_requirements.description: Enterprise update rings must not defer security-channel browser updates beyond 24h.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2022-26486 is an in-the-wild Firefox WebGPU IPC sandbox escape fixed out-of-band on 2022-03-05 and KEV-listed 2022-03-07; a no-deferral browser-update posture with forced relaunch removes the resident pre-97.0.2 parent process within the day, closing the window in which a chained content-process RCE crosses into the privileged process.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2022-26486 entered KEV on 2022-03-07 as an actively-exploited sandbox escape; the KEV SLA's 'verified mitigation' bar forces confirmation that the privileged browser process was relaunched onto 97.0.2, closing the UK-CAF-B4 and A.8.8 running-build gaps this entry cites even though no public exploit code exists.

attack_vector.description: A crafted page frees an XSLT stylesheet parameter via a script callback during value conversion, then reuses the freed txVariable to corrupt memory in the Firefox content process and execute code.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; the attacker needs only that the victim load attacker-controlled content (UI:R).
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; the reentrant free is triggered deterministically from script, with no race or separate leak required.
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Reported by Qihoo 360 ATA; the 'ATA' brand is a human threat-analysis team, not evidence of AI-assisted discovery.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Deploying the 2022-03-05 out-of-band Firefox 97.0.2 / ESR 91.6.1 build and forcing a browser relaunch so the vulnerable process is replaced.
prevention.adequacy: The patch fully closes the UAF, but only once the browser restarts; an installed-not-relaunched build stays exploitable.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alerting on content-process crashes with a txMozillaXSLTProcessor use-after-free signature.
detection.adequacy: A successful exploit avoids the crash; detection catches failed attempts and unstable variants, not clean exploitation.

response.what_would_have_worked: Forcing browser relaunch fleet-wide after the emergency update and reviewing browsing telemetry for the exposure window.
response.adequacy: Content-process RCE is a foothold; response must also consider a chained sandbox escape (CVE-2022-26486).

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: SI-2 is met by the 2022-03-05 Firefox 97.0.2 release, but the control does not verify the vulnerable pre-97.0.2 build is no longer running; the fix is inert until relaunch, so an installed-not-restarted browser stays exploitable at EPSS 0.138.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: Patch-management under Article 21 lacks a browser-restart SLA for an actively-exploited UAF, so the KEV-listed (2022-03-07) txMozillaXSLTProcessor flaw persists on running sessions past the emergency release.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: B4 maintenance can attest Firefox 97.0.2 deployed while long-lived sessions still run the vulnerable XSLT code, because the process-relaunch requirement unique to browser fixes is not part of the attestation.

AU-Essential-8-App-Hardening.gap: Application-hardening cannot disable XSLT parameter processing, which is core rendering functionality, so it does not reduce this attack surface and only the 97.0.2-class patch removes the exposure.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Application-patch currency scoring tests the installed version, not the running one, and a browser can be patched on disk while the exploited build remains resident in a running process.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: A.8.8 closes CVE-2022-26485 on Firefox 97.0.2 deployment but does not force verification that no pre-97.0.2 session persists, which for an in-the-wild browser UAF is the meaningful remediation state.

new_control_requirements.name: BROWSER-MANAGED-UPDATE-NO-DEFERRAL
new_control_requirements.description: Enterprise update rings must not defer security-channel browser updates beyond 24h.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2022-26485 is an in-the-wild Firefox XSLT use-after-free fixed by an out-of-band release on 2022-03-05 and KEV-listed 2022-03-07 at EPSS 0.138; a no-deferral browser-update posture (with forced relaunch) is what removes the running vulnerable build within the day rather than at the next monthly cadence.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2022-26485 entered KEV on 2022-03-07 as an actively-exploited browser RCE with public PoC (mistymntncop); the KEV SLA's 'verified mitigation' bar forces confirmation that the vulnerable pre-97.0.2 process is actually replaced, closing the UK-CAF-B4 and A.8.8 running-build gaps this entry cites.

CVE-2021-21973.name: VMware vCenter Server and Cloud Foundation Server Side Request Forgery (SSRF) Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: An unauthenticated attacker reaches vCenter's vROPS plugin endpoint on port 443 and supplies a URL the plugin fails to validate, so vCenter issues the request on the attacker's behalf and returns internal data — an SSRF used for internal reconnaissance and disclosure.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; the endpoint answers before authentication.
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; a single request to a reachable port 443 triggers it, with no other precondition than network reachability.
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Reported by Mikhail Klyuchnikov of Positive Technologies; no AI involvement.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Upgrading to 7.0 U1c / 6.7 U3l / 6.5 U3n (or Cloud Foundation 4.2 / 3.10.1.2), or immediately applying the KB82374 workaround to disable the vROPS plugin, plus restricting vCenter 443 to the management plane.
prevention.adequacy: The workaround removes the vulnerable plugin without the upgrade window; the patch is durable, but neither helps an EoL 6.5/6.7 line that must be migrated.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Monitoring vCenter for outbound SSRF egress to internal addresses and for getvcdetails access-log hits.
detection.adequacy: Detects exploitation attempts and reconnaissance, but the disclosure may already have occurred by the time egress is noticed.

response.what_would_have_worked: Reviewing what internal services were reachable via the SSRF during the exposure window and treating co-exploitation with CVE-2021-21972 as possible control-plane compromise.
response.adequacy: Because the SSRF was published and exploited alongside the RCE, response should assume the pair, not the SSRF alone.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: SI-2 is met by the 7.0 U1c / 6.7 U3l / 6.5 U3n upgrade, but a quarterly virtualization patch window leaves this pre-auth SSRF (reachable since 2021-02-23, KEV 2022-03-07) open on the control plane at EPSS 0.876; the KB82374 config workaround is the interim SI-2 action the control does not require.

NIST-800-53-SC-7.gap: SC-7 boundary protection is undercut by treating vCenter's 443 as trusted-internal; the CWE-918 SSRF weaponizes that reachable port into a pivot, so a boundary posture that does not restrict who reaches vCenter's management interface does not contain it.

NIS2-Art21-network-security.gap: Article 21 network-security does not by default segment the vCenter management interface, yet reachability of port 443 is the entire precondition for this pre-auth SSRF against getvcdetails.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: B4 secure-configuration attested as 'vCenter patched' misses that until 7.0 U1c or the KB82374 workaround the vROPS plugin proxies attacker-chosen URLs, an outbound-validation defect the maintenance record does not represent.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Application-patch currency on this control-plane appliance cannot be met on the affected 6.5/6.7 lines, which reached end of general support on 2022-10-15; for those, migration rather than patching is the only remediation and the currency metric cannot express it.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.22.gap: A.8.22 network segregation applied to user networks but not to the management plane leaves vCenter's 443 reachable from general segments, allowing the getvcdetails endpoint to be used as an internal-reconnaissance proxy.

new_control_requirements.name: CONFIGURATION-SIDE-LIVE-PATCH-INVENTORY
new_control_requirements.description: For any web-fabric vulnerability with a configuration-side mitigation path: that path must be inventoried, tested, and deployable independent of the vendor-patch path. Operators cannot wait for nginx 1.30.1+ if a named-capture refactor mitigates immediately.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2021-21973 has exactly such a configuration-side path: VMware KB82374 sets the vROPS plugin to incompatible, neutralizing the getvcdetails SSRF without the vCenter upgrade window — critical because the fix (7.0 U1c / 6.7 U3l / 6.5 U3n) requires an appliance restart and the 6.5/6.7 lines are end-of-life. Inventorying and pre-testing that workaround is what lets an operator close this KEV item (added 2022-03-07, EPSS 0.876) immediately.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2021-21973 is a pre-auth SSRF on the vCenter control plane, KEV-listed 2022-03-07 (due 2022-03-21) at EPSS 0.876 and published alongside the RCE CVE-2021-21972; the KEV SLA forces either the U-release upgrade or the KB82374 workaround plus management-plane segmentation on a compressed clock rather than a quarterly window.

CVE-2020-8218.name: Pulse Connect Secure Code Injection Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: A crafted admin URL injects an OS command through the license-download CGI's unsanitised txtVLSAuthCode argument, executing on the VPN appliance after a second request triggers the staged Perl in a writable cache file.
attack_vector.privileges_required: high — PR:H; a valid administrator session is required, though it can be driven by phishing an already-logged-in admin.
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; a single GET with a deterministic payload, no race or memory-corruption primitive.
attack_vector.ai_factor: None; manual review of the admin CGI by GoSecure's penetration-test team.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Upgrade to 9.1R8 and reboot; until then, restrict which networks can reach the admin web interface and enforce anti-phishing controls on administrator accounts.
prevention.adequacy: The fix is complete, but the admin-session precondition invites deprioritisation, and restricting the admin interface does not stop a phishing link opened from an admin workstation already inside the trust zone.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alert on downloadlicenses.cgi requests carrying metacharacter-laden txtVLSAuthCode values and on writes to the setcookie.thtml.ttc cache file.
detection.adequacy: Effective only if appliance telemetry is shipped off-box; logs held on a concentrator where the attacker has command execution are within that attacker's reach.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treat a suspected-exploited concentrator as compromised: config export, rebuild, and rotation of any credential that transited the device.
response.adequacy: Patch-in-place alone leaves a pre-9.1R8 implant intact; response has to assume persistence planted through the command-execution primitive, which the write-up shows reaching the appliance filesystem.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: The control gets operators to 9.1R8 but on a server-grade cadence, whereas an RCE on the tunnel terminator listed in KEV on 2022-03-07 needs a perimeter-specific accelerated SLA the base control never states.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: A generic patch-management attestation covers the appliance without singling out that this device is the remote-access authentication boundary, so an admin-link-triggered RCE is scored like an ordinary server patch.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: B4 vulnerability management assumes admin-only endpoints are safe behind authentication; CVE-2020-8218 fires from a single administrator GET, so the phishing-delivery path is outside what the principle routinely tests.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: The 48-hour internet-facing patch expectation applies since 9.1R8 shipped 2020-07-29, but Essential Eight gives no extra weighting to the concentrator being the perimeter trust boundary rather than a generic web service.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: A.8.8 detects the sub-9.1R8 version but closes on the upgrade; it cannot surface an implant left from the pre-patch window, so a version-check pass reads clean on a device that may still be compromised.

NIST-800-53-SI-4.gap: SI-4 monitors the appliance in principle, but without a requirement to forward gateway telemetry to a separate trust zone the exploitation record sits on the very device the attacker is executing commands on and can erase.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2020-8218 on Pulse Connect Secure was KEV-listed 2022-03-07 with a 2022-09-07 due date, though the 9.1R8 fix had been available since 2020-07-29; the six-month official window is far slower than a perimeter RCE at EPSS 0.32 (98th percentile) warrants.

new_control_requirements.name: FIREWALL-EGRESS-TELEMETRY-SEPARATE-TRUST-ZONE
new_control_requirements.description: Firewall and other perimeter-trust-boundary devices must forward syslog, threat logs, and authentication logs to a SIEM hosted in a separate trust zone (different management plane, different credentials, different authentication path). Telemetry stored on the compromised device is destroyed by the attacker; telemetry on a separate-trust-zone collector survives.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2020-8218 gives an attacker OS command execution on the Pulse Connect Secure concentrator itself, KEV-listed 2022-03-07 against a fix that shipped 2020-07-29, so the admin-portal and system logs that would record the downloadlicenses.cgi request sit on the same device the attacker is executing on; only telemetry already shipped off-box before exploitation survives to reconstruct the intrusion.

CVE-2019-11581.name: Atlassian Jira Server and Data Center Server-Side Template Injection Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: A crafted template expression in the ContactAdministrators or SendBulkMail field is evaluated server-side, executing Java and OS commands in the Jira process; the ContactAdministrators path is unauthenticated where the contact form and SMTP are enabled.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N for the ContactAdministrators path (contact form and SMTP must be configured); administrator for SendBulkMail.
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; a single crafted POST, no memory-corruption or timing primitive.
attack_vector.ai_factor: None; Atlassian's advisory credits Daniil Dmitriev with finding it, and the public exploits that followed were written by human researchers.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Upgrade to a fixed Jira build and restart; interim, apply both halves of the advisory's workaround — disable the Contact Administrators Form and block /secure/ContactAdministrators to remove the unauthenticated path, and block the three SendBulkMail endpoints to remove the administrator path.
prevention.adequacy: The fix is complete, but the interim mitigation is a configuration action a patch-only process does not prompt.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alert on ContactAdministrators/SendBulkMail requests carrying template syntax and on the Jira JVM spawning shells.
detection.adequacy: Requires request-body inspection; authentication logs alone miss the unauthenticated ContactAdministrators path.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treat a hit as code execution in the Jira service context: rotate Jira credentials and integration tokens, and review for persistence.
response.adequacy: Restarting onto the fixed build stops new exploitation but does not undo actions already taken in the Jira process context.

NIST-800-53-SI-10.gap: SI-10 is the defeated control — user input reached a template evaluator unsanitised — and a policy attestation cannot see that a named field is an expression sink; only the vendor fix or source review closes it.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: SI-2 reaches the fixed builds on a normal cadence, but gives no priority weight to the unauthenticated ContactAdministrators path, so a pre-auth RCE at EPSS 0.846 is treated like a routine application patch.

NIS2-Art21-vulnerability-handling.gap: Tracking the CVE satisfies Art21, yet the control never forces the check of whether the contact form and SMTP are enabled, which is what decides if the instance is unauthenticated-exploitable.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: B4's patch-centric framing does not surface the disable-contact-form configuration mitigation, leaving instances that cannot upgrade at once without the control that removes the unauthenticated reach.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: The 48-hour internet-facing expectation applies with fixes out since 2019, but the control does not distinguish the pre-auth ContactAdministrators reach from the admin-only SendBulkMail one.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.28.gap: A.8.28 secure coding applies to the organisation's own code, not Atlassian's template handling, so the injection is inherited with no A.8.28 evidence covering the third-party product.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2019-11581 in Jira Server/Data Center was KEV-listed 2022-03-07 while fixed builds had shipped in 2019; at EPSS 0.846 (99.7th percentile) with public PoCs, the unauthenticated ContactAdministrators path warrants immediate mitigation rather than a routine application-patch window.

new_control_requirements.name: MITIGATION-ACTIVE-PATCH-PENDING-VERDICT-CLASS
new_control_requirements.description: Compliance verdicts must distinguish three states: (a) binary patch deployed (vulnerability eliminated), (b) vendor-mitigation rule active, no binary patch (residual risk: any defect in the mitigation rule reopens the vulnerability), (c) no mitigation, no patch (full exposure). Audit reports must surface (b) as a distinct compensating-control state with an associated time-bound action item, not as a 'patched per SLA' outcome.
new_control_requirements.evidence: For CVE-2019-11581, disabling the Contact Administrators form is a genuine state-(b) mitigation that removes the unauthenticated path without upgrading Jira; an audit that records such an instance as 'patched' hides that a version-level RCE remains and that re-enabling the form reopens it.

CVE-2017-6077.name: NETGEAR DGN2200 Remote Code Execution Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: An authenticated POST to ping.cgi injects a shell command through the ping_IPAddr field, running arbitrary commands on the router's Linux OS; default and hardcoded web credentials make authentication trivial.
attack_vector.privileges_required: low — authenticated to the router web UI, but default/hardcoded credentials reduce this to near-zero on many units.
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; a single POST with a metacharacter payload, no timing or memory primitive.
attack_vector.ai_factor: None; published as an Exploit-DB entry by a human author.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Install DGN2200v1 firmware 1.0.0.55 and let the router reboot onto it, change the administrator password away from the default, and keep remote management off so the web UI is not reachable from the WAN.
prevention.adequacy: 1.0.0.55 closes the injection outright. The vendor's fallback — changing the administrator password — leaves the vulnerable ping.cgi handler in place and reachable to whoever obtains the new password, so it is protection contingent on that password holding.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Inspect ping.cgi request bodies for metacharacters in ping_IPAddr and alert on router-originated outbound traffic.
detection.adequacy: SOHO routers rarely emit inspectable telemetry, so detection usually depends on upstream network monitoring.

response.what_would_have_worked: Reset the router to factory defaults, reflash DGN2200v1 firmware 1.0.0.55 from the Download Center rather than trusting the running image, and set a new administrator password.
response.adequacy: A firmware reflash does not evict configuration changes an attacker made; a full reset or replacement is the reliable path.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: SI-2 assumes managed assets; an unmanaged DGN2200 consumer router usually has no inventory entry, so the KEV-listed command injection has no owner to remediate within any SLA.

NIST-800-53-CM-7.gap: CM-7 would counsel disabling the ping diagnostic that carries the injection, but the DGN2200 UI offers no way to remove ping.cgi, so the only least-functionality lever is not exposing the admin interface.

NIS2-Art21-network-security.gap: Art21 network-security assumes manageable devices; a router reached with shipped default credentials is exploitable by anyone at its web UI, and the control does not force the credential-change and isolation that actually mitigate it.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: B4 presumes a managed patch pathway, and this one ends at a consumer Download Center where DGN2200v1 firmware 1.0.0.55 has to be fetched and applied per unit by its owner. NETGEAR's advisory also treats changing the administrator password away from the default as protection against the command-execution flaw, so two units on the same build can be in opposite states while B4's version-keyed evidence records them identically.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Patch Applications does not scope consumer router firmware, so an estate can be compliant while a DGN2200 at firmware 10.0.0.50 or below sits exploitable on its edge.
