ISO-27001-2022-A.8.9.gap: A.8.9 configuration management is the real gap: the exposure comes from shipped default credentials and an exposed interface, and an ISMS that omits SOHO routers from its baseline never records that these devices ship exploitable.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2017-6077 on the NETGEAR DGN2200v1 was KEV-listed 2022-03-07 at EPSS 0.682 (99.3rd percentile), with a working Exploit-DB shell (41394) public since February 2017 and NETGEAR's fix, firmware 1.0.0.55, published in the same advisory that documents the flaw. The fix is a manual per-unit download rather than a pushed update, so meeting any SLA on this asset class means either that manual reflash or the vendor's documented alternative — changing the administrator password from the default — recorded explicitly as a compensating control.

new_control_requirements.name: MITIGATION-ACTIVE-PATCH-PENDING-VERDICT-CLASS
new_control_requirements.description: Compliance verdicts must distinguish three states: (a) binary patch deployed (vulnerability eliminated), (b) vendor-mitigation rule active, no binary patch (residual risk: any defect in the mitigation rule reopens the vulnerability), (c) no mitigation, no patch (full exposure). Audit reports must surface (b) as a distinct compensating-control state with an associated time-bound action item, not as a 'patched per SLA' outcome.
new_control_requirements.evidence: NETGEAR's advisory offers two different things for CVE-2017-6077 on the DGN2200v1 and an audit has to tell them apart: firmware 1.0.0.55 is state (a), while 'If you change your admin password from the default password, your router or modem router is protected from the remote command execution vulnerability' is state (b) — the vulnerable ping.cgi handler is still shipped, still concatenating ping_IPAddr into a shell command, and still reachable to whoever holds the new password. Recording the password change as 'patched per SLA' erases that difference on a KEV-listed flaw at EPSS 0.682.

CVE-2016-6277.name: NETGEAR Multiple Routers Remote Code Execution Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: An unauthenticated request whose /cgi-bin/ path-info begins with a semicolon runs arbitrary OS commands on the router; the public PoC opens telnet, and NVD's CWE-352 tag reflects the optional crafted-link delivery.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; the /cgi-bin/;command injection needs no credentials.
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; a single crafted GET, though NVD records UI:R for the lure-a-victim delivery option.
attack_vector.ai_factor: None; published by human researcher Acew0rm and coordinated via CERT/CC.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Install the per-model fixed firmware and reboot, and keep the router administration interface off the WAN and untrusted client networks.
prevention.adequacy: The production firmware closes the injection outright. Two things blunt it: NETGEAR states a unit left on the earlier beta build still carries the command-injection potential, and the advisory names no fixed version, so 'updated' and 'fixed' can only be reconciled per model on its own firmware release page.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Inspect for /cgi-bin/; path-info with $IFS or command syntax and alert on new router-side listening services.
detection.adequacy: Depends on upstream inspection; the router itself provides little usable telemetry.

response.what_would_have_worked: Reset the router to factory defaults, install the production firmware for the model from NETGEAR's firmware release page, and re-enter configuration by hand rather than restoring a backup taken while the unit was exposed.
response.adequacy: Command execution allows persistent config changes, so a firmware reflash alone may not evict the attacker.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: The evidence SI-2 collects is that firmware was updated, and for this CVE that does not settle whether the flaw is closed. NETGEAR's advisory disowns its own beta build — the production version is required or 'the potential for this command injection vulnerability remains' — and gives no fixed version number for any of the eleven affected models, so an SI-2 record has nothing to compare a reported build string against and reads the same either way.

NIST-800-53-SC-7.gap: SC-7 is the operative control — an unauthenticated /cgi-bin/ injection is neutralised by keeping the admin interface off untrusted networks — but enterprise SC-7 rarely enumerates SOHO routers as the boundary they are.

NIS2-Art21-network-security.gap: Art21 assumes the device enforces its own boundary, but the router answers unauthenticated command injection, and NVD's open-ended model list makes the affected inventory hard to scope fully.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: B4's periodic patch rhythm is far slower than the continuous automated exploitation an EPSS-0.998 wormable flaw attracts, so exposed units are hit well within any patch window.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Patch Applications does not scope SOHO router firmware, so an estate can be compliant while an unpatched R7000 or R8000 answers unauthenticated RCE, with no weight given to the flaw being wormable.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.22.gap: A.8.22 network segregation bounds the exposure by isolating the admin interface, but an ISMS that treats the router as infrastructure rather than an in-scope asset never applies it to the device's management plane.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2016-6277 across the NETGEAR R6xxx/R7xxx/R8xxx line was KEV-listed 2022-03-07 at EPSS 0.998 (99.96th percentile) with public Metasploit and Exploit-DB code; the near-certain exploitation probability makes immediate mitigation — fixed firmware or WAN-side interface isolation — mandatory rather than a periodic-patch item.

new_control_requirements.name: PERIMETER-COMPROMISE-REBUILD-NOT-PATCH
new_control_requirements.description: Pre-rehearsed IR runbook for any perimeter device that suffers a pre-auth RCE CVE in active exploitation MUST default to config-exfil + rebuild + credential rotation, not patch-in-place. Patch-in-place leaves attacker-installed implants intact.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2016-6277 is a pre-auth RCE on an edge router with EPSS 0.998 and a public telnet-opening PoC; a unit exposed to the WAN must be assumed to carry attacker config changes (e.g. an added listening service), so a firmware reflash alone is insufficient and the device needs a from-baseline rebuild.

attack_vector.description: ColdFusion 9.0, 9.0.1 and 9.0.2 disclose sensitive server information through vectors Adobe and NVD both leave unspecified. Adobe's phrasing is the operative constraint: 'information disclosure from a compromised server', which reads as an outcome available once the host is already held, not as a way in.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N per the CVSS vector.
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; the specific mechanism is unpublished by Adobe and NVD, but the CVSS records low attack complexity.
attack_vector.ai_factor: None; credited to human researchers Will Fuller and Charlie Arehart.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: In 2013, the APSB13-03 hotfix and restart; today, migration off end-of-life ColdFusion 9.x to a supported release.
prevention.adequacy: The hotfix was complete at the time, but on a dead runtime only migration remains, which a patch-only process does not surface.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Monitor ColdFusion admin/component endpoints for anomalous disclosure responses and restrict them from untrusted networks.
detection.adequacy: The unspecified vector limits signature precision; network isolation of the admin surface is the more reliable lever.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treat a ColdFusion 9.x server on which this flaw is suspected as already compromised — that is the state Adobe's own wording assumes — and rebuild it, rotating every credential and key the server could read.
response.adequacy: Rebuilding removes the host but not the consequence: anything the server could read stays valid until it is rotated, and since Adobe publishes no mechanism there is no way to bound what was read.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: SI-2 was met by the 2013 hotfix, but ColdFusion 9.x has been end-of-life since 2014-12-31, so no current patch exists and the control's patch framing offers no path but migration.

NIST-800-53-SC-28.gap: SC-28 encryption-at-rest presumes a trustworthy platform, but the ColdFusion 9.x server itself leaks information, so at-rest protections do not address a disclosure through the application's own code.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: Art21 assumes a supported product with updates; ColdFusion 9.x has neither, so the control cannot be met by patching and the unsupported-software risk falls outside its framing.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: B4 points at applying vendor fixes, but an end-of-life 9.x install has none, so the required migration-or-retire outcome is outside what the principle expresses.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Patch Applications cannot be satisfied on a past-support ColdFusion 9.x runtime; the honest posture is decommissioning, which the patch metric does not capture.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: A.8.8 flags 9.x as vulnerable but its timely-remediation expectation is unmeetable on an end-of-life runtime, so the retirement decision belongs to lifecycle controls A.8.8's version check does not drive.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2013-0631 was KEV-listed 2022-03-07 for ColdFusion 9.x, a runtime already end-of-life since 2014-12-31; with no current patch, the required mitigation within the SLA is documented isolation of the admin surface pending migration off the dead version.

new_control_requirements.name: MITIGATION-ACTIVE-PATCH-PENDING-VERDICT-CLASS
new_control_requirements.description: Compliance verdicts must distinguish three states: (a) binary patch deployed (vulnerability eliminated), (b) vendor-mitigation rule active, no binary patch (residual risk: any defect in the mitigation rule reopens the vulnerability), (c) no mitigation, no patch (full exposure). Audit reports must surface (b) as a distinct compensating-control state with an associated time-bound action item, not as a 'patched per SLA' outcome.
new_control_requirements.evidence: An end-of-life ColdFusion 9.0.x install is a state-(c) asset — no vendor fix is available for CVE-2013-0631 — so an audit must record it as full exposure with a migration action item rather than as patched; interface isolation is a documented state-(b) compensating control, not a fix.

attack_vector.description: A ../ path parameter to cfcexplorer.cfc reads files outside the component directory; where no ColdFusion password is set the traversal is unauthenticated, and it can be chained with the CVE-2013-0632 auth bypass otherwise.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N where the Administrator/RDS password is unset; otherwise credentials or the CVE-2013-0632 bypass.
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; a crafted GET with ../ sequences, no memory or timing primitive.
attack_vector.ai_factor: None; credited to human researchers Michael McDowell and Harry Lane.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: In 2013, the APSB13-03 hotfix and restart, plus setting RDS/Administrator passwords; today, migration off end-of-life 9.x/10.
prevention.adequacy: The password step closes the no-credential path but not the traversal itself; on a dead runtime only migration fully remediates.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alert on cfcexplorer.cfc requests carrying ../ path parameters and restrict the admin surface from untrusted networks.
detection.adequacy: The traversal shape is distinctive and detectable, but detection does not prevent a single successful read of a secret file.

response.what_would_have_worked: Assume any file readable via the traversal was read; rotate exposed secrets and rebuild a server implicated in the 2013 chain.
response.adequacy: Files disclosed before remediation stay compromised until their contents are rotated.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: SI-2 was met by the 2013 hotfix, but ColdFusion 9.x and 10 are end-of-life (2014-12-31 and 2017-05-16), so no current patch exists and only migration remediates.

NIST-800-53-AC-3.gap: AC-3 is the defeated control — cfcexplorer.cfc serves files outside the component directory, and with no password set enforcement is absent — so an application-layer AC-3 attestation does not stop the path-parameter escape.

NIS2-Art21-vulnerability-handling.gap: Tracking the CVE meets Art21, but the control does not force the interim RDS/Administrator password step that closes the no-credential traversal on un-hotfixable installs.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: B4 points at the vendor hotfix, but end-of-life 9.x/10 have none, so the password-hardening interim and migration outcome fall outside its patch framing.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Patch Applications cannot be met on past-support 9.x/10, and it does not capture that the traversal is unauthenticated exactly when the Administrator password is unset.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: A.8.8 flags the traversal but timely remediation is impossible on an end-of-life runtime, and its version check does not surface the unset-password precondition of the no-credential path.

new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2013-0629 was KEV-listed 2022-03-07 for ColdFusion 9.x and 10, both end-of-life; with no current patch, the required mitigation within the SLA is setting RDS/Administrator passwords and isolating the admin surface pending migration.

new_control_requirements.name: MITIGATION-ACTIVE-PATCH-PENDING-VERDICT-CLASS
new_control_requirements.description: Compliance verdicts must distinguish three states: (a) binary patch deployed (vulnerability eliminated), (b) vendor-mitigation rule active, no binary patch (residual risk: any defect in the mitigation rule reopens the vulnerability), (c) no mitigation, no patch (full exposure). Audit reports must surface (b) as a distinct compensating-control state with an associated time-bound action item, not as a 'patched per SLA' outcome.
new_control_requirements.evidence: For CVE-2013-0629, setting RDS/Administrator passwords on an un-hotfixable ColdFusion install is a state-(b) mitigation that removes the unauthenticated traversal path without eliminating the flaw; an audit must record it as compensating-control-active with a migration action item, not as patched.

attack_vector.description: On a ColdFusion 9.x install with no password set, an attacker bypasses authentication into the Administrator and chains it to RCE by scheduling a task that fetches and runs a .cfm payload in the CFIDE webroot.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N where the Administrator/RDS password is unconfigured.
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; a sequence of administrator HTTP requests once the password-less state is confirmed, no memory primitive.
attack_vector.ai_factor: None; credited to human researchers Michael McDowell and Harry Lane.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: In 2013, the APSB13-03 hotfix and restart, plus setting the Administrator and RDS passwords; today, migration off end-of-life 9.x.
prevention.adequacy: Setting the password closes the bypass immediately, but on a dead runtime full remediation is migration; the interim step is easily missed.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alert on password-less Administrator logins and on scheduler tasks that publish files to CFIDE from external URLs.
detection.adequacy: The scheduler-drop pattern is distinctive, but detection fires only after the admin path is already reached.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treat an implicated server as compromised: remove attacker .cfm files, rotate secrets, and rebuild if part of the 2013 chain.
response.adequacy: RCE via the scheduler means persistence may survive a password change; rebuild is the reliable outcome.

NIST-800-53-IA-2.gap: IA-2 is the defeated control: a password-less ColdFusion 9.x install accepts admin access with no credential, so an attestation assuming accounts are password-protected misses a state where authentication is absent.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: SI-2 was met by the 2013 hotfix, but ColdFusion 9.x is end-of-life since 2014-12-31 with no current patch, so only migration remediates the auth-bypass-to-RCE.

NIS2-Art21-identity-management.gap: Art21 identity management assumes authenticated admin access, but the password-less state means there is no identity on the admin path, and the control does not force the password-setting interim closure.

UK-CAF-B2.gap: B2 presumes credentials gate privileged functions, but an unconfigured-password ColdFusion install grants admin and then RCE to anyone who reaches it, a state B2's attestation does not surface.

AU-ISM-1546.gap: ISM-1546 requires authentication before access, yet the unconfigured-password state admits an attacker with no authentication event, so the control reads as met while the product accepts access without a credential.

ISO-27001-2022-A.5.15.gap: A.5.15 access control is defeated by the missing-password condition: the flaw is the absence of the control A.5.15 assumes, so an attestation that access is restricted does not catch a runtime granting admin without a credential.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Patch Applications cannot be met on past-support ColdFusion 9.x, and it does not capture that the bypass is conditional on the Administrator password being unset.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2013-0625 was KEV-listed 2022-03-07 for ColdFusion 9.x at EPSS 0.938 (99.8th percentile) with a working Metasploit auth-bypass-to-RCE chain; on this end-of-life runtime the required mitigation within the SLA is setting the Administrator/RDS password and isolating the admin surface pending migration.

new_control_requirements.name: MITIGATION-ACTIVE-PATCH-PENDING-VERDICT-CLASS
new_control_requirements.description: Compliance verdicts must distinguish three states: (a) binary patch deployed (vulnerability eliminated), (b) vendor-mitigation rule active, no binary patch (residual risk: any defect in the mitigation rule reopens the vulnerability), (c) no mitigation, no patch (full exposure). Audit reports must surface (b) as a distinct compensating-control state with an associated time-bound action item, not as a 'patched per SLA' outcome.
new_control_requirements.evidence: For CVE-2013-0625, setting the Administrator password on an un-hotfixable ColdFusion 9.x install is a state-(b) mitigation that removes the bypass without eliminating the underlying flaw; an audit must record it as compensating-control-active with a migration action item, not as patched.

attack_vector.description: A single crafted AMFX/XML message to the BlazeDS remoting gateway defines an external XML entity that the parser resolves, returning a local file or internal resource to an unauthenticated caller.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; the gateway answers unauthenticated remoting requests by design
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; one crafted POST, no groom or leak. NVD's vector carries UI:R; the mechanism described does not require a second party, and the divergence is recorded rather than reconciled
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Human researchers at Security-Assessment.com disclosed it; no AI tooling involved.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Disable XML external-entity resolution in the BlazeDS/messaging parser and apply apsb10-05 to every embedding product.
prevention.adequacy: Preventive where the hotfix reaches the embedded BlazeDS layer, with two limits: a product-version patch may leave the bundled library at a pre-fix level, and on every embedding line named here — ColdFusion 7.x, 8.x and 9.x, the LiveCycle ES 8.x.x and ES2 9.x.x components, and LiveCycle Data Services 2.5.x, 2.6.x and 3.0.x — it leaves a runtime past Adobe's end of extended support, the last of those dates being 2016-12-31, where the closing action is migration or removal rather than a hotfix.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alert on gateway responses returning filesystem content and on inbound XML carrying external-entity declarations.
detection.adequacy: Detects exploitation only after data has already been read; confidentiality loss is not reversible by detection.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treat any successful read as disclosure of whatever the app-server account could read and rotate exposed secrets.
response.adequacy: Bounds the blast radius after the fact but cannot recall data already returned to the attacker.

NIST-800-53-SI-10.gap: SI-10 input-validation is nominally in place, yet a legal XML DOCTYPE passes syntactic validation while the parser still resolves the external entity — the control checks input shape, not the dangerous parser feature that CVE-2009-3960 abuses.

NIS2-Art21-vulnerability-management.gap: A vulnerability-management process keyed on current advisories deprioritises a 2009 CVE, but its EPSS of 0.90012 on 2026-08-20 and the KEV ransomware flag show it is still actively targeted inside unpatched ColdFusion/LiveCycle stacks.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: B4 system-security tracking that follows the ColdFusion or LiveCycle build number reports current while the embedded BlazeDS 3.2 runtime remains pre-apsb10-05 and continues to resolve external entities.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Not one of the embedding products this CVE reaches is still supported: Adobe's extended support ended 2012-02-07, 2014-07-31 and 2016-12-31 for ColdFusion 7.x, 8.x and 9.x, 2014-07-31 for the LiveCycle ES 8.x.x components and 2016-12-31 for the ES2 9.x.x components, and 2014-06-30, 2015-09-30 and 2016-12-31 for LiveCycle Data Services 2.5.x, 2.6.x and 3.0.x. A metric computed over applied vendor updates therefore has nothing left to measure on any of those hosts. Closing CVE-2009-3960 means moving the messaging tier onto a supported runtime or removing it, and neither is expressible as patch application.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: A.8.8 registers keyed on product names rather than embedded libraries will not surface a host where ColdFusion or LiveCycle is present but the bundled BlazeDS 3.2 never received apsb10-05, leaving the XXE exposure invisible to the vulnerability register.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Adobe BlazeDS CVE-2009-3960 was KEV-listed 2022-03-07 (ransomware: Known) with EPSS 0.90012 (99.784th percentile) on 2026-08-20; the apsb10-05 fix existed since 2010, so the operative clock is KEV-listing-to-verified-mitigation across every embedding ColdFusion/LiveCycle/Flex Data Services instance, not patch availability. What counts as verified mitigation is migration to a supported runtime or removal of the Flex/AMF messaging tier, because every embedding line Adobe's lifecycle matrix dates is past its end of extended support: ColdFusion 7.x, 8.x and 9.x on 2012-02-07, 2014-07-31 and 2016-12-31, the LiveCycle ES 8.x.x components on 2014-07-31 and the ES2 9.x.x components on 2016-12-31, and LiveCycle Data Services 2.5.x, 2.6.x and 3.0.x on 2014-06-30, 2015-09-30 and 2016-12-31. Flex Data Services 2.0.1 is the one line the matrix does not date at all, so there is no published support end to plan against and removal is the assumption that holds. External-entity resolution disabled at the parser is the documented compensating control until the migration or removal lands.

CVE-2022-20708.name: Cisco Small Business RV Series Routers Stack-based Buffer Overflow Vulnerability (CVE-2022-20708)

attack_vector.description: A low-privilege request to the RV340/RV345 management component, sent from a segment attached to the router, carries shell metacharacters that the firmware passes to the OS, executing the attacker's command on the device.
attack_vector.privileges_required: low — PR:L; any valid authenticated session suffices, and NVD's AV:A places the sender on an adjacent segment before that
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; no interaction or groom, one crafted request injects the command
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Credited to external human researchers.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Upgrade to firmware 1.0.03.26; interim, restrict management reachability and the credentialed user population.
prevention.adequacy: The firmware fix adds input neutralisation; the interim measures reduce who can reach the flaw but do not remove it.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alert on management requests bearing shell metacharacters and on unexpected router child processes or egress.
detection.adequacy: Both signals are produced by the device the injected command runs on, so they are trustworthy only where the router already forwards management logs to a collector it does not control.

response.what_would_have_worked: Rotate device credentials and rebuild configuration if command injection from an authenticated session is suspected.
response.adequacy: Required because command execution on the router can establish persistence beyond the injected command.

NIST-800-53-SI-10.gap: SI-10 form-level input validation still lets a metacharacter-bearing value reach the OS command interpreter, because the missing neutralisation is inside the RV340/RV345 firmware and is fixed only by 1.0.03.26.

NIS2-Art21-network-security.gap: Controls that rely on the router as enforcement point are undercut when a low-privilege session runs OS commands on it. At EPSS 0.14863 on 2026-08-20 the only pre-firmware measures are narrowing which attached segments can reach the management interface and which accounts can hold a session at all — a perimeter rule facing the WAN does not bound an AV:A attacker who is already on an attached segment.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: B4 network-device hardening does not cover the unsanitised-input path that turns any valid RV340/RV345 session into execution of an attacker's command on the device's Linux operating system, so the posture passes while the path stays open until 1.0.03.26.

AU-Essential-8-App-Hardening.gap: Application hardening of endpoints does not touch a network device's own web-management component, so the RV340/RV345 executes injected commands regardless of the control's coverage.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.28.gap: A.8.28 secure-coding attestations about the operator's own software cannot reach a coding defect inside Cisco firmware, so the concatenation of user input into an OS command is closed only by the vendor fix in 1.0.03.26.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Cisco RV340/RV345 CVE-2022-20708 is an authenticated OS command injection KEV-listed 2022-03-03 (due 2022-03-17) with EPSS 0.14863 on 2026-08-20; the fixed firmware 1.0.03.26 already existed, so the operative clock is KEV-listing-to-verified-mitigation, with restricted management reachability and a limited credentialed population as the documented compensating controls until the upgrade lands.

CVE-2022-20703.name: Cisco Small Business RV Series Routers Stack-based Buffer Overflow Vulnerability (CVE-2022-20703)

attack_vector.description: The RV-series routers install and boot an unsigned or modified software image because their digital-signature verification can be bypassed, letting an attacker replace the firmware the device runs.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N, but AV:A/UI:R: adjacent-network position and an initiated install are required
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; no memory groom, the difficulty is arranging for the malicious image to be installed
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Credited to external human researchers.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Upgrade to 1.0.01.07 / 1.0.03.26; interim, control who can initiate installs and verify image provenance out of band.
prevention.adequacy: The firmware fix restores signature verification; the interim controls depend on the operator, since the device itself cannot be trusted to reject an unsigned image.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Compare staged image hashes against published Cisco signed builds and alert on installs outside change windows.
detection.adequacy: Detects a bad image only if provenance is checked out of band, since the device's own reported version can be forged.

response.what_would_have_worked: Re-flash from a known-good signed image and rebuild configuration if a modified image is suspected.
response.adequacy: Necessary because a malicious image is persistent firmware that a normal upgrade may not fully displace.

NIST-800-53-CM-3.gap: CM-3 change control that approves 'a firmware update' cannot tell an authorized image from an attacker's unsigned one while the device's signature check is bypassable, until 1.0.01.07 / 1.0.03.26 restores verification.

NIS2-Art21-supply-chain.gap: Supply-chain assurance that trusts the RV-series device to reject unsigned software has no compensating control on this line once the signature bypass exists, so image provenance must be enforced out of band until firmware is applied.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: B4 that trusts the boot image because the device 'only accepts signed firmware' is defeated by exactly this bypass, letting a modified image run as legitimate firmware with no integrity signal to the operator.

AU-Essential-8-App-Hardening.gap: Application hardening of the management UI does not touch the firmware-install path where the image-signature enforcement fails, so the control leaves the install-time bypass entirely unaddressed.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.9.gap: An A.8.9 baseline check that reads the reported firmware version cannot distinguish a genuine 1.0.03.26 image from a modified one presenting the same version string while the signature bypass remains.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Cisco RV-series CVE-2022-20703 is a software-image signature-verification bypass KEV-listed 2022-03-03 (due 2022-03-17) with EPSS 0.09203 on 2026-08-20; the fixed firmware (1.0.01.07 / 1.0.03.26) already existed, so the operative clock is KEV-listing-to-verified-mitigation, with out-of-band image provenance verification as the documented compensating control until the upgrade lands.

CVE-2022-20701.name: Cisco Small Business RV Series Routers Stack-based Buffer Overflow Vulnerability (CVE-2022-20701)

attack_vector.description: A low-privileged local session on the RV340/RV345 escalates to root because the web management component does not enforce authorization on certain operations.
attack_vector.privileges_required: low — PR:L; an authenticated low-privilege session is the precondition
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; once the foothold exists the escalation is deterministic with no race or groom
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Credited to external human researchers.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Upgrade to firmware 1.0.03.26; interim, constrain who can obtain any authenticated session on the device.
prevention.adequacy: The firmware fix restores the privilege boundary; the interim measure only reduces the population that can reach the flaw, it does not close it.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alert on privilege transitions within a single management session and on root-context actions from non-admin accounts.
detection.adequacy: Both signals come from the device's own web-management audit, so they exist only where session-level records are already forwarded off the router; where they are not, the escalation leaves nothing that survives it.

response.what_would_have_worked: Rotate all device accounts and rebuild configuration if a non-admin session is suspected of having escalated.
response.adequacy: Bounds the damage but only after the escalation; the firmware fix is still required to remove the path.

NIST-800-53-AC-6.gap: AC-6 least-privilege attestations pass while the firmware lets a low-privilege local session cross to root, because the missing authorization check is in the device, not in the account rights AC-6 governs, until 1.0.03.26.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: The 2022-03-03 KEV clock is satisfied only by firmware 1.0.03.26, which reboots the RV340/RV345 and has no live-patch alternative, so any device kept in service between the listing and its upgrade window sits with the local-to-root path open. At EPSS 0.09747 on 2026-08-20 the measure records the patch process rather than that interim state, whose sole control is how many accounts can raise a session on the device.

UK-CAF-B2.gap: B2 controls scoped to who may log in do not address an already-authenticated low-privilege session escalating to root, so tightening login does not close a path the firmware's missing authorization check opens.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: The Essential Eight patch window is long relative to a local escalation that chains with the bundle's unauthenticated flaws, and it does not require the interim constraint on who can obtain an authenticated session that is the only pre-firmware lever.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: An A.8.8 register that collapses the advisory bundle into one item understates that this CVE specifically needs an existing account and is remediated only by firmware 1.0.03.26, distinct from the unauthenticated members.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Cisco RV340/RV345 CVE-2022-20701 is a local-to-root escalation KEV-listed 2022-03-03 (due 2022-03-17) with EPSS 0.09747 on 2026-08-20; the fixed firmware 1.0.03.26 already existed, so the operative clock is KEV-listing-to-verified-mitigation, with constraining authenticated access as the documented compensating control until the upgrade lands.

CVE-2022-20700.name: Cisco Small Business RV Series Routers Stack-based Buffer Overflow Vulnerability (CVE-2022-20700)

attack_vector.description: The RV-series web management interface performs privileged, root-level management actions for an unauthenticated remote caller because authorization is not enforced, allowing full device takeover from a single request.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; the management interface fails to require authentication for privileged functions
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; no groom or interaction, only reachability of the management interface
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Credited to external human researchers in the Cisco advisory.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Upgrade to 1.0.01.07 / 1.0.03.26; until then, restrict the management interface to trusted sources and remove WAN-side management.
prevention.adequacy: The firmware fix restores authorization enforcement; the interim restriction is effective only where the operator actually removes management reachability.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alert on privileged management actions with no preceding authentication and on new admin sessions from unexpected sources.
detection.adequacy: A privileged action with no preceding authentication event is an unambiguous signal, but the record of it is written by the device the caller has just taken control of, so it is dependable only where the router already ships management logs to a collector elsewhere.

response.what_would_have_worked: Rebuild the router configuration and rotate credentials after any suspected unauthenticated takeover.
response.adequacy: Required because root-level control can leave persistent changes a firmware upgrade does not undo.

NIST-800-53-AC-3.gap: AC-3 is the enforcement this CVE removes: the firmware grants privileged functions without authorization, so an access-enforcement attestation passes while an unauthenticated caller reaches root, and only firmware 1.0.01.07 / 1.0.03.26 repairs it.

NIS2-Art21-network-security.gap: Network-security controls that rely on the router to mediate access cannot help when its management plane fails open; at CVSS 9.8 and EPSS 0.05655 on 2026-08-20, only removing management reachability mitigates before firmware is applied.

UK-CAF-B2.gap: B2 identity-and-access assumes the device checks credentials before privileged actions, but the RV-series firmware never checks them here, so strong administrator credentials do nothing against a path that is never authenticated.

AU-ISM-1546.gap: ISM-1546 authentication implemented at the login page does not cover the unauthenticated management path this CVE reaches, because the privileged operation runs for a caller who was never authenticated in the first place.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.22.gap: Segregation is the control that bounds this flaw, and the boundary has to be drawn around the management interface itself rather than around user populations, because AV:N/PR:N leaves no credential step between reaching the interface and executing privileged functions. A.8.22 can be recorded as implemented on a design where that interface still answers a client network or the WAN, and on such a device the unauthenticated escalation stays open until 1.0.01.07 / 1.0.03.26 is applied.

new_control_requirements.name: PERIMETER-DEVICE-ZERODAY-SLA-TIER
new_control_requirements.description: Compliance frameworks must define a distinct patch SLA tier for pre-auth RCE on perimeter-trust-boundary devices (firewalls, VPN concentrators, WAFs, edge load-balancers). Tier requirement: vendor-mitigation deployed within 4 hours of KEV listing OR isolation of the vulnerable interface; standard 14/30-day SLAs do not apply because the device IS the trust boundary.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2022-20700 is an unauthenticated, network-reachable root privilege escalation on the RV160/RV260/RV340/RV345 management plane (CVSS 9.8), KEV-listed 2022-03-03 with EPSS 0.05655 on 2026-08-20; because the router is the trust boundary, the fix to 1.0.01.07 / 1.0.03.26 or isolation of the management interface belongs on an accelerated tier.

new_control_requirements.name: PERIMETER-COMPROMISE-REBUILD-NOT-PATCH
new_control_requirements.description: Pre-rehearsed IR runbook for any perimeter device that suffers a pre-auth RCE CVE in active exploitation MUST default to config-exfil + rebuild + credential rotation, not patch-in-place. Patch-in-place leaves attacker-installed implants intact.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2022-20700 grants unauthenticated root-level control of the RV-series router and CISA's 2022-03-03 KEV listing asserts in-the-wild use, so an exposed unit cannot be assumed clean after firmware 1.0.01.07 / 1.0.03.26; its configuration must be rebuilt from a known-good baseline and credentials rotated.

CVE-2022-20699.name: Cisco Small Business RV Series Routers Stack-based Buffer Overflow Vulnerability (CVE-2022-20699)

attack_vector.description: One oversized HTTPS request to the RV340/RV345 SSL VPN daemon on 8443 overflows a 0x4000 stack buffer and, with an RWX stack and minimal ASLR, runs attacker shellcode as root without authentication.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; the SSL VPN listener answers pre-authentication
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; RWX stack and near-absent ASLR remove the usual leak/ROP steps, ~65% reliable in the public module
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Discovered by the Flashback Team for Pwn2Own; no AI assistance.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Upgrade to firmware 1.0.03.26, or disable SSL VPN / restrict 8443 to trusted sources in the interim.
prevention.adequacy: The firmware fix eliminates the overflow; the interim network restriction is fully effective while it remains in force, and it costs the remote-access feature either wholly, where SSL VPN is disabled, or for every source outside the allowed set where 8443 is filtered instead.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alarm on 8443 requests exceeding 0x4000 bytes and on sslvpnd restarts or unexpected router-initiated egress.
detection.adequacy: Both signals are generated by the router the exploit takes root on, so they are only dependable where syslog is already leaving the device; where it is not, the record of the oversized 8443 request and of the sslvpnd restart does not survive the compromise that produced it.

response.what_would_have_worked: Rebuild the router configuration and rotate administrative and VPN credentials rather than patching in place after exposure.
response.adequacy: Necessary because a root RCE on the perimeter can leave persistence a firmware upgrade does not remove.

NIST-800-53-SC-7.gap: SC-7 treats the RV340/RV345 as the boundary enforcer, but the vulnerable sslvpnd listener is on the boundary device itself, so a compliant SC-7 remote-access posture still exposes the pre-auth overflow on 8443.

NIS2-Art21-network-security.gap: Art.21 network-security controls that rely on the RV340/RV345 as the enforcement point cannot mitigate a defect in that point; with EPSS 0.72458 on 2026-08-20 and a public module, only disabling or restricting 8443 helps before 1.0.03.26.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: The configuration B4 would call secure before 1.0.03.26 is the one with SSL VPN disabled or TCP 8443 closed, which removes the remote-access feature itself — so the vendor default is both the justified configuration B4 accepts and the one that leaves a pre-auth root overflow answering on the WAN. Applying the fix costs a reload that drops every VPN session, which is why the assessment can be honest and the exposure can persist across it.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: The Essential Eight internet-facing patch window is far longer than a pre-auth root RCE with working exploit code warrants, and it does not mandate the interim disable-SSL-VPN step that closes the path before firmware lands.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.9.gap: An A.8.9 baseline that accepts the shipped RV340/RV345 remote-access configuration leaves SSL VPN enabled on the WAN, so the vulnerable listener stays exposed instead of being a reviewed, restricted surface.

new_control_requirements.name: PERIMETER-DEVICE-ZERODAY-SLA-TIER
new_control_requirements.description: Compliance frameworks must define a distinct patch SLA tier for pre-auth RCE on perimeter-trust-boundary devices (firewalls, VPN concentrators, WAFs, edge load-balancers). Tier requirement: vendor-mitigation deployed within 4 hours of KEV listing OR isolation of the vulnerable interface; standard 14/30-day SLAs do not apply because the device IS the trust boundary.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2022-20699 is a pre-auth root RCE on the RV340/RV345 SSL VPN listener (8443), KEV-listed 2022-03-03 with a public Metasploit module (cisco_rv340_sslvpn.rb) and EPSS 0.72458 on 2026-08-20; the device is the perimeter, so the fix to 1.0.03.26 or isolation of 8443 belongs on an accelerated tier, not a standard patch window.

new_control_requirements.name: PERIMETER-COMPROMISE-REBUILD-NOT-PATCH
new_control_requirements.description: Pre-rehearsed IR runbook for any perimeter device that suffers a pre-auth RCE CVE in active exploitation MUST default to config-exfil + rebuild + credential rotation, not patch-in-place. Patch-in-place leaves attacker-installed implants intact.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Because CVE-2022-20699 yields root on the RV340/RV345 and CISA's 2022-03-03 KEV listing asserts in-the-wild use, a unit exposed on 8443 cannot be assumed clean after applying 1.0.03.26; its configuration and administrative credentials must be rebuilt from a known-good baseline.

CVE-2021-41379.name: Microsoft Windows Installer Privilege Escalation Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: A low-privileged local user redirects a SYSTEM-context Windows Installer file operation through a symbolic link, overwriting the Microsoft Edge Elevation Service to run code as SYSTEM.
attack_vector.privileges_required: low — PR:L; an existing low-privileged local account is required
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; a file-operation race, but the public PoC is engineered to win it reliably
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Found and weaponised by independent researcher Abdelhamid Naceri without AI assistance.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Apply both the November 2021 (CVE-2021-41379) and December 2021 (CVE-2021-43883 bypass) Windows updates and reboot.
prevention.adequacy: Fully preventive only once both updates are applied and the host reboots; the November update alone left the demonstrated escalation open.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alert on non-admin ACTION=ADMIN MSI installs, junction/symlink creation during MSI operations, and Edge-elevation-service modification.
detection.adequacy: Detects the public PoC's specific behaviour but a re-tooled exploit may pick a different SYSTEM-writable target.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treat a host with a confirmed SYSTEM escalation as compromised, isolate it, and investigate follow-on activity given the ransomware association.
response.adequacy: Necessary because this LPE is commonly a chain step; SYSTEM code execution can seed persistence and lateral movement.

NIST-800-53-AC-6.gap: AC-6 least-privilege attestations pass while a legitimate low-privilege account reaches SYSTEM through the Windows Installer service; because the attacker is already authorized, tightening account rights does not contain the escalation, only the November/December 2021 updates do.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: The November 2021 fix for CVE-2021-41379 was incomplete, and the public bypass (CVE-2021-43883, EPSS 0.19381 on 2026-08-20) stayed exploitable, so a patch-management record marking the November update as closure left hosts open until December.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: B4 that closed CVE-2021-41379 on the November 2021 update alone left the SYSTEM-escalation path open, because that vendor patch did not remediate the flaw the public PoC demonstrates until the December bypass fix.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: An Essential Eight posture treating one monthly OS rollup as closure understates that this LPE needed two Windows updates; the November 2021 fix did not remediate the demonstrated escalation, which required the December bypass patch.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: The NVD record for CVE-2021-41379 carries Microsoft's CNA metric of CVSS 5.5 (C:N/I:N/A:H) alongside NVD's own 7.8 (C:H/I:H/A:H), and a register that takes the first ranks a SYSTEM-escalation flaw as availability-only while CISA lists it with the ransomware flag. Scope fails the same register a second time: unless the CVE-2021-43883 bypass is carried as its own item, closing the base CVE leaves the exploited path open.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Microsoft Windows Installer CVE-2021-41379 was KEV-listed 2022-03-03 (ransomware: Known) with EPSS 0.19381 on 2026-08-20 and a public SYSTEM-escalation PoC; because the November 2021 fix was incomplete, the verified-mitigation clock is only satisfied when both that update and the December 2021 CVE-2021-43883 bypass fix are applied and hosts reboot.

CVE-2020-1938.name: Apache Tomcat Improper Privilege Management Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: A single AJP/1.3 connection to TCP 8009 carrying three servlet include attributes makes Tomcat serve any file under the web application, and dispatch any file to the JSP servlet. Where the application stores uploads beneath its own root, that second capability turns an unauthenticated read into unauthenticated code execution.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; the AJP connector answers before any application authentication, and the trust decision Tomcat makes is based on the protocol, not on the peer
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; no race, no groom, no info leak needed. The real constraint is reachability of port 8009, which the affected builds granted by default on all configured addresses
attack_vector.ai_factor: None recorded. Tenable's analysis and the Metasploit module's own credits both attribute the finding to Chaitin Tech, and the defect is protocol analysis of which request attributes the AJP connector will honour rather than an automated discovery.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Removing or loopback-binding the AJP Connector in conf/server.xml on every Tomcat instance that does not front onto a reverse proxy, independently of the upgrade to 9.0.31 / 8.5.51 / 7.0.100.
prevention.adequacy: It closes the path completely where it is applied, and Apache's own text says mitigation is only required if the AJP port is reachable by untrusted users. It reaches only the Tomcat instances an operator can find, which is where it fails on estates whose Tomcat arrives inside OFBiz, TomEE or Geode.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alerting on AJP-originated requests whose translated path resolves inside WEB-INF or META-INF, and on any connection to 8009 from an address that is not the configured proxy.
detection.adequacy: Tomcat's access log records the translated path, so the file-read stage is visible without additional tooling. It is a post-hoc signal: by the time WEB-INF/web.xml appears in the log the datasource credentials it holds have already left.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating any Tomcat that exposed 8009 to an untrusted segment as having disclosed the contents of its web application, and rotating every credential held in WEB-INF configuration before restarting on the fixed build.
response.adequacy: Rotation is the only action that survives the upgrade, because the read is silent and leaves nothing to remediate on the host. It does not address the RCE branch: where an upload directory sat under the application root, the response is a rebuild rather than a credential change.

NIST-800-53-CM-7.gap: Least functionality is nominally met because the baseline was built from the vendor's own conf/server.xml, in which the AJP/1.3 Connector is already enabled on all configured addresses across 9.0.0.M1-9.0.30, 8.5.0-8.5.50 and 7.0.0-7.0.99. CM-7 has no clause that puts a shipped default in scope for removal, so a host whose only exposure is a connector it never uses is compliant and exploitable at once.

NIST-800-53-SC-7.gap: Boundary protection is evidenced at the internet edge, and port 8009 on an internal Tomcat host is inside that boundary. Apache scopes the required mitigation to cases where the AJP port is reachable by untrusted users, which makes an internal segment the decisive question SC-7 evidence never asks. At EPSS 0.9927 on 2026-08-20 the assumption that internal reachability is low-risk has no support in the exploitation data.

NIS2-Art21-network-security.gap: Segmentation and perimeter evidence satisfies the measure while leaving the actual defect untouched, because the defect is a protocol-level trust grant rather than an exposed port count. Tomcat accepts javax.servlet.include.request_uri from any AJP caller as though a reverse proxy had set it, and no Article 21 network-security assessment inspects which request attributes a listener will honour from an unauthenticated peer.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: B4 assesses secure configuration against a documented baseline, and the baseline here is the vendor default that carries the flaw. Apache states the upgrade to 9.0.31, 8.5.51 or 7.0.100 will likely require configuration changes because the AJP defaults changed, so a B4 process that treats drift from the baseline as the risk penalises the remediation and rewards the exposed state.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Patch Applications would drive the upgrade if the application were in the inventory, and on a standalone Tomcat install it is. It is not where Tomcat ships inside Apache OFBiz, TomEE or Geode — all three appear in this CVE's own reference set — because the asset register names the embedding product and the maturity assessment measures against what the register holds.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.9.gap: Configuration management is genuinely performed and still passes: the Connector element is in the reviewed configuration because Apache placed it there, and A.8.9 has no test that compares listening protocols against protocols actually carrying traffic. The evidence that separates paper compliance from the real state is a socket listing showing 8009 on a non-loopback address alongside an access log with no AJP-originated requests in it.

new_control_requirements.name: CONFIGURATION-SIDE-LIVE-PATCH-INVENTORY
new_control_requirements.description: For any web-fabric vulnerability with a configuration-side mitigation path: that path must be inventoried, tested, and deployable independent of the vendor-patch path. Operators cannot wait for nginx 1.30.1+ if a named-capture refactor mitigates immediately.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Apache Tomcat is the case this control describes exactly. Apache's own advisory text states that mitigation is only required if an AJP port is accessible to untrusted users, which means commenting out or loopback-binding the AJP/1.3 Connector in conf/server.xml removes the exposure with no upgrade at all — while the vendor-patch path to 9.0.31, 8.5.51 or 7.0.100 additionally requires configuration changes and a Tomcat process restart. With EPSS at 0.9927 on 2026-08-20 and Exploit-DB 48143 public since February 2020, the two-year gap between exploit publication and the 2022-03-03 KEV listing is exactly the window a configuration-side path exists to cover.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Apache Tomcat's fixed releases 9.0.31, 8.5.51 and 7.0.100 shipped in February 2020 and CISA listed the CVE on 2022-03-03 with a due date of 2022-03-17, so on this entry the later of the two triggers is the KEV listing and the four-hour clock is measurable against it. The documented-compensating-control branch is what makes the SLA achievable here: Apache's own connector-removal guidance is deployable immediately, where the upgrade path needs a change window for the AJP configuration changes and a process restart.

CVE-2020-11899.name: Treck TCP/IP stack Out-of-Bounds Read Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: A crafted IPv6 packet on the device's own link makes the Treck stack read beyond the end of the received packet buffer. The stack acts on the out-of-bounds bytes rather than returning them, so what an operator sees is a device that misprocesses traffic or drops off the network, on hardware that carries no version string and no update mechanism of its own.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; the stack processes the packet before any application-layer identity exists on the device
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; the packet is a fixed shape with no race or groom. The binding constraint is AV:A: the attacker needs layer-2 reachability, which on the printer, building-management and clinical segments these devices occupy is normal rather than exceptional
attack_vector.ai_factor: None recorded. CERT/CC VU#257161 credits Moshe Kol and Shlomi Oberman of JSOF with the research, coordinated through CERT/CC because the component reaches the market through dozens of device makers.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Segmenting devices that embed the stack away from any untrusted layer-2 neighbour, and applying CERT/CC VU#257161's packet-hygiene mitigations — dropping IP fragments where fragmentation is unsupported, disabling IP tunnelling, blocking deprecated IPv6 features and unused IPv6 multicast — at the segment boundary.
prevention.adequacy: It is the only lever an operator holds where the device vendor has published no fixed firmware, and it removes the AV:A precondition for attackers outside the segment. It does nothing about a compromised host already inside the segment, and where the device's function requires user workstations to reach it — a printer, a clinical device — the segment cannot be closed to them without taking the device out of service.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Passive Treck fingerprinting on the segment — the IP/TTL, TCP and ICMP artefacts the Corelight Zeek package keys on — to produce the device inventory the vulnerability record needs and no asset register holds.
detection.adequacy: It answers 'which devices run this stack', which is the question that actually blocks remediation. It does not detect exploitation of this id: the Suricata coverage published for Ripple20 by advanced-threat-research names CVE-2020-11901, CVE-2020-11897 and CVE-2020-11896, and carries nothing for this one.

response.what_would_have_worked: Holding each affected device's vendor to a written Ripple20 status and a firmware date, and converting 'status unknown' into a dated replacement decision rather than an open item.
response.adequacy: It is the only path that closes the exposure permanently, since the operator cannot compile a fixed stack into someone else's firmware. It is slow by construction — CERT/CC listed more than forty vendors as status unknown — and a risk acceptance carrying no replacement date leaves the device in service indefinitely.

NIST-800-53-SR-3.gap: Supply-chain process evidence is collected against the device vendor, which is the supplier the organisation contracts with — and the defective component sits one tier further out, licensed by that vendor from Treck. CERT/CC VU#257161's split between roughly twenty confirmed-affected vendors and more than forty of unknown status is the measure of the gap: SR-3 can be fully satisfied while the answer to 'does this printer contain Treck below 6.0.1.66' remains unobtainable.

NIST-800-53-SC-7.gap: The control is met at the perimeter and the exploit does not cross the perimeter. With AV:A the attacker is already on the device's link, and where the segment these devices occupy is flat — a printer VLAN, a building-management network — every host on it already satisfies the precondition. The mitigations CERT/CC actually prescribes are link-local packet rules, which sit below the layer SC-7 evidence is normally gathered at.

NIS2-Art21-supply-chain.gap: Supplier due diligence is performed and documented against the device maker, and the vulnerable code was licensed by that maker from a third party it may not name. Neither of the version numbers in the record — Treck before 6.0.1.66 from NVD, 6.0.1.67 or later from CERT/CC — is something a regulated entity can act on; the only actionable artefact is a firmware release, and Article 21 provides no mechanism to compel one.

UK-CAF-A1.gap: Risk management is genuinely exercised and produces the wrong ranking on accurate inputs. A 5.4 base score with C:N/I:L/A:L sorts below most of a register, the affected asset count cannot be established without packet fingerprinting, and the KEV due date of 2022-03-17 is the only signal pointing the other way. A1 has no clause that overrides a low severity score when the population of affected devices is unknown.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: The patching controls are measured against managed endpoints with readable software inventories, and every device in scope here is outside that population: no package, no host-readable version for the embedded stack, and no agent on firmware that supports none. Top maturity is honestly attainable while the affected printers, UPS units and controllers all still run Treck below 6.0.1.66, because the assessment's unit of measurement never included them.

ISO-27001-2022-A.5.21.gap: Supplier agreements for ICT products can be complete and still not answer the question this CVE poses, because A.5.21 addresses the agreement rather than the composition of what is delivered. The missing requirement is a firmware bill of materials — without one, 'which devices contain Treck below 6.0.1.66' is answered by fingerprinting traffic, and that answer expires the next time a device is swapped.

IEC-62443-3-3.gap: The standard's system-level framing is the right one for a device its owner cannot patch, and its zone-and-conduit model gives a workable isolation answer where no vendor firmware carrying Treck 6.0.1.67 or later exists. What it does not give is a time bound: an asset placed in a restricted zone because it is permanently vulnerable can remain there for the life of the plant, and 62443-3-3 supplies no criterion that forces the replacement decision.

new_control_requirements.name: TIER-3-DEPENDENCY-INVENTORY
new_control_requirements.description: Supply chain inventory must extend to tier-3 dependencies (dependencies of dependencies of direct dependencies). SBOM coverage for libsystemd-class transitive dependencies cannot be omitted under SR-3.
new_control_requirements.evidence: The Treck TCP/IP stack is the embedded-firmware form of exactly this problem: an operator buys a printer, a UPS or a controller, that device maker licensed the stack from Treck, and the fixed level — before 6.0.1.66 per NVD, 6.0.1.67 or later per CERT/CC VU#257161 — is invisible to every inventory the operator runs. CERT/CC listed more than forty vendors as status unknown alongside roughly twenty confirmed affected, so for a large share of the market the tier-3 question could not be answered at all during the 2022-03-03 to 2022-03-17 KEV window. A component-level record for firmware is the artefact that turns this from a fingerprinting exercise into a lookup.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: For the Treck stack the SLA's documented-compensating-control branch is not a fallback but the branch that remains available: the stack level is not deployable by the asset owner at all, and where the device vendor has published no Ripple20 firmware there is nothing to install. The mitigations CERT/CC VU#257161 sets out — dropping IP fragments where unsupported, disabling IP tunnelling, blocking deprecated IPv6 features, disabling unused IPv6 multicast — are deployable at a segment boundary within hours of the 2022-03-03 listing, where a firmware campaign across printers, UPS units and controllers is measured in quarters. Binding the clock to the compensating control rather than to the unavailable patch is what makes the KEV due date of 2022-03-17 meetable.

attack_vector.description: An oversized EHLO argument overflows a heap buffer inside string_vformat in Exim's string.c. The command is the opening move of an SMTP session, so the vulnerable code runs before authentication, before TLS is a trust decision and before any filter has content to examine.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; EHLO precedes every authentication step in the protocol, so any host that can open TCP/25 reaches the parser
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; one oversized command, no race and no groom. The real constraint is on impact rather than access: the advisory places the documented path after privileges have been dropped, though it notes other vectors into the same code may exist
attack_vector.ai_factor: None recorded. The Exim advisory credits QAX-A-TEAM; a research-team brand is not evidence of AI-assisted discovery, and neither the advisory nor the bug thread describes automated analysis.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Upgrading to Exim 4.92.3, or the distribution build carrying it such as Debian's exim4 4.92-8+deb10u3, and restarting the daemon so the new binary serves connections.
prevention.adequacy: It is the whole remediation and the only one — the advisory states there is no known mitigation beside updating the server. Its limit is operational rather than technical: the fix is inert until the listener process is restarted, so a package version of 4.92.3 on disk can read as remediated while the 4.92.2 process is still accepting connections.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alerting on exim child processes terminating abnormally during session setup, correlated with EHLO argument length recorded from the SMTP transcript.
detection.adequacy: The crash signal is reliable, because the effect the advisory describes for the known proof of concept is a crashed process. It is weak against a working code-execution attempt, which by construction does not crash, and EHLO argument length is only available where the mail-log pipeline was configured to retain it.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating a crashed exim on an internet-facing MX during the exposure window as a possible code-execution attempt rather than as an availability event, and examining the host before restarting the service.
response.adequacy: It is the right reflex for a pre-auth memory-corruption flaw on a service that answers the internet. It is also the reflex least likely to survive contact with a mail outage, where the pressure is to restart the listener and restore delivery before anything is preserved.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: Flaw identification and the remediation timeframe are both documented, and the control still leaves an unmitigated window because its usual relief valve does not exist here. Exim's advisory states that beside updating the server there is no known mitigation, so the compensating-control clause SI-2 procedures rely on while a change window is scheduled has nothing to record. Every hour of deferral on 4.92 through 4.92.2 is full exposure, not reduced exposure.

NIST-800-53-AC-6.gap: Least privilege is real here and is recorded as complete when it is partial. The advisory places the documented EHLO path in message reception, after privileges have been dropped, which genuinely bounds the outcome — and the same advisory says other vectors into the vulnerable code may exist, while NVD's 9.8 with C:H/I:H/A:H scores the unconstrained case. AC-6 evidence has no field for 'mitigates the known path, not the class'.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: Patch management is in place and cadence-based, and cadence is the wrong axis for this defect. The vulnerable parser handles the opening command of every SMTP session on a host whose job is answering TCP/25 from the internet, so exposure is continuous and pre-authentication from the moment the branch is deployed. Article 21 offers no tier that separates a pre-greeting parser on an internet-facing listener from an internal application on the same monthly cycle.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: The outcome is met on its own terms: Exim 4.92 was supported and current, and the estate that had moved to it promptly was doing what B4 asks. That is what makes the gap sharp — NVD's range is 4.92 through 4.92.2, so currency was the exposure and a host left on 4.91 was outside the range. B4 has no notion of a recently introduced defect making the newer supported release the riskier one for a window.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: The control names the application and would drive the update, but its accelerated window depends on an exploit-availability input that is false here. Exploit-DB, Metasploit and the ProjectDiscovery templates carry nothing for this id, while Exim's own advisory records that a crash proof of concept exists unpublished and CISA lists the CVE as exploited. A scheduling rule keyed to published exploits places a pre-auth heap overflow on an internet-facing MTA in the slow lane.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: Technical-vulnerability management is exercised and the intake worked — advisory, DSA-4536-1 and NVD all within days. The prioritisation step is where it breaks, because A.8.8 does not require the process to separate 'no public exploit was found' from 'this is not exploitable'. Here the exploitation evidence is the KEV listing rather than an artefact, so an exploit-weighted ranking pushes CVSS 9.8 with PR:N below lower-scoring flaws that happen to have a module.

new_control_requirements.name: MITIGATION-ACTIVE-PATCH-PENDING-VERDICT-CLASS
new_control_requirements.description: Compliance verdicts must distinguish three states: (a) binary patch deployed (vulnerability eliminated), (b) vendor-mitigation rule active, no binary patch (residual risk: any defect in the mitigation rule reopens the vulnerability), (c) no mitigation, no patch (full exposure). Audit reports must surface (b) as a distinct compensating-control state with an associated time-bound action item, not as a 'patched per SLA' outcome.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Exim is the case where the middle state does not exist, and saying so explicitly is the point. The advisory for 4.92 through 4.92.2 states that beside updating the server there is no known mitigation, so every host that has not reached 4.92.3 — or Debian's 4.92-8+deb10u3 — is in state (c), full exposure, for the whole period between the 2022-03-03 KEV listing and its restart on the fixed binary. The verdict class also has to separate 'package upgraded' from 'daemon restarted', because an MX running a 4.92.2 listener process under a 4.92.3 package on disk is still in state (c) while every inventory report shows it patched.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: This entry is where a KEV-triggered clock outperforms an exploit-weighted one for Exim. Exploit-DB, Metasploit and the ProjectDiscovery templates all carry nothing for this id, so any scheduling rule keyed to published exploit code leaves a CVSS 9.8 pre-authentication heap overflow on an internet-facing MTA in the ordinary queue. The KEV listing of 2022-03-03 with its 2022-03-17 due date is the signal that is actually present, and binding the four-hour clock to it — with completion measured by a restarted exim listener on 4.92.3, not by a package version on disk — is what closes the window.

CVE-2019-1652.name: Cisco Small Business Routers Improper Input Validation Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: The router's certificate generator interpolates the certificate subject fields into an OpenSSL shell command with no server-side escaping, so a crafted common_name in a POST to /certificate_handle2.htm?type=4 executes arbitrary commands as root on the device's Linux shell. The published tooling first reads the device configuration through the sibling disclosure flaw, so the administrative session the CVSS vector requires is supplied rather than assumed.
attack_vector.privileges_required: high — PR:H; the endpoint sits behind an administrative session, which the Metasploit module obtains by chaining CVE-2019-1653 rather than by holding a credential
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; a single deterministic POST with no race and no reliability problem. The practical constraint is reaching the web management interface, which the router serves to its own LAN by design
attack_vector.ai_factor: None recorded. Cisco credits RedTeam Pentesting GmbH, whose advisory RT-SA-2018-004 describes manual analysis of the firmware's OpenSSL command construction.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Firmware Release 1.4.2.22 or later on every RV320 and RV325, verified per unit against the running version rather than against the advisory date, with the reboot onto the new image taken.
prevention.adequacy: It is the only measure that removes the injection, and the version check has to be against 1.4.2.22 specifically because Cisco recorded the earlier fix as incomplete on 2019-04-04. It does nothing about a unit already compromised: root command execution means firmware alone does not evict what was left behind.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Forwarding the router's syslog to a collector outside the device, and alerting on certificate-generation events no administrator initiated and on outbound connections from the router to non-peer addresses.
detection.adequacy: Off-box telemetry is the only form that survives an attacker who lands as root on the device. It has to be in place before the compromise, and it has to be verified as reaching the collector rather than merely configured on the device — a silently failed forwarder and a quiet router look identical.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating any unit that was reachable during the exposure window as compromised: rebuild its configuration from a known-good baseline rather than carrying it across the upgrade, and rotate every credential the configuration held, including VPN pre-shared keys and any reused administrative password.
response.adequacy: It is the correct response because the chained disclosure step reads the configuration before the injection runs, so the credentials are gone before the command executes. The rotation scope is the difficulty: where one administrative password was reused across a fleet of branch routers, the scope is the fleet.

NIST-800-53-SI-10.gap: Input validation is not implemented in the product and cannot be implemented by the operator — the concatenation of certificate subject fields into an openssl shell string happens inside firmware, with filtering only in client-side JavaScript that an attacker bypasses by not using the browser. The only SI-10 evidence available on an appliance is the vendor's assurance, and here that assurance was issued and then retracted when 1.4.2.20 proved incomplete.

NIST-800-53-SC-7.gap: Boundary protection is nominally satisfied by the presence of the device, which is what makes it inadequate: the RV320 and RV325 are the boundary, so there is no outer control to place the fix behind. Removing the management interface from the WAN side is the only SC-7 action available and it leaves the router's own LAN — the general user network at a branch site — with unchanged access to the vulnerable endpoint.

NIS2-Art21-network-security.gap: The measure is discharged through the very asset that fails. Root command execution on a dual-WAN VPN router means the compromised device is the one enforcing the segmentation and tunnel policy the rest of the Article 21 programme depends on, and the obligation contains no clause putting the enforcement point on a distinct, faster remediation clock than the workloads it protects.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: Secure configuration and maintenance were performed and the assessment read clean for the ten weeks between Cisco's January 2019 advisory and the 2019-04-04 update recording the initial fix as incomplete. B4 measures whether the operator applied the vendor's remediation, which the operator did; it has no mechanism that revalidates a closed finding when the vendor changes which release constitutes the fix.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: The control is largely not covered rather than covered-but-insufficient, because a router updated by hand through its own web page is inside the managed-endpoint population the maturity model measures only if the estate deliberately put it there. Where they are inside it, the model still cannot express the situation between 1.4.2.20 and 1.4.2.22 — a device recorded as patched, on a release the vendor subsequently withdrew as incomplete.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: Technical-vulnerability management ran correctly on the information available in January 2019 and produced a closed record. The standard has no re-opening criterion tied to an advisory revision, so Cisco's 2019-04-04 statement that the initial fix was incomplete does not propagate into the vulnerability register, and the January evidence continues to satisfy an audit while the device stays exploitable.

NIST-800-53-SI-4.gap: Monitoring reaches this device only where its syslog was deliberately pointed off-box, and the structural problem is worse than absence: the router writes its logs to itself, and a successful exploit is root on that same host, so any local record of the compromise is under the attacker's control. Off-box syslog forwarding is the only configuration that produces usable evidence, and it has to have been in place before the exposure window rather than added during the response.

new_control_requirements.name: INCOMPLETE-PATCH-SEQUENCE-SEVERITY-MULTIPLIER
new_control_requirements.description: Vulnerability-management programs must apply a severity multiplier when a CVE is the Nth in an incomplete-patch sequence on the same primitive (third MOTW bypass, second AMSI bypass, etc.). Framework controls treating each CVE as discrete obscure the structural defect; the Nth CVE in a sequence implies that future bypasses on the same primitive are likely.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Cisco's own advisory for the RV320 and RV325 records the sequence explicitly: the fix published on 2019-01-23 was found to be incomplete, and the 2019-04-04 update names Firmware Release 1.4.2.22 as the complete one, leaving 1.4.2.20 inside the affected range it was supposed to close. That is an incomplete patch on the same command-injection primitive in the same certificate-generator endpoint, on a perimeter device where Cisco's PSIRT simultaneously recorded public exploit code and active network scanning. A programme that treats the January and April advisories as one closed item cannot distinguish the units on 1.4.2.20 from the units on 1.4.2.22.

new_control_requirements.name: PERIMETER-COMPROMISE-REBUILD-NOT-PATCH
new_control_requirements.description: Pre-rehearsed IR runbook for any perimeter device that suffers a pre-auth RCE CVE in active exploitation MUST default to config-exfil + rebuild + credential rotation, not patch-in-place. Patch-in-place leaves attacker-installed implants intact.
