It will not test the SNMP view, which is the configuration state that makes the flaw reachable, and it has no mechanism to convert an outstanding-patch finding on a live access switch into a scheduled reload, so the same finding can be carried from one assessment to the next without either the release or the view changing.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Read against the maturity model's scoping, a management-VLAN-only Catalyst 2960-L is not an internet-facing service and is not a workstation or server operating system, so the fast clock keyed to "within 48 hours if an exploit exists" does not obviously attach to it. An organisation at a given maturity level can therefore be fully assessed as compliant while this switch runs a four-year-old vulnerable image; that is a reading of the model's scope rather than a quoted exemption, and it is worth resolving explicitly with the assessor.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.9.gap: A.8.9 is nominally met by a switch configuration baseline under change control, and such a baseline will contain the SNMP community, the ACL and the SNMP version. Unless it also enumerates view contents, the presence of the Cisco flash MIB inside a permitted view — the exact configuration state this CVE requires — is invisible to the control while the estate remains formally compliant.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Cisco fixed this Catalyst 2960-L and Digital Building 8P/8U flaw in the 2018-03-28 bundled publication; KEV listed it on 2022-03-03 with a 2022-03-17 due date, and Cisco's own advisory revision of 2022-12-15 records attempted exploitation in the wild in March 2022. The control's alternative branch is what matters on a switch: the documented compensating controls — the SNMP flash-MIB view exclusion and the collector ACL from cisco-sa-20180328-snmp — land inside hours without a reload, whereas the image upgrade needs a change window on a device carrying access ports.

new_control_requirements.name: MITIGATION-ACTIVE-PATCH-PENDING-VERDICT-CLASS
new_control_requirements.description: Compliance verdicts must distinguish three states: (a) binary patch deployed (vulnerability eliminated), (b) vendor-mitigation rule active, no binary patch (residual risk: any defect in the mitigation rule reopens the vulnerability), (c) no mitigation, no patch (full exposure). Audit reports must surface (b) as a distinct compensating-control state with an associated time-bound action item, not as a 'patched per SLA' outcome.
new_control_requirements.evidence: This CVE produces state (b) on a large 2960-L population: the SNMP view exclusion and collector ACL are active, the vulnerable image is still running, and every EPSS refresh — 0.04667 at the 91st percentile on 2026-08-20 — is scored against a device an audit will show as mitigated. Any drift in that view, a rebuilt switch restored from an older configuration, or a new collector added to the ACL reopens the CPUHOG path with no new CVE and no new advisory to trigger a re-review.

CVE-2018-0159.name: Cisco IOS and XE Software Internet Key Exchange Version 1 Denial-of-Service Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: Crafted IKEv1 packets sent during an IKE negotiation hit unvalidated handling in the IOS and IOS XE IKEv1 implementation and reload the device. The packets reach the listener before any peer authentication occurs.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; the attacker needs only IP reachability to a bound ISAKMP socket on UDP 500, 848, 4500 or 4848, which on a remote-access or DMVPN head-end is open to untrusted networks by design.
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; no negotiation state, valid identity or pre-shared key is needed. The only variable is reachability, and Cisco scores the resulting reload as scope-changed (S:C, 8.6) where NVD scores S:U (7.5).
attack_vector.ai_factor: Cisco records the find as internal security testing. No AI-assisted discovery is asserted, and there is no AI-branded research arm in the attribution to mistake for one.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Only the fixed image. Cisco states there are no workarounds; the nearest partial measure is restricting inbound UDP 500 and 4500 to enumerated peer addresses on site-to-site head-ends, which narrows the source set without removing the defect.
prevention.adequacy: Peer-address filtering is unavailable on a remote-access head-end, which must accept arbitrary sources, and it is defeated by a spoofed source on any head-end since the crash happens before authentication. It reduces opportunistic reach only.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Off-box syslog and IKE negotiation logging retained on a collector, so the negotiations preceding a reload survive the reload, plus NetFlow on UDP 500 and 4500 to show source diversity.
detection.adequacy: This tells you afterwards which sources were negotiating when the head-end went down. It does not distinguish a crafted packet from a legitimate malformed one at the time, and it cannot prevent the reload.

response.what_would_have_worked: A pre-agreed head-end failover path — a second gateway or a documented branch fallback — so that a reload during exploitation does not require the same change window as the fix itself.
response.adequacy: Failover moves the outage rather than preventing it, and if both head-ends run the same vulnerable release the attacker simply repeats against the second one. It buys the window in which the upgrade can be scheduled.

NIST-800-53-CM-7.gap: The control is met by a documented list of permitted services in which IPsec appears with justification, and that justification is written at fleet level. Nothing in CM-7 requires it to be re-tested per device, so a router carrying ISAKMP configuration without an operational tunnel keeps a bound UDP 500 socket while passing least-functionality review — and that socket is the entire attack surface for this CVE.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: SI-2 is satisfied by having flaw-remediation timescales and evidence of tracking, and this flaw has been tracked since 2018-03-28. The control cannot express the constraint that actually governs the outcome: with no workaround published, the only compliant state is a reloaded head-end, and every day of delay is a business decision about tunnel downtime that SI-2 records as an open remediation item rather than as an accepted exposure to a pre-authentication reload.

NIS2-Art21-network-security.gap: An in-scope entity can hold every network-security measure the Article contemplates — segmented management, authenticated peers, encrypted transport — and remain fully exposed, because the crash occurs in the packet handling that precedes peer authentication on a port the VPN service requires to be open. The measure has no expression for a service whose own protocol entry point is the vulnerable code.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: A CAF B4 review of an IPsec gateway confirms the configuration is intentional and the release is inventoried, both of which are true here and neither of which is protective. The assessment has no field for the fact that no compensating control exists, so a gateway with a known pre-authentication reload defect and no available mitigation records identically to one awaiting a routine patch.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Unlike an internal switch, a remote-access or DMVPN head-end is unambiguously an internet-facing service, so the maturity model's faster clock attaches once an exploit is known — and the KEV listing plus Cisco's March 2022 attempted-exploitation note supply that trigger. The organisation is then measured against a deadline it can only meet by reloading its VPN head-end, which is why this control is met on paper by scheduling and failed in substance by deferral.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.21.gap: A.8.21 covers the security mechanisms and service levels of network services, so the evidence it invites for an IPsec gateway is the mechanism the service uses. Here that mechanism is the failing component: the IKEv1 negotiation is both where the peer would be authenticated and where the device reloads, and the reload happens first. The control prompts no inventory of which gateways still enable IKEv1 rather than IKEv2 only, which is the surface-reduction question this CVE raises.

new_control_requirements.name: MITIGATION-ACTIVE-PATCH-PENDING-VERDICT-CLASS
new_control_requirements.description: Compliance verdicts must distinguish three states: (a) binary patch deployed (vulnerability eliminated), (b) vendor-mitigation rule active, no binary patch (residual risk: any defect in the mitigation rule reopens the vulnerability), (c) no mitigation, no patch (full exposure). Audit reports must surface (b) as a distinct compensating-control state with an associated time-bound action item, not as a 'patched per SLA' outcome.
new_control_requirements.evidence: cisco-sa-20180328-ike-dos states there are no workarounds that address this vulnerability, so every Cisco IOS or IOS XE device with a bound ISAKMP socket on a pre-fix release sits in state (c) and none of them can occupy state (b). That distinction carries the whole entry: restricting inbound UDP 500 and 4500 to enumerated peer addresses is the measure most available to record as compensating, and it is defeated by a spoofed source because the reload happens before any peer is authenticated, and it cannot be applied at all on a remote-access head-end that must accept arbitrary sources. An audit that books peer filtering as state (b) is recording a mitigation the vendor did not publish, on a defect whose EPSS reads 0.06915 at the 93.6th percentile as of 2026-08-20 and which Cisco reports drew attempted exploitation in March 2022.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: On this Cisco IOS and IOS XE IKEv1 flaw the control's three branches collapse to one, because the advisory publishes no workaround: there is no live patch for IOS and no documented compensating control, so the only compliant action is the fixed release and the head-end reload it requires. That is worth stating in the runbook before the next KEV listing rather than discovering it at the deadline — the 2022-03-17 due date fell fourteen days after the listing on a defect whose only compliant end state is a reloaded head-end.

CVE-2018-0158.name: Cisco IOS and XE Software Internet Key Exchange Memory Leak Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: Repeated crafted IKEv2 packets sent to a bound ISAKMP socket make Cisco IOS and IOS XE consume memory without releasing it, ending in a reload. Exposure follows from ISAKMP being enabled; no IKEv2 feature configuration is needed.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; the attacker needs reachability to UDP 500, 848, 4500 or 4848 and nothing else, and the packets are processed before any peer is authenticated.
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; the only added cost over a single-packet crash is duration, since memory has to be exhausted rather than corrupted. That duration is also the defender's one chance to see it happening.
attack_vector.ai_factor: Attributed by Cisco to handling TAC support requests — vendor staff working customer cases. No AI-assisted discovery is claimed.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: The fixed image, since Cisco publishes no workaround. On a site-to-site head-end, permitting UDP 500 and 4500 only from enumerated peers reduces who can sustain the packets, but it is neither a vendor workaround nor available on remote-access gateways.
prevention.adequacy: Source filtering does not survive a spoofed source, because the leak occurs before authentication and the attacker needs no reply. It narrows opportunistic scanning traffic and nothing more.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alerting on free-memory decline per head-end against its own baseline, rather than against a fixed threshold, with the series retained off-box so the reload does not erase the evidence.
detection.adequacy: The signal exists before the impact does — free memory falls while the attack is still running — but it is only usable if the baseline exists beforehand. After the reload, memory looks healthy again and the trend that would have proved exploitation is gone unless it was already stored elsewhere.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating a memory-driven reload on an ISAKMP-enabled device as suspected exploitation, capturing the free-memory series and IKE logs from the collector before they age out, and bringing the upgrade window forward.
response.adequacy: There is no confidentiality or integrity impact to contain, so response is about deciding whether to accelerate the outage rather than about eviction. If both head-ends in a pair share the release, response has to plan for the second one failing the same way.

NIST-800-53-SC-5.gap: Denial-of-service protection implemented as boundary rate limiting and bandwidth headroom is calibrated for volume, and this attack does not need volume — it needs persistence against a listener that must stay open. The resource exhausted is IOS heap on the device itself, behind whatever boundary control SC-5 evidences, so the control can be fully implemented and never observe the attack at all.

NIST-800-53-SI-4.gap: SI-4 is nominally satisfied by monitoring that covers these devices; the inadequacy is in what the monitoring is wired to do with a free-memory series where one is collected. A threshold set for capacity planning does not alert on a slope, and because the reload restores free memory, an estate can experience this attack repeatedly and record each occurrence as an unexplained device restart.

NIS2-Art21-availability.gap: An availability measure evidenced by a redundant head-end pair and a documented recovery time is real, and neither half addresses a defect that is reachable pre-authentication on every device sharing the release: the same repeated packets exhaust the standby in turn, so the measured recovery time assumes an independence between the two devices that the common software version removes.

UK-CAF-B5.gap: A B5 assessment will find resilience designed in — dual head-ends, tested failover, documented recovery. What it does not test is software-version diversity across the resilient pair, and that is the only property that would have made failover survive this CVE, since an attacker who can exhaust one IOS release can exhaust the identical one next to it.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: The internet-facing scoping puts this squarely inside the mitigation strategy, and the KEV listing supplies the exploit trigger for the faster clock. The gap is that compliance is assessed as a point-in-time patch state while the exposure is cumulative: a leak-based denial of service becomes cheaper to trigger the longer a head-end runs without a reload, so two estates with identical patch-compliance percentages are not carrying identical risk.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.16.gap: Evidence for A.8.16 will show that head-end devices are monitored and that alerts are actioned, which is true. The control does not ask whether the specific anomaly this defect produces — a slow, monotonic decline in free memory with no workload explanation — is among the conditions that generate an alert, and where it is not, the monitoring holds the data that would have proven the attack and raises nothing.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Cisco published the fix for this IOS and IOS XE IKEv2 leak on 2018-03-28 and states there is no workaround, so for this CVE the control's clock runs from the 2022-03-03 KEV listing straight to a head-end reload with no interim state to occupy. EPSS stands at 0.07237, the 93.8th percentile as of 2026-08-20, on a defect the vendor reports as having drawn attempted exploitation in March 2022 — an SLA that cannot name a compensating control for VPN head-ends is an SLA that will be missed by design.

new_control_requirements.name: FIREWALL-EGRESS-TELEMETRY-SEPARATE-TRUST-ZONE
new_control_requirements.description: Firewall and other perimeter-trust-boundary devices must forward syslog, threat logs, and authentication logs to a SIEM hosted in a separate trust zone (different management plane, different credentials, different authentication path). Telemetry stored on the compromised device is destroyed by the attacker; telemetry on a separate-trust-zone collector survives.
new_control_requirements.evidence: An IOS or IOS XE VPN head-end is the perimeter-trust-boundary device this control governs, and the premise transfers with one substitution: here the telemetry is destroyed by the reload rather than by an attacker. The pre-impact signals this CVE produces are the free-memory slope and the IKE negotiation records that precede exhaustion, and both live in volatile device state that the reload clears — so unless syslog and the memory series already reached a collector outside the device, an estate that suffered this attack has nothing left to distinguish it from a hardware fault. That distinction decides whether the upgrade window gets pulled forward.

CVE-2018-0156.name: Cisco IOS Software and Cisco IOS XE Software Smart Install Denial-of-Service Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: A crafted packet to TCP 4786 on a Smart Install client switch is validated improperly and reloads the device. Director-role devices are not affected; the exposed role is the one provisioning leaves behind.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; the Smart Install client protocol authenticates nobody, so reachability to TCP 4786 is the whole requirement.
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; a single crafted packet, no state to build and no credential to obtain. The only variable is whether the switch is in the client role, which the advisory has operators establish with `show vstack config`.
attack_vector.ai_factor: Cisco records internal security testing as the source. Third-party Smart Install research published in 2018 addressed a different CVE in the same feature, so it is not attribution for this one.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Running the advisory's `show vstack config` check across the switch estate and applying `no vstack` everywhere Smart Install is not operationally required — the vendor's own workaround, effective without a reload.
prevention.adequacy: It removes the listener rather than the defect, so a switch reimaged or restored from an older configuration comes back with the client role and the exposure. The disable has to be part of the build template, not a one-off sweep.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alerting on any TCP 4786 connection whose source is not the Smart Install director, and treating unexplained access-switch reloads as a security event rather than a hardware ticket.
detection.adequacy: Port-4786 telemetry exists only where the campus network is instrumented between access switches, and the reload destroys the switch's local log buffer, so detection depends on syslog having already reached a collector.

response.what_would_have_worked: On a suspected reload, capture `show vstack config` before any reprovisioning, disable the feature fleet-wide as the immediate containment, then schedule the fixed image.
response.adequacy: Containment is genuinely available here: `no vstack` is a vendor workaround that removes the listener without a reload, which the fixed image cannot. What it does not do is address CVE-2018-0171 in the same feature, which is a code-execution defect on the same port and needs the same disable plus the image.

NIST-800-53-CM-7.gap: An organisation can document its permitted services, justify each and pass CM-7 while every access switch runs a Smart Install client, because the client role is inherited from provisioning rather than configured by an administrator and therefore never enters the service inventory the control is assessed against. Least functionality assessed from documentation cannot see a listener that no document mentions.

NIST-800-53-SC-7.gap: SC-7 is met by controlling communications at external boundaries, and TCP 4786 on a campus access switch sits well inside them. The attacker this CVE needs is a host on the same user VLAN, so the boundary controls the organisation evidences are all in place, all working and all irrelevant to the path, since a boundary control has no expression for denying a workstation access to the provisioning port of the switch it is plugged into.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: The vulnerability-handling measure operates on an asset list, and this CVE's affected condition is not on that list: it is a runtime role visible only from `show vstack config`, not a version string. An entity with mature patch management, complete switch inventory and a tracked advisory can therefore report full coverage while the switches that actually need the fix were never enumerated as affected.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: The secure-configuration outcome is nominally met because the switch configurations are baselined, reviewed and clean — and they are clean precisely because the vulnerable feature does not appear in them. B4 evidence built from configuration review rather than from running the advisory's own runtime check will report a compliant estate that is fully exposed on TCP 4786.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Beyond the scoping question of whether a campus access switch attracts the mitigation strategy at all, the deeper inadequacy is that patch-compliance percentages are computed over inventoried assets in a known-affected state. Here the affected state is invisible to inventory, so the metric is accurate about the wrong population and rises to full compliance without the exposed switches ever being counted.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.22.gap: Network segregation can be documented, implemented and audited in full and still not contain this: the Smart Install client answers on the VLANs the switch already serves, so segregation between the campus and the internet, or between users and servers, leaves an attacker on any user port inside the segment that reaches port 4786. The control constrains lateral movement between zones, not access from a zone to the switch that carries it.

new_control_requirements.name: BUG-FAMILY-MITIGATION-PERSISTENCE
new_control_requirements.description: When a CVE patch lands, retain the pre-patch compensating controls (module blacklists, sysctl restrictions) until the patched code has soaked for a stated review period. Patches for one bug in a primitive class can introduce sibling bugs in the same class; the original compensating control may still apply to the sibling.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Smart Install is the clearest case of the sibling problem in Cisco's 2018-03-28 bundle: CVE-2018-0156 is a reload defect on TCP 4786 and CVE-2018-0171 is a code-execution defect on the same port and feature, disclosed the same day, with a public crash proof-of-concept published as Exploit-DB 44451 on 2018-03-29. The `no vstack` disable that cisco-sa-20180328-smi gives as this CVE's workaround is the control that covers both, so removing it once the image is upgraded discards protection against the sibling class — and a switch restored from an older configuration or reimaged in the field comes back in the client role unless the disable lives in the build template.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: This Cisco IOS and IOS XE Smart Install flaw is one where the control's compensating-controls branch is genuinely reachable inside the window: `no vstack` is a documented vendor workaround that needs no reload, so the 2022-03-03 KEV listing and its 2022-03-17 due date could have been met on the day across an entire access-switch estate. EPSS sits at 0.08195, the 94.4th percentile as of 2026-08-20, and the vendor's own advisory reached version 1.7 in December 2022 to record attempted exploitation the previous March — the SLA was satisfiable and the estate-wide runtime check is what it depends on.

CVE-2018-0155.name: Cisco Catalyst Bidirectional Forwarding Detection Denial-of-Service Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: An incomplete BFD header meets insufficient error handling in the Catalyst 4500 BFD offload path, crashing iosd and reloading the switch. The advisory scopes the trigger to a crafted BFD message sent to or across the device.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; no BFD session, credential or peer relationship is needed, and the packet may simply be transiting the switch.
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; the input is a truncated header rather than a groomed heap state. The only precondition is BFD offload being active, which the licence level determines by default on this platform family.
attack_vector.ai_factor: Found by Cisco during the resolution of a TAC support case — a customer outage traced back to a defect. No AI tooling is claimed in the attribution.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: The advisory's two measures: disabling BFD on switches that do not use it, and on those that do, a CoPP policy that permits BFD packets from known peers only and drops all other BFD traffic.
prevention.adequacy: Cisco is explicit that these limit exposure rather than address the vulnerability. The peer-restricted CoPP policy is genuinely useful, but it must be authored specifically — a generic campus CoPP policy protecting against volume will pass this packet through.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Off-box collection of supervisor crash events and iosd process telemetry, so a crash-and-reload sequence is visible as a pattern across the estate rather than as isolated chassis incidents.
detection.adequacy: A crash is detectable after the fact and gives no warning beforehand — unlike a memory leak, there is no slope to watch. What detection buys is correctly classifying the second occurrence as an attack rather than as a recurring hardware fault.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treat a repeat iosd crash on a 4500-class supervisor as suspected exploitation: apply the peer-restricted BFD CoPP policy immediately, then schedule the image upgrade rather than replacing the supervisor.
response.adequacy: The response containment is real but partial, and the failure mode it prevents is expensive misdiagnosis — a defect that presents as a hardware fault invites a supervisor swap that changes nothing, since the replacement runs the same image.

NIST-800-53-SC-5.gap: A control-plane policing policy satisfies SC-5 on paper, but a policy dimensioned against traffic volume reaching the CPU does not describe this attack. This attack is one truncated BFD header, so it passes any rate-based class cleanly; only a policy that restricts BFD to enumerated peers — which the advisory has to spell out because it is not the default posture — actually limits the exposure.

NIST-800-53-CM-7.gap: CM-7 is assessed by reviewing what has been enabled and justifying it, and BFD offload on these supervisors is enabled by the licence rather than by an administrator. An estate that has genuinely minimised its configured services still runs the vulnerable feature everywhere, and no least-functionality review that reads configurations rather than platform defaults will discover it.

NIS2-Art21-business-continuity.gap: Continuity measures for a distribution layer are evidenced by redundant chassis, tested failover and documented recovery objectives, all of which are met. They assume failures are independent, and this defect is common-mode: the same crafted BFD message crossing the path takes the partner supervisor if it runs the same affected release, so the documented recovery time is computed against a scenario that does not describe this CVE.

UK-CAF-B5.gap: A CAF assessment finds a resilient design and confirms failover works, which is true and insufficient. The advisory's scoping — a message sent to or across the switch — means the packet reaching one chassis has a natural path to the other, so resilience premised on an attacker having to target each device separately does not describe the exposure, and B5 evidence contains nothing that would surface the shared-release dependency.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Reading the maturity model's scoping, a campus distribution switch is neither an internet-facing service nor a workstation or server operating system, so the shorter clock does not clearly attach and the platform may fall between the two patching mitigation strategies entirely. An organisation assessed at a given maturity level can therefore evidence compliance while a supervisor engine that a single truncated packet reloads runs pre-2018 software; that reading is worth settling with the assessor rather than assuming either way.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: The control is met by a functioning vulnerability-management process fed by vendor advisories, and this advisory was published on 2018-03-28. What the process cannot do is evaluate applicability, because applicability here depends on the supervisor engine model and the software licence tier, and where the asset register holds neither attribute for network hardware the evaluation cannot be completed at all. A.8.8's evidence does not distinguish an unassessed CVE from an assessed one, so this defect can sit as possibly-not-applicable across successive review cycles.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: For the Catalyst 4500 and 4500-X family this control is satisfiable through its compensating-controls branch and not through its patch branch: a peer-restricted BFD CoPP policy can be pushed to a distribution pair inside the window, whereas the fixed image reloads the chassis. The 2022-03-03 KEV listing with its 2022-03-17 due date, against EPSS 0.07793 at the 94.2nd percentile as of 2026-08-20, is exactly the case for writing the CoPP policy in advance so it is a deployment rather than an authoring exercise when the clock starts.

new_control_requirements.name: MITIGATION-ACTIVE-PATCH-PENDING-VERDICT-CLASS
new_control_requirements.description: Compliance verdicts must distinguish three states: (a) binary patch deployed (vulnerability eliminated), (b) vendor-mitigation rule active, no binary patch (residual risk: any defect in the mitigation rule reopens the vulnerability), (c) no mitigation, no patch (full exposure). Audit reports must surface (b) as a distinct compensating-control state with an associated time-bound action item, not as a 'patched per SLA' outcome.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Cisco's own wording forces this distinction on the 4500 family: the advisory says there are no workarounds that address the vulnerability, then offers measures that limit exposure — disabling BFD where unused, and a CoPP policy permitting BFD from known peers only. A switch carrying that policy is in state (b), and the residual risk is concrete rather than theoretical, because the policy is the state rather than the code: a supervisor replaced, or a configuration restored from before the policy was written, comes back without it and returns the chassis to full exposure with no CVE, no advisory revision and no audit event to notice it. The opposite drift announces itself instead — a new BFD peer that is never added to the policy has its BFD dropped and its session fails to establish, which the operator sees.

CVE-2018-0154.name: Cisco IOS Software Integrated Services Module for VPN Denial-of-Service Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: Crafted VPN traffic reaching a router's ISM-VPN crypto engine is handled insufficiently and the device hangs or crashes. The vulnerable component is the offload module, so the affected set is defined by installed hardware.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; the advisory describes an unauthenticated remote attacker sending crafted VPN traffic, with no tunnel or credential established first.
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; the constraint is reaching a router that has the module installed, not defeating a protocol state machine. Cisco scores the result S:C (8.6) where NVD scores S:U (7.5).
attack_vector.ai_factor: Cisco attributes the discovery to the resolution of a TAC support case. No AI-assisted discovery is claimed, and no research brand is involved that could be mistaken for one.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: The fixed IOS release, since the advisory publishes no workaround. Where the ISM-VPN is present but unused, taking the module out of the crypto path removes the affected component entirely.
prevention.adequacy: Removing an unused module helps only the minority of sites that have one idle. For the rest the module is doing the branch's crypto, so prevention reduces to the upgrade and its site outage.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Off-box syslog from branch routers so the crypto-engine state before a hang survives the reload, and WAN-side flow records showing traffic arriving from outside the configured peer set.
detection.adequacy: A hang can leave less behind than a clean crash, and where a branch router's syslog is not shipped off-box, the recovery reload takes the local buffer with it. Detection here mostly serves to stop the outage being closed as a hardware fault.

response.what_would_have_worked: On a repeat crypto-engine hang, run `show crypto engine brief` and the release check before dispatching a replacement chassis, and schedule the fixed image with the site instead.
response.adequacy: The value is diagnostic rather than protective: a replacement router built from the same image and the same module returns the site to the identical exposure, which is the specific way this defect survives an otherwise competent incident response.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: Flaw remediation is evidenced by advisories ingested, mapped and tracked, and this advisory has been tracked since 2018-03-28. The mapping step silently fails because the affected attribute is an installed accelerator card rather than a software version, so the CVE maps either onto every IOS router, which is far broader than the advisory's own vulnerable-products scope, or onto none. Both outcomes are indistinguishable from a functioning SI-2 programme in the evidence the control produces.

NIST-800-53-SC-5.gap: The organisation can hold WAN-edge rate limiting and upstream scrubbing and satisfy SC-5, and neither addresses crafted VPN traffic arriving at normal volumes to a module that exists to accept VPN traffic. The control's design assumption — that malicious traffic is distinguishable by quantity at a boundary — is what this defect does not satisfy.

NIS2-Art21-availability.gap: Branch availability evidenced by spare-chassis arrangements and a target restoration time will be met when a router carrying this defect hangs. They restore service into the identical exposure, because the spare is built to the same image and takes the same module, so the availability measure functions perfectly and the cause persists through every invocation of it.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: A B4 review of WAN routers supporting essential functions will confirm they are inventoried, supported and patched to policy, using chassis model and IOS release as the keys. Neither key distinguishes the routers with an ISM-VPN installed, so the assessment can report full coverage of the router estate while never having identified the subset this CVE actually affects.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Scope is not the problem here — a branch WAN router terminating IPsec is internet-facing, so the mitigation strategy and its exploit-driven clock both apply once KEV listed the CVE on 2022-03-03. The inadequacy is that maturity is measured by policy and coverage rather than by whether the estate can actually take the outage: with no workaround available, every affected site must accept a WAN reload, and a policy that mandates a deadline it cannot schedule reports as compliant while the images stay in place.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: The control is met by a vulnerability-management process with vendor feeds, defined roles and review cadence, all of which existed here from 2018 onward. Its exposure-evaluation step depends on asset data at card level — which routers hold an ISM-VPN — and where the register records chassis only, the evaluation cannot be performed at all, so the CVE remains permanently in an unassessed state that the control's evidence does not distinguish from an assessed one.

new_control_requirements.name: MITIGATION-ACTIVE-PATCH-PENDING-VERDICT-CLASS
new_control_requirements.description: Compliance verdicts must distinguish three states: (a) binary patch deployed (vulnerability eliminated), (b) vendor-mitigation rule active, no binary patch (residual risk: any defect in the mitigation rule reopens the vulnerability), (c) no mitigation, no patch (full exposure). Audit reports must surface (b) as a distinct compensating-control state with an associated time-bound action item, not as a 'patched per SLA' outcome.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Every router carrying an ISM-VPN on a pre-fix IOS release is in state (c), and that is the finding an audit must show, because cisco-sa-20180328-dos states there are no workarounds: no CoPP class, no feature disable and no filter is available to occupy state (b), and the only route to state (a) short of the fixed image is physically removing the module, which is only available where that module is not carrying the site's crypto. Where an estate has recorded WAN-edge filtering or upstream scrubbing as the compensating control for this CVE, that record is false — which matters because EPSS stands at 0.07117, the 93.7th percentile as of 2026-08-20, on a defect the vendor reports as having drawn attempted exploitation in March 2022.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: The KEV clock opened 2022-03-03 with a 2022-03-17 due date on a Cisco IOS defect whose fix shipped 2018-03-28, so the binding constraint was never patch availability — it was knowing which routers hold an ISM-VPN module and getting a WAN reload window at each of those sites. An SLA measured in hours is only meaningful for this CVE if the hardware-level inventory that `show crypto engine brief` establishes already exists when the listing lands.

CVE-2018-0151.name: Cisco IOS Software and Cisco IOS XE Software Quality of Service Remote Code Execution Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: A crafted packet to UDP 18999 defeats incorrect bounds checking in the IOS and IOS XE quality-of-service subsystem and overflows a buffer, yielding code execution with elevated privileges on the device or, short of that, a reload. Only traffic addressed to the device triggers it; transiting traffic does not.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; no credential, session or user interaction is involved, and the packet is processed by the control plane on arrival.
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; the constraints are that UDP 18999 is bound and that the packet is addressed to the device rather than passing through it. Cisco's assessment steps make the bound socket the operator's test.
attack_vector.ai_factor: Cisco records internal security testing as the source. No AI-assisted discovery is claimed by the vendor, and no AI-branded research programme is credited.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: The advisory's CoPP policy denying traffic to UDP 18999 on devices not using Adaptive QoS for DMVPN, including the entry that ignores fragments, or the police-rate variant where the drop keyword is unsupported — then the fixed image.
prevention.adequacy: Cisco states the workaround is unavailable on device families that support CoPP only on specific ports and protocols, naming the ASR 900 Series, and it must be removed if Adaptive QoS for DMVPN is later configured. So it protects most of the estate, leaves a named remainder exposed, and creates a configuration dependency that a future feature change silently invalidates.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Counters on the CoPP class for UDP 18999 exported off-box, so attempts are visible as drops rather than inferred from an outage, plus alerting on device-originated connections to unexpected destinations.
detection.adequacy: Drop counters prove attempts against devices that have the policy; on devices that cannot take it there is nothing equivalent. Successful code execution on IOS produces little that ordinary network monitoring surfaces, which is why image verification matters more than log review after the fact.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating a device with UDP 18999 bound and no CoPP policy as potentially executed-against: extract the configuration, verify the running image against the vendor-published hash, rotate every credential the device held, and rebuild rather than patch in place.
response.adequacy: This is the only path that addresses the actual impact and it costs far more than the upgrade, so it needs authorising before the incident rather than during it. It is also what distinguishes this CVE from the availability-only defects published alongside it on 2018-03-28: there a reload restores a clean state, and here it does not.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: A CVSS-tiered SI-2 policy places a 9.8 in its fastest remediation band, and that band is discharged by scheduling rather than by outcome. No field in the control distinguishes a network device where code execution means the control plane from a server where it means one host, and none holds the contradiction between CISA's known-exploited assertion of 2022-03-03 and cisco-sa-20180328-qos's statement, unrevised since 2018-04-27, that PSIRT is not aware of malicious use.

NIST-800-53-SC-7.gap: Boundary protection at the network edge is fully compatible with this attack succeeding, because the packet is addressed to the router itself and can originate from inside the WAN, a branch, or any peered segment. The control-plane policy that would actually filter it is a device-level construct, and on the platform families Cisco names as supporting CoPP only for specific ports and protocols it cannot be built at all — leaving SC-7 formally implemented and locally unenforceable.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: The measure is met by a documented vulnerability-handling process fed by vendor advisories, and this advisory has been in that feed since 2018-03-28. The process has no rule for the situation that arose in 2022, where CISA asserted in-the-wild exploitation and the vendor's advisory — last revised 2018-04-27 — did not, so two entities with equally compliant processes will reach opposite urgency decisions and both will be able to evidence conformity.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: B4 evidence built from network design documentation answers the question "do we run Adaptive QoS for DMVPN?", and a negative answer closes the risk. The advisory's own test asks instead whether UDP 18999 is bound, which is a runtime property of the release rather than of the design, so the assessment reaches a confident negative on a question that does not determine exposure.

UK-CAF-D1.gap: A response and recovery plan for network infrastructure written for loss of availability — failover, spares, restoration targets — is nominally in place and addresses none of what this defect produces. A router that may have run attacker code with elevated privileges needs image verification against vendor hashes, credential rotation for everything the device held, and a rebuild, so the plan can be complete and exercised while the scenario this CVE creates has no runbook at all.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: The mitigation strategy's faster clock is conditioned on an exploit existing, and this CVE is the case where published sources disagree about that: CISA lists it as known-exploited from 2022-03-03, while Cisco's advisory still states PSIRT is not aware of malicious use. An assessed organisation can meet the strategy under the vendor's reading and miss it under CISA's, with no adjudication in the model itself — the gap sits in the standard's silence about which source governs, not in the estate's diligence.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: The organisation evaluates exposure using the advisory's product scope, which reads as all IOS and IOS XE devices running a vulnerable release — an answer so broad it cannot be acted on, and one that A.8.8 accepts as a completed evaluation. The evaluation that would be actionable requires querying every device for a bound UDP 18999 socket, and nothing in the control prompts an estate-wide runtime query as part of vulnerability assessment.

new_control_requirements.name: PERIMETER-DEVICE-ZERODAY-SLA-TIER
new_control_requirements.description: Compliance frameworks must define a distinct patch SLA tier for pre-auth RCE on perimeter-trust-boundary devices (firewalls, VPN concentrators, WAFs, edge load-balancers). Tier requirement: vendor-mitigation deployed within 4 hours of KEV listing OR isolation of the vulnerable interface; standard 14/30-day SLAs do not apply because the device IS the trust boundary.
new_control_requirements.evidence: This is pre-authentication code execution with elevated privileges on Cisco IOS and IOS XE, reached over UDP 18999 on devices whose Adaptive QoS for DMVPN role makes them the VPN trust boundary — the exact tier this control exists to create. The control's own alternative branches are both available and both constrained: the advisory's CoPP policy for UDP 18999 is deployable in hours, and Cisco states it is unavailable on families such as the ASR 900 Series that support CoPP only on specific ports and protocols, where isolation of the vulnerable interface or the upgrade is all that is left. A 14- or 30-day tier applied to a 9.8 on the device terminating the WAN is the specific failure this tier is meant to prevent.

new_control_requirements.name: PERIMETER-COMPROMISE-REBUILD-NOT-PATCH
new_control_requirements.description: Pre-rehearsed IR runbook for any perimeter device that suffers a pre-auth RCE CVE in active exploitation MUST default to config-exfil + rebuild + credential rotation, not patch-in-place. Patch-in-place leaves attacker-installed implants intact.
new_control_requirements.evidence: The trigger condition has to be stated exactly for this CVE, because the two authorities disagree: CISA listed it as known-exploited on 2022-03-03, while cisco-sa-20180328-qos has not been revised since 2018-04-27 and still records that PSIRT is not aware of malicious use. Where an operator takes the KEV listing as the trigger, this runbook is what it should invoke — a Cisco IOS or IOS XE device with UDP 18999 bound, no CoPP policy and a pre-fix image is a device that may have executed attacker code with elevated privileges, and upgrading the image afterwards neither proves nor removes what ran. The rebuild path is image verification against vendor-published hashes, configuration extraction and rotation of every credential the device held.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: KEV listed this on 2022-03-03 with a 2022-03-17 due date, four years after Cisco shipped the fix, and EPSS now stands at 0.14287 — the 96.3rd percentile as of 2026-08-20. The control's compensating-controls branch is what makes the four-hour figure meetable here, since the advisory's UDP 18999 CoPP policy deploys without a reload, and the branch also forces the estate to identify the platforms Cisco says cannot take that policy, which are the devices where the SLA can only be met by upgrading or by isolating the interface.

CVE-2017-8540.name: Microsoft Malware Protection Engine Improper Restriction of Operations Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: A file the attacker composes is scanned by the Malware Protection Engine, whose script emulator frees a string object that native code is still holding on the unmarked native stack, then calls a virtual method on it. The scan is what triggers it, so the attacker's problem is delivery — a download, an attachment, an upload into a directory a scanning server watches — and the payoff is execution as LocalSystem on the machine doing the scanning.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; the attacker holds no account on the target and needs none. The only requirement is putting a file where real-time protection will read it.
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; the trigger is a short script with no heap groom and no information leak, and the engine parses it automatically. NVD's UI:R reflects the file having to land locally, not a user opening the payload.
attack_vector.ai_factor: Found by hand. Ian Beer of Google Project Zero reasoned about which pointers the collector marks and which frame the GC-disable flag covers, rather than fuzzing for a crash; no AI-assisted discovery or weaponization is claimed by Microsoft, by Project Zero, or in the Exploit-DB entry.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Holding the loaded engine at or above 1.1.13704.0 and verifying that version endpoint by endpoint. The fix needs no reboot and no window, so the only failure mode is the definition channel not reaching the host.
prevention.adequacy: It closes this defect completely and closes nothing about the class: mpengine parses attacker-chosen content as LocalSystem by design, and Project Zero filed several separate engine defects in the same period, of which CVE-2017-0290, CVE-2017-8541 and the CVE-2017-8535 through CVE-2017-8538 group are the publicly indexed neighbours.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alarming on MsMpEng.exe faults and antimalware-service restarts, on any child process created under that service, and on a host whose engine version stops advancing while definitions keep updating.
detection.adequacy: Partial at best. The engine runs as LocalSystem, so telemetry produced on the compromised host by the compromised security product is the weakest evidence available; the engine-version-lag signal is reliable but only shows exposure, not exploitation.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating a host that loaded an engine at or below 1.1.13701.0 while processing untrusted inbound files as a LocalSystem compromise candidate, and reviewing the scanned-file corpus for the arrival that preceded a service fault.
response.adequacy: Bounded by retention. The engine update leaves nothing behind that distinguishes a host that was exploited from one that was merely exposed, so the response scope has to be drawn from mail, proxy and file-share records rather than from the endpoint's own antimalware history.

NIST-800-53-SI-3.gap: The estate is fully compliant — antimalware deployed, real-time protection on, definitions current — and that compliant state is the one in which a crafted file is parsed by mpengine as LocalSystem. SI-3 has no provision for treating the scanner as attack surface, so the control is met at the exact moment the exposure is maximised.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: Flaw remediation is evidenced from the monthly rollup, and the fix for this CVE is engine build 1.1.13704.0, which never appears in a rollup. An SI-2 record can be complete for every host while those same hosts load 1.1.13701.0, because the artefact the control collects and the artefact that carries the fix are different things.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: Patch management is nominally in place for operating systems and applications, and the vulnerable component is neither: the engine updates on its own channel, several times a day, without a change record. Compliance is therefore demonstrable while the fixed build 1.1.13704.0 has not reached a single endpoint, and nothing in the measure requires proving the definition channel works.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: Secure configuration is assessed and passes, because the assessed configuration — Defender enabled, real-time protection on — is the vendor-recommended one and also the precondition for this flaw. B4's maintenance expectation is where the outcome would change, but only if the evidence collected is the loaded engine build measured against 1.1.13704.0 rather than the presence of the product.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Patch targets for operating systems and applications can both be met while engine 1.1.13701.0 remains loaded, because on my reading the bundled scanning engine falls into neither category and no maturity-level measurement is taken against it. The 2022-03-24 KEV due date therefore attaches to a version string that the estate's patching evidence does not contain.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.7.gap: Protection against malware is implemented, monitored and reported, and the implementation is the vulnerability: the engine parses attacker-chosen content by design and runs as LocalSystem while doing it. A.8.7 can express that the control exists but not that the control's own parser needs vulnerability management, which is why this CVE reads as a clean audit and an open exposure at the same time.

CIS-Controls-v8-10.1.gap: Anti-malware is deployed and centrally managed on every asset, which is exactly the uniformity that makes one engine defect a fleet-wide condition. The console satisfies 10.1 by reporting coverage and definition freshness; unless it also reports the engine build against 1.1.13704.0, the same console shows green across an estate that is entirely unremediated.

new_control_requirements.name: SECURITY-TOOL-INTEGRITY-VERIFICATION
new_control_requirements.description: Security tools (AV/AM, EDR, vulnerability scanners) must be treated as in-scope of vulnerability management with the same SLAs as other privileged software. Definition-update channels must use TLS with certificate pinning. Compliance audits must include a trust-anchor-inversion test: deliver a crafted input to the security tool in a sandbox and confirm rejection.
new_control_requirements.evidence: The Microsoft Malware Protection Engine is the vulnerable component in this CVE, not the thing that would have caught it: Microsoft's own description has a crafted file scanned by mpengine executing in the security context of the LocalSystem account, and the trigger published as Exploit-DB 42088 on 2017-05-30 is a short script that needs neither a credential nor a user action. The trust-anchor-inversion test this control asks for is the exact test that distinguishes a Defender estate that is protected from one that is uniformly exploitable, and the version boundary it would have to be run against is 1.1.13701.0 last affected versus 1.1.13704.0 first fixed. CISA gave the engine a 2022-03-24 remediation due date for a defect Microsoft's own exploitability index had rated 'Exploitation Less Likely'.

new_control_requirements.name: EDR-PLATFORM-UPDATE-DISTINCT-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: EDR / AV platform-update channels must be tracked as distinct patch surfaces with their own SLA, separate from OS-update SLA. Defender platform updates, CrowdStrike Falcon-sensor updates, SentinelOne agent updates, etc. ship outside the OS-patching cadence and require dedicated monitoring and SLA tracking.
new_control_requirements.evidence: This CVE is remediated by Malware Protection Engine 1.1.13704.0 and by nothing else — no rollup, no KB, no reboot. Because the engine reaches endpoints on the malware-definition channel, an estate that tracks Windows patching alone has no field in which the remediation state of this CVE can even be recorded, and the KEV clock from 2022-03-03 to 2022-03-24 runs against a build number its reports do not contain. The separate SLA this control requires is what turns 'definitions are current' into the checkable claim that the loaded engine is at or above 1.1.13704.0 on every host named in the affected list, from Windows 7 SP1 laptops to Exchange Server 2013 and 2016.

new_control_requirements.name: SECURITY-AGENT-ENGINE-CURRENCY-AUDIT
new_control_requirements.description: Treat the EDR/AV agent's own engine/platform build as a first-class, audited remediation target: verify (not assume) that the deployed Microsoft Defender Malware Protection Engine is >= the fixed build (1.1.26040.8 for CVE-2026-41091) on every endpoint, and alarm on hosts whose engine build lags despite an auto-update policy. A SYSTEM-privileged security agent's flaws are LPE-to-SYSTEM by construction.
new_control_requirements.evidence: The control names the measurement this CVE needs, with a different fixed build: for CVE-2017-8540 the audited threshold is Malware Protection Engine 1.1.13704.0, against 1.1.13701.0 as the last affected version, on the Forefront and Defender installs NVD scopes to Windows 7 SP1 through Windows 10 1703, Windows Server 2008 SP2 through 2016, and Exchange Server 2013 and 2016. The 'verify, not assume' half is load-bearing because the engine updates automatically by default, which is exactly the assumption that lets a host with a broken or filtered definition path sit below the fixed build while its auto-update policy reports as applied.

CVE-2017-6744.name: Cisco IOS Software SNMP Remote Code Execution Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: A crafted SNMP request sent to a Cisco IOS or IOS XE device overflows a buffer in the SNMP subsystem's handling of one of the MIBs cisco-sa-20170629-snmp lists. The attacker supplies the device's read-only community string or an SNMPv3 user credential and gets either arbitrary code execution with full control of the device or a reload, and the MIBs are reachable by default as soon as SNMP is turned on.
attack_vector.privileges_required: low — PR:L; the read-only community string on SNMP v1 or v2c, or SNMPv3 user credentials. Read-only is enough: the credential is a precondition for the parse, not an authorization check on the write.
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; one request to the device's own address, with no user interaction and no configuration prerequisite beyond SNMP being enabled. Reaching reliable code execution rather than a reload is image-specific, which the advisory's separate treatment of exploitation and exploit code reflects.
attack_vector.ai_factor: Cisco states the vulnerabilities were found during internal testing, so discovery is vendor product-security work with no outside reporter, no tooling described and nothing AI-assisted claimed.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Applying the advisory's snmp-server view exclusions to every community string and SNMPv3 group on publication in 2017, then upgrading to the fixed release the Cisco IOS Software Checker names for the device's train.
prevention.adequacy: The exclusion is genuinely preventive and needs no reload, but it is a running-configuration state that a template push, a device replacement or a rollback silently removes, and it left eight further CVE ids from the same advisory to be tracked separately. Only the upgrade removes the code.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alerting on SNMP requests to device management addresses from sources outside the polling baseline, and treating an SNMP-process reload as a security event rather than a stability one.
detection.adequacy: Weak on its own. The attacker is using the same protocol and often the same credential as the monitoring system, so the only separating feature is the source address and the OIDs requested — and if the outcome is code execution rather than a reload, the device's own logs are under the attacker's control.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating a device that answered SNMP from an untrusted source while unpatched as a candidate compromise: comparing the running configuration and image against a known-good copy held off the device, and rotating the community strings and SNMPv3 credentials that transited it.
response.adequacy: Bounded by where the baseline lives. A configuration comparison is only meaningful against a copy the device cannot reach, and credential rotation is fleet-wide wherever one community string was configured across many devices.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: The flaw-remediation process runs, and it stalls at the first step for this CVE because cisco-sa-20170629-snmp names no fixed version — the target build comes from the Software Checker per running version and per train. A programme that records fix availability as one boolean per CVE cannot represent a fleet where some trains have a fixed release and others do not, and the correction is a reload of a routing asset.

NIST-800-53-CM-7.gap: Least functionality passes because SNMP has a business justification, and the assessment stops one level above where the exposure is. The advisory records its MIBs as enabled by default whenever SNMP is enabled, so a device with a clean CM-7 finding is exposing all of them; the control has no natural place to record a per-MIB view restriction as the required configuration.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: A patch-management measure keyed to vendor release date closed this item in 2017, and the KEV obligation opened on 2022-03-03 with a 2022-03-24 due date. Nothing in the measure reopens a satisfied window, and nothing in it accommodates a fix identified by a lookup tool rather than a published build string, so compliance and exposure coexist without contradiction.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: Secure configuration and maintenance are assessed and pass on an estate that keeps SNMP inside a management VLAN, yet the credential the attack requires is the one the polling system itself presents. The maintenance action is a device reload, argued for on an EPSS of 0.07158 at the 93.776 percentile as of 2026-08-20 against a change freeze, on a CVE Cisco states it has observed being exploited.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Patch windows keyed to the release of a vendor patch were satisfiable in 2017, and on my reading nothing in the maturity model reopens a window once satisfied. A device that later drifted onto a train with no fixed release is exposed again with no control event to mark it, because the model measures upgrade cadence rather than the running version's verdict from the Software Checker.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: Technical vulnerability management ingests nine CVE ids from one advisory sharing one description, and both dispositions are wrong: nine tickets yield nine identical assessments against the same asset, one ticket closes on the first fixed release that lands. Neither answers whether CVE-2017-6744 is still reachable on a given device, which only the running train plus the presence of an snmp-server view exclusion can settle.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: This is the case the control's 'documented compensating controls' clause exists for. Cisco IOS and IOS XE remediation for CVE-2017-6744 is a reload on a routing asset with no fixed version published in the advisory text, so a four-hour patch is not available to most estates — but the snmp-server view exclusion in cisco-sa-20170629-snmp is, and it is a configuration push. The KEV listing of 2022-03-03 with a 2022-03-24 due date, on a CVE Cisco records as exploited, is the trigger; treating the exclusion as the deployed mitigation and the upgrade as the scheduled one is what the SLA can actually be met with.

new_control_requirements.name: INCOMPLETE-PATCH-SEQUENCE-SEVERITY-MULTIPLIER
new_control_requirements.description: Vulnerability-management programs must apply a severity multiplier when a CVE is the Nth in an incomplete-patch sequence on the same primitive (third MOTW bypass, second AMSI bypass, etc.). Framework controls treating each CVE as discrete obscure the structural defect; the Nth CVE in a sequence implies that future bypasses on the same primitive are likely.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2017-6744 is one of nine CVE ids Cisco published simultaneously against one primitive — buffer handling in the IOS and IOS XE SNMP subsystem — with eleven bug ids behind them and ten MIBs in the workaround filter. Treating it as a discrete finding produces an 8.8 that reads like any other high, and loses the structural signal: the advisory's revision 1.11 on 2025-07-30 added a further MIB to that filter, eight years after the initial 2017-06-29 publication, which is the same primitive yielding more surface long after the sequence was assumed closed.

CVE-2017-6743.name: Cisco IOS and IOS XE Software SNMP Remote Code Execution Vulnerability (CVE-2017-6743)

attack_vector.description: One crafted SNMP request to a Cisco IOS or IOS XE device, authenticated by a read-only community string or an SNMPv3 user, overflows a buffer in the SNMP subsystem and yields code execution with full control of the device or a reload. The MIBs that carry the defect are enabled by default whenever SNMP is enabled, so nothing has to be configured for the surface to exist.
attack_vector.privileges_required: low — PR:L; a read-only community string on v1 or v2c, or SNMPv3 user credentials. On v1 and v2c that is a shared secret sent in cleartext on every poll, not an account with a privilege level.
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; a single request to the device address, no user interaction, no groom. The difficulty is reaching UDP/161 and holding the string, both of which are ordinary conditions on a monitored network.
attack_vector.ai_factor: Vendor internal testing per the advisory's Source section. No researcher credit, no tooling described, and no AI-assisted discovery claimed or implied.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Binding an snmp-server view that excludes the advisory's MIB OIDs to every community string and SNMPv3 group, and constraining UDP/161 by access-list to the polling hosts, ahead of the upgrade the Software Checker specifies.
prevention.adequacy: Effective and reload-free, but it survives only as long as the running configuration does: a template push, an RMA replacement or a rollback to an older configuration drops the view and restores the full MIB surface with no alert.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Baselining which hosts poll which devices and which OID subtrees they request, then alerting on SNMP from anything else inside the management segment.
detection.adequacy: Only as good as the baseline. The attack uses a permitted protocol from a permitted segment with a valid credential, so source and OID scope are the only distinguishing features, and neither is recorded by default on the device.

response.what_would_have_worked: Rotating community strings and SNMPv3 credentials across every device the exposed string reached, and comparing running configuration and image against copies held outside the device.
response.adequacy: Rotation scope is the honest problem: where one string was configured across many devices, the rotation is fleet-wide, and it is not complete until the polling platform holds the new secret as well as every device that answers to it.

NIST-800-53-SC-7.gap: Boundary protection is implemented and the SNMP flow is one of the flows it deliberately permits, so the control delivers the packet rather than stopping it. Reducing this CVE at the boundary would need a cut between the polling hosts and everything else able to reach UDP/161, which is finer than the segment-level enforcement SC-7 is usually evidenced with.

NIST-800-53-AC-3.gap: Access enforcement is in place and never consulted: the overflow happens while the SNMP subsystem parses the request, before any object-level read permission applies, and on v1 or v2c there is no subject to enforce against at all. A read-only credential and a read-write credential produce the same outcome, which is the clearest sign the control does not sit on this path.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: The remediation record cannot be completed from the CVE alone, because the fixed build for CVE-2017-6743 is whatever the Cisco IOS Software Checker returns for that device's running train and the advisory publishes no version list. SI-2 also has no field for the snmp-server view exclusion, so the state most devices sat in between 2017 and the 2022-03-24 due date is unrepresentable in the control's evidence.

NIS2-Art21-network-security.gap: Management-plane segmentation and SNMPv3 privacy both satisfy the measure and neither touches the defect: the request is authorised, the encryption protects it in transit, and the parser is reached exactly as intended. Nothing in the measure expresses restricting which MIB subtrees a permitted flow may request, which is the only network-layer reduction short of disabling SNMP.

UK-CAF-B2.gap: SNMP v1 and v2c present no user for B2 to assess — the community string is the credential and the authorization scope at once, held by a device configuration and a polling platform rather than by a person — so the register B2 is evidenced from has no natural place for it. A complete review of named administrators and their privileges therefore leaves untouched the one secret whose presentation runs code on every device it reaches, and a single disclosure of a fleet-wide string is a fleet-wide precondition rather than a single-device one.

AU-Essential-8-MFA.gap: There is no multi-factor path into SNMP: v1 and v2c present a shared community string, v3 presents a username with authentication and privacy keys, and none of the three supports a second factor. Recording this as covered would claim protection the protocol cannot offer, so the honest statement for CVE-2017-6743 is that MFA maturity, at any level, leaves the precondition untouched.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.22.gap: Network segregation is implemented and it does bound who can send the packet, but the bounded set is precisely the set that must reach UDP/161 for monitoring to work. Every device stays exploitable from the monitoring platform and from anything else with a route into that segment, so the control reduces the attacker population without reducing the exposure of any individual device.

new_control_requirements.name: MITIGATION-ACTIVE-PATCH-PENDING-VERDICT-CLASS
new_control_requirements.description: Compliance verdicts must distinguish three states: (a) binary patch deployed (vulnerability eliminated), (b) vendor-mitigation rule active, no binary patch (residual risk: any defect in the mitigation rule reopens the vulnerability), (c) no mitigation, no patch (full exposure). Audit reports must surface (b) as a distinct compensating-control state with an associated time-bound action item, not as a 'patched per SLA' outcome.
new_control_requirements.evidence: State (b) is where CVE-2017-6743 leaves most Cisco IOS and IOS XE devices for as long as the reload is deferred: the advisory's snmp-server view exclusion suppresses reachability of the listed MIB OIDs while the vulnerable SNMP parsing code stays resident, and the exclusion is a running-configuration statement that a template push or a device replacement removes silently. Recording that as patched hides a residual risk with a specific failure mode — one missing OID exclusion reopens the path — which is not hypothetical here, since advisory revision 1.11 of 2025-07-30 added a further MIB to that same filter. The time-bound action the control demands is the Software Checker upgrade, tracked against the 2022-03-24 KEV due date.

new_control_requirements.name: FLEET-CONTROL-PLANE-ADMIN-PRIVILEGE-TIER
new_control_requirements.description: Administrators of fleet-control-plane systems (MDM/UEM, EDR consoles, identity providers, container orchestrators, configuration management) must be classified as a distinct privilege tier above application admins, with: PAM-jumphost-only access, FIDO2 step-up per session, just-in-time elevation with approval workflow, separate identity from any other admin role, and dedicated PAW (privileged access workstation) hardware. Compliance frameworks must enumerate this tier explicitly rather than collapsing it into 'admin'.
new_control_requirements.evidence: The network monitoring platform is a fleet control plane by the definition that matters for CVE-2017-6743: it holds the SNMP credentials for every Cisco IOS and IOS XE device it polls, and those credentials are the sole precondition for arbitrary code execution on each of them under a CVE Cisco records as exploited and CISA listed on 2022-03-03. Treating its operators and its credential store as one tier above application administration is what puts the community strings and SNMPv3 users inside the identity register at all, which is the step that would let an estate answer how many devices one disclosed string reaches. The control's FIDO2 and jump-host requirements protect the platform that holds the secret, which is the only place a second factor can exist on this path, since SNMP itself supports none.

CVE-2017-6740.name: Cisco IOS and IOS XE Software SNMP Remote Code Execution Vulnerability (CVE-2017-6740)

attack_vector.description: An SNMP request crafted against one of the MIBs cisco-sa-20170629-snmp lists overflows a buffer in the Cisco IOS or IOS XE SNMP subsystem while the request is parsed, over IPv4 or IPv6, directed at the device itself. The result is full control of the device or a reload, and the credential required is the read-only community string or an SNMPv3 user.
attack_vector.privileges_required: low — PR:L; read-only SNMP access is sufficient, because the flaw is in parsing the request rather than in acting on it.
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; no information leak, no groom, no chained protocol, and the affected MIBs are on by default with SNMP. Only traffic addressed to the device works, so the attacker needs a route to the management address rather than an on-path position.
attack_vector.ai_factor: Internal Cisco testing per the advisory. No external credit, no method described, nothing AI-assisted claimed.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: The snmp-server view exclusion applied to every community string and SNMPv3 group at publication, held in the configuration template so rebuilds keep it, followed by the Software Checker upgrade.
prevention.adequacy: It removes reachability of the affected OIDs without a reload, and it is exactly as durable as the running configuration. It also has to be maintained against a moving list: the workaround filter gained another MIB at advisory revision 1.11 on 2025-07-30.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Exporting syslog and flow records to a collector outside the device's own trust zone, and treating an SNMP-process reload as a security event rather than a hardware or stability one.
detection.adequacy: Off-box telemetry is the only kind that survives successful execution, and it still shows reachability rather than exploitation. Where the outcome is a clean code-execution path, nothing on the device is trustworthy afterwards.

response.what_would_have_worked: Comparing running configuration and image hash against copies held off the device, rotating the SNMP credentials that reached it, and rebuilding rather than patching in place where execution cannot be ruled out.
response.adequacy: The comparison is only meaningful against a baseline the device could not write to, and an upgrade applied over a compromised device removes the defect without removing anything the attacker left in the configuration.

NIST-800-53-CM-7.gap: Least functionality is applied at the service level, where SNMP survives review because it is needed, and Cisco's own mitigation lives one level below that, at ten specific MIB OID subtrees. The advisory removes the fallback of assuming an unconfigured default is safe by stating that the affected MIBs are enabled the moment SNMP is enabled, so a passing CM-7 finding and full exposure to CVE-2017-6740 are the same state.

NIST-800-53-SI-4.gap: Monitoring is in place and the monitored asset is the one that fails: if the overflow reaches execution, the device's logging configuration and local buffer belong to the attacker, so SI-4 evidence about the router is produced by the router. Only telemetry already shipped off-box before the request retains value, which makes the control's adequacy a question about collector placement rather than about coverage.

NIS2-Art21-vulnerability-management.gap: The measure ingests CVSS 8.8, CWE-119 and EPSS 0.10788 at the 95.484 percentile as of 2026-08-20, and none of those fields carries the decisive fact that Cisco lists this id among vulnerabilities it has seen exploited. Prioritisation built on the scored fields therefore ranks a vendor-confirmed exploited network-device RCE alongside ordinary highs, and no step in the measure requires reading the advisory's exploitation section.

UK-CAF-C1.gap: Security monitoring coverage is demonstrable across servers and endpoints while the routing estate contributes almost nothing that would show this attack: the failure outcome looks like a stability reload, and the success outcome looks like nothing. Detecting CVE-2017-6740 would require SNMP source and OID baselining plus off-box telemetry, neither of which a coverage-based C1 assessment asks for.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Upgrade cadence can be evidenced against target windows without ever establishing what this CVE needs — that the running IOS or IOS XE version is one the Cisco IOS Software Checker reports as fixed for cisco-sa-20170629-snmp. On my reading the model measures the process rather than the per-device verdict, and the 2022-03-24 KEV due date attaches to the verdict.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.9.gap: Configuration management determines whether the only available pre-upgrade mitigation survives, because the snmp-server view exclusion exists solely as running configuration. Drift detection against a baseline that includes the exclusion catches its loss; restore-from-golden-template practice that predates the workaround removes it on every rebuild and reports success while doing so.

new_control_requirements.name: FIREWALL-EGRESS-TELEMETRY-SEPARATE-TRUST-ZONE
new_control_requirements.description: Firewall and other perimeter-trust-boundary devices must forward syslog, threat logs, and authentication logs to a SIEM hosted in a separate trust zone (different management plane, different credentials, different authentication path). Telemetry stored on the compromised device is destroyed by the attacker; telemetry on a separate-trust-zone collector survives.
