NIST-800-53-SI-3.gap: Where malicious-code protection is deployed, it has nothing to judge in this chain until the chain is over. The attack arrives as an HTML page, a SWF and an FLV, and the only thing wrong with the FLV is that its Nellymoser audio is larger than the decoder expects — a property of media data, not a payload signature. SI-3 evidence describing engine coverage and definition currency is complete and irrelevant to the moment of compromise.

NIS2-Art21-vulnerability-management.gap: Vulnerability management is present and its unit of work hides the finding. CVE-2015-3043 and CVE-2015-3113 are one decoder defect fixed twice, in APSB15-06 and APSB15-14, and a register handling each as an independent item shows an April closure and a June opening with nothing connecting them. The signal that matters — the same primitive failing twice in a quarter — exists only across records the process never joins.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: B4 assessment depends on version data being read in the right direction, and this record uses exclusive boundaries throughout: below 13.0.0.281, from 14.0.0.125 to below 17.0.0.169, below 11.2.202.457. Those three builds are the fixes and are not affected. An assessment that treats them as the last affected versions produces false findings against remediated hosts, and the inverse error passes vulnerable ones — either way the attestation is wrong for reasons that have nothing to do with the estate.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Patch application is achievable at any maturity level for this CVE and its measure carries no memory. Applying APSB15-06 in April 2015 and APSB15-14 in June 2015 both count as timely patching, and the maturity score improves for having done them. Nothing in the mitigation records that the second fix addressed the first fix's own root cause, which is the fact that should have moved Flash from the patch queue to the removal queue.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: Identification and evaluation of technical vulnerabilities is in place, and the evaluation is performed per CVE. Evaluated alone, CVE-2015-3043 is a critical remote code execution with a vendor fix and a clean closure. Evaluated with CVE-2015-3113 beside it, it is a component whose audio decoder failed the same way twice under two Adobe bulletins, and the correct output is a decision to remove Flash — a conclusion an A.8.8 register organized one row per CVE has no field to hold.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Adobe Flash Player's Nellymoser decoder flaw has been publicly exploitable through Metasploit and Exploit-DB 37536 since 2015, carries CVSS 9.8, and sits at EPSS 0.74448 on 2026-08-20 — the 99.451st percentile of that publication. CISA listed it on 2022-03-03 with a 2022-03-24 due date and a required action of disconnecting the end-of-life product, so the verified mitigation this control demands is the runtime's absence per host, not flash-plugin 11.2.202.457, which closes this CVE and not the sibling defect that followed it.

new_control_requirements.name: INCOMPLETE-PATCH-SEQUENCE-SEVERITY-MULTIPLIER
new_control_requirements.description: Vulnerability-management programs must apply a severity multiplier when a CVE is the Nth in an incomplete-patch sequence on the same primitive (third MOTW bypass, second AMSI bypass, etc.). Framework controls treating each CVE as discrete obscure the structural defect; the Nth CVE in a sequence implies that future bypasses on the same primitive are likely.
new_control_requirements.evidence: The Metasploit module for this CVE is the documentation of the sequence: modules/exploits/multi/browser/adobe_flash_nellymoser_bof.rb lists both ['CVE','2015-3043'] and ['CVE','2015-3113'] in its References and states that the later flaw is effectively a regression to the same root cause as the earlier one. Adobe patched the Nellymoser decoder in APSB15-06 and again in APSB15-14 two months later, and one exploit implementation covers both — which is exactly the structural signal a per-CVE register discards.

CVE-2015-2590.name: Oracle Java SE and Java SE Embedded Remote Code Execution Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: Attacker-supplied bytes reach ObjectInputStream.readSerialData() in the JDK Libraries component and reconstruct object state the security manager was meant to gate, giving execution with the privileges of the JVM process. The delivery route is either untrusted Java code the user runs (applet, Web Start) or an application interface that deserializes untrusted input.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none -- PR:N; Oracle's matrix records remote exploit without authentication across Java SE and Java SE Embedded
attack_vector.complexity: low -- AC:L; no groom, no leak and no configuration precondition is recorded, so the real constraint is having a path that deserializes attacker bytes
attack_vector.ai_factor: No AI involvement in discovery or weaponization is claimed by Oracle, Red Hat or any advisory read; the upstream record is JDK issue 8076401.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Reaching the July 2015 Critical Patch Update level on every Java runtime in the estate -- OS packages, Oracle installers and embedded JREs alike -- and restarting each JVM afterwards.
prevention.adequacy: Complete where the runtime is reachable by the patch process, and silent where it is not: a JRE shipped inside an appliance is remediated only when that vendor reships, and the KEV due date does not change that.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alerting on a JVM spawning a shell or script interpreter, and on outbound connections from an application server to destinations with no prior history.
detection.adequacy: Generic: the exploitation itself is in-process Java, so there is no file drop or service creation to key on, and detection begins at the attacker's first post-escape action rather than at the escape.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating an exposed JVM as a credential-holding process -- rotating the keystores, database credentials and API tokens it could read -- rather than closing the ticket on the package upgrade.
response.adequacy: Bounded by knowing which JVM was exposed and for how long; where the affected runtime was embedded and unmanaged, the exposure window is not reconstructible from package history.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: Nominally satisfied by any organisation with a patch cycle, since Oracle shipped the fix in July 2015 and the distributions followed within weeks. It remains inadequate because SI-2's completion signal is the installed package version, while this remediation completes only when the JVM restarts -- the RHEL and IBM errata both say so -- so the control reports done while the running process keeps the vulnerable code mapped.

NIST-800-53-CM-7.gap: Where least functionality is attested as removal of the Java browser plug-in, that genuinely removes the applet route. It does not touch the server-side route: Oracle rates the CVE remotely exploitable without authentication across Java SE and Java SE Embedded, and an application listener that deserializes untrusted objects reaches readSerialData() with no browser present.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: An entity can evidence a patch-management policy, a cadence and a scanner, and still not answer the only question this CVE asks: which running Java runtimes exist and who ships each of them. With Oracle, five Linux repackagers, IBM and an unknown number of embedding application vendors in play, a policy scoped to OS packages produces compliant evidence over an unremediated runtime.

NIS2-Art21-supply-chain.gap: Where supply-chain measures are evidenced by supplier assessments and contract terms, both of those were in place while the same Libraries defect propagated into Red Hat, Ubuntu, Debian, openSUSE, Gentoo and IBM builds. The missing artefact is a component inventory that lists embedded runtimes by build, which no supplier questionnaire produces.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: Secure configuration and maintenance is met on paper by a managed baseline that installs vendor updates. It is inadequate here because the maintenance action has two halves and only one is observable in the baseline: 1.8.0.51 installed, and every JVM restarted. A long-running service that has not been restarted since the update passes B4 evidence and executes the pre-fix code.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Maturity against patching applications is assessed from scan results, and the scan sees what the inventory declares. The Java builds named by Oracle -- 6u95, 7u80, 8u45, Embedded 7u75, 8u33 -- are discoverable when the runtime is OS-managed and invisible when it ships inside an appliance or a per-user install, so a high maturity rating and an exposed runtime coexist without contradiction.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: A vulnerability-management process fed by CVE feeds is exactly what A.8.8 asks for, and for this entry the feed carries an unspecified vulnerability related to Libraries with no CWE. Without pulling Red Hat's identification of the ObjectInputStream.readSerialData() deserialization defect (JDK 8076401), the risk owner cannot decide whether an in-house application that deserializes untrusted input is in scope, so the assessment defaults to the runtime version alone.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Oracle Java SE 6u95, 7u80 and 8u45 and Java SE Embedded 7u75 and 8u33 were fixed in the July 2015 Critical Patch Update, and CISA still had to list the CVE on 2022-03-03 with a 2022-03-24 due date -- roughly six and a half years of exposure after a fix existed. EPSS on 2026-08-20 is 0.25469 (97.785th percentile), so the flaw is still being scored as attractive. The verification half of this control is what the CVE needs: RHSA-2015:1228 and RHSA-2015:1485 require every running JVM to restart, so 'mitigation deployed' means package plus restart, per host.

new_control_requirements.name: TIER-3-DEPENDENCY-INVENTORY
new_control_requirements.description: Supply chain inventory must extend to tier-3 dependencies (dependencies of dependencies of direct dependencies). SBOM coverage for libsystemd-class transitive dependencies cannot be omitted under SR-3.
new_control_requirements.evidence: One JDK Libraries defect reached Oracle Java SE and Java SE Embedded, OpenJDK builds from Red Hat (java-1.8.0-openjdk 1.8.0.51), Canonical (openjdk-7, USN-2696-1), Debian (DSA-3316, DSA-3339), openSUSE and Gentoo, and IBM Java (java-1.7.1-ibm 1.7.1.3.10-1jpp) at the same time. The Java runtime is the tier-3 case this control describes: it is rarely a declared application dependency and routinely an embedded one, so an estate cannot answer which products carry an affected build without an inventory that reaches below the installed application.

CVE-2015-2545.name: Microsoft Office Malformed EPS File Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: A crafted EPS image inside an Office file drives the shared EPS import filter into memory corruption, and the attacker executes code as the current user. Delivery is a mailed document or one hosted for download; where Word is the Outlook message reader the preview pane alone is sufficient.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none -- PR:N; the exploit runs at whatever rights the opening user holds, which is why Microsoft's severity framing distinguishes administrative from restricted accounts
attack_vector.complexity: low -- AC:L with UI:R; the constraint is user interaction, not exploit difficulty, and the analysed sample resolved its own module bases and bypassed EMET 5.5
attack_vector.ai_factor: No AI-assisted discovery or weaponization is claimed in the bulletin or in the public analysis; the exploit was reverse-engineered from live samples by human analysts.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Applying the November 2015 re-release of the MS15-099 packages, and before that, denying all users access to EPSIMP32.FLT so no Office application could import EPS.
prevention.adequacy: The re-released package closes it; the ACL workaround only holds while it is in place, breaks legitimate EPS rendering, and Microsoft states 'This setting must be reverted before installing future security updates'. That makes it a state no update cycle carries forward: on a host still relying on the workaround, the next Office update ends with the ACL removed, and it protects again only where someone re-applies it deliberately.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alerting on Office applications spawning child processes or writing executables, particularly for documents that arrived by mail.
detection.adequacy: Behavioural rather than specific: nothing distinguishes this exploit's parent-child pattern from other Office document exploits, and the preview-pane path means the alert may be the first sign a user was ever involved.

response.what_would_have_worked: Hunting the implant artefacts published for this campaign -- wordpade.exe under %ALLUSERSPROFILE%\Accessories, http.exe from a CAB, the trojanised PotPlayer.dll -- on any host that opened a suspect document.
response.adequacy: Those artefacts describe the campaigns Kaspersky documented, not the vulnerability; an operator using a different payload leaves none of them, so the hunt confirms a match and cannot clear a host.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: An organisation that deployed the September 2015 Office updates can evidence full SI-2 compliance for this CVE and still be exploitable, because Microsoft re-released every affected package on 2015-11-10 to address it comprehensively. Flaw remediation records the identifier and the date installed; it does not carry the bulletin revision, so nothing in the control's own evidence distinguishes a September install from a November one.

NIST-800-53-CM-7.gap: Least functionality is nominally satisfied by a hardened Office baseline, and the specific function that mattered here -- EPS image import through EPSIMP32.FLT -- is not one any standard baseline enumerates. Microsoft had to publish a takeown-and-deny script and a Fix it to disable it, and attach a warning that the ACL must be reverted before later updates, which is a maintenance obligation the control does not track.

NIS2-Art21-vulnerability-handling.gap: Vulnerability-handling procedures are met by a documented intake-to-remediation flow, which ran correctly in September 2015 and produced an incomplete result. The inadequacy is structural: the process keys on the CVE identifier, and the second, complete fix arrived on 2015-11-10 under the same identifier as a bulletin revision, so there was no new record for the flow to consume.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: Secure configuration for end-user devices can be fully in place here and still not reach the path. With Word as the default Outlook reader, Microsoft states the preview pane requires minimal user action to arrive at the vulnerable EPS filter, so where B4 evidence includes any control that acts at the moment a user chooses to open something — an attachment warning, an enable-content prompt, awareness training — that control has no decision point to attach to on this CVE, and the only B4 measure that bites is the EPSIMP32.FLT access denial or the re-released MS15-099 package itself.

AU-Essential-8-App-Hardening.gap: User application hardening can be assessed at a high maturity level -- macros disabled, OLE restricted, browser hardening in place -- while this exploit path stays fully open, because it runs through the graphics import filter rather than any scripting or embedding feature. The hardening measures the assessor tests and the code the exploit reaches do not intersect.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.7.gap: Anti-malware and exploit-mitigation controls are documented and deployed, which is what the control asks. Their adequacy was measured publicly against this exploit and found wanting: the analysed sample bypassed EMET 5.5 outright, and the first public detection content for the associated implants is dated 2016-05-25, eight months after MS15-099, so the control's evidence describes protection the observed samples had already defeated.

new_control_requirements.name: INCOMPLETE-PATCH-SEQUENCE-SEVERITY-MULTIPLIER
new_control_requirements.description: Vulnerability-management programs must apply a severity multiplier when a CVE is the Nth in an incomplete-patch sequence on the same primitive (third MOTW bypass, second AMSI bypass, etc.). Framework controls treating each CVE as discrete obscure the structural defect; the Nth CVE in a sequence implies that future bypasses on the same primitive are likely.
new_control_requirements.evidence: MS15-099 is the documented case: published 2015-09-08 for the Office EPS filter flaw, then revised to V5.0 on 2015-11-10 stating that to comprehensively address CVE-2015-2545 Microsoft re-released the security updates for all affected Office software -- 3085620, 3085560, 3085572 and 3085635. An Office estate that installed the September packages carried a closed remediation record over a live vulnerability for two months, and EPSS still scores the CVE 0.80467 (99.591st percentile) on 2026-08-20.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Microsoft reported limited targeted attacks against Office 2007 SP3 through Office 2016 when MS15-099 shipped on 2015-09-08, and the verified-mitigation wording is what this CVE needs: the documented compensating control is the EPSIMP32.FLT deny-all ACL from KB3092845, and the patch state that counts is the 2015-11-10 re-release rather than the September build. CISA listed the CVE on 2022-03-03 with a 2022-03-24 due date.

attack_vector.description: A crafted Office document triggers an out-of-bounds write in Office's file parsing and the attacker runs code as the opening user. Observed delivery was RTF attachments carrying geopolitical lures, so the file that reaches the parser is a Word document even though the CVE is catalogued under PowerPoint.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none -- PR:N; the code runs with the rights of the account that opened the document
attack_vector.complexity: low -- AC:L with UI:R; the only precondition is that the recipient opens the attachment in an unpatched Office build
attack_vector.ai_factor: Nothing in MS15-070 or in ESET's indicator set attributes the discovery or the exploit development to automated or AI-assisted analysis.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Installing every MS15-070 package offered for the Office products present -- both the PowerPoint and the Word packages -- rather than the one matching the product named in the vulnerability record.
prevention.adequacy: Complete for this CVE and only for it: MS15-070 offers no workaround, so between the exploitation Microsoft records and the package install there is no partial state to occupy.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Hunting the ESET-published Sednit attachment indicators at the mail boundary and alerting on Office processes spawning children on workstations that received them.
detection.adequacy: The lure filenames are campaign-specific and disposable; the process-lineage rule is durable but fires on any Office document exploit, so it identifies a compromise class rather than this CVE.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating a hit as nation-state intrusion rather than commodity malware -- scoping to every recipient of the same lure, and checking for the Sednit persistence artefacts published alongside the exploit detection.
response.adequacy: Depends entirely on making the attribution early; handled as a single blocked attachment, the response closes at the mail gateway and never reaches the workstation that opened an earlier copy.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: Remediation is genuinely performed -- MS15-070 shipped on 2015-07-14 and enterprise patching cycles picked it up. It is inadequate because the control inherits the product scope of whatever record drives it: the KEV entry says PowerPoint, the vendor table says PowerPoint and Word across six separate packages, and an SI-2 record showing 2965283 and 3054963 installed reads as complete while 3054996, 3054973 and 3054990 are missing.

NIS2-Art21-incident-handling.gap: Incident-handling processes exist and are exercised, and would work if the entity knew what it was looking at. The gap is upstream of the process: Microsoft's bulletin says only that the CVE was exploited, with no actor, no lure and no artefact, and the material that makes an incident recognisable is published separately as a research indicator set. The procedure is adequate; its inputs are not.

UK-CAF-C1.gap: Security monitoring is in place in the sense C1 describes -- endpoint and mail telemetry collected and reviewed. It falls short here because the detection content is external and dated to a research publication rather than to the bulletin: the CVE was patched in July 2015 and the indicator set naming its use appeared later, so an estate monitoring correctly through that window had no signature, no lure list and no detection name to apply.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: An estate can hold a strong maturity rating for patching applications and still take this CVE at its normal cadence, because the assessment does not read the vendor's own exploited flag. MS15-070 marks five of its memory-corruption CVEs not exploited and this one exploited, and no part of the Essential Eight patch-applications measurement distinguishes them, so the item most likely to be used in the wild inherits the queue position of the ones that were not.

ISO-27001-2022-A.5.7.gap: Threat intelligence is documented, sourced and reviewed, which satisfies the control on paper. For this CVE the operative intelligence is a specific vendor's indicator repository entry -- a detection name, four RTF lures and a persistence registry key attributed to the Sednit group -- and an intelligence function scoped to advisories, feeds and bulletins does not touch it. The result is a threat-intelligence programme that can describe the vulnerability and not the campaign.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Microsoft marked CVE-2015-2424 exploited in MS15-070 on 2015-07-14 and CISA listed it on 2022-03-03 with a 2022-03-24 due date; EPSS on 2026-08-20 is 0.38497 (98.455th percentile). The verification clause is what matters on this Office estate: MS15-070 provides no workaround, and verified mitigation means every product-specific package -- 2965283, 3054996, 3054963, 3054973, 3054999, 3054990 -- present for the products installed, not a single suite-level record.

new_control_requirements.name: NATION-STATE-INITIAL-ACCESS-IR-ESCALATION
new_control_requirements.description: IR runbooks must include an explicit nation-state-initial-access escalation path triggered by APT28/APT29/Lazarus/Volt-Typhoon/etc. attribution on a confirmed exploit chain. Standard malware-infection IR under-escalates nation-state activity by treating it as commodity threat.
new_control_requirements.evidence: ESET's published indicator set places this CVE's exploitation in the Sednit group's email-attachment tooling, detected as Win32/Exploit.CVE-2015-2424.A and delivered with lures such as Exercise_Noble_Partner_16.rtf and Iran_nuclear_talks.rtf against policy and defence targets. A blocked RTF attachment handled as commodity malware closes at the mail gateway; the same indicator set lists the group's post-exploitation persistence and command-and-control artefacts, which is the scope an escalation path would actually search.

new_control_requirements.name: PRIMARY-SOURCE-INTAKE-VENDOR-BLOG-COVERAGE
new_control_requirements.description: Threat-intake pipelines must cover vendor security blogs (Microsoft / Sysdig / Trail of Bits / Project Zero) in addition to advisory feeds (Qualys / RHSA / USN / ZDI / kernel.org / oss-security / JFrog / CISA). Silent kernel patches with delayed-disclosure research publications fall through advisory-only feeds — vendor blogs are the canonical signal channel for that class.
new_control_requirements.evidence: For CVE-2015-2424 the advisory feeds carry one bit of operational content -- MS15-070's Exploited: Yes -- and nothing about who, how or what to hunt. The lure filenames, the detection name and the associated persistence key exist only in a security vendor's research indicator publication, which is precisely the channel this control requires an intake pipeline to cover.

CVE-2015-2387.name: Microsoft ATM Font Driver Privilege Escalation Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: Code already running on the host -- in the chain US-CERT describes, inside a sandboxed renderer reached by a Flash exploit -- feeds crafted font data to the kernel-mode Adobe Type Manager Font Driver, corrupts memory and executes in kernel mode. The result is the sandbox and integrity-level containment around the first-stage exploit ceasing to apply.
attack_vector.privileges_required: low -- PR:L; the attacker needs an existing execution context on the host, which the Flash flaws named in TA15-195A supply remotely
attack_vector.complexity: low -- AC:L; no race or leak is documented as a precondition, and compiled exploit binaries tested on Server 2003 SP2 and Windows 7 SP1 are publicly downloadable
attack_vector.ai_factor: No AI involvement is claimed: the bulletin records public disclosure without naming a finder, and the public exploit builds carry no such attribution.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Setting DisableATMFD to 1 on Windows 8 and later, or renaming atmfd.dll on earlier builds, followed by KB3077657 and a reboot.
prevention.adequacy: The workaround is genuinely preventive and genuinely costly -- Microsoft states embedded font rendering breaks -- and it is unavailable on Server 2003, where active file protection blocks the rename and only the update remains.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alerting when a sandboxed renderer or Office process is followed on the same host by SYSTEM-level execution that no service or scheduled task explains.
detection.adequacy: Weak against this specific flaw: the escalation happens inside the kernel with no file written and no service created, so the earliest reliable signal is the attacker's next action rather than the escalation itself.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating a host that rendered untrusted Flash or document content while unpatched as compromised at kernel level -- rebuild rather than clean -- and rotating credentials cached on it.
response.adequacy: Proportionate given kernel-mode code execution, and expensive enough that it needs the sandbox-bypass framing in TA15-195A to be authorised; without it the incident reads as a contained browser crash.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: Windows update management satisfies SI-2 and did deliver KB3077657 in the July 2015 cycle. The inadequacy is the gap between installed and effective: this is a kernel-mode driver, so the fixed atmfd.dll is not the loaded one until the host reboots, and on the Server Core installations the bulletin lists that reboot competes with availability windows. The control's evidence records approval and installation, neither of which is the moment exposure ends.

NIST-800-53-CM-7.gap: Least functionality is attested through hardened baselines that disable services and features, and the feature that mattered here is a font driver loaded by the graphics subsystem on every affected Windows version since NT 4.0. Microsoft had to publish a registry value and a takeown-and-rename procedure to disable it, which tells you it was not reachable through any normal configuration surface, and no baseline that predates the bulletin contains it.

NIS2-Art21-vulnerability-management.gap: Vulnerability management is in place and would have processed MS15-077 normally. It is inadequate because it treats this CVE as a discrete item in a driver that has produced repeat findings -- KB3077657 supersedes MS15-021's 3032323 in the same code -- so the natural process behaviour, applying the update and reverting the DisableATMFD mitigation to restore font rendering, removes the one control that would still have applied to the next finding in that driver.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: System security is documented, and the documentation depends on the containment this flaw removes. A CAF submission that accepts browser and document risk because renderers run sandboxed and Office opens untrusted files in Protected View is describing exactly the protections TA15-195A says this vulnerability bypasses, so the residual-risk statement behind B4 is invalidated by the CVE rather than merely stressed by it.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Patching operating systems is measurable and was measurable here, and the measurement starts at the wrong moment. MS15-077 shipped on 2015-07-14 recording both public disclosure and limited targeted attacks already in progress, so an estate hitting even an aggressive post-release timeframe still spent the whole pre-release window exposed to an exploit whose compiled builds now sit in public repositories.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.9.gap: Configuration management is documented and the DisableATMFD value or the atmfd.dll rename can be recorded in a baseline, which satisfies the control. It is inadequate because neither setting survives the operations that reinstate a vulnerable state -- an image restore, an in-place upgrade, a rebuild from media predating the change -- and A.8.9 evidence showing the baseline definition does not show per-host re-verification after those events.

new_control_requirements.name: BUG-FAMILY-MITIGATION-PERSISTENCE
new_control_requirements.description: When a CVE patch lands, retain the pre-patch compensating controls (module blacklists, sysctl restrictions) until the patched code has soaked for a stated review period. Patches for one bug in a primitive class can introduce sibling bugs in the same class; the original compensating control may still apply to the sibling.
new_control_requirements.evidence: ATMFD.DLL is the case this control describes. KB3077657, the fix for CVE-2015-2387, is recorded in MS15-077 as superseding 3032323 from MS15-021 -- an earlier bulletin in the same kernel-mode font driver -- and the compensating control for both is identical: the DisableATMFD registry value on Windows 8 and newer, or renaming atmfd.dll on earlier builds. An operator who reverted that setting on 2015-07-14 to restore embedded font rendering removed a control that costs nothing to keep and that applies to the whole class of findings in this driver, not just this CVE.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: MS15-077 shipped on 2015-07-14 already recording public disclosure and limited targeted attacks, and US-CERT issued TA15-195A the same day describing the Flash-to-kernel chain. The documented-compensating-controls clause is the operative one for this flaw, because the DisableATMFD registry value and the atmfd.dll rename are deployable in minutes while KB3077657 waits on a reboot window -- and on the Server Core installations the bulletin lists, that window is the constraint. CISA listed the CVE on 2022-03-03, due 2022-03-24.

attack_vector.description: Code running as an ordinary local user drives improper object handling in win32k.sys into a user-space callback, reads the EPROCESS structures of its own process and of the System process, and copies the System token into its own. The observed delivery of that first-stage code was a Flash exploit served from a link, not an interactive logon.
attack_vector.privileges_required: low -- PR:L; MS15-051 states the attacker must have valid logon credentials and be able to log on locally, and that the vulnerability could not be exploited remotely or by anonymous users
attack_vector.complexity: low -- AC:L; the constraint is obtaining the initial execution context, which in the documented campaign came from CVE-2015-3043 in Adobe Flash
attack_vector.ai_factor: Discovery came from analysts examining live campaign traffic and the public exploit from an independent researcher; no AI-assisted discovery or weaponization is claimed by any source read.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Installing KB3045171 and rebooting on Server 2003 SP2, Vista SP2, Server 2008 SP2 and Windows 7 SP1 -- and, where the GDI+ regression bit, installing KB3065979 alongside it instead of removing the security update.
prevention.adequacy: Complete for this CVE, with no fallback: MS15-051 lists no workaround, so a host that cannot reboot has no intermediate state, and the only other lever is denying the first-stage exploit its execution context.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alerting on a user-mode process acquiring a System token with no corresponding service creation, scheduled task or injection event.
detection.adequacy: Requires token-level telemetry; where an endpoint deployment collects process-creation and persistence events only, it sees nothing at the moment of escalation, because the same process simply continues running with a different token.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating a confirmed hit as nation-state initial access rather than commodity infection -- scoping to every host that rendered the same Flash content, and rotating credentials cached on any host where the escalation may have succeeded.
response.adequacy: Effective only if the chain is recognised as a chain; handled as an isolated browser crash or a single blocked payload, the response never reaches the kernel escalation that followed it.

NIST-800-53-AC-6.gap: Least privilege is implemented and auditable, and it is the wrong shape for this flaw. The exploit does not need any privilege the account model grants -- it takes the System token out of kernel memory and writes it into the token of the process it is already running in -- so an estate that can evidence no standing local-administrator rights has satisfied AC-6 in full while an ordinary user session remains one exploit away from System.

NIST-800-53-SI-4.gap: System monitoring is deployed and collecting, which is what the control asks. It is inadequate against the observable this exploit produces, because there is none of the usual kind: no binary is dropped by the escalation itself, no service or scheduled task is registered, and the elevated code continues inside the same user-mode process. Detection realistically begins at whatever the attacker does next, which is after the privilege boundary has already gone.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: Patch management is documented and operating, and it produced the exact failure mode this CVE rewards. KB3045171 broke applications creating text-outline-based path objects with GDI+ on Windows 7 and Server 2008 R2 and earlier, and Microsoft's own remedy was an additional update, KB3065979, published fifteen days later. A change-control process that responds to a broken line-of-business application by uninstalling the security update restores exposure without producing any record that says so.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: Secure configuration and maintenance is evidenced by a managed baseline, and the baseline's granularity is the problem. Affected and unaffected Windows versions sit next to each other here -- Server 2008 SP2 is affected, Server 2008 R2 is not; Windows 7 SP1 is affected, Windows 8 is not -- so estate-level patch-compliance figures conceal exactly the population that carries the risk, and B4 has no expectation that would surface it.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Patching operating systems is measured from the 2015-05-12 release, and by 2015-05-18 hfiref0x had published a working local exploit while Microsoft was already recording limited targeted attacks. A maturity rating earned by meeting the standard timeframe is therefore consistent with an estate that was exposed to a public kernel exploit for the whole of that window, and the control has no separate tier for a reboot-gated kernel fix under active exploitation.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: A functioning technical-vulnerability process is in place, fed by CVE data, and that feed is the defect here: NVD's description names Server 2003 SP2, Vista SP2 and Server 2008 SP2 and omits Windows 7 SP1, which MS15-051 rates affected and which the public exploit and the Metasploit module both target. Remediation scoped from the register therefore excludes the largest and most exploitable population, and the register looks complete.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: MS15-051 shipped KB3045171 on 2015-05-12 while Microsoft was aware of limited targeted attacks, a public exploit followed on 2015-05-18, and CISA listed the CVE on 2022-03-03 with a 2022-03-24 due date and a known-ransomware-use flag. Verification is the operative half on this Windows population: the fix replaces win32k.sys and is inert until reboot, and MS15-051 offers no workaround to occupy the interval, so mitigation counts as deployed only once each Server 2003 SP2, Vista SP2, Server 2008 SP2 and Windows 7 SP1 host has restarted.

new_control_requirements.name: NATION-STATE-INITIAL-ACCESS-IR-ESCALATION
new_control_requirements.description: IR runbooks must include an explicit nation-state-initial-access escalation path triggered by APT28/APT29/Lazarus/Volt-Typhoon/etc. attribution on a confirmed exploit chain. Standard malware-infection IR under-escalates nation-state activity by treating it as commodity threat.
new_control_requirements.evidence: FireEye's Operation RussianDoll analysis assesses APT28 as probably responsible for the 2015-04-13 activity that paired Adobe Flash CVE-2015-3043 with this win32k flaw against an international government entity, and the escalation left no service, task or dropped binary to alert on because the exploit copied the System token into the running process. An IR path that stops at the blocked Flash payload never looks for the kernel escalation that followed it, which is precisely the under-escalation this control names.

attack_vector.description: A crafted file opened in Office 2007 SP3, Office 2010 SP2 or Office 2013 SP1 corrupts memory during Office's file handling and yields code execution as the opening user. The vendor describes the class and nothing further; no public analysis identifies the file format, the parser or the primitive.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none -- PR:N; execution lands with the rights of whoever opened the file
attack_vector.complexity: low -- AC:L with UI:R; the only stated precondition is a user opening the file in an affected build, and no published analysis supports a stronger or weaker claim than that
attack_vector.ai_factor: No finder is named by Microsoft, the linked iDefense report is gone, and no source read attributes discovery or exploit development to automated or AI-assisted analysis.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Installing 2687409, 2965310 or 3039734 for the Office version present and relaunching the applications.
prevention.adequacy: It is the only control on offer -- MS15-081 publishes no workaround and no mitigating factor for this CVE, so an estate that defers the package has no partial position to hold.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Generic behavioural rules on Office processes -- child-process creation, executable writes, unexpected outbound connections -- applied to documents arriving from outside the organisation.
detection.adequacy: Unavoidably generic: with no public sample or campaign detail, there is nothing CVE-specific to write, and the rules that do exist fire identically for any Office document exploit.

response.what_would_have_worked: Scoping an investigation by which Office build the affected host was running and which external files it opened, since exposure is determined by version state rather than by any recognisable artefact.
response.adequacy: Slow and inconclusive: without an indicator to search for, an investigation can establish that a host was exploitable and cannot establish that it was exploited.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: Any organisation on a monthly Office patch cycle satisfies SI-2 and would have taken this fix in the August 2015 rollup. It stays inadequate because prioritisation inside that cycle runs on the evidence attached to the record, and this record is nearly empty -- no mechanism in NVD, a dead iDefense reference, no public exploit -- so a flaw the vendor marked as exploited presents as the least interesting item in its own bulletin.

NIST-800-53-SI-4.gap: Monitoring is deployed across endpoints and mail, and the control is met in the sense of collection and review. Its adequacy against this CVE cannot be demonstrated at all: no sample, hash, filename or network artefact has been published, so there is no way to test whether the deployed rules would have fired, and the coverage claim rests on generic Office behavioural detection that was written for other flaws entirely.

NIS2-Art21-vulnerability-management.gap: An entity can evidence a complete vulnerability-management cycle over MS15-081 and still have handled this CVE indistinguishably from the four non-exploited Office memory-corruption CVEs published beside it. The control asks for risk-based prioritisation without requiring the vendor's own exploitation flag to be an input, and CVSS 7.8 is what the process actually sees.

UK-CAF-C1.gap: Security monitoring is in place and reviewed, which is what the outcome describes. The gap is evidential rather than operational: for this CVE there is no published detection content in existence, so an organisation cannot show that its monitoring would have caught the activity Microsoft says occurred, and a C1 submission claiming coverage is asserting something that no available artefact can confirm or refute.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Patching applications is straightforwardly achievable here -- three packages, three Office versions, standard distribution -- and an estate can reach a high maturity level on this bulletin. The inadequacy is that the maturity level is earned by the calendar rather than by the risk: MS15-081's table marks this CVE exploited and its siblings not, and nothing in the patch-applications measurement reads that column.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: A technical-vulnerability register fed from NVD holds this CVE with a CWE, a score, three product lines and no mechanism. That is enough to schedule the update and not enough to answer the questions a risk owner asks around it -- whether a compensating control exists (MS15-081 says none), whether a specific document workflow is exposed, or whether the absence of a public exploit means anything given the vendor recorded exploitation before one existed.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Microsoft marked CVE-2015-1642 exploited in MS15-081 on 2015-08-11 for Office 2007 SP3, Office 2010 SP2 and Office 2013 SP1, and published no workaround, so the only mitigation this control can verify is the package: 2687409, 2965310 or 3039734, with the applications relaunched. CISA listed the CVE on 2022-03-03 with a 2022-03-24 due date and EPSS on 2026-08-20 is 0.53213 (98.896th percentile), which is the risk signal an estate has in place of the missing technical detail.

new_control_requirements.name: MITIGATION-ACTIVE-PATCH-PENDING-VERDICT-CLASS
new_control_requirements.description: Compliance verdicts must distinguish three states: (a) binary patch deployed (vulnerability eliminated), (b) vendor-mitigation rule active, no binary patch (residual risk: any defect in the mitigation rule reopens the vulnerability), (c) no mitigation, no patch (full exposure). Audit reports must surface (b) as a distinct compensating-control state with an associated time-bound action item, not as a 'patched per SLA' outcome.
new_control_requirements.evidence: MS15-081 lists no mitigating factors and no workarounds for CVE-2015-1642, which removes state (b) from this entry entirely: an Office 2007 SP3, 2010 SP2 or 2013 SP1 installation is either carrying 2687409, 2965310 or 3039734, or it is in full exposure to a flaw the vendor marked as exploited. That makes any audit line reading 'mitigated' or 'compensating controls in place' for this CVE false by construction, and the control's three-state discipline is what surfaces it.

CVE-2014-4114.name: Microsoft Windows Object Linking & Embedding (OLE) Remote Code Execution Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: An OLE object in an Office document points at a remote share; Object Packager downloads the referenced files into a temporary folder and, on a presentation command that selects the verb handler, hands the .INF to infDefaultInstall.exe, which installs it and runs the payload fetched alongside it as a fake image. Delivered as a PowerPoint Show file, the installation raises no User Account Control prompt.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none -- PR:N; the code runs as the user who opened the document, and Microsoft's mitigating factor is that accounts with fewer rights are less affected
attack_vector.complexity: low -- AC:L with UI:R; the attacker needs a reachable SMB or WebDAV share for the two staged files, which is also where the practical defence sits
attack_vector.ai_factor: Found through incident investigation by iSIGHT Partners and ESET researchers, both credited in MS14-060; no automated or AI-assisted discovery is claimed.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Installing KB3000869 and MS14-064 together, and until then disabling the WebClient service, blocking TCP 139 and 445 outbound at the perimeter, and deleting the inffile Install command verb.
prevention.adequacy: Each workaround is real and each removes functionality operators may be using -- WebDAV, CIFS and printer sharing, and INF-driven installers -- and KB3000869 alone is incomplete because CVE-2014-6352 bypassed it weeks later.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alerting on outbound SMB or WebDAV from a user workstation to an external host, and on infDefaultInstall.exe running with an INF path in a temporary folder.
detection.adequacy: Unusually strong for a document exploit, because the retrieval step crosses the network boundary and the execution step uses a named system binary -- but both fire only after the document has already been opened.

response.what_would_have_worked: Scoping a hit to every recipient of the same document and to every host that contacted the staging share, then treating those hosts as compromised at user level rather than cleaned.
response.adequacy: Workable because the staging share is a hard network artefact that appears in proxy and firewall logs, and limited by retention: the Sandworm activity NVD dates to June through October 2014 predates the bulletin by months.

NIST-800-53-SC-7.gap: Boundary protection is implemented wherever it is audited, and the direction of enforcement decides this case. Inbound filtering was never the question for this CVE: the exploit needs the workstation to reach out to an attacker's SMB or WebDAV share, which is why Microsoft's own workaround blocks TCP 139 and 445 in both directions. An SC-7 control set that documents perimeter firewalls and inbound rules can be fully compliant while permitting exactly the outbound session the exploit depends on.

NIST-800-53-CM-7.gap: Least functionality is met by disabling unnecessary services and features, and nothing in a normal baseline reaches the artefact that matters -- the Install verb registered for .INF files, which is what turns a downloaded configuration file into an executed installer through infDefaultInstall.exe. Microsoft had to publish registry-editing instructions to remove it, and any host rebuilt from an image predating that change silently regains the handler.

NIS2-Art21-network-security.gap: Network security measures are in place and would be evidenced by segmentation, firewalling and monitoring. They are inadequate here because the exploit's network step looks like ordinary file access: an outbound SMB or WebDAV connection carrying a small file. Stopping it means prohibiting a protocol the entity uses legitimately, which is a policy decision rather than a configuration one — and where an Article 21 evidence pack does not carry that decision, nothing in it stands between the crafted OLE object and the remote share it fetches the payload from.

NIS2-Art21-vulnerability-handling.gap: Handling procedures ran correctly over MS14-060 in October 2014 and produced a state that lasted weeks. CVE-2014-6352 defeated that fix, public exploits for the bypass reached Exploit-DB by mid-November 2014, and MS14-064 was needed on top -- so the entity's own records show a closed vulnerability while the primitive stayed reachable, and nothing in the procedure reopens an item when a different CVE identifier reports that its patch was bypassed.

UK-CAF-D1.gap: Response and recovery planning exists and is exercised, and its default classification is the failure. The reporting parties for this flaw were incident-response firms describing an intrusion set that had been active from June 2014, so the correct response to one blocked attachment is a retrospective hunt across every recipient and every host that touched the staging share. A plan whose malicious-attachment path terminates at the mail gateway satisfies D1 and finds none of that.

AU-Essential-8-App-Hardening.gap: User application hardening can be assessed at a high maturity level against macro and OLE-control settings while the control that Microsoft actually names as mitigating -- files from untrusted locations opening in Protected View -- depends on the untrusted-origin marking surviving the delivery path. Files arriving through an unmarked file share or extracted from a container reach the OLE handler without it, and no part of the hardening assessment tests that the marking is still attached.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.22.gap: Segregation of networks is documented, and where that documentation describes internal zoning between user, server and management networks it answers a different question than this exploit asks. The path this exploit takes leaves the estate entirely -- workstation to an external SMB or WebDAV share -- so an architecture that satisfies A.8.22 through east-west separation gives no answer at all to the north-south question, and the retrieval of the .INF and the disguised payload crosses a boundary the segregation design does not model.

new_control_requirements.name: INCOMPLETE-PATCH-SEQUENCE-SEVERITY-MULTIPLIER
new_control_requirements.description: Vulnerability-management programs must apply a severity multiplier when a CVE is the Nth in an incomplete-patch sequence on the same primitive (third MOTW bypass, second AMSI bypass, etc.). Framework controls treating each CVE as discrete obscure the structural defect; the Nth CVE in a sequence implies that future bypasses on the same primitive are likely.
new_control_requirements.evidence: The Windows OLE packager primitive produced exactly the sequence this control describes: MS14-060 shipped KB3000869 on 2014-10-14 for CVE-2014-4114, CVE-2014-6352 bypassed that fix, six Exploit-DB entries cite the bypass with three of them dated 12 to 14 November 2014, and MS14-064 was required to close it. A programme treating the two identifiers as unrelated items records the October patch as complete remediation of a primitive that was demonstrably still reachable in November.

new_control_requirements.name: NATION-STATE-INITIAL-ACCESS-IR-ESCALATION
new_control_requirements.description: IR runbooks must include an explicit nation-state-initial-access escalation path triggered by APT28/APT29/Lazarus/Volt-Typhoon/etc. attribution on a confirmed exploit chain. Standard malware-infection IR under-escalates nation-state activity by treating it as commodity threat.
new_control_requirements.evidence: NVD records this flaw as exploited in the wild in a Sandworm attack running June through October 2014, and MS14-060's acknowledgments credit iSIGHT Partners and ESET researchers -- the flaw surfaced from intrusion investigation, not from a bug report. The escalation path is what converts a single blocked PowerPoint attachment into the right question: which other recipients opened an earlier copy, and which hosts contacted the attacker's SMB or WebDAV staging share during the four months before KB3000869 existed.

CVE-2014-0496.name: Adobe Reader and Acrobat Use-After-Free Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: A crafted PDF, opened in an affected Reader or Acrobat build, drives the renderer into following a pointer to memory it has already freed. Attacker-controlled content occupies the reclaimed allocation, so the stale pointer resolves into data the attacker chose and execution lands at the privilege of the process rendering the document. The record classifies the flaw as CWE-416 without naming the object involved.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; the attacker supplies a document and holds no account on the target. UI:R makes the user's act of opening or previewing it the only gate.
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; no race, no information leak and no prior foothold are required to reach the freed allocation. The real constraint is arranging a heap layout from inside the document, which is exploit engineering rather than access.
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Adobe assigned the CVE and made it public on 2014-01-14, and APSB14-01's acknowledgements credit Soroush Dalili (@irsdl) — an outside researcher. No automated or AI-assisted discovery is claimed, and no research arm, AI-branded or otherwise, appears in the bulletin, the MITRE record or the NVD record.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Reaching Adobe's 10.1.9 or 11.0.06 build on every Reader and Acrobat install and relaunching the applications, plus handing web-delivered PDFs to the browser's own renderer instead of the Adobe plugin so that a page visit is not a delivery route.
prevention.adequacy: The build change closes this CVE and leaves the host on a line Adobe stopped supporting on 2015-11-15 (10.x) or 2017-10-15 (11.x), so it buys remediation without maintenance. The delivery-route change removes web-served documents as a path but not the opened attachment that the vector's UI:R describes. Neither reaches a copy the inventory does not list.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alerting on AcroRd32.exe or Acrobat.exe spawning a child process or writing an executable, and on clustered renderer crashes traced back to a single document source.
detection.adequacy: Both are post-exploitation signals — the child process is the payload, not the use-after-free. The crash signal only appears where the attacker's heap layout failed, so a reliable exploit produces neither.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating any host that opened a suspect document while below the fixed build as executed-on rather than merely exposed: retain the document, review process creation around the open, and rebuild instead of closing the ticket on the update.
response.adequacy: Bounded by evidence retention. The interval between the 2014-01-14 fix and the 2022-03-03 KEV listing is longer than the log retention that would let an operator answer the question for the period when the exposure was live.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: An SI-2 attestation can be produced honestly for an estate still running Adobe Reader 11.0.5, because the control asks whether identified flaws are remediated on the organisation's timeline and identification is fed by vendor bulletins that stopped naming this CVE after 2014-01-14. The gap is the interval to the 2022-03-03 KEV listing: SI-2 has no mechanism for re-opening a flaw already closed when fresh exploitation evidence appears against the same version range.

NIST-800-53-CM-7.gap: CM-7 is met wherever the desktop build is documented and enforced, and it stays met with the affected renderer installed, because a PDF reader is a business-required application rather than an unnecessary service. What the control cannot express is that one renderer is reachable two ways — an opened attachment and a PDF a web page serves into the plugin — so removing the second halves the delivery surface without changing the CM-7 verdict in either direction.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: An operator inside NIS2 scope can hold a documented and audited patch-management process and still carry this exposure, because the process is measured against vendor releases and Adobe's release for this CVE is 2014-01-14. No Article 21 trigger is tied to a US catalogue, so the KEV listing that is the sole exploitation evidence produces no European deadline; the 2022-03-24 due date binds federal agencies under BOD 22-01 and nobody else.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: Where B4 evidence for a managed desktop is a build standard and its enforcement record, both are machine-level artefacts. This CVE is fixed at 10.1.9 on one Adobe track and 11.0.06 on another, so 'the build is compliant' is not a statement about either track unless the standard names the product and the stream. An assessor reading a conformant image is given no prompt to ask about a second Adobe product on the same host, nor about the fact that both tracks left Adobe support on 2015-11-15 and 2017-10-15 and cannot be maintained further.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: The mitigation can be assessed at maturity while this CVE stays live, and both routes turn on scope rather than patching discipline. An asset register that no longer lists Reader or Acrobat 10.x/11.x removes them from assessment without removing them from disk, and the timing runs from the vendor release of 2014-01-14 rather than from the 2022-03-03 listing or the EPSS 0.40243 score recorded 2026-08-20.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: A.8.8 conformity is demonstrated with a vulnerability-information source, an evaluation record and a remediation decision, all of which can be complete here and all of which run off the inventory. Two products share one renderer and one CVE across two version tracks — 10.1.9 fixes the 10.x track and 11.0.06 the 11.x track, and both Adobe Reader and Adobe Acrobat exist on both tracks — so an inventory line that does not separate the two products yields an evaluation that is right about one of them and has never looked at the other. The CVE record gives no push toward that split: its description names Reader and Acrobat together while NVD's configuration carries only cpe:2.3:a:adobe:acrobat.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Adobe shipped 10.1.9 and 11.0.06 for Reader and Acrobat on 2014-01-14; CISA listed CVE-2014-0496 on 2022-03-03 with a 2022-03-24 due date. Patch availability and KEV listing are eight years apart on this CVE, which is exactly the case the control's 'whichever is later' clause exists for — the trigger that matters is the listing, not the release an estate may have closed out in 2014. EPSS still reads 0.40243 at percentile 0.98523 on 2026-08-20, so the deployment this control forces is against a live rather than a historical exposure, and on a desktop renderer 'deployed' has to mean the application was relaunched onto the new build.

CVE-2013-5065.name: Microsoft Windows Kernel Privilege Escalation Vulnerability (CVE-2013-5065)

attack_vector.description: A user who can log on to the machine maps the NULL page, writes a token-stealing stub into it and sends the NDProxy driver a device control request whose buffer carries an index the driver never validates. The unvalidated index resolves into the page the attacker just wrote, and the driver calls into it in kernel mode. The process the attacker started with then holds SYSTEM.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N in the CVSS record, but Microsoft's own precondition is that the attacker holds valid logon credentials and can log on locally; the flaw is not reachable remotely or anonymously.
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L; the NULL page is mappable on these platforms, so the attacker places the target of the bad fetch rather than racing for it. The real constraints are reachability and build: the Routing and Remote Access service must be running for the device to open, and the escalation stub is written per operating-system build.
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Microsoft credits FireEye, Inc. in MS14-002's acknowledgements — a security firm working from in-the-wild attack samples, which is human incident analysis, not automated discovery.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Installing KB2914368 and taking the mandatory restart; before that shipped, applying Microsoft's ndproxy-to-null.sys reroute on hosts that do not need Remote Access Service, dial-up networking or VPN.
prevention.adequacy: The update is complete for this CVE but leaves the host on a platform whose bulletin directs out-of-lifecycle customers to migrate. The workaround is narrower than it looks: Microsoft verifies it only for environments with non-default, limited user privileges, it removes Telephony-dependent services outright, and it must be reversed before the update installs.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alerting on a NULL-page allocation followed by a device control request to NDProxy from a non-administrative process, and on any process whose token changes to SYSTEM outside a service start.
detection.adequacy: Both need kernel-level process and syscall telemetry from Windows XP and Server 2003 hosts, already being collected before the escalation runs. Neither signal fires until the exploit has already run; the escalation itself is a single device control call with no crash, no dropped file and no service change to match.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating a host where this ran as fully compromised rather than as a patched machine: every credential that authenticated to it during the exposure window rotated, and the host rebuilt rather than updated in place, since SYSTEM code execution predates any evidence the update leaves behind.
response.adequacy: Rotation scope is only knowable where interactive logon records were retained, and the exploit needs an account that logs on legitimately, so the authentication record it produces is indistinguishable from ordinary use.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: SI-2 was satisfiable throughout the period this flaw was most dangerous, because between Advisory 2914486 and MS14-002 on 2014-01-14 there was no vendor flaw remedy to be delinquent on, while Exploit-DB 30014 had been public since 2013-12-03. After the fix the control tracks installation, and installation is not the remediation event here — MS14-002 makes the restart mandatory, so an SI-2 dashboard reading 100 per cent installed can still describe a fleet running the old driver.

NIST-800-53-CM-7.gap: A CM-7 baseline can hold the null.sys reroute as a hardening item and pass its own audit while quietly disabling Remote Access Service, dial-up networking and VPN on every host — Microsoft names all three as casualties. The control has no concept of a setting that is correct only until a patch arrives, and MS14-002 requires this one be reversed before KB2914368 installs, so CM-7 conformance and correct remediation actively pull apart.

NIST-800-53-AC-6.gap: An estate can evidence least privilege completely and remain fully exploitable, because the attacker here is an ordinary authorised user and the flaw is the privilege boundary inside the driver failing. AC-6 is not irrelevant, though: Microsoft scopes the verified effectiveness of its workaround to environments with non-default, limited user privileges, so AC-6 posture determines whether the interim control works while doing nothing about the defect.

NIS2-Art21-vulnerability-handling.gap: Article 21 is met by an entity that receives vendor disclosures and acts on them, and this vulnerability was disclosed in two acts with different remedies — a workaround in Advisory 2914486, then KB2914368 in MS14-002. An entity that closed the item on the first act is compliant on paper and, if the reroute was later reversed for the sake of VPN, exposed again with no obligation to reopen anything.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: B4 can be evidenced for a Windows XP or Server 2003 host with KB2914368 applied, because the patch exists and was taken. What the assessment does not reach is that this is a terminal platform: MS14-002's own guidance to customers on out-of-lifecycle releases is to migrate, so the maintenance B4 asks about cannot continue past this bulletin regardless of how diligently the estate applies what is available.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Maturity in the operating-system patching mitigation is measured against patches the vendor makes available, so a host carrying KB2914368 is assessed as current no matter how long its platform has been out of supply. The mitigation asks whether patches are applied and never whether the platform still receives them, which for Windows XP and Server 2003 is the only question left after MS14-002.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: Where an A.8.8 record holds one evaluation and one measure per vulnerability, the correct answer changed underneath it: the reroute was right until 2014-01-14 and wrong immediately afterwards, because MS14-002 requires it be undone before the update installs. A register with one row per vulnerability cannot carry that inversion, so the residual state — patched host, Telephony services still disabled — has nowhere to surface as an open item.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Microsoft shipped KB2914368 for Windows XP and Server 2003 on 2014-01-14 in MS14-002 while stating it was aware of limited, targeted attacks, and Exploit-DB 30014 had been public since 2013-12-03 — the exploit preceded the patch. CISA listed the CVE on 2022-03-03 with a 2022-03-24 due date. The control's value on this entry is its explicit acceptance of documented compensating controls, which is what an operator had during the Advisory 2914486 window, and its insistence on verified mitigation: MS14-002 makes a restart mandatory, so verification here means the host booted onto the new driver, not that the installer exited zero.

new_control_requirements.name: MITIGATION-ACTIVE-PATCH-PENDING-VERDICT-CLASS
new_control_requirements.description: Compliance verdicts must distinguish three states: (a) binary patch deployed (vulnerability eliminated), (b) vendor-mitigation rule active, no binary patch (residual risk: any defect in the mitigation rule reopens the vulnerability), (c) no mitigation, no patch (full exposure). Audit reports must surface (b) as a distinct compensating-control state with an associated time-bound action item, not as a 'patched per SLA' outcome.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Windows XP and Server 2003 hosts spent this CVE's exposure window in exactly the control's state (b): Microsoft Security Advisory 2914486 published the ndproxy-to-null.sys reroute with no binary patch, and KB2914368 followed in MS14-002 on 2014-01-14. A host in that state had lost Remote Access Service, dial-up networking and virtual private networking, and Microsoft scopes the reroute's verified effectiveness to environments with non-default, limited user privileges — so it is a compensating control with a stated defect condition, not a fix. MS14-002 then requires the reroute be undone before the update installs, which is the time-bound action item this control demands be attached to state (b) rather than folded into a patched verdict.

CVE-2026-73570.name: Zimbra Collaboration Suite (ZCS) OS Command Injection Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: An unauthenticated attacker gets a value carrying shell metacharacters into the field Zimbra uses as an SNMP notification target. The trap-sending code interpolates that value into a shell command without neutralising it, and the swatchdog service runs the result as the zimbra user — the account that owns the mail store and the server's Jetty web roots. CERT Polska's hunt strings show the injected text landing in /var/log/zimbra.log where a service name should be. The route by which the value arrives is not settled: the CNA describes specially crafted SMTP requests, CERT Polska names no delivery method, and the one public script drives the parameter over HTTP without establishing that it works — so hunt on the injected value and the artefacts it leaves, not on a request shape.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N and UI:N; no account, no session and no victim action are involved. What stands in for a credential is configuration: the optional zimbra-snmp package installed and SNMP notifications enabled.
attack_vector.complexity: high — AC:H, and the complexity is entirely the configuration precondition rather than the exploitation. Where zimbra-snmp is installed, snmp_notify is set and swatchdog is running, the path is deterministic and needs no race, leak or memory grooming.
attack_vector.ai_factor: None recorded. The vendor advisory lists the fix without a finder and shows CVSS and Zimbra rating as TBD; CERT Polska names no researcher and no threat actor.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Taking Zimbra 10.1.20 after its 2026-07-20 release and confirming the Zimbra services cycled onto it; failing that, removing the optional zimbra-snmp package or disabling SNMP notifications, which removes the precondition the injection needs.
prevention.adequacy: The upgrade is complete for this CVE and closes nothing that was already done through it. Disabling notifications is a genuine removal of the path rather than a filter, but it costs the SNMP monitoring the package was installed for, and it can only be applied where the package inventory shows the package is present.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Reading /var/log/zimbra.log for service-status lines whose service-name field contains shell metacharacters, and running a file-creation sweep for content written by the zimbra user under the Jetty web roots and /tmp/ during the exposure window.
detection.adequacy: Both work and both depend on the log surviving. The injected text is written into an ordinary informational log line, so it is invisible to alerting keyed on errors or on authentication events, and a retention window shorter than the interval from the 2026-07-20 release to the 2026-08-21 listing cannot answer the question at all.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating an exposed server as executed-on: inventory and remove attacker-written content under /opt/zimbra/jetty/webapps/, /opt/zimbra/jetty_base/webapps/ and /tmp/, rebuild from a known-good baseline rather than upgrading in place, and rotate credentials and tokens the zimbra account could read.
response.adequacy: CISA's required action points at its Forensics Triage Requirements alongside the patch, which is the right sequence, but the triage is only conclusive where filesystem timestamps and logs predating the campaign survive. On a mail store, rebuilding also means separating the mailbox data from everything else on the host, which is the step that makes this expensive rather than difficult.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: An SI-2 programme could report this CVE as in-hand on 2026-08-21 and be telling the truth, because Zimbra released 10.1.20 on 2026-07-20 and a standard high-severity window had not expired. The control's weakness on this entry is what it does with the exploitation evidence: neither CERT Polska's 2026-08-17 campaign report nor the KEV listing four days later restarts an SI-2 clock, and the EPSS value of 0.00539 available that day pointed the other way.

NIST-800-53-CM-7.gap: Least functionality is satisfied by a justified software list, and zimbra-snmp is justified wherever anyone wanted SNMP monitoring of the mail platform. The control therefore records the package as intended rather than as the switch that decides whether an unauthenticated command-injection path exists, and it has no visibility of snmp_notify at all, which is configuration rather than an installed component and is the second half of the precondition.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: The obligation is met by an entity running a documented patch process against vendor releases, and Zimbra's release was available from 2026-07-20. Article 21 gives that entity nothing that distinguishes 10.1.20 from the other patch releases in its queue, even though one of its nine fixes was under active exploitation by 2026-08-17 — the escalation signal exists outside the framework, in a national CERT bulletin the process has no obligation to consume.

NIS2-Art21-incident-handling.gap: An entity can hold a complete, exercised incident-handling procedure and never invoke it here, because nothing raises an incident: the injection writes an ordinary-looking status line into /var/log/zimbra.log and the follow-on artefacts are files under the server's own web roots owned by the account that legitimately owns them. The procedure is adequate once triggered and there is no trigger, which is a detection dependency Article 21 does not name.

UK-CAF-D1.gap: Where D1 planning for a mail platform covers outage and data recovery, this incident is neither. The recovery decision is whether the host can be trusted after code ran as the zimbra user, and the plan needs to say in advance that upgrading to 10.1.20 is not that decision — the upgrade removes the injection path and leaves any file written through it in place and still served.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: The mitigation is assessed against elapsed time from vendor release, and the release predates the exploitation evidence by a month: 10.1.20 on 2026-07-20, CERT Polska's campaign report on 2026-08-17, the KEV listing on 2026-08-21. An organisation can therefore be assessed as meeting this mitigation for the whole period the campaign was running, and the assessment is not reopened by the campaign becoming public.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: Conformity is demonstrated with an evaluation of exposure, and a product-level evaluation of 'ZCS below 10.1.20' is the wrong granularity for a flaw whose reachability is decided per server by two switches. The record cannot say which instances are exploitable today, so it cannot order the upgrade queue by exposure and cannot identify the servers where disabling snmp_notify would have removed the path the same afternoon.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Zimbra published 10.1.20 on 2026-07-20; CERT Polska reported an ongoing campaign against this flaw on 2026-08-17; CISA listed CVE-2026-73570 on 2026-08-21 with a 2026-08-24 due date. Any SLA measured from vendor availability had a month to run before the KEV clock even started, and EPSS still read 0.00539 at percentile 0.43183 on the listing date, so a queue ordered by score would have deprioritised a Zimbra mail server under confirmed exploitation. This control fires on the listing rather than the score, and on this product 'verified' has to mean the Zimbra services cycled onto 10.1.20 — or, as a documented compensating control, that snmp_notify is off.

new_control_requirements.name: PERIMETER-COMPROMISE-REBUILD-NOT-PATCH
new_control_requirements.description: Pre-rehearsed IR runbook for any perimeter device that suffers a pre-auth RCE CVE in active exploitation MUST default to config-exfil + rebuild + credential rotation, not patch-in-place. Patch-in-place leaves attacker-installed implants intact.
new_control_requirements.evidence: This is an internet-reachable Zimbra Collaboration server taking pre-authentication command execution as the zimbra user while a campaign was running, and CERT Polska's hunt guidance is precisely the implant case the control describes: files written by the zimbra user in the last 30 days under /opt/zimbra/jetty/webapps/, /opt/zimbra/jetty_base/webapps/ and /tmp/, inside the application's own web roots. Upgrading to 10.1.20 replaces the SNMP notification path and deletes none of that content, which is still served by the same host under the account that owns the mail store. CISA's required action for this CVE points stakeholders at its Forensics Triage Requirements alongside the patch, drawing the same distinction the control does.

CVE-2023-49105.name: ownCloud WebDAV Pre-Signed URL Authentication Bypass

attack_vector.description: An unauthenticated attacker who knows a username constructs a WebDAV request to /remote.php/dav/files/<username>/<path> with forged pre-signed URL parameters. Because the verification path accepts a signature when the file owner has no signing key configured - ownCloud's stated default - the server serves the request as that user, granting read, write and delete over their files.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none (unauthenticated network request; only a valid username is needed)
attack_vector.complexity: low - a single request whose signature is computable offline from the URL with an empty salt
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered. The advisory is ownCloud's own and credits no AI tooling; the exploitation tooling Hunt.io recovered was hand-written Python.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Upgrade owncloud/core to 10.13.3 as ownCloud's remediation post directs, or take the targeted patch from ownCloud support; as an interim, configure a signing key for every account so no owner sits in the keyless state the check mishandles.
prevention.adequacy: Insufficient on its own after the fact - the flaw grants read, so anything the instance held before the upgrade must be treated as taken and any credential or key material stored in it rotated.
