ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: Management of technical vulnerabilities requires that vulnerability information be obtained and acted on. Acting on it means moving from 1.27.0 to 1.27.1, and until that lands A.8.8 offers no interim measure for this flaw: the advisory names no supported workaround, and the only levers - removing the diffpatch route or reducing who holds repository write - are availability and access-model changes an A.8.8 process is not scoped to authorise.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: 4h KEV-listing mitigation SLA applies.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CISA allowed three days between the 2026-08-25 KEV listing and the 2026-08-28 due date for a CVSS 9.8 flaw whose fix had been available since 2026-07-27 and whose first public exploit repository appeared 2026-07-29. EPSS on 2026-08-28 was 0.84554 at the 99.692nd percentile. The action a four-hour clock can actually deliver here is not the version upgrade but the access-model change: disable open registration and re-scope repository write, then schedule 1.27.1. A clock anchored on the KEV listing also binds on whatever product CISA named, which is how a self-hosted application reaches a patch programme scoped to operating systems.

new_control_requirements.name: CONTROL-PANEL-PLUGIN-USER-SURFACE-MUST-NOT-REACH-ROOT-OPERATIONS
new_control_requirements.description: On a multi-tenant hosting control panel (cPanel/WHM and similar), no function reachable from the unprivileged user-end plugin surface may execute as root or run tenant-supplied scripts with host privileges. Privileged operations must live behind an administrative trust boundary with their own authorization, and the user-facing surface must only request them through a constrained, validated interface. The distinguishing test: from an ordinary tenant account on a staging panel, invoke each user-end plugin function (including enable/disable and configuration calls) with a payload that attempts a root-level action, and confirm the action is refused before any privileged code runs - a panel that passes an OS-hardening audit but wires a tenant-callable function to a root operation still grants user-to-root escalation.
new_control_requirements.evidence: This control is written for cPanel/WHM-class panels and is the closest existing entry to the defect here; the class is identical. A registered Gitea user - an unprivileged tenant of the instance - reaches diffpatch, and the patch content that user supplies becomes an executable file under $GIT_DIR that Git runs as the Gitea service account, which owns every tenant's repositories and the instance's own secrets. The operational test is not a version check: submit a patch that creates a path under hooks/ against a scratch repository and confirm the endpoint refuses it.

new_control_requirements.name: AI-ML-DEVELOPER-TOOLING-INVENTORY
new_control_requirements.description: Organizations using AI/ML systems must maintain a separate inventory of developer-tooling control planes (notebook servers, experiment trackers, model registries, vector-DB admin UIs, agent frameworks) with: exposed network endpoints (HTTP, WebSocket, gRPC), authentication mechanism per endpoint, blast-radius mapping (which model artifacts/training data/production deployments are reachable from each tool), and patch SLA tier separate from generic application patching.
new_control_requirements.evidence: The control's existing wording enumerates AI/ML developer tooling; it is the closest existing entry and the class it names - developer-tooling control planes held outside the main asset register - is exactly what a self-hosted Gitea is. Execution as the service account reaches every hosted repository plus the database credentials and OAuth tokens the advisory names, so this host belongs in the same inventory tier as a model registry rather than in the general application estate. For this product the inventory must additionally record whether open registration is on, since that is what turns a write-access precondition into an unauthenticated one.

CVE-2026-21962.name: Oracle HTTP Server and WebLogic Proxy Plug-in Access-Control Bypass (CVE-2026-21962)

attack_vector.description: An unauthenticated attacker sends one HTTP request to an Oracle HTTP Server, Apache or IIS front end that loads the WebLogic Server Proxy Plug-in. The front end applies its <Location> access-control rules to the raw path, which it does not collapse; WebLogic normalizes `..;` (a servlet path parameter followed by a parent reference) and serves the resolved path. A request such as `GET /foo/..;/internal-admin/cont/.env` is therefore authorised against the permissive prefix and answered from the protected one. Public reproduction against Oracle HTTP Server 12.2.1.4.0 and 14.1.2.0.0 fronting WebLogic Server 12.2.1.4 leaks the protected file while the canonical request to the same path returns 404.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none - unauthenticated network access to the front-end proxy port over HTTP; Oracle's risk matrix answers 'Remote Exploit without Auth.?' with Yes
attack_vector.complexity: low - a single crafted request-target, no user interaction, and the proxied prefix is auto-detectable rather than secret; CISA's SSVC record sets automatable to yes
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered and not AI-weaponised. The working exploit is manual lab reproduction with captured evidence; the only AI-adjacent element is a public hypothesis that some of the non-working 'PoC' repositories which appeared within 48 hours of disclosure were machine-generated.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Apply the January 2026 Critical Patch Update to Oracle HTTP Server and to every host carrying the WebLogic Server Proxy Plug-in, and independently duplicate each front-end path restriction on the WebLogic side so that no backend path depends on a proxy-layer rule alone.
prevention.framework_requiring_it: CISA BOD 26-04 via the KEV listing (added 2026-08-24, due 2026-08-27)
prevention.adequacy: The CPU closes the defect. The duplication of restrictions is the half that keeps working: this class of bug is a disagreement between two parsers, and the next disagreement will use an encoding nobody has enumerated yet.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alert on raw request-targets carrying `;` adjacent to `..` at the proxy tier, and reconcile front-end against backend access logs for the same request - a proxy log showing `/foo/..;/x` where the backend log shows `/x` is the bypass itself.
detection.adequacy: Reliable for the reproduced encodings and for the log-divergence signature, which is mechanism-level rather than string-level and therefore survives new encodings. It depends on backend access logs being collected at all, which on a proxied deployment is often the log nobody ships.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treat every backend path reachable behind an affected proxy prefix as read by an unauthenticated party: rotate credentials held in files the backend serves, and review backend access logs for normalized paths that the front-end policy should have refused.
response.adequacy: Bounded by log retention on the backend rather than the proxy, and by whether anyone recorded which paths the <Location> rules were protecting. Where the leaked material is a configuration or credential file, the response is a rotation exercise whose scope is the backend's own filesystem.

NIST-800-53-AC-3.gap: Access enforcement worked, twice, on two different readings of the same path. The front end matched `/foo/..;/internal-admin/cont/.env` against its permissive `/foo` rule and enforced that rule correctly; WebLogic normalized the path and served what it was asked for, also correctly. AC-3 requires approved authorisations to be enforced; it does not require the component that makes the access decision and the component that serves the resource to agree on how a path is canonicalized first. An AC-3 assessment that tests the protective rule with the canonical path is actively misleading here, because that request returns 404 on a fully vulnerable deployment - the reproduction relies on exactly that pair to prove the bypass.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: Article 21 measures the patch obligation against availability of the fix. Oracle released the fix on 2026-01-16 inside a quarterly Critical Patch Update, so an operator who applied that CPU inside its normal window is compliant and remediated, and the seven months between the CPU and CISA's 2026-08-24 listing are compliant time for everyone else. Nothing in the control shortens a window because a coordinator's exploitation assessment changed - and CISA's own SSVC record read exploitation 'active' from 2026-01-21, the day after publication. Oracle publishes no out-of-band unit for this CVE, so the control's only lever is the quarterly it already accommodates.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: The system-security outcome expects vulnerable software to be identified and updated, and identification is where this breaks. The vulnerable artefact is a plug-in binary on a web server - mod_wl_ohs.so or iisproxy.dll - not the WebLogic installation an asset register is most likely to hold; CISA's own product string for this entry, 'HTTP Server and Oracle Weblogic Server Proxy Plug-in', names two things that are usually owned by different teams. A CAF assessment that confirms WebLogic is patched and its port 7001 is not exposed passes while the Apache or IIS tier in front of it still loads the vulnerable plug-in, and scanning 7001 - the obvious move - bypasses the vulnerable component by construction.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Essential Eight patch timeframes run from vendor release, and the vendor release here is a quarterly. An estate that applied the January 2026 CPU inside its timeframe is compliant and fixed; an estate that deferred it has been non-compliant continuously since January without the maturity model escalating, and CISA's August window of three days is shorter than any timeframe the model defines. The model has no input for a catalogue listing arriving seven months after the patch, and none for the fact that the mitigating configuration change - rejecting `..;` at the front end - is available immediately and is not a patch at all, so it earns no credit under a patch-timeframe control.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: Management of technical vulnerabilities requires vulnerability information to be obtained and exposure evaluated. The information available at the time was Oracle's risk-matrix row and nothing else: no technical detail, no credited reporter, no advisory prose beyond the matrix. The first public root-cause analysis with reproducible evidence did not appear until 2026-08-27, and what circulated in between was actively wrong - non-working 'RCE' tools aimed at port 7001, which a January 2026 public credibility analysis identified as architecturally impossible. The control does not say what to do when the vendor's disclosure model makes exposure unevaluable, and it carries no trigger that reopens a closed evaluation when the real analysis finally appears.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: 4h KEV-listing mitigation SLA applies.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CISA allowed three days - added 2026-08-24, due 2026-08-27 - for a fix that has only ever shipped inside Oracle's January 2026 quarterly Critical Patch Update, with no out-of-band unit to apply. An hours-scale SLA cannot deliver a CPU across a Fusion Middleware estate, but it can deliver the thing that needs no outage: a front-end rule rejecting request-targets that carry `;` adjacent to `..` in the raw path, which is what the four reproduced encodings all rely on.

new_control_requirements.name: CONFIGURATION-SIDE-LIVE-PATCH-INVENTORY
new_control_requirements.description: For any web-fabric vulnerability with a configuration-side mitigation path, that path must be inventoried, tested and deployable independently of the vendor-patch path.
new_control_requirements.evidence: This CVE has a configuration-side path and a patch path that reach different owners. The patch is a quarterly CPU applied to the front-end plug-in binary; the mitigation is a request-target rule at the same front end plus duplication of each path restriction on the WebLogic side. Building the mitigation forces the inventory the patch also needs and that a WebLogic-keyed asset register does not produce - which mod_wl_ohs.so and iisproxy.dll builds exist, and which backend paths are protected by a proxy <Location> rule alone.

new_control_requirements.name: MITIGATION-ACTIVE-PATCH-PENDING-VERDICT-CLASS
new_control_requirements.description: Compliance verdicts must distinguish binary-patch-deployed from vendor-mitigation-active-without-patch from no-mitigation-at-all, and must surface the middle state as a time-bound compensating control rather than as a patched-per-SLA outcome.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Three states are genuinely distinct here and a single boolean collapses them. 'WebLogic is patched and 7001 is closed' is not the patched state, because the defect is in the front-end plug-in. 'The `..;` deny rule is deployed' is a real reduction but leaves the parser disagreement intact for the next encoding. Only the January 2026 CPU on the plug-in binary eliminates it. Note that no catalogued control addresses normalization parity between a proxy and the backend it fronts; this is the closest existing fit, and it is attached because the verdict-class distinction is what stops the middle state being recorded as compliant.

attack_vector.description: An unauthenticated attacker connects to port 4307/TCP on a TrueConf Server - open by default per the product documentation - and submits a script. The script runs in an isolated environment that is supposed to deny access to operating-system functions; this defect escapes that environment and executes arbitrary code on the host. In the observed campaign the resulting code ran as NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM, a web shell was placed at ...\public\js\locale.php, and the TrueConf Client distribution the server publishes was replaced with a build carrying the PhantomCore backdoor.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none - the connection is unauthenticated and the port is open in a default deployment
attack_vector.complexity: high per the CVSS 4.0 vector (AC:H, AT:P), which describes the cost of building the escape rather than of using it; the technique was used in production intrusions once built, and it is the second half of a chain whose first half is Kaspersky's KLCERT-26-057
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered and not AI-weaponised. The advisory credits a named human researcher and no source consulted describes AI involvement in either the discovery or the exploit.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Upgrade to the fixed build for the branch in use - 5.3.9, 5.4.9 or 5.5.5 - and restrict port 4307/TCP at the network boundary to the hosts that need it.
prevention.framework_requiring_it: CISA BOD 22-01 (KEV remediation - CVE-2026-72530 added 2026-08-20, due 2026-09-03; companion CVE-2026-72529 added the same day, due 2026-08-23, and the same upgrade closes both, so 2026-08-23 is the governing date)
prevention.adequacy: Sufficient against this defect, and insufficient on its own for the estate the campaign actually hit. The fix existed from 2026-06-18 and exploitation was detected in July, so upgrading now closes the door on a server that may already have published a backdoored client installer. The port restriction is the half that needs no outage and is therefore the half deliverable inside a short SLA.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alert on any process spawned by the TrueConf Server service, on inbound connections to 4307/TCP from outside the expected host set, and on the campaign's named indicators - the locale.php web shell, the SysExcSvc / SysReadSvc services, and the CLSID InprocServer32 registry key.
detection.adequacy: The process-spawn signal is the durable one: the whole point of the isolated environment is that scripts in it do not reach operating-system functions, so any child process of the server is definitionally outside intended behaviour. The published campaign indicators are reliable for this actor and will not survive infrastructure rotation. The PhantomGraph channel is harder - it uses OneDrive, so the egress is to a destination most estates allow by policy.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treat the host as compromised at SYSTEM: rebuild rather than clean, rotate the credentials for all potentially affected accounts including the conferencing database, verify the published client distribution against the vendor's original, and identify every endpoint that installed a client from this server since the earliest possible intrusion date.
response.adequacy: Bounded only if the client-side half is included. Rebuilding the server and rotating its credentials leaves every workstation that installed the trojaned client still backdoored, and those endpoints are conference participants - which in this campaign meant staff across the victim organisations rather than a server-administration subset.

NIST-800-53-SC-7.gap: Boundary protection is the control that would have removed reachability here, and the reason it did not is that the exposure came from the vendor's documented default rather than from a misconfiguration. Port 4307/TCP is open by default per TrueConf's product documentation, so an estate that implemented SC-7 by allowing the ports its conferencing vendor's deployment guide specifies has an accurate, reviewed, compliant boundary policy that admits the attack. SC-7 asks that the boundary be defined and enforced; it has no clause requiring a vendor-default port to be justified against what it actually exposes, and nothing in the control distinguishes 4307/TCP as a scripting interface from the media and signalling ports beside it in the same documentation.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: The Article 21 patch-management obligation is measured against the availability of a fix, and here the timeline defeats that measure from both ends. TrueConf shipped the fixed builds on 2026-06-18. Kaspersky detected the campaign in July 2026 - inside the window any reasonable patch policy would allow for a conferencing server that has to be taken out of service to upgrade. CISA then listed the CVE on 2026-08-20 with a 2026-09-03 due date, two months after the fix existed - and listed the other half of the same chain, CVE-2026-72529, on the same day with a 2026-08-23 due date, so the deadline that actually binds the host is three days rather than fourteen, and the identical upgrade to 5.3.9, 5.4.9 or 5.5.5 satisfies both. An operator who patched to their documented schedule can be simultaneously compliant with Article 21 and compromised, and the obligation carries nothing that shortens the window when a fix lands for a pre-authentication path to SYSTEM on an internet-facing server.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: The system-security outcome expects vulnerable software to be identified and updated, and identification is where this one fails in a specific, checkable way: there is no single version to compare against. Three supported branches carry three different fixed builds, so a CAF assessment that confirms an update process exists and runs will accept a 5.4.7 host and a 5.5.4 host as evidence of the same working process, while both remain vulnerable. Worse, the outcome is framed around the software being updated, and updating the server does not address the client installers it had already published - the artefact that actually reached the victims' endpoints in this campaign is outside what B4 asks about.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Essential Eight patch timeframes are keyed to vendor release and to whether the software is internet-facing, and this case satisfies the letter of the model while missing its intent twice over. The fix was released 2026-06-18 and exploitation was detected in July, so even the tightest Essential Eight timeframe for an internet-facing service can be met by an organisation that was compromised in the interval. Beyond that, the Essential Eight is entirely a patch-currency model: nothing in it triggers the compromise assessment that a post-patch exploitation campaign demands, and nothing in it covers verifying that the client distribution the server publishes is still the vendor's own.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: Management of technical vulnerabilities is scoped to the vulnerabilities of the information systems the organisation uses, and that scoping is what leaves the exposure open here. Both halves of the chain are inside the identifier space an A.8.8 process consumes - CVE-2026-72529 for the missing authentication on 4307/TCP and CVE-2026-72530 for the escape from the isolated environment, both from the same CNA and both in KEV - so the process obtains the information, evaluates exposure correctly and upgrades to 5.3.9, 5.4.9 or 5.5.5. What it has no step for is the artefact the campaign was built to reach: the TrueConf Client distribution the compromised server publishes to its own users. A replaced installer is not a technical vulnerability of a system in use, carries no CVE and appears in no feed, so a fully conformant A.8.8 process closes both flaws it can name and never asks whether the software its own server handed to staff is still the vendor's build.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.22.gap: Segregation of networks is the control that would have bounded the consequence rather than prevented the flaw. The observed path runs from an unauthenticated connection on 4307/TCP to SYSTEM on the conferencing host, then to the conferencing database, then to the client distribution that server publishes to every participant. A.8.22 asks that networks be segregated according to trust levels, and a conferencing server is routinely placed on the trusted internal side precisely because meetings involve everyone - the control's own logic puts this host where its compromise reaches furthest, and it has nothing to say about segregating a server from the software distribution channel it also happens to own.

new_control_requirements.name: SERVICE-INTERNAL-PROTOCOL-DESERIALIZATION-HARDENING
new_control_requirements.description: A server product that exposes an internal coordination protocol — build-agent polling, cluster membership, node replication, management RPC — must not deserialize input arriving on it without both authenticating the peer and constraining the deserializer to an explicit allow-list of expected types, and the listener must be bound to the coordination network rather than to all interfaces. Default-permissive type handling in the serialization library counts as no allow-list at all. The distinguishing test: from an unauthenticated host on a segment that can reach the coordination port, send a serialized object of a type the protocol never legitimately carries and confirm the connection is refused or the type rejected before any object is constructed — a product whose internal protocol is documented as trusted, but which listens on 0.0.0.0 and accepts whatever the library will rehydrate, is exploitable by anyone who can reach the port.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Attached as the closest existing control, and the fit is partial: the control is written around deserialization, and 4307/TCP does not deserialize - it interprets a submitted script, so the deserializer allow-list clause has no counterpart in this CVE. What does carry over is the rest of the requirement, and it is the half that was absent. The port is a server-side management surface the product documentation records as open by default, and the companion flaw Kaspersky tracks as KLCERT-26-057, CVE-2026-72529, is a missing authentication for a critical function on that same port - so input reached the interpreter with no peer authentication at all, and the vendor's containment answer was an isolated environment rather than a decision about who may connect. Authenticating the peer and restricting the listener to the hosts that require it removes the reachability the whole chain depends on, and unlike the upgrade it needs no outage, which matters because the upgrade stops the conferencing service.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: 4h KEV-listing mitigation SLA applies.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CISA added CVE-2026-72530 on 2026-08-20 with a 2026-09-03 due date, but that is not the clock that governs the host. The same day CISA listed the other half of this chain, CVE-2026-72529, with a due date of 2026-08-23 - three days rather than fourteen - and both are remediated by the identical upgrade to 5.3.9, 5.4.9 or 5.5.5 on the same server. A federal operator who schedules the work against 2026-09-03 misses a binding deadline eleven days earlier, so the shorter clock is the one to plan against. The upgrade itself cannot honour an hours-scale SLA on a conferencing server, because applying it stops every meeting in progress and the fixed build differs per branch. What an hours-scale response can deliver here is the mitigation the vendor's own vector statement points at: restrict 4307/TCP to the hosts that need it, which needs no outage, removes reachability for the whole chain, and is the only action that fits inside a three-day window at all. The patch date of 2026-06-18 against a July detection is the reason the SLA has to bite on the mitigation rather than only on the upgrade.

new_control_requirements.name: INDEPENDENT-INTEGRITY-VERIFICATION-OF-SIGNED-VENDOR-INSTALLERS
new_control_requirements.description: Where a server or updater is the delivery channel for software an organisation installs, the delivery channel is the trust anchor: the retrieved installer must be verified against the vendor's own published artefact before it is executed, and the channel itself must be treated as a privileged surface.
new_control_requirements.evidence: This control is written in the catalogue around the Notepad++ WinGUp update path and is attached here as the closest existing control for the same construction, because the substance matches exactly: Head Mare's objective on the compromised TrueConf Server was replacing the TrueConf Client distribution it publishes with a PhantomCore-carrying build (infected installer MD5 748c9f8cb1065000616204935f96207f), so the conferencing server became the delivery channel to its own client population. The consequence is what makes this a separate requirement from patching: upgrading the server to 5.3.9 / 5.4.9 / 5.5.5 closes the flaw and does not touch an installer already published or already installed.

CVE-2026-72529.name: TrueConf Server Missing Authentication for Critical Function Vulnerability (CVE-2026-72529)

attack_vector.description: An undocumented function on TrueConf Server's 4307/TCP listener runs a caller-supplied script without checking who the caller is. Kaspersky ICS-CERT withholds the function name, so the hunt surface is what the execution leaves behind rather than the request that triggers it. Head Mare paired it with KLCERT-26-058, an environment breakout, and came out at NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM; the payload was PhantomCore plus PhantomGraph, whose two modules SysExcSvc.dll and SysReadSvc.dll were installed as Windows services under C:\Windows\System32\inetsrv\ and held through a COM InprocServer32 registry entry.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N and UI:N. No account, no session and no victim action. The only precondition is TCP reachability to port 4307, which Securelist describes as open by default.
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L and AT:N. A single function call on an open port, with no race, no leak and no memory grooming. What made the intrusions harder than the CVE was the second stage: reaching SYSTEM needed the separate KLCERT-26-058 breakout.
attack_vector.ai_factor: None recorded. Kaspersky credits Vyacheslav Kopeytsev with the discovery and describes Head Mare's tooling as PhantomCore and PhantomGraph without claiming AI assistance in either the finding or the weaponisation.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Taking 5.3.9, 5.4.9 or 5.5.5 after the 2026-06-18 fixes and confirming the server components cycled onto the new build; failing that, restricting 4307/TCP to the conferencing clients and endpoints that need it, which removes the pre-authentication path entirely because the function is only reachable on that port.
prevention.adequacy: The upgrade is complete for this CVE. The port restriction is a genuine removal of the path rather than a filter, and it is the only control that was available during the two months between the 2026-06-18 fix and the 2026-08-19 CVE publication — but it can only be applied where someone already knew 4307/TCP was the conferencing service port, since no advisory existed to tell them.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Sweeping for the service names SysExcSvc and SysReadSvc, for the DLLs under C:\Windows\System32\inetsrv\, for %TEMP%\cmd_cmd_*.bat, and for the CLSID {0340F119-A598-4ed9-B0AC-6F6A12D3E755} InprocServer32 registry entry; and matching outbound traffic against 81.177.32.12, 194.87.239.71, penzadogshelter.site and trendy-market.site.
detection.adequacy: These are strong indicators because Kaspersky published them from live intrusions rather than from a lab reproduction, but every one of them is post-execution. Nothing here detects the function call itself, because the advisory withholds which function it is — so an estate that hunts these and comes back clean has ruled out this campaign's payload, not exploitation of the CVE. The DLL path under System32\inetsrv\ and the CRT-lookalike filename api-ms-win-crt-time-l1-1-0-2.dll are both chosen to survive a casual directory review.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating a reachable unpatched server as executed-on: rebuild rather than upgrade in place, remove the service registrations and the COM registry entry, and rotate credentials for every account the server could reach — which is what Kaspersky's own advisory instructs when its indicators are found.
response.adequacy: It is the correct sequence, and Kaspersky writing the password reset into the advisory rather than into a separate incident-response note is what makes it actionable. The limit is scope: the chain reached NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM, so the credential set at risk is everything the machine account and any service account on that host could reach, and on a conferencing server that is a directory-joined machine with an address book. Deciding that boundary is the expensive part, not removing the two DLLs.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: The fixed builds existed from 2026-06-18 and the CVE was not published until 2026-08-19. An SI-2 programme keyed to CVE publication or scanner findings had no flaw to remediate during the two months in which Kaspersky observed Head Mare using it, and the 0.01554 EPSS score published on 2026-08-28 still ranks it low enough to be deprioritised by a score-ordered queue.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: Patching to 5.5.5 satisfies the article and leaves an implanted host implanted. Kaspersky pairs the upgrade with an antivirus rescan, an indicator hunt and a password reset, none of which Article 21's patch-management measure requires — and on a flaw that reached NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM through the KLCERT-26-058 chain, the upgrade is the smaller half of the remediation.

UK-CAF-D1.gap: A D1 response plan sized to 'the conferencing server is down' is the wrong plan for this incident. Kaspersky records SYSTEM-level access, two backdoor modules registered as services and COM-based persistence, at industrial and energy organisations. CAF asks for a proportionate plan but supplies no trigger that reclassifies a conferencing-server outage as a fleet credential event, so the escalation depends on the responder recognising the indicators.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Kaspersky's fixes shipped on 2026-06-18, the CVE published on 2026-08-19 and CISA listed it on 2026-08-20 with a due date of 2026-08-23 — three days, one of the shortest in the catalog. Any SLA measured from CVE publication had a two-month blind window while Head Mare was operating, and the EPSS pair published on 2026-08-28 (score 0.01554, percentile 0.72934) would place this below dozens of unexploited CVEs in a score-ordered queue. This control fires on the listing rather than the score, and on this product 'verified' has to mean the server reports 5.3.9, 5.4.9 or 5.5.5 — or, as a documented compensating control, that 4307/TCP is restricted to known conferencing endpoints.

new_control_requirements.name: PERIMETER-COMPROMISE-REBUILD-NOT-PATCH
new_control_requirements.description: Pre-rehearsed IR runbook for any perimeter device that suffers a pre-auth RCE CVE in active exploitation MUST default to config-exfil + rebuild + credential rotation, not patch-in-place. Patch-in-place leaves attacker-installed implants intact.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Attached as the closest existing control rather than an exact one: TrueConf Server is a conferencing server, not a perimeter appliance, but this is precisely the pre-authentication-RCE-under-active-exploitation case the control governs. Kaspersky documents SysExcSvc.dll and SysReadSvc.dll installed as services under C:\Windows\System32\inetsrv\ and persistence through the CLSID {0340F119-A598-4ed9-B0AC-6F6A12D3E755} InprocServer32 key. Upgrading to 5.5.5 closes the undocumented function and deletes none of that. The advisory's own guidance — rescan, hunt indicators, reset passwords — is the control's config-exfil-plus-rotation half written by the finder.

new_control_requirements.name: NATION-STATE-INITIAL-ACCESS-IR-ESCALATION
new_control_requirements.description: IR runbooks must include an explicit nation-state-initial-access escalation path triggered by APT attribution on a confirmed exploit chain, so that a confirmed APT finding leaves the standard vulnerability-response track rather than being handled as a routine patch item.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Kaspersky explicitly reclassifies Head Mare from hacktivists to an APT on the strength of the TTPs in this campaign, and describes a two-CVE chain — KLCERT-26-057 for execution, KLCERT-26-058 for the environment breakout — terminating at NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM, against manufacturing, electronics, transportation, energy, IT and software organisations. That is the attribution-plus-confirmed-chain trigger the control names. Without it, the TrueConf finding enters the queue as a KEV patch item with an EPSS of 0.01554 and never reaches the credential-rotation and rebuild decisions the intrusion actually requires.

CVE-2026-64849.name: MLflow Webhook Test Endpoint Unauthenticated SSRF to Cloud Metadata

attack_vector.description: An unauthenticated caller registers a webhook whose URL points at attacker-controlled public infrastructure, passing MLflow's _validate_webhook_url() check, then calls POST /api/2.0/mlflow/webhooks/{id}/test. The delivery path follows redirects and re-resolves the hostname without pinning the validated address, so the second hop lands on 169.254.169.254 or an internal host, and the test endpoint returns response_status and response_body to the caller.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none - the webhooks test endpoint is unauthenticated on a default MLflow tracking server, which is why the CVSS vector reads PR:N
attack_vector.complexity: low - three ordinary API calls, fully automated by the public Nuclei template; the redirect or rebinding response is supplied by infrastructure the attacker already controls
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered and not AI-weaponised. The advisory credits named human reporters and the public reproduction in issue #24179 is a short hand-written Python script.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Upgrade to MLflow 3.15.0 or later, which validates the peer IP of the connected socket after TCP connect rather than validating the URL string beforehand. Before the change window, deny egress from the tracking server to link-local and RFC 1918 destinations and require authentication in front of the API.
prevention.adequacy: Sufficient going forward, insufficient backwards. Any cloud role credential the server could fetch is disclosed rather than merely reachable, so the upgrade does not undo a successful pre-patch read; and pull #24258 honours the pre-existing MLFLOW_WEBHOOK_ALLOW_PRIVATE_IPS setting at connect time, so a patched server with that variable set still fetches private and link-local addresses.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alert on any outbound request from the tracking server to 169.254.169.254 or a private range, and on the create/test/delete webhook sequence appearing from one client inside a few seconds.
detection.adequacy: Effective where the tracking server's egress is observed, which a link-local destination usually defeats - traffic to 169.254.169.254 is answered by the hypervisor and never crosses a network sensor, so this detection has to run on the host or in the cloud provider's own metadata-access logging rather than at a boundary.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treat the instance role the tracking server runs as compromised: rotate it, review cloud audit logs for use of that identity from any address other than the server, and audit the webhook store for destinations no operator created.
response.adequacy: Decisive on the credential side. Weaker on scope: the same primitive reads any internal HTTP service the server can route to, so credential rotation alone does not bound what was read from internal endpoints that answer without authentication.

NIST-800-53-SC-7.gap: Boundary protection governs traffic crossing a system boundary. The request this flaw produces never crosses one an SC-7 control set inspects: the MLflow tracking server opens the connection itself, and 169.254.169.254 is link-local, answered by the hypervisor rather than routed through any perimeter device. The attacker's inbound half is an ordinary POST to /api/2.0/mlflow/webhooks/{id}/test on the port SC-7 already authorises. Nothing in a boundary-protection baseline separates MLflow 3.14.x from 3.15.0, because the difference is a peer-IP check taken after connect inside the application, not a filtering rule at the boundary.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: Art. 21 requires vulnerability handling and disclosure measures, which here resolve to moving to 3.15.0. The fix commit merged 2026-07-02 and the advisory was published in the GitHub Advisory Database on 2026-08-02, so an entity running a release-cadence patch process had a month-long window in which the fix existed, the reproduction in issue #24179 was public, and no advisory had told it to act. Art. 21 sets no obligation that begins at the upstream commit, and for this flaw that window is the whole exposure, because the endpoint needs no credential.

EU-AI-Act-Art-15.gap: Art. 15's accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity requirements attach to the high-risk AI system placed on the market. MLflow 3.14.x is the experiment-tracking and model-registry infrastructure used to build such a system, not the system itself, so an Art. 15 conformity argument about the deployed model's robustness can be complete and correct while the tracking server's /webhooks/{id}/test endpoint hands out the cloud credential that reaches the model artefacts. The obligation and the exposed asset sit on opposite sides of the placing-on-the-market line.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: The system security outcome expects services to be configured and maintained so they resist attack. An estate could meet that on this system and still be fully exposed: 3.14.x was a current MLflow release before 3.15.0 shipped, the webhooks API is a documented feature, and _validate_webhook_url() was the vendor's own control - the operator had no configuration decision available that would have refused the redirect, because the validated address was never pinned to the socket the delivery code opened.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: The Essential Eight patching controls run their timeframes from the vendor release that carries a fix, and are scoped to operating systems, named application classes and internet-facing services. A tracking server reachable from an untrusted network is an internet-facing service and so is in scope, and the shortest timeframe does attach to the 3.15.0 upgrade - the gap is where that clock starts and what the assessment inspects. The reproduction in issue #24179 was public on 2026-06-26 and the fix merged on 2026-07-02, but MLflow 3.15.0 did not ship until 2026-07-31, so for roughly five weeks a working public technique existed against an unauthenticated endpoint with no released build to move to. Through that window an organisation at its target maturity level is exposed and fully compliant, because the model has nothing to measure until a release exists. When the clock did start it started on 2026-07-31, not on the GitHub Advisory Database publication of 2026-08-02: an estate that keys its patch timeframes to advisory feeds rather than to vendor releases begins two days late, which on the shortest internet-facing timeframe is most of the window it was allowed. The second half is the unit: a patch timeframe is assessed against an installed version, and the residual on this CVE is a configuration item rather than a version - MLFLOW_WEBHOOK_ALLOW_PRIVATE_IPS set on a 3.15.0 server restores the private-address fetches while every version check still reports the patched release.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: Management of technical vulnerabilities requires that vulnerability information be obtained and acted on; acting on it means 3.15.0. Between the advisory and that upgrade A.8.8 supplies no interim measure for this flaw, because the advisory documents no workaround. The two levers that do work - denying egress to link-local and private ranges, and putting an unauthenticated endpoint behind authentication - are network and access-model changes that an A.8.8 vulnerability-management process is not scoped to authorise.

new_control_requirements.name: AI-DATA-PIPELINE-IMPORT-SSRF-PROTECTION
new_control_requirements.description: An AI data-pipeline or MLOps platform that fetches from caller-supplied URLs or endpoints must validate and allowlist the destination before issuing the request, reject private, loopback, link-local and cloud-metadata addresses and non-HTTP schemes, and resolve and pin the host so the address that was validated is the address that is connected to. Restrict who may configure server-side fetches. The distinguishing test is to point the fetch at an internal or metadata address on a staging instance and confirm the server refuses it.
new_control_requirements.evidence: This is the control the MLflow fix implements. Before 3.15.0 the platform did allowlist the destination - _validate_webhook_url() rejected non-global addresses - but validated the URL string rather than the socket, so a redirect or a second DNS answer moved the connection to 169.254.169.254 after the check had passed. 3.15.0 pins the peer IP immediately after TCP connect, before TLS or any HTTP exchange. The operational test for this CVE: on a staging tracking server, register a webhook whose host redirects to 169.254.169.254, call POST /api/2.0/mlflow/webhooks/{id}/test, and confirm the response carries no metadata document - and check MLFLOW_WEBHOOK_ALLOW_PRIVATE_IPS is unset, because a patched server with it set fails this test.

new_control_requirements.name: AI-ML-DEVELOPER-TOOLING-INVENTORY
new_control_requirements.description: Organizations using AI/ML systems must maintain a separate inventory of developer-tooling control planes (notebook servers, experiment trackers, model registries, vector-DB admin UIs, agent frameworks) recording each exposed network endpoint, the authentication mechanism per endpoint, the blast radius reachable from that tool, and a patch SLA tier distinct from generic application patching.
new_control_requirements.evidence: An MLflow tracking server is an experiment tracker and model registry, which is exactly the class this control enumerates, and this CVE shows why the per-endpoint authentication column is load-bearing: /api/2.0/mlflow/webhooks and /api/2.0/mlflow/webhooks/{id}/test answer unauthenticated on a default server, so an inventory that records the deployment as 'behind the VPN' still misses that any principal on that network reaches a credential-yielding endpoint. The blast-radius column for this host is the instance role, not the experiment data - the flaw returns response_body, so a metadata fetch is credential disclosure. The distinct patch tier is what would have started a clock at the upstream fix of 2026-07-02 rather than at the advisory a month later, which is the interval a release-cadence process spends exposed here.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CISA allowed 14 days between the 2026-08-19 KEV listing and the 2026-09-02 due date for an unauthenticated CVSS 9.3 flaw whose fix had been public since 2026-07-02 and whose reproduction had been public in issue #24179 since 2026-06-26; EPSS on 2026-08-28 was 0.1641 at the 96.806th percentile. What a four-hour clock can actually deliver here is not the version upgrade but the two compensating controls: deny egress from the tracking server to link-local and RFC 1918 ranges, and put the unauthenticated webhooks endpoints behind authentication. Schedule 3.15.0 behind those.

CVE-2026-33824.name: Windows IKE Extension IKEv2 Fragment Reassembly Double Free

attack_vector.description: An unauthenticated attacker sends crafted fragmented IKEv2 IKE_AUTH traffic to UDP 500 or 4500. Improper ownership handling of a heap-allocated blob pointer during fragment reassembly frees the same allocation twice - once by IkeDestroyPacketContext, again by IkeFreeMMSA - and the resulting corruption is turned into execution in the context of the Windows IKE service.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none (unauthenticated network traffic to the IKE listener; no VPN credentials, no user interaction)
attack_vector.complexity: low to reach the defect, high to weaponise reliably - the public prototype is self-declared non-functional while private operators have landed callbacks
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered - credited to Microsoft's WARP and MORSE teams. The actor Unit 42 reports used AI models autonomously elsewhere in the same campaign, but the IKE exploitation is recorded as manual.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Apply the April 2026 Microsoft security update and reboot on every Windows host running the IKE service; disable IKEEXT on hosts that do not terminate IPsec or IKEv2; restrict UDP 500 and 4500 to genuine VPN endpoints and expected peer ranges.
prevention.adequacy: Sufficient going forward, and insufficient backwards: a host that was reachable and unpatched between April and August 2026 may already be holding an implant the update does not remove.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alert on IKEEXT service crashes and restarts, on ikeext.dll faults, and on any egress session opened from the IKE service context.
detection.adequacy: Crash telemetry catches unreliable attempts; a successful exploitation that does not destabilise the service leaves the callback as the only signal, which is why egress monitoring from the service context carries the weight.

response.what_would_have_worked: Rebuild rather than patch-in-place for any endpoint with evidence of exploitation, and rotate the credentials and certificates the VPN endpoint held.
response.adequacy: Necessary because code runs pre-authentication in a service context - there is no authentication record to scope the intrusion from, so patching alone cannot establish that the host is clean.

NIST-800-53-SC-7.gap: Boundary protection cannot close this path on the hosts that matter. UDP 500 and 4500 have to be reachable from untrusted networks for IKEv2 remote access to function at all, so the boundary control is correctly configured and the crafted IKE_AUTH fragments arrive on the port the policy deliberately allows. SC-7 does help on hosts that merely have the service running without terminating VPN traffic, which is why the service-disable path belongs in the same remediation record.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: Microsoft shipped the fix in the April 2026 security updates and CISA listed the CVE on 2026-08-18 with a 2026-08-21 due date. A patch-management process running a monthly or quarterly cycle on internet-facing Windows hosts had four months in which the fix existed, the flaw was public through ZDI's 2026-04-22 analysis, and Unit 42 was already recording reverse-shell callbacks by its 2026-07-30 publication - the gap is not the absence of a patch process but a cadence that treats a VPN-terminating Windows host as an ordinary endpoint.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: System security assurance for remote access typically evidences that VPN authentication is enforced. This defect sits before authentication - the double free is reached during fragment reassembly of the IKE_AUTH exchange - so every assurance statement about credential strength, certificate validation or MFA on the tunnel remains true while the host is compromised without a tunnel ever being established.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: The Essential Eight requires internet-facing services to be patched within a stated window of an update becoming available, and here the window is measured from April 2026 while the KEV due date is 2026-08-21 - a maturity-level assessment that scores patch application against the fortnightly-or-monthly cadence would have recorded compliance throughout the period in which Unit 42 observed callbacks on three IKE VPN endpoints.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: Management of technical vulnerabilities depends on the organisation knowing where the vulnerable component is. There is no per-SKU fixed build published in the sources consulted, and the vulnerable code is a Windows service extension rather than an inventoried VPN product, so an asset register built around named appliances does not enumerate the Windows hosts that happen to run the IKE service - the inventory question this control assumes is answerable is the part that fails.

new_control_requirements.name: PERIMETER-COMPROMISE-REBUILD-NOT-PATCH
new_control_requirements.description: Pre-rehearsed IR runbook for any perimeter device that suffers a pre-auth RCE CVE in active exploitation must default to config-exfil plus rebuild plus credential rotation, not patch-in-place, because patch-in-place leaves attacker-installed implants intact.
new_control_requirements.evidence: This is a pre-authentication remote code execution on the host that terminates the VPN, confirmed exploited: Unit 42's 2026-07-30 report records 'Reverse shell callbacks targeting three IKE VPN endpoints (CVE-2026-33824)'. The exploitation leaves no authentication record to scope from - code runs in the IKE service context during fragment reassembly, before credentials are validated - so an operator who applies the April 2026 update and reboots has restored the fixed ikeext.dll and established nothing about what ran in the four months the host was reachable. The distinguishing precondition here, unlike an appliance, is that the perimeter device is a general-purpose Windows host: the runbook has to name what 'rebuild' means for a machine that may also carry roles beyond VPN termination, and rotation must cover the certificates and pre-shared keys the endpoint held.

new_control_requirements.name: DEPRECATED-VPN-KEY-EXCHANGE-DISABLE-AND-MACHINE-CERT-ENFORCEMENT
new_control_requirements.description: Deprecated VPN key-exchange protocols (IKEv1 and similar) left enabled on a perimeter gateway are a latent authentication-enforcement surface; a certificate-validation logic flaw there yields an unauthenticated remote-access foothold. Require: inventory every gateway's enabled key-exchange protocols, disable deprecated protocols (IKEv1) for remote access unless a documented legacy-client need exists, require a machine certificate for remote-access connections, and remediate any confirmed-exploited gateway auth bypass on a KEV-tied expedited clock with a reboot-required hotfix. The distinguishing test: on a staging gateway with IKEv1 remote access enabled, attempt a remote-access connection without a valid user password and confirm it is refused before any tunnel is established — paper 'VPN authentication enforced' policies do not detect a deprecated-protocol certificate-validation bypass that grants an interior foothold to a ransomware affiliate.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Attached as the closest existing control, with its mismatches stated plainly: the control is written for a deprecated protocol such as IKEv1 while this flaw is in the current IKEv2 fragment-reassembly path, so disabling a legacy protocol does not close it, and the control's machine-certificate limb does not reduce this exposure either - the double free is reached during fragment reassembly, before any certificate or credential is examined. What transfers exactly is the inventory obligation and the reason for it - the listener on UDP 500 and 4500 is present on Windows hosts whether or not they terminate a VPN, and on those that do not, stopping the IKE and AuthIP IPsec Keying Modules service removes the attack surface entirely. What also transfers is the remediation clock and its shape: the fix ships in the April 2026 cumulative update and the host reboots before the fixed ikeext.dll loads, against a KEV due date of 2026-08-21. The distinguishing test is a listener check rather than a policy statement - enumerate which hosts answer on UDP 500/4500 and which of those genuinely terminate IPsec, because a paper statement that 'VPN authentication is enforced' says nothing about a pre-authentication double free.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: 4h KEV-listing mitigation SLA applies.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CISA listed CVE-2026-33824 on 2026-08-18 with a 2026-08-21 due date. EPSS on 2026-08-28 was 0.72695 at the 99.419th percentile. The mitigation an SLA measured in hours can deliver is not the cumulative update - that needs a reboot window on a VPN endpoint - but the reachability cut: disable IKEEXT where it is not needed and restrict UDP 500/4500 to expected peers, then schedule the April 2026 update and reboot inside the due date.

CVE-2026-59310.name: Broadcom VMware vCenter Syslog Path Traversal (CVE-2026-59310)

attack_vector.description: A directory-traversal flaw in the vCenter Syslog server, reachable by anyone with network access to the appliance, that Broadcom states leads to arbitrary code execution. Observed post-exploitation is a cron job on the appliance running reverse_ssh outbound to attacker infrastructure, which gives persistent interactive access to the control plane for the whole virtual estate.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — unauthenticated network access to vCenter is the entire requirement; no vSphere credential, SSO session or user interaction is involved.
attack_vector.complexity: low — no workaround exists on any affected line, so the appliance is exploitable until the fixed build is applied. The practical complexity sits with the defender: two of the eight affected product lines have no ordinary update path, and vCenter 7.0 has no published fixed build at all.
attack_vector.ai_factor: None claimed or observed. Reported to Broadcom by Phil Brass and Matt South of Atredis Partners; the exploitation campaign QUIRSO documented carries no AI attribution.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Applying the fixed build within the five days between the 2026-07-29 advisory and the 2026-08-03 first observed compromise: 9.1.0.0300, 9.0.2.0100, 8.0 U3k or 8.0 U2f. For vCenter 7.0 and Cloud Foundation 5.x, network isolation of the appliance, because neither had a same-day update path.
prevention.adequacy: Adequate only where the update path existed. Broadcom offers no workaround, so an estate on vCenter 7.0 without an extended support contract, or on Cloud Foundation 5.x facing an async patch under KB88287, had nothing it could deploy inside the window.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Filesystem and crontab integrity monitoring on the appliance, and egress monitoring that treats an outbound session initiated by vCenter as an anomaly. QUIRSO's generic YARA rule for reverse_ssh client binaries covers the payload.
detection.adequacy: Weak in the state most estates were in. vCenter is usually a log source rather than a monitored endpoint, the traversal request shape was never published, and QUIRSO withheld the infrastructure indicators — so between 2026-08-03 and public reporting, the only self-service signal was an appliance behaving unusually on its own network egress.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating a confirmed hit as compromise of the virtualisation control plane: capture the appliance configuration, rebuild rather than clean, and rotate SSO signing material and every credential vCenter held for ESXi hosts and integrations before restoring management.
response.adequacy: Correct and rarely rehearsed. Patching in place leaves the cron entry and whatever the reverse_ssh session already reached; and because vCenter holds credentials for the hosts it manages, a response scoped to the appliance alone leaves the estate's trust material in the attacker's hands.

NIST-800-53-SC-7.gap: SC-7 is written for inbound reachability and the persistence here is outbound. A boundary policy that correctly restricts who may reach vCenter, and says nothing about what vCenter may reach, is compliant and blind to a reverse_ssh session the appliance initiates to attacker infrastructure.

NIS2-Art21-incident-handling.gap: The 24-hour early-warning obligation starts at awareness, and awareness was unavailable: QUIRSO had confirmed 361 compromises across 47 countries by 2026-08-07 but withheld the indicators for law-enforcement reasons, and Broadcom's advisory carries no request signature. An entity could hold a KEV listing and an unpatched appliance and still have no evidentiary basis on which to start the clock.

UK-CAF-C1.gap: The evidence of compromise is a crontab entry and an outbound connection on a closed appliance — neither is a vSphere event, so neither appears in the telemetry vCenter normally forwards. C1 can be assessed as achieved on an estate that monitors everything vCenter manages and nothing about vCenter itself.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Patch applications measures whether the update was applied in the window, and on two affected lines there was no update to apply: vCenter 7.0 has no published fixed build outside an extended support contract, and Cloud Foundation 5.x requires an async patch to 8.0 U3k under KB88287. The maturity level records a failure to perform a task the vendor did not make available.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.16.gap: Monitoring activities on this estate is fed by vCenter rather than aimed at it. The two artefacts that would have surfaced the compromise — an unpackaged cron entry and an appliance-initiated outbound session — are host-level and fall outside a monitoring scope defined by the vSphere event stream.

new_control_requirements.name: PERIMETER-COMPROMISE-REBUILD-NOT-PATCH
new_control_requirements.description: Pre-rehearsed IR runbook for any network-reachable appliance that suffers a pre-auth RCE CVE in active exploitation MUST default to config-exfil plus rebuild plus credential rotation, not patch-in-place.
new_control_requirements.evidence: QUIRSO observed compromise of vCenter appliances beginning 2026-08-03, five days after Broadcom's 2026-07-29 advisory, with persistence established through a cron job running reverse_ssh. Applying 9.1.0.0300 or 8.0 U3k closes the traversal and removes neither the cron entry nor whatever the outbound session already reached. Because vCenter holds SSO signing material and stored credentials for every ESXi host it manages, the rotation scope is the estate rather than the appliance.

new_control_requirements.name: EOL-ASSET-DECOMMISSION
new_control_requirements.description: Network-reachable devices with no vendor patch path must be isolated and decommissioned within a bounded window; mandatory compensating segmentation applies until removal.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Broadcom's response matrix gives no fixed version for vCenter 7.0 against this CVE — the Fixed Version column reads 'Contact Broadcom Support if you have extended support contract' — while listing the same 9.8 severity as for the patched lines, and records no workaround anywhere. An estate on 7.0 without that contract therefore has an unauthenticated-RCE control plane with no vendor remediation, and segmentation plus a migration deadline is the only remaining control.

new_control_requirements.name: HYPERVISOR-VM-ESCAPE-TENANCY-ASSUMPTION
new_control_requirements.description: Treat the virtualisation control plane as a distinct trust tier: management interfaces reachable only from an operator network, egress from the appliance constrained and monitored, and the workloads it orchestrates treated as within its blast radius.
new_control_requirements.evidence: The 361 victim IP addresses across 47 countries QUIRSO identified by 2026-08-07 are appliances an unauthenticated attacker could reach over the network, which is the precondition Broadcom's own attack-vector statement names. The persistence mechanism was outbound rather than inbound, so the tenancy boundary has to be enforced in both directions to matter here.

attack_vector.description: Four independent weaknesses in SharePoint's JWT validation compose into unauthenticated impersonation: signed tokens are not required, the actor token's key is resolved from an attacker-controlled x5t header without verifying that token, an unknown certificate causes the issuer to be accepted rather than rejected, and the signature check tests only that a signature field is non-empty. An unauthenticated caller who knows a SID or UPN forges a token SharePoint accepts as that identity.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; the attacker needs network reach to a web front end and a target identifier, which the published exploit obtains from the domain controller after assuming any identity.
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L, UI:N. No grooming, no race, no configuration precondition. Microsoft's release-time temporal metric was E:U, which the public record overtook within a month.
attack_vector.ai_factor: Three named human finders are credited by Microsoft, and Rapid7 describes the work as a Pwn2Own Berlin entry. No AI-assisted discovery or weaponisation is claimed by any party; the public exploit is authored by the finder's own employer.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Installing KB5002882, KB5002883 or KB5002891 on every server in the farm, released 2026-07-14. Between the release and the completed farm-wide update the only available lever is restricting who can reach the web front ends, because no vendor configuration mitigation exists.
prevention.adequacy: The update is complete for this defect. Its weakness is measurement: Microsoft records Restart Required as Maybe, and a farm is only fixed when every front end is on the fixed build, so a deployment report showing the KB as installed does not establish remediation.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alerting on privileged SharePoint activity with no corresponding authentication event, and on unauthenticated access to /_layouts/15/metadata/json/1 followed by /_api/web/currentuser from the same source.
detection.adequacy: This depends on per-request IIS access logs from the front ends being retained and forwarded — authentication-event logging alone cannot see this attack, because the point of the flaw is that no authentication event occurs.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating a confirmed forged-token access as an identity incident scoped to whatever the impersonated account could reach: enumerate the sites, lists and documents that identity had rights to, and review changes made under it back to 2026-07-19.
response.adequacy: Scoping is bounded by front-end log retention rather than by the investigation, and the flaw grants no persistence of its own, so an attacker who used it to plant a durable foothold leaves that foothold behind after the patch.

NIST-800-53-IA-2.gap: The control is fully satisfied by a farm that uniquely identifies and authenticates every organizational user, and this attack never reaches the code that does that. IA-2 assesses the authentication requirement, not the integrity of the token handler that implements it, so nothing in a compliant assessment would have surfaced RequireSignedTokens being false or GetTokenSignature accepting a non-empty string.

NIS2-Art21-identity-management.gap: The measure is discharged by operating strong identity controls, and all of them sat upstream of the failure. There is no clause that asks whether the application's own enforcement point can be bypassed, so an entity with exemplary MFA, privileged-account handling and session policy was exposed exactly as much as one without.

UK-CAF-B2.gap: B2 asks whether access is granted only to verified identities. The forged token presented a verified identity — SharePoint's own — so the outcome's question was answered affirmatively while an unauthenticated caller acted as a site administrator. The assessment has no place to record that the verification itself was the defect.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: The strategy's clock starts at the vendor release, and exploitation attempts begin five days after it. An estate inside the model's window for internet-facing services is compliant across that period, and the internet-facing classification the faster window depends on is not settled by the strategy for a farm published to named partners.

ISO-27001-2022-A.5.15.gap: Access control as an annex control governs the rules an organisation writes and how it reviews them. Every rule was correct and every one was applied to an identity the attacker chose. The control produces the same evidence on a vulnerable and a patched farm, which is the definition of a verdict that carries no security information for this defect.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Microsoft shipped the fix on 2026-07-14 and CISA listed the CVE on 2026-08-18 with a 2026-08-21 due date — the compressed tier. The first exploitation attempt Defused Cyber records is 2026-07-19, five days after the release, so the whichever-is-later clause resolves to patch availability and puts the obligation a month before the KEV listing. Verified mitigation here means a per-front-end build check against 16.0.19725.20434 / 16.0.10417.20175 / 16.0.5561.1001, not a deployment-tool success report.

new_control_requirements.name: ENTERPRISE-ERP-MANAGEMENT-FUNCTION-AUTHENTICATION
new_control_requirements.description: An enterprise platform must authenticate every management-plane and identity-bearing function before it can be invoked, and must not expose any takeover-capable function to an unauthenticated network caller. Segment the management surface from untrusted networks and place it behind authenticated access control. The distinguishing test: send an unauthenticated network request to each such endpoint on a staging instance and confirm it is refused before any privileged action runs - paper access-control policies that attest user-login authentication while leaving a takeover-capable function reachable without credentials still permit unauthenticated takeover.
new_control_requirements.evidence: The control as inventoried names ERP platforms (PeopleSoft, E-Business Suite, SAP); SharePoint is a collaboration platform, and this is the closest existing control rather than an exact category match. The requirement transfers exactly: SharePoint's server-to-server token endpoint is a takeover-capable function reachable without credentials, and the distinguishing test the control specifies — send an unauthenticated request and confirm refusal before any privileged action runs — is the test that fails on every build below the July 2026 fix and the test that no identity-management or access-control assessment performs.

CVE-2026-65400.name: Apple macOS Screen Sharing Improper Authentication Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: screensharingd's SRP frame-length validator returns a stale success status, so the daemon marks the connection authenticated and continues without the cryptographic protection SRP should have produced. From that state the root-owned helpers SSFileCopySender and SSFileCopyReceiver provide arbitrary file read and write as root, which the public exploit converts to code execution by writing a LaunchDaemon plist or replacing a binary. Apple's fix is described as improved state management.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N and UI:N. The bypass precedes every account check, so the allowed-users list, the VNC password and account hygiene are all downstream of it.
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L. One connection to TCP/5900, deterministic, with public read-only and read/write exploits available. The only gate is whether Screen Sharing is enabled and the port reachable.
attack_vector.ai_factor: None recorded. Apple credits Alfredo Pesoli (@__rev) via Bynario Atlas; no AI tooling appears in Apple's advisory, in Huntress's analysis or in the NCSC-NL reporting, and the public exploits are hand-written Python.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Taking macOS Sequoia 15.7.9, Sonoma 14.8.9 or Tahoe 26.6.1 after their 2026-08-06 release and restarting; or, where that could not land inside CISA's 2026-08-21 date, disabling Screen Sharing and Remote Management or removing TCP/5900 reachability from untrusted networks.
prevention.adequacy: The update is complete for this CVE. Disabling the service is a genuine removal of the path rather than a filter, and is the only measure deployable inside a three-day window on a fleet. What must be stated alongside it is what does not work: pruning allowed users, disabling legacy VNC password authentication and rotating the VNC password are all evaluated behind the bypass, and an administrator who applies them has changed nothing.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alerting on Endpoint Security ES_EVENT_TYPE_NOTIFY_SCREENSHARING_ATTACH events with authentication_type SRP rather than RSA-SRP, and on any Screen Sharing session whose username is root; network-side, matching the RFB 003.889 banner on 5900 and flagging sessions that continue without the expected cryptographic protection.
detection.adequacy: The Endpoint Security discriminator is precise and cheap, and the public Zeek package covers the network half. Both depend on the estate collecting macOS Endpoint Security telemetry or inspecting 5900 at all, which is exactly the gap on the standalone and lab Macs most likely to be exposing the service.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating an exposed, unpatched host as rooted: inventory /Library/LaunchDaemons/ for new plists, check /var/root/.ssh/authorized_keys and user authorized_keys files, look for xmrig in /tmp and ~/Downloads, review pf rules and log integrity, and rebuild from a known-good image rather than updating in place. Rotate any credential, certificate or token the root account could read.
response.adequacy: The artefact list is concrete because Resecurity and NCSC-NL published it. Its weakness is the anti-forensic step in the same list: cleared or truncated logs and modified pf rules mean a clean hunt on a host that was exposed between 2026-08-06 and patching is not evidence of a clean history, which is why rebuild rather than in-place update is the safe default.

NIST-800-53-IA-2.gap: Every IA-2 artefact for Screen Sharing — allowed-users list, account inventory, VNC password state — is evaluated on the far side of the flaw. Apple's fix, 'an authentication issue was addressed with improved state management', names the problem: the enforcement mechanism reported success without performing, and IA-2 has no test for an authenticator reaching an authenticated state no credential produced.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: Apple released the fixed builds on 2026-08-06 against a 2026-08-21 KEV date, so a patch process measured from vendor release reports compliance. NCSC-NL's incidents were hosts already rooted with XMRig installed, where applying the update satisfies the obligation and leaves the LaunchDaemon and planted keys in place — Article 21's patch limb does not convert an exploitation report into a recovery obligation.

UK-CAF-B2.gap: B2's documented answer for Screen Sharing is the allowed-users list plus a VNC password, and both are what this flaw steps in front of; Apple's fix changes neither. A B2 assessment recording Screen Sharing as access-controlled before 2026-08-06 was recording controls that were never reached.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: The window from Apple's 2026-08-06 release to CISA's 2026-08-21 date fits inside even the model's faster bands, so the control reports success without applying pressure. It also has no field for the mitigation that actually removes exposure on a Mac that must defer the update — disabling Screen Sharing or removing TCP/5900 reachability.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.21.gap: An A.8.21 record naming SRP as Screen Sharing's security mechanism is accurate and useless, because the defect is the SRP state machine returning a stale success and continuing in cleartext. The control distinguishes services that offer an authentication mechanism from those that do not; it has no test distinguishing SRP offered from SRP performed.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2026-65400 — KEV-listed 2026-08-18 with a 2026-08-21 due date, three days, against a fleet-wide OS update that needs a restart on every host. The compensating-controls limb is what makes the SLA satisfiable: disabling Screen Sharing and Remote Management removes reachability immediately and needs no reboot, while 15.7.9 / 14.8.9 / 26.6.1 roll out behind it.

new_control_requirements.name: AI-INFERENCE-SERVER-AUTH-ENFORCEMENT
new_control_requirements.description: Authentication on a service's control plane must be enforced on every request path and proven complete, not assumed from the presence of an authentication mechanism.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2026-65400 — attached as the closest existing control for authentication completeness, noting its description is written for AI inference servers while the service here is macOS screensharingd. The requirement matches exactly: Huntress records the SRP frame-length validator returning a stale success so the connection is treated as authenticated, and Apple's fix is 'improved state management'. Proving the authenticator cannot reach a success state without a credential is the test that would have caught this, and it is the test neither IA-2 nor A.8.21 contains.

new_control_requirements.name: PERIMETER-COMPROMISE-REBUILD-NOT-PATCH
new_control_requirements.description: Pre-rehearsed IR runbook for any device that suffers a pre-auth RCE CVE in active exploitation MUST default to config-exfil + rebuild + credential rotation, not patch-in-place. Patch-in-place leaves attacker-installed implants intact.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2026-65400 — attached as the closest existing control, noting it is written for perimeter devices while the exposed assets here are macOS hosts. It applies for the same reason: NCSC-NL reported root access and XMRig installation on every internet-exposed Mac it was notified about, and Resecurity records LaunchDaemon persistence, authorized_keys additions, modified pf rules and cleared logs. Updating to 15.7.9 or 26.6.1 removes the bypass and leaves all of that running, which is precisely the failure this control exists to prevent.

attack_vector.description: JavaScript on a visited page uses the onpropertychange event handler to free a CDisplayPointer object in mshtml.dll while CDoc::ScrollPointerIntoView still holds a reference to it. Reclaiming the freed allocation with attacker-controlled data turns the stale reference into a controlled pointer dereference and code execution inside the Internet Explorer process, at the privileges of the user browsing. The in-the-wild exploit was served from web pages and gated so that it ran only for its intended targets — Internet Explorer 8 on Windows XP, for Korean and Japanese victims.
attack_vector.privileges_required: None on the target host, but the user must visit the page (UI:R). Code lands at the browsing user's privilege level, so the flaw is initial access; anything beyond the user's own data requires a second escalation.
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L. The exploitation primitive is ordinary script, and from 2013-10-08 a Metasploit module made a working exploit available to anyone. What limited the observed attacks was deliberate targeting, not technical difficulty.
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. The flaw surfaced as a live in-the-wild exploit found by Websense Security Labs and analysed by hand; no automated discovery or AI assistance is credited by Microsoft, Websense or Palo Alto Networks.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Installing MS13-080 / KB2879017 on 2013-10-08 and restarting, or — for hosts where Internet Explorer serves no purpose — removing user reachability to the browser entirely, which closes the delivery path without depending on an update channel.
prevention.adequacy: Complete for the CVE and unavailable for the twenty days that mattered: Websense observed exploitation from 2013-09-18 and the update did not exist until 2013-10-08. On hosts still running Windows XP after 2014-04-08 the update channel closes for good, and the only adequate prevention left is removing the host or the browser.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alerting on iexplore.exe spawning child processes, and reconciling repeated mshtml.dll faults in Windows Error Reporting against browsing history rather than treating them as stability noise.
detection.adequacy: Workable and heavily dependent on where the campaign chose to fire. Because the exploit served itself only to a narrow victim profile, an estate outside that profile sees nothing at all — absence of detections is not evidence the page was not visited, only that it did not return the exploit.
