AU-Essential-8-App-Hardening.gap: User application hardening reduces the attack surface of the user applications on an endpoint - browsers, Office and document readers - and its Office-side reach is the part that bears on this CVE, since what Office is permitted to activate as an embedded object determines whether an OLE-embedded SWF ever reaches the Flash control at all. Two things it does not settle. Hardening is applied and evidenced per application, and this runtime is resident three ways on one host - the browser plugin, the standalone player, and the ActiveX control Office invokes - so a baseline attested against the browsers leaves the third surface at 11.3.300.270. And hardening configures an application the organisation still runs, while the component carrying the defect is a withdrawn runtime with no supported version to configure toward: the action this CVE now requires is removal, which belongs to end-of-life decommissioning rather than to a hardening baseline.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: Management of technical vulnerabilities requires an accurate picture of where the vulnerable component sits. Flash Player of this era is present as a browser plugin, a standalone player and an ActiveX control invoked by Office, and the exploited path was the third - an inventory that records 'Flash Player, version 11.3.300.270' as one line per host cannot answer which of those surfaces is reachable, which is the question that decides whether uninstalling the browser plugin actually removed the exposure.

new_control_requirements.name: EMBEDDED-MEDIA-PARSER-LIBRARY-INVENTORY-AND-PATCH-PARITY
new_control_requirements.description: An organization must inventory every place a high-risk embedded media-parsing library (font, image, codec and document parsers) is statically or dynamically bundled - including copies vendored inside individual applications - and apply the security update to all of them, not only the OS-level package.
new_control_requirements.evidence: The parser here is Flash Player's own OpenType font handler, and Flash of this era is bundled at least three ways on one Windows host: the NPAPI browser plugin, the standalone player, and the ActiveX control that Office invokes for an embedded SWF. The exploited path was the third - NVD records exploitation 'with SWF content in a Word document' - so an estate that updated the browser plugin and left the ActiveX control at 11.3.300.270 remained fully exposed while its inventory read as patched. The distinguishing test is per-surface: after the update, confirm the ActiveX control's registered version as well as the plugin's, because APSB12-18's fixed versions (11.3.300.271 Windows/Mac, 11.2.202.238 Linux) apply per installed build, not per host.

new_control_requirements.name: EOL-ASSET-DECOMMISSION
new_control_requirements.description: Network-reachable end-of-life components with no vendor patch path must be isolated and decommissioned within a bounded window; mandatory compensating segmentation applies until removal since no remediation exists.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Attached as the closest existing control, and it is a software runtime rather than the network-attached device the control is written around - stated so the fit is not overread. What transfers exactly is the terminal state: Adobe ended Flash Player support on 2020-12-31 and began blocking Flash content on 2021-01-12, so a surviving installation has no upgrade destination for this CVE or any later one, and the compensating measure until removal is keeping the host away from untrusted documents rather than segmenting a listening port. The bounded window matters because the exploit is not theoretical - a Metasploit module with build-specific ROP chains has been public since 2012-08-17, and EPSS still put the CVE at 0.70384, the 99.354th percentile, on 2026-08-28.

new_control_requirements.name: ARCHIVE-CONTENT-TYPE-PROVENANCE
new_control_requirements.description: Archive and document handlers must dispatch rendering and execution on the content-verified file type rather than the displayed name or extension, and must propagate Mark-of-the-Web to every extracted file.
new_control_requirements.evidence: The delivery route for this zero-day was a Word document that reached a Flash runtime: the user opened a .doc, and Office dispatched an embedded OLE object to the Flash ActiveX control, which then parsed an attacker-supplied OpenType font. The provenance question this control asks - what is this content really, and where did it come from - is exactly the one the document handler did not ask before handing the payload to a media parser. For this CVE the control means the document handler treats an embedded active object as content whose type must be verified and whose internet origin must follow it into the component that renders it, so that an emailed attachment does not silently reach a font parser with local trust.

CVE-2012-0507.name: Oracle Java SE AtomicReferenceArray Type Confusion (CVE-2012-0507)

attack_vector.description: Deserialising an AtomicReferenceArray without verifying the backing array is an Object[], combined with direct reference stores through sun.misc.Unsafe, gives an untrusted applet a type confusion. That is enough to reach a privileged ClassLoader, define a class with full permissions, and turn off the SecurityManager — after which the applet is an ordinary local process. Delivery was a web page serving a JAR.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — an unauthenticated remote page, with the user's browser visit as the only action required.
attack_vector.complexity: low — Oracle scored it CVSSv2 10.0 and called it easily exploitable. Being a logic flaw rather than memory corruption, it is deterministic and cross-platform from a single exploit body, which is why it reached commodity exploit kits within weeks.
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Reported to Oracle on 2011-08-01 and fixed in the February 2012 CPU; the mechanism was published by third-party researchers whom NVD records Oracle never confirmed.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Moving to 1.7.0_03, 1.6.0_31 or 1.5.0_34, or — faster and not dependent on a vendor — disabling the Java browser plugin, which removes the untrusted-applet and Web Start path Oracle names as the only one.
prevention.adequacy: The patch was adequate where Oracle shipped the runtime and inadequate where Apple did: an entity current on Oracle CPUs still had exploitable Macs until Apple released separately, which is the interval Flashback used. The configuration route had no such dependency and was available on day one.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alerting on the JVM creating child processes, and antivirus coverage for the exploit class — Microsoft shipped Exploit:Java/CVE-2012-0507 as a named detection.
detection.adequacy: Serviceable but late. The escape itself happens entirely inside the JVM and produces no host event; the first observable is the child process, by which point arbitrary code is already running as the user. Signature detection worked against Blackhole output and less well against the targeted SabPub delivery.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating a hit as user-context compromise: credential rotation for the account, and on macOS a check for the Flashback and SabPub persistence artefacts rather than assuming the platform was not a target.
response.adequacy: Adequate in scope, undermined by an assumption of the period — that macOS was not a malware platform. Flashback's 600,000-plus infections and SabPub's link to Luckycat both landed on machines where the response playbook did not exist.

NIST-800-53-CM-7.gap: Least functionality is the control that fully closes this CVE and it is assessed at the wrong granularity. Oracle scopes exploitation to untrusted applets and Web Start only, so 'is the browser plugin enabled' is the whole question and 'is Java installed' is not it — a headless JRE on a build agent is not exposed and scores identically to a plugin-enabled workstation that is.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: The measure presumes the software vendor is the patch vendor. On Mac OS X the Java runtime came from Apple, not Oracle, so an entity that applied the February 2012 CPU on the day it shipped still had an exploitable estate — and that gap, not any failure to patch, is what Flashback monetised in April 2012.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: The protection B4 would credit here is the Java sandbox, and the flaw is a sandbox escape reached in a single type confusion. Oracle's matrix records the result as operating-system takeover, so the assessed protection and the actual outcome are unrelated.

AU-Essential-8-App-Hardening.gap: Blocking Java from the internet in browsers is the correct answer and the assessment does not price the exception. Estates kept the plugin enabled for a line-of-business applet under a documented exemption, and those machines carried the entire risk while the maturity score reflected the policy rather than the carve-out.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: The register cannot answer the two questions that decide exposure — whether the JRE is reachable from a browser, and whether it comes from Oracle or Apple — because software inventory records neither. CISA's 2022 KEV listing, a decade after the fixed baselines shipped, indicates registers that never closed it.

new_control_requirements.name: CONFIGURATION-SIDE-LIVE-PATCH-INVENTORY
new_control_requirements.description: For any client-side vulnerability with a configuration-side mitigation path: that path must be inventoried, tested and deployable independent of the vendor-patch path, so operators are not gated on a vendor release.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Oracle scoped this flaw to untrusted applets and Java Web Start only, which makes disabling the browser plugin complete remediation rather than a partial mitigation. That mattered because the patch path was not uniform: Oracle shipped 1.7.0_03, 1.6.0_31 and 1.5.0_34 in February 2012, but Mac OS X took its runtime from Apple on a separate schedule, and the Flashback campaign that reached more than 600,000 Macs in April 2012 ran inside that gap. Every one of those hosts could have been closed by configuration on the day Oracle published.

new_control_requirements.name: EOL-ASSET-DECOMMISSION
new_control_requirements.description: Software with no vendor patch path must be isolated and decommissioned within a bounded window; mandatory compensating configuration applies until removal.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Java SE 5.0 was already outside its public update stream when the February 2012 CPU shipped 5.0u34, and the browser-plugin runtimes that carried this exploit on consumer and macOS estates had no managed update channel at all. CISA's 2022 KEV listing of a 2012 CVE with a Known ransomware association is the measurement of how long an unretired client runtime stays exploitable.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: The operative word for this entry is verified, and the verification target is the runtime the browser loads rather than the newest JRE present — a workstation with 1.6.0_31 installed alongside an older plugin-registered runtime is not remediated. CISA listed the CVE on 2022-03-03 with a 2022-03-24 due date and a Known ransomware association, ten years after the fixed baselines shipped, so the SLA has to be measured against browser-visible runtime state, not against install date.

CVE-2011-3544.name: Oracle Java SE Rhino Script Engine Sandbox Escape (CVE-2011-3544)

attack_vector.description: An untrusted applet builds an Error object carrying a custom toString() that is later invoked from a privileged context inside the Rhino script engine. The applet's code escapes the sandbox, disables the SecurityManager and executes arbitrary Java as the browsing user. Oracle records the sub-component as Scripting with a CVSS 2.0 base of 10.0 and Note 1 confining the reach to untrusted applets and untrusted Java Web Start applications.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — the attacker needs no account; the victim only has to load a page that serves the applet.
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L, no configuration precondition beyond the plugin being installed and enabled. The Metasploit module ships four platform targets and states it works on any Java-capable browser.
attack_vector.ai_factor: Found by hand by a named researcher, Michael Schierl, and disclosed through ZDI as ZDI-11-305. The finding is from 2011 and no automated discovery is claimed by any party.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Removing or disabling the Java browser plugin and Java Web Start, which closes the only paths Oracle documents at any JRE version, and applying the Java SE Critical Patch Update of 2011-10-18 or later.
prevention.adequacy: The plugin removal is complete and version-independent, which is why it outlived the patch as the operative control. The patch itself is complete but only takes effect once every browser process holding the old plugin has been closed.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Process-lineage alerting on a JVM launched from a browser and then spawning a child or connecting outbound, together with the Exploit:Java/CVE-2011-3544 detection family already shipped by anti-malware vendors.
detection.adequacy: Signature detection was mature for this CVE because it ran in commodity kits for years, but it fires after the applet has executed, so it bounds dwell time rather than preventing the escape.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating any host with a family detection as a second-stage investigation rather than a cleanup, since kit delivery of this exploit existed to install something else.
response.adequacy: The exploit itself leaves little; what matters is the payload, and identifying that requires telemetry from the moment of the applet load rather than from the moment of detection.

NIST-800-53-CM-7.gap: The control that would have closed this completely is also the one whose baselines do not enumerate the relevant item. CM-7 lists services, ports, protocols and installed software; the Java browser plugin registration is a side effect of installing a runtime for something else, so it is invisible to the baseline while being the entire attack surface Oracle's Note 1 identifies.

NIS2-Art21-vulnerability-handling.gap: A handling process consumes advisories, and there are none for an unsupported runtime. An entity running Java 6 for a legacy application receives no vendor input, records no open finding, and is compliant, while the EPSS score on 2026-08-28 sits at the 99.882nd percentile. The measure has no trigger for a component whose vendor has stopped publishing.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: The outcome examines secure configuration and management but does not direct the assessor at whether a browser will hand untrusted content to a runtime. An estate can be assessed as achieving B4 while every workstation will still execute an attacker's applet, because the configuration item that decides it is created by an installer rather than by policy.

AU-Essential-8-App-Hardening.gap: The strategy directs that browsers do not process Java from the internet, which closes the applet half. It says nothing about the Java Web Start handler, which Oracle names in the same Note 1 as the other route to this code, so an estate at the strategy's top maturity can still reach the defect through a .jnlp the user is persuaded to open.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: The control's evaluation step is fed by a fifteen-year-old CVSS 2.0 score, which cannot distinguish a historical finding that stayed theoretical from one that shipped in commodity exploit kits for years. The distinguishing input exists — EPSS 0.96714 at the 99.882nd percentile — but A.8.8 does not require it, so both findings are evaluated identically.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: For an unsupported runtime the operative clause is the one accepting documented compensating controls, because for an estate pinned to Java 6 no vendor patch path exists at all. Disabling the browser plugin and Java Web Start is deployable in that window and closes the only vector Oracle's Note 1 documents. CISA added the CVE on 2022-03-03 with a 2022-03-24 due date; the vulnerability-handling measure produced no obligation at all across that period because the vendor was publishing nothing for the deployed versions.

new_control_requirements.name: EOL-ASSET-DECOMMISSION
new_control_requirements.description: Network-reachable end-of-life software and devices with no vendor patch path must be isolated and decommissioned within a bounded window; mandatory compensating segmentation applies until removal since no remediation exists.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Removing the runtime is the only action that closes every path at once. Blocking Java in the browser leaves the Web Start handler that Oracle's Note 1 names alongside applets; keeping the JRE for a legacy application leaves an unsupported component with a CVSS 2.0 10.0 and an EPSS of 0.96714 at the 99.882nd percentile on 2026-08-28. The bounded-window requirement is what none of the four covering controls supplies — CM-7 does not enumerate the plugin, B4 does not ask about it, the app-hardening strategy stops at the browser, and A.8.8 has no disposition for a component with no fix stream.

CVE-2011-1889.name: Microsoft Forefront TMG Client Winsock Provider Remote Code Execution Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: The Forefront TMG 2010 Client installs a Winsock layered service provider that every Winsock application on the host loads. Its NSPLookupServiceNext implementation did not bound the data it copied out of a name-service lookup response, so specific requests handled through the client corrupt memory inside the calling application and run code in that application's security context. MS11-040 fixed it by setting proper bounds on the function.
attack_vector.privileges_required: The retrofitted CVSS 3.1 vector says PR:N and UI:N. Microsoft's own framing is narrower: the attacker leverages a client computer to make specific requests, and networked clients running the TMG firewall client are the systems primarily at risk — so what is needed is a position able to shape the lookups the provider processes.
attack_vector.complexity: The bulletin records no mitigating factors and rates the issue Critical. Against that, no public exploit has ever appeared for this CVE, so exploitation requires original work against a discontinued Winsock provider rather than running a published tool.
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. The bulletin predates AI-assisted vulnerability research by years, and no AI tooling appears anywhere in the disclosure or in the KEV record.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Applying MS11-040 / KB2520426 and restarting, verified by client file version 7.0.7734.182. Where that was not possible, Microsoft's own tested workaround: disable the TMG 2010 Client, which stops FwcWsp.dll and FwcWsp64.dll loading into Winsock applications.
prevention.adequacy: The update is complete for this CVE and has been available since 2011-06-14. Its adequacy expired as a posture rather than as a fix: extended support for Forefront TMG 2010 ended on 2020-04-14, so from that date the patched client is simply the last version that will ever exist, and the workaround — disabling the client — becomes the only lever for any future defect in the same provider.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Enumerating the Winsock catalog for FwcWsp.dll and FwcWsp64.dll to find which hosts load the provider at all, then checking client file version against 7.0.7734.182 and watching for crashes in ordinary Winsock applications with the provider on the faulting stack.
detection.adequacy: Winsock-catalog enumeration is reliable and is the only method that finds the surface, because the provider is inside other processes rather than in a service of its own. Version checking is the weak half: MS11-040 states that no registry key verification exists for this update, so the check has to read a file version, and the update-detection tooling the bulletin names — MBSA, SMS 2003 ITMU, Configuration Manager 2007 — is retired.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating a suspected hit as code execution inside whatever application made the call: capture the process, disable the TMG 2010 Client on the affected hosts to remove the provider from the socket path, and rotate credentials the affected user context could reach.
response.adequacy: Disabling the client is decisive and available immediately. Response is otherwise poorly served here because there is nothing to hunt for: no public exploit, no campaign report and no published indicators exist for this CVE, so an investigation has only the crash artefact and the host's own telemetry to work from.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: An SI-2 finding closes truthfully once MS11-040 is installed, and has been able to since 2011-06-14. What it cannot express is that the product left extended support on 2020-04-14, two years before the 2022-03-03 KEV listing: SI-2 records a patch state, not a servicing state, and the host keeps loading an unserviced provider into every Winsock process.

NIS2-Art21-vulnerability-handling.gap: The obligation assumes a supplier still issuing fixes. Extended support ended 2020-04-14, so there are no future advisories to ingest and no clock to run. The only remaining action is the workaround Microsoft published in 2011 — disable the TMG 2010 Client — which Article 21 does not frame as vulnerability handling.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: A B4 build review inventories installed applications and records the TMG 2010 Client as required, because outbound access depends on it. It does not record that the client is a layered service provider inserting FwcWsp.dll and FwcWsp64.dll into the socket path of every process, which is where the attack surface actually is.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: The requirement to remove vendor-unsupported applications is the operative limb, and Forefront TMG 2010 crossed that line on 2020-04-14 — but removing the client breaks the outbound path the TMG deployment provides, so it becomes an exception. The model grades the exception on the application and has no input for the unserviced provider the exception keeps inside every Winsock process.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: MS11-040 names MBSA, SMS 2003 with ITMU and Configuration Manager 2007 as its detection tooling, all retired, and records that no registry key verification exists — confirmation depends on reading the client's file version. Whether a current platform still carries that check is not established by anything found for this CVE, and A.8.8 has no limb requiring the organisation to establish it: the control obliges a vulnerability-management process to exist, not to prove it can see a given component, so an unknown result and a clean result look the same in its output.

new_control_requirements.name: EOL-ASSET-DECOMMISSION
new_control_requirements.description: Network-reachable end-of-life devices with no vendor patch path must be isolated and decommissioned within a bounded window; mandatory compensating segmentation applies until removal.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2011-1889 — attached as the closest existing end-of-life control, noting it is written for devices while the unserviced artefact here is a client-side Winsock provider. Forefront TMG 2010 left extended support on 2020-04-14 and CISA listed this CVE on 2022-03-03, so from the listing date the estate was carrying a component that could take no further update. The control's bounded decommission window and mandatory interim compensating measure map directly onto Microsoft's own workaround of disabling the TMG 2010 Client.

new_control_requirements.name: SCANNER-PAPER-COMPLIANCE-TEST
new_control_requirements.description: A vulnerability scanner that reports 'patched' based on kernel package version alone is paper compliance. The operational test: does the scan account for the actual mitigation surface, and does it verify the build carries the specific patch rather than merely a version newer than it?
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2011-1889 — attached as the closest existing control on scanner-derived verdicts, noting its description is framed around kernel packages while the artefact here is a Windows client-side Winsock provider. MS11-040 states that no registry key verification exists for KB2520426 and that installation is confirmed by file version 7.0.7734.182, and the tools it names as detecting the update — MBSA, SMS 2003 ITMU and Configuration Manager 2007 — are all retired products. The operational test this control demands is therefore concrete and cheap here: stage a host known to be missing KB2520426 and confirm the platform reports it, rather than accepting a clean verdict that may reflect no check having run against this component at all.

new_control_requirements.name: KERNEL-MODULE-INVENTORY-AND-DISABLE
new_control_requirements.description: Maintain an inventory of loaded kernel modules. For modules not required for business function (RxRPC, unused crypto modules), disable via modprobe blacklist as a least-functionality control. Review quarterly.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2011-1889 — attached as the closest existing least-functionality-on-loaded-components control, noting its description is written for Linux kernel modules and modprobe blacklists. The Windows form here is the Winsock catalog: FwcWsp.dll and FwcWsp64.dll load into every Winsock application on a TMG-client host, so an application inventory sees one optional client while the real surface is a provider inside every process. Microsoft's own MS11-040 workaround — disable the TMG 2010 Client — is exactly the disable step this control requires.

CVE-2011-0611.name: Adobe Flash Player Remote Code Execution Vulnerability (CVE-2011-0611)

attack_vector.description: A crafted .swf carries a size inconsistency in a group of included constants which the ActionScript runtime resolves into an object type confusion; ActionScript that adds custom functions to prototypes and uses Date objects grooms the heap so that the mismatched type overwrites a pointer and redirects execution. The same file runs in the browser plug-in, in the standalone Adobe AIR runtime, and in Authplay.dll / AuthPlayLib.bundle inside Reader and Acrobat — which is how Adobe's APSA11-02 describes the observed attacks reaching victims: a .swf embedded in a Word or Excel file sent as an email attachment, with no browser in the path.
attack_vector.privileges_required: None on the target. UI:R — the user opens a document or visits a page. Code runs at the user's privilege level in whichever runtime hosted the .swf.
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L, and lowered further by Exploit-DB 17175 and the Metasploit module adobe_flashplayer_flash10o shortly after disclosure. The complexity that remains is entirely on the defending side: one CVE, four affected products, and one platform (Reader X on Windows) that had no binary fix for two months.
attack_vector.ai_factor: None recorded, and none plausible for 2011. Adobe's advisories credit no finder and mention no tooling; the discovery source is recorded as unknown rather than assumed.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Taking the 2011-04-15 updates on every affected runtime rather than only the browser plug-in: Flash Player 10.2.159.1, Android 10.2.157.51, AIR 2.6.19140, and Reader / Acrobat 9.4.4 or 10.0.3. On Windows Reader X, where Adobe shipped no fix until 2011-06-14, the vendor's own position was that Protected Mode blocked exploitation — so the equivalent action there was verifying Protected Mode was enabled, not waiting.
prevention.adequacy: Adequate only if all four paths were walked. Updating the browser plug-in alone — the reflex when a CVE is filed under 'Flash Player' — leaves Authplay.dll inside Reader and Acrobat untouched, which is the exact component Adobe says the in-the-wild attacks used. On a current estate none of this applies: Flash support ended 2020-12-31 and removal is the only complete answer.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alerting on Office applications and PDF readers spawning child processes, and on AcroRd32 or Acrobat loading Authplay.dll during document rendering; mail inspection for Office attachments containing an embedded SWF stream.
detection.adequacy: The process-tree signal is strong and generic; the Authplay load is the specific one and it is only visible where module-load telemetry is collected, which is a deeper collection tier than process creation. Neither helps if the .swf arrived through the browser plug-in instead, where rendering Flash was ordinary behaviour in 2011.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating a confirmed document open as user-context execution: capture the attachment and its embedded .swf, preserve the process tree and outbound connections from the rendering application, rotate the user's credentials, and remove the Flash-bearing runtimes from the host rather than only updating them.
response.adequacy: Sound, and its weak point is scoping — the mail that delivered the document reached more mailboxes than the one that triggered the alert, so the response has to be a mail-corpus search rather than a host investigation. On modern estates the removal step is unambiguous, since Adobe blocks Flash content from 2021-01-12 and no supported configuration needs the runtime.

NIST-800-53-CM-7.gap: Least functionality would close this by removing components, and four separately removable components carry the flaw. But an inventory that lists 'Adobe Reader 9.4.3' as an approved application never names the Flash interpreter bundled inside it, so the component whose removal matters is invisible to the control that authorises removals.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: One CVE, four vendor fixes on three dates — and for Reader X on Windows, no binary fix at all until 2011-06-14, only Adobe's statement that Protected Mode prevents exploitation. Article 21(2)(e) has no state for vendor-asserted mitigation without a patch, so the entity either records the CVE as open for two months or records it as closed on a claim.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: B4 gives the same verdict to a configured, click-to-play Flash plug-in as it would to a maintained component. Adobe ended Flash Player support on 2020-12-31 and blocks Flash content from 2021-01-12; on a current estate the hardened state is absence, and the assessment has no way to say so.

AU-Essential-8-App-Hardening.gap: The mitigation is scoped to browsers, Office and PDF software not processing Flash content. Adobe AIR is none of those and NVD lists AIR before 2.6.19140 as separately affected, so an AIR application on the desktop keeps the vulnerable ActionScript interpreter with the browser and Office policy fully enforced.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: The failure is at identification, not prioritisation. Authplay.dll and AuthPlayLib.bundle have no version of their own in an asset inventory, so a scan that correctly reports the Reader version has already reported the vulnerable runtime without naming it — and remediation planned from that inventory chases the plug-in and misses the document path Adobe says was exploited.

new_control_requirements.name: EMBEDDED-MEDIA-PARSER-LIBRARY-INVENTORY-AND-PATCH-PARITY
new_control_requirements.description: An organization must inventory every place a high-risk embedded media-parsing library (FreeType, image/codec/font/document parsers) is statically or dynamically bundled - including inside other vendors' products - and drive remediation from that inventory rather than from the top-level product version.
new_control_requirements.evidence: This CVE is the bundling problem in its purest form: the vulnerable ActionScript interpreter ships as the Flash plug-in, as the standalone AIR runtime, and as Authplay.dll / AuthPlayLib.bundle inside Adobe Reader and Acrobat — and Adobe's APSA11-02 says the in-the-wild attacks used the last of those, via a .swf embedded in a Word or Excel attachment. Adobe's own fixes reflect the split: 10.2.159.1 and AIR 2.6.19140 on 2011-04-15, Reader and Acrobat 9.4.4 / 10.0.3 in a separate bulletin, and nothing for Windows Reader X until 2011-06-14. An inventory keyed on top-level product versions reports 'Reader 9.4.3' and never names the interpreter inside it, so the remediation that closes the exploited path is the one no ticket exists for.

new_control_requirements.name: MITIGATION-ACTIVE-PATCH-PENDING-VERDICT-CLASS
new_control_requirements.description: Compliance verdicts must distinguish three states: (a) binary patch deployed (vulnerability eliminated), (b) vendor-mitigation rule active, no binary patch (residual risk: any defect in the mitigation re-opens the flaw), (c) neither.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Adobe Reader X for Windows sat in state (b) for two months by the vendor's own design. APSB11-08 shipped no fix for that platform; Adobe stated Reader X Protected Mode mitigations would prevent an exploit of this kind from executing and scheduled the binary fix for the 2011-06-14 quarterly update. NVD encodes the same split — Reader 10.x 'through 10.0.1' affected on Windows against '10.x before 10.0.3' on macOS. A two-state compliance model forces that estate to be recorded either as unpatched-overdue or as patched, and both are wrong: the accurate statement is that a sandbox the vendor vouches for is holding, and that the residual risk is a Protected Mode escape.

CVE-2010-3333.name: Microsoft Office RTF pFragments Stack Buffer Overflow

attack_vector.description: An RTF document or rich-text mail message carrying an over-long pFragments shape property. Word's RTF parser copies it into a fixed stack buffer with no length bound, overwriting the return address and executing attacker code with the rights of the logged-on user. From Office 2007 onward Outlook calls the same parser to render rich-text mail, so previewing a message reaches the flaw without a file being opened.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none - code runs as the user who opens or previews the document
attack_vector.complexity: low - a plain stack overflow against releases with no meaningful exploit mitigations, packaged as a Metasploit file-format module
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Disclosed and fixed in 2010, weaponised publicly the same period, and in continuous builder-kit use long before AI-assisted exploit development existed.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Apply the MS10-087 update for each installed Office product. Where that lags, deploy the RTF File Block policy and configure Outlook to read mail in plain text - both are published in the bulletin and both are policy-deployable.
prevention.adequacy: Sufficient against this CVE. Every affected Office release has since left support, so on a surviving host the honest remediation is migration rather than the 2010 update.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alert on WINWORD.EXE or OUTLOOK.EXE creating a child process or writing an executable, and inspect RTF for an over-long pFragments value at the mail gateway.
detection.adequacy: Process-lineage detection is decisive and cheap. Content inspection is worth having but was widely evaded at the time - Microsoft's own family signature exists because generic RTF parsing checks were not catching the samples.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treat a hit as user-context compromise on the endpoint, pull the delivering message from every mailbox it reached, and check for the downloader behaviour Microsoft documents rather than assuming the exploit was the whole payload.
response.adequacy: Adequate where mail-gateway retention allows the message to be traced to all recipients; the Outlook preview path means recipients who never consciously opened anything are in scope.

NIST-800-53-CM-7.gap: Least functionality is the control that matches the available mitigation exactly - MS10-087 ships an RTF File Block policy - and it is the control least likely to be applied to a document format the organisation's own users exchange. Worse, CM-7 is normally assessed against installed software and enabled services, and the RTF parser is neither: it is a code path inside Word that Outlook 2007 and later call to render a message, so nothing in a CM-7 inventory records that disabling RTF has an email-side effect.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: MS10-087 was released on 2010-11-09. CISA added the CVE to KEV on 2022-03-03 with a 2022-03-24 due date, eleven years later, because the exploit stayed in active use against installs that never took the update. Article 21's patch measure is written for a supported product estate; every Office release named in MS10-087 has since left support, so the obligation it generates on a surviving host is removal, which the measure does not express.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: Secure configuration for Office is assessed on macro policy, add-in control and trusted locations. None of those sit on this path: the exploit is a malformed property in the RTF body parsed before any macro decision is reached, so a B4 baseline that records Office as hardened to the recommended settings is describing controls that the pFragments overflow bypasses by construction.

AU-Essential-8-App-Hardening.gap: The Essential Eight's macro control is genuinely off this path - the exploit carries no macro, it is a stack overflow in the RTF parser - so an estate can be at full macro-configuration maturity and still render the document that carries the attack. User application hardening is not off the path. From Maturity Level Two it blocks Microsoft Office from creating child processes, from creating executable content and from injecting code into other processes, and it requires ACSC or vendor hardening guidance for Microsoft Office to be implemented, which is where MS10-087's File Block and plain-text-mail workarounds live. What the model does not do is name them: the hardening rung points at a guidance document rather than at a setting, so an assessment can record that guidance was followed without recording which of the bulletin's two mitigations is actually in place. The lineage blocks are also downstream of the overflow rather than on it - they stop the stage after the return address is taken, so an ML2-compliant host still executes attacker code inside WINWORD.EXE or OUTLOOK.EXE and loses the payload, not the parser defect. Maturity Level One asks for none of the Office rungs, so an estate at the model's entry level has nothing on this path at all.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: Technical vulnerability management driven from an application inventory sees 'Microsoft Office' and reconciles against the installed product's update state. It does not see that the same RTF parser is reached through two different products, so an estate that has patched Word but left an unpatched Office 2007 Outlook rendering rich-text mail retains the exposure, and A.8.8 evidence of an Office patching process does not distinguish the two.

new_control_requirements.name: CONFIGURATION-SIDE-LIVE-PATCH-INVENTORY
new_control_requirements.description: For any web-fabric vulnerability with a configuration-side mitigation path: that path must be inventoried, tested, and deployable independent of the vendor-patch path.
new_control_requirements.evidence: MS10-087 publishes two such paths and both are policy artefacts rather than code: the Office File Block policy for RTF (FileOpenBlock\RtfFiles = 1, or File Block Settings with Protected View in Office 2010) and reading Outlook mail in plain text. For this product the control means having those registry values and the Outlook setting staged for fleet push before a disclosure, knowing which business processes actually receive RTF, and having tested that File Block survives an Office update. Precondition: both are holding measures with user-visible cost - File Block refuses RTF from every source, and plain-text reading strips rich content from all mail, with Microsoft noting signed or encrypted messages are unaffected by the setting and still render in their original format.

new_control_requirements.name: EMBEDDED-MEDIA-PARSER-LIBRARY-INVENTORY-AND-PATCH-PARITY
new_control_requirements.description: An organization must inventory every place a high-risk embedded media-parsing library (FreeType, image/codec/font/document parsers) is statically or dynamically bundled.
new_control_requirements.evidence: This CVE is the document-parser case of exactly that shape. The RTF parser is Word's, but from Office 2007 onward Outlook calls it to render rich-text mail, which turns a file-open bug into a message-preview bug and doubles the affected surface without appearing twice in any inventory. The bulletin's own product list reinforces the point: the same parser ships in Office XP, 2003, 2007, 2010, three Mac releases and the Open XML File Format Converter for Mac, each patched by a different KB. The operational test is whether the estate can answer 'which products render RTF' without reading a Microsoft bulletin to find out.

new_control_requirements.name: MITIGATION-ACTIVE-PATCH-PENDING-VERDICT-CLASS
new_control_requirements.description: Compliance verdicts must distinguish binary-patch-deployed from vendor-mitigation-active-without-patch from no-mitigation-at-all, and must surface the middle state as a time-bound compensating control rather than as a patched-per-SLA outcome.
new_control_requirements.evidence: The three states are concrete here. Patched means the MS10-087 KB for that specific product is installed. Mitigated means File Block or plain-text reading is set while the update is pending - which stops the attack but leaves the parser defect and blocks legitimate RTF, so it needs a review date rather than a closure. Neither means the host renders attacker-supplied RTF with an unbounded copy in the parser. A verdict driven from 'Office is patched' cannot separate them, because each affected product carries its own KB and an estate can be current on Word while an Office 2007 Outlook still previews rich-text mail through the unpatched parser.

CVE-2010-0232.name: Windows NTVDM Kernel Exception Handler Privilege Escalation (KiTrap0D)

attack_vector.description: A user with local logon rights on a 32-bit x86 Windows host crafts a VDM_TIB structure in the Thread Environment Block and calls NtVdmControl to start the NTVDM subsystem. Certain BIOS calls in that state are not properly validated, and the general-protection fault they raise is mishandled by nt!KiTrap0D, leaving the attacker running arbitrary code in kernel mode. 64-bit editions are not affected, and the path closes entirely if 16-bit application access is disabled.
attack_vector.privileges_required: low (valid logon credentials and the ability to log on locally; Microsoft states the flaw cannot be exploited remotely or by anonymous users)
attack_vector.complexity: low and deterministic - no race, no memory grooming, and public exploit code has existed since 2010-01-19
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered. Exploit-DB 11199 is authored by Tavis Ormandy and predates the patch; MS10-015 credits him for the co-fixed CVE-2010-0233 and names no one for this id, which reached Microsoft as a public disclosure.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Apply MS10-015 (KB977165) and restart. Before the patch, or where a change window is unavailable, enable the vendor-tested workaround: 'Prevent access to 16-bit applications' under Administrative Templates / Windows Components / Application Compatibility, or its automated form in KB 979682.
prevention.adequacy: The patch is complete but needs a restart, and on a host whose operating-system files an infection has modified the post-2010-03-02 package logic will refuse to install it - so installation must be verified rather than assumed. The workaround is genuinely effective against the attack vector and costs every 16-bit application on the host.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alert on NtVdmControl calls and on ntvdm.exe launching from a parent that is not a user starting a 16-bit application, paired with local-to-SYSTEM transitions that carry no service installation or elevation record. Treat bugchecks implicating nt!KiTrap0D as attempted exploitation rather than as flaky hardware.
detection.adequacy: Workable precisely because the legitimate use is now vanishingly rare - on a modern estate any NTVDM activity is worth an alert. It is weak on the hosts that most need it, since the NT, 2000, XP and Server 2003 population that remains affected rarely carries an endpoint agent capable of producing that telemetry.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treat SYSTEM on the host as reached: rotate every credential cached on it, re-image rather than clean, and audit for accounts and services created during the window - the primitive gives kernel-mode execution, so nothing running on the host is authoritative afterwards.
response.adequacy: Necessary. Its weakness is scoping: with public exploit code available since January 2010 and no telemetry on most affected builds, the window an incident responder can bound is usually shorter than the window that was actually open.

NIST-800-53-CM-7.gap: Least functionality is the control that could have blocked this before February 2010, because Microsoft's own tested workaround is a least-functionality change: enable 'Prevent access to 16-bit applications' and the attack vector is gone. The gap is that CM-7 is assessed by confirming a documented baseline exists, and the state that matters here - 16-bit application support reachable - is the shipped default on every affected 32-bit install, so a baseline that was never written to disable it passes the assessment while leaving NTVDM callable by every logged-on user.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: Patch management can only apply what the vendor still publishes. MS10-015 dates from 2010-02-09 and most of the affected list - NT 3.1 through Vista and Server 2008 - has had no servicing channel for years, so when CISA set a 2022-03-24 due date there was no update to deploy on those hosts and the process has no state to record other than not-applicable. There is a second, quieter failure: the bulletin's 2010-03-02 revision makes the package refuse to install on systems whose operating-system files a virus has modified, so even on a serviceable host the patch-management report can read installed-and-compliant when the update never landed.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: System security expects the kernel to hold the boundary between a logged-on user and ring 0. Here the boundary fails inside the exception handler itself - the #GP trap handler nt!KiTrap0D mishandles the fault a crafted BIOS call produces after NtVdmControl starts the subsystem - so no hardening measure an operator can apply to the kernel changes the outcome. The only operator-side lever is removing the path to the subsystem entirely, which is a functionality decision rather than a system-security one, and it costs every 16-bit application on the host.

AU-Essential-8-App-Hardening.gap: Essential Eight application hardening is written around the internet-facing content handlers - browsers, Office, PDF readers, Java, Flash - and the hardening that closes this flaw is none of those: it is disabling the 16-bit application subsystem through Group Policy. An organisation can hold full application-hardening maturity and have NTVDM reachable on every 32-bit host, because the model does not name that surface and there is no browser, macro or content-handler setting that touches it.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: Technical vulnerability management driven from current advisory feeds will not resurface a 2010 bulletin, and the exposure this id represents in 2022 is not a missing patch on a serviced host - it is the presence of 32-bit NT-family hosts nobody re-inventoried. A.8.8 also has nowhere to record the platform precondition that decides everything here: 64-bit editions are not affected at all, so a vulnerability register keyed on release name rather than architecture overstates the affected population and buries the hosts that genuinely need the workaround.

new_control_requirements.name: CONFIGURATION-SIDE-LIVE-PATCH-INVENTORY
new_control_requirements.description: For any vulnerability with a configuration-side mitigation path: that path must be inventoried, tested, and deployable independent of the vendor-patch path.
new_control_requirements.evidence: This CVE has an unusually clean example of such a path, tested and published by the vendor itself: enabling 'Prevent access to 16-bit applications' under Administrative Templates / Windows Components / Application Compatibility, with KB 979682 automating it. Microsoft states both what it does - blocks the known attack vector without correcting the underlying vulnerability - and what it costs: users can no longer run 16-bit applications. For this estate the control means knowing, before the next disclosure, which hosts still need 16-bit support and which do not, because that answer is what decides whether the mitigation can be pushed in an hour or has to wait behind an application owner. It matters here specifically because the patch requires a restart the 2022-03-24 due date may not allow for, and because the policy setting works on the end-of-life hosts where no patch exists at all.

new_control_requirements.name: ACTIVELY-EXPLOITED-OS-LPE-REMEDIATION-WINDOW-ENFORCEMENT
new_control_requirements.description: When an OS vendor's fix for a KEV-listed local-privilege-escalation flaw is applied, the update must be both installed and rebooted into, and the installed state verified on the host rather than taken from the deployment report.
new_control_requirements.evidence: MS10-015 states the restart requirement without qualification - 'Yes, you must restart your system after you apply this security update' - so a host that has taken KB977165 and not rebooted is still exploitable by the public code in Exploit-DB 11199. Verification is not optional paperwork for this bulletin either: the 2010-03-02 revision added package installation logic that deliberately refuses to install where an infection has modified operating-system files, because installing there could cause the computer to restart repeatedly. That means the population most likely to be compromised is the population most likely to show as deployed-but-not-installed, and only a per-host check of the installed-update list distinguishes them.

new_control_requirements.name: EOL-ASSET-DECOMMISSION
new_control_requirements.description: Network-reachable end-of-life systems with no vendor patch path must be isolated and decommissioned within a bounded window; mandatory compensating segmentation applies until removal.
new_control_requirements.evidence: The affected list runs from Windows NT 3.1 through Windows 7, and every entry on it except Windows 7 was already unserviced when CISA listed the id on 2022-03-03 - Windows 7 itself ended extended support in January 2020. On those hosts the KEV due date of 2022-03-24 cannot be met by patching because there is no patch to obtain, so the terminal state is removal. Until then the two available compensating measures are the 16-bit application Group Policy setting, which works on every affected release, and restricting who holds local logon rights, since Microsoft states the flaw cannot be exploited remotely or by anonymous users.

CVE-2010-0188.name: Adobe Reader Bundled libTIFF PDF Memory Corruption (CVE-2010-0188)

attack_vector.description: A PDF carries a malformed TIFF image. When Adobe Reader or Acrobat parses the field holding it, the bundled libTIFF code overflows a buffer during decode and execution transfers into attacker-controlled data, with the rights of the user who opened the document. No scripting is involved, so disabling Acrobat JavaScript does not block it. Delivery in the documented in-the-wild use was the Blackhole exploit kit - drive-by download, SEO poisoning and malicious spam links.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none for the attacker; the victim opens a PDF
attack_vector.complexity: low - two public exploits and a Metasploit module have existed since 2010 and require no adaptation
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Disclosed by Adobe in February 2010, long before AI-assisted discovery or weaponisation.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Update Adobe Reader / Acrobat to 9.3.1 or 8.2.1 per APSB10-07, or apply the distribution package update such as RHSA-2010:0114. In the longer run, move off the end-of-life 8.x and 9.x branches entirely.
prevention.adequacy: Complete for this CVE and insufficient as a position - both fixed branches are out of support, so 9.3.1 is a floor, not a destination.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alert on the reader process spawning a child, writing an executable or making an outbound connection after a document open, rather than relying on the per-CVE antivirus families alone.
detection.adequacy: The process-behaviour signal is durable; the signature signal is not - the lettered variants in the Microsoft, F-Secure and Kaspersky family names record the exploit being repacked past each detection.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treat a confirmed open as user-context compromise of the workstation, and pull the reader version inventory across the estate rather than the single host.
response.adequacy: Adequate. CISA's ransomware-Known marking means the plausible follow-on is encryption, so the response must assume the payload had time to act, not just that the exploit fired.

NIST-800-53-SI-3.gap: Malicious code protection is the control that fires on this CVE, and it fires on a moving target. Microsoft, F-Secure and Kaspersky all ship dedicated per-CVE detection families (Exploit:Win32/CVE-2010-0188.A, Exploit:W32/CVE-2010-0188.B and .C, Exploit.Win32.CVE-2010-0188) - the existence of lettered variants is itself the record of the exploit being repacked past each signature. SI-3 asks that malicious code protection be deployed and updated; it does not ask whether the mechanism being relied on is signature-matching against a document format whose exploit generator is a public Metasploit module.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: Patch management resolves this CVE at Adobe Reader 9.3.1 or 8.2.1. Both of those are end-of-life releases, so an operator whose reconciliation is against the CVE's fixed-version boundary records the estate as remediated while it runs a document reader that will never receive another fix. The obligation is expressed in terms of vulnerabilities handled rather than supported software maintained, and the gap is exactly the difference between those two.

UK-CAF-C1.gap: C1 covers security monitoring, and the monitoring signal available for this CVE is the wrong shape. The exploit arrives as a document, executes inside the reader process with the user's own rights, and its published indicators are antivirus family names rather than network or host artefacts. A monitoring capability built to detect anomalous authentication, lateral movement or beaconing sees nothing at the moment of exploitation - the first observable is whatever the dropped payload does afterwards, which the Blackhole delivery chain deliberately varied.

AU-Essential-8-App-Hardening.gap: User application hardening covers PDF readers by design, and part of what it prescribes does sit on this exploit's path: from maturity level two the measure requires PDF software to be blocked from creating child processes, hardened to ASD and vendor guidance, and locked so users cannot change its security settings - and the reader spawning a child process or writing an executable shortly after a PDF opens is the primary behavioural indicator of successful exploitation here. What the measure does not reach is the compromise itself. The overflow is in the libTIFF copy bundled inside the reader and runs in-process with the user's rights before any child process is requested, so a payload that stays inside AcroRd32.exe, reading the documents that user can read and using the reader's own outbound access, is untouched by the child-process block at any maturity level. Below maturity level two none of the measure's PDF requirements apply at all, and the reader hardening the advice of the period centred on - disabling Acrobat JavaScript - is inert here, because the TIFF decode runs with script off.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: Technical vulnerability management depends on knowing which components are present. The vulnerable code here is libTIFF bundled inside Adobe Reader, not an operating-system libtiff package, so a vulnerability scan that inventories distribution packages does not see it, and the NVD entry describes the vulnerability as unspecified with no CWE assigned, which gives the assessment nothing to classify. A.8.8 requires information about technical vulnerabilities to be obtained; it does not require the inventory to reach inside a vendor's application bundle.

new_control_requirements.name: EMBEDDED-MEDIA-PARSER-LIBRARY-INVENTORY-AND-PATCH-PARITY
new_control_requirements.description: An organization must inventory every place a high-risk embedded media-parsing library (FreeType, image/codec/font/document parsers) is statically or dynamically bundled - including inside third-party applications that ship their own copy - and drive patching from that inventory rather than from the operating-system package list.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2010-0188 is a defect in libTIFF code bundled inside Adobe Reader and Acrobat, not in an operating-system libtiff package. A scanner reading the distribution package list sees a patched system-wide libtiff and reports nothing, while the reader carries its own vulnerable copy reached whenever a PDF's TIFF image field is parsed. Red Hat had to ship an acroread package update (RHSA-2010:0114) precisely because the fix lived inside the application, not the shared library. For this CVE the control means the inventory record is 'Adobe Reader 9.x bundles libTIFF', and the patch trigger is an Adobe bulletin, not a libtiff advisory.

new_control_requirements.name: EOL-ASSET-DECOMMISSION
new_control_requirements.description: Network-reachable end-of-life software and devices with no vendor patch path must be isolated and decommissioned within a bounded window; mandatory compensating segmentation applies until removal.
new_control_requirements.evidence: The fixed versions for this CVE are Adobe Reader / Acrobat 9.3.1 and 8.2.1, and both the 8.x and 9.x branches reached end of support years ago. Applying APSB10-07 therefore closes CVE-2010-0188 and leaves the host running a document reader that will never receive another fix, which is a terminal state rather than a patched one. The distinguishing test for this product is the branch, not the build: any 8.x or 9.x install needs a migration date to a supported reader, and 9.3.1 is only the floor that holds until that date.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: 4h KEV-listing mitigation SLA applies.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CISA added CVE-2010-0188 to KEV on 2022-03-03 with a 2022-03-24 due date and marked ransomware use Known, twelve years after APSB10-07. EPSS on 2026-08-28 is 0.88246 at the 99.761st percentile, which is what two public Exploit-DB entries (11787 and 16670) plus a Metasploit module produce. The action the SLA delivers inside hours is the reader-version inventory and the removal of any 8.x or 9.x install below the fixed builds - and it must explicitly exclude 'Acrobat JavaScript is disabled' from the mitigation list, because the vulnerable TIFF decode runs with script off.

CVE-2009-3129.name: Microsoft Excel FEATHEADER Record Memory Corruption (CVE-2009-3129)

attack_vector.description: A spreadsheet carrying a FEATHEADER record with an invalid cbHdrData size element is delivered by mail. Excel uses that value to compute a pointer offset without validation, so attacker data determines where an object is believed to be and the following virtual function call dispatches there. The in-the-wild shellcode drops and runs %temp%\wuauclt.exe, then opens a clean copy of the spreadsheet so the user sees a working document.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none beyond the rights of the user who opens the file
attack_vector.complexity: low - a single self-contained .xls, generated by a public Metasploit module since 2010
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered and not AI-weaponised.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Apply MS09-067 to Excel, the Excel Viewers and the Office Compatibility Pack separately. Where the update is not available - every affected product is now out of support - block the legacy binary format with the Excel FileOpenBlock policy or route it through MOICE.
prevention.adequacy: The update closes the parser. The workarounds close it too, at costs Microsoft states plainly: legacy files become unopenable outside a configured exempt directory, and MOICE conversion drops macros and refuses password-protected or rights-managed documents.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alert on excel.exe writing and launching an executable in %temp%, and specifically on a wuauclt.exe outside the system directory.
detection.adequacy: Effective and cheap, because the payload's own masquerade is the signal - the legitimate Windows Update client does not live in %temp%. It fires only after code execution, so it is a containment control rather than a preventive one.

response.what_would_have_worked: On a host that opened one of these files, treat the user's rights as the boundary of the compromise and check for the %temp% duplicate spreadsheet, which confirms the exploit ran rather than merely arrived.
response.adequacy: The duplicate-document artefact is a clean discriminator between delivery and execution, which most document-exploit responses lack. It does not bound anything the dropped payload did afterwards.

NIST-800-53-SI-3.gap: Malicious code protection is present, and Microsoft's own threat entry shows what it was up against: the dropped payload is named wuauclt.exe and placed in %temp%, taking the Windows Update client's name, and a clean copy of the spreadsheet is then opened so the user sees a working document. Six vendors carry the family under six different names (Trojan-Dropper.MSExcel.Agent.bc, Troj/DocDrop-Q, Bloodhound.Exploit.306, TROJ_EXELDROP.A and others), which is what per-vendor signature coverage of one document family looks like from the outside. The control does not require detection of the masquerade, only of the file.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: Every affected product - Excel 2002, 2003, 2007, Office 2004 and 2008 for Mac, the Excel Viewers and the Office Compatibility Pack - is past end of support, so an estate still exposed in 2022 when CISA listed this, or in 2026, has no patching action available at all: the obligation resolves to removal or isolation, which is not what a patch-management process produces. The Article 21 wording does not distinguish the two outcomes, so 'no patch applied' and 'no patch exists' record identically.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: The identification half of the outcome fails on component granularity. The Office Excel Viewer and the Office Compatibility Pack for Word, Excel and PowerPoint 2007 File Formats are separately installed products that handle the same FEATHEADER record and are patched separately from Excel. An estate inventoried by Office version will show a patched Office and will not show the Compatibility Pack sitting alongside it, which is the component that leaves the record handler reachable.

AU-Essential-8-App-Hardening.gap: User application hardening is the Essential Eight strategy that matches Microsoft's own workaround for this CVE, and the gap is that the workaround is not one of its published measures. Blocking the legacy binary spreadsheet format by File Block policy, or routing it through MOICE, is the control that actually closes this parser - and both carry stated costs Microsoft documents: legacy files become unopenable outside a configured exempt directory, and MOICE-converted files lose macros and cannot handle password-protected or rights-managed documents. Nothing in the maturity model asks an organisation to have made that trade-off in advance.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: Management of technical vulnerabilities assumes exposure can be evaluated from the vulnerability information available. Microsoft's mitigating factors for MS09-067 read reassuringly - the vulnerability cannot be exploited automatically through e-mail, and users are prompted with Open, Save or Cancel first - and an evaluation that stops there under-rates it, because the exploit reopens a clean copy of the document afterwards so the prompt the user answered produces exactly the outcome they expected. EPSS now puts this at 0.85731, the 99.715th percentile, driven by a Metasploit module public since 2010.

new_control_requirements.name: CONFIGURATION-SIDE-LIVE-PATCH-INVENTORY
new_control_requirements.description: For any web-fabric vulnerability with a configuration-side mitigation path: that path must be inventoried, tested, and deployable independent of the vendor-patch path.
new_control_requirements.evidence: MS09-067 ships two such paths and both are registry-deployable without the update: the Excel FileOpenBlock policy (BinaryFiles=dword:00000001 under the Office 11.0 or Policies\Office 12.0 Excel security key) and MOICE (ASSOC .XLS=oice.excel.sheet plus the .XLT and .XLA equivalents). For an estate on any of the affected products - all of which are now out of support - these are not an interim measure but the only measure. Their costs are stated by the vendor and have to be accepted in advance rather than discovered during an incident: legacy binary spreadsheets become unopenable outside an exempt directory configured per KB922848, and MOICE conversion drops macros and refuses password-protected or rights-managed documents.

new_control_requirements.name: EOL-ASSET-DECOMMISSION
new_control_requirements.description: Network-reachable end-of-life devices with no vendor patch path must be isolated and decommissioned within a bounded window; mandatory compensating segmentation applies until removal.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Written for devices, applied here to software because the situation is identical and no closer control exists in the catalogue. Every product MS09-067 covers - Excel 2002 SP3, 2003 SP3, 2007 SP1/SP2, Office 2004 and 2008 for Mac, the Open XML File Format Converter for Mac, both Excel Viewers and the Office Compatibility Pack - is past end of support. CISA's 2022-03-24 due date is therefore not satisfiable by patching for anything still exposed: the bounded window has to end in removal, with File Block or MOICE as the compensating control until it does.

new_control_requirements.name: MITIGATION-ACTIVE-PATCH-PENDING-VERDICT-CLASS
new_control_requirements.description: Compliance verdicts must distinguish binary-patch-deployed from vendor-mitigation-active-without-patch from no-mitigation-at-all, and must surface the middle state as a time-bound compensating control rather than as a patched-per-SLA outcome.
new_control_requirements.evidence: A host here can hold a patched Excel and an unpatched Office Compatibility Pack or Excel Viewer at the same time, because MS09-067 patches them as separate products while all three handle the FEATHEADER record. 'Office is patched' is therefore not a verdict about this CVE. The distinguishing test is per-component and not per-suite: enumerate the Excel Viewer and Compatibility Pack installs independently, and where File Block or MOICE is carrying the load instead of the update, record it as mitigation-active with a dated removal action rather than as remediated.

CVE-2009-1123.name: Windows Kernel Desktop Object Validation Privilege Escalation

attack_vector.description: A user who can already log on locally runs a specially crafted application. The Windows kernel fails to properly validate a change to certain kernel objects, and the application gains kernel-mode execution - complete control of that host, including installing programs, altering data and creating accounts with full user rights.
attack_vector.privileges_required: valid logon credentials and the ability to log on locally; Microsoft states the flaw cannot be exploited remotely or by anonymous users
attack_vector.complexity: low once the logon precondition is met - running one crafted application is the whole technique
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered and not AI-weaponised; the flaw was publicly disclosed and patched in 2009.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Apply MS09-025 (KB968537) and reboot. Because every affected release is end-of-life, the durable action is replacing the host with a supported Windows version rather than holding it at the patched 2009 level.
prevention.adequacy: Sufficient for this CVE and nothing beyond it. Microsoft identified no workarounds, so on an unpatched host there is no partial position; and on a patched end-of-life host the next kernel flaw has no fix at all.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alert on a standard interactive user's process chain reaching SYSTEM, on unexplained local account creation, and on kernel bugchecks tied to a specific user session.
detection.adequacy: Weak on these platforms specifically. Windows 2000 and XP-era hosts predate the kernel telemetry modern EDR depends on, so the detection that would work is largely unavailable on exactly the systems that are vulnerable.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treat kernel-mode execution as total host compromise: rebuild rather than clean, rotate every credential cached or used on the machine, and review accounts created since the suspected window.
response.adequacy: Correct, and cheap in the sense that these hosts should be leaving the estate regardless - rebuild-to-a-supported-OS is both the incident response and the standing remediation.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: Flaw remediation is satisfied by having applied MS09-025, and on these products that is the last thing SI-2 can ask for - the fix shipped in June 2009 and every affected release then reached end of support, so there is no subsequent patch level to remediate to. An SI-2 assessment on a Windows 2000 SP4 or Server 2003 SP2 host that carries KB968537 records full compliance while the host has no vendor security-update path at all for anything found since.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: Patch management presumes a supplier still shipping patches. For every product MS09-025 covers that supplier relationship ended years ago, so an Art. 21 patch-management procedure applied to these hosts produces no finding and no action: there is nothing outstanding to install. The obligation the situation actually carries is decommissioning under a bounded timetable with compensating segmentation until then, which patch management does not reach.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: The system security outcome asks that systems be configured and maintained to resist attack. A fully-patched Windows XP SP3 or Server 2008 SP2 host is maintained to the maximum its vendor permits, so the outcome reads as met. What defeats it is not this CVE's fix but the class: Microsoft states no workaround exists for this flaw, and an end-of-life kernel accumulates successors for which no fix will ever ship, so 'maintained' and 'defensible' have come apart on these hosts.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: The Essential Eight patch-operating-systems requirement is explicit that operating systems that are no longer supported by the vendor must be replaced, and every product in MS09-025's affected list is in that state. The gap is that the maturity model measures the patching timeframe, so an estate that applied KB968537 promptly in 2009 and never moved scores on the timeframe while sitting on the replacement obligation the same control carries - and CISA's 2022-03-03 listing arrived thirteen years after the only fix.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: Management of technical vulnerabilities requires that identified vulnerabilities be evaluated and appropriate measures taken. For this CVE the appropriate measure is unambiguous and finite - KB968537 plus a reboot - and once taken A.8.8 has no further hold. The control cannot express that the evaluated measure terminates: the same host remains exposed to every post-2009 kernel flaw with no update to evaluate, and the only remaining measure, removal, is a decision A.8.8 records rather than compels.

new_control_requirements.name: EOL-ASSET-DECOMMISSION
new_control_requirements.description: Network-reachable end-of-life devices with no vendor patch path must be isolated and decommissioned within a bounded window; mandatory compensating segmentation applies until removal.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Every product in MS09-025's affected list - Windows 2000 SP4, XP SP2/SP3, XP x64 SP2, Server 2003 SP2 across three architectures, Vista through SP2, and Server 2008 through SP2 including Server Core - is past end of support, and KB968537 is the terminal fix for this flaw on each. Applying it does not make the host supported. The distinguishing test is not whether the update is installed but whether the host has a vendor security-update path for anything found after its end-of-support date; where it does not, the register entry is a decommission date with segmentation until then, not a patch status.

new_control_requirements.name: ACTIVELY-EXPLOITED-OS-LPE-REMEDIATION-WINDOW-ENFORCEMENT
new_control_requirements.description: When an OS vendor flags a privilege-escalation flaw as exploited in the wild and it is KEV-listed, the cumulative update that fixes it must be applied and the host rebooted within the stated window rather than deferred to a routine maintenance cycle.
new_control_requirements.evidence: MS09-025 states 'Restart required? Yes, you must restart your system after you apply this security update' and lists HotPatching as not applicable, so the fix is not deliverable inside a no-reboot window. It also states 'Microsoft has not identified any workarounds for this vulnerability', which removes the usual option of holding a mitigation until the next reboot cycle. For this flaw the reboot is the control, and an unrebooted host that has staged the update is unprotected rather than partially protected.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: 4h KEV-listing mitigation SLA applies.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CISA listed this CVE on 2022-03-03 with a 2022-03-24 due date, thirteen years after the June 2009 fix and long after every affected product left support. The four-hour action is therefore an inventory question, not a patch one: identify every Windows 2000, XP, Server 2003, Vista or Server 2008 host still reachable, and confirm whether KB968537 is present via the registry Filelist key MS09-025 documents. EPSS on 2026-08-28 was 0.04918 at the 91.515th percentile - low in absolute terms, which is consistent with a local-only escalation whose affected platforms have largely left service.

CVE-2008-3431.name: Sun xVM VirtualBox VBoxDrv.sys Kernel Write (CVE-2008-3431)

attack_vector.description: An unprivileged local user on a Windows host with VirtualBox installed opens \\.\VBoxDrv and issues a fast-path IOCTL. Those IOCTLs use METHOD_NEITHER, so the I/O manager passes the caller's raw pointers to the driver, and VBoxDrvNtDeviceControl writes the integer status from supdrvIOCtlFast to pIrp->UserBuffer without validating that it points into user space. The caller therefore chooses any kernel address and has a value written there, repeatably - enough to patch kernel code or a kernel pointer and execute in ring 0. The published trigger uses control code 0x228103 with the target address 0x80808080 and produces a bugcheck.
attack_vector.privileges_required: low - an ordinary unprivileged local account; the device is openable by any user, which is the defect
attack_vector.complexity: low - one CreateFileA and one DeviceIoControl; the public artefact stops at the crash and leaves the ring-0 conversion undemonstrated
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered and not AI-weaponised - 2008 manual reverse engineering and source review by a vendor research team.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Upgrade to Sun xVM VirtualBox 1.6.4 for Windows and reboot; uninstall VirtualBox from every host with no virtualization role; enforce HVCI plus the vendor recommended-driver blocklist so the vulnerable VBoxDrv.sys cannot load anywhere in the estate.
prevention.adequacy: The upgrade closes the installed copy and nothing else. Only the driver blocklist addresses the case that actually persists eighteen years on - the vulnerable binary carried to a host by an attacker rather than by an installer.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alert on handles to \\.\VBoxDrv opened by processes that are not VirtualBox components, on DeviceIoControl to that device with control code 0x228103, and on driver-load events for VBoxDrv.sys on hosts with no virtualization role.
detection.adequacy: The device-handle signal is durable because opening the device is unavoidable for any exploit of this driver. The specific control code is not: it comes from one published proof of concept, and two other fast-path IOCTLs reach the same unchecked write.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treat a successful exploitation as full host compromise at ring 0 - rebuild rather than clean, and rotate any credential the host held or could reach, since kernel-mode code defeats every user-mode control on the machine including the EDR agent that would report it.
response.adequacy: Correct and expensive, and it is the only defensible response to a confirmed ring-0 write. The practical difficulty is confirmation: the successful case leaves less evidence than the failed one, because the public artefact's signature is a bugcheck and a working exploit does not crash.

NIST-800-53-CM-7.gap: Least functionality is the control that fits and it is aimed at the wrong object. CM-7 restricts the functions, ports, protocols and services a system provides; the exposure here is a kernel driver that a virtualization product installs on every host it is deployed to, whether or not that host ever runs a virtual machine, and which any unprivileged user can then open. A CM-7 baseline that approves VirtualBox as permitted software approves the driver with it, and the control has no step that asks whether the kernel-mode component of an approved application is needed on each host that carries it - which is the only question that would have reduced this estate's exposure before 2008-08-04.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: The patch obligation runs from availability of the fix, and the fix - Sun xVM VirtualBox 1.6.4 for Windows - has been available since 2008-08-04. That produces a compliant record for any estate that upgraded in 2008 and says nothing about the estate CISA addressed in 2022, whose problem is not a missed window but an unmanaged binary.
