The control also has no handling for the bring-your-own-driver case: patching every installed copy of VirtualBox leaves the 1.6.2 VBoxDrv.sys perfectly loadable on a host where the product was never present, and no patch-management obligation reaches a file an attacker brings with them.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: The system-security outcome expects vulnerable software to be identified and updated, and identification fails on a naming mismatch that no assessment would think to test. The affected product is 'Sun xVM VirtualBox' and CISA's KEV entry for the same defect reads vendorProject 'Oracle', product 'VirtualBox' - a rename that postdates the affected versions. A CAF assessment that confirms an inventory exists, is queried against KEV, and returns no Oracle VirtualBox hosts, passes while Sun-branded 1.6.x installs sit unpatched, and the artefact that actually matters, VBoxDrv.sys on disk, appears in no software inventory at all.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Essential Eight patch timeframes measure from vendor release, and the vendor release here is eighteen years old, so an estate that upgraded in 2008 is compliant and an estate that did not has been non-compliant continuously since then without the maturity model escalating - CISA's 2022 listing changed nothing in the model. More sharply, the mitigation that works for this defect is not a patch at all. Core's advisory states 'No workarounds exist', so the two effective actions are uninstalling the product from hosts that do not need it and blocklisting the driver binary, and a patch-timeframe control gives credit for neither.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: Management of technical vulnerabilities requires information about the vulnerabilities of information systems in use to be obtained and the organisation's exposure to be evaluated. For a defect this old the obtaining half has quietly degraded. Sun's own bulletin is gone - sunsolve.sun.com no longer resolves at all - and NVD marks the Secunia advisory 31361, both SecurityFocus records, SecurityTracker 1020625, securityreason 4107 and the VUPEN advisory as Broken Link. What still carries the technical detail is Exploit-DB's verbatim reproduction of the 2008 CoreLabs advisory, which NVD tags Exploit, alongside the Core Security advisory page, which NVD tags Exploit and Third Party Advisory and does not mark broken. So the evaluation input the control asks for survives, but as a mirror on an exploit archive rather than as anything the vendor still publishes, and nothing in A.8.8 requires an organisation to preserve the evidence its own risk decisions rest on or to notice that a 2008 identifier re-entered scope fourteen years later.

new_control_requirements.name: VULNERABLE-DRIVER-BLOCKLIST-ENFORCEMENT
new_control_requirements.description: Enforce a kernel vulnerable/malicious-driver blocklist (HVCI plus the vendor recommended-driver blocklist) so a signed-but-vulnerable driver cannot be loaded for bring-your-own-vulnerable-driver privilege escalation.
new_control_requirements.evidence: VBoxDrv.sys 1.6.2 is a textbook member of the class this control exists for: a legitimately signed Windows kernel driver whose device any unprivileged user may open and which carries an arbitrary kernel write. Because the primitive belongs to the binary rather than to the installation, patching or uninstalling VirtualBox across the estate does not remove the exposure - an attacker who brings the file to a host that never had VirtualBox gets the same write. The blocklist is the only listed measure that addresses that case, and it is the reason this eighteen-year-old CVE is still worth a KEV entry. It is also what recovers the identification the CAF gap describes, because a blocklist entry is keyed on the driver binary: it does not depend on an inventory holding the product under the name the affected versions actually shipped under ('Sun xVM VirtualBox' rather than the KEV record's 'Oracle'), nor on the product appearing in the software inventory at all. Two limits, since this control is easy to over-credit: it prevents the load and remediates nothing on a host already exploited, and it is only as good as its telemetry - a blocked load has to raise an event, or the control passes silently on exactly the host where someone is trying.

new_control_requirements.name: ACTIVELY-EXPLOITED-OS-LPE-REMEDIATION-WINDOW-ENFORCEMENT
new_control_requirements.description: When an OS vendor flags a local-privilege-escalation flaw as exploited in the wild (and it is KEV-listed), the monthly cumulative update that fixes it must be applied and rebooted across the entire affected endpoint fleet within the KEV remediation window, not on the normal patch cadence, and account-privilege policy must not be relied on to contain it. The distinguishing test: enumerate the fleet's installed build numbers against the fixed build for each SKU and confirm zero endpoints remain below it past the due date - a paper patch-management policy that ships monthly rollups on a 30-day cadence still leaves an actively-exploited LPE open during the window the vendor flagged it as exploited.
new_control_requirements.evidence: The fix replaces a loaded kernel driver, so it does not take effect until the host reboots - and CISA's window was three weeks (added 2022-03-03, due 2022-03-24). Core's advisory removes the usual escape hatch by stating outright that 'No workarounds exist for this issue', so a deferred reboot is not a mitigated state, it is an unmitigated one. The control's account-privilege half holds exactly as written: the device is openable by any unprivileged user, which is the defect, so tightening who holds local administrator rights contains nothing, and the enumeration the control asks for has to be by installed VirtualBox build against 1.6.4 rather than by who is privileged. The catalogued control is written for an OS vendor's monthly cumulative update; the stretch to a third-party product's driver replacement is deliberate, because the reboot dependency and the absence of any interim configuration lever are identical.

new_control_requirements.name: CVE-REGRESSION-WATCHER
new_control_requirements.description: Threat-intake pipelines must surface PoC announcements that reference historical CVE IDs (CVE-YYYY-NNN where YYYY <= current_year - 2) as candidate silent-regression cases.
new_control_requirements.evidence: This entry is the shape the watcher exists for: a 2008 identifier that became an operator obligation when CISA listed it on 2022-03-03, fourteen years after the fixed release shipped, with a public trigger sitting on Exploit-DB since 2008-08-10 the whole time. A pipeline keyed to current-year advisory feeds never resurfaces an identifier that old on its own, and here the feeds that once carried it cannot do it either - sunsolve.sun.com no longer resolves and NVD marks the Secunia, SecurityFocus, SecurityTracker, securityreason and VUPEN references Broken Link, leaving an exploit-archive mirror of the CoreLabs advisory as the source that still holds the technical detail. So the intake requirement is concrete: ingest exploit-archive and research material that names old identifiers, and let a hit on one reopen the affected-asset question on its own authority rather than deferring to whatever the register recorded as resolved in 2008. Stated as a limit, because this control is easy to over-credit: it detects nothing on an endpoint and remediates nothing. It converts a historical identifier reappearing in current material into a work item, and the work it hands off to is the upgrade to 1.6.4 plus the host reboot - or, for the bring-your-own-driver half it cannot reach at all, the driver blocklist.

CVE-2008-2992.name: Adobe Reader and Acrobat Input Validation Vulnerability (CVE-2008-2992)

attack_vector.description: A user opens a PDF. The document's embedded JavaScript calls util.printf() with a crafted format-string argument, which overflows a stack buffer in the Acrobat JavaScript engine inside Adobe Reader or Acrobat, and code executes with the privileges of the user who opened the file. NVD records the defect as a stack-based buffer overflow related to CVE-2008-1104 in the same API surface.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none on the target - the attacker supplies a file
attack_vector.complexity: low - the whole exploit is one document, with no server or network position required; the only precondition is that Acrobat JavaScript is enabled, and on the target platform of the day a single hardcoded return address sufficed
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered and not AI-weaponised. The work is from 2008 and no AI tooling is credited or plausible.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Disable Acrobat JavaScript in Reader and Acrobat, and move off the 8.x line to a supported release.
prevention.framework_requiring_it: AU Essential Eight user application hardening (PDF software); CISA BOD 22-01 for the KEV listing added 2022-03-03, due 2022-03-24
prevention.adequacy: The JavaScript setting closes this path immediately and without a patch cycle, and it breaks document workflows that rely on scripting - which is the trade-off that has to be decided rather than assumed. Moving off 8.x is the durable half, because that line has no supported build and closing this one CVE inside it leaves everything found since.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alert on the PDF reader process spawning a child process, and on reader crashes on document open.
detection.adequacy: The child-process signal is sound and independent of the specific overflow. The crash signal only catches failures - an exploit tuned to the target build does not crash - so it is a floor, not a ceiling.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treat the endpoint as compromised at the opening user's privilege level, rotate that account's credentials, and identify every other recipient of the same document.
response.adequacy: Bounded by the user's authorisation. The recipient-list step is the one usually skipped and the one that matters: a weaponised document is delivered to a list, so a single detected open implies a population to check rather than a single host.

NIST-800-53-CM-7.gap: Least functionality is the control that closes this without a patch, because the trigger is a scripting feature that can simply be turned off. What CM-7 does not do is force the question. Acrobat JavaScript is a documented, vendor-supported feature of a business-required application, so leaving it enabled is a configuration decision rather than a deviation, and CM-7's exception process accommodates it indefinitely. The control has no clause that ties an enabled scripting feature to the vulnerability history of the interpreter behind it - and this interpreter's history includes CVE-2008-1104 in the same API surface, which NVD explicitly links to this CVE.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: The Article 21 patch-management obligation measures against fix availability, and the fix has been available since 2008. That produces a clean compliance record for anyone who patched then and a finding that has been open continuously for eighteen years for anyone who did not, with no mechanism in the obligation that escalates on duration. It also cannot express the disposition that now applies: the 8.x line has no supported build, so there is no vendor patch to apply and the correct action is replacing the application - which is a procurement decision the patch-management obligation has no language for.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: The system-security outcome expects vulnerable software to be identified and updated, and identification here has a specific blind spot: the same rendering code exists twice on many hosts, once as the standalone application and once as a browser-embedded plugin, with separate update paths. An inventory that records 'Adobe Reader 8.1.3' as installed satisfies the outcome while the browser still renders PDFs through an older embedded copy. The outcome asks about software being updated and receives an answer about one of the two copies.

AU-Essential-8-App-Hardening.gap: User application hardening is the Essential Eight control aimed directly at this - PDF software is one of the application classes it names, and disabling scripting features in it is the shape of what it asks for. The gap is that the control is stated as a configuration posture without a verification obligation tied to the specific interpreter: an organisation can hold the control at a documented maturity level while an application update, a profile reset or a user preference change re-enables Acrobat JavaScript on individual endpoints. Nothing in the model requires the setting to be re-checked per host after those events, which is when it drifts.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: Management of technical vulnerabilities requires vulnerability information to be obtained and exposure evaluated. Both steps ran here and the available information was thin in a way A.8.8 does not account for: the vendor bulletin that would state the affected builds per platform is no longer retrievable, and five of the eight NVD references point at Secunia, a service that no longer resolves. The control assumes vulnerability information remains obtainable; for a defect this old the primary sources have decayed, so the exposure evaluation is performed against NVD's summary alone, and A.8.8 has no provision for recording that the evidence base for a still-listed KEV item has degraded.

new_control_requirements.name: CONFIGURATION-SIDE-LIVE-PATCH-INVENTORY
new_control_requirements.description: For any vulnerability with a configuration-side mitigation path, that path must be inventoried, tested and deployable independently of the vendor-patch path, so that operators are not dependent on a patch cycle to remove reachability.
new_control_requirements.evidence: The mitigation here is a single application preference: the trigger is an Acrobat JavaScript call to util.printf, so disabling document scripting in Reader and Acrobat removes reachability without a version change, and it covers the linked CVE-2008-1104 in the same API surface at the same time. It has to be inventoried per host rather than assumed, because the setting is user-reachable and is reset by profile changes and application updates - and it has to be tested first, because it breaks scripted document workflows, which is precisely why estates left it enabled.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: 4h KEV-listing mitigation SLA applies.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CISA added CVE-2008-2992 on 2022-03-03 with a 2022-03-24 due date, fourteen years after the fix shipped. An upgrade off the 8.x line is not an hours-scale action - it is an application replacement - so what the SLA can deliver is the scripting-disable push, which needs no package deployment and no reboot. Recording that as the mitigation, with the replacement dated separately, is the only honest way to close the item inside the window.

new_control_requirements.name: EOL-ASSET-DECOMMISSION
new_control_requirements.description: A network-reachable component with no vendor patch path must be isolated and decommissioned within a bounded window, with mandatory compensating segmentation or disablement applying until removal completes.
new_control_requirements.evidence: This control is written in the catalogue for end-of-life devices and is attached here as the closest existing control for the same terminal state in software. The affected boundary is Adobe Reader and Acrobat 8.1.2 and earlier, and the public exploit targets Windows XP SP3 - a host still in that range has no supported build to move to inside the 8.x line, so the bounded window is a replacement window with Acrobat JavaScript disabled as the compensating control in the interim. The related point the control forces is that the browser-embedded PDF plugin is a second copy on its own update path and has to be removed on the same clock.

CVE-2004-0210.name: Microsoft Windows POSIX Subsystem Privilege Escalation Vulnerability (CVE-2004-0210)

attack_vector.description: An unchecked buffer in psxss.exe, the POSIX environment subsystem on Windows NT 4.0 and Windows 2000. A locally logged-on user passes crafted parameters, possibly manipulating message length values, and overflows the buffer into complete system control. MS04-020's fix is to validate the message length before the copy. The subsystem is optional and, on a host that runs no POSIX software, is present only because it was a default — which is why the registry workaround costs nothing on most estates.
attack_vector.privileges_required: low — PR:L and AV:L. Microsoft is unambiguous: valid logon credentials and the ability to log on locally are both required, and the flaw cannot be exploited remotely or by anonymous users. The second precondition is the Posix value being present under Session Manager\Subsystems.
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L, no race and no leak. The bounded part is reachability, not exploitation: workstations and terminal servers are the primary risk, and servers only where non-administrative users can log on and run programs.
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. A 2004 responsible disclosure credited to Rafal Wojtczuk working with McAfee.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Applying MS04-020 (KB841872) for the platform, or — where no POSIX software runs on the host — deleting the Posix data value under HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager\Subsystems per KB 101270 and restarting.
prevention.adequacy: Both are complete for this CVE, and the registry change is the unusual case of a workaround that is strictly better than a filter: it removes the vulnerable code path rather than blocking a route to it, at the cost of POSIX programs that most estates never had. The limit is that it needs a restart, and the hosts still carrying this flaw in 2026 are exactly the ones nobody restarts.

detection.what_would_have_worked: A configuration sweep rather than a behavioural one: is the Posix value present, and is Psxss.exe at or above 5.0.2195.6929 / 4.0.1381.7269 / 4.0.1381.33567. Behaviourally, psxss.exe spawning a child process or a non-administrative account gaining SYSTEM after invoking a POSIX binary.
detection.adequacy: The configuration sweep is decisive and cheap, and it answers the question no CVE feed can. The behavioural half is close to useless on these platforms: NT 4.0 and Windows 2000 predate the process-creation auditing that would make 'psxss.exe spawned a child' visible, and no source publishes exploitation artifacts for this CVE to hunt against.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating a hit as full system compromise — MS04-020 names account creation with full privileges among the outcomes — so the response is local account enumeration, credential rotation for anything the host held, and rebuild rather than patch.
response.adequacy: Correct in principle and hard to execute on the platform in question: forensic tooling and log retention on a Windows 2000 host are usually absent, so 'was this exploited' typically cannot be answered and the response collapses into rebuild-or-decommission. That is the right call, but it is a decision about the asset's existence rather than about this CVE.

NIST-800-53-CM-7.gap: Least functionality would eliminate this flaw at zero cost on any host running no POSIX software, and CM-7's evidence surface does not reach it: an environment subsystem registered under Session Manager\Subsystems is not a service, port, protocol or installed application, so it appears in none of the enumerations a CM-7 assessment walks.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: The maturity level is graded from vulnerability-scanner findings, and scanners generally do not fingerprint Windows NT 4.0 or Windows 2000 hosts. The asset most likely to carry this flaw is the one least likely to appear in the scan the control is assessed against.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: Evaluating exposure requires two host-level facts — the presence of the Posix registry value and the Psxss.exe file version — that no CVE feed or scanner output supplies. A.8.8 can be run correctly and still leave the appropriate-measures decision taken on an unknown.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: MS04-020 shipped 2004-07-13 and CISA listed the CVE on 2022-03-03 with a due date of 2022-03-24. The 'documented compensating controls' branch is what carries this entry, because for hosts on platforms Microsoft stopped servicing in 2004 the patch branch may no longer be obtainable — and the compensating control here is exact and complete: delete the Posix value under Session Manager\Subsystems per KB 101270. 'Verified' has to mean the registry value is absent or Psxss.exe reads 5.0.2195.6929 / 4.0.1381.7269 / 4.0.1381.33567, since the installer record alone does not establish it on these platforms.

new_control_requirements.name: EOL-ASSET-DECOMMISSION
new_control_requirements.description: Network-reachable end-of-life systems with no vendor patch path must be isolated and decommissioned within a bounded window; mandatory compensating segmentation applies until removal.
new_control_requirements.evidence: MS04-020 records on its own face that Windows NT 4.0 Workstation SP6a and Windows 2000 SP2 had already reached the end of their extended support on 2004-06-30, that Microsoft released this update anyway as an exception, and that it 'did not anticipate doing this for future vulnerabilities affecting these operating system versions'. Any host still running an affected platform in 2026 is therefore in the state this control describes — no vendor patch path for the next flaw — and CISA's 2022 KEV listing put it on the clock regardless. The control is attached for the asset rather than for this CVE specifically: MS04-020 closes CVE-2004-0210, and nothing closes the next one.

new_control_requirements.name: MITIGATION-ACTIVE-PATCH-PENDING-VERDICT-CLASS
new_control_requirements.description: Compliance verdicts must distinguish three states: (a) binary patch deployed, so the vulnerability is eliminated; (b) a vendor-mitigation rule is active with no binary patch, leaving the residual risk that any defect or gap in the mitigation reopens the flaw; (c) neither.
new_control_requirements.evidence: This CVE has two genuinely different remediated states and a scanner cannot tell them apart from a version check. State (a) is Psxss.exe replaced at 5.0.2195.6929 / 4.0.1381.7269 / 4.0.1381.33567. State (b) is the KB 101270 workaround, where the vulnerable psxss.exe is still on disk at its original version but the Posix value is gone from Session Manager\Subsystems, so the subsystem never starts — a host in state (b) reads as unpatched to any file-version check and is in fact not exploitable, and a host that later has the value restored for a POSIX application silently reverts to state (c). Recording which state a host is in is the only way that reversion is visible.

CVE-2002-0367.name: Windows Debug Subsystem Handle Duplication Local Privilege Escalation (MS02-024)

attack_vector.description: An unprivileged user who can log on interactively runs a program that attaches to the Windows debug subsystem without the privilege check firing, duplicates a handle to a process running as LocalSystem, and commands that process to launch a program of the attacker's choice. The launched program inherits the debuggee's security context, so the attacker obtains SYSTEM.
attack_vector.privileges_required: an ordinary interactive account on the host, at the console or through a terminal session, plus the ability to run a program of the attacker's choosing - both stated as preconditions in MS02-024
attack_vector.complexity: low - documented APIs against an authentication check that does not fire; the public DebPloit demonstration predates the patch by ten weeks
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered and not AI-weaponised; the disclosure is from 2002.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Install the Q320206 patch from MS02-024 and reboot, or run Windows 2000 at Service Pack 3 or later, which contains the fix. On a surviving host today, remove the host from service - there is no current servicing stream for these platforms.
prevention.adequacy: Sufficient for this CVE, insufficient for the asset. Patching closes this flaw on an operating system that receives no other updates, so the host remains exposed to everything disclosed since - which is why the durable remediation is decommissioning rather than the hotfix.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alert on a process running as SYSTEM whose parent is a service that does not launch programs, and on administrative account creation following an ordinary interactive logon.
detection.adequacy: Weak in practice on this platform generation: the telemetry that would carry process lineage is not native to Windows NT 4.0 or Windows 2000, and modern endpoint agents do not support them - so the realistic detection surface is the domain and network around the host rather than the host itself.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treat a confirmed escalation as full host compromise: rebuild rather than clean, and rotate every credential the host held or that was used to log on to it, including any domain account with a session on the machine.
response.adequacy: Adequate for the host and inadequate for the domain if the machine was a domain member - SYSTEM on the host reaches cached credentials and machine account material, so the blast radius of the response has to extend to the accounts, not just the box.

NIST-800-53-SC-39.gap: Process isolation requires the system to maintain a separate execution domain for each process. That is precisely the property this flaw removes, and it removes it through a facility the operating system provides deliberately: MS02-024 describes the debugging facility as granting an attaching program 'the same level of control over the running program as it has itself'. An SC-39 assessment of a Windows NT 4.0 or Windows 2000 host would record process isolation as an inherent platform property and find nothing to test, because the defect is in the authentication that gates the documented cross-process channel, not in the isolation model the control describes.

NIST-800-53-AC-6.gap: Least privilege is the control this flaw is designed to defeat, and the defeat is total rather than partial: the attacker starts as an ordinary interactive user, which is the privilege level AC-6 would assign them, and finishes as LocalSystem. An estate can hold a perfect AC-6 attestation - no standing administrators, every account scoped to its function - and every one of those correctly-scoped accounts still reaches SYSTEM on an unpatched host. The control has no expression that distinguishes a host carrying Q320206 from one that does not.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: Art. 21 patch-management measures presuppose a vendor supplying updates. Windows NT 4.0 and Windows 2000 have no servicing stream, so for a host still running one the measure has no artefact to apply beyond the 2002 hotfix, and every subsequent flaw in the same platform remains permanently open. An Art. 21 process that records Q320206 as installed and moves on states something true and irrelevant: the correct Art. 21 outcome for these hosts is a migration or isolation decision, which a patch-management measure is not scoped to make.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: The system security outcome expects services to be configured and maintained so they resist attack. Between the public exploit on 2002-03-13 and the bulletin on 2002-05-22 there was nothing to maintain to - no patch existed, and the only configuration change that helps, withdrawing interactive logon rights, is exactly the function that workstations and terminal servers exist to provide. Today the same outcome fails for the opposite reason: the platform cannot be maintained at all, so B4 is unmeetable on any host still running it.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: The Essential Eight patch-operating-systems control requires the most recent or the immediately preceding vendor-supported release, and requires that unsupported operating systems be replaced. A Windows NT 4.0 or Windows 2000 host fails that requirement outright, independently of this CVE - which means the Essential Eight verdict on such a host is already 'replace', and applying Q320206 changes neither the maturity assessment nor the exposure to everything else unpatched in the platform.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: Management of technical vulnerabilities requires vulnerability information to be obtained and acted on. For this CVE, acting on it in 2002 meant Q320206 and a reboot; acting on it on a surviving host means decommissioning, because the vendor publishes nothing further for the platform. A.8.8 has no vocabulary for that terminal state - it treats a vulnerability as something to remediate rather than as evidence that the asset itself must leave the estate, and an A.8.8 register that carries this CVE as 'patched' misses that the host is unpatchable for everything since.

new_control_requirements.name: ACTIVELY-EXPLOITED-OS-LPE-REMEDIATION-WINDOW-ENFORCEMENT
new_control_requirements.description: When an OS vendor's fix addresses a local privilege-escalation flaw that is KEV-listed, the update carrying it must be driven across every affected host on the KEV clock rather than folded into the next routine rollup, with completion measured by each host's installed build against the fixed build and by the restart having actually been taken - and the control must record that account-privilege tightening does not contain an escalation whose attacker is already an authorized local user.
new_control_requirements.evidence: This entry is the archetype the control's second half describes: MS02-024's precondition is an ordinary interactive logon, so every least-privilege and identity control on the host can pass its attestation while the flaw stays fully exploitable. Completion here is measurable from the registry rather than from a console - Q320206 under the Hotfix or Updates key - and the bulletin records 'Reboot needed: Yes', so a host that took the hotfix without rebooting still carries the vulnerable code. The population to enumerate first is the one the bulletin rates Critical: workstations and terminal servers, where unprivileged interactive logon is the normal operating state rather than an anomaly.

new_control_requirements.name: EOL-ASSET-DECOMMISSION
new_control_requirements.description: Network-reachable end-of-life assets with no vendor patch path must be isolated and decommissioned within a bounded window; mandatory compensating segmentation applies until removal, since no remediation exists.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Windows NT 4.0, Windows NT 4.0 Terminal Server Edition and Windows 2000 - the three platforms MS02-024 lists - are all long past vendor support, so a host still exposed to this CVE in 2026 is by definition unpatchable for everything disclosed since 2002 as well. That is why the KEV listing on 2022-03-03 does not resolve to a patch action: the operative decision is a removal date, with interactive logon rights withdrawn and network reachability cut as the compensating segmentation until that date arrives. The distinguishing test: query the asset inventory for hosts on these operating system versions, and treat any entry without a recorded decommissioning decision as the finding.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CISA listed this on 2022-03-03 with a 2022-03-24 due date, twenty years after the vendor fix and the public DebPloit exploit; EPSS on 2026-08-28 was 0.04919 at the 91.515th percentile. Because the patch predates the listing by two decades, the four-hour clock cannot be a patch clock - what it can deliver is the documented compensating control the bulletin itself names: withdraw interactive logon rights from unprivileged users on any surviving NT 4.0 or Windows 2000 host, and cut its network reachability, with removal scheduled behind that.

CVE-2022-24682.name: Zimbra Collaboration Suite Calendar Attribute XSS (CVE-2022-24682)

attack_vector.description: HTML carrying executable JavaScript is placed inside element attributes that the Zimbra Calendar feature renders without escaping. The script executes in the Zimbra origin inside the victim's already-authenticated webmail session, reaching mail, attachments and session material. In the observed campaign the trigger was a spear-phishing link that redirected to attacker infrastructure and fired only when the recipient was concurrently logged into webmail.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none for the attacker; the victim must be an authenticated webmail user who follows a link
attack_vector.complexity: low - attribute-context injection with a scope change into the application origin; the operational work is the phishing sequence, not the exploit
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-assisted. Volexity's 2022 incident-response findings describe a human-operated spear-phishing campaign.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Apply Zimbra 8.8.15 patch 30 update 1 or later and verify the patch level rather than the base version. During the zero-day window there was no vendor fix, so the only preventive lever was reducing the phishing-link click surface.
prevention.adequacy: Adequate for the flaw and blind to the window: exploitation began in December 2021 and the hotfix landed on 5 February 2022, so patching says nothing about mailboxes read before it existed.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Per-request webmail access logging forwarded off-box, correlated against the last authentication event for the session, plus inspection of calendar items for markup in element attributes.
detection.adequacy: The only telemetry that works - authentication-event logging records nothing, because the payload rides a session the user legitimately opened.

response.what_would_have_worked: Invalidate webmail sessions, review mail rules, forwarders and delegated access for the exposure window, and treat mailbox contents reachable by an affected session as read.
response.adequacy: Decisive where per-request logs were retained; without them the exposure cannot be bounded, only assumed.

NIST-800-53-SI-10.gap: Information input validation is the right control and it is being applied on the wrong side. The defect is output encoding, not input filtering: NVD states the injected markup 'becomes unescaped' when the Calendar feature renders it inside an element attribute, so content that passed validation on the way in is what executes on the way out. An assessment that evidences input validation on the mail and calendar ingest path finds nothing wrong.

NIS2-Art21-incident-handling.gap: Incident handling keyed to authentication anomalies has nothing to key on. Volexity's actor sent links that fired only when the recipient was already logged into Zimbra webmail, so the malicious activity flows over a session the user legitimately established - no failed login, no new device, no impossible travel. The obligation this CVE creates is per-request webmail logging with enough retention to reconstruct a session after the fact, which the incident-handling requirement does not itself specify.

UK-CAF-C1.gap: Security monitoring assumes the monitored events distinguish the attacker from the user. Here they are the same session: the script runs in the victim's own authenticated webmail context and reads their own mailbox, so mailbox-access telemetry shows the account doing what that account normally does. Volexity's disclosure on 2022-02-03 came from incident response on a customer, not from a monitoring alert.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Zimbra announced its hotfix on 2022-02-04 for availability on 5 February 2022, two days after Volexity's public disclosure, and CISA set a 2022-03-11 due date - but the exposure ran from December 2021, when NVD records exploitation beginning, so the patch clock started well after the mailboxes were being read. Patch timeframes cannot address a period in which the vendor had no fix; the estate-side action for that window is session and credential response, which the control does not require.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.28.gap: Secure coding is the control that matches the defect - output encoding in the Calendar feature - and it binds the supplier, not the operator. An ISO-certified operator of Zimbra can evidence secure-coding practices across everything it writes and still be running a webmail client whose attribute rendering is unescaped; the only operator-side lever is patch level and supplier assurance, neither of which A.8.28 asks for.

new_control_requirements.name: OWA-PER-REQUEST-SIEM-INGESTION
new_control_requirements.description: Webmail per-request access logs, not just authentication events, must be forwarded to an external SIEM with at least 90-day retention, because authentication-only logging misses XSS-stage telemetry - the malicious request flows over an already-authenticated session.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Written for Exchange OWA and applied here to Zimbra webmail, which is the same architecture and the same failure: Volexity's actor sent links that fired only when the recipient was concurrently logged into Zimbra webmail, so the injected script read the mailbox inside a session the user had opened legitimately and produced no authentication record of its own. The retention figure is load-bearing for this CVE specifically - NVD records exploitation starting in December 2021 and the vendor hotfix landed on 5 February 2022, so reconstructing the exposure needs logs spanning at least that two-month window, which authentication-event retention alone would not cover.

new_control_requirements.name: PRIMARY-SOURCE-INTAKE-VENDOR-BLOG-COVERAGE
new_control_requirements.description: Threat-intake pipelines must cover vendor and researcher security blogs in addition to advisory feeds, because research publications ahead of a vendor advisory fall through advisory-only intake.
new_control_requirements.evidence: The first public account of this flaw was Volexity's blog post 'Operation EmailThief' on 2022-02-03; Zimbra announced a hotfix the next day for availability on 5 February 2022, the CVE identifier came later, and CISA's KEV listing came on 2022-02-25. An intake pipeline reading only advisory feeds learned of an actively exploited zero-day in its webmail platform three weeks after the researcher published the indicators - the domains update.secretstep[.]tk, mail.bruising-intellect[.]ml, spiritfield[.]ga, amazon-check[.]cf and playquicksand[.]cf and four IP addresses - which were the only actionable material available during the window when no patch existed.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: 4h KEV-listing mitigation SLA applies.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CISA listed CVE-2022-24682 on 2022-02-25 with a 2022-03-11 due date and marks ransomware use Known without naming a family. EPSS on 2026-08-28 stood at 0.30931, the 98.168th percentile. What an hours-scale SLA delivers here is not the patch - Zimbra's fix was already available from 5 February 2022 - but the session response: invalidating webmail sessions and auditing mail rules and forwarders for accounts active since December 2021, because patching the encoder does nothing about a mailbox already read.

CVE-2017-8570.name: Microsoft Office Composite Moniker Remote Code Execution (CVE-2017-8570)

attack_vector.description: A document embeds a composite moniker that binds a scriptlet moniker, which Office resolves without the constraints that should apply to an embedded object. The public chain uses the Packager control to drop a .sct into %TEMP% and then runs it through the moniker, giving code execution as the opening user. No macro is involved, so no macro prompt appears.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none for the attacker; the payload runs at the privilege of the user who opened the file.
attack_vector.complexity: low — a document generator rather than an exploit chain. packager_composite_moniker.py produces a working file deterministically, with no memory-corruption stage and no version-specific offsets, which is why it stayed in commodity malspam for years after the fix.
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Credited by Microsoft to Haifei Li of the McAfee Security Team in the July 2017 acknowledgements; the public builder appeared six months later from Rich Warren.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: The July 2017 Office update for the installed line — KB3213640, KB3213624, KB3213555 or KB3213545 — verified by build rather than by approval, plus content-provenance enforcement and a block on script-host execution from user-writable directories.
prevention.adequacy: The update is complete but its application is conditional: Microsoft marks restart as 'Maybe', so it can sit pending on the workstations that keep Office open all day. The compensating controls cut the second stage and do not depend on the package landing.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alerting on an Office process writing a .sct into %TEMP% and on Office spawning a script host or unexpected child, and network-side signatures on the document itself such as Juniper's HTTP:STC:MS-CVE-2017-8570-RCE.
detection.adequacy: Effective where the process-lineage telemetry exists and unreliable where detection rests on file signatures — the document carries a moniker and a Packager object rather than shellcode, and Zscaler's Lokibot campaigns kept landing long after the fix.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating a confirmed open as user-context compromise: rotate the user's credentials, hunt the second stage the document fetched, and check the rest of the mail flow for the same generator's output.
response.adequacy: Proportionate, and the scope is usually understated. The exploit is an initial-access primitive whose value is what it delivers, so response bounded to removing the document leaves whatever Lokibot-class payload it dropped in place.

NIST-800-53-SI-3.gap: The delivered artefact is a composite moniker and a Packager object, and the executable content is a plain-text scriptlet written at open time — very little for a signature capability to match. Zscaler's reporting on RTFs still delivering Lokibot through this CVE years after the July 2017 update is the evidence that a compliant, well-updated anti-malware capability did not stop it.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: Microsoft classifies the restart requirement for all four July 2017 Office packages as 'Maybe', so approval and effect are different states and the measure only records the first. The workstations that hold Office open continuously are both the most likely to stay pending and the most likely to open external documents.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: Office hardening on most estates is macro hardening, and this exploit contains no macro. Trust-centre policy, macro signing and the enable-content prompt all leave the composite-moniker path untouched, so B4 can be assessed as achieved against a document that executes on open.

AU-Essential-8-App-Hardening.gap: The exploit falls between two strategies: the Office macro strategy does not apply because there is no macro, and user application hardening is scoped to browser content rather than to OLE and moniker resolution inside Office. High maturity on both leaves the Exploit-DB 44263 document working.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.7.gap: Malware protection here leans on detection and user awareness, and neither engages. There is no prompt for a trained user to refuse, and the malicious content does not exist until the document is opened, so a transit scanner sees a document with an embedded object and nothing else.

new_control_requirements.name: ARCHIVE-CONTENT-TYPE-PROVENANCE
new_control_requirements.description: Archive and document handlers must dispatch rendering and execution on the content-verified file type rather than on the displayed name or extension, and must propagate Mark-of-the-Web to everything they extract or write.
new_control_requirements.evidence: The published chain writes a Windows Script Component into %TEMP% through the Packager control and then executes it through a composite moniker — a file the Office process creates itself, at open time, from data embedded in an inbound document. Nothing about the original attachment's extension describes what runs, and the dropped .sct inherits no provenance marking, so every downstream reputation and provenance control is bypassed by construction rather than by evasion.

new_control_requirements.name: DOWNLOAD-PROVENANCE-ENFORCEMENT
new_control_requirements.description: Enforce Mark-of-the-Web and content provenance on all internet-sourced files, and block execution of provenance-stripped shortcuts, installers and script hosts regardless of a reputation verdict.
new_control_requirements.evidence: This is the compensating control that works when the July 2017 package is pending, which Microsoft's 'Maybe' restart classification makes a normal state on always-open Office workstations. Blocking script-host execution of scriptlets from user-writable directories cuts the published chain at its second stage without waiting on the update, and it applies equally to the Office 2007 SP3 estate that has had no vendor path since October 2017.

CVE-2017-0222.name: Microsoft Internet Explorer Memory Corruption Remote Code Execution (CVE-2017-0222)

attack_vector.description: A crafted page drives Internet Explorer into using an object after its lifetime has ended; the freed allocation is reclaimed with page-controlled data and the corrupted object is used to execute code as the browsing user. Microsoft describes the delivery — a crafted site, a compromised site, or an advertisement or user-content block on a legitimate site — and modifies how Internet Explorer handles objects in memory as the fix, without publishing the object involved.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; the attacker needs no account on the target, only that the user loads the page.
attack_vector.complexity: NVD records low (AC:L); Microsoft records high (AC:H) in its own CVSS 3.0 scoring, with a temporal E:P indicating proof-of-concept-grade code at release. Either way the gate that matters is UI:R.
attack_vector.ai_factor: Microsoft credits no finder, so the discovery route is not on the record. The exploitability assessment reads Exploited: Yes with Publicly Disclosed: No, which places the defect in in-the-wild activity before the fix, but no source names who found it or how.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Installing the May 2017 update for the SKU and restarting. Before it existed there was no vendor workaround, so the available preventions were content-boundary controls on the three delivery paths Microsoft names, none of which is specific to this defect.
prevention.adequacy: The update is complete for this defect but not in effect until the host restarts, and Microsoft marks all eight KBs Restart Required: Yes. The content controls are partial by nature: they narrow which pages reach the browser rather than making the browser safe to render them.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Process-lineage alerting on iexplore.exe spawning a child or connecting to a host unrelated to the page, plus crash telemetry for repeated iexplore.exe faults on a single site.
detection.adequacy: Both fire after the page has been rendered, so they bound dwell time rather than preventing execution, and both depend on process-creation telemetry being collected from user workstations rather than servers.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating any host that showed the lineage pattern as a second-stage investigation, since a zero-day used before public disclosure is spent on delivering something worth the exploit.
response.adequacy: Scoping is limited by the absence of any published indicator: Microsoft named no hashes, domains or actors, so the investigation has nothing to pivot on beyond its own endpoint telemetry.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: The control is met by installing the May 2017 updates on schedule, and exploitation was already detected on current and older releases when they shipped, so compliance covered none of the exposure. It also counts installation as remediation while Microsoft marks every one of the eight KBs Restart Required: Yes, so a fully compliant report can describe hosts still running the vulnerable engine.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: The measure has nothing to act on before the vendor publishes, and Microsoft published no workaround for this CVE at all. It also has no way to record the restart residual, so an entity can evidence full patch cadence across a population that installed the fix and never rebooted into it.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: There is no configuration item for an object-lifetime defect in a rendering engine, so a B4 assessment has nothing to examine and returns a clean result on an estate where every workstation will render an attacker's page through the vulnerable path.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: The fix travels as an operating-system patch inside the May 2017 IE cumulative update or the SKU's monthly rollup, so it inherits the operating-system deferral ring. The strategy counts deployment rather than effect: Microsoft marks all eight KBs Restart Required: Yes and the strategy requires no live-patching capability, so a fleet reported as patched inside the 48-hour ML3 target can still be loading the vulnerable engine on every host that has not restarted.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: On the down-level SKUs the measure the control anticipates — install the vendor update — is the last one that engine will get, and A.8.8 provides no alternative disposition for a component whose fix stream has ended. Its evaluation input, an 8.8 CVSS from 2017 with no KEV-aware response category, cannot distinguish a defect the vendor recorded as already exploited from a routine high-severity browser bug.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Microsoft published the fix on 2017-05-09 with exploitation already detected on current and older releases, and CISA listed the CVE on 2022-02-25 with a six-month due date of 2022-08-25. The clause that carries the weight here is verified mitigation: Restart Required is Yes for all eight KBs, so the verification is a per-host build-and-uptime check rather than a deployment-tool success report, which is exactly the distinction the patch-cadence measures do not make.

new_control_requirements.name: BROWSER-MANAGED-UPDATE-NO-DEFERRAL
new_control_requirements.description: Enterprise update rings must not defer security-channel browser updates beyond 24h.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Internet Explorer's fix is not a browser update in the modern sense: it arrives inside the May 2017 IE cumulative update or the SKU's monthly rollup, so it inherits the operating system's deferral ring rather than a browser update channel. That is precisely why an operating-system patch assessment and a system-security assessment can both pass while the engine stays unpatched — the browser has no independent security channel to keep current, and the control's requirement is what supplies one.

new_control_requirements.name: EOL-ASSET-DECOMMISSION
new_control_requirements.description: Network-reachable end-of-life software and devices with no vendor patch path must be isolated and decommissioned within a bounded window; mandatory compensating segmentation applies until removal since no remediation exists.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Part of the affected list is past its fix stream: extended support for Windows Server 2008 SP2, Windows 7 SP1 and Windows Server 2008 R2 SP1 ended on 2020-01-14 and their Extended Security Update years have since closed, Windows 8.1 and Windows RT 8.1 ended on 2023-01-10, and Windows 10 1507 ended on 2025-10-14 with 1511 and 1703 earlier still. On those SKUs the vendor update named in the advisory is the last one the host will ever receive for this engine, so the vulnerability-management control's own remedy has no future instances and a bounded decommission window is the only disposition that resolves the state. The requirement does not reach the rest of the list: Windows Server 2016 runs to 2027-01-12, the Windows 10 Enterprise 2016 LTSB branch to 2026-10-13, and Windows Server 2012 and 2012 R2 sit in a paid Extended Security Update year to 2026-10-13, so those hosts belong on the patch path rather than the decommission path.

CVE-2014-6352.name: Microsoft Windows OLE Packager Code Injection Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: The Windows OLE packager instantiates an OLE object embedded in an Office document without correctly validating its use of memory, so an executable payload carried inside the object runs when the document is opened. Because the payload is embedded rather than linked, the MS14-060 update — which addressed the linked-file case in CVE-2014-4114 — did not stop it, and the public exploit is described as an MS14-060 patch bypass. The observed attacks used crafted PowerPoint files.
attack_vector.privileges_required: None, but UI:R: the user must open the file, and in the observed attacks then dismiss a UAC consent or elevation prompt. Code runs in the context of the current user, so an administrator account turns a user-level compromise into a full one.
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L, and effectively zero technical work since Metasploit modules and Exploit-DB entries 35235 and 35236 shipped from the 2014-10-21 disclosure date. Reliability is highest on Office 2013 and Office 2010 SP2 per Rapid7's module record.
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. The disclosure is from 2014 and predates AI-assisted vulnerability research; no AI tooling appears in the advisory, the bulletin or the KEV record.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Installing KB3010788 from MS14-064 on 2014-11-11 and restarting. In the twenty-one days before it, the KB3010060 'OLE packager Shim Workaround' Fix it, Microsoft's EMET 5.0 Attack Surface Reduction configuration, and keeping UAC and Protected View enabled.
prevention.adequacy: KB3010788 is complete for this CVE and supersedes the incomplete MS14-060 fix. The interim measures are genuinely partial and Microsoft says so: the shim covers PowerPoint only and not 64-bit PowerPoint on x64 Windows 8 or 8.1; the EMET profile has to be imported by hand; and UAC and Protected View are prompts a user can dismiss, which is exactly how the observed attacks reached execution.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Process-lineage alerting on Office applications spawning executables or command interpreters, and inspecting Office documents for embedded OLE package objects whose packaged content is an executable — the embedded payload being the distinguishing feature against CVE-2014-4114.
detection.adequacy: Process lineage is reliable and would have caught the payload regardless of the shim state. Content inspection is the weaker half: the container is a legitimately structured Office file, and Microsoft notes that many document types beyond Office can carry the affected object, so an inspection scoped to PowerPoint because that is what the October 2014 attacks used will miss the general case.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating an opened document as executed: capture the file and any executable the Office process wrote, establish whether the user was running with administrative rights, and rotate credentials reachable from that user context.
response.adequacy: The scoping question is answerable because the impact is bounded by the user's own rights — Microsoft states the attacker gains the same rights as the current user. What complicates it is delivery: the same document can arrive by mail or from a web page, so a response scoped to the mail gateway alone leaves the web-delivered half of the population unexamined.

NIST-800-53-SI-3.gap: The carrier is a legitimately structured Office document and the payload is an OLE package object inside it. Microsoft's own pre-patch answer between 2014-10-21 and 2014-11-11 was the KB3010060 shim, not detection, and that shim covered PowerPoint only and not 64-bit PowerPoint on x64 Windows 8 or 8.1. SI-3 records anti-malware as deployed; it has no field for a legitimate file type carrying an embedded executable object.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: Measured against vendor release the process performs well — advisory 2014-10-21, update 2014-11-11. What it cannot carry is that KB3010788 supersedes KB3000869 from MS14-060: this is the second defect on the same OLE packager primitive, and an organisation that had deployed MS14-060 had been told the problem was closed.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: Every mitigation Microsoft published is a client hardening setting — the KB3010060 shim, the EMET_CVE-2014-6352.xml Attack Surface Reduction profile, UAC and Protected View. B4 measures a build against a baseline, and no standard baseline carried a per-CVE Fix it for one application or a hand-imported EMET profile, so a fully compliant build could carry none of them.

AU-Essential-8-App-Hardening.gap: The control hardens applications — browsers, office suites, PDF readers — and the defect is in the operating system's OLE handling, fixed by the Windows update KB3010788. Microsoft states that all Office file types and many other third-party file types can carry the affected OLE object, so hardening every enumerated application class still leaves the same primitive reachable through any other handler that instantiates one, and the control has no limb reaching outside that set. Microsoft's own interim measure was narrower again: the KB3010060 shim covered PowerPoint only, and not 64-bit PowerPoint on x64 Windows 8 or 8.1.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.7.gap: Both mitigations Microsoft observed working in the real attacks are dialogs: a UAC consent or elevation prompt, and Protected View, which the user must leave. A.8.7 records that malware protection and user awareness are implemented; it has no test distinguishing a control that blocks from one that asks, which is the whole difference here.

new_control_requirements.name: ARCHIVE-CONTENT-TYPE-PROVENANCE
new_control_requirements.description: Archive and document handlers must dispatch rendering/execution on the content-verified file type rather than the displayed name or extension, and must propagate Mark-of-the-Web to every extracted file.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2014-6352 — the payload is an executable carried inside an OLE package object inside an Office document, and the packager instantiates it on open, so the extracted-file case the control names is here the object the packager unpacks and runs. Two halves apply. Dispatching on the verified content type of the packaged object, rather than on what the container presents, stops an executable being run because the packager instantiated it; propagating the container's internet provenance onto what is written out keeps it under the same Protected View constraint the parent document was opened with. Microsoft's own account of the observed attacks is that UAC prompted before the file executed and Protected View had to be left first — both user decisions, which is what a handler-level rule replaces. This is the layer that reaches the handlers Microsoft says can carry the affected object, including the 'many other third-party file types' outside any enumerated application set.

new_control_requirements.name: INCOMPLETE-PATCH-SEQUENCE-SEVERITY-MULTIPLIER
new_control_requirements.description: Vulnerability-management programs must apply a severity multiplier when a CVE is the Nth in an incomplete-patch sequence on the same primitive (third MOTW bypass, second AMSI bypass, and so on).
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2014-6352 — KB3010788 supersedes KB3000869 from MS14-060, making this the second defect on the Windows OLE packager after CVE-2014-4114, and the public exploit is literally named and described as an MS14-060 patch bypass. An organisation that deployed MS14-060 in October 2014 had been told the OLE packager problem was closed; the multiplier is what would have flagged the November bulletin as a re-close rather than a routine month.

new_control_requirements.name: DOWNLOAD-PROVENANCE-ENFORCEMENT
new_control_requirements.description: Enforce Mark-of-the-Web / content-provenance on all internet-sourced files and block execution of provenance-stripped shortcuts, installers, and script hosts regardless of a reputation verdict.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2014-6352 — Protected View, the mitigation Microsoft names as enabled by default, is driven entirely by the file's internet provenance, and it is a prompt the user leaves rather than a block. Enforcing provenance as a blocking policy on documents delivered by mail or download, instead of as an advisory mode, removes the click that stands between the attachment and execution in the attacks Microsoft describes.

CVE-2022-23131.name: Zabbix Frontend SAML Session Forgery Authentication Bypass (CVE-2022-23131)

attack_vector.description: Zabbix stores session state client-side in a base64 zbx_session cookie with a sign field, and verifies that signature only when the sessionid field is read. The SAML SSO login path reads the username attribute and saml_data from the same cookie without that check, so a forged cookie naming an existing user completes the SSO login as that user with no assertion from the identity provider. Naming a Super Admin gives full frontend administration, and Zabbix frontend administration defines the scripts and system.run items the platform executes on every monitored host — so a cookie becomes command execution across the estate the monitoring server was installed to watch.
attack_vector.privileges_required: None. PR:N and UI:N. The practical requirements are configuration and reconnaissance: SAML SSO enabled (Zabbix states this is non-default) and knowledge of an existing Zabbix login name, or the guest account enabled — guest is disabled by default.
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L. One HTTP request with a crafted cookie, no race and no memory work. The public nuclei template reduces confirmation to two requests against /zabbix/index_sso.php and /index_sso.php, matching a 302 to the dashboard.
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Thomas Chauchefoin of SonarSource found it by reading Zabbix's custom session handling; it is a logic finding, not a crash, and neither SonarSource nor Zabbix credits automated or AI tooling.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Upgrading the frontend to 5.4.9 or 6.0.0beta1 and cycling PHP workers; or, without an upgrade window, disabling SAML SSO authentication, which removes the only path that reaches the unverified fields, and confirming the guest account is disabled.
prevention.adequacy: The upgrade is complete for this CVE. The configuration mitigation is a genuine removal of the path rather than a filter, and its cost is real — it takes the SSO integration offline, which is the control the organisation deliberately built. Neither action invalidates sessions already issued, so an upgrade alone leaves a pre-upgrade forged session working.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Reconciling Zabbix frontend logins against identity-provider authentication events — a SAML login with no IdP record is the flaw's fingerprint — and alerting on creation or modification of global scripts and system.run items.
detection.adequacy: The reconciliation is decisive because a genuine SSO login cannot exist without an IdP event, but it requires the two logs to be joined, which is not something either system does by itself. The script-creation alert catches the consequence rather than the entry, and only where frontend audit records are shipped off the box.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating an exposed instance as administered by the attacker: invalidate all frontend sessions, audit users, roles, global and host scripts and item definitions for changes, rotate every credential the Zabbix server holds for monitored hosts, and then examine the monitored hosts themselves, since frontend administration reaches them by design.
response.adequacy: Correct in shape and expensive in scope — the credential rotation is across the monitored estate, not the monitoring server. Its limit is retention: the CVE was published in January 2022 and the fix shipped 2021-12-23, so the window an investigation has to cover starts before most instances had any reason to be watching.

NIST-800-53-IA-2.gap: Federating Zabbix to a corporate identity provider satisfies IA-2 completely, and none of it is load-bearing: the login name is read from the client's own zbx_session cookie, whose signature Zabbix checks only when sessionid is read. The authentication decision is made from attacker-supplied data before the federated protocol is consulted at all.

NIS2-Art21-identity-management.gap: Article 21(2)(i) access control policies and Article 21(2)(j) multi-factor or continuous authentication are both met by implementing SSO, and enabling SSO is the precondition for the bypass. Since Zabbix states SAML is non-default, the exposed entities are exactly the ones that did the identity-management work the Articles ask for, and neither requires evidence that the application enforces the assertion it receives.

UK-CAF-B2.gap: Roles, group permissions and the IdP integration were all correctly configured and the attack defeats none of them — it enters where the authorisation decision reads an unauthenticated field. A B2 review of privileged access finds every control in place and no evidence that any of them was engaged.

AU-Essential-8-MFA.gap: MFA enforced at the identity provider is a maturity pass for an internet-facing service, and the forged cookie is accepted at /index_sso.php without the request ever reaching the provider. Multi-factor authentication placed somewhere the attacker does not travel is not a compensating control, and the maturity model has no way to record the distinction.

ISO-27001-2022-A.5.15.gap: A.5.15 audits the access-control rule set, which here was correct — roles, user groups, per-host-group permissions. It assumes the subject those rules apply to has been established truthfully, and the subject is supplied by the client. Nothing in the control requires evidence that the identity was authenticated by the party claiming to have authenticated it.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Zabbix shipped the fix on 2021-12-23 and CISA listed the CVE on 2022-02-22 with a 2022-03-08 due date, so a routine application-patch cadence had two months in which public exploit tooling — a nuclei template and several public repositories — was reaching a pre-authentication admin takeover on an internet-facing monitoring frontend. This control fires on the listing, and on this product 'documented compensating controls' has a concrete meaning that does not require an upgrade window: disabling SAML SSO removes the only path to the unverified session fields, and confirming guest is disabled removes the no-username variant.

new_control_requirements.name: SENSITIVE-DATA-IN-LOGS-LINT
new_control_requirements.description: Identity middleware must lint log output for credential-shaped strings at every severity level; CI must reject builds whose log statements emit secret-tagged fields.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Attached as the closest existing control on identity middleware handling its own credential material, and applied here to the session cookie rather than to log output — no catalog control covers 'verify the signature on every field of a client-held session, not only the one field the original code path read'. That is precisely the defect SonarSource found: the sign field on zbx_session is checked when sessionid is read and not when the SAML username attribute is read, so the same cookie is trusted or untrusted depending on which line of code opens it. The testable requirement for this CVE is that every read of client-held session state passes through one verification, and that the SAML login path cannot reach a username without it.

CVE-2022-23134.name: Zabbix Frontend setup.php Unauthenticated Configuration Access

attack_vector.description: An unauthenticated HTTP request to setup.php on an already-installed Zabbix Frontend. The file gates its steps on wizard state rather than on the caller's role, so steps that should be super-administrator-only after installation remain reachable, letting an attacker override the existing configuration files and, per SonarSource, reach the dashboard with a highly-privileged account.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none - unauthenticated network request against the frontend
attack_vector.complexity: low - no prior knowledge of the target, automatable, and covered by a public Nuclei template
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Found by manual source review of the frontend's PHP during SonarSource's December 2021 attack-surface study; no AI tooling credited in discovery or in any observed exploitation.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Upgrade the Frontend to 5.4.9, 6.0.0beta2 or the 6.0 LTS stable release, or to 5.0.19 or 4.0.37 on the older branches. Immediately, deny /setup.php at the reverse proxy - the installer has no purpose on an installed instance.
prevention.adequacy: Sufficient against the flaw. It does not settle an instance already touched: the effect is a config write, so the configuration file and every credential the frontend holds must be checked and rotated rather than assumed intact.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alert on any request to setup.php on an installed instance, and on modification of the frontend configuration file without a matching super-admin audit entry.
detection.adequacy: Both are decisive and near-zero-noise, because neither event has a legitimate cause after installation. Authentication-event logging alone detects nothing here - the request never authenticates.

response.what_would_have_worked: Rotate the Zabbix database credentials and frontend-issued API tokens, audit host macros and item configurations for stored credentials, and review what monitoring data and agent reach the platform exposes to a super-admin session.
response.adequacy: Proportionate to what the platform holds. Restricted where audit retention is short: the flaw was listed alongside CVE-2022-23131 and reporting does not separate exploitation of the two, so scoping must assume either path.

NIST-800-53-AC-3.gap: Access enforcement is present on setup.php and it answers - it simply answers on the wrong question. The file checks which wizard step the caller is on, not who the caller is, so an unauthenticated request that satisfies the step condition is served. An AC-3 assessment that verifies an enforcement mechanism exists on the path passes on a mechanism that CWE-284 and CWE-287 were both assigned against.

NIS2-Art21-vulnerability-handling.gap: The fixed builds shipped in late December 2021 and CISA listed the CVE on 2022-02-22 with a 2022-03-08 due date, so the handling window is two weeks against a fix already two months old. The harder problem the measure does not reach is version scope: the published version data names 5.4.0-5.4.8 and the 6.0 pre-releases from 6.0.0alpha1 to 6.0.0beta1, while SonarSource's own write-up puts the affected boundary at 5.4.8, 5.0.18 and 4.0.36. A handling process reconciling against the vendor range alone records a 5.0.x instance as unaffected on the researcher's affected side.

UK-CAF-B2.gap: Identity and access control assumes a credential mediates access to a privileged function. Here no credential is presented at any point - the request reaches installer steps that pre-date the existence of accounts, and the outcome the CAF measures has nothing to say about a path whose design assumption is that nobody has logged in yet because the system is not yet installed.

AU-Essential-8-MFA.gap: Multi-factor authentication on the Zabbix login is the Essential Eight control that appears to cover privileged access to this platform, and it sits entirely off this path. setup.php never reaches the login flow, so an instance at full MFA maturity is exactly as exposed as one with none, and the assessment produces no signal that would say so.

ISO-27001-2022-A.5.15.gap: Access control policy governs who is granted access to which functions. No policy an operator can express in Zabbix changes setup.php's behaviour before 5.4.9, because the file is not part of the role model - it runs before roles exist. The only policy-side action available is a web-server rule denying the path, which is a network control standing in for an access-control one.

new_control_requirements.name: CONFIGURATION-SIDE-LIVE-PATCH-INVENTORY
new_control_requirements.description: For any web-fabric vulnerability with a configuration-side mitigation path: that path must be inventoried, tested, and deployable independent of the vendor-patch path.
new_control_requirements.evidence: The configuration path here is a single deny rule for /setup.php, and it is available on every instance that sits behind a proxy the operator controls. For this product the control means knowing before a disclosure whether the frontend is proxied or serves directly, having the deny rule in the proxy's version-controlled configuration rather than added by hand, and re-verifying it after any proxy rebuild. Precondition: it is a holding measure. The step check is unchanged before 5.4.9, so an instance whose proxy configuration is restored from an older backup is exposed again with no signal.

new_control_requirements.name: FLEET-CONTROL-PLANE-ADMIN-PRIVILEGE-TIER
new_control_requirements.description: Administrators of fleet-control-plane systems (MDM/UEM, EDR consoles, identity providers, container orchestrators, configuration management) must be classified as a distinct privilege tier.
new_control_requirements.evidence: This control is the closest existing fit - it names configuration-management and orchestrator control planes rather than monitoring platforms, and Zabbix belongs in that class for the same reason: a super-admin session on the frontend reaches agent configuration, host macros and stored credentials across every monitored system. SonarSource's stated impact for this CVE is access to the dashboard with a highly-privileged account, obtained with no credential at all, which is the tier boundary being crossed. Treating the Zabbix frontend as an application rather than as a control plane is what puts it behind a single MFA-protected login and nothing else.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: 4h KEV-listing mitigation SLA applies.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CISA listed this on 2022-02-22 with a 2022-03-08 due date, a day after public proof-of-concept code for the companion CVE-2022-23131 began circulating. EPSS on 2026-08-28 was 0.84657 at the 99.695th percentile. The action an hours-scale SLA can deliver on this CVE is the proxy deny rule for /setup.php, which needs no change window; the frontend upgrade to 5.4.9 or the 6.0 LTS release follows on the normal one.

CVE-2022-24086.name: Adobe Commerce Checkout Template-Filter Unauthenticated Remote Code Execution

attack_vector.description: An unauthenticated visitor places a guest order whose shipping and billing address fields carry Magento template directives. The checkout path passes that data into the email template filter without neutralising it, so the directives are interpreted: the published payload calls getTemplateFilter().addAfterFilterCallback(system) and then supplies a command line, yielding arbitrary code execution as the web server user. The whole chain is four ordinary REST calls against the guest-cart endpoints.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none (unauthenticated guest checkout; no user interaction, per Adobe's own advisory)
attack_vector.complexity: low - the exploitation traffic is indistinguishable from a customer buying something, and the payload is public in a Nuclei template and eleven GitHub repositories
attack_vector.ai_factor: No AI tooling appears in the record. The flaw was found in the wild and Adobe credits no researcher; the published analyses are post-patch reverse engineering.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Upgrade to 2.4.3-p2 or 2.3.7-p3 per APSB22-12 as revised on 2022-02-17, which also carries CVE-2022-24087 on the same template surface.
prevention.adequacy: Necessary and insufficient on its own. Sansec observed live exploitation from 2022-02-21 and documents backdoors that survive the upgrade, so on any store that was internet-facing and unpatched after 2022-02-13 the patch closes the door on a room the attacker may already be standing in.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alert on Magento template syntax appearing in customer-supplied order fields, on the web-server user spawning a shell during template rendering, and on any PHP file appearing under pub/media - the directory is for uploaded media and should never hold executable code.
detection.adequacy: The filesystem signals are strong and cheap. Network signatures are weak by design here: Sansec records attackers varying endpoints specifically to defeat request-path rules, and warns that the obvious '{{ }}' body match produces false positives.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treat the store as compromised rather than merely vulnerable: review the webroot for planted PHP, rotate admin credentials, integration and API tokens, payment gateway keys, the crypt key and database credentials, and scope the incident as a payment-data event because the groups working this flaw are skimmer operators.
response.adequacy: This is the part that decides the outcome and the part most often skipped. Sansec's TrojanOrders reporting shows the November 2022 surge landing on stores that had already patched, and describes groups scanning for other groups' backdoors - which only works because the backdoors outlived the patch.

NIST-800-53-SI-10.gap: Information input validation is the control this CVE is filed under - Adobe and NVD both class it as improper input validation - and it is the one that reads as satisfied while the flaw is live. A checkout form that validates a firstname for length and character class still passes the string on to a template filter that treats '{{var this.getTemplateFilter().addAfterFilterCallback(system)...}}' as a directive, because the defect is not at the input boundary but at the point where validated data is interpolated into a template. SI-10 assessed by confirming that input validation exists on the checkout path returns pass for exactly the deployment that is being exploited.
