NIS2-Art21-vulnerability-handling.gap: Vulnerability handling that closes an item when the named fixed version is deployed gets this one wrong twice. Adobe revised APSB22-12 on 2022-02-17, four days after publication, to add CVE-2022-24087 on the same checkout template surface - so a handling record closed against the 2022-02-13 bulletin is closed against a superseded document. And the handling process has no state for the thing that actually determines outcome here: Sansec documents backdoors installed before the patch that persist after it, so a store can be fully patched, fully compliant with the 2022-03-01 KEV due date, and still under attacker control.

UK-CAF-C1.gap: Security monitoring is where this flaw is won or lost, and the CAF outcome does not reach the specific difficulty. Exploitation arrives as guest checkout traffic - add to cart, post an address, post payment information - so a monitoring capability watching for anomalous access patterns sees an ordinary order. Sansec records attackers deliberately varying endpoints to defeat request-path rules and notes that the obvious content signature, '{{ }}' in a POST body, produces false positives. The signal that does work is not in the monitoring stack at all: it is a new PHP file under pub/media and orders whose customer names read like 'system' or 'pwd'.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: The Essential Eight patching timeframes for internet-facing applications are the tightest in the model and this deployment can meet them and still lose. Adobe published on 2022-02-13, Sansec observed live attacks on 2022-02-21, and the mass exploitation Sansec named TrojanOrders arrived in November 2022 against stores that were by then largely patched but already backdoored. Patch-timeframe maturity measures the window from vendor release to deployment; it has nothing to say about a webshell installed inside that window, which is what actually kept these stores compromised.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: Technical vulnerability management driven by version reconciliation records a store on 2.4.3-p2 as remediated. That statement is true about the code and false about the system, because the remediation this CVE requires includes a webroot integrity review that A.8.8 does not call for. The control also has no way to represent the revised-bulletin problem: the authoritative version of APSB22-12 is the 2022-02-17 one, and an organisation that reconciled against the 2022-02-13 text has a complete and correct-looking vulnerability register that is missing CVE-2022-24087.

PCI-DSS-4.0.1-11.6.1.gap: The payment-page change-detection requirement is the closest existing control to the real outcome here, and it is aimed one layer above the attack. It watches the HTTP headers and script content delivered to the consumer browser, which catches a skimmer injected into the checkout page; it does not watch the server-side filesystem, where this exploitation lands first as a PHP file under pub/media. A store meeting 11.6.1 gets an alert when the skimmer reaches the payment page, which is after arbitrary code execution, after the backdoor, and potentially after card data has already been taken server-side.

new_control_requirements.name: ECOMMERCE-PLATFORM-EXTENSION-UNTRUSTED-DESERIALIZATION-GUARD
new_control_requirements.description: An e-commerce platform (Magento / Adobe Commerce and similar) and every third-party extension it loads must never pass request-supplied data (cookies, headers, body, query parameters) into a template filter or rendering context that can interpret it as a directive.
new_control_requirements.evidence: The exploitation is the control statement read backwards: a firstname submitted at guest checkout reaches the email template filter and is interpreted, and the published payload uses that to register PHP's system() as an after-filter callback. Sansec names the file where the boundary should have been - vendor/magento/module-email/Model/Template/Filter.php. The extension half of the control matters as much as the core half here, because the same filter is reachable from any module that renders customer-supplied fields into a transactional template, and a store that has taken 2.4.3-p2 has fixed the core path only.

new_control_requirements.name: INCOMPLETE-PATCH-SEQUENCE-SEVERITY-MULTIPLIER
new_control_requirements.description: Vulnerability-management programs must apply a severity multiplier when a CVE is the Nth in an incomplete-patch sequence on the same primitive, and must re-open the item rather than treating the first fix as terminal.
new_control_requirements.evidence: APSB22-12 was published on 2022-02-13 for CVE-2022-24086 and revised on 2022-02-17 to add CVE-2022-24087 - a second 9.8 on the same checkout template surface, four days later. That is the signature the multiplier exists for: the first patch did not settle the primitive, so a store that deployed on 2022-02-14 and closed its ticket was unpatched again by the end of the same week, inside a KEV window that closed on 2022-03-01. The operational rule this produces is that a bulletin carrying an in-the-wild flag should be re-read at its current revision before an item is closed, not at the revision that was current when the item was opened.

new_control_requirements.name: PERIMETER-COMPROMISE-REBUILD-NOT-PATCH
new_control_requirements.description: Pre-rehearsed IR runbook for any internet-facing system that suffers a pre-auth RCE CVE in active exploitation MUST default to config-exfil review plus rebuild plus credential rotation, not patch-in-place.
new_control_requirements.evidence: This CVE is the clearest available case for the default. Adobe flagged in-the-wild exploitation on 2022-02-13, Sansec saw live attacks on 2022-02-21 from 45.134.20.11, and Sansec's TrojanOrders reporting then documents remote access trojans - often in pub/media/health_check.php - that persist after the store is patched, with rival groups scanning for that filename to take over stores somebody else had already backdoored. A patch-in-place response therefore produces a store that is compliant with the 2022-03-01 KEV date and still controlled. The rotation half is not optional either: code execution as the web user reaches admin credentials, API and integration tokens, gateway keys, the crypt key and the database, and the operators working this flaw are card skimmers.

CVE-2022-0609.name: Chrome Animation Use-After-Free Exploited by DPRK Operators (CVE-2022-0609)

attack_vector.description: A crafted HTML page drives a use-after-free in Chrome's Animation component and corrupts the heap in the renderer process. Delivery was through hidden iframes on both attacker-owned and compromised legitimate sites, preceded by heavily obfuscated JavaScript that fingerprinted the visitor so the exploit was served only to selected targets. Two North Korean government-backed groups ran it as Operation Dream Job (250+ people at 10 organisations in media, domain registrars, web hosting and software) and Operation AppleJeus (85+ users in cryptocurrency and fintech), from 2022-01-04 until after the 2022-02-14 patch.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none; the victim loads a page, in the observed campaigns on a site they already used
attack_vector.complexity: low to trigger from a page; high to weaponise - the operators guarded the exploit with one-time links, per-stage AES encryption and time-windowed serving, and Google TAG could not recover the post-RCE stages
attack_vector.ai_factor: None credited. Found by Google TAG analysts from live attack traffic; no AI tooling appears in the Chrome release note or the TAG report.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Update Chrome to 98.0.4758.102 and restart the browser; separately update every other Chromium-based browser in the estate, since CISA names Microsoft Edge and Opera as affected.
prevention.adequacy: Insufficient for the exposure window - the kit was in deployment from 2022-01-04, six weeks before a fix existed, so an organisation in the named target sets must hunt rather than close.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Hunt proxy history for the three attacker domains and for traffic to options-it[.]com or tradingtechnologies[.]com between 7 and 9 February 2022 from browsers below 98.0.4758.102; alert on renderer crashes clustered on a routinely-visited site.
detection.adequacy: Retrospective only, and deliberately degraded by the kit - one-time links mean a replay returns nothing and per-stage AES encryption means the captured traffic does not analyse. Proxy history retention is the limiting factor.

response.what_would_have_worked: For a confirmed hit, treat the workstation as compromised beyond the renderer and rotate the credentials it held, since the recovered chain was staged and the follow-on stages were never recovered.
response.adequacy: The only defensible posture. TAG could not obtain the post-RCE stages, so the honest statement is that the depth of any given compromise is unknown, not that it stopped at the sandbox.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: Flaw remediation begins when a fix exists, and for this CVE that is 2022-02-14. Google TAG's earliest evidence of the exploit kit in active deployment is 2022-01-04 - six weeks during which no SI-2 activity was possible, against an adversary that had already compromised two legitimate fintech sites the targets used. SI-2 also does not reach the second half of the problem: the same Chromium code shipped in Microsoft Edge and Opera, and remediating Chrome to 98.0.4758.102 leaves that copy untouched while the flaw-remediation record shows the CVE closed.

NIS2-Art21-incident-handling.gap: Incident handling is triggered by a detected event, and the kit was engineered to prevent one being detected. Google TAG records that it served the iframe only at specific times, used one-time-click links keyed to unique IDs, AES-encrypted each stage and halted if a prior stage failed - TAG itself was unable to recover the stages after the initial Chrome exploit. An operator in one of the named target sets (news media, domain registrars, web hosting, software vendors, cryptocurrency, fintech) therefore has no artefact to open an incident on, and the honest handling posture is a hunt keyed to the 2022-01-04 to 2022-02-14 window rather than an incident record.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: B4 covers secure configuration of systems, and there is no configuration of Chrome that closes this. The vulnerable path is the Animation component reached from ordinary HTML rendering, so disabling extensions, plug-ins, or any policy-controlled browser feature changes nothing. The one configuration decision that mattered is one B4 does not phrase: whether the browser update channel is allowed to apply on its own schedule, and whether users restart the browser, because Chrome fixes take effect on restart and a browser left open for days keeps running the vulnerable renderer.

AU-Essential-8-App-Hardening.gap: User application hardening is the Essential Eight measure aimed at web browsers and its prescriptions - blocking Flash, Java and web advertisements - are all delivery-channel controls. The AppleJeus campaign delivered through hidden iframes placed on options-it[.]com and tradingtechnologies[.]com, two legitimate fintech sites the targets visited deliberately between 7 and 9 February 2022; the Dream Job campaign delivered through spoofed Indeed and ZipRecruiter pages reached from recruiter mail. Neither is an advertisement, a Flash object or a Java applet, so an estate at the highest maturity level for this measure was exposed identically to one at none.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: Technical vulnerability management on a browser reduces to reading the vendor's version boundary, and the boundary here is misleading in one specific way: NVD states 'prior to 98.0.4758.102 in Google Chrome', while CISA's KEV entry states the vulnerability could affect multiple Chromium-based browsers including Microsoft Edge and Opera. An A.8.8 process that reconciles installed Chrome versions against the NVD string produces a clean result on a fleet whose standard browser is Edge, because the affected-product string never named it.

new_control_requirements.name: BROWSER-MANAGED-UPDATE-NO-DEFERRAL
new_control_requirements.description: Enterprise update rings must not defer security-channel browser updates beyond 24h.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Chrome 98.0.4758.102 shipped on 2022-02-14 and Google TAG records exploitation attempts continuing after that date, so every deferred day was a day inside a live campaign. Two details make the deferral question sharper for this CVE than for a normal browser update: the fix takes effect on browser restart, not on install, so a ring that reports deployment while users keep the browser open has not delivered it; and the same Chromium code shipped in Microsoft Edge and Opera, which run on their own release trains, so the ring must cover every Chromium-based browser in the estate rather than Chrome alone.

new_control_requirements.name: NATION-STATE-INITIAL-ACCESS-IR-ESCALATION
new_control_requirements.description: IR runbooks must include an explicit nation-state-initial-access escalation path triggered by state-actor attribution on a confirmed exploit chain; standard incident severity does not apply.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Google TAG attributes this exploit kit to two North Korean government-backed groups running Operation Dream Job and Operation AppleJeus, and states that it was unable to recover the stages following the initial Chrome remote code execution. That combination is what the escalation path exists for: the depth of any given compromise is unknown by construction, the operators used one-time links and per-stage AES encryption specifically to keep it unknown, and the targeting was sector-specific (news media, domain registrars, web hosting, software vendors, cryptocurrency, fintech). A standard browser-exploit incident closes at the sandbox; this one cannot be closed there.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: 4h KEV-listing mitigation SLA applies.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CISA added CVE-2022-0609 on 2022-02-15, one day after the Chrome fix and five days after Google TAG reported it, with a 2022-03-01 due date. What the SLA can deliver inside hours on a browser CVE is not a patch push alone - Chrome updates apply on restart - but a forced browser restart across the fleet plus an inventory pass over every Chromium-based browser, since CISA's own listing names Microsoft Edge and Opera and the NVD affected-product string does not.

CVE-2019-0752.name: Internet Explorer Scripting Engine Type Confusion (CVE-2019-0752)

attack_vector.description: A page rendered by the Internet Explorer engine at document emulation level 8 or lower assigns an object to a DOM property such as scrollLeft. A DISPATCH_PROPERTYPUTREF operation is routed through the _FastInvokeTable entry holding the property's get method, producing a write-what-where primitive bounded below 0x001767dd. The public exploit escalates that to arbitrary read by corrupting array elements and then to command execution by corrupting COM objects, using no native shellcode.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none - the rights of the user browsing
attack_vector.complexity: high per CVSS for the memory grooming, low per victim - the delivery observed was an exploit kit served from web content, and the working exploit has been on Exploit-DB since 2019-05-24
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered and not AI-weaponised. The vulnerability came from human research at the Zero Day Initiative.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Apply the 9 April 2019 Internet Explorer cumulative security update or the corresponding Windows monthly rollup, verifying by resulting build. Remove or disable the IE rendering engine, including where it is embedded in other applications, to close the class rather than the instance.
prevention.adequacy: Sufficient and available from day one - Microsoft shipped the fix with 'Exploitation More Likely' attached. Insufficient where the estate updates the default browser but not the embedded engine, which is what the exploit kit reaches.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alert on any child process of a browser process, and on web content forcing X-UA-Compatible emulation to IE8 or lower outside a documented legacy allowlist.
detection.adequacy: The child-process rule is the only reliable signal, because the exploit carries no native shellcode - there is nothing for a content scanner to match. The emulation-level rule is a genuine precursor signal, since the bug is unreachable above level 8.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treat a host that spawned a process from the browser as executing attacker code at user rights, rotate that user's credentials, and look for the loader stage before the ransomware stage arrives - in the documented campaign the ransomware was fetched from command-and-control after the loader landed.
response.adequacy: There is a real interval to act in, because the kit delivers a loader and pulls the encrypting payload separately. That interval is the whole response opportunity and it is short.

NIST-800-53-SI-3.gap: Malicious code protection has nothing to inspect. Zuckerbraun's exploit reaches command execution with no native shellcode - it corrupts COM objects until a PowerShell command line runs - so the artefact crossing the wire is script text and the artefact in memory is a corrupted object graph. The documented delivery reinforces the point: the RIG kit served this from web content, so there is no file for the control to scan before execution and the first executable thing on the host is a signed interpreter.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: The patch has been available since 9 April 2019 and Microsoft's exploitability assessment said 'Exploitation More Likely' on the day - so a patch-management obligation applied competently would have closed this in April 2019. The gap is what happened next: Bitdefender found RIG serving it in February 2021, and CISA listed it in February 2022, which means the exposed population is hosts where patch management is not reaching Internet Explorer at all. For that population the obligation has no escalation step; it just keeps producing the same finding.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: The system-security outcome is written around identifying and updating vulnerable software, and the software here is not only a browser. The Internet Explorer rendering control is embedded in other applications, so a CAF assessment that establishes 'Internet Explorer is not the default browser' or 'IE is disabled' does not establish that the engine is unreachable. The delivery in the documented campaign was an exploit kit reached from web content, which does not require anyone to have chosen IE.

AU-Essential-8-App-Hardening.gap: Essential Eight user application hardening covers web browser configuration, and the specific configuration that matters for this CVE - preventing the document emulation level dropping to 8 or lower, where the IDispatchEx confusion becomes reachable - is not among its measures. Nor does the strategy reach the embedded rendering control, which is where an exploit kit lands. Hardening the browser the organisation has chosen does not harden the engine the organisation has not noticed it still runs.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: Management of technical vulnerabilities evaluated this correctly at disclosure: CVSS 7.5, vendor exploitability 'Exploitation More Likely', a fix on the day. What the control has no step for is the re-evaluation when the public exploit lands - Exploit-DB 46928 was published on 2019-05-24, six weeks after the patch, and is build-specific to Windows 10 17763.316. From that date the cost of exploitation for anyone still unpatched was a download, and EPSS now records 0.81551 at the 99.624th percentile.

new_control_requirements.name: BROWSER-MANAGED-UPDATE-NO-DEFERRAL
new_control_requirements.description: Enterprise update rings must not defer security-channel browser updates beyond 24h.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Microsoft shipped this fix on 9 April 2019 already carrying the assessment 'Exploitation More Likely'. A working exploit reached Exploit-DB on 2019-05-24, and the RIG exploit kit was still finding unpatched Internet Explorer to serve it to in February 2021. Every day of deferral in that window was a day on the wrong side of a public, build-specific exploit. The control needs one extension for this CVE: the deferral limit has to apply to the Internet Explorer rendering engine wherever it is embedded, not only to the browser the organisation considers its own.

new_control_requirements.name: PROTECTION-MECHANISM-FAILURE-CLASS-REGRESSION
new_control_requirements.description: Detonation chambers, EDR rules, and AppLocker/WDAC policies covering protection-mechanism classes must include class-level coverage rather than per-instance signatures.
new_control_requirements.evidence: The published exploit 'uses no shellcode' - it reaches a PowerShell command line by corrupting COM objects, and it works from a clean process with Enhanced Protected Mode enabled or disabled. Two protection mechanisms are therefore bypassed at once: content inspection has no binary to inspect, and EPM does not change the outcome. The class-level rule that survives is a process-lineage rule - any child process of a browser process - together with a content rule on legacy document-mode requests, since the confusion is unreachable above emulation level 8.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: 4h KEV-listing mitigation SLA applies.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CISA listed this on 2022-02-15 with a 2022-08-15 due date - six months, the long-form KEV window, for a CVE marked as used in ransomware campaigns with a public exploit since 2019. The hours-scale action available on listing day is not the update, which is nearly three years old by then; it is enumerating where the Internet Explorer engine is still reachable, including embedded instances, and putting a browser-child-process rule in front of it while the estate is fixed.

attack_vector.description: A crafted page or an Office document that embeds the Internet Explorer rendering engine defines a VBScript class whose Class_Terminate handler raises the reference count during destruction, leaving a dangling pointer to a freed VVAL structure. Reallocating a class object over that memory corrupts two objects and retypes one as an Array, giving arbitrary read and write in the process and then code execution as the current user.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none beyond the current user; the victim opens a document or visits a page
attack_vector.complexity: rated AC:H for the heap-layout dependency, but effectively low downstream - Exploit-DB 44741 and fifteen public repositories package it, and Kaspersky records the technique as adapted from published CVE-2014-6332 proof-of-concept code
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered and not AI-weaponised. Kaspersky's sandbox found it in live attacks; 0patch credits Kaspersky and 360 with the analysis.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Apply the May 2018 Windows security update and reboot. For Windows 7 and Server 2008 hosts that could not, deploy 0patch ZP-320 or ZP-321 as a bridge, and block the IE rendering engine from instantiating inside Office documents.
prevention.adequacy: The update is complete. The micropatch is not a substitute - it covers only oleaut32.dll 6.1.7601.23775 on Windows 7 and Server 2008, leaving the Windows 8.1, 10 and Server 2012 through 2016 members of the affected list untouched.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alert on any Office process loading vbscript.dll or the IE rendering engine, and on browser or Office processes spawning script hosts or shells after a document open.
detection.adequacy: Strong and cheap on modern endpoint telemetry, because the module-load signal is specific: Office loading the IE engine is rare in an estate that has retired Internet Explorer, which makes it a high-signal event rather than a threshold to tune.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treat execution as the user: rotate that account's credentials and tokens, review what it could reach, and hunt for script-host and scheduled-task persistence created in the same window.
response.adequacy: Necessary and not sufficient on its own given CISA records ransomware use as Known - a response scoped to one user account underestimates a foothold whose documented downstream use is estate-wide encryption.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: Flaw remediation gives a remediation timeframe from patch availability, and CISA's own window for this one ran from 2022-02-15 to 2022-08-15 - six months for a CVE with a Known ransomware association, a working Exploit-DB entry since 2018-05-21 and fifteen public exploit repositories. An SI-2 programme tracking to that due date is compliant for the whole half-year, and the flaw was four years old and fully weaponised before the clock even started.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: Patch management against this CVE reads as a single Windows cumulative update, which is accurate and hides the split: the 0patch micropatch that covers the interim only reaches Windows 7 and Server 2008 on oleaut32.dll 6.1.7601.23775, while Windows 8.1, 10, Server 2012, 2012 R2 and 2016 are equally in NVD's affected list with no interim option. An Art. 21 procedure that records 'mitigation available' at the CVE level is asserting for the whole estate a bridge that exists for part of it.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: The system security outcome is satisfied by a maintained, patched Windows build - and it was, for hosts on the May 2018 update. What it does not reach is the delivery path this flaw actually used: the VBScript engine is instantiated by Office documents through the embedded IE rendering engine, so an estate that had already retired Internet Explorer as a browser, and would report the browser risk as closed, still executed the exploit when a user opened a document.

AU-Essential-8-App-Hardening.gap: Application hardening in the Essential Eight covers configuring browsers to block or disable web content of exactly this kind, and doing so is the single most effective non-patch measure here. It is also the one the estate is least likely to have applied where it matters: hardening is scoped to the browser, and the exploit's document path runs through Office instantiating the IE engine, which a browser-scoped hardening baseline does not cover. The measure is right and its usual scoping misses the vector.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: Management of technical vulnerabilities requires evaluating exposure and taking timely measures. The evaluation input for this CVE is unusually strong - CISA records ransomware use as Known and EPSS on 2026-08-28 stood at 0.88508, the 99.765th percentile - yet A.8.8 provides no mechanism to convert that signal into a shorter clock than the one the organisation already set. The control ensures the vulnerability is on the register; it does not distinguish it from the rest of the register.

new_control_requirements.name: LIVE-PATCH-CAPABILITY
new_control_requirements.description: Where live-patch is available (kpatch / canonical-livepatch on Linux servers), it must be deployed and tested quarterly.
new_control_requirements.evidence: The control names Linux live-patching tools; the Windows analogue applies here and this is the closest existing entry. 0patch shipped a one-instruction micropatch on 2018-05-15 - 'mov word [rbx], 0' in oleaut32!VariantClear, identifiers ZP-320 and ZP-321. The quarterly test this control mandates must, for this flaw, verify coverage as well as function: the micropatch binds to oleaut32.dll 6.1.7601.23775 on Windows 7 and Server 2008 through April 2018, so a fleet-wide 'live patch deployed' claim silently excludes every Windows 8.1, 10, Server 2012, 2012 R2 and 2016 host in NVD's affected list.

new_control_requirements.name: BROWSER-MANAGED-UPDATE-NO-DEFERRAL
new_control_requirements.description: Enterprise update rings must not defer security-channel browser updates beyond 24h.
new_control_requirements.evidence: This is a browser-engine flaw and the control is the right shape, but for this CVE it has to be widened or it misses the vector entirely. The VBScript engine is reached both by Internet Explorer directly and by Office documents that embed the IE rendering engine, so an update ring scoped to the browser product leaves the document path served by the same unpatched engine. The concrete requirement is that the ring key off the engine - vbscript.dll and oleaut32.dll - rather than off the browser application, and that Office be treated as a consumer of that engine.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: 4h KEV-listing mitigation SLA applies.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CISA gave this CVE a six-month window - listed 2022-02-15, due 2022-08-15 - while recording ransomware use as Known, which is the longest due date in this chunk attached to the strongest exploitation signal in it. Exploit-DB 44741 had been public since 2018-05-21. A four-hour clock changes what is done first: block the IE rendering engine from instantiating in Office and deploy the 0patch bridge where it applies, then take the cumulative update on the reboot cycle. EPSS on 2026-08-28 was 0.88508, the 99.765th percentile.

attack_vector.description: A user extracts a crafted archive with WinRAR 5.61 or earlier. The bundled 2006 library unacev2.dll treats a filename field beginning with a drive-letter sequence as an absolute path, replacing the chosen destination folder with an empty string, while its CleanPath sanitiser strips the leading `C:\C:` and leaves the rest intact. WinRAR's own callback aborts on `\..\`, `\../`, `/../` and `/..\`, but each of those needs a leading slash, so the traversal written as `C:../` passes it. The archive therefore writes a file of its choosing to a path of its choosing - the public chain targets the per-user Startup folder - and the payload executes at the next logon. The archive need not be named .ace, because WinRAR dispatches on content.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none on the attacker side; the write occurs with the extracting user's privileges, and user interaction is required (CVSS UI:R)
attack_vector.complexity: low - a generated archive; the public builder reached Exploit-DB two days after the vendor analysis was published. The constraints are placement, not skill: the archive must be extracted from one folder inside the user profile, and a logon must follow
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered and not AI-weaponised. Manual fuzzing and reverse engineering of an unsymbolised 2006 binary.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Upgrade WinRAR to 5.70 or later, where ACE support and unacev2.dll are removed; before that, delete unacev2.dll from the installation directory. Enforce Mark-of-the-Web on internet-sourced archives and require it to propagate to extracted files.
prevention.adequacy: Deleting the library is complete and immediate and does not need a change window, which the upgrade does. Neither addresses payloads already written; provenance propagation is the only one of the three that would also have blocked the execution half.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alert on an archive handler writing outside the selected extraction directory, on executables appearing in per-user Startup folders without a deployment record, and on archives whose content format does not match their extension.
detection.adequacy: The out-of-destination write is the highest-fidelity signal because it is the defect itself and has no benign form. The Startup-folder signal is later and noisier but survives variants that pick a different write target, and it is the one that still fires when the extraction was not observed.

response.what_would_have_worked: Sweep every per-user Startup folder on hosts that ran WinRAR 5.61 or earlier, correlate any executable found against archive-extraction times, and treat a hit as user-context code execution predating the upgrade.
response.adequacy: Necessary precisely because upgrading is not remediation for this defect - the drop persists across the upgrade. Its limit is that the published chain's target is one convenient location among many the absolute-path write can reach, so a clean Startup folder is not a clean host.

NIST-800-53-SI-3.gap: Malicious code protection is positioned to inspect the file that arrives and the file that runs, and this defect exploits the gap between them. What arrives is an archive, commonly named .rar, whose malicious property is a filename field rather than executable content; what runs is an ordinary executable in the user's Startup folder, at a later logon, with no parent-process link back to the archive. SI-3 requires malicious-code protection at entry and exit points and periodic scanning; it does not require an archive handler to be treated as a file-writing privileged operation, nor does it require provenance to survive extraction, which is the only property that would connect the two halves.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: The Article 21 obligation measures against availability of the fix, and the fix here is not a patch - RARLAB removed unacev2.dll and ACE support in 5.70 beta 1 rather than issuing a corrected library, so there is no patched 5.61 and no fixed version of the vulnerable component to detect. An estate that upgraded WinRAR is compliant and remediated; an estate that deleted unacev2.dll and did not upgrade is remediated and shows as unpatched. The control has no representation for a vendor whose remediation is deletion of a feature, and none for the residue: a payload already in a Startup folder is unaffected by any version of WinRAR.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: The system-security outcome expects vulnerable software to be identified and updated. Identification fails on ownership rather than on technique: the vulnerable artefact is unacev2.dll, a 2006 third-party library bundled inside another vendor's product, so an inventory keyed on installed applications records 'WinRAR 5.61' and never sees the component that carries the defect - and the same library bundled by any other product is invisible for the same reason. The update half also under-delivers, because a CAF assessment that confirms WinRAR is now 5.70 or later has confirmed nothing about the executables the vulnerable version already wrote outside their extraction folders.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Essential Eight patch timeframes run from vendor release and produce a compliant record for an estate that upgraded WinRAR inside its window. Two things escape that framing. The effective interim action - deleting unacev2.dll from the installation directory - is a file removal, not a patch, and earns no credit under a patch-timeframe control despite closing the path completely. And the timeframe measures deployment of the fix, while the exploitation window that matters here closed earlier: the archive is delivered and extracted at one moment and the payload runs at the next logon, so an estate that patched inside its timeframe may still be executing payloads dropped before it did.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.7.gap: Protection against malware requires controls for detection, prevention and recovery combined with user awareness. Every element was present and none of them addressed this. Detection saw an archive whose malicious property is a path string; prevention allowed an archive utility to write where it was told, which is what archive utilities do; awareness told users not to run attachments, and the user did not run anything - they extracted one, and the executable ran at the next logon with no visible connection to the archive. The control has no requirement that an extraction operation be constrained to its destination folder, which is the single constraint that would have made all three effective.

new_control_requirements.name: ARCHIVE-CONTENT-TYPE-PROVENANCE
new_control_requirements.description: Archive and document handlers must dispatch rendering/execution on the content-verified file type rather than the displayed name or extension, and must propagate Mark-of-the-Web to extracted content.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Both halves of this control are the defect. WinRAR dispatches on content, so an archive named .rar reaches the ACE library and no extension-based control sees it coming - and the same property means an operator cannot block ACE by blocking a file extension. On the output side, extracted executables carried no Mark-of-the-Web, so an executable written into the Startup folder by an internet-sourced archive was indistinguishable at logon from one an administrator installed. Propagating provenance across extraction breaks the chain at the execution step even when the write itself is not prevented.

new_control_requirements.name: DOWNLOAD-PROVENANCE-ENFORCEMENT
new_control_requirements.description: Enforce Mark-of-the-Web / content-provenance on all internet-sourced files and block execution of provenance-stripped shortcuts, installers and script hosts regardless of a reputation verdict.
new_control_requirements.evidence: The gap between the two halves of this attack is measured in logons: the archive is extracted at one moment and the dropped executable runs at the next, with no process lineage joining them. Provenance enforcement is the only control listed that spans that gap, because it attaches to the file rather than to the moment. It also covers the residue the upgrade cannot reach - a payload written into a Startup folder before WinRAR was upgraded is still a provenance-stripped executable at every subsequent logon.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: 4h KEV-listing mitigation SLA applies.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CISA allowed six months here (added 2022-02-15, due 2022-08-15), which is generous for an action that needs no change window at all: deleting unacev2.dll from the WinRAR installation directory closes the path completely, because that library is the entire ACE implementation, and the only capability lost is opening a format the vendor itself discarded in 5.70 beta 1. An hours-scale SLA is achievable for this CVE in a way it is not for most, and the same window should be spent sweeping per-user Startup folders, since the upgrade does not remove what the vulnerable version already wrote.

attack_vector.description: A user opens a file - in the public proof of concept, an Office document carrying an embedded Flash object; Tenable's record also describes a maliciously crafted RAR file. The Flash Player runtime uses a com.adobe.tvsdk.mediacore.metadata object after it has been freed, and code executes with the privileges of the user whose application loaded the runtime.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none on the target - the attacker supplies a file
attack_vector.complexity: low in practice - the exploit is one file and a public proof of concept existed nineteen days after the vendor bulletin; the authorities disagree on whether the vector is local (NVD, 7.8) or network (Red Hat, 8.8), which is a scoring dispute about delivery rather than about exploitation difficulty
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered and not AI-weaponised. No AI tooling is credited in any source consulted, and the acknowledgement that would name the finder is in a vendor bulletin that is no longer retrievable.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Remove the Flash Player runtime from the estate - standalone installations and the copies embedded in Chrome, Edge and Internet Explorer 11 - and block documents carrying embedded Flash objects at the mail and web gateway.
prevention.framework_requiring_it: AU Essential Eight user application hardening (blocking Flash content in web browsers); CISA BOD 22-01 for the KEV listing added 2022-02-15, due 2022-08-15
prevention.adequacy: Sufficient and, since 2020-12-31, the only correct disposition - Adobe ended support on that date and blocked Flash content from running from 2021-01-12. Updating to the 2018 fixed build was sufficient against this CVE alone and left every later Flash defect open.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alert on the Flash runtime being instantiated by a document application, and on any child process created by the runtime or by the application that loaded it.
detection.adequacy: Reliable and cheap on a modern estate, because the base rate is now zero: any Flash instantiation at all is an anomaly worth investigating. On a 2018 estate that still used Flash content the same signal was noisy, which is precisely when it was needed.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treat the endpoint as compromised at the opening user's privilege, rotate that account's credentials, and identify every recipient of the same document or archive.
response.adequacy: Bounded by the user's own authorisation. The recipient-list step is the one that converts a single detected open into an accurate scope, since a weaponised document is delivered to a list rather than to a host.

NIST-800-53-CM-7.gap: Least functionality is the control that removes this surface, and by 2018 it had a clear target: Flash was already deprecated, already click-to-play in the major browsers, and already scheduled for end of life. What CM-7 does not do is force removal of a component that a named internal application still requires, and Flash's remaining 2018 install base was almost entirely that population - legacy internal dashboards and training content. The control's documented-exception route holds the exception open indefinitely, and it does not distinguish 'this application needs Flash' from 'every document this user opens can now instantiate the Flash runtime', which is the distinction the embedded-object delivery path exploits.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: The Article 21 patch-management obligation is keyed to fix availability, and the fix has been available since 2018-12-05. The gap is that 'patched' is not a single fact for this product. Two release tracks carry two different boundaries, and the runtime exists both standalone and embedded in three browsers with independent update channels - so an organisation can hold a complete, accurate, defensible patch record for the standalone estate and remain exposed through browser-embedded copies. The obligation asks whether fixes were applied within a timeframe; it has no language for a component whose version is not a single answerable value.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: The system-security outcome expects vulnerable software to be identified and updated. Identification fails here on the same duplication: the same runtime is present as a standalone installation and inside Chrome, Edge and Internet Explorer 11, and an inventory answers for whichever one it can see. Beyond that, the outcome's verb is 'updated', and the correct disposition for this component since 2020-12-31 is removal - a CAF assessment that confirms a working update process is confirming the wrong process, because there is nothing left to update to.

AU-Essential-8-App-Hardening.gap: User application hardening is the Essential Eight control that names web browsers and blocking Flash content specifically, and it is the right control - which makes this a maturity-model gap rather than a missing one. The requirement is a browser configuration posture; it carries no obligation to verify per host that the runtime is actually absent rather than merely blocked, and no obligation to re-verify after a browser update, a profile reset or the installation of an application that bundles its own Flash copy. An organisation can hold the control at a documented level while individual endpoints still carry a loadable runtime at or below 31.0.0.153.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: Management of technical vulnerabilities requires vulnerability information to be obtained and exposure evaluated, and the information available for this CVE is materially incomplete in a way the control has no way to register. Adobe's bulletin APSB18-42 - the vendor record naming the fixed builds and crediting the finder - is no longer retrievable; NVD's description is version-only; the class name that identifies the affected code comes from CISA's KEV title rather than from the vendor. A.8.8 assumes vulnerability information is obtainable and evaluates exposure against it. Here the primary source has decayed, and the control provides no way to record that an exposure evaluation was made against a degraded evidence base.

new_control_requirements.name: EOL-ASSET-DECOMMISSION
new_control_requirements.description: A network-reachable component with no vendor patch path must be isolated and decommissioned within a bounded window, with mandatory compensating segmentation or disablement applying until removal completes.
new_control_requirements.evidence: This control is written in the catalogue for end-of-life devices and is attached here as the closest existing control for the same terminal state in software - which for Flash Player is not a projection but a completed fact: Adobe ended support on 2020-12-31 and blocked Flash content from running from 2021-01-12. There is no build to move to that carries fixes for anything found after that date, so a host still able to load the runtime is in the removal case by definition. The bounded window has to cover both copies - the standalone installation and the browser-embedded one in Chrome, Edge and Internet Explorer 11 - because they are removed through different channels.

new_control_requirements.name: CONFIGURATION-SIDE-LIVE-PATCH-INVENTORY
new_control_requirements.description: For any vulnerability with a configuration-side mitigation path, that path must be inventoried, tested and deployable independently of the vendor-patch path, so that operators are not dependent on a patch cycle to remove reachability.
new_control_requirements.evidence: The configuration-side path for Flash is browser and document policy - click-to-play, disabling the ActiveX control, blocking embedded Flash objects in documents at the gateway - and it is the half that could be deployed on an estate whose legacy internal application still needed the runtime for one specific site. It has to be inventoried per host rather than assumed from policy, because the delivery path in the public proof of concept bypasses browser policy entirely: the object is embedded in an Office document, so a browser-scoped configuration leaves the reachable path open.

new_control_requirements.name: MITIGATION-ACTIVE-PATCH-PENDING-VERDICT-CLASS
new_control_requirements.description: Compliance verdicts must distinguish binary-patch-deployed from vendor-mitigation-active-without-patch from no-mitigation-at-all, and must surface the middle state as a time-bound compensating control rather than as a patched-per-SLA outcome.
new_control_requirements.evidence: For this CVE 'patched' is not one fact and cannot be recorded as one. Two release tracks carry two boundaries (31.0.0.153 main, 31.0.0.108 extended support), and the runtime exists both standalone and embedded in three browsers on their own update channels - so a verdict of 'patched' derived from the standalone inventory is a middle state, not a remediated one. The honest verdict for a host that still needs Flash for a legacy application is 'runtime blocked in browsers, embedded-object path filtered at the gateway, removal pending' with a date, which is exactly the class this control requires and which a two-state patched/unpatched record cannot express.

attack_vector.description: eval-stdin.php reads php://input and evals it. A request body starting with '<?php ' therefore runs as the web-server user, with no authentication anywhere in the path — and because php://input is the request body rather than a POST-specific stream, the verb is irrelevant, which is why the public Nuclei template sweeps with GET while NVD describes the flaw in terms of POST data — the file was written for a test harness that talks to itself over a pipe, so there was nothing to authenticate. It becomes an internet-facing code-execution endpoint the moment a Composer vendor/ tree is served from inside the document root, which is why the exposure tracks deployment shape rather than PHPUnit usage: applications that never run tests in production are hit exactly as hard as those that do.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N and UI:N. One unauthenticated request. Code runs as the web-server user, which on a typical PHP host can read the application's .env and database credentials.
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L, no race, no leak, no chaining. The only unknown is the deployment path, and the public Nuclei template enumerates seventeen of them in a single pass, so path variation costs an attacker one request set rather than any reconnaissance.
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Public disclosure is credited to B4bay of Vulnbusters on 27 Jun 2017, and the fix that preceded it was Bob Weinand's November 2016 commit; no AI-assisted discovery or weaponisation is claimed anywhere in the reference set.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Building production artifacts with composer install --no-dev, or placing the Composer vendor/ directory outside the document root. Failing either, upgrading PHPUnit to 4.8.28 or 5.6.3, deleting src/Util/PHP/eval-stdin.php, or denying /vendor/ at the web server.
prevention.adequacy: The two deployment controls are the durable ones and they are strictly stronger than the version bump: they close this file and every future file in the same shape, on any PHPUnit version. The version upgrade closes eval-stdin.php alone and leaves a dev dependency tree published to the internet. Ranking them the other way round — patching the library and leaving vendor/ in the docroot — is the choice most estates made, and it is why a nine-year-old CVE still reads 0.99999 on EPSS.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alerting on request bodies beginning with '<?php ' whatever the HTTP method, on any request to a path containing eval-stdin.php, and on the web-server user spawning a shell or a fetch utility; plus a build-time check that the deployed vendor/ tree contains no require-dev package.
detection.adequacy: The request-level signatures are precise and cheap because the trigger is a literal substring in the body and the paths are a closed, published set — this is one of the few flaws where a log query answers the question outright. Their weakness is that they detect the attempt, and given the EPSS of 0.99999 the attempt is continuous background noise; the signal that matters is the response, not the request. The build-time check is the one that prevents rather than reports.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating any successful hit as web-server-user code execution: sweep the docroot for files created since the exposure began, rotate every credential the web-server user could read — .env, database, API keys, mail credentials — and rebuild the deployment from a --no-dev artifact rather than deleting the one file.
response.adequacy: Credential rotation is the load-bearing step and the one most often skipped, because the visible damage is a web shell while the durable damage is the application's own secrets. Rebuilding from a corrected build artifact is right and also fixes the root cause in the same action. The limit is retrospective: with EPSS at the top of the distribution and the flaw public since 2017, 'when did the exposure begin' is usually unanswerable from logs, so rotation has to be assumed necessary rather than proven.

NIST-800-53-CM-7.gap: Least functionality is applied to installed software, enabled services and open ports. A Composer dev-scope package inside the application's own deployed tree is none of those, so a conformant CM-7 baseline can coexist with an internet-reachable eval() endpoint that no one ever chose to enable.

NIS2-Art21-supply-chain.gap: The supply-chain measure builds a register of direct suppliers and service providers. PHPUnit is a require-dev entry usually inherited from a framework skeleton, so it will not appear there, and the real defect — a build pipeline that shipped require-dev into production — is a pipeline property the measure does not reach.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: The patches have existed since 2017, so a scanning-and-patching programme should close this. It does not, because an authenticated scanner reading composer.json sees PHPUnit scoped to require-dev and reasonably concludes it is not in production — the exact inference this flaw punishes. Detection requires probing the deployed path, not reading the manifest.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: PHPUnit fixed this in 4.8.28 and 5.6.3 in 2017; CISA listed it on 2022-02-15 with a due date of 2022-08-15, and on 2026-08-28 EPSS still reads 0.99999 at the 99.994th percentile — the top of the distribution, nine years after the fix. This is the entry where a score-ordered queue and the KEV clock finally agree, and it is still unremediated at scale. 'Verified' here must not mean the PHPUnit version, because the version check passes on a host that still publishes its entire vendor/ tree: it has to mean an HTTP request to the eval-stdin.php paths returns 404, which is the same check the public Nuclei template performs.

new_control_requirements.name: TIER-3-DEPENDENCY-INVENTORY
new_control_requirements.description: Supply chain inventory must extend beyond direct dependencies to the dependencies pulled in behind them; SBOM coverage for transitive and non-runtime-scoped packages cannot be assumed from a direct-dependency manifest.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Attached as the closest existing control, with one scope difference stated plainly: PHPUnit here is a development-scoped dependency rather than a tier-3 transitive one. The failure mode is the same and is the one the control names — the package that carries the vulnerability is not in the inventory anyone reads. PHPUnit is typically inherited from a framework skeleton rather than chosen, it is scoped to require-dev so a manifest reader classifies it as absent from production, and the deployed vendor/ tree is the only artifact that shows it is actually there. The Nuclei template's seventeen path variants exist precisely because the file turns up under /laravel/, /yii/, /zend/ and /lib/ prefixes — deployments whose owners did not know they had shipped it.

CVE-2014-1761.name: Microsoft Word RTF listoverridecount Memory Corruption (MS14-017)

attack_vector.description: A crafted RTF document manipulates a listoverridecount field so that Word's parser misinterprets one data structure as another type, producing an out-of-bounds write and code execution as the current user. The document arrives as a mail attachment or a web download, and reaches the parser through the Outlook reading pane as well as through an explicit open, which is why Microsoft's tested workarounds include reading mail in plain text.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none beyond the victim's own session; the code runs with the current user's rights, and with complete control of the machine if that user is a local administrator
attack_vector.complexity: low - a single malformed field value rather than a heap-grooming race, weaponised in the wild before the patch and reproduced in a public exploit module two days after it
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered and not AI-weaponised. MS14-017 credits three named Google Security Team researchers, and the public module was built by reverse-engineering an in-the-wild sample.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Apply the MS14-017 update to every affected component, not only desktop Word. Before it was available, the Fix it 'Disable opening RTF content in Microsoft Word' (KB 2949660) or the equivalent Office File Block policy, which Microsoft states prevents exploitation, plus reading email in plain text.
prevention.adequacy: Sufficient once every carrier is patched, and that is the qualifier that matters: Word Viewer, the Office Compatibility Pack and the server-side rendering services each take their own package, so an estate can be attested as patched and still open crafted RTF through a copy the inventory never listed.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alert on WINWORD.EXE - and on Office Web Apps or Word Automation Services worker processes - spawning a child process, and treat repeated Word crashes on a single document as an exploitation attempt rather than a stability problem.
detection.adequacy: The process-lineage rule is durable because it keys on the consequence rather than on the sample. Content-based detection is weaker here: the malicious document differs from a benign one by a field value, and Microsoft's own account of the attacks as limited and targeted means prevalence signals contribute nothing.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treat a confirmed exploitation as user-level compromise of the workstation: rotate the user's credentials and cached tokens, recover the delivering message and check who else received it, and on a server-side hit treat the Word Automation Services or Office Web Apps service account as exposed.
response.adequacy: Adequate for the endpoint. The gap is scope discovery - a targeted campaign sends few messages, so establishing who else was addressed depends on mail-gateway retention rather than on anything the compromised host holds.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: Flaw remediation asks that flaws be identified, reported and corrected, and the correction here is not a single artefact: MS14-017 ships separate packages for Word 2003/2007/2010/2013, Word Viewer, the Office Compatibility Pack, Office for Mac 2011, Word Automation Services on SharePoint and Office Web Apps. An SI-2 process keyed to the inventoried Office installation records the flaw as corrected while the same RTF parser is still reachable through a Word Viewer copy outside managed distribution, or through a SharePoint conversion service that opens documents with no user involved at all.

NIST-800-53-SI-3.gap: Malicious code protection assumes the malicious artefact is recognisable. The carrier here is an RTF document differing from a benign one by the value of a listoverridecount field, and the exploitation Microsoft describes is 'limited, targeted attacks' - the low-volume case in which reputation and prevalence signals contribute nothing. Between Security Advisory 2953095 and the 2014-04-08 bulletin, SI-3 was the control organisations were relying on, and it was being asked to distinguish a type confusion in a parser it does not model.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: Art. 21 measures resolve to installing MS14-017. The window this CVE opens is the one before that existed: Microsoft published Security Advisory 2953095 with a Fix it while attacks were already under way in March 2014, and the update followed on 2014-04-08. An Art. 21 patch-management measure has no instrument for that interval - the action available was a File Block policy that stops Word opening RTF at all, which is an application-functionality decision rather than a patch, and Art. 21 neither requires it nor provides a route to authorise the resulting loss of function.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: The system security outcome expects services to be configured and maintained to resist attack. An estate fully current on Office in March 2014 met that and was exploitable anyway, because the flaw was being used before the fix existed. The configuration lever that did work - blocking RTF through the File Block policy, and reading mail in plain text - is a deliberate reduction in what the software does, so meeting B4 through it means accepting a functionality change rather than performing maintenance.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: The Essential Eight patch-applications control names office productivity suites explicitly and runs its timeframes from vendor release, so its clock on this CVE starts 2014-04-08 - after the targeted attacks Microsoft describes and after Security Advisory 2953095. An organisation at the target maturity level is therefore compliant throughout the exposed period, and the control's scoping compounds it: Word Viewer and the Office Compatibility Pack are the carriers least likely to be enumerated as part of the office suite, and both are rated Critical for this CVE.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: Management of technical vulnerabilities requires vulnerability information to be obtained and acted on. Here the vendor did supply an interim action - the Fix it and File Block policy - which makes this a case where A.8.8's weakness is not the absence of a measure but the classification of one: an estate running the File Block workaround is in a different state from an estate running the update, and an A.8.8 register that records both as 'addressed' loses the distinction between a mitigation that can be reverted or misconfigured and a binary patch that removes the defect.

new_control_requirements.name: MITIGATION-ACTIVE-PATCH-PENDING-VERDICT-CLASS
new_control_requirements.description: Compliance verdicts must distinguish three states: binary patch deployed (vulnerability eliminated); vendor-mitigation rule active with no binary patch, carrying the residual risk that any defect in or reversal of the mitigation reopens the vulnerability; and no mitigation and no patch (full exposure). Audit reports must surface the middle state as a distinct compensating-control state with a time-bound action item, never as a 'patched per SLA' outcome.
new_control_requirements.evidence: This CVE spent a defined period in the middle state: Microsoft Security Advisory 2953095 shipped the Fix it 'Disable opening RTF content in Microsoft Word' while attacks were under way, and MS14-017 delivered the binary patch on 2014-04-08. The two states are materially different - the Fix it is an Office File Block policy setting that a user or a later policy change can undo, and Microsoft explicitly notes it need not be removed before the update, so a host can carry both, one, or neither. The distinguishing test: report Fix-it-applied and update-applied as separate columns, and treat any host in the first without the second as an open item with a date.

new_control_requirements.name: EMBEDDED-MEDIA-PARSER-LIBRARY-INVENTORY-AND-PATCH-PARITY
new_control_requirements.description: An organization must inventory every place a high-risk document or media parser is bundled - including copies shipped inside separate products, viewers, compatibility packs and server-side rendering services - and confirm each copy reports the fixed build, rather than closing the remediation ticket when the primary inventoried product updates.
new_control_requirements.evidence: MS14-017 rates this same RTF parser Critical in Word 2003 through 2013, Word Viewer, the Office Compatibility Pack Service Pack 3, Office for Mac 2011, Word Automation Services on SharePoint Server 2010 and 2013, Office Web Apps 2010 and Office Web Apps Server 2013 - eight or more separately-packaged carriers, several of which are not part of the office-suite line in an asset register. The server-side ones invert the threat model as well: Word Automation Services opens documents with no user to convince. The distinguishing test: after the update lands, enumerate each of those components across the estate and confirm none still reports a pre-fix build, rather than reading the desktop Office version alone. The bulletin records a conditional restart, so a component updated but not restarted is not yet remediated.

new_control_requirements.name: ARCHIVE-CONTENT-TYPE-PROVENANCE
new_control_requirements.description: Document and archive handlers must dispatch rendering on the content-verified file type rather than on the displayed name or extension, and untrusted-origin marking must be applied at the ingress boundary and preserved through whatever container the file is delivered in, so the sandboxing decision does not depend on attacker-supplied metadata.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Word dispatches on content, so an RTF payload carrying a .doc extension reaches the vulnerable parser while an extension-based mail or gateway rule sees a Word document - which is why Microsoft's own workaround is a File Block policy on the RTF content type rather than an extension filter. The provenance half is what makes the reading-pane path defensible: MS14-017's second tested workaround is reading mail in plain text precisely because a message rendered as Rich Text reaches the parser without the user opening anything. The distinguishing test: send an externally-sourced RTF renamed to .doc through each ingress path and confirm the handler treats it as RTF from an untrusted origin, rather than confirming only that a policy is enabled.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CISA listed this on 2022-02-15 with a 2022-08-15 due date - six months, the longest window class in the catalogue - for a flaw with a verified public exploit module since 2014-04-10 and an EPSS of 0.7746 at the 99.535th percentile on 2026-08-28. Because the vendor patch has existed since 2014-04-08, a four-hour clock here resolves to the compensating control rather than the update: apply the RTF File Block policy and force plain-text mail reading on any host that still reports a pre-MS14-017 build of any affected component, and schedule the update behind that.

CVE-2013-3906.name: Microsoft Graphics Component TIFF Integer Overflow (CVE-2013-3906)

attack_vector.description: A crafted TIFF embedded as a drawing in an Office document drives a DWORD calculation in GDI+ past 32 bits, so HeapAlloc is asked for zero bytes; attacker-controlled EXIF data is then memcpy'd into that chunk, overwriting a function pointer later called through OGL!GdipCreatePath. The observed delivery was an emailed Word attachment.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none, but the victim must open the document; code runs with the opening user's rights
attack_vector.complexity: low - deterministic parser arithmetic with the heap groomed via ActiveX; a Metasploit module followed the bulletin
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-assisted. Reported by Haifei Li of the McAfee Labs IPS Team from in-the-wild samples in 2013.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Apply every MS13-096 package applicable to the products installed on the host - 2901674, 2850047, 2817641, 2817670, 2899397 - and restart. Before 2013-12-10, the TIFF-codec registry workaround (Fix it KB 2908005) on the platforms where it applies.
prevention.adequacy: Adequate only when applied per product; an OS-only patch pass leaves the codec reachable through Office, the Viewers or Lync.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alert on Office, Viewer and Lync processes spawning children after a document open, and on GDI+ faults during image rendering.
detection.adequacy: Behavioural only. Microsoft describes very limited targeted attacks, so volume-based detection would not have fired.

response.what_would_have_worked: Establish which MS13-096 packages the host actually received, apply the rest, and reverse the Lync data-collaboration workaround from Advisory 2896666 once patched.
response.adequacy: Necessary because the bulletin's five packages make a partial patch look like a complete one in any per-host record.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: Flaw remediation scoped by operating system misses this entirely. Microsoft's own affected-software table records Windows 7 SP1, Windows 8, 8.1, Server 2012 and Server 2012 R2 as unaffected at the OS level while marking those same platforms affected when Office 2007 SP3, the Compatibility Pack SP3, Excel Viewer or Lync is installed - so an SI-2 process reconciling OS build numbers reports full compliance on hosts that need updates 2817641 or 2899397.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: MS13-096 is five separate update packages for one CVE - 2901674, 2850047, 2817641, 2817670 and 2899397 - and which of them a host needs depends on the Office, Viewer and Lync products installed on it. A patch-management process that tracks one bulletin as one action per host closes the ticket when the first package lands, while the codec remains reachable through whichever affected product did not receive its own update.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: Secure configuration and maintenance treats the workaround and the update as interchangeable evidence of 'the vulnerability is addressed'. Here they are not: the TIFF-codec registry workaround does not apply to Windows 8, 8.1, Server 2012, Server 2012 R2, RT or RT 8.1 at all, and the separate Lync data-collaboration workaround from Advisory 2896666 has to be reversed after patching or it silently keeps a business function disabled - neither state is 'patched', and the CAF outcome does not require them to be recorded apart.

AU-Essential-8-App-Hardening.gap: Application hardening focuses on blocking untrusted content in browsers and Office macros. This exploit needed neither: the payload is a TIFF image inside a Word document, rendered by GDI+ during ordinary document display, so macro settings, protected-view rules and browser hardening leave the parser reachable. The hardening measure that would have worked - disabling the TIFF codec - is not part of the standard baseline and is unavailable on the newer Windows versions.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: Management of technical vulnerabilities depends on the asset inventory answering where the vulnerable component is, and GDI+ is bundled across the OS, four Office generations, three standalone Viewers and four Lync builds. An inventory recording products but not the update level of each affected product cannot tell an operator which of the five MS13-096 packages a given host still needs - which is exactly the question that decides whether the exposure closed.

new_control_requirements.name: EMBEDDED-MEDIA-PARSER-LIBRARY-INVENTORY-AND-PATCH-PARITY
new_control_requirements.description: An organization must inventory every place a high-risk embedded media-parsing library (font, image, codec and document parsers) is statically or dynamically bundled - including copies vendored inside individual applications - and apply the security update to all of them, not only the OS-level package.
new_control_requirements.evidence: MS13-096 is the exact case the control describes and states the divergence itself: the OS-level GDI+ update (2901674) covers only Windows Vista SP2 and Server 2008 SP2, while the same codec ships inside Office 2003 SP3, 2007 SP3 and 2010 SP1/SP2, the Office Compatibility Pack SP3, Word Viewer, Excel Viewer, the PowerPoint 2010 Viewer and four Lync builds, each with its own package - 2850047, 2817641, 2817670 and 2899397. Microsoft's table marks Windows 7, 8, 8.1, Server 2012 and Server 2012 R2 as unaffected at the OS level and affected through an installed Office or Lync product, so the distinguishing test is per-product: after the OS pass, enumerate each installed Office, Viewer and Lync build and confirm it carries its own MS13-096 package, because the host-level verdict cannot see the bundled copies.

new_control_requirements.name: CONFIGURATION-SIDE-LIVE-PATCH-INVENTORY
new_control_requirements.description: For any vulnerability with a configuration-side mitigation path: that path must be inventoried, tested, and deployable independent of the vendor-patch path.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Microsoft published Advisory 2896666 on 2013-11-05 with the vulnerability under attack and no update until MS13-096 on 2013-12-10, so for five weeks the only available action was the configuration path: a GDI+ registry entry disabling the TIFF codec, automated by the Microsoft Fix it in KB 2908005, plus a separate 'Disable data collaboration in Lync' measure. The control's inventory obligation is what makes that deployable in five weeks rather than improvised - and this CVE also shows its limits, stated in the bulletin: the TIFF-codec workaround does not apply to Windows 8, 8.1, Server 2012, Server 2012 R2, RT or RT 8.1, so part of the estate had no configuration-side option at all, and the Lync measure has to be reversed after patching or file, poll and whiteboard sharing stays broken.

new_control_requirements.name: ARCHIVE-CONTENT-TYPE-PROVENANCE
new_control_requirements.description: Archive and document handlers must dispatch rendering and execution on the content-verified file type rather than the displayed name or extension, and must propagate Mark-of-the-Web to every extracted file.
new_control_requirements.evidence: The exploit is an image, not a macro or an executable: MSRC's account is an emailed Word attachment containing a malformed graphics image, which Office hands to GDI+ during ordinary document rendering. The provenance the control asks to be carried is precisely what is missing - the TIFF inherits the document's rendering context rather than its internet origin, so a parser with no notion of untrusted input handles an attacker-supplied EXIF blob. For this CVE the control means the document handler treats an embedded image stream as content whose type is verified and whose external origin follows it into the codec, rather than dispatching on the drawing's declared type inside a file the user has already been persuaded to open.

attack_vector.description: FrameLoader::loadInSameDocument holds the SerializedScriptValue state object as a raw pointer. A History API same-document navigation changes focus, the focus change fires blur, and script in the blur handler calls history.replaceState — freeing the state object mid-use. Reallocating it under attacker control gives the usual WebKit use-after-free route to renderer code execution. Delivery is a web page.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — an unauthenticated remote page; UI:R is satisfied by a navigation.
attack_vector.complexity: low to exploit, and cheaper than a novel bug: the same defect was fixed in 2013 and reintroduced in 2016, so five years of public prior art on the original applied. Renderer execution alone is not device compromise; a full chain needs a sandbox escape that neither Apple nor Project Zero describes.
attack_vector.ai_factor: None claimed or evidenced. Apple credits 'an anonymous researcher' with no affiliation, so the discovery route is unknown rather than attributable.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: iOS/iPadOS 15.3.1 or macOS Monterey 12.2.1 on 2022-02-10, or Safari 15.3 verified by build number on Big Sur and Catalina. For devices outside the support list, replacement — there was no other control.
prevention.adequacy: Adequate where a fixed build existed and unavailable where it did not. The macOS split is the trap: a Big Sur host can be fully current on OS updates and still run pre-15.3 Safari, and the fix only takes effect once Safari is restarted.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Renderer crash telemetry naming SerializedScriptValue or FrameLoader::loadInSameDocument, and content inspection for script calling history.replaceState from a blur handler.
detection.adequacy: Almost nothing to work with in practice. Project Zero had no access to the exploit sample, so no infrastructure, hash or URL indicator was ever published, and on iOS the crash reports that would carry the signal are not routinely collected by enterprise tooling.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating a suspected hit on a high-risk user as device replacement rather than remediation, since renderer execution on a mobile device cannot be cleaned in place with any confidence.
response.adequacy: Correct and rarely actionable: with no indicators published there is usually no basis on which to suspect a specific device, so the response plan is triggered by intelligence the organisation does not have.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: Three different fixed identifiers cover one CVE — iOS 15.3.1, macOS 12.2.1, and a Safari build number on Big Sur and Catalina. A scanner reading the OS version marks a fully-patched Big Sur host with old Safari as remediated, and SI-2 has no expression for a component version that is not the operating system's.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: Apple excluded pre-iPhone-6s, pre-iPad-Air-2 and pre-iPad-mini-4 devices from the 15.3.1 release, so for that part of the estate there is no patch for the process to manage. The measure records an open item indefinitely rather than the decommissioning decision the situation actually demands.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: Browser choice is treated as an available hardening lever and on iOS and iPadOS it is not one — every browser is required to use WebKit, so standardising away from Safari changes the interface and not the engine. An estate can evidence a browser-hardening decision that has no bearing on this flaw.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: The strategy's application-patching windows assume an application with one update mechanism. Here the same engine is patched as a browser component on two macOS versions, as a full OS release on two other platforms, and not at all on excluded devices — three different remediation shapes that the maturity model scores as one.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: The register must track a Safari build number, two OS versions and a WebKitGTK/WPE version under WSA-2022-0003 as separate entries for a single CVE. Operating-system inventory produces one of those, so the register can be complete against its own scope and silent on the engine that renders untrusted content.

new_control_requirements.name: MOBILE-ZERO-CLICK-HARDENING
new_control_requirements.description: High-risk mobile users must operate in a reduced-attack-surface mode (e.g. Lockdown Mode) that disables automatic processing of untrusted message attachments, fonts, link previews and just-in-time compilation.
new_control_requirements.evidence: This CVE is the argument for the control existing rather than a case where it was skipped: Apple's advisories of 2022-02-10 report the issue as possibly actively exploited, and no reduced-attack-surface mode existed on iOS at that date — Lockdown Mode was announced later that year. The estate therefore had exactly two states, patched and exploitable, with nothing in between and nothing available to devices outside the iPhone 6s / iPad Air 2 / iPad mini 4 support floor. Where the mode now exists, it is the only control that acts before the vendor's release.

new_control_requirements.name: MOBILE-ENDPOINT-MDM-ENFORCED-KEV-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: Declarative device management must enforce a 24-hour KEV update SLA on mobile estates, measured against the OS build actually running on each enrolled device.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Apple shipped iOS and iPadOS 15.3.1 on 2022-02-10 and CISA listed the CVE on 2022-02-11 with a 2022-02-25 due date — one day between availability and listing. On an estate where mobile updates are user-initiated, the measurable quantity is the build each device reports, and enforcement has to distinguish the devices that can take 15.3.1 from those the support list excludes, because the second group needs a replacement decision rather than an update push.

new_control_requirements.name: BROWSER-MANAGED-UPDATE-NO-DEFERRAL
