new_control_requirements.description: Enterprise update rings must not defer security-channel browser updates beyond 24h, and must track the browser or engine build as a version distinct from the operating system's.
new_control_requirements.evidence: On macOS Big Sur and Catalina the fix for this CVE is Safari 15.3, identified by build 16612.4.9.1.8 and 15612.4.9.1.8 respectively, and not by any change to the OS version — while on Monterey the same fix is OS release 12.2.1. An update ring or scanner keyed to the operating-system version reports the Big Sur population as current while it runs the vulnerable engine, and the new build only loads once Safari is restarted.

CVE-2021-36934.name: Microsoft Windows SAM Local Privilege Escalation Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: Permissive ACLs on %windir%\System32\config from Windows 10 build 1809 let any user read the SAM, SYSTEM and SECURITY hives out of a Volume Shadow Copy of the system volume, recovering local account hashes and the boot key that decrypts them and reaching SYSTEM. No memory corruption is involved; the whole chain is file reads against a copy the operating system made.
attack_vector.privileges_required: low — PR:L; an ordinary interactive account with no elevation path is sufficient.
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L, UI:N. The only precondition is that a shadow copy of the system volume exists, which System Protection creates when enabled. Microsoft's temporal metric at the time was E:F, functional exploit code.
attack_vector.ai_factor: Reported by Jonas Lykkegaard and named by Kevin Beaumont, who published the first exploit. No automated discovery is claimed; the finding is a comparison of file permissions between Windows builds.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Both halves, in order: correct the ACLs (the manual icacls workaround, then KB5005030 / KB5005031 / KB5005033 with a restart), and delete every Volume Shadow Copy of the system volume per KB5005357.
prevention.adequacy: The pair is complete. Either half alone is not: the ACL fix leaves the old copies readable, and deleting the copies on an unpatched host leaves the next copy exposed. Microsoft's FAQ makes the ordering explicit and exempts hosts that did the manual workaround and the deletion before the update.

detection.what_would_have_worked: File-access auditing or endpoint telemetry on reads of SAM, SYSTEM and SECURITY from GLOBALROOT shadow-copy paths by a non-SYSTEM token, and alerting on shadow-copy enumeration by a standard user.
detection.adequacy: The read is the entire attack, so detection here is genuinely close to prevention — but it fires on an action the operating system permits, which means it needs the token context to be part of the rule rather than the path alone.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating a confirmed read as a credential incident rather than a host incident: rotate every local account password on the affected build image, on the assumption that the hash is shared across the image, and hunt for reuse of the local administrator hash against peers.
response.adequacy: Rotation scope depends on knowing which hosts share a local administrator password, which is an inventory question most estates answer only after the incident. The flaw grants no persistence of its own, so the credential is the whole of the loss and the whole of the response.

NIST-800-53-AC-6.gap: AC-6 governs privileges the organisation assigns; the failing boundary is a file permission the vendor shipped from build 1809. The control is fully satisfied by an estate whose users are all standard users — which is precisely the population that can carry out this attack — and nothing in an AC-6 assessment inspects discretionary ACLs on operating-system files.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: The measure ends at deploying the vendor update, and the vendor says in the same advisory that the update does not fully mitigate the vulnerability. An entity fully compliant on patch cadence is still exposed through every shadow copy taken before the install, and the measure contains no obligation and no record for the deletion step that closes it.

UK-CAF-B2.gap: The outcome protects access to systems and data through verified identities, and the store those identities are verified against was world-readable on the host. B2's subject matter was being undermined by something B2 does not look at, so an estate with exemplary identity controls scores the same as one without while any standard user can lift the local administrator hash.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Patch cadence is the wrong unit of measurement for a defect whose vendor states the patch is insufficient. Top maturity on this strategy is achievable and achieved on a fleet that is still exposed, and the shadow-copy deletion that actually remediates has no representation in the model at all.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.9.gap: The configuration in question is a vendor default rather than an organisational setting, so it enters no baseline and produces no drift finding. A.8.9 can be fully implemented, documented, monitored and reviewed on a fleet where a one-line icacls check would have shown the built-in Users group holding read access on the SAM file.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Functional exploit code was public from 2021-07-20 and the update followed in August 2021, so for this CVE the whichever-is-later clause resolves to patch availability and the KEV listing of 2022-02-10 arrives long after the risk did. The clause that matters operationally is 'verified mitigation': for this defect verification is the icacls check plus the absence of pre-update shadow copies, not the presence of a KB, and the Essential Eight's cadence measure cannot express that difference.

new_control_requirements.name: ACTIVELY-EXPLOITED-OS-LPE-REMEDIATION-WINDOW-ENFORCEMENT
new_control_requirements.description: When an OS vendor flags a local-privilege-escalation flaw as exploited in the wild (and it is KEV-listed), the monthly cumulative update that fixes it must be applied and rebooted across the entire affected endpoint fleet within the KEV remediation window, not on the normal patch cadence, and account-privilege policy must not be relied on to contain it. The distinguishing test: enumerate the fleet's installed build numbers against the fixed build for each SKU and confirm zero endpoints remain below it past the due date - a paper patch-management policy that ships monthly rollups on a 30-day cadence still leaves an actively-exploited LPE open during the window the vendor flagged it as exploited.
new_control_requirements.evidence: The control's second clause is the one that answers the least-privilege gap directly: account-privilege policy cannot contain this flaw, because PR:L means an ordinary standard user is the attacker the control is designed to permit. Its first clause answers the patch-management gap on timing — all three KBs are Restart Required: Yes, so the fleet enumeration must be against installed build and uptime rather than deployment success. For this CVE the enumeration needs a second column that the control's own wording does not yet carry: the presence of shadow copies predating the install.

new_control_requirements.name: MITIGATION-ACTIVE-PATCH-PENDING-VERDICT-CLASS
new_control_requirements.description: Compliance verdicts must distinguish three states: (a) binary patch deployed (vulnerability eliminated), (b) vendor-mitigation rule active, no binary patch (residual risk: any defect in the mitigation rule reopens the vulnerability), (c) no mitigation, no patch (full exposure). Audit reports must surface (b) as a distinct compensating-control state with an associated time-bound action item, not as a 'patched per SLA' outcome.
new_control_requirements.evidence: This CVE is the case the control was written for, inverted: the binary patch is deployed and the vulnerability is not eliminated, because Microsoft states that installing the update does not fully mitigate it until the shadow copies are deleted. Until a verdict class exists for 'patched, residual exposure pending an operator action', a configuration review under A.8.9 and an access-control assessment under B2 both close the item on a host where the hives remain readable, and neither produces the time-bound action the deletion needs.

CVE-2020-0796.name: Microsoft SMBv3 Compression Remote Code Execution Vulnerability (SMBGhost)

attack_vector.description: Srv2DecompressData in srv2.sys sizes its destination buffer from the OriginalCompressedSegmentSize field of the SMB2 COMPRESSION_TRANSFORM_HEADER without validating it, producing an integer overflow, an undersized allocation and a controlled kernel pool overflow. Compression is negotiated in the SMB 3.1.1 handshake before authentication, so no credential is involved, and the defect is symmetric — a malformed compressed message to a listening server, or a malicious server answering a client that connects to it. Execution is in kernel context, hence S:C and a 10.0 base score.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N and UI:N. The compression capability is negotiated pre-authentication, which is the property that makes this wormable rather than merely severe.
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L. The early public RCE was self-described as unreliable, but the Metasploit modules that followed reduced exploitation to selecting a target, and EPSS reached 0.9981 at the 99.958th percentile. The only genuine constraint is population: only builds 1903 and 1909 implement SMBv3.1.1 compression.
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. The disclosure and the exploit development are from 2020 and no AI tooling is credited in Microsoft's advisory or in the public analyses.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Installing KB4551762 on 2020-03-12 and restarting, or today moving the host to a supported Windows build. In the two days before the patch, and afterwards where a restart could not be scheduled, setting DisableCompression to 1 under HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\LanmanServer\Parameters and blocking TCP/445 at the perimeter.
prevention.adequacy: The update is complete. The workaround is not, and its incompleteness is directional rather than partial: DisableCompression applies to the SMB server role, so a 1903 or 1909 client that connects to an attacker's SMB server is exploited through the identical code path with the workaround in place. Blocking 445 at the perimeter addresses none of the east-west spread that makes a wormable SMB flaw dangerous.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Matching SMB2 NEGOTIATE requests that carry a SMB2_COMPRESSION_CAPABILITIES context and COMPRESSION_TRANSFORM_HEADER messages whose OriginalCompressedSegmentSize is implausible for the message size; host-side, alerting on srv2.sys bugchecks and on unexpected children or threads in spoolsv.exe and winlogon.exe.
detection.adequacy: The network signature is precise because the malformed field is the primitive itself, and it is observable pre-authentication. Its dependency is inspection of internal SMB, which is exactly the traffic most estates do not decode east-west — and the process-injection targets only cover exploitation by the two Metasploit modules, not by bespoke code.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating a hit as kernel-level compromise: rebuild rather than patch in place, rotate every credential and machine account the host held, and check whether the host had initiated outbound SMB to servers outside the file-service inventory, since the client-side path leaves no server-side artefact.
response.adequacy: Rebuild is the only defensible outcome for code execution in kernel context. Scoping is the hard part: failed attempts bugcheck the host, which is visible, while successful exploitation leaves the machine running, so an absence of crashes across an estate is not evidence of an absence of compromise.

NIST-800-53-SC-7.gap: SC-7 is assessed at the boundary, and ADV200005's own network measure is a perimeter block on TCP/445 against a vulnerability whose worst case is east-west. SC-7 also has no direction: a 1903 or 1909 host connecting outward to a malicious SMB server is exploited through the same defect, so a perfect inbound posture covers half the vulnerability.

NIS2-Art21-network-security.gap: The obligation is met by segmenting and filtering the service, and the service is the one every segment needs. It offers nothing distinguishing SMB traffic to a 1903 or 1909 host from any other, and an entity that deployed exactly Microsoft's recommended DisableCompression setting still left the client direction of a CVSS 10.0 scope-changed flaw open.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: The available hardening is DisableCompression=1 on LanmanServer, published 2020-03-10. A B4 build standard carrying it records a hardened build without a field for either limit: it covers the server role only, and it does not remove the vulnerable Srv2DecompressData code.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: SMB on an internal file server is not normally classed internet-facing, so a CVSS 10.0 pre-auth kernel flaw with EPSS 0.9981 inherits a slower band than a lesser internet-facing bug. And because the affected population is exactly builds 1903 and 1909, an estate-wide OS-patch percentage can read high while every host with the vulnerable code is behind.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: The timeliness signals were maximal — ADV200005 on 2020-03-10 before a patch existed, KB4551762 on 2020-03-12, a public LPE on 2020-03-30, a public RCE on 2020-06-02. What A.8.8 does not carry is the denominator: only 1903 and 1909 hold the vulnerable code, so an exposure evaluation across all Windows hosts measures the wrong population.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2020-0796 — KEV-listed 2022-02-10 with a six-month due date of 2022-08-10 on a pre-auth kernel RCE with CVSS 10.0, S:C and EPSS 0.9981. The four-hour clock with a compensating-controls limb is what would have driven the DisableCompression registry value and 445 filtering out immediately while the restart for KB4551762 was scheduled, instead of leaving a half-year window on a wormable flaw.

new_control_requirements.name: MITIGATION-ACTIVE-PATCH-PENDING-VERDICT-CLASS
new_control_requirements.description: Compliance verdicts must distinguish three states: (a) binary patch deployed and the vulnerability eliminated, (b) vendor-mitigation rule active with no binary patch, carrying explicit residual risk, and (c) neither.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2020-0796 — DisableCompression=1 on LanmanServer is state (b) and looks identical to state (a) in any inventory that records 'mitigated'. The residual risk is specific and directional: the setting covers the SMB server role only, so the client half of a symmetric pre-auth kernel flaw stays exploitable, and the vulnerable Srv2DecompressData code is still present. A verdict model that cannot express (b) reports those hosts as done.

new_control_requirements.name: SCANNER-PAPER-COMPLIANCE-TEST
new_control_requirements.description: A vulnerability scanner that reports 'patched' based on package version alone is paper compliance. The operational test must account for the actual mitigation state, and the reported population must be the population that holds the vulnerable code.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2020-0796 — the vulnerable code exists only in Windows 10 and Server 1903 and 1909, because SMBv3.1.1 compression was added in 1903. A scan result expressed as a percentage of Windows hosts patched dilutes that sliver into an estate-wide figure that reads well, and the same scan cannot distinguish a host carrying only the DisableCompression workaround from a patched one.

CVE-2018-1000861.name: Jenkins Stapler Web Framework Deserialization of Untrusted Data Vulnerability

attack_vector.description: Stapler routes URLs onto Java objects by reflection, and Jenkins checks access at the entry point rather than at each method the routing can reach, so a crafted URL invokes methods never intended to be called over HTTP. The published chain reaches CpsFlowDefinition's checkScriptCompile endpoint and submits Groovy containing @GrabConfig(disableChecksums=true), @GrabResolver pointing at an attacker-controlled repository and @Grab naming a dependency — compiling the script fetches and runs attacker code as the Jenkins controller account, which holds the credentials store, build secrets, signing material and deploy tokens for everything the instance builds.
attack_vector.privileges_required: None on the published unauthenticated path, but only up to a point: Rapid7 documents the ACL-bypass gadget in the public Metasploit module as specific to Jenkins 2.137 and earlier. Between 2.138 and 2.153 the same reflection flaw needs a session with some read access, so version alone does not tell an operator whether their instance is internet-exploitable or insider-exploitable.
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L, a single HTTP GET, with a Metasploit module, a nuclei template and a vulhub reproduction environment all publicly available.
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Jenkins credits researchers from Apple Information Security, CloudBees, Tenable and DEVCORE, and independently Orange Tsai; the finding is an architectural observation about where the ACL check sits relative to Stapler's routing, and no automated tooling is credited.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Upgrading to weekly 2.154 or LTS 2.138.4 / 2.150.1 and restarting the controller. Where the upgrade is blocked by a validated plugin set, refusing /securityRealm/user/*/descriptorByName/* at the reverse proxy and removing the controller from networks it does not need to serve.
prevention.adequacy: The upgrade is complete. The proxy rule is explicitly a filter on one known route and not a fix — Stapler's reflective routing reaches more than the checkScriptCompile endpoint, so blocking the published path narrows the public tooling without closing the class. Neither action addresses what the controller already handed out if it was reachable while unpatched.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alerting on any request to a descriptorByName path carrying @Grab, @GrabResolver or @GrabConfig; alerting on the controller process spawning shells; and treating outbound dependency fetches to non-organisational repositories as an exception rather than as build noise.
detection.adequacy: The request signature is high fidelity and cheap, and it only catches the published chain. The controller-spawns-shell signal is broader but noisy on a machine whose job is executing arbitrary build steps — which is exactly why the Watchbog and Kerberods payloads reported in 2019 could establish cron persistence without standing out.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating an exposed controller as a supply-chain incident rather than a host incident: rebuild the controller from a known-good image instead of upgrading in place, rotate the credentials store, build secrets, signing keys and deploy tokens, and enumerate the artefacts published during the exposure window to decide which downstream consumers need telling.
response.adequacy: Correct and rarely rehearsed. Upgrading in place is the default reflex and it leaves cron persistence and any injected build step in place; the credential rotation reaches every system the controller could deploy to, which is usually a larger list than the CI owner maintains. The artefact-provenance question is the hardest part, because most instances cannot say what they signed on a given day.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: Jenkins released 2.154 and LTS 2.138.4 / 2.150.1 on 2018-12-05, three years before the 2022-02-10 KEV listing and its unusually long 2022-08-10 due date. SI-2 reports the CVE remediated wherever the LTS train is followed and offers nothing but an overdue ticket for a controller pinned to an old core because a plugin set was validated against it — which is the population still exposed.

NIS2-Art21-supply-chain.gap: The Article's supplier-assessment framing points outward at the entity's suppliers. Here the entity's own build controller is the supplier to everything downstream: execution as the Jenkins account reaches signing material and deploy tokens, so the entity's published artefacts are what becomes untrustworthy, and nothing in Article 21(2)(d) asks it to look in that direction.

UK-CAF-D1.gap: A build-server recovery plan written around availability restores the controller and restarts the pipelines. The decision this incident needs pre-agreed is that every credential the controller held is exposed and every artefact built in the window is suspect — and Watchbog's cron persistence, reported against this CVE in 2019, means a restored-not-rebuilt controller comes back compromised.

AU-ISM-1808.gap: ISM-1808 governs the software an organisation consumes. Jenkins is simultaneously consumed software and the machine that produces the organisation's own software, and the control reaches only the first half — it imposes no requirement to establish what a controller signed or published while it was running weekly 2.153 or LTS 2.138.3.

ISO-27001-2022-A.5.21.gap: The clause's instruments are supplier agreements, assurance and monitoring, and none of them applies to a controller the organisation runs itself — which is where the credentials for the entire downstream chain are concentrated. The supply chain A.5.21 examines runs inward from suppliers; this one runs outward from the entity's own machine.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Jenkins fixed this on 2018-12-05 and CISA listed it on 2022-02-10 with a due date of 2022-08-10 — a six-month window, far longer than KEV's usual two weeks, on a pre-authentication code-execution flaw with a Metasploit module, a nuclei template and a documented 2019 botnet campaign. The 'whichever is later' clause is what makes the listing itself the trigger on a controller that stayed pinned to an old core for plugin-compatibility reasons, and 'documented compensating controls' has to mean the proxy block on /securityRealm/user/*/descriptorByName/* plus network removal, recorded as a filter with a known gap rather than as a fix.

new_control_requirements.name: ORPHAN-COMMIT-RELEASE-DETECTION
new_control_requirements.description: Reject release tags whose target commit is not reachable from the default branch (git merge-base --is-ancestor). Forged orphan-commit releases are a signature of the maintainer-impersonation class.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Attached as the closest existing control on build-output provenance, and extended here from the tag case to the controller case: this CVE gives an unauthenticated HTTP request the Jenkins service account, and with it the credentials store, signing material and deploy tokens for everything the instance publishes. The provenance question the control asks about a release tag is the same one nobody can answer about an artefact built on a controller that was running weekly 2.153 or LTS 2.138.3 while reachable — which is what turns this from a host compromise into a downstream one. The testable requirement is that every published artefact is traceable to a commit reachable from the default branch and to a build whose inputs are recorded, so that an exposure window can be converted into a specific list of suspect artefacts rather than a blanket assumption.

new_control_requirements.name: PERIMETER-COMPROMISE-REBUILD-NOT-PATCH
new_control_requirements.description: Pre-rehearsed IR runbook for any perimeter device that suffers a pre-auth RCE CVE in active exploitation MUST default to config-exfil + rebuild + credential rotation, not patch-in-place. Patch-in-place leaves attacker-installed implants intact.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Written for perimeter devices and applied here to a CI controller, which occupies the same position — a reachable machine whose compromise invalidates the controls layered behind it. The 2019 campaigns reported against this CVE are the concrete case: Alibaba Cloud describes Watchbog persisting through scheduled tasks after exploiting Jenkins, so upgrading to 2.154 removes the route and leaves the cron entry, the miner and any injected build step exactly where they were. The runbook has to default to rebuilding the controller from a known-good image and rotating the credentials store, signing keys and deploy tokens, because the compromised asset here is the credential concentration rather than the service.

CVE-2017-9791.name: Apache Struts 1 Plugin ActionMessage OGNL Remote Code Execution

attack_vector.description: An unauthenticated HTTP request submitting an OGNL expression in a form field that a Struts 1 action passes as a raw message to ActionMessage. Struts renders the message through OGNL, so the expression executes on the server as the servlet container's user. The bundled Struts Showcase application meets the precondition as shipped.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none - unauthenticated request to a reachable application
attack_vector.complexity: low once the precondition holds: the Struts 1 plugin must be loaded and a Struts 1 action must carry user input into a message
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Reported by icez of Tophant Competence Center in July 2017 and weaponised publicly within days; no AI tooling credited in discovery or exploitation.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Remove struts2-struts1-plugin where the application does not use Struts 1 actions, undeploy struts2-showcase from production, and where the plugin is genuinely used, apply Apache's coding fix - pass a resource key to ActionMessage rather than a raw message.
prevention.adequacy: Sufficient, but not deliverable by a patching team - Apache names no fixed 2.3.x build, so the work belongs to whoever owns the application source or the deployment manifest.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alert on the servlet container spawning a shell, which is the step no legitimate Struts action performs, and inspect form fields for OGNL syntax.
detection.adequacy: Process-lineage detection is decisive. Request-signature detection is measurably weak here: Gigamon found in November 2017 that most publicly available detections for this CVE and its siblings failed against real attacks.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treat a hit as code execution as the container user: pull the deployed application, rotate every credential in its configuration and datasource definitions, and check the deployment directory for written files.
response.adequacy: Adequate where the container's process and file audit history survives. The six-month KEV window means an affected estate may have carried the exposure for a long period before anyone scoped it.

NIST-800-53-SI-10.gap: Information input validation is the control the CWE points at, and it is the control that cannot be satisfied at the perimeter here. The untrusted value is syntactically ordinary text - a name field - and only becomes dangerous because ActionMessage hands it to an OGNL evaluator. Gigamon's November 2017 research found that most publicly available detections for this CVE and its siblings failed against real attacks, so an SI-10 posture resting on request filtering has measured evidence against it.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: Article 21's patch measure presumes a patch. Apache's S2-048 advisory names no fixed 2.3.x build and prescribes an application-code change - use resource keys - or a move to the 2.5.x series. CISA's own six-month window, 2022-02-10 to 2022-08-10 rather than the usual fortnight, reflects the same thing. A patch-management process cannot discharge this obligation at all; it has to be routed to whoever owns the application source.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: Secure configuration would have closed this outright, and in a way patching cannot: the Struts Showcase application meets the vulnerable precondition as shipped, so a baseline that forbids sample and demonstration applications in production removes the exposure entirely. B4 assessments of a Java application estate rarely enumerate what is inside a deployed WAR, which is where struts2-showcase and struts2-struts1-plugin both live.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Patch applications in the Essential Eight is measured against vendor-released updates and version currency, and there is no version to be current on. Apache did not ship a fixed 2.3.x release for this; the third-party 2.3.33 boundary that scanners use is not the vendor's own remediation. An estate can reach full maturity on the patching control while every deployed Struts 1 action still evaluates user input as OGNL.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.28.gap: Secure coding is precisely the right control and it is scoped to the wrong code. Apache's remediation is a coding rule - never pass a raw message to ActionMessage - but it applies inside a third-party plugin's integration pattern and inside a sample application the organisation did not write. An A.8.28 programme covering the organisation's own development standards produces no requirement that anyone read the Struts 1 actions in a deployed WAR.

new_control_requirements.name: MITIGATION-ACTIVE-PATCH-PENDING-VERDICT-CLASS
new_control_requirements.description: Compliance verdicts must distinguish binary-patch-deployed from vendor-mitigation-active-without-patch from no-mitigation-at-all, and must surface the middle state as a time-bound compensating control rather than as a patched-per-SLA outcome.
new_control_requirements.evidence: This CVE has no first state available on the 2.3.x branch. Apache's S2-048 advisory names no fixed build and prescribes a code change or a move to 2.5.x, while Tenable's plugin 112762 is titled 'Apache Struts 2 < 2.3.33 Remote Code Execution (S2-048)' - so a scan reporting 2.3.33 as clean is asserting a boundary the vendor never stated. The distinguishing test is not a version string: read the deployed WAR for struts2-struts1-plugin, enumerate the Struts 1 actions, and confirm none passes a raw user value to ActionMessage. Removing the plugin or undeploying the Showcase app is the middle state and needs a dated review, not a closure.

new_control_requirements.name: TIER-3-DEPENDENCY-INVENTORY
new_control_requirements.description: Supply chain inventory must extend to tier-3 dependencies (dependencies of dependencies of direct dependencies).
new_control_requirements.evidence: The vulnerable component here is not the framework the application declares - it is the Struts 1 plugin the Struts 2 distribution carries, and the Showcase sample application deployed beside it. Apache's affected-software line is 'Struts 2.3.x with Struts 1 plugin and Struts 1 action', which is a statement about what is inside the deployed artefact rather than about a declared dependency version. The operational test is whether the inventory can answer 'which deployed WARs contain struts2-struts1-plugin' without unpacking them by hand; where it cannot, neither the exposure nor the remediation can be scoped.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: 4h KEV-listing mitigation SLA applies.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CISA listed this on 2022-02-10 and set the due date at 2022-08-10 - six months rather than the usual fortnight, because the remediation is application code rather than a package. EPSS on 2026-08-28 was 0.98908 at the 99.925th percentile, the highest band in this set after the SonicWall entry. The action an hours-scale SLA can deliver is the deployment-side one: undeploy struts2-showcase and strip struts2-struts1-plugin from applications that do not use Struts 1 actions. The code fix follows the application release train.

CVE-2017-8464.name: Windows Shell LNK Icon-Parsing Remote Code Execution

attack_vector.description: An attacker places a shortcut file where the shell will render it - a removable drive, a network share, a WebDAV path, an extracted archive. The shortcut carries a dynamic icon pointing at an attacker-supplied module, and Windows Shell loads and executes that module while drawing the icon, before any file is opened. The public exploitation sets the SpecialFolderDataBlock folder id to the Control Panel to bypass the CPL allowlist.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none for the exploit itself; the code runs as the user whose shell rendered the folder
attack_vector.complexity: low - no memory corruption, no reliability problem, and the required user action is viewing a directory rather than opening a file
attack_vector.ai_factor: No AI tooling in the record. The discovery is uncredited; ZDI's June 2017 review notes only that the Stuxnet-era LNK icon pattern resurfaced through a ZDI program submission.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: The June 2017 security update for the specific Windows branch, applied and rebooted into - per-build on Windows 10, so 1511, 1607 and 1703 each need their own package.
prevention.adequacy: Complete, and available since 2017-06-13. It does nothing for the out-of-support members of the affected list - Windows RT 8.1, Server 2008 SP2, the superseded Windows 10 branches - where the honest remediation is removal and, until then, cutting the delivery path.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alert on explorer.exe loading a DLL from a removable, network or WebDAV path, and on any child process of explorer.exe that follows a directory listing with no user file-open action. Inventory .LNK files whose SpecialFolderDataBlock names the Control Panel.
detection.adequacy: Effective where endpoint telemetry covers module loads, which is exactly what the older members of the affected list are least likely to have. Vendor signatures for the class exist and are worth enabling, but they are pattern matches on known samples rather than coverage of the primitive.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treat the user context as compromised, trace the shortcut back to the device or share that carried it, and check every other host that mounted the same device or browsed the same path - the delivery mechanism is self-propagating in the removable-media case.
response.adequacy: Sound, and it needs to run wider than the first host. The removable-media path means the interesting question is which other machines saw the device, and that is answerable from mount history only if it is being collected before the incident.

NIST-800-53-MP-7.gap: Media use is the control that matches the delivery path, and its usual implementation is aimed at the wrong risk. MP-7 restrictions are typically written to stop data leaving on removable media and to stop users executing files from it; this flaw needs neither. Windows Shell executes the referenced module during icon display in Explorer, so a policy that blocks running programs from a USB device while still allowing the device to mount and its contents to be browsed leaves the attack fully available. Only a restriction that prevents the shell from rendering the device's directory listing at all reaches it.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: Patch management measures deployment against vendor release, and Microsoft released on 2017-06-13 with the flaw already under active attack per ZDI's review of that month's updates. CISA then set a due date of 2022-08-10 - six months after listing, and five years after the fix. The gap the process cannot express is that both dates are about the update, while the exposure that matters on the affected list is architectural: Windows RT 8.1, Server 2008 SP2 and the older Windows 10 branches on the list are out of support, so for them the answer is not a patch cycle at all.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: System security expects the platform to distinguish between displaying a file and running one. Here it does not: the shell resolves and loads a module in order to draw an icon, so the boundary between viewing a directory and executing code does not exist on an affected host. No CAF-aligned hardening measure changes that, because the executing component is the shell doing its documented job - which is also why user-awareness measures aimed at not opening suspicious files miss the actual action.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Essential Eight operating-system patching measures from vendor release, and the release is 2017-06-13. An estate that met the timeframe then is compliant and unexposed; an estate that did not has been exposed for the whole intervening period with a Metasploit module and two Exploit-DB entries available since July and August 2017 respectively, and with Unit 42 documenting commodity malware carrying the exploit as late as 2020. The maturity measurement produces the same score for a host patched in 2017 and one patched in 2022 to meet the KEV date, while the risk those two carried differs by five years.

ISO-27001-2022-A.7.10.gap: Storage media controls govern how removable media is handled, labelled, transported and disposed of. The exposure here is none of those things: it is that inserting a device and looking at its contents in Explorer is enough to execute code. An A.7.10 implementation can be complete - media registered, encrypted, handled under policy - while every workstation still renders an attacker-prepared shortcut on any device that is allowed to mount. The control also does not reach the non-media delivery paths, network shares and WebDAV, that carry the same shortcut.

new_control_requirements.name: DOWNLOAD-PROVENANCE-ENFORCEMENT
new_control_requirements.description: Enforce Mark-of-the-Web / content-provenance on all internet-sourced files and block execution of provenance-stripped shortcuts, installers, and script hosts regardless of a reputation verdict.
new_control_requirements.evidence: This CVE is the case that makes the shortcut clause of the control load-bearing rather than incidental. The executing artefact is a .LNK, the trigger is the shell drawing its icon rather than a user opening it, and the delivery paths named in the Metasploit module - removable drives and network shares - are precisely the ones that carry no Mark-of-the-Web at all. A provenance policy that only inspects files arriving over HTTP therefore covers none of the delivery for this flaw, and a reputation verdict on the shortcut is irrelevant because the payload is the DLL the icon reference names, not the shortcut itself.

new_control_requirements.name: PROTECTION-MECHANISM-FAILURE-CLASS-REGRESSION
new_control_requirements.description: Detonation chambers, EDR rules, and AppLocker/WDAC policies covering protection-mechanism classes (MOTW, SmartScreen, AMSI, ASR, WDAC, Driver Block Rules) must include class-level coverage rather than per-sample signatures.
new_control_requirements.evidence: The public exploitation for this CVE is a deliberate bypass of a named allowlist: the Metasploit module sets the folder id in the SpecialFolderDataBlock to the Control Panel specifically to get past the CPL allowlist, and the module itself describes the bug as a variant of MS15-020 on the same LNK icon-parsing primitive that Stuxnet used. Signature-level coverage of individual samples has demonstrably not held that line across three iterations of the same primitive. Class-level coverage here means an application-control rule that refuses DLL loads initiated by the shell from removable and network locations, which holds regardless of which shortcut construction the next variant uses.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: 4h KEV-listing mitigation SLA applies.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CISA gave this id an unusually long window - listed 2022-02-10, due 2022-08-10, six months rather than the standard two weeks - for a flaw that ZDI recorded as under active attack when the patch shipped in June 2017 and that Unit 42 found inside Lucifer's LNK resource section in 2020. The action a compressed SLA delivers here is not the six-month update campaign; it is the same-day delivery-path restriction, because blocking shell rendering of removable and untrusted-share content can be pushed by policy while the branch-by-branch update work proceeds behind it.

CVE-2017-10271.name: Oracle WebLogic wls-wsat XMLDecoder Unauthenticated Deserialisation (CVE-2017-10271)

attack_vector.description: An unauthenticated POST to /wls-wsat/CoordinatorPortType carries a SOAP body whose work:WorkContext element contains a java.beans.XMLDecoder document naming java.lang.ProcessBuilder. WebLogic's WorkContextXmlInputAdapter hands the XML to XMLDecoder without validating what it may construct, so the server builds the ProcessBuilder and runs the supplied command as the WebLogic process. The same path is used to write a JSP web shell under the AdminServer's internal deployment directory. Observed use from late 2017 was mass scanning followed by Monero mining.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none - the endpoint answers before any credential is evaluated, which is why NVD assigns CWE-306
attack_vector.complexity: low - one HTTP request; Oracle's own advisory calls it easily exploitable, and a Nuclei template, a Metasploit module and a reproduction environment have been public since 2017-2018
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Disclosed in Oracle's October 2017 Critical Patch Update, before AI-assisted discovery or weaponisation.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Apply the October 2017 Oracle Critical Patch Update (or a later superseding CPU) to the WebLogic version in use and restart the domain. Where that could not be scheduled, undeploy the wls-wsat application or block /wls-wsat/ at the proxy.
prevention.adequacy: Complete for this endpoint, and narrow. WebLogic exposes other deserialisation sinks over T3 and IIOP, so a domain that took only this CPU and left T3 open to untrusted networks remains exposed to the class.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alert on POSTs to /wls-wsat/ carrying the XMLDecoder and ProcessBuilder element names, and on the WebLogic java process becoming the parent of a shell.
detection.adequacy: Both are reliable and both need to be in place beforehand. The request-body signature requires the proxy to log or inspect bodies, which most do not by default; the process-parentage signal does not.

response.what_would_have_worked: Inventory JSP files under the AdminServer internal deployment directories against the deployment record, rotate every credential in the domain configuration, and rebuild rather than clean where a web shell is found.
response.adequacy: Necessary. The WebLogic process holds application database credentials, so a confirmed hit is a credential-rotation event for the applications the server hosts, not just for the server.

NIST-800-53-SC-7.gap: Boundary protection is the control an operator reaches for here and it can genuinely close this - blocking /wls-wsat/ at the proxy removes the reachable endpoint. What SC-7 does not do is distinguish that state from a patched one. The endpoint is an application deployed inside WebLogic, so any redeployment, domain restore or newly added managed server that bypasses the proxy path reopens it silently, and the boundary control's evidence - a rule in a proxy configuration - looks identical on the day it works and the day something routes around it.

NIS2-Art21-network-security.gap: Network security obligations sit on the assumption that an unauthenticated request reaching an internal application server is the failure to prevent. Here the request is a legitimately-shaped SOAP POST to a web service the product publishes by default at /wls-wsat/CoordinatorPortType, arriving on the same port as the applications the server exists to serve. There is no network-layer property that separates it from ordinary traffic, and CISA's six-month KEV window - 2022-02-10 to 2022-08-10 - concedes that the remediation is an application-stack change, not a network one.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: B4 asks that systems be securely configured, and the configuration change that matters here is undeploying an application the vendor ships enabled: wls-wsat is present by default and most WebLogic deployments do not use WS-AtomicTransaction at all. B4 gives no basis for identifying which vendor-shipped applications inside a middleware container are unused, and no WebLogic-level access-control setting blocks the request, because the endpoint answers before any credential is evaluated - which is why NVD classifies this as CWE-306 missing authentication.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Essential Eight patch timeframes for internet-facing applications are measured from the availability of the vendor patch, which is October 2017. Two things the measure cannot express for this CVE. First, Oracle expresses the fix as a CPU applied to each of 10.3.6.0.0, 12.1.3.0.0, 12.2.1.1.0 and 12.2.1.2.0 rather than as a fixed version, so a scanner comparing installed version strings against a fixed-version boundary has nothing to compare and can report either state. Second, a server exposed after the 2017-12-23 proof of concept and patched later is compliant with the measure while still hosting whatever JSP web shell was written in the interval.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.22.gap: Segregation of networks is the ISO control that would keep the T3 and wls-wsat surfaces off untrusted networks, and it is written for network zones rather than for protocol exposure inside a zone. WebLogic publishes its remoting and web-service endpoints on the same listen port as the applications it serves, so segregating the server does not segregate the endpoint from the users who must reach the application. The control has no way to express 'this port serves both the business application and an unauthenticated object-graph constructor', which is the actual configuration.

new_control_requirements.name: APPSERVER-REMOTING-PROTOCOL-RESTRICTION
new_control_requirements.description: Application servers that expose binary remoting protocols (Oracle WebLogic T3/IIOP, and equivalents) must restrict those protocols to trusted hosts and apply vendor critical patch updates on the vendor's published quarterly cycle.
new_control_requirements.evidence: NVD's description of this CVE records network access via T3 as the attack path Oracle names, and the four affected versions - 10.3.6.0.0, 12.1.3.0.0, 12.2.1.1.0, 12.2.1.2.0 - are all fixed by a single quarterly CPU rather than by a version bump, so the patch cadence and the protocol restriction are the two levers that exist. For this product the control means: the wls-wsat application and the T3/IIOP listeners are inventoried as remoting surface, restricted to the hosts that legitimately use them, and the October 2017 CPU is applied to the running version rather than a fixed build being awaited.

new_control_requirements.name: SERVICE-INTERNAL-PROTOCOL-DESERIALIZATION-HARDENING
new_control_requirements.description: A server product that exposes an internal coordination protocol - build-agent polling, cluster membership, node replication, management RPC - must not deserialize input arriving on that protocol into arbitrary object graphs.
new_control_requirements.evidence: wls-wsat implements WS-AtomicTransaction, a distributed-transaction coordination protocol, and its WorkContextXmlInputAdapter hands the request body to java.beans.XMLDecoder, a general object-graph constructor. That is the pattern exactly: a coordination endpoint that must accept structured state from a peer, implemented by rehydrating whatever the document describes, so a work:WorkContext element naming java.lang.ProcessBuilder is constructed and run. The distinguishing test is not whether the endpoint authenticates - it does not, hence CWE-306 - but whether the decoder is constrained to the transaction-context types the protocol actually needs.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: 4h KEV-listing mitigation SLA applies.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CISA added CVE-2017-10271 on 2022-02-10 and, unusually, allowed until 2022-08-10 - six months - because the remediation is an Oracle CPU against a running middleware domain rather than a package update. EPSS on 2026-08-28 is 0.99993 at the 99.987th percentile, effectively certainty of attempted exploitation. The action the four-hour SLA can deliver against that six-month remediation window is the interim one: undeploy wls-wsat or block /wls-wsat/ at the proxy the same day, and hold it until the CPU lands.

CVE-2017-0263.name: Windows Win32k Menu Use-After-Free Privilege Escalation (CVE-2017-0263)

attack_vector.description: An attacker already executing locally - in the documented chain, via CVE-2017-0262 in the Office EPS filter - creates 256 window classes whose windows carry 512 bytes of extra kernel memory beside their tagWND. Destroying a context menu frees the menu memory without zeroing the pointer; a crafted tagPOPUPMENU is laid into the reclaimed space, NtUserMNDragLeave drives HMAssignmentUnlock to execute 'add dword ptr [rdx+8],0FFFFFFFFh' against a chosen address, flipping tagWND->bServerSideProc so that SendMessageW runs the window procedure in kernel mode. Token theft follows and the attacker holds SYSTEM.
attack_vector.privileges_required: low - local code execution as an ordinary user; the observed chain supplied it with a second zero-day in the same phishing message
attack_vector.complexity: low once local - one arithmetic write against one bit, with no ROP chain and no kernel shellcode staging
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered and not AI-weaponised; this is hand-written state-actor tooling from 2017.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Apply the May 2017 Windows security updates and restart the host. Independently, disable the Office EPS filter by policy, which removes the documented first stage (CVE-2017-0262) that gives this escalation its starting position.
prevention.adequacy: Insufficient at the time, because this was a zero-day: the fix and the disclosure arrived together, after the intrusions ESET documented. The EPS-filter change is the only measure that was available beforehand, and it works on the entry point rather than on this CVE.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alert on a process creating many window classes with extra window memory followed by menu create/destroy activity and a call to NtUserMNDragLeave, and on any user-mode process acquiring a SYSTEM token without a service or scheduled-task creation.
detection.adequacy: The token-acquisition rule is the durable one, because it describes the outcome rather than the technique - a different win32k escalation reaches the same end state. The grooming signature is specific to this exploit and will not survive a rewrite.

response.what_would_have_worked: Search retrospectively for the published hashes and the mutex flPGdvyhPykxGvhDOAZnU, and on a hit escalate to a nation-state response path rather than a malware clean-up, because ESET attributes the chain to Sednit/APT28.
response.adequacy: Decisive where endpoint telemetry retention reaches back to the intrusion window. A host that reached SYSTEM through this chain cannot be remediated by removing the payload, because everything on it after that point was under attacker control.

NIST-800-53-SC-39.gap: Process isolation is the control this defect dissolves. The exploit does not break out of a process boundary - it flips tagWND->bServerSideProc so that a window procedure the attacker already owns is executed by the kernel instead of by user mode, which means the isolation boundary is honoured right up to the moment the kernel decides the attacker's code is its own. An assessment that confirms the operating system maintains a separate execution domain for each process passes on the day the exploit runs, because the mechanism it verifies is the mechanism being subverted.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: This was a zero-day: ESET published the exploitation detail on 2017-05-09 and Microsoft shipped the fix in the same month's updates, so there is no availability-to-deployment window in which patch management could have prevented the documented intrusions. The obligation also stops short of the reboot - win32k is a kernel driver and the update is not in force until the host restarts, so an estate that reports the May 2017 update as deployed but defers restarts is recorded as compliant while remaining exploitable.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: The system-security outcome expects vulnerable software to be identified and updated, and the identification here is straightforward - NVD lists the affected Windows releases explicitly. What the outcome does not reach is the chain: the escalation is only reachable because CVE-2017-0262 in the Office EPS filter supplied the local code execution, and that entry point is governed by an entirely separate part of an assessment. Treating the two as independent findings means the compensating action that was actually available - disabling the EPS filter - never gets attached to this CVE.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Essential Eight patch timeframes for operating systems are measured from the release of the vendor fix, and the fix and the disclosure arrived together in May 2017 - so the maturity model has nothing to say about the period in which the intrusions ESET documented actually happened. The model also treats a deployed update as the end state, while for a kernel driver the end state is a restarted host; the gap between the two is invisible to it.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: Management of technical vulnerabilities is fed by vulnerability information, and for a zero-day used by a named state actor the information arrives after the fact - ESET's write-up on 2017-05-09 is a post-mortem of intrusions already completed, complete with the decoy filename Trump's_Attack_on_Syria_English.docx and four sample hashes. The control produces a correct patching action and no retrospective action, when the retrospective one is the load-bearing half: the organisations in scope needed to establish whether that chain had already run on their estate.

new_control_requirements.name: ACTIVELY-EXPLOITED-OS-LPE-REMEDIATION-WINDOW-ENFORCEMENT
new_control_requirements.description: When an OS vendor flags a local-privilege-escalation flaw as exploited in the wild and it is KEV-listed, the monthly cumulative update that fixes it must be applied and rebooted rather than merely staged.
new_control_requirements.evidence: The fix for this CVE is inside the May 2017 Windows cumulative update and it replaces win32k, a kernel-mode driver, so it takes effect only after a restart. An estate that deploys the update and defers reboots holds a compliant deployment record and an exploitable kernel. CISA's listing of 2022-02-10 with a 2022-08-10 due date is satisfied by the deployment record and not by the state of the machine, which is precisely the distinction this control forces.

new_control_requirements.name: NATION-STATE-INITIAL-ACCESS-IR-ESCALATION
new_control_requirements.description: IR runbooks must include an explicit nation-state-initial-access escalation path triggered by APT28/APT29/Lazarus/Volt-Typhoon and equivalent attribution on a confirmed exploit chain.
new_control_requirements.evidence: ESET attributes this exploit chain to Sednit - APT28, Fancy Bear, Sofacy - operating since at least 2004 with confidential information as the objective. The chain is two zero-days in one phishing message (CVE-2017-0262 for entry, CVE-2017-0263 for SYSTEM) delivering the Seduploader reconnaissance downloader, with published artefacts to hunt on: mutex flPGdvyhPykxGvhDOAZnU and SHA-1 hashes d5235d136cfcadbef431eea7253d80bde414db9d, 18b7dd3917231d7bae93c11f915e9702aa5d1bbb, 6a90e0b5ec9970a9f443a7d52eee4c16f17fcc70 and e338d49c270baf64363879e5eecb8fa6bdde8ad9. A hit on those is not a malware clean-up; the host reached SYSTEM and the objective was collection, so the response is scoped to what was taken, not to what was installed.

new_control_requirements.name: KERNEL-EXPLOITATION-DETECTION
new_control_requirements.description: Deploy auditd or eBPF-based monitoring rules for kernel privilege escalation indicators. Alert within 60 seconds of detection.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Attached as the closest existing control; it names Linux mechanisms and this is a Windows kernel flaw, so what it means here is the equivalent endpoint telemetry - process-creation and handle/token auditing with a rule on a user-mode process acquiring a SYSTEM token without an intervening service or scheduled-task creation, which is the observable outcome of the tagWND->bServerSideProc flip. The 60-second bound matters because the escalation is instantaneous: there is no staging phase between the arithmetic write and SYSTEM in which a slower alert would still be useful.

CVE-2017-0262.name: Microsoft Office EPS Filter forall Type Confusion

attack_vector.description: A .docx carries a crafted EPS image. When Office renders it, the EPS interpreter in EPSIMP32.FLT runs inside FLTLDR.EXE and a forged type-confused procedure object abuses the `forall` operator to control the operand stack; a 0x7ffffff0-length string object yields arbitrary read and write, the module base leaks through a vftable, and a fake file object plus the `bytesavailable` operator pivots to shellcode. The observed attacks then chained CVE-2017-0263, a win32k!xxxDestroyWindow use-after-free, to escalate and escape the filter sandbox, delivering GAMEFISH.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none - the victim opens the document
attack_vector.complexity: low for the operator, high for the author: a full exploitation chain across two zero-days, one for execution and one for escalation and sandbox escape
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered and not AI-weaponised; FireEye credits its own analysis of live attack samples.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Apply Microsoft security advisory ADV170005 to disable the EPS filter - this removes the interpreter the exploit runs in and closes the class, not just this CVE - and take the May 2017 Office update for 2010 SP2, 2013 SP1 or 2016.
prevention.adequacy: The EPS disabling is unusually strong for a pre-patch measure because it eliminates the attack surface rather than hardening it - FireEye found this second EPS zero-day only after Microsoft had already disabled the filter in April 2017, which is the evidence that the class kept producing bugs.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alert on FLTLDR.EXE spawning children, writing files or making network connections, and on connections to wmdmediacodecs.com.
detection.adequacy: High-signal and low-volume once the filter loader is in monitoring scope, which is the catch - a rendering-filter subprocess is not a surface most monitoring baselines enumerate, so the rule has to be written before it can fire.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treat APT28 attribution as an escalation trigger rather than a label: preserve the host, rotate the user's and any reachable service credentials, hunt GAMEFISH persistence, and confirm whether the chained CVE-2017-0263 escalation succeeded.
response.adequacy: Appropriate, but it depends on the attribution reaching the responder - the initial event looks like one user opening one document, and without the FireEye context the incident is closed at the wrong severity.

NIST-800-53-SI-3.gap: Malicious code protection owns the weaponised-document case, and the delivered artefact here was a .docx with an embedded EPS image - no macro, no scripting prompt, nothing the user could decline. FireEye's own account is that this was the second EPS zero-day it found after Microsoft disabled EPS in April 2017, so at the time of the attacks the content type carrying the exploit was one SI-3 tooling had no signature for and the vendor had already judged unsafe enough to switch off.

NIS2-Art21-incident-handling.gap: Incident handling scales response by impact classification, and the classification inputs available at detection understate this one: a single user opening a document, code running in a sandboxed filter process. FireEye's attribution changes what the incident is - APT28, the GAMEFISH payload, and a chained win32k escalation via CVE-2017-0263 that escapes the FLTLDR.EXE sandbox - and Art. 21 incident handling has no trigger that reclassifies an event upward on nation-state attribution arriving after the initial triage.

UK-CAF-C1.gap: The security monitoring outcome expects the organisation to detect malicious activity from its collected data. The detectable events here are specific and documented - FLTLDR.EXE behaving abnormally, connections to wmdmediacodecs.com, the lure hash f8e92d8b5488ea76c40601c8f1a08790 - but they only become detections once FireEye published them on 2017-05-09. Before that the monitoring is looking for an EPS filter process misbehaving, which is not an event class most estates model at all, and the CAF outcome does not require that a rendering-filter subprocess be in monitoring scope.

AU-Essential-8-App-Hardening.gap: Application hardening is the control that actually closes this, and unusually the vendor had already done it: Microsoft disabled EPS in the April 2017 Patch Tuesday and published ADV170005. The gap is that Essential Eight hardening guidance is written around macros and browser content, so an estate implementing it to the letter can score on the mitigation while never having considered the EPS filter - the specific component FireEye names as the one to disable - because no maturity-level requirement points at it.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.16.gap: Monitoring activities requires networks, systems and applications to be monitored for anomalous behaviour. Applied here it monitors Office and the workstation, which is the right altitude for almost everything and the wrong altitude for this: the exploit executes inside FLTLDR.EXE, a short-lived filter subprocess spawned to render an image, and an A.8.16 monitoring baseline built around applications and hosts does not enumerate rendering-filter subprocesses as a monitored surface at all.

new_control_requirements.name: CONFIGURATION-SIDE-LIVE-PATCH-INVENTORY
new_control_requirements.description: For any vulnerability with a configuration-side mitigation path, that path must be inventoried, tested, and deployable independent of the vendor-patch path so operators are not gated on the patch cycle.
new_control_requirements.evidence: This flaw has the strongest example of such a path in this chunk, and the vendor built it: Microsoft disabled EPS in the April 2017 Patch Tuesday and published ADV170005, which FireEye recommends to all customers as defence in depth against EPS filter vulnerabilities. Disabling the filter removes the interpreter the exploit executes in, so it closes the class - FireEye found this bug only after that disabling, which proves the class kept producing zero-days. The inventory obligation is to know, before the next disclosure, which Office builds have EPS still reachable and what breaks when it is switched off, since documents embedding EPS images stop rendering.

new_control_requirements.name: NATION-STATE-INITIAL-ACCESS-IR-ESCALATION
new_control_requirements.description: IR runbooks must include an explicit nation-state-initial-access escalation path triggered by APT28/APT29/Lazarus/Volt-Typhoon and equivalent attribution on a confirmed exploit chain, replacing the standard commodity-malware response.
new_control_requirements.evidence: FireEye attributes this activity to APT28 delivering GAMEFISH against European diplomatic and military entities, chained with CVE-2017-0263 for escalation and sandbox escape. Every input available at first triage points the other way - one user, one document, a sandboxed filter process - so without an explicit trigger the event is handled as commodity malware and closed. The trigger conditions for this flaw are concrete and checkable: the lure hash f8e92d8b5488ea76c40601c8f1a08790, the C2 wmdmediacodecs.com, or FLTLDR.EXE originating network traffic at all.

new_control_requirements.name: EMBEDDED-MEDIA-PARSER-LIBRARY-INVENTORY-AND-PATCH-PARITY
new_control_requirements.description: An organization must inventory every place a high-risk embedded media-parsing library (FreeType, image/codec/font/document parsers) is statically or dynamically bundled, including copies shipped inside other products.
new_control_requirements.evidence: EPSIMP32.FLT is precisely the class of component this control governs - an image-format parser bundled inside a larger product and invoked automatically during rendering. For this flaw the inventory has to reach one level deeper than the Office install: the parser executes inside FLTLDR.EXE, a subprocess most asset registers never name, so 'Office 2016 is installed' does not tell an operator whether the EPS interpreter is reachable. The inventory entry must record the filter and its enablement state, which is also what makes ADV170005 verifiable rather than assumed.

attack_vector.description: An attacker reaches TCP 445 on a Windows host with SMBv1 enabled and sends crafted packets that the SMBv1 server mishandles, executing code in kernel context. This is one of six defects fixed together by MS17-010; the public exploit chain, ETERNALBLUE, cites all six identifiers and drives its overflow through the SrvOs2FeaListSizeToNt transaction path, so no public artefact separates this CVE's own trigger from its siblings'.
attack_vector.privileges_required: low - CVSS records PR:L for this record, which is a more constrained reading than the family's wormable reputation implies; the packaged tooling nonetheless requires only network reach to 445
attack_vector.complexity: low - a maintained Metasploit scanner and exploit pair that has shipped since April 2017
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered and not AI-weaponised. The exploit reached the public as a leaked state-developed tool, and the subsequent reverse engineering was manual.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Apply MS17-010 and reboot; disable SMBv1 on client and server estate-wide; segment TCP 445 away from general-purpose networks for embedded medical and industrial systems that can take neither action.
prevention.adequacy: The patch closes six CVEs; disabling SMBv1 closes the protocol they live in, which is the stronger guarantee for a codebase of that age. Neither reaches the embedded population, where segmentation is the whole of the available control.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alert on SMBv1 dialect negotiation where SMBv1 should be disabled, on TCP 445 crossing zone boundaries that have no file-sharing relationship, and on horizontal 445 scanning from a single internal host.
detection.adequacy: The dialect-negotiation signal is the strongest because it fires on the exposure rather than on an exploit attempt, and it needs no signature. The scanning signal fires late - by the time it is loud, lateral movement is already underway - but it is the one that catches the campaign shape this family is known for.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treat a successful exploitation as kernel-context compromise: isolate the host, rebuild rather than clean, rotate credentials the host held, and check for named-pipe implant persistence of the DOUBLEPULSAR kind that the original toolkit paired with this exploit.
response.adequacy: Correct for a single host and insufficient as a plan, because this family's defining property is that one compromise is rarely one host. The response that matters is the containment decision on TCP 445 across the estate, taken before the per-host work.

NIST-800-53-CM-7.gap: Least functionality is the control that would have removed this surface and it is not written to reach it. SMBv1 is not an add-on service an operator chose to install - it is a protocol version enabled inside a component the operating system requires, so a CM-7 baseline that enumerates and disables unnecessary services legitimately records file sharing as required and leaves the legacy dialect enabled underneath it. The control has no requirement to enumerate protocol versions within a required service, which is the level this defect lives at, and it therefore gives no credit for the one action that closes all six MS17-010 CVEs at once.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: The obligation measures against availability of the fix and MS17-010 has been available since 2017-03-14, so an estate that patched in 2017 is compliant and the estate CISA addressed in 2022 has been non-compliant continuously for five years without escalation. The control also cannot express the two states that actually matter here. A listed build with SMBv1 disabled is not exploitable and reads as unpatched; and the embedded population on this CVE's own reference list - Siemens and ICS-CERT advisories for medical and industrial equipment - has no operator-applicable patch at all, so measuring it against fix availability produces a permanently open finding with no action attached.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: The system-security outcome expects vulnerable software to be identified and updated. Identification succeeds for general-purpose Windows and fails precisely where the risk has persisted: the affected build inside a medical device or an industrial controller is not in the software inventory, is not scannable without disrupting the device, and is owned by clinical or engineering teams rather than IT. A CAF assessment that confirms every managed Windows host carries MS17-010 passes on an estate where the exploitable hosts are the unmanaged ones, and the CVE record itself names that population through three separate vendor and government advisories.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Essential Eight patch timeframes for operating systems are measured from vendor release, and the release here is nine years old - so the model has nothing further to say to an estate that has carried this since 2017, and CISA's six-month window in 2022 was longer than any Essential Eight timeframe rather than shorter. The deeper mismatch is that the effective control for this family is not patching but disabling a protocol version, which no patch-timeframe measure records, and that several of the affected builds are now end-of-life, putting them outside the model's patch scope entirely while leaving them on the network.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.22.gap: Segregation of networks is the control that still applies nine years on, and it is written as a design principle rather than a testable state. For the embedded population this CVE names, segmentation of TCP 445 is the only available mitigation, yet A.8.22 requires groups of services and systems to be segregated without specifying that a legacy file-sharing protocol reaching a medical or industrial device from a general-purpose network is a segregation failure. An assessment that confirms network zones exist, with documented boundaries, will pass while port 445 remains routable between the office network and the device network - which is the exact path both major campaigns using this family took.

new_control_requirements.name: KERNEL-MODULE-INVENTORY-AND-DISABLE
new_control_requirements.description: Maintain an inventory of loaded kernel-level and protocol components; for components not required for business function, disable them as a least-functionality measure rather than relying on the patch level of code that remains enabled.
new_control_requirements.evidence: SMBv1 is required by nothing in a modern estate and enabled almost everywhere the affected builds run. Disabling it closes all six MS17-010 CVEs simultaneously and, unlike the patch, closes whatever else is still undiscovered in a protocol implementation of that vintage - which is the argument the KEV listing nine years after the fix implicitly makes. The catalogued control's wording is Linux-shaped (modprobe blacklists of unused kernel modules); the mapping to a Windows protocol dialect is a scope stretch, attached because the principle and the required inventory step are identical and no narrower control in the catalogue covers protocol-version enablement.

new_control_requirements.name: EOL-ASSET-DECOMMISSION
new_control_requirements.description: Network-reachable end-of-life devices with no vendor patch path must be isolated and decommissioned within a bounded window; mandatory compensating segmentation applies until removal.
new_control_requirements.evidence: This CVE's own reference list names the population the control exists for: Siemens ProductCERT SSA-701903 and SSA-966341 and ICS-CERT ICSMA-18-058-02, covering medical and industrial equipment that embeds affected Windows builds. Those systems cannot take MS17-010 from their operator and in many cases cannot have SMBv1 disabled without breaking the product. Several general-purpose builds in the affected set - Vista SP2, Server 2008 SP2, Windows 10 Gold, 1511 and 1607 - are also past end of life. For all of them the honest remediation is bounded-window segmentation with a dated replacement, not a patch record.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: 4h KEV-listing mitigation SLA applies.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CISA allowed six months (added 2022-02-10, due 2022-08-10) for a patch that had been available for almost five years, which tells you the constraint was never the window. The action an hours-scale SLA can actually deliver for this CVE is not MS17-010, which needs a reboot on every affected host, but the SMBv1 disable and the TCP 445 zone rules - both estate-wide, both effective against all six family members, and neither dependent on a maintenance outage.

CVE-2017-0144.name: Microsoft SMBv1 Remote Code Execution Vulnerability (CVE-2017-0144)

attack_vector.description: An attacker sends crafted packets to the SMB service on TCP 445. A size-calculation error in the Srv!SrvOs2FeaToNt memmove path overflows a groomed kernel pool buffer in the SMBv1 server, and code executes in kernel context. WannaCry and NotPetya both used this to propagate laterally across internal networks without operator credentials.
attack_vector.privileges_required: NVD records PR:L, but the observed worm propagation required no supplied credentials and the widely-used Windows 7 exploitation path needs none - treat it as pre-authentication wherever TCP 445 is reachable and SMBv1 is enabled
attack_vector.complexity: low - a packet sequence with no user interaction, shipped as a Metasploit module with a paired scanner and as three standalone Python exploits; target selection is the only operator-side work
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered and not AI-weaponised. The exploit is credited to the Equation Group as original research and became public through the Shadow Brokers' disclosure of the FuzzBunch toolkit.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Disable the SMBv1 server feature, block TCP 445 between client subnets as well as at the perimeter, and apply MS17-010 with a reboot for the exact build.
prevention.framework_requiring_it: CISA BOD 22-01 (KEV remediation, added 2022-02-10, due 2022-08-10); Microsoft's own SMBv1 deprecation guidance predates the 2017 attacks
prevention.adequacy: Sufficient, and the ordering matters: the two configuration actions need no reboot and no change window on the affected host, while the patch does not take effect until the host restarts. In 2017 the organisations that came through intact were largely those whose internal networks did not permit 445 east-west, not those that patched fastest.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alert on SMBv1 dialect negotiation anywhere in the estate, on TCP 445 traffic crossing subnet boundaries, and on horizontal 445 scanning from a single internal host.
detection.adequacy: The dialect signal is now close to a zero-base-rate detection, because SMBv1 has been off by default since 2017 - any negotiation is an exposure finding in its own right. The scanning signal fires during propagation, which on a worm timeline is minutes rather than hours; it is a containment trigger, not a prevention one.

response.what_would_have_worked: Isolate at the subnet boundary rather than per host, treat every reachable host on the segment as compromised at kernel level, and rebuild rather than clean.
response.adequacy: Per-host response is the wrong unit for this defect. Execution is in kernel context, so no user-level containment applies, and the propagation is automated - by the time one host is confirmed, the population is whatever 445 reaches. The credential-dumping step ATT&CK records for NotPetya means the response also has to extend to every account that had a session on any affected host.

NIST-800-53-CM-7.gap: Least functionality is the control that would have closed this, because SMBv1 was already a deprecated protocol in 2017 and disabling it was already Microsoft's guidance. The reason it did not close it is that CM-7's documented-exception route was where the entire exposed population lived: SMBv1 was retained not by oversight but because named applications, network-attached storage and printer firmware required it, and each of those was a legitimate, reviewed exception. The control asks that unnecessary functions be disabled and provides no mechanism that ages an exception, re-tests whether it is still needed, or escalates when the protocol behind it becomes the subject of a wormable pre-authentication defect.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: The Article 21 patch-management obligation measures against the availability of a fix. MS17-010 shipped 2017-03-14 and WannaCry ran in May - the fix was available for two months, so the obligation's own measure was satisfiable by any organisation with a monthly cycle. What the obligation does not measure is the gap this defect actually ran through: the fix is in a kernel-mode driver and is not in effect until the host reboots, so a compliant deployment record and a still-vulnerable host are the same record. Nothing in Article 21 requires the compliance evidence to be the effect of the patch rather than its installation.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: The system-security outcome expects vulnerable software to be identified and updated, and identification fails here in a way that is specific and checkable. Two hosts at identical patch levels differ completely depending on whether the SMBv1 server feature is enabled, and two hosts with identical SMBv1 configuration differ depending on whether each has rebooted since MS17-010 was installed. Neither property appears in a software inventory. A CAF assessment confirming that vulnerable software is identified and updated will accept a patch report as evidence, and that report answers a different question from the one that determined whether an organisation was hit in 2017.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Essential Eight patch timeframes are keyed to vendor release and to whether the software is internet-facing, and by that measure MS17-010 was a normal monthly item for an internal file-sharing service. The model's structural gap for this defect is that it has no control at all for disabling a deprecated protocol - the decisive action here - and no control for east-west network filtering, the action that would have bounded the propagation.
