No authentication strength, no privileged-access-management arrangement and no account-separation scheme addresses a service that correctly identifies its caller and then acts with the wrong token.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Patch operating systems is the right measure and it is satisfiable, with one wrinkle specific to this CVE. Microsoft records the fix against 41 separate product entries in the March 2020 release, delivered as per-release cumulative updates, so compliance is a question of update presence rather than of a version boundary. The measure's timeframes are also driven by severity, and the vendor severity input here was 'Exploitation Less Likely' - so an estate that met the measure at the rating it was given still carried a bug with a public exploit repository and a Metasploit module rated Excellent.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: Technical vulnerability management evaluates exposure from the published characterisation, and the published characterisation was wrong in the direction that matters: MSRC's exploitability assessment of 'Exploitation Less Likely' stands unrevised while itm4n's exploit repository and a crash-safe Metasploit module have been public since 2020, and EPSS on 2026-08-28 sits at 0.42524, the 98.649th percentile. A.8.8 requires the vulnerability information to be obtained and evaluated; it does not require the evaluation to be re-run when the exploit landscape contradicts the vendor's original judgement.

new_control_requirements.name: ACTIVELY-EXPLOITED-OS-LPE-REMEDIATION-WINDOW-ENFORCEMENT
new_control_requirements.description: When an OS vendor flags a local-privilege-escalation flaw as exploited in the wild and it is KEV-listed, the monthly cumulative update that fixes it must be applied and the host rebooted within the KEV due date - installed-not-rebooted is not remediated.
new_control_requirements.evidence: This CVE is fixed only by the 2020-03-10 Windows cumulative update for each of 41 product entries, and a cumulative update does not take effect until the host reboots - so a fleet reporting the KB as installed can still be running the vulnerable BITS binary. The reboot gate matters more here than for a server-side flaw because the affected population is workstations that stay powered for weeks. CISA allowed 2022-01-28 to 2022-07-28 while Microsoft's own record still reads 'Exploitation Less Likely', so the KEV listing, not the vendor rating, has to be the trigger.

new_control_requirements.name: MITIGATION-ACTIVE-PATCH-PENDING-VERDICT-CLASS
new_control_requirements.description: Compliance verdicts must distinguish binary-patch-deployed from vendor-mitigation-active-without-patch from no-mitigation-at-all, and must surface the middle state as a time-bound compensating control rather than as a patched-per-SLA outcome.
new_control_requirements.evidence: For CVE-2020-0787 the middle state does not exist and the verdict must say so. BITS cannot be disabled - Windows Update, SCCM and third-party installers depend on it - and the defect lives in the service's own state-recovery path, so there is no configuration lever to record as a compensating control. A verdict system that permits 'mitigated' to be asserted from a service-hardening measure will accept a false one here. The distinguishing test is the file, not the policy: compare C:\Windows\System32\WindowsCoreDeviceInfo.dll against the component store and confirm the March 2020 or later cumulative is present and the host has rebooted since.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: 4h KEV-listing mitigation SLA applies.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CISA listed CVE-2020-0787 on 2022-01-28 with ransomware use Known and a 2022-07-28 due date - twenty-two months after Microsoft shipped the fix and rated it 'Exploitation Less Likely'. The point of the SLA on this CVE is which signal starts the clock: the vendor's exploitability index said no action was urgent and never revised, so a programme that waits for a vendor severity change waits indefinitely. The KEV listing is the trigger, and the action inside the window is a fleet-wide check for the March 2020 or later cumulative plus a reboot count, since there is no interim mitigation to fall back on.

CVE-2017-5689.name: Intel AMT Manageability Digest Authentication Bypass (CVE-2017-5689)

attack_vector.description: An attacker reaches the Intel manageability interface on TCP 16992 or 16993 and sends an HTTP request whose Digest Authorization header has an empty response field. The firmware compares the response using the client-supplied length, so the empty value matches and the request is served as admin regardless of password. The attacker then holds out-of-band control of the platform - keyboard-video-mouse, power, boot device, serial-over-LAN - beneath the operating system and invisible to it. NVD records a second path in which an unprivileged local attacker provisions the manageability features first.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none - unauthenticated network access to a provisioned manageability SKU; the local variant needs only an unprivileged account
attack_vector.complexity: low - one HTTP request with one header field blanked; Embedi's public exploit is a mitmproxy script and Metasploit ships a scanner for it
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered and not AI-weaponised.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Block TCP 16992, 16993, 16994 and 16995 and the RMCP ports at every boundary; unprovision AMT and ISM where manageability is unused; remove the Local Manageability Service; and obtain corrected firmware from the system manufacturer, verifying the resulting build number carries the four-digit form beginning with 3.
prevention.adequacy: Port blocking is immediate and effective against the network path. Unprovisioning is undone by any unprivileged local user, per the CVE's own description. The firmware fix is the only remediation and it depends on the OEM having produced one for the model, which is not within the operator's control.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Inspect for HTTP Authorization headers with an empty or short Digest response field on the manageability ports, and alert on any inbound connection to 16992/16993/16994/16995 from outside a designated out-of-band management segment.
detection.adequacy: Network detection is the only detection available. The management engine runs beneath the operating system, so nothing that happens through it reaches a host agent's telemetry - an estate relying on endpoint detection here has no coverage at all, not weak coverage.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treat a machine reached through AMT as compromised below the operating system: reinstalling the OS does not clear the management engine's state, so the response is firmware update, credential and provisioning-state reset, and re-verification of boot configuration.
response.adequacy: Correct but hard to trigger, because the event that would prompt it leaves no host-side trace. In practice the response has to be initiated from network evidence or from a provisioning-state audit, not from an endpoint alert.

NIST-800-53-IA-2.gap: Identification and authentication is present, answers every request, and returns 'admin' for a request that proves nothing. The manageability firmware compares the supplied Digest response using a length the client supplies, so an empty response field matches - a control assessment that confirms the AMT interface requires authentication is confirming the existence of the mechanism that is itself the defect. Nothing about credential strength, rotation or storage on that interface changes the outcome, because no credential is presented.

NIS2-Art21-identity-management.gap: The Article 21 identity and access-management expectation operates on accounts and their credentials. Here the account is the firmware's built-in admin, the credential is never checked, and the interface is on the chipset rather than in any system an identity programme enumerates - AMT is reachable on TCP 16992 and 16993 while the host is powered off, so it is outside the lifecycle of every operating-system account the obligation contemplates. An organisation can hold a complete, well-governed identity inventory and have no entry for this interface at all.

UK-CAF-B2.gap: The identity and access-control outcome assumes access to a system is mediated by identity. This request presents an Authorization header with an empty response field and is served as admin, so there is no identity in the transaction to mediate. Multi-factor authentication, privileged-access workstations and session recording all sit on the operating-system management plane; AMT is beneath it, and an attacker with keyboard-video-mouse and boot control does not need to traverse any of those.

AU-Essential-8-MFA.gap: Multi-factor authentication for privileged access is the Essential Eight strategy that would nominally cover an administrative interface like this, and it cannot engage: the bypass short-circuits the first factor, so there is no point at which a second one is requested. The strategy's scope is also the problem - it addresses authentication to systems and remote services, and the Intel management engine is neither in the operating system's account model nor visible to it, which means an estate at the highest maturity level for this strategy has done nothing about this interface.

ISO-27001-2022-A.5.15.gap: Access control policy governs who is granted access to what. It cannot reach a firmware comparison routine that treats a zero-length response as a match, and there is no access rule an organisation can write inside AMT that changes it. The only policy-side actions available are outside the product - block 16992/16993/16994/16995 at the boundary, unprovision, remove the Local Manageability Service - and the CVE's own description undercuts the second of those by stating that an unprivileged local attacker could provision the manageability features.

new_control_requirements.name: FLEET-CONTROL-PLANE-ADMIN-PRIVILEGE-TIER
new_control_requirements.description: Administrators of fleet-control-plane systems (MDM/UEM, EDR consoles, identity providers, container orchestrators, configuration management) must be classified as a distinct privileged class with controls to match.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Attached as the closest existing control; Intel AMT is not in its enumerated list but is the same thing in hardware - an out-of-band control plane over every machine that carries it, offering keyboard-video-mouse, power and boot-device control while the operating system is not running. What this CVE adds to the control is that the privileged class here has no account to govern: authentication is bypassed with an empty Digest response field, so the classification has to attach to the interface and its reachability - which network segment 16992/16993/16994/16995 are answerable from, and who can change a machine's provisioning state - rather than to a set of named administrators.

new_control_requirements.name: MITIGATION-ACTIVE-PATCH-PENDING-VERDICT-CLASS
new_control_requirements.description: Compliance verdicts must distinguish binary-patch-deployed from vendor-mitigation-active-without-patch from no-mitigation-at-all, and must surface the middle state as a time-bound compensating control rather than as a patched-per-SLA outcome.
new_control_requirements.evidence: This CVE produces the middle state by construction. Corrected firmware only reaches a machine through its system manufacturer's BIOS/ME package, so for any model whose OEM never shipped one the estate is permanently in mitigation-active: ports blocked, AMT unprovisioned, Local Manageability Service removed - and the comparison bug still in the firmware. The distinguishing test is not a version string but the build number's shape: Intel's fixed builds carry a four-digit build beginning with 3, the published example being 8.1.71.3608, so an inventory comparing only the first three components will report a vulnerable machine as remediated. Unprovisioning specifically must be recorded as mitigation and never as remediation, because the CVE's own description states an unprivileged local attacker can provision the features.

new_control_requirements.name: FIREWALL-EGRESS-TELEMETRY-SEPARATE-TRUST-ZONE
new_control_requirements.description: Perimeter and other trust-boundary devices must forward syslog, threat logs and authentication logs to a SIEM hosted in a separate trust zone with a different management plane.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Applied here to the out-of-band management plane rather than to a perimeter appliance, because the failure mode is the one the control exists for and no closer control is in the catalogue. Intel AMT runs beneath the operating system, so an intrusion through it produces no host-agent telemetry whatsoever - the absence of incident reporting for this CVE is at least partly a property of where it lives. The only observation point is the network: inbound sessions to 16992/16993/16994/16995 from outside a designated out-of-band segment, and Authorization headers whose Digest response field is empty. That collection has to happen in a zone the management engine itself cannot reach.

CVE-2014-1776.name: Internet Explorer CMarkup Use-After-Free (Operation Clandestine Fox)

attack_vector.description: A crafted web page triggers a use-after-free around CMarkup::IsConnectedToPrimaryMarkup in Internet Explorer 6 through 11. The in-the-wild exploit paired it with Flash to leak memory and defeat ASLR, then executed code in the browser process at the current user's privilege - a drive-by requiring only that the victim load the page.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none - a network-reachable page load, with no interaction beyond navigation
attack_vector.complexity: low to trigger, high to make reliable across IE 6 through 11 and across platforms including Windows XP, which lacks ASLR entirely
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered and not AI-weaponised; FireEye found it in live targeted attacks in April 2014.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Apply MS14-021 and restart. In the window before it shipped, EMET plus Enhanced Protected Mode, and removing Flash - which CERT/CC identifies as the component the exploit used for its ASLR bypass.
prevention.adequacy: The bulletin is decisive. The interim set is not evenly effective: CERT/CC states EMET's protection is limited on XP and Server 2003 for lack of ASLR, which are the platforms the campaign specifically targeted.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alert on iexplore.exe spawning children, and on pages serving crafted markup alongside a Flash object from the same origin.
detection.adequacy: The process-lineage half is reliable. The content half is not, in 2014 terms - Flash alongside HTML was the ordinary composition of the web at the time, so the pattern has almost no discriminating power without the specific exploit content.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treat browser code execution as full user compromise: rebuild the host, rotate that user's credentials, and review what they could reach - and decommission any XP or Server 2003 host involved rather than returning it to service.
response.adequacy: Sound. The decommissioning half is the part that gets deferred, and it is the part that matters, because the MS14-021 XP update was an exception Microsoft did not repeat.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: Flaw remediation measures from patch availability, and the sequence here inverts that: NVD dates exploitation to April 2014, FireEye disclosed on 2014-04-26, and Microsoft's response arrived first as advisory 2963983 - guidance, not a patch - before MS14-021 shipped out of band. For the days that mattered SI-2 had nothing to schedule, and the actions available were the workarounds in the advisory, which SI-2 does not govern and one of which Microsoft itself describes as not touching the vulnerable code.

NIS2-Art21-vulnerability-management.gap: Vulnerability management assumes a supported product with a patch stream. Internet Explorer 6 through 11 spans platforms that were already outside support when this shipped - Windows XP reached end of support on 2014-04-08, eighteen days before FireEye's disclosure - and Microsoft's decision to issue an XP update anyway was an exception. An Art. 21 process that recorded the XP estate as remediated on the strength of that exception recorded a one-off as a patch path that does not exist for the next flaw.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: The system security outcome expects systems to be configured and maintained to resist attack. The estate could be fully maintained and still exposed: every supported Internet Explorer version from 6 to 11 was affected, so there was no configuration or version choice within the product that avoided it. The only genuinely protective configuration was not using the product, which is a service-design decision the B4 outcome does not reach.

AU-Essential-8-App-Hardening.gap: The Essential Eight is unusually well-aimed here because it calls for configuring web browsers and for blocking or removing Flash, and CERT/CC records that the in-the-wild exploit used Flash to leak memory and bypass ASLR. Removing Flash therefore breaks the exploit's reliability chain without touching the CVE. The gap is that this is a side effect: the hardening measure that would have helped is filed under a separate mitigation from browser configuration, and neither is credited with defeating a use-after-free in the browser's own markup code.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: Management of technical vulnerabilities requires appropriate and timely measures once a vulnerability is known. For the window between FireEye's 2014-04-26 disclosure and MS14-021, the only measures available were the CERT/CC set, and A.8.8 cannot tell an organisation that one of them is illusory - unregistering VGX.DLL was widely deployed as remediation, and Microsoft's clarification carried in NVD is that VGX.DLL does not contain the vulnerable code. The control records that a measure was taken; it has no way to record that the measure was exploit-specific.

new_control_requirements.name: CONFIGURATION-SIDE-LIVE-PATCH-INVENTORY
new_control_requirements.description: For any vulnerability with a configuration-side mitigation path, that path must be inventoried, tested, and deployable independent of the vendor-patch path so operators are not gated on the patch cycle.
new_control_requirements.evidence: This CVE is the cautionary version of the control. Three configuration-side measures were published - EMET, Enhanced Protected Mode, and unregistering VGX.DLL - and they are not equivalent. NVD carries Microsoft's clarification that 'VGX.DLL does not contain the vulnerable code leveraged in this exploit', so that one blocks the observed exploit and nothing else, while breaking every application that renders VML. CERT/CC separately limits EMET on Windows XP and Server 2003 for lack of ASLR. The inventory must therefore record, per measure, whether it removes the defect, raises the cost, or only breaks one known exploit - because all three were deployed under the same word.

new_control_requirements.name: EOL-ASSET-DECOMMISSION
new_control_requirements.description: Network-reachable end-of-life devices with no vendor patch path must be isolated and decommissioned within a bounded window; mandatory compensating segmentation applies until removal.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Windows XP reached end of support on 2014-04-08 and CERT/CC records this campaign as targeting XP systems specifically. Microsoft shipped an XP update in MS14-021 anyway, which is exactly the event that undermines the control: an estate that received the exception can record the XP hosts as patched and defer the decommission, when the vendor made a one-off judgement it did not repeat. The register entry for such a host must be a removal date, and a vendor's exceptional out-of-support patch must not reset it.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: 4h KEV-listing mitigation SLA applies.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CISA listed this CVE on 2022-01-28 with a 2022-07-28 due date - six months for a CVSS 9.8 drive-by that had been exploited in the wild since April 2014 and whose EPSS on 2026-08-28 stood at 0.88013, the 99.757th percentile. The four-hour action is not MS14-021, which any current Windows build already carries; it is answering whether Internet Explorer 6 through 11 is still reachable anywhere in the estate, and on which hosts, since the surviving exposure is legacy XP and Server 2003 systems retained for a line-of-business application.

CVE-2014-6271.name: GNU Bash Shellshock Environment Variable Code Injection (CVE-2014-6271)

attack_vector.description: An attacker places text after a shell function definition in a value that will become an environment variable in a bash process on the other side of a privilege boundary. bash through 4.3 executes that trailing text while importing the function, before running anything it was invoked for. The documented paths are Apache mod_cgi and mod_cgid, the OpenSSH sshd ForceCommand feature, and DHCP clients that export lease options into the environment; for the CGI path the carrier is an ordinary HTTP request header.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none - unauthenticated network access to any service whose request data reaches a bash environment; the code then runs with the invoking process's privileges, which for a DHCP client hook is root
attack_vector.complexity: low - a crafted header, with maintained Metasploit modules and a dozen vector-specific public exploits still shipped twelve years later
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered and not AI-weaponised. Manual source reading of bash's function-import path in 2014, disclosed to the maintainer before publication.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Apply the full bash patch series - the 2014-09-24 update was incomplete and CVE-2014-7169 covers what it left - and verify by behaviour rather than version string. Where the shell cannot be fixed, close the invocation path instead: disable CGI handlers that shell out, and remove ForceCommand configurations that pass caller-supplied text.
prevention.adequacy: The patch series is sufficient where it can be applied. Path closure is the half that reaches appliance firmware, where the operator has no shell to patch, and it is the only prevention available for out-of-support devices.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alert on request headers carrying a shell function-definition prefix followed by trailing text, and on a web server, CUPS or DHCP client process spawning a shell that then opens a network connection.
detection.adequacy: The header signature is trivially reliable and trivially evaded by encoding variants, so the process-lineage signal is the durable one - a CGI handler spawning a shell that spawns a network client has no benign form. Internet-facing volume makes the header rule an alerting problem rather than a detection problem.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treat the invoking service account as compromised - rotate its credentials, review what it could reach - and re-check the patch state against the follow-on CVE-2014-7169 patches rather than the first update, because an incompletely patched host will be re-exploited after cleanup.
response.adequacy: Adequate for the CGI vector, where the blast radius is the web server account. It is understated for the DHCP-client vector, where the hook runs as root and the response is host rebuild, and it does not reach an appliance whose firmware the operator cannot inspect.

NIST-800-53-SI-10.gap: Information input validation requires inputs to be checked for accuracy, completeness and validity, and every application in the path did that to the inputs it recognised. The environment is not one of them. An HTTP header validated by the application is copied verbatim into an environment variable by the CGI mechanism and parsed by bash before the application's code runs at all, so the validation happens after the compromise and on the wrong side of it. SI-10 has no requirement that the channel by which a process passes data to a child be treated as an input channel, which is the entire mechanism here.

NIS2-Art21-supply-chain.gap: The supply-chain obligation addresses relationships with direct suppliers and service providers, and bash has neither - it is a component with no commercial relationship, present because the operating system includes it, and reached in this case through a vendor appliance that bundles it three layers down. The advisories on this CVE's reference list from Cisco, Juniper, F5, Citrix, VMware, Check Point, Arista, QNAP and IBM are all the same discovery: an organisation could not answer 'which of my devices contain bash' from any supplier relationship it had documented. The control produces a supplier register that would not have contained the affected component under any name.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: The system-security outcome expects vulnerable software to be identified and updated, and both halves fail in unusual ways here. Identification cannot use version strings, because distributions backported the fix into unchanged version numbers, so the same 'bash 4.2' string describes both a fixed and an exploitable host. Updating does not settle it either: the first upstream fix was incorrect and CVE-2014-7169 covers what remained, so a documented, verified, complete patch deployment on 2014-09-24 produced a still-vulnerable estate and a clean assessment simultaneously.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Essential Eight patch timeframes measure from vendor release, and here there were several vendor releases for one defect - the incorrect first fix and the follow-on patches covering CVE-2014-7169 - with the timeframe clock restarting invisibly for anyone who tracked the first. The model also has no place for the population that dominated this event's tail: appliance firmware bundling bash, where the operator has no patch to apply on the model's schedule and must wait for a vendor image, or has no path at all because the device is out of support.

ISO-27001-2022-A.5.21.gap: Managing information security in the ICT supply chain requires requirements to be agreed with suppliers and their delivery monitored. The component that broke was not delivered by a supplier under any agreement - it is the system shell, bundled inside products by vendors who did not enumerate it, and reached across privilege boundaries by mechanisms (CGI, ForceCommand, DHCP hooks) that no supply-chain register describes. A.5.21 as applied would have produced a supplier list and a set of contractual clauses, and neither would have answered the only question that mattered in September 2014: which of these products contain bash, and which of them invoke it with attacker-influenced environment variables.

new_control_requirements.name: AI-FRAMEWORK-CLI-SHELL-INPUT-NEUTRALIZATION
new_control_requirements.description: Tools and services that invoke external commands must never build a shell string, or a shell environment, from caller-supplied data: use argv-array execution without a shell, or neutralise the data before it can reach a shell parser.
new_control_requirements.evidence: The CGI mechanism does exactly what this control forbids, one layer below where anyone looks for it - it does not build a command string, it builds an environment, and the shell parses that environment before the invoked program runs. Every affected path shares that shape: ForceCommand passes caller-supplied text into a shell environment, and DHCP client hooks export lease options the same way. The catalogued wording is scoped to AI-framework CLIs; the stretch to a 2014 CGI handler is deliberate, because the invariant - caller data must never reach a shell parser, whether through argv or through the environment - is identical and is what the defect violates.

new_control_requirements.name: TIER-3-DEPENDENCY-INVENTORY
new_control_requirements.description: Supply chain inventory must extend to tier-3 dependencies - the dependencies of dependencies of direct dependencies - and coverage for system-level transitive components cannot be assumed from a supplier register.
new_control_requirements.evidence: In September 2014 the operative question was not how to patch bash but where bash was, and the answer took the form of vendor advisories arriving one at a time from Cisco, Juniper, F5, Citrix, VMware, Check Point, Arista, QNAP, IBM, Oracle and Apple - each disclosing that a product an organisation owned contained the component. That list is on this CVE's reference page and it is the failure of inventory made visible. An inventory reaching system-level transitive components would have produced the same list on day one, from the organisation's own records, instead of over the following weeks from the vendors'.

new_control_requirements.name: EOL-ASSET-DECOMMISSION
new_control_requirements.description: Network-reachable end-of-life devices with no vendor patch path must be isolated and decommissioned within a bounded window; mandatory compensating segmentation applies until removal.
new_control_requirements.evidence: The bash package update reaches general-purpose systems immediately and reaches embedded firmware not at all. For a device whose vendor never shipped an image - and by 2022, when CISA listed this, many of the products named in the 2014 advisories were out of support - there is no patch state to reach and 'apply updates per vendor instructions' cannot be executed. The verdict this control forces, bounded-window segmentation with a dated replacement, is the only honest one for that population, and it is also the answer to the version-string problem: a device you cannot query is not one you can assess.

CVE-2014-7169.name: GNU Bourne-Again Shell (Bash) Arbitrary Code Execution Vulnerability (CVE-2014-7169)

attack_vector.description: An attacker sets an environment variable that crosses a privilege boundary into a Bash invocation - an HTTP header consumed by Apache mod_cgi or mod_cgid, a value reaching OpenSSH sshd's ForceCommand, or a DHCP option processed by a client script. Bash imports the value as a function definition and, because the CVE-2014-6271 fix was incomplete, still processes the trailing string after certain malformed definitions. NVD's stated impact is that the attacker can write to files, or have unknown other impact.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none - each named boundary is reachable pre-authentication
attack_vector.complexity: low to reach, and the impact is disputed: NVD scores 9.8 and Red Hat 5.1 on the same defect, because NVD's own wording gives a file-write primitive rather than the direct command execution CVE-2014-6271 provided
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered and not AI-weaponised. The CVE was assigned within a day of CVE-2014-6271 going public and both NVD and Red Hat describe it purely as an incomplete fix for that CVE.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Install the distribution's fixed bash build for the release, restart every service that spawns bash across a privilege boundary, and verify behaviourally rather than by package version - on Ubuntu 14.04 specifically, confirm 4.3-7ubuntu1.3 and not 4.3-7ubuntu1.2.
prevention.adequacy: Sufficient only with the verification step attached. Without it, this is the case where doing the required thing promptly and recording it correctly still left the host vulnerable, because the package published as the fix on the most widely deployed affected release did not contain one.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alert on the '() {' sequence appearing in HTTP headers, query strings or DHCP option values, and on any CGI executable spawning a shell or network client.
detection.adequacy: The header signal is cheap and effective for the HTTP boundary and it is where most scanning lands. It does nothing for the DHCP boundary, which is not in any web log and which NVD names explicitly - that path needs client-side visibility that most estates do not collect. The child-process signal covers both and is the one that survives obfuscation of the prefix.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treat the service account as compromised and audit for written files rather than only for executed commands, since the primitive NVD attributes to this CVE is a file write - then check whether anything on the host executes what was written.
response.adequacy: The file-write framing is what makes this response different from the CVE-2014-6271 one, and skipping it is the common error: an incident process hunting only for command execution will find nothing on a host where the attacker dropped a file that a later cron job or CGI request executes.

NIST-800-53-SI-2.gap: Flaw remediation is the control this CVE was created by. CVE-2014-7169 exists because the fix for CVE-2014-6271 was incomplete, and SI-2 has no clause that re-opens a closed finding when the remediation that closed it is later shown to be partial - the finding was closed correctly, against the vendor guidance available at the time, and the closure was wrong. The same failure then repeated one layer down: Ubuntu shipped 4.3-7ubuntu1.2 as the fix, it did not contain one, and USN-2363-2 respun it as 1.3. An SI-2 process that records remediation as applied on the strength of a published advisory produced two consecutive false closures on the same defect, and nothing in the control detects either.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: The Article 21 patch-management obligation is measured against fix availability and deployment inside a timeframe, and both were satisfiable here within days in September 2014. What the obligation cannot express is the failure mode that actually occurred: the deployed fix was defective on Ubuntu 14.04, so the compliance record and the security state diverged for every organisation that patched promptly on the first advisory - the promptest were the most exposed to it. Article 21 asks that patches be applied; it has no requirement that the effect of a patch be verified independently of the fact of its deployment.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: The system-security outcome expects vulnerable software to be identified and updated, and identification fails here on the field being compared. The exposed property is a bash patch level, not a version: a host at bash 4.3 can be fully vulnerable or fully fixed depending on a suffix that most inventories either truncate or never collect, and on Ubuntu 14.04 the distinction between 4.3-7ubuntu1.2 and 4.3-7ubuntu1.3 is the entire finding. A CAF assessment that confirms an update process runs and that hosts report bash 4.3 has confirmed nothing about this CVE.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Essential Eight patch timeframes are keyed to vendor release and to whether the software is internet-facing, and by that measure this was a fast, well-publicised, universally-deployed patch that any maturity level would have met. The model has no control for the case that governed the outcome: a vendor package published as the fix that did not contain it. Nothing in the Essential Eight requires post-deployment verification of a patch's effect, so an organisation that installed 4.3-7ubuntu1.2 inside its window scores full marks on the patch control while remaining vulnerable to the CVE it was patching.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: Management of technical vulnerabilities requires vulnerability information to be obtained and exposure evaluated, and here the vulnerability information was itself the problem rather than the input. NVD carries no references at all for this CVE, so an A.8.8 process consuming the CVE record obtains an identifier, a description and nothing to act on; the fixed package versions and the 1.2-to-1.3 respin exist only in a distribution's tracker. The control assumes obtainable vulnerability information leads to an evaluable exposure, and gives no handling for a CVE whose remediation detail lives entirely outside the vulnerability record it is keyed to.

new_control_requirements.name: INCOMPLETE-PATCH-SEQUENCE-SEVERITY-MULTIPLIER
new_control_requirements.description: Vulnerability-management programs must apply a severity multiplier when a CVE is the Nth in an incomplete-patch sequence on the same primitive, treating the sequence itself as evidence that the underlying defect is not yet understood.
new_control_requirements.evidence: This CVE is the second entry in exactly such a sequence and is defined by it - NVD's own closing note is 'this vulnerability exists because of an incomplete fix for CVE-2014-6271', and Red Hat's description is the same. The sequence did not stop there: CVE-2014-6277, CVE-2014-6278, CVE-2014-7186 and CVE-2014-7187 followed on the same parser, and Exploit-DB's code lists for the Shellshock artefacts carry all of them together. An organisation applying this control after the second entry would have treated the Bash function-import parser as unresolved rather than treating each identifier as a discrete patch to close.

new_control_requirements.name: BUG-FAMILY-MITIGATION-PERSISTENCE
new_control_requirements.description: When a CVE patch lands, the pre-patch compensating controls must be retained until the patched code has soaked for a stated review period, because a patch for a defect in an incomplete-fix sequence is itself a candidate for being incomplete.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Ubuntu 14.04 LTS is the case this control is written for. The bash package 4.3-7ubuntu1.2 was published as the fix under USN-2363-1 and, per Ubuntu's own tracker, 'a build issue prevented the fix from being applied properly' - a respin to 4.3-7ubuntu1.3 followed under USN-2363-2. An organisation that dropped its mod_cgi restrictions and its request filtering on the strength of the first advisory was undefended for the interval, and the interval was invisible to it because the package version had changed and the advisory said fixed. Retaining the compensating controls across a soak period is what makes that interval survivable.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: 4h KEV-listing mitigation SLA applies.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CISA added CVE-2014-7169 on 2022-01-28 with a 2022-07-28 due date, seven years after the fix. What an hours-scale SLA can deliver here is not the bash package - which is fast to install and slow to verify - but the boundary actions: disabling mod_cgi and mod_cgid where no CGI application exists, and filtering requests carrying the '() {' prefix. Those remove the reachable boundaries NVD names without depending on a package whose first published fix on the largest affected release did not work.

attack_vector.description: A multipart/form-data POST names getMultipartRequestHandler as a parameter. Commons BeanUtils 1.7 populates the ActionForm by walking public getters, so the request reaches a method that was public for the framework's own use and was never meant to be addressable from request data — CWE-749, exposed dangerous method. Through it the request gains further access to the CommonsMultipartRequestHandler implementation and to BeanUtils, and the application stops serving. Nothing is injected and nothing is read; the impact is availability alone.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N and UI:N. One unauthenticated multipart POST to any action that binds an ActionForm.
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L, no race and no leak. The preconditions are both on the defender's side rather than the attacker's: Struts below 1.2.9 and Commons BeanUtils 1.7 together on the classpath, and an action that accepts multipart/form-data.
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. A 2006 disclosure with no finder named in any source read.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Upgrading Apache Struts to 1.2.9, the release NVD identifies as carrying the fix. Where the application cannot be rebuilt, rejecting multipart part names containing multipartRequestHandler and bounding multipart body size and part count at the reverse proxy.
prevention.adequacy: The upgrade is complete for this CVE. The proxy controls are derived from the mechanism NVD describes rather than from vendor guidance — the Struts 1.2.9 release notes that NVD tags as the authoritative reference return HTTP 404 — so they are proposals to validate against the application, not documented mitigations. That is the honest state of the remediation record for a twenty-year-old CVE on a framework with no maintained successor line.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Matching multipart part names against the literal string multipartRequestHandler at the proxy or in access logs, and correlating application-context restarts with individual form submissions rather than with load.
detection.adequacy: The string match is precise because the trigger is a literal method name, and the correlation test is the one that separates this from an ordinary capacity incident: a single request preceding an outage is a very different signature from a flood. Both depend on the proxy logging multipart part names, which most do not by default — and on the outage being investigated rather than absorbed by a restart, which is what usually happens to an availability-only fault.

response.what_would_have_worked: Restarting is sufficient to restore service and settles nothing. The response that matters is the artifact question: enumerate WEB-INF/lib across deployed applications for struts below 1.2.9 beside commons-beanutils 1.7, and decide per application whether it can be rebuilt or must be fronted by the proxy controls.
response.adequacy: Correct, and it is a portfolio exercise rather than an incident action — which is why it rarely happens. Availability-only impact means there is no compromise to investigate, no credential to rotate and no data to account for, so the incident closes at the restart and the underlying dependency pair stays deployed. That gap between 'service restored' and 'exposure removed' is the whole substance of this entry.

NIST-800-53-SC-5.gap: SC-5 denial-of-service protection is built around volume — rate limits, connection caps, upstream scrubbing. This is one well-formed multipart POST, indistinguishable by volume from a legitimate upload, so a fully implemented SC-5 offers no protection against it.

NIS2-Art21-availability.gap: Continuity and restoration measures are satisfiable and prevent nothing: the application restarts and the same request takes it down again. The measure never asks which deployed applications carry the Struts-below-1.2.9-plus-BeanUtils-1.7 pair, which is the only question that ends the exposure.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: Evaluating exposure requires reading two JAR versions inside a deployed WAR and knowing whether any action accepts multipart/form-data. A software inventory that records deployed applications rather than their bundled libraries cannot answer either, so the CVE arrives and the evaluation cannot be performed.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Struts 1.2.9 carried the fix and CISA listed the CVE on 2022-01-21 with a six-month due date of 2022-07-21 — one of the long-window listings, matching the fact that the impact is availability-only. EPSS reads 0.54635 at the 98.968th percentile on 2026-08-28. The 'documented compensating controls' branch is the branch that matters here and it is also the weakest: the vendor reference NVD tags as authoritative returns HTTP 404, so there is no vendor-documented mitigation to deploy, and the proxy-level controls are derivations from the NVD mechanism that an operator must validate before relying on. This control's requirement that the mitigation be documented is what forces that gap to be recorded rather than assumed away.

new_control_requirements.name: TIER-3-DEPENDENCY-INVENTORY
new_control_requirements.description: Supply chain inventory must extend beyond direct dependencies to the dependencies pulled in behind them; SBOM coverage for transitive and non-runtime-scoped packages cannot be assumed from a direct-dependency manifest.
new_control_requirements.evidence: This CVE is defined by a dependency pair, not by a product version: NVD states the flaw for Struts before 1.2.9 'with BeanUtils 1.7', so neither JAR alone establishes exposure. Commons BeanUtils is pulled in behind Struts rather than chosen, which is exactly the tier the control names, and the deciding version sits in WEB-INF/lib inside a deployed WAR where no application-level inventory looks. An inventory that records 'Struts 1.2.8' and stops cannot express the condition; one that reaches the transitive layer can answer it directly, which is the difference between evaluating this CVE and receiving it.

CVE-2012-0391.name: Apache Struts 2 ExceptionDelegator OGNL Remote Code Execution (S2-008)

attack_vector.description: An unauthenticated request supplies a parameter value that cannot be converted to the target action property's declared type. Struts 2's ExceptionDelegator handles the resulting conversion error by interpreting the supplied value as an OGNL expression, which reaches the JVM object graph and starts a process as the servlet container's account.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none - the trigger is an ordinary request to an ordinary action URL, which is why the CVSS vector reads PR:N
attack_vector.complexity: low - one request, no session, no memory primitive; the public module is Excellent-ranked and portable across Java, Linux and Windows targets
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered and not AI-weaponised. S2-008 credits Johannes Dahse of SEC Consult Vulnerability Lab and Bruce Phillips, and the exploit module is hand-written.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Upgrade struts2-core and xwork-core to 2.2.3.1 or later and redeploy. Enumerate shaded and repackaged copies of the library, not only the declared dependency.
prevention.adequacy: Sufficient going forward and insufficient backwards: execution as the container account exposes database credentials, keystores and session-signing keys, and the upgrade rotates none of them. S2-008's parameter-filtering advice narrows the reachable surface but does not close this issue.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alert on the application-server process spawning a shell, and on request parameters carrying OGNL syntax against typed properties. Treat a spike of type-conversion exceptions with unrecognised parameter names as an exploitation attempt rather than a client bug.
detection.adequacy: The process-lineage rule is the durable half; the parameter-content rule is evadable by expression obfuscation, and the exception-log signal only exists where application logs are shipped and retained, which a default container configuration does not do.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treat the host as compromised: hunt for JSPs and servlets under the deployed tree that no build produced, rebuild the application server rather than cleaning it, and rotate database credentials, keystores and session-signing keys before returning it to service.
response.adequacy: Decisive on the credential side. Weaker on scope: OGNL execution inside the JVM leaves little on disk unless the attacker chose to write a shell, so an in-memory-only intrusion is bounded from network and log evidence rather than from the host.

NIST-800-53-SI-10.gap: Information input validation requires that inputs be checked for validity, and here the check is what triggers the flaw: the value fails type conversion, which is validation working as designed, and the failure path then evaluates the rejected value as an OGNL expression. An SI-10 implementation can be complete and correct at the application layer and change nothing, because the defect is downstream of validation rather than in place of it. The control also gives no way to distinguish struts2-core 2.2.3 from 2.2.3.1 - both validate the same way; only one evaluates the rejected input.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: Art. 21 measures resolve to moving struts2-core and xwork-core past 2.2.3.1. The gap is dependency visibility rather than timeliness: the vulnerable component is a library inside a deployed artefact, and an Art. 21 patch-management measure applied to servers and their installed software packages does not reach a JAR shaded into a WAR that the organisation or a supplier built. The flaw is unauthenticated and remotely triggered, so any application whose dependency graph is not enumerated is fully exposed while the measure reports the host as current.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: The system security outcome expects services to be configured and maintained to resist attack. On this CVE there was no configuration to get right: S2-008's own mitigation - stricter parameter-name filtering - narrows what reaches the conversion path but does not stop a permitted parameter with a mismatched type being evaluated, and the bulletin's other recommendation, disabling development mode, addresses a different issue in the same advisory. Meeting B4 here requires the version change and nothing short of it.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: The Essential Eight patch-applications control runs its timeframes from vendor release and is scoped to named application classes plus internet-facing services. A Struts 2 application is an internet-facing service and so is in scope, but the unit the control operates on is the deployed service, while the artefact needing replacement is a transitive library version inside it. An organisation at the target maturity level that patches its application server and its own releases on schedule can still ship a WAR pinned to struts2-core 2.2.3, and the assessment records compliance.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.28.gap: Secure coding is the control aimed at this defect class - untrusted input reaching an expression evaluator - and it is aimed at the wrong party. The evaluation happens inside the framework's exception-handling path, not in code the adopting organisation wrote, so an A.8.28 programme covering the organisation's own source can pass entirely while the flaw sits in a dependency. The control's useful expression here is a dependency-review requirement rather than a code-review one, which is a different practice than the one A.8.28 is usually implemented as.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: Management of technical vulnerabilities requires vulnerability information to be obtained and acted on. Acting on it means the 2.2.3.1 upgrade, and A.8.8 supplies no interim measure for the window before it: the vendor documents no workaround that closes this specific issue, and the parameter-filtering lever S2-008 describes changes the exposure without removing it, which is exactly the state an A.8.8 register is prone to record as 'mitigated'.

new_control_requirements.name: ECOMMERCE-PLATFORM-EXTENSION-UNTRUSTED-DESERIALIZATION-GUARD
new_control_requirements.description: A web application platform and every third-party component it loads must never pass request-supplied data - cookies, headers, body or query parameters - into a native interpretation sink on an unauthenticated request path. Patch-management and secure-coding programmes must enumerate every bundled component as part of the code-execution surface, not only the core platform.
new_control_requirements.evidence: The control's wording is written for e-commerce platforms and native deserialization; it is the closest existing entry to this defect and the class is identical - request-supplied data reaching an interpretation sink on an unauthenticated path, inside a framework component rather than in the adopting organisation's own code. Here the sink is OGNL evaluation in Struts 2's ExceptionDelegator and the trigger is a parameter whose value cannot be converted to its property type. The enumeration half is the load-bearing part: the vulnerable artefact is struts2-core or xwork-core below 2.2.3.1, which can be shaded inside a WAR that no host-level inventory sees. The distinguishing test: send an unauthenticated request supplying a non-numeric value with an OGNL construction to a typed property on a staging deployment, and confirm it is rejected without evaluation.

new_control_requirements.name: SCANNER-PAPER-COMPLIANCE-TEST
new_control_requirements.description: A vulnerability scanner that reports 'patched' from a package or product version alone is paper compliance. The operational test is whether the scan resolves the actual component that carries the flaw - including copies embedded inside deployed artefacts - and whether it verifies the specific fixed build rather than any version newer than some other fix.
new_control_requirements.evidence: This CVE is a clean instance. The affected component is struts2-core or xwork-core below 2.2.3.1, and a host-level scan sees a Tomcat or JBoss package that is fully current while the vulnerable JAR sits inside a deployed WAR. The version question is also easy to get wrong from the advisory alone: S2-008 as it stands today records the bulletin's overall range as Struts 2.0.0 through 2.3.17 with an upgrade recommendation of at least 2.3.18, because a different issue in the same bulletin persisted - so a scanner keyed to the bulletin rather than the CVE will produce a boundary that is wrong in one direction, and one keyed to the deployed server package will miss the artefact entirely. The distinguishing test: resolve every deployed artefact's dependency graph, including shaded copies, and assert the struts2-core coordinate is at or above 2.2.3.1.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CISA listed this on 2022-01-21 with a 2022-07-21 due date - six months for an unauthenticated CVSS 9.8 remote-code-execution flaw whose fix has existed since 2.2.3.1 and whose verified Metasploit module has been public since 2012-06-05; EPSS on 2026-08-28 was 0.75599 at the 99.493rd percentile. Because the patch is a decade old, a four-hour clock here is a discovery clock rather than a deployment one: the deliverable is enumerating which deployed artefacts still bundle struts2-core below 2.2.3.1, with the redeploy scheduled immediately behind that.

attack_vector.description: Code already running on the host drives a Win32k user-mode callback - Metasploit names the path NtUserSetWindowFNID - so that Win32k mishandles an object in memory and kernel state can be corrupted, taking the calling process to SYSTEM. It is the escalation step, not the entry step: it converts a phishing or commodity-malware foothold into full host control.
attack_vector.privileges_required: local code execution as any user; no administrative rights
attack_vector.complexity: low given a foothold, but build-dependent - the public module carries offsets for specific builds and is flagged crash-OS-restarts
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered. Kaspersky's automatic exploit prevention flagged the behaviour and human analysts characterised the flaw; no AI tooling is credited.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Apply the October 2018 Microsoft security update for each affected SKU and reboot. Microsoft published no configuration-side workaround, so the only other lever is denying the local code execution the exploit needs - application allowlisting, macro and script restrictions.
prevention.adequacy: Sufficient once installed and rebooted per SKU; least-privilege policy is not a substitute, because SYSTEM is exactly what the exploit grants.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alert on a non-elevated process acquiring a SYSTEM token outside a service or scheduled-task path, and on win32k.sys bugchecks with no driver or hardware change.
detection.adequacy: The bugcheck signal catches failed attempts, which the build-specific offsets make common; a successful escalation is quiet, so the token-acquisition signal carries the weight.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treat a confirmed escalation as full host compromise - rebuild rather than clean, and rotate every credential and cached token the host held, since SYSTEM reaches all of them.
response.adequacy: Necessary given the documented ransomware use: Sodin/REvil escalated with this CVE before encrypting, so the escalation is a pre-impact indicator, not a post-incident finding.

NIST-800-53-AC-6.gap: Least privilege is the control operators reach for on a local privilege escalation, and it is precisely what this flaw voids. The exploit takes any code already running - a standard user's process, a macro, a service account - to SYSTEM through the Win32k callback path, so the privilege boundary AC-6 establishes is the one being crossed. Restricting who holds administrative rights changes nothing about the outcome.

NIS2-Art21-patch-management.gap: The fix has been available since October 2018 and CISA set a 2022-07-21 due date on the 2022-01-21 listing. The gap NIS2 patch management leaves is the reboot and the SKU spread: the CVE affects Windows 7 through Windows 10 and Server 2008 through Server 2019, each with its own fixed build, so a process that tracks 'the October 2018 rollup was deployed' does not establish that every SKU reached its fixed build and restarted.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: System security assurance treats a local privilege escalation as second-order because it requires an existing foothold. Kaspersky's two reports show why that ordering fails here: the same CVE served FruityArmor's targeted intrusions in 2018 and Sodin/REvil's ransomware in 2019, so the exploit is the step that converts a routine phishing foothold into domain-wide impact - the assurance case that ranks it below remote-code-execution flaws is ranking the wrong property.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Essential Eight patch timeframes for operating systems are met by shipping the October 2018 rollup within the required window, and this CVE shows two ways that verdict can be true while hosts stay exposed - an update installed without the reboot that loads the corrected Win32k code, and a legacy SKU in the affected list, Windows 7 or Server 2008, that the estate's patch tooling no longer covers at all.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: Management of technical vulnerabilities has to prioritise, and the inputs it normally prioritises on understate this one: CVSS 7.8 with AV:L reads as a local, second-order issue, and NVD assigns no CWE at all, so a risk-rating process keyed on severity and weakness class ranks it below remote flaws - while Kaspersky documented it inside ransomware that used it to escalate before encrypting.

new_control_requirements.name: ACTIVELY-EXPLOITED-OS-LPE-REMEDIATION-WINDOW-ENFORCEMENT
new_control_requirements.description: When an OS vendor flags a local-privilege-escalation flaw as exploited in the wild and it is KEV-listed, the monthly cumulative update that fixes it must be applied and rebooted across the entire affected endpoint fleet within the KEV remediation window, not on the normal patch cadence, and account-privilege policy must not be relied on to contain it.
new_control_requirements.evidence: The control's two clauses are both load-bearing here. The reboot clause: the fix replaces kernel-mode Win32k code in the October 2018 update, so an installed-not-rebooted host keeps the vulnerable component loaded. The privilege clause: the exploit's entire purpose is to reach SYSTEM from an unprivileged process, so a compensating story built on restricting administrative rights is describing the boundary being crossed. The distinguishing test the control names applies directly - enumerate installed build numbers against the fixed build per SKU across Windows 7, 8.1, RT 8.1, 10 and Server 2008 through 2019, and confirm none remains below it - because MSRC publishes no single cross-SKU version boundary. CISA listed the CVE on 2022-01-21 with ransomware use Known, and Kaspersky documented Sodin/REvil embedding an exploit for it to escalate before encrypting.

new_control_requirements.name: KERNEL-EXPLOITATION-DETECTION
new_control_requirements.description: Deploy monitoring rules for kernel privilege escalation indicators. Alert within 60 seconds of detection.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Attached as the closest existing control, with the platform difference stated: the control names auditd and eBPF, which are Linux mechanisms, and this is a Windows kernel component - so for this CVE it means the equivalent Windows telemetry, kernel-mode ETW providers and EDR token-integrity events, not the named tooling. What transfers exactly is the indicator and the latency. The indicator is a non-elevated process acquiring a SYSTEM token outside a service or scheduled-task path, plus win32k.sys bugchecks with no driver or hardware change - the public module for this CVE is offset-dependent and flagged crash-OS-restarts, so failed attempts are noisy. The 60-second latency matters because Kaspersky documented Sodin/REvil using this escalation immediately before encryption, which is the window in which the alert is still actionable.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: 4h KEV-listing mitigation SLA applies.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CISA listed CVE-2018-8453 on 2022-01-21 with a 2022-07-21 due date - six months for a flaw with a documented ransomware implementation and a public Metasploit module. EPSS on 2026-08-28 was 0.70042 at the 99.344th percentile. There is no configuration-side mitigation an hours-scale SLA can deploy, since Microsoft published no workaround, so what the SLA delivers is the fleet enumeration: identify every host below the fixed build for its SKU and every host on a SKU the patch tooling no longer reaches, and schedule the update and reboot against that list rather than against a rollup-deployment percentage.

CVE-2021-35247.name: SolarWinds Serv-U LDAP Query Input Validation (CVE-2021-35247)

attack_vector.description: The Serv-U web login passes username input into an LDAP query without escaping filter metacharacters, so an unauthenticated request can alter the filter the server builds against the corporate directory. The primitive is query manipulation and a relay from the internet into an internal directory service, not code execution on Serv-U.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — an unauthenticated request to the web login of an internet-facing service.
attack_vector.complexity: low to reach and uncertain in effect. SolarWinds reports that the LDAP servers it examined ignored the improper characters, so the demonstrated downstream impact is nil; what an arbitrary directory does with a malformed filter is a property of that directory rather than of Serv-U.
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Found by Microsoft's Jonathan Bar Or during Log4j threat-hunting in December 2021, from observing attack traffic originating from serv-u.exe.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Upgrading to Serv-U 15.3, or — available immediately and independent of the vendor — removing LDAP authentication from the web login path or taking that login off untrusted networks.
prevention.adequacy: The upgrade is complete and SolarWinds offers no workaround alongside it, so the compensating routes are the operator's own inference from the vendor's scoping rather than supported guidance. Both change service behaviour, which is why they need a decision rather than a change ticket.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Logging and alerting on LDAP filter metacharacters in the Serv-U web-login credential fields, and on LDAP traffic leaving the Serv-U host for anything other than the configured directory server.
detection.adequacy: Achievable and rarely in place. The signal that actually surfaced this flaw was not on the Serv-U host: Microsoft saw attack traffic attributed to serv-u.exe while hunting something else entirely, which is a vantage point most operators of a single file-transfer appliance do not have.

response.what_would_have_worked: Reviewing the directory side rather than the Serv-U side — checking what the LDAP server actually did with the submitted filters, since that is where the impact is decided and where the vendor's 'no downstream effect' claim would be confirmed or refuted for the specific estate.
response.adequacy: Correct and easily skipped, because the CVE is filed against Serv-U and the evidence lives on a different system owned by a different team.

NIST-800-53-SI-10.gap: The validation that failed is inside the query-construction path, not at the perimeter or the field level — SolarWinds' fix is described as updating 'the input mechanism to perform additional validation and sanitization'. An SI-10 assessment evidenced by request filtering and form validation is satisfied while the LDAP filter is still assembled by concatenation.

NIS2-Art21-vulnerability-handling.gap: Handling starts at disclosure and here exploitation came first: Microsoft found the flaw by observing attacks already coming from serv-u.exe. The vendor's own statement that no downstream effect was detected then gives an entity a documented reason to rank a KEV-listed, actively exploited CVE below its two-week due date.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: The system being assessed is not where the risk lands. Serv-U is doing exactly what it is meant to do — authenticate users against the corporate directory — and the flaw turns that intended relationship into an unauthenticated path from the internet to an internal LDAP query. Hardening the file transfer service does not address a defect whose consequence is on the directory.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: SolarWinds' boundary is 'versions 15.2.5 and earlier', so 15.2.5 is vulnerable and 15.3 is the fix; an inventory rule written inclusively at 15.2.5 passes every affected instance. The strategy also has no way to record the configuration precondition, so two hosts on the same build score identically while only the LDAP-bound one is exposed.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.28.gap: Secure-coding review concentrates on SQL parameterisation and command construction; LDAP filter assembly sits in authentication plumbing and is rarely treated as a query interface at all. The control can be implemented thoroughly against the surfaces it names and never reach the function that built this filter.

new_control_requirements.name: DB-ABSTRACTION-LAYER-PARAMETERIZATION-VERIFICATION
new_control_requirements.description: Parameterization must be verified at the data-access or query-construction layer itself, not assumed from application-layer input validation or a perimeter WAF. This applies to every query language the application composes, not only SQL.
new_control_requirements.evidence: This is the closest existing control and it needs its scope stated explicitly, because the vocabulary's version is written around SQL and this defect is in an LDAP filter. SolarWinds describes the flaw as the web login 'allowing characters that were not sufficiently sanitized' on the LDAP path and the fix as updating the input mechanism — both located in query construction. Microsoft's Jonathan Bar Or put the property plainly: 'you could feed Serv-U with data and it'll build a LDAP query with your unsanitized input'. No perimeter control catches a username that is only dangerous once the filter is assembled.

new_control_requirements.name: MITIGATION-ACTIVE-PATCH-PENDING-VERDICT-CLASS
new_control_requirements.description: Compliance verdicts must distinguish three states: (a) binary patch deployed and the vulnerability eliminated, (b) a configuration or vendor mitigation active with no binary patch, and (c) neither — with the residual risk of (b) stated rather than recorded as compliant.
new_control_requirements.evidence: This CVE produces exactly the ambiguity the control exists for. SolarWinds states that 'no downstream affect has been detected as the LDAP servers ignored improper characters' and separately that Log4j attempts failed because Serv-U does not use Log4j, while CISA listed the CVE as exploited on 2022-01-21 with a 2022-02-04 due date. An estate on 15.2.5 with LDAP authentication disabled is in state (b) and is neither vulnerable-as-shipped nor remediated, and no single verdict describes it honestly.

attack_vector.description: The backend password-reset flow compares the caller-supplied reset code against the stored code with PHP's loose equality operator. Supplying the boolean true satisfies the comparison through type juggling, so an unauthenticated caller who knows an administrator login requests a reset, sets a password of its choosing and signs in. Four HTTP requests, no timing or memory dependency.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none — PR:N; the attacker needs no account, only network reach to /backend and an administrator's login name, which the advisory names as a precondition.
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L, UI:N. EPSS records 0.90418 at the 99.794th percentile on 2026-08-28, consistent with a chain that a scanner template can drive end to end.
attack_vector.ai_factor: Found by manual source review by Solar Security CMS Research and credited to five named researchers in GHSA-mxr5-mc97-63rc. No automated discovery is claimed.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Upgrading october/system to Build 472 or v1.1.5, published 2021-08-26, and restricting network access to /backend. The upgrade closes the comparison; the network restriction removes the only surface it is reachable through.
prevention.adequacy: The upgrade is complete for the defect and, because this is a PHP application, takes effect on the next request with no restart window. It is not complete for the incident: a password the attacker already set survives the upgrade, so rotation is part of prevention for anyone who patched after exposure rather than before.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alerting on a password-reset POST whose body carries a non-string code value, and on a successful backend sign-in that follows a reset the account owner did not request.
detection.adequacy: Both are cheap and specific, and both require web access logs that record request bodies or at least the reset-endpoint path with its token segment. A site logging only status codes and URLs without the reset path sees four ordinary 200s and a 302.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating a confirmed reset as a full backend compromise: rotate every backend password, invalidate sessions, and review every theme file, CMS page and plugin for changes since the earliest reachable date rather than since the detection.
response.adequacy: The review is bounded by how far back the site's access logs and file history reach, and the exposure window opens at the deployed version rather than at the advisory date — a site running Build 471 since before 2021-08-26 has been reachable for the whole of its life on that build.

NIST-800-63B-rev4.gap: The guidance can be satisfied in full by a verifier whose comparison operator coerces types. It specifies what must be checked and how strong the secret must be, not the semantics of the check itself, so a site meeting every authenticator and verifier requirement still accepts a boolean where a reset code belongs.

NIS2-Art21-vulnerability-handling.gap: A complete public advisory existed for nearly five months before the exploitation reporting, so the measure had everything it needed and still produced no obligation for an entity that does not carry its CMS as a tracked dependency. The measure requires a handling process rather than proof that the process can see every deployed component, which is where the exposure sat.

UK-CAF-B2.gap: Every element the outcome examines was correct: the account model, the privileges, the authentication control. The failure is in the recovery path, which B2 does not direct an assessor at, so the assessment returns the same result on a site that can be taken over in four requests and one that cannot.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: The strategy is correctly aimed and correctly triggered here, and it still leaves the residual: it measures whether the update was applied, and the outcome of this flaw is a credential that survives the update. Top maturity is achievable on a site where an attacker-chosen administrator password is still valid.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.28.gap: The control binds the organisation's own development practice. The defect is a single comparison operator in a third-party package, so an organisation can apply secure coding principles impeccably to everything it writes and inherit the flaw whole from the dependency it did not write.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: The fix was available from 2021-08-26 and CISA listed the CVE on 2022-01-18 with a 2022-02-01 due date, four days after the Ukrainian government website attacks began. The whichever-is-later clause therefore resolves to patch availability and puts the obligation almost five months before the KEV listing — precisely the interval in which the vulnerability-handling measure produced nothing for an entity that does not track its CMS as a dependency.

new_control_requirements.name: AI-APP-PASSWORD-RECOVERY-INTEGRITY
new_control_requirements.description: An application's password-reset / account-recovery flow must (1) generate reset tokens with a cryptographically secure RNG, making them long, single-use, and short-lived; and (2) verify the reset token server-side, bound to the requesting account, with a type-safe comparison, before accepting a new password - the reset endpoint must never perform a reset without a valid, matching, unexpired token. Rate-limit reset attempts. The distinguishing test: on a staging instance, POST to the reset endpoint with a wrong, absent, or non-string code value and confirm the password is not changed.
new_control_requirements.evidence: The control as inventoried is scoped to AI applications; October CMS is a general-purpose PHP CMS, and this is the closest existing control rather than an exact category match. Its second clause is the defect exactly: the reset endpoint accepted a new password without a valid matching token because the comparison coerced a boolean to match a string. The distinguishing test — POST a non-string code value and confirm the password does not change — is a single request, and it is the check that the authenticator guidance, the identity-and-access outcome and the secure-coding control all leave unasked.

CVE-2021-25296.name: Nagios XI Windows WMI Config Wizard OS Command Injection

attack_vector.description: windowswmi.inc.php appends the request-supplied plugin_output_len onto the check command string after --forcetruncateoutput and passes the result to PHP's exec(). The parameter is only ever a truncation length, but nothing checks that it is numeric and nothing neutralises shell metacharacters, so a value like `9999; <command>;` executes as the web user on the Nagios XI server. The same pattern in switch.inc.php and cloud-vm.inc.php produces CVE-2021-25297 and CVE-2021-25298.
attack_vector.privileges_required: PR:L — an authenticated session, and Fastly records that the config wizards are reachable by non-admin users as well as admins, so the exploitable credential is the lowest tier the product issues.
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L. One authenticated HTTP request, no race and no memory corruption, and Metasploit automates authentication and the version check as well as the injection.
attack_vector.ai_factor: None recorded. Fastly attributes the public proof of concept to fs0c-sh in early 2021 and no AI tooling appears in any analysis; Unit 42's exploitation report describes conventional cryptojacking tooling.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Upgrading beyond Nagios XI 5.7.5 and confirming the services cycled, verified directly against the wizard files rather than against the changelog. Failing that, cutting the set of accounts that can reach the config-wizard surface and removing the monitoring server's reachability from untrusted networks, since the flaw needs an authenticated session.
prevention.adequacy: The upgrade removes the injection. Its weakness is verification rather than efficacy: Nagios's published changelogs for 5.8.0 through 5.8.3 do not name CVE-2021-25296, CVE-2021-25297 or CVE-2021-25298, so an operator cannot close the KEV item against a vendor statement and must confirm the fix in the wizard files themselves. Restricting accounts is a genuine reduction, but it is a smaller gate than it appears because the wizards are reachable by non-admin users.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alerting on any config-wizard request whose plugin_output_len parameter contains a non-digit, and on the Nagios XI web user spawning curl, wget, tar or a Python interpreter. Network-side, comparing the server's egress against the enumerable set of hosts it is configured to poll.
detection.adequacy: The parameter check is exact, because the field has one legitimate form and any metacharacter in it is the attack. The process-lineage half is harder on this particular target: the Nagios XI web tier legitimately builds and executes check commands, so process creation by the web user is normal traffic and the rule has to discriminate on binary and arguments rather than on the fact of execution.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating the monitoring server as a credential store that has been read: rotate every WMI account, SSH key and SNMP community the Nagios XI installation held, then hunt the host for the Unit 42 payload set and the systemd-imitating persistence scripts, and rebuild rather than clean.
response.adequacy: Credential rotation is the step that bounds the incident, because the value of this host to an attacker is the estate it can reach rather than the host itself. The hunt is unusually concrete since Unit 42 published file names and hashes, but that specificity is also its limit: it identifies one 2021 cryptojacking chain, and an operator who finds none of those files has ruled out that chain and not the vulnerability's exploitation.

NIST-800-53-SI-10.gap: plugin_output_len is only ever a truncation length and is concatenated onto a shell command passed to exec() with no numeric check and no metacharacter neutralisation — precisely the failure SI-10 names. But SI-10 binds the system owner, and the owner of a purchased monitoring product cannot edit windowswmi.inc.php and stay supported, so the control is fully covered on paper and structurally unsatisfiable in practice.

NIS2-Art21-supply-chain.gap: Nagios's published changelogs for 5.8.0 (2021-01-13), 5.8.1 (2021-01-15), 5.8.2 (2021-02-25) and 5.8.3 (2021-03-31) name other CVEs but none of CVE-2021-25296/25297/25298. A supplier-assurance process cannot establish from the vendor's own release notes which release removed the flaw, so it cannot record a remediation date against the 2022-02-01 KEV due date.

UK-CAF-B2.gap: B2 assessments of a monitoring platform concentrate on who holds administrative access, which is the wrong tier: Fastly records the config wizards as reachable by authenticated non-admin users as well as admins. A finding that Nagios XI admin is tightly held bounds nothing about this vulnerability.
