AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: The affected band spans two minor lines, 5.5.6 through 5.7.5, so an estate that moved from a 5.5.x to a 5.7.x build during the window improved every patch-currency measure the control produces while remaining vulnerable at both ends. The control measures movement rather than the boundary that matters.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: NVD names only xi-5.7.5 while Rapid7 and Fastly both place the range at 5.5.6 through 5.7.5, so an exposure assessment built from the CVE record alone concludes a 5.6.x or 5.7.0 installation is out of scope when it is not. A.8.8 contains no requirement to reconcile the CVE record against vendor and researcher version claims.

new_control_requirements.name: AI-FRAMEWORK-CLI-SHELL-INPUT-NEUTRALIZATION
new_control_requirements.description: Tools and applications that invoke external commands must never build a shell string from user-supplied arguments or configuration: use argv-array execution with no shell, or neutralize the argument at the boundary.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2021-25296 — attached as the closest existing argv-array execution control, noting its description is framed around AI-framework CLIs while the code here is a PHP monitoring wizard. The required property is identical and is exactly what is missing: windowswmi.inc.php appends plugin_output_len onto $disk_wmi_command after --forcetruncateoutput and passes the string to exec(). An argv-array call would have made the parameter a single argument and a semicolon in it inert, which also closes the sibling defects in switch.inc.php and cloud-vm.inc.php.

new_control_requirements.name: FLEET-CONTROL-PLANE-ADMIN-PRIVILEGE-TIER
new_control_requirements.description: Administrators of fleet-control-plane systems (MDM/UEM, EDR consoles, identity providers, container orchestrators, configuration management) must be classified as a distinct privilege tier with its own access, review and monitoring requirements.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2021-25296 — a monitoring server is a fleet control plane by the same argument: it holds the WMI credentials, SSH keys and SNMP communities for every host it polls, so command execution on it reaches the monitored estate. The tiering this control requires would also have surfaced the specific gap here, which is that the exploitable surface is not the admin tier at all — Fastly records the config wizards as reachable by authenticated non-admin users, so a control plane's low-privilege accounts need the same treatment as its administrative ones.

new_control_requirements.name: MITIGATION-ACTIVE-PATCH-PENDING-VERDICT-CLASS
new_control_requirements.description: Compliance verdicts must distinguish three states: (a) binary patch deployed and the vulnerability eliminated, (b) vendor-mitigation rule active with no binary patch, carrying explicit residual risk, and (c) neither.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CVE-2021-25296 — this entry cannot honestly be recorded in state (a) from vendor evidence, because Nagios's changelogs for 5.8.0 through 5.8.3 name none of CVE-2021-25296/25297/25298. The truthful record is 'running a release later than 5.7.5, with the fix confirmed by inspecting windowswmi.inc.php, switch.inc.php and cloud-vm.inc.php, and no vendor statement tying any release to these CVEs' — a state a two-valued patched/unpatched verdict cannot express, and one that also covers the interim posture of restricting config-wizard access.

CVE-2021-25297.name: Nagios XI Switch Wizard OS Command Injection (CVE-2021-25297)

attack_vector.description: The Switch/Router configuration wizard in Nagios XI passes the device address the operator supplies into a shell command without neutralising it — Fastly names the ip_address parameter — so an authenticated user appends commands that run on the monitoring server under the web account. The consequence is larger than the host: a Nagios XI server holds the check definitions, SNMP communities and monitoring credentials for the estate it polls, and its command and event-handler definitions execute on a schedule, which is both the reach and the persistence mechanism.
attack_vector.privileges_required: PR:L — any authenticated Nagios XI account, at any privilege level. A read-only monitoring login is sufficient, which makes the credential requirement a much weaker gate than it appears.
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L, a single HTTP request, with a Metasploit module (exploit/linux/http/nagios_xi_configwizards_authenticated_rce, disclosure 2021-02-13) that authenticates, version-checks and exploits whichever of the three affected wizards is reachable.
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. The proof of concept came from fs0c-sh in early 2021 and Fastly's Security Research Team extended the analysis to the full 5.5.6-5.7.5 range across three wizards; neither credits automated discovery or AI assistance.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Upgrading Nagios XI beyond the 5.5.6-5.7.5 range and verifying the fixed build against the vendor's current changelog rather than assuming one; restricting the web interface to a management network so a leaked monitoring credential has nowhere to be presented; and reducing the number of accounts that can authenticate at all, since PR:L makes every account exploitation-capable.
prevention.adequacy: Incomplete on its own terms, because the fixed version cannot be established from a Nagios source — the GitHub advisory records both affected and patched versions as unknown, and the range in circulation comes from Fastly and Metasploit. The network restriction is the mitigation that does not depend on that ambiguity, and it is the one an operator can verify.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alerting on shell metacharacters in configuration-wizard parameters in the web server access log, on the web account spawning shells, and on the login/version-check/wizard-submission sequence the Metasploit module produces within seconds from one source.
detection.adequacy: High fidelity and cheap, because a device address field has no legitimate reason to contain a semicolon or a backtick. Its weakness is retention and location: the evidence is in the Nagios XI server's own web logs, on the host the attacker now controls, so it has to be shipped off the box to survive the incident it documents.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating the monitoring server as executed-on: rebuild rather than upgrade in place, audit check definitions, command definitions and event handlers for entries that execute attacker content on schedule, and rotate every credential the server held for monitored devices — SNMP communities, SSH keys, WMI and API credentials — because those are what the compromise actually reaches.
response.adequacy: Correct in shape and larger in scope than a single-host incident, since the credential rotation runs across the monitored estate. The scheduled-execution audit is the step most often skipped, and it is the one that decides whether the attacker survives the rebuild.

NIST-800-53-AC-6.gap: Read-only Nagios XI accounts satisfy least privilege on paper, and PR:L means any of them reaches command execution through the configuration wizard. AC-6 assesses the role assignment and cannot establish whether the application enforces it — which here is the difference between a read-only user and a shell on the monitoring server.

NIS2-Art21-vulnerability-management.gap: The control's input is missing. No Nagios advisory reviewed names the fixed build, the GitHub advisory records affected and patched versions as unknown, and the 5.5.6-5.7.5 range in circulation comes from Fastly's research and the Metasploit module. A process that closes findings against a vendor-stated fixed version has nothing to close this against.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: B4 examines the platform build, and the exposure that matters here is inbound reachability of the web interface plus how many accounts can authenticate to it. On an internet-reachable Nagios XI a read-only monitoring login is an unauthenticated-equivalent path the moment the credential leaks, and the assessment does not ask that question.

AU-ISM-1546.gap: The control measures an Essential Eight Maturity Model window anchored on the vendor advisory date, and there is no clearly published vendor release to anchor to. The Metasploit module carries a 2021-02-13 disclosure date and CISA listed the CVE on 2022-01-18, but no reviewed Nagios advisory names the fixed build — so neither the assessor nor the operator can state when the clock started.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: A.8.8 remediates by CVE, and CVE-2021-25296, CVE-2021-25297 and CVE-2021-25298 are one injection defect in three sibling wizards that a single public module exploits interchangeably. Closing this entry and reporting the vulnerability handled leaves the instance exploitable through the windowswmi or cloud-vm wizard with the same credential and the same tool.

new_control_requirements.name: AI-FRAMEWORK-CLI-SHELL-INPUT-NEUTRALIZATION
new_control_requirements.description: AI-framework CLIs and tools that invoke external commands must never build a shell string from user-supplied arguments or config: use argv-array execution (no shell), or neutralize the argument.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Attached as the closest existing control on the defect itself, applied outside its AI-framework framing to a monitoring product built on the same construction. Nagios XI's switch wizard interpolates the ip_address value into a shell command in /usr/local/nagiosxi/html/includes/configwizards/switch/switch.inc.php, and Fastly established that the identical pattern exists in the windowswmi and cloud-vm wizards as CVE-2021-25296 and CVE-2021-25298. That is what makes the class-level requirement the right one: a fix expressed as 'sanitise ip_address in the switch wizard' leaves two live injection points that the same public Metasploit module already exploits, whereas requiring argv-array invocation across every wizard that shells out closes all three and any wizard added later.

new_control_requirements.name: FLEET-CONTROL-PLANE-ADMIN-PRIVILEGE-TIER
new_control_requirements.description: Administrators of fleet-control-plane systems (MDM/UEM, EDR consoles, identity providers, container orchestrators, configuration management) must be classified as a distinct privileged tier.
new_control_requirements.evidence: The control names fleet control planes and a monitoring server is one: Nagios XI holds the SNMP communities, SSH keys and API credentials for every device it polls, and its command and event-handler definitions execute on a schedule with the server's privileges. This CVE collapses the tier boundary the control asks for, because PR:L means the account that reaches command execution need not be an administrator at all — a read-only monitoring login is enough. The requirement this adds is that every account able to authenticate to the monitoring web interface is treated as a control-plane credential regardless of the role recorded in the application, with the scoping, rotation and network restriction that implies.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CISA listed this on 2022-01-18 with a 2022-02-01 due date, eleven months after the Metasploit module's 2021-02-13 disclosure date. The 'documented compensating controls' branch carries the weight here more than usual, because the fixed build cannot be established from a Nagios source — the GitHub advisory records affected and patched versions as unknown. What can be verified and written down is that the web interface is unreachable from untrusted networks and that the account inventory has been reduced, which is a defensible mitigation state even when 'upgraded to version X' cannot be evidenced.

CVE-2021-25298.name: Nagios XI Cloud-VM Config Wizard OS Command Injection

attack_vector.description: An authenticated Nagios XI user submits shell metacharacters to the cloud-vm configuration wizard, whose PHP at /usr/local/nagiosxi/html/includes/configwizards/cloud-vm/cloud-vm.inc.php interpolates the input into an OS command without sanitising it. The injected command runs as apache on the monitoring server, which holds credentials for and network reach into every host it monitors. Two sibling wizards in the same releases carry the identical defect.
attack_vector.privileges_required: low - any authenticated Nagios XI account; no administrative role required
attack_vector.complexity: low - a single HTTP request, packaged in a Metasploit module tested against stock vendor OVAs
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Disclosed in early 2021 with a public proof of concept credited to fs0c-sh; no AI tooling is credited in discovery or exploitation.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Upgrade above the 5.5.6 to 5.7.5 affected range, remediating all three sibling CVEs together, and remove shared or automation-held operator accounts so the authenticated session the exploit needs is harder to obtain.
prevention.adequacy: Sufficient against the flaw, with a caveat that has to be stated: no vendor advisory naming the fixed build was retrievable, so the target version has to be confirmed against Nagios's own security disclosures rather than inferred from an exploit module's stated range.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alert on the apache user spawning a shell on the Nagios XI server, and on shell metacharacters in configuration-wizard input - with the alerts sent somewhere other than the Nagios instance itself.
detection.adequacy: Effective, provided the destination is external. Detection routed through the monitoring platform is detection an attacker with apache on that platform can suppress, which is the specific failure mode of this CVE.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treat it as compromise of the monitoring control plane: rotate every credential Nagios XI stores for monitored hosts, review check and notification configuration for suppression, and scope the monitored estate rather than the single server.
response.adequacy: Proportionate to the platform's reach. Weak where the platform's own audit history is the only evidence available, since that history is writable by the account the exploit lands in.

NIST-800-53-AC-6.gap: Least privilege is applied to the user, and the flaw defeats it below that level. Any authenticated Nagios XI account - not an administrator - reaches the cloud-vm wizard, and the wizard shells out as apache, so the privilege the attacker ends with is the web server's, not the account's. An AC-6 review that confirms operator accounts hold no administrative role in Nagios XI passes on the exact configuration this CVE exploits.

NIS2-Art21-vulnerability-management.gap: Vulnerability management needs a fixed version to reconcile against, and the record for this CVE does not supply one: NVD names only xi-5.7.5 and carries no reference at all, GitHub Security Advisory GHSA-6gq5-wx57-577c mirrors that text without adding a version range, and the 5.5.6 to 5.7.5 range comes from Rapid7's exploit module rather than from Nagios. CISA listed it on 2022-01-18 with a 2022-02-01 due date, so the process has a fortnight to reconcile against a boundary inferred from an exploit's stated range rather than read from a vendor advisory.

UK-CAF-B2.gap: Identity and access control treats an authenticated session as the outcome it exists to protect. Here the authenticated session is the precondition, not the prize - the attacker needs any account, and the escalation happens inside the application afterwards. Multi-factor authentication and account review both raise the cost of getting the session and change nothing about what the session then reaches.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: The Essential Eight patch-applications timeframes measure currency against vendor releases, which requires knowing which release is current and which is fixed. Nagios XI's affected range here is carried by a GitHub advisory rather than a vendor bulletin, so an estate can be current on the version it knows about while sitting inside 5.5.6 to 5.7.5. The maturity model measures the process, not whether the process had a fixed version to aim at.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.16.gap: Monitoring activities is the control most directly undermined, because the compromised system is the monitoring system. Command execution as apache on the Nagios XI server puts the attacker inside the thing that would otherwise report the intrusion, able to suppress checks, edit thresholds and read the credentials the platform holds for every monitored host. An A.8.16 assessment that verifies monitoring coverage exists has no way to express that the coverage and the compromised asset are the same system.

new_control_requirements.name: FLEET-CONTROL-PLANE-ADMIN-PRIVILEGE-TIER
new_control_requirements.description: Administrators of fleet-control-plane systems (MDM/UEM, EDR consoles, identity providers, container orchestrators, configuration management) must be classified as a distinct privilege tier.
new_control_requirements.evidence: This is the closest existing control - it enumerates configuration-management and orchestrator control planes rather than monitoring platforms, and Nagios XI belongs in the same tier for the same reason: the server holds check credentials and network reach into everything it monitors. This CVE shows why the tier has to cover ordinary users and not just administrators: the wizard is reachable by any authenticated account and executes as apache, so the privilege boundary that matters is 'can log in to Nagios XI at all', not 'holds an admin role'.

new_control_requirements.name: FLEET-COMPROMISE-IR-PLAYBOOK
new_control_requirements.description: Pre-rehearsed IR playbook for fleet-control-plane compromise including: MDM-pushed certificate revocation, device-trust-state invalidation, configuration-profile audit since the suspected compromise date.
new_control_requirements.evidence: The monitoring-platform instance of this playbook has its own steps: rotate the credentials Nagios XI stores for monitored hosts, audit check and notification configuration for suppression since the suspected compromise date, and re-establish an alerting path that does not traverse the compromised instance. Rehearsal is what supplies that last step - an organisation discovering apache-level execution on its Nagios server needs somewhere else to send the alerts before it starts investigating, and the platform it would normally use is the one under investigation.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: 4h KEV-listing mitigation SLA applies.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CISA listed this on 2022-01-18 with a 2022-02-01 due date, against a flaw whose public proof of concept dated from early 2021 and which now ships in Metasploit alongside its two sibling CVEs. EPSS on 2026-08-28 was 0.74979 at the 99.481st percentile. The action an hours-scale SLA can deliver before the upgrade is account-side: disable shared and automation-held Nagios XI logins, because the exploit's only real precondition is an authenticated session.

CVE-2021-40870.name: Aviatrix Controller Unauthenticated File Upload Path Traversal Code Execution

attack_vector.description: An unauthenticated caller posts to /v1/backend1 with account_name set to a traversal path under the web root and data set to PHP source. The endpoint does not enforce authentication and does not neutralise the traversal, so the file is written to /var/www/php and then executed by requesting /v1/<name>.php. Two requests, no credentials, and the result is code execution on the control plane that manages the organisation's cloud networking.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none (the endpoint accepts an unchecked CID parameter that resembles a session credential)
attack_vector.complexity: low - deterministic, two requests, public exploit code in four repositories and a Nuclei template that also ships the Shodan query for finding targets
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered. TradeCraft's advisory TC-2021-0002 credits Mark Steward; the finding is manual API review of endpoints behind an authenticated interface.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Upgrade to the fixed build for the deployed line - 6.2-1804.2043, 6.3-1804.2490, 6.4-1804.2838 or 6.5-1804.1922 - and restrict reachability of the Controller web interface to a management network in the meantime.
prevention.adequacy: The upgrade is complete but restarts the network control plane, and CISA allowed fourteen days. The network restriction is what covers the interval, and it is genuinely effective because both halves of the exploit are HTTP requests to the controller - but it does nothing about a caller already inside the network.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alert on POSTs to /v1/backend1 carrying traversal sequences in account_name, and on any GET for a .php path under /v1/ that is not part of the shipped product. Inventory /var/www/php for files the product did not ship.
detection.adequacy: Precise and cheap, because the exploit's request pair is highly specific. It requires the controller's web access logs to be shipped somewhere the controller does not control, which for an appliance that has just executed attacker code is the difference between having evidence and having a log the attacker could edit.

response.what_would_have_worked: Rebuild the controller rather than upgrade it in place where it was internet-reachable while unpatched, and rotate the cloud credentials, API keys, gateway secrets and administrative accounts it holds.
response.adequacy: The rotation half is the part that determines whether the incident ends. Code execution on a cloud network controller reaches the credentials it uses to manage cloud accounts, so an upgrade that leaves those credentials in place closes the entry point and leaves the access the attacker took through it.

NIST-800-53-AC-3.gap: Access enforcement is present, visible and mediates the user interface - which is why an assessment passes. The TradeCraft advisory states the actual position: many API calls do not enforce a check for authentication, and /v1/backend1 is one of them. The request even carries a CID parameter that looks like a session credential and is simply not validated, so an assessor reviewing traffic sees an authenticated-looking API call. AC-3 evaluated by confirming that access enforcement exists on the product returns pass for a controller that will write a PHP file into its own web root for an anonymous caller.

NIS2-Art21-vulnerability-management.gap: Vulnerability management here has to reconcile against a per-line fixed build, and the CVE text does not present one: 'Aviatrix Controller 6.x before 6.5-1804.1922' reads as a single upgrade target while the vendor shipped four. A management process that records a 6.3 controller as needing 6.5-1804.1922 will either raise a migration ticket nobody can execute in the fourteen days to the 2022-02-01 KEV due date, or - more often - mark the item not-applicable because the deployed line is not 6.5. Both outcomes leave an affected controller running, and both look correct in the register.

UK-CAF-B2.gap: Identity and access control assumes that reaching a privileged function requires an identity. On this endpoint it requires nothing: the caller presents CID=x, the value is not checked, and the file lands. Multi-factor authentication, role separation and privileged-access management on the Controller's user interface are all intact and all irrelevant, because the exploit never touches the interface those controls sit in front of. The B2 outcome has no way to represent an API surface that is behind the login screen in the product's design and in front of it in fact.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Essential Eight patching for internet-facing services is the tightest timeframe in the model, and this deployment stresses it in a way the model does not capture. CISA allowed fourteen days, from 2022-01-18 to 2022-02-01; the upgrade restarts the network control plane, so the constraint is a change window on the system that manages cloud connectivity rather than the availability of the fix. The maturity level also scores the same for a controller upgraded to a fixed build and one upgraded within its line but short of the fixed build, because the model measures currency rather than the specific per-line boundary that decides exposure here.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.8.gap: Technical vulnerability management needs both the advisory and the asset to be in the right place. The authoritative technical description of this flaw is a third-party advisory, TC-2021-0002; the vendor's own record is a dated security note inside product release notes rather than a security bulletin published to a feed. Meanwhile the asset is frequently registered as cloud networking infrastructure rather than as an internet-facing web application, so an A.8.8 process can be operating exactly as designed and still never route this CVE to anyone who owns the controller.

new_control_requirements.name: FLEET-CONTROL-PLANE-ADMIN-PRIVILEGE-TIER
new_control_requirements.description: Administrators of fleet-control-plane systems (MDM/UEM, EDR consoles, identity providers, container orchestrators, configuration management) must be classified as a distinct privileged tier, and the control planes themselves must be inventoried and protected as that tier rather than as ordinary infrastructure.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Aviatrix Controller is a cloud networking control plane, so unauthenticated code execution on it is not an appliance compromise - it reaches the cloud credentials, API keys and gateway secrets the controller uses to manage the estate's connectivity. The tiering matters for this CVE in a specific way: the flaw is exploitable by anyone who can reach /v1/backend1, and the Nuclei template ships a Shodan fingerprint for locating such controllers, so a control plane classified as ordinary infrastructure ends up with ingress rules nobody would have written for a tier-0 system. The control's inventory half is what makes the fourteen-day window to 2022-02-01 workable at all, because it answers which controllers exist and who owns their change window before the clock starts.

new_control_requirements.name: PERIMETER-COMPROMISE-REBUILD-NOT-PATCH
new_control_requirements.description: Pre-rehearsed IR runbook for any perimeter or internet-facing device that suffers a pre-auth RCE CVE in active exploitation MUST default to config-exfil review plus rebuild plus credential rotation, not patch-in-place.
new_control_requirements.evidence: The exploitation writes a PHP file into the controller's own web root and executes it, so the first thing an operator has to establish is whether one is there - the artefact is an unexpected .php under /var/www/php and a /v1/backend1 POST paired with a /v1/<name>.php GET in the access log. The credential half is what makes rebuild the default rather than an escalation: this appliance holds the cloud provider credentials that manage the network estate, and an upgrade to the fixed build closes the write primitive while leaving every one of those secrets exactly where the attacker found them.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: 4h KEV-listing mitigation SLA applies.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CISA listed this id on 2022-01-18 with a 2022-02-01 due date - fourteen days for an unauthenticated remote code execution on a cloud network control plane whose upgrade requires a change window on the system that carries the estate's connectivity. The action the SLA can actually deliver inside hours is the reachability restriction rather than the upgrade: /v1/backend1 is only exploitable by a caller who can reach the Controller's web interface, so the first hour's work is establishing which controllers are externally reachable - the template's Shodan fingerprint answers that from the outside - and closing that ingress while the four per-line upgrade targets are scheduled.

CVE-2021-33766.name: Exchange Server ProxyToken ECP Authentication Bypass (CVE-2021-33766)

attack_vector.description: A request to /ecp/ carrying a non-empty SecurityToken cookie and a valid ECP canary token makes the Exchange front end defer authentication to a back-end DelegatedAuthenticationModule that is not enabled by default, so neither side authenticates it. The attacker then drives Exchange Control Panel functions against an arbitrary mailbox - ZDI's demonstration configures a forwarding rule that copies all incoming mail to an attacker-controlled address, converting one unauthenticated request into a standing exfiltration channel.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none for the bypass; an attacker holding Exchange credentials faces fewer restrictions on the ECP functions reachable, and forwarding to an arbitrary internet destination without credentials additionally requires global forwarding to be enabled
attack_vector.complexity: low - one HTTP request with a forged cookie and a canary lifted from an error response, with a public exploit script available
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Reported by Le Xuan Tuyen of VNPT ISC via ZDI in March 2021 from manual analysis; no AI tooling is credited.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Apply KB5001779 to reach 15.0.1497.15, 15.1.2176.12, 15.1.2242.8, 15.2.792.13 or 15.2.858.10 as appropriate, or a later superseding cumulative update.
prevention.adequacy: Necessary and not sufficient. The attack's product is a persistent mailbox rule, and the update does not remove one already planted - patching without auditing forwarding configuration leaves the exfiltration running.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alert on POSTs to /ecp/RulesEditor/InboxRules.svc/NewObject returning HTTP 500 and on any /ecp/ request carrying SecurityToken= returning HTTP 500, per the published Sigma rule; and reconcile every mailbox forwarding change against an authentication event.
detection.adequacy: Works only where per-request webserver logs are collected and retained. Authentication-event logging alone sees nothing, because the request never authenticates - which is the whole defect.

response.what_would_have_worked: Audit mailbox forwarding and inbox rules across the whole estate for the exposure window, remove any not attributable to the mailbox owner, and treat the mail those rules carried as taken.
response.adequacy: This is the decisive step and the one a patch-only response omits. Where per-request /ecp/ logs were not retained, the exposure cannot be bounded from logs and the rule audit is the only evidence available.

NIST-800-53-AC-3.gap: Access enforcement is present on both halves of Exchange and answers on neither. The front end sees a SecurityToken cookie on the /ecp/ request and concludes the back end will enforce; the back end's DelegatedAuthenticationModule is not enabled in a default installation, so nothing enforces. An assessment that confirms an access-enforcement mechanism exists on the Exchange Control Panel path passes on both components while the request passes between them - the control is satisfied by each element in isolation and defeated by the handoff, which AC-3 has no vocabulary to describe.

NIS2-Art21-vulnerability-management.gap: Vulnerability management prioritises with vendor exploitability information and reconciles against publication dates, and this CVE breaks both inputs. Microsoft's record still reads exploited 'No', publicly disclosed 'No' and 'Exploitation Less Likely', unrevised, while CISA listed it as known-exploited on 2022-01-18 with a two-week due date. And the CVE published on 2021-07-13 for a fix that shipped in April 2021, which MSRC states was omitted from the April release notes - so a process that opens a finding on the July date against an April-patched server produces a false positive, and one that assumes July-dated CVEs need July-dated patches produces a false negative.

UK-CAF-B2.gap: B2 covers identity and access control and would be read as satisfied by an Exchange estate with strong authentication on OWA and ECP. This request presents no credential at all: it carries a SecurityToken cookie whose only required property is being non-empty, plus an ECP canary the attacker takes from an error response. Multi-factor authentication on the Exchange login surface sits in front of a path this request never traverses, and the outcome - a forwarding rule on a mailbox the attacker never authenticated to - is a legitimate ECP function invoked without an identity.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: The Essential Eight patch-applications timeframes are measured from patch availability, and the patch has been available since April 2021 - so an estate that met the measure was never exposed after that point. What the measure cannot express is the consequence that outlives the patch: the exploit's purpose is to configure a mailbox forwarding rule, and installing KB5001779 does not remove a rule already created. A server compliant with the measure can still be copying a director's mail to an attacker, and nothing in a patch metric surfaces that.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.15.gap: Logging is the control that would have caught this and the default Exchange logging posture does not. The exploitation is a single POST to /ecp/RulesEditor/InboxRules.svc/NewObject, or a request to an /ecp/ path carrying SecurityToken=, and it never authenticates - so an authentication-event log records nothing at all. The Sigma rule published for this CVE (id 56973b50-3382-4b56-bdf5-f51a3183797a) matches on webserver request logs with HTTP 500 responses, which is a source A.8.15 does not require to be collected, forwarded or retained.

new_control_requirements.name: OWA-PER-REQUEST-SIEM-INGESTION
new_control_requirements.description: Exchange OWA and ECP per-request access logs (not just authentication events) must be forwarded to an external SIEM with at least 90-day retention; authentication-only logging misses request-level abuse that never authenticates.
new_control_requirements.evidence: The published Sigma rule for this CVE (id 56973b50-3382-4b56-bdf5-f51a3183797a) is a webserver-log rule: it matches POST /ecp/RulesEditor/InboxRules.svc/NewObject with HTTP 500, and any /ecp/ request containing SecurityToken= with HTTP 500. Neither pattern appears in an authentication log, because the ProxyToken request is authenticated by neither the front end nor the back end. For this CVE the control means the IIS request logs for the /ecp/ virtual directory must already be forwarded and retained: a mailbox found forwarding to an external address is otherwise undatable, and the exposure window cannot be bounded.

new_control_requirements.name: MITIGATION-ACTIVE-PATCH-PENDING-VERDICT-CLASS
new_control_requirements.description: Compliance verdicts must distinguish binary-patch-deployed from vendor-mitigation-active-without-patch from no-mitigation-at-all, and must surface the middle state as a time-bound compensating control rather than as a patched-per-SLA outcome.
new_control_requirements.evidence: This CVE needs a fourth state the usual three do not cover: patched-but-still-exfiltrating. KB5001779 closes the bypass; it does not remove a mailbox forwarding rule the bypass created, and the rule is the attack's entire product. The verdict must also survive a date trap - MSRC's revision note states the fix shipped in the April 2021 updates and the CVE was inadvertently omitted from the April release notes, publishing only on 2021-07-13, so a server on 15.1.2242.8 patched in April is remediated despite predating the CVE. The distinguishing test is two-part: build number at or above the fixed build, AND a completed forwarding-rule audit for the exposure window.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: 4h KEV-listing mitigation SLA applies.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CISA added CVE-2021-33766 on 2022-01-18 with a 2022-02-01 due date, while Microsoft's record still reads exploited 'No' and 'Exploitation Less Likely' and has not been revised - so a programme keyed to vendor severity would take no action at all. EPSS on 2026-08-28 stands at 0.98136, the 99.910th percentile, against a public exploit script. Inside the SLA window the two deliverable actions are confirming every Exchange server sits at or above its fixed build (15.0.1497.15, 15.1.2176.12, 15.1.2242.8, 15.2.792.13, 15.2.858.10) and disabling global forwarding to arbitrary internet destinations, which ZDI names as the condition that lets an unauthenticated attacker route mail out of the organisation.

CVE-2021-21975.name: VMware vRealize Operations Manager Pre-Auth SSRF Credential Theft (CVE-2021-21975)

attack_vector.description: An unauthenticated POST to /casa/nodes/thumbprints supplies a JSON array of node addresses. The vROps appliance issues a GET to each one with the maintenanceAdmin HTTP Basic credentials attached, and URI fragment syntax steers the request to an attacker-controlled listener, which receives the Authorization header. Those credentials open CVE-2021-21983, an authenticated arbitrary file write at /casa/private/config/slice/ha/certificate, and the chain reaches remote code execution as the admin Unix user on a management appliance holding monitoring credentials for the virtual estate.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none - unauthenticated network access to the vROps API, plus a listener the appliance can reach
attack_vector.complexity: low - a single POST; Metasploit has shipped the full chain since the advisory date of 2021-03-30
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered and not AI-weaponised; reported through coordinated disclosure by a human researcher.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Update to 8.4.0 or later, or apply the per-version patches under KB85382 / KB85381 / KB85380 / KB85379 / KB85378. Where the update cannot be scheduled, remove <sec:http pattern="/nodes/thumbprints" security='none'/> from casa-security-context.xml and restart CaSA on every node of the cluster.
prevention.adequacy: Sufficient for 8.0.x through 8.3.0. Not available at all for 7.0.0 and 6.7.0, which VMware marks 'No patch planned' - for those the workaround is the permanent state and the honest disposition is decommissioning.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alert on POST requests to /casa/nodes/thumbprints in /usr/lib/vmware-casa/casa-webapp/logs/casa.log, on vROps-originated outbound connections to addresses that are not monitored nodes, and on any use of the maintenanceAdmin credential from a source other than the appliance.
detection.adequacy: The log evidence exists and Rapid7 names the file, but it is on the appliance - an operator who does not forward casa.log off the appliance has the evidence only until the appliance is rebuilt, and rebuilding is the likely response to a suspected compromise.

response.what_would_have_worked: Rotate the maintenanceAdmin credential and every monitoring credential the appliance holds for the estate it watches, then check for JSP files under the CaSA web application directories and for the certificate-upload requests that mark the file-write half of the chain.
response.adequacy: Credential rotation is the load-bearing step and patching does not perform it: the fix stops the appliance attaching credentials to SSRF-triggered requests, and does nothing about a credential that already left. The onward exposure is whatever vROps was configured to reach.

NIST-800-53-SC-7.gap: Boundary protection assumes the traffic crossing the boundary originates from the attacker. Here it originates from the vROps appliance: the attacker's POST to /casa/nodes/thumbprints causes the appliance to make the outbound request, and it is the appliance's own credentials that leave. Inbound filtering is satisfied - the POST is a legitimate API call to a legitimate endpoint - and outbound filtering on a management appliance that is expected to reach arbitrary monitored nodes has no rule that distinguishes the attacker's listener from a node it is meant to poll.

NIS2-Art21-network-security.gap: The network-security obligation is met by segmenting the management network, and this vulnerability is the case where that segmentation is the thing being borrowed rather than the thing protecting. vROps sits inside the management segment by design and holds monitoring credentials for the estate it watches; the SSRF turns it into a request origin inside that segment. VMware's own workaround is not a network control at all - it is removing one line from casa-security-context.xml on every cluster node - which is the tell that the obligation's instrument does not reach the defect.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: The system-security outcome depends on knowing which systems are in scope, and the affected component ships under three product names: vRealize Operations Manager, VMware Cloud Foundation 3.x and 4.x, and vRealize Suite Lifecycle Manager 8.x. An estate that inventories by product name and finds no vROps still runs the CaSA API inside Cloud Foundation. The version boundary compounds it - 'prior to 8.4' means 8.3.0 is affected and 8.4.0 is not, and the widely-copied third-party phrasing '8.4 and earlier' inverts it.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Essential Eight patch timeframes assume a patch exists to apply within them. VMware states 'No patch planned' for vRealize Operations Manager 7.0.0 and 6.7.0, both of which VMSA-2021-0004 lists as affected, so for those versions the timeframe is unsatisfiable and the maturity model offers no alternative disposition. CISA allowed fourteen days from 2022-01-18 to 2022-02-01; for a 6.7.0 or 7.0.0 appliance that window can only be met by the configuration workaround or by removing the appliance.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.22.gap: Segregation of networks is the control an operator would reach for on a management appliance, and this flaw is served by the segregation rather than stopped by it. The appliance is placed inside the management network precisely so it can reach what it monitors, and the SSRF makes it issue requests from that position with the maintenanceAdmin credential attached. No segregation rule an organisation writes changes an endpoint that is exempted from authentication by a line in casa-security-context.xml, and VMware's own remediation removes that line rather than adjusting any network boundary.

new_control_requirements.name: CONFIGURATION-SIDE-LIVE-PATCH-INVENTORY
new_control_requirements.description: For any web-fabric vulnerability with a configuration-side mitigation path: that path must be inventoried, tested, and deployable independent of the vendor-patch path.
new_control_requirements.evidence: VMware published exactly such a path for this CVE, one KB per affected release - KB83210 (8.3.0), KB83095 (8.2.0), KB83094 (8.1.1 and 8.1.0), KB83093 (8.0.1 and 8.0.0), KB82367 (7.5.0) and KB83287 (7.0.0 and 6.7.0) - and it is a one-line edit: remove <sec:http pattern="/nodes/thumbprints" security='none'/> from /usr/lib/vmware-casa/casa-webapp/webapps/casa/WEB-INF/classes/spring/casa-security-context.xml and restart CaSA. For this product the control means knowing, before a disclosure, that the file is per-node and that the edit plus restart has to be repeated on every cluster member, because a cluster mitigated only on the primary is still reachable through its replicas. Precondition to record with it: the workaround closes the endpoint but does not fix the credential-attachment behaviour, which is what the vendor patch changes by switching to a non-authorised REST template.

new_control_requirements.name: EOL-ASSET-DECOMMISSION
new_control_requirements.description: Network-reachable end-of-life devices with no vendor patch path must be isolated and decommissioned within a bounded window; mandatory compensating segmentation applies until removal.
new_control_requirements.evidence: VMSA-2021-0004 lists vRealize Operations Manager 7.0.0 and 6.7.0 as affected and marks them 'No patch planned'. That is the exact condition this control governs, applied to an appliance rather than a device: CISA's fourteen-day window from 2022-01-18 to 2022-02-01 is unsatisfiable by patching for those versions, so the bounded window has to end in removal or upgrade, with the casa-security-context.xml workaround VMware published for those two versions as KB83287 serving as the compensating control until it does. Recording those appliances as 'workaround applied' with no end date converts a decommissioning decision into a permanent exception.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: 4h KEV-listing mitigation SLA applies.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CISA added this on 2022-01-18 with a 2022-02-01 due date - fourteen days - for a CVE marked as used in ransomware campaigns, with a Metasploit module carrying the same disclosure date as VMware's advisory. The action that fits inside hours is not the appliance update: it is the one-line casa-security-context.xml edit plus a CaSA restart on every node, followed by rotation of the maintenanceAdmin credential, because the vulnerability's entire output is that credential and no patch un-leaks one already taken.

attack_vector.description: An attacker supplies an array rather than a string to a parameter that reaches si.services(), si.processLoad(), si.inetLatency() or si.inetChecksite() in the systeminformation npm package. The library sanitises strings and not arrays, so the array element - carrying a shell substitution such as $(wget ...) - is concatenated into an OS command and executed as the Node process's user. Where an HTTP route forwards a request parameter into one of those calls, the bracketed name[]= notation produces the array for free.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none where a route exposes the parameter; NVD's PR:L reflects the library's local call surface rather than an embedding application's
attack_vector.complexity: low - a single request with a bracketed parameter, fully automated by a default-set Nuclei template
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered and not AI-weaponised; the advisory was published by the package maintainer and credits no external reporter.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Resolve systeminformation to 5.3.1 or later - including through an override where it is transitive - and restart the process. Where that is not possible, apply the vendor's workaround at every call site: allow only strings, reject arrays.
prevention.adequacy: The upgrade is complete and cheap. The workaround is only available to code the organisation controls, which excludes the common transitive case entirely.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alert on the Node process spawning a shell or network utility, and on request parameters arriving in bracketed array notation on routes that expect a scalar.
detection.adequacy: The process-spawn signal is decisive because a diagnostics library legitimately shells out - so the discriminator has to be the argument content, not the spawn itself. The array-notation signal is cheap to add at the reverse proxy and catches the probe before execution.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treat execution as the service account: rotate its credentials and any secrets in its environment, review outbound connections since the first array-notation request, and re-verify the deployed artefact.
response.adequacy: Effective where request logs retain query strings. Where the proxy logs paths only, the bracketed parameter that identifies the attempt is not recorded, and the exposure cannot be bounded from the logs alone.

NIST-800-218-SSDF-PW.4.gap: PW.4 governs reusing well-secured software: acquire components from trusted sources, track them, and confirm they meet security requirements. systeminformation passes every test PW.4 can pose - it is a widely used, actively maintained package whose maintainer published the advisory himself on 2021-02-14 and shipped the fix in 5.3.1. The practice verifies the provenance and maintenance of the component and has nothing to say about whether the consuming application hands it an array, which is the entire defect condition.

NIS2-Art21-supply-chain.gap: Supply-chain risk management under Art. 21 is oriented to direct suppliers and their security practices. The exposure here is usually not a direct supplier at all: systeminformation is commonly pulled in transitively, so the organisation has no contractual or assessment relationship with it, and the only remediation available - forcing the resolved version to 5.3.1 - is a build-tooling action rather than a supplier-management one. An Art. 21 supplier assessment of the vendors an organisation actually contracts with will not surface this package.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: The system security outcome expects the service to be built and maintained to resist attack. A service can meet it and still be exposed, because whether this flaw is reachable depends on something the outcome does not examine: whether any route passes a request parameter into one of four named library functions. Two services on identical, fully-patched platforms with identical dependency trees can differ entirely on that point, and B4 gives no way to tell them apart.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Patch applications is the right control and its unit of work is wrong for this. The Essential Eight measures whether applications are patched within the maturity-level timeframe, and here the vulnerable artefact is a package nested inside an application's dependency tree - not something an application patching regime enumerates. CISA allowed fourteen days (2022-01-18 to 2022-02-01), and an organisation can meet that window for every application it tracks while never resolving systeminformation to 5.3.1, because nothing in the process asks it to.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.28.gap: Secure coding is the control that owns this defect, and it identifies it correctly - building an OS command from externally-influenced input is the textbook A.8.28 finding. Its limit is jurisdictional: the insecure construction is in the library, not in the organisation's code, so a secure-coding programme reviewing the organisation's own source finds nothing. The vendor's own workaround shows where the control could bite - reject arrays at every call site - but that requires A.8.28 to be applied to how third-party functions are called, not to what the organisation writes.

new_control_requirements.name: MCP-SERVER-ARGV-NOT-SHELLSTRING
new_control_requirements.description: Components spawning subprocesses MUST use argv-array spawn primitives (execFile / spawn with array args / posix_spawn) rather than shell string concatenation of caller-supplied values.
new_control_requirements.evidence: The control is written for MCP servers and is the closest existing entry; the defect class is identical and the fix is the same one. systeminformation constructs a shell command string from parameters passed to si.inetLatency(), si.inetChecksite(), si.services() and si.processLoad(), and an array element bypasses the string sanitiser the vendor relied on - the advisory's workaround, 'do only allow strings, reject any arrays', is a description of a sanitiser standing in for argv-array execution. Under argv-array spawning the array element becomes an inert argument rather than a shell substitution, so the flaw does not exist. The verification test is a code search for shell-string construction in any dependency that shells out, not a version check.

new_control_requirements.name: TIER-3-DEPENDENCY-INVENTORY
new_control_requirements.description: Supply chain inventory must extend to tier-3 dependencies (dependencies of dependencies of direct dependencies); SBOM coverage for transitive dependencies cannot be assumed from direct-dependency tracking.
new_control_requirements.evidence: systeminformation is a diagnostics helper that most estates hold transitively rather than as a declared dependency, which decides the remediation: the vendor workaround requires control of the call sites, and a consumer that only inherits the package has none, leaving a forced resolution to 5.3.1 as the sole lever. The inventory must therefore record the RESOLVED version from the lockfile rather than the declared range, because a range that permits 5.3.1 does not mean 5.3.1 is what shipped. CISA's fourteen-day window from 2022-01-18 to 2022-02-01 is not achievable without that resolution already being queryable.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: 4h KEV-listing mitigation SLA applies.
new_control_requirements.evidence: CISA listed this CVE on 2022-01-18 with a 2022-02-01 due date, and EPSS on 2026-08-28 stood at 0.90675 - the 99.797th percentile, the highest in this chunk - which is consistent with a route-level probe shipping in the default Nuclei template set. The four-hour action is not the dependency bump, which needs a build and deploy: it is blocking bracketed array-notation parameters at the reverse proxy for routes that expect scalars, which stops the documented probe shape while the resolution to 5.3.1 goes through the pipeline.

CVE-2021-22991.name: F5 BIG-IP TMM URI Normalization Buffer Overflow (CVE-2021-22991)

attack_vector.description: An unauthenticated attacker sends a request to a BIG-IP virtual server. TMM's URI normalization mishandles it and overflows a buffer. F5 states the result as a denial of service and describes bypass of URL-based access control and remote code execution as theoretically possible in certain situations. The request shape is undisclosed by the vendor and no public analysis has established it.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none - any client that can reach a virtual server, which is the device's ordinary traffic
attack_vector.complexity: low to reach the stated outcome, unknown for the qualified ones - the vendor asserts only the crash, and no public artefact has demonstrated more in five years
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered and not AI-weaponised, so far as any source shows; there is no public discovery narrative at all, so this is an absence of information rather than a positive finding.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Upgrade each device to its own branch's fixed release - 16.0.1.1, 15.1.2.1, 14.1.4, 13.1.3.6 or 12.1.5.3 - verifying by running version per branch; treat an EoSD branch as unassessed and migrate it rather than upgrading within it.
prevention.adequacy: Sufficient and only available as an outage. There is no configuration mitigation, because the trigger is ordinary traffic to a virtual server and URI normalization is not optional, so an operator who cannot take the outage inside the window has nothing smaller to deploy.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Ship BIG-IP syslog, threat and authentication logs to a SIEM in a different trust zone before they are needed, and alert on TMM restarts and core files correlated with inbound request timestamps - including on clustered HA failovers, which is how a successful trigger presents on a pair.
detection.adequacy: This is a floor, not a ceiling, and unusually so: the crash is the only observable F5 asserts, the request shape is undisclosed so no signature can be written, and a clean bypass need not crash anything. The HA-failover correlation is the part that catches what a standalone-device view would miss.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treat a confirmed trigger on a perimeter device as a device compromise rather than a patch event: export and preserve the configuration, rebuild from a known-good image at a fixed version, and rotate every credential and certificate the device held, including those for backend pool members.
response.adequacy: Proportionate to the vendor's own uncertainty - F5 will not rule out code execution, so patching in place accepts a risk the vendor has not characterised. The limit is evidentiary: with no request signature and device-local logs, establishing whether a trigger occurred at all is usually not possible after the fact.

NIST-800-53-SC-7.gap: Boundary protection is the control, and on this estate the boundary protection device is the vulnerable component. SC-7 requires monitoring and control of communications at external boundaries and at key internal boundaries, implemented through managed interfaces - and here the managed interface is TMM, reached by exactly the traffic it exists to accept. The control offers no treatment of the case where the enforcing device is itself the target: it has no requirement that the boundary device be reachable only through another boundary, no requirement that its failure mode be defined, and no way to express that the same request which the device is meant to inspect is the request that crashes it.

NIS2-Art21-network-security.gap: The Article 21 network-security obligation is satisfied by having and operating network security measures, and this estate has one - the BIG-IP. What the control does not require is a second, independent judgement about the security of the security device, and that gap is sharpened here by the vendor's own uncertainty: F5 states the denial of service as the outcome and puts access-control bypass and code execution in the theoretical column. An organisation applying Article 21 has no basis on which to decide whether its network-security measure failed open, failed closed, or failed at all, because the vendor has not said.

UK-CAF-C1.gap: The security-monitoring outcome expects an organisation to monitor for and detect malicious activity, and this CVE removes the material to do it with. F5 describes the trigger only as 'undisclosed requests', so no request signature exists to write a rule against, and no public artefact has appeared in five years to derive one from. The single reliable observable is a TMM crash - which is generated on, and logged by, the device that is failing, and which on an HA pair is masked by a successful failover. A CAF assessment that confirms monitoring coverage of the perimeter passes on an estate that cannot detect this at all.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Essential Eight patch timeframes for internet-facing services run from vendor release, and F5's release was 2021-03; CISA's two-week window followed ten months later. Neither accommodates the operational shape of this fix: the upgrade restarts the data plane, so on an HA pair the timeframe is consumed by change scheduling rather than by work, and there is no interim configuration mitigation to fall back on because URI normalization cannot be disabled. The model also has no state for an EoSD branch, which F5 explicitly did not evaluate - a device there has no fixed version to patch toward and therefore no timeframe that can be met or missed.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.16.gap: Monitoring activities requires networks, systems and applications to be monitored for anomalous behaviour with appropriate action taken. Two things defeat that here and neither is a coverage failure. The event to monitor for is undefined, because F5 published no request shape and no public analysis has supplied one; and the log source for the only defined event - a TMM crash - is the device that crashes, whose logs are typically retained on the device and reviewed after an incident rather than streamed off it. A.8.16 has no requirement that a perimeter device's telemetry leave its own trust zone before it is needed, which is precisely when it becomes unavailable.

new_control_requirements.name: PERIMETER-DEVICE-ZERODAY-SLA-TIER
new_control_requirements.description: Perimeter devices such as VPN concentrators, gateways and load balancers require a separate compressed-SLA remediation tier, distinct from the general patch schedule.
new_control_requirements.evidence: The remediation here is a data-plane restart on the device every external connection traverses, so it competes for the same change windows as the business traffic it carries - and CISA allowed two weeks (added 2022-01-18, due 2022-02-01) with no configuration mitigation available, because URI normalization cannot be switched off. A general patch schedule will always lose that argument to availability; a compressed tier that pre-authorises the failover-and-upgrade sequence for perimeter devices is what makes the window reachable at all.

new_control_requirements.name: FIREWALL-EGRESS-TELEMETRY-SEPARATE-TRUST-ZONE
new_control_requirements.description: Firewall and other perimeter-trust-boundary devices must forward syslog, threat logs and authentication logs to a SIEM hosted in a separate trust zone with a different management plane.
new_control_requirements.evidence: The only observable F5 asserts for this defect is a TMM crash, and TMM is the process that writes the log. Device-local retention therefore puts the evidence for the event on the component that failed, and on an HA pair a successful trigger presents as a failover that looks routine from inside the cluster. Forwarding the logs off-device before they are needed is the only way the crash-plus-request correlation survives the event, and it is the sole detection available given that the request shape is undisclosed.

new_control_requirements.name: PERIMETER-COMPROMISE-REBUILD-NOT-PATCH
new_control_requirements.description: The pre-rehearsed IR runbook for a perimeter device that suffers a pre-authentication vulnerability in active exploitation must default to configuration exfiltration, rebuild and credential rotation, not patch-in-place.
new_control_requirements.evidence: F5 will not rule out remote code execution on this defect - the wording is that it 'may theoretically allow' it - while CISA asserts active exploitation by listing it. Patching in place under those two statements accepts a risk neither party has characterised, on the device that terminates every external connection and holds the certificates and pool-member credentials for everything behind it. A runbook that defaults to rebuild removes the need to resolve the vendor's ambiguity before acting, which is fortunate, because with no request signature and device-local logs it usually cannot be resolved.

CVE-2020-14864.name: Oracle Business Intelligence Enterprise Edition Path Traversal (CVE-2020-14864)

attack_vector.description: An unauthenticated attacker issues a single HTTP GET to /analytics/saw.dll?getPreviewImage&previewFilePath=<path> against an Oracle Business Intelligence Enterprise Edition server. The function reads the named file with no containment check and returns its contents. The public Nuclei template demonstrates it with /etc/passwd and matches root:.*:0:0: in the response body.
attack_vector.privileges_required: none - PR:N, and the public check performs no authentication step
attack_vector.complexity: low - Oracle's own text is 'easily exploitable'; the whole exploit is one GET, and a Nuclei template reduces it to a single line in a mass scan
attack_vector.ai_factor: Not AI-discovered and not AI-weaponised. Both public artefacts are authored by a named human researcher, Ivo Palazzolo.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Apply Oracle's October 2020 Critical Patch Update to the installed version, and in the meantime reject requests to /analytics/saw.dll carrying getPreviewImage at the proxy while removing untrusted-network reachability to the BI server.
prevention.adequacy: The patch is sufficient and needs a service outage; the filter and the reachability change are sufficient against this path and need neither. The reachability change is the strongest of the three in practice, because a reporting server that untrusted networks cannot reach is out of scope for the whole class rather than for this CVE.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Alert on any request to /analytics/saw.dll carrying getPreviewImage with a previewFilePath outside the expected image directory, and on 200 responses to those requests whose bodies are not image data.
detection.adequacy: Unusually reliable, because the exploit request and the detection signature are the same string and both are public. The response-content check is the half that distinguishes a scan from a successful read, and it is the one usually omitted - logging the request alone records that someone tried, not whether they got a file.

response.what_would_have_worked: Determine which files were returned from the access log, then rotate every credential reachable from those files - the data-source connection details the BI server holds are the point of a read primitive on this host, not the files themselves.
response.adequacy: Bounded only if the credential-rotation step runs. Treating this as an information-disclosure incident and stopping at 'files were read' misses that the read is a staging step: the impact lands on the data sources whose credentials the BI server stores, which are systems the incident scope would not otherwise include.

NIST-800-53-SI-10.gap: Information input validation is the control the defect is a direct violation of, and the gap is in where it is verified rather than in what it requires. SI-10 asks that information inputs be checked for validity, and an assessment of this application would find input validation implemented across its authenticated user-facing surface while the previewFilePath parameter of getPreviewImage - a path-bearing input on a servlet endpoint - takes an absolute path and returns the file. The control is satisfied at the layer the assessor can see and violated at the layer that matters, and nothing in SI-10 requires that path-bearing parameters specifically be canonicalised and containment-checked rather than merely 'validated'.

NIS2-Art21-vulnerability-management.gap: The Article 21 vulnerability-handling obligation is measured against identifying and remediating known vulnerabilities, and the identification half has a specific defect here that the obligation does not address: Oracle's Critical Patch Update publishes this under the component 'Installation', which is also how NVD records it, while the exposed surface is the Analytics servlet. An organisation triaging a quarterly Oracle CPU by component - the normal way a hundred-plus-CVE bundle is made tractable - routes this to whoever owns installation and provisioning rather than to whoever owns the internet-facing reporting endpoint. The obligation asks that vulnerabilities be handled; it does not require the vendor's own classification to be validated against the reachable surface.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: The system-security outcome expects vulnerable software to be identified and updated. Identification fails on the shape of the fix: the remediation is a Critical Patch Update bundle applied to an installation that keeps its existing version string, so a patched 12.2.1.4.0 and an unpatched 12.2.1.4.0 report the same version. A CAF assessment that confirms an update process exists and that the estate runs a supported OBIEE version has confirmed nothing about this CVE, and the only reliable evidence - issuing the getPreviewImage request and observing whether file content comes back - is a test the outcome does not ask for.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Essential Eight patch timeframes for internet-facing software are the tightest tier in the model and would have applied here correctly, since Oracle published the fix in its October 2020 Critical Patch Update. The gap is that the Essential Eight measures patch currency and has no control for the compensating action that is available immediately and needs no outage - filtering the single known path and parameter at the proxy, or removing untrusted reachability to a reporting server that has no business being internet-facing. An organisation inside its patch window and an organisation that filtered the endpoint on day one score identically under the model, and only one of them was defended during the interval.

ISO-27001-2022-A.8.28.gap: Secure coding is the control that would have prevented this, and the specific requirement it is missing is directional path handling. A.8.28 asks that secure coding principles be applied to software development; it does not name canonicalisation-then-containment for file-path parameters as a required practice, which is the single check whose absence is this CVE. The consequence is visible in the fix's own shape: Oracle corrected one function, getPreviewImage, in one Critical Patch Update, rather than the class - and an A.8.28 assessment of the same codebase after the patch would find the control just as satisfied as it did before, because nothing in it distinguishes a path parameter from any other input.

new_control_requirements.name: AI-WEBUI-FILE-ROUTE-CONTAINMENT
new_control_requirements.description: A file-serving route must enforce strict directory containment: canonicalise the caller-supplied path and verify that the resolved path stays under the allowed root before any read, rather than validating the raw parameter or relying on a perimeter filter.
new_control_requirements.evidence: This control is written in the catalogue around ML demo and UI frameworks and is attached here as the closest existing directory-containment control, because the requirement it states is precisely the check getPreviewImage does not perform: the previewFilePath parameter accepts an absolute path and the function returns the file, which the public Nuclei template demonstrates with /etc/passwd and a root:.*:0:0: match. The distinction the control draws between canonicalising-then-containing and merely validating is the one that matters here, since a proxy filter on the literal path and parameter is evadable by encoding while a resolved-path containment check is not.

new_control_requirements.name: CONFIGURATION-SIDE-LIVE-PATCH-INVENTORY
new_control_requirements.description: For any vulnerability with a configuration-side mitigation path, that path must be inventoried, tested and deployable independently of the vendor-patch path, so that operators are not dependent on a patch cycle to remove reachability.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Two configuration-side paths exist here and both beat the patch on time-to-deploy, because the patch stops the BI services and they do not: rejecting requests to /analytics/saw.dll carrying getPreviewImage at the reverse proxy, and removing untrusted-network reachability to a reporting server whose only stated exploitation precondition is network access via HTTP. Both need testing before they are relied on - the filter because it is a literal path-and-parameter match, the reachability change because a reporting application usually has legitimate external consumers someone has forgotten to enumerate.

new_control_requirements.name: MITIGATION-ACTIVE-PATCH-PENDING-VERDICT-CLASS
new_control_requirements.description: Compliance verdicts must distinguish binary-patch-deployed from vendor-mitigation-active-without-patch from no-mitigation-at-all, and must surface the middle state as a time-bound compensating control rather than as a patched-per-SLA outcome.
new_control_requirements.evidence: The middle state is unavoidable on this CVE and a two-state record cannot hold it. The October 2020 Critical Patch Update does not change the installation's version string, so 'patched' cannot be read from an inventory at all, and the interim posture - proxy filter active, external reachability removed, patch scheduled for the next reporting outage - is a genuine and defensible state that a patched/unpatched field records as unpatched or, worse, as patched. This CVE also supplies the direct test that makes the verdict provable: issue the Nuclei template's own request and observe whether file content is returned.

CVE-2020-13671.name: Drupal core Un-restricted Upload of File (CVE-2020-13671)

attack_vector.description: Drupal's defence against a dangerous upload extension is to insert an underscore into the filename. Certain filenames do not get sanitized, so a double-extension name such as filename.php.txt is stored intact and is then served with the wrong MIME type — or executed as PHP where the web server resolves multiple extensions that way. Drupal is careful to scope the execution outcome to 'certain hosting configurations', which means the same stored file is a content-type confusion on one site and a web shell on another. The advisory's hunt guidance names the extensions that decide it: phar, php, pl, py, cgi, asp, js, html, htm, phtml.
attack_vector.privileges_required: low — PR:L. An account with any file-upload permission: attaching a file to content, a comment or a media entity. On a site with open registration and file-enabled fields that is close to unauthenticated.
attack_vector.complexity: low — AC:L, UI:N, no race. The uncertainty is not in the attack but in the outcome, which depends on a web-server setting the attacker cannot see and the site owner has usually never examined.
attack_vector.ai_factor: None. Reported to the Drupal security team by ufku, Mark Ferree, Frédéric G. Marand, Samuel Mortenson and Derek Wright; no AI assistance claimed.

prevention.what_would_have_worked: Updating Drupal core to 9.0.8, 8.9.9, 8.8.11 or 7.74; and, independently of Drupal, ensuring the web server does not resolve multi-extension filenames to the PHP handler, which is the configuration that turns the stored file into execution.
prevention.adequacy: The core update is complete for future uploads and, by Drupal's own account, incomplete for the site — it changes sanitization and removes nothing already stored. The web-server hardening is the more durable of the two because it removes the execution outcome for this flaw and for the next filename-handling defect in any application on that server, which is why it belongs alongside the update rather than behind it.

detection.what_would_have_worked: Running the advisory's own audit: sweep the public and private file directories, and the file_managed table, for names carrying a dangerous double extension without an underscore, prioritising phar, php, pl, py, cgi, asp, js, html, htm and phtml. Alongside it, alert on the web-server user executing PHP from the files directory.
detection.adequacy: Unusually good, because the vendor published the pattern and the extension list rather than leaving operators to derive them — the sweep is a deterministic filename query with a defined answer. Its limit is that it detects the artifact rather than the upload: a file renamed or moved after placement will not match, and the audit cannot distinguish a malicious double-extension name from a badly named legitimate one without inspecting content.

response.what_would_have_worked: Treating a matching file as placed rather than accidental: quarantine it, determine which account uploaded it from the file_managed ownership and the upload logs, review what that account could reach, and rotate the site's own secrets if the file was executable on that server.
response.adequacy: The account trace is the strong part, because PR:L means an account exists and Drupal records who uploaded each managed file — there is a name attached to the artifact, which is rarer than it sounds. The weak part is the execution question: whether the file ever ran depends on the web-server configuration at the time, and on a site that has since been migrated or reconfigured that is frequently unanswerable, so the credential-rotation decision has to be made on exposure rather than on evidence.

NIST-800-53-SI-10.gap: Drupal's underscore insertion is SI-10 implemented, and the defect is that it did not fire on certain names. SI-10 gives an assessor no way to establish that a working validation routine has a bypass, and it is forward-looking only — it governs input at the boundary and says nothing about files that crossed it before the routine was corrected, which is the half the advisory's remediation is about.

UK-CAF-B4.gap: Whether a stored filename.php.txt executes is a web-server property, and Drupal scopes the outcome to 'certain hosting configurations'. Standard PHP and web-server hardening baselines cover the .php handler mapping but not multi-extension name resolution, which is the setting that decides whether this CVE is MIME confusion or remote code execution on a given site.

AU-Essential-8-Patch.gap: Version scanning detects this reliably and the two-week window closes the Drupal half — the control works as designed and then stops. Nothing in the maturity model asks whether a file uploaded before the patch is still stored and still reachable, so Maturity Level 3 on patching coexists with continuing to serve the artifact.

new_control_requirements.name: CISA-KEV-RESPONSE-SLA
new_control_requirements.description: For any CVE listed in CISA KEV: deploy verified mitigation (patch, live patch, or documented compensating controls) within 4 hours of KEV listing or patch availability, whichever is later.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Drupal shipped 9.0.8, 8.9.9, 8.8.11 and 7.74 in 2020 and CISA listed the CVE on 2022-01-18 with a due date of 2022-07-18; EPSS reads 0.35350 at the 98.374th percentile on 2026-08-28, high enough to surface but well below the entries a score-ordered queue would take first. The control's value on this entry is what 'verified' has to mean. A core version check is not verification here, because SA-CORE-2020-012 makes the audit of previously uploaded files part of the remediation — so verified means the version is at or above the branch fix AND the double-extension sweep of the file directories has been run and come back clean.

new_control_requirements.name: ARCHIVE-CONTENT-TYPE-PROVENANCE
new_control_requirements.description: Document and file handlers must dispatch rendering or execution on the content-verified file type rather than on the displayed name or extension, and must carry provenance markings through to the stored or extracted content.
new_control_requirements.evidence: Attached for its first clause, which is this CVE exactly; the provenance-marking clause is a Windows Mark-of-the-Web mechanism and does not apply to a Drupal file directory, and that scope difference is stated rather than glossed. The flaw is dispatch on the displayed name: a stored filename.php.txt is served or executed according to how the web server reads its extensions, and Drupal's whole defence was a name transformation — inserting an underscore — rather than a determination of what the file is. Drupal's own audit guidance is a filename-pattern search across phar, php, pl, py, cgi, asp, js, html, htm and phtml, which is a name-based hunt for the consequences of a name-based dispatch. Serving stored uploads under a fixed, content-verified type removes the outcome regardless of what the filename says.

CVE-2020-11978.name: Apache Airflow Example DAG Command Injection

attack_vector.description: An attacker triggers a run of example_trigger_target_dag - a DAG that ships with Airflow and loads by default - supplying a run configuration whose message field carries shell metacharacters. The DAG's bash_task interpolates that field into the command it executes, so the injected commands run as the account running the worker or scheduler, depending on the executor in use.
attack_vector.privileges_required: any authenticated Airflow user per the vendor description; none in practice where the Experimental REST API's permissive default auth backend (CVE-2020-13927) is in place, which is the pairing both public exploits use
attack_vector.complexity: low - the DAG, task and conf field ship with the product and are identical across deployments, so the exploit needs no knowledge of the target; EPSS is 0.99189 at the 99.932nd percentile
